reviews.comment: I wish I could go back in time to stop myself. I have never met a more condescending professor that loves to trample on your feelings and your inadequacy for fun. She requires you to participate in class discussions but will humiliate you. She showed us a basic in class activity then expects us to spit out professional industry analysis.

Go look at course critique PLS1.Grades unpredictably and no rubrics 2.Did not put in over 50 percent of earlier grades until post final 3.Cares A LOT about participation and attendance; That said, she is very passionate and if you enjoy the material you will like it, but your grade likely will suffer still. Less than 35 percent of class got As

This class is so so so intense. She's very knowledgeable and will push you. You'll learn a lot, but expect stress, anxiety, and lost sleep. The semester-long group project is insane, and minimum effort won't pass. Participation is required in every discussion and her grading is very subjective, so you can put in the most and still fail. Good luck!
She is such a difficult teacher, the tests were nothing like the practice exams. She is scary.

i took her for both foundations and corporate strategy. it definitely takes work to get an A, and you actually have to do all of the readings. however, it is very rewarding in the end because the class discussions are really fun. go to office hours if you want to do better on exams. also please actually contribute to the group project.

Very harsh grader even if you put so much effort in. I had to take her for both foundations and corporate strategy, and it was awful. Lectures are very boring and long, be prepared to speak in every class for a good participation grade. Group essay at the end was a terrible idea and no matter how much you change, she doesn't give a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I have ever had. Just know that it is not a walk in the park, it requires an honest effort to understand the material and to contribute to discussions. You get a ton of value out of the class if you genuinely participate. Show up to class prepared, her office hours are very helpful. Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The case studies were actually very interesting, I enjoyed reading them. You have to participate a lot, and even if you do participate, you also have to go above and beyond for the group project. I had a very high grade until the group project, which was a very tedious and uninteresting process to do- lots of deliverables, and very strict grading.

She's very strict regarding participation. You gotta talk in her class. Her group essays are the worst idea ever. Her class discussion questions are confusing, and if you don't see what she wants, you will do poorly, especially on the exams. Overall, she's a very opinionated professor on strategy, which is based on several interpretations.

The TA's worked painstakingly hard to make a good final exam for us. Two days before our final exam, A professor who goes my the name of Kuldeep Meel said: "Hmmm this exam isn't hard enough, the students need to suffer more" so he made an insufferably difficult exam that doesn't reflect the review or ANYTHING for that matter. everything else great

Literally the hardest final I have ever taken. It was actually insane the disparity in difficulty between the coursework/homework and exams. Exams have very little structure and resources to help you perform well; it feels like the course is made for you to do poorly. He cares more about the grade distribution than the amount of work you put in.

Final exam was significantly harder than expected, and I felt that no amount of studying could have truly prepared me for it. Although we were allowed unlimited cheat sheets, they ended up being unhelpful. Additionally, the difficulty of the practice exam did not accurately reflect what was on the actual final.

TAs and prof tend to penalize hard work with harder subsequent assignments. TAs told us we are cooked for the final because project grades were higher than anticipated. The whole course felt like it was being made up as we went

A major assignment for this class is a competitive tournament against TA designed bots. Most students got an A, which was apparently unintended. Therefore, due to our good performance, the final has been adjusted to be significantly more difficult. It makes NO sense for students to be doing WELL and be punished for it, hence the rating.

Very nice prof, but lectures are not helpful for quizzes/hw. TA's run the lab completely separately from lecture, and there is clear disconnect between what is taught. He teaches his material well but the material on hw/quizzes are often different enough to stump you. TAs create hws & quizzes at professor discretion, but prof couldnt always help

He teaches very well but there is a slight disconnect in the material tested vs. what is taught in class. The TA's are not really helpful and even reading the textbook does not give the context needed. This is a survey course so it is different (3 exams + 1 final and 8 homework's other class has 4 homework's and 1 midterm and 1 final).

ngl at the beginning of the yr I hated this class, but Hillegass & TAs did great at taking feedback to fix the tests & structure. We had an AI tournament that was super fun and differen!  In general, I think I learned a lot from the hws (time-consuming but useful). Class is hard, but Hillegass is passionate about his subject and is a helpful prof!

Hillegass is the GOAT. Dude does it for the love of the game. He's a professor that actually cares about the content he teaches. Lecture is not required but I heavily recommend you go. You really don't want to miss out on them. If you genuinely put effort into learning AI for this class, you'll really come to enjoy his class, which I did.

Prof. Hillegass is a caring and genuine guy. From what I've heard, the exams were a bit harder than in previous semesters, but everything ended up working out, and studying for the difficult exams is rewarded with a deeper understanding of the material. The final competition project was super fun and was an amazing way to apply what we learned.

not an easy class by any means, but hillegass is a great lecturer who clearly knows and cares about the material. while i didn't get to interact with him directly, i've heard that he is very personable. there were some hiccups at the beginning of the semester, but he was more than fair with correcting and accounting for any issues with the course.

Hillegass is amazing! He's trying to change the class to be better so there have been some bumps with the exams and homeworks, but you can tell he really cares. It is challenging, but I think better for actually learning the content if you take it genuinely. Also has very real world experience that he likes to share.

If you want to actually learn the basics of AI, this is the best option. Hillegass is personable, you talk to him once and he makes his best effort to remember your name even in a class of 200+. Homework every week with only one submission a day but they provide local tests and if you pass those you get a 100 on the autograder.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
changed format to be very difficult and much more accelerated, making it difficult to understand. You basically have to read the textbook yourself.

Can only submit homework once a day. Exams are very difficult with a low average. Cool guy, but not worth it. Take the other section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: just take the other section.

The exams are extremely challenging (average 59, no curve given) and the homeworks are very time consuming and only 1 submission per day. The lectures are quick and do not give a good understanding of the topics. The textbook is also very challenging to read. Overall, this makes for a very challenging course.
Professor Hillegass was an absolutely amazing professor. By far the easiest professor I've ever had! The exams were so much fun! The professor is extremely nice and the projects are very easy!
Loved the exam and being challenged. I'm learning tons!
just take the other section

HW is already hard but the one-submission-a-day made it mad hard. Nice guy, hard course. I didn't like that all HWs and (especially) exams were completely autograded because no partial credits were awarded. At the end, there was a bonus quiz which is nice but some of the quizzes were really hard. Other sections are a lot easier.

Professor is very caring and willing to help. But the class is unexpected HARD. Other section is totally different and much easier(really). I think I prepared well for the exam and did well in the previous HARD homework, but the real one hurts me. Be ready to spend tons of hours weekly on this course if you really want to take his.

Professor only allows one submission to autograder per day, making it incredibly difficult to do homework. Homework is also extremely time consuming and covers material not taught in class. Material covered in lecture is very simple but then material expected to know in homework is complicated.

Amazing class. He really knows his stuff and wants to help the class succeed. Lectures were engaging and the homework concepts were cool. He added a lot of extra code so that you could visualize your results on the homework and play around with what you made after you finished.

Took both 3600 and 3510 with Professor Hillegass. Great guy, super understanding, and you'll actually learn the material. Explains things clearly and cares about students. One of the few professors where you walk away really knowing the content. He brings real industry experience, so he knows what actually matters. Highly recommend.
GOAT. He understands students better than any professor I've learned from at Tech.

I had him for both CS3600 and CS4641. He knows his stuff and does a pretty good job explaining difficult concepts. He was also successful in the industry and would drop lots of advice throughout the semester. He is also very caring and understanding. Overall, a very cool guy. Take him if you can
Passionate and nice young guy but extremely tough grading... no mercy
Big chiller. Great guy. Knows the stuff. Passionated about the class... when you're one of 20 people remaining in the class at end and learning about random stuff it's so much fun.
Hillegass is an amazing professor with incredible experience and life advice. Would definitely recommend him for any class.

Amazing professor, highly recommend. He has real-life experience in the industry which he brings to his lectures. Very caring, talk to him if you have a problem, he will more than likely help you out. Very smart, sometimes makes small mistakes on technicalities but then fixes it next class.
Great lecturer, fascinating life experiences, funny, very passionate about what he's teaching. The course itself is standardized materials.
Mega Squid. Evil class.

He doesn't know how to explain basics, bases 90% of the class on exam grades, and gives shallow examples straight from the textbooks for the entire lecture without taking the time to explain basic concepts beforehand. Gives 4-6 points of extra credit for every test, but doesn't do much.
Wow. Just wow. I absolutely cannot believe how bad this class is. It made me hate accounting. Don't take.

Really nothing good to say here. Most boring class I've ever taken. Lectures are extremely dry and monotone. 90% of your grade is tests that require extensive knowledge from the two $60-90 textbooks that he requires you to buy (one of them is his). 0/5. Don't take his class.
lectures are very drawn out and boring and does not give much material to review: often felt lost on what to study: did give some extra credit though
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reading was excessive, professor didn't really teach and rushed through the class to get us to buy his textbook. Not a fan at all.

This professor wasn't as bad as the reviews made him out to be. He's ok. lectures are kinda boring but he gives extra credit. Your final grade is based on tests and homework, there aren't any projects or anything like that. You get a cheat sheet on the tests. He grades pretty easy and gives partial credit where he can.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Schneider gets a lot of bad reviews but I personally thought he was fine. The lectures aren't the most engaging but if you can deal with that you'll be good. This definitely isn't the kind of class you'll be able to just skip lectures and teach yourself though, as he does sort of jump around the textbook and nothing will be posted on Canvas to help
Awful. grades solely on quizzes and exams which questions do not reflect the practice Q's he went over.

Did not care about his students - wrote chicken scratch notes for every lecture that were based off accounting text books. Talks way too fast and writes so quickly/poorly, that it is just better to read the textbooks. Exams are extremely difficult and practice problems were not representative of biomedical engineering applications. Avoid Avoid!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Class time purely goes over examples from the book - don't expect to go into lectures and actually learn anything, the expectation is that class time clarifies what you've already learned. 

In class he reflects his hand-writing on screen and its awfully scratchy - it's incredibly hard to read and follow along. 

Terribly downgrade from Deby
Expects you to know the content. Lectures are pointless. Read the textbook and Youtube or you will not learn.
Dr.Schneider was a great professor. I think a lot of people do not enjoy his teaching style because it is very old school. uses pen and paper, traditional note taking style, but you do learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prepare to teach yourself. Lectures are monotone, there's no time to solve the problems he works in class, so you're basically writing the answers without learning them. He wrote the textbook, so if you don't understand his lectures you won't understand the textbook.

Lectures somehow go too fast and too slow at the same time. He handwrites notes in class. Its supposed to line up with the textbook (that he wrote himself) but he jumps around like crazy and doesn't even cover everything in the chapter. Reading the textbook is equally difficult. Nothing is clear and practice problems don't have answers. Avoid avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Absolute no. Take literally anyone else. His exams are literally impossible. The supposed "study guide" are previous exams from other years that are a joke because they are nothing similar to the final exams. The 3 exams essentially make up 87% your final grade so either you fail or don't it's still stupid. 0/10.

By far the WORST professor at tech. Lectures and HW was extremely basic but when it came to the tests, they were very difficult and complex compared to what was practiced. This was a summer course so it was also extremely crammed and unrelatisitc, and required us to buy $170 worth of textbooks for 4 WEEKS. Do everything you can to avoid taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure if my mistake was taking this course online or not, but it was really difficult to learn the content from the online slides as the information on the slides didn't convey the information needed to do well on the quizzes. I had to learn majority of the course from someone else on YouTube (and it was still too late to save my grade).

Hes really a nice person and definitely knows a lot about accounting. I learned nothing from his lectures. Also he hand writes all the notes and projects them and I seriously hated that. his canvas page is so blank and is just the in-class hand written notes. I withdrew LOL. Good luck if you're taking him!

Course=Lecturing. Unless you have a pre-existing understanding of the material and therefore can read the posted lecture notes, you need to go to class nearly all the time. Class moves quick, minimal participation and HW, and has 4 decently hard tests, each with extra credit. Material is dry, and the hardest part is wanting to care, but doable
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was not a hard class, what was hard was trying to stay awake during lectures. He is the most bland person ever, but if you come you can get up to 10 bonus points on every test. You can use a sheet of notes on every exam - just fill it with example problems and his exams are not bad. That being said, he's rude and I hated this class. Take Dr. Rupar.

We were allowed one sheet of paper to write any notes to use during each exam. Also, we got 10 extra credit points for each exam, which you are almost guaranteed if you attend lectures and take notes. He was always clear about what we were and were not expected to know for the course. You definitely have to do practice problems to succeed, though.
Reading is important.
He did not care about the well-being of his students and when I asked for help he told me he could not do anything.

His lectures are designed to be way to heavy for the average biomedical engineering student learning financial accounting for the first time. 

He's not tech savvy and relies on hand written notes way too much.

Pretty heavy on tests and exams and covers the material way to in depth for what should be an introduction class.

Dr. Schneider teaches primarily by example, so if that's how you learn, take him. But I have to admit his class is not the most accessible. I personally enjoyed him, but many of my classmates disagreed. The extra credit opportunities were plentiful, you could get ~10 bonus points on each test.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schneider is not accessible at all. There are extremely few grades, and he is the least accommodating professor I have ever had. We had a gust professor come in to class one day and they themselves were critical about the structure of the class. Would not recommend, this was my second class with this professor. Never again.
Try to avoid it if possible. Homeworks and lectures do not prepare you for the tests.

Accounting is a hard class, but I really liked Dr. Schneider. He's a pretty funny dude if you give him the chance. You get about 10 points of extra credit per exam if you attend class and do the "bonus questions" at the end (they're easy if you paid attention). Exams are hard with mostly writing and few multiple-choice, but doable if you practice.

I grossly underestimated the amount of outside work that needed to be done for this class. Unless you are an accounting god, I highly recommend working on this class for at least 30 minutes a day. Do the self study problems or else you will fail the test! Nice guy, but the material is dry and hard to understand. EXTRA CREDIT IN CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He did not teach very well considering how hard the exams were.

DO NOT TAKE! We only have 5 grades that were all tough exams with VERY little practice problems to study. I had to buy quizlet plus to get answers to the book, so I would have more practice. You are basically teaching yourself the course because he only teaches through terrible recorded powerpoints! It was a STRUGGLE the whole semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the online class and I didn't enjoy it. It was almost all self study with little prof or ta support. Format was bare bones - plain ppts with attached audio, self study problems, few grades (6), and no extra credit. Asked about more practice qs & ec; he said what he provided was enough so I get the sense he's a you get what you get kinda prof

Took it asynchronous so it was pretty challenging. Just do all the practice sets given and read the textbook in detail and you should be fine enough, but there's very few grades, so recovering from bad grades is tough
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of those professors who is just there to deliver a lecture and hand out tests. Isn't good at answering questions regarding material and doesn't care if you understand the class material or not.

Attendance mattered. Could get extra credit in lectures. Tests were somewhat similar to examples in class. Best bet would be to do textbook problems. No note handouts which sometimes made things confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Schneider for an early short summer course in Acct. 1. He is a great lecturer, in my opinion, clearly explains each topic and almost always works an example from the book for each topic he is discussing. Provides a lot of EC opportunities like participating in class, and his homework is basically completion grade. Great prof IMO, made it fun

He's a great guy and really cares about his students. He sometimes has flashes of hands-on teaching, but most classes are him lecturing dryly and taking notes on the projector. He moves quickly and it's difficult to keep up. He uses his own textbook, so no new perspective there. The subject matter doesn't help. Rounded up my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Schenider is a solid professor. He knows his class is an ISYE elective and expects that level of participation. Open note open book tests make the textbook a must, and a day of cramming will get you an A on every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Schneider is incredibly boring. The class is very dry. Make sure you study the problems he gives in class as well as the self study solutions. If you know those well, the tests will be easy. If not, you'll bomb them. He didn't give participation like he said he would. Make sure you participate an excessive amount if you want the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He can be quite condescending when answering questions, but the class overall is a piece of cake. Open book/open note tests, plus there's extra credit just for class participation. The class isn't interesting, but it's easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: At first, he is kind of intimidating, but then you realize he's pretty cool. He's done a lot of really cool things like for example, he worked on a movie called "The Accountant" and helped right the script for it. Also he is kind of a savage. He will call you out in class for talking and it's kinda funny tbh. But just pay attention and you're fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He gives you a lot of opportunities to make a good grade in this class; there isn't a final, the tests aren't cumulative, and all four tests are open-notes and open-textbook. However, your grade is 92% tests and 8% homework. I didn't study at all for the first test and bombed it; you do actually have to study. DO the practice problems!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. He wrote a terrible textbook and makes it mandatory to buy it, which should be illegal. He goes through examples with little explanation, and does not give much oppurtunity to ask questions, nor does he act like he wants to answer them. I would take another professor if possible.

Dr. Schneider is a professor who is very knowledgeable about Accounting and really makes an effort to help students succeed in the class. His Tests are open note and open book, which with some studying and reading are very manageable tests. Participation is  huge extra credit opportunity, so go to class. Overall a great professor!

Mr. Schneider knows accounting very well and ask lots of questions during class to get class participation, but I could never participate unless I read the chapters before hand.  Its all about working problems.  The material isn't hard but its not an easy A.  He isn't very eager to answer questions and can often be condescending.

He is a terrible teacher. Wrote his own textbook so he expects everyone to be on his level. Only works examples during class - no actual teaching. Tests are hard and very long; having notes is no help at all during the exam. Rude to students and doesn't care if you pass/fail or even understand the material.

Go to class, and pay attention. He makes it extremely easy to learn as long as you take the time to do the homework and ask questions if necessary. He doesn't make it boring, and really knowledgeable about the subject.

I had no interest in or knowledge of accounting prior to my class with Prof. Schneider.  We covered financial and managerial accounting (2 textbooks) at an extremely fast pace, but he was extremely clear in his lectures.  Tests were difficult, but manageable.  Overall, I would definitely recommend taking a course with Prof. Schneider.

One of the hardest teachers in accounting. Doesn't care if you pass or fail. Wont accept anything late. He's a good person and knows accounting very well, but when it comes to helping you pass, your on your won. All tests are open book and notes including final, but he makes the tests really long so you pretty much have to know everything cold.
Accounting Nazi - postpone graduation if necessary to avoid him.

Flipped classroom, lectures are unclear if you don't have a background in digital design, not accessible outside of class (never responds on Piazza), and there is an immense lack of practice material. He is a nice guy, but it did not make this class any easier. This class was my first B. His exams were confusing since he used Gemini to make them.

The flipped classroom style while not for all, worked very well for me in this course. Professor Anderson was very good at assisting students with homework and tests and really wants students to focus on learning and not about the grade they will receive.

I took his flipped classroom class, in-person lectures were pretty useless unless u directly asked him something about the HW and the HW answers are searchable online. Tests are straightforward and not worth much but concept heavy. He's a funny dude tho his lectures are just him talking about his stories and he lets you out early.

Dr. Anderson is a very nice person and makes very easy tests. The only issue is that his hw assignments are crazy difficult and he's not very good at teaching. You will be fine if you take his course, but be prepared to teach yourself a lot of things and be very confused at times. The class ramps up very hard.

Anderson is not an all star at explaining topics but the man tries very hard to explain it as well as he can. He is available for questions and extra help. Hes a good guy that cares whether you learn it or not and you get a good grade. He is actively trying to get better as a teacher each semester. We should want more professors like him.

Anderson is like a father-figure. He's very funny and passionate and likes to tell stories. Lectures aren't as helpful as recitation, in fact, attendance is extraordinarily optional. Worth going to class to learn about practical DSP applications, such as how to protect your hearing.

Professor Anderson was a nice guy who was pretty funny during lectures with his stories. However, he taught DSP terribly with slides that he didn't even make and he rambled about concepts in a non-intuitive way that didn't help prepare me for the tests at all. Recitation was much more useful, and I learned more there as we did actual practice.
Great professor.  Makes lectures interesting with his stories and does a good job teaching the material.  He's very helpful if you need it.
Awesome prof!

Basically, I didn't learn much if anything from lecture. I learned most stuff about DSP from recitation. By far the hardest class I've taken at Tech, and I honestly don't think it really matters who you get for a professor. Anderson's a nice guy, but isn't a great lecturer. I stopped going about halfway through the year.
pretty good

He is super chill and make the class as easy as it could be while still being fair. Orgo 2 is gonna be hard no matter what but his practice worksheets and practice exams were super similar to the tests so there were never any surprises. He has EC 15 pts on the final and remediation for exam 3 plus you can exempt final with 78 avg on midterms.

Lectures were overall very boring, I think Dr. Azoulay seems like the type that definitely cares more about his research than actually teaching. Overall I was very reliant on the Wiley textbook, and I would really only show up to class to get PRS points. Tests were pretty hard but fair, and it was easy to get 100s on homeworks which were worth 35%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If your goal is to get an A in orgo 2, Azoulay is a great option. He isn't the best lecturer but grading scheme is awesome. 40% of the grade was homework/participation, and the lowest test grade was dropped (including final). As long as you read textbook and do all the practice problems its chill, just be prepared for self learning.

Exams were detailed and difficult, but his grading scheme makes it near impossible to fail. He does care, but he is absent a lot. I asked him for help after making a VERY low grade and he sent me a riddle.

Orgo II is a notoriously difficult class no matter who your teacher is. Dr. Azoulay was clear on what was expected and put out great practice materials. He was also very accessible outside of class in office hours and by appointment. The first exam might humble you (like it did to me), but if you put in the work in this class, you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Azoulay is solid for 2312, way better than Kim. His lectures are fine, you'll have to self-study a lot as a few things he covers in lecture aren't in the textbook and vice versa, and both are testable. Posts a lot of practice sheets and exams though, if you can do those you'll be fine. He also drops the lowest test score which includes the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolute goat of organic chemistry. Very nice and always gives extensions or corrects prs points if it's not working. Tests are very fair and doable. Lectures do lack the level of detail we get tested on but honestly if you actually study you'll be ok. Great professor overall and he's very chill.

He prepares us well for tests with homeworks and practice tests, which are representative of the real tests. If you don't understand a concept, speak to him after class or in office hours, or speak to a TA. This can be a tough class, but the people that complain are the ones usually not showing up to class every time.

The other class has insane curves. They get half credit back on every q they get wrong while we just get cooked. How is this fair? Even exam 1, class avg in the other class was like 50ish while ours was 60 smth. yet they got at least half credit back while we got nothing.

He was generally chill and has awesome TAs. Likes to read straight off the PowerPoint slides in lecture. Exams were very straightforward and what we were prepared for. Grading scheme sucks compared to other professors, so you might get screwed over compared to other available sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wasn't an amazing lecturer— sometimes it felt like he cared more about his lab than the class especially when he would bring it up super often but he was really nice and his TA is amazing and carries the class for sure. Super accessible out of class though, and has a ton of extra credit. Definitely not a bad person, just not the best at lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff but he usually just reads from slides. The TA was amazing and really helped me learn the entirety of the course. From all the outside of class opportunities from recitation and review sessions she helped me figure out the best way to learn the content for this course. They care about the students and want to see them succeed.

Azoulay is not the best lecturer but is super nice, really cares about his students, and is super accessible. Exams were very straight-forward (very similar to posted practice exams) and he gives so so so many opportunities for extra credit. Really wants to see his students get and A and is wiling to help if you reach out. Would recommend!

He mostly read off the slides, but I enjoyed the class. Grading criteria was clear and we were offered multiple extra credit opportunities. 40% of grade is HW (completion), 45% tests, and 15% final. The TA Abby was really good, and her lectures were AMAZING. If you read the textbook before class, getting an A is completely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He literally read the slides word for word and does very little teaching. The TA Abby was awesome though and she taught sometimes. He also scales the class so an 85 is an A, a 75 is a B, and a 60 is a C, so that helps.

Forty percent of the grade (HW) is an easy 100 as long as you do it. The other 60% comes from exams which are pretty straightforward. If you do the practice problems the TA gives (the TA is awesome) and read the textbook, you'll be fine. Azoulay isn't the best lecturer as he mostly reads off slides, but he's really nice. Would recommend!

Although he's not the best lecturer (reads straight off the slides which are straight out of the textbook), he made it so easy to do well in his class. Homework (which was basically completion from the online textbook) was 40 percent of our grade. And y'all honestly his tests were not bad at all if you do the review/practice. Good choice for orgo 2

Not the best lecturer and mostly reads off slides to explain material. Makes the expectations of the course simple however and the HW is super simple. Class comes down mainly to tests which aren't out of the ordinary and are relatively straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good amount of grade was from homework, which was good. The average on the exams was usually around a 60, no curve is applied. Would choose another professor if possible. TA was great though!

I'll go against the grain here and say that Azoulay isn't a terrible option, especially for a class as notorious as Orgo II. Trust me when I say that it could be a LOT worse. While he was absent for a good bit of semester due to his research, it's entirely possible to do well in this class. Just keep up with the material - it moves quickly!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really chill dude, but not an amazing teacher. He's nice if you go up and talk to him, but was absent a lot in class and his TA did a fair bit of the lectures. When she did, she would teach 1000x better than him. Without his TA, who was the most amazing TA I've ever had, this class would have been really hard for me.

The material is simple and the tests are very straightforward, but you have to learn and memorize everything yourself. He rarely shows up to class (GTA teaches for him) and if it weren't for the GTA we wouldn't have any prep material/piazza responses. Homework is on wileyplus and is annoying, but a grade boost. Does not care if we actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Get ready to self-study. Dude comes into class and speed reads off the textbook slides (if he's not at a research conference, which is often). TA carried this class-did all recitations, made worksheets/exams, monitored piazza, answered questions, etc. Very clear professor cares more about his research than his students.
He preys on his students. Stay away.
Too technical, experience given for granted, too many speakers.

One of those teachers yaps each and every class period. This class has a lot of potential, but unfortunately, professor Asensio makes it far too theoretical. If you want a relatively easy class and need to fulfill degree requirements, take this class and push through. If you want to learn, STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Offers no learning value.

OS is always a brutal class and projects are always hard, but his lectures focus much more on system design over anything. Incredibly knowledgeable for system design, but in terms of the concepts you'll either have to have a strong foundation in 2200 or self-learn to keep up.

He has no concern for learning. The course is designed to be a rough experience. The course is not well organized, has no clear guidance or material, ridiculous exams, and unrealistic time requirements.

The professor is great at teaching and is very knowledgeable. However, as a course coordinator, the course is set up in a way to ensure all tables are turned against you. Nobody is helpful when it comes to labs and they ask hard viva questions. Exams cover nuances never discussed in lecture. Exam syllabus was vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's clearly an intelligent guy and knows his stuff very well, but is exceptionally rude and egotistical.

Really cares about students (stays after lecture to answer questions, brings in qualified guest lecturers, attends lab sections, semi-active on Piazza) and is highly knowledgeable on system design. Yes the class is hard (projects are time-consuming), but you learn a lot in this class

I don't attend lecture, but the slides are pretty good. I have a really tough time paying attention, but he definitely got better as the semester went on. Labs take time, but the work is proportional to the reward. Exams are awful.

This is the worst course I have taken at Tech by a landslide. I love sysarch and until this class always found my courses reasonable, but this is on a different level of cruelty. When taking this class you have two choices -- spend 20+hr/week on just this ONE course, or get a bad grade. Alexey is rude and out-of-touch with the student experience.
very passionate professor. hopefully classes can be brought back to 1hr 15min because it is clearly needed. i agree that the exams are atypical but i think they are fair
Exceptional professor, makes learning OS fun and engaging. Certainly a very difficult and time demanding class, but overall very worth it investment.

Lectures are interesting and the material covered is super useful to industry. Exams so poorly written, don't understand how a 10yr+ course has exams like this, they are literally a waste of everyones time.
The lectures are very engaging. The labs are hard, but they helped me learn a lot. The class has an interesting emphasis on tradeoffs that I haven't come across before.

Really knows subject matter and it's clear hes excited to teach, I came in with a not so amazing understanding of cs 2200, the main pre req, and was able to fully understand all the material. He tends to relate things back to real life practices and decision making when desinging systems. TA's are  cracked too, just ask questions!!

Very unapproachable professor and lectures are very mediocre. In terms of labs, they are insane and made them worse by adding additional parts to each project from the previous semesters. I also had an issue with my partner refusing to work, mentioned it to him and he did not really care to solve it so had to double the work...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful at teaching, and extremely unhelpful with clarifications on the homework's or the subject matter. None of the TA's knew what they were doing and made the already difficult class that much harder. The expectations in this class were impractical. And the professors attitude in an out of the class was overall negative.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor was horrendous at teaching and not helpful whatsoever. The TAs provided limited help and didn't seem to care much, just like the professor. It could've been a good class but alas it wasn't. Please avoid this class, the course content is sub-par, the difficulty is insane and expectations are unrealistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor and TAs, I did not enjoy the class, he was very unhelpful with matters such as labs and especially exams, my online exam refreshed 5 times but they blamed it on me, no help provided. The professors tone on emails seemed very unwelcoming and unfriendly. Labs were insanely long and expected effort was not correctly disclosed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He seems to care a lot about the source material, but it was a struggle to follow. The projects are absurdly time consuming and the instructions were unclear. If a certain few TAs didn't exist this class would be impossible if you're new to the topic. Lots of information but I feel like I barely gained any knowledge due to the lack of clarity.
Amazing course. Had a lot of fun going to lecture, the projects were helpful. Learned a ton!

Really interesting lectures, but I recommend this class be avoided if at all possible: the projects take absurd amounts of time. I typically spent in excess of 15 hours per week working on them. The project specs are always very unclear, and getting clarifications out of the course staff is time-consuming, often futile, and invariably frustrating.

Robinson is a passionate and knowledgeable lecturer. He breaks down topics in a digestible way and welcomes all questions. BUT he gives zero partial credit for exams. He gives no points for showing work or explaining your process, so you literally have to know the right answer. Also, the final exam is straight evil and again NO PARTIAL CREDIT!
Great professor. Very humorous. Answers questions helpfully.

His lectures were really good, but the rest of the class was not great. The labs take way longer than the designated lab time, and the exams and lab quizzes are a massive time crunch. Thankfully, even though it takes a lot of time, it's not difficult to get good grades on the homeworks and lab reports.

Dr. Robinson is an amazing lecturer - writes everything out on the board. Cleared up many misconceptions from 2040. Exams are super time-limiting. Labs are extremely time-consuming. If you can separate the very stressful exams and lab structure from the great lecture content he is amazing.

~6 hours a week on lab. 6 HW ~3hr . Lectures are GREAT. you must go! Nice person but you need to contact him in person, because he is very slow to email. he has a lot going on (W/F in office only i think). Homeworks and exams graded very harshly, and prep material is limited, but I dont care because I like Robinson and I learned a lot. ~4 pt curve?

He is a good lecturer but has absolutely no concern for the well-being of students. Never replied to students' emails, and impossible to find for office hours. He had confusing due dates and assigned difficult homework, barely relevant to the class, which made everything seem poorly organized.

Robinson was a good professor, he had a deep understanding of the class content and taught relatively well. However, the structure of the course is very frustrating and the lab manual that guides this course is severely outdated and needs updating. There is no extra or supplementary material to learn from. Lab's are long and not well explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Robinson is very good at breaking down complex topics into simple ideas, but his lectures are only 50 minutes so they move fast and aren't long enough. Labs each week take varying amounts of time and closer to the end you almost will have to go to open lab hours. Though, if you read the theory in the lab manual beforehand it'll halve the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Labs are long, expect to go in during open lab, around 4-6 hrs on each one in general. Tests are straightforward but short on time since its 50 mins. Material is gone over quick, mainly use the lab manual/practice tests to study. There is barely any partial credit so double check your test and HW with multisim.

Robinson is a super strict teacher that grades very harshly on exams and has the TAs grade just as harshly for quizzes and homework. He sets the class grading up so that he can achieve a similar grade distribution every semester (mostly Bs and some A's and C's, but hardly anyone fails), so just do your best and put in a ton of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The time taken per lab depends on mistakes, not knowledge. 2hr labs can take 9hrs, so you'll be using open lab. Lab quizzes and tests are tough, this class is graded like a weed-out class. Definitely use office hours, 1 hr/week of lecture probably isn't enough, and prof is REALLY good in office hours

Amazing lab. The assignments are well written and really help you learn. Prof gives extra time if he notices a lab is taking longer than usual. Lab reports are also pretty chill, as long as you did the work.

I don't understand all the bad reviews about Dr. Robinson. He is a very caring and helpful professor in my opinion. His lectures are extremely helpful and he's always down to help. The only thing I wish he did was be a bit lenient on grading exams.

This class is only lab. You have to come to every single one or else you will not do well. You are expected to know everything before class. The lab is run by TAs and all you do is get an experiment that takes 3 hours and a hard quiz each lab. This class was literally the bane of my existence as a non-ECE major.

He cares more about your final answers on tests than how you got there and tests go wayy above and beyond lecture material, which isn't great because other than a lab manual that doesn't cover that material either, you don't have a textbook. Also, tests don't provide enough space or time for you to finish.
Cool class! Play Name That Frequency!

My favorite professor at Tech. He grades the memo very thoroughly, but I felt like the quizzes were graded generously. Gives great feedback, and definitely wants specifics. Make sure you always read all instructions. Its very important to build a relationship with him outside class, he is a great guy and has lots of good advice and connections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor super knowledgable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Barke was a cool guy and I would love to hang out with him and have a coffee. BUT, I lowkey would never take this class again. He's a very niche grader and sometimes would give me and my peer different grades for writing the same thing on quizzes. Exam and quizzes follow the written format and your most important assignment will be the memo.
Enjoyed this professor, however, extremely reading heavy. Quizzes are very very specific so you must know pretty much everything from the text book. Doesn't reply to emails very much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think this was a pretty enjoyable class and I definitely learned a lot. It is very hard and you need to read and UNDERSTAND everything. He has very specific quizzes where he looking for a specific answer based on the readings and his final is cumulative and based on lectures (wish I knew that) as well. Overall he is a good professor.

Dr. Barke's class was one of my favorites. While his exams can be overly specific, they're almost entirely based on readings, so make sure to do them before each exam. For the policy memo, take advantage of office hours. He is very happy to help and you will do much better on it if you go to him before. Read all his instructions and rubrics well.

Great professor who is also an amazing connection to have if you're pursuing PubP! His lectures can be a little dry, but he has great stories from his years in the policy world. Make sure to establish a relationship with him and get him invested in your memo topic, like other people have said, I feel like he grades better if you talk to him more.

great professor, crammed readings by skimming before quizzes, learned a lot, follow writing tips for memo (no contractions, avoid "all," "every," "nobody," etc. introduce yourself (if he knows you and your interests as a person I feel like he grades you better.

Dr. Barke is one of my favorite profs! His lectures aren't always the most helpful for tests, but idc b/c he is very interesting and shares his vast experience and expertise. He does have strong views but backs it up with evidence and doesn't disregard other POVs. Tough grader, but if you read and follow directions, you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tough grader. The tests are just "define that word in the bottom of the slides from 3 months ago." The guy has strong political views and does not appreciate any feedback from class other than the one that praises the course. In the final class survey he literally said that only wants positive feedback and nothing else.

Does not acknowledge any point of view other than his own. Tried asking for help and got accused of my identity and background. Little useful feedback on papers. Vague criteria. Unproductive lectures. The course was a waste of time and money.

A mandatory class without any options for time and professor. The class is 99% life stories. Highly politicied, but does not admit that. Absolutely unclear syllabus. Strict grading, unclear rubric. Narcissisic, but pretends to care about you. The class in 2 words: "recommended requirement"

Professor Barke is the reason why I love PUBP so much. While he does require a lot of reading, detailed studying for quizzes and assessments, and counts attendance, he will prepare you to be a better writer and policy student. His lectures are interesting and passionate and he was so helpful in connecting me to people in the world of policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Barke cares about you and your future, and he gives genuine feedback on lots of the work you submit. I believe this class exponentially improved my writing style. Barke also has a ton of real-world experience to back his lectures. Would recommend getting to know him outside of the classroom. He has lots of connections!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Barke is a very intelligent professor and has very insightful lectures. However, you have to sit in your seat for 75 minutes straight and listen to a man talk, and his class offers little class discussion. His class also requires LOTS of reading, and on exams, if you don't read the material, you won't get a good grade.

Tips 1. He's professional and warm at the same time. He's hard to hate, but he's a strict grader. 2. Do the reading!!! 3. He looks for a specific type of answer. Quiz answers need to reflect, not regurgitate. 4. He's a big part of the program. Learn a lot from him through office hours. 5. Don't do the policy memo the night before. Use libguides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is VERY heavily focused on reading - if you don't read, don't expect any higher than a B. Class is a LOT of work and lectures can get VERY boring. He is a very meticulous grader with NO extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Barke's class is a tough challenge, but your time and effort are worthwhile investments. He keeps every lecture interesting and assigns engaging homework. The reading is moderately heavy in this course and will require 2-3 hours a week. Overall, great professor and I would recommend putting the work in for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Barke is a wonderful professor; easily accessible and has parties with his students! I wouldn't have taken POL 1101 with anybody else!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: -hard tests. study guides are basically "repeat everything in the textbook" and don't mesh with the test. -attendance required. -not interesting, what he says isnt really on the test. -tests are all writing and explaining. -you could definitely find a better teacher, he's been one of my least favorites. -a lot of work for a poli1101 class. :Z
Amazing professor.  I am definitely not a fan of political science, but his class is definintely worth taking.  The tests are difficult, but he's always willing to help.  Highly recommended.
No Comments
He is very good, and the class is fun! just study hard for the test!

I love her, simply. Actually goated, made my semester so much less stressful for circuits by moving class online I'm so serious. Class was basically self paced and she is actually really good about responding to emails and her TA's too. W prof and so chill and take if you are not interested in pursuing circuits
Amazing professor, Gives a tons of extra credit. My only complaint is that she cancels class regularly and posts online lectures instead.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor. Provides amazing notes. Has a tendency to cancel classes and keeps online classes instead. However, overall lectures are very clear. The exams are similar to practice questions give during class. posted a 5 % extra credit lab and also gave a 10 point extra credit question during exam.

i think people aren't noting that her notes are actually really good. I learned a LOT from them, really they are the best way my friends and I learned the content for 2020. I understand the async part wasn't excusable but yall at least give credit where credit is due.

One of the least professionally run things I have ever been a part off. Exams run by TAs without guidance and a majority of lectures where canceled without makeup. Enough extra credit given to help guarantee an A, but I would recommend anyone else so you can actually learn the material. Complete self-study, but lecture videos provided.

Honestly don't understand the hate. She is basically async but her lectures are great and if you really lock in you can easily get the content. This class was still pretty hard in my opinion especially the hw but the extra credit and curve at the end makes getting an A easy. A low stress class where you can focus on learning material which is great

Everyone is undercutting the fact that you do not necessarily need ECE 2020's knowledge to succeed in future ECE classes, so it is absolutely okay in my honest opinion that she is somewhat inactive in class so long as we get A's, seriously. It's not that deep.

She curves super generously so you will probably get an A, but you will come out very unprepared for the future. This is why she has decent reviews, her classes are always super easy and she turns them all remote with pre recorded lectures. Paying 17k out of state tuition for this level of teaching is embarrassing. Do not take for 2020.

Lectures basically all online (as other reviews say), some are Zoom and others are prerecorded videos from years ago. Notes are spread across multiple different places so it's hard to compile and understand everything. Midterm 1 content is easy but gets way harder after. Not hard to get an A but came out of the class feeling unprepared for future

Nowhere to be seen. In-person class, but provides online pre-recorded lectures or disorganized handwritten notes. Important information is often hidden in multiple paragraphs of written fluff. Made it very difficult to learn the material.

She registers her classes as in person but then moves them to remote EVERY SINGLE SEMESTER. As someone who needs to be in person to learn, it is extremely frustrating. She just posts pre recorded lecture videos as if it was always planned to do this. I went into ece 2031 knowing very little. Avoid at all costs, take a prof who actually teaches

This class was more difficult than it needed to be. It was listed as a synchronous course, but the professor stopped giving lectures after the first week. Tests weren't bad, as they were similar to the mock exams given. Overall, I got a good grade but did not learn much.

No prior knowledge for class- the first unit's lectures all explained it well but after that became more confusing and harder to follow with lacking explanations and only recorded lecture videos to follow. Felt harder than it should have to learn the content properly and get help for it. Didn't learn much. Self study course as someone else said.

Professor Bhattacharya curves generously (more than she states), so most students get an A. However, she was often absent and her lectures unclear. Homework, labs, and midterms are tough and graded harshly, but the final has enough extra credit to help your grade. Fine if you just want credit, but not ideal for building a strong foundation.

Lecture videos were fine and sometimes helped/gave the answers to the homework. Labs were straightforward and not that long. The first exam caught me off guard due to the length so had to lock in after that. Make sure you have time to watch 3 hour videos for each lecture over the summer.

Course was very hands off. Async 2 weeks in and self studying is default. TA's did majority of all grading, to be precise, all grading I believe. Recorded/posted lectures were helpful when self studying. Tests were difficult and open book (so moderately hard with notes) with mock exams posted before the tests. A self study course tbh.

This class should not have been as difficult as it was. It's tough to learn online when the prof isn't really accessible and everything is async.

Other than that, her videos are pretty good and the tests aren't too bad. She is also caring, gave me 2 extensions after I emailed her.

Took her class online during the summer. She hosted class during the first week, but never did so again. All we got for the rest of the semester were lecture recordings from years ago at 360p quality. Class/content itself is not bad, and her "mock exams" are very similar to the actual exams. She also allows cheat sheets, so the tests weren't bad.
This professor makes the class async 2 weeks in. She dors not match with the textbook so you can't get outside help. She disappeared man this sucks. World class education my ass.
I had no prior knowledge going into this class but her explanations are amazing. Take her if you can for any course ever

Very prepared, well organized. Also good at explaining the material but be prepared to have online zoom lectures. Attendance is not mandatory and she opens a zoom call every day and records every lecture.
She's patient and nice. Recommend.

She's nice and explains things well, but where is my professor man. This class started synchronous remote and is now asynchronous. You can catch her on office hours, but they've been changing from 3pm to 8am. This class should be easy and I might just be dumb because I'm struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: HW is much harder than the topics covered in the lecture, but the exams are very similar to the mock exams she gives (but slightly harder). This is a class you should probably not take online since there is so much info to cover. Otherwise, the prof is chill.

Probably would have been better in person but this class was run very poorly online. Be prepared for random assignment dates, policies that change at a moment's notice, and unclear instructions for all labs.
This professor did a great job of teaching circuit analysis. She couldn't always attend the class in person but her online lectures were extremely helpful when studying for exams.

Very interesting course and Bhattacharya's notes are very organized and easy to follow. She frequently cancels classes, we probably only met in person around 50% of the time this semester. She is very accommodating and moved midterms and homework deadlines when the class requested. Overall I enjoyed it, but her zoom lectures can be boring.
Explained material very clearly and set expectations upfront. Two midterms and a final that accounted for 70% of the grade but weren't particularly difficult.

Amazing lectures. All of them are recorded so catching up is very easy.
Exams are super fair.
However be prepared to have randomly canceled classes (Online instead).

She is very nice and is good at teaching this class. The exams were very easy, the labs were pretty easy, and the homework was hard, leading to a high GPA and averages. But, if I am paying good money to attend a university, I want my teachers to be in person teaching. She fully left halfway through the year, leaving us with a TA who I felt bad for.
Was absent most of the semester, but was accessible essentially immediately to make up for it with good prerecorded lectures

She was, while she was around, a very nice and caring teacher. She frequently cancelled class but always had a video lecture or zoom call ready. However, she went on medical leave very early on into the semester, and left a grad TA (who, granted, was an awesome dude) in charge of the class. If you're bad with online lectures, you won't learn much.

Prof Nivedita is one of the best teachers I had at Tech! She reached out to me after I performed poorly on a test and explained how I could do better going forward! I haven't seen a more caring Professor! Her class notes are also amazing and she explains hard concepts clearly.

I took her a few years ago and she was very nice and caring (responds quickly but cancels every class), but does not teach you the material. I know it can be tempting to take a class for an easy A but if you care about your education, please do not take her for 2040. I am still struggling to catch up after having her as a professor in 3040/3043

Amazing professor! Would take her again and again. Everything was so clear and her notes were so detailed and clear as well. Truly enjoyed the class! She's caring and approachable, and always ready to help. Class was asynchronous and had many TAs, which was great! Tests reflected exactly what we learned in the lectures, very useful material!

Prof. Bhattacharya is a very caring professor and can explain tough concepts to students very well. However, she has a habit of turning classes originally advertised as in-person to solely online classes. She has done this numerous times in different classes too. Once again, really good professor, but that is my only criticism.

A good amount of lectures ended up being remote, and she posts all the materials in terms of notes, slides, and lecture videos which is very helpful. The lectures are very slow pacing and have a lot of examples which could be good or boring.

Dr. Bhattacharya is the only professor I've ever had that has cared enough about me to check in after tests. She has an awesome sense of humor, & always made time to meet with me when I needed it! Her class wasn't easy, & I felt that it got disorganized towards module 6 & the final exam - but over all the professor alone made this class! 10/10 prof

She is the best. Extremely helpful at all times, very kind and really just wants to help you learn. She is very quick in email response time and is very willing to help you with any questions on the homework and is super understanding. Class went from synchronous online -> async but her video lectures are good and she explains concepts well.

Prof. Bhattacharya is an amazing teacher and her class notes are the best! She provides a lot of learning resources and explains concepts very clearly. But what stands out most of all in my opinion is her respect for the students.

Prof Bhattacharya is extremely knowledgeable and very good at explaining difficult concepts. I understand problems so much better once she explains it. She is also very kind and understanding and helped me with a homework very late at night before it was due.

Overall, Prof Bhattacharya is a great lecturer and very caring as well as understanding.  She patiently answers any student's question during lecturer and with minimal wait time outside of lecture (i.e. piazza/email).  The only reason I don't give a 5/5 is because she lectured online the whole semester; the class was supposed to be in-person.

She was a true gem virtually. Whenever I needed some clearing up or had a question on piazza, she answered in LESS THAN AN HOUR. Her lecture videos were very well done. Even when I had technical issues on the first exam, she let me email my exam to her with no complications, she was totally understanding. I WISH I COULD TAKE HER AGAIN!

One of the best professors at Georgia Tech hands down. Professor Bhattacharya is very caring and she really just wants you to understand the material. If you have any problems she will understand and help. The only downside is that the class was fully online this semester, but at least the lectures are recorded.
Easy but asynchronous lectures make hard to learn. We did not finish the material in time which was later in 3043 so I wasn't well prepared.

She's good at lecturing, but is so lazy. Class went from in-person, to online zoom calls, to asynchronous classes from PREVIOUS semesters, and she cancelled review sessions over and over again. All of her excuses is because she's "feeling unwell."

Professor Bhattacharya was very knowledgeable and delivered clear and informative lectures.
She doesn't go too fast, and you can tell she cares about her students. Also answers questions thoroughly.
Very clear on how to succeed in the class, and she provides numerous resources like class notes and practice
exams to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bhattacharya is one of the best professors I have had at GT. She is very accessible and helpful. She will respond to emails very quickly, and if your question can not be answered via email, she will set up a private call with you. As a non-ECE major, I felt she did a fantastic job at making the content understandable and not too complex.

This is my second course with Prof Bhattacharya. She is extremely knowledgeable and very compassionate. Her lectures and notes are amazing and she explains hard concepts in a clear manner. Her classes always fill up very fast so register early!

Prof Bhattacharya is the best teacher I have had at Tech! Although she was ill this semester, she did video calls all the time to help students. She once hopped on a call with me at 11pm on a Sunday as we had a HW due. She really wants her students to succeed and is very passionate about teaching and the subject matter. Her class notes are the best

She is a very lenient grader and gives a lot of extra credit, but lectures are a drag and poorly delivered. They started as going into class to watch a video call, and turned to watching asynch recordings of previous semesters' lectures instead, making the class feel very unpersonalized. Many of my classmates and I have never even seen her face.

Really caring professor, even gave extra credit opportunity. Really cares about teaching. Homework was reasonable, and the projects. Grading on exams was reasonable. Would def recommend taking her again!

Professor Bhattacharya did a good job overall at teaching ECE 2040. Class grades tended to be pretty high, but this semester most of the course ended up being taught remote asynchronously (although it was listed as fully in-person). So a lot of it ended up being self-taught through videos and notes. Lecture was about 2.5 h/w and homework was 2 h/w.

Prof Bhattacharyas lectures and notes are amazing. She was very accommodating throughout the semester and I learnt way more than I expected. The videos were very helpful in studying for the exams and overall the course prepared me for a career in Computer Engineering.

Bhattacharya is one of the most caring professors, always willing to help students or move deadlines/exams upon request. However, my experience turned quickly from (expected) in person to fully online asynchronous. She would just post lectures from previous semesters which led to lack of interaction/motivation. Tainted my experience.
Learned so much. Difficult class but Bhattacharya makes it much better. Class was very flexible but don't fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's so kind and caring. I found out that I had three midterms land on one day (one of them being for her class), so I emailed her about it on a Saturday night, and 10 minutes later, the test was moved forward a week. Her lectures are great: she makes relatively hard concepts easy to understand, and if you ever need help, she's there for you.

Dr Bhattacharya is the G.O.A.T.  simply the best. She taught a rather difficult online semester and was remarkably patient and understanding. I never had a more caring professor at Tech. Take all her courses.
Dedicated to teaching and the university, but not very responsive when communicating over email or in person.
She's the best. If you can take her. Made 2035 and a tough online semester so much more bearable. she is the best.
Legitimately one of the most caring and understanding profs ive ever had. Theres no better teacher for 2035.
One of the best professors at Tech!! She has no flaws as an instructor (at least, I haven't seen one yet)
The class is heavy in material, but Professor explains concepts very well. I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot
She's super caring and really wants you to succeed. She can go super fast during lectures, but always willing to answers questions. Take her!

She's an amazing professor. She cares so much about her students, gives back great feedback, is very knowledgable and the class is a breeze if u pay attention. For ECE 2020 I can say for certain you should take her class.

Really caring professor and provides practice content for midterms. The HWs come from the textbook and if you don't understand something, she is always willing to help outside of class. Honestly, one of the best ECE professors here at Tech.

Professor Bhattacharya is the most caring professor I've had so far at Tech. She is super considerate and accessible out of class, her lectures are clear and her notes are easy to read. Definitely the best ECE 2040 professor.

Prof Bhattacharya has so far been the best professor that I have met at Tech. She is very caring and considerate of her students in these difficult times. Her lectures are amazing and very clear and her notes are very well written. I had a great learning experience and she was always there to clear any doubt almost any time of the day. TAKE HER.

Best Prof I've had so far! She is so caring and makes sure everyone understands! Will go out of her way to answer any and all questions! It is true that it is an easy class compared to the other sections, but if you're worried you won't learn, fret not! The learning is still there! The HWs are especially informative and the labs were neat! TAKE HER

She is literally the most caring and nicest Professor I have ever had in my entire life. This is my first year at tech during a stressful time, and it is so nice to have someone as caring and kind as her as a professor. She constantly helps and reaches out to her students and is very attentive to where we are struggling.

She was so sweet and really cared about all of her students passing. I had when everything was online and she would answer/check any of my work or questions. She was super understanding and always helped TAKE HER

Probably the best professor I've had at tech. She cared a lot for her students and the material and took the time to explain everything in detail. One of my homeworks didn't upload correctly and she emailed me to let me know and gave me extra time to submit it. She was always there if you had a question! 100% recommend
Prof Bhattacharya is very kind and caring and spent a lot of time outside of the class to help me. Her lectures are great and she provides a lot of supplementary material to study.

Well okay, if in short, she responded to the EdDiscussion post that was about the difficulty of the exam 2 (later got the average 72 and she said it was good) by sending a meme which had text "go take the m-train" meaning transfer to business management. Okay(????????) Lectures were not bad at all, 1/5 is more about the 2211. 0 structure.
I love this professor. She's just so fun to watch and you can tell in her voice and the way she teaches how much she loves physics. Her lecture series on 2212 is a must watch!
Alicea is the absolute best. If you can get a seat in her class, take it!
One of the kindest individuals I've ever met. She and Dr. Padukka were incredible. Highly recommend.
Clearly loves teaching, her exams are fair. She makes sure to communicate what will be on each exams. The exams vary a lot by semester.

Dr. Alicea made it easy to understand the material, and the tests weren't difficult at all as long as you did enough practice questions. There's a lot of opportunities for extra credit and the grading scheme is very forgiving. The only thing that bugged me a bit was how she made it seem like no student could ever love physics as much as her.
Dr. Alicea was good at teaching

Dr. Alicia is an amazing professor who genuinely wants students to succeed. Do extra credit and stay on top of homework, it can take time some weeks. GPS helps explain concepts well, lectures are excellent, and tests are fair. Highly recommend!

Dr. Alicea is the best professor I had at my first semester of Tech. Patient, thorough and witty, she professionally handled the fearsome Exam 3 (alien question, iykyk), giving transparency in how the question was vetted then working through the full solution during her lecture – made possible when she is always, without fail, ahead of schedule.

Although I had a different instructor, I regularly attended Alicea's lectures because of her clear, structured teaching style. She explained each concept effectively, welcomed questions, and covered content efficiently without falling behind compared to other professors. I would highly recommend her for this course.

THE GOAT! Such engaging and easy to understand lectures. Cares about her students so much. At the end of the course, she literally individually reviews any borderline grades (ex: 89.45) to try and fairly bump up to the next letter grade, which tells you everything you need to know. Exam difficulty varies by unit, but partial credit carries.

díos mio my goat. if u are bad at physics and can't learn in these horrible 200+ person lectures for phys 2 i highly recommend watching her lectures. they are super thorough and she doesn't skip steps and verbalizes her work perfectly. i love her. wish i could've gotten an a but putting that on me and no fault of her. best resource here for gt phys

Dr. Alicea is hands-down the best PHYS 2211 prof you'll probably ever have at GT. She's amazing at going through key concepts and in-class problems (usually from old tests), making sure you truly understand how to solve everything STEP-BY-STEP. Her exams this sem were on the rough side but she is super accessible on Ed Stem and prepares you well!

She's pretty funny and her lectures aren't hard to understand. Actual concepts are doable, but exams are HARD. The problems aren't like the ones you do in class, so do ALL the test practice for each concept. But, Dr. Alicia truly cares about the success of her students and she's very approachable!!

She's the goat. Coming into Georgia Tech, I knew nothing about physics and was really worried for this course. Dr. Alicea was great, I feel like I now know physics on a high level and I was able to do well on the tests.

Not my direct prof. simply the coordinator however I will say, she genuinely loves her job. She subbed once for my section and I understood SO MUCH from her in that one lecture. Very responsive on Ed Discussion; I even asked her to create learning objectives for every weeks of the semester and she did! She really wants students to succeed.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! One of the best professors I've had at Tech! Her lectures explain the concepts so thoroughly and accessibly, and I've never had physics taught to me as well as how she taught. If you get her, you'll still have to work hard, but you'll be well-equipped for the exams/finals if you put in the work to understand. :)
Class was very difficult, Alicea gives a lot of resources to use to study outside, and on edstem has good information about what will be on each test.

As someone who doesn't have to take any physics classes besides PHYS 2211, this class and it's exams felt HORRIBLE. Still, Dr. Alicea is by far the best lecturer you can take for the class, to a point of making me look forward to the class at least a bit. The grading scheme still makes it fine to do well in the class, and labs are trivial.
She is a great teacher, and she makes physics fun. But the tests are extremely difficult for no reason. I feel like there is no reason for the test to be so much harder than the homework.
she's so funny and somehow makes physics relatively understandable. her tests are horrendous though!

Great Teacher, who truly cares about our students. You are given many resources to succeed, although the tests are difficult. However, with a nice grading scheme, and lots of partial credit on the exams, this class is very doable.

Her lectures are super helpful and consists of tons of examples that help you learn the material. Exams can be difficult as they cover material learned in class but is sometimes hard to understand what's going on at first to be able to start the problem.
