Luckily, there's partial credit and the 5/10/15 split of the 3 exams help with your grade.

Physics 2 is known to be a demanding class, but alicea tries to make it easier to grasp. Summer semester goes fast and is very time consuming, but doing the GPS, lecture videos, and practicing past exams will prepare you well. I took phys 2211 here last sem with alicea, and phys 2212 had higher average exam scores surprisingly.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best Physics Prof at Tech. She takes complicated information and presents it in an easy-to-understand way with TONS of examples. Physics II is a challenging course, and the tests reflect that. However, the grade breakdown allows you to succeed even if you don't do very well on the three midterms and final.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best professor for Physics. For those who say her exams are hard and beyond what they believe was taught, you're wrong. As long as you understand the content well and its applications, no matter the question given, you'll be able to apply what you know. Not to mention the generous partial credit given. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

The lecturer does a great job at giving you ample amounts of practice material, relevant examples through labs and group-work problems over teams, and has access to many helpful TA's while being very responsive to emails and questions on Ed-Stem. Tests are hard, with self-studying being necessary to pass. Hard class, good teacher.
Best professor for physics 2. Took this course online and it was easy.

She is an outstanding professor. I took this class online and found it much easier than the in-person version. The recorded lectures explain the concepts very clearly, and the ample practice tests prepared me well for exams. As long as you pay attention to the recorded lectures and utilize the GPS and practice tests, this class is a breeze.
The professor is a very nice and engaging lecturer, but she makes the multiple exams so difficult! Nearly all the exams are curveballs.

EXTREMELY hard exams! The professor doesn't do a good job of preparing you for the tests that are unnecessarily difficult. On one of the lecture videos, the professor said that a test 3 median of around 74 is considered "better than expected"!

I don't understand the other positive reviews; the lecturer does the bare minimum and teaches the formulas and theorems, but that's it. The content and exams are also extremely difficult. The exams especially have questions you've never seen before. There's also too much busy work, such as homeworks, which are long and don't prepare you for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best PHYS2211 teacher available! Physics is a hard class in general so no matter what teacher you get, it will be hard and up to you to learn the material. However, Alicea explains the content amazingly and will help you graciously if you ask. She truly is amazing. She posts her annotated notes after class so you can look at them when studying.

She was very good at lecturing, but sometimes could forget that not everyone knew physics like she did, and skipped over some basic stuff in problems later on. She also has really millennial-like humor, which isn't a bad thing, just cringey. Very easy to get a B in class, if you are better at physics or really lock in, you can for sure get an A.

Dr. Alicea is the best physics 1 prof. I didn't have physics in hs, and this class was REALLY HARD. If you have never taken physics, get a weekly tutor. Grading scheme is kinda forgiving. You can bomb one test and still get an A (I got a 56 on exam 1 and finished with a 91). Go to class, do all the practice problems, and use the Ed Discussion.

The content in this class was just a lot over a short period of time. If you want to do well I'd say put in the extra effort to rewatch Alicea's lectures and make sure you understand the concepts. Labs peer graded so easy and plenty of extra credit available. Not all assignments are mandatory but it is still a lot of work. Alicea is an amazing prof

Dr. Alicea is nice, but this class is not structured well at all. There is barely any leniency with the grading and, after hearing how peers did in previous semesters, it seems that they have recently restructured the course to make it harder. No cios incentive, barely extra credit ("bucket points"), no grade replacement etc.

Dr. Alicea herself is a kind & caring person. However, this course as a whole is just brutal. I've never had to worry too much about my grades & have a decently high GPA. If your past physics experiences were poor, tests may be even worse as a certain thought process is required. Little opportunity to catch up if you lack beginning knowledge prior.

This class is not designed for success. Many people who did well in this class had prior knowledge from AP physics. Dr. Alicea was pretty dry and intimidating via ed-discussion, a platform that was supposed to make students feel more comfortable with reaching out. There are way too many students taking this class for you to actually learn anything.

Dr. Alicea is a great lecturer who cares about her students. She is very knowledgeable about physics and always provides proofs to support her claims, rather than saying, "trust me bro." This class is hard, especially for those with little physics background in high school, but Dr. Alecia makes it better by working out A TON of examples in class.

She is very nice and a great professor. She is very passionate about physics, and very accessible outside of class. There are attendance points that go into a bucket category, but you can do other things to get the points so you don't need to go to class. Partial credit on exams is very generous as long as you show some understanding of physics.

Don't go to class, just watch her videos. Alicea is miles better than any other physics prof. She is EXTREMELY sweet and a fantastic lecturer. She always gives enough time for clickers and does lots of explanations with physical objects to reinforce knowledge. The exams are notoriously very hard, but are graded fairly + you can regrade request.

She is a good lecturer and attendance isn't mandatory, you just need to do clickers. She also uploads a LOT of resources to try and help you. Her tests are crazy hard and way harder than any practice problems in lectures. Really sweet person. Be prepared for hard tests and hard labs.

Had her for PHYS I over the summer, meaning pre-recorded lectures. They were amazing. I am now watching her PHYS II lectures as I take it on campus, because she is x1000 better than my current lecturer. Highly recommend you take her course, or use her lectures to supplement your worse professor's lectures.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is amazing! Her lectures convey physics principles in a way that is easy to understand (I daresay even fun!). I attended her office hours after missing 3 weeks with bronchitis and she was very patient and helpful. The grading structure was generous and in the students' favor. Do not take physics 1 or 2 with anyone else at GT.

Dr. Alicea is an amazing physics professor. Her lectures are engaging and she genuinely cares about student learning. The coursework is challenging but manageable with regular attendance and using resources like Unstuck AI for practice.

She's actually the GOAT. I always hated physics, but I LOVED the way she taught and made it accessible for everyone to understand. She was funny, and a true gem. The exams were not too difficult if you do practice problems and pay attention in class. The best thing is, she was very open to changing based on feedback, which many teachers don't do.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: actual goat teacher

I didn't do great in AP Physics C in high school, so I was scared coming into the course. But, the way Dr. Alicea taught the content made a lot more sense to me than how I previously learned it. Even if you don't have her, all of her lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas. The example problems she does in them are really helpful.

ALICEA THE GOAT! She's the best physics teacher ever. Watch her recorded lectures! I didn't even have her as a teacher but her video lectures were the only reason I got an A. She even healed everything that went wrong in high school AP Physics. She's also a super responsive and organized course coordinator. I understand physics now, thanks to her!

Since the course is graded by so many things, you do not have to do extremely well on exams to get an a. Dr Alicea is a wonderful person, she respects her students and is very caring. She streamed and posted her lectures online which made learning really accessible as I had difficulties physically going to lectures. Wonderful person 10/10 recommend
Dr. Alicea-Munoz is very caring and teaches very well. She cares a lot about people understanding the content and is generally responsive to students and with grade curves.

I took PHYS 2211 in the Summer of 2022 while it was an online course. Alicea-Munoz was an extremely caring professor who evidently loved what she was doing while she was teaching. The course consisted of difficult tests and Python-based homeworks. While the tests were difficult, partial credit was awarded which made it easy to do okay in the class.

She is an amazing professor that truly cares about her students doing well. She is always available to help you out to make sure you understand what you need to. Physics is a difficult class, but it is very easy to do well in it with her as a professor.

Alicea is passionate about the concepts she teaches and clearly cares for her students' understanding. I have never taken a class this organized that provides as many resources to succeed. Lectures are very helpful and offered virtually which is very nice. Many practice questions available to study for midterms and the final.

Stopped going to my professor's class after a few weeks and starting going to Alicea's. They were fine but Dr. Alicea is awesome, I do not understand how someone can be so consistently straightforward with all of their teaching. She cares a lot, and she always responds on the ed discussion board to all sorts of questions.

Her love for Avatar and Physics are apparent in every lecture. There are a lot of comments about Test 3 but me and most of my friends/lab ppl said they felt fine about it. Tests aren't easy, but fair. It's physics, it's hard. But if you put in the work, you will do well. The lowest test is only 5%. The course is designed so you can have "slip-ups".

She is truly an incredible professor, the best I've had at GT. I'm taking physics 2211 right now as a sophomore and she has really made things click for me unlike they did in high school physics. Homework really helps for tests and also the GPS worksheets so make sure you can do those on your own and you should be set for the exams

She's such an amazing professor! I'm not good at physics, but the way she teaches it makes the material a lot easier to understand. She goes over lots of examples in detail, and exams are usually pretty similar to questions she goes over in the lectures. There's also tons of material for extra practice in order to succeed

ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT TECH. Amazing lecturer, as well as a caring teacher, Tests are reasonably difficult. As long as you attentively participate in lectures, you do not need to stress at all in her class.  Basically recommended by everyone.

She has the lecture material online, so you can use it for review. But it's still recommended to attend lectures online or in person. You will have a lot of homework, but they're not too difficult. She prepares students for the exams well and has resources that can help you prepare for them. It's a difficult class, but she makes it manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The reviews are true, she really is a great professor. I could never manage to do well in high school AP Physics, but Dr. Alicea helped me finally understand physics concepts and make things click. Her lectures are very helpful, and if you do the practice tests you should be good for the exams, though they can be quite hard so definitely study.

Dr. Alicea is a wonderful course coordinator and lecturer! Her accessibility both in class and online provide a huge advantage to students, and she is really good at introducing new topics while being mindful of the level of preparedness of students!
Hands down best 2211 professor!

Physics 1 at Tech is super hard. In my opinion, it's the hardest class I've taken, but Dr. Alicea explained things so well. If you can't get her as your professor for 2211, don't worry because you can just watch all her videos that she puts on Canvas. The only downside is that the labs use a lot of coding and we are never taught how to code.

LOVE LOVE LOVE HER!! Her greatest quality are her lectures are also very easy to follow and learn from. Her in class demonstration is also very helpful. You can also see that she is very passionate in teaching physics!

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! If you get the chance please take her for physics 2211. I actually didnt even have her but i went to her lectures and she makes the class so engaging. She also has the most amazing online system for feedback, lectures, etc. All past material can be accessed digitally. I honestly appreciate her tech savviness so much.

SHE IS TRULY SPECIAL! The greatest professor I've taken and that's saying something considering she's teaching PHYS 2211. She is so funny, easy to understand in lectures. Easy midterms and she runs the course so well. If you're in the HP section, she even makes the final optional for them sometimes and they do an easy final project. Labs easy.

Amazing professor. Highly highly recommend making a one on one appointment with her in review for exams, shes amazing at explaining and clarifying concepts. Super nice and helpful, she wants you to do well in the class.
Such a good teacher. Super kind, very understanding, makes excellent videos.
Hands down the best physics professor on Tech. I had a different teacher but reviewed her lectures and was extremely helpful. Engaging and just a genuine good professor. 100% rec

The tests were pretty easy compared to the difficulty of the homework. Homework had a flexible deadline. Class was calc based but was almost exactly the same as algebra based. Labs were about 30 minutes of working on problems. You have to turn in lab assignments based in vpython. They take some time but aren't bad and were peer graded.

Dr Alicea is without any doubt one of the best professors at Tech - if not the best! Her lectures were in depth, and she always kept us engaged. She made sure to answer any questions, even though it was a very large class and cares a lot about the students. It is very sad that she is not teaching Physics 2 this semester. Take her if you can!!!

Though she was only the course coordinator, Dr. Alicea was one of the best professors I've had in my 3 years at Tech. She was caring about her students and really just wanted us to succeed. She was very understanding with deadlines (with technology crashes or personal issues) and her class was the most organized class ever. Would 10000% take again.

Phenomenal lecturer and great professor. I was never bored by the any of the lectures, and the instead of just reading bullet points she inserts a large amount of examples into her lectures. Even with the difficulties of Physics 2 as a subject, she made it easy and my favorite class I've taken thus far.

Physics is tough, but her grading system made it very possible to get an A even if you struggled with testing. Ample study materials provided, clear test topics, and great recorded lectures. No curve, but the grading system is fair enough to help you out. Very helpful in office hours.
I hardly attended in-person lectures, and instead used the online videos. It cannot be understated how much Alicea absolutely CARRIES this course with her content.

Great professor, there is an option to go to class or not, definitely go to class and don't fall behind in lectures, as content can build up quickly. There are weekly group problem worksheets, which can be difficult, but are only for credit and sometimes very similar questions to the tests.

didn't have her as my professor, but I watched all of her video lectures. I was behind about 3 weeks in lectures (don't do that please) so I binged all her lectures and did practice, and I was still confident on the exams. keep up with her and an A is beyond attainable. no boring lectures, very inciteful. there's a reason why she only has 5 stars.

Her lectures are not boring at all and she clarifies any questions you might have. She's very caring towards students and is obviously very passionate about what she does. Lectures are also streamed on Teams & recorded. There are a ton of resources! If you put effort into it you can do well (even if you're not good at physics).

At Georgia Tech, I have discovered that many professors don't have a passion for teaching. That was until I discovered Dr. Alicea. Because of her instruction style and engaging dialogue I started to look forward to her lectures, and rediscovered my eagerness to learn. As a woman, I look up to her and hope one day I'm as strong as she is!

If you get the chance to take her class, I highly recommend going to lecture and paying close attention. The lectures aren't boring and she seems to really care that everyone in the class understands what she is teaching. I won't say it's easy, but you have the tools to do well in the class.

Great professor, hard class. Always a tough combination but it's not an easy A. Easy B at best. Try not to fall behind on lecture, she will give you "bucket points" for attendance but not necessary and lectures are recorded.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is by far the sweetest professor I have taken at GT. I took PHYS 2211 online over the summer, and watching her lectures made it so understandable. It is a hard class for sure, but she makes it easy for students to succeed. I wish I could give her 6 or 7 stars because she is truly amazing.
Best physics professor!! Awesome lectures that made content so understandable. Actually made me feel like physics 2 was easier than physics 1.

Greatest prof ever, she's actually the GOAT. Phenomenal lectures that make abstract concepts understandable and fun, well-structured resources, super caring and cares about not just your grade but your approach towards Physics. Reignited my love for the subject after high school. She should 100% be the face of teaching in GT.

Dr. Alicea is the best option for PHYS 2212! She has very helpful lectures and notes and is the most accessible professor ever. She really cares about her students and does her best to help us learn the material from physics 2, which was definitely harder than physics 1. Tests get harder as the semester goes on, but they are doable. You got it!

Dr. Alicea may be the best professor on campus. During the year, she took time to make sure all the students were doing ok in the class - whether it be their grade or their understanding of the concepts. At the end of the year, she went through each individual student's assignments to try and improve their grade as much as she could. 5/5 no doubt.
The best of the best! I'm so lucky that I got to learn from her! Absolutely incredible as a person and as a teacher

The greatest physics professor for both PHYS 2212 and 2211. I don't think I would've passed this class so easily without her because my professor was professor Jiang who is an okay lecturer but Munoz is on another level. I would watch her videos and understand concept easily and that would translate to good exam scores. Take her if you can!

I didn't even have Prof. Alicea as my professor for this class, but I had access to her lectures as she paired with my professor. Her lectures are super thorough and she does a really good job of explaining the content. She is also super nice and flexible with her students.

Dr. Alicea is not only the best physics professor but literally the best professor I had in all my four years at Georgia Tech. She provides many, many options to help student climb their grades up from difficult exams and also extra credits.
Just here to say anyone who hates her class is really just an Opp and is 1000% at fault. Best professor I've had for physics ever. took physics 1 and 2 with her !

Incredible Professor. I naturally suck at Physics, but she explained it thoroughly and did great demos during lectures. If you can't get her at least get modern so you can watch her videos. Truly a lifesaver, I thought I'd fail this class. Available to help students, and wants the best for you. She carries the entire Physics department on her back.

One of the best teachers I've ever had, absolutely incredible at teaching difficult concepts in ways students can fundamentally understand. Super fun and caring, and her lectures and PPTs are fantastic. Wholeheartedly deserves the only-5s rating she's got on here.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is awesome for Physics I. She is extremely knowledgeable and approachable. All of her lectures were recorded in case you wanted to refer back to an example she covered (super helpful when studying for midterms and the final). You can expect to have a solid understanding of the concepts all while enjoying the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not have her as my physics professor, but I relied on her videos of the solutions to the Group Problem Solving sessions to succeed in Modern Physics 1. Absolutely phenomenal explanations! Tests were hard, but she gave me a great foundation to physics problem-solving. TAKE HER IF YOU GET THE CHANCE! Modern Physics 2 will be a breeze with her!

Hear me out: she is the best professor ever! Physics is a hard subject itself but her lectures are so comprehensive. She cares about her students, has the best humor, is very relatable, and has several grade repair options. If you want to survive physics, she is literally the best option at Georgia Tech. Make sure you do practice exams, lifesaver!
Dr. Alicea is amazing! I went into the class scared of physics and came out as someone who genuinely enjoyed the class! She is a great lecturer and the tests are fair. 10000/10 would recommend
I've never liked physics too much but Dr. Alicea was excellent in her clarity and ability to make physics effortless. 100% recommended!

Probably the best teacher I've ever had. Phenomenal lectures and slides, enjoyed labs, loved the course structure and methods of teaching (the Procedures in the PPTs are amazing). Great resources, super caring + accessible. Genuinely understood concepts fundamentally as opposed to using formulae, and it really paid off. Undisputed teaching GOAT.

Dr. Alicea is the greatest professor! Her lectures are engaging and she makes hard physics concepts easy to understand by focusing on real-world problems instead of derivations and etc. She's also very caring and easy to reach out to when you have an issue.

Dr. Alicea is awesome! She has moved back some lab deadlines and is willing to be helpful in ed discussions (forum discussions) to answer questions about lectures and tests. I would 5/5 recommend taking her for either physics I or II as you will learn a lot and be entertained while doing so.

PHYS 2211 is a challenging class, no matter who you take it with. Prof. Alicea moves very fast which can take some time to get used to, but she breaks down & explains concepts very clearly and provides a plethora of study resources. She records all of her lectures which are incredibly helpful to review and beyond all, is incredibly caring & sweet.

I struggled with AP Physics C in high school, mainly with the angular momentum and motion topics. Also the mv^2/R stuff used to be confusing.
Dr. Alicea explains it really well and she's EXTREMELY helpful on Ed discussion and office hours. She made physics so engaging too for many, something that is quite the accomplishment. Take her if you can.

Amazing professor, provides video lecture recordings for all sections of PHYS 2211 so that even students outside of her lectures can be prepared to succeed in the class in addition to being extremely caring and flexible for her students

Alicea is the GOAT, you should absolutely take her class if you have the chance to. You'll be way better at physics for it, and you'll have a good time in class. Lectures are engaging and worth attending.

Dr. Alicea is an amazing professor! She is extremely passionate about physics, and her excitement made the lectures engaging. She does a good job of making physics fun. I came into the class knowing absolutely nothing of physics, and although I had a rough start, the resources she provides us with really helps! Definitely take her if you can!!

Most amazing professor I've had for any class. I've taken physics classes in high school and grown a hatred for them but she actually made it fun for me. As long as you do the work, it is very easy to succeed.  I am honestly kind of sad to be leaving her class because she was just such a kind hearted and enjoyable professor.
Great! Take her class if you can. Truly the best :)

I suck at physics, I was never able to do well in high school and then when I took Dr. Alicea's class I did really well. The labs are relatively easy and while the tests were hard, there's lots of partial credit. Dr. Alicea also teaches really well! Also, she's super accessible and there are weekly assignments with flexible due dates!

TAKE PROF ALICEA! I took it over the summer. She thoroughly explains concepts, her examples are always relevant, and she is very caring. She is also always available and wants to help you succeed! I didn't have any physics knowledge coming into this class, and she made it so enjoyable. Labs are very fun and GSP problems are very similar to tests.
i took the online version of physics over the summer and prof alicea made it so easy. interesting material and the tests were pretty similar to the hw

The course was asynchronous so my experience was pretty rough because of that. With that being said lectures were pretty good for prerecorded lessons. Professor had ~1 week lead time to respond to emails but was more than willing to have 1 on 1 meetings (She arranged one w me on an Institute holiday which was very nice).
Tests/HW similar to lecture

She's attentive to students and makes herself very available and transparent outside of class. She changed the lab report rubric based on student feedback and gave us a detailed reason why (based on numerous reports of unfair grading and harassment in the group chats). The tests were hard but not anything you wouldn't have been taught in class.

Took the online async version of 2211. Despite being recorded, lectures were clear, informative, and she does a great job of explaining student misconceptions and providing detailed answers. She did a great job of making herself known and accessible through weekly updates on Ed. Grading is very generous and she is an extremely caring person.

Physics 1 with Dr. Alicea-Munoz is the way to go. I was nervous since it's Physics at Tech, but if you go through all the recorded lectures and the homeworks you are completely fine. She is incredibly thorough and there was never a problem where I was confused after she went through it. Highly recommend taking it async with her over the summer.

I took this as a summer class online. Alicea herself was amazing; her weekly review videos were really clear to understand and she was easily available for questions. Not super happy with the formatting of the class as all the lectures were recorded from other professors. The class is difficult but there's generous partial credit.

Dr. Alicea is a great lecturer! Once you get used to her fast paced teaching style (takes about a week), her explanations are really easy to understand, and she answers questions thoroughly so you never leave feeling confused. Her lectures are fun, and she is very accessible outside of class through EdX and office hours.

One of the best profs I've had. Genuinely cares about her students both in and outside of class. Gave me some extensions and rounded some grades to help me finish with an A in the class. Makes boring topics more fun, and is super easy to reach. Overall an amazing professor that anyone would be lucky to have.

One of the best, if not the best, professors I've had at Tech.  Very caring and offers plentiful opportunities for success.  Always available through Ed, office hours, email, or even after class.  Exams were easy if you take the provided practice tests and get help if you need it.  Highly recommend!

Dr. Alicea was one of my favorite professors from this semester and the only reason I didn't get an A was because I kept sleeping through class and got really behind. She explains concepts very thoroughly and makes them easy to understand. If you are taking physics, take it with her and go to class.

Dr. Alicea-Munoz is an amazing professor, she teaches so well and really understands the needs of her students. The grading is super fair and she makes everything make sense. A super enjoyable professor and I recommend anyone who can takes her for physics.
She's a great professor, especially if you have never taken physics before. But, this class is not an easy A. She is the better professor out of everyone else. I highly recommend taking her!

Best teacher I have taken in Tech. Excellent lectures and great communication with students. Every lecture has in-class participation questions that are graded just for submission, so you will need to attend lectures. If you go to lectures and understand the examples she gives, you will do well. Use old exams to practice for tests.
Alicea is the sweetest, kindest, most generous, caring, and wonderful teacher I have taken at tech to date!!!

Dr. Alicea was a gem to have. She's extremely accessible outside of class- willing to help with lab or questions about homework. She posts very helpful review material and overall cares about her students/their grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had her as the lab coordinator for physics 1. Always responds to emails quickly and really cares about her students. Def take physics with her if you can.

Dr. Alicea is the most understanding professor I've had thus far at Tech. I was going through some very unexpected health issues and not once did she make my life harder, she only offered her unconditional support and help. She also is excellent when it comes to asking for academic help. Overall, amazing professor and person.

Probably the most caring person at Tech. Genuinely a treat to have her and Professor Fenton for 2211. Her structure added to the class and communication with students is the biggest asset for anyone taking the class. Definitely do what you can to take her for 2211!
Very nice and helpful
Dr. Alicea is a very caring instructor who is always willing to help students succeed. She made physics 2 a very smooth and enjoyable experience.
This class was very good, very good lecturer. Explained the concepts well, and was super accessible
Truly cares about her students. Tried to make the course as doable as possible.

Dr. Alicia-Munoz is just awesome, plain and simple. She's so accessible, interactive, and helpful. She truly understands student needs and always makes sure to stay in touch with the general student population. She's also an amazing teacher in general and is just awesome all around!
Awesome Professor! The class was set up poorly, but Professor Alicia was able to adapt and release better lectures. She is kind and understanding, would 100% take her class again.

She is very organized, knowledgeable, and caring: exactly what you need to succeed in your first physics college class. She is very accessible outside of class and won't stop explaining material until you fully understand. Her lectures and office hours were great for studying for exams. Loved taking the class with her!

Dr. Alicea was a very involved lecturer, and extremely enthusiastic. There was a point where we had to ask her to stop answering every single question from students because she was just that involved. Take her class if you can.

Dr. Alicea made Physics 1 a very enjoyable experience. The mini-tests/final are all very reasonable, and she made an effort to reduce the stress caused by the pandemic. Multiple extra credit opportunities were given, and the textbook provided was optional.

Given the remote format and additional strain caused by the pandemic, Dr. Alicea was very caring and made the effort to make the class more flexible to accommodate students and reduce stress. There were many extra credit opportunities and easy participation points (HW, clickers) helped offset a low test grade. Textbook in syllabus but not used.

Professor Alicea was a great lecturer and explained physics concepts very clearly. She does a ton of practice problems in class and recitation which are very helpful for the tests. I didn't need to touch the textbook at all. She's very dedicated, enthusiastic, caring, and fun. Class grading scheme is pretty forgiving and the tests weren't too bad.

Dr. Alicea clearly cares about her subject and works hard to make class fun and interesting. She uses clicker questions, some of which were just Avatar and Spongebob memes, during lectures for attendance, however the attendance portion of the grade can be substituted with other optional assignments. She is the most caring, pure professor, 10/10.

Honestly the only reason I got through physics. Extremely caring and explains things very well. I actually took physics with the other section/professor but sat through her lectures and used her notes because she was so much more effective of an educator. Easily accessible outside of class and very kind and funny

Dr. Alicea is the only reason I was able to do well in Intro Physics I. The class is tough but she was very accessible and made it easy to ask her questions about homework, labs, or lectures. She is definitely a great professor and is dedicated to her students. She was also very engaging but beware the tests are tough!

Alicea was extremely helpful during office hours and clearly enjoys teaching the course content. Her summary notes before each test were incredibly useful. She is very responsive through email and Campuswire. Previously, she was a head TA for this class for many years and her experience really shows.
Just take Dr. Alicea if given the option. You won't regret it.
Very talented at lecturing, very accessible, very knowledgeable in Physics, and a wonderful person overall. Unbelievable that this was her first semester lecturing.

She's an amazing professor who cares deeply about her students. She trusts all of her students and wants them to succeed so bad. She even gave lecture right after getting surgery because it was right before a test. Please take her for PHYS 2211. You will not regret it. (Also her test problems are pretty easy :) )
Dr. Alicea is such an awesome professor! Her lectures are fun an interesting and she's very enthusiastic about class. It is very obvious that she cares about all of us, even in a 200 person class!

Dr. Alicea really cares for her students and this class despite being met with hundreds of student initials on her computer every morning. She's so dedicated that she would lecture even though she had to undergo surgery right before our final midterm. You can tell she knows the material well and makes sure to answer every question thrown her way.

Despite the course being online, Dr. Alicea did a great job of energizing the class and interacting with the students. She's a legend and was extremely invested in the class. You could tell she really enjoys teaching and makes classes fun. If you skip lectures or doze off, you probably will struggle but stay focused and Muñoz will carry you through

Although this class was online, Dr. Alicea really made it one that I enjoyed attending. She explained some complicated topics pretty well and made it an overall great experience. She also captures my attention nicely with some well-designed clicker questions to help our understanding of the subject. Labs were a pain, but to no fault of her own.

Dr. Dixon's class was difficult, but he had clear expectations and was generally very helpful. His lectures were good, and all of his exams and quizzes were fair. The class is graded with participation, 2 midterms, 6 quizzes (one of which is dropped), and an optional final. Overall good choice for fluids.

I gave my utmost, yet it did not suffice. Lectures, oft obscured and broken by a chorus of questions, unraveled any steady thread of sense, thus I turned to the texts for light. The exams are fair, yet the marking hand is severe. The hardship lies less in the matter than in the manner of its telling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Didn't have the most organized lectures, quite difficult to follow. Had to rely on reading the textbook a lot! Overall, not a too tough grader, but just be prepared to do a lot of self-studying.

Every time I enter this mans classroom I leave more confused. He acts as if his goal is to discourage students from every pursuing anything related to fluids. One of the woprst professors I've had at this school. Do not take him if you have any other option. The textbook is a better professor.
Poor lectures which he is obviously unprepared for. Tough grader with little partial credit, but the exams and quizzes are not difficult. You may pass, but you will not learn fluids if you take him.

I am a third year ME at GT and haven't liked a single class so far except this one, this guy is an amazing teacher and professor. Grades tough sometimes, but if you show up to class and learn he's incredible. Textbook is complete dogwater, just make sure you completely understand his notes which he posts on canvas. Give ample past exams too

It was his first-semester teaching fluids online. Before starting a new topic he'd group students together and waste more than half of class throwing us a problem on a topic he didn't cover yet which ended up being an awkward room of silence because no one knew how to solve the problems, such a waste of time. Also side tracks a lot during lecutres
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures can be a bit confusing at times, and fluids is a hard class. I would recommend reading the textbook a lot to understand some of the surrounding material that is not gone over in class. The examples are also from the textbook and he can move a bit fast so the solutions are helpful. Reading the textbook helped me the most before finals.

Best professor I have ever had. I took Dr. Dixon for Fluids and ME 4758 in the same semester. His exams are straight forward, I recommend doing all the homework and working back through the IN CLASS EXAMPLES. He has a great sense of humor and was super chill and fun to talk to during office hours.

Very good lecturer. Grade distribution can be rough (15% A, 20%B) but I personally learned a lot. Some people really hate him but I don't quite understand why. Probably the best lecturer I've had at Tech, and the class structure is straightforward and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer, I really enjoyed learning in his class. But his exams are so poorly created, the do not reflect the work you have done in the class. I have never taken a class that is graded so harshly.
during lectures he would often skip steps leaving me clueless; weekly quizzes are very difficult and solutions for homeworks are never posted. This has been my hard class at Tech so far
Dr. Dixon is a great teacher, he is a tough grader but very fair. I took both fluids and numerical methods with him, and enjoyed both classes. I would recommend him to anybody.

Prof. Blann cared about his students, and wanted them to learn. He was especially attentive about ODS accommodations, and never once made me feel uncomfortable about asking for what I needed. His grading scheme was forgiving, so long as you put forth the effort needed. My only regret is not having more time to dedicate to his class.

Blann is very caring and considerate. The class is mostly comprised of 4 exams, 10 quizzes, and textbook work. To prepare for the exams you'll typically have 2-3 practice exams. Homework sets help you prepare, too. You'll also be allowed one note card for exams. For homework, the textbook is very helpful. Extra credit opportunities were given.

Such a fun class and professor! Unique approach of teaching valuable acct content in an enjoyable and low-stress format. Assignments include many small group projects, a few pop quizzes, and the final was a slightly larger group project. One of my fav classes I have taken at GT, so ABSOLUTELY take it if you need an extra MGT/accounting elective!

Professor Blann is super nice and accommodating!! His lectures are alright, but the class is pretty straightforward. I would only say that I felt like the online section got much better grades than the in-person section (I was in-person section). Attendance is basically mandatory since he has mini quizzes for attendance almost every class

Professor Blann is very kind and accommodating. The tests are pretty fair and there are daily quizzes to make sure you are keeping up with the content. He is always looking for ways to improve his course by asking for feedback and implementing it. I would recommend!
Very caring and sweet professor! He grades very fairly and leniently, sets clear expectations for how the class is laid out. Only downside is lectures are a little boring.

Professor Blann is a great professor! Although the class is a little boring and lectures are mostly just him reading slides, Professor Blann provided several extra credit opportunities, homework's that really helped for the test, and a flash card on each test. He also is very understanding and will help you if needed. Overall, good class!

Such a unique way to teach this course, but truly made my day every time I went to his class. It's not anything like any other accounting class here– it's more project based learning. But it's such a stress free environment. Love him.
Prof Blann is fair and kind. He is good at explaining concepts, accommodating, and works with you to make sure you get your best grade. He's awesome!

Graded on only tests and quizzes which were not too hard. He listened well to feedback and was able to adapt the class according to. Many extra credit opportunities and dropped lowest test grade too. Overall very kind and caring. Take him if you can!

Dr. Birol is a great lecturer, but it definitely seems that he enjoys teaching his other classes more than BIOS2600. Overall, the readings were a lot and he made the homeworks difficult, but you got two attempts and you could see the answers after you missed them the first time. His tests are also hard but manageable if you study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He explains things well in lecture. The exams align with the lecture well and there are a lot of practice problems that help.

Made physiology very interesting and made topics relatable. Exams were straightforward, but some questions were difficult. Final exam was light, 60% of it came from previous midterms. You can do well by going to class or self-studying with the book. Homework = easy grade booster. Pre-lecture quizzes were annoying timing-wise, but he dropped a lot.

the course is a lot of memorization but he seems passionate what he is talking about. the tests are pretty straightforward as long as you know all of the learning objectives and almost everything on every slide. he will emphasize in class what is important to know so that is helpful and he does try to help his students

Dr. Birol's lectures were extremely helpful, and I felt that exams accurately reflected content taught in class. Pre-readings were required for this class. If I did not understand a pre-reading, I knew that if I went to class Dr. Birol would clarify it for me. Great teacher!!
To do well, attendance isn't necessary. Just rely on the textbook.

Birol is kind/willing to help students succeed. Lectures are boring (not really his fault, physiology is just boring). Homework/assignments are easy grade boosters. Exam questions are SO TRICKY. Read very carefully and prepare to study hard for all the tests. Several midterm questions reused for the final, but still plenty of new ones.

Dr. Birol co-taught this class with Dr. Richards. Birol is clearly passionate about biology. I went to 70% of the lectures and made an A. He is a good speaker and helps us understand material better. The only issue is that some of the exam questions were based on what was said in lecture and not found in the slides, but it wasn't that big of a deal

co-taught w/ robbie richards. birol focused on animals and was generally better. didn't ramble as much. he tries to draw focus to what goes on the test, but there's just a great amount of content. recitation is helpful. some tests focus on what is explicitly talked about in class and not clearly shown on slides, but attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he's clearly very knowledgeable about the subject, but sometimes the lectures are hard to follow solely based on the obnoxious amount of material for the class. there is a lot of reading and sometimes the questions on exams were worded very weirdly. other than that, he's actually a nice guy and would crack a joke every now and then.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taught w/ Richards (who carried). Goes through lecture material very fast but often explained it in a confusing manner. so long as you take notes on the readings(especially if birol is teaching for that day) and lecture, study LOs and do practice exams you'll get an A. TAs office hours/recitations/exam review sessions helped get an A too.

This class has been my favorite class at tech yet! Dr. Birol has a very fair grading policy in my opinion. Exams are not weighted too heavily which allows room for improvment. I did not start the course off strong, but if you attend lecture, an A is very likley. Plus, his lectures are great. He relates topics to things in the real world!

Did not teach genetics that well, and the tests were way too long. Gave extra credit though. The homework was also very difficult, but you get two attempts, and the first attempt tells you the answer.

Before each lecture, students are expected to read a "chapter" of the assigned textbook. The readings weren't hard but they were dense. He reiterated the readings in class so lectures were redundant. He does go over homework/assignment questions in class (if time permits); however, sometimes the powerpoint and the readings contradicted each other.

Consistently admitted to not knowing information he was supposedly teaching so I ended up learning more from TAs/ the internet than him. He is very distant from students and the grading criteria was extremely vague. Co-taught this course with Torres and there was little discussion between the two about the logistics of this, creating confusion.

He is very knowledgeable in biology, but is not always the greatest at explaining the material. The class has a lot of material that is overwhelming to memorize and learn, and tough. exams. Hard to study for exams because they cover so much content, and you are tested on some minute details. TAs were decently helpful.

I had Dr. Birol once before in 1108 and I was excited to have him for physiology but was incredibly disappointed by this class. His lecturing made this one of the most boring classes I have ever taken and the grading was heavily based on tests that asked questions that were so specific, making it difficult to do well despite studying heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I've had at GT. I've had him for both BIOS 1107 and 1108, and I recently had him over the summer for BIOS 3755. He is very passionate about his teaching, explains content in depth, and welcomes questions form the students. Attend class because the powerpoints are posted but not everything as in depth as class.

Great professor, this was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Tech. Dr Birol is a very good teacher, but his lecture slides are awful. You will not do well if you do not go to class because the lecture slides do not contain much content. Tests are hard but if you go to class you'll be fine. He recycles test questions for the final.

A lot of the tests had extra credit and all you really had to do was do the readings and finish the learning catalytics to get a good grade.  Stopped going to class towards the ends but still did good on the tests cuz of the readings.

I never really went to class and studied two days before my exam. Just read the textbook and take notes you will be fine. Heavy on memorization though. Homeworks/participation is graded on participation not the actual grade which was really good. The homework questions were similar to the ones on the test and he reuses questions for the final!

Great professor, used recycled test questions on final. However, if you don't like reading, you're going to fall behind fast. Bit of an accent, but didn't interfere with my learning. Also, you're going to have to spend 12 dollars for the program he uses for homework. Taught the course with Prof. Datta
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are based off of things he emphasizes in class so make sure you go. Take really good notes in class and study them + the powerpoints and you'll get an A. Tests are kind of hard/detail heavy, but the final is really easy because probably 80% of the final is recycled test questions (which you have access to for studying).

cares so much about the students and the material. he does tend to get distracted and go on tangents, but he is such a good lecturer. i recommend using flashcards for any classes he teaches because it's definitely a lot of memorization and understanding of the material. loved taking a class with him and wish i could take more.

Dr. Birol is a great professor. He is truly passionate about what he teaches, and it only makes you more interested in the subject. His lectures contain a lot of information, but he explains it clearly and leaves time for questions. His tests are closed notes and do need a good amount of memorization, but if you go to class you should be fine.

The class has a lot of material that is nearly impossible to memorize and learn, with dense exams. The textbook is poorly written with grammatical errors and it is hard to study for exams due to the amount of content and because you are tested on the smallest details in the textbook. If you are looking for a simple class, do not take this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class only just became closed note and that's obvious. There is far too much information to learn before exams and while he says he doesn't expect you to memorize the material, this is a lie. If you work hard, you will do well, but I would pick a different class if you're just looking for an easy A. There's also so much homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He is extremely caring and understanding, and he is truly passionate about biology. The class is not bad at all if you pay attention and keep up with the material.

Very well-spoken and very passionate. The setup of the class is nice where you learn the content the night before and he teaches it the morning after (reinforcing knowledge). The class is now closed-notes, even though it was open-note in the past. Crib sheet on final. Textbook is tedious but worth it to read. Exams were not hard at all.

The textbook is extremely tedious to read. All the exams are just random details from the textbook. There's a lot of information and lectures move extremely fast. He's a great guy and very passionate about bio, but his lectures can get overwhelming with unnecessary information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing and passionate lectures. Be ready to STUDY STUDY and MEMORIZE. SO MUCH CONTENT! But a good professor!

This class is full of random details that you must find in the textbook. In person lectures don't help much as the exam asks the most minute and randomly detailed questions. You have to memorize the craziest small details that is not covered. Overall, I expected this class to build off 1107 or AP Bio but I couldn't be more wrong.

If this class is required for you, GOOD LUCK!! Horribly structured course with a bunch of non-correlating information. Lectures are all around useless, slides are horrendously formatted, key points conveniently cut-off. Very passive aggressive if you have questions. Exams are all random details from the readings, neglecting the bigger picture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures consisted of the same content covered by the textbook readings required to have been completed before class. Tests consisted of very specific questions from the textbook, oftentimes neglecting bigger topics from the course for smaller sections of the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He's alright.
The class itself is not difficult, but most of the content feels useless.
In my opinion, lectures are only useful because he sometimes tells you what you should know/ not know what's on the test. Other than that, its pretty much useless. 
The tests contain specific textbook questions and other random information as well.

All information on tests comes from readings that are done outside of class. Lectures during class are vague and consist of reused pictures from the readings. Tests are not open-note anymore and questions on the test are very specific from the readings
I do not know much about Dr. Birol's lectures since I never went to class, but the online resources provided were more than enough to understand all the material required and tests were a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very poorly structured course with tons of content that is touched on once and never mentioned again. Although the tests are open-note, you have so little time it's not feasible to search through everything (I had ~400 pages by the end of the semester). Professor doesn't seem to care about students and just speeds through lectures

Dr. Birol is a great professor. He covers all the material you need to know in lecture which is nice. He also emphasizes the important concepts in class so you know what to write down/ study. He's very nice as well and engaging in class. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Birol was a good lecturer and was excited about what he was teaching. It is helpful to do the reading before class as the course has a lot of information, and he doesn't always cover everything in lecture. Overall, he's a good professor - the class is just a lot of information.

The class was very easy. Tests are online. zoom meetings of classes, making attendance, not mandatory. There are participation clicker points in the class, and there are several writing assignments all of which are fairly easy.

Great lecturer and passionate about his units within this course! Goes at a great pace (unlike Montoya) and wants students to thrive. He makes sure that everyone's questions are answered. He was definitely the BEST bio professor by a long shot! We were begging for him to come back at the end of the semester because Montoya was so rough.

Dr. Birol is a pretty decent professor. He's a bit more understanding than many other professors and does some things to account for students having off-days. He's also fairly interested in the course matter. However, the class itself is super information-heavy, so get ready to absorb a lot of info.

Emphasizes studying ABC but tests on XYZ ~500 slides of notes this semester of stuff to just memorize which sucked. You then get to the test, and after studying all the important things emphasized (all the steps of transcription/gene repression) you get asked only about genomes. Very frustrating because there are no practice exams or crib sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is an amazing professor! He can be very direct at times but he is truly passionate about this subject and that makes it a super enjoyable class. If you do the work in this class its not difficult to do well, just make sure you keep up with the readings and listen to the lectures, which you can come in person or join online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol was one of my favorite professors this year! He has an undeniable passion for the subject and is incedibly understanding. There is a lot of content on each exam, but if you read the textbooks and quiz yourself on the concepts and learning objectives, you'll turn out just fine. The scientist spoltights and LCs are nice grade cushions, too!

He honestly could be a little warmer to students but overall he's pretty straightforward with what you need to learn if you pay attention. He definitely isn't the type of person to hold ur hand the whole way but he's nice with the extra-credit and LCs to help boost grades. If you want to pass you need to work for it. Just wish content wasn't dense
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is in fact clearly passionate about biology and his lectures are far more than just reading from a powerpoint. In fact, this class made me very intrigued about evolutionary and ecological biology. However, whoever made the final was so out of pocket for that. All our hard work for an exam that was mostly a topic we spent a couple days on.

I was excited for physiology after taking anatomy but this was an awful class with so much lecture content and reading that it wasn't even that helpful for the tests since they tested really specific things or processes. wouldn't recommend him for physiology
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is fantastic! It is open-note and open-book because he places an emphasis on you learning the material. If you stop showing up to lectures halfway through the semester and Ctrl-F on every test, you won't do well though. It is a lot of info and you need to know some of it without needing to look it up. Pretty easy, highly recommend it!
He goes through a crazy amount of material and his exams test you on such specific information. It's hard to tell what will be on the tests. No study guide or practice tests.

Birol is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He makes his tests overly difficult and is not open to the student's concerns. The test is in 50 minutes and I have to search through over 500 pages of notes so you're set up for failure. He doesn't respect students at all/very passive-aggressive. I would avoid him if you need to take BIOS 1108.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is very passionate about biology, and while I did not care at all and only took this class because I had to, it did make it a bit more bearable. He taught the first and last units and I did the best on those two in terms of test grades. He is easy to reach and a solid guy all around

I was excited to take physiology but his lectures are so dense and he runs through them so fast that it's so hard to know exactly what to study for tests even if you combine the lectures with the readings.
Dr. Birol is the best professor I have ever had for biology. He is nice and the tests are not that hard. Highly recommend!

Lecture content is super heavy and feel like he's competing in a race to finish lectures as fast as possible - before you can even process one topic he's already moved onto a new one. Exams are MC/SA and the amount of material can be pretty overwhelming if you don't review every week. I was excited for this class but Birol really dulled my spirits
Great professor who is willing to explain concepts as much as needed. Lectures is very notes and discussion heavy, if you attend lecture the tests should be fairly easy.

Birol is a good professor but I would say the best part about the class is the resources. I was able to do well even as someone who does not love bio. His lectures are good but sometimes do not always cover all the information. Reading the sections and asking questions can for sure fill any gaps.

Easily one of the top profs to take for bio, and I'd take him again. Super chill, caring, gives extra credit opportunities if possible. Pay attention in class tho since certain topics that are glazed over once or heavily emphasized can still be mentioned on the exams. Email responses are prompt.Give back the same energy he gives and you'll be fine.

This class was taught with Dr. Harrison and I think Dr. Birol was better at explaining some of the concepts and more accessible and willing to discuss material out of class. He was new this semester but by halfway through the course you wouldn't be able to tell. The examples he goes over in lecture are the same as the ones he puts on the exams

Dr. Birol is extremely thoughtful and caring! He responds to emails, and always tried finding ways to explain material in a different way if you were confused. I didn't go to office hours a lot, but when I did, they were super helpful and you could tell that he cares a lot. He's also unintentionally funny, which made lectures fun. Loved it!

I dislike biology and this class did nothing to change that. On the other hand, it's a manageable A in the class. Make sure to stay on top of the written assignments and just use the website links from the syllabus, and you should end the class with an A. Make sure to participate! Attendance is not necessary at all. *(Taught with Colin Harrison)*
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Birol is a great professor! He is always willing to help students and always answers his emails. He also knows biology really well.

The class is super chill and is an easy a if you do assignments. She's a chill lecturer and cares about the material and her students. The new group project was interesting, but I'm sure she'll improve it for future semesters. Great professor if you want a stress-free class
Dr. Baradel is super sweet and this class is easy peasy!

Professor Baradel is amazing! All you had to do was complete the homework (generally very quick and easy, not graded harshly at all) and show up to class (she gives like 4 free absences though). She is super sweet and accommodating with assignments, too!

Overall, this class isn't very difficult in terms of content. You typically have one or two writing assignments due every week that just ask you to reflect on what you discussed in lecture or an external website. Attendance is mandatory, but slides are uploaded to Canvas; most people do other work during lecture since there is no midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She really cares about the topic and students and generally grades fairly leniently.
I took the online 1040 course, and it was very light. We had an average of 2 assignments per week, and max it would take if you're focused is two hours each week. Highly recommend the online course.

Took this course asynchronously. We had a lecture and a few assignments posted each week. The lectures were quite engaging and required little work. Class focused on dimensions of wellness and helped me learn a lot of strategies to improve each! Overall, great class with a great professor and TAs who are always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Baradel is extremely caring and her class is super easy. Tons of busy work HW, but not graded harshly. Overall, I enjoyed the class. She takes PointSolutions attendance for small portion of your overall grade.

Amazing professor. APPH 1040 is a easy class, easy A. Just do the homeworks and you'll be fine. No tests or quiz. She's very clear and caring towards the students too. One of the nicest professors I've met.
It's a straightforward online class, about 2 to 3 assignments per week that take very little time, especially if you do an audio submission. No exams or finals either.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, no exams or finals, but there's a good amount of busy work. Extremely kind teacher and is very enthusiastic about her topics. Would def take again
She is a very nice person, but there is just so much work for the class. Talked to friends in other sections w/ other profs and they had it way easier. Be prepared for a lot of writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are just looking to get the required health credit done take this course! Mandatory attendance at lectures will take up about 2 hours, and then there's only like 2 hours of busy work a week. No tests, no quizzes, no long essays. Very nice professor, and lectures are interesting if you do decide to pay attention

It's a required health course but Prof. Baradel is really caring and enthusiastic about it. There are no tests or quizes and the primary assignments are just quick summaries/takeaways of the lecture slides.
mandatory attendance but its just a health class, amazing lecturer tho

Really nice person, very easy class. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss a few without any consequences (i think 4 or smthn). Don't have to pay attention in lecture most of the time, there are no tests but there are hws, not time consuming at all though. Great prof, I def recommend.

Took online async, 2-3 assignments open up per week due Monday 11:59pm. Slightly frustrating cuz some weeks I had more time and could've knocked out the next month's worth of assignment but only opens up 2 per week. Always sent out weekly announcements and plenty of reminders and always responded within the next couple hours of emailing her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very responsive to email and made the class as easy as possible. Sent out opportunities for career opportunities, which I thought was very sweet.

Professor Baradel was very responsive via email and did not want the class to be difficult. She wanted us to learn about our mental and physical health and sends out opportunities for career and academic development. I definitely recommend taking her class!

Classes = lectures - people do work for other classes. She wants devices away during videos 3 group projects Attendance = mandatory - point solutions.  2-3 assignments/week = journal entries or worksheets, busy work & max 1 hr/week, no quizzes, self-improvement project due at end of the semester. really nice professor w/passion for teaching
Makes class as easy as she can-- and very informative! Just stay on top of submitting the homeworks. They are essentially participation credit, but there is a lot of them
Class is mostly busy work by Dr Baradel is very caring and knows about the subject. Class was mostly used as time to work on other classes and the assignments were graded very liberally.
You can find lecture slides on Canvas for assignments, in case you miss a class or didn't pay attention.

Professor Baradel's class was very easy and convenient. The assignments were sometimes a bit tenuous but graded very lightly -- mostly busy work. The attendance was mandatory, but given a few absences and also lectures were very informative and interesting.

Professor Baradel is an amazing person and you can tell she is very passionate about this subject. She is caring and understanding. However, lectures are somewhat useless and boring. No quizzes or tests, but there is a lot of busy (albeit very easy) work. The Canvas page is well organized and everything you need is on there.

Good professor and a great human being who seems friendly. No quizzes or assessments, but a LOT of busy work. Grading standards were extremely simple and easy, but this was just time-consuming and I felt it was not worth the effort. Attendance was also mandatory, would recommend an async section instead. The lectures were not that useful.

The lectures are mostly useless, but attendance is mandatory. There are three assignments every week that are annoying, but are easy. It's very hard not to get an A if you turn everything in (it's only 5% per day late too), but the class is still a headache. Not bad as an only option, but I'd try to find someone more lax or take health online.

Professor Baradel is very friendly and passionate about what she teaches and made sure that her class was not causing additional stress for students. Class grade was mostly made up by the weekly assignments which were easy and did not take long to complete. Lectures sometimes felt a little pointless but did learn some meaningful wellness concepts.

Great professor. She lectures and then you complete reflection assignments outside of class on your own. It is busy work, but I'd rather do personal reflection than quizzes and tests like other health teachers. Overall great and helpful lectures on health.

Professor Baradel does care about the course but for students looking for a chill health class this is not one of them. There are 25+ assignments throughout the semester (not hard just tedious and annoying) all outside of class and attendance is required. Do not recommend.

Professor Baradel is an enthusiastic teacher, but that's why I gave her a low rating. This is a health class, so I don't think she should ask students to shut off their laptops to watch TED Talks or assign three busy-work assignments a week. I recommend choosing a different health professor because most students take this class for an easy credit.

Professor Baradel is great! She convey's all of the information relevant to APPH 1040 in an interesting and concise way. She understands that APPH 1040 is an institute requirement, so she makes all of the assignments easy to follow! The grading in this class is amazing and she really focuses on providing the material for success in this class.

I had her for the short summer semester and she was great. She emphasizes that she tries to make this class as less stressful as possible, and it really was. The assignments are helpful and not just busy work, and she tries to involve everyone in class discussions. There are some presentations, but as an introvert, they helped me better my skills.

Prof Baradel was the perfect person to take APPH 1040 under. It was a quick and easy course, and her lectures were engaging. I would also recommend taking the summer short-semester version, as I was able to knock it out pretty easily even with an internship. Highly recommend! Just pay attention to her announcements to log things enough days.
Such a great professor! I took a lot from her class and found her to be incredibly kind and caring. Definitely recommend!
Very easy professor. She's wonderful; try to speak up in class if you can (or want to -- it's not required), because she genuinely feels interested in her students.

She's a very engaging lecturer who truly cares about the material and her students. The quizzes were straightforward if you referenced her slides, and all of the assignments were fairly simple if you followed directions. My only complaint is that attendance was ungraded until around halfway through the semester when she made it mandatory.
Dr. Baradel is very passionate. The assignments and quizzes are easy, and she provides great feedback.

This class was SO easy. All assignments are open note (a.k.a. open Canvas), so it was very easy to succeed! She is so nice, knowledgeable, and fun! I found her lectures super interesting, too. A little disorganized, but that's okay.
TAKE HER! Very helpful and responds quickly. This was a very straight-forward class and her instructions were very clear. Great experience!
Probably the best professor to take for 1060.  Do your work and participate, and you'll be fine.

An easy A if you turn everything in and attend. She's knowledgable. Rating of 3 because she changed the syllabus a few weeks into the semester (past the drop deadline) to make attendance 10% of our grade. She also posts assignments way too late, so you can't do stuff early. Disorganization and late policy changes made it hard to stay organized.

When I took APPH 1040, I only showed up to less than 25% of lectures and still got an A+. In the classes I did attend, Professor Baradel seemed to be enthusiastic and made learned health more enjoyable. I recommend her over other professors as the graded components were extremely easy to complete as long as the rubric was followed.
Easy course and kind lady. Take APPH 1040 with her, you won't regret.

Took during late short summer term. Very easy class as long as you turn in your assignments and follow very clear, straight-forward grading criteria. Easy extra credit opportunities. Very passionate lectures. Open note quizzes.

Very easy professor, took this class for short summer session 1 and everything was online async open note. I reached out once for help on an assignment and she replied very quickly and was very helpful. 4 weeks long and around 1-3 quizzes due on sundays every week. Assignments and projects were very easy, so just make sure to do everything.

As others have noted, just turn in everything on time and you'll end up with an A. If you get B's in the majority of your quizzes but turn in all of your assignments on time, you'll still probably end up with an A. Overall, a very straightforward, pleasant, and fun class.

Super light class that somehow actually helped my health during the semester -- Like it helped me identify and eliminate negative stuff and create some healthier habits. A few quizzes and small submissions, and the asynch structure helps save tons of time. She's a great professor, and this course is awesome.
Definitely take her! Each week had a video lecture with a quiz and/or assignment that were fairly short. The assignments were pretty fun and she was easily reachable and super understanding.

Def take her! I had APPH online, each week had 1/2 hr vids coupled with short quizzes or some activities. Very caring, she gave us weekly emails, very passionate about health subjects too. Do activities/personal project (pretty much participation) and take the quizzes and you'll get an A.
Easy class. Short weekly assignments and online lectures. Pretty easy A.
Great professor, and a very light asynch course you can use to supplement others. Just stay on top of weekly stuff and don't miss deadlines, which is super easy and not even really time-consuming.
don't even need to watch lectures to get an A on the hw/quizzes. super easy class just submit everything on time and you're guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pref Baradel's lectures were educational and helpful. But she did give lots of quizzes and assignments. I'd say it's still an easy A if you finish all of them on time.

I absolutely loved her. Easy class, little work, if that's what you care about, but lectures were amazing. I legitimately felt inspired by her lectures and the content she taught. She loves the content, and does a great job getting us to love it too. I could note rate any higher. Please take and show up to class, she deserves the participation.
She is very passionate about the subject material and does a great job lecturing. Although she gives a lot of assignments and quizzes, they are very easy and don't take much time. No final/midterms.

she is chill. attendance isnt mandatory. she assigns a decent bit of work but its all pretty easy. there are quizzes too but they take home and open note/internet... just do the work and you get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Brings confident and knowledgeable vibes into lectures

I took her during the Ignite 5-week term. While there is more assignments, assignments are easy to complete and quizzes are relatively straightforward. She gives a ton of extra credit and overall it was a good class with not that much effort to get a good grade. There were also no tests and everything in class was posted on canvas.

Lots of lectures and articles are posted but most of the quizzes are common sense. She cares a lot about her students and is a good resource to have at Tech. Great professor to get health credit for with minimal effort, while still learning and improving your health
Glad she doesn't take mandatory attendance and overall good professor
Easy class. Informative if you want. Some of the activities are questionably useful, but it's fine because they're short anyway. Baradel cares!

This is the sweetest lady at the school. I enjoyed her lectures because you actually learn very useful information in this class. You don't have to go to class because she posts her powerpoints but I would recommend going as much as you can just because shes such a great lady. Do your assignments and open note quizzes and you make an A

The EASIEST class at GT. You'll get an A if you spend 1-2 hours on this course weekly. You don't even need to show up to any of the classes or do the extra credit she offers (+3 point to overall grade). Everything (including lecture recordings) are online. Quizzes and assignments are easy. Just turn everything in ON-TIME and you will get an A.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! She gives so much extra credit and has the best lectures and she knows exactly what she is discussing. Also, her class was very enjoyable and there were no midterms or final just bi-weekly quizzes that were all open note. Easiest class I have ever taken, would defiantly take her again. She really does care about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super easy wellness credit. If you do all of the homework assignments on time with a regular amount of effort, you should do very well in the class. The lectures are a little long sometimes, but the weekly quizzes are simple if you take the time to listen to them/read the slides. Overall, solid choice.

Such a sweet woman. she is extremely knowledgeable about health and wellness and her lectures are very educational. quizzes are pretty easy and lots of opportunities for extra credit. one annoying thing was the self- improvement video project, but it wasnt even too bad.
