Very passionate and approachable. Always available to help outside of class. Hilarious. Respects his students.

If you have not taken a calculus class before him, I do not suggest taking his class. He assumes that you've already had a strong base with calculus so he skips over fundamental concepts, but if you are struggling he is more than willing to spend extra time with you going over whatever you're struggling with in detail
Dr. Barone is really nice and tries to explain the topics clearly but as others have mentioned, he can get a bit tricky in his tests. Pay attention and get a really good TA and it won't be too bad.

Honestly an awful professor who makes his tests far more challenging than any other calc I professor at this school. I took AB and BC AP calc in high school, got a 5 on the exam, and decided to not take the credit so I could make sure I really understood calc I before moving on to calc II. Progressively throughout the semester Barone got worse.
Very good professor - helps you learn the course material and provides practice tests. He usually tosses in a few tricky ones so be sure to study enough unlike me.

Great professor! explains things well, but make you keep up with some of the harder topics. Moves kind of fast through topics. willing to help you when need and actually cares about the class. His test can get tricky, but overall good teacher

Absolutely awesome professor. He's tests can be very hard and there's always at least one question on there that's a curveball. However, reviewing your notes and more importantly reading the textbook sections will help.
Very clear lectures, interacts with students, and provides help whenever you need it. Amazing professor.
Awesome.

dr. winter was an amazing professor! he really encouraged us to be critical about everything we read and was overall super kind and laid back. there was a decent amount of homework, but everything built towards the end product and the little assignments we had to do along the way made the end portfolio so much easier to put together.
Definitely choose Dr. Winter for ENGL 1102, you won't regret it. Clear guidelines, class time spent for major projects/homework, interesting subjects.

Mr. Winters is a great ENGL 1102 professor. Although he teaches a class that most are forced to take, he makes it bearable by breaking up the larger tasks into smaller digestible pieces and only assigning busywork that helps progress towards a major project. Very caring and super chill as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Very caring and engaging professor. Anything boring he teaches is what Tech requires him to teach under the 3403 class name. (Some lectures/slides seem like a tangent to the rest of the work)
Overall a funny guy; sort of a lot of busy classwork but an A is almost guaranteed if you do the work.
There were lots of smaller assignments, but they weren't too bad. He cares about his students, and is willing to work with you if anything comes up. Loved this class!

This class is way too much busy work. There are several random assignments every class, and the larger assignments don't make a whole lot of sense when you think about what you're supposed to be learning in this class.

Winter was a nice guy but he made many references to politics during lectures and it was obvious what his leaning was. I didn't think this was appropriate for a business communication class. He also can be a tough grader on writing assignments and gives a lot of busywork that takes hours. I'd avoid him if possible but he's not too bad

assigned a ton of busy work but easy grader

HATED his lecture vids(100% personal taste tbf), but he seemed condescending/pretentious.

For a "business communications" class, we barely covered stuff actually used in offices, instead making a podcast + commercial, skills 99% of us will never use. That might be Tech's fault but still demotivating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Winter is an outstanding professor who makes attempts to get the audience involved in interesting topics covered in his class. Interesting class about authenticity and belonging in the Jim Crow Era. You will pass with a C with minimal effort, and dedicating about 3 hours per week outside of lectures will get you an A. Country Robert Downey Jr.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you're looking for an easy English class don't take Professor Winter. Don't get me wrong; he is an amazing professor, but an assignment is due almost every day of the week (basically busy work). He is also a pretty tough grader (he reads everything and leaves tons of feedback), but revision opportunities after every Artifact should get you an A.

It is clear that he cares for students. His feedback is personalized for each assignment. He has such a happy attitude despite his class being so early in the morning: it is contagious. He clearly has a passion for English.

He's willing to work with students. And he allows 5 absences, no questions. He is understanding. I would take his class again

I genuinely enjoyed Dr. Winter's class (and that's saying a lot given the fact that I despise english/language arts). He takes attendance, so make sure to show up to class. He grades pretty easy, so as long as you do the work, you'll get a decent grade. He would often crack jokes and has a cool, chill personality/vibe to him.

Easy class, but a bit of work! Dr. Winter is a professor who truly cares about his students. He leaves constructive yet kind feedback on nearly every piece of work. He's easily accessible to students and overall an understanding, patient, and respectable professor!

You don't really learn much, but you get the A as long as you follow bare minimum rubric guidelines, which are stated clearly. If you are looking for a typical English class where you read novels and discuss/write, get ready for a huge disappointment in that regards. He talks a little too much but overall a really nice person and a solid teacher!

Loved english with Dr Winters, the artifacts are pretty standard and he is really clear about grading criteria. Some assignments are more like busy work, but I never spent more than 1-2 hrs on HW per week. Also gives the opportunity to revise your artifacts to get extra credit. I would recommend taking him, funny professor & cares about students.

He's pretty good, I thought he was annoying but that might just be because I had him at 8 am. The class itself is pretty easy, just a little time-consuming and he's a harsh grader on papers. The bare minimum effort will get you at least a B though because of extra credit and revision opportunities.

Pretty good professor, makes it very clear whats going to be on the exams. the 2 projects are weighted the same as the 3 midterms, so gotta start those projects early. Lots of opportunity for extra credit with the projects, and very lenient late policy.

2 projects with plenty of extra credit. All lecture slides are online. Make sure to start projects and homework early. Plenty of practice tests available on canvas. Office hours help a lot from what I have heard. Great professor, but I have heard Wills might be slightly better, but both are great. Pretty easy class, not very test heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There were 2 projects with opportunities for extra credit if you put in significantly  more work. Imo project 2 way easier than project 1. The first half of the semester was insanely easy but everything is concentrated in Late October->December so plan for that. He has a tendency to not understand your question so you need to be specific.
A really enjoyable and light class. Exams are extremely fair and there is ample opportunity to get extra credit on the two projects. Though, both of them are pretty time consuming. Highly recommended
Easy class, never showed up and still got an A. just do the practice exams before each exam; they are very similar. 2 pretty easy projects and a few hw. 3 exams + a final
I enjoyed taking his class. There were clear expectations for success in his class, and everything was manageable if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Collins is so caring. I had a mental breakdown at the start of my semester and he was very understanding. Work hard on the projects and the homework!!! Attend every lecture. This course has amazing TAs and a great professor. In my opinion, there's no reason not to get an A in this class, because the prof and TAs actually want to help you.

He's a very no BS professor and can occasionally be a LITTLE dry but the class is so cool and he genuinely knows what he is teaching very well. So long as you pace yourself, pay attention and, most importantly, start exam prep and projects EARLY, you will end up fine... Lots of bonus points and awesome TAs!!! Collins was a big help too :)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was pretty good. The lectures did their job and made everything understandable. There were not very many homeworks, but projects were pretty big, and you should start early. The projects are also a pretty good way to get some extra credit to buffer if you spend more time on them.

It is a difficult class for sure, but if you listen to Collins' lectures you'll get on fine. There is a lot to study for and Project 1 is incredibility time-consuming, but afterwards the class is not so bad. Office hours get full VERY fast and you should come prepared to wait and have something meaningful to get help with. TAs are VERY helpful.

Loved Professor Collins, he was very personable and he taught lectures very well. The class itself is very clearly structured and it's in your favor. There are 3 exams worth 10% each, a final and two projects. The two projects were very enjoyable and you learn quite a bit. Would definitely take Collins again, also the Head GTA was the goat, RD!

Kinda dry but still a good explainer if you ask questions. Lecture slides/videos are useful. Homework is easy. Projects are easy but very time consuming; no big deal if you plan ahead. Office hours can get very busy. Exams are very similar to practice exams and very fair.

Overhated. Lectures can be a little dry, but he teaches the content well and is very understanding when answering questions. Not very easy to talk to outside of class, but not mean. Start the projects early(especially project 1) and utilize the crib sheet policy.

Dr. Collins was not very caring for the students and the class reflected that, there was a high workload that demanded constant perfection in order to do well. Too much work for a 2 credit class and there was a lack of support for students.

He was an assistant teacher to Dr. Johnson in Spring 2023. He was not active in the class, but he seems decent and knows what he's talking about. Wished he was more available to help, as that class was extremely difficult for me.

Collins isn't a terrible professor. His lectures aren't bad and can often get the point across. Wills's recorded lectures are course resources and are more than effective if you don't like Collins's lectures. The course is difficult and you'll find yourself working pretty hard on projects, but overall, you'll learn a lot.

He is very rude in piazza and will make you regret asking for help. He is a good lecturer and explains stuff relatively well compared to other GT professors. Most of the course is TA based anyway. good luck getting a hold of a TA during their office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a cool guy. Kinda comes off as uncaring or rude over email. Teaches well.

Figured this needed an update and professor Collins deserves less hate. The course has improved since COVID-19 era (technically still is a pandemic right...?). The condescending tone is pretty much the same on piazza along with Kevin but that's not the case; how they talk on the internet and it's misinterpreted. They've taught this course for 10+yr
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I only took the class because I had to. Hes rude, condescending, will make you feel like crap for having issues you cant control or for even just asking questions. Piazza replies are always did you even pay attention. Absolutely awful and he completely ruined my mental health. He should be paying for my therapy since he comes up so often.

So much reading. Labs take freaking forever, and prelabs have to be done before lab session. While giving a presentation to Collins, it felt like I was talking to a brick wall. 0 feedback whatsoever. Not even a head nod or anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is the definition of an elitist donkey at absolutely does not care about his students and actively makes them feel stupid. He's the only one who teaches the class so you have to take him, but be aware that he'll ask for your feedback and then spend an entire lecture telling you why you're stupid for suggesting anything other than his OG plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was just fine. Not great not bad. Gets too much hate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is one of the most active professors outside class I've ever had. This class is ton of work and makes you really work for the grade. Final exam was very tough but was curved a bit. Labs can take 3-6 hours for sure plus about 30-45 mins on reports if you want good grades. His lecture felt monotone at times but mostly due to bad mic on his end.

Tbh I didn't interact with Prof Collins as much as the other Prof (who imo is more active). Mostly lectured on technical aspects and was pretty clear. Really reinforced concepts from ECE 2020. ECE 2031 is just a lot of work in general and you gotta work for your grade. Rough final exam (but curved) and get a good group for the final project.
Very rude and condescending! If you ask a question, be prepared to get laughed at or be told to "read the syllabus". I wish there were other professors who taught this class.

The course is had enough for a 2credit hour but despite the prof "trying to improve" his attitude just makes the course more aggravating. Collins makes you feel bad for asking dumb questions and gives canned feedback to very simple clarification questions. The worst is that they tell the TAs so little so they can't help at ALL on the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Collins tries his best to improve the course from student feedback and data every semester. The course is generally difficult but it's Georgia Tech and I can also say that I have a better understanding of a lot of topics from ECE2020 because of the lectures and labs in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An alright professor, but the course is horrible. It took me an average of 1.5 labs sections to finish each lab due to the overwhelming amount of tedium in each one. The reading checks expect students to read 20-40 pages every week and are worth more than the project you spend half the semester on.

The prelab quizzes weighed the most out of the entire class and asked about very obscure details from the book. Hardly anybody finishes during the lab hour so open-hour lab is always filled with other people, so the only way to finish your lab on time is to do it outside of lab, IF you even can do it outside of the lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I know two people who have lost their 4.0's in this class. To do well prepare to spend 10+ hours a week. There were always people in open hours because hardly anyone finishes during the lab. It is super helpful if you have already taken 2035. The lab report instructions are vague and they will take points for the smallest mistakes.

Class is terribly structured - the only guidance you have is the manual, the textbook is not helpful for prelab quizzes or labs and the lecture is very surface level. GTA and UTAs in lab are the only sources of help as the instructors are very hands-off, especially Collins. Unhelpful answers on piazza. Ruined my interest in the subject.

This class sucked the life out of me, all I wanted to do was go in lab and get out as soon as possible. I don't feel like I learned anything because after I finished the lab I forgot what I did. Lectures are dry and don't help much and professor is slightly condescending on Piazza, but iS responsive on there. Only one exam that is heavily weighted
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is a CMPE class. The entire final project is based on assembly code which you learn a week before starting the project. The pre-lab quizzes are worth too high of a percentage of the final grade and are extremely nitpicky. Also Collins doesn't give a rat's ass about students and just cares about his own ego.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Collins was pretty good at reviewing 2020 concepts in lecture which helped during the labs. The labs were also pretty easy to do within the section. However, the prelab quizzes were outrageous and were weighted far too high for our grade imo. Also, there was a ton of work for the final project which made the class not seem like a 2 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Skip the pointless reading from Rapid Prototyping and lecture. Labs are as simple as following the (confusing) lab manual. Second practical exam was basically impossible, and the ONE exam asks about details so specific they're basically irrelevant. Extremely condescending when asked about grading mistakes. Pre-labs and lab reports are lengthy.

Lectures were ok, with a lot of material being review of ECE 2020. New concepts were explained clearly, and instructions for future assignments and projects were clearly communicated. Final project does take some time, and can only be tested on in the lab. In lab tests seem to be significantly easier than past years.

Tough Class that's aware of itself and curves accordingly. Quizzes are tough and there's no real way to prepare for them outside of reading the dry manual. Labs often can't be completed in one class and require you to return over the weekend or during another class to complete them. The one test is tough but curved generously so no real worries.

2031 lectures are boring and for the most part unnecessary. You will spend many many many hours completing labs and the final project although most of your grade is made up of two tests (both very difficult) and pre-lab quizzes. Collins pretty much stays out of the picture but does give good feedback if you ask for help. Prepare to work hard.

I hated this class-- mainly because I'm an electrical engineer, yet I have to take this computer engineering design course. Anyway, I had a near 100% lab and project average, but because I didn't know the error messages for Quartus and screwed up the stupid prelab quizzes I got a B. Anyway, you'll love Collins' class if you're Comp E. I did not.
cool prof. but lecture is real boring.
nice guy.  too bad the lab has no money left to fix anything.  you'll hate the robots too.

Lecture is really boring and he goes very slowly.  Class lasted five minutes extra almost every time.  He doesn't seem to ever understand anyone's question.  Lecture for this class is unecessary, though.  He is a nice guy.

Goes on tangents instead of teaching in lecture. Exams are way harder than they need to be. If you do not know how to code beforehand, prepare to spend your life on this class if you want a decent grade. The TA's carry. The other prof for this class is better. He's good at public speaking, but he just talks about his failed football career.

There is no point in going to lectures besides taking the quiz at the end. You'll learn nothing in lecture as he just yaps about football career and flex his two degrees. He'll teach the material that you needed for last weeks homework. Test are very rough and prepare to spend hours on the homework. Whole class was just a comedy show...

Stallworth is an okay lecturer - goes on tangents and spends forever on the same example. Also always behind where you are in the homework - which is basically the foundation of the class. I would recommend going to recitation instead and going to lecture just to get your dose of doomscrolling in.

5/5 if this were Rate My Comedian, but his ramblings, including but not limited to figure skating, cost of attendance, race, and GT sports, left little class time to learn MATLAB. You are often exposed to a topic for the first time in homework, leading the GOAT TAs to do all the heavy lifting. My apologies to anyone with no prior coding experience.

Lectures were not very useful but mandatory with 1 question quizzes each lecture, but some are dropped at the end. The final can be exempted if you have an A before the final. Homework takes a few hours but if you do them yourself, they help a lot for the exams and reduce how much you need to study.
Spends class talking about football, not CS. Don't take the class if you don't already know how to code. The TA's carry this class.

Changed the curriculum he wanted to do 1 week before the exam, and did not provide the resources for those topics. Only way to study that new material was to find one or two pictures of his MATLAB scripts during lectures, as no other previous sections had done the material, nor was any other video or script published. Very disorganized

He's decent. Hilarious guy. Meh lecturer - rambled a lot, uncoordinated with his TAs. I found it fine since I had prior experience with coding/MATLAB, but if this is your first coding class, be ready to do a lot of learning yourself. Exams were sometimes a bit long, but mostly fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He's funny...I'll give him that. But he has no coordination with the TAs, the tests are long and difficult, the homework can take hours out of your week, and he rambles during lecture. I got Bs on the first two midterms, which isn't too bad, but I know a lot of students who did way worse.

This guy... tests are ridiculous. Never enough time. Homework is extremely long and arduous, so by the time you reach the extra credit portion you have already been working for hours. Testing periods are 300+ people, which are on a lockdown browser. You have to scroll up and down continuously to see the question and code. Also, lectures ramble.

I'm choosing peace and kind words but I really really do not like him. You learn nothing in lecture, have a quiz for participation that's all or nothing in EVERY class, he is disrespectful to accommodations, and I could keep going on and on. The exams are impossible and only test writing like 100+ lines of code 5 times.

Unc did not teach 😭. The coordination amongst the TAs and Stallworth was also clearly not the best. exams took nearly a month to grade and recitation material didn't always match lecture. Best way to study is use all the practice resources provided and practice intensely with MatLab coding (especially if you have minimal prior coding experience).

He was an alright professor. He had the tendency to go on relatively long tangents but did teach the course content well. I had previous coding experience, which made it easier, but it still could have been a lot better.

He gets distracted super easily and rarely covers everything that we were supposed to cover. The homeworks are super lengthy, although they are very good practice for tests. STUDY FOR THE TESTS, OR THEY WILL KICK YOUR BEHIND. Do the extra credit, you will probably need it. Overall, the extra credit and test-drop make up for the lack of teaching.

Professor Stallworth is very funny, but lectures mainly skim topics and attendance is mostly for mandatory quizzes. Homework is much harder and is very time-consuming since you must learn the content yourself. Recitations are hit or miss, tests are super hard, but grading helps.

Took an online section of his MATLAB class. Lectures were optional and he tended to go off topic during them. However, exam review sessions were very informative. 
Be ready for long homework grinds! Do the extra credit!

Professor can go off topic on completely unrelated tangents for 10-15 minutes at a time, but his explanations of MATLAB were solid. Course is very manageable if you have previous coding experience, but can be challenging if its your first time coding (like basically any other coding class).
Like Doug from Up, distracted by everything he notices. Incredibly hard tests and over-worked TAs.

Stallworth is pretty entertaining, but his time management skills are not great (you learn the info the day before homework is due). The tests are the hardest part of the class, especially the tracing problems. Overall, Stallworth is a great guy but a frustrating and difficult teacher for those with no prior coding knowledge.

I got a 58 on the first exam and was absolutely devastated and thought I was gonna fail the class (freshman canon event), but I studied really hard and managed to get an A in the class. I learned the most by going to recitations and the TAs (shout out to Victor!). The MATLAB grader is extremely useful for exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

He was very nice, but got off topic very fast and very often. If you have never coded before, you can never miss class, because everything builds off the lecture before. Lecture is optional, but he does in-class quizzes that count for a grade. I will say that I did pretty bad on exams 1-3, but did well on the final and homeworks and still got a B.

Funny guy, but bad lecturer. Goes off topic and rants a lot, making students unprepared for his very difficult tests. TAs are way more useful; go to them if you need help. If you're like me and came into this class inexperienced with coding, you're gonna have to practice A LOT for an A. Self-taught the whole class pretty much... good luck.

Pros: Funny prof, lots of opportunity for extra credit, makes practice exam questions, good TA's 
Cons : HARD exams (graded slow - TA's are overworked) , end of lecture quizzes , useless lectures (to which he is always late to)

Cool and funny guy, but really cant teach the material very well. Maybe its time for retirement.

Nice guy but not a great teacher, he would get very sidetracked and spend half of lecture reviewing material from the week before, making us fall behind on concepts for that week's homework. Homework can be tricky but will prepare you for the tests so actually do it, recitation is goated, each lecture has a quiz at the end with a code.
He was a good teacher when he decided to teach, but he showed up 10 minutes late every day and was often off-topic. Was a very entertaining professor.

He's a great guy but he gets off topic easily. I knew how to code coming into this class and still had a hard time. The tests are VERY hard. Thankfully the final can replace a test grade so that was how I got an A but definitely wasn't easy.

All he does is talk about his daughter or his 2 minutes on the Packers as their kicker. Rarely talks about the topics actually needed on exam. Wouldn't want to blame him for the course structure, except he's the AD and could make this MATLAB class not so 'python-y'. He has super hard tests, and also loves getting power tripping TAs.

He's a funny guy, and I love his stories in classes, but his teaching style just wasn't for me. If I was a complete newbie at coding, I'm not sure I would have been able to keep up with the class. The online videos he has on the Canvas were far more helpful.

He tended to go on rants and not get through all the content needed to complete homework, so often had to find other resources to learn it. Recitation is extremely helpful. He is interesting and funny though!

Went into this course with no coding experience, but felt lectures and recitation were enough to succeed. Homework can be time consuming, but it prepares you well for tests. Also gave lots of extra practice and mock exams to prepare for the tests. Up to 5% EC and final exam is optional. Only gripe is that getting test grades back took quite a bit.

Great professor with lots of knowledge on the subject, which is more evident in the lecture videos than lecture because of the side tracking. There is a daily quiz that you take at the end of lecture as well. The exams will change for next sem so I will not make a comment on that, though the grades coming back takes quite a while.

Exams do not evaluate your understanding. They say they try to give you partial credit but I lost 20 points due to typos on an exam. Besides that everything else is easy and Stallworth is great; y'all are hating on him for no reason. Also the exams should change starting in the spring so that you can actually code (so my complaint becomes obsolete)

If you have a previous understanding of basic CS concepts, this class is easy. He does yap a lot but that honestly kept me more interested/let me pay attention to the lecture. The videos are also helpful to watch, and the homework and exams were hard, but interesting (at least to me). If you put in the work this class is not hard.

He yaps a lot. He gets off topic easily and I got very little from the lectures. He's a funny guy, but I'm there to learn matlab. He has lecture videos up that I watched instead of going to class. The videos were great and way better than lecture.

Dude straight up creates the hardest exams - gives a lot of hw- and yaps about NFL/sports/ or some side quest 50% of the class. Just don't go to lectures and show up in the last 15 mins for the quiz, really. Everyone basically failed Exam 1.

Good teacher when he stays on task. The homework does take a while and sometimes he hasn't taught what's covered in the homework. Attending recitation is helpful and gives extra credit for the class. He knows what he's talking about but it's frustrating when he gets off task. The tests are pretty difficult, but there is plenty of practice available

He's a really funny guy, but gets sidetracked all the time in lectures. Spends half the time talking about his football career and the other half doing an amateur stand-up routine. You will spend hours on your homework, and tests are hard. His lecture notes and videos are really good. Sometimes homework will be due before he covers its content.

Lowkey the goat. Informative lectures as are the recitations with his TAs (+1.25 EC if you attend all). There're like 24 five-min quizzes of which 16 best matter (sometimes you can get a free 100% if lecture is too long). Lectures are fun and engaging through personal stories. 3 exams + final can be dodged. Hw comes with EC part and can be tedious.

Stallworth is a nice and funny guy, but yikes this class is awful. It's put forward as a beginner's class, but if you have no coding experience you will struggle. Get ready to spend hours on homework. There are EC opportunities which is nice. But yeah I can't wait to be done with this and never take another coding course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
1371 is by no means a "beginner" programming class. Even if you have some experience, getting used to MATLAB takes some time. The homework can be a massive time suck if you're new to programming but the TAs are great during recitation.

That being said, Stallworth is extremely funny and a great guy. Just be prepared to put a bit of effort in.

He's a great guy and pretty funny, but he can tend to get off topic during lectures. I stopped attending lecture and just used the videos provided on canvas, which were amazing! You can learn everything from the videos and go as fast or slow as you need. Recitation is extremly helpful, especially when preparing for exams. Do the practice tests too!
Had him for challenge. Easily the most inspiring teacher I've met. He keeps his students engaged and pushes them to do their best.
SO BAD. TEACH YOURSELF....b/c he tells stories during lecture. Good luck :)

Honestly did not go to class after the first week b/c the online videos are super great. Prof. Stallworth did seem like a really great and funny guy though, and apparently he alludes to exam questions in lecture sometimes. Make sure to do all practice exams to prepare, and sometimes you have to memorize approaches to be efficient (esp. last unit)!

I was TERRIFIED to take CS1371 at tech because...ive never TOUCHED code before, however Mr. Stallworth really does try and teach you from the very beginning assuming no one even knows what a function is. Make sure you go to recitation, he is super funny and made my 8am class a little easier to get up for. GO TO OFFICE HOURS if your struggling

I didn't really go to class due to Stalworth being kinda a slow lecturer.  He is pretty funny and all but he doesn't teach the material all that well imo.  The tests are straight forward just time is such a constraint like u legit need to memorize how to solve problems not solve them during the exam or else u will run out of time.  TIME Y

This was my first CS class, so I was intimidated at first, but Stallworth offers a lot of resources to help you succeed. He does sometimes go off topic during class but he's a funny guy. I learned most of the content in recitation or through the lecture videos on Canvas.

He's an amazing guy, the tests can be a little tedious, but what else can you expect at a Georgia Tech CS class especially made for engineers. The class isn't easy, but the professor does want you to succeed! I say go to lectures, and then fill in the gaps with his videos and recitation. His lectures are slow but perfect for introductions.

Stallworth is a very fun prof, however this does not translate to the quality of his teaching. Most stuff was not gone over very well and homework was easy in the beginning and VERY difficult towards the end. Class seemed to just ramp up out of nowhere. Lectures went over the same stuff 2-3 times yet I still learned most content in recitation.

Funny and personable, but was usually super late to lecture and I never really got much out of his lectures, he tended to ramble off topic. Course material was relatively easy and exams were fair, just go to recitation and watch online lectures, lecture wasnt really worth attending.

Great lecturer but the man can yap. Easy course and prof if you've coded before, but he goes slow enough for someone who hasn't coded to understand and learn. Go to recitations, the extra credit for it is a great whole grade booster. The final grade is exam heavy, but if you can do the homeworks without needing ChatGPT then you'll be fine.

Took in summer, 10 HW's which all took very long, anywhere from 12 to 18 hours. 3 exams and 1 final, tests were 70% of your grade. Quiz at every lecture. Extra credit if enough recitations are attended. Teaches well, but near impossible to get a hold of outside of class. Had an injury over the summer and it took him a month to respond to me.

Professor Stallworth is a cool guy and very funny. A lot of times his lectures may feel like a ton of yap about unrelated topics, but the class itself is pretty easy. He gives you all the resources you need to succeed in the class -- recitation, videos, and extra credit. The final is optional so do good on your tests.

Professor Stallworth is a hilarious lecturer, and even though he may not cover everything in class, the recitation, videos, and extra credit are more than enough to succeed in this class. Final is optional, he is the GOAT for 1371 rn.
Funny and good at teaching, but kind of talks a lot during lecture

I love how he would try to make topics in class relatable to his students. He does an amazing job of breaking down the information. CS1371 is a challenging class, so you still have to put in the effort, but Professor Stallworth will do everything he can to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stallworth doesn't tell as many stories as he used to. The class itself is structured weirdly. I took 3 years of programing before this and did not do too well on all the midterms/exams. MATLAB is very niche, so if you're good at it, more power to ya.

Similar to what I have seen this prof does ramble on at times and gets easily distracted but is also a fun guy. Since all the topics already have video lectures and in person lectures were not mandatory, the class itself is easy but make sure to sign up to and go to a recitation both for extra credit and to learn more!

hilarious + awesome guy, not the greatest professor. rambles on a lot and feels like 10 mins of content in a 75 minute class. for 1371, he had online videos and those were great, so class didn't really feel useful after that. exams can be tricky but there's plenty of practice problems from past sems, optional final

is a good professor but gets sidetracked a lot so I would just rely on his video lectures which are a great resource. the class has a lot of homework every week and missing just one can take a hit on your grade. however, there is a good amount of extra credit and the tests were pretty fair. do the hw and go to recitation.

His lectures aren't very useful especially if you're new to coding. It's very rare he'll even have Matlab on the screen. Very cool guy just not a good professor. If you have ODS accommodations I strongly recommend finding another prof for CS because Stallworth is not a fan of responding to emails in the slightest. The online videos help a lot.

Wasn't a hard class but he wasn't a good professor. He constantly went on tangents and most of the learning I did in 1371 was from his videos and the canvas modules, not his lectures. That said, he is decently funny and pretty fair when it comes to grading & understanding circumstances.
The professor did not ever teach and only yapped about random things in his life.

Pretty standard, can sometimes get very off-topic or do too much background on the subject and not actually teach the subject fully, but he posts separate videos that you can look back to. Might have to do some of your own learning esp if this is your first coding class. Exams are straightforward, hws are tougher but lots of options for help.

Professor Cedric makes lectures really interesting and fun. He does rant and go off tangent sometimes but all the things you need to learn he will teach, so as long as you listen and do the HWs you're fine.

I came into this course with no coding background and found it very heavy on coursework and studying needed. BUT thats not to say I didn't love it. The TA's are AMAZING; you should sign up for a recitation, they provide great insight. I have insanely fond memories of this class and Stallworth was a very passionate professor (he did yap at times..).

1371 is a personal class. Everyone starts with different amounts of coding experience so Stallworth starts slowly, however once the class gets rolling he can't teach everything. The best way to study is to do homework problems and practice exams and figure out what works for you. Stallworth is engaging and nice. There are many resources available.

Difficult class if you don't have coding experience. Stallworth's a funny guy, but the homeworks are a little more complicated than what he teaches in class. Definitely use other resources like his lecture videos, Kantwon, and recitation. Beware of tests. If you struggle with time management the midterms will be hell.

Super funny lecturer, but would sometimes go on side tangents that weren't related to the lecture at all. Clear that he cared for all his students. Applying concepts taught in class was sometimes tricky, but it really depends on how much prior coding experience you had.

The teacher was often late to class, and often went on tangents not related to the class. Your grade consisted of 3 exams and a final, the first exam is relatively easy, so the second and third exam usually is a grade dropper and no curves. there is opportunity for extra credit, and the TA's are great.

The lecture was somewhat useful for understanding, but the class is hard if you haven't coded before. The homeworks weren't too time consuming, and the tests are formatted exactly like the practice tests posted in canvas.

Not a good professor. Late to class, jokes a lot, tells stories about chick-fil-a or football. Explains some CS concepts and MATLAB functions, but not how to solve problems. I spent a lot of time on the homeworks and had to get help from TAs.

I mean he's not bad. Compared to the notorious rickard landry who is on administrative leave for eating a tampon in class, but like eh. He's not that great either. He would often get off topic and just teach so slow that its pretty hard to stay focused. But he knows what he's talking about and the tests and hw are easy.

He's the best. Loved his lectures for the one month I went to them. Made my mornings really energetic and since I transferred from UGA it was funny hearing him talk about it. Learned the concept initially from his lectures but later just went to recitation to understand it throughly. I would definitely take him again if I had to take CS again.
Okay lectures, homework could sometimes be rough. Go to recitation and/or take Kantwon for best understanding. Exams were graded a bit harsh, but offered multiple grading schemes.

The class is not necessarily hard, especially if you are familiar with another coding language. There is almost no structure to the class. Combine that with him being a D1 yapper and classes fall short often. Be prepared to learn independently of classes. Homeworks take forever but are often similar to exams. Between that and recitation you'll pass

Not a great lecturer, but not a bad one either. His ranting honestly didn't bother me much but sometimes he falls behind on material which makes it hard to do homework. Mostly taught myself from posted notes, help desk, and recitation. Def make use of the TAs and recitation, they're really great. overall not that hard, esp if you've coded before

Great guy. He spends most of lecture ranting about different things. MATLAB isnt neccesarily hard to learn. HW does a great job of teahing you the content. After first few lectures I stopped showing up. Recitation. TA's were my main source of knowledge. 2 extra points of extra credit are available.  you should be fine w him. go to recitaion

MID ass prof, his lectures are fine for the first half of the semester but after that going to lecture is useless.  Just ask chatGPT to teach you matlab tbh its not that bad of a language especially if you've coded before.  A lot of people swear by Kantwon's lectures (which are also recoreded) so just go to those bc the class is standardized.

Professor Stallworth is a good professor, making this course as simple as possible. MATLAB as a coding language is not preferred, but he gives shortcuts to make it as easier. Within lectures, he adds a bit of humor and rants slightly. There are multiple chances for extra credit. I didn't need to go to recitation or the Friday lectures and did well.

His lectures aren't phenomenal, but he ultimately teaches you everything you need to know. The most important thing is to take advantage of the homework, because if you understand the homework problems then the exams should be easy. There is also extra credit in the form of some extra homework problems and recitation attendance.

got a 72 on the first midterm, but got 97s on the other two midterms. wouldn't say that stallworth helped me much, I found much better luck sitting in kantwon's lectures. i enjoyed how funny stallworth was and he occasionally had good rants. would show up 10-15 minutes late towards the end of the semester though. the final is optional :)

Great guy, but lectures were rough. I survived by recitations and help desk. Overall a very nice guy but I felt that there was no need to even go to lecture. highly recommend going to recitations and help desk especially for the homework.

Professor Stallworth is an amazing person, and and I loved his class. However, I found it hard to pay attention to the actual material as he would sidetrack during class. If you can follow along with Stallworth, amazing, but because of my learning style I wasn't able to adapt, so I sat in on Kantwon's lectures instead.

Stallworth was really annoying as a prof. He seems like a really nice guy but as a prof he could never stay on topic to the point that we never actually covered the needed material in class. The content wasn't too hard but trying to learn it from him would be immensely difficult. Just go to one of the weekly recitations or watch Kantwon's lectures
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had never coded coming into this course and I had a hard time in the course itself. Stallworth as an introductory CS professor does not do a great job. His lectures do not go into much detail. They cover the very basic concepts and are not very useful for the homework. His final was horrible; I had to resubmit my answers multiple times.

This class is solely homework and tests. All homework is structured the same for each unit. Stallworth knows what he is talking about and makes lecture enjoyable. He is a funny guy. There are lots of study aids available, final is optional and does not hurt your grade.

Very solid guy, went through Tech as a student too and understands the culture here better than most professors. While he does tend to ramble, he always eventually covers the course content. Super cool guy. His explanations are simplistic and clear, very good for those who don't know a ton about coding. Just do the homework and you'll be fine.

For CS 1371 all students will complete same homework and tests regardless of professor. Nice guy, tends to ramble, eventually covers all the important information. Having never coded before, he did a fine job of teaching the concepts and covering everything necessary for the course.

I'd never taken a CS class before this, but Stallworth made 1371 enjoyable. Sometimes the lectures can get dry, but Stallworth will at least throw in a joke or two to make it more bearable. If you actually do your homework, you'll be fine. This is not a hard class per se, it just takes some effort.

CS 1100 is a pretty boring class honestly, the class is essentially just listening to Stallworth or a guest speaker talk about career advancement. Stallworth himself is super engaging, and about half the time brings in a really engaging guest as well. For a class where showing up is basically the whole deal, Stallworth does it right.

Personally, this class was difficult for me since I'm not great at CS, and I had to spend many hours on homework per week. The lectures often did not include a thorough explanation of things we needed to be able to understand for the exam. If you struggle in this lecture, other professor's lectures are also posted on canvas.

Stallworth's lectures were literally entertainment and mostly got the material across. He is very genuine and wants you to succeed, but he's not very accessible outside of class. The homework took a long time each week, but if you can do the homework, you are set for the tests.

Great personality and loves to interact with students. Tends to go off-topic a lot, but we still get all of the material by the end of the lectures, and he answers any questions as they are asked throughout the lecture. I only attended ~50% of lectures, and still got all of the material I needed through the lecture notes posted in Canvas.
He knows the class but doesn't teach it well. He frequently goes off on tangents talking about things not related to CS at all and wastes class time.

though professor stallworth was fun during lecture, this was not very helpful in learning the material of the course. he would go off on tangents and it felt like a waste of time. for someone that has never coded or has not coded is 2+ years, he is not very helpful. he never posted office hours either so there was no way to recieve help from him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man never showed up but I mean it was an okay class. It's only one credit and it doesn't matter who you have, so if you get Stallworth don't worry about it. The class is standardized. You don't really do much the assignments are just annoying.

I felt underprepared for this course as a first time coder. Stallworth would share funny stories and was an overall funny and genuine guy; however, I would not recommend taking his section if you are not an experienced coder. The course was very test heavy, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities to raise your grade. The TAs carried.

The TAs really carried this class. I am a first-time coder and this class was a struggle for me. He was a really funny guy with stories but did not help me pass my exams and learn to code well. Do not take this teacher as a first-time coder. He is really good if you already have prior knowledge.

I really liked this class and stallworth a lot!! it was super interesting and really satisfying when you get the code right. the homeworks take up time each week, but if you can complete the homework and practice problems, you can do well on the exams.

Stallworth is an energetic, amazing lecturer who will teach you MATLAB and CS principles from the ground up. As a former NFL player and a dean in the COC, his lectures are energetic and engaging. I'd highly recommend attending them. He can be rather inaccessible outside of lecture, but is willing to answer questions afterwards.

what the hell, how are there not any 1 star reviews? Summer '22 was a mess. Test material was only revealed 12hrs before the exam, and the TA's did ALL the heavy lifting for this course. Stallworth cant even show up to class on time and for some reason makes us speedrun exams.
Tests were very poorly planned and communicated. Spends lots of time on somewhat entertaining but useless tangents. Go to recitation.

Honestly, I never went to lectures in this class and learned each week's worth of content in about an hour from the lecture notes, which were clear enough. Not super accessable outside of class or good with communication, and TA's carried the class to prepare for exams. Not a terrible professor, put in the work and you'll get an A.

Was a great professor for an intro to programming class, he is clear on his grading criteria and offers the equivalent of half a letter grade on extra credit. On the down side professor Stallworth is known for going off in tangents and having a conflicting schedule. Recitation will be key, especially early in the semester to have good foundations.

Professor Stallworth's 1371 class was a great experience. Lectures are hilarious and are also geared towards doing well on the homework assignments which are worth a large part of the grade. If you have some experience with coding, you'll have no trouble, and if you don't, it's a great time to learn!

I took this class in the Spring of 2021 when it was fully online, so I cannot speak to how he does as an in-person lecturer. However, he was an amazing professor. The lectures were extremely helpful. The homeworks were shared across all of 1371, but I was always fully prepared for the homeworks. I had never coded before 1371, and I had no troubles.

Professor Stallworth has to be my favorite professor at Georgia Tech. I had him for Matlab (1371) and he was fantastic. He lays out the course expectations clearly and is very organized with everything. I would highly recommend him.
One of my favorite teachers at Tech. Lectures are informative and easy to follow.

The homework load and difficulty in this class was insane, though that wasn't necessarily his fault. His lectures are funny and pretty good, but he is terribly difficult to reach after class. He also almost always showed up at least five minutes late (one time around 15 minutes) to my 50 minute classes.

If you have no previous coding experience, this will be a hard class. Otherwise, not terrible but a lot of work. He doesn't actually teach much in class, but he's very entertaining so you actually do pay attention to the stuff he does teach. He doesn't utilize class time well but the homework teaches you basically everything. Google will teach you.

He's very nice, personable, and a great teacher. He was one of the only teachers whose lecture I enjoyed going to. Regardless, he would get off topic sometimes since he wanted to connect with us but he hits everything that needs to be taught. There is a lot of hard homework though so GO TO RECITATION and make sure to make friends to help on hwk.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stallworth seems to be a really good guy and great at coding however having him as a prof was super stressful. This class relies on the TAs to make all the hw, tests, etc. so he wasn't really aware of what assignments we were doing nor what was on them. I've heard that the other CS1371 profs were better at explaining and giving examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very funny and engaging professor, however, don't rely solely on lecture material to complete the homework.

Cedric is pretty nice guy but is absurdly tough grader. He lacks clear grading criteria and absolutely horrific feedback. He'll cut off say 5-10 points and only write positives instead of telling us what to improve on. He is one of the better choices for JRD 2 so keep that in mind. He also put in grades pretty late this sem which was stressful

TAKE KANTWON! I do not recommend taking Stallworth for CS 1371. His lecture is always behind the homework, so you end up teaching yourself by reading other instructor's notes. We had to email the dean to get him to not give us a test the day after our "wellness day."

Stallworth was so good a professor that I ended up changing my major to CS. He's hilarious, a great lecturer, and his passion for the material was contagious. Everyone talks about how great Kantwon is an that's no doubt true, but Stallworth is not to be underestimated. He is a fabulous professor in every way
Class is chill. Polls are fun. Cool guy but can be a little slow at times.

He is good at giving real world examples for coding concepts and overall is a great teach for an intro to coding class. He projects his screen and goes through code and examples in MATLAB. The recitations are super helpful though when he forgets to mention a needed function for the hw & on Fridays he would go over helpful tips for HW.

Prof. Stallworth is awesome. He definitely cares a lot about his students and is willing to work as hard as he needs to help you succeed. His explanations are thorough and he's been teaching the class for years so he's pretty understanding. He's also a fun guy - plays music and puts up a poll at lectures to keep things interesting. Would recommend.
Awesome class! Stallworth will make you work for the grade, especially with the long and arduous weekly homework. TAs are super cool and very accessible, 10/10 would take again.

I took this class remotely and to have no prior experience in programming it went great. There are lots of resources available to use and its good to always reach out to TAs or other classmates for help. Totally recommend Prof. Stallworth, he is very knowledgeable, experienced, explicit, and caring.
A good professor and really knows how to teach MATLAB. But he is a tough grader, and it's not a good idea to take this course with him over the summer

Do not take this course over the summer with Stallworth. I took this course during the pandemic so of course somethings are gonna be bad by default but Stallworth clearly didn't know what he wanted this course to be I think. The lectures feel unorganized, the tests can be unfair, and the homework is a lot of work for 20% total. Doesn't curve stingy

I entered this course with no prior coding experience. The class was a little rough at first, but eventually things started to click and I began to love computer science due to professor Stallworth's teaching style. Advice:attend recitation, start homework early, and use the CS1371 website for help. If you do this an A or B is possible.

CS1371 is a tough class, especially for those without prior coding experience, but Stallworth makes it so much better. Lectures are educational and entertaining. Homework is tough, and there's lots of it but you usually have at least a week+ to do it. Tests are tough but fair, and the final is optional but can replace your two lowest test scores.

Stallworth is way underrated among the CS1371 professors. The dude is a real 10/10. He teaches to really know MATLAB, and he always goes over that weeks homework on Fridays. He provides so many extra resources, and he's always available for questions. MATLAB can be a pain to learn, and Stallworth understands that. I would take him over Kantwon.

Stallworth was a great professor! It's important to note that this isn't an easy class and you will have to put work in. The tests are hard but reaosnable, and the homework gets pretty challenging as the semester goes on. Stallworth was a great lecturer and explained concepts very clearly. He also went over homework a lot which was nice.

Amazing professor! Lectures are as entertaining as Kantwon's and the content is the same. He gives a lot of help with home problems, so going to class is enjoyable and worthwhile, even though not required. Comment the hw problems to get extra credit and beaware that they can get pretty hard by the end of the semester, so plan ahead.

Stallworth doesn't get the same hype as Kantwon, but he is nevertheless a great professor. I didn't go to class very often, but when I did I really enjoyed his lectures. He's very funny and can make a 300 person lecture hall feel like a more personal experience. Highly recommend taking.
Absolutely loved him for junior design and was such a treat! You could see he really cared about the students! 10/10 would recommend

Stallworth is a solid professor who teaches a really hard class. He tends to get off topic pretty frequently which can be pretty entertaining but isn't always super helpful. He's very personable and a solid choice for a 1371 professor.
His lectures are entertaining. He's good at explaining the basics, but a lot of learning takes place outside of class. He does go over the homework in class, which helps a lot.
Stallworth is an excellent professor. He makes his lectures very entertaining and engaging. He very clearly cares about his students and wants them to succeed.
CS1371 is really tough and time consuming. Kantwon and Stallworth are both solid choices.

Stallworth teaches it like it is. Get in, get out, get an A. Awesome dude who cares about learning and loves teaching CS. Do the homeworks, use the CS1371 website for data banks and review videos, and find a recitation with a good TA to go to to help learn the material even more. Just don't slack off and you'll have a good time.

Stallworth really knows his stuff and is a solid prof for 1371. Kantwon is a little better but Stallworth is way better than having Smith. That said, the class is just difficult in general, but he makes lectures funny and entertaining. Go to class it makes it way easier.

Stallworth is a fantastic lecturer. Although I prefer Kantwon's lecture code, I find his lectures to be just as educational. He explains things well and teaches what you need to know for the homework and tests. On top of being good at teaching MatLab, Stallworth is a really entertaining and funny. I enjoy being in his class.

He's a very good teacher -- makes sure to give lots of examples and demonstrations. Very personable as well, constantly tells funny stories when he has extra time in the lecture. My one complaint is that he doesn't communicate well with the TA's so he is often teaching material for homeworks that were already due.

Cedric is very personable, no doubt, however he is not very professional. He doesn't respond to emails and has no office hours, technically. It is up to you to personally track him down. He did not post 2 assignments over the course of 3 weeks. He's also a slow grader. Otherwise I like his enthusiasm. He makes complex concepts tolerable.

To do good in CS 1371, all you need to do is go to recitation and do your homework, nothing more.  BUT Stallworth is a great teacher, and will make the class alot easier.  His greatest trait is that he is very entertaining, while still very good at explaining concepts.  You will not find a better CS professor than him.

Awesome lecturer. The best you'll have for CS 1371. He's entertaining and explains concepts very well. Go to class, do the homework, and the review sessions you'll be fine. This is a very time-consuming class, so plan your schedule accordingly.

Awesome and funny professor. I only attended his lectures to be entertained. MATLAB is tough at first but gets easier once you know the basics. Actually do the HW because you need to know how to code on the tests. Review sessions by the TAs are very helpful. Do well on the final and he replaces your poor test grades. Got an A in this class.

Class is extremely difficult.  He knows the subject, but sometimes explains simple things too in-depth and complicated things very lightly.  The only good thing about the class is the resources available (tutoring, review sessions, etc.) to try and help people pass the class.  Would recommend because he is at least a funny guy and knows his stuff.
Great teacher, makes cs tolerable. He knows how to explain concepts and show appropriate examples well. One of the best lectures, especially for a cs class.

Awesome professor, he's a pretty good professor and he makes class very entertaining.  Definitely try to get him if/when you take CS 1371 (and if you're an engineering major, you will).  The class can be kinda tough if you don't pay attention and work at it though, just a warning.

The best CS1371 teacher.  A must have.  He is funny and both well paced and versed in the material.  The tests are hard as hell but the staff will do their best to help you out.  The class and homework overall are very time consuming.  Be warned.

He is the best out of all the CS teachers. Lectures are by far the least boring. The class itself is hard as hell, but this former NFL player tries his best to make class enjoyable. Besides, all the teachers use the same tests and final anyway, so you might as well pick the most interesting professor.
A good teacher and a really funny guy. take him in if you want to have fun. test are prepared by TA's, but go to reviews and u should be good.

He is the best professor who teaches 1371. The class itself is hard as hell, but that has nothing to do with Stallworth, since he is not the one who makes up the homeworks and tests. There are a lot of chances to make up points (labs, mini-quiz) in the class though. If nothing else, got to class and Cedric will always make u laugh. He is a blast.

Amazing Professor that keeps you intrested in a pain in the butt course.  Extremely nice and lots of fun! And take this advice from someone who has taken and failed the course once... YOU WANT STALLWORTH OVER ANYONE ELSE!!!

Good teacher and pretty enthusiastic in lectures, but I feel like she purposefully writes exams to be more difficult than needed. Homeworks were graded pretty harshly too and they were worth a lot of your grade. She gave us crib sheets on the exam though which was very useful. Overall not hard to get an A as long as you pay attention and study.

her lectures were more engaging than the other professor, and it just seemed like she cared a little more. nice when you had questions and always answered them but prepare for weird exam questions that can easily trip you up. go to recitation and study on your own. attendance not mandatory but they had in-class work that counted towards ur grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Spencer's half of the lectures were more engaging and informative than the other professor's lectures. The midterms are difficult but not if you've been doing what they suggest, like reading/note taking, and understanding the LC assignments. Not amazing, but definitely not terrible or anything.

She is really nice and a decent lecturer. The class itself was not bad, but make sure to read the online textbook! It covers all the content on exams. The course TAs were not great -- recitation was not helpful and they were slow graders. Overall a pretty decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: When professor Spencer taught I was able to fully graspy and understand all of the material. Participation technically isn't part of your grade but there are TICAs which are in class quizzes based on participation for a grade. She is very sweet and very thoughtful and would have loved to only have her teach me biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are 5 exams and the average on each were 60-70, but there is a lot of other assignments that easily boost your grade. The lectures were meant to "add on" to the textbook readings, but you could prepare for exams by solely reading through the textbook. Overall, she was a good professor even though the class format didn't fit my learning style.

Spencer was better than Kerr and more passionate about biology. Most of my learning came from the textbook and not lecture. Lecture was useless imo. Participation matters. Lots of busy work and stupid assignments. If you are willing to put in the work, the class is not hard.

Dr. Spencer was a good lecturer, but much of the content is best learned outside of class. The material itself was decently hard, but the only thing that I reviewed were the IKEs and TICAs and I got an A in the class, so it's definitely not impossible if you are willing to review some. Extra points built into the class to give you some wiggle room.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is an intro biology class, so it's going to be memorization-heavy. There were short writing assignments on non-exam weeks which didn't reflect course content a ton but were easy grade boosters if you followed the rubric. 5% EC on the final average and on exams. Dr. Spencer is a very caring person who is highly receptive to feedback.

She never really taught the class, it was mainly taught by Dr. Montoya. She is a very caring and you can tell that she genuinely likes what she does. Very cheery as well which was nice. She's good at lecturing, but she doesn't really do it often. She's pretty helpful when you ask her questions and she definitely knows what she is talking about.

This class was so exam heavy. If you don't do the readings before EACH lecture; YOU'RE COOKED!! Exams are almost impossible to pass, and we are not even talking about the final: A HORROR STORY. There are NO extra credit available. Makes TICAs and IKEs and exams questions SO hard that she gets confused about the questions herself. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Spencer's lectures had some good information, but disorganized. She is very passive-aggressive in her emails and in-person when asked a question. Her response is always rude and condescending no matter what the question is. She assigned very long homework assignments that had nothing to do with the class and were simply political indoctrination.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very poor communication of expectations. Lack of course structure and coherence. Assignments are not geared towards your betterment, but more so political indoctrination. The final is not an accurate representation of the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor- taught very well and made the content interesting. She is also highly respected in the BIOS world at Tech and would recommend getting to know her if you're a Biology major. Class was pretty easy besides Montoya (other lecturer), but there is so much extra credit that your grade will be fine regardless.

Got very confused when explaining some topics and did not know some typical, basic, classic content (such as the Labrador retriever example with epistasis). Taught wrong then corrected it the next day, but it still confuses the students. Taught with Montoya and was very animated when talking! The class content was a bit too basic, but ok overall.

Doesn't teach the class. Another professor taught the majority of the class and was equally as bad. She taught the last bit of the material but wasn't helpful at all. She said to understand the TICA's and IKE's but not helpful and way too many of them to understand every question completely. Doesn't give good feedback either. Avoid if you can.

I took Prof Spencer for the genetics lab. She was very nice and knowledgable about the material (mainly because we were participating in her research). I had some bumps throughout the semester, but she always allowed for extensions and ensured I had everything I needed.

Dr. Spencer is nice and very enthusiastic about biology, but the class is heavy in reading the textbook before class and doing participation IKEs and TICAs. Tough grader on free response, but fair mc questions.

Horrible professor. Lectures are unhelpful and don't make sense and don't feel cohesive at all. Tests have mc section and written section and the written section is always graded so hard and feedback given is very vague. This course was taught with dr montoya and he was equally as bad. avoid if you can

Prof. Spencer is an ok professor, but she did not teach the lecture. She was more of a grader off to the side. TICAS and IKES are due for each lecture and TICAS are in class questions. The course relies heavily on the "textbook" and powerpoints.
She was not understanding of my religious priorities and did not help me in any way.

Dr. Spencer was the worst. You have to complete so much reading before class and during the class for participation points. Every lecture Dr. Spencer speeds through the slides and doesn't give us time to write our notes down before skipping to the next slide The class is even graded on a curve. I barely scraped by and got my A from the small curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Spencer isn't a great prof. She can be very passive-aggressive during class and is disorganized with her lectures. i asked her a question once about the tica assignment in class and she was really rude when answering it like I was expected to know the answer. tests are really hard the averages are in the 60s and 70s, some extra credit though

I had Dr. Spencer in Fall 2020 and I really enjoyed her as a prof! She has a clear passion for biology (especially genetics) which really comes through in her lectures. If you show you care about her class she is dedicated to helping you succeed. Kind mom energy!

Dr. Spencer is very nice and respected, but we had pop quizzes every single week, which was a lot. I did not do too well on all pop quizzes, but I managed to get an A through HW, participation, and attendance. The final was not too difficult.

Didn't really like the style of lecture and found very hard to understand but what made the rating so bad is the fact that her attitude comes off as very passive aggressive. Not very helpful regarding feedback of any sort and very slow in grading to the point where the semester will be over and half of the grades were missing. Really disappointing.

Dr. Spencer is amazing. I took her for a lab that was grant proposal writing-based, and while it was a lot of work, everything was doable in class with minimal work outside of class with your group. She gives you all the tools you need to succeed in her class. I would definitely take her again if I had the chance. She's very accessible and kind.

Shes an enthusiastic lecturer but can sometimes come off a little petty or passive aggressive. She is slow to grade and grades pretty tough on short answers (doesnt give good feedback either). I wouldnt exactly recommend her but you wont be screwed if you have her. Just put in the work/pay attention and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Spencer was a fine professor. You have to complete the readings before class for participation points and to simply be able to follow along in class. She is super enthusiastic and only means well.

Dr. Spencer is awesome. She's down to earth and easy to talk to. She's really reasonable too and understands that students have lives too. Grading is usually okay, but sometimes she can be confusing as to what she is taking off points for. Overall, loved having her as my professor.

Dr. Spencer was my lap teacher for Genetics and she was a great teacher. Very nice and helpful, but also strict when she needs to be. I learned a lot in this course. Don't procrastinate the writing assignments and use the rubrics as a guide. Writing the final lab report in one night is ill-advised.

We didn't have any big tests, just quizzes every week or every other week. Make sure you read her textbook online, it's honestly a really easy formatted and free online textbook written by Dr. Spencer herself so the quizzes come right from there. There is one project and make sure you attend most classes since participation counts.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The module 4 and 5 lectures may be a little weaker but overall the class is very doable. Reviewing Learning Catalytics IKEs, showing up the class (do TICAs), and paying attention to lectures is all you need to succeed. I usually went to Spencer's office hours before tests and she was a great clarifying resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Spencer is very nice and a decent lecturer. She always answers all questions and attempts to cover everything comprehensively, which sometimes prevents her from covering all test material in class. She gives students all the tools they need to succeed, however, and was an enjoyable professor all around.
Spencer is fun and makes sure the class understands the material by using engaging activities.
Very good professor overall. Lectures were made up of practice problems and tests were difficult but manageable. Multiple extra credit opportunities as well. Gave out candy during lectures.

Very clear on grading an expectations, basically lets you know about what's going to be on the exam in class. As long as you are attentive in class and participates, it is very easy to do well. He also gives a group project that has to opportunity to earn 1% extra credit if you do well. Gives candy to anyone who answers questions. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and genuinely wants you to succeed in the class, optional final which replaces your lowest midterm, however there is one group project. His tests are also reasonable, slightly more difficult and a little longer question wise compared to other sections but overall not bad at all.
I really enjoyed this class. The lectures are easy to follow, fun, and really engaging. The professor is really caring and understanding. Would take again 100%.
10/10. Take him!!!
One of the most caring and engaging professors I've had the privilege to witness teaching. Gives great examples and tailors the class to fit the needs of students in terms of content and extra help.

Overall great professor, sped through the unnecessary parts of lectures to focus on practice problems. 90% of lectures had at least 15 minutes to work lecture problems or homework and get feedback from him or TAs. He also incentivizes with candy to encourage participation, but does not have much of a good throwing arm, so beware.

Overall great professor. Could sometimes speed through lectures, as his focus was learning through practice. About 90% of lectures were able to have 15+ minutes of practicing problems and being able to get feedback from him or the TAs. During lectures, he also incentivizes active participation by awarding candy just for raising your hand to try.

He's one of the nicest people I've ever met. Most exams are just setting up equations and barely any computation. He tries to give as many partial credits as he can and lots of chances for extra credit!! Lowest hw grade gets dropped and optional final

Awesome guy. Goes above and beyond and truly cares about his students. Exams test concepts (FBDs, setting up force and moment equations), not calculations (actually solving difficult equations that you would just plug and chug anyway). He will try to find points for you. Homework amounts to a 2 credit class. Take him if you can. THWg!!!

This professor truly cares about his students succeeding. His exams were fair and the homework was time consuming, but if you put in effort you can succeed. Also, there's a group project with an extra credit opportunity for the class.

One of my favorite professors here at Tech. Very good lecturer and makes it clear what you are expected to know. Exams are more conceptual than computational, and he is generous with partial credit, so if you understand the material you will succeed in his class.

Lectures include time to work though example problems, so you're able to get help right after learning the content and see exactly how the concepts apply. Homeworks were difficult, but really helped to prepare for the exams. He stays after class to answer questions and is very accessible outside of lectures if you need additional help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Very approachable and easy to talk to, will 100% help you out if you just ask.
He is very accessible and always stays after class to answer any questions. He really wants his students to do well. The homework was difficult and time consuming but the tests were very fair.

Great prof. His lectures are mostly him working through example problems with the class, so you get a good grasp on how to handle many kinds of problems. He gives candy to ppl who participate in class. Homeworks can take a while, but they are vital for understanding content. Exams are fair, and he gives lots of partial credit. Take him if you can.
