This class is enjoyable

Take Professor Caraway's classes! He was approachable, outlined exactly what he expected from you, and gave plenty of examples. He was willing to stay late to help you understand a concept. Always funny and good-humoured.

Very direct lectures that do not waste the 50 minute block. The in class practice questions and the homework questions prepare you well for the tests. Be prepared to spend some time on the homework questions and do not procrastinate. Office hours are also very helpful for better understanding course material and homework problems.

He's by far one of the most approachable and captivating professors I've had. He teaches practically and does everything in his power to ensure students have what they need to succeed in the class. He's a new professor, so the memories of being a student are still fresh in his mind. He is very empathetic.

Professor Caraway has been one of my favorite professors! We always start each lecture with a "To Hell with Georgia!" chant and his lectures are very clear and student oriented. His exams are also very straight forward. Most exams had you either setting up equations without solving them out or writing steps to solve problems.
Very chill and very helpful

This is the professor who will bring candy during a midterm & is very helpful with questions The lectures are example heavy, so expect to get a lot of practice. The grading scale can be kind of harsh if you are not on top of your assignments like me, but even so I've learned a lot in the class.  If you put in the effort, you will get a good grade.

Prof Caraway is an awesome teacher and person. He makes lectures and expectations clear. He is very available outside of class and gives great advice on how to improve. Some of the homeworks are challenging but they prepare you well for the exams. I recommend to take if you have the chance.

VERY kind and respectful. Its clear he wants you to succeed, NOTHING is meant to trick you or set you up for failure. Come to class and do the HW. Exams are VERY fair and grading is forgiving. Effort is rewarded. Lectures could be better tbh (concepts need time to marinate, not totally his fault), but if confused watch Jeff Hanson on YT. Good Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Caraway made statics way easier by being open to all questions to ensure everyone understands the material and being lenient on exams and grades. Class feels less forced to attend since he keeps lectures concise, fun, and engaging, and his final project was really fun to work on. 10/10 instructor who genuinely cares about your success.
Very clear lecturer, open to questions, keeps class engaging. Was very clear about expectations for exams and always tried best at giving partial credit even when the answer is wrong.

Loved him! He was a great lecturer that explained things in a way that made sense, but he was also great at answering questions about things that don't make sense. He was always friendly, told us what exams would be like and never put things on exams that we didn't go over in class, and tailored homework to be perfectly aligned. Highly recommend.
Excellent professor, forgiving grading on exams.

This has honestly been my best class at Tech so far (even though I've only been here 2 semesters). Caraway is extremely good at explaining content in a comprehensible way, he's funny, homework covers everything you'll need to know, and exams are fair and easy to prepare for. Our final project has been a lot of fun to work on as well!
Overall, a pretty good professor who cuts the crap and focuses on what's important.
Very knowledgeable, supportive and helpful

Exams are open-note, open-book, but on a lockdown browser. Topics covered were quite simple. Her lectures were great if you care about HR. Had a group project which was quite easy (Just wish we had more in-class time to meet up with our groups). Overall, a kind professor!
She is a great teacher. Attendance is required, but she pretty much just lectures the whole time. End of the year group project about a company. Super nice and understanding.

Basically, it's a free class. I didn't even go to class the last 3 weeks and ended with a 94. The exams are open note. And the final is remote.... if the class does the CIOS teacher evaluation. Her lectures are kinda long and boring, but an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are a little boring but the material is pretty easy to understand. The tests are open note and there are very few homework assignments. She is very nice and definitely cares a lot about her students.

Super easy class. Open note exam. When we reached the CIOS she let us take our final (not cumulative) remotely, and it was still open note. Very sweet professor and very accessible. Just read the slides and you'll be fine. Attendance sporadically taken throughout the semester. Take her if you can!

Tests are open note. Final project is leniently graded. CIOS gets your final to be from ur house. You do have to go to class, but she doesn't always check which is annoying bc you don't always get credit for going. Really nice, really easy. Case studies are auto 100. Research windows are easy to miss so look out for those.

tries her best to make the subject interesting and is very enthusiastic about it, but its just not an interesting subject, so take that how you will. Her tests are easy though and shes an easy professor

Descent professor overall. Lectures are pretty dry, but very informative. Lots of participation in lectures. Small homework assignments and three exams that are open note. Final group project that is pretty straight forward. It's HR... just show up and get through it and you will be fine.
very nice but very hard to focus.. kinda boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: really sweet prof, but the class is insanely boring. not sure if i was catfished by the previous reviews or what, but it's genuinely dismal. she's really nice and caring, but attendance is also mandatory, and you need to spend lots of money on textbooks. exams are pretty in-depth too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: In agreement with other recent ratings. Class is engaging/informative but very manageable. Professor is very sweet and knowledgeable. Highly recommend!
This is a no brainer. Take this class with her, it's very manageable, very easy. She makes the content interesting as well.

I loved her! This class was pretty easy, just some case homework and occasional participation and speaking activities in class. There was a group project in the end but that also was pretty easy. This is a very simple and easy class and she is very nice.

Dr. Colakoglu is a caring professor. Occasionally there are discussions or participation activities for attendance, but as long as you show up, its not bad. As long as you do your work on time and organize your notes, you should be fine. One time she brought pop rocks as an incentive for kahoot.

Dr. Colakoglu is an extremely caring professor. The HR class she teaches is pretty easy if you review the lecture slides and skim the textbook. The slides aren't great themselves, but they do tell a clear story. She's just very nice and lenient in general. The class material would be pretty low-level taught by ANYONE, so I'm glad it was her.
Easy A as long as you show up. Exams are open book, open note, and open browser.

Dr. Colakoglu makes a pretty boring topic interesting with real world examples. Grade is 3 non-cumulative tests, minimal classwork, 2 cases, and a group project (5 person teams). Tests are open book and remote. I personally felt that you needed the book to do well on the exams. My only complaint is that she takes a long time to grade assignments.

You need to take her class... she's great! A genuinely kind person, good lecturer, easy grader. I didn't even buy the book but still survived bc her lecture notes are pretty thorough. The coursework is so minimal and the tests (if enough people ask) are REMOTE. There is a final presentation at the end, but it's literally so easy. easy A class
Dr. C is a really kind and knowledgeable professor. The assignments and tests are very reasonable, and putting in the effort will ensure that you succeed.

The professor is very nice and most of your grade comes from 3 exams. They don't check attendance often and the lectures can be boring, but the class is easy. Overall, a good option if you want an easy grade.

Professor C is a great teacher who tries to engage her students, however lectures are very boring. I would recommend taking this class and OB at the same time so that you only have to do the research requirements once and not twice. 3102 was graded mostly on 3 tests and one large project

I loved this class! All the exams were open note and it was really easy, and there was one group project that was really leniently graded as well! Dr. C is super accessible by email and very caring and compassionate towards her students, definitely take if you can!

I loved Dr. C's class. There is a heavy emphasis on the lectures, which can become a little dry over time. There is minimal homework and one group project. The tests are fairly straightforward and open note. Dr. C is genuinely an incredibly kind and friendly person, and I hope I can take another class by her in the future.

Cares a lot about the material and presents well overall (a few lectures dragged on but nbd) - tests are a breeze, buy the text and it's almost a certain A. Likes to engage the class, and the group project was graded pretty leniently. Definitely take her if she's offered

Spring 2021 - Remote She is a great professor and really cared about trying to make online learning similar to normal classes. Canvas was really well-organized and she would post what to expect for the upcoming week. There's one group project that we had to present, but she's not a tough grader so just get the work done.

(Take during COVID-19 Spring 2021.) Incredibly kind and understanding professor. The class was very easy as long as you kept up with the lectures and read the textbook. Semester project involved that's not too bad and graded based mostly on three exams. Definitely would take again.

I really enjoyed the class. Her lectures are relatively interesting, and the content is pretty straightforward. As long as you pay attention in class the tests are not bad at all. There is also one group project that is worth a good percentage of your overall grade, so make sure to put a lot of effort into the project.

I enjoyed her class and her as a teacher. Lectures are interesting and she brought in some good guest speakers. Class is mostly group work and if you have a good group (which I did) then you are fine. If not, then the class could be a struggle. There were probably 8-10 group assignments and 3 tests which were not that difficult.

Class is based alot on group assignments and she isn't that understanding when it comes to group members not cooperating. By far the worst professor I've ever had, she's an uncompassionate person and doesn't even respond to emails.

HR is boring but she tries to make it interesting with anecdotes and videos. Tests can be a little tricky but generally aren't too bad. Group work every few weeks that's a little annoying, but overall, decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Only 2 exams for the entire course, no final at all, exams are weighed pretty heavily, and if you do badly on one, it's hard to increase your grade. Attendance is mandatory. A lot of required reading and preparation before each exam. Does not accept late work or curve grades. Be ready to study for this class.

Boring lectures. Easy tests. Extremely passionate about international business as a subject. Truly cares about her students. One of the few genuinely kind professors I've taken at Scheller even if the subject and way she teaches it are uninteresting.
Really nice and solid professor. care about her students a lot

Very straightforward class. Exam 1 - 30%, Exam 2 - 30%, Project - 20%, Homework - 10% (graded by completion), and Attendance - 10%. I believe the lecture material alone was good enough to get by with an A if you study it. Professor values student engagement, and offers extra credit to those who participate in lectures and discussion boards.

Dr. Caceres is a very invested professor & one of the more caring professors I've had. I reached out to her to clarify some potential misunderstandings I had, and she sat down for nearly 2 hours to explain the concepts and real world applications. The course is exam/project heavy, but there is also ample opportunity for extra credit. Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sweet prof! Emailed her regarding attendance policy yesterday because I was concerned about personal conflicting schedules, and she not only replied quickly but also made a clarification post on Canvas and notified me about it too. Chill class - would def recommend :)

literally so unclear on attendance policies. made students stay an extra day into spring break for "mandatory" class that she did not even take attendance for. threatened to decrease final grade if students didnt show up to class, even thought attendance does not even count for grades in the syllabus. never answers her email. do not take.

Class graded by 2 exams + group project (30% each), 10% homework. Prof seems genuine and sweet, but lectures are so boring + straight out textbook. Stopped going 1.5 months into the semester. Says participation mandatory but doesn't take it, causing students to stay extra day before spring break. Tests detail heavy, but study guide has answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool class, brings in some neat guest speakers within international business. Only grades are 2 tests (30% each), a project (30%), and HW (10%). The tests are pretty comprehensive so do study the content in depth. Ample extra credit opportunities. Put in a decent amount of effort, and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only 3 grades in the semester which consists of 2 exams and a project. Offers extra credit for participating in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was more student led and class discussions, but the exam was straight forward from the reading and lecture slides. So it was a really easy class and she is not a harsh grader. The class can get boring but she brought in guest speakers and offered extra credit for participating which was cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was very flexible and the supplemental readings were very interesting. She is a very considerate professor and you learn a lot if you pay attention and do the readings :) You can definitely do well in the class if you complete the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grade was comprised mostly of two 15+ page papers but was not overly critical in her grading. Class discussions were largely student led. Had a tendency to change expectations relatively often. Long readings for every class but you weren't at a huge disadvantage if you don't do them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: (Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) Easy. You get out of this class what you put into it. I've learned quite a lot while still having simple tests. As long as you complete the assignments and do well on the tests, you'll be fine. The course is test heavy, so make sure you do well on the tests. Definitely would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a teacher not a fan. Doesn't want to teach to the test so gives real examples. Enjoyed them, but literally says nothing outside the powerpoints... There's a homework for every chapter that you are to complete before going to class. So you have to read the chapter. Use quizlet and then use those questions to study from. Changes her mind ALOT

Lectures consist of him reading the notes directly, so you can get the same content by reviewing the notes on your own. However, the class does not focus much on how to apply concepts, theorems, and formulas to problems not shown in class. As a result, exams can feel significantly harder than the material covered in class.
he is pretty soft spoken, and sometimes hard to understand, but he writes everything u need in his notes that he posts after class. lowkey feel kinda maternal towards him he's so sweet.

It is kind of hard to understand his notes but his exams/quizzes are predictable and there is no hw for the class (only quizzes), he gives partial credit on exams and provides practice, the textbook is optional

UNDERRATED PROFESSOR!! We need more profs like him at Tech, he geniunely cares about his students and isn't afraid to adjust his HW/Exams/policies to prioritize fairness for students. Very available to help, he posts about his office hours often and is very helpful even if you are super lost. He isn't trying to trick you, he wants you to do well.

Professor Yip is a very caring and approachable person. His lectures are straightforward, delivering content in a clear, easy-to-understand way. The exam questions are very similar to those in his lectures and on the sample exams. He is always responsive, answering students' questions and addressing their needs.

He's one of the kindest and most organized professors at Georgia Tech. His clear structure made it easy—and genuinely fun—to follow along and learn. He's also very understanding of students' diverse situations. We need more professors like him who truly invest time and effort in teaching.

Professor Yip is a great professor who is not only knowledgeable but also very caring and understanding. He's a little soft-spoken but he explains concepts well and is always willing to spend extra time with you if you don't understand something. He's also very nice and reasonable with grading quizzes and exams.
Professor Yip likes to clap to get everyone's attention. He is a very gentle teacher.

Machado was an extremely understanding professor. She does not require a lot of work other than the occasional group projects. Extremely lenient grader. The class does not have any exams nor does it have a final.

Very passionate and engaging professor! The exams were all online + take-home and were very easy. The class participation helped enhance our learning and she is super lenient on grading, so no stress at all. You will probably end up with a high A in this class even if you just do the bare minimum. Book is required for HW, but super useful.

Sra. Machado is very caring and wants all of her students to do well. I took her for 3040 and 3064, and class was extremely fun and engaging. I was encouraged to speak and feel a lot more confident after taking her classes. She chooses assignments that help you learn and grades based on effort, allowing you to learn from mistakes without penalty.
She is awesome. The work is well divided throughout the semester. It is a nice and light class.
Had her for both 3064 and 3040.  She is very passionate about teaching and makes sure the workload is very light.  The quizzes are online.

Dr. Machado is amazing! She is extremely caring and makes sure that the class is manageable for her students. She is always open to moving deadlines if students have a busy week. Her class is also amazing and super interesting, even if you aren't pre-med! It's also a great safe space to work on your Spanish skills.

Caroline is one of the best Spanish teachers I've had! She is a fantastic professor, very passionate about teaching, and so kind. I learned a lot in her class but the workload was light. She told us she never wanted us to be stressed about her class. She is accommodating and easy to contact. I would highly recommend taking her class!

Amazing professor, has great lecture structuring for numerical that introduce complex topics extremely naturally. Only catch is he goes at a decently fast pace. Homework is reasonable and exams are mostly fine. 11/10, would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A fine enough course except the fact that you need to type homework into LaTeX, which doubles the amount of time spent on these assignments. All else was fine, but if you want the easiest version of this class, take it during the summer.

This professor is a classic case of out of touch. He knows his material exceptionally well and expects the students to know it just as well. If he teaches the lecture at a problem difficulty of 4/10 and the textbooks has a problem difficulty of about a 5/10 expect the tests to have problem difficulties of 9/10.

Dr. Dieci is nice, clear during lectures, and accessible during office hours. He gives a long optional homework and then collects a subset to grade. The exams are literally exactly from the homework, so if you do & understand all the homework, tests are easy A's if don't make arithmetic mistakes. Grading is not bad. The textbook is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dieci is a decent lecturer and definitely wants students to succeed, but lectures alone didn't always give good intuition for ODEs and how to use them; the "optional" practice problems he gives are actually essential practice if you want to do well on exams. The class initially felt fast-paced, then slowed down; don't be afraid to ask for help.

At the beginning it's easy but it gets very complicated very fast. Make sure to get good homework grades as those are weighted heavily. OK at explaining but is very available for office hours. He grades exams lenient but the homework grades was really tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is one of those classes where the whole class is just lectures and exams with homework scattered in between.

This class was so bad. Luca was a great person but as a teacher... he didnt aid in learning the material at all. The textbook isnt mandatory but since you wont get much out of lectures, the textbook and study groups is your best hope. And there is a huge curve on the class so you will probably be curved up a whole letter grade.
Very nice guy but his lectures were useless. Tests were pretty hard compared but studying his practice tests help. Final was HARD.

It's linear algebra, so it's going to be hard. He's very accessible outside of the office, so camp out at office hours and DO YOUR HOMEWORK!!! He is compassionate and loves the subject, but you need to do your fair share of the work and do the practice exams he posts. Great choice, just the final exam was something else, so study!!!

Probably worst professor Ive had. Very nice guy, but you get absolutely nothing from lectures. I think the lectures actually confused me more so rely on teaching yourself from the textbook. Tests were crazy hard compared to other professors. Honestly, I would rather skip taking him and wait to take the class until there is someone else available.

He is a clear and understandable lecturer. However, his tests are difficult compared to the sample midterms that are available to all 1553 students, and they have lower averages than other professors, so be wary.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: lecture is pointless, but attendance is semi-mandatory (polls). MATH 1553 is hellish no matter who you have. Prepare to learn 90% of the information on your own or in studio (assuming you get a good TA).

I loved Dieci as a person and professor. He usually explained concepts very clearly and did good examples in class. Sometimes, however, his lectures were proof heavy. However, he helped reinforce many concepts in office hours (which I would recommend going to). The tests and quizzes were sometimes really hard, so doing homework is a MUST.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is absolutely necessary to stay on top of homework. If you do it as it is assigned, it will suffice in terms of studying and the pace is manageable. I ended up procrastinating for every test and learning all the material the night before, which made the class miserable. Survived this class because of intense studying and tons of partial credit.

Excellent Professor. Very comprehensive and well organized. Teaches in a direct, easy to understand manner. All the quiz questions are from the homework, so if you can do the homework you will be good. Very friendly and cares about the student's success. All in all, one of the top math professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very clear explanations of the course content and reasonable course expectations. Questions from quizzes and exams are from the textbook questions he assigns. Has a little bit of an accent, but manageable and won't be a distraction to learning.

One of the less useful professors I've had at Tech. His accent is very strong and he mumbles and speaks to the board. No chance of understanding him if you're sitting anywhere besides the first 2 rows.   Most of his lecture time is just proofs and confusing examples. The only beneficial notes I took were from recitation. Overall, not satisfied.
Great Professor. Clear and detailed lectures. Homework is optional, but really it's mandatory if you want to understand the material and do well on exams. Would take his class again.

Fantastic professor. He maintained a consistent organization throughout class, used very helpful examples, and only focused on the important topics. Test questions were barely harder than the  example problems he gave from the book (though the final was unnecessarily hard). He never tested over material that wasn't covered by the book examples.

Chill guy who was fair with the class. Moved at a relaxed pace, and didn't try to screw you with super difficult problems so commonly encountered in the math dept. Explained everything very clearly, and concisely. I found his tests fairly easy and straightforward if you understood even the basics of the material.

Be prepared to work in his classes. Good lecturer. Assigns a lot of math problems for non-credit but quizzes given are based off homework, sometimes exactly the same problems. Fair grader and tends to give BONUS problems on quizzes/exams. Highly recommended professor if you want to really learn and remember the material at the end of the course.

Sucky teacher I think, but easy class.  He does problems wrong all the time in class.  His voice level rises for no apparent reason and can starting yelling in his sentence.  Cannot say "if" right and asks "is that fair?" at least 10 times a class.  He tells you what the test questions will be before the test though so they aren't bad.

Professor Das imparts little to no useful information throughout the semester. He delayed a midterm exam by over a month for no apparent reason, and proceeded to cancel all classes between said midterm exam and the finals, despite having new material in the final exam which have not been discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I highly recommend against taking Suman Das. I learned nothing helpful from this class. He showed up late, and delayed one of our exams for a total of 42 days.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Das was extremely passionate about teaching design and manufacture, but he liked to go off on lots of tangents (usually pretty interesting though) that only sort of related.
Tests were easy, just read the textbook & lecture slides and make sure you know everything on the quiz reviews.
Homework not bad and you can do it in groups of 3.

Professor Das cares a lot about manufacturing and knows a lot about it too. He would often ramble in lectures but would solve homework problems in class to make sure you understood them. Had no issues until he tried to change the grade cutoff to a 95 for an A after the final. Not a terrible professor and probably one of the better options for 3210.

Dr. Das is a good professor who tries to deliver the concepts of manufacturing to his students through pretty long lectures. The best way to ace his tests is to study whatever he suggests on his study guide which is all detailed in the book(Kalpakjian). Pretty long tests so make sure to pace yourself-he doesnt provide time updates. Wear a watch!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: How to do well(A or B): Test1 and 2 try to find one of his previous test, he usually goes off of those. Be sure to answer questions verbatim as seen in slides or he tends to take of points Final - study his final study guide, 90% of the final is not the stuff from previous tests, but the stuff he tells you to study on the study guide. Fall 2015

Absolutely no respect for students. Said he would upload homework solutions, but didn't. Gets very defensive when asked about grading questions on exams. Does not seem to care for students and gives off attitude that students aren't worth his time.  Lured me into liking the class at first with passion of manufacturing, but ended up being useless

3210 was very insteresting with him. Class was enjoyable. However, he reads right off of slides from a different class (ME 4210), and will simply skip over sections. It makes it difficult to understand what you are responsible for. However,given the other professors that teach this class, he is one of the best, and really isn't too bad.

His tests aren't impossible, since he takes a lot of inspo from old exams, but I found that there's always one heavily weighted question that he barely talks about prior, which sometimes cooks your score, so he's predictable, but not yk? He's also kinda rude. His grading scale is a lot less forgiving, but I did better here than in regular physics 1
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the class itself is difficult, Darnton is a great professor and truly has a passion for physics. The exams are by no means easy but the grading is pretty chill and he gives a ton of partial credit and bonus points. He kinda rambles about random physics background so just do the practice exams and you are golden
Super chill and funny, added like 10 points to each of our exam scores. He made physics slightly less tedious for us premeds.

class is pretty chill the tests are the same as the practice exams and they are always curved. the labs are peer graded so ur lab grade should be high. Dr. Darnton himself is a good guy but you can definitely tell he's overqualified and doesn't want to teach this. Very accessible outside of class though if you need help.

I wish there was more grade forgiveness with the exams. I felt like you had to do well on all the exams to do well in the class. However, I am glad I took the LS section for physics 2. The lectures are boring, but he does offer the zoom option and he is very helpful in office hours. Exams are not too difficult.

2212 was a tough class. That said, Dr. Darnton is more than willing to help if you go to his office hours. I did most of my extra practice there. Lectures are a little boring and can drag along but that is inevitable.
Not a very good professor, very full of himself.  Nothing special, really.

I love his enthusiasm for physics. He's really knowledgeable, and thus, he sometimes gave extra information (interesting to know but not applicable to the exams) and might confuse students that aren't focusing 100%. I'm not sure who wrote the exams, so I can't say anything. My semester, the exams required you to actually understand the content.

I like Dr Darnton, he's a really nice guy and he seems really smart and passionate about physics. The class is really hard (it is life science based) and you learn a lot of material that is not typically covered in regular intro physics courses. In total, tests (3 midterms and a final) make up 75% of your grade. However, he curves exams + CIOS!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was a pretty hard course, and you definitely have to work hard for an A, but professor Darnton's lectures were clear and definitely helped make the course manageable. He is very knowledgeable in physics and his lectures are fairly example heavy so if you learn well from seeing practice problems solved you should go to his lectures.

Dr. Darnton is a clear and enthusiastic lecturer, but all of that falls apart when exams roll around. Exams don't reflect practice exams and quizzes, and he introduces new principles and types of problems that you haven't seen before. Many students didn't finish exams because they were composed of 4 short-answer questions with 4-5 parts each.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Danrton's exams were horrible even though it was a summer semester. Every exam had to be graded in some stupid way to make up for the difficulty. The final was very tough and had many stuff you have never seen before. He answered ed stem questions, however every time I asked a question I received a vague answer that makes the thing more confusing.

Physics 2 content is alright. However, Darnton's exams were very tough. Even with hours of studying (by myself and with others), I did mediocre on them. The final was the worst out of all, though. Darnton created the exams despite someone else being listed so not too sure what happened there. Stressful summer, not going to lie.

For me, this was a difficult class. However, for many of my friends they breezed through this course. I think it really depends if you have taken physics before; I came in with 0 physics knowledge and a weak algebra background. In the end, I managed to get an A in this class. Just keep working hard, almost every day, and learn how to learn. :)

Dr. Darnton makes physics pretty manageable. His lectures aren't very useful but he was super helpful in office hours. There's a lot of homework, but it's all bucket points so you technically don't have to do all of it. He gives past years tests and quizzes for practice. Doing all of those and going to office hours easily makes an A/B attainable.

Dr. Darnton definitely cares about physics and seems enthusiastic about the material. However, there isn't much good to say about an intro to physics life science class. He also lectures over the allotted time every single class and remarks on how slow the class is going, despite it being his fault. Not great, but the best possible option.

Great lecturer and easy to follow. He would give long and unnecessarily difficult homeworks that were due at annoying times, but gives lots of practice content for tests and quizzes. If you study thoroughly, a B or an A is definitely manageable.

Great professor with good examples during class. Lots of homework and quizzes that don't always line up with lectures; just don't have lab the day after a test and it's fine. Tons of extra practice materials offered that thoroughly prepare you for tests. This class is a lot of work, but if you put in the time, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's okay at explaining concepts, but he gives WAY too much homework. Don't register for a Tuesday lab because you'll have quizzes over things he hasn't covered in lecture. Also, he always goes over time and sometimes has clicker questions for attendance AFTER the class has ended.

Dr. Darnton did a good job with physics for life sciences and making physics accessible to people in biology. I thought tests were fair as he always provides a ton of practice material before quizzes and exams. Timing of assignments, quizzes, and lectures sometimes didn't work out super well, but overall Darnton was a good prof

He's a good prof, but his tests are monsters. The first test was solid, but afterwards, he ramped the difficulty up exponentially. In addition, his tests in the Spring 2021 semester deviated from tests in the past content wise. It's the best physics class for GaTech, but beware of the tests and final, they will kill your grade if you're not careful
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Darnton is very knowledgeable about the subject and he gives good explanations of the general concepts. However, he does not give clear indications of what to expect on exams. On the first test, the average was somewhat high (80) and he made sure that the tests for the rest of the semester were significantly harder. Lots of homework too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good at teaching, so you'll get the solid GT-Physics experience. Certainly knowledgeable and willing to adapt. As for the class, do the practice tests and complete the other material. Do not take shortcuts to learn the material.

Great prof, keeps lectures interesting. Available at office hours& did good moving online in spring2020 (lectures were rough live but were also recorded, tests were MC w/ partial credit answers + unique questions). Exams are difficult but VERY similar to the practice tests plus questions in the reading. You DO need the reading, textbook is free.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Darnton is the best for classical physics 1. The tests are pretty hard (I failed 2 of them), but there is a lot of extra credit, so getting an A is definitely achievable. Lots of homework, but if you put in effort you should be fine

Physics can be a difficult and time consuming class at Tech, but I'm glad I had Darnton. He tends to give more traditional lectures compared to the entirely clicker-question based lectures of some other physics professors. The tests are hard, but you have lots of material to study with (definitely do all the old exams). Expect to read before class.

Dr. Darnton is the best choice for classical physics 1. He LOVES clicker questions, but he has started to work more examples in lecture. He does a good many demos and answers any question. Murray is the course coordinator, but Darnton teaches better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Darnton is great, I took him for PHYS 2212 the IPLS section. He always made sure the students were understanding the material as we went along, and he was understanding and caring in that he made great accommodations for the class during COVID-19. I feel like our class vibe was a bit lackluster, but I could tell he was really passionate.
Professor darnton is good at explaining the content, even though physics is a hard class for most people. His lectures are easy to follow and he does a lot of clicker questions

Insanely smart guy and is a great lecturer. Honestly didn't read the textbook at all and learned everything from lecture. Lots of hw, but eh that's the price of physics, right? Funny guy and makes lectures interesting too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Darnton teaches the material well and definitely isn't boring. MasteringPhysics is a nightmare and daily warm-ups are forgettable, but the teaching experience is really great. Make sure to use past exams and go to help sessions to get a good grasp of the material. For people who've never taken physics before, you'll need to work twice as much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Darnton is a solid professor for physics, he is great at teaching and very helpful in office hours. He is compassionate for physics and makes lectures entertaining. Exams are not that bad and he tells you almost everything you need to know

I went to all lectures but a lot of people didn't. His lectures were good but fell behind the HW a bit. The book is useful if you need help. Tests are uniform for all lectures and curved if scores are low. Darnton had the best test average. You can work around doing HW if you want but doing it does help learn. Practice tests are good exam prep.

Darnton is ok. Lecture is pretty boring. He seems nice enough though. Didnt really have office hours. Clicker questions for participation and basically homework everyday. Do the hw for the bonus!!! Book reading is only for bucket points.

Physics 2-modern (run by Greco) is standardized across sections, so lectures is the only difference in professor, as all tests and assignments are identical. I think Dr. Darnton's lectures are clear and helpful. He was also helpful in office hours. He answers questions well (except ask Greco for any administrative questions) and is sometimes funny.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Darnton! His teaching style and the way he explained physics concepts really clicked with me. He is good at covering the underlying theory of these principles, but tended to go off on tangents about stuff that was more complicated than we needed to know.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, though Clicker Questions were tricky at times. Helpful with hw in office hours. Study and go to Greco's OH before tests. Physics 2 (modern) wasn't as bad as I'd heard it was, but still challenging because I hadn't had E&M before. Similar grading and problem-solving strategies as my Physics 1 (classical) so it's no walk in the park
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Darnton is really good at covering the basics that you need to know for Physics, but when it comes to the harder problems that show up on homework and tests, you likely won't see them in class. For us the other professor (Greco) created the tests, but as long as you had a buddy in Greco's class, you should be fine.

Can be hard to understand at times because of how quickly he goes over stuff, but is expected from a physics 2 professor. Overall a great professor, not amazing though. Simply put, you need to study ALOT outside of lecture to pass with an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nick Darnton is an awesome teacher; He was always accessible outside of class and made a real effort to help his students. I would gladly take any other class where he is the teacher.

Most people find Phys2 pretty difficult, and that's going to be the case with any prof. Darnton is funny, easy to follow, and very willing to answer even the most basic questions in class or over email/in office hours. He would be my choice of Phys2 professors.

It isn't that he is difficult, it's that PHYS 2212 is difficult, plain and simple. Greco handles test making and gradin etc. so the only thing Darnton is responsible for is teaching his sections, of which he does a respectable job. No accents or mumbling or rushing to worry about here, just steady clean teaching. Wont get much better for 2212.

Not a bad professor, his lectures are too in depth (stuff you will never be tested on).  To give an example on the second or third class he spent the entire lecture doing a Taylor series problem to prove one equation in the book we only had to memorize.  Better be able to learn on your own (hes very helpful during office hours though, lecture notso

Physics 2 is inherently a hard class, but Darnton was good at lecturing about it. Homeworks were hard, and the tests were hard, but the lectures were somewhat lighthearted and he was good at giving you the information you needed to succeed.

Darnton is pretty funny and informal guy who formerly taught at UMass before this semester. He goes off on tangents during his long-winded, unnecessary lectures that do not prepare you for  tests. Attendance is monitored by clickers though. Stock up on all the word you can as tests closely resemble old tests.  Note that Greco admins the course.

It's fairly hard and a good amount of work but that's the nature of the course.  If you pay attention, read, and do the HW, you should be fine for an A, at least a B.  Tests are straightforward usually but that's done by Greco.  Not the best but would take again.  Attendance by clickers.

He's great and takes the time to connect what is being taught to more familiar terms to make sure people understand the content. Exams and quizzes were not difficult and mainly tested on concepts taught and not hard math. Go to office hours with questions or concerns as well! He's really understanding and cares about students being able to succeed

Stopped going to lecture because he just read off of the slides that were posted anyways. He sped through class because he would skip things or not explain. He was nice if he understood what you were talking about. Has an accent but it's not impossible to understand.

His teaching was horrible. I don't know if it's because he's new to teaching but he basically reads off slides only; literally shows us what's on there and that's it with almost no explanations. Learned the entire course on Youtube with "Professor V" instead and used old exams as practices, got away with a solid B in the course

This professor is genuinely funny, and I really enjoy visiting his office hours—we always end up talking about our favorite video games. He's incredibly kind, and after every exam he reassures me that partial credit will be given, which is always comforting. The class itself is very straightforward as long as you attend PLUS sessions and studios.

Every calc 2 class takes the same exact exam, so the only difference between each class is who you take it with. Dr Ding is a very nice person but it is difficult to learn from his lectures. It's significantly easier to learn from Dr. Grodzinsky's lecture videos on canvas then go to class. 
Grade breakdown 
15% homework 
2% extra credit
85% exams

He's honestly a very caring person, but has a horrible teaching method. He has a habit of not thoroughly explaining the example problems and showing the full steps, just reads off the slides, and when asked a question, he doesn't explain it fully.

You're better off just attending another professor's lectures. My grades improved after doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares so much but very hard to understand. His pencil broke so he just shows the practice problems on the board with no context and poor explanations. Better off learning on your own or going to a different lecture. But he is very sweet and cares.
Amazing lecturer

High-quality teaching; well prepared for his material; intuitive explanation that is easy to understand; easy exams of conceptual, multiple-choice questions; generous grading for team project. Late in HW gradings though (I personally blame TAs for this). Overall, Prof Davenport is an extraordinary professor with excellent teaching skills.
I enjoyed this class, a good amount of homework, and as long as you did your reading this class was fine!

The guy is using the lecture notes of his predecessor without foolproofing them. His explanations are not always clear and doesn't tell you how what you are learning is relevant in the big picture of the course. The course material is mediocre (found way better/clearer from other universities).

Great lab and lecture! She was hilarious and cares about students a lot. Very clear grading criteria for this lab. Had a few instances where lab was a little unprepared, but it was very rare and never too big of a deal. Overall great experience!

Professor van de Wouw makes Synth Lab very manageable, much more than it used to be so I've heard. Very considerate of student needs and concerns as long as they are reasonable. Pre and postlabs take a while but the grading scheme is pretty good and the rubrics are clear. Technique finals are tough but she has a lenient retake policy which helps.

Overall she was okay but is very rude over emails. I had missed a lecture due to personal issues and she didn't accept it. I had discussed the issues I was having and she still seemed to not care. I was very surprised since I had heard good things about the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. van de Wouw made synth lab one of my most favorite courses I've taken. This class is supposed to be super difficult, but she made it so manageable. I knew exactly what I needed to do to get an A, and it wasn't unrealistic. She explained what should be difficult organic chemistry topics in simple terms. I took orgo 2 concurrently and was fine.

The specifications grading makes this class very easy. For every assignment, if you meet enough requirements on the rubric you get a grade of "complete". The only semi-hard part was the technique finals. The token system means you get to redo them if you fail, so you'll be fine. Easy and fun class, professor was very sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself seems pretty random honestly but she's a great professor. She tries her best and really takes into account student feedback to treat this as a 2 credit course (she inherited the course). Specs grading can seem really weird at first but it works out in the end so I wouldn't worry too much. Sometimes the work felt like a waste though

Specifications grading makes this class easy. Dr. van de Wouw is kind and approachable. Your grade really depends on the TA you have but most are chill. Token system to re-attempt assignments really helps. Everyone gets an incomplete on the first lab report; don't panic, you can revise it.

Great professor. Only issue is that the pre lab lectures were mandatory (only 1 skip given) but they were honestly helpful in doing the pre labs and the post labs so I would reccomend going. She gives out a lot of "tokens" than can be used to resubmit assingments throughout the semester. Everyone I know got an A with minimal stress.

Synth lab was a class I was worried about taking but she made it very manageable and interesting. She is newer to teaching the course, so she is very open to student feedback about making the course fairer to students. She cares about everyone being successful and prioritizes that.

Great instructor who changed the class structure/grading to better fit students' needs. All the assignments are pass/fail, which felt intimidating, but they're not super difficult after doing the same ones for each lab. Pre-lab lectures feel annoying and inconvenient time-wise, but they really help with the experiments and writing post-lab reports.

During our 5-9 PM section lab, van de wouw is always there helping out and having fun with the students conversing with them. Additionally, she understands that student's have other obligations and works to address this constantly (with her easy specs grading scheme and removing certain assignments). TA Feedback, though sometimes harsh, is fair.

Dr. van de Wouw really listens to her students and tries to modify the course to best accommodate their needs. She genuinely cares about making sure that Synth Lab is a reasonable course that students can still take a lot out of.

She is new to GT and chem 2380. Seems to be trying to make the course easier for students as it is a pretty labor intensive class as designed by a previous instructor. She is open to student feedback, but lectures are not at the best time.

This professor truly cares about her students. Genuinely, don't listen to any other reviews that say something bad about this class/professor because she's a good professor, understanding about personal lives, and also grades accurately

Very deceptive professor. Gave us a 'surprise' or 'gotcha' Adobe Express Final Case assignment at the last minute to substitute to a 'Final Exam' while we were in the midst of doing our Driving Traffic Final Presentation prep. Syllabus said 45% is on Driving Traffic, 35% on quizzes, & 20% on class prep/attendance/contribution. This is NOT included.
Halfway through the semester, and unsure about her. I'll update later. Overall positive though

If you can respectfully, take another professor. I mean I still locked in an A but for context an average on the third exam was a 40%... and he sent out an email on why he "couldn't curve it because we need to actually understand the material". Also overall just not a really understanding person so keep that in mind.

If you're here for the bare minimum, Dr. Erickson isn't for you - he will teach you so much cool math beyond what any other professor offers. If you're here for the love of the game, you will learn representation theory, character theory, ring theory, field theory, and get a glimpse of basic Galois theory. Amazing prof, would 100% take him again!

Admittedly, Dr. Erickson's classes are not for the weak of spirit, but if you are willing to invest as much time (or more) outside of class to understand the material, you will learn an astonishing amount in a short time period. Dr. Erickson made a semester or abstract algebra feel like a story unfolding- he is precise, engaging, and passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bro was one of those teachers who was too smart to explain content as a teacher. Worst averages on his exams out of any section and would never curve. Only reason I got an A was from watching other teachers lectures.
if you're not religious then pick a religion and pray.

Genuinely take any other professor. Tests were triple as hard as any other class. 2/3 midterms had failing averages. Final also had failing average. He doesn't care to curve the class and you will get a lower grade. Grading scheme is also worse than other professors. On the way to exams I wished I got run over. Please don't do this to yourself!

Exams were hard, and the content was challenging, but realistically, if you paid attention in class and followed his examples, you would be prepared for the exams. Finals were an easy way to improve your grade in class. The professor got much better at explaining the content by the end of the semester.

literally take anyone else for multi. the worst professor i have ever had. he doesn't know how to explain anything in a way that makes sense, exams are extremely difficult to the point he can't even curve them because everyone would STILL be failing his class. genuinely the worst class and professor i have ever had.

I would not take him for Math 2551 because he doesn't explain material well and what we learn in class is almost never applied to what the exam is testing us on. He also makes the exams harder compared to all other teachers (Average of a 46 on the 3rd midterm). He also believes failing is a good grade, so don't assume he will ever curve.

I've truly tried to give this professor the benefit of the doubt. I've gone to tutoring, used all my resources, but he teaches as if we're already at his level and tests us on things he barely covers or explains in class. The midterm averages have been failing, yet he refuses to curve despite this. I'm sorry, but not curving a 46 average is INSANE

Do not take this class. Lectures are incredibly confusing, and going to class did not help at all. The midterms are very difficult and test on things that were barely taught. The averages on the midterms are very low, but when asked to curve, he says no. Worst professor I've had by far.

He doesn't know how to teach. Lectures only made things more confusing, so everyone resorted to watching Lehmann's lectures online and teaching themselves multi. Still, he wrote stupid exams where every average was failing (3rd was a 46), and refused to curve the exams or the class. Even with full HW and Quiz credit, I barely scraped by with a B.

Useless lectures, everyone stopped showing up after the first 2 weeks when they realized its impossible to keep up with him and his lack of structure when you could watch Lehmann's lectures. Lowest averages and hardest exams, had to grind out of getting a C after being 10-20 points above the mean on exams and having full HW/quiz credit. DONT TAKE
don't take
Seemingly strict and intimidating but he means well and is great at explaining concepts clearly.
Just very kind and helpful to his students
would give gawkgawk 3000 don't care about nuffin this man is a saint and wonderful lecturer
He's so cute. He touched my heart in many ways.
He touched me emotionally. This class was inspiring and all the kids loved him! Would take again

He's my favorite professor at Georgia Tech. Great lectures with discussion questions. Labs are very well designed with extra credit, clearly documented and commented. ACA is definitely a challenging course — especially since I hadn't taken the prerequisite (ECE 3057) and no C++ experience. Despite that, I managed to make it through successfully.
Unfortunate name, but great prof. Is quite strict about talking or eating in class. Great otherwise.
Despite his name he's a pretty cool dude.
Workload is with reasonable amount. The exam will not be a trouble for you if you reviewed all the hw and slides carefully.

Good lecturer, light work of homework, recommend to go to his lecture. He sometimes sound mean and sounds like he has an attitude but does his job pretty good. Grades really fast but gives no partial credits. Tests are pretty easy but the harsh gradeness evens it out so the tests are pretty average.

A great lecturer. He really allows you to see the implications of what you learn in 2020. The class overall is not hard at all. Go to lectures and you will understand the material and do well on the exams. The exams are heavily weighted, online, and have little partial credit, but are overall fairly easy. Would easily recommend.

Very solid lecturer. The exams are very easy, straightforward, and relay concepts shown up in homeworks & lecture slides. Even though attendance not mandatory, you should go to class to avoid getting lost. Something to note is he has a bit of an unintentional passive aggressive attitude at times, but it's not too much of an issue.

Love his lectures. He's passionate about the topics and made sure everybody was on track. He explained the materials very well and every class was genuinely interesting. Grading is clear and exams are fair. Would love to take his other classes.
This Professor was Amazing. His exams were decently straightforward, and there was never any guesswork about what to prepare for. I wish he were teaching the sequel class.
Her lecture notes and presentations are great, but the quizzes and projects are hard. Don't take her class unless you really want to learn. It's not an easy class!

By far the most frustrating professor I've had. Doesn't respond to piazza posts or emails (only when convenient), 2 quizzes worth 40% of your grade with extremely minimal prep, homeworks sometimes skipping lectures ahead. When I asked what I could do to improve my grade, I was told that she was not God from her directly. Do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The structure of this class has it to where two quizzes taken during the beginning of the course have a LARGE impact on your grade but really they are both tests. She is also not receptive if you don't form a quick understanding of topics in the course and is very hard on regrades even if there are actual mistakes in the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 quizzes each worth 20%, 1 is a review of 2027. 2 projects each worth 20% with 2 hours to complete them. She's rude when you ask questions and moves to fast when going over simio. Half of her HWs have nothing to do with what we learned in class. Always finding myself using previous notes to do her HW. Not a "hard" class but she's unbearable.

SHOW UP TO CLASS. Zhou is pleasant and will use her lectures to walk you through problems; if you do not attend and take notes, you will fail your projects, but pay attention and you will be fine. Her quizzes are reasonable and she is quite lenient with homework.

The previous ratings don't apply anymore, she completely changed the course syllabus. She has two "quizzes" which are 20% each and covers maybe half the material in the class. The midterm and final project are really difficult and are not a good representation of the material taught. Teaching is ok but it is hard to follow the presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She knows the course materials well and is very clear in lectures (her lecture notes are amazing). Her classes are not math heavy and focus a lot on the application side. There are a lot of quizzes and labs. Some of them are challenging, but you can drop two of these. If you follow her lectures and do the homework carefully, you should get an A.

She is honestly one of the meanest professors I have ever had. Stops our presentation in the middle of the slide to tell us she doesnt need to know something. She laughs at us. Does not even read the documents we send her and leaves the rudest comments. Also interrupts all the time while we are still talking. Such a mean and rude professor.
The labs were incredibly difficult, but the tests weren't too bad. She has a very good layout for presenting material.
Great professor! A lot of quizzes and labs in one semester, but also offer more opportunities to gain points during the semester.  Plus, her grading policy is lenient.

She was very caring and considerate, and was incredibly focused on helping us learn the material. She always ensured there is enough room and comfort to ask questions about the material. She presented good background information. She knows the industry and had good examples. Her homework is difficult, but she offers great help at office hours.

Probably the worst professor at Tech. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She will spring surprise assignments on you due dead week, if you ask her for help she'll tell you about her straight A college career, and she reads off of he other professor's slides. She has no idea what she's doing. 10/10 would not take her class again.

40% Grade is Online HW that you can get 100% on. 4 tests, each 20%,1 gets dropped. Attending his class is unnecessary, slides have all the information. His multiple choice questions are memorization and have nuances to trick you. He's alright, probably would be fine if attend all classes, but it's pretty boring. Dr Condie's a kind professor, though

Not terrible, but the test were pretty hard especially the multiple choice. The practice exams his TA made did NOT help at all. He himself was pretty nice and chill and attendance wasn't mandatory. I would still recommend taking mostly because he gives a lot of extra credit and lets you drop one test which is pretty nice.

40% of the grade is hw which is unlimited submissions and auto graded, so you can get a 100 on it if you do each early enough before the deadline. this means you need an 80% average on the tests. there are 3 midterms and a final. you can drop one. best 2101 professor in the game. Really nice, really boring. I never went to class.

Dr. Condie is incredible! He loves accounting and is passionate about helping students succeed. His lectures aren't always the most interesting and exams are tough, but he has lecture videos and lots of in-class exercises that he posts to help assist in studying. He also offered 5 total additional points if 80% of class filled out CIOS.

Not the most interesting lectures, but if you can pay attention in class he will go over all material that will be on the tests and do ample practice problems to get you prepared. Tests are way easier than what I've heard they are like for other Accounting I professors, all multiple choice and always very similar to what's done in class.

Prof. Condie was a great professor. I hated accounting as a whole, but he made it more bearable for me! Cares about his students and is super passionate/knowledgable when it comes to the content. Highly recommend!

Condie is a great professor who knows how to make a boring topic seem at least a little interesting. The content can be difficult but the practice resources he has available are very helpful. Attendance is not required and he does post recorded lectures, but I would still go as there are some hints he gives for the exams. Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Condie is amazing! I was expecting ACCT I to be dreadful and he made it make sense. The homework can be long so dont put it off but I did it the last minute sometimes and I was chillin. Cares about his students & is willing to help if you ask. Would be his student again in a heartbeat. He lowk made me like accounting. Put in the effort!

LOVED HIM! he KNOWS what he's talking abt (he used to be a senior accountant) + taught the material in a very organized way. His TA's extra studying sessions were a really big help as well. This class can be really difficult and boring BUT his class made it easy. the homework can take a while but he's very accessible for help!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Condie is one of the best professors I've had so far. Accounting isn't easy, but he gave us so many exercises and practice problems so we could understand. You have to put in the work though, the homework assignments help a lot. Attendance isn't mandatory, but recommended.

Professor Condie is so caring. Homework is worth 40% of your grade and you can check your work unlimited times so if you completed it, you got a 100. Class is set up for you to succeed and I personally enjoyed the lectures. Tests can be tricky but doable. Ask for help if you need it and make sure not to fall behind because the class moves quick!

Such a sweet guy! Made me want to go to lectures even tho not mandatory. Material itself can be hard but he teaches well. Can drop one exam (including final), and hw has unlimited attempts + weighs a lot. Responds fast to emails and questions too. Def recommend!
Such a sweetie. I loved failing the tests. Still ended with an A because he is caring and if you put in the work you will eat.

Professor Condie was very caring and super accessible to students outside of class for help. He genuinely wants to see students succeed. However, I will say that his tests were very difficult as opposed to the actual content of the class but it is evened out by the large percentage of your grade being homework and being able to drop an exam.
Homework was very long and exams were somewhat difficult but he teaches the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Eric Condie is such a kind professor who really about his students. The class itself is pretty difficult, and you have to be ready to put in a ton of work for this class. But he's very accessible outside of class and will help you until you get it. Highly recommend! Just be ready to work hard.

His 3 exams were kinda hard, but he probably is still the best Accounting 1 professor if you compare the reviews of the other professors who teach this course. I definitely should have put more work into this class and studied more, but the material and lectures were just soooo boring. He always wanted to help all of his students though.

I really enjoyed Professor Condie! He conveyed ideas and material that were easily confusing in a manner that made them easier to understand, and tried to get us students intrigued by what many may find a boring subject. He does curve exams. Participate and show improvement! He may try to work with you if you are close to the next letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He wasn't the most interesting but he was a good teacher. He makes sure that students can get the material and records really good lectures. He is very bad at gauging time needed to take an exam so many of us didn't finish but he did curve it in the end. he is very accessible/willing to help his students and is very good at explaining.

Professor Condie is my favorite professor bc he's so caring. The class material isn't easy, but he set us up well. We had weekly homeworks that had an unlimited check your work feature (so basically if you did it, you got 100%). Tests weren't easy, but there were only 3 (including the final). Just make sure you do the hw & study.

He is a caring person to students and is diligent in teaching. Since there are bi-weekly tests, this online class does require efforts to understand the concepts. As the students request for help to solve difficult questions using emails, he teaches you passionately and finds a good way for you to understand. You will be lucky to take his classes.

He was very enthusiastic about accounting and uses good examples to help understand content. There are a lot of homeworks and they take a while but he uploaded all the homeworks and lectures before hand so you could go at your own pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From the bottom of my heart, please don't take this class with this professor. He just reads off of the slides and takes attendance based on how much you participate which is really subjective (he asks questions he wants specific answers to and puts you on blast when you get it wrong). Tests and homework are really long and hard. A tough grader.

This class was momumentally more difficult than it's pre-req: ACCT 2102. There are only 2 tests and the final. You must attend lectures because attendance is taken randomly through participation activities. He reads off the slides all of class. Visiting office hours is useful & he is accessible. Liked him as a person, but not as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Three exams and a final. Only 3 of 4 count towards the grade so the final is optional.  The best way to study for exams is practice tests and reviewing the lecture notes and slides. If you do that you will get an A in this class.
Easy A. That's all I gotta say.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ingall is a good option for EAS2600. Grade is 75% tests (lowest test is dropped) and 25% lab. You don't need the lectures to pass tests because they're given online and open note. Lectures themselves are interesting if you do decide to go to them, but you don't need them. Labs are easy and straightforward, you only need an hour to do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade is solely exams and lab, no homework. Labs are easy and don't take the full three hours and for exams, questions from old exams are reused so if you review lecture slides and old exam questions you'll get an easy A.

Grades entirely based on exams and lab work. Lab work is pretty fun, easy most of the time. Content itself is on the more interesting side imo. Don't have to attend lecture, reading the slides is enough. Exams are online and unproctored. Read the slides and do practice exams and the exams shouldn't be too difficult. Get to drop lowest exam score
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thermo with Ingall is pretty easy. He is SUPER nice and knowledgeable. Sometimes lectures were hard to follow or homework was quirky, but he is very accessible outside of class and the grading is lenient. (He will zoom if you need help!) The material covered is basic, but it touches all the bases. Highly recommend attending class and participating.

Dr. Ingall is a great professor! He makes thermo concepts easy to grasp. Lectures aren't mandatory, but I would recommend going because there are helpful worksheets in every class. Homework can be hard, but office hours are very helpful, Dr. Ingall is always available. Also, he is so kind and rounded me up to an A because of my effort he noticed.

Dr. Ingall is a great lecturer who made thermo seem approachable. We didn't focus on any atmospheric stuff this year, but all the concepts needed were covered. Grading was very lenient and there's a non-mandatory worksheet each class that helped a ton. Tests were solid measures of understanding, but right in the middle of the road for difficulty.

professor really cares and it's an easy class. no homework, just labs, which are relatively easy. the classes are pretty boring but there is also just not much you can do to make sediments and rocks fascinating. make sure to review before exams bc they have random info. study old practice tests because they are similar.

Dr. Ingall was a caring, enthusiastic professor who made lectures interesting. The grades are based entirely on tests, which makes it difficult if you're not great at test-taking. However, the lowest test grade gets dropped. Heavy focus on memorization and the tests were closed book, but most questions were taken from past exams.

Ingall is a good professor who is enthusiastic about what he teaches, definitely recommend. Just remember to use the practice exams for the exam because a majority of the questions are drawn from them.

Really easy class; the only thing the non-test part is graded on is the test, but you can use digital notes (just know that if you didn't review it's a lot of questions and you'll run out of time). Really nice teacher and lectures are thoroughly explained.

Dr. Ingall's lectures follow the textbook sections. Although it's not required, I recommend getting the textbook to reinforce some of the content. Make sure you do the practice exams he gives because they're super helpful in preparing you for exams. HW counts for 30% of your grade so try to keep a high HW average. You also get to drop 1 exam!

Professor Ingall I a great professor. I was usually the last to leave the labs but everyone else seemed to get everything quickly. He is very excited about his topics and the topics themselves are interesting. No HW, only exams and labs. It is not hard to pass this class, but if you want an A, you better study! I recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is entirely memorization, but he gives you access to all previous exams all the way back to 2004. As long as you don't try to memorize everything the day before a test you should be fine. Lectures are not mandatory, but he is a pretty nice and enthusiastic guy attending can be interesting.

Although lectures can be boring, Ingall is very excited about the material he teaches. Your grade is determined by three tests and a final (one drop allowed) plus an easy lab portion. LOTS OF MEMORIZATION. Tests aren't always based on lectures and you study for them basically by memorizing the practice tests he posts online.

He's really quirky. His lectures can be a little dry, but he's really nice and cares about his students. posts all lectures and old exams on canvas, so easy to pass, although he does highlight important notes in lecture, so going to class is helpful.

Labs are pretty easy and don't require the full 3 hours. You can best prepare for the tests by reading the slides and previous tests. No textbook necessary. Some chapters are interesting, others aren't. I would definitely recommend this class overall.

All you have to do to study for his tests is take 2-3 practice tests. So many of the questions are re-used that if you just memorize the material from previous exams you're going to do fine. Labs are super easy, just show up and you'll make the grade. Relatively easy A if you're good at memorizing

He is very excited about the material and his lectures are semi-helpful. His PowerPoints are very poorly crafted and difficult to study from.  He provides practice tests and there is a lot of question reuse. However, the tests are meaningless and cover very odd and specific material. Be prepared to memorize a lot of little things if you want an A.

EAS2600 is MEMORIZATION.  If you have a photographic memory, you'll ace the class easily.  Otherwise, BRACE YOURSELF.  The labs are stupidly easy.  Memorizing lecture notes is important, as is knowing everything on his practice exams.  I wouldn't say the textbook is really important, unless if you don't understand basic geological concepts.

This class is somewhere between a 3 and a 4 on easiness. I loved this class. He is a very kind man and loves his field of study. I learned a lot. He posts all his old test to study and the majority of each test are the same questions. Most people had an 88 average in the class. You can also drop one of your tests.

Professor Ingall is such a nice guy, and he is very passionate for what he teaches. His lectures are not the most exciting, but occasionally he will crack a few jokes. His tests are full of old test questions, so if you study the old exams, you will get As on his tests.

What we study in class is boring...unless you like rocks, but he definitely is good at keeping everyone interested. Go to his lectures and he is more inclined to help you. Use his practice tests as most questions are recycled!

He is a wonderful guy. The class and its subject matter were not of much interest to me, so I wasn't looking forward to the class, but he's pretty jovial and enthusiastic so it makes the class more than just bearable. The tests aren't too difficult, as they recycle lots of questions from previous tests (which he puts online). Overall, a good class.

Can seem unapproachable but cares about her students. Introduced the class to the many resources available and helped us set up Linkedin profiles and resumes. Very clear teaching style, some lectures seemed redundant

Some of it felt pretty redundant but the stuff about resumes and setting up a LinkedIn profile were very helpful. Great class to meet some people and Dr. Miller is an easygoing professor. She is very helpful and gets back quickly with communication. Do the work and participate, and you'll do well.
