She's a really sweet person who clearly cares about her students. While some of the projects did feel unnecessary at times, they were reasonable enough, and you can definitely learn *something*. She's extremely friendly and approachable, and I will miss having her class next semester!
Ensured we were prepared for our professional life and knew all the different opportunities GT had to offer

Absolutely lovely human being. Dr. Miller was a super caring and sweet professor for ENGL 1102. Her course theme is Dark Academia which is a lot more interesting that you'd think. There was only 1 essay, and 2 group projects that were fun to complete and very engaging. She is also super understanding about other classes and workload. Loved her!

I took her English 1102 class, and the class was incredibly easy yet interesting. We only wrote one essay while the other two big projects were unique group projects of creating a podcast and a website. Both projects were thought provoking and highly interesting. Dr. Miller explains everything well and is very flexible, truly caring for you.
She definitely is very organized and ready for class!! I felt as if she really cared about our well being and making sure we are prepared for the future!

Elizabeth is great! She is a very caring and kind person. Her first priority always seemed to be our wellbeing and how we were adjusting and doing in more difficult classes, and the coursework was simple and very helpful like creating a resume or linkedin profile or just meeting with our academic advisor.

Great lectures, but the grading on hw/tests is very tough. He has TAs write all of the homeworks and exams, which are graded harshly and not always fair to students. Was very accessible outside of class and had helpful office hours.

Dr. Filler is a very good professor. I was very nervous coming into the class, but he was not nearly as evil as I was expecting. He is so smart and cares for students. He is very accessible outside of class. The exams are very challenging, but it pushed me to understand the material more deeply.

Very engaging lectures, exams were tough, and homework was graded extremely harshly. Filler cares about students and is open to feedback. He restructured the course to encourage AI use on homework, but still feel like I learned a ton.

Summer 2025. My parents wanted me to change majors from seeing me struggle so hard with this class. His lectures are good and he's a very nice guy who wants you to succeed but the tests were AWFUL. Our average on test 2 was a 36. THIRTY SIX. I was also told this is not a weed out class??? which idk about but good lord it felt like it.

This course was combined with Abramson's section and the exams were still unnecessarily hard and the keys were not helpful for understanding. Filler is condescending and rude when asked questions in class and in office hours. He doesn't care about students' wellbeings or if you are doing poorly in the course. Computational assignments are brutal.

Good lecturer, awful professor. He showed up to lectures and knew the content, but thats all he did for the course. He gave every other part of the class to the TA's, exams, HW, Coding assignments, etc. This led to an overall extremely poorly run course riddled with errors and miscommunication making the overall difficult course harder.

Dr. Filler is a good lecturer, but his exams are almost to the point of being unfair. The entire grade of his class was based off of SIX assignments, and the exams were far removed from what was covered in class. He failed about 15/120 people the semester I took him and he has the lowest GPA in the ChBE dept. 

If value your grades, don't take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A kind of entertaining lecturer, however he presents nothing of substance. All the homework assignments were Matlab, not kinetics. Exams were full of questions starting with "We didn't cover this in class..." and the grading/curving were very ambiguous. Terrible professor and would delay graduating over taking him again.

Dr. Filler is an engaging speaker who will make you forget that you have no idea what he's talking about during the lecture. He very rarely details what is and isn't important in lecture, leaving us guessing. He's heavily focused on writing exam questions that are outside of the realm of his teaching while relishing in bad exam averages.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While his lectures are engaging, they're unhelpful because it's unclear what is an example and what is concrete information. He deliberately writes exams to have low averages and dislikes it when students are clever about solving the problems. He curves the class but he's vague about how he'll curve the entire time, causing anxiety and distress

Took Kinetics. Hard to reach outside of class. He can be condescending. The exams and homework are not that comparable to what is being taught in class. Does not really care how students are learning in his class. He loves the low averages. It seems like he just lectures, makes exams and then dips and leaves the Q&A to the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor never solved solid questions in class and that caused all exam averages to be very low. The class is eventually curved but it does take a mental toll on one to see those scores. Hard to reach outside of class.

Grading scheme unclear and curves strangely. It was impossible to calculate our own grade before the final because the curves were different for every test. Told us the final would have 4 problems and only ended up having 2, because he "only felt like grading 2." Hard to reach outside of class.

Michael Filler is a fantastic lecturer and set us up to do well in spite of the difficult test and homework problems. The tests are a reasonable length and difficulty, and the class is curved in a way that makes a B feasible. It is difficult to get an A in Filler's class. Homework doesn't take too long and felt appropriate for the course.

He is a tough grader for sure (fair tho), but a GREAT lecturer. You will learn what you need to know in a very structured way, which is very different from what I observed from other professors. I didn't get A, but I learned a lot and don't regret taking him. Try to do and work problem sets given on your own and know how to do them smoothly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wasn't my main professor for 2100, but was in charge of some of the test problems, grading, and problem solving sessions. He somehow came up with a problem for one of the midterms that was UNSOLVABLE, then graded it unfairly.

This class was extremely difficult. I feel that Filler was passionate about the field and cared about the students success. Every test was curved according to the average. This class requires A LOT of outside practice problems to succeed. Filler communicates that hours of work is needed to understand and be comfortable with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Always busy, not usually available outside of class apart from office hours. Good lecturer but tough grader and reluctant to give you back credit. Not a lot of homework but lots of quizzes.

Filler is a tough, but fair professor. His class is difficult, but if you put the work in you will pass. Most importantly, he is passionate about his field and will want you to be passionate too. He really tries to show the importance of what you learn in class. I always found him very approachable in office hours and after class.

He makes everyone fail the tests, then he does a curve based off the average and standard deviations. I had a high C and so did 3 of my friends, then he failed us all after the final. He's just a bellcurver who cares more about failing people than being fair, not cool, you'll have better luck with literally anyone else.

Professor Fritz is very very understanding of his students and puts us first. He is a great professor that knows what he's talking about. Only reservation is that he sometimes skips steps in his practice problems, which can make them hard to follow. I would definitely recommend taking him!

Fluid Mechanics is not an easy class. However, Dr. Fritz breaks it down very simply and does many many examples in class. The tests are usually pretty similar to the examples he does so they are really not that hard. He also gives a generous curve.

Teaching style is mostly doing practice problems in class, which I found effective. Wiley homework is often irrelevant to class content, but due dates are sometimes extended for this, and they're not impossible. Exams are way easier than the homework. One side of paper for crib sheet, +1 for each exam (2 for exam 2, 3 for exam 3, etc.)

Course consisted of Wiley plus homework, 3 midterms, and a final exam. Lectures were mostly spent on example problems. I recommend watching videos on Youtube for more in-depth explanation of topics covered. The midterms were fairly easy, and the final was not cumulative. Overall, Dr. Fritz was very flexible and never gave unfair exam questions.
Two classes taken. Repeated information. Not worth the time.

Very solid professor and clear expectations. Class is just lecture, online Wiley homework, midterms, and final. Everything about the class is pretty straightforward, questions on the test were fair and reflected the examples done in class. A good healthy amount of examples during lecture. He teaches you what you need to know.
Really nice and funny guy! He is a very flexible grader and wants everyone to do well. All of the lectures are recorded. Online homework weekly, three exams, and a final.

Dr. Fritz is a great professor who provides high-quality notes/material. He has an accent + can ramble/go off topic, so understanding him in-person was a bit troublesome sometimes, but the ability to rewatch his lectures balanced that out. He would answer all questions I have during and outside of class too. Also, his tests & HWs were pretty fair.

Gives great lectures and uploads them after class, so I never had to open the book. Confused at all, go to his OH. 10 Wiley HW's worth 20% w/ 3 attempts/problem. 3 Midterms and 1 Final, either top 2 midterms 26% each and final worth 38% or midterms 20% each, final 30%. Midterms can be 3-4 questions long and worth over 100%, final was 7 problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pretty chill. He doesn't make it known until the end, but if you pass the final you are guaranteed to pass the class. Gives lots of good information about the profession from experience in lectures. Online HW used through WileyPlus and he allowed 5 tries. Get a minimum of 50% on a lab report just for showing up.
Do not take this course without prior Python experience.

It is hard to rate Professor Joyner as he is extremely inaccessible. The professor rating is largely for the ta's who handle most of the interactions with students, and they were quite unorganized and ineffective I would say. I think this is just the issue of letting ta's run a very large, mandatory class. Also yes the course is just hard.

Super hard for an intro course. For something as hard as this, I'm surprised they STILL have a professor teaching it that is so unavailable, doesn't meet in person, and does not give ANY leeway whatsoever. Pls just do the in-person for your own sake
just too hard of an intro cs class. prof is COMPLETELY unavailable, it's an async course. just learn python on your own or choose a different section, please.
DO NOT TAKE. Such a stressful class for no reason
h0rrRble. way too much hw, very hard tests (all or nothing), just too much for an intro course

Dr. Joyner is a very knowledgeable and caring; he is highly respected at Tech, and it is clear to see why. However, as an online course, the TAs do most of the communicating, and make it very unstructured. Tests are difficult, especially without a CS background. All or nothing, no partial credit. Lots of homework as well.
bad prof. and bad TA's. NOT a good class to take. Feels like I was taking a free python online course somewhere. Didn't feel like an actual class with a prof.

The course was very easy, and a week's worth of material could be done in about 3 hours. The homework can be a touch long, but is nothing compared to CS1331. I breezed through the course, as the tests were straight coding and as long as you did the homework like a human and without AI, it was easy to get a 100 on every test.

Please please please be cautious when signing up for this class. If you have a heavy workload, STAY AWAY! This has been my heaviest and most difficult class in high school and I am doing DE Math @ Tech and have taken 12 APs. It is a lot of work.
unstructured course. give too much hw for the course it is. tests are not forgiving. All or nothing. Expect you to already have known python before taking course.

The professor himself is a very knowledgeable and busy guy. He truly doesnt have time to teach this course. The course is the problem. Its basically run by TA's and I tell you they are really annoying. So just dont take this online course and save yourslef from the stress.

Don't take this course. I'd recommend taking the Inperson course. There isn't any communication with the professor everything goes through the TA's! It's not a very helpful course and really difficult exams. Homework is okay but they give way too much for the type of course this is. Save yourself from the stress, choose a different professor.
unstructured course. I learned most of the material from an online python course. The class was of zero help. Very disappointed.
Everything in this class is self learning and the modules don't help at all. You'll need to find your own study materials in order to do well.
Don't recommend taking this course.
The exams in this course are really hard.
AVOID. DONT STRESS YOURSELF OUT ITS NOT WORTH IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very frustrating class. The workload is excessive, and the exams are extremely difficult, especially since they require perfectly written code with no partial credit. This is tough for students who are new to coding. The grading process also felt unclear at times.

If you don't already have knowledge w/ CS this can be a very long and challenging course. Wayyyy too much HW for an intro class, but there is extra credit. The tests are hard because they are all or nothing, so it's easy to get a poor grade if you don't write out the solutions perfectly.
Very low quality of professor.
The best online course I've ever taken, every video is clearly related to homework and practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His online section itself isn't bad at all. He has video lectures that explain most concepts well and understanding is not difficult, but you have to be disciplined and make an effort to try. Homeworks are relatively easy A's but the exams can be difficult (the later in the course, the more difficult the exam). Will round your grade up though.
Really good.

This class was very easy. The first few units are simple, even if you don't have experience, the videos and practice assignments make everything understandable. The practice quizzes/tests are very similar to the real ones, so just study those. The class is organized well. Overall, as long as you do the work and stay on track, you're guaranteed a A.

Only good thing about this class is that he gives lots of extra credit and it's basically impossible to fail. Other than that his tests and quizzes are way harder than the HW he assigns and gives way too much HW in the first place for a 3 credit class.

I succeeded in the class due to my commitment to it. It is very easy to fail this class, but also easy enough to get an A. Know this class won't be easy, watch the vids (don't skip ANY), and do the work without AI and you'll secure an A. The grading scheme is in your favor. Commit to the class and put forth time and effort & the A is yours to earn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Joyner is the best! Was nervous about taking CS but the online lectures and practice sets made it easy to follow through. Definitely make sure you understand the earlier units. The class builds on itself towards the end.
He's an awesome person. Great lectures, great resources. Lots of chances to get your grade up and recieve extra credit.
Not very considerate and communicates very poorly.

I thought this class was fairly easy, just time consuming sometimes. As long as you do the assignments and not entirely Chat GPT them, you'll have enough understanding of the content to do well on the tests/quizzes. The final was difficult but its only worth 10% of your grade and you have the opportunity to add 2% to your grade with extra credit.

Best prof for 1301 - genuinely a class for beginners and no prior cs knowledge expected. Test questions are all or nothing but there's a lot of extra credit to earn back points. Final is definitely significantly harder than other tests but manageable if you study.

This class was surprisingly really difficult. The work was really time consuming and the tests were all-or-nothing (meaning if you messed something up, you get 0 pts). Although I had some prior coding knowledge, I still really struggled and the test formatting really dropped my grade. The best part of the class is that you get extra credit points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As a non cs major, it was a lot and it took up a lot of my time, and I still didnt do as good as I wanted to. the smallest mistake on a test makes you lose 12 points. Way too much irrelevant work for this class.

If you don't have any experience on python it would be worst of your grade, i'm really sure this course required more than intro stuff.
**for the test you have to make sure every single letter have to be perfect, one mistake ruin yr grade.**
My fall semester went worst

Honestly speaking, this class was really overwhelming as someone who is not a CS major. If you have a hard time understanding coding or just have no interest in the matter, I would recommend you take a different section of this class. The tests and quizzes are all-or-nothing & the homework is HEAVY. I wish I took it in person as the tests are hard.

I took CS1301 for Dual Enrollment, Mr. Joyner's the best, gives you 4 extra credit points if you just complete some tasks. Do the homework and practice quiz/tests as exactly those same concepts show up on the test/quiz with tweaked questions. It was a really fun class. You should definitely take him! Study really hard for test 3!

I took CS1301 for Dual Enrollment, Mr. Joyner's the best, gives you 4 extra credit points if you just complete some tasks. Do the homework and practice quiz/tests as exactly the same concepts show up on the test/quiz with just tweaked questions. It was a really fun class! You should definitely take him!

I took CS 1301 with David Joyner as a Dual Enrollment student. Honestly, I barely scraped an A (with 4 points of extra credit). Do good on the first 2 tests as after that, it gets much harder. I got a 55 and a 40 on the last 2 tests while i got a 100 and 76 on the first 2. Despite his tests being incredibly difficult, I still managed to get an A!

Best professor you could take for CS1301! We have the chance to get 5 points of extra credit. Grade was not too test-reliant. You can fail a few tests and still pass the course with an A! Great grace period, but avoid getting behind, as it is a lot of work with difficult material. Also, exams are quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Intensive coding assignments, and participation. Projects disconnected from the theory of this class. Total 13 coding homeworks + 2 exams. Very intensive class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class can be quite a lot if you happen to fall behind during the middle of the semester. The unit 3 test is quite difficult so be prepared for that. Other than that, the course is great. Up to 5% of extra credit for the overall grade and 50% of your grade is just doing online classwork which you are guaranteed to get a 100% on. He's the goat.

Look, he is about as good as it gets. If you truly struggled in this class, you should honestly be thanking him for making you realize you're just terrible at CS. One of the easiest classes I have ever taken and the work load is perfect, not to mention you actually LEARN a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class online, and it was fine. I really wish I took this class in person because it was so easy to tune this class out. Pretty easy if you don't fall behind and you can tell he's really passionate about CS through his post.

Just dont take the class, it is literally a god awful amount of work and takes so much time out of your day, take anything to get the credit besides this class. like geniunely dont ever take it, i thought he was a cool guy but for 3 credit hours you literally spend your whole life on this class. it made me hate cs and hate school
HES MY GOAT I LOVE HIM MWAH

This professor has refined this course over the 7 years it dropped, and it is pretty good. The concepts are hard if you are not familiar with coding, but the learning format is really easy. I took the summer semester and it was pretty difficult but that's because I am not the coder. 5 extra credit points. If your dual enrollment, take it! Why not?
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Had clear instruction and generous grace periods that allowed students to complete work even a week after the deadline. Work was not very hard and extra credit opportunities were plentiful. I enjoyed Professor Joyner's class a lot.

The grading scheme of this course is so forgiving, especially with 5 points added to your final class grade if you do all the extra credit. I had no knowledge of CS before this class, but Dr. Joyner's lectures made it so easy to understand. Tests can be challenging, so make sure you do as good as you can on the first 2 tests because they get harder

Dr. Joyner is an amazing teacher, never took cs before. The homework was pretty reasonable for each week and there was always a grace period for no penalty. There was lots of extra optional practice for the quizzes/tests(good gage for exams). Online tests so each problem is all or nothing for pts but you get to run as many times as you like.

This was my first dual enrollment cs class and Professor Joyner made it very easy to understand concepts and data structures and algorithms. He was very available and offered a lot of extra credit. I would recommend taking his course!

Best CS professor you can get. Online Async is the way to go, it makes learning flexible. His method for teaching online is the best, ever. Learning was so easy because of how good of a teacher he is. There is A LOT of homework, lectures, test/quizzes to do, but that is mostly expected.

I was personally TERRIBLE at CS (as I've never done anything like it before), but Joyner was so caring and extra helpful when I needed it! He offered lots of extra credit, and the lectures were helpful and engaging. I would definitely recommend this course with him! Just make sure not to get behind- it works out terribly.

This class was very well-structured for an online class. It is imperative that you keep up because it is easy to fall behind and takes a lot of work to catch up as the problem sets are intensive. The practice quizzes are like the actual quizzes, but the practice tests aren't like the exams imo. Joyner is great and someone is always on Ed to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you struggle with coding or have little/no experience, I highly recommend Prof Joyner. The tests can be difficult, but he is very gracious with extra credit. Since the course is fully prerecorded, it may seem like he isn't super involved, but if you need guidance, reach out to him! He really wants to help you succeed!

Not very involved in the class, but the TAs are very helpful. Prof is nice. Very possible to get an A, just make sure not to get behind and do your best on the first two tests, because they get very hard after. No extensions, but he does give 5 points extra credit. The final was brutal.

The class overall was awesome and the first few test were similar to the previous test but the final this year was different, so do the credits and average a 50 on the exams and you'll get a B in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't very engaging. It is taught through an online medium, but I think the tests were wayyyy too difficult that there should've been some curve or other measures taken. The final was insane.
He decided to give an insane curveball of a final this year. Not sure what the thought process was behind it, but it was nothing close to the practice finals.

Joyner is a great professor, but the tests and quizzes can definitely get really difficult. Do as best you can in the beginning! There isn't really any extra credit that counts for much. The problem sets and lectures also take a bit of time to do. With that in mind, do NOT get behind. There's a grace period but it'll be a lot of work built up.

My goat. Dual enrolled this class my senior year of high school, and it's still the best CS class I've ever taken. The material is easy enough with any level of experience. Plus, you can compile and run your code during exams with provided test cases. This is so rare and so helpful!

Going into this class everyone said it was so easy, but DO NOT BE FOOLED. The class is a lot of work and I had a wake up moment when I got a 35% on the Unit 3 exam after getting a 100% on Unit 2. Still came out with an A but the class was just a lot more work than what I was expecting.

Joyner is an exemplary professor. Every class he teaches is well structured with clear grading criteria. He seems to strike the perfect balance between setting a high bar for excellence and also making sure no single assignment completely tanks your ability to do well in the course. Passionate about what he does and a cares a lot about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Pretty cool guy. He structures and lays out the course materials really nicely. Make sure that you don't stay behind on topics because you will end up struggling on the exam (proctored). The coding problems on the midterm look fairly similar to the homeworks you do, so super helpful.

I took this class fully online in summer and loved it! I have zero CS experience but didn't struggle with this class at all. It's nice taking it online so you can choose how long to spend on different topics. His course is so well structured and organized with very clear and helpful examples and explanations. Amazing class! Take him if you can!
Classes take a long time, esp. the exercise sets. Easy if you do the work. last test was the hardest test

Professor Joyner provided amazing videos for the students to learn from before taking quizzes and tests. MAKE SURE to look through all the videos, practice problems, quizzes, and tests BEFORE taking them if you are not a strong student in CS. It took a lot of effort to receive an A but it is possible. Just practice, practice, practice!

There is no partial credit on the tests. So do your VERY BEST on the first few ones cuz the later ones get harder. So get those 100s dude! Do not push it to the end of the semester. I missed it by a few marks, do better. Very sweet professor, also instant replies to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved this class and how it was formatted. Crazy amount of flexibility since it was asynchronous. Make sure to stay on top of assignments. Really good late policy. Should be an easy A if you have any coding knowledge. 3-4 hours of work per week, which includes watching lectures.
David Joyner is a great and respected professor! His lecture videos were clear and the practice exams were very similar to the tests. I recommend taking his classes!

Being required to take a cs class at tech is challenging for people like me who study neuroscience and have no interest in computer science but this online course was phenomenal. The material is easy to grasp and there is a lot of practice. The tests are very straight forward and exactly like the practice. There is also tons of extra credit.

I could check many other tags - get ready to read, participation matters, inspirational, caring, so many papers, accessible...

Most of the 1.0 ratings seemingly misunderstand the nature of HCI coursework, where open-endedness is a feature and not a bug, because the goal is precisely to weigh tradeoffs in the face of no definitive, 'right' answers.

Honestly, it is an A that you have to work for, however it is definitely possible. Just DO NOT fall behind on work, especially if you take this class over the summer. The majority of the class makes perfect sense, even if you have no previous coding knowledge.

Such a good professor
Tells you everything and more that you need to know, the course is really easy (easier than high school comp sci) 
Course is also set up very simply

All in all, if you get Joyner - know you are in for a good time
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The online course was setup very well with the lecture videos by Dr. Joyner being very clear.

Joyner's class is honestly structured very well for an online class. 4 unit exams (all coding and kinda difficult tbh) worth 10% each and 4 unit quizzes (no actual writing code) worth 3% each. Extra credit opportunities up to 5% on the final overall grade. Take advantage of the TA helpdesk early on and plan ahead of time. Do NOT fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: online 1301 is hands down the best way to take it (especially since its required for basically everyone) It can still be hard sometimes, and the problem sets can feel never-ending, but nothing you do is busy work and its a million times better than any of the experiences I've heard from my friends who took 1301 in person. Don't fall behind though

For an online course, the class was structured extremely well, and the lectures were very detailed and informative. There was also plenty of examples and practice problems that made learning the content very easy. Some weeks the workload is pretty heavy but manageable. Would highly recommend him for CS 1301!

I loved this class. You are constantly coding throughout lectures and for homework versus just learning through lecturing, which is how I learn best. The tests can be a bit difficult and frustrating, but each test is only 10% and with extra credit you can get a 70 on each exam and still come out with an A. Great professor and class!

Solid online class, self guided with a few deadlines. Some of the lecture videos can be a little confusing, but the practice helps. I would recommend taking this class in person, but it's solid for an online class
great professor! HIGHLY recommended CS 1301 with him! he simplifies concepts so they are easy to understand

HCI now added 20% 4 quizzes close book. and TA is a tough grader.  I was a good student, but now my grade is so awful. Every week I receive negative feedbacks. Even I evaluate 3 peer HW a week, I just got 0.1 point in the end. This is first OMSCS class I took, my grade is so low, and now I am about to quit. Thank you for ruining my CS degree dream.

took dual enrollment gtcs. This guy is the absolute goat you type code instead of handwrite it and its infinite attempts and the practice stuff he gives you is almost same as the test. like if u understand how to do practice ur guaranteed an A. easy gpa boost and fun class. recommend for all HS DE students and dont sell and end up not taking this.

Although this class is entirely taught through videos, he does a good job explaining concepts and creating examples. The class is structured very nicely, although some weeks have longer problem sets that shouldn't be done last minute. The TAs do a great job answering questions on the forum and nothing is graded very heavily.

I took CS6750 and learned SO much from Dr. Joyner's lectures. However, this was probably the most intense class I have taken throughout my time in the Masters program. 8 page (max) papers due every week, 12 page (max) individual paper due towards the end of the semester, and a 30 page (max) group project due as the final. Be prepared!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I am proud to say I was taught by David Joyner, especially after taking multiple online courses in coding and never really learning a thing until this class. I was barely able to scrape by with my A, but I can say with certainty that although this class was hard, it wasn't impossible. Just very, very work heavy. If you do the work, expect an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this course as a dual-enrolled high school student. I felt like this course was easy, having taken AP CSP and CSA. It is organized very well, but there are a few technical issues in the beginning of the year. However, Professor Joyner and his TA's understand that. It is easy to get help from the TA's. Tests are easier than the quizzes.

Amazing online course set-up, clear lectures, but don't fall behind. Those who don't do well are those either just bad at coding or do not have the responsibility to stay on track themselves. The only drawback is all or no credit on test questions, but practice tests mimic the actual ones. Easy to get an A with the number of graded assignments

Okay, I took his online CS1301 class and barely managed an A. He is very kind and funny; he offers extra credit up to 5% of the course grade. The exams are fully online, so they use an autograder to check your code, meaning that if there is one thing wrong with your code, you'll get 0 points. Don't fall behind.

Great professor! This class was easy but useful and informative. I went into this class already knowing some Python, but you really don't need to because he teaches everything from the beginning. There is a lot of flexibility because you have the whole weekend for quizzes and tests and homework is only due at the end of each unit.

Best CS 1301 professor!! If you have the chance to take 1301 definitely do it is so much better. I had no coding experience before this class and was still able to excel through his easy to follow lectures.

I took CS1301 online and it was great. He was very clear about grading and expectations and gave a window of time to complete online quizzes and tests (usually Friday to Monday). He also provided a schedule at the beginning of the semester outlining when every single assignment, quiz, and test was due.
Professor Joyner is the best!
He's the GOAT. Not much else to be said
Dr Joyner is an excellent teacher, clear concise explanations of concepts, a lot of work but valuable and meaningful. It is my second class with him and would happily take any course he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Joyner is a top tier professor. Incredible structure for the whole course. There's a lot of mandatory reading though, and the peer reviews are not my favorite, but this course is very relevant for front-end development. Could not recommend it more!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: David Joyner is an amazing professor who engages us with his funny humor and detailed explanations. The course is structured extremely well and everything is very organized. He is very caring and understanding of situations. Overall, I received a strong grasp of the material and had an amazing experience.

He does not explain concepts well or thoroughly in his online 1301 class. There is no partial credit on tests, so even if you get most of the code right, the online software where the tests are taken marks you completely wrong. It is a very tough class for those who have never coded before, despite it being an intro class.
best teacher

Professor Joyner's CS 1301 lays a great example of how online classes should be. The class is very engaging and Dr.Joyner makes great analogies and jokes along the way to keep the course interesting. The content is taken step by step and is easy to follow through. Highly recommended!
I want to take all of my courses with professor Joyner!  What a joy (ha) to have him as professor!
Very laid back and forgiving of any work I could not complete in time.

Overall a good professor, however his class is not the easiest or most straightforward class.  Expect tedious assignments and a large amount of readings.  It is possible to get an A in his class, as long as you put in the work.

Truly a professor who cares deeply about his field, Dr. Joyner is both passionate and enthusiastic in his lecture videos. Joyner's course is structured in a very intuitive and well organized manner. You will learn a lot more than you think in this course. A perfect introduction for anyone interested in CS.

The class itself is easy, but the tests are ridiculous. coding takes a long time and we are only given a short amount of time to completely code almost 10 problems. there is NO PARTIAL CREDIT on the tests. all or nothing. it's very possible to get a zero on a test. you can still get an A or B if you do the hwk and problem sets so don't stress.

I took his class for CS1301 and it was a blast. He's an awesome professor, really easily accessible outside of class and provides ample extra credit to get an A. His tests are also organized in such a good way where you can run the code to test it out before you submit it which is so convenient. If you put in the work this class is an easy A.
He was incredible

Joyner is a great professor. Caring guy, willing to work with you, overall very positive. Course itself can be tricky; if you do not have any background in CS and you have a busy semester schedule (me), then this course can be difficult to get an A in. DO NOT FALL BEHIND, IT IS VERY DIFFICULT TO CATCH UP ON.

Dr. Joyner is one of the most caring professors I have met at Tech. He is very flexible, understanding, and a great teacher. His online lectures can be a bit confusing at times, but he is very understanding and even adjusts due dates if students need extra time for assignments. Take him if you can!

Joyner is great, he let me resume my final after my internet crashed, which saved my A. Without a prior background in CS, this class will be difficult. Be ready to work on this course weekly, but it is doable. Do not get behind, because catching back up is hard. Overall, great professor, a hard course.
Dr. Joyner is a truly inspirational person and the best instructor I have had yet. This class is amazing and I would recommend anyone to take it. Just don't fall behind!
Great. You can see his passion, and will learn a lot.

Hmm.. He is surely a nice professor, however, that doesn't mean he is a good professor. His videos seem to be organized with subtitles in it. When you move on each chapters, however, his lectures are messy. His tone is enthusiasitc but I'm not sure if his explanations are concise. I can hear his voice but now what he is saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is really a great teacher that understands how to teach programming to those who are completely new to it, especially explaining concepts that can get confusing and how they truly work on the computer (such as reference types and such, which made much more sense to me when he explained it).
Dr. Joyner truly and utterly cares about his students and about the program. Take all the Joyner courses you can.

Probably one of the best professors I've had at Tech. His class and amazing video lectures gave me a wonderful foundation in computer science and the Python language. I dealt with some things during the semester, and he was willing to work with me and help me catch up which prevented me from dropping the class and falling behind an entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you do not have any prior coding experience, be wary. While it is an intro level CS class, if you happen to fall behind at any time in the semester, it is very hard to catch back up if you have 0 experience already. No partial credit on tests, typically similar to practice tests, but genuinely know your stuff don't memorize them!

Dr. Joyner was an amazing professor. Lecture videos are very short and informative. For those dual enrolling like I did, try not to get behind and procrastinate. Previous CS experience can be very helpful, but doing problem sets last minute can get stressful!

Amazing class, and amazing teacher! Very lenient and understanding, lecture videos are short and informative, and all tests and quizzes have multiple, very helpful practice versions that are almost identical to the real ones. Problems aren't very hard, but there's a lot of them!

BEST PROFESSOR IN COMPUTER SCIENCE! Joyner is amazing, his lectures are perfect and his test format is really manageable. Amazing course; took for dual enrollment and made me declare my major as CS. Take him!
Very helpful and the online class structure is one of the best online classes I have taken.

So glad I took him for this online class. I came in with absolutely no CS experience and still found it very easy. Just keep up, because it's easy to let it slip and you fall behind. Problem sets can also get a bit tedious but it's good practice. Quizzes and tests are very generous, often allowing multiple submissions per question.

Mr. Joyner was a wonderful professor. He was absolutely helpful and considerate to any personal issues that I had and adjusted the course directly for me. He was an amazing teacher and was very helpful. I would definitely recommend any class with Prof. Joyner!

I didn't expect much from an online asynchronous class, but his class exceeded my expectations and actually got me interested in taking more CS classes. There is a lot of work, but if you stay on track the class is very well-designed and fun.

A pretty well-organized class, but it's super easy to fall behind considering how many problem sets/homework/lessons are required. The class felt pretty heavy for an intro class, so it gets to be pretty overwhelming if you aren't a CS/Engineering major (which I wasn't). No partial credit on exams but fair amount of grade cushioning is available
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Class was decent just be ready to move fast through the material. I hated the fact that everything was auto-graded so there's no partial credit even if you basically got the codes correct. The videos were good and very informational. Make sure you have a lot of time to dedicate towards it!

This is my favorite professor I've ever had. I dual-enrolled in this course and Professor Joyner inspired me to pursue Computer Science as my major. His class was the most organized online course ever, and his videos were engaging and to the point. Thank you, Professor Joyner, I wish I could take every CS class with you!

Very easy class compared to McDaniels' 1301 class. Uses Edx platform for the course but created his own videos and such to teach you. I had 0 python experience and I didn't really have to watch most of his videos until lists, dictionaries, file i/o. Homeworks are excessively long though. Tests are easy and straightforwad just dont procrastinate.

When I saw other students saying it's so easy to fall behind, I thought they were wrong. Halfway through the course, I realized they were right. Try to stay on top of things. I'm ending with an A. But I think that's because I had prior coding experience in HS. Put in the work if you don't have prior experience and you'll get an A. He's awesome

AMAZING guy. I went through some rough stuff at the beginning of the semester, and he offered to let me take an incomplete and said to return to the course when I was ready to (just worked through it when I had the time and a good mindset). He cares about his students more than he does the class and WANTS you to learn. VERY clear and easy to follow

Professor Joyner is absolutely phenomenal and a skilled educator. He is reasonable but still requires effort, and truly cares about his students success with computer science. His lectures are really really really well made and I cant recommend him more. When taking the asynch class be careful not to procrastinate, though. Best GT prof Ive had.

David Joyner is a fantastic professor. His lectures are engaging, entertaining, and informative, and he gives the right about of homework to allow students to learn the content effectively. If you're a total beginner at CS (like I was), it'll be a solid amount of work, but as long as you don't get too behind, you'll do great. 10/10 would recommend
David is a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Joyner did a great job creating his CS 1301 class. The class was built to be virtual asynchronous, so I did not have many live interactions with him, but his recorded presentations and the structure of the class were fantastic. Made it really easy to learn. Spent about 5 hours/week on this class to complete the material and get an A.

True gem of a professor, but the class is a LOT of work! It's asynchronous and you just have to complete assignments before the unit deadline passes. However, there are soo many problems to complete in each unit so start early! He's very understanding about extensions. Also, his practice quizzes and tests are super helpful/similar to the real thing

Although this completely an online EdX class, Prof. Joyner has created and taught it beautifully. The content is such that it is impossible to not learn the concepts. Prof. Joyner was also flexible with deadlines and gave extensions as technology naturally brought its complications. If you keep up with the class, you should do well and learn a lot!

The entire course is so well laid out and fully put together. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. I went to one recitation and still got an A. He gives out extra credit every unit and he give practice quizzes and exams THAT MIRROR THE REAL quizzes and exams. He was super helpful with trouble shooting during exams. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I was told that I needed to take Dr. Joyner's asynchronous class at all costs for my required CS credit, and they were right! Even though the class is asynchronous, I really felt connected to Dr. Joyner. He is a great lecturer and I LOVED the way this class was structured. If all classes were like this online class, I'd be so happy.

Such an amazing professor. It was online but this course was MADE to be online. Everything was accessible and convenient and there were so many chances to practice problems and to understand the material. He really cares about his students and he is a fair professor. 10/10 would take him again.

The class is all online, so there was very little interaction with David directly. However, his prerecorded lectures are concise, engaging, and informative. Also, in the few correspondences I had with him, he was very friendly and understanding. I would definitely take a class with him again.

David Joyner is awesome. I did the online section. The class was hard since I had not a lick of coding experience however I still did well and he gives a ton of extra credit. I would recommend it but keep in mind it's incredibly time-consuming if you do not have a clue about coding.

This is the best CS class for anyone who needs to fulfill their computer science credit at tech. Its asynchronous and allows you to go at your own pace. The test and quizzes are very straight forward if you put the effort into learning the material and practice with the practice tests and quizzes he gives. Also there is lots of extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: David Joyner is the best prof I have had. He is very kind and obviously cares about every single student
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is by far the best online class that I have ever taken. The lecture videos are easy to follow. You have unlimited attempts on all of the exercises and coding problems and even have multiple attempts on the tests. If you've never coded before this class might be somewhat difficult but I don't think its too hard to get a A.

If you can get in his online section DO IT. He is by far one of the best professors Ive ever had and the way this class is structured if you do the work theres no way you wont learn it. Great guy, always willing to communicate with you outside of class and he genuinely cares about the success of his students

Dr. Joyner was a great professor for CS1301 (online). His tests are similar to the practice exams, and there are many opportunities for extra credit and help. If you keep up with the class, you should do well. It is not an easy A, but if you put in some effort you will learn a lot and succeed! I knew very little about coding entering the class.

I already had experience with Python, so this class was pretty easy for me. Even so, I did watch some of his lectures and they were very good. The videos are broken up into smaller sections and there's lots of practice problems to solidify understanding. If you have experience with coding, I would recommend trying to test out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I haven't taken any other online classes, let alone CS classes, but Dr. Joyner's class is exemplary. His videos are really easy to understand, the exercises are great practice, the tests and grading are fair, and he is available to answer questions. If you do the work on time and have an open mind about learning Python, you will be good.

Literally the nicest prof at tech. He's so lenient with deadlines, makes the course so flexible, and is so easy to reach out to. The course itself is pretty easy as long as you don't procrastinate the problem sets, but the exams are usually easier than the homework and he gives extra credit opportunities for every unit. You have to take him
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing prof. As long as you don't mind online classes, he is THE best. His online course is SO good, and I even feel like I learned a lot. I did a lot of the work the weekend before the tests are due (would not recommend), but if you do the work, you'll get an A. Great guy.

GREAT prof, GREAT course. Super interesting, and great lectures. Class if fully online, so easy to pace yourself. There are practice exams for every test and you can get up to 3% of extra credit, so there's no reason not to do well in this course. I had an A before taking the final. Dr. Joyner is FANTASTIC - definitely take his course!!!

One of the best professors ever. I came in with no programming experience and still managed to do alright. He is extremely caring and considerate and always works with students to accommodate their needs as much as possible. Seriously saved my CS grade and I cannot thank him enough. Truly one of Tech's finest faculty.

Best online class I have ever taken. If you have the choice choose online with Joyner! If you do the lessons you will get an A. Just put in a bit of work for this class and you will be rewarded! Much easier than in person and you learn in a better way (in my opinion)

Joyner does a really good job in the online class. He was super accommodating during the pandemic. Make sure you follow at the recommended pace because you can easily fall behind. Anyways, I recommend taking this online one over the in class one.

CS1301 online is an amazing class--asynchronous and lots of practice problems/examples. Dr. Joyner is very accomodating and caring; he sends weekly update emails to make sure you aren't falling behind. Lectures are easy-to-follow, and practice exams mirror actual exams. The piazza for this class will be your best friend.
The online CS 1301 class is great! It allows you to be extremely flexible (especially if you have a heavy semester). Professor Joyner was extremely accommodating and helpful
Best online class I've ever taken. Straightforward, caring, and always there if you need help. Great structure to the course and very enjoyable.

Class isn't too bad if you keep up with the work, and pay attention to each short lesson. The class is test heavy, but the practice material he releases is near identical to the tests. There was 3-4% of extra credit up for grabs at any point throughout the semester, so it's not hard to get an A if that's your goal.

I loved the flexibility I had with online CS1301. While the material progressively got harder, as long as you dont fall behind watching the lectures, you should be fine. Professor Joyner is very nice and understanding and wants to see his students succeed!
David Joyner single-handedly saved my academic career god bless I am tragic at CS and I personally thought this class was very hard but the professor is amazing

Easy online class, much easier than the in person version! I loved the recorded lectures and the tests were very straightforward/tested us on things we already practiced in practice problems. The professor is nice too and accessible during his office hours. TA Help desks and piazza also helped a lot if you get confused on something.
Class content was solid. Tested on the class content. Responded quickly to questions. Overall good experience.

Dr. Joyner is so caring. He is very clear about how to succeed in the class. He also gave us several extensions on tests and assignments throughout the summer. If you have any problems with the class or need a personal extension, he is so willing to help. Additionally, there were several resources we could use if we got stuck.

One of the best put-together classes I've taken at Tech. Everything you need is online and you can take it completely at your pace. You can learn basically everything from the guided "assignments" and then solidify your knowledge in the homework and tests. Why can't every class be like this?

in the online cs1301 course, prof. joyner is very understanding and gives you a lot of time to complete assignments, which is really nice. also, even if you suck at coding like me, if you complete all the homework/problem sets/extra credit and still bomb the coding section of the tests, you could still very well end up with a B
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the best online class I've ever taken. Dr. Joyner is really on top of things, and the interactive format of the class really helps you learn the material. You'll be tempted to wait until a couple days before the test to start the lessons. I did this and got an A, but it was a near miss, so don't do that. Wish he taught more CS classes.

The homework are very subjective and frankly, they don't provide much value. There are a lot of ambiguous questions which can drive people crazy. It almost feel like Joyner is actively trying to set most of students to fail rather than inspiring them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Joyner clearly loves to teach and is very good at it. You'll work hard in his class, but he's very available and helpful, and you'll learn a lot.

Took a class with him, lots and lots of paper. Even though the homework provided lots of insights of the concepts of the course but barely learned any new techniques from the course. Prof. Joyner is more suited to teach conceptual based courses but I wouldn't recommend any AI/ML related classes. Overall, decent professor, bad class design.
Hard class, but I am also not that great at CS. Lots of people i know made As. Pretty good for an online class. Lots of lectures.

Dr. Joyner is the best teacher I've had at Georgia Tech and I took the CS 1301 online class with him. His video lectures were clear and concise. I had never taken any CS course before this one. I only had to complete 3 problems on the final for a 95 overall in the class. Definitely recommend him.

This is perhaps the best class I've taken. You can go at your own pace, and you cannot receive less than a one hundred on any homework assignment unless you give up. You get multiple attempts on test questions, and you can submit coding problems as many times as you want before you get it right. This class is very easy and works to any schedule.

Just to provide a different insight to this class, if you are serious about pursuing CS you shouldn't take the online class. For example, I don't think we learned about strings/lists/dictionaries until the very end of the semester for a week or two. OOP and other algorithms are barely covered. I felt super unprepared when moving on to 1331.

The best class I've taken at Georgia Tech. I am a business major, and it made me think about switching to CS. The online format is amazing and so much better than in person. You get to run/test/debug your code as many times as you want before you submit it on a test (other CS sections are paper only). You can complete material at your own pace.

This guy is awesome! He made the class really accessible and makes it interactive and engaging even though its online. You will actually learn from examples and videos if you pace yourself and don't wait till last minute. Since you get 1 or 2 attempts for each mc and unlimited submissions for coding problems there isnt partial credit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Joyner is the best CS professor I've ever had a class with by far. I took the online section, which is definitely worth it. Pretty simple A if you do your work and his recorded lectures are really good. Definitely worth taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take CS 1301 online!! This course is a really effective way to learn it. Joyner's video lectures are really concise & the lessons are broken up by exercise questions so you don't get distracted/bored; vids are 3 mins long on avg. Really manageable class; its schedule is properly paced and very flexible, but don't procrastinate or you'll struggle.

Videos for learning are very good. Schedule is a bit flexible since it's online, but don;t get too far behind because it's a decent amount of work. Test are legit even though online- they very much monitor you, but if you do the learning an homework and put just a little forethought into the test you should do well. Responds quick to questions.

The online section of CS1301 is great,do not be apprehensive because this class is online. The majority of the grade comes from lessons and problem sets that have unlimited attempts, and the tests are simple . Requires a little bit of effort, is an easy A, and you'll learn as much as the inclass section without having to take trips to the help desk

I never really write reviews on here, however I had to with this professor. He is hands down the most caring professor I have ever had. He wants every one of his students to succeed and will go above and beyond to make that happen! Take him!!! You will not regret it.

Even though I didn't leave with an A in the class, this is without a doubt the best course I will probably take at Tech. You need self-discipline to do the work though because he usually gives you until the day before the test to turn in the work. It'll start off a bit slow, but don't let that fool you. Just do the work in a timely manner to pass.

Best class I've ever taken, online or not. His Piazza responses are very detailed and helpful. If he's not available, Piazza falls apart, even though we had many students answering questions, too. Bc it's a large class, there are a lot of questions. If you can't reach him by Piazza, he is very good about Slack responses. Tests taken online

First time taking online class and it was great. You watch short videos and you do exercises throughout. Take good notes and do the problem sets and you should be golden for the test. I never had to go to office hours. Plus, some of the tests he would give you the questions beforehand. If you have to take CS1301, DO IT ONLINE. You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken online classes before and had terrible experiences, but both the layout of the course and the professor itself are excellent. It takes self-discipline like any online class, but the professor is very qualified, passionate, and answers emails, slack, and Piazza questions promptly.

David is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's extremely involved with his students, going above and beyond to get in touch with them. The class I took him for (CS 6400) was extremely freeform and he did a fantastic job allowing students to pursue something that interested them while still accomplishing all of the learning goals.
He's really nice and very fair but don't expect a good grade. Lectures make a lot of sense but don't necessarily help with tests and hws. No partial credit!!!!

Pretty tough class with a tough professor. He goes through the material pretty fast during lecture but show up and pay attention during lecture because test questions were similar to ones he did in lecture. Tests were pretty hard and really tested your understanding of the material. Read a textbook, practice, and go to TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader and doesn't teach you anything that is required for the harder IE classes in the future.

[Duplicate review for more characters] Lectures not mandatory, but no released lecture notes so SHOW UP. Homeworks are decently straightforward, reference the free pdf textbook for additional help. Never went to office hours so can't say anything there. 12 homeworks and 3 very hard and very broad exams is all the class is, assignments wise. Chiller
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading scale is every 20 points: A = [100,80] B = (80, 60] etc. Very hard and broad material, very hard and broad tests. Made a 28/100 and 20/100 on the two mid-terms, did better on the final (still sub 65), and this absolute GOAT flat curved my finishing grade up an unholy amount of points that I'm not telling as to not set precedent.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from the lectures, you learn as you're doing hw. Hw is due on Sunday 6 pm. Shoutout the TAs for the review session tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i was a happy girl who always smiled. After taking isye 2027 with foley, all of that joy quickly disappeared. I studied for DAYS for that final just to end up right below the A mark, and he never even told us about curving and wa so unclear. SO hard pls be warned.
Theres only 2 exams and a final which are 5 questions each and no partial credit. Class average on the second exam was a 43% and still no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First of all, his lectures are so hard to understand, he has no powerpoints, and does not take lecture recordings. Also, he states in the syllabus if you take your own lecture recordings he should not be in the video. His tests are hard and his practice tests do not have answer keys so you do not know if you are right.

Dr. Foley is very unorganized and teaches in an outdated manner with no online materials. Lectures lack structure, and exam expectations are unclear and inconsistent with past exams. He answers questions but shows little concern for grades or feedback. Final grade details are not provided, leaving grading and any potential curve unclear.

Dr. Foley is a super understanding professor. He is very accessible to answer any questions and clearly knows a lot about the material. It is a difficult class, but his tests are pretty fair and the homeworks are challenging, but help a lot.

Yes Foley is hard. He teaches in a very different way then most. Once you get used to they way he teaches he is not bad! He would let our questions guide his lectures. He was very helpful with all questions. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! Don't get behind and ask questions when you are confused and you will do fine in the class. He is very nice guy. SHOW UP!

He's an incredibly kind and intelligent professor, however he posts next to no resources on canvas, gives no partial credit, and the textbook does not correlate at all to what happens in class or what is on homeworks/the exams.

Foley knows that it is very test heavy and is very forgiving. If you show that you care and come to all of the lectures, Foley will give you a leg up when it comes to a curve. Foley genuinly cares about his students which can be shown if you go to his office hours or stay a bit after class. He doesn't want to see you fail but you also have to work.

Professor Foley is very knowledgeable and caring, but he is very disorganized when it comes to lectures. Don't skip lectures tho. Exams are difficult and don't exactly cover the topics that you expect it would cover. Although this class is difficult, it is not impossible. Attending TA office hours old exam problems are probably the best resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is very caring, but the class is very unforgiving. 80% of your grade is determined by three tests with no partial credit. Tests are very similar to previous exams (posted online), and he goes over great examples in lectures. Tough with no answer keys, but if you put lots of effort into understanding everything, you will do very well.

Professor Foley is such a sweet & smart man, but a horrible teacher. No partial credit is given on ANY exam which leaves the average scores being around a 50%-60%. Additionally he does provide practice exams but getting solutions, or even a direct answer to questions regarding the test, is IMPOSSIBLE. A TA literally said "I dont remember the ans"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NO partial credit on tests - doesn't even look at your work. Example tests from 1998 but NO ANSWER KEYS FOR ANY. time-consuming hw, but only worth 20% and is graded harshly. Lectures consist of him writing all over the board, switching topics with no warning. If you require some sort of structured plan to learn, you probably shouldn't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking his class. No partial credit means that getting a tiny part of any question wrong instantly reduces your grade by a significant factor. Practice tests for midterms are given, however there is no way to tell how you're doing on them because solutions are not provided.

Does not do a good job of really making this class feel like a learning environment, he just goes on tangents during all classes. Does not provide answer keys to tests, no partial credit which makes these tests almost impossible. Class is extremely difficult for no reason.

Might be one of the worst teachers I've ever had.
Partial credit on tests = 1 small thing wrong on one of the parts of the questions is an immediate 70%
'Textbook' is a lecture notes pdf.
Canvas is as barebones as it gets.
Lectures ramble on nonsensically.
Provides old tests back from 1998, but does not give solutions to any of them.
8 a.m lecture.

Very good professor -- funny, caring, and explains concepts clearly. The homework can be difficult and time consuming, but if you put in the time, and review notes after each lecture, the tests will be fairly easy.

No partial credit, lecture recordings, or practice test answers; writes on a whiteboard; teaches through examples- it is a big ole struggle bus. Would not recommend taking him even if he's the only option. Great and funny guy, but tests on stuff that's not very similar to the examples in class. Can work together on homework; crib sheet=harder test

Foley is great in lecture and will prepare you extremely well for future ISyE classes. Unfortunately, you will likely have to sacrifice this grade for those long term benefits because this class is insanely hard. No partial credit on tests, homeworks are difficult and he doesn't post the lectures on canvas. He does post previous tests to study
Great professor. Grades are pretty fairly given out and he is happy to help you understand the material. Really personable and knowledgeable professor.

ISYE 2027 was an interesting class with Professor Foley. On one hand, he was incredibly nice and just a genuinely caring teacher (he tried to learn every students name in his class). On the other hand, the class was pretty difficult, and sometimes lectures were hard to follow. Be prepared for lots of homework assignments as well.

Fantastic professor.  Very receptive to feedback and makes lectures engaging, and he's always available via email to respond to questions.  Exams are simple if you really know the material, but no partial credit.  Lectures are usually amazing, but can be slow at times to set up future concepts - don't miss classes though, or you'll fall behind!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Foley is very smart and knows what he teaches. However, he is not a good teacher. Lectures are based on examples and not on explaining topics. Sometimes I did not even know what topic he was giving. I would not recommend this professor at all. He is a very good person but not a good professor. What saved my grade was the curve.

hardest class ever but he's hard to hate bc he's so nice. hw = hard & graded for accuracy. only grades in canvas are hw, 2 midterms, & final. class avg for every midterm is usually an F/low C. class is gonna be curved, but u won't know where u stand until final grades are released. rly hard to get an A unless u devote most of ur time to this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Foley is a good lecturer but that is where the compliments end. he refuses to give partial credit despite it being an engineering course, the homeworks and tests are always far more complex than the examples in class and the textbook is next to useless

Foley is amazing, his lectures are always very well put together and he is extremely knowledgeable . Answers questions in class. Since class is all about probability, no partial credit on exams. Class has 2 exams, weekly homework, and a final. Homework can be tough but the professor answers a lot of questions via email and sends them out 2 everyone
Easy grade, but prof is unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very unorganized but answers questions

Such a great profesor. He is clearly very knowledgable and knows how to teach to multiple teaching styles. If you take the time to participate in lecture, ask him questions outside -- he makes himself very easily available -- and focus on homework, you will be totally set for an A.

Dr. Foley is extremely caring, understanding, and responsive. He is very easy to reach if you ever have any questions about the material and will make sure you understand the concept after you ask him questions about it. Although his exams are hard, the homeworks give you a cushion and help you understand the material thoroughly.

I really liked the content of the class, and Dr. Foley presented it in a great manner in the online lectures. There is a large emphasis on homework, as it was 70% of our grade, and the other 30% was tests and the midterm and final. Definitely watch the lectures and take notes, as otherwise, it'll be very difficult to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance, definitely take a class with him before you leave. The homeworks were very difficult, but you derive properties that help you really understand the core concepts of probability. I dont think I couldve learned better with any other prof for this class. No partial credits on tests, but he always grades on a curve. 10/10.

Foley was honestly my favorite prof at Tech so far, and he made the 8 am worth it. The homework is challenging, but very cleverly made in order to build upon itself and teach the material. Don't be scared when the test averages are super low, he understands and the class is curved. A great and super-intelligent man!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For lecture, besides going over the material, he also does example problems that appear in the homework and tests. Understand how to do the homework and examples from class, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super caring professor that wants you to succeed. Not an easy class but if you work hard and do the practice tests you can get an A.

Foley is a great guy. Really cares about whether or not students are learning the material. I would say try to go to as many lectures as possible. Attendance isn't really required, but his in class examples and discussions will really help a ton on exams and homeworks. He usually teaches an 8am, but if you work through waking up, it really helps!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley has been the best professor I've had at Tech. He makes classes interesting and easy to understand. There are many tough assignments, but they usually boost your grade and help you understand the class material. You need to go to class and take notes to get a good grade. His exams are tough (no partial credit), but he curves at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Foley is such a sweet old man- he cares so much about his students. However, lectures are extremely hard to follow, and he doesn't post notes anywhere so you HAVE to go to class. HWs: hard af but grades easy. Tests: hard af and no partial credit. But he curved my final grade of 54% to a B, so it all works out. Not a bad prof if you want a B
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good professor. Hard class. Hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures make no sense, I only survived this class because of the textbook- after weeks of begging him to send out the text sections we should be responsible for (his class notes did not correlate at all). Tests are nearly impossible to do well on- 18 short questions with no partial credit. Class is curved a ton but not worth the stress

Dr. Foley really cares about students. He's not that great of a lecturer and his notes are sometimes confusing, but he gives you a lot of homework and tests you over similar concepts. He grades on a curve. I ended up with a grade much higher than I was expecting because of how I was doing so poorly. So I'm definitely glad I took him.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is an excellent professor. His homeworks are time-consuming and difficult, however, they're helpful and the grading is lenient. His exam questions are basically an extension of what you've already done. Use recent past exams and homeworks to study for his exams. Lectures are disorganized, but he's happy to stop and explain whenever.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Foley is a great professor who really wants you to do well. You'll most likely do poorly on every test, but you'l most likely end up with a B in the class. The class isn't that time consuming, and the homework is helpful. Go to office hours. An A is attainable so don't use his GPA as an excuse to be lazy.

Dr. Foley is awesome. He's a great guy. You will end up with a B in the class NO MATTER WHAT. Keep that in mind. He's a stickler for his GPA, so he legit rounds at least 90% of the class down/up to a B. So don't worry if you are sitting at a 50 or 60 in the class. You're fine. HW is difficult. Find old HWs. Practice old tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very good teacher, cares a lot and is very accessible after class to go over material. However, the lectures can be a bit unorganized at times, and the tests do not have partial credit, so do not be alarmed by your low test score, there is a curve. Also make sure to start homework early, it is long and an important part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Spent a lot of time studying for this class, but often was disappointed by results on tests (short answer math, no partial credit). Homeworks take hours to complete, and it is difficult to prepare for tests because he doesn't give answers to practice tests. Great lecturer, answers questions; if you put in effort, expect a B.

Amazing professor, very helpful in and out of class, however, there's no structure for ISYE 2027, and classes from previous years do not reflect the content and speed of coverage for the current class. Homework is very tedious but tests are easier. He likes to keep the average GPA between 2.9 and 3.0, so that's how the curve will be determined.

Dr. Foley is by far one of the best professors I've had so far. He genuinely cares about every student and is very clear and specific in his explanations.
