His tests are fair - they stem mainly from lecture notes and HW questions, but the HW can be quite difficult. However, he always sends emails to the entire class answering questions, which is a +
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at Tech. The class wasn't easy and homework's are long and difficult, but he is very willing to help, responds to emails quickly, and the classwork and homework are very indicative of what tests will be like. Very nice guy. Would take one of his classes again

Was my favorite course of my freshman year even though it was the only one I got a B in. The lectures are very interesting and very free flowing. They have a nice flow between him directing the lecture and taking student requests for better explanations. If you ever needed help he was there during office hours too.

Foley is a really sweet guy.   However, 80% of his class's grades are made up of two tests and a final, and he never gives partial credit.  The other 20% of his class is made up of 6 or 7 impossible homeworks that very often include things he doesn't cover in the class. He gives you practice exams, but won't give you answer keys.

He is one of the best professors I've had. It's not going to be an easy A. You have to work for it. The hw's are difficult and he assigns them every week, but the tests arent as hard as the hw. If you understand the hw, then you'll do fine in the test. No partial credit for the tests, which messed my grades up a bit. He curves at the end.
Great teacher , solid course.

He was overall a very good teacher. Didn't really use the book much except for a few homework problems. Homeworks were difficult and took a lot of time, but helped teach you the concepts. Tests werent terrible, but you had to study quite a bit. Very willing to help if you have questions though.

Pros: Really nice guy, really good teacher. Cares a lot about the material and his students. You will learn a lot if you show up, pay attention, and ask questions. Tests are pretty manageable. Just make sure you can do his old practice tests and you'll be set. Cons: Homework is every week, and hard as sh!t.

This class is one of the hardest I have ever taken. The homework is insane. The midterms and final are extremely tricky. The course material is not that hard, Dr. Foley just chooses to make it really hard. However, he generously curves the final grades. I never got above a 50 on a test, and I finished with a C. He has your best interest at heart.

Dr. Foley is a great guy.  However, HWs are very hard and most of the time do not involve what we cover in class.  Study, go to the TA for HW, form a study group, and study.  Tests are not bad, but he does not give partial credit so don't mess up.  Don't expect an A if your scores are not 20-30 points above the average.
Very smart teacher. Tests are tricky, but fair. Homework is barely related to material covered in class, and does not provide much help to students for it.
Very confusing class. HW is difficult and takes a long time, and test questions are random. Go talk to him when you need help - better learning environment. (TA's are great for hw help!)
very cool in class. you'll dislike the class when you have him, but after you finish, you'll thank him

hard teacher, but good teacher and helps you learn some important ISYE material. hw was pretty difficult. tests averages were about a 60. good teacher overall. no open notes or calculators. practice tests are pretty similar.
The best teacher for a intro to probability class there is at Gatech. If I had another chance to take this class I wouldn't take it with anyone else.

best way to describe him is the coolest tough professor. his class is based pretty much on student's questions, and homework is based mostly on what we talk about in class. smart guy, explains things very well. exams are not too bad if you STUDY. you need to study, and you need to do hw. he grades on a curve that is based on class performancce
Must go to lectures if you want to learn anything. Very helpful if you got a question. Do all the practice tests and you'll be fine. If you do really well, definetely will get a B or an A.
I thought he was an excellent teacher.  He kept lecture very interesting, and a barely had to crack my textbook.  I would definitely reccomend him to anyone.
No Comments
Easy as nuts! Not an IE major, but Probability is so freaking easy. How could you not get an A in this class? Imaginary Engineers.

I didn't like him, he is very undecisive about his teaching.  He doesn't write stuff until someone in the class says it and if someone in the class asks a question he makes someone else answer it instead of answering it himself.  The homework was ridiculously tough and the tests were easy.
His slides aren't helpful and even when going to lecture it still doesn't make sense. Overcomplicates things and just talks at a much higher level than he teaches.

Very unorganized. Good person who's bad at teaching. Grading is unnecessarily complicated and the homeworks take forever. The tests are poorly written and when asked for clarification, he just reads the question again, which is entirely unhelpful and condescending.

The pre-PSS lectures are longer than they should be for the amount of content they cover. His expectations are unrealistic and will lowkey try and gasliight you into thinking that you did not read the instructions clearly, when he CHANGED THE INTSTRUCTIONS after multiple groups submitted and he realized he does not like it

The lead instructor (not PSS) for 2250. Nice guy & fun to talk, but class was severely unorganized with assignments not clearly posted on Canvas (deadlines very hard to find). Chaos ruled and TAs + PSS Professor greatly helped in guidance, but class lacked structure and was a hodgepodge of work to do, found BMED 2310 to be much better organized

He will confuse you and likes to make his expectations seem higher than the actual grading criteria. He loves to yap so he'll ask you super deep questions that you don't actually have to answer or consider for deliverables. Way too much "busy work" for a like 1 hr course and just a giant group project but it is what it is. He is nice tho.
Todd had unrealistic expectations. The homework assignments took several days to complete and contained no practical knowledge.

Todd clearly cares about your success. However, his questioning and guiding is unclear. He will let you redo a portion of the course if he feels your work is not good enough, but then you are missing out on 1/3 of the course material. The lecture content is unhelpful. Why wait until the presentation to tell you that you are on the wrong track?

Amazing professor! I had him for BME 1000 for a few months as my previous professor had left. In class, his lectures were very engaging as he is a great storyteller. Outside of class, he was very helpful during office hours, not only helping me with my queries but encouraging me to go above and beyond with assignments. Would highly recommend!
Homework and tests for this class take an unreasonable amount of time.
Very friendly, engaging, and comprehensible lectures. Chill class in an otherwise not-chill environment. Tries to make the best out of everything.
Very nice professor, but homework and tests  are killer, extremely long take 8+ hours to complete.

He's a caring professor who made this class as easy as it should be while also getting you thinking about your career as a biomedical engineer. Assignments are not difficult at all. Attendance is mandatory and checked. If you take the time and treat the class as a guide for you, you will learn a lot of information that you'll use for other classes.

The best professor I've ever had. Such a kind, caring guy who knows exactly how to guide your thinking to lead you to discover things for yourself, which is very important for 2250. This class is so dependent on how good your prof and TAs are - he absolutely made it for me and everyone else there. Highly, highly recommend.

Todd SLAYS. I went into BMED1000 (not BMED 2400 stupid rate my professor) not really thinking I was going to get much out of it, but you so do if you just pay attention and learn the things he's actually trying to teach you. He is so funny and inspirational and understnading. 10/10 human being and 10/10 class.
Dr. Fernandez is one of the kindest, most considerate, and helpful professors I've had. He really cares about his students which unfortunately isn't common practice at Georgia Tech.

Todd was the nicest professor Ive had at GT. His care for students is exceptional, and he made statistics really interesting. I know a lot of people consider taking ISYE stats, but if Todd is an option I would recommend him. The homework is time consuming but helpful. If you do what he says and stay on top of your work, an A is definitely possible

Professor Faulkner is legitimately the best lecturer I've had in my life. He breaks down complex topics really well and seems to understand them incredibly deeply. He's also available to talk to about class topics, especially real-world applications and justifications, outside of class. If you're taking 1332 don't go to anyone else's lectures.

Good lectures that go through multiple examples to grasp the different data structures/algos. Grade is nicely balanced between homeworks, tests, and projects. Class does a great job of honing programming skills.

Good professor he uses the entire class to teach as much as he can. Perfect talking speed, organized, and he draws everything out. Hard class in general with big projects. Definitely, go to office hours and get help right at the beginning there are many resources that can help you throughout the course. Do not fall behind and start EARLY!!

Lectures are goated, enjoyed every single one. Diagramming is super clear and cool, very first-time learner friendly. Even though I disliked debugging coding assignments for 20+hrs in TA lab (be sure to start early) and ragequitted CS to become a pirate (Fred joke for introducing DFS), I still love data structures and algorithms in CS theory.
The best lecturer I have had. The class consists of mostly of homework and tests. Highly recommend using office hours, all the TAs were very good.
I love the way 1332 is structured. Never went to class because he recorded and uploaded the videos. Generally love the way he teaches as well as Mary's video, and I love how you can exempt the final!

lectures are pretty heavy in material. homeworks take a long time .tests focus on the stuff you see in lectures and practice tests are also helpful.he explains content well, but its sometimes hard to recall the giant amount of information he dumps in previous lectures. pay attention and review often
Clear lectures, lots of material, and tests that align to the course content. Homeworks take time but there's a lot of resources online and in the lecture to help with that.

Professor Faulkner is an excellent professor. His lectures are clear, well-paced, and easy to follow with annotated OneNote slides. If you pay attention and use the provided pseudocode, getting an A is very doable. Exams are fair and similar to the practice exams. There is also a lot of extra credit and a final exemption option.

Faulkner is a GOAT professor. In terms of learning from lectures, his lectures are far easier to follow than HB's, as he keeps things at a moderate pace with annotated notes on OneNote. He always keeps things straightforward, and if you pay attention in class, it is p easy to get an A if you also use the pseudocode they provide in course materials.

1332 itself is a very straightforward class, and Professor Faulker's lectures were easy to follow and understand-- most of the time I didn't require any review after paying full attention in class. He does speak really fast so if you plan on watching recordings, you'll most likely need to keep it at the normal speed.
My glorious king
Great lecturer, not really too keen on speaking to students personally but he explains concepts insanely well from the ground up. Would recommend!

Literal goat professor. Explained topics so clearly. Exams were very fair and similar to the practice exams, and there is a bunch of extra credit. You can exempt the final too. One thing I recommend is to take the hybrid version because they get recorded lecture videos which are up for a week, and can still attend lectures if you wish.
Very solid professor for 1332. Take if possible

Overall great lectures that are to the point. Explains things well and clearly. 

Uses OneNote instead of a PPT, which is so much better IMO. I hate lecturers that just use slides.
Best 1332 prof. Clear expectations and grading criteria, lots of extra credit and you can exempt the final.

Faulkner is the GOAT. Lectures are extremely well done and informative, and there are videos on canvas if you don't attend. Tests were very fair and you can exempt the final if you do well on them. Homework is manageable, especially with the help of CSVistool. Overall, definitely take 1332 with Faulkner.

Great guy, great professor, great course. I will say lectures lowkey take too long though just watch Prof MHB's module videos on canvas, they explain a full week's information in like 20 minutes. But nonetheless lectures are pretty good for understanding. Try to exempt the final cos it's worth it, exam 1,2,3 are pretty easy imo
Pretty good professor but definitely overglazed on rate my professor. Lectures are not very good for actually learning, but are decent for reinforcing prior knowledge.

Very good lecturer, really knows his stuff. However, he speaks extremely fast. So, I would learn the content before coming into class and then understand while he speaks rather than taking notes. Tests are standardized. Can watch MHB videos as review after going to Faulkner lecture. Very nice guy and good teacher. Also, he posts lecture videos.

He's an amazing lecturer, he is quite funny at times, and to be honest he seems really chill. But the thing is that this class is hard, and you're gonna need to put time into it outside, I'd say study for this class everyday for 45 mins to an hour, especially if you don't understand the content in lecture. Also practice alot with the given practice

Amazing lectures that go well with the HW's and exams. You will understand so much about every data structure and algorithm after this class. Also they added demos this semester which were alright just a little stressful under time pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
1. Extremely knowledgeable TA's who are of great help
2. Great lecturer- love the real life examples
3. Easy homework that aids your learning a lot (dont GPT it!)
4. Structure of the class is smart and fun
5. Exams are tough

Great class! He organizes everything very well and you truly get out what you put into it. I would take any class w/ him.
Lots of cheating and giving away exam questions. His TAs definitely write some of these reviews to make them look better
Extremely good at teaching material, watching his recording + doing practice exams should be enough to do well on exams.

Fun class overall, the difficulty does increase over the semester. Make sure to take advantage of the early tests, as the later ones become harder and harder. He's very good at teaching as he explains almost every concept and goes through examples.

Phenomenal lecturer overall; engaging and funny at times but knows how to explain the concepts of the class really well. I took a hybrid section so I went to lecture in-person one day and watched a recording the other way, both of which were high quality (eventually, I just went to both in-person sections though, since attendance isn't checked).
Great prof, very structured, well made lectures. Always does examples and answers questions well. You can skip the final if you do well on the midterms too!

Go to his lectures if you can!! His explanations of data structures and process for tracing are straightforward and clear. The weekly homework makes you write up the data structures you're learning which is a bit of work but really helps with understanding

One thing I'll add to Professor Faulkner's list of compliments is how well he introduces ideas. He explains what situation you'd find yourself needing a data structure or algorithm before even teaching it- and this made understanding everything so much easier. He's a great professor.
great prof, good lectures, insanely difficult tests, make sure your study for them

I don't usually rate professors, but Faulkner deserves this 5. He talks a little fast in his lectures, but he somehow manages to explain everything clearly. I never struggled with any of the homeworks or exams, and all I relied on was his lectures and CSVisTool. This is coming from someone whose only prior coding knowledge is CS 1301 and 1331.
Cool dude, lectures are mostly useless (at least for hybrid), make sure to utilize office hours. Pretty easy class as long as you utilize csvistool well.
good teacher; difficult class (at least for me).

Faulkner's lectures are the best I've ever seen. He does a great job at giving you the intuition behind DSA to the point where it can sometimes feel like we're inventing it ourselves. He doesn't just tell you how things work, he makes you understand WHY they work that way and why it makes sense for them to be that way. HWs are fine, exams are fair

Dr. Faulkner is nothing short of a genius. He teaches things by introducing the problem first, piquing your interest before showing you how the solution was devised. The class will give some difficulty, but even if you don't pay attention, he gives you every resource you need to succeed x100. You can't go wrong in this class—shoutouts to CSVistool!

Faulkner is truly one of the best professors at Tech. He somehow finds a way to dissect a hard topic to make it understandable to the class. He can answer questions outside of class content and goes deep in a structured way into each topic. Gives lots of opportunities for the class to ask questions. Would definitely recommend taking him for CS1332!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: terrible exams, decent lecturer. bs policies

Very doable class and not too time consuming. Make sure to actually understand the data structures and be able to visualize them rather than trying to memorize the hws. Faulkner was great and an entertaining lecturer, but I ended up watching the online videos instead and using his online notes as a supplement. CSVistool is very useful.

Faulkner is an amazing lecturer. He brings clearly planned out notes and navigates through the topics of the course effectively. He teaches everything you need and sometimes even more! There are so many resources for this course, so there are plenty of ways to be successful. I would love to take another course with Faulkner.
Great professor. His lectures were engaging and really made me learn.

Prof. Faulkner is a great professor for CS1332. His lectures are sometimes a little fast and dry, but he gets the information across in an understandable manner. Exams are also fair, and homework is not that bad (just copy the CSVistool pseudocode if you're lost).
lectures are so easy to understand, exams are super straightforward, if you study you will get an A.

The combo of Faulkner's lectures and HB's videos is great. I appreciate his understanding of the material and his ability to clearly explain the topics of the course. csvistool is an excellent resource. The beard has major aura.

Lectures weren't too helpful but attendance was not mandatory. Video lectures on Canvas from HB were amazing. A lot of resources to succeed. CS vistool is extremely helpful in learning concepts. Homeworks are a bit difficult, and you can lose a lot of points very quickly. TAs are hit or miss. Overall a great course that I learned a bunch in.
good prof, but i stopped showing up to lecture after maybe a month lol. i took 1332 hybrid and the class itself is def not a joke - it's been my worst cs class so far.

Faulkner does talk very fast, but he makes almost all 1332 concepts digestible. The class is actually pretty intuitive so as long as you can draw out or visualize everything, coding and answering questions should be fairly straightforward. Definitely recommend him, but HB's videos are also good as well.

Honestly I feel like most of these reviews are written by his TAs. He's a good lecturer and understands the material. But his handwriting is SO BAD. Entirely illegible if you want to review his notes. The exams also feel really shoddy and like they want to make hard questions just because they can
Best prof at tech, 100% recommend for 1332, lectures were great

The Best Professor at Georgia Tech. He is hilarious but this doesn't take away from the course content. He answeres the questions perfectly providing just enough information. His teaching style is immaculate, with the perfect mixture of allowing students to think themselves and guiding them to the solution. 
Professor Faulkner is the GOAT

Absolute GOAT, this class is beyond easy so I didn't learn much from lectures, but his notes are amazing and he clearly knows the topics. If this was my first introduction to data structures, I don't think I could've asked for a better professor. Homework doesn't take longer than 30 mins and tests are all super easy.

Faulkner is the GOAT. He answers questions well in class (even those that go beyond the scope of the class), and has very good lectures with time for in-class practice. I went to his class more than any other class and attendance wasn't even required
This man is the goat. Easy to understand class and funny at times. Will take his class again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Faulkner is great at using OneNote to draw pictures as he is explaining things that easily breaks down dense topics and makes them digestible. He is funny, tests are fair, and I highly recommend him for the fully in person lecture setup instead of the hybrid

The class was fairly straightforward. Faulkner is a good lecturer, and everything covered in class showed up on homeworks and exams. The Canvas was combined with virtual sections, so finding online resources was easy.

He is probably the best CS professor out there. I highly recommend taking him for 1332. He made the class look pretty easy. Attendance was not mandatory but I attended every single lecture (This is the first time I did that for any class so far). If you do the homework honestly, you will be fine with exams. I exempted the finals as well. Good Luck.
Great lecturer. Tests are fair and so is homework but homework can be very long and you kind of have to hope that other students write very in-depth test cases (or write your own obviously)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Faulkner was great. Obviously knows what he is doing and explains concepts very well. You must start the homework early, and do it completely unassisted besides office hours if you want to succeed in the class. Set up perfectly. Exams were fair, just study the previous ones posted in canvas. Great class, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Faulkner is a great lecturer. He is fast paced, but will circle back to answer questions if you have any. Advice for tests: check out the past forms provided on Canvas. I would advise starting the HW assignments early.

Awesome professor. He teaches everything you need to know and made this seemingly tough class into one of the classes I did the best in. The TAs are also awesome in helping you with any confusion. The module videos are also cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a legend. Prof. Faulkner is an excellent professor, and his lectures were top notch. I would highly recommend anyone taking CS1332 to attend his lectures

Professor Faulkner was a great professor. He taught the content very well, so I would attend lecture. Homeworks are often straightforward, but can be a lot of work. Exams are fair, especially since we have practice exams.  Overall, just do the work and enjoy your grade.
He may not have any emotions, but I feel for him. Frederic is an advanced specimen with interesting qualities
Not bad

Honestly is probably one of the best professors I have taken at tech. He always explained everything thoroughly and demonstrated how everything works. He also did a good job covering edge cases and explaining the time complexities of every operation/algorithm. Exams were fair as long as you do the homeworks and understand how each algorithm works.

Faulkner is by far the preferred choice for 1332. He shines best during his lectures as he explains every aspect of the course excellently, despite problems with legible handwriting. If you're gonna take 1332 I'd recommend you do it with Faulkner, he's newer than the other professor, but based on her online lectures I'd go with Faulkner.
Favorite CS professor thus far. This dude is so chill and nice. Literally have no complaints.

He is literally the best teacher I've encountered in the CS department so far. I didn't need a lot of extra resources to succeed in this course as his lectures very extremely helpful in making this class easy for me. He presents information in a clear and concise manner and covers most of the edge cases you require to understand.
He is a good professor, even though he can be boring at times. Better than all other 1332 professors. Exams are worth so much that if you mess up on one your grade is done for.

He was the best professor ever! He helped me understand the course material better, and as a result, I ended up getting an A in his class. I really like his teaching style, it was very inspirational. Additionally, this class has a very cool final exemption policy where you can have your final exam exempted if you achieve a test average above 94.

Not a good professor but better than HB. Talks very fast and does not make sure students understand. Course is not structured well and puts a lot of emphasis on memorization over understanding. Grading scheme is awful. Also, Faulkner does not answer emails, so don't expect to be able to get in touch with him outside of class.

Faulkner truly has a gift for lecturing. 

He's able to teach at a quick pace without glossing over important details. He's great at explaining the "Why?" part of material and is great at condensing information as well. He explains his reasoning very thoroughly in his notes, so you can learn the content well even if you didn't go to class.

I loved Faulkner's lectures! He explains concepts so clearly. If you pay attention to lecture, exams are extremely straightforward. He goes over plenty of examples and diagramming. Really can't recommend taking him enough!! My favorite professor at Tech so far.
One of the best CS professors I have ever had; explains every concept in a clear, understandable manner; gives the class a lot of materials to prepare for exams
I love this man. I've taken him for 2050, 1332, and will this summer for 3510, and I thank all the gods there may be that I'm going to be able to take him for that class.

Faulkner is a truly caring professor.  He always answers questions and ensures the content is accessible online for everyone and understandable.  He doesn't care about staying perfectly on track, he just wants you to learn.  The bad thing with that is he has to rush at the end of the semester, but otherwise he is the perfect professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Faulkner is amazing. He speaks very clearly and down-to-earth. The course itself is structured very well and Faulkner does a great job teaching the content. Would definitely recommend for any class he teaches!
Amazing professor! His lectures made the concepts easy to understand and were very engaging. Not a super difficult class if you stay caught up with material and take advantage of resources.
handwriting hard to identify, lectures at a fast pace, 15 weeks have 16 modules need to learn.

Truly a terrific professor. Extremely knowledgeable and caring. His lectures worth always worth attending, even if his handwriting was at times a bit illegible. This class is crucial for CS, and he does a great job making sure that you master concepts.

Pretty good and approachable lecturer who explains concepts very well, though he goes a little too fast that sometimes doesn't allow you to digest the content. Exams were very fair and TONS of resources (like past exams, practice worksheets, review sessions, office hours, etc.) were provided to help prepare. Solid choice for 1332 overall!

Data structures and algos wasn't my thing, so I barely squeaked by with a B. But make sure to attend lectures! Faulkner is a really good lecturer (maybe not handwriting tho), and will prepare you well to complete the homeworks.

Faulkner is an amazing lecturer. Overall great professor although his handwriting was hard to read. You can learn from HB's module videos but his lectures are way more concise and understandable. The TAs are great, and you just have to put in the effort to get an A. If you took 1331 asynchronous, you will be glad that 1332 tests are way more fair.

Professor Faulkner does provide a very solid quality lecture but at times it can be difficult to follow along because of his hand writing and talking pace. CS1332 itself is heavily based on exams and looking back in hindsight, all the exams were super fair but do put in the time to study everything and really learn all the coding homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor, CS 1332 is very test heavy, but Professor Faulkner does a stupendous job in ensuring his students get ample opportunities to thoroughly master Data Structures and Algorithms. Withstanding his handwriting, his socrative polls, examples, and pseudocode lectures in class are absolutely top-notch. AMAZING PROFESSOR!

One of the best lecturers on campus; he was so adept at explaining course material that it was worth going specifically to his lectures rather than the internet in order to learn course material. Only caveat to this course is their reliance on specific implementations of algorithms, meaning that if you learn off the internet, you may lose points.

Great lecturer that is passionate about what he is teaching. He goes through many examples in his lectures that are very useful for the exams. He is thorough in answering questions and if you attend all his lectures, you will be well prepared for this class's exams.

Minor cons are that he speaks pretty fast and has pretty bad handwriting.

Faulkner's lectures are very straightforward, easy to understand, and I personally thought he had the perfect pace to prevent students from getting bored. He is extremely knowledgeable and clearly knows what he's doing (unlike some professors at this school). Quite possibly the best CS professor I've had. WE LOVE YOU PROFESSOR FAULKNER

the goat. sometimes goes too fast, which makes sense given the amount of content in the course, but you can catch up using all the online resources. very well structured lectures and course, and hes a great guy overall

Knows what hes teaching and very knowledgable. Final exemption is also a big plus. Knew the material and taught it in a way where I didnt have to do any outside studying to understand it. Very good professor would def take again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was very good in lecture, you can easily understand what he is saying and you will truly understand the content just by showing up to lecture. He has a likable personality

absolutely fantastic! i was technically in the online section, but went to his lectures every day because it was the only way i could grasp the topics. he does plenty of examples, explains difficult topics in a way that makes them easier to comprehend, and knows how to link concepts together. this is my first A in a GT CS course because of him!
Explains concepts extremely well. Very friendly. Always maintains his composure.
Explains concepts extremely well. Very friendly. Always maintains composure.

There is a bountiful amount of tools, resources, and practice that is provided for this course. However, the resources and practice can be attributed to previous professors. This professor is great in that he is understanding towards his students and gave me strong advice when I wasn't sure if I could pass this course or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor and fantastic dude. Knows his stuff when it comes to course content and knows how to explain things extremely well. Always had a reasonable answer for everything and never lost his composure. Also no busy work. Tests were hard but fair and grading was lenient. Only nit-pick is his handwriting but aside from that he's the GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You're in great hands if you're taking his 1332 class! While the course is lecture-heavy, he teaches in a very clear and intuitive manner ensuring you actually learn the material in a logical way. While some complain about his handwriting, you can still follow and his teaching pace is manageable. Recitations help a lot too for one-on-one stuff.
The professor's lectures are very clear and easy to understand and the homework/tests are hard but fair.

The absolute GOAT. It was his first time teaching Discrete in a while I think, but he did a fantastic job and the lectures were very helpful. Pretty funny and nice guy too. In general the class is pretty easy though and his informative lectures definitely put you in good shape for the exams. Definitely recommend if you can take him.
Truly an amazing class and an amazing professor. Absolutely 0 complaints.

Professor is incredibly good at explaining things, even with his somewhat messy handwriting. Great lecturer, you never get bored during lectures. And incredibly helpful when you have any questions. Highly recommend this prof when he teaches 2050 again - he clearly knows what he's doing.

This class was pretty easy itself, but professor made is more simplified and explained content very well. His lectures are pretty worth it, but you don't necessarily have to go since the content mainly is on Zybooks (which you have to do as an assignment). Easy A, but he does have a preference for two-column table proofs which can get annoying.

Absolute god. He is such an amazing lecturer and person. He teaches so well and explained concepts so visually. The TA's provided us with so much material to prepare with. Definitely have to second the statement that he is the epitome of a civil servant. Absolutely loved the class (very helpful for the future btw) and loved the professor even more.
Goatner

Faulkner is a good lecturer. Makes concepts very easy to understand, but his handwriting isn't great. HB videos are on Canvas if you ever miss class. Tests are either "you'll have 30 minutes of free time" or "you won't finish the test", no in between. Homework is relatively straightforward and reality checks are free participation.

Talks way too fast and handwriting is borderline illegible. If you want someone slower, take HB. But, Faulkner is very knowledgeable. He's good at explaining things and knows what he's talking about. Exams are fine but not enough time at all. Ridiculous. HW's are fine as well.

Professor Faulkner's lectures are always clear, straightforward, and understandable. The only unclear thing is perhaps his handwriting. That's why you'd better go to his lectures, though now 1332 has online modules that cover all content of the course. An enjoyable and amazing professor.

Highly recommend, this professor was absoluetly amazing. Although the course content can be challenging at times, he throughly explained all of the different data structures and algorithms so that we were prepared for the exams. There's also plently of online resources to help as well, along with practice exams and worksheets.

Probably one of the best professors I've had. Very calm, lectures are great, and he's so good at explaining things. You're always engaged during lecture. Tests and homework were reasonable (though I do have to note that test 2 was quite brutal). Only problem is that he has bad handwriting on OneNote, but he's great overall.
Amazing dude with lectures that are very important, make sure you do the homework well cause it prepares you really well for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Faulkner is a good lecturer, but I don't really get the hype for him. Lectures are a bit mundane and his handwriting is borderline unintelligible. He teaches the topics very well though and is a very caring person. Tests aren't too difficult, but you are not given enough time. Def time yourself when you practice for exams. HW is boring but fine.

Professor Faulkner taught us MATLAB, what most CoE students need to know in the CS realm. Lectures were S tier (based off the legendary Prof. Kantwon) with a great balance of conceptual practice and helpful in-line comments. He also taught us WHY CS matters, with connections to every field of engineering. The tests are fair, but study >= 2 hrs.

Faulkner was a great professor for 1332. He covered everything you needed to know for tests and homeworks in lecture and he publishes lecture notes(albeit hard to read). Most material is shared between professors, including tests, so choose Faulkner for his lectures.
Loved him for CS 1371! Really great lecturer and funny, too. Definitely would recommend.
All the materials of CS1332 were online and attendance wasn't mandatory but I enjoy going to his lectures a lot. He's patient with questions and does his best to help you succeed.

FOR CS1371. Great professor! Easy to follow lectures, though he goes a little fast sometimes. Posts recordings and notes for each lecture. Material is fairly easy to grasp as long as you pay attention and do the homework. HW has extra credit!
Professor Faulkner has amazing lectures and makes the subject very interesting. He paces the class very well and seems to be one of the most inspiring and funny professors I've had.
Professor Faulkner is an excellent professor for DSA. Great lectures, enthusiastic and a good overall experience.
This man is the epitome of a civil servant.

Really great professor, funny and caring in class and has interesting and engaging lectures. I learned a ton in this class, and felt challenged at the right times, but grading was very fair and you could get a high grade if you tried.

I LOVED THIS CLASS
Faulkner is an amazing teacher. Very patient and caring about students. TAs wrote amazing notes that helped describe the class. Hopefully he teaches 4510 again so I can take it with him

Great guy, very smart and is good at teaching as well. TAs gave great notes. There was a ton of extra credit throughout the entire course, and they are extremely generous on grading all exams, with a very generous grading scheme as well. If you want to get an A in 3510, take Faulkner.

Easily one of the best profs I've taken at tech. The lecture notes one of the TAs wrote every class were really helpful in learning the concepts better and Faulkner is a great lecturer himself. He heavily emphasizes his exams on learning rather than nonsense memorization.

One of the best professors I've ever had. In the lectures after every lesson he teaches he constantly answers questions the class has and actively tries to clarify hard concepts so everyone understands. Gives a ton of extra credit opportunities too! Just study the homeworks and read the lecture notes and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Favorite prof in all my years of Tech. Normally in lectures, I always look at the clock to see when it's over, but his lectures are excellent. He has a nice weighting system on exams so they don't penalize your grade too hard and offers a good amount of extra credit. His handwriting is messy but he uploads detailed typed lecture notes afterward.

Prof Faulkner actually makes the material in 4510 extremely interesting. His style of teaching allows you to build intuition about stuff in step-by-step fashion. He answers students question with patience. I like how he provides practice problems during lecture as well.

He is hands down a superb professor. I think he should get a promotion/bonus!

One of the best lecturer's in my four years at Tech. Automata is a hard class but he does a great job at presenting the info in a clear way with just enough explanation to help students understand how concepts connect. He offers lots of small bonus opportunities, and he's nice about asking clarifying questions in class. Definitely take him!

Professor Faulkner was a fantastic professor who geniunely wanted his class to succeed. The two minor gripes I have with him is he tends to move fast and write a bit messy, but outside of that, he's an excellent explainer, and breaks down complex concepts exceptionally well. The dynamic programming unit was a highlight.

Professor Faulkner, despite being new, is clearly very experienced in and passionate for his field. The material was pretty difficult for me, especially near the end, but through attending lectures and office hours the homeworks and tests began to feel pretty easy and very fair. Lots of extra credit opportunity. Highly recommend his section.

Faulkner's 4510 was definitely a lot of work for me. I depended on weekly office hours and attended every lecture. However, that work paid off. At first I was a little lost, but with consistent effort and help, things clicked. I learned how to think and learn differently. Honestly, Faulkner restored my love of computer science.

I have taken many CS and MATH classes at GT. Faulkner is a new professor, but is easily one of the best lecturers I've had at GT. On top of that, his lecture notes are extremely in-depth and are enough to do well on his exams (along with the hwks) without even attending his lecture. He also dropped the lowest exam/final at the end of the year.

CS 4510 with him was my favorite class this semester! Faulkner's a great lecturer, who is entertaining and clear, and who was patient when repeating himself or even when answering my dumb questions. His grading is fair, and he gives tons of extra credit making the class easy and enjoyable, while still feeling like I've learned a lot. 11/10.

Frederic Faulkner is the goat in terms of automata and complexity understanding and communication. He's been an all-around delight to learn from. As someone who typically struggles with test-taking, professor Faulkner has made this class both challenging and insightful without breaking my spirits. You will be very lucky to have him as your prof.

Overall a good professor. He takes the time to explain things well and cares about students. His policy on exams and homeworks are also very fair. Personally I found the material in CS 4510 to be abstract and non-intuitive at times, but taking 4510 with Faulkner was the way to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures and notes have absolutely nothing to do with tests or homeworks. It's as if he's out to make students' lives as difficult as possible by not providing resources before homeworks and exams, not answering questions on Piazza, and being extremely inflexible on regrades. Avoid at all costs.
Explains concepts really well! Come to class and do the homework and you will get an A. Would take him again!

Hes a very new professor and already acts very entitled. Hes quite rude both inside and outside of the classroom. Be prepared to spend half of class trying to read whatever hes scribbling on the whiteboard and the other half wishing you had taken literally any other professor; quality of life in this class is worse than this guys handwriting.
Grading can be inconsistent

She is an excellent professor willing to be flexible on deadlines, and she gives well-constructed feedback to make students stronger writers. Outside of class, Dr. Fried is also very accessible. I couldn't recommend her enough if you have the opportunity to be a part of the class.

Dr. Fried is an awesome professor. She understands students are preoccupied with major specific classes and is flexible with deadlines as long as a student shows commitment in class and in other assignments.

Great professor, she actually cares that you understand the material and doesn't assign too much readings. Lectures could be a lot sometimes and the work can pile up fast if you aren't paying attention, not a free A but definitely achievable if you put in a bit of effort.

Overall, I would say Prof. Fried made lectures enjoyable and offered a lot of support for students even as a first-time professor at GT. I would pay close attention to the topic you want for ENGL1101 before choosing, but -- if you don't mind learning about the Victorians -- I would absolutely recommend taking Dr. Fried!!

Dr. Fried made English, a subject which I dreaded in high school, much more enjoyable. Empathized with students and focused on useful learning outcomes, rather than assigning endless amounts of readings. She is quite flexible with due dates, and gives plenty of chances for re-submissions on assignments.
Good enough teacher but do not take her if you want an easy A on the class

Her tests are lowkey tricky and not very easy to study for, but I wouldn't say I had a bad experience in this class. You have the same group all semester that you don't get to choose and unfortunately mine wasn't the best, but she's a fairly gracious grader. Participation is very necessary though, which is annoying
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Foundations of Strategy is a tough class in general. To her credit, professor fuller does a good job in incorporating real world events to the class. The exams are challenging, but she is always there to help. You do need to pay attention in class but really if you just show an interest in strategy in any way she will help you succeed in the class.

If you like being called on, this class is for you. She expects you to know the material from Connect homework due before class. Lectures follow the textbook closely, tests are tricky, and there's a group project that didn't make much sense in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This course is a capstone for strategy students and includes a team major project. Professor Fuller brings in some good discussion on articles about consulting. She also designed the course with some great guest speakers that talk about their varied career paths in strategy. The project is hypothetical but each team has an industry consultant.

This course is different than many bc it is based around a simulation. Dr. Fuller uses the class periods to discuss some of the key points of running the simulated firm though she really wants the students to dig in for ourselves to discover some of the key factors for success.

The course is centered on a pretty interesting simulation. Pick a good team and be sure you learn all the major decisions as you will need them for the mid-term exam (also a simulation). I learned a lot about the different parts of running a company.
I learned a lot

One of my favorite profs at Tech but definitely hit or miss for some people. Makes you work for your A but 2/3 of my class got As. Participate often with insightful comments and you're all set. Learned more from her class than I have in most other courses. Be ready for group projects and to be challenged but well worth it

If you have ever wanted to be randomly called on to answer questions in front of the entire class then Fuller is for you. The most frustrating part of the whole course is that she refuses to lecture any material and expects students to teach themselves content outside of class, while spending the hour and fifteen minute class cold calling students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be ready to be called on and get assignments that don't count right before she wants them for participation. The group projects aren't clear what she wants. She graded very harshly on them, but our group didn't really know what we were suppose to be doing. I made an A after the curve. She gave a curve because everyone did bad on the group project.

Dr. Fuller is a great professor to take Corporate Strategy with. You'll have to read case-studies and other readings before class, but it's super engaging and you'll definitely get value out of this course if you're an S&I Concentration.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr Fuller runs this simulation intensive course like she is a director in a holding company. Though she is available and seems interested in how the students are doing, she does not answer direct questions very often. Sometimes initially frustrating but I have to admit I learned a lot by digging it out with my teammate through the help provided.

Dr Fuller uses a textbook as the course core and brings in classroom discussions to make the material more engaging. I found the class fun to attend and feel like I learned a lot from the course. There is also a major group project and my team came together well and I enjoyed the project also. There are two tests which are mostly from the text.

If you speak up and don't have the exact answer she is looking for you'll be cut off and mildly ridiculed in front of the class. Dr. Fuller's lectures don't provide anything of value as she can't seem to handle ambiguity. Her participation scoring will tank your grade unless you dominate the discussions. Feedback you receive is vague and unusable.

the thing with a Business Strategy class is that there is rarely just one right answer, but Dr. Fuller is one of those professors where only her ideas are correct. Considering about 1/2 of your grade will come from a project and class discussions where you are proposing corporate strategy, good luck. her lectures are also incredibly boring.

Mixed feelings on Dr. Fuller. She is a nice person, but her lecture-heavy class is very boring. She expects you to read the textbook before class, and then her lectures offer nothing you haven't already read, but get ready for lots of cold-calls. Grade is determined by 2 tests and 1 long group project. Previously taught at California State.

5 tests is kind of insane but cheat sheets are allowed and easy to make. Doesn't take much prep to ace an exam. Forgiving attendance policy, lectures are fine, overall an easy lab science credit. I'd def recommend. I have no interest in this subject but some content in the class was actually pretty cool. A lot of credit comes from easy online work
Very understanding and reasonable professor. Fair exams; go to lecture and you'll do perfectly fine in class!

If you're looking for an easy lab science, this class is perfect. Homework is an easy 100, labs are graded fairly, and all tests (even optional final) are open note. If you're a student genuinely interested in astrobiology--Dr. Rivera-Hernandez is a great professor. She's very knowledgeable + willing to chat about the field/opportunities.

Some people just want to watch the world learn; Dr. Rivera-Hernandez had an amazing passion for the subject that was reflected in her lectures. Likewise, the class itself is easy: you get an almost unrestricted cheat sheet per exam, homework is short but informative, and you have to show up to only 12/27 lectures—I got a >100% grade in this class.

Genuinely the easiest 4 credit lab science at GT. Prof. Rivera allows a cheatsheet for every exam (which you can just copy the slides onto it) and the lab assignments are all busy work. I didn't pay attention to a single lecture (or show up to 3/4 of them) and easily got an A in the class.

Pretty easy class just take notes and put everything on your crib sheet and you will likely get a B or higher on each test (5). busy work on argos but really not that bad just takes 45min-hour each week to do it. labs arent too bad, just a lot and tedious if you are lazy like I am. mommy behavior during lecture and yells at you when you are talking

This class was honestly one of the most interesting and fun courses I've taken at GT, and its in no short reason due to Dr. Rivera-Hernandez. She cares a lot about the content she teaches and it shows. She also is very respectful to the students, plus she's a really lenient grader. I honestly don't see how anyone could not like her.

She possesses a level of contempt toward the students that far exceeds that of other professors, and it is unclear whether she realizes how visible it is. Her disciplinarian theatrics — including raising her voice when she has 'lost the floor' and giving students the 'evil eye' — are not typical of a Georgia Tech-caliber professor.

This is more so a complaint of the head lab TA, who creates incredibly time-consuming labs which are not graded for months, and then out of nowhere we get 5 weeks worth of lab graded released. There is no way to see where you stand.
The teacher has quite an attitude and even counts down from 3 to get our attention like we are kindergarteners.

Had to do participation via Canvas Quizzes protected by a password released in class. 1 crib sheet was allowed for each quiz, which could be tricky occasionally due to specific questions and computations. Study each lecture on the quiz. She's a good lecturer but labs were time-consuming and took 2-3 hours weekly, even when moving quickly

One of the best professors I've had. She is very excited about what she's teaching and the lectures are interesting. There are also no big exams, just many quizzes and they are really easy. The labs are kind of tough but if you just read the prelab and pay attention to the lectures then you'll do fine in both the lab and the quizzes.

There isn't very much content in the course, so the lectures are fairly slow-paced and repetitive. Prof Rivera-Hernandez is very knowledgeable in astrobiology and that is apparent in her lectures. The class is very easy as long as you pay attention to lecture and take some notes. However, the tests sometimes have material not covered in lecture.

She was an ok lecturer; usually moves very fast and it's hard to comprehend and process everything. Tests were open note but very harsh and difficult, and includes some questions that weren't really covered in lecture. Very inaccessible outside of class (and even in class, as lectures are on Zoom). Labs were pretty easy though.

She's the most annoying and most frustrating lecturer ever. In every sentence, she says the word "uh". She took literally 5 weeks to grade our Exam 2 when there were only 2 written questions on the exam. You'll get an A if she keeps the tests open note when she teaches in person. Lectures are just filled with so much information. Take EAS1600.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely would take Professor Gebraeel's class again. He is what a teacher should always bec because he is really tough on students but always makes them better. His material is exaclty what you would expect on a test! TAKE HIS CLASS!

I like Professor Gebraeel, but his teaching style is terrible. He reads off slides that he barely knows and gives you no practice or homework to learn except for an online "quiz" once a week. His bad teaching style doesn't matter that much because the slides have videos of a better prof explaining it on canvas. Class ends before thanksgiving tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think this professor teaches well. His rubrics rely on pop quizzes which can ruin your grade on a bad day. His lectures may seem like rambling and concepts aren't really clear but he will expect you to understand what he is saying regardless in case he brings up a pop quiz. Keep up with the classwork as I don't think it is that hard.

Dr. Gebraeel, is a great professor. He is effective in caring for his students and teaching effectively what you should know in class. Though I would say the hardest part of the class are the test which are questions from the professional engineering exam. I would say coming to class is good and going to recitation is really useful.

Not great overall. best way to approach the class was via excel but he never taught it. Video assignments didn't match in-class lectures/examples. Not great at explaining concepts and all tests/in-class quizzes were a mess. On every test he has to make clarifications/change the question in the middle of it. Online quizzes weekly but those are fine.

Professor goes over most obvious concepts in class. Online videos barely teach; they simply guide you through an example of a problem. Do not expect to learn from the slides (they suck).

Everyone flunked the final - guaranteeing Bs/Cs as final grade. Would be surprised if professor is available for next semester as I expect he is fired by then.

Doesn't teach the most effective way to do the course (spreadsheet) so lectures are useless. Doesn't proctor exams, just uses canvas (many people will use ChatGPT). Final exam wasn't multiple choice, wasn't from the same question bank as everything else, wasn't do-able with just the tables (though he said all would be true). 51% final avg.

Professor Nagi gave us weekly quizzes worth 50% of the grade with one midterm and final worth 25% each. Zero partial credit as they were multiple choice. On the final, he threw a curveball by asking for exact answers without specifying the significant figures. He didn't curve the final exam grade despite the mean score being 51%.

Nagi is one of the nicest, most passionate professors I've ever had. He is very lenient with grades and mostly cares that you understand the material. His stories are really funny and he has expressed his own struggles of getting Bs in college. The one complaint I do have is that there isn't much structure to the class- just try your best!

His syllabus was practically thrown away halfway in the class. His grading criteria was dismantled and he gave false promises of more quizzes etc up until the last two weeks of class. Horrible teacher. Does not captivate anyone's attention in class nor structures his class to reinforce material. Hard grader and doesn't outline his expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is very willing to help others, but he expects too much from you and almost expects you to learn it immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Understood a lot when I talked with Nagi but the problem is that the class is totally online.  I think it would be much more fun if he taught it as a regular class.  Furthermore, the online lectures are by different professors.

Pretty willing to work with students, however class is taught entirely online with lectures.  Lectures are not mandatory and there are only 4 tests per semester.  Fairly easy class, but be sure to take proper measures to study because if not it will definitely catch up with you.

20% DFW rate. Lectures lack any student engagement; he'd teach the same to a pile of rocks. Forces you to buy his own textbook. The grading structure is a GPA killer and will delay your graduation with impossible exams in formats you've never seen. HWs are so convoluted even the internet can't help. Avoid unless you have years of prior "intuition".

The professor has stuck-up attitude. Explains the material very quickly and does not share slides and forces students to buy his book. The book itself doesn't have any text, only equations and circuits.

Worst IC Design Teacher I have ever taken a class with. Stuck up. Go over concepts with classmates to understand them, the textbook is garbage. His textbooks are not written with an intent to explain the concept. Now that I understand the material, I could literally write his textbook better than him. Would give him a -5 rating if I could.

He's a legend in the world of IC design. He does not know how to teach though. Most of the classmates I know are lost in pretty much all the lectures. Get ready to self-teach the material. Neither his textbook, nor his slide book is explanatory. Do not take ECE 6445 alongside other hard classes!
Very passionate, love him.

He is definitely well respected in the industry, but not a very good lecturer. He does not post lecture slides online, conveniently forcing students to buy his book, which is just a collection of slides. His lectures go extremely quickly and the slide book is a mess of equations, circuits and charge with little to no explanation. Stuck-up attitude

Dr. Gabriel is really patient and kind. He conducts office hours every week to answer questions. This course is mainly about the theory that he proposes, so be careful because there isn't enough material for you to look up, so the best way to figure out questions is to ask him. He usually reply the email in time.

Dr. Rincon Mora is hands down the best IC design professor at Georgia Tech. He does have high expectations for his students and is NOT available outside of office hours. Overall if you are considering Electronic Design do consider taking this course. Be warned that he doesn't hesitate to hand out Cs if you're in the lower percentile of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: do want to take his course again

Took AI Foundations with Ghassan. As he did create this class, I think critiques here are valid. Content was a bad combination of overly tedious derivations and non-basic AI/ML models taught relatively poorly. The lectures were uninformative, homework/tests were super tedious (and not a good rep. of knowledge) but the studio was cool! Shoutout GTAs

Do you want to get overworked and feel like there is no tomorrow, take Ghassan's class. Do you want TA minions under this professor who will literally take marks off of your assignments that aren't apart of the assignment in the first place?, take Ghassan's class. I took both ECE 2026 Intro to Signal Processing and ECE 2806 AI First and it was bad.

Did well in the class but the Prof is  rude, scary, and egotistical. He is not there to support his students. He came, he did his lectures, and left. Additionally, according to the ta's he is horrible to the people in his lab and gets away with mistreating them. He brings huge amounts of money to Georgia Tech via research so he gets away with it
I respect this guy so much. Great professor. Cares about his students. Explains the topics very thoroughly and thoughtfully, unlike many other professors. He's funny too.

One of the nicest professors I've every met at Tech. Great guy, great professor. Couldn't ask for more out of a professor, since he actually cares about his student's wellbeing. Answers every question thoughtfully and with humility, no matter how dumb the question is. God knows I was the idiot of that class. He carried me through.

Has a good attitude. Puts good effort into lectures. I've seen some people ask very stupid questions but he is very patient and takes everyone seriously. I did not follow some lectures, but there is a good chance that I am dumb. I needed to read the textbook regularly to understand everything 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Lecture material is somewhat inflated and it can be difficult to locate the relevant main points. Mid-terms are garbage. Group project at the end which is ok. Otherwise a very nice guy, typically fine lecturing, but 1.5hr lectures will send you to sleep. Typically useful material to cover.

Professor Alregib is very caring. He cares about students well-being and loves questions. I never saw him treat any question as a stupid question. The reason I give him a 3 is because lectures became less and less clear after we finished the Fourier series. They were not amazingly insightful. Seems like a great guy, just not an amazing prof.
He changed my life.
Lack of dynamism and enthusiasm. Completely disappointed by this class.

You'll learn a lot from this class, but make sure you don't fall behind on the weekly homeworks and tutorials. Prof. Giarrusso is accessible outside of class and is good at explaining things one-on-one, but his lectures could be more engaging.

Tony is an amazing professor. The homework assignments take a while, but he wants you to reach out and ask for help if you need it and responds very quickly to emails. It is relatively easy to get an A in this class and there are lots of opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. Passionate about the subject. Generally a lot of homework (weekly assignments based on lecture, textbook reading) but nothing unmanageable. Lectures are helpful. Half the lectures for my section were optional based on if you submit homework early.

Very enjoyable class if you like the topic. Weekly homework based out of textbook. Follow the guidelines and project specifications and you will do well. Lots of extra credit opportunities. He is super accessible outside of class, especially via email. Go to class and he will be very helpful if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Good professor, just goes too fast and covers too much content in a short amount of time. Offers a great late policy so long as you keep up with it. Moves really fast and lectures aren't particularly helpful. Accessible for questions/concerns, but is a tough grader on projects and major assignments.

He was an alright professor but his teaching style focuses more on making you learn the fundamentals and even though it wasn't a 4 credit math course there is a lot to uncover for each unit. Keep up with lecture videos and definitely focus on practicing the study guide he gives because it is very similar to each exam. Do lots of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found his lectures difficult to follow, it seems to be a case of "knows what he's talking about, doesn't know how to teach it." He started posting his lectures (which are based heavily on the textbook) after the first exam, and the exams are based off practice problems that he posts the solutions to. Manageable class, and he's a nice guy.
good luck if you decide to take him. he was genuinely the worst teacher i've ever had in my entire life!!

He clearly knows what he's doing but does a terrible job explaining it. He reads the textbook and just does the problems on paper, not explaining how it works. Also has the heaviest accent so have fun trying to understand. Tests are standardized so feel free to sign up for him and go to someone else's lectures or just read the textbook yourself.

Although he does have an accent, it did not interfere with his teaching. He very obviously knew the material well and every concept was clear. Plenty of example problems during lecture. Combined with the studio, I had no complaints with Dr. Goldsztein.

Underrated, knowledgable, and funny guy. Lectures confusing and rambles, but he does teach you what you need to know with a lot of extra stuff. He deserves more credit as a prof. Jankowski's lecture videos are WAY more helpful though. Do the practice tests! They prep you for the tests and final. Take him if you don't get Jankowski. 1553 can be hard

Professor Goldsztein is honestly underrated, although I do see why some people couldn't really learn well from his lectures. I went to every single one of his lectures and did pretty decent in the class overall. Give him a chance before deciding to go to another professor's lectures or watching Jankowski's lectures. Also do the practice tests pls.

He makes class enjoyable but I do not think that I learned anything in class. Luckily Linear Algebra is not too hard and there are a ton of resources available to help you learn outside of class. Overall, all 1553 professors have the same tests and grading scales so it does not matter who you get as a professor as long as you can teach yourself.

DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE 1553. Had to stop going to this guys lectures because he did not explain concepts well at all. Seems like a good person, but his teaching ability needs work. Ended up just watching Jankowski's lectures which is what i would recommend if you have to take him. Also study your butt off for your exams, you absolutely need too.

Lectures were fine, but a little disorganized and confusing at points. I ended up skipping his classes and going to Jankowski's lectures after the first exam. He is a fun professor, but I recommend watching Jankowski's lectures instead.
Lectures were fun to sit through, but the content was sometimes unorganized. Still a great professor but I ended up watching Jankowski's lectures.
amazing at explaining things, I promise you'll do better if you not just go to class but PAY ATTENTION

I love him!... as a person. No but really, you can tell he cares about the content but his lectures confused me so much. I ended up going to class because I enjoyed him and his jokes,but i mainly watched other professors online. He goes through topics very quick and the lectures are not structured at all. class was fun, just not helpful sadly :(

Funny guy. Very funny guy. 

I wish he was as good at teaching as he is funny. 

Tbh all the linear profs are bad except for jankowski. I would take him again bc his classes were comedy sessions.

Ended up skipping class and watching Jankowski's old videos to learn. Went to his class for a comedy session. I'll certainly miss this man next semester bc of his hilarious lectures, but he's DEF not good at teaching. For example, he doesn't introduce the topic, just writes a paragraph, messing something up, sighs, and sounds fed up after.
Notes were not great, ended up just going to Simone's lectures
Goldsztein is a pretty funny guy if you attend his lectures. They aren't the most clear but with the other resources given to us, I feel like he was a decent enough teacher.

Hard to understand during lectures, to the point I stopped going to them altogether. Additionally, does not use the powerpoint notes posted to canvas, instead writing rewriting them all during the lecture (but the handwriting is difficult to read as well), so it was easier to just teach the material to myself. Also, tests extremely conceptual/hard.

His lectures are ok. I disagree with people saying they were awful, but I still didn't get much from all of them. Some were a bit scattered. My TA (Saksham Malik) hard carried me through this course via the studio. Go to a good TA's studio and the review sessions and you will be fine, don't even need the lecture tbh. Better choices, but not bad.
Very bad

Avoid at all costs. Made me feel I'm stupid but turned out he is just a shi**y professor. I gave up on his lectures and started watching old recorded lectures of another professor. Also, gets angry when you ask him respectfuly for something. Sends very weird emails that make you confused on the test.

I presented a problem to him that many students had after a test (in a respectful matter), and he emailed me very angrily claiming I was attacking professors and putting pressure on them. I just wanted to know if we could get partial credit for a problem. So I'm gathering that he is not very understanding or accommodating to students. Beware.

The only thing that I did was go to class and attend the studios and solve problems outside class, and it worked out fine for me. He has some accent when he speaks, but it was totally fine for me. He is a funny guy, and I love his personality. He answers questions enthusiastically during lecture and after lecture ended in the classroom.

Dr. Goldsztein was fine. Nice guy, I just didn't get a ton from the lectures. I learned mostly from studio and Dr. Jankowski's videos. This class was unified though, so it didn't really matter where you got it from.

Frankly, I stopped going to Dr. Goldsztein's lectures because I could not learn anything from him. He is reluctant to answer questions and not accessible outside of class. Linear algebra is already a hard class, and Dr. Goldsztein just made it harder. I ended up going to another prof's lectures. I would not recommend taking MATH 1553 with this prof

He seemed like a good guy and was amusing, but, though he understood the concepts, he had a tough time explaining the concepts of linear algebra, something where a good instructor is key. He also did not answer questions well, especially when students tried connecting them to other related 1553 topics. To succeed, I needed to rely on the textbook.

The textbook is your only friend, but is written badly and relies on you memorizing a bunch of seemingly arbitrary mathematical properties. The course is written poorly and this professor is pretty boring. The lectures are hard to follow from how slow he is. Thankfully, it's not a difficult course, just taught very poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly gives very mediocre lectures. I stopped going three weeks in because they weren't at all helpful. Very difficult to follow and didn't contribute anything more than the textbook itself, which is available online and a great resource, I highly recommend using it. Didn't answer any of my emails.

This class was awful. People with other professors did not suffer as much as we did. Dr. Goldstein is nice, but his teaching lacks a great deal of necessary information. I learned most of the information from the textbook and I know I would have failed without it. Practice tests are the saving grace.

goldsztein was funny but his lectures practically never finished the material and then you had to finish the lecture outside of class on your own. my grades drastically improved when i started going to jankowskis lectures instead. homework, textbook, and old exams were really useful
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He did a good job going through and explaining examples of how to do calculation-based problems but mostly neglected to explain conceptual ideas in detail. The class is formatted so that way all of 1553 have the same homework and exams due at the same time. Id say go to you TA or another lecturer if you need help understanding the material better.
Funny guy, but basically have to teach the class yourself.

His lectures are okay, but I wouldn't have passed the class without reading the textbook. He is genuinely very funny and sweet, but the course is really hard, and you might end up teaching yourself the material. He seems to cover everything during lectures, but once you read the textbook you realize how much he missed.

If you can, don't take Guillermo's class. Linear algebra is standardized so the tests and homework for all of the professors is the same, but his lectures are definitely worse than other professors to the point where showing up to class seemed unnecessary. If you take his class, expect to do a lot of self-teaching, but he's a nice guy.
Relaxed guy who liked to crack jokes every now and then. He covered the material well, giving adequate notes with examples. Has an accent but did not affect my learning.
Impossible to understand with thick accent, very slow too. Ended up skipping class and just reading the book. The class isn't a cakewalk, but moderately diligent studying will get you an A
A good professor. He wasnt amazing, but he prepared you for the exams and will answer any questions you have.

He did not explain his problem solving well nor did he answer conceptual questions well. He did not really care for the students. His thick accent was very hard to understand through the lecture videos at times.

GGold is such a cool teacher. He is a funny guy as well. He made lectures for the class to view on their own time and then would answer any questions we had in class. He would go above and beyond to fully explain and walk through any problems which was very helpful. He did have a thick accent but I actually enjoyed it.

Lectures are not the best but are okay if used as a supplement to reading the textbook. His accent is fairly strong but understandable. He is willing to go through homework questions during office hours, so take advantage of that. Overall a funny dude but due to the nature of the material, you probably have to study to get a good grade.

This class is a 2 credit course that ALL majors have to take. the GT math department has somehow managed to make THIS class the absolute hardest for no reason. The professor doesnt even make the quizzes or exams so lectures are completely irrelevant and useless. tests purposely ask you questions in twisted ways so you can only make a B OR C.

He has relatively average explanations that leave a lot of holes and questions even if you read the textbook (I read the textbook, was taking the khan academy course, and used Youtube as well). However, during office hours he is "willing to answer" questions. I cannot express how many times my questions were ignored or my intelligence was insulted.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very nice and funny guy, I feel like he *wants* to be a good lecturer but he just isnt. Sit up close cuz he talks to the board. Has a bit of an accent but you get used to it quickly. Will answer ANY questions very well during/after class so definitely ask them. Exams are very similar to the practice ones & the textbook+examples are VERY helpful.
Just another one of those classes where you have to learn the material yourself and you have no idea what's going on in the class.

Professor Goldsztein had a tendency of just covering stuff directly out the book, but that wasn't necessarily a bad thing. We never missed a topic or a major theorem and he was pretty good at explaining some of the more abstract concepts. Not to mention he liked to crack jokes. Just make sure you understand and do the homework to do well.

Nice professor that cares about his students, but has a tendency to just go and "run away" with his lectures. If you're not very comfortable with linear algebra, get ready to struggle. The textbook is going to be your friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he just reads out of the online textbook and explained things in the most abstract way possible.
