Recitation and YT videos are better teachers as I often left the class more confused than beforehand. only after the 1st exam i realized i didnt know anything. I never skip class out of principle but this class was the exception. quizzes are easy tho.

He is a funny person, but his lectures are confusing, especially after the eigenvalue chapter. What he writes on the board are exactly the same as what appears on the textbook, and he forgets to mention many important theorems during lectures. However, his quizzes are straightforward, and as long as you put in some work you should be fine.

Dr. Goldsztein is a great person and he is funny. However he does have a heavy accent which can make it difficult to understand him at times. He will answer any questions you have and he wants everyone to understand. As long as you pay attention in lecture and study a little bit you'll pass his class.

This is the guy you take if you want to get an A without having to work too hard. Skipped every lecture and got away without any issues. Exams are practically carbon copies of practice exams he provides.
Dr. Goldsztein is a great guy - he's funny and super chill, but his lectures are sometimes confusing. If you put in work, an A is achievable.

Really approachable. Lectures are confusing but just study the practice tests. Is really great about taking all questions, no matter how basic. Quiz every Friday which is annoying but he tells you what the quiz will cover so not difficult. Doesn't care if you sleep or text in lecture

When you're in class you have no clue what's going on, and it's pretty easy not to pay attention. But, this professor really cares about how his students do, and he is always willing to answer a question. The tests are super easy and the practice exams are basically what you should expect on the actual final. Easy A for most people.
His lectures are confusing sometimes and he has a hard time explaining the material, but the tests are easy and exactly like the practice exams. Good professor
Not much to say. He's not a professor I'm going to remember for ages. Never have I felt that he did not provide enough information, but at the same time he's no messiah if you're not good at math.

He's nice, and but he's not the best at explaining everything. He's happy to explain something multiple times, but it might not be any clearer than the first time. Tests mostly had basic questions, with only two or three hard ones (out of ten questions). This was Honors Calc II.
Loves his students, not the best at explaining and clarifying. Tests can be challenging but he will be fair.

After being behind due to a major change, I was able to catch up with his class. Has a bit of a heavy accent, but wants to make sure his students understand the material, which is always reassuring. Cool guy in general- pretty laid back and approachable.

It's very important to him that his students understand the material, which is more than I can say about most of the professors at Tech. Unfortunately, he's not the greatest at explaining things, so you may have to rely on the textbook or your TA a little.

He is a really nice guy. He actually cares about his students and asks for input. He is always willing to answer questions. He gives practice exams to help us study, which is similar to the tests. I recommend him to anyone that needs to take a course. He has an accent, but as long as you write what is on the board and go to recitation, it's fine.

He wasn't an amazing teacher, but if you asked for help he gladly gave it to you. His test varied on difficulty level depending on the material. The final was decent, but you had to know the material well. Overall it was a good class.

Goldsteinz is a rare breed at Tech. He actually cares about his students. Others may says hes hard to understand but thats only moderately true. He once gave my class an insane test and spent the rest of the semester giving us easier tests to make up for it. I wish all professors are like him. He is a great man. Take him if you get the chance.
No Comments

I had to drop his class midterm. He tries really hard, but he's so brilliant that explaining Calc 1 was hard for him. He even said in class, "I'm not a very good teacher." I don't recommend him for lower level math.

Gumbart is a really good professor. Great lectures and makes things very digestable for this class. Class is course coordinated but has good grading scheme, exact same as physics 1. Greco (CC) will also post what problems are relevant to exam just be sure to do as many practice problems as possible.

Great lecturer. responds to questions even in a massive lecture room. understands what he's doing. it's a common course so tests and syllabus are shared - not in his control. Take him for his lectures, imo hes the best physics prof.

Lectures weren't bad, and he explained everything very clearly. Very approachable. The class's syllabus was confusing at first, but once you get the hang of it, it's all good. Testing advice - don't leave the test questions blank EVER. If you write something (even if you're confused) you could still get points.

Gumbart is one of the clearest lecturers for physics I've ever had in my life. He makes all of the topics appear simple and walks through difficult problems methodically. Second test was weirdly hard but got curved. Labs are easy 100s, and you have options to do homework, previews and class attendance points. Generally easy and fruitful.

Physics 2 is hard, but he did a great job of covering what was needed to succeed on homework and tests. Kept class engaging with practice problems during lecture. Knowledgable when asked questions. Easy to understand.

Big distinction: Gumbart is NOT the course coordinator, who will be the source of most problems with this class.

From a lecturing standpoint, Gumbart gives great lectures and often uses entertaining real-world examples of Physics phenomena. He's got a great knowledge of the material, and he explains things clear enough that you'll understand.
He was pretty good. Struggled to answer questions in lecture sometimes. Overall, though, he stuck to what you needed to know rather than going into a lot of theoretical / conceptual stuff.

Best 2212 prof. His lectures are well-paced and helpful. He was also good at answering questions in lecture. Midterms are weighted based on score which is nice. Labs are free but time consuming. Lab TA's have been great, but I will say regrade requests can be annoying. Be warned: the tests can look very different from practice/old tests and hw.
Nice and kind and encouraging!
Nice person, encouraging
nice and approachable

This class is not easy - but Dr. Gumbart did his best to help us out. He's the most sane out of all of the Physics profs available, and actually teaches the material you'll need - instead of rambling about theory. His notes are clean and uploaded at the end of class, I don't think I realized how lucky I had it until I got done with his section.

Out of all of the PHYS 2212 professors, Gumbart seems to have the best lectures. He points out what is fluff in his slides and what is important for tests, which makes the class much easier. I would defiantly recommend him!

I did TERRIBLE in Physics I. Having Prof. Gumbart as my prof really gave me confidence that I could understand physics due to his clear explanations and walking carefully through every step. If you pay attention, Physics II is really not that daunting of a course with him as a professor.

Dr. Gumbart's lectures are pretty boring, and his explanations are not always the best. Go to lecture; his annotated lecture slides can get confusing otherwise. He's passionate about physics and his research. Exams are long, but fair. Two weekly homework assignments, labs are long, and there are lots of study/practice material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gumbart is kind, cares about his students, and presents the course content clearly and in an easy to understand fashion. The expectations for the course are very clearly laid out.

A bit of a boring guy at first, but he knows his stuff. Going to lecture is key to keeping up with the class. A lot of homework (2 probsets per week) but that's expected with phys. Exams are long, but fair. If you can get through his slightly monotone voice, he does great inclass demos, great example problems, and tries to keep class engaged.

Very clear and organized lectures, but there are still usually a few questions on the hw that are hard to get. These will either not show up on the test or he will go over them in class the next week. If you just take solid notes and understand all the examples in the powerpoints expect at least a B. Also plenty of EC.

He is a great professor and is always prepared with a powerpoint and tries pretty hard to keep the class interesting. Always has in-class demonstrations and stuff but his lectures do not help for the homework and the hw and lectures do not help for tests. Tests make up a majority of your grade so it sucks that nothing is connected.

Good teacher, but just good. Lectures are confusing at times and, in my opinion, not necessary. If you don't have any physics background it will likely be difficult to do well. There are many opportunities for extra credit though so it is not impossible to get a good grade.
Dr. G is a wonderful professor, she makes learning fun and interesting.

Dr G is literally the perfect professor. She makes lectures that cover something many people consider extremely boring into something fun using her dog, his love interest, and best friend as a big piece of the course. I was always interested in coming to class and she always found a way to make it entertaining. If you have the option, take her!
Very nice professor! Miles is great too!
The person complaining about her dog is so miserable lol. God forbid she try to make it entertaining. She's the kindest soul, take her.

JG was prob the best professor I've had at tech. She is very well versed in the material and structures the lectures in a way that makes the content relatable for students and easy to understand. She also values hard work and improvement throughout the semester, so if you're borderline between letter grades she's pretty reasonable. Take her!!

Very enthusiastic and fun! Has a great way of connecting course content with real life examples. But hard to get a hold of her, left my email unanswered for 3 days about retaking an exam. Gets side tracked ALOT, rushed at the end of the year. 3 tests and optional final + classwork + weekly videos.

She's amazing! Was worried about the pace since I took ES summer, but it was perfect! She goes over everything you need to succeed (She explains excel)! Very caring and funny professor, take her if you can!  Graded on attendance, 10 video assignments (easy), and 3 exams (not cumulative). You also get a crib sheet for each exam! dont skip & ur set!

This was the 2nd time I had Dr. G. Financial Modeling was super chill and honestly another very easy A. No exams, just 3-4 hw and 4 group case projects. Her lectures were following excel and sometimes gave a start to the cases. This is a good Finance elective if you need some balance in your schedule. She's awesome! Love Miles (her dog) as well :)

Wish I had another professor, because the class itself wasn't bad. She was. She never responded to emails (well written, professional, and polite emails). Even after telling me to email her after trying to better understand a concept in class. If I was a male athlete though.... I imagine it would have been a different story.

Prob 1 of the best profs I've taken at Tech. Very patient w/ students. She breaks down complicated finance concepts very well. As long as you're up to par with classwork, attendance, & do decent on exams, you'll be fine. Her exams are almost exactly like the practices. Her lectures are very useful for budgeting & financing you'll need in life.

Dr. G is the best! This is a excel heavy course where you just follow along with her during class. You can miss 3 classes without grade penalty. Tests are very easy if you review the study guide and practice test. She is always there to help if you are struggling. She legitimately cares about all of her students and wants you to see you succeed.

She is a very enthusiastic teacher she really loves what she is doing. attendance is mandatory (3 free skips with no consequence) there is a range of EC available (most 2.3% added to your total overall grade) EC is earned by participation, kahoots, and CIOS. the practice test are exactly the same as test and you can have an index card cheat sheet!

Take this class with her! She is so sweet and really does want students to succeed. She goes over topics in detail and promotes asking questions. Exams are very similar to the practice exams, and she gives lots of resources to prepare. Final is optional! Also, she uses lots of metaphors (her dog, sports) to make concepts easy to understand! 10/10!
Dr. G is very kind and I genuinely enjoyed attending her lectures. Loved seeing her dog, Miles, too!

the actual goat. class work makes up a lot of the grade and its super easy to get a 100 on. It would take  a lot to do poorly in this class. Dr G herself is an awesome professor who loves her dog and is big into sports, but she's knows finance thru and thru so she communicates it very well. Highly recommend
Loves athletes

Very informative lectures, exams are pretty much copies of the practice exams which is very helpful. She provides videos and practice files on each topic so that you can go back and review for exams as well. Very sweet, cares about your success but expects you to work hard to earn your grade.
Its awful to listen to her lectures, most of them are outdated. As of now I don't think I learned a single thing from her class but every week I have to dedicate 5-20 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is the most chill professor I've had at Tech so far. This is a super easy A. The practice tests are useful. There are 3 exams and a final worth 12.5% each, but you can exempt the final. She is a super cool person if you get to know her. Low time commitment. Know your excel for this class. Can earn up to 3 bonus pts on final grade.
Such an amazing professor. Classwork is super easy if you pay any attention, and the tests are copies of the class work. No reason not to succeed with her.

LOVE HER. Great lectures, engaging with students, nd makes learning finance not as difficult. Class is not mandatory but that's how you learn and you have to submit excel class work. Tests are VERY similar to practice tests and the homeworks give your grade a good cushion. TAKE HER.

Amazing and not difficult class. I learned a lot and it is pretty easy to make an A. Weekly homework assignments that did not take much time. Class is mandatory, but it is how you learn. Definity recommend this professor.

Everyone leaves her class understanding some aspect of personal finance. The course is graded based on homework (easy 100s as long as you pay attention in class), three tests and an optional final exam. She spends a lot of time making sure people understand the material, so take advantage of asking questions if you have any trouble.

Dr. G's number one prerogative is that you leave the class being more financially literate. She goes over things often, explains tough topics in easy-to-understand ways, and is always available for extra help if you need it. One of the funniest, kindest, and caring professors I've ever had. I would take her again in a heartbeat, she is fantastic.
The class content was pretty simple and easy but Dr. Garner made sure that students not only succeeded in the class but were financially literate in their real life.

Garner is amazing! She is a very good teacher and you will do great in her class as long as you pay attention. Her grading style is very forgiving. There were 3 tests throughout the semester. She wants everyone to get an A and will personally reach out to help you achieve this!
Dr. G is absolutely wonderful! She explains things so clearly and is full of creative analogies. She always makes me laugh and brings such great energy. I hope I can take her again soon!

Great lecturer and cares about everyone doing well. Solid balance of classwork, homework, and exams. If you have a lot of other hard classes and can't prioritize this one, focus on knowing how to do everything on the practice exams that she provides (extremely similar to real exams). Gain up to 3 extra points to your final grade thru extra credit.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Dr. G. She's a fantastic professor and the class is a breeze. As long as you pay decent attention, complete the assignments, and study the provided pre-exam materials, the class is super easy. One of the best courses in Scheller.

The eLectures are long.  There were several weeks where the lectures exceeded four hours.  You are given the templates and they are filled out in the lectures cell by cell.  If one watches the lectures, it is IMPOSSIBLE to not get an A.  The professor is amazing and knowledgeable, but in an effort to make grading easier the class is a breeze.
Dr. G is an amazing professor! She will make sure you understand the topic. Guides you through problems step-by-step. Recommend 100%

Dr. G is quite simply one of the best professors at Georgia Tech. She turns a course that could be super difficult into one that is interesting, engaging, and fun. Her exams are very similar to her practice ones and her classwork always applies to the real world. Hands down the best choice for any finance class at Tech.
There is a lot about nothing in this class. She is good with undergraduate classes probably. Would rather take someone else if you are in graduate school. Sometimes rude to students.

Simply the best. She's amazing at explaining the content and is willing to go over anything if someone doesn't understand. She's super kind and energetic, which makes early morning classes much more bearable. You should definitely take her if you have the opportunity.

Dr. G is one of the best professors I will ever have hands-down. She is a master of her field and is so good at walking you through finance step by step so you can see how all of the pieces tie together. Got a ton out of her class, you did it wrong if you went through GT without taking her!

Georgia Tech's best professor! Her lectures are excellent, and she makes it very clear what you must do in class in order to receive an A. She is always willing to help and gives respectful feedback. Participate in class!

Dr. Garner might be the best professor at Georgia Tech. Her lectures are very good, and she makes it very clear what you need to do in the class to get an A. She is always happy to answer any questions and is very accessible outside of class. Participation is important so make sure to attend class. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is a ray of sunshine, and really has a talent for breaking down content in an easy to understand way (and I hate math). Tests are very similar to homework and examples in class. She's always available for help. I highly recommend!

Professor Garner was very caring and sensitive to all the students. She turned an online summer class into an interesting one. The material was re-enforced so the tests weren't bad at all. I only wish I had her for a longer class!

Dr. G is AMAZING! I came into Finance thinking I would hate it and barely pass, and I got an A!! Her tests are just like the practice tests, the homework lets you try until you get it right, and she goes over everything until everyone understands. You can get a significant amount of extra credit for participating in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Just understand the Sharpe ratio and you'll be fine. If you know what that is and don't get an A then it's your fault. Not hers. Super easy class

I knew Dr. Garner was an incredible teacher but wasn't prepared for how much I would enjoy her class. She's one of those few professors that can make an 8:00 am enjoyable and is engaging in every lecture. The only compliant is she was slightly difficult to meet with outside of class. She makes it easy to succeed and interacts with each student!

Dr. Garner is one of the best professors in the business school. She cares, makes plenty of time in class to review concepts with several examples, and is easily accessible outside of class. Show up to class, pay attention in class, and **watch her videos**, and an A will fall into your lap. Chegg is super helpful for the homework. Take her class!

If you find a spot in her class, don't think twice about taking it. She only had a 9 AM section when I took it but she's a great prof and it's worth waking up to take her class. She manages to help the people struggling without losing pace of the course and I might not have been interested in finance if I didn't end up taking her.

Dr. Garner is an AMAZING professor and made this class by far the best one I have taken at Tech. Her teaching made learning the content seamless, as the mix of going over the content as a reasonable pace with her relevant/entertaining analogies makes retaining the info easy. Simply put, if you go to lectures you can easily get an A.

One of the best profs I've taken so far. So easy to follow and actually made me care about the class. She is also super nice and makes the class very straightforward. You definitely have to participate for credit but also makes that really easy to obtain because you will want to come to class and listen to her jokes lol they are always entertaining

Garner is BY FAR the best professor I've had during my entire time at Georgia Tech. She is incredibly kind and funny, and I've walked away from her class with a solid understanding of basic Finance concepts (I entered with zero experience in the field). She frequently checks for understanding and is very available outside of class. TAKE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is one of the best professors that I've taken at Tech. I didn't think that I would really enjoy finance, but she does a great job of explaining concepts in class and is very willing to take extra time and explain concepts outside of class. Overall I felt like I learned a lot and highly recommend Dr. Garner's class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Garner. She was extremely caring, and was always there to help her students. She was very clear as to what her expectations were and was't trying to trick you. If you do the homework and go to class then you should be fine. Also, she is extremely funny which I think made me actually enjoy the class.
Very helpful professor who genuinely cares about the students. Main piece of advice is that attendance (especially for participation grade) is pretty crucial.
Dr. Garg was a very good teacher! She gave a lot of chances for improvement and encouraged questions in class. Tests were sometimes a little bit of time crunch but doable with extra credit!

The lectures could be a little fast paced but as long as you watched the pre-lecture videos and ask her questions you would be fine. It's an easy course overall. The content are not deep and the extra credits are given very generously. Dr. Garg is also a really easy-going person and I could see her dedication to teaching.

Dr. Garg is super nice and caring for all of her students. Her lectures can be hard to follow and quite boring at time, but if you pay attention she gets the point across. The tests weigh a lot, but they are extremely easy and you will get a ton of partial credit if you just write random equations down. She also pretty much tells you whats on them.

Dr. Garg is not great at teaching, and she goes through material too fast; It is not uncommon to cover 2 chapters of material in one day.
BUT, she basically tells you exactly whats on each test (and exactly how to do the problems), and grading is so lenient that you could sneeze on the paper in the shape of a "Ka" and you'd still get half points.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Garg is super caring and one of the nicest people I know but the way this class is set up is an absolute travesty. It feels like she tripped over herself trying to teach at times and her lectures were very boring and all over the place. TAs running recitation saved the class however
Just do the work and you'll get an A. Everyone hates on her, but she really isn't that bad. Just show up for class for pop quizzes. I failed like every quiz but got an A+ so it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garg is probably one of the most caring professors I've come across at GT. You can tell that she really wants to see her students do well. She also gives us a ton of resources to help prep for the exams which I haven't seen a lot of other professors do. My only issue was the length of the exams and the number of spontaneous quizzes.

While it was clear that she is a kind professor and wants students to succeed, her methods for the class were frustrating and while she says that she's open to feedback, that doesn't seem to be the case. Regular pop quizzes in class were frustrating, tests were long, and she constantly reiterates to figure things out at home instead of in class.

Has a bad attitude when students ask questions during class. Lots of pop quizzes and almost everyone fails them and she doesn't care. She refuses to record lecture too. All she does is read off of the lecture slides, so I have to teach myself everything from the textbook. The class is so disjointed from the lab
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her tests are long and they always felt rushed when taking them. Her class is mandatory, she has pop quizzes semi often for attendance, but they are actually graded on accuracy. When she lectures she just reads off the slides, and often times is confused by her own work.  If you don't understand the material in lecture, you aren't going to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my best professors, thus far. Dr. Garg demonstrates a great deal of care for her students' success, and she is extremely personable.

Her exams are so long and she doesn't take feedback well, even when there are real issues. She kind of talks at you during lecture, and has pop quizzes as her attendance. She isn't a great professor and often turns issues around back on students. Skipping lecture could mean you miss a lot of content, and there's a lot of reading to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Garg is incredibly sweet, and it's clear that she cares about her students and their well-being. The only nit-pick I have for her is that she makes attendance semi-mandatory by having unannounced, spontaneous quizzes during some lectures.

Dr. Garg's not super clear during lectures and success in the course relied on your ability to learn the materials elsewhere, her tests were mostly predictable but exams were EXTREMELY long. She even acknowledged this, and did not make them any shorter. This was disappointing because silly mistakes from rushing at the end cost me a letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 50/50 syllabus midterm and final. Canvas page is incredibly disorganized with incomplete practice problems and typos. Lecture notes are incomplete so the textbook is how you learn. Offset by the fact that the tests are largely pretty easy, but the syllabus makes them incredibly scary and getting an A requires preparing for every possible edge case

50% midterm and 50% final was the grading scheme, with the midterm across two lectures so you had to stress about it for almost the entire week. Lectures weren't well taught. Provided homework sets didn't cover content and were incomplete.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatzell is literally one of the best professors I have had at GT. Even though I had her for a VIP, she was very caring and gave a lot of feedback for our group work. I am excited to keep working with her PhD students in her lab.

Her lectures were extremely unclear because she kept making mistakes. She would have to correct the equations she had on the board 3 times before putting the right thing up. This happened with most of the problems she solved. The only reason she has a high rating is because she is an easy grader. She is a terrible lecturer.

Thermodynamics can be hard, but Dr. Hatzell does a good job just teaching you the basics of it. As long as you pay attention in class and spend some time outside of it reading the textbook an A is definitely possible. Biggest complaint is the lack of useful examples in class. This caused some confusion when the material got harder towards the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Hatzell does a good job of explaining her content during lectures and answers all questions posed to her. Although, she was very strict on the in-person attendance, so during the last third of the semester she stopped uploading the live lectures (for replay) to BlueJeans. Additionally, she is hard to get in contact with outside the classroom.

Dr. Hatzell is a great professor to take during COVID times. She started giving weekly quizzes instead of tests, most of which were open note in some form, and she dropped the 3 lowest quizzes. She isn't the best teacher but definitely very understanding and easy. She runs a flipped class tho, and the prerecorded videos can get very long.

Probably the easiest Thermodynamics professor at Tech. Getting an A is hard as she does not curve but anyone in the top 50 percent is guaranteed a B. The test problems are usually similar to her practice problems so MCQ's usually make the difference between an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatzell is a good choice for Thermodynamics at GT. Lectures were based upon the chapters in the book, and she hands out note packets for each section. Homework was time consuming, but Dr. Hatzell's office hours were a good resource. Tests were preceded by reviews and were based on the homework content, but were easier than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Solid professor overall. She definitely seemed to accelerate the pace of the class as it went on so definitely try to stay ahead. Her tests are fair and mostly reflect slightly easier versions of HW questions. Multiple times, we had HW questions that werent possible without computer programs. Be sure to notify her if this is the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She was super enthusiastic throughout the whole semester. You can tell she really enjoys teaching to the new generation. The homework took a long time for me to complete (6+ hours) and had it due about once a week. Tests were fair and weren't a blindside based on the lecture material. Also very kind and approachable for questions after class.

Hatzell is a good professor overall, I enjoyed my experience taking Thermo. I think the subject itself can be difficult but she does a good job breaking it down for students. She clearly cares a lot about the subject and has a good understanding, but sometimes struggles to get the more difficult concepts across. Homework is 25% and 3 tests also 25%

I took 1211K with him, and it was genuinely such a breeze. His lectures are really easy to follow along with, and there's so much practice he provides that it's kind of impossible not to pass his class. He's the BEST professor I've had so far and makes chemistry so simple. Take him!

Dr. Huynh is one of the most caring professors you will ever have the pleasure of meeting. CHEM 1310 is a hard course, but by attending lecture and doing the work, you will do very well. He is very accessible outside of class and he is truly a fantastic teacher. He is the type of teacher that will break down tough concepts to make them easier.

Mioy is a beyond amazing professor, and I would 100% retake his class just to see him. He's very clear, concise, and knows what he's talking about. He's also a very nice person to talk to about any issue you have. You'll probably see him drop by your lab and help you (even if it's at 8:00 a.m., like mine was).
Very very good at lecturing, and grading policy is fair. Mioy is an absolutely fantastic chemistry teacher and made sure that all students had ample resources outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class after 2 and a half years without taking chemistry. To be honest it wasn't super easy but he is an amazing prof. who you can tell not only cares about the students learning the material, but he also is really interested in what he teaches. The lab component can be annoying but he doesn't do that. Absolutely take his class if you can.
He made chem really easy to understand. Amazing lectures!

This guy is the absolute goat. His lectures were usually put in a very intuitive and direct way where what you see is what you get. Everything that is on the exams is explained somewhere in the lectures, so as long as you go to them, you'll be fine. The class definitely gets harder as it progresses, but as long as you stay locked you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Huynh was excellent at explaining the concepts and his lectures weren't boring. He supplied skeletal notes for each chapter that he filled in throughout the lectures, making it easy to take notes. Homeworks weren't too hard, but the lab reports were sometimes long.

All the chem professors use the same slides, teach the same content, and give the same exams/homeworks but Dr. Huynh was still a good lecturer. The class moves by really fast but as long as you keep up and utilize ALL the practice materials (homeworks, mini review quizzes, practive exams, etc.) before the exams, you'll be fine. 3 exams and 1 final.

Professor Huynh is the goat. His lectures are great and he explains chem concepts really well. As long as you go to class and do the work, the tests are easy and the class is an easy A. He's very nice and funny and super accessible outside of class. Chem lab on the other hand will suck the life out of you, but there's nothing he can do about that.

Chem 1310 is decently hard (and really, really not my thing) but he made this class no harder than it needs to be. His lectures were super clear and on-point. Exams were only 52% of the grade too! His unanimous 5 star ratings speak for themselves.

Professor Huynh's greatest strength is his ability to simplify the most advanced concepts in the course while still teaching exactly what you need to know for exams. Even though attendance is not mandatory, I would strongly recommend going to his lectures, as consistently going to class was my and many of my peers' only resource for getting an A.

Professor Huynh is great and despite lectures sometimes being rapid paced, the content is pretty simple and easy to follow. He is also very caring and genuinely wants to see you succeed in this class. Highly recommend!

Chemistry has always been a subject I've struggled with, but he explains everything in such a digestible way. He is also incredibly caring- even though my lecture section had around 300 people, he still emailed each of us to give personal feedback after exams. The course did require a fair amount of studying (at least for me) but I def recommend!

I went to his office hours 3x per week and got to know him, he's an amazing professor and know's HOW TO EXPLAIN SIMPLY!!! I was actually happy to get up a 9am and go to his lectures as they weren't rushed, and were a great start to my morning.

The other lecturers are good but Mioy Huynh is by far my favorite and such an amazing intro to college.
Good proffessor got A's on all the midterms except the second because I stopped going to lecture. Just attend lecture have a good crib sheet and youll be fine he really cares for his students
Amazing Prof and person. Highly reccommend for chem. Sets you up very well for success. Just go to lecture and he'll take care of the rest.

Good teacher, easy to understand, and the skeletal notes for the class are very helpful to go along with lectures. I would definitely take Mioy over Anh Le because the times I've seen her when she proctors the exams she is very hard to understand and speaks very fast. Just to give you the heads up, the lab section that's linked to this class sucks.
So goated at teaching chem do all the practice tests cop an A

Came into this class with very little experience with chem and was scared to take. However, the lecture notes are great, has a ton of practice problems, and has prerecorded videos on solving problems. Also you get a ton of practice exams (in addition to a ton of practice problems). A lot of material covered, but cribsheets are allowed.

Dr. Huynh is an excellent lecturer who really cares about the class. Assignments and labs make up nearly half of your final grade, and it is very doable to get full credit on them. Exams allow cribsheets and are very doable. The final can replace midterms. The canvas course is incredibly organized and plenty of resources are available for studying.
Exams are pretty tough but fair and honestly a great professor who has a lot of passion for the subject and his students

Amazing professor, you can really tell that he cares about the students and developing a foundational understanding within everyone. The tests are fair, and he also puts an extraordinary amount of effort into test prep and lecture notes. Most caring and best professor I've had at tech
Cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. I am so bad at chemistry but he made the class interesting and easier to understand.

Very good lecture and professor; very easy to learn in this class. class participation and lab sections can be some work, but helps the overall grade in the class greatly. the final can replace all of the exams, so if you mess up on the exams, it is not a big deal. easy A if you pay attention and do the work!
By far one of the best professors I have ever had, made chem a breeze

Great lecturer who explains concepts clearly and does lots of practice problems in class. Incredibly well organized canvas page that makes finding information and resources easy. Plenty of practice for exams as well.

I had him for 1211K, he has been one of my favorite professors at Georgia Tech. He makes it extremely easy to understand what is going on in lecture, and it probably helped that he taught a relatively small lecture, but he provided so many opportunities for students to learn. Absolutely loved him.
I hate chemistry but this guy made it so easy. Lectures were super clear and I was always prepared well for lab and exams.
Mioy was a great lecturer and clearly explained all concepts. The exams are similar to practice tests, so as long as you complete them, you should be okay.

Best CHEM1310 teacher there is. Take him! 
He teaches the class very well and takes time to focus on harder concepts to make sure everyone understands the concepts. There are plenty of practice and review sources for exams. The mini review quizzes and practice exams are similar format of that to the real exam.

Great professor for a class most people are taking to fulfil a requirement! The homework is a little annoying: lots of small assignments due throughout the week; the class is set up to allow you to succeed. He holds office hours regularly & expands during midterm and final weeks. Example problems online for almost all the concepts covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mioy is by far the best professor for CHEM 1310! He is incredibly kind and available outside of class. His notes and lectures are extremely informative and made some of the complex topics in chem very understandable. For exams make sure to use the canvas example exams as they are the best resource to prepare for exams. I strongly suggest taking him
Heavily weighted on attending lecture---so be there!!! Great otherwise

1310 is structured weirdly here and covers A LOT of material but he helped make it easier to understand. He has videos that cover example problems which help a lot. Lectures do move very fast and you can fall behind very quickly but I blame it on the structure of 1310 not him. Read the textbook before lectures as they kind of build on each other.
The course moves fast and covers a lot of content, but Dr. Huynh made it accessible and digestible

He really wanted everyone to succeed and was always available to meet. Lectures aren't mandatory, but the slides won't be posted online. There is a textbook to use, but not required to read it. Overall, a great professor and would 100% recommend him for this class.

Chemistry is one of the hardest classes to take as a freshman at GT; however, Mioy made it so much easier. He is very kind and genuinely cares for this students. For instance, after each exam he send a personalized messaged to each student depending on how well they did. He is very approachable and has many office hours.

Dr. Mioy is an incredible professor. Lectures move fast (because of course structure of 1310) but he provides a ton of his own recorded videos and outside resources which makes it managable. Really good professor who so clearly cares about his students and incorporates their feedback and notes into his teaching.

Great professor, would definitely take again. A lot of small assignments due throughout the week, but it's manageable. Lectures are easy to follow, but if you don't like them all of the info is in the online textbook.

Great lecturer who made an otherwise very chaotic class fairly straightforward. Posted lots of extra helpful resources and was always easily accessible. There are a lot of things I'd like to see changed about chem1310, but Mioy did a phenomenal job with what he was given to work with

Very good at teaching chem and explains the topics in a comprehendible way. Lots of practice available for tests. Midterms are somewhat straight forward; they like to integrate math/concepts together but are similar to past exams. He has a lot of office hours online and in person for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caring and respectful professor, definitely one of my favorite lecturers from this semester. He is great at explaining concepts and you can always go to his office hours if you need assistance. Lots of homework but I don't think he is in control of that. Great communicator and professor overall.

I had Dr. Huynh at 8:25 am this semester, and the class was great. I went to office hours occasionally, and he is a fantastic teacher who makes chemistry easy to understand, even for some of the most challenging topics. The lectures are beneficial, and honestly, if you make the cribsheets you get access to on tests well, it is an easy A.

He was a very good lecturer. He clearly explained concepts, and made sure everyone understood before moving on. The format of the class in general was not the best, but that was not determined by Mioy Huynh. The in class assignments were skipped sometimes, but he would always give you a ballpark answer to allow you to answer it at another time.

One of the professors that care the most about lecturing I have met in my years at GT. Lectures were good and concepts are doable. There are quite a few issues with the format of the class, but too bad. Too many assignments

Great professor. Did not overcomplicate material, but explained concepts simply and effectively. Communicated clearly what was expected of us on tests, and gave us a lot of resources (pre-lecture videos, plenty of office hours). Course had a lot of small assignments due throughout the week, which I was not a fan of, but the teaching was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A friend recommended I take Mioy's chem and I see why. He used to teach at Yale and did work at other good schools. His notes he posts online are really good, the website is very organized, his lectures are very easy to follow. I actually had to take 1211k for Mioy instead of 1310 but it didn't matter for my degree and it was a good decision.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: An amazing professor who kept me engaged with a topic that isn't necessarily my favorite. He was helpful outside of class and was very kind. While attendance is not mandatory, attending makes it easier to get extra homework credit and know what to write down on exam crib sheets.

AMAZING!!! His lectures were so good. I came into this course with essentially no prior chem knowledge and he did a phenomenal job of making everything make so much sense. For the exams, take advantage of the practice exams posted on Canvas, they're a great representation of what the exam is like. Beware of timing too! This class was great!

Dr. Huynh is a great lecturer and really tries to explain problems in a way that everyone can understand. 1310 is a tough class but he really tries to lead students through it. He hade tons of extra time for additional office hours each week so that if normally scheduled ones didn't work, there was often a pop-in time or online session offered.

Easy class, good professor. Didn't go to class for the last three months and still got an A reading the textbooks. Just make a few friends to study with and do the assignments together and you'll be fine.

In my opinion, Unit 1 was very easy. It was completely memorization/could be learned using flashcards. However, Unit 2 was extremely difficult as it was very application heavy. The literature project/group project grading was harsh Class was overall difficult. Would recommend taking another professor if that's an option.
the worst class i've ever taken, she genuinely made me rethink being a neuroscience major major.

Exams were difficult unless you had every little thing from the unit (and the units before) memorized (crib sheet available). Lectures weren't really helpful until the last week where she offered bonus points, so self-taught was the way to go. Her TAs are extremely harsh graders on every project assignment we had. Homework/Reading was easy.
Just honestly very bad.

This class made me rethink neuro. Absolutely everything is accuracy based and nothing to help buffer the exams which are really difficult compared to lectures. Dislike how much of this class is based on scientific literature projects because many groups were getting barely passing or failing grades on these projects and its worth 25% of our grade.

I'm confused by the positive ratings so I'm convinced that she's writing positive reviews. She is a yeller so beware of that. Also, exams are extremely hard. I was fortunate to already have a background in cellular and molecular neuroscience but I was basically self-teaching the material from the slides as well. Just be aware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great content and professor. My favorite neuroscience class so far.

I don't understand why there's so many good ratings. Bad lecturer and tests are very hard. The grading is harsh and you can't afford to do bad on any assignments. Her slides are disorganized, but they have all the info you need, so my advice to do well is to just teach yourself everything. Her explanations only make the material more confusing.

tests are pretty hard. she's really nice outside of class and will offer help but in class she zooms through the material and i found it helpful to just take notes on her slides. her slides cover everything you need to know so you dont really need to go to class except on the days that it matters.

Dr. Steele isn't the best lecturer, but her slides are very clear, and the exams are hard but fair (she does not expect you to know anything that isn't on her slides). She's also extremely accessible outside of class and is very helpful in office hours! Attendance isn't a grade but there are activities that count toward your grade on specific days.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class hard but she goated, take her

Kind of funny to see all these high ratings- did we take the same class as you last semester? Maybe she's on her rating herself high to try to save herself? Either way something's up because this class was taught horribly

Definitely one of my favorite classes I've taken at tech. There is a lot of content but it's really interesting and the tests are pretty fair. Dr. Steele isn't the best lecturer but everything you need to know are on her slides and she's very sweet and accessible outside of class. There is also a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Steele is an excellent teacher. The powerpoint slides are written well and cover all the material needed to succeed in the course. The tests are fair and align with the content from the lectures. Dr. Steele also provides plenty of resources to help students succeed and is always willing to offer help. Overall, it's a very interesting class.

Painfully monotone and rushed lectures with zero effort to teach. Slides were often wrong and contradicted what was expected on exams. Tests didn't reflect class content at all, and low averages were ignored. Clearly did not care about student learning or grades. Genuinely poured everything into this class and felt no payoff. Avoid at ALL costs.

Dr Steele is a great professor. She cares a lot about her students and always makes time for them outside of class, even though she's super busy. Her slides and class structure is so organised, genuinely one of the most I've seen. Would take again.
Great teacher. Puts all the resources for students to succeed. If you need help, she is always available and is very helpful. One of my favorite classes at Georgia Tech.

Dr. Steele is a great professor, and I enjoyed the content in this class. She is very clear about what is expected to succeed. While the tests are challenging, they are very fair and based directly on lecture material. The class is content heavy but if you stay engaged and keep up with the material, it is very manageable.

Dr. Steele is kind, approachable, and genuinely cares about her students, especially if you show effort. This was my favorite neuro class I've taken by far. It's definitely challenging, but if you keep up with lectures, study with others, and use the practice quizzes, you'll be fine. Make sure to put in extra time during exam weeks and go to OH.

The class was hard but Professor Steele was great. Super caring about her students, quickly to reply to emails, frequent office hours, etc. if you attend lecture consistently and study the nuances in her material, you'll do well in the course. Would one hundred percent take a course with Professor Steele again!

Genuinely the worst teacher I've ever had in my life. If you are planning to take this class in the spring, please drop it and take it later because she wakes up in the morning with the intent to make every single person in her class's lives miserable.

i have never taken a worse class in my life. haley, if you are reading this, i hope that karma comes back to bite you because you truly made this class unbearable. please quit your job instead of making pre-med students' lives a living hell.
I would rather walk into oncoming traffic than take this class again.

if you wanna know what it feels like to be absolutely screwed over by a professor who genuinely does not want you to succeed, then take this class. her test averages were 70s and lecture slides (which are the primary resources for tests) are completely unorganized. she is a prime example of someone who should quit teaching and stick to research.

I honestly don't understand how this class is allowed to run in its current form. The workload is completely unreasonable and feels like three classes crammed into one. The lectures are huge info dumps with way too much detail and no prioritization. Test averages are around 70, and instead of showing concern, she seems proud of it.

Consistently incorrect information on the slides. She also tells us wrong information when you ask her in office hours that both contradicts her slides AND contradicts what the actual answer is.  Reprehensible teaching honestly wouldn't be surprised if this was some sort of experiment to see how students respond to adversity.

I'm actually a member of the faculty here, and I'm writing this to advise students reading this to not take this professor. I've heard her behind closed doors say that her class is one "talented students should fail." Reprehensible thing to admit. She has an odd pride about failing students, and I hope they can work on getting someone better.

Has a VERY clear grading structure with leeway for missing assignments and lectures. Her tests are definitely meticulous, but it's all in her slides, and practice exams are accurate. She had some engaging activities to help remember things, but I did well because I dedicated a solid amount of time to studying. Harsher grader for the group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: bro the test are so cooked

Wow. If the Neuro department at GT has an ounce of integrity left she will not be teaching after this next semester because I know that after this next round of CIOS reviews, she'll be investigated. She graded every assignment insanely harsh, and the tests were nearly impossible to do well on. Maybe she has personal problems. Avoid at ALL costs
who wouldve thought she could somehow make 3001 the hardest class ever. Please I am warning you: save yourself. She is the spawn of satan

If you're a fellow neuro major, I am sorry if you have to take this class with her. Both exam averages were Cs, even the "easy" assignments are graded harshly, she rushes through every lecture, and the exams are actually IMPOSSIBLE. Any good review under Steele has to be her on burner accounts because this class genuinely made me hate my major.

I made an A easily in both NEUR 2001 and NEUR 3003. With this class I'll be lucky to get a B. It's unlike any class I've ever had in that the teacher really does not want you to do well. I truly believe the good reviews on here are just her on burner accounts. Maybe she's a great researcher but she shouldn't be teaching at all... at any school.

When we received our fist tests the class average was in the low 70s, and instead of addressing any sort of problem she said she was "very happy" with how they went. Honestly just tells you everything about her right there. She wants students to fail and 100% has a vendetta against undergraduates. Literally avoid at all costs you will not do well.

You need to actively pay attention to not get lost in lectures, but that's because the content is very detail-oriented. She definitely knows what she's talking about and is always helpful if you have questions.The exams are pretty hard and super specific. You definitely need to study thoroughly but the rest of the assignments are easy.

There are 2 midterms (15% each) and a final (25%). There is a group project (10%), and the rest of the points are checkpoint quizzes, Perusall, and participation. Lectures are slightly monotone, but she is clear with exam topics (no surprises). This is a 3000 course, so you should expect to be able to synthesize knowledge and interpret figures.
She is horrible. Period. Horrible lecturer, tests are unbelievably hard. Do not take her, don't even think about it .

Class was manageable because she taught 1/3, any more of her and it would have been diabolical. Never been her biggest fan and never will be. Grade deflation on tests and quizzes (avg ~70 and never curves), not a great public speaker, not approachable or caring. She is like this with every class she teaches but hey at least she is consistent.

One of the worst in the Neuro dept only second to holder. Condescending whenever asked a question extremely monotone and boring to listen to. Makes courses way harder than they need to be, save yourself the trouble and take Reagan
Avoid at all costs. Tons of busy work, bad lectures, and poorly written test questions.

Dr. Steele was the Unit 1 professor of NEUR 3002 during Spring 2025. Her tests mirrored the powerpoints, but the questions were applicational and stimulus-based because the tests are open note. However, the quiz was very difficult because we were still getting use to those types of questions.  The group project was decent, and she is accessible.

I agree with the comment about Unit 2 feeling unrelated. This professor can sometimes show unprofessional behavior toward students, so you should hope you're on her good side. Her slides are helpful, but the tests are exceedingly difficult. She's okay, but I'd suggest choosing a different professor for 3001. Her 2001 and 4803 courses are better

Prof Steele makes her tests exceptionally hard for no reason. She tests you on minute details and most questions are "trick" questions. Test averages are low and she does not seem to care. She constantly gets concepts wrong in class and has to backtrack and correct herself, making an already complex subject even more confusing.

Dr. Steele is objectively an all right teacher. It is extremely lecture heavy and there is usually no stopping for the entirety of the one hour and fifteen minute lectures. Did not help that it was 8 am either so I'm left learning 300 slides of content all over again a week before the test. She is very accessible for extra help though.

Dr. Steele made my summer semester amazing. She had amazing lectures, great feedback, and was very accessible after class. She made the class fun and the things we learned were very helpful for my classes the next semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is the second time I have taken a class with her, and she doesn't get any better. Her lectures are information heavy, homework doesn't align with class content, and in class activities meant for kindergartners. Despite this, the second unit test in no way aligned with the actual unit because she has a bias in learning her research.
Dr Steele does not teach well. Take Ragan, who is a much better teacher. Steele does not explain concepts and rather just throws them at you. She also treats her class like we are Kindergarteners.

Prof is very kind & clear on expectations. Lectures were information overload but content tested was fair- but when she says cumulative she means cumulative exams. The big project was extremely time-consuming and far more than expected for this class but it was helpful at the end of the day. Much more helpful one-on-one or in small group settings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found her to be a dry lecturer who just sort of moves through the PPT. I found that asking her questions individually was more helpful than in a lecture setting (though she didn't always have great answers; eg "we don't need to know about that"). She is very kind, makes herself available for students, and provides extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Steele is a wonderful professor who is passionate about what she teaches. She is very accessible, whether via email, office hours, or Piazza. Lecture ppts were posted on Canvas, and lectures were very organized. She makes class time engaging, and she is very kind. I would absolutely recommend her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Steele is an incredible teacher. Her class is designed for you to get an A. She truly cares about her students and loves the material. Even with minimal effort an A is very easy to achieve in her course. She is very accessible outside of class and is a very quick grader.

I absolutely LOVE Dr. Steele. Her lectures are clear and engaging. She uploads a PDF of the slides for you to look over at any time. She gives out plenty of study materials and is a fair grader. She obviously loves neuroscience and is really good at teaching it too. She truly cares about each of her students and is so fun to talk to. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take her 10000%. Makes a genuine effort to get to know her students and wants you to succeed. Is very clear on what you need to do to succeed and is a very kind grader as long as you put effort into what you do. Encourages questions. THE GOAT
She was very good at explaining biology and her lectures made sense. The class itself is not too difficult but it does take some time outside of class to go through the material.

She teaches at a very nice pace to follow, and she is quick to answer somebody's question. The main reason for the mandatory attendance is the Learning Catalytics, but you can miss a few of them without any penalty if you can't make it to a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I found her lectures slightly more engaging than Dr. Kerr's, yet I still found them not very helpful. It's a miracle I even passed this class I'm not gonna lie.

Good lecturer, but unnecessary extra work included in the intro bio course. A written assignment every week, mostly unrelated to biology content. She's nice and can explain things in much more detail in office hours, but lectures go by fast with lots of content. Need to know the content in lots of detail because exam questions were tricky.

Dr. Smith is an exceptional teacher. She made biology more interesting through her passion. As a non-bio major, if you plan on taking this class, make sure you go into class with energy, determination, and dedication. Sitting near the front helps as it makes it harder to fall asleep oops. As much as I did not do well in the class, it was on me.
amazing, no notes. TAKE HER. does a great job at explaining concepts and passionate about being here!

Dr. Smith is a great professor and lectures really well. The course is pretty content heavy and its important to start studying for exams well before and trying to keep up with the content as you go. She tries her best to make the course very engaging and active.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was way more involved in the lab experiments than every other lab professor I have had. She cares a lot about her students and is very good at explaining course concepts. Her class is great first experience into biology research and is worth taking the more difficult 2610 lecture to be able to take her lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was very difficult for me, however, she is a very good lecturer and is very well at conveying and explaining the concepts of the course while remaining engaging. I did struggle throughout this course; however, when she taught the lectures, I understood the material better than when the other professor lectured, as the two rotated units.

She is a very nice and approachable person. Also her lectures are fantastic and she keeps them super interesting. Exams are not too bad and if you pay attention in class only need to study like 1 day beforehand. However, attendance is like super mandatory.
She's super fun to be around and the way she explains everything makes the topic a lot easier to learn. Her way of teaching is also entertaining and never boring.

This is probably my absolute favorite professor at Georgia Tech. She is fantastic at explaining concepts and consistently asks the class if she is going too fast or too slow. She makes 8 am lectures somehow enjoyable, and I always find myself wanting to go to class. Dr. Hope is wonderful and has made me more confident in my abilities as a student.

10s across the board. phenomenal lecturer and would highly recommend taking her if you're a melanated woman. she's very diff from many of the other NEUR professors who just care about their research and not their students. makes me excited to go to class

Dr. Hope is an incredible professor. Highly recommend her for NEUR 3003. Lectures were very engaging, and she cares a lot about students. She connects topics to real-world scenarios and even made playlists for each lecture (on theme!). Paying attention during lecture is the key to success. Up to 3% of extra credit on course grade was offered.
Glad to be her first reviewer on here. Great professor, very kind and cares for students. Take her Neur 2010 section next semester!!
Had to put in my everythign to get an A in this class. She makes her lectures quite confusing and wanders off topic. Also not a very pleasant person to speak with.

Genuinely one of my fav professors at Tech. She is witty/engaging, responsive outside class, and caring toward students. Tests are fair, and in-class assignments are easy. No final, just a term paper (which is a good grade booster). Offers extra credit opportunities. If you pay attention in class and do assignments, it's an easy A honestly.
Not very helpful

She made things unnecessarily complicated and her lectures were difficult to follow. She stumbles over her words a lot and struggles to form cohesive thoughts. She's also very rude when students try to seek feedback or help. The class is doable and tests weren't hard besides the second one, but it's just a lot of self teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For NEUR 2001 I really enjoyed having her as my professor. The way the class is structured you are guaranteed a B in the class. With that being said, if you want in A in the class you have to do good on exams. There is no practice exams or quizzes for this class. I strongly recommend attending lecture because her slides are not good.
extremely rude, in person and over email. she shows very little compassion and is often snarky or condescending when questions are asked. avoid her!!!!

While I know many found Dr. Holder's lectures confusing, I think combined with her slides they were easy to follow. She does get off track at times, but is overall a good lecturer. The course was very well structured! Attendance wasn't mandatory, but lecture recordings weren't posted and the slides did not always have everything discussed in class.

Dr. Holder's lectures felt very scattered. Her voice would trail off at the end of sentences, and she would use a lot of abbreviations but not explain what they meant. It's clear that she tries, but I found it really difficult to pay attention to her lectures.

Dr. Holder isn't a great lecturer and often seems unsure of what she's talking about. She has a hard time putting together cohesive thoughts, which makes it tough to understand concepts during class. I ended up having to teach myself most of the material. It wasn't too difficult, but it was definitely a lot to learn on my own.
Dr.Holder was a bad lecturer, and simply has no idea what she is talking about. She has a hard time formul
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!! I don't know why her rate my professor is so low, she has been my absolute favorite teach I've had at tech and my favorite neuro class I have taken. She cares so so much about her students and their success and the exams are usually super straight forward with no tricks.

I LOVEEED THIS CLASS PLS TAKE IT!!!!!!!!  She was the most direct and clear lecturer I have ever had at gatech!  She is so genuine, relatable, and down Earth!!!  I love her, and I wish I could take this class again!!!   I LOVED HER PLS TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!!

I loved Dr Holder as a professor because she was very caring about her students and has a passion for teaching. Her lectures were great and she really values participation. 3003 was a really tough course work wise (ex. term research paper), but Holder had great feedback and made it clear on what it took to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rude, horrible advisor, unlikeable as a person. The worst professor in the department and I pray for anyone that is forced to take her. Good Luck!

i absolutely adore her. she's one of the most caring professors i've ever had, and i almost wish i were a neuro student so i could take more of her classes. she's not necessarily easy, but she'll give you extra help/attention if you ask for it. she's the kind of professor i'd go to office hours just to chat with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Please NEVER take a course with this professor if you care about your gpa alot. She is okay with lecturing but her grading rubric and other specs are awful. Honestly worst class and professor i have had at tech so far and im a third year. Also, it is very clear that she has certain class favorite students and kinda rude towards other students.
Dr. Holder does an amazing job at overcomplicating simple content. Her lectures are convoluted and her slides often don't have enough information for you to teach yourself.

She doesn't seem fully there in lectures- often drifts off and doesn't finish thoughts. Lectures could be a lot more engaging and she's pretty dismissive of students. Tests are decent (unit 2 is hardest), make sure to go to IID days since they help a lot with practice and feedback.
Rude, condescending, difficult to work with.
Her lectures were somewhat erratic, and I felt the tests didn't accurately reflect the material that was taught. Additionally, she wasn't very receptive to feedback.

The format of this class was amazing. Lectures were engaging albeit being at 8:00am. We got crib sheets for exams and alot of practice with reading and writing papers. Not too much work, I think it was perfectly paced and I actually learned alot.

Dr. Holder was a great professor for 3003. She is a detailed & entertaining lecturer. She does challenge you on the exams but if you thoroughly study you will do okay and it is fair. She made 3003 a class I thoroughly enjoyed and it is probably my favorite neuro class. I definitely miss the class, especially in comparison to other neuro classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's nice and easy to reach, and the course structure is good (no final exam, just a grant proposal you work on the whole semester, lots of completion points). However, there's very few resources for the exams-- basically just one quick review session with barely any practice questions, so it's hard to prepare even though you get a crib sheet.

The tests can be hard to grasp because it is a lot of backwards thinking, but the lectures do hold the material needed..just need to be able to apply that material. Dr. Holder is a great professor and can explain any topic in depth.

We had almost daily plickers which are very similar to the exam questions and you also get three practice quizzes. I studied last minute, never went to class, and got a high B. If you actually go to class and put in some work and this is an easy A. BUT GO TO CLASS. Exams were open book/ notes but they're all application just like all neuro classes
Very average professor, can be a bit demanding at times. Not a very good academic advisor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The material isn't too hard to grasp; the textbook and lecture slides give you everything you need. The TA graded really harshly which made the class harder than it needed to be. You'll get an A as long as you do well on the tests which are worth 60%, despite a ton of extra assignments in the class that don't weigh much in comparison.

Behavioral pharmacology is a tough class. The content is interesting but there are a lot of assignments and one HUGE literature review. I think it depends on your TA. Mine was a tough grader. Take this if you care about the subject matter/ aka if you're pre-health. Otherwise, it's a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is an incredible professor! The class itself isn't easy by any means, but she cares a lot about her students and offers plenty of opportunities to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is a phenomenal professor. She is one of the most caring professors I've ever had, which is especially nice during this pandemic. The class has a lot of outside work, but the lectures are really interesting. The class time is never straight lecture: she always includes in-class activities, like group discussions and case studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: A Neuroendorinology Special Topics Class. Emphasized skills useful for grad school. Material was organized clearly, and she would take a day to review with us before the tests. Research paper and 20-min presentation, but she gave good feedback throughout the semester to prep you for it. Go to class and ask questions, and you'll do well.

Her lectures seem to be put together at the last minute as they usually are disorganized and not the most helpful. This class was mostly graded by tests, and the test questions often time did not make a lot of sense/ were not clear. There is also no practice questions ever given or any help with grades really. This class in general is just sucky.

Dr. Holder is probably the worst lecturer I have ever come across. Her slides are horrible and her commentary adds nothing to them and she often stumbles over her own words. You are going to have to teach yourself everything. Also, pretty rude to students and looks down on us. Exams do not match up with class material. Avoid her...

Really bad professor that makes it very difficult to understand what will be tested on the exam. Exam is not representative of what is taught in class and little emphasis of what is going to be on the exam is provided during class. I'm going to get an A in the class and suggest anybody looking to take this class to wait for a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is really interested in Neuroscience, but her lectures aren't the best. Make sure you follow along with the key points and know all the vocabulary. Be able to interpret scenarios as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I know many students don't attend lectures for this class b/c there are already lectures posted online, but for me, Yanli's lectures have been abundantly helpful. I attended them all. She curates her own annotated lecture slides and cares deeply about her students, always offering support. This subject wasn't easy, but her lectures helped me a lot.

She is a very kind person but her lectures are difficult to understand. For 1553, it doesn't matter what section you take as Dr. Jankowski posts all of his lectures online, class is not mandatory, and the HW, tests, and quizes are made by him, not the individual lecturers.
Combo is notoriously difficult, but Hao makes it easier than all the other professors. Lectures notes and practice exams are your best friends. Grading is pretty lenient.

Professor Hao has very understanding and caring towards all her students. She even apologized to the class when someone has a hard time understanding her. She is very sincere and tries her best to help all her students and is very approachable and kind.

The professor was excellent. The grading gave ample headroom even if you got questions wrong on the homework or missed lecture.

The lectures were clear and the notes were very helpful, with examples and practice problems for each concept.

The exams were also fairly easy if you understood the material.

Prof Hao is really nice and is very approachable. The only complaint I have is that it is next to impossible to ask questions and have her understand. Other than that, her notes are pretty good and she provides lots of materials to study for exams. Not the best, but also not the worst.

Prof. Hao was very approachable and obviously really cares about her students. All tests and homework were very fair and were graded leniently. Lectures were difficult to understand but annotated lecture slides were helpful.

Not the biggest fan of her lecture style (she goes very quickly through slides because this class covers a lot of content, but she annotates them and posts recordings/annotated slides afterwards), but otherwise chill weekly homework and reasonable tests. She clearly cares about the students and is accessible outside class. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Hao gave great lectures, I always understood everything very clearly, her homeworks and tests were very fair. Overall, if you come to class and do your work you will get a good grade in this class. Prof. Hao is super understanding and caring of her students. Highly recommend her!
Her lectures are pretty straight forward. Grading is too. If you want to succeed, you have to come to class and pay attention (so basically a normal class).

Professor Hao very clearly cares about her students. Tests were moderately difficult, but not insanely so. Definitely go to office hours if you don't understand something on the homework, as the class goes over a lot of material.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Exams are quite difficult even for those with calculus knowledge. Grade is just exams and quizzes. There is no homework BUT u need to hundreds of practice problems to understand the topic as her lectures are quite vague. She teaches straight from the textbook. DO NOT RECCOMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
