reviews.comment: This professor does not take into account the level at which her students enter the class. I often felt I was expected to understand material I had never previously seen. Your overall grade is based solely on exams and quizzes.

I would only recommend Hampton if you're a student with some calc knowledge going into college. Her Canvas page is very open with full access to worksheets, textbook, etc., which is nice since she doesn't give HW or attendance. Otherwise, it can get hard to keep up since she is otherwise middling at her job. Tests are surprisingly difficult too.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just be careful taking this class because there is no HW outside of class so majority of your grades are based on only Exams and Quizzes. I would only reccommend this professor if you have experience in calc in high school. Also, there are some pros to this class. Like there is a lot of stuff that isn't included in the course like sin,cos,tan, etc

Honestly, a fine class/professor. Your grade is determined mostly by exams, however, if you go to her lectures, which are helpful, and do some of the practice problems you should be pretty well off. She also provides the textbook which is nice. One thing to know is a lot of the answers for the practice problems are not provided.

Students who already took a calc course struggled less with her. There are suggested problems you HAVE to do to succeed (even though there is "no hw"). For an intro calculus class for non-STEM majors, she offered "reading the textbook" as a way to improve performance. She writes out definitions and walks through practice problems rather than teach.

She isn't even a true professor, this class took up tons of study time. By the end of the semester we had been given over 800 practice problems, not mandatory but they are the only way to prepare for the test. The problems she goes over in lecture are a fraction of the difficulty of what shows up on the test. 0/10 class avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I know many had a negative opinion on her, but she wasn't bad, I enjoyed lecture. At the end of the semester she went through everyone's grades and tried to get everyone to a C (minimum). Her exams were very difficult, if you have no calc knowledge, but she adjusted as we went on. Go to office hours, she noticed any effort on your part.

Ambiguous feelings about Dr. Hampton. All the lecture notes are posted online. Quizzes 1x a week. No homework. Lectures were straightforward, not in depth. Don't blow off lecture though. Exams are fair, she gives an extra credit Q on each. Not a great class for people who have never took calculus. She tries her best to help our grades. Just study.

Midterms and Exams usually have some sort of extra credit, and the bottom 5 quizzes are dropped. If Lectures aren't really your thing, you can probably only show up to the studio class, and do practice problems and still achieve a passing grade. She is a fun teacher and listens to student's concerns.

No attendance or homework, heavy portion of the grade is based on three exams. Teaches directly from the textbook and is unwelcoming to questions. In-studio quizzes are much much easier than exams, so we were unprepared for how hard exams would be. The tests don't give you an idea of how many points each question is worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the greatest professor but the class is really easy especially if you took calc in high school. No attendance but if you don't know calc then I would recommend going because it's kind of hard to learn on your own. 15 quizzes and she drops the worst 5, and 2 midterms and a final.
Genuinely a miserable human being. A mean person who does little to nothing to help students, and your ENTIRE grade hinges on tough midterms. Avoid class at all costs.
optional hw but exams are hard
She does very good lectures, but it is important to go to all of them. Read the syllabus and don't ask dumb questions, she will clock you. I'd recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was surprised to see such negative comments about her because my experience wasn't terrible at all. Although some may find it boring, I actually enjoyed her lecture style. She gives so many optional practice problems that undoubtedly show up on the test, so literally just do the work and you're fine.

One of the strictest graders I've ever had and barely gives partial credit on exams that she makes hard af. Tests also weigh a big chunck of your grade in this class and it felt like the way exams are graded is pretty unfair/unforgiving given the grading scale. It wasn't communicated that the exams were gonna include such complex problems either.

Not a very engaging lecturer and sometimes made mistakes on problems in lecture so she would have to send out an announcement later in the day correcting herself. She seemed a bit unprepared as a new professor and was uncertain on what some of the conventions (like what content was emphasized) and homeworks were like at GT.

This professor is, without a doubt, the worst instructor I've ever encountered. She puts in the bare minimum effort to teach but somehow expects students to solve the most ridiculously complex problems on exams. She's unenthusiastic, unforgiving, and doesn't care about her students' success in the slightest.  

Avoid. Avoid. AVOID!!!

Made an objectively hard class pretty easy to digest. Attendance isn't mandatory & a lot of people didn't come to class, but lectures were extremely helpful. Work is straightforward but the tests are hard.

One of my favorite professors. Her lecture style doesn't work for everyone, but I liked that she was concise, explained concepts well, and made sure we learned what we needed to. You can always supplement her lectures with Barone's, as his are recorded online, to get a different way of teaching if you don't understand something.

Pretty good for first time teaching linear algebra at Georgia Tech. Tests can be hard, but there are plenty of practice tests online. Highly recommend watching and taking notes on the videos for each lesson before the lecture and do the homework assignments. You don't have to go to studios and I didn't find them to be too helpful.

Good pick for a non-math major looking for easy A. Pretty much just reads slides, not very engaging, explains well enough. Don't need to attend class, most people don't. imo, she has a really shallow understanding of the stuff she's teaching, does the bare minimum of required content, but if you don't need anything past LinAlg she's a good pick
Good Professor overall, very good lecturer, rather have her than any other professor, and arguably better than Barone and many ways.
Hard to understand handwriting at times, sometimes doesn't cover material that we then had to go over in studio afterwards. Caring but doesn't teach very clearly

It wasn't an option above but I took him for MATH 1711. He's hard to understand and has iffy handwriting so sit near the front if you can. Sometimes doesn't go over everything practiced in studio. My TA was good, so I relied more on studio for learning and put in ample time outside of class. Lowest midterm was dropped but you can't drop the final.

he's kinda difficult to understand and i don't think he explains the concepts well, but it was his first semester so i guess it's understandable. i will say he seems like a nice, genuine guy. i personally stopped going to class after the first couple lectures and instead watched the videos from cuyler warnock or sal barone, which i found helpful.

Although he is very caring and respectful of his students, I personally did not understand his teaching style, and his lectures did not make sense to me. However, this is his first year, so hopefully it will improve over time.

linear is a hard class. not many attend the lectures, but they are helpful to get the content down, although some lecture can be self taught. he's helpful and explains hard content well. the harder questions are usually the conceptual questions so you need to have a great understanding of theorems which is very hard to do in this class.

The only negative thing I have to say is that sometimes he didn't explain certain concepts very well or would skip through them during lecture, but he made up for it by always being available after class to explain better, other than that he was great. This was also his first year teaching so I'm guessing he will improve over time.

He was very kind and always present for asking questions, but the lectures could be hard to follow so I had to rely heavily on the 50-minute lecture videos that Math 1554 Common leaves up. I won't be too harsh though, it was his first time teaching a weed-out class at Georgia Tech, and he has all of the qualities of a good professor.

Dr. Nometa is a great professor. He explains concepts very clearly and connects the topics of Linear Algebra together very well (which is a necessity for this class). He's very accessible outside of class and cares about his students. The only downside is his accent, which can be hard to understand at times, but you'll get used to it.

Very nice and lenient with students on grading & due dates. SF is her area of expertise which shows in how passionate her lectures are. If you love the genre, you would love her class. Her lectures can get fairly scattered and rambly somewhat often, but is ultimately manageable if you participate a fair bit.

She was an amazing and enthusiastic professor! I actually enjoyed the class and would look forward to coming. The work wasn't too bad- just some presentations an a paper with some discussion posts in the mix. Overall, a great class that I'm glad I took. If you're considering animation, I'd 1000% recommend you take it with her!!
Very caring, kind professor. The class was entertaining. The only issue was that no grades were put in before the last month of the semester, but it was an easy A.

Sweetest person ever. Very accomodating to deadlines. Very few assignments, and they're pretty open ended. Cool lectures on animation, won't always be super interesting but I still enjoyed them. Had many options for extra credit. Always open to give feedback on assignments. Clearly very passionate about what she teaches, which is refreshing to see!

Ida is super sweet and definitely cares a lot about her students. Attendance is mandatory but she is pretty excited about the subject matter so the lectures are actually enjoyable to go to. However if you dont like writing, dont take the class. It is purely essays and discussion posts. Extra credit opportunities throughout the semester though

The class is pretty easy. You can not pay attention during lectures and do well. You watch films every week outside class and write an analysis to post. She gives feedback on everything you dot. Overall, you are basically graded on completing the discussion posts & easy group project & 2 papers(midterm & final). Great professor and easy/fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love her! She's so nice and caring and really wants her students to succeed. She clearly states what you need to do to get an A and has a TON of extra credit opportunities for students. She is also super lenient with extensions. She has a ton of knowledge about films. If you have the change, please take her!

He's probably one of the best GA Tech has to offer. His lectures were very engaging and entertaining. I'd say the content also isn't difficult. He's also funny, and his exam was just the homework problems but with different numbers. Final is a report, but easy.

I've taken 3030 and 4031 one with. No doubt worth every second of my life. Ethan makes you strong in term of math skill and R skill. Definitely takes his class if you wanna be a better Engineer and have a solid foundation. The GOAT.

Strikes the best balance of hilarious, engaging lectures + excellent teaching that I've seen at Tech. Lengthy homeworks requiring R but I guarantee you'll understand the material better than if you took any other instructor. Only complaint is no practice tests and difficult exams which is unfortunate, but learn the material well and you'll succeed.

Ethan is one of the best professors I've had. He cares for all his students and knows everyone's names. He really wants u to learn the material so his exams are more difficult than the other sections, but it is completely worth it. He's hilarious and u will know way more than the other sections. He makes u learn R and curves! Please take him!
The GOAT. He's so funny.

Makes you feel stupid for asking questions at office hours. HW is basically coding in R, and the exams are difficult with very little partial credit and unnecessarily difficult instructions intended to confuse you. Attendance is mandatory but lectures are very boring. Be prepared for a hard time if you take his class.

Ethan is a great professor. His homeworks can be extensive and take time to complete, but they make sure you learn the material well. His exams are weighted heavily and really require you to know the material inside and out, but he is very accommodating for one-on-one help and will help you succeed if you work at it.

The GOAT!

My favorite lecturer at Georgia Tech. Ethan wants his students to succeed, and as long as you show up and put in the effort you will be rewarded. Please take him for 4031 if you are given the opportunity, and I promise you will not be disappointed.

A genuinely good professor for a very simple class. He was funny, engaging, and taught the material in a fun way. Easy to follow and very well-organized. You'll have to learn R, but this took negligible time. Pay attention to how good (appearance) your homework and report assignments look and you'll do fine.

This class was way harder than it should be. The entire semester felt overwhelming while taking it. I struggled a lot to understand what was happening during lectures, and the homework assignments were extremely time-consuming. The professor used an R program to randomly call on students, which added to the stress of attending class.

Ethan is definitely an entertaining professor & his banter alone made me go to class. Homework can be time consuming, but if you are interested in Data Science & want to learn R, definitely take Ethan. His tests & grading are fair, but beware that there is virtually no practice material for exams.

Most entertaining professor I've had at Georgia Tech by far. He is outspoken and brutally honest about his expectations for his students. This guy made me want to come to lectures, even if just for a good laugh. My only issue is that 60% of your grade is based on one midterm and a final exam, for both of which zero review material is provided.

He has very high expectations and can make you feel stupid if you ask questions. Above all else though, the homeworks are grueling. Not necessarily because of the content but because it must be types in R. I almost lost my mind several times this semester because of having to code the hw which took hours.

Oh my god Ethan blows.  Do not take him.  Such a hard grader and especially for an introductory stats class.  If hes ur only option id go for the math or ece alternative.  His homework is done in R and learning adds so much time at the start of the course.  Also only one midterm and then a final.  Will end in a A/B but only bc I took AP stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ethan's not so bad in general but don't work for him as your boss

Extremely harsh grader and offered an extremely rude response when I reached out seeking better feedback on my assignment. This is not a stats class - it's an R class. His midterm consists of writing your own questions which takes hours, and if your questions match the difficulty of the textbook you'll receive "between a B and a C"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ethan is the type of professor that you either love or hate. His classes are rigorous but give you an exceptional understanding of the material if you take the time to attend lecture, do the homework, read the textbook and go to office hours if needed. He teaches using R which is free and useful outside of classes. Wouldn't recommend for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best and favorite professor I've ever had at Tech.  4031 can be a difficult class, but Ethan explains concepts incredibly well and lecture notes/R codes are very helpful.  Attendance counts with occasional pop quizzes, but his lecture banter alone makes it worth it to attend class.  Sit up front and pay attention - he's an all around great prof.

He's making a class that is straightforward unnecessarily and annoyingly difficult. Lectures are boring and he could've gone over some content in half the time. Refuses to give practice materials for the midterms despite how much it is worth in the final grade.

He's not a bad professor in terms of his teaching; however, this class is a lot more work than the other ISYE 3770 sections. All homeworks are written in R and they are quite time consuming. He has 2 in class "projects" that test your knowledge of how to use R. Also, the final is a decently large portion of the grade. Edit: HE CURVES THE FINAL!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, though lectures could've slightly been better. Loved his hilarious personal stories, which really helped reinforce concepts, and class was overall easy, except for the final, which was 35% of our grade. Overall, fun guy, but was a challenging professor, who is determined to help you succeed, "make sure to study or you won't do well"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Somewhat difficult course for people with no background in statistics. The final exam and midterm make up more than half of the grade. He said the midterm was easy so he was going to make the final harder. Did well in every other category except the final, ended up dropping my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching was good and things were fine until the final. For whatever reason, he said that the midterm was easy so he would make the final harder and ended up screwing us over. I worked hard and got good grades on everything except the final. Dropped an entire letter grade and nothing I can do about it

Lectures are really boring. His teaching style is pretty mid. Homeworks are time consuming but I guess its helpful for learning LaTeX and R. Overall extremely mid prof but at least he's kind of funny.

He takes your attendance during lecture, but Ethan's lectures were pretty interesting. His HWs are weekly but pretty easy. The in person projects are a piece of cake as well. A lot of his exam questions are based on HW questions, so as long as you do the hw, the exams will be a breeze.

Did not like his teaching style at first and did bad on the midterm. I realized that you really just need to take his advice from the beginning: understand all the lecture problems and HW questions. He can come off as harsh, but I think he means well. He was true to his word about expectations. And he will bump grades if you do well on the final.

If it's your only option, take Ethan, but if there's a better prof., you could do better. Homeworks are very time consuming, and it's difficult to bounce back from a bad grade. Also, would recommend reviewing R before taking him.

Ethan's 3030 & 4031 are fantastic. He uses R in all classes which is so useful to learn. His lecture style is very structured & straight-forward: attendance is tracked, exams are from lectures. If you do the HW & study the slides, you'll do well in the midterm & final. But also GO TO OFFICE HOURS & ISYE Tutoring, it's heavy content so ask for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely not an easy professor, but I learned a lot. Class is very R heavy and time intensive, so stay on top of the lectures and HW.  Exams are in person and HARD and make up the bulk of your grade (1 midterm + 1 final,) but he curved very generously at the end. He may come off as harsh, but he really cares about his students.

Extremely tough grader and grading policy has gotten more difficult post-COVID with exams now in person. He is a good person as a teacher who seems to care, but he takes years to grade, has 8 AM office hours, and is hard to reach at times. He curved his class to a 3.0 GPA, but the averages were very low so you didn't know your grade until the end.

Do not take Ethan for 3030. He cannot entirely control all of these things, but the ZERO-tolerance makeup policy (for exams too), 8 am office hours, extremely late grading, and difficulty I had understanding him in class did not make the class worth it. He curved so the class would have a 3.0 average. Preserve your GPA. It's not worth it.
Lecture can be a little dry, lots of homework, but he is always willing to help. Learning R is super helpful and I recommend taking 3030 with Ethan

Ethan is THE TOUGHEST grader I've seen. Ridiculously unforgiving grading policy, and he openly admits to playing favorites when it comes to final grades (Positive/Negative). He is personally well meaning and nice, but if your interest is in having a good GPA, I cannot recommend this professor. The effort required to succeed is easily above average.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lee is an amazing professor. Gets to the point and tests relevant material. He likes to teach supplemental material as well. Very R heavy but, if you don't know much R, you should still be fine to take the class as he starts off from the basics. Very few grading categories and he can be a hard grader. I'd take him for all my ISyE classes if I could

All notes are posted online so youll be able to review them as needed. He cares about the students and the class is fairly easy, with exam questions coming from homeworks and lecture notes. However, only one midterm which makes up a lot of your grade, and he can take forever to grade (we didnt get midterm grade back for many weeks).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor and nice guy. He's a pretty harsh but fair grader. Tests are the vast majority of your grade, but he prepares you well for them. Even though I did poorly in the class, I still feel like I learned a lot and would take his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ethan is really sweet as a prof and definitely cares about his students. He may try to scare you out of taking his class - DONT listen! He's an amazing prof and his exams are similar to homework and class examples. He wants his students to succeed and you learn a lot as well. Not an easy class, but he teaches it very well with his own examples.

i am not sure why there are so many good ratings even for my semester ending May'20... maybe it's just freshmen being freshmen... this was one of the worst class I had taken... it's like you're back in HS if you're into that go for it. weekly HWs graded hard (if not very). all weight lies in midterm and finals. both graded harshly, no extra credit

The one midterm and final make up a huge chunk of your grade so there really isn't any room for error. But he is extremely clear about what you will see on the tests so make sure you go over practice questions and HW and you'll be set. He'll try to make you drop the class on the first day but don't listen to him; his bad jokes are worth it.

His lectures and amazing but the weighting of the midterm and final can really mess with your grade. I love the way he teaches but you need to practice the HW really well to score great. Went from a C to an A in the class with his advice. Always reach out when in need. He takes attendance but there are three free days. HW is based on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Midterm is a time crunch. Doesn't give a ton of partial credit, but the questions themselves aren't too bad. Useful/entertaining lectures across the board. He pretty much tells you how the class is going to be on syllabus day and that's the way it is. Would take again.

Never listen to Ethan when he tries to make you drop at the beginning of the semester (he did that with us). Staying in his class was the best decision I have ever made. He is, hands down, the best professor I have had. His passion for his students is unparalleled. His class is also not too difficult and it measures what you know.

(Homework questions are from the textbook.) Ethan is a really good lecturer and gives good examples that help you understand the concepts and he keeps the lectures interesting too. The only thing about his class is (at least for my semester) we mainly had one midterm and the final for our grades. so make sure to study
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I created an account here just to rate this professor. I probably will get a C on this class, but I am pretty bad at statistics/prob. Ethan is in my top 5 at tech. Cares about you, gives you help, pushes you, and even lets you work with TA from his others classes to get help. Classes are funny. Besides, he's a real yellow jacket fun.

He is a very good teacher and he is very willing to listen to his students for feedback. He makes a big effort to give partial credit to everyone in exams. His lecture notes are very complete and useful. Exams are fair in difficulty, he clearly states what you need to do to succeed in the course. I really enjoyed his class!

Very nice guy. Lectures not the best, but puts entire lecture as word doc on canvas post-class. Class made to be easy, but people underestimate class + that's why scores are low. You can pass if you skip class but read + understand notes at home (but attendance is graded so have a friend sign you in) + do HW and check with chegg AFTER.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really like Ethan's class. He sincerely cares about his students and lecture is very clear. He tells us exactly what will be on the exam. If you do the homework and understand class lecture examples, the exam is going to be easy. I don't think homework is too heavy. Usually 5-6 questions taking up 2 hours each week. Will recommend
Doesn't care much about lectures. Talks random stuff about his family all the time and uses very confusing examples. Passes an attendance sheet every class. Homework is large. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You need to attend lectures or watch the recordings to understand content since the slides can't really stand alone. There's 2 open note exams and then weekly open note quizzes. The questions can be tricky-ish but if you attend and listen to lectures it's easy! We also had written assignments that are lengthy but easy. Really cool content though!

Anna is really knowledgeable with the course topics, but it can be hard to follow along in lecture sometimes due to either the content being confusing without enough prior knowledge or the disorganization and lack of clarity on the notes slides. Lecture recordings and everything being open notes makes it easy to do okay in the class, though.
Stopped going to lectures because she kind of assumes that we can catch up to what she's saying (i cannot
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOTS of EC offered, if you do it easy to get an A. Open-internet tests but info is obscure and difficult to find online/slides. Best to transcribe lecture notes. Dr. Ivanova is extremely knowledgable but was unapproachable and unfriendly in office hours. I really liked the head TA Will. Fun, easy, but lengthy assignments make up majority of grade.

Very interesting class, and Dr. Ivanova clearly knew a lot about it! While attendance isn't mandatory and everything is posted online, weekly quizzes mean you cannot get behind in the class. However, everything is open note so as long as you listen to the lectures and complete the assignments, I didn't find the assessments hard.

It's a straightforward class with open notes on exams and quizzes. There's a quiz every week so don't get behind. The only concern was the assignments are long and they take FOREVER to grade those, so you pretty much won't know your grade until the last day of finals.

professor ivanova was great! she's a great lecturer, and the class is really interesting. there's only two exams (midterm and final), about 11 quizzes (you can drop one), and four assignments with extra credit opportunity. all the exams/quizzes are open note, so as long as you go to/watch lecture, you'll have a very easy time in this class!

Found the exams/quizzes a little difficult but the content is interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory but would recommend going because she explains a lot of her slides and her slides are mainly pictures or graphs. Provides extra credit on assignments (four in total), but they are kind of time-consuming.

The exams are a little difficult and the lecture slides have barely any information on them, but Anna is a very passionate and knowledgeable teacher! There's a lot of extra credit in the class and exams are open note. The class covers very interesting content.
good professor with open note exams. clearly very knowledgeable on the course material

honestly, i only attended two lectures all semester and still did great. very easy, textbook's definitely not required and assignments are absolutely loaded with extra credit. i still learned a lot, the content was fascinating. lovely teacher, and she brought in lots of guest lecturers. recorded lectures in canvas media gallery.
Her lectures are amazing and intrigued me into learning more about the content. However, her tests can be hard, just beware. It is open note and open internet though.

Exams are open note. Weekly quizzes are short but ensure your basic understanding of the material. Content is interesting and Anya (Anna) is very knowledgeable, but lectures can be boring still. The slides can be confusing, as the slides themselves don't really explain the material, it might just be a picture with a couple words.
He is welcoming and clearly passionate about the subject, making this an interesting course.

He is passionate about physics, and the class is not hard. People love to complain. How are you getting an A+ and giving him a one? I did not show up to class, but when I did, he taught as well as I expected him to. He is a good person and is passionate and cares about the material. What else can you ask for?
Nice guy, but gets stuck in his own work and gets behind in class easily. Be prepared to learn a lot on your own.
If you don't have to take him, don't choose to
All the profs for this class, except the coordinator, suck. He's really not that great, but if you have an interest in the math behind mechanics, he's an ok option.

Not that bad of a lecturer but could never answer any questions no matter the difficulty level and constantly made mistakes in the practice problems during lecture. Not the worst if u get him though bc the grading is standardized across sections so just watch dr. alicea's recorded lectures.

Do NOT stress about your 2211 Professor!!! Course Coordinator posts all lectures online and I watched them while sitting in Kolvins class. Prioritize other things in your schedule since ur prof here doesn't matter. Clicker questions but you can get code from a friend. I wouldn't listen to his lectures cuz he goes on tangents.
He is my friend's dad!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Seemed really nice and interested in physics but was a terrible lecturer. Take Dr. Alicea if you can. I only did well because I took physics in high school and watched Dr. Alicea's recorded lectures. Spends most of the time doing irrelevant derivations and is just really dry.
Don't take this guy if you want an A
I like the pace that he goes at and the depth at which he covers things
He was knowledgable and his slides were pretty good.
Professor Kolvin was very enthusiastic about physics and he felt very kind and welcoming.
solid lecturer, just taught from the same physics slides as everyone else.

Take Dr. Alicea if given the chance, but he wasn't that bad. I mostly just struggled in the tests in this course, which were the same for every professor. He wasn't great, but he could've been worse. Watch Dr. Alicea's lecture videos, make sure you understand the lab GPS's, and go to the PLUS sessions to give yourself the best chance of doing well.

Pretty horrible lecturer. He was confusing, his organization was bad, and spent too much time on useless proofs and got behind in the course pretty quickly. However, there are ways to get around attendance requirements (bucket points), and if you're okay at self-studying you can just watch the course coordinator's (Dr. Alicea) lectures and be fine.

Was really bad at lecturing— I came in with a really low basic understanding of physics and he really did not help me learn anything in what's supposed to be an introductory physics class. He kinda expected us to come in with prior knowledge and would get really into detail about the wrong things and was super behind compared to the other sections.

Genuinely the worst teacher I've had in my entire life. Seems like a nice guy, too bad he is an awful professor! The course is structured poorly, and I probably lost physics knowledge over the course of the semester.
He always got lost within his own problems, almost like he was learning how to do Physics along with the students. One of the worst for sure

Probably the singlest worst professor/teacher i've had in my life, actively regressed my previous knowledge of physics. Never take, literally will make it seem like a 12 credit class. Principles and content that was going to be in exams was just never covered and lectures were always a week behind.

People really exaggerate the difficulty of this class, I went to every one of his lectures, took notes, and did well on all my tests with minimal studying. He is super kind and if you reach out about any issues you have he will attend to them super fast and well. People who don't like his lecturing likely aren't seeking help they need from him.
lectures were not helpful at all. if you have to take him for phys 1, go to lecture for attendance but watch dr alicea's lectures on canvas, that is the only way i passed this class
Awful teacher and very difficult to understand. Going to lectures is mandatory but you won't learn anything. You will just end up watching another professor's online lectures. Avoid at all costs!

His lectures are hard to follow. Much of the time is spent worrying about things that do not relate to the requirements of the course. He goes over few relevant examples in each class and does a poor job explaining example problems. The only way to do well in physics with him as a teacher is by watching someone else's lecture videos online.
Bro this guy doesn't know how to teach. I just had to study. I'm literally writing this in a lecture as he spends 30 minutes on an irrelevant problem. Take literally anyone else.
He seems like a nice, caring guy but is an awful lecturer. Gets his own examples wrong, takes eons to explain basic examples, and quickly falls behind schedule.
He is super awesome a the kindest person I've ever met

Awful professor. For reference, in the very second lecture we somehow went from vectors to Taylor approximations to coding, and then back to unit definitions all within the same period and presumably no link between all of the concepts. This course has been 100% self study, as his explanations are subpar at best.

Literally the worst educator I've ever had in my life. I took AP physics in high school and taking his class is regressing my knowledge. The concepts are not that hard to understand but he somehow makes it the most confusing subject in the world. DO NOT TAKE!!

A truly engaging and passionate professor. The studio was demanding and expected a great deal from me, and I consistently felt challenged. However, I also feel that I grew the most in this studio precisely because of the rigor it required.

Very smart and passionate in her own right, but quite obsessive in her student's individual projects. Will say one thing and want another and will not defend you in front of the jurors even if they make a point on something that SHE recommended for YOUR design. Unrealistic expectations and run her section way more difficult than the other studios.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super intellectual and in her own mind. I am sure she had some brilliant thoughts, but she could not communicate them well. I question the validity of her position working with the level of students I was a part of, as she expected us to sacrifice a lot (eat, sleep, fun) to achieve a level in our work that she didn't even know if was possible.

This is the only instructor that I have had where studio is my least favorite class. She does not give good feedback, and has unrealistic expectations. She has no care for students at all. While her work is good and she is definitely smart, she does not know how to teach at all. She pushes her designs on everyone, and CANNOT communicate at all.

She really expects you to sleep for 4 hrs or less. She also expects you to be doing work at every hour of the day which is unrealistic. She wants to put pressure on students to make them better but she just does it in an unhealthy and harmful way to her students.

She has a great ability to connect. It is a great pleasure to have had her as an amazing instructor to link architecture to a struggling mind in concentration, and developing my own connection that will produce greater results in my future. Highly recommend her as she brings more students to light, who aren't quite there yet. Gives amazing advice.

She is extremely proud that she has taught at Harvard and hence claims she knows what she is doing. Pushes her design agenda without prompting students to think for themselves. Doesn't follow up with ideas and expects you to sleep for 4 hrs or less to thrive. She micromanages each line that is being drawn. Would definitely not recommend.

Great Professor, and very insightful and inspiring to learn about for topics in Biomedical Instrumentation.  Attendance is not mandatory, but content taught is not on slides. Picks project apart, make sure you choose the right topic, and get feedback before he grades. Could've been a bit more Canvas-savvy. No practice quizzes, likes design quizzes.

3 exams lowest dropped. 1) sig proc, 2) heart anatomy, 3) research design. Project is a lot of work, and Inan will pick your project apart, but has many office hours to get help before youre graded. Really nice and smart person. lectures cover stuff not on exams but you will benefit from going. ~3.7 GPA is accurate.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class as a BME with little circuit knowledge not knowing how circuit heavy it was. His lectures are taught at a very high level assuming you know alot of the terminology with op ams and filters. I would make friends with EE's in the class early and use chat gpt to look up concepts from this class and you should be fine.

I was EE that took this with BMEs. About 3 homeworks graded on a scale 1-4 (4100, 170) and weren't long (encouraged to work together on them)--got 4 on all. 3 Tests with lowest dropped: 1 EE, 1 BME, 1 design. Made 80, 59, 100 on them. DON'T SKIP LEC, exams fair but were drawn from HW/whiteboard. 50% project at end but report/effort more vital

ECE 4781 is tougher than 4782 but it is still a great class. I got an A by averaging 99 on exams, 100 on HW and an 80 on the project. He grades the projects harder and lowers your score if you pick the easier review project, but if you want to pass the class you don't need to put much work in. Still drops a test and HW, so don't worry about them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Inspirational

reviews.comment: One of my favorite profs at Tech. Only graded by 3 easy 100% HW's and the highest two test grades. The Group Project is 50% of the grade and is pretty time consuming, but not worse than what you've already done in the curriculum already. Class always ended 30min early and we still learned a lot of interesting material. More of a grad student class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fairly easy class. You need to study it on your own because the lectures are not very helpful. Pretty easy to learn, takes at most 2 hours a week if you skip the lectures. I only showed up on quiz days and went to recitation every week. Go to recitation, the TAs are great.
If you take this class, remember to breathe when it goes in.

So you can no longer not attend the 8am and self learn, she made the mini quizzes only accessible to those who attend her lectures...Her lectures are pointless, she brushes over actually important points, if you depend on her you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you ever have another option, please don't take her class. And if you don't, just take it another semester, LIFE IS NOT THAT DEEP. I honestly dont even k why she was hired in the first place, Let's just say she's not very good at explaining the material she teaches. All I can say is thank you to the TA for all the amazing work they did for her.

Just take CS1301 over the summer if you can't get a spot, lectures does not help, vague powerpoint, irrelevant examples, not accessible for question, her answers confuses student more(by making references to overly complicated topics), basically all self learn. A sweet person tho(?) she tells students to stay hydrated...
She acts like she is being tortured when she teaches.
She doesn't know the content.

While attendance is "mandatory" with daily reality checks, I would highly suggest just not ever showing up and only going to recitation. It's not worth it to wake up for an 8 am class when you'll end up learning more by going to office hours and recitation. Heavily relies on (the wonderful) TAs to actually teach.

While Kearse is not the best, you will do fine in her class if you do the work. TA's create all hw and exams, and grade them as well. Do not do the robotics lab, as you will struggle to reserve a robot and most TA's don't have experience with them to help you out. Labs and the final have extra credit.
The GOAT of CS 1301. Immediately switch to her class.

Firstly, do NOT take the robotics labs. They are unorganized and are beyond the classroom material. Second, the professor is inaccessible outside of class. Her teaching consists of reading outdated slides in a monotone, slow voice, as if reading them out loud makes the material understandable. I learned NOTHING in her class. Take someone else.

THIS WAS THE HARDEST CLASS I EVER TOOK IN MY LIFE not even because of the content but BECAUSE OF THE TEACHER. The tests are IMPOSSIBLE and she does not teach or explain the concepts properly. Unless you have had cs experience before DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS you WILL FAIL. The only thing that may save your grade is the homework and labs.

I rarely attended lectures since she mostly read directly from the slides. I suggest just learning on your own. The content wasn't hard, but dealing with her was. She rarely responded to emails and made it difficult to succeed. If possible, take a different professor. If you take her, choose the web dev focus over robotics for an easier class.
If she's your only option left, just wait for next semester and choose someone else. She relies too much on the TA's and you usually end up teaching yourself the material.

Nice person unfortunately lectures are not engaging. I learned most of the content through recitation, which is taught by the TAs who are amazing. However, coursework is very doable especially if you do not procrastinate the weekly homework, attend recitation, and review lecture/recitation slides outside of class.
Such a boring class and the professor just reads off the slides. You're better off just skipping and studying on your own.

She isn't even that bad she just isn't good. She's fast paced but I fear this is GT and it's going to be. An A is 100% possible as long as you DO NOT procrastinate. Her TAs are also not good so you're basically teaching yourself. Good luck and take advantage of extra credit on labs.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Doesn't deserve the hate. Very accessible after class for things like coding miniquizzes etc. I hadn't taken any python before and the class was tough at first but eventually doable making use of office hours and whatnot. Best piece of advice (though it doesn't relate to professor Kearse) is avoid the robotics lab track- not worth it at all.

She's very kind and understanding in office hours. Some of the reviews are a bit dramatic, but understandable. Most topics aren't explained very well and in comparison to other instructor's sections  it was definitely harder. DO NOT SKIP RECITATION the TAs will carry the course. If you want to pass take advantage of their help.

Tests aren't bad and there are a lot of points that are easy to get through homework and projects. Lecture was not really helpful, but she's not as bad of a professor as everyone says. TAs are super helpful for lab and homework errors, but learn the content on your own if you get her.

okay she's not thatt bad. but she's not great. if you ask questions you're not going to get that great of an answer or she'll give you a weird look. her lectures feel more like she's vaguely reviewing content rather than teaching it. i did have an issue with my lab 3 group and she was helpful and efficient with fixing it. just get a different prof.

weekly homeworks and biweekly quizzes. There is daily participation but you don't have to be in class to do it. The content itself is pretty easy and you can learn it on your own, and there is a lot of study materials. I didn't go to recitation very often and I did fine in the class.
just reads from ppts, doesn't really explain anything, reaches stuff outside syllabus, just confuses u more, will make you wanna die from courseload

I read these reviews at the beginning of the year scared because were so low but lowkey she wasn't that bad (at least not 1.6 star bad). I am just horrible at computer science which is why I didn't end up with the best grade but I would definitely just use the TA's and if you feel like your aren't learning in her lectures, just don't go.

Do what everyone else says and do not go to lectures, just recitation. Some of what she teaches is not even relevant to the class, and it feels like she doesn't really know what she's talking about at times. If you do the practice quizzes and go to recitation I feel like the class is an easy A.

Just let the TAs teach this class at this point

Gets her own questions wrong, HW is difficult, reads directly off of slides. If you get banished to this class, go to recitation for in person instruction. Tech and the CoC should be ashamed of themselves for letting unsuspecting freshmen register for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Graduated from Bowling Green State University for a reason. Has no understanding of CS. Calls "strings" as "str"s (like "stirs") and reads off the slides. Nobody comes to lectures, only reason anyone shows up is because of participation quizzes. I've punched a duck- figured illustration of her face in the Office Hours room at least 10 times. Hated.
Awful. Don't recommend.
Just do your work! She is not here to hold your hand. This is GT reality.

She's not mean like people say but not a great teacher. Avoid if you can but if you get her it's not the end of the world. Just do all the homeworks, don't do the robotics lab track. Start EARLY on labs because helpdesk gets incredibly crowded the week they're due.

I came into GT with no background CS. The tests were pretty difficult, and HW was time consuming, but the TA's were phenomenal. She was a boring lecturer and was extremely rude to her students on multiple occasions. I would highly recommend you take someone else.

GUYS Kearse is not a good teacher but that doesn't matter because you don't need her to teach you. Go to recitation.The TAs teach it all there, they write the quizzes, they give you answers to the homework and the quizzes. You learn everything from the TAs. You don't even have to go to class, you just take a quiz over class content for attendance.

I feel ike I would like the class a lot more if it were not for the fact that I had this teacher. While the class interests me, her teaching style is not it. Lots of presentation slides with little teaching. Very dismissive and is not easy to reason with. Mini quizzes that are due in the middle of class, not the end of the day, do not miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Over complicates the most basic things. TAKE ANYONE ELSE.
You will learn more by just looking it up.
She doesn't teach, just dont go to class
only realized this class should have been easy when I taught myself everything, the only C I've ever gotten and I took infinitely harder classes at Tech
If I had the option of having a potato teach me instead of her, I would take it, 100%.

kearse is extremely strict with grading/deadlines, but the class is very doable. TAs are phenomenal and readily available to help. it's not the end of the world to take this class, but i would suggest just taking 1301 if you can. i came in with 0 CS knowledge and ended with a 98, so you'll be fine

awful professor. doesn't know what she's talking about. often mean and rude when she's having a bad day and takes it out on students. actually made it harder to learn.

TA are life saviours. the only reason i knew what was going on.

Content is pretty simple, I could learn almost all of the stuff with the lecture slides and the recitation slides. Lectures are basically useless, and the professor is passive aggressive when you send her emails or ask questions. She is hard to get a hold of via email, and whenever she does get back to you, she is not helpful in the slightest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't that helpful and students struggled to get their questions answered during lecture. Homework was tedious but that's somewhat to be expected of a coding class.

Genuinely, the worst professor I have ever had. Lectures are horrible; she reads off the slides, and if someone has a question, she tells you to Google it. Such an unlikeable personality, too. She is so dismissive, and she does not know her own assignments at all. I am doing well in this class because of the TAs and recitation is VERY helpful.

The professor is dismissive, doesn't know her own assignments, & makes it more difficult. If you ask her a question she will leave you more confused than before and her lectures are essentially useless. The TA's are angels on this earth & know the homework and quizzes (GO TO RECITATION) way better than her. Without them everybody would be failing.

Let's be real, if you took this class, you've regretted it. The coursework isn't difficult, but it's hard to understand when her lectures are wrong and asking for clarification is useless. The TAs carry this class and might as well teach it, so go to recitation and skip class. Attendance isn't mandatory. HW every week and bi-weekly quizzes.

She made me question the sanities of the people who hired her, and it's interesting to me that my mother has a higher degree than her. Without the three TAs I bothered so much that we became friends, I would've ripped my hair out.

Lectures were not useful AT ALL. In a 120 ish people class, maybe only 10 show up to lecture, and even if you go, you learn so much more from the TAs at recitation. Because the content is easy, it's not too difficult to end with an A or a B, but lots of homework and projects because of the format of the class.
Kearse is such a bad teacher, but if you read the slides on your own and go to TA office hours, you'll be fine.
I never wore my seatbelt while driving to school because i wanted to die before making it to her class.

Very poor lecturer. Lectures are basically pointless and not informative. Online attendance checks that change all the time. TA office hours are the only way to get through this class. Biweekly quizzes, weekly homeworks, and a final exam. Really don't know how she hasn't been fired yet. Different professor in the summer you should take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She doesn't seem to understand Python at all and just recites what's written on the slides. I'm sure she knows Python to an extent, but not able to actually apply it to anything. For example, when someone asks a comprehensive question, she has no idea how to respond and directs it to the TAs. Try to take someone else!

She's not as bad as people say, you'll be fine. Not the best lecturer, but if you go to recitations for quiz reviews, it's an easy A. Quizzes were identical to recitation reviews NOT practice quizzes. Just cram the night before. Do homework during TA office hours, you'll finish in like 1–2 hours. Chill class overall. Attendance is not enforced.

She is not great at teaching, I stopped going to class about 1/4 way through the semester, and just did the participation quizzes on my own. My time was better spent teaching myself the content, as she spent a whole class barely going over what I could teach myself in 10 minutes. She doesn't know the content that she is teaching either.

The class itsself was pretty easy, as long as you can follow the sequence the code is not too bad. However, she is an awful teacher. Reads straight from the slideshow and does not explain anything, if you ask her a question she just reads what she can from the slide and maybe calls on a TA to answer for her. Is really annoying and aggressive too.

Reads straight off the slides, without explanation. Often cancels class for "Digital Learning Days." Assigns large homework assignments. Work on these as early, they will take time, but are graded easily. The quizzes aren't bad. The TAs and Chat GPT taught me everything in this course. Make sure to do participation assignments.

CS1315 was known to be the easier of the two classes Dr. Kearse teaches, and I would agree lecture material itself is not difficult. However, the lectures were utterly useless, with sometimes incorrect information and teaching directly off the slides. If you can go to recitations, absolutely do. The TAs saved this class for me personally.

How she was able to get this position is beyond me. For a introductory python course, she did little to actually teach the material. In class, she often got her own miniquiz questions wrong. She taught for 30 minutes without realizing she was reteaching the previous lecture. When asked questions her response was to ask chatGPT. Tests were dumb.

This class was so easy if you go to recitation, I went to class like once a month for the downloads. Showing up to class actually made me understand less than if I looked over the slides on my own. She messed up her own in class examples sometimes.

The lectures are not helpful because a lot of times the teacher didn't know what she was talking about, and the majority of lectures involved her reading directly from the slides. The TAs are the only reason this class was doable. If you have never taken CS this class would be hard. The content isn't horrible but the teacher just doesn't teach.

She doesn't really know what she is talking about during lectures and they are not very interesting. When I attended another professor's lectures, I learned way more. I went back to her lecture and I got confused. Don't take.
She just read off the slides and was mad when no one understood anything she said.
Only read off the slides. I had a better experience learning python on YouTube.
Terrible Professor, Lectures were very uninspired and boring, essentially had to try and self teach the entire course to myself

I don't think she knows how to code python outside of basic technical stuff. There were a lot of errors on her slides. Not to mention she only reads off the slides. Shes not really teaching anything at this point, I basically learned everything by reading the textbook. Don't bother going to class except for quizzes. The TA's were really helpful.

She's clueless about Python. Bugs on slides that she REFUSES to admit clearly shows she doesn't code Python outside of lectures at all. If you have a decent CS background, don't even frustrate yourself with correcting a lecturer who doesn't know what amortized big-O is. Class ran by TAs, who are clueless, but at least admit. Test out if you can.
Good thing she teaches easy material and has good TAs because without them, we would all surely fail the class. While she is very nice, her explanation of concepts is lacking.

She only reads off of the slides which have mistakes in them a lot of the time. The content of this class is pretty easy to learn by yourself so if you have her its not the end of the world. Her class is being saved by the TAs. Everytime I asked her a question, she would point me to the TAs. She doesn't really know what she's talking about.

Easy class, especially if you have any foundational CS experience. However, the professor has no idea what she's talking about and just reads off the slides. She says many things in lectures that are wrong. I'd still take her class again if it fit my schedule, as you can just read the lecture slides on your own to learn the content.
I can't decide which is more incredible: the fact that she thinks she's qualified to teach or the fact that someone at CoC agreed and decided to let her teach.

Avoid at all costs. 
No point in going to lecture - she will just tell you somehing wrong that the TAs will correct later in recitations. This class was so bad I almost switched out of my major to avoid taking more CS, because she's managed to make the subject intolerable. The fact that she has a job made me lose faith in Tech's integrity.

I would say that she is a kind person but very bad at teaching/lecturing... she's not particularly good at answering questions in class and tends to go through the slides way too quickly and when she does go through the lecture notes, she just reads off of them and doesn't explain. I had to learn everything for this class on my own in the CS lab.
I don't know where to start. I think my knowledge of computer science decreased over this semester. PLEASE FOR YOUR OWN SAKE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.

AVOID HER IF YOU CAN. She's not a good professor; she just reads off the slides and doesn't properly explain the code. Not to mention, if you answer a question incorrectly in class she's kinda condescending about it. If she's your only option for this class, I'd say you're better off waiting till a later semester to get it done.

Probably the worst lecturer of all time. You are better off doom-scrolling on TikTok than attending irettas class. Her teaching style consists of reading of the slides, and having no idea what she is talking about. The only way to get a good grade in this course is by going to TA office hours and workshops. It baffles me she is an actual professor.

With absolutely no exaggeration, she was horrible. Her test averages were consistently much lower than the other professors and I don't think she knew the content. Would make mistakes and get called out by students just to ignore them and act like she was right, despite her code erroring. The TAs knew what they were doing but she definitely did not

Whoever rates this woman above a 2 (AT MOST) either has prior experience or has a lot of outside help. No one's being harsh or exaggerating. No one's blaming her for a bad grade. teaching isnt her thing. there were multiple times duringlecture where she would get her own code wrong. lectures are really just her saying things. she is a cool person just not a good prof. i do not give her credit for my grade class is passable no thanks to her. course itself isnt too bad. take advantage of the TA's and knack and youll b good

Ms. Kearse is a lovely woman one on one and she is very kind to students. That goes to say, I unfortunately would NEVER take her class again. Quizzes constantly had mistakes, TA's did most of the work, and she is very monotone when lecturing. I hope she changes her teaching methods or GT finds a more suitable teacher for 1315.

Professor Kearse was a decent professor, though sometimes uses overly technical language. Overall the course material was simple enough, and you can definitely succeed in this class with very little effort. She was nice and taught the very simple material relatively well. The TA's are also really helpful.

she used a for loop to sum a list of numbers instead of using sum()
kinda summarizes the whole class experience

I took this section because it was at a better time than the other one and boy was that a mistake. Listen to the reviews. Do not take this section. She's nice one on one, but mean in class and she will not answer any of your questions (I don't think she knows the answers). She writes code on the board that literally errors wish I was kidding

Terrible lecturer just reads off the slides and poorly explains the coding process. The TAs saved my grade and were very helpful with homework and quiz review. Definitely go to recitations especially before quizzes. I went to most lectures but honestly didn't learn much from them. I would recommend another professor if you want an easier experience

Terrible. Take the online class with Joyner! She is harsh, completely unyielding, and a terrible teacher. It's clear she has no idea what she is doing, and she makes what should be a fairly straightforward class 10x harder. There are no chances to make up exams, and good luck getting an exemption. No grade replacement/drop opportunities either.

nothing special. class is boring but material is relatively straightforward and self-teachable. lectures are uninspiring and boring, i honestly dont know why i keep going to class. quizzes every other week are annoying and lengthy homework is harshly graded for no reason. if you have a brain you should be able to pass easily with an A or B.

Literally a horrible professor. Class was so pointless because the TAs make all the hw/quizzes/final. Never went to lecture, the TAs are AMAZING for this class though (8 of them) and they are the only reason I got an A. If you go to office hours weekly you will be fine, but don't expect to learn anything in her lecture.

Absolute worst professor I have ever taken. She reads directly off the slides, does not teach, and when she does do a practice problem, she gets them wrong about half of the time?!? The TAs are also clueless. So much work, such a terrible professor. DO NOT RECOMMEND if you enjoy happiness.

Lengthy homeworks every week, timed quizzes every other week, and overall a very unpleasant woman. I had to stop paying attention to lecture halfway through the semester because she only confused me more. Honestly not the best professor. If I don't play my cards right, I may end up having to retake the class. She is not very good at explaining. this professor is horrid, she is not understanding of mistakes, no partial credit ever, no dropped hw or quizzes despite having long hws due each week and quizzes every other week. Never really understood much because most of the stuff was not explained well at all. She also redid the same lecture, and didn't realize it.

Learned more staring at a wall than I did in all of this persons lectures combined. It could be that she might excel in another coding language, but if you have this teacher for intro matlab you should resort to using the help desks and videos of other lecturers.

Worst professor I had that semester. Was not good at teaching and was VERY condescending and rude that I almost cried in her class because of her. she yelled at me one time for having my laptop.... in a comp sci course.... so I never went to her lectures again and still somehow learaned more than when I did.

I had this professor in Fall 2023 and she was the worst. She was not good at teaching, and I basically relied on the TAs to review the content and I basically taught myself. Fire her.
