reviews.comment: Impossible to find outside of lectures, would always be late to office hours. Homework did not relate to the test content at all. The only way to get through the tests is to go to TA led office hours and review sessions. Attendance not mandatory but does canvas quizzes for credit.

Kearse isn't the best professor, but she does answer questions well during office hours. Honestly, lectures aren't really necessary for this course, the notes and homework are enough to prepare you for the tests, especially if you have previous CS class experience. A lot of students ended up attending Kantwon's lecture in our semester.
Lectured so bad I had to visit health services for the brain cells I lost.
This is the teacher you want. Homework can be hard but

Great lecturer and clearly understood fluid mechanics very well. Approached each concept from different POVs  and had fair tests/quizzes. The grading scheme is kinda scary though and weights exams/quizzes to be 85% of the overall grade, with each of the two 20-minute quizzes being 12.5% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't really need to go to class because she uploads her notes which are very detailed. Exams are also very similar to the practices to the point where you know what kind of problems/concepts are going to be on the test beforehand. Very lenient with grading.

You need to go to recitation to learn things. The content isn't hard, but she overcomplicates everything. Her tests aren't hard as long as you go to recitation and practice the homeworks. It is very consistent. As a teacher, I wouldn't take her though because it is obvious she doesn't really care about her students' learning experience.

he's a nice guy but the pacing was too fast, a bit hard to follow, and he didn't really prepare you for the exams too well. i ended up watching cuyler warnock's recordings instead. very open to questions and accessible though.

Great at answering questions, clearly cares about the material. Can be hard to understand at times, skips over certain processes, rushes through content. Make sure to ask questions if you don't understand, and read the textbook before class as that is one thing that proved helpful.
Overall not a respectful professor
just take literally anyone else

He was a kind soul, but his accent was pretty heavy. A majority of the class ended up attending other professors' lectures. In the grand scheme of things, your linear grade will likely be the same since everyone takes the same exams. He's a decent lecturer. Oftentimes, he ends up rambling/stuttering, but he is always down for questions.

Lectures were rather proof and example based rather then going through how to actually solve problems in practice and intuition. Professor does make himself available before and after class to answer questions. Would rather recommend reading the textbook then going to lectures as he goes a bit fast.

Dr. Belegradek is a great lecturer whose passion for mathematics shows, with dense but interesting lectures. He is accessible and will happily slow down to help your understanding. The syllabus is fair and ensures that you can get a good grade in the class if you put in the effort. Not the easiest course, but he makes sure you will learn a lot.

Professor Igor is always eager to help you out and will respond quickly to any questions on piazza or email, and cares about the success of his students. Lectures can be a little scattered, but he makes sure to emphasize main points. I would recommend Linear Algebra Done Right by Axler to peruse throughout the semester alongside his notes.

The course is tough but all of the resources are there to do well. I primarily self-studied using his wonderfully written "detailed course notes" since I found the lectures a bit all over the place. He is extremely accessible and making use of this is the key to passing the course. Do not stay confused, put matters into you own hands!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework was once a week and difficult, but only 1-3 problems. Decent lecturer; nothing exceptional, but prepares you very well for quizzes and exams. Sometimes quizzes will expect you to have specific equations on your cheat sheet, but he typically emphasizes what's important for exams during lecture and on canvas. Very available for office hours.

Any hate on professors for the structure of this class is unwarranted. This is a known weed out class that is super inflated. As for Igor, super sweet dude but his accent is incredibly hard to understand and his teaching style will not help you succeed. Just watch Sal Borone's online lectures unless you understand thick accents and proofy lectures.
EXTREMELY HARD TO UNDERSTAND. He responds fast to emails tho lmao
Horrible Teacher

This class was fascinating, but the professor ruined the subject for me. The homeworks and tests were made so hard to the point of not being able to comprehend what the questions were asking. The professor was inaccessible outside of lecture, none of which helped past a rudimentary level with preparing for the homeworks and tests.

The absolute worst experience I've had with a professor so far. I barely scraped out an A and I put as much time into this one class as I did all others combined. He barely covered the material tested on and all averages were below a C. Comments on homework were either missing or irrelevant. Ignored requests for clarification or help.

prof was very accessible outside of class. this class is tough but if you are systematic and put in work, you will be fine. ASK questions and don't allow yourself to stay confused. if you take this prof., you have to be ready to take action when you get lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Belegradek is a solid choice. Not great, but far from the worst. Dedicated to really making sure you understand the material and is very blunt about it. The grading is very fair and consistent. 85+ to get an A.

The exams and homework that Igor gives are very well designed. They are rewarding to complete and truly strengthen your understanding of linear algebra at a conceptual level. In office hours, Igor gives as much guidance as possible while still allowing you to make the essential insights that deepen your understanding.

Linear algebra can be its own difficult thing. Igor tends to teach the proof side of things and can be hard to hear at times. I personally attended every lecture and just went on my phone (only looking up when he would say something I didn't know). Please do all of the review materials and attend your studio. Also, it is essential to read.

Although his accent may be tough to understand, approachable outside class. Would recommend not skipping lecture although reading the textbook will put you back up to speed. Belegradek usually curves his class, but with the coronavirus pandemic, an insignificant curve was provided. Is passionate and cares about his students, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Igor knows the subject of linear algebra well and conveys it in-depth to his students. He was open to questions during lectures and accessible outside of them as well. The tests were difficult but fair and based on the homework. He was accomodating during Spring 2020 with a take-home midterm and optional final. Phenomenal professor!

This class will require to do work, but the teacher is really nice and fair. Understanding when you ask for extensions or being excused, helpful in office hours, and a good amount of homework and test difficulty is not hard because of it. Igor really cares, sending me emails which helped me not miss finals (online due to COVID), which is nice.
He is a very responsible professor and replies to emails quickly. The content of this course is not difficult. However, it spends time to understand his accent
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fair grader and releases practice problems that are helpful for the tests. Be sure to sit near the front of the lecture hall as his accent can be hard to decipher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Igor is a fair grader, and I guess he's an alright lecturer, not always the clearest explainer. Sit towards the front of the lecture hall because he's kinda difficult to hear. He also has a fairly thick accent, definitely not impossible to understand, but I had trouble understanding him during 8am lectures. Fair grading scale. 85+ is an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Belegradek can get a little bit confusing during lectures but is always willing to answer questions and really cares to make sure that all of his students fully understand the material in the end. If you make the effort to ask him questions and go to his office hours, you will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Igor Belegradek makes sure we really understand the concepts in Linear Algebra instead of just doing computations. The tests are highly conceptual but these tests are based on the practice problems he releases before the test. He always answers questions on Piazza in a detailed and specific manner. Best Math Professor I have ever had.
Igor's style of teaching is difficult to grasp at first, but if you put the time into the class, you will do well. Practice problems and reading the textbook are key to doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It certainly felt impossible to succeed. I skipped lecturesarned through recitations, tutoring, and the textbook. Practice problems are given out before each exam that mimic questions on exam-if you have ALL answers to these problems, you are solid. Obtaining sufficient answers to theory questions is easier said than done; Piazza is a life saver

DO NOT TAKE HIM!!! He is horrible at teaching. He doesn't respect you at all. When you ask him a question he just quotes the syllabus or tells us to look at the syllabus. He has a strong accent and is hard to understand even though I speak his language. He is to fast and the exams our way to theoretical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Igor was a horrible teacher in that his entire lecture philosophy seems to be based off of two key "facts" - that everyone comes into the class with a background in linear algebra (not necessarily true) and that people understand what he his saying. He is both fast-paced and unclear and makes tons of mistakes in lectures. Take virtually anyone else

Belegradek has a pretty thick accent that takes some getting used to. TAs can be hit or miss for the class. Lectures are organized and informative, but the textbook is easier to understand. Weekly quizzes and homeworks were easy. Tests are typically 20 points over 7 questions, but grading is fair. A is an 85%, B is 70% and so on.

Has an accent and is very hard to understand in lecture. Tests all all theoretical (given this, prove why... ), and he gives easy online homework that takes up a good chunk of the grade. An okay class and professor, but you may find yourself learning it all out of the textbook.

Homeworks are easy. Igor has an accent but is still understandable. Quiz every recitation, pretty straightforward, totally hit or miss though, dropped bottom 3 so it was fine. Tests are all theory and he teaches the class like an honors class according to my TA. Very approachable for office hours. Reading textbook can almost substitute for lectures

He's a very smart person, and he knows his linear algebra, but he isn't the greatest teacher. His lectures are difficult to understand and he cannot engage his students. His tests are also difficult, it's largely based on theory.

Be prepared to teach yourself linear algebra. If you have a hard time understanding a Russian accent, skip lecture. Plus side of the class is getting to use crib sheets during the test and final. Take another professor if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Belegradek is a really good teacher who tries his very best to make sure his students are actually learning. The homework takes up to ten minutes every week, he gives out questions before quizzes and tests and usually asks similar ones on the tests. His accent is a little problematic but it's not that big a deal. Grades are curved, 85 is A.

Weekly quizzes on ungraded HW and MyMathLab enforce learning. Tests are straight-forward, and based on the HWreview sheet but can be tough even so. Russian accent forces you to concentrate to follow the lecture. Attendance helps understanding- Igor is very enthusiastic about the material. Grades were slightly curved at the end: 85  A, 70  B, etc
If you take the limit of this guy's awesomeness, it goes to "Infiniteh."

Igor has a great sense of humor, but has a thick Russian accent that may be hard to understand for some people (although not the case for me). My TA was baller so I was ok with the class. Advice: do hw (although optional for the class), and ask questions during lectures or recitation on HW problems you did not understand.
Good class, he just changes numbers from practice test for actual test, plus lets you bring sheets of notes to test

The material was very understandable once it was explained by a great tutor. The professor is completely ineffective as a teacher, his heavy accent and writing make him impossible to follow. He also confuses even himself during lecture, not to mention all the students, he makes very simple concepts and theorems seem inexorably complex.

Got an A. Good teacher. You get a front and back cheat sheet each exam and two on the final. Provides practice tests online and basically just changes the numbers a bit of the actual tests. Not a difficult Calc 2 class at all.

Hey was bad, I'm not going to lie but there were great curves and the TA's were fantastic so I came away with a very good grade. Take him, but do so knowing there will be a lot of study on your own. Another good thing about him is that you can use a cheat sheet on the tests so you can write important equations.

Jumps all over the place, with no organization. I had a hard time understanding him, much less, learning the material. He curves quite a bit since everyone fails the tests. Its a difficult class, but not impossible. Hey, I passed it

Horrible professor, one of the worst, if not the worst one I have ever had at tech.  His lectures are useless because he is hard to understand and he jumps all over the board with his example.  I passed the class, but learned very little.
I did good in the class, but not because of the teacher...he is the worst teacher I have had at Georgia Tech, take anybody but him for diff eq.

One of the worst professors I've had at Tech.  His lectures are very unclear and he is hard to understand when he talks.  Tests were very difficult with averages as low as the 50s.  He was forced to have massive curves.  Don't take this class if you want to learn anything.
Dr. James Thomas Stroud is a great lecturer and cool guy. As long as you show up to class and pay attention, BIOS 2300 is a breeze.
Dr. Stroud is a highly engaging and effective professor who is very caring about his students. Loved his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Why does he not have a 5/5? This is the easiest science class I've ever taken at Tech; so fair and so fun to be in. I've learned a lot but haven't lost any sleep over this class, and Dr. Stroud is a fantastic professor who cares about us and is clearly passionate about ecology. Do not listen to the one/two bad reviews bro.
Very chill guy, loves to talk about his research. Tests are all written but manageable if you do the practice exams.
Professor Stroud is a decent professor, but the exams are graded so much harder than needed. You have to give the exact answers he is looking for and the exams are weighted a lot.
Grade is composed mostly of exams. Exams are graded so harshly and there is no cushioning.

Super engaging professor and talks a lot about his own research and other research at Tech. As long as you can validly explain your answer you'll get credit. In-class activities are really helpful for test-prep, and he drops 6 (so you can miss 6 free classes). Grading scheme is pretty test-heavy, but the tests are all written so grading is fair.

Professor is really nice and cares a lot about the students. He also does not accept any bs from his students and believes you should put in 110% work. He cares A LOT about ecology and genuienly passionate about his work. He is tough grader and he looks very specific answers which is sometimes difficult to figure out during a test.

You'll see a lot of 1 star reviews on here: students (myself included) panicked after Test 2 when the average was a 28. Since then, there's been a dramatic turnaround, as he was very open to student feedback, with generous policies and restructured tests. He is a caring person, and I expect his grading to improve as he becomes accustomed to GT.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For the first half of the semester, I resented Dr. Kim and thought I was cooked. You'll come to find, however, that he takes student feedback very well, is quite caring, and will adjust accordingly. He won't just let his entire class fail. He's very new, learning like the rest of us, and needs to be cut some slack. He's funny, smart and reasonable.

The first two tests were completely unfair and diabolically difficult beyond reasonable expectations for this level, but Dr. Kim adjusted well by the third. Great remediation opportunities and CIOS bonus for grade replacement. I think in future semesters he will be a great option. He takes feedback, he is kind, and he cares about us. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hard class and very test heavy, but he is very flexible and willing to adapt. He's a funny and nice guy.

reviews.comment: I initially rated Dr. Kim lower because his exams were very hard and 85% of the course grade. Most people did bad on them, specifically the second exam, but Dr. Kim responded well to these set backs. He provided remediations for 50% points on our exams for every exam and he provided an insane final exam replacement incentive!

Justin Kim is such a wholesome guy. He is so caring and wants to see his students succeed. But the tests were impossible. However, he understands when there is an issue and provides test corrections and curves when needed.  Next sem will be better
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just for context the bad ratings on here are from Exam 2 which had an average of ~30%. He's a caring prof and he gave us remediation for every exam and bonus points. This class is obvi a hard class so the low averages aren't surprising but he acknowledged that his exams were too hard and made the next ones easier to meet the needs of the class.

The first 2 exams felt harder than what was covered in class. Initial rigor was high. However Dr Kim has been very adaptable this semester and actively trying to adjust his material/exams to be digestible by students. The third exam was much more doable. He wants his students to succeed, is a funny lecturer, and is not as bad as my peers have said.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Justin Kim does not understand that his head writing is not good. It is impossible to use his lecture material due to his handwriting. Every student should get a Free A because this class has been a mess.

I think Professor Kim is very nice and smart. However, his grading scheme sucks for such a difficult class. reviews.comment: This is a weed out course, but there is a difference between difficult and down right impossible. Only giving a 2 since he's offering remediation and changes for exam 3.

reviews.comment: Guys! The class average for the second exam was a 31 OUT OF 110 with the highest grade as an 82. I don't know why we're suddenly rating him high?!?!?

reviews.comment: Despite his sternness and high expectations, Justin Kim is a hardworking professor. During class he always makes sure to point out a few test-relevant mechanisms and even adds some nerdy humor. His exams are rigorous but fair... Orgo 2 is a weed-out course. If you read the book when concepts aren't clear, you'll be just fine.

While this professor is extremely difficult and expects a lot of us, I appreciate his ability to take feedback and adjust the course to help. The first two tests have been pretty bad, but he created a method of remediation to get points back. I do believe his expectations are too high but if he continues to adjust I think we can finish strong.

Good lecturer, smart guy. He has bad ratings because the first two exams were way too hard, but hes super receptive to feedback and has altered the course structure multiple times to help us now. Hes a new prof learning what works and adjusting accordingly, I think hes okay now because hes new but will be better in future, again, very receptive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
What can I even say?

Much more difficult/less forgiving than other Orgo II professors here. 85 percent of the grade is made up of tests, whose difficulty is off the charts. Unforgiving exam structure, and despite revisions being offered, it doesn't change the class's structure.

Complete lack of teaching ability and an even more extreme gap between what he believes he is teaching and the content that appears on the exam. this class actually exceeded the limits of my anxiety medication. Ochem 1 class was less work and I took the  self-study course. sad sad sad

reviews.comment: I had to withdraw from this class. He is one of the worst professors at Tech and needs to be fired. this is just sad.

He thinks he's the best and smartest professor, but his handwriting is illegible , gives hard exams even though I averaged 3 hours of sleep each night because I'm studying, not really helpful, doesn't take criticism and requests.

He's a nice dude, would be great for grad students who already know the material. With 85% of your grade being exams, and 15% being accuracy based problem sets, there is no padding to your grade. Exams are extremely difficult and at a level of difficulty that should have a crib sheet and are not representative of resources given in class.

The exams are unfair. The lectures are not worth going to because they don't relate to the exam content and the professors hand writing is not legible. The professor has these handouts that he claims are the greatest thing since slice bread, however the professors hand writing is unreadable.

Do not take this professor. Exams were unreasonable and an incredibly high portion of the grade. I studied for over 30 hours for the most recent exam and left with half the problems blank. He is not an enjoyable professor to have, and I would not recommend him in any form or fashion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unfair exams, not like review materials
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Kim forgets that we're learning new material for the 1st time, with our previous knowledge of Chem 2311 being so far back. No amount of feedback and critiques would ever change his mind because of his ego. Apparently he went to prestigious colleges, so he thinks he's the smartest and greatest of mankind. He's not! Opposite actually.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim's exams felt significantly harder than the practice materials, making it difficult to prepare effectively. After the first exam, where the class average was very low, the review session felt somewhat tense and not very supportive. I believe when more than 115 students are below a 50, we must reconsider our methods.

I did every single practice problem available (400+ online WileyPlus questions), textbook problems, practice tests, PLUS session practice problems, problem sets, material review, and STILL did not recognize anything on the exam. Miserable experience, I would not take this prof if you can avoid it. I will probably end up dropping this class.

(in-person).This professor does not know how to lecture. Constant complaints about his volume, teaching style, and messy handwriting. Exams are difficult and he's not forgiving. He needs to be reported to the dean for how he is lecturing the course and grading. Entirely self study, but if I wanted self study, I would have chosen an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The criteria for doing well in this class is not at all clear. I lost a lot of points on reports because of unclear grading criteria. You only have to go to lab ~6 times per semester though, with 4 lab reports (25% of your grade). These take a lot of time. The lectures were incoherent and slow, but you also only have 4 of those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Snoozefest! He may be an emeritus prof, but he can't really teach or use technology. Stopped going to class after about a week. Lab reports are graded using a rubric and are very time consuming. Expect each to take 10-15 hours of time. They are tediously graded and the TA's are strict about including specific things. Suck it up and get it done.

Lectures are unclear and unhelpful. Grading was highly ambiguous, subjective, and nit-picky (TAs' fault primarily). Course schedule is structured poorly so if you're in section X you'll have weeks of back-to-back lab reports that are extraordinarily time intensive. Responses on Piazza are vague and conflicting, if you even get one.

This is one of the worst classes I've taken at this school. The lab manuals are incredibly unclear, and the course has major organization issues. The TAs will take points off for things that are clearly in your report, and you won't ever get a report back before the next one is due, meaning you will make the same mistakes over and over.

Dr. Jagoda: course professor. The real reason I'm here is the trash TA's. We had 3 labs: 25%, 40%, and 25% (10% notebook). They couldn't correctly grade if someone moved their fingers for them. Had to put infinite regrade requests for things that were blatantly correct if you took a few seconds to read the reports. Over a month to get grades back.

This class is basically the lab course, and you meet a couple times per semester to go over the next lab. Class is kinda messy (one of our four labs got entirely canceled due to timing issues yay) but not difficult. The labs are graded easy, and are pretty much busy work but also a little fun.

This teacher was good; I saw him like 5 times total. This lab class is not hard, but the grading can be rough if you do not follow the rubrics to a T. Want advice? Separate 15 hours per lab report (four total, 25% each) and read EXACTLY as the rubric says. They are grading if you include everything. Class is only about the writing, not the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AE 2610 is not supposed to be a hard lab class, but with Jagoda, the lectures were extremely boring, and the labs anything but clear. Would definitely not recommend taking with him if you have the choice. During lecture, most of the class was either asleep or doing other work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely poor management of the class, obviously did not care about teaching this intro class. Never once taught his own lecture. Lab materials were poorly written and contradictory, with huge penalties for errors made as a result. This class that is supposed to be very easy became a nightmare of guessing at what the lab handbook actually wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Obviously has no interest in teaching this class, is barely even present at class and relies entirely on TAs to teach. The TAs don't know what they're doing, and the documentation for the labs is so bad that it conflicts with itself, causing you to miss data collection that is required in the reports but not listed in the procedure.

Maybe the best professor I have had. AE2010 is a very hard class, but he is an excellent teacher. He grades the tests himself and is very understanding with partial credit. If you make a dumb mistake but clearly understand how to do the problem, he will give full credit. If you do and understand the homework, you will do well on the tests.

After the first lecture you will be in despair because Jagoda is not a great lecturer. But he is the most caring prof in Tech, all you have to do is talk to him outside of class. He meets with you anytime (even sundays) and as long as you reach out, he will spend as much time as needed 1v1 till you understand it. In short - TALK TO HIM !!

The class was definitely difficult and he isn't the best lecturer, but he's super accessible outside of class. He's always willing to help and I've found he's a lot better at explaining concepts one-on-one. Definitely would recommend talking to him in office hours, he's really nice.

Lectures are not his strong suit. Hes somewhat hard to understand at times and just used slideshows that dont always make much sense. Attending recitations is definitely a must. His class is graded on a really generous curve of around 20% and he grades the homework and exams super leniently. You definitely have to put in the work to study though.

Wow this guy is bad. Lectures were from slides that he didn't make and most of the time were just long derivations with no explanation. There was no way to reference the textbook from his lectures. Overall course grade was never available, just had to guess. Not sure if he graded on a curve even though the class average was around a 65. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sometimes hard to hear, but great professor and lecturer. He will go out of his way to help students that ask for it. Tests were not easy, but were pretty fair
Overall definitely learned a lot, and liked how he taught the last sections. Only complaint is that lectures don't align with the homework, and neither align with exams as much as you would hope.

Ok lecturer but doesn't answer questions properly. Grading is mostly decided by grad ya for lab records and project. The exams have a lot of multiple select questions (mcqs). Overall fine course content. But not the best professor.

Lecture once a week for 50 minutes then 40% of your grade is determined by 2 tests whose questions are derived mainly from the content on the lab readings or from a derivative of them. Many of the test questions are meant to trick you which tests your knowledge very poorly. Prof's communicationu is lacking.
It's his first time living too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is well designed, although the labs are really not worth that many points considering how much effort goes into them. The professor is the bad part of the class. Really just unnecessarily rude, unclear and excessively preachy regarding his philosophy of teaching. Some of the assignments are graded very oddly also. Easy enough class still
Teaching level does not match how he grades

He is remarkably pedantic and rude. It's impossible to get any information from him; to date I haven't seen him answer a question on Piazza with something that wasn't a cryptic question or a rude comment. It's an easy class thats well designed, if a lot of work.

This is the worst class I have ever taken at GT. For a class that requires 8 labs (half of which take 8+ hours to complete) there is no reason why exams should be weighted 40%. There is also a group project worth 20% of your grade during the final week of classes. Project requires insane amount of work.
setup and hold time does not happen

Not a bad class content wise. You learn a lot of stuff that is useful for digital electronic design. The main issues with the class is that there are so many assignments that make up your grade and that all written assignments are graded strictly. Not a bad lecturer but doesnt clarify doubts properly. Exam are somewhat difficult as well.

Labs and final project take wayyy too much time for a 2 credit hour class. Exams are just random trivia from the prelab reading. Deadlines are set up so the prelab reading quiz is due a week before the actual lab as we are actively doing another lab.

For a lab design class the grading is extremely heavy on tests. For only being a 2 credit hour class Kevin expects too much studying / prep for these tests on top of all the time already spent for labs. Furthermore, everything is graded extremely harshly for little to no reason.
Sometimes we are asked to get good at something we have no talent for, or we excel at something we will never have the opportunity to prove.

ECE 2031 is a very interesting class. It is only two credit hours, however, one should not expect that amount of time to be spent on it. Kevin is quite rude, and grading policies are harsh, often without potential for partial credit.
it seems like kevin puts all of his teaching effort into making this course less fun.

He's decent, but the way this class is, the lecture's more of a hassle than helpful. Lab is WAY too structured, didn't feel like I'd learnt from the ground-up, more so just getting an answer and moving on to the next check-off. After a few labs, it gets better, as you can't rly study for this class since this isn't a traditional lecture-first class

Kevin is the only professor for this required class. He isn't as bad as everyone says, but still he is very detail orientated for assignments and for a 2 credit hour class there is a lot of work. Content wise very simple, but tests often cover very niche things which make it hard to study for. Make sure u do your pre lab asap and the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Labs are pretty time heavy, exams are basically tests of trivia, and the group project is pretty awful if you're put with people who don't care. Don't really feel like I learned too much overall.

Honestly not a bad intro course, but I feel like my thinking skills as an engineer aren't improved, but rather, forced. If you're a CS major taking this course, you will be fine, half of this course is an easier version of CS 2110 anyway.

Ngl this class isn't as bad as people say it is. No more pre lab quizzes. Some of the labs (breadboard ones) are time-consuming but most of them are really useful for developing hands-on skills. However the weekly lectures are kinda pointless since the material is covered in the lab manual.
kev is lowk chill and the content isnt that hard but exams r 78% so u need a high test avg
Kevin Johnson actively stifles creativity and innovation in his classes.

Pretty poorly designed course. Labs typically take 8-10 hours. Wish we had more time to digest the content, as it's actually interesting content. Exams are odd. Very poorly phrased questions and pretty subjective. Doesn't make sense for a 2 credit class to have 8 labs, and 2 exams, and a group project. It seems like too much for the credits

The class is tedious for 2 credit hours. The labs were manageable. Projects were fun with a good group. Worst are the tests, with review material being outdated(past exams), and each accounting for 20% of the grade (2) with no final. The material for said tests was random from all 150+ pages of the past 5~ labs and hard to study for.

Took for 2031, class just has a ton of work for a two credit course. Two Midterms, 8 Labs, a Final Project, and weekly small check-in homeworks is a lot to deal with when you go in assuming "6 hours per week" of work. Johnson is fine, he's very technical and picky, only 1 lecture/week so he doesn't impact the course experience that much.

Asks too many stuff just for a 2 credit class. Test questions are based on your understanding on the lab. Has lab every week with lectures which are useless. He needs to change the structure of the course.
This course is designed as 2 credit hours because they want you to have a lower deduction on gpa after getting a B/C.

Lab reports are graded harshly by your lab GTA so I'd ask for feedback before turning it in. The lab quizzes at the start of every section tested some obscure stuff. Instructions for the project worth 20% were incredibly vague. He comes off as condescending when answering questions bc he doesnt want to just "give you the answer" so hes vague :/

For a 2-credit hour class, the amount of work is absurd. Test prep material is non-existent (on 2nd exam he basically say to review everything). Even though lab work is fun, the lab report is taken way too serious and grading was harsh, which tbh depend on your GTA. Attendance is 5% and basically just a content review.
Take the class if you enjoy guessing. If not, DON'T TAKE IT, though I know you cannot avoid this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
RUN!!! 
RUN FAST !!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Quizzes and exam is filled with gotcha questions - doesn't really test your knowledge, just your memory. Really nitpicky grading with the lab reports and just too much work for a 2-credit course. He's not a terrible person but I am certainly feeling relieved that this is the last I'll ever have him as a lecturer - his responses can be condescending

Terrible professor. Condescending on Piazza and laughs in your face if you ask questions. Only took the class because it was required. Lab quizzes were hilariously difficult, mandatory attendance for pointless lectures, vague grading, unclear rubrics, insane workload for 2 credits, and zero respect for students. Avoid at all costs if you can.

It's a shame how long Kevin has taught this class and didn't listen to any student feedback. Lab quizzes are just there as a "got you" instead of really testing if you read through the manual. Unnecessarily harsh grading by the GTA and points can be taken off for literally any reasons since the rubric isn't clear. Way too much work for 2 credits.

A little disappointed to see how low the reviews are. The way he runs this class teaches the engineering side of things. It takes effort from you, it wasn't perfectly organized, but he was more than lenient (let me take the exam late which I literally missed because I forgot about it). He's nice, and helpful, and I would absolutely take him again.
Literally one of the worst classes I have ever taken in Georgia Tech. Graded harshly for no reason. Group project is the worst. If you have to take this class, just deal with it till it's over.

His lectures were a waste of time that will interrupt your day for no reason. Lab quizzes are hardly related to the actual lab activity and are usually more over random semantics in the lab manual that you could easily miss. It's definitely possible to get an A if you are responsible though, but the class just feels like it's out to get you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable about the course material. Lectures weren't too bad actually, but I didn't learn too much. This class is difficult to get an A, the project was very ambiguous, but the labs were pretty neat and I did actually learn a considerable amount in this class. Overall, I'm glad I took this class, but I would've preferred a diff prof.
The grading criteria for lab reports is pretty fair but strict, the lab quizzes are pretty tough but overall, the class was enjoyable and I learned a lot.

Avoid at all costs. His tests are completely unreasonable and he takes off every single point imaginable, even for correct answers. Also, he's extremely arrogant when asking questions or approaching him, very incompetent, and has no communication at all. 

Save your mental health and avoid.

I found the labs in this class super fun and interesting! The rest of the class is buns though- pre lab quizzes are full of random ultra-specific facts, the lectures are useless and have attendance, all submitted items are graded under a microscope (very dependent on lab TA), and practical exercises were annoying. Kevin trolls your grade for fun.
Pre-lab quizzes were foul. Lectures were lowkey nothingburgers. Super interesting course shafted by its structure and Johnson.

This class is just a lot of work and is graded very strictly. The work itself is not difficult I would say; there is just a lot of stuff to keep up with. Lectures are mandatory but not really too useful. Lab quizzes are oddly specific to some random facts, so just memorize the reading. The labs themselves are okay. Just be ready to work hard for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: shout out to kev helped me get an A, good luck to everyone else, you gonna need it.

Extremely sarcastic and condescending when you speak to Kevin. If you have any questions, contact your GTA or a TA instead. Lectures are mandatory but obsolete — only covers content that's already mentioned in the prelab. Expect the quizzes and exam to test random facts from the reading more so than true understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hope u have a lenient GTA grading ur lab reports. Prelabs can take a while, and read it throughly so u can do well on lab quizzes. Some labs can def take a long time, requiring you to go back into lab another day. Interesting class, but def not a 2 credit hour workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kevin's been involved with 2031 since was an undergrad: he knows how to teach the class well. 2031 is the equivalent of a 3 credit hour class in terms of workload. Kevin and his GTAs are notoriously rigid when it comes to grading: Lab Reports are annoying, don't teach you much, make up a big chunk of your grade, yet are graded under a microscope.
Worst possible professor for ece 2020
If you can take any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a ton of prelab work, but you need to do it before lab and make sure everything is right or the lab will take too long. The grading on lab reports and the final project components are a bit arbitrary and strict, and the lab quizzes test random nitpicky knowledge. Kevin does not answer questions and instead is just condescending.

The lab quizzes and in class exam ask overly specific questions and lab reports are graded very harshly. Start labs early because lab point are easy grade padding same with the project. Ask UTAs or GTAs if you have questions they give better answers then Johnson
Unnecessarily annoying lab quizzes.

You get absolutely cooked by the lab reports and pre lab quizzes. I went to office hours for help on my lab reports and still got a C on it. I'd just accept the B in this class and move on, trying to get an A requires more work than any 2 credit hour class needs. Also Kevin decides to troll you instead of answering your emailed questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Trolls your grade you for fun
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is not a 2-credit course and requires more time to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kevin Johnson is a solid professor. He is clear, reiterates concepts on which students demonstrate a lack of understanding, and provides slides which are very helpful to review. MAKE SURE TO TALK TO THE GTA WHO GRADES YOUR LAB REPORTS. Just a simple conversation with Kevin or your GTA can clarify any misunderstanding in grading criteria.

Lab quizzes tested on minute details and were weighed heavily for your grade. The midterm exam (aka final exam) was also very tedious. Lab reports were also graded harshly. Kevin loves to respond to students asking about his own unclear instructions on piazza with "well, did you read xyz?" instead of just answering questions.

This class is called Digital Design Lab yet the majority of the assignments are about semantics. Kevin treats Piazza as a way to give students a scavenger hunt instead of just simply answering questions brought from the confusion of his own instructions. Also assignments seem to have random due times, sometimes 11:59 pm sometimes 6:30 pm, or 8:00.

The last exam isn't called the "final exam", but still takes up 20% of your grade. 

A lack of a rigorous definition for how a lab report should be graded makes this class very difficult as different TAs grade different.

This may be a 2 credit hour course, but expect to spend minimum ~4-5 hours each week in/out of the lab.

Kevin is Super Nitpicky and chooses to destroy your grade on any given assignment based on the smallest mistakes. The class should be fun but it's a major slog for a 2-credit hour course. TAs were good, but everyone this semester dislikes Kevin's teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Outside of the Lab Quizzes, your grade is completely based on the head TA you have for your lab section. Labs are sometimes cool but the project work was extremely redundant at times. My TA was pretty incompetent on all the labs and extremely strict on lab reports and presentations. I don't think the class was too much work but the test was bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kevin himself is a good professor. He obviously clearly understands every assignment intricately, and knows exactly what you are going through. However, ECE 2031 is much more difficult than the 2 credit hours tech gives it.  Be prepared to do a lot of work before lab and especially at the end with the project. I love the class, but it is a lot.

The test and the quizzes were based on how well you can remember miniscule details instead of actual comprehension. Kevin himself is very narcisitic and unhelpful when you ask any type of question. Dont even try asking a question on piazaa, as he will simply answer it with another question making you even more confused.

Class structure is horrible, the pre lab quizzes somehow are worth more than the actual labs. The quizzes focus on minute details of the pre lab and actually don't test your knowledge on Digital Design concepts at all! The labs were actually quite fun and engaging and the TA's are awesome. Kevin himself is sort of just there. Final is horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you can take another professor for 2020 do it. Kevin's lectures are overly dry and simple especially compared to homeworks and exams. His grading criteria is very unclear and he'll take off a lot of points on tests with no clear reason. Somewhat condescending when you ask questions. TA was great though.

This class is a joke. It's 2 credit hours, but with pre-labs, lab reports, lab quizzes (which can trip you up even if you thoroughly read the pre-lab information), as well as the lab and lecture periods it feels like a heavy 3 credit hour class. Professor also stressed not to do too much work, and just take a lower grade, which nobody does.

Worst ECE class I took (about to graduate). As mentioned, quizzes were gotchas asking useless details of the readings. Group project was vague and the final was rushed and low avg.  Every assignment felt like it was designed to hurt you. It's common knowledge 2031 is a bad class. Profs showed no sign of caring/were cold overall. "2hrs" what a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Just a good professor.

Kevin Johnson is not a bad professor. The class is demanding like most other ECE courses. There are weekly 3 hours labs which contain short lab quizzes; the quizzes require a pretty thorough comprehension of the background reading and prelab. The course as a whole requires active effort put toward each topic and final group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Literally the worst class I've ever been in, horrible grading, horrible lectures and a general sense of despair. Labs were fun, TAs are great and you can learn a fair bit but a large part of your grade is decided by these absurd quizzes that have absolutely nothing to do with applicable knowledge

One of the most universally hated profs I've ever seen, and the single worst structured class I've been in. Quizzes have no intention of testing understanding, and ask hyperspecific random info that is somehow worth more than labs. In theory this class should be fun, but with atrocious grading, tedious lectures and a terrible environment, it sucks.

I didn't find the class to be as much work as other people make it out to be (do the pre-labs before lab and you should be fine), but the quizzes will expect you to know wildly irrelevant specific details so read lab material closely. As for Kevin, he comes off as cold and unapproachable. He sucks the fun out of an potentially enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Other reviews are true.

Kevin Johnson was ok, the class structure itself is not great. He could show a little more care to his students and try to understand the workload of the class. The lab quizzes are a huge pain and the group project is very dependent on the group you get. Overall it was too much work for a 2 credit class and it felt like there was no assistance.
Kevin Johnson is like Lays sour cream & onion. A solid choice. He is no honey bbq, but if you need a chip sour cream & onion will do the job.
Class is unnecessary amount of work, I don't learn anything either

This professor gives very difficult and detail oriented quizzes. The course has little to no practice material for assessments. There is a lot of background reading and prerequisite digital design knowledge needed to succeed. This lab course(worth 2 credits) has a workload of 4 credits due to the difficulty of the assessments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chill lectures, but everything is learned in lecture. Essentially mandatory to go (or watch recording). Tests were butter. Homeworks were completion grades. Just pay attention in lecture and you will probably be fine never studying a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson really could not be a part of ECE2031 and it would continue onward. It really is a solid course that is well laid out with labs, lab quizzes, a midterm, and a final group project. The class is a lot of work for a 2-hour course, but worth it. The lectures are useless as they go over material from the lab background, but have attendance.

One of the most difficult classes at GT and a terrible professor. Class is very test/lab quiz heavy, and they're stupid hard/unclear. It's like a 5-6 credit hour class when it's 2 hours. Definitely don't take this if you're taking over 14 credit hours in total or you'll hate yourself. Prepare to spend over half the week some weeks to finish labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His most redeeming quality is that he is lightning-fast to respond to questions on Piazza. Other than that, his delivery during lecture is dry, his responses to questions can often seem vague or rude, and he is an overall awkward man. There are no other professors that teach this course, so unless he moves to another job, you will have to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class doesn't reflect "2 credit hour" rating, you spend effort like a 4 credit hour class for prelabs, 3 hour lab, and lab report. Kevin is very responsive on Piazza, but his tone can be rude. Single exam and lab practicals are hard, prepare in advance. Class has a time-consuming start and chill end with group project, if your group is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult at first and has lots of work and lots of reading. For each lab you have to do background readings, prelab reading and work, the 3 hour lab, and then a lab report. There's also some reverse classroom materials that have to be done. Group project and final have lots of partial credit. Tough beginning and moderate end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have mixed thoughts about Professor Johnson, I think he's an interesting person and I learned a lot in his lectures, but he's condescending when people ask questions. Also his homeworks were pretty different from lecture examples, I did them with a friend and was amazed we were taking the same course since my friend knew the answers and I didn't

Passed. Final exam was absolute (c)anal. Pre-lab reading is long, pre-lab quizzes make you question your reading skills and are not reflective. Someone should create a pre-lab quiz for the instructors and see if he could take it. If it wasn't for GTA and TAs I would've dropped out of this class and probably go eat some nachos. Play LoL depression.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kevin has the capacity to be funny. He just doesn't convey it at all on piazza. If I hadn't met him in-person I would've been very agitated by his apparent internet tone. I agree with the other reviews that say this class deserves to be more credit. It's a lot of work and pre-lab quizzes are so esoteric even for ECE folks. Kevin does care though.

He was okay! If I could take someone else I would. The homework was a bit confusing at times since the problems never mimicked the lecture material. The lecture notes were more easy than the homework and exams. Study hard for the exams because they can definitely be tricky and difficult and not match what you learn too much. Get a study buddy!

Pretty good professor. The lectures were straightforward and it was easy to understand the material. The tests were harder than expected though. Definitely do the practice tests to prepare. Homework is not very intensive.

Condescending! For the classes he is not the only option, GO TO ANOTHER PROFESSOR! For those he is, sorry :( He has this aversion to teaching basic things. Makes an easy class hard. Only take him if you are a past nobel prize winner in ECE or something since that is his perceived student audience. Homework & Lectures wont prepare you for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kevin is smart, but lectures were incredibly boring. The material is not hard and is an easy A if you study. Did not enjoy the class or material. Try a different ECE professor if you can
Very condescending and full of himself. Doesn't care about his students. Tests are ridiculously hard, nothing like his lecture notes. Take anyone BUT this guy.

Overall he is very active on Piazza but his feedbacks some times feel rude which he is working on. GTAs are not very clear on what to expect for lab reports which really lowers class grade. His lectures are fine and does a decent job of explaining things. Final exam is just brutal and feels you don't have enough time. He sounds monotone at times
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of work and ways to lose points lol, but imo Kevin did a solid job of answering questions and being very active for Piazza. The profs shouldn't be punished for the ECE department not giving more credits for this course. Final exam was rough and GET A GOOD GROUP FOR THE FINAL PROJECT. There's no peer evaluation so some ppl may just dip.

I've never had a more unpleasant experience in a class than ECE 2031 with Kevin. He is condescending toward students, his expectations are never clearly defined and change weekly, and his grading practices are never explained. It's a shame that he's the only 2031 professor, as I don't even want to take another ECE class after this one.

Lots of students think that Kevin is a condescending guy, but I personally just think he is straightforward. His responses on Piazza are blazing quickly. Do not take his comments as personal attacks because he cares. If you put the effort into asking questions, going to office hours, and READING THE MANUAL, you will definitely enjoy this class.

The worst class I have taken so far! This guy is very condescending and will blame you for not knowing things he never taught. He will almost always avoid answering any questions you might have or answer them very vaguely.

He cares about the students and answers quickly, but sometimes vaguely, on Piazza. Although lab manuals were clear, the final project was a mess. We weren't given any clear instructions, rubric, or helpful feedbacks before we had to present our final product, and the grading seemed very subjective. The workload is also a lot more than expected.

He doesn't present information in the most interesting way but he looks at things objectively and presents information accurately. If you have a question about anything in the lecture, ask Piazza and Kevin is usually there to respond in a heartbeat which is much appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Johnson has pretty good lectures that cover the material in the course. He doesnt waste tome going over things that dont matter and makes sure he spends time on the more confusing parts of the course. If you have questions during lecture he is happy to answer them in detail to make sure everyone understands.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kevin has an average response of 5 minutes on Piazza. His answers are usually vague since he wants you to figure it out by yourself. 2031 was the hardest class I've taken so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Seems a lot nicer than Tom Collins. He didn't give a lot of lectures but the ones he did give were pretty dry, but easily understood. Sometimes he wasn't the most helpful on Piazza, but in general seemed liked he cared. He also makes memes about the final project which are much needed at that point of the semester.

Kevin was a decent professor. He was the main guy who ran the lab and did the technical communication stuff during lectures. He made the labs pretty organized through Canvas and he was also very accessible through Piazza (answered pretty quickly). However, he was a very boring lecturer who just rambled and answered very vaguely on Piazza.

If you are an IE, listen to me. TAKE KEVIN! I have heard 2020 is so hard but with Kevin it is an easy A. Just show up to every single lecture and take good notes. The concepts are not difficult but if you fall behind it would be hard to catch up. Lectures can be boring, but it is necessary to learn the material. Test averages were B+ every time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a pretty decent teacher. As an IE major, I appreciated his clear lectures, even if they weren't the most interesting. He's very knowledgeable, and a reasonable guy. You can tell he enjoys what he teaches. The grade is based off of 4 tests, 2 labs, homework, and pop quizzes (for participation). If you go to class and study, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor, just wish he wasn't my first ECE professor. I think if he didn't make lecture completely boring, it would have resulted in me having a better grade in the class. Also, I wish he gave out homework assignments that were more like the lectures, or at least gave lectures more in tune with his view of real world applications .

Kevin Johnson is alright as a teacher. As a non EE major, I didn't find that he catered to outsiders well, but if you're an EE, I'm sure you would enjoy his teaching. Not phenomenal, but he won't make you flunk either. You should gain a proper understanding of the material.

Having been in his class for two semester (2020 and 2031), I would say he's not bad. He presents lots of stuff in the lecture and usually in a boring way.  I understand more materials by asking him questions than by listening his lecture. Tests' not easy but they curve a lot. Btw he is not the expert to explain things straightforwardly and simply.

Johnson gave a couple of lectures, most of them long and boring. He is most helpful on Piazza. If you post a question he will usually answer within minutes. Overall not a bad guy, if you have questions about 2031 go to Kevin Johnson. You will also find out he only owns one shirt.

you definitely have to teach yourself all the material to succeed in this class. as long as you go through the textbook and use the practice resources, getting an A is entirely possible despite unhelpful lectures. i literally skipped lectures the entire second half of semester and still managed to pass the exams so don't waste your time
I studied over a week just for this class exam. The exams felt like they are genuinely made to fail you. Do not take this class!

This professor makes her exams impossible. Even if you get the question correct they mark it as wrong. Which is really careless and frustrating. They only want specific answers in their words and if you were to write a correct answer in your own words they wont accept it.
stingy with extra credit. doesn't care about the students sadly. grades harshly

Lectures are pointless as they don't encompass the whole textbook and you are tested on the textbook material. There is a writing assignment every week that does not reinforce material. However, Dr. Kerr is very good at explaining material and answering questions. Also, Dr. Kerr gives a lot of good study material to use before each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: shes passionate but whats the use. Doesn't help students succeed.

I took this class because the reviews from last semester were pretty reasonable and overall a good avg rating. However this semester there was a huge decline in teaching, grading and structure of the course itself. I don't know what happened, but class is very stressful you need to put in at least 60+ hours of studying on your own for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bio is heavy. But in this class all you have to do is study on your own. The prof and class arent helpful at all. Dont take this prof.
not a good prof. doesn't care about students.
Class is heavy. very stingy with extra credit. Compared to other professors who care about their students and give them good cushion. prof and TA are not helpful when you have questions on content.
bad prof. Unstructured course.

She is NOT a good prof. Class is so not worth your time she reads everything off the slides. Her exams are extremely content heavy and the way they grade your exams IS HARSH. The TAs do not grade fairly, it seems rushed. Prof does NOT respond to your emails either, dont take this class with this prof.
The TAs grade the tests unjustly taking points off for no reason…
This class is very fast paced and not to mention, the free response on the exams are difficult and long. You basically have to study by yourself, the textbook helps alot.
dont take her class tests are really heavy on material with no cushioning at all.

The most important thing to do is to read and take notes on the textbook, as her lectures are basically regurgitating that. You can get around the participation by doing the learning catalytics from home; going to the lecture isn't necessary as long as you read the textbook. The tests can be difficult, but reading the textbook helps.

Her tests are so hard, and she barely gives us any grace on the exams. The wording of the exam questions are so wordy and difficult, and doesn't reflect anything she teaches in class. Very dissapointed..

The lectures don't help. And the Tests do not reflect what is taught or even the information on the textbook. Her test are worded so badly its like she wants to fail you. And not enough time on exmas..... DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS.
Her lectures covered all the material needed and made sense. The exams were not too difficult but sometimes she covered material very quickly in class so it made it difficult to follow.
Already a week into this class the amount of busy work is insane.

She's very sweet and it is clear she's passionate, her lectures are just not engaging at all. I have no clue how I passed this class. I went to her office hours and she was definitely very helpful there!

Talks way too fast, and there is so much content. Assignments every week that were essentially busy work, most of them unrelated to biology. Lots of unnecessary information in lectures as well, like long case studies that were never on exams. Need to know essentially all content in almost perfect detail to apply to difficult exam questions.

Took for cellular and molecular biology lab. Poor grading criteria and a lot of work. Even the TAs would complain about how much work they had to put in. She also did not follow teh syllabus and make pre lab quizzes for completion like she said she would.

Dr. Kerr is an extremely passionate and excellent teacher. I am not a bio major and did pretty bad in this class, and while I did not enjoy it too much, Dr. Kerr and Dr. Smith's excitement made the class enjoyable. Definitely go into class and with enough sleep though, as I blame my failure on poor sleep, bad studying habits, and lack of passion.

SHES AWESOME, prob best professor u can get. very good at explaining topics and super approachable. only downfall is that there is a lot of material in this class. its not her fault but just a lot of content

Dr. Kerr and Dr. Smith split the lecture material, and both did an amazing job explaining the content! Dr. Kerr is super sweet and she answers questions really thoroughly! She believes 1107 works best if students read the textbook and take notes before class, then strengthen their understanding by attending lecture and asking questions.

She talks fast in class but it's all very understandable. You can tell she knows what she's talking about. I think shes a great teacher and super easy to reach for help if you're confused. Shes very kind.

Truly surprised that Dr. Kerr does not have a higher rating on this website. She is one of the kindest profs at GT and a clear lecturer. Like any intro bio, this class has a lot of content and requires a good bit of effort. But she is a passionate and willing to answer any question w/o making a student feel small for asking. Literally my queen.

some assignments are completely unrelated to biology. Like why am I learning about cornell notes if I'm not going to use them? She talks really fast in the lecture as well, so u should read the material beforehand.

Dr. Kerr is an amazing teacher. She very clearly cares about what she is teaching and is always ready to help during office hours (very accessible outside of this too). Also, there are a lot of good study resources available that make the tests pretty easy.

Dr. Kerr truly cares about her students, and this is clearly shown through her eagerness to teach and her transparent expectations/grading. At times, she does go a little fast during lectures but all of the content is pulled from the textbooks and is clarified in the PowerPoints posted!

It's very clear that Dr. Kerr wants her students to get As in the class. There's A LOT of content in the class, so her lectures are very fast-paced, but she does a very good job covering it. She's clear with what she expects from you and what you need to do to be successful in the class. When she tells you to use something to study, USE IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a nice person, but she goes very fast during lectures. This is probably because the amount of information in this class is extremely extensive, so the textbook is mandatory to keep up. The tests are fairly straightforward, but because of the amount of content, the questions are quite specific. Thankfully, there is in-built extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr's lectures are really fast, but if you read the assigned textbook reading and take notes on it beforehand, you're well prepared to understand what's going on in lecture. The written homework assignments might feel pointless, but if you do well on them then you have a good grade boost and don't have to worry about test scores as much.

I really enjoyed Dr. Kerr's lectures. At the beginning, it was hard to keep up because she talked so fast, but after the first unit or two you get the hang of it. Read and take notes on the textbook before class even though it's incredibly dense, otherwise you will be lost. Exams were fairly easy if you've been keeping up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While her lectures are very fast-paced, if you do the notes before class and keep up with the content, you will be successful. She cares about her students, and is very approachable during her office hours. She includes a lot of wiggle room in the grading system, so it is easy to get an A in the class.

She goes so fast you cannot possibly take notes, and doesn't explain things well. She doesnt take time on the parts that are the most confusing, and goes on long tangents about stuff that isnt relevant. There are assignments unrelated to the content are harshly graded, and take up time. During office hours she is condescending and confusing.

Wonderful professor. I knew nothing about biology coming in and still managed to pull a good grade. She explains things perfectly! There is a lot of reading and assignments to do, and the writing assignments can be tedious, but overall definitely worth it. Participation is the main grading criteria which was also great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice, but spoke very quickly during lectures. Easy to access outside of class but a majority of the class is mainly based on the online textbook, so I would just say to rely on the textbook and actually understand the material. Lectures were semi helpful but relying on the lectures alone will not guide you to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a decent lecturer but make sure to read the online textbook before class. She spoke super fast, making it hard to understand her at times. Nice but the lectures are REALLY dry. It was hard staying awake at times. I would say that the tests are fair, just make sure to read the online textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I like the way this course was structured. At the beginning it was very difficult to figure out what they wanted you to know, however, as the semester progresses you begin to understand how to study and what is expected of you. Professor Shana spoke way too fast and when she taught me and my fellow peers did not understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate about biology. She gives great lectures, however talks extremely fast to the point where I would often have to consult the powerpoints outside of class because she talked faster than I could type. She gives 1 second for group discussions (not an exaggeration). Extremely lecture heavy & attendance matters. Overall, a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Passive aggressive if the class don't know a slight little detail.Her content was really hard and her explanations was basically repeating the same thing from the lecture or textbook. Exams are so hard and almost impossible to pass and the final was also catastrophic; 70 questions and probably only 20 of them were from the semester's content. Avoid

In-class assignments show little relevance to biology, existing more for political reasons than for improving your education. Assignments are then graded by TAs who lack proper oversight and take off for the smallest reasons. The exams poorly represent topics, and the final lacks structure and coherence. Poor communication of expectations.

She is very sweet and works well with students. You will have to go to lecture to participate in the in class assignments which can open at different times during lecture. You are given an online textbook read which I would recommend actually reading because it helps with the class content which there is a lot of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a very sweet and caring professor that wants everyone to succeed in the class. 100% recommend. As long as you read the online textbook and take notes on what you read, you should be fine ! Also the homework and in class activities are very helpful and graded based on participation, not accuracy.

BIOS 1208 is very very content-heavy, but Dr. Kerr makes it doable. I'd recommend either doing the readings OR going to lecture, as the two are pretty much the exact same, and it's super repetitive. Grading is super kind as exams are worth such a small portion of your grade. Just put in the effort and you will do well in this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: lecture just goes more in depth on reading u need to do before class. just review recitation slides and LC questions, and you'll do great on exams. in 1208, we were allowed a notecard with notes on each exam. dr. kerr is very kind and is clearly passionate about biology! she truly wants you to learn biology, and her course is relatively stress-free
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kerr was a very engaging and thorough lecturer and was responsive to feedback. The flipped classroom style was very effective for me and this should be an relatively easy class if you do the readings, which there can be a LOT of. Try to stay ahead early on because the last few midterms are tougher.

Her lecturing was pretty clear and interesting. Reverse classroom structure, but still taught in class so it was redundant. Unnecessary writing assignments. Content was very easy first half, but hard second half. In class participation, but grades participation and HW based on completion. Grading system makes it easy to get a good grade.

This class was incredibly reliant on the textbook, which was dense and hard to get through at times. As this was a flipped classroom model, Dr. Kerr usually brushed over topics in class and focused on the more "difficult" topics, which only helpful at times. The grading scale was incredibly helpful, and so were the recitations.

It is pretty easy to make an A and the class is not too much work. One thing to note is that there is quite a lot of at-home reading assigned. You can get by without doing the reading but your life would be a lot less stressful if you just did the reading.

Her lectures are very quick and information-dense, but ultimately not necessary because of the flipped classroom model and in-class participation questions you can access from anywhere. The class is easy if you read the textbook and watch videos. The tests are similar to the practice tests. Grading scheme is very forgiving.

Dr. Kerr personally is very kind and passionate about biology. This class is not hard necessarily, but is a lot of textbook reading, writing assignments, and learning catalytics work. I did not attend lecture as pretty much everything covered was in the textbook/IKES/TICAS. Test scores averaged around a 75 and participation points are easy to get.

Dr. Kerr is a great organismal professor. Syllabus lays out grading clearly and writing assignments are built in to give students wiggle room. Exams are easy given you have a rudimentary understanding of class content. Textbook is a lifesaver. Readings are dense but skimming and attending class will get you a high A. Accessible and values feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a sweet professor, but I thought the pace she went at for lecture was ridiculously quick given how dense/much material there was to cover. Fair amount of busy work, and the questions from the exams were sometimes on the most trivial little detail that did not stand out as important. The textbook is your best friend for this class.

Dr. Kerr is a respectable and caring professor. I personally didn't like how the course was delivered (textbook heavy and sometimes 1-2 hours for each assigned reading lecture as a refresher) but I think the course is fair if you do all the readings and maximize participation (easy points), you can get an A in the class since exams are open note.

Best lecturer I've had at this school thus far. Super clear and concise instruction even though she covers a lot of dense material. She's super approachable and cares a lot about student success and learning. Only downside is the class has a lot of busy work and requires a decent time investment outside of lecture
Lectures were very heavy and lots of material was covered so get ready to memorize but Dr. Kerr is a very kind professor who definitely cares about the class and her students.

Dr. Kerr is a really nice professor and she cares about her students. She makes changes to the class based on feedback which is awesome. Lectures pretty fast. Make sure u do the Learning Catalytics. The textbook is free & online but u have to pay for access to LC. She makes the class so that participation matters more than ur test performances!
