Dr. Kerr teaches fast. Really fast. Her lectures move so quickly that I didn't take notes. You'll have to read the "online textbook" - it's free and not official, so don't worry about cost. She's very nice and passionate about biology, and the tests are straightforward (and honestly not that hard). No quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher. No pop quizzes, but sometimes the textbook (put together by her) did not cover the in-class material. Knew what she was doing but would go on tangents at times. Sweet, but a LOT of work. Participation in classes counts and if you don't take notes before lecture from textbook, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a caring prof, but the way the class is structured makes it super contentheavy. I regularly spent 15+ hours study for each exam (there are 4 plus 1 final). Bio lab is also really time consuming. I never went to lecture, but learned from the textbook. Concepts aren't hard, just the sheer amount of material. There is 6 pts extra credit though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was passionate and cared about her students.

If you are choosing between taking bio or taking eas, take eas. This class is stupid content heavy and so much memorization is involved. Dr Kerr is really nice and she really cares but this class is a ton of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is really knowledgeable about what she's teaching, and her enthusiasm comes across. She does talk fast, but it wasn't to the point of not being understandable. She expects a lot of participation from the class, but as long as you do the reading and participation assignments and come to class, you should be fine.

She is clearly very interested in Biology and wants her students to succeed. It can a lot of work, but go to every class, do all the homework, and study using the learning objectives and you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: People give Kerr a hard time because they don't get the best grades with her. She knows and loves what she talks about. Learn and study with her learning objectives and you'll get a B at least on the tests. Very clear lectures, so use them to study, and you're pretty much golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reasonable, nice, and cares about your success. Class consists purely of lectures, so come to class having read the assigned materials and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is an approachable professor and enthusiastic about the subject. She goes a bit fast in class but is willing to explain more in office hours. Her style of teaching is half lecture half group activities/questions.

Kerr seems approachable and nice when you first start out, but it is quite the opposite! She talks faster in her lectures than any human should ever be able to speak. Be prepared to "infer" (her words) what parts of the book you should be reading because the readings don't match the homework or the lectures and of course not the test.

For me, Dr Kerr does not seem to grasp what she is talking about or communicate it very well. Maybe she has something going on elsewhere in her life but I have found her to be inarticulate and not especially helpful. Maybe it will improve... Here's hoping!

She speaks fast in her lectures and didn't go as in depth on some topics as I would've liked. She very much expects you to come to class having read the blog and the textbook. Her tests aren't too bad if you put the work into the class and go over learningcatalytics sessions!

You  need to go to class. The PowerPoints have little text, and the book doesn't always cover everything you're expected to know (like in-class examples). That said, Dr. Kerr is a very dynamic and engaging lecturer. I didn't reach out for one-on-one help, but she answered the questions I did have fully and respectfully.

I saw the other rating, and it's accurate. She appears nice and approachable but when contacted one-on-one does not care about the success or feelings of students. Also, her lectures are a little all over the place because she often loses her train of thought and often can't answer questions confidently.
Seems really approachable in class BUT BEWARE if you go to her office. You will likely see students in tears.  She is not known for her personality!

Gives informative but boring lectures focused on the definitions and theorems we learned, not much student interaction. She grades exams very harshly, so include every step and write it perfectly no matter how unimportant it seems. I lost 10 points on one of the exams just for work on problems I got correct, and others had this happen too.
good at explaining things, but the first exam is very difficult. exams are worth 80% of the grade. Course gets easier as you go, but there is also a lot of memorization.

she makes the class very difficult and test heavy, makes her exams really hard, and same time has no decency to help students. she's so smirky and always gets annoyed or irritated when asking her questions like how is she a professor

She's a pretty good professor with a deep understanding of the content. The first half of this class was very difficult for me, but the second half was, in comparison, a total breeze. Study LP/IP formulation like your life depends on it and make sure to do well on quizzes (can be tough and worth a lot of your grade) No homeworks or attendance req!

Dr. Moug is very knowledgeable and organized and gives you plenty of practice in order to do well in the class. If you just do all the practice and stay on top of the content, this class is extremely manageable. Exams/quizzes were always reasonable and straightforward. My studio TA was AMAZING too which helped me do well in the course too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you do not get her for studio, or at least a good TA for studio, it is on you to learn a lot. My studio TA was okay (had a thick accent and was taught optimization differently) so I did not learn a lot there. I had to depend on AI and her recorded videos to teach me, and the occasional office hours (which were kinda scary).
Super organized, lot of practice help, she is strict and a lot of the class depended on the studio teacher but she was a good lecturer and the course was structured very well to succeed.

Took her for a short summer session. The class was very fast-paced, so I needed to spend a lot of time on this class for those five weeks, but it wasn't too bad. The homework and tests were pretty straightforward, and she gave us practice tests before the tests. She also gave us a bump to our grade at the end of the semester.

Took Dr. Moug during the 5-week summer session. The class was fast paced and I had to spend more time on the class but it wasn't abnormal. The lectures are great at teaching the content as I came in with zero knowledge and did well overall. She is very accessible in office hours and is active on Piazza as well. I would recommend taking her.

Moug is an alright lecturer. She got the point across eventually, but her lectures were hard to follow. She isn't super enthusiatic and is sarcastic at times. VERY vauge about tests and test concepts. She isn't horrible but def not the best. But the tests were fair and she never tried to trick us.

I took Dr. Moug's hybrid 3133 summer section where you could either attend in-person lectures or watch the recordings online. Her lectures were very clear and helped you succeed on the exams. She was also extremely knowledgeable in answering questions in the in-person section and I got an easy A. Highly recommend her if you put in the work
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Moug! She explained concepts really well (a lot of the time more in depth than necessary). Her office hours were super helpful and she was able to clear up anything that wasn't super clear in lecture. Graded participation was annoying but only 5% of your grade. Tests weren't hard they had nothing we hadn't seen before.

Dr. Moug is one of the best professors I've ever had. 80% of the grade is tests but the tests are so incredibly easy if you know the content at even an elementary level. Homeworks can be difficult but the TAs can help at office hours. There is also graded class participation. Overall, she is very knowledgable and truly cares about student success.

Dr. Moug is an amazing prof. Don't listen to the other ratings! She may come off aloof, but she knows her material well and cares about her students. Although she is a harsh grader for hw assignments, (go to office hrs if ur struggling and the TAs will help), her exams are the same difficulty as the hw, if not easier and graded more leniently!

Very harsh grading - 2 midterms, one worth 20% and one worth 25%, with a cumulative final worth 35%. Lectures were boring and often badly paced. Moug claims to encourage participation, but her lack of enthusiasm and general disregard for student experience made the classroom often dead silence. Almost unreasonable with late HW and participation.

Despite the numerous mistakes she consistently made throughout the course, the instructor liked to hold students to a high bar and was harsh with grading. She finds the most trivial things in your work and takes off a significant number of points. For our midterms we only had our homework to review for exam prep. Do not take this course with her.

She was very vague and would explain concepts without defining them which was very confusing. Wasn't very good at teaching content; she just said things. Also refused to answer questions. If you asked a yes/no question she would respond with check piazza. Took off points on hw even when our answers matched lecture. Tests were pretty fair though.

I had her for studio, and she was a great lecturer and teacher, would go into topics very well, making sure we'd understand it, missed lot of studio and was late to the quizzes but she was always pretty nice about it, very tough grading though, one small mistake can cost you a letter grade, other than that, great teacher but be ready to work hard
Fairly good lecturer and personally had a good experience with her (she always gave good feedback on the optional practice problems). Can see why her personality turns some people off though.

Kati Moug is the best professor I've had since freshman year. She's a fantastic explainer, she cares about her student's success, and she is available to help however possible as long as you put in the effort. She does not grade quizzes easily, but this makes exams 10 times easier. I highly recommend if you are interested in learning the content

Professor was kinda mid, but the class was easy enough to where lecture was unnecessary. If you're able to take a better professor definitely do, but we only had one option and honestly you learn better in studio, which is also where attendance is taken, so don't worry too much about it. Class itself was actually pretty fun!

She is kind and knows the material well, but she is absolutely brutal with quizzes and exams, and will make you fail a quiz for one tiny mistake. She does give very helpful and detailed feedback on assignments, but you will need to study your tail off to do well on exams, there is no way to breeze by in this course.

I wonder how Kaitlyn was hired to the ISyE department. She has no clue what she is doing nor how to properly teach. She has no sympathy towards students, and she lacks discipline with properly applying fair grading schemes. Too many of my friends have tried to ask her questions, and she responds snarky. Who does she think she is? TAKE SOMEONE ELSE

Dr. Moug is one of my favorite professors I've had at Tech. She's incredibly knowledgeable about 3133 and does a great job explaining tough concepts to students who've never seen it before. She provides lots of practice problems that are helpful for exams. The exams and quizzes are very fair and there have been no curveballs. 100% reccommend Moug!

Professor Moug is arguably one of the best ISYE professors you'll get. Good course organization & structure, plenty of available practice for Midterms & quizzes, & it's easy to understand her teaching style. For one of the most important & foundational ISYE classes you'll take, definitely take it with Professor Moug if you get the chance.

I think Dr. Moug is a great professor! If you attend lecture and studio and pay attention, the tests and quizzes are very straightforward. She also gives you the opportunity to submit optional practice problems before every quiz and get detailed feedback on your answers which is really helpful. I have never heard her be rude to a student in lecture
Rude af. Asked a question during second week of lecture and got a snarky condescending response. Didn't show up to lecture again after that.

Unnecessarily harsh and unforgiving. She had homework and quizzes over both 4th of July weekend and Thanksgiving week. Many of my friends had to completely change Thanksgiving plans, and I even know a guy who had to cancel his flight because she wouldn't let him make it up before/after. He didn't end up seeing his family for Thanksgiving bc of her.

Does not really care about students well being. She has been very rude throughout class. She understands the material well and is a good teacher but is a very tough grader. Her grading scheme does not really make sense, and students score bad on topics they know well and good on topics they do not know at all. Not empathetic or helpful.

Prof. Moug lacks a lot of empathy imo. I've heard from other students that they were yelled at for asking questions about the test, and I've observed a negative tone when she answers questions

She clearly understands the content and is a good instructor in terms of teaching but personality wise, not the best.

Fantastic professor.  At least for my experience, class was very organized and grading criteria was clear.  Grading is: 10% studio attendance/participation, 10% total for 3 group projects, 20% for 10 quizzes (drop lowest 2), 30% for 2 midterms, and 30% for the final. Very manageable and she explains the concepts pretty well.  Would take again!

Dr. Moug might be the worst professor at GT. Not only are her lectures super disorganized, they also make a relatively simple subject extremely complicated. The problems on the exams do not match the quiz or homework problems, so there is no good way to prepare. Finally, she pretends to be caring, but outside of class, she is not sympathetic at all

Learning is so hard in this class. Slides are messy and overwhelming, yet they barely cover what will actually be on your exam. Kostas does not teach well; he rambles on and on until you lose track of what he is even talking about. Practice exams are usually posted which does help; other than that there are very few helpful resources in this class.

His team is toxic. At least 5 Ph.D students graduated last and this year without any celebration, including myself. He just does not want to. It feels like you are not important at all despite spending 5 years. Almost all Ph.D defense celebration I attended is big, wonderful and became a key moment in one's life. Here in his lab, nothing.

You go to this class that is mandatory attendance but learn close to nothing in class. You have to teach yourself everything from the book. His usefulness is comparable to Arash Yavari, negative usefulness. I have no idea how teachers like this are still teaching, especially when their the only teacher for the subject. Made my life 100x harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I see most negative comments below. I also want to share my experiences. Academically, I think he is fine, just needs to be more generous, not too mean on students and collaborators. I am not sure he will see this but I will still say it here. If one student or collaborator does not like you, ok. When there are so many, doomed.
It seems there are only 2 Ph.D students left in the lab (one is on TA, 4th year and another 3rd year). No funding unless you want to do a TA.

He thinks he knows ecology and try to solve ecological problems from the perspective of microbial genomics. However, none of the papers he had published had strong statistical support. He knows little about statistics. Genomics is his strength but this was not applied in a proper way to solve ecological problems.

Lecture heavy professor that can underplay the significance of topics, omits needed values on homework, and expects a strong background in certain topics. However, he is passionate about the topic, is very open to questions, and tries to test your knowledge during lectures. Further, he is a very lenient grader and will go in your favor. Participate

Most or all 1.0 ratings since Jan 2023 are irrelevant and unfair, none of those criticisms are related to CEE 2300; they are related to research, Ph.D. students, research funding, publication fee, FastANI vs ManHash, etc. Seems like some don't like him for other reasons. The course is tough for engineering students as it involves chemistry, etc.

The course material is pretty vast and challenging. Lectures can be boring but he just wants you to learn. Very responsive to emails/questions and he's nice enough. He's not that harsh of a grader and gives pretty good partial credit. Show him you'll put in the effort and you'll succeed.

I feel he is going to fail the rest of his research career because he did not have students in the past 3 years. No funding. Refuse to pay for a publication fee higher than $2000, which means he cannot afford to publish nature or baby journals. Say bad things about his competitors who publish nature, but he still does not realized why no funding.

I am extremely surprised to learn that he declares he made significant contribution to a famous tool FastANI but he did not know, or never heard of what a MinHash is, and what a minimizer is. How can he be the corresponding author of a highly cited paper without knowing what exactly it is?

I am surprised to see that my fellow lab mates had the same feeling. And the several comments below is exactly what I heard from others. He will postpone your proposal as late as possible so that he can extract more from you while paying less (salary improved after successful proposal), This is my case.

He is very mean, to a level that I dot no know how to describe it. This year, he kicked again 1 Ph.D student, who is now 4th year, out of the lab. Everybody think he is very impolite. Can you imagine a professor said to his Ph.D student that he is very disappointed at somebody? Not once, many times, to many students. Run away!!!

He was honestly a very easy grader. The course could be overwhelming in terms content until you realize how easily he grades and that an 80+ is an A. For example if you write down the basic mass balance equation (the first step in a problem) then you get majority of points of the question even if nothing else is right lol.

I want everybody know that he kicked more than 8 Ph.D student out of the lab (in total he has about 10 graduated), meaning he cannot deal with Ph.D student and he is a difficult person.He is also mean, I mean on stipend for Ph.D, he will try his best to reduce it, until you go to the department head and sue him.

I do not think that he is a good professor. Many people taking this class are second years and he treats it as if the class is a 4000 level. The tests are super hard and he gives you vague content and his lectures are awful. Here is how his tests are formatted: it is as if he teaches you the English alphabet and tests you on arabic.

Deserves a 0 rating. Gives minimal material to study and gets upset when the class average low. Very lecture heavy, he could briefly mention a topic and it could very easily end up being a question worth 20 points on a test. Actual tests are nothing like the practice tests/HW. Terrible lecturer. Problems are so complex that YouTube doesnt even help
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is not a good professor. He's vague, his lectures are vague, and his tests are nothing like the homework or practice exams. My issue with his method of teaching is the lack of it. He thinks that because he gives vague information, we can solve any of the complex examples that he gives us. The textbook doesn't help all that much either.

He's smart but is obviously hired for research. He structures the course with prefectures and uses lectures for clarification. However, in lectures, he is not specific and does not show many examples. He has a slide of minimal info and goes on tangents, then skims important math or info. He is overall too vague and formats it like a 4000 level.
Wouldn't recommend, try taking the other professor for 2300.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Intentionally makes problems more difficult than necessary. His work on problems are difficult to read, and contain many mistakes with little explanation. Pretty confusing. On difficult homework problems, he states that he wants to "challenge" you to search through the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Man oh man, i dont know where to begin. First of all Kostas is an extremely intelligent individual, i think for this reason he expects his students to comprehend the material as clearly as he does. Many of the students, being engineering majors have not taken a chemistry course in years . He formats the course like a 4000 level. DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!!!

He expects you to understand a multitude of chemistry, physics, and biological concepts with very simplistic explanation behind it (such as the way cells work). He isn't really good at explaining material and can have very confusing notes. The tests were extremely hard and preparing for them would be tough. His HWs were hard too, would not rec him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a really nice professor but his teaching style needs an improvement. When there are math questions he has the solution written out in the most undetailed way possible and just skims through it. He would especially do this on the chemistry part. The exams are really hard & doing well on the practice exams will not guarantee you a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gives unclear, incomplete lecture notes and doesn't explain concepts clearly during lecture. Doesn't provide much preparation material for exams. . You have to work more than you should to rake in the grade.

Very confusing in class. Gives few practice problems but only answers, not how to do them. Problems worked in class he just skims through how to do it and doesn't actually work through it. First test he gave us a 30% problem that he briefly covered in one lecture and didn't post in the slides. Hard to understand. Really just awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sometimes I feel like he makes things intentionally difficult by not communicating clearly. If you put in the effort the class is fine.

Ppl say the class is hard and that he's not clear in class, and that his test aren't far. I think that that's an exaggeration. He knows the class is hard and because of that an A is an 80% . His lectures can be confusing at times, but the test material comes straight from the homework and the class material. Form a study group, and actually study.

AWFUL! Avoid him at all costs for 2300. Tests are not fair AT ALL for what is covered in class and do not represent difficulty of homework or are at all close to homework questions. Has NO practice exams, so you have no idea what to expect from exams. Does NOT answer your questions or tell you anything helpful. Most frustrating person & class

He's a good lecturer, and generally if you listen to the lectures or read the textbook and take the practice problems given then you should get an A, and learn the economics pretty well. No complaints from me.

He is one of the easier econ professors. His lectures are just ppt and tests are based on the practice exams and resources provided. As long as done the hw and test prep easy to get a good grade. Participation is extra credit and really nice. Highly recommend.

He posts his slides on Canvas which are extremely helpful. The midterms and final closely resemble the examples and problem sets given in class, so as long as you understand and review them it's pretty easy to get a good grade.

He is a good professor, and his practice exams closely resemble the midterm and final. The exams are worth a lot, and there are only two, plus the final. He has a heavy accent, but his lectures are clear and rely on PowerPoint. My only issue is that he doesn't round grades; I had an 89, and as stated in his syllabus, he doesn't round.

Professor Kang is really knowledgeable about the subject. He has quite a thick accent which made it a little difficult to understand at the beginning. There are weekly homework assignments which are pretty free and easy. There are 2 exams and a final in which each is about 20-30%. He provides some extra credit which is quite helpful.

Fall 2024. Pretty sure I took 2106 macro not 2105. Heavy accent on some words. Good examples (growing his garden, his son's toys) made it easier to understand. All multiple choice tests and easy homework. 4 random easy quizzes with a code provided in class for attendance.

Prof. Kang makes content clear and easy to understand. He has a thick accent but he's still very clear and it never got in the way of my understanding his lectures. Weekly homework is very quick with p-sets every 6-7 weeks that take a little longer. Gives very helpful practice exams. Would take again.

Very thick accent, hard to understand. Has many TA's and open hours. Attendance optional, and slides are posted so if you want to teach yourself and never go to class you can. Mandatory $75 textbook to complete weekly homework. Only take if you have the discipline to teach yourself what you miss. will not round/bump grades but has extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Online textbook is required for you to do HW (~$75), but other than that, prof Kang is very enthusiastic in his teaching. He's knowledgeable and always updates his OH if there are changes. I recommend doing the practice tests he provides on Canvas. He also gives plenty of extra credits in class, though attendance isn't required.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Each week has optional extra credit assignment - 5 mins. 2 midterms during the semester - required effort & studying. His lectures are kind of boring and he is not the best explainer/hard to understand sometimes. Attendance is not mandatory, he posts the slideshows for each week on Canvas.

Gives plenty of extra credit opportunities, just make sure to go to lectures to get the most out of it. Slides were excellent in studying for exams and the practice tests he gives will generally follow the same format as the exams, with very similar questions. Just for me a lot of HW.

Lectures covered everything needed for exams. Didn't need to read the textbook. Just study the slides and do the practice tests. Provided plenty of extra credit, some from in-class quizzes, but attendance is optional.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Kang is very direct on what will be on the exam. His lectures cover exactly what will be on the midterms. His class has 2 midterms plus the Final. For the midterms I recommend really looking at the slides and reviewing the concepts. He also offers a good bit of extra edit, do it if you can. Go to office hours if you have questions!

Dr. Kang was a great and caring professor. Lectures weren't required but, in my opinion, they were really helpful.  Meet him during office hours if you have any questions. He goes a bit quickly for his lectures because there is a lot of content to cover, but he posts the slides on Canvas so that helps a lot. Loved his class and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really enthusiastic and makes lectures really interesting. Clearly cares and wants us to understand the concepts. Homeworks and practice tests prepare you very well. Study for tests and you should be fine, the final was old test questions reused. Go to office hours if you need help. Don't skip lectures, he teaches you exactly what you need to know.
His enthusiasm for economics makes the lectures interesting. You can tell he wants us to understand the concepts. Just study for the tests and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kosal has interesting content. he covers 5-6 presentations and 1-2 books per test but the test will be heavily focused on 1-2 presentations from what was covered. Glad she's not teaching this next sem.
Very interesting lectures. Content and tests are not too difficult. You'll do well if you go to class.

Dr. Kosal is a certified expert on what she teaches. The makes the course incredibly interesting and relevant to today and I was always engaged. At the end of each of her lectures I'd be blown away. Not to mention her achievements. Her resume is a mile long. Would 100% recommend this class to anyone even if they're not an INTA major.

Professor Kosal doesn't care for her students. She doesn't give information on the exams, and when asked what kind of questions there will be (MCQ vs FRQ) she just shrugs vaguely. Lectures are also poorly put together, and she doesn't provide any resources for the class. If you take her, you are honestly on your own. Good Luck
Class was not always enjoyable. Lectures tended to be boring. Prof is not the best.
Prof Kosal does not outline what she expects from her students in terms of test preparation. Tests are mcq and sometimes frq (frq is random she doesnt say). Content is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kosal is accomplished in her field but should not be a professor. Class is very lecture heavy with presentations being mostly pictures. Reading heavy class as well. Tests often over target one section of the material and have questions which are meant to trip you up. She will give you no practice questions or direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic but arrogant and a bit moody.  Her course was more about her experiences,  therefore pay attention to her lectures.  Her grading is subjective.
Extremely brilliant prof who knows what she is talking about! Recommend her to everyone! Lectures are interesting and tests are not too difficult if you show up to class and pay attention.

She is an amazing professor. I highly recommend anyone to take her. She knows what she's talking about. Her stories are usually pretty interesting and she has a right to be proud of her accomplishments.

I took her for INTA 2040, or Science, Technology, and International Affairs. One of the best teachers I've ever had. She is kinda arrogant, but she's allowed to be, on account of her achievements. Although INTA, she does target the class toward science and engineering, and will curve fairly decently.

Kosal teaches a pretty standard INTA class. Lectures. Slide shows. A good bit of reading. 3 tests throughout the semester. Not too difficult. Admittedly, she's a bright girl and knows the material well, but, Christ, she's cocky. I got irritated with her and hated listening to her, but the class could have been worse. She also sports a festive coat.

She is very excited about her class and she teaches very good and class is not too hard. But her personality is a disaster and not humble like experienced professor who are confident in their knowledge and personality.  If you ask a lot of questions she will perhaps like you more.
The midterms and final are just memorize the text book. Did not feel like a real math class

Tries to fit in too much content into lectures so that the lectures aren't actually helpful, and even then she has to skip a lot of content or skim through it, forcing extra self-studying. Gives long homeworks that don't actually help with understanding the material. She admits that exams are long and says the solution is to just "study more".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is for MATH 6635. Kang tries, but it obvious she doesn't really care about finance and is more interested in PDEs. She moves arounds alot in lecture and doesn't seem interested in answering actual questions. Your gonna need the textbook and AI bot to understand the content sometimes as she doesn't want to help with work, unless its conceptual.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures extremely fast; will often ask if people are "with me" but doesn't wait for an answer to keep going. Exams are heavily weighted and difficult. Expect averages in the 50s if the class does well. She is nice and accessible outside of class, but does not handle the course very well. Used 3 different textbooks which was hard to keep track of.
Lectures were pretty good, and she is very caring and accessible. Exams were a bit on the long side, but the problems would be fairly straightforward.

Great lecturer, poor teacher. Super fast, difficult exams, and a hypocrite. Treats grad students like "super" undergrads that recently covered these topics. Skips around saying "oh you guys already know this". Tells us "solve ODEs while cooking". Unfairly manipulates exam grade distribution by lowering points of specific exam questions.

She is amazing; please take her. She is very nice and caring. Her lectures are pretty good and she is always open to questions and gives good answers during class. There is extra credit offered throughout the course. The homeworks are long. The tests and quizzes are very similar to the homeworks. Attendance quizzes were 5% of the grade.

After 8 semesters of classes at GT, she is still easily my favorite professor. I've never had another professor care so deeply about her class and her students. She wants to get to know you and for you to succeed. The subject material was inherently difficult, and she made it engaging and entertaining. Love this professor, and highly recommend her.

Best math professor I've ever had at Tech. She's very caring and is ready to answer any questions you may have. All she wants you to do is to learn something throughout the semester. She also gives partial credits for midterm problems you missed, if you get it right on the final exam. Exams are kiiinda tough. Definitely recommend her!

Prof. Kang is very nice and helpful. She answers questions patiently and she cares about everyone. The course is difficult, and she rushes through the material very fast, so be ready to read the textbook since the lectures won't help a lot. Exams are not easy, but you can definitely do well if you completely understand the material and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is super fun and animated. Her lectures degrade throughout the semester, to the point where she will just write the major ideas and you have to use the textbook to really understand what is going on. Her tests are very hard (she said "I don't believe in easy classes" at some point). She's great but it's a hard class and her lecture style is eh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kang is fine. Lectures weren't great, but usually conveyed the point. Difficulty is fine. Attendance was 5% taken most/some days.

She is extremely sweet, and as much as I want to give her a 5, I just can't. She really is not good at lecturing. She goes way too fast on all the material, and eventually the lectures became ineffective for me, and I read the textbook. Everything else in the class was spot on, though.

She is such a gem. She is genuinely so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She wants you to fully understand the material, so she doesn't get bogged down by the exact grades & gives lots of extra credit. The class definitely gets much harder throughout the semester, but she tries her best to help you through it. class  hard, prof  QUEEN
A great professor who cares about her students. The homeworks were long and the tests were difficult, but she offered generous amounts of extra credit and students learned a lot.

Amazing lectures, everything that came out of her mouth instantly made sense, so I'd def recommend coming to class. You need to put in effort to succeed, but it's absolutely possible. Do the homework! I got A's on the exams and the final, but my quiz average was rough because they are hard quizzes in a short amount of time

Dr. Kang can be a little hard to understand during lectures but she will do anything to help her students and she is absolutely a solid choice for DiffEq. She can be harder than the rest of the diffeq professors but by the end, you'll know diffeq pretty well.

To succeed in this class, you will need to do the optional homework and read the textbook really well. She takes attendance quizzes which is 3% of your grade, and trust me, you'll need every percent you can get, so attend lecture. Def go to recitation, they don't post the answers. Her lecture notes are posted but aren't very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She gives very little mandatory homework, there are attendance quizzes. She does go a little fast but is very understanding and stops for questions frequently. Recitation is important, but optional. She'll curve specific quizzes and test forms.

Kang is an amazing lecturer but her class is hard. The tests and quizzes are similar to the optional homework but Kang is EXTREMELY helpful in office hours. I spent a lot of my time in office hours and she is one of the most caring people I have ever met. I do recommend her just be prepared to do a lot of homework problems.

Kang isn't that bad for DIFF EQ. For some reason the average on the first test was in the 50s... People obviously don't know how to do their homework and study. If you ask your TA for help, do the homework, and study a week before each test, you'll ace it. It's simply just following the same steps to answer a question, like all diff eq.

She truly cares for her students and wants to make sure everyone learns the material. That said, do not be surprised when you make a 49% on the first test which can be quite disheartening... This semester she allowed grade replacement with the final which was super helpful! The best advice I an give you is to go to ALL of her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Test average can get down to mid 40s, her lecture goes super fast and it's very hard to understand and follow. I agree that you can learn a lot of things in her class, but I don't think it's fair for most students to get a low grade with the amount of effort put in. Don't take her unless you don't have other time-consuming courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's no doubt that she cares about each student individually and wants everyone to succeed in her class. However, her lectures are very hard to follow and we go through the material very quickly. She does curve and drop quizzes. Also extra credit projects. Homework is not for a grade but you definitely need to do it. Be prepared to work.
Just no. She is like we need to get things done. Other profs are just slow as heck when she is absolutely fast as heck.
Quiz every week. Fast teacher. She seems obsessed with just completing the lectures without being sure if all her students are catching up. I literally was studying on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She goes over the topics way to fast when all she does is repeat what the textbook says. Although she curves and gives grade replacements, there is always a catch. She makes her test hard. She is a hypocrite. She tells her students that she hates memorizing, but all her exams are based  on memorization of formulas and equations. Don't take her.

Kang is one of the most caring profs I've had, and she curves A LOT. She lectures super fast and her tests and quizzes may be a little more difficult than the other professors who teach the class, but by the end of the class, you WILL know diff eq. As long as you make the effort and show you care, she will make sure you get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kang FLIES; she teaches like she is tied to train tracks with a steam engine barreling towards her. However, she really cares for her students and tries her best to help everyone (can't emphasize this enough). She is very accessible and curves very graciously to compensate for the difficulty of the course and her high expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great professor! She cares a lot about her students and tried to know each student's name by the end of the semester. She goes through the material quickly but will carefully explain anything that you do not understand. Do most of the problems on the homework assignments, and you will do well on the quizzes and tests.

She is a great professor and cares a lot about her students. Covers material quickly but will gladly help students. She made it a point to learn the name of every student in the course. The course isn't terribly hard, though tests and quizzes occasionally seemed a little long. I would definitely take her class again if the option presented itself.

She takes interest in her student's success. I had an extenuating circumstance during finals week and she agreed to give me an I for it. She made the experience of having to take final after a semester bearable with her understanding. She is willing to go out of her way to help and is a great resource. I'd recommend making a personal relationship.

Incredible teacher. Yes, she blows through material like there's a gun to her head, but she's always available to help you through it. Cares about students more than any other prof on campus; I think she actually memorized everyone's name by the end of the course. Top quality - definitely take her because it will help you later.

Honestly one of the best professors I've taken at Tech. She goes through material fast but is always willing to help. Quizzes and exams are heavily based off homework that hardly anyone seems to do. This is probably why so many people think they are so difficult. If you get the chance to take her, then do it. A great professor and a great person.

A good professor, she goes very fast, but if you ask her to slow down, she will.  Diff EQ is not an easy class but if you go to lecture and do the homework, you should do fine (textbook is very helpful).  I would reccommend taking her if you can because as long as you try, you'll do well.

Absolutely horrible professor. If you're taking diff eq, get anyone other than her. She goes over the material so fast that it's impossible for me to comprehend what she's teaching. Her tests are also a bit ridiculous. Too many questions, and extremely difficult to finish. If you do end up taking her, you'll be teaching yourself diff eq.

she is a really good teacher...i failed a test and she said she would basically drop it if i showed that i did well on the remaining tests...the extra credit helped out so much that i ended up with an A without her dropping it...i lucked into this class and was happy..except for waking up at 8

Great teacher! Shows enthusiasm in teaching.  Really wants students to understand (keeps saying this is important, you must know it).  If you attend every class and follow along (without drifting off... she will wake you up though), you can pass her class easily.  Her tests are related to what she taught, with a lot of extra credit problems.

She REALLY cares how well students do in the class and she makes it VERY easy if you do the work, go to class, and pay attention. Every test and quiz has bonus questions that are not any harder than regular questions. Some tests even have a possible 125% or so. The class is easy, but also you really do learn the material while getting a good grade.

If you have this teacher, congratulations, you just missed getting one of the four horsemen. This is one of the easier Calc II teachers at Tech. The only bad thing about her is that she goes REALLY fast in lecture. The way the tests are graded are based solely on partial credit, which is nice. Also, every test/quiz she gives has bonus points.

Dr. Jacobs is one of the best professors i've had. He has a tendency to get off track during lecture, but still did a great job explaining the topics. The class is graded around 8 hws, 3 tests, and an optional final. He provides ample past tests, which the new ones are similar to. Overall great professor.

Larry is a gem. Clearly cares about teaching and students and is super passionate every day. He is very clear about what it going to be on the 1 quiz and 3 midterms, and they are very similar to previous years. Great at explaining conceptual concepts during lectures, super available during and outside of class and is the funniest prof ive ever had.

He was probably one of the funniest teachers I've ever had. he is very all over the place, which can make his notes hard to read sometimes, but if you just do the exam study guides and memorize the problems and what to do it's a pretty easy class.

He's very good at teaching the material, and funny. 8 HW's, and 3 exams, with a final that can be exempt if you have an A in the class after exam 3. Only complaint is he always seems to be eager to get out of his office hours/review sessions/lectures early to go answer emails or go to a meeting. Also, the whiteboard in lecture gets very very messy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nah, the guy below me: "often speaks sour of those who do not get an A" is straight up tweakin

Easy A. NYC dude with several unusual verbal tics. Very messy board work. All assignments involve using past exams, which are nigh-identical to new exams. As a consequence, your flexibility and comfort with the constraining physics is gated due to the limited applications. Not a very kind guy - often speaks sour of those who do not get an A.

He uploads previous tests from semesters (huge help), and also has videos on his canvas in case you miss a lecture or just need it. He's incredibly nice and remembers his students' names as well as directly tells you what will and won't be on the test. His lectures can be hard to follow but he answers questions clearly and thoroughly.

Dr. Jacobs was one of the best professors I've had at Tech. He has very clear expectations for exams (there's 10ish years of practice exams), and if you do well enough on them, you can skip the final. He clearly cares about his students too - he learned all of our names, and he has weekly review sessions for homework and exams. Amazing professor.

He is the best professor I have had so far at tech! He really cares about his students and how well they do. His lectures are a little messy but if you pay attention, it is easy to follow along. He is very helpful in office hours and will take the time to get to know you. He knew most of his students by name by the end of the class.

Professor Jacobs is a very clever professor but his lectures are very disorganized. He writes his teaching material everywhere on the whiteboard and his handwriting is not on the pretty side. His grading is test-heavy but exam problems are reused from old exams and he posts every old exam on Canvas, so studying for the exam is pretty easy.

Not a bad Professor but lectures are very disorganized and sometimes hard to follow, grading is 90% exams with no crib sheets do not take if you test badly. At the end of the semester he decided students with an A were exempt from the final, worth 30% but it was required for all other students and could negatively impact grades. Overall chaotic.
Professor Jacobs might be the best professor at Georgia Tech, this man is a no-brainer for Def Bods. Take him and you will know what you are doing.
Great professor overall. Teaches concepts well in-depth. Work on projects ahead of time. Just grind practice exams and midterms will be fine.

Honestly if you spend a good amount of time on the projects, you should be set for the class. I got a 50 on the 1st project and still ended with an A after doing extra credit on proj 2. Exams are fine as long as you do the past exams she gives out! Pretty fun game project.

Dr. Wills is a great professor and I would highly recommend her for ECE 2035. I was teetering between taking 2035 or 2036 bc I'm EE, but I chose to take 2035 because I heard she is a great professor and that was definitely true. Clear lectures and expectations. Just make sure to pay attention in class and you will be ok!

Very easy class, exams are very easy as long as you practice. Start on the projects way ahead of time. Lots of opportunities to get extra credit and good grades. Weak lecturer in my opinion, but not too bad. Overall, class was very fun and the content was very interesting to learn
She's a nice lady. she always will try to answer your questions to the fullest of her ability. the work takes some figuring out regardless. take her if you're taking 2035.

I wish I did better in this class- the first project was hard and I randomly bombed a test I thought I did well on. Through all of this though, Linda has been the most caring professor I have ever had. She is patient and very fair, which reflects through her TAs who are the same. Go to her and TA office hours, they are awesome!
Linda Wills is soooo caring and nice in test grading!
I will forever miss my goat Rudrunshu Datta
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just a good professor.

Dr. Wills is very good at what she does, she understands the class and its contents well and does a great job of understanding the class. The tests are tough but she is fair on grading, the projects are a time sink but not too difficult. She is always willing to help students so don't be afraid to reach out to her.
Wills is a good professor. Take her if you can. Weren't the most engaging or funny lectures, but good.

Her enthusiasm is awesome and she clearly wants us to succeed and learn a lot.  Sometimes she can be monotone so class can be boring, but the content is incredibly fascinating.  This class has by far been my favorite class at tech.  I will say the projects are actually challenging and intriguing, so I suggest to give it more time than you'd think.

I would say that ECE 2035 is a very tough course. Dr. Wills has helped me out a lot outside of class and she does care about her students. I think the style of teaching is very hard to understand the topics. This course will take a lot of time but there are different ways to do well in the course with the way the grading is.
God Bless Linda Wills

Very project and test heavy courses. TAs are hit or miss but professor Wills is an amazing professor. She developed most of the content for the course and knows exactly how to teach it. Do the extra credit for the first project and START EARLY! Do not get behind like everyone does. You will thank your past self when that day comes around.
Professor Wills is one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech, she cares so much and will set aside time to help you if you ask for it :)

Absolutely take Prof. Wills for 2035. Super caring and helpful in office hours. GTAs were helpful but UTAs were mostly clueless. I thought the exams were pretty easy and past exams are provided but averages were around 75. Homeworks and projects were good and taught a lot! I enjoyed the performance based grading of the first project.

This class may just be very difficult because of the topics but the lectures are hard to follow and the projects given in class have a very rigorous timeline that was pushed back because of how fast it was. The tests are difficult but are graded in a fair way keeping the average at least a 75.

2035 is hard already as is but Wills is very understanding and willing to work with you on anything. Her office hours helped me understand the concepts better but beware of some of the TAs, they are literally no help. Start the homework and projects early because they are very time-consuming and confusing. Prepare to dedicate 15 hours each week.

The secret to this class is if you are stuck go to Dr. Wills office hours. Even if you are not in her section the other professor is usually not the best. The TA's are absolutely useless for this class, do not go to them for help, they never know what they are talking about and they will actually hurt your grade more if you get help from them.

ECE 2035 is brutal, but Dr. Wills makes this class super accessible and interesting. She genuinely cares so much about her students, and will help you out if you're confused with the projects/content or find yourself in a rut with the workload. There's no question about it, take Wills for 2035.

Professor Wills is tough and will require you to learn in order to pass tests and complete the projects. However, she is very available for discussion and highly flexible on due dates. If you need an extension, she'll grant it. If you need suggestions, she'll readily help you reach a solution. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A real gem of a professor. She is extremely caring and wants everybody to succeed. There is tons and tons of extra credit available, and tests are extremely fair. Would highly recommend.

Dr Wills is a great professor for the 2nd year ECE student. 2035 is a lot of work, which is kind of annoying, but it strengthens your problem solving and makes you think, and she will guide and help you if she can! There's also so much extra credit. Hard work is rewarded, and she notices! Lectures are chill. Make a good life decision and take her!

Honestly my favorite teacher I have had at Tech. She gives great lectures and is a very caring and generous professor. There was a lot of work to do in this class but you learn so much and she gives plenty of resources (office hours, TA office hours, extension resources) to lighten the burden. TAKE HER FOR THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE OPTION!!!

Dr Wills is a caring professor but the course is extremely and often unnecessarily hard. Dr Wills often explains incoherently and its hard to follow from one concept to another. At the end it felt like I learned some techniques and skills but did not acquire any knowledge.
Her class was extremely hard for me but she is perhaps the most caring and nicest professors/teachers I have ever had. Just an absolutely amazing human being.

A real gem. She cares so much, and teaches really well. The projects are admittedly hard, but you learn so much by doing them, and when you're done, it feels amazing to look back on what did. Extremely friendly and easy to approach/talk to.
Absolutely fantastic professor.
She's super nice but her class is unnecessarily hard. Not sure if it's her fault but one of the hardest classes I've taken
She was great.

Was honestly probably the best professor I've had here at Tech. She was extremely passionate about the subject and helping her students. Very accessible and reasonable. Also offers heavy EC on projects which is helpful, especially for those who may not excel on timed exams.
Very accessible and cares about her students. Offers extra credit on both major projects. Tests are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome prof! Go to lectures, start projects early and get the extra credit, and ask when you need to (prof and TAs are all very accessible). Grading is relatively lenient. No textbook needed. Just take her! Compiler Appreciated.

Great choice for ECE 2035! Engaging lectures that provided practice for exams and examples for homework. Projects have lots of room for extra credit. Tests are not too difficult, but you definitely need to prepare for them. She is always willing to go over questions in office hours or at the end of lectures.

Don't even scroll any further down the page! JUST TAKE HER!!! Tips: - Start the final project as soon as you get the PDF. I started the final project the week before thinking I would have enough time but was not able to finish - Don't undermine the extra credit - Practice exams are golden resources for the exams. Do as much of them as possible
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ECE 2035 is a very hard course in my opinion but Professor Wills teaches the content really well and offers many resources to students and is really generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wills had sometimes convoluted lectures, but she's very easy to understand, answers questions carefully, is extremely accessible and is really understanding and caring. 2035 is a very well structured class and a lot of emphasis is put onto projects with opportunities for extra credit.

The best professor in the ECE department, period. She needs to teach some higher level ECE courses because many of those courses are poorly structured (which is why I switched to CS), and we need professors like her to teach them (also considering the fact that she has 3 degrees from MIT!!!!!!).

2035 is a class with rather difficult material, but she is so passionate about it and teaching that you can effectively pick it up, and if you don't immediately, she is one of the most generously available profs outside of class I've had. She truly cares about each and every one of her students and their success. The last project has generous EC.

A genuine teacher with a very kind heart. She actually increased class size pre-semester to accommodate me (an international student) who could not register early, took personal interest to ask why I did marginally in the beginning of the semester and gave extra credit just to emphasize the fact that I completed the projects by myself. A+ prof.

Very good lecturer. May get confusing at times bc she is very passionate about the content and knows it well. More than willing to help you after class. Content is difficult. Study hard. Start homework and projects early, and use Piazza. Never misses class. Attendance is mandatory to pass, bc online resources don't explain it all & text is useless.

Prof Wills was great for 2035. Sometimes she can be a little scattered during lectures but she is very intelligent and knows what she is doing. If you don't understand something in class she is very approachable during office hours and will help you. The projects can be difficult, but some involve extra credit. Tests can be tricky. Study study.
Very helpful

Nicest lady ever.  Explains material clearly and always offers to help you privately.  Brought candy and cookies to class several times.  Super-easy project that was basically a free A test grade.  Tests are extensive and thorough and require some studying.  Fun class.

Sankar likes Dad jokes but he'll occasionally slip in a good one. His lectures were very insightful and thorough, and I feel I learned a great deal in this course. His exams and homework were also fair with some conceptual and math problems. Just don't get on your phone or laptop because he will call you out in class. Otherwise, he's great.

Lectures are amazing and intuitive, and you will learn a lot. Homework and exams are fair. He is old-school though. Even at the graduate level, he requires attendance. No laptops or phones. He will stop class to call out late students, and will single out anyone he thinks isn't paying attention

Overall, class is good but will feel like high school

Summer AE6701 MS. Was way too much info. had to use an old Software required to complete the papers. it was not easy to use if your not familiar. He post videos of how to use the software but its still too much info. He is a very tough grader too. The papers just get worse and more time demanding. Don't trust your good grade on the first paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Sankar is the best professor I have ever had. He makes lectures enjoyable; homework is difficult but short. Its obvious that he loves teaching and cares about his students. Be prepared to take notes on an Ipad or notebook (he doesn't like laptop notes) He is a very fair grader and throughout an awful semester he was the one bright spot.

Dr. Sankar is a great professor who loves dad jokes. Be sure to attend class and pay attention, as the homework follows his lectures and the exams often come from the homework. Most example problems willl be done in recitation while lectures focuses more on concepts. Also he hates people using laptops and phones while he's lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely a bad professor for vehicle performance. Class was easy but his projects were tedious and a waste of time, especially when he would tell us to his ignore his explicit instructions and redo the entire project the day before it was due. Lectures were about as entertaining as listening to your grandpa ramble about the good old days.

This is for his summer AE/ME - 4701.

If you are an ME student, who has 0 knowledge of aerodynamics or wind foils, this class can be extremely challenging and feel like you're drinking water from a fire hydrant. I don't know who thought it would be a good idea to try and make a year long class into a 5 week class.

Watch the lecture videos very closely, write the report as you watch. Grading seems to be based on concept understanding more than calculated correctness. 5 reports are the total grade, 3 wks apart ea. Prof was available outside of class. Rprt 3 (airfoil design) is analysis heavy, look at the Weibull excel doc in the next module, it does it helps.
I also took AE 4701 with Dr. Sankar. Very nice guy. Fair grader, especially with tougher assignments. Clearly very knowledgeable. Would love to take more classes with him.

He is incredibly smart and tries his best to give you that knowledge. While the material can be confusing, that's kind of the point with aerodynamics. No collaboration allowed on homework and the tests have moderate difficulty, but for the Limerick students he gave us all a liberal "good faith curve". Just make the effort to pay attention in class.

(This is a late rating but I took him in Fall 2022), but hands down made Aerodynamics my favorite class of Fall 2022. He has incredibly good lectures, and was always open to questions throughout. I loved that we worked with industry-level tools like XFOIL and AVL as that definitely helped with my extracurriculars. Would definitely recommend him.

3 tests, HW 25% each. STRICT about 0 collaboration on HW. Grades HARSH (tests), but the 3rd test (which subbed as final) was LIBERALLY graded, where we were happily SHOCKED to get a class avg of 96%. CARES for his students. Lectures well. Go to him and he will help. Over time, I gained IMMENSE respect for him. Makes you work, but you get rewarded.

Prof Sankar is really nice, his classes aren't hard as long as you listen to his lecture (he gives you a list of things that will be in the exam, so if you have that there is no chance you'll fail). He doesn't prepare you in the best manner for grad school (if you plan on going to grad school), but I still recommend him.

Professor Sankar is a great teacher, and I learned a lot in his class. Homework isn't bad, tests are not too bad and weekly quizzes are pretty easy. He cares about his students but can sometimes be unclear in conveying his expectations for assignments.

Dr. Sankar is an excellent professor that is extremely clear on what he wants and is readily accessible to clarify any questions you have. One of the best in the department. I highly suggest you take him if you have the chance.
great prof
Really helpful and lectures are very clear.  Tests follow up on what was taught in homeworks, easy A
Um...other than the fact that GT 1000 is a joke; let's see, he knows everyone in the AE department, which can be extremely beneficial.
Great teacher. Easy if you attend class. Very helpful
Easiest A I've ever gotten
Pretty easy tests. Had good grade distributions in all his classes.
Extremely nice and helpful.  Very boring though.  Overall, however, I'd recommend him.
I'm sorry if you have Dan
Dan Lotan was an inspiration to me. His instruction has changed the course of my life. He is the songbird of our generation.

major discord mod vibes, confusing instructions 
takes himself way too seriously 
zero social awareness 
don't take his lab unless you enjoy wasting tuition
he reminds me of a discord mod and talks with a lisp. whatever you do, don't take his class.
rage. bait.
yikes. no bueno
1 credit special topics "Professional Skills for Math" (not multi). Very informative and not too time-consuming, great way to meet other math majors in your class.

When I took this class in Summer 2025, Lehmann had been working on reworking his grading system. TLDR, He would give us multiple chances to show mastery in each learning objectives, spread throughout multiple tests, quizzes, etc. If you obtained enough of these mastery points for each topic, you would move up in the grading scale.

I'm not even in his course I'm in 2550 but I'm using his lecture videos from Spring 2025 to self-study and this guy is actually the goat. He's great at explaining the concepts and watching his videos at 2x has been awesome.

His grading scale makes it very easy for you to get an A. As long as you do well earlier in the semester, you can basically guarantee an A. Topics are hard but if you practice the material he gives on Canvas, his exams and quizzes are exactly the same. He explains everything in lecture very well too so going to lecture would help.

He is a great lecturer and covers lots of helpful examples in class. The tests were difficult at times but fair and he gives lots of practice sets to help prepare for quizzes and exams. He also gives lots of opportunities to do well in the course so you could fully get a 0 on a midterm and still have an A overall.

He changed the grading structure drastically this semester (multiple attempts to complete set learning targets). Difficult exams and quizzes like previous semesters, but an almost guaranteed A if willing to put in the work. Best math department lecturer I've had; fantastically knowledgeable and engaging. Take him if you enjoy math!

He's a good lecturer, do the practice for every learning objective and you are prepared for all of the quizzes and tests. His grading system is very fair and gives a decent amount of extra credit if you put in a little of effort. What you put into this class you will get out, and nothing is too difficult with plenty of chances to make up past prob.

Y'all should be grateful this man isn't teaching multi next semester. Tests are nowhere near easy if you're not good at what he's good at in terms of sketching and thinking about math. He's a good lecturer, just don't know why he thinks that's a good excuse to give complicated exams that deal with small little details we barely wen't over in class.

Really good lecturer and explains the concepts well! He restructured his class to make it easier for students to get an A which I appreciate. The tests are much harder than the studio quizzes so I would try my best to get all the quizzes correct. Attendance in class and studio is not mandatory but does count towards extra points towards your grade

Dr. Lehmann is a good lecturer and a good person but his tests are god awfully hard if you're not math inclined like he is. Computationally very heavy and it makes a Calc class more like precalc for literally no reason. Beware he also isn't kind enough to recycle questions and most of what I've heard is that the final is even harder. Just beware

Dr. Lehmann is a caring professor who wants his students to do well, however, his class is very test-heavy, and the tests themselves are very difficult. I have heard he is the best lecturer compared to others, so I was excited for this class, but I did not expect the class to be so test-heavy.

Three exams and they pretty much determine your grade in the class. However, go to studio because that 1.5% grade boost from studio participation will matter later. I had a bad TA, and I definitely think this made the course much harder for me than it had to be. Studio questions are hard, but the level of difficulty resembles exams somewhat.

He makes the course wayyy harder than it needs to be. Multi concepts are easy but the exams were difficult. There's grade replacement on the final exam (replaces each exam) but don't rely on it because the final was a lot harder than exams. Definitely look over the T/F questions on past exams since he reuses them with slightly different wording.

Rude in office hours, toughest grader I've had at Tech. Just watch his lectures; he speaks the clearest English. Other profs have easier exams. I was failing all semester but got a B from the final. Expects you to be a great mathematician and talks down to you if you're not. I was so excited for multi, but he ruined it for me just glad I'm done.

I didn't go in person since before the first test and I had no issue learning the content from his videos he posts. Very test heavy course, but very few if any tricks on tests and they are very similar to past exams. He gives plenty of opportunities if you mess up, and the final is optional which was huge during finals week.

Dr. Lehmann's lectures are really engaging and he's good at explaining difficult concepts. His exams are def harder than other sections, but I do think his amazing lectures make up for that. He also gives 1.5% extra credit for attending studio. He really cares about his students and is just overall a nice guy. One of the best profs I've taken!

It is unfortunate that his exams are so insanely difficult - completely beyond HW level questions and often required very creative applications of concepts. Lectures are well structured and all recorded and uploaded, which was helpful. I had a bad TA who did not know what he was doing, which did not help. Great guy otherwise.

Good lecturer, however, tests are unreasonably difficult especially when comparing to the other professors. You're better off watching his lectures online and taking another professor. Multivar concepts are not hard to grasp, but he makes the tests annoying.

By far one of the best professors I have had at Georgia Tech. Yes, his tests are harder than that of other sections however I think that is compensated by the fact that he is such an amazing lecturer. His passion about the topic is evident and he is caring and very accessible outside of class. 10/10 professor.

By far the best lecturer for Multi, no doubt about it. I will say, his exams tend to be noticeably harder than other professors' (b/c he is the course coordinator), but if you go to class you will get an amazing grasp on the concepts with no issues. To prepare for each exam, I suggest taking all available practice midterms and you will do fine.
Lectures are excellent (and recorded). Quizzes and homeworks prep you well for exams, and the final is optional. Exams aren't super easy but they're straightforward--if you study, you'll do okay.

Best professor I've had at Tech so far. He makes guided notes for every lecture that are posted online WITH recordings, so you never actually need to go to lecture. Past exams are super similar to the real deal, and even though they are hard, they are never surprising. Super receptive to feedback as well! Could not recommend him more.

Amazing lectures and explanations are pretty good, with that being said I would rather take a different Proffesor class and watch his lectures, test are harder than they are supposed to be, but good content overall.
Great professor. He definitely cares about his students. Keeps students involved during class, which helps a lot with understanding concepts. Optional exam was nice.

Pretty good lecturer, incredibly hard exams. I worked my tail off in this class and got an A, but it was not worth the headache after seeing the difficulty of other prof's exams. He's not the worst, but I would've rather watched his lecture videos and take another prof's exams.

Lecture was great and easy to understand. Cares if students understand the math. Lectures were recorded, and full grade replacement on the final. The final is broken into 3 parts. Doing practice exams, homework and showing up to lecture helped me succeed on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good prof and class, exempting the final is easy as long as you actually try on his exams, don't count on replacing grades later. You can't blow off the homework or the quizzes, it makes up way more of the grade than you think. If you go to class, he tells you everything you need to know and sometimes gives hints about stuff.

Nice guy, okay prof. Studio quizzes are MUCH harder than they had to be. I'd say the tests were mostly fair (with a few exceptions). Use chat for all HW, it's irrelevant. Guided lecture notes. Got a 56, 74, 76 on exams. Final was grade replacement (I took part 1, got a 90, ended the class with a B). It's a doable class, just study hard for tests.

he ruined my grade. he made the tests so difficult. i swear to god i saw other classes and they were much easier than ours. the final was supposed to replace our test grades but the average of them were a 75. you'd think he'd help his students and make the final at least easier but nope, his test consists of stuff we barely go over.

Dr. Hunter is a great professor in general. His teaching style and the quizzes were easy. But the exams are extremely difficult compare to any of the past exams. He would literally gives our the hardest/confused questions on the exams and the finals. The class average was 75% and people constantly complaining about the difficulty of the exams. RUN
He is a good lecturer, but his tests are the most difficult out of all the multi professors. He is also rude during office hours, and his class is 75% tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is very hard, and Lehmann doesn't make it any easier. He is rude whenever answering questions and seems like he doesn't want to be answering questions in the first place. His tests are also much harder compared to other professors. I would've just taken a different professor with easier exams and watched Lehmann's lecture videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly a standout professor at GT. Besides being incredibly smart, Dr. Lehmann is caring and passionate about his professing. He is extremely consistent in his lecture structure, making it easy to follow despite the very fast nature of teaching Multi. He also responds to every single email within 5 minutes and was very responsive to a health issue.

Easy: here's how I did well without going to a single lecture after test 1. ChatGPT all homeworks, they arent that relevant to what youre gonna get on the tests. Study the day before for studio quizzes through practice problems in his lecture videos. Just watch all lecture videos the weekend before exam and you will do fine. He is a great lecturer

He's a decent professor overall but be ready to deal with tricky questions and sometimes obtuse homework. He can be rude somethings during office hours even if he doesn't mean it. Tests are easier than HW and Wrkshts and the Math Lab comes in clutch. Overall,not terrible but not perfect, take him if no better options. Also there's redo's on finals.

He is an ok professor overall. I dont know why but his exams are brutally difficult and do not line up with the practice questions he goes over in lectures. You can exempt the final if you get a good grade on your 3 midterms. Multi is a difficult course and has a lot of workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally think he makes the content more difficult than it needs to be. Lectures don't align with problems in HW or tests. Workload is reasonable

Prof Lehmann seems to not care about students' success in his class. Not very understanding either. If you go to office hours he will watch you struggle to work through a problem, giving little/no guidance. Tests are difficult and partial credit is minimal.

I unfortunately did not do well on the first exam even after tutoring, PLUS, etc. I studied very hard for the second exam, and I thought I did well (I did not).He refused to let me see my exam paper before the drop deadline, so I could not request a regrade and had to drop. His class is notorious for harsh/incorrect grading. He has no empathy.

Dr Hunter is a good professor his lectures are good but really slow. By the end of the semester I stopped going to class and then just watched the lectures later in 2x speed. Hes really nice but the exams are hard and grading is difficult too.

His lectures were great, plus they were all recorded which was a huge help. He is also really nice if you ever need help or have an excused absence. The class material and tests are a pretty difficult and are graded pretty harshly though.

Great lectures. Good notes, recorded lectures. His website has previous semester materials. Helpful in office hours, responds to emails fast. Easy on studio quiz grades, drops 1 default + another for doing cios. Hard exams, 25% each but optional final improves exam grades. Lots of practice content on canvas+webwork hw. Great guy take his class!
