Goes a bit slow but makes sure you understand everything. Also he makes an effort to learn everyones names. As long as you pay attention in lecture and ask questions you should be fine. Really helpful in office hours.

Don't listen to the hater that rated Prof. Lehmann a 1. His test are by far the easiest one out of all the multi teachers here at GT. The lectures are filled with examples, all lectures are recorded so you can rewatch if needed. Final are formatted so that its optional and it can only improve your grade (can never hurt your grade).

Lehmann makes his class more difficult than it needs to be and he grades very very hard. His lectures do not line up with homework or studio worksheets. His tests are very difficult and hard to do well on. Would not take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 weeks into the course I am already impressed by how well Dr.Lehman teaches. He makes the effort in a large lecture hall to remember students names and his lecture notes are well organized and easy to follow. The absolute GOAT.

I struggled in this class but Dr. Lehmann is a phenomenal professor. The class is very organized with clear expectations. The tests are pretty difficult and may contain a problem you haven't seen before. But overall a very fair class with a caring and involved professor.
Dr. H is the best and always willing to help. His exams are really tough so prepare well ahead of time.
Dr. H is the love of my life. Amazing professor, super understanding of students, highly recommend.
I would die for this man

Multi is not an easy class, but Dr. H tries to make it as intuitive and logical as possible. You will heavily dive into concepts you learnt in calc 1 and 2 so you need to be incredibly sharp about those before this class, otherwise you will struggle immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lehmann knows his material well and teaches with genuine passion. Expect a quiz every week and reasonable amount of homework. My only advice is that you have to actively try keeping up with the course material or they'll pile up; he's hard to follow when there is too much information. Overall, a caring professor who knows what he's doing.

Hunter is great he really cares about his students. expect quizzes every week. The exams were decent if you study well they are fine. I would definitely recommend hunter I had no problems other than some occasional messy hand writing lol

Great teacher. His lectures were dry but he was always very receptive to questions and is very patient to walk you through the material if necessary. Going to office hours is also very helpful. The exams were tricky but if you keep up with lectures and work through homework problems/studio worksheets, you'll be fine.

Very caring guy but a bit monotone, which for a 3 PM class is brutal. Overall good job at covering material, some units better than others (oof line integrals). Extremely accommodating and was willing to move exam/quiz dates for me because of a non-academic conflict. Didn't do as well as I wanted this semester but that mainly falls on me.

Very caring a kind prof, and also super accommodating when you're sick. Had the semester from hell and probably would've withdrawn if I didn't have Lehmann. Only thing is he's a little monotone, and his test problems can be pretty difficult. Plenty of resources given though.
Great professor imo. Tests generally don't have a lot of calculations and instead revolve around understanding of concepts which is great. I think the course is pretty fairly assessed.

Very nice and caring professor. Very clear about what will be on the exam and what won't be. Exams can be a bit tough and long, but fair. Quizzes are also very fair. I would highly suggest taking him.

Super monotone and almost put me to sleep every lecture. Literally couldn't tell the difference between background noise and him lecturing, dude needs to learn how to present and teach. He's decent, but I'd find a teacher that's better if you have the opportunity.

Dr. Lehmann is a very caring professor and very clear in his grading and instruction. He wants his students to succeed and is conscious of his students' needs. His lectures are a bit dry, but he his thorough in his explanations and goes at a very reasonable pace. He is definitely worth taking.
Amazing, understanding professor who gives great lectures and wants his students to succeed. He is not only very knowledgeable but a great teacher; he makes his classes easy to understand.

I sat in the front row, didnt miss a lecture, and took notes. Didnt matter, the tests had nothing to do with the lectures or the homework. The only reason the test averages go up is because half of the class dropped. Dont take this dude.

Genuinely such a bad professor, tests were insanely hard for no reason compared to other classes, no cios incentive, no extra credit, lectures sometimes gave wrong information, and homeworks did not reflect exam questions. Past exams also do not reflect the exams he gives now. don't take him
Bad lecturer, and bad study materials, tests were too difficult and tested too niche of topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this guy at all cost if you wanna save your grade. I'd give 0 zero stars if I could. His exams are so much worse than the other classes for no reason.

I would give zero stars if I could. Professor docks points for not showing work in the exact format he has in his head. Students shouldn't be punished for actually understanding the material. If the answer is right, the thinking was right. Avoid if you have any other option. Your grade will reflect his inane standards, not your actual knowledge.
Powell is a really good lecturer and works very hard (especially in office hours) to ensure that every student has an understanding of the material.
Great professor across the board. Clear expectations, fair exams and homework, provides practice midterms/finals, best handwriting I've ever seen across all my schooling. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Powell is one of the greatest professors I've encountered- not only are his lectures phenomenal, they're accessible for people of all ability levels, and he is very approachable for question and clarification- including mid lecture.

Best professor I had this semester. Very passionate about abstract linear algebra. Exams and quizzes are manageable if you are willing to work. The class was tough due to many abstract concepts but it was fun and worth it. Definitely choose over MATH 1554, but expect to work harder.

The class material was so hard for me, but that's typical for Multivar at GT and wasn't really because of the professor. He's one of the better ones for this topic in my opinion. He's clearly knowledgeable and engaged in this topic and explains it quite clearly. However, the tests were like two levels more difficult than the practice and lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although professor doesn't really matter for large classes, I will say this professor teaches like you're reading a mathematics proof textbook. He introduces topics in a very formal and theorem based way followed by examples I found helpful. It works for some ppl and doesn't for others. He's a knowledgeable guy, but remember it more abt the TAs.

I liked Matthew Powell's classes! His lectures are all recorded online, so you don't have to go to class to stay up to date. He has really nice handwriting, super organized, and really knows his stuff. Super chill and kind guy. He really makes you think on his tests tho. If you want to get a good foundation in multi, take his class!!

He gave me a higher grade than I deserved which I'm very grateful for and why I'm rating him higher than I would have normally. However, his midterms were nothing like the past midterms he gave us for practice. I also had a hard time understanding his lectures. Also I think he weighted the midterms way too heavily and they were graded harshly.

Great lecturer and posted everything online. I attended lectures maybe 3 times the entire semester and scraped by with an A. Would have been way easier if I actually showed up, which is how calculus classes tend to be. His video lectures were great and the textbook is one of the few actually decent calc textbooks.

I really liked Powell. He was funny and you can tell that he truly cared about teaching. His lectures were a bit tedious at times, but he posts them on Canvas after class. His handwriting is IMMACULATE. Would recommend.

Prof Powell was a nice guy, but his long, yapful lectures were brutal. His tests were also hard next to the simple practice in class and practice for the final. His tests normally had one or two items that were mentioned once in lecture and never again. You may notice how many times I mention tests and that is because 3 midterms are 75% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OK lecturer, but very hard tests. He makes them much harder than the practices for some reason and compared to other teachers. Avoid if you wanna do your best

{J}:There really isn't anyone like him. I mean come on, what a man. His tests are so unpredictable and {O}:exciting that you really never know what's coming next! I was on my toes the entire semester. His {K}:powerful voice and deep tone strike the multivariable knowledge straight into my heart. Prepare to {E}:learn a lot about your self respect :D

Avoid this guy at all costs. Lectures are 75 minutes of pointless rambling for 10 minutes of real content. Exams cover random throwaway comments from weeks ago, not the actual material. His voice is worse than putting a cheese grater to my ear and yet somehow sleep-inducing. You'll leave more confused than when you started. Total waste of time.
Intuitive and engaging lectures (which are also recorded). I believe the exams are noticeably harder than the other sections, but not to the point where it should affect a letter grade.

I emailed him about something important, and it took NINE days for him to respond. His lectures were detailed, but confusing. I only understood the material when my studio TA explained it in a better way. My advice - do/go to everything, the homework, the studio worksheets, the lectures, the studios.

A good teacher who helps students understand the difficult topics that multi presents. At first the class in general seems very complicated but you get the hang of things as the course goes on, and the teacher will make it as "easy" as possible for you to be comfortable with the topics as well.

Don't be fooled by the bad reviews. Powell is a very good teacher, multi is just a class that combines linear algebra and calculus so people dont do well. His lectures are very clear and paced well, and you are encouraged to ask questions or solve examples in class. I would definitely reccommend taking his class.

Mathew is not a very good lecturer. I found his lectures very uninteresting, and the examples he teaches don't prepare you for the exams at all. The examples he gave in class were very easy and simple but the test questions were much harder. I definitely recommend taking a different professor.
Pretty good lectures and tests were very similar to practice tests. He also gives plenty of examples in class that are similar to exam questions.

Professor Powell was decent, examples in class were fairly similar to exam questions. Lectures were fairly dry but mainly because of the material and not the prof. Exams are fairly easy if you attend lecture.

Matthew Powell is everything you want from a teacher. His tests are similar to his practice tests, and the final is a grade replacement for the midterms. For Fall 2024, he made the final extremely achievable if you studied. Overall, I definitely recommend taking him because he is fair with grading and a great lecturer.

Matthew Powell was not a great lecturer. Our tests were incredibly difficult compared to other sections, and we had constantly lower averages than the rest. Lectures are boring, and the examples he gives you do NOT prepare you well. TAs are the only saving grace for this class.

He is an okay professor. His lectures are boring and not very engaging. He talks too slow, and terrible at explaining. His exams are more difficult than the other sections, and it doesn't help that his TA's this semester weren't that great. The only good thing is that he records his lectures.

Powell is a nice dude and is very good at teaching, but his exams are weighted heavily and are much harder than what's seen in class. On the 3rd midterm, each multiple choice question was worth 10% (which comes out to 2.5% of your FINAL grade). Tough to get an A, there are easier multi professors, but if you want to really learn, Powell is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, made concepts very clear. Records all lectures. Tests are kind of hard but I feel that the questions in lecture were good preparation unlike what others are saying. Just go to lecture and studio and you will be ok. You do not have to take the final unless you want to replace a midterm grade, useful if you have a lot of finals

He's not that bad of a professor, but he's not that good either. Some of the topics seen on the test sometimes weren't what was gone over in class which is what I think contributed to the low average test scores.

Dr. Powell is a good lecturer, but his exams are notoriously difficult. His sections averaged around 10% worse than the others for each midterm. He showed a lack of empathy towards students worried about the exam scores during class. It honestly feels like he's trying to prove himself as a tough professor, as this is his first year at Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rumore is a super chill prof. Just show up to class, complete the assignments, do the readings, talk a bit in class and you will do fine. Take this guy for ENGL 1102

Dude is genuinely just a great guy, very forgiving and his class is a free A if you just show up and say one or two things. Great feedback on every assignment and the topic was interesting (for me personally). Lectures are a little boring, but if he sees you try he wont let you get anything below an A.

Pretty funny guy and makes the class very straightforward: do the assignments, you'll do fine. Can go on tangents about simple things, but overall enjoyed the class. Can miss ~4 lectures before being penalized. Does keep track of attendance of every lecture.

Very chill grader and lenient with deadlines. will not let u get below an A if u show up. topic is boring. you dont really need to pay attention but he's really nice and cares and is fun to listen to. there are textbooks but you dont need to get them. would deffo recommend for an easy A

although some of the projects were time-consuming, this class was easy overall and follows the syllabus clearly. professor rumore is a laid-back, nice guy who teaches well and offers extensions on assignments through an organized log. if you do what he asks, then you're basically guaranteed an A for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Rumore is a super chill and nice guy. Like most English classes, your grade is based on 4 big projects, which he gives you lots of time to work on. However, lectures are extremely boring, which is not really his fault. You aren't given class time to work on projects, so expect to spend time outside of class working on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: As easy as it can possibly get in terms of grading, but accompanied by very dry lectures. Rumore is incredibly kind and understanding, which is fantastic - though I have strong suspicions he recycles feedback for students, which feels pretty disingenuous. If you just want to get by English with 0 stress and a guaranteed A, then Rumore is your guy,
He's chill lowk a lil boring but hes pretty easy on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is a GUARANTEED A... if you do the assignments with some effort. For lecture, most of the time he is just talking about stuff, but he will let you work on assignments in class. In addition, he makes sure everyone is track with deadline and offers extensions when needed. Projects/artifacts require some effort, but it is nothing too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rumore is a pretty good professor. He is a pretty easy grader and tries to make his lectures engaging. Lectures were pretty boring though and attendance is mandatory. There are three big assignments that are graded, but the deadlines are also really flexible. This class is pretty easy as long as you show up and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rumore's class was so chill. Other than actual assignments, I barely had to do any readings/homework. His lectures are boring and attendance is mandatory, but it was so worth it. He's a really easy grader and gives extensions on all the assignments. He's really nice and approachable overall. Definitely recommend taking him!
Awesome guy. He is super nice and just overall a really compassionate guy. Take him!

Professor Rumore is very passionate about English, but his class is very boring. I felt like I could get an A without even going to class, but attendance was mandatory. He takes over 2 months to grade assignments which is a little annoying, but overall it's a very easy class.

Gives a 100 for almost all assignments as long as you submit everything on the rubric. Attendance is mandatory and his lectures are pretty boring. But does give extensions for all assignments and very approachable by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! He was as fun as a professor could be for a long time block. Few projects throughout the semester. Readings were interesting and, while not actually required, were engaging. Would totally reccomend.

Tries his best to make lecture as interesting as possible for an english class. While there's not a lot of work to do, the couple of projects over the semester do take a considerable amount of time and effort.
He was a great teacher who cared a lot for his students. Easy A and gave a 100 for completion on pretty much all the assignments. Highly recommend you take him!
His lectures are a little long and boring but other than that everything is very easy. He is a super easy grader and the assignments are not complicated.
take this class for an easy A, gave out a lot of 100s. the projects are a bit of effort, but nothing more than what is expected of a GT english class. 10/10 recommend for engl1102

Prof. Rumore is a really great professor- take him if you have the chance. Besides the class time being a little too long for any teacher to make interesting, he does try his best, and is truly the sweetest teacher I had all year. you get more time on projects if needed and is a lenient grader. he also gives awesome feedback and guidance.

Very easy prof, lot of reading hw but I didn't do any of it and was totally fine, mostly just for in class discussion. Lectures are boring and go until the end or slightly late, but he does talk about some interesting stuff. Take for an easy A, grading is really lenient.

Dr. Rumore really cares about the topics he teaches and a lot of thought goes behind his assignments and lectures. He sets you up for success for the Final Portfolio, as you are required to create multiple drafts and really work through your assignments. Now...the lectures are BORING as all get out, but overall it's a really easy class!

The class was pretty easy. Good amount of outside reading. The lectures/class discussions felt repetitive sometimes. The projects are somewhat difficult but he is very clear with what it takes to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading was clear and easy. Just go to class and do your work and you will be fine. He is very passionate about the topic. Only complaint is that his class never gets out early and sometimes the lectures are long.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and is very interested in the class topic, which is appreciated. The class is very little work, with some readings at the beginning of the semester + 3 projects. He's very positive with his feedback. My only complaint is that the lectures are long and repetitive, and class never ends early.
Professor Rumore is really nice and grades fairly easily and cares about his students, but I found his class kinda boring
make sure you dont skip any class u will fall behind
Amazing lecturer. Wants you to succeed and learn from the class. Extremely passionate about what he teaches. The GOAT.

Naeemi was a good professor and managed well through a very difficult subject. He understands the content very well and provides a lot of supporting material to help students gain a better understanding. He is very accommodating and supportive and wants to see students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Naeemi is da GOAT. He prioritizes learning over making the class unnecessarily hard and his lectures are super easy to follow along with. When he asks the class a question and we can't answer, he goes back over the material like a bro. Great prof, great guy, take his class.

Rigorous professor without being unreasonably difficult. He knows the material really well and genuinely enjoys teaching students. He emphasizes class participation and his lectures are informative. Most of the grade came from biweekly quizzes and homework assignments. 10/10 would recommend.
The course was okay in terms of contents. The professor did not cover materials that appeared in the exams.

This course was broad and ranges from device limitations to system limitations. Dr Naeemi was amazing at getting concepts across to students of different backgrounds within electronics, and the transitions felt very smooth. This was the best course I took at Gatech until date- mainly cause of the teaching style. I strongly recommend this experience

Naeemi is such a bro! Seriously, I want to give him a hug he's so awesome. At Gatech a teacher of this caliber is unheard of! If you're wondering what professor to take 3040 with: STOP! This is him! Great teaching, prepares you for test, gives similar practice test online, and really cares about his students. Naeemi is a God!

Professor Naeemi did an excellent job of articulating the subject matter. He was very approachable and seemed genuinely interested in your understanding of the topics. Dr. Naeemi emphasizes classroom involvement, so make sure you're up to date before coming to class!

Best professor @ GT. Very sharp and enthusiastic about course material (akin to his area of research). Approachable and fair. Was exceptional at determining what might be the students' stumbling block(s), and addressing said topics lucidly . Would recommend without reservation or hesitation.

Prof. Nagy is a cynical but very funny guy. He's invested in his students' learning but his assignments aren't exactly straightforward. Rather, he wants you to develop a strong intuition for controls. HW makes up most of the final grade and can tend to be long/difficult but reasonable as long as you are extremely thorough & don't wait last minute.

The class is very homework intensive with it being 60% of the grade. Many of the problems require double checking the slides and textbooks. This made the quizzes and final seem super easy. No material was given for the exam but none was really required. Prof Nagy is very caring and accessible outside class.
funny and puts effort into lectures, controls sucks so avoid but he made it better- very understanding guy

Controls is inherently difficult, and whilst occasionally tough to follow the lectures do serve the purpose of explaining the material, and even further, preparing us for real world engineering. Quiz feedback has been prompt, and expectations are outlined clearly.

Very very tough. Lectures were not useful and his slides were not helpful to understand the content. Homeworks were incredibly difficult and did not match lecture content. Grading was slow and feedback was unhelpful and sometimes demeaning. Final exam was very difficult with no preparation material provided. Avoid.

Extremely unintuitive lectures with zero example problems at the level of difficulty of the homework assignments, which led to tens? of hours spent completing each homework. Textbooks, random pdfs from other universities, and controls YouTubers taught me most of the relevant material I needed to complete the assignments.

Considering the difficulty of the class, Professor Nagy is incredible at explaining the concepts- yes, quizzes are tough, but they've been given back with helpful feedback and chances to improve. A great guy, open to helping always, and I would take the class again. The difficulty is high, but the Prof is great.

Worst professor and class I have ever been subject to. Lectures made zero sense. He cannot explain concepts clearly. Even the lecture slides jump all over. Homeworks extremely difficult, quizzes extremely easy, final was difficult with absolutely no way to prepare. He took forever to grade some homeworks and constantly gave weak excuses. Good luck.

Professor Nagy is a good guy but I would not take controls with him again. There are 5 homeworks which are 60% of the grade and the average on all of them was about an 80. You never really learn the stuff because the only test is the final. The final was very difficult and I felt very unprepared by the class for it.

The majority of your grade will be decided by homework assignments which are graded extremely strictly. Minor algebraic errors will affect your entire problem with no leniency for propagation of error and no consideration of actual understanding of the material. Frequently creates trick questions in the homework and quizzes. Lectures are mid.

Class was lecture heavy and he primarily speaks from powerpoint slides, which are posted alongside video lectures on canvas. Exams were open note/book and fairly straightforward. He does not know how to use Aspen and had the TAs teach that section, which was highly confusing. The class will be more difficult if you have not used Aspen before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. Can't complain.

Nair is clearly not enthusiastic about teaching; lectures are dry and willingness to compromise with students is minimal. He required a final exam for a 1 credit hour class. His homework requires the textbook extensively and examples covered in lecture are irrelevant for quizzes. Attendance is required even though he reads verbatim off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nair treats his safety class like middle school students with minimal respect for students concerns. Textbook use is heavy for homework despite only being a 1 credit hour class. He is not enthusiastic about the course which shows in his dry lectures. When brought up that the textbook use is too heavy for 1 credit hour he just said "I disagree".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagel is so out of touch with the current experience of working in tech despite teaching "Technical Communications." A lot of things that she teaches are self-explanatory which leaves the class being a combination of useless lectures and time-consuming projects. I have never seen a classroom as miserable as hers :(

The most life-draining class I've ever taken in my life. It is actually insufferable to listen to her lecture about genuinely the most pointless things that clearly nobody cares about. The assignments are all just busy work to take time out of your other important classes. The worst is that she treats her class and students like high schoolers.

Student asks clarifying question about a provided sample for an assignment. Nagel lambasts it assuming it's the student's work. When corrected that it's in fact from her own example document, she still doesn't clarify. Of what use is this professor if she cant make a coherent assignment or even realize shes critiquing her own example as inadequate?

Every week, 150 precious minutes of my life are ripped away in the most agonizing fashion. Her lectures, where are often devices banned, feels like enduring purgatory. I wonder what I could accomplish with that time. Maybe I could cure cancer or rediscover joy. I'll never know, thanks to this painfully redundant and utterly uninspiring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Waste of time, talking non stop abt the same thing multiple times
nothing but bs

This is a class wherein even if you put effort to be creative and get out good content, its all nullified by the professor and some of her TAs and in-turn your grade is cut out for not following EXACTLY what she wants with her rubrics (which aren't even followed while grading, with no justification). Moreover you get 0 value& waste a lot of time.

This class is meaningless and provides absolutely 0 value to us. Moreover, the work is meaningless and is graded very harshly. Creativity is killed in this class. Rules and rubrics dont make sense and are not even following for grading (in a bad way, because they mess up your grade, and post it late, and you have to fight and live in anxiety)

You may be reading all the other reviews thinking "surely it can't be THAT bad."


It's that bad.
CS1100 is super easy, but Dr. Nagel is incredibly condescending and talks to students like they're in kindergarten. This class felt like a huge waste of time.

Kind of a rude person, did not enjoy her lectures at all, but attendance is a very big part of your grade and you can only miss so many (i think it's 4, don't remember) or you fail the class. Very easy class, of course, so it doesn't matter at all who you have, but if possible maybe avoid her just because the hw and her lectures are annoying.

There's not much to say about Dr. Nagel for a class like 1100. I thought the topics she covered were good and she made most of our work clear. But she has to be the most condescending person I've worked with post-high school. She will treat you like you're in elementary school and that alone made this class offputting.
How does she have a PhD? Horrible class, to much busy work every week, she does not know what she is doing.
useless class. whole class is just busy work honestly. professor didnt really accomodate learning or whatever this class is about anyway. really mid experience just had to run it for grad.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: 5 assignments a week. Irrelevant coursework. No real schedule. No living schedule. Condescending. Dress code mandated. Attendance required and taken through quizzes. Ambiguous grading criteria and system. Lengthy yet redundant assignment descriptions. More importance is placed on how you present rather than the actual content of the presentations.

Tons of assignments, many of which are posted without warning to students because the live schedule is constantly changing and out of date. The assignments are typically busy work. The assignment instructions are unclear and sometimes factually wrong. When called out on it, Nagel is rude and condescending. To be clear, the class isn't hard

nice besides the condescending tone and not letting you get your point across. NOTHING relates to workplace professionalism-nonstop busywork w unclear instructions, constant mistakes, and disorganized. Tried to communicate technical issue (that SHE made), got yelled at for having said issue, then told I needed to communicate my issues. Take 8am LMC

Wow! This is truly the worst course I've taken so far I'm actually impressed. The reviews are true and I would just be redundant at this point. Contradictory and disorganized yet extremely strict and harsh on her students. If you're going to put the students through such a high standard, then you should at least know how to use canvas at least :\

being a student in this class is like being told to wear business casual to an interview, wearing business casual to the interview, then getting ripped to shreds because you wore glasses (it doesn't make sense!) and also imagine there are 5 of these interviews a week. assignment descriptions are always unclear, and the professor is always confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please try your best to get this course with a different professor. I have never had a more exhausting and infuriating class. There are around 5 full-length assignments EACH WEEK. She is never clear in her rubrics, and nothing is straightforward. She contradicts herself constantly, and I just wanna graduate man.

This is quite literally the WORST class I have taken at Georgia Tech. I have never felt so patronized in a class and the professor seems to place a particular emphasis on the things no one cares about in industry. Don't be late because I've seen her yell at students for this. Also, there are way too many menial assignments that take way too long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Incredibly disorganized course, with unclear expectations such as a "required" but unused textbook and changing expectations during presentations. Continuously assigned what amounted to hours of busywork, with droll lectures that repeated what was stated the previous lecture. Strangely strict despite not being organized herself. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: please please please do not take this professor, assigns 7 assignments a week (10+ hours for group) that are all busywork and pertains NOTHING to actual career communications. every class is a circus show

So much uneccessary work (>4 assignments weekly). Unclear grading criteria and assignments don't carry any coherence. What really pushes me over the edge is her attitude. Condescending, treats students like little kids, multiple instances of yelling at students (actual raising of the voice), refusal to heed feedback. Would've rather taken the 8am.

MOST UNPROFESSIONAL TEACHER. Yells at students and goes on full on rants infront of the entire class for being late or running into genuine technical issues. Treats students like 4th graders and I honestly dread going to this class. Please don't take her, all the reviews are 100% accurate. Seems unbelievable, but all of them are true.

CS 4510 is a cakewalk infront of this class. Almost 70+ assignments (sometimes 10+ a week), each of them 4-5 page reports and memos about absolutely useless stuff. As a professor she isnt the most adept at managing canvas, has multiple duplicate assgnments with titles like "NEW" "DONT USE" and and super chaotic and hard to keep track of your grade.
Take her if you want to be yelled at like you've never been before :)

Atrocious overall. Lectures rambled on about useless content, and pop quizzes in class were used only for attendance. The prof was consistently unhelpful and dismissive when people asked questions. Assignments lacked clear instructions, and her struggles with technology made class a joke. Would not recommend taking this "easy" class with her.

See all of the reviews below and above (I know I will not be the last to complain). Nothing of use was learned, attendance was required for no gain to the student, and assignments gave me flashbacks to when I had a substitute teacher in English class.
Absolutely terrible. Whatever it takes, do not take this professor. Just read what other people are saying. Too many assignments, extremely rude, strict, and not understanding at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Constant homeworks, group assignments, and incredibly disorganized. Many times she will create duplicate assignments to correct unassigned groups, wrong due dates, and wrong assignment types. Incredibly boring lectures, but the few times I've gone up to talk to her she's had a nasty personality to students asking questions.

Manages to somehow lecture about nothing for the entire class. Legitimately did not learn a single thing. Additionally, she takes away valuable group time to ramble about unclear assignments and rubrics in the most roundabout way possible. Over 60 assignments. Mandatory attendance (7 absences = fail). Avoid at every cost possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is terrible. To be fair, she is a pretty nice person but the class is unbelievably poorly planned, structured, and executed. There are 4+ assignments per week that take an insane amount of time. She does not take feedback. This takes up an insane amount of time for what should be an easy class.

The prof is a pretty good and tries her best. If you do not follow her directions then she can get irritated, but I had no problems with her. There is lots of homework and group assignments and if you get a bad group you'll have to do a lot on your own, but that's any class with group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please save yourself & your senior year, & do not take Tech Communication with this professor. Not only is she rude & impatient, she redesigned the course halfway through the semester to give us a ton of assignments for no reason. She veers off the course schedule & adds so many assignments everyday. SAVE YOURSELF, TAKE A DIFFERENT PROF!

this is my 2nd rating for this prof. this individual has caused me immense distress. she's a slow, tough grader who treats us as if we're petulant, disobedient children. she's ineffective at delivering instructions and constantly she yells (yes, yells) at the class. every time i hear the words "attendance quiz" i foam at the mouth. what a waste!!
Hardly breathing yet screams at students

I agree with every single other person's reviews on this professor. She is rude and condescending, and will put you to sleep during here waste of time lectures. Having a class this boring with MANDATORY (6 absences max) attendance is outrageous. Unsure how she got a job teaching, but I hope no other student has to go through one of her courses.

Kristine had an exceptionally poor management of this course. She frequently messed up assignments (creating duplicates, mixing up sections, failing to assign group-work). The required workload is absurdly high relative to the equivalent LMC course and the assignments seemed to prioritize quantity over meaningful content. Not attending = fail.

Genuinely the worst professor I have had in my entire life. I do not know how this individual has a PhD and can stand up there talk about complete nonsense while the entire class is not paying attention. I suggest she takes a permanent break from teaching this course for the sake of the student body's mental health. I wish I never went to GT.

Mandatory attendance (6 absences = fail). Endless busywork for no reason, w/ unclear grading criteria. She asked for feedback and was told the assignments were too much, to which she replied "you should just work harder". 
I have industry experience and this has been a waste of time. The other sections only had a few deliverables. We had 41 so far.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF UNLESS YOU NEED TO GRADUATE! If you don't have a good group, you will suffer under the intense workload: 4+ in class assignments per week, mandatory attendance, $75+ textbook that is never used. Unnecessary lengthy business memos, unclear guidelines for all assignments. She is incredibly disorganized and rude to students.

She's condescending and rude to students, and she's incompetent with tech but expects you to know how to do everything. There are about 4 assignments due every week, none of them useful (business memos??), and the instructions are often unclear. She asked for mid-semester feedback and then didn't change a thing. Do not take her!! Waste of time!

Do not take this class, she is the worst teacher ever. So much busy work all to learn nothing. Avoid taking her at all costs, it is not worth it. Makes what should be the easiest class a major headache for no reason. Doesn't understand how to use technology (Canvas) or communicate.

This prof will make you hate any form of communication all together. Lectures are spent droning over presentations that simply are not relevant to any professional endeavor. Assignments have due dates sprawled across the week. There is no feedback on assignments that matters. The class fails in all aspects. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF PLS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful prof. Gives us a ton of assignments and spends all lecture explaining super vague rubrics with no additional details to clarify them. Treats us like middle schoolers who have never done a presentation in their lives. Has not taught anything past the basic premise of "know your audience, understand different perspectives."

She is a terrible teacher. The class seems to be made up on the fly with constant bust work assignments. The lectures are terrible. Be prepared for never ending busy work and to learn nothing. She is rude and makes what should be a laid back enjoyable class terrible, unenjoyable, and no one takes anything from this class.

The worst teacher I've ever had. She's condescending towards students for questions. She asked for feedback, then ignored the feedback. Constant assignments. Always has tech issues on Canvas despite being a CS teacher. Unclear instructions on assignments leading to longer than expected work. Admitted assignment was too long and just said "oops"

She tried making the class helpful but its the most draining time of my day and I learn nothing. It is literally just her talking without caring if the class is engaged. I was hoping to gain something from this class but instead I am just stressing over 10+ assignments every single week. No clear guidelines and very confusing and useless work.

Kristine Nagel gives an extraordinary amount of homework with very little meaning behind it. She asks for feedback, but then completely ignores it and says that everyone just needs to work harder. Her lectures are boring, mandatory, and completely pointless. For a communications class, there is absolutely nothing applicable to real communication.

terrible class. Can't name a single uselful thing i learnt. useless lectures but mandatory attendance with an insane amount of assignments. 

Feedback - have more assignments on how to document code rather than buisness memos for random things. More engaging and interactive classes -- currently feels like I am watching a youtube video just live.

Ruined my last semester with so much busy work with absolutely NO LEARNING and unproductive assignments. 

This class is too intensive all the grad level classes seem easy infront of this. Feedback that she should've made it more engaging instead of only her talking. 

The assignments are completely misaligned from job expectations of a CS grad.

Ridiculous and completely useless information. Lectures are so dry and feels like I am in middle school. I am doing more work than any other CS 4000 level class. She is also very rude during presentations and very unapproachable. There are constantly technical glitches during her lecture but there is no room for you to mess up. Do not take please!!

Awful experience in my last semester as a CS major. So much useless writing (buisness memos and Pecha Kucha) that I would never ever use as a SWE. Attendance is mandatory and there are things due EVERY SINGLE DAY. Take the LMC version atleast the work there helps you build an online portfolio. This is the worst class ive taken at Tech by a mile.

- Tedious work for very little gain (work is not relevant to the real world)
- Written assignments due every lecture
- Unorganized structure, will have multiple vague projects being worked on at once
- Claims that assignments are due on Wednesday at the start of the semester however then proceeds to have assignments due on random days of the week
yikessssss
Do not take her class. So much unnecessary busy work, required attendance, and makes you buy a brand new completely useless textbook. Take literally anyone else.

Nagel is fine just because 1100 is not a hard class at all, although I bet having a different professor would make it more of an enjoyable experience. Lectures can get boring with guest speakers and assignments are a bit pointless, but overall the class doesn't take much time out of your schedule and is pass/fail.
She was chill fr junior design was fine. she liked to lecture a lot about random things

Class is very guest-speaker heavy, and you have to take notes with pen and paper (which are graded). If you're caught with your phone or god forbid your computer, she'll call you out for it. She's incredibly mean-spirited, but she *does* want you to succeed. Don't ask her any questions; she'll assume you weren't listening. Easy/helpful class though

This class is a complete waste of time but it's incredibly easy despite what people here say. You should never spend more than 10 minutes on an assignment. Unfortunately Professor Nagel requires attendance and her lectures are incredibly boring. You fail if you skip more than 3 classes. Do not take her under any circumstances.

Take someone else. Despite only being 1 credit hour it feels like the work of 5. In person event assignments can be solved by dropping in, signing into the lecture, taking a selfie with your ID, and leaving.

She is incredibly out of touch with her students. She takes every opportunity to talk down to and scold her class. Lectures and assignments are ineffective and a general waste of time as they are just busy work. Try and take a different instructor if you can as Nagal makes coming to class more of a burden than a learning opportunity.

assignments are unnecessarily kinda frequent, you could benefit from networking but not many guest speakers were worth connecting with. she relies on them to present for the class, its annoyingly required to attend and you need to take notes which is annoying, you arent allowed to do anything else in class but listen, lowk felt like a waste of time

IDK What these other reviews are saying she's not that bad. Easy 1 credit hour course that barely took up any time. Did I pay attention to any of the speakers? Absolutely not. But it's a mandatory course and she does her best.
If you decide to take her, all I can say is good luck
Take literally anyone else. This 1 credit mandatory class had more work than the rest of my credits combined. Terrible assignments, boring guest speakers and mandatory attendance.

Professor Nagel herself is fine; at worst the way she talks might come off a bit annoying, but she herself is a fine lecturer. The class is designed around guest speakers every class period , so I wouldn't say not to take her based on other ratings since she isn't that present anyway. The class itself is a good bit of busy work, but beneficial.

The professor makes this INTRODUCTORY class far more challenging than it needs to be. It's supposed to help students transition into life at Tech, but instead it feels like a burden. Assignments are overly tedious, and she gives a zero for participation if you're even one min late. Also the way she talks is mad annoying - constantly stuttering

mean professor. not understanding about other commitments (I have 5 other classes and a part time job) and if you are > 5 minutes late to her 8:25am class she will shrug and basically tell you to f off. she doesnt even teach, and actually leans on guest speakers to do all the work for her. worst professor ive had at tech sofar been here for 2 years

Professor Nagel clearly cared about her students and the course she was teaching, and really did her best to uplift her CS1100 class from something you blow off into a true opportunity for learning about CS. If you ACTUALLY pay attention & take advantage of the guest speakers/resources she brings in, you could make some really great connections.

Dr. Nagel is not a super engaging professor and didn't set up the course too great outside of a few activities. I can tell she cares, so it is nice to see her be passionate about this intro class, but I believe the structure of the class could be redone to focus on more important topics.

There have been times she gave us low grades on assignments and asked us to redo and resubmit. I asked her to see if part of my new response looked good; she said yes, but I hadn't changed anything. I'm not sure if she actually reads the entire response or not.

I'd rate her 0 if possible. She treats students childishly and seems to skim through homework, assigning low grades. Her strict attendance policy differs from other professors' more lenient ones. Although the course content is interesting and includes guest speakers, she barely engages in the 50-minute sessions.
She's so picky. you have to make sure your submission is 200% more than her require. AND attendance is mandatory

CS 1100 is only interesting when there are guest speakers. It's clear that Dr. Nagel just goes on tangents to fill the whole 50 minutes when she doesn't have much to talk about. It feels like a huge waste of time to attend this class.

This class is very easy and like base-line effort is needed for the projects. However, she isn't a very engaging instructor and seems like she hates her job. There are attendance quizzes but they honestly are pretty easy to guess on. Just sit in class and do other work.

Pointless class. CS 1100 is easy and it doesn't matter who you get, but I wish Dr. Nagel would have fostered a better class environment and treated her students with more respect (felt like we were being talked down to). She seems like a nice person in real life, but every class was a waste of time.

No one I knew in this class liked this professor. Confusing grading, hard (if even possible) to reach, and treats students like small children. Avoid at all costs if you want to be respected as an adult and want to keep your sanity. For reference, I did more work (work that is also meaningless and tedious) in this class than in my grad class.

Treats us like 12 year old delinquents. Very condescending. Class assumes everyone wants to be a corporate drone. Class is ez obv, it is just an intro seminar, but something about the class and her personality made me like an industrial product. Very strange woman. Attendance is required and part of the grade.
Professor Nagel became the CS 1100 professor mid-semester. As a 50 minute seminar, I have never wanted to skip a class so badly.

This professor made coming to class harder every week. She treats us like kindergartners and made me less inclined to participate in class. Attendance quizzes are required for grade but she only leaves them open for 5 minutes and, at times gives the wrong answers so even if you show up, you get partial attendance credit. I did not enjoy her at all.
I had Dr. Roy for CS2340. She was an amazing professor, very fair grader, great lecturer, and a genuinely caring person. Would recommend!
She was a very kind prof. The material was boring but the project was fun.

She seemed sweet but led to a huge amount of stress and uncertainty throughout. She failed to communicate, gave no support for the entirety of the project, and had material that was riddled with mistakes and inconsistencies. 
She misled about changing due dates, if she would regrade, and what we were being graded on. Workload was also insane.

Course is already poorly structured, but professor somehow makes it worse. Course relies on a group project where your group can make or break your grade. Lectures are super dense of information that is pointless outside a few filler assignments and exams that build off of a fraction of the group project (AKA 99% of your work). Hope for a good TA🙏
Helpful class. Easy A. Roy is pretty good.

The class is project-based with plenty of extra credit. You can choose your own team, and the projects are manageable with good planning, but they require a lot of learning outside of lectures. The midterm and final are fairly difficult due to the broad range of topics, though CRIB sheets are allowed and very helpful.

I would advise to take another professor for 2340. She gives a midterm and final exam on top of a pretty heavy workload for the projects. I did not learn much throughout the class. Grade depends on the TA you get for your project (some are not good). She is a very kind professor, but I think other sections are less work.

Prof is good, lectures are a bit boring, but the notes on them are good. I think she does a good job for what this class is. That being said 2340 is dependent on your group (I did not get a good one and TAs can only do so much) I really hated this class because of that. Make sure to fix your group by the 2nd sprint b/c you can't change after that.
Project based class that's an easy A if you get a good group. Prof. is caring and a good lecturer.

Caring professor, with too much work assigned. Sprint projects were very long, especially if your entire team wasn't 100% on board. That combined with extra work, exams, etc. was a lot to deal with. She also seems a bit jumbled sometimes, when lecturing especially early on in the semester when things are still getting going.
Just project based, a couple midterms but take home. Just focus on the projects and focus on participation.

Despite the course begin hybrid, Roy was a great professor. As long as all work is completed, it's difficult not to get an A, even with a bad group. The midterm consists of an individual portion (crib sheet allowed) and a project group portion. The final is completed as a group and is not difficult.

Roy is honestly a good prof, but this class is kinda hit or miss depending on your group. She's fair with grading and actually cares if you're struggling, but a lot of the work relies on your teammates pulling their weight. If you get a solid group, it's not bad, but if not good luck lol. I like that you can showcase your projects at the end.

If you are reading this, do not take Nimisha. Her sprint requirements are incredibly unclear and convoluted. This makes the assignments incredibly frustrating and time-consuming. On top of this, the tech stack (Android Studio) sucks. We learned literally nothing remotely applicable.

By far the most rage-inducing class I've taken. Please take Pedro

The Fall 2024 semester saw a hybrid online/in-person class, which was no fault of hers. She is clear on grading and the A is easy with a good group. One midterm, which is easy if you keep up. She is very accommodating in the event of getting a bad group (you can choose groups of 5-6). Project grades are dependent on TA evaluation. Okay course!

CS3300 this semester had a focus on AI, which lined up with Prof Roy's research focus. The group projects are manageable if you have solid teammates. This semester the criteria were very open ended which made it difficult to know exactly what we needed to complete. The emphasis on testing and AI seemed not fully baked sometimes too.

Genuinely isn't even Professor Roy's fault entirely. The class is poorly designed and your grade is entirely based off the random group you receive. Luckily for me I had an amazing randomly assigned team but for others they weren't so lucky loll. Roy is caring and she tried her best to make sure everyone got a decent grade. Bad class, nice prof.

The professor was a decent person, but the class structure was really awful. Lecture videos were incredibly long as opposed to something like 1332 where videos were max 13 minutes long. Hope you get a good group that are able to plan out sprints and not start them the weekend they are due.

Roy is a good professor, her in-person lecture reviews were nice. The project is manageable, as long as your team is willing to put in the work. Opportunities for EC as well. The only thing I did not like is the hybrid setup of the course, so if you want to really learn, you have to watch online lectures. Great professor, but try to avoid hybrid.
Prof Roy is great, but the async class is so not it if you actually want to learn the material.

I took this course in Fall 2023. This course is an easy A with Roy. There are a number of assignments that your group must complete throughout the semester, but none of them are hard. She was also very lenient with due dates. She seemed detached from the course, since the goal of the class is to have your group operate professionally with a client.
3300 was fun this semester. We used AI tools for developing projects. Would recommend.

Would've given a 2/5 a month ago, but has improved the structures of the course (Sprints 3 and 4 were clear, plus my familiarity with Android has increased in this time). The group project is challenging without much instruction, but the TAs were generally helpful. Though, she will not be teaching until Fall 2025.

Don't know if it's the professor perse, but the class is just implemented poorly. It's a hybrid course with a semester long group project, so unless you're doing this with friends, get ready for the majority not even trying in your group. The project is also very vague in what it wants from you and I learned very little from this course all in all.

Prof. Roy did a great job with the hybrid format, although I am not a fan of the format.  She figured out a balance between hybrid, providing long-form videos with in-depth notes while summarizing the important details in class. Getting a good team in class really helps.

Dr. Roy has insane expectations. The Sprints are vague and confusing at best and have tight deadlines, not the mention the ridiculous amount of required features and the pedantic guidelines for the GitHub repo. She does little to help when it comes to group conflicts and shows little to no sympathy for struggling groups. Take pedro.
The professor is very caring towards the success of the students. I have an amazing group and we are loving the project.

absolutely horrible. tas are unhelpful and don't care about the class, and each sprint has functionality we've never ever learned in class. rubrics and instructions don't match, and we all end up stressed asf before the deadlines because no one answers helpfully on ed discussion

Taking 2340 in the hybrid model (75 min/wk). Sprints contain a significant amount of work and contain very specific requirements in order to receive full points. On top of that, we are expected to watch 2+ hours of lectures and complete time consuming modules weekly, equating to more work than the non-hybrid class. She's nice but avoid if possible.

agree with other reviewers in that ur experience rly depends on whether u get a good group or not. MAKE SURE u get a good group (or switch) so ur not bogged down by project work all sem like me 😭 class is p hands off and material isn't too difficult, but assignments + tech (android studio) can get annoying and stack up if ur not on top of things
Enjoying the class so far! I recommend but your success is dependent on how good a group you get assigned/you choose.
Prof. Roy has been great. The course is hybrid, so it is a bit difficult to manage things around teammates. But overall, I'm enjoying this course and learning a lot.

Prof. Roy is overall a great Prof! She cares for students and tries to make the lessons enjoyable. Not really her fault, but if you get a bad group, this class will suck (groups are assigned somewhat randomly and hard to change). The exams are not bad as long as you make some effort to study. Overall I recommend taking classes with her.

Roy seems like a reasonable professor, but she advocates for a strange class structure. The main project has little relevance to the design patterns taught in class, is very tedious without a competent group, and seems like just busywork for the most part. Also, requirements for diagrams and assessments are often unclear.

Pretty easy class with a group project, 1 individual midterm, 1 group midterm, and a group final. There's some participation here and there and extra credit almost every class. Really sweet prof. who genuinely cares about her students and is trying to make the course better and more rewarding for everyone.
Great professor. Design patterns and principles are industry standard topics that I learned. Project was cool and rewarding but had a steep learning curve.

Good professor, but terrible class structure. There was very little correlation between what we did in class and the project implementation and TAs were largely unknowledgeable and unhelpful, which made the sprints basically impossible. Take Pedro, your life will be so much easier.
Professor Roy is a good professor. She's a good option for 2340 and pretty accommodating to students and their busy schedules.

This class is probably the worst I've taken here during my time at Tech. Attendance for this class is mandatory. The class is at 8 AM, and if you miss five classes, they will fail you. How nonsensical. This class is the epitome of "this could have been an email." If you have to make attendance mandatory, make your lectures worth my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice professor who really cares about students. For instance, a project was due on one day (on living schedule), but there was a canvas mistake where it said it was due 5 days later, so she moved the deadline to 5 days later to accommodate. Some of the content (design patterns) is boring, but the class teaches app development and Firebase.
Enjoying the class so far. Recommend her.
Just a good professor.

The course contents in this class can sometimes be mundane but you can really see that Professor Roy put in a lot of effort to make the class fun with the post lecture Quizizzes and group activities. The group project ended up being very fun for me and not only I learned a lot more about design patterns but also made some really good friends along.

Roy was definitely the nicest professors at GT. She cares about students' feedback about the course and would change her lecture styles accordingly. She was not the most interesting lecturer, but I can't blame her for it as the course itself is very boring. The group project was fun, but the TAs were not the best at the most times.

Her as a professor was fine for me, she had decent lectures and provided EC in class. But, beware the group you choose, try to meet your teammates and choose them before they assign you teammates because some people in this class are absolutely useless but not the professors fault. It's just the TAs are the backbone of the class so good luck.

Outstanding professor to take for a class that people only appreciate after getting an internship. There are a lot of people who are just rude to a really good Professor. Professor Roy makes the class interesting and while there are a lot of work, people need to keep in mind this is not a 2 credit hour course.
She makes a boring class like 2340 fun by her lectures and quizizz.
She is very nice and caring about the learning process of the students. She is very flexible too.
Changes grading criteria last minute and doesnt excuse assignments for valid things like interviews. Heavy accent too. Don't take her.
Prof Roy is so caring and she teaches so well.  The class is also fun because of quizziz.
Great teacher!
Professor Roy teaches complex topics very well. I loved having her as my teacher.
Useless class, dumb grading scheme for project
Professor Roy is a great teacher. She is very enthusiastic about the material and teaching. She really cares about the students. Highly recommend.

2340 is an awful class, but Professor Roy did a good job running it, and was very responsive to questions and overall helpful. The midterms and "mini-assessments" don't weigh a lot but require you to actually learn the "content", which led to poor performance that seemed to bother her more than it did the students. A fine professor for a bad class.

LOVED this professor. She was so kind and helpful and provided us with whatever we needed to succeed in the class. Content wasn't the most interesting, but we learned a good amount and were able to come out of the course more prepared. Lots of extra credit opportunities and pretty relaxed assignment load.

Pretty great teacher. Was very receptive to feedback and genuinely wanted to improve the course. Lectures are pretty fast, but I found that to be a plus. Overall, 2340 as a class just sucks, but Prof. Roy tried her best to make it somewhat enjoyable.

This class is incredibly boring and monotonous(regardless of professor). It was her first time teaching, so she mainly just read off the slides adding to the boredom. The tests are easy but the individual portion of them are focused on incredibly mundane details that are hard to memorize. Overall, not the worst professor, just an awful class.
Amazing Professor. Highly recommend her classes.

This was her first semester teaching a large class, and she could benefit from some better content organization. Also, taking away crib sheets for exams was the dumbest they ever did on this course, as quizzes/midterms now test on the most little insignificant details.
She is a great professor and helped me understand the practicalities of early stages of software engineering well.

By the nature/structure of the class itself, it feels pretty boring. Stopped going to lectures a few weeks in. Before both of the mini-assessments, all you need to do is go through the lecture slides a few times. Kind of poor classroom management, but that's also because everyone was super rude and would talk over her, so not all her fault at all.

It is easy to expect what will be on an exam (exam 2 is notoriously hard). She is a great teacher, and honestly cares about what is going on with her students outside of class. She values communication, so make sure to communicate things on time. There are so many resources for the class, and enough practice to really succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was not a hard class. There are daily quizzes for class and video lectures to watch for the other day of the week there is class. The exams are very fair and the review material prepares you very well for them. The project is not bad either, some phases take more time than others.

This class is not as "hard" as people have said its gotten. The handouts are extremely helpful and really all you need. The coding can be tough but lecture will not prepare you for it, it is something you must practice on your own. The group projects can be done within a week if group members all work together.

Course design was great, daily-activities and in-person exams (11%) weren't too much of a hit on grade (Substantially more difficult than practice tests and increases difficulty every semester to maintain grade distributions). Lectures are very monotone, but handouts/practice are great. Do those, and you'll get an A. Beware of AI usage in project !
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hybrid Class, Group Project worth 40% of grade (3 Parts), 3 Midterms (11% Each), Final worth 20%, and 7% In-Class Attendance Quizzes. Luckily there is no homework, but study because the tests and project are all quite difficult. Melinda doesn't seem the most knowledgeable about SQL. The TAs know more but some are bad and condescending. Uma is good.

The class is manageable if you have a solid project group and utilize the practice exams. The exam difficulty has increased recently, and the lectures can feel a bit dry. Focus your studying on the coding portions and make sure to prepare a very thorough crib sheet for the tests!

Class is well organized, lectures are decent. Project isn't too bad if you have a good group and go to OH. Exams 1 and 3 were very reasonable, but exam 2 and the final felt really long and difficult. Definitely don't take the class lightly but if you stay on top of everything and practice a lot you can definitely get an A.

She didn't seem to be a master of SQL but knew what she needed to. Her lectures weren't super helpful but you had to go for quizzes. Tests don't define the class, I got a 61 on the 2nd exam and still ended with an A. (91 on the 1st. 91.6 on the second and 97 on the final) Nothing will prepare you for the second exam. TAs liked making things hard.

Honestly don't think this semester class was too bad. The overall class is based on tests, daily participation quizzes, and the project. As long as you have a good team, the project is not too bad. To me, the tests did not seem too bad except for the coding parts for the later exams. I think its a lot of content so make sure you keep up.

Both the TAs and the professor frequently make mistakes and get confused when explaining content. Group project heavy, so make sure you get a good group. Tests were more difficult than previous years. Many students complain about the difficulty of the sql coding portion, however with proper preparation (not cramming last minute) it isn't too bad.

This semester or absolutely in shambles. Gives the most absurd test for exam 2, project grading criteria was horrible. All the TA's really cared about was who used AI, even though they use it themselves for content, occasionally accusing ppl even without definitive proof. Final exam for section b was pretty difficult, on top of no internet.

the final exam was soo chaotic, for our section the internet was sooo slow. i lost so much time during the coding part of the exam and even if they gave extra 10 mins, it still wasn't enough to make up for the amount of time i lost waiting for the test to even load. I asked for extra time but she didn't give me any which is so unfair.

There is a lot of practice for this course, but it seems to be AI generated often times. They should clearly have an AI acknowledgement where they at least are transparent about it. Exam 2 was extremely harder than the other exams. The project is easy given you don't have bots for teammates.

Forever grateful to the TAs because without them I would have had a very lonely semester...because they screwed me every chance they got. I can't with these people. I hope I pass because I don't ever want to try to print output statements from page long SQL functions where they DECREASE THE FONT SIZE SO THE ENTIRE THING COULD FIT ON ONE PAGE

The professor is sweet but that's it. The class is ran by TA's who fight AI by having AI generated material. The exams are significantly harder then previous semesters despite being gaslit by the entire teaching staff that the averages are comparable and that makes it okay! The TA's during office hours often gave contradicting information.

Way harder than I expected as a 4th year CS major. Exams are all time-crunch oriented which seems like a bad way to test knowledge. Group project is alright. They grandstand on how unacceptable AI use is in a 4000 level course but accidentally released course content that had the phrase "Actually, let me reconsider" in it. Would avoid this class

the tests are actually impossible. you get these long and complex questions that are time consuming but you get little to no time to answer them, the only way to answer all of the questions on the written portion of the exam is to straight up guess, you dont have time to think. and absolutely nothing will prepare you for the coding portion.

the other reviews aren't lying about the tests and how she lectures. im here to warn you about the group projects. for the love of god please already come into the class with a trusted group or at least try to find people with brains. you'd think since we go to GT the people here cant be THAT dumb, but THEY ARE!!!!

The TAs genuinely run the whole class. She tends to mutter and race through the lectures and half the time none of the students dont even understand. It's not the TAs' faults at all. Please structure this course better with a new professor because the topics are actually interesting. She always tries to scare us about grades etc as well.
It's just a disaster.

The tests this semester are made so hard for no reason, even though the class is being gaslit into thinking it's not as hard. They say project scores are higher than the exam scores, thus students must have used AI, even though the project is easy and takes 2 weeks while the exam is hard and given 35 minutes to code hard solutions.

The TAs who created the test have written the exams to be much harder than in prior years. I would love to see the professor take the same exams because she is so incompetent that she would not be able to finish them. It is clear she does not look over the exams at all because the difficulty is exponentially more difficult than any practice given.
They declared war on AI by declaring war on us.

Tests this semester were considerably more difficult than previous sessions, and the system for coding - Honorlock - was downright horrendous. Projects are fun, but the some of the TAs seemed far less than competent, while a handful of other most likely enjoy making coding exams difficult to torture GT's already mentally struggling student body.

I did everything right including doing every single practice as well as all the past papers and coding exams, getting near 100s in all of them under time pressure. I am convinced that the TA that made the exams this semester must have gotten their heart broken by someone in the class right now because they doubled the difficulty for no reason.

The professor and TA's decided to make the tests in this class significantly harder than previous semesters. I came in with prior experience using SQL and am still struggling.  Also, just not a very good lecturer. Way too much going on and exam logistics are so bad that students lose out on time because of mistakes by the professor and TA team.
Terrible. Disorganized. Way too many students in each section. Both 20 TAs and Professor all seem confused. Coding exams are all or nothing, avoid if you can.

The course difficulty increased dramatically. Our test scores were the lowest among all previous years. They released the previous exams as study material but it is significantly easier than the current. The study material they provide is AI generated with incorrect answers and the TA's did not help at all when going to office hours.

She is so sweet and a great professor, but the class is unsweet, lots of practice is needed so don't take if your schedule is overloaded or just stay up all night doing queries or else your coding portion will be low!
Very very organized there are so many resources to do well in the class. As a lecturer, she is not great, very boring and the weekly quizzes are annoying. Overall she does a good job

This class is DRAMATICALLY harder than previous semesters. The last exam had the lowest averages in course history. Not to mention the professor is absolute buns. I genuinely think she doesn't even know the material -- she constantly relies on her TAs to tell her if she is correct or not during lecture

If you think that you're going to do well on the exam just because you put in the time, did all the practices they provided, and did the past papers on time and well, you are sorely mistaken. They decided to drastically up the difficulty this semester for whatever reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my least favorite professors ever. She talks to herself all lecture and TAs run the whole class. She is always in a rush and no one learns anything in lecture.

The group projects in this class were actually pretty fun, but I didn't get much out of her lectures. I wish she had spent more time explaining *what* everything does instead of *how* it does it. Exams are tougher than anticipated, I knew SQL going in and studying was absolutely necessary. I would take her class again. Get a good group!
Prof McDaniel was totally sweet. In class, her teaching could have been more focused at times, but overall I had a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McDaniel's lectures were ok. She spent lots of unnecessary time on theory when we should be focusing on practicing coding and logic questions for the exams. Practice exams are way easier than actual exams. Easy to mess up on coding and that final was brutal. Project is fairly easy, don't procrastinate it. Class could use some improvements

Practice tests are way too easy and not indicative of the difficulty of tests. Despite this, I got an easy A+ on most tests, yet barely pulled a C on the final. Also, by nature of databases, there are a few correct ways to interpret a problem, but it looks like TAs only want one answer. TAs also give conflicting answers sometimes.

Went to OH a lot during the project to get help and the TAs often had contradicting advice. A TA used ChatGPT right in front of us. For exams, they were more difficult than any practice given to us. The testing environment was distracting because TAs were talking with students trying to fix issues right next to students trying to take the test.

I think the professor herself is nice and understanding at times and the project is chill. However, my frustration lies with the exams. I spent so much time studying but it felt so pointless because none of the lectures or practice was even close to the difficulty of those exams. It was insanely difficult.

I liked the way she taught 2316 but I didn't like she taught 4400. Lecture slides were lengthy and hard to process, learned more reading the TA's documents and doing the practice problems. Project is time consuming but with a good group it should bring your grade up. Exams keep getting harder compared to past exams.

It is a fundamental course in software engineering, but Melinda unfortunately doesn't provide enough for the students, and relies on the TA's to run the class. Group projects are chill, but exams are magnitudes harder than practice exams, with little assistance. I unfortunately didn't get what I was hoping for from this course.

Melinda was a horrible professor. She talked about how she owns a tesla way too much. If any questions come up, she makes the TAs handle it.
