Go look at course critique PLS 1.Grades unpredictably and no rubrics 2.Did not put in over 50 percent of earlier grades until post final 3.Cares A LOT about participation and attendance; That said, she is very passionate and if you enjoy the material you will like it, but your grade likely will suffer still. Less than 35 percent of class got As

Prof Rebekas is very knowledgeable. But for an intro class, she is nitpicky and a harsh grader. If you're an SI concentration, take her. If not, avoid at all costs. You must attend every lecture and contribute to discussion or get a 65%. She complains about having too much to grade, but it's because she assigns a ton of work... **grading=subjective

Not the best professor, grader, or personality. As stated syllabus "if you are present in class sessions but do not contribute, your grade will not exceed 65%." You need to participate. Group projects are tough and time-consuming. You will learn, but DON'T expect A's (75-90). Procrastinates on grading. Maybe that's why classes are far from full. ;)

If ur strategy concentration, you should take her because you're gonna have to for 3664 and it makes it much easier. Otherwise take an easier teacher. You need to read case study before and discuss EVERY class. Show up to class no matter what's going on in ur life. Group projects graded between 82-92. Tests easy if you study. Good, passionate, hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor cares a lot so just try and do what she wants. You need to go to every class and read at least a summary of the 20 page course pack to contribute something of substance to the discussion to get full participation. Tests easy if you study. Projects graded between 82-92 regardless of effort.

Very picky grader and most of her grading is very subjective. For example, on the midterm and final exam, point values are not assigned to each question. Instead, she marks which ones are right and wrong and then arbitrarily determines your exam grades. Very difficult professor for an introduction to a concentration.

I really enjoyed the lecture and discussions for this class. Professor Rebeka is very knowledgeable and guides the case discussions. However, the tests are pretty confusing and can be difficult at times. Be ready to work hard for an A but you will learn a lot along the way. The group project reports were very time consuming.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her class is so fun and interesting, and she really made me excited to learn strategy. Her lectures are engaging and she is so knowledgeable. Overall great class and I am so glad I got to take her for 3659! Wholeheartedly recommend!

Avoid at all costs!!! Class is discussion based, but if you don't agree with her then you are automatically wrong. She will embarrass you in front of the whole class. She does not provide rubrics and then grades harshly. Her grading on tests is confusing and unclear. DO NOT take her class. She takes it too seriously for an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE especially if you are not a strategy concentration. Be prepared for attending every class, no grades in the gradebook to know anywhere near where you stand by the time of the final exam, and no sympathy from her about anything. Her grading is also very chaotic and makes no sense
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation matters so much in this class if you show up and don't speak it doesn't count. Her tests are fair. I was in the upper quartile in every grade I received and I still barely made an A.

i loved this class, it truly taught me a lot of relevant things in the business world that i can apply. professor rebeka's class is very attendance/participation/lecture heavy. you have to come prepared with the readings and be able to participate but it becomes a lot easier as it goes and it ends up being a really effective way to know the content

I have to take her again next Fall, so I'll let you know if this changes, but despite her grading EXTREMELY TOUGHLY and expecting you to know exactly what to do WITHOUT ANY RUBRICS, I found her to be very knowledgeable and an overall good professor. Just be prepared to completely guess on your assignment details/formatting.

Class is very interactive and interesting. Prof. Aleks clearly outlined her expectations from the beginning and was very accessible for questions. Your critical thinking skills will be tested but in the best way. Exams are very fair and there is ample time/direction provided for the group project. If you use her as a resource, you'll be golden.

Extremely picky about grading. It doesn't matter if you give a strong and valid opinion about something. If your ideas or concepts don't align with what she thinks is correct, it's completely wrong. For a strategy class that's opinion oriented, she thinks she has the final say in everything. Highly recommend not taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rebeka was one of the best professors I've had in college. She's a very tough grader but you learn a lot in her Foundations of Strategy class. If you do the work and participate in class discussion you'll get an A- don't expect to get an A for just showing up. Start early on the homework and you'll be fine.

Dr. Rebeka was a fantastic professor who had a great way of teaching the concepts through direct participation in class (YOU HAVE TO PARTICIPATE). The projects were on the heavier side, especially the last presentation but overall a well-weighted course and interesting.
Attendance mandatory but material is pretty boring. Easy A if you have a good group

Shirke is definitely the better pick for this class since she's kind and actually listens to student feedback. The homework is A LOT but manageable since the rubrics are clear. The TAs are helpful if you ask and fairly lenient. The class is assignments, presentations, and a group project later on. Overall, much better than Nagel.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Shirke is approachable and genuinely wants students to succeed. She explains expectations clearly and is open to feedback. The lectures can feel boring at times and assignments can pile up, so be prepared. On the bright side, you get to use your laptop during class, so that helps. Easy A if you do the work and have a good group for projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: HOLY.... this class was so much work for it being something seemingly simple. There is way too much busy work. The prof and the TA's are nice but the amount of work you dedicate to this class can really stress people out especially if your team is bad. Make sure to pick a good group of team members.

Best professor for OB! Weekly open note quizzes, no exams. Usually, let us leave Zoom a few minutes early. There was a group project which was quite easy, and she usually gave us class time to meet up with our groups. Attendance was required for lectures. A great professor for sure!

Prof Johnson was amazing. Super chill and laid-back class, as long as you keep up with her announcements (she posts every week which is super helpful to stay on track) and put at least a tiny bit of effort, you'll get the A for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory when I took her, but this is the easiest class I've ever taken. Quizzes are open-book. Lectures are pretty slow and boring. There is one group project, but she listens to feedback and was willing to change the group project presentation to online and things like that. Definitely take her!

Barely attended this class and got an A, definitely take for a GPA boost.  This class can be done independently, with no tests and only weekly quizzes and discussion posts online. There is a textbook and a couple supplemental readings. Dr. Johnson makes it very clear what is required for an A. There is one group project.
I went to class three times and ended with a 98, a very easy course. There are quizzes, discussion questions, and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I LOVE her class and I really enjoyed taking this course. There are no exams, only a few quizzes. (these quizzes can take at home). Also, there is one group project.

HR isn't the most riveting topic, but Dr. Johnson is fantastic. She tries her best to make the class interesting, but also understood that COVID makes things hard so she tried to make the class as easy as possible. She's a great professor and as long as you put in the work and listen to her, you'll do well. A fantastic choice for MGT 3102.

I really enjoyed the environment that Dr. Johnson provided for our class. The class is on HR, so most of the lectures were focused on student-centered seminars based on textbook readings. Most of the grades are based on team projects, and if you did the work thoroughly, an A was a certainty. Overall, I liked the class and her style of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class, and I would recommend it to others.

This class is a very easy A but incredibly boring. Majority of your grade is based on attendance for long, attendance mandatory lectures, with most of them being presented by different speakers each week. Besides that, there's weekly quizzes and a final project where you "improve your health".
Class changed and had mandatory attendance when I went to first lecture. Annoying, but overall fine class.

Probably the easiest A you'll ever get. Every class lecture was basically just going over a powerpoint, so you could easily use the class as a study hall. Super easy assignments and easy grading. Attendance was 5% of your grade but you could walk out any time. She's also very nice as a person and isn't strict about anything
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, kind of treated you like a high schooler, however all the assignments were extremely easy and its basically a free A.
Took during ignite, attendance was 5% of the grade, was a sign in sheet passed around the 100+ person classroom. Quizzes and assignments are very easy, have common sense and this class is a free A.
Took APPH1040 over Ignite, super easy. Just go to class to be respectful, many left when she would have breaks. Class ended early every day.

Some of the most mundane, vacuous, and directionless lectures I've ever seen - BUT.... a very easy grader who doles out more A's than the Yellow Jackets dole out wins to the opposite team. 

If you want a free GPA boost, Taube is the way to go, but the price tag will be questioning your life choices midway those never-ending powerpoints...

Attendance was not on the syllabi when it was first released (week before class started) but after the first class she went and edited it to include attendance. Don't know why that's allowed but oh well. I think she did it to punish us for not showing up the first day. Avoid, especially for the summer.

Had her for the short summer sem and she would lecture the full three hours. There were always required readings and the lectures were never engaging. There were also quizzes after every lecture. Although we didn't have a final just a project that was pretty easy. Definitely gave more work than a health class should ever require

Someone on this complained about how it's obvious that the instructors clearly put low effort in the class, and it shows with typos, test formats changing, incorrect options on quizzes. Weird how teacher will require attendance and effort from student when they themselves don't show too much!

Her whole rate my professor was basically false advertising (haha). She didn't have attendance mandatory in syllabus before the class started and all of a sudden after the first day, she decides to incorporate it into our grade. The lectures are as boring as you can imagine, do NOT take her (especially for the summer).

Please don't take this APPH professor. Her lectures are quite boring and will make you want to fall asleep. The class itself feels mostly useless, and she enforces mandatory attendance. If at all possible, pick a different instructor and it will save your sanity.
Super good class + easy, one weekly assignment/essay and attendance optional
This is the APPH prof to take. No mandatory attendance. Don't bother with lecture. The quizzes and projects can be done by looking at the posted lecture materials. That's all you need.
Easiest A ever. Take this class to fulfil health requirement. Only online quizzes and no mandatory class you're good.
Never attended a lecture, weekly quizzes, sometimes easy essay/homework assignment. Easy semester self improvement project. Easy A, redundant course material.
One assignment per week. Quizzes are open-note
Very easy assignments and weekly canvas quizzes, lectures were once a week but you never had to go.
Let's just say I have no clue what the professor looks like or where the class is even held.
You either have an assignment or canvas quiz every week due before every lecture. Light workload and optional attendance.
Clear assignment criteria. Lectures aren't mandatory. Assignments and quizzes are the only assignments and they are online and easy. Chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely went to this class once in the entire semester. Posts all of the lecture slides for required quizzes. Other assignments (reflection papers, etc) were also pretty short and not difficult.

Her class is mostly fair, being graded on some online quizzes and infrequent assignments throughout the semester. I'd take her class for APPH 1040 again. However, she sometimes puts no effort into the coursework in ways that are obvious. Frequently makes spelling errors and has incorrect information on slides that don't correspond to homework.
Long lectures weren't fun, but the course material was great and she made a few statements throughout the year that have stuck with me and benefitted me since.

Good professor! Easy class. The section I had was comprised of one long lecture per week which was boring, so I only attended about 50% of the lectures, and when I went, only 15-20% of the class was full. Weekly quizzes over lecture material that gets posted in Canvas. A few other assignments and projects, but overall, a pretty stress-free class.

Had Dr. Taube for APPH1040 and she did a great job at teaching the class. It was a long lecture every Friday, but it was only once a week and attendance was not mandatory. You can find her lectures online after the fact, and as long as you pay attention to the content, the weekly quizzes will be incredibly easy. I would recommend her 1040 section!

This professor is really kind and makes the class pretty easy. With online quizzes and only a few assignments, it was an easy A, but the lectures were not the most fun (luckily attendance isn't mandatory).

His tests aren't hard as long as you follow close to the lecture and practice the provided sets before quizzes and exams, they're almost exactly the same. It is a tough course but Prof Ried is trying his best to ease the pressure. If you're a theory lover please attend and tell Prof Ried your passion, he'd be really happy about it.

Very difficult first midterm but he learned from his mistakes and made the following quizzes and midterm muuuch easier. I think that if he teaches this course again it should be fairly easy. Professor Ried is very passionate about math and helpful if you attend office hours!

professor reid was the best math prof i've had at tech. he really cares about his students and wants feedback for how he can improve the class for us. exam 1 was a disaster but he wrote a long apology note and made an extreme effort to make things right. stand up guy, fairly easy quizzes for such a difficult course

He really cares about his students and is very passionate about teaching. After a rough exam 1, he was very generous and gave a bunch of extra credit. He asked how he can better prepare us for the next exam, and answered students' requests by putting practice problem sets in Canvas that accurately reflected future exams.

It's his first year teaching an American class. A lot of the current reviews were written just after Exam 1. He saw we struggled on Exam 1, sent us a very heartfelt apology, made the hard questions extra credit, and made our second exam more in line with other sections. He's not an amazing lecturer, but he's a very nice guy who clearly cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are far more difficult compared to the other sections both this year and in previous years. Exams include content outside of the curriculum and content that he said would not be on the exam. His lectures are a bit monotone, and he gives homework during academic breaks. Overall nice guy but would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice person and professor. He very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell. However, if all differential classes were theory heavy I wouldn't have a problem, but comparing test to different sections it's kind of ridiculous. If you like theory take it with him, if you want an easier A just take it with someone else.

Professor Ried is a great professor. The lectures and tests are theory focused, yet he cares about what he teaches. He wants his students to succeed. When he gave a hard exam, he clarified he did not intend any harm, and gave a great curve for the whole class. He is very caring and is energetic during lectures every day.

I am pretty sure this is his first class, so he didn't really have a great grasp of what type of exam to give. He sounds like a nice guy in class, but the first exam was diabolical. There are a lot of improvements he can and should make as a professor overall, but outside of that exam, I cant really hate him. Pray in his next class he improves.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will say this. Professor Reid is a very kind and caring man, and he genuinely does seem like he wants success for his class. I emailed him to speak a bit louder and a tiny bit slower during lectures, and the very next day he made the improvement. That said, he operates using the European style of teaching, which can be rough if you're like me.
Very chill class. Worth going to lecture but not strictly necessary. Exams were not difficult and were quite reasonable. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Rosbruck was great, she wanted students to participate and kept the lectures pretty dynamic for a health class. It's APPH1040 so cant expect it to be that hard but she was great

I think about this class maybe once a month. Your grade is determined by a few super-easy exams and quizzes (which are all open note) and a grand total of two assignments. Attendance is not mandatory. I haven't been to class since Week 1. Couldn't have had it any better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I haven't gone to class since January. It is April. I have a 99% in the class.
No attendance required, just do the work and do it on time and you are guaranteed an A.
Very small amount of work, everything is open note.
No attendence required, just do the work and do it on time and you are garunteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i love this woman. attendance isn't mandatory, tests and hw are super easy, and theres soooo much extra credit its impossible not to get an a. also shes lowkey pretty funny
I stopped going to lecture a few weeks into this class. There is hardly any work to do for this class and it is super easy. Definitely the best choice for the Wellness requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor to take for health! She was great, attendance not mandatory, and work very light. Love her!
Her class is all tests that are on canvas, and asynchronous. Attendance not mandatory, and up to 4 extra credit points through different things during the semester. VERY EASY class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class. Definitely take 1040 over any of the other health classes if you can. You don't have to show up at all to this class if you don't want to. Only 8 grades, 3 tests, 3 quizzes and 2 writing assignments but they're graded really easily. My high school health class was more advanced than this.

Highly recommend!! Attendance not mandatory and she cancels in-person classes occasionally too. You don't even need to fully pay attention in class to do well. The tests and quizzes are easy, and as long as you do the assignments on time you're chilling.

Take her for APPH. Attendance was not mandatory. Tests are super light if you use your resources ;)
Can't recommend more. Probably spend 1 hour a month on this class and I have a 97%.

This professor is so funny sometimes.This is a health class no one goes to after a while so people just stop coming and no one responds to her questions in the lecture so she'll crack jokes at that and it's honestly amazing, this professor deserves so much better because at the end she takes it so sweetly and still makes lectures fun and engaging.

Super easy class. Attendance isn't mandatory so stopped attending classes early on. There's 3 exams, 3 quizzes, and 2 writing assignments. I would just be very careful about not missing one of the 8 things because ur grade will drop hard. There's also 4 points of extra credit in case you mess up a bit.

Wonderful professor and is so easy— this class is definitely designed to be a brain break from all your other classes. You don't have to go to lecture to do well, but she interacts with students and checks in with them so it can be a really nice break through your day. Content was super easy and all within the notes and extra credit is available.

The easiest class I have ever taken, I heard of some APPH 1040 sections having time consuming group projects. Rosbruck had 3 unproctored exams, 3 unproctored quizzes, and 2 writing assignments. Class barely took any time, I stopped attending lecture after the first exam. There's also up to 4 points of extra credit.
I didn't show up to a single lecture after the first week and got an A. Easiest APPH class, take her if you don't care at all about APPH (like most students).

Very easy class. For the online section, all assignments were very easy to do and did not require much time. In addition, the exams were all open note, so the entire class was a very easy A as long as you did the work. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit as well.

Her online class was very easy. All the tests and quizzes were open note and all her questions are answered in the notes. She has extra credit. Overall this class took almost none of my time. There was no final.

Extremely easy class as everything is online. As long as you read the syllabus and do the exams, you should be fine. Exams were an accurate reflection of material learned. Class did not require an abundance of time to be spent on it. Highly recommend Prof. Rosbruck for APPH 1040 as it was very easy and minimal effort was required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely take her for APPH 1040. I didn't even watch the lectures and got a good grade. Quizzes and exams are open note and most answers are online. If you put in effort for the written assignment you will get a 100. Easy class and low time commitment.

Didn't attend class once and got a 97 in the class. Tests are worth 72% of your grade but they are extremely easy and questions are pulled directly from the notes. Tests are also open note. Rosbruck offers SO MUCH extra credit (up to 4 percentage points to final grade) so I can't imagine not getting an A in this class as long as you do the tests.

She is not a bad professor. It's health so you dont really learn anything important, but she does not make it more work than necessary. The only annoy part is that the tests, which are only multiple choice autograded by canvas, would take around a month to get back to us, which makes no sense.

It's hard to not get an A in this class. Use the textbook and slides on tests and quizzes, you don't need to go to class. Use your brain when doing the other assignments, and you will end with an A. Tons of extra credit if anything happens.
You have to try to not get an A in this class.
Online tests and quizzes. Did not show up, easiest class ever.
Class is extremely easy especially with exams being online and open note. Don't really see how anyone rates her beneath a 4, she has a sense of humor and cares about everything she talks about.

The class is very easy; most people don't show up to lectures. Midterms are taken online in your own time, and lectures are cancelled on the days midterms are due. Rosbruck clearly cares a lot about the topic and seems excited/energetic every class. No final exam.
Really easy class, although it is not the highest in terms of structure and quality. Did not attend any lectures after the first few but still managed to easily pass.
The easiest class I have ever taken, never went to lecture, just online quizzes, and open notebook exams. 10/10
Requirements to get an A: be a living human being (Optional)

If you have a pulse, you will get an A in this class. Never went to a single class except the first day. 8 total assignments (3 quizzes, 3 exams, 2 assignments), everything is open note, online, and take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever, barely need to go. Rosbruck is nice and her exams are online so you can take them when you want during the day of the exam. Barely any assigments, no final.

I imagine this is going to be one of the easiest classes I will ever take in college. As long as you stay somewhat aware of deadlines there is no reason you shouldn't get an A. The tests are all online at-home tests and are free A's as well as quizzes. There were only two assignments and both were very easy.

Not hard. Barely attended class although would recommend watching lectures before exams because some test info can only be found there. Textbook isn't that useful. Best part is she gives lots of extra credit. Worst part is you can't miss a single assignment/turn in anything late for credit. Stay on top of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. But, if you miss an assignment you're already down a grade letter. There's extra credit in the end - about 3 - 4%. so it can raise a 88 to a 91.
Super Easy A. Practically no homework, no final, and all of the tests are open note with answers easily searchable in the textbook and guest lecture slides. Didn't learn much, but it's health.

Really easy A. Exams/quizzes are open note and straightforward and she gives out a lot of extra credit at the end. No real need to go to class, just make sure you look over powerpoint slides before the exams

No need to attend lecture. Go through the slides that she posts, maybe read the textbook if you are interested. Only a few, very easy assignments and quizzes. Tests (online, proctored) tend to get detailed and specific at times, but the material is straightforward nonetheless. Study a little before and you'll be fine. Three midterms, no final.

Don't bother going to lectures unless you're genuinely interested. The tests cover very specific things from textbooks, lectures, etc., but you can still get an A if you don't attend lectures. Lots of extra credit opportunities. I've heard other APPH 1040 professors are easier but honestly it doesn't matter.
There's nothing much to say. The assignments are super easy to get an A on. Exams and quizzes are open resource.

Attending lecture is not mandatory. more than half of the class stopped attending class after the first couple of weeks... She records the lectures and posts the lecture slides weekly. I'm not sure if it was due to COVID-19 or not, but exams and quizzes are all online and taken open-note at home. It's a super chill 2-credit hour class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Stopped going to lecture after the first week. Do your assignments on time and study an hour and a half before the 3 exams. No final.

It's a Health class at a technical university. Don't expect great things. Don't need to go to class because it's the same as reading the textbook, and overall you can forget about the class until an assignment or exam is due.
Nothing much to say, honestly. In the online period the class was pretty easy. 3 tests and a few quizzes. Lectures were all asynchronous and not really necessary to watch. Might be harder in-person.

Took this class online, Buzzport said sync but we only ever watched async lectures from 2017/2018, which is sad because I really did want to learn the curriculum here. Also never ever got responses to any of my emails. Def don't need the textbook. But the class was really easy and I got an A easily so there's nothing I can really complain about tbh

Easy A. Couple quizzes and small assignments every few weeks and that's it. No final. Entire class ended up being async (no live meetings/lectures), but it honestly was kind of nice to not have to worry about lectures for health on top of everything else. There's no reason to not take her, so she gets a 5.

I took this in Fall 2020 in a virtual environment due to COVID. It said on Buzzport that the class was going to be synchronous, but there was never a single live lecture. In fact, she used recordings from lecture that came from 2017. Other than that, I would say the class is pretty easy and just do the work and don't forget the tests.

Rosbruck made health the easy class that it should be. I went to most lectures and found them interesting and relevant. I didn't purchase the textbook and kept up fine. The tests were a bit tricky, but all the info is directly off her slideshows. She gives a ton of extra credit opportunities, so you can get an A even if you get Bs on all the tests.

Health is a stupid class already, but the tests were unnecessarily difficult. Some questions were statistics that didn't really feel useful to the class. Rosbruck is a cool person, just not the best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clear lecturer. Attendance not mandatory or necessary but still go if you can. She gave me extra credit for coming. HW is on Pearson and is easy. Don't read textbook at all. (Don't buy Pearson with textbook. Save money.) 3 tests are fair. Study the slides really well. Know the statistics. Statistics from slides are on the test. Do all extra credit.

She cares about her students - tons of extra credit, gave us extensions for almost every assignment after the online transition. Lectures are amazing, but her tests are oddly specific and you need to study for them. Assigns readings that most people don't do, but they are helpful for the tests. Overall an easy A with just a little bit of effort.
Lecture is super boring and exams are really specific on minute details briefly mentioned in class.
Class is a joke as long as you do the work and memorize the slides before tests. There's no final which is nice.

This class wasn't too hard, and there were lots of opportunities for extra credit. She covers everything you need to know in lecture, and the content is also in the textbook. Overall a pretty easy class.

Read the book, do the book's practice questions, and look over the PowerPoints. Tests are rather difficult, but between the extra credit and easy homework assignments, it's not hard to do well. She's a very enthusiastic, clear lecturer, but many people don't show up for class. Guest lectures are almost as important as content lectures for tests.

Health a pretty straightforward class. I like the energy that she has when teaching the material. During the lectures, you don't need to be alert 100% of the time, since the exams are not too difficult. I especially appreciate the countless extra credit opportunities she gives.

I only went to class to take the midterms. You only need to study the powerpoints since she pulls test questions straight from there. Don't waste your time reading or even buying the textbook. With the extra credit, it's an easy A if you just study the powerpoints. Not sure what these other reviews are talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Does not lecture well and tests are ridiculous in why they ask for. You are tested on very minor details of one part of a lecture. Extra credit is helpful but still a tough class to study for.

Her class is confusing, no one really knows what's going on and her reply to everything is "reach out to the TAs", who never respond. APPH is supposed to be an easy class, but she makes your life difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy class, enjoyable professor. She's a pretty good lecturer as well, which makes a class that I don't really care about a lot better. She's very well educated and has had a lot different life experiences that add to her ability as a professor.

Go to lectures and (sometimes) read the textbook- if you do this, you'll pass tests and get an easy A. Don't need to put in much work. She gives 4 extra credit points to your grade if you do some easy assignments. She definitely designs the course to NOT be work heavy, and she doesn't want you to stress about the class. It's supposed to be easy.

Health is incredibly easy with her. Either go to lectures or read the chapters (there's no need to do both) and you'll be fine for homeworks, tests, and quizzes. You can also get up to 4% of your total grade in extra credit assignments which are quick and easy.

Professor Rosbruck is your best bet for 1040. She knows what she's talking about and is very passionate about the material and her students. There is a chance for 4% extra credit, and as long as you study for the tests (which can be surprisingly hard) and keep track of deadlines, you'll do okay. Most work (quizzes & assignments) is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosbruck is very passionate about what she teaches and makes health as interesting as its going to be. The tests are a bit harder than you'd think they'd be, but if you go to class and do the abundant extra credit you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit given. Posts all lecture notes and guest lecturer notes to course page- really likes to have guest speakers in class. You will do better on the tests if you go to class since some questions come directly from the lectures. Funny in class. Easy quizzes and online assignments.

First, textbook is needed for this class. The textbook is extremely useful when it comes to studying for tests, but she posts her lecture slides on T-Square as well. The tests are simple enough and no trick questions are in them, so they are easy as long as you study properly. Homework and quizzes are easy, and she offers extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Inspirational class! Makes you care about your health and understand the importance with scientific data to back it up. You get to apply a lot of the knowledge you learned with interactive class work. Rosbruck is passionate, caring, and is a dynamic professor making health interesting to learn about.

Rosbruck was an awesome professor.  She manages to make a class of over 250 students to be discussion based and interactive. She truly cares about her students and is enthusiastic about the material. I find her teaching to be inspirational and it got me to care more about my health and the importance of health on all levels not just physical.

More lectures were given by guests from Health Promotions than by the actual professor. The lectures Rosbruck gave herself were terrible. However, tests are easy except for a few inevitable questions on random statistics. Read the book, take the class somewhat seriously, and you'll make an A.

I didn't show up to class unless I had to turn in an assignment (she makes you do it in person) & all I did was read the book before the tests & I got an A. She lets you know exactly what you have to do/know to get a good grade & puts everything on her syllabus. She's also very enthusiastic about teaching. Loved her, definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Going to lecture is all you need to do to get an A really (that and do like 2 of the extra credit options), but you'll still do fine if you don't go and simply read the notes she posts online. Personally I thought she went too fast during lecture, and sometimes you had guest speakers who were really interesting
Don't need to go to lectures, do the extra credit and all the online assignments and read the book.

I barely ever showed up to class and still got an A. The lectures and guest speakers are actually really interesting but attendance is not mandatory by any means. Rosbruck is very nice and she cares a lot about her students. Tests are easy as long as you read the textbook beforehand, but I never took notes. Overall she's the easiest health teacher.

Easy peasy class if you put the work in- either read or pay attention to lectures. Guest lecturers are sometimes there and their info will be tested on. Just come to class and use common sense if you want an automatic/easy A. There is also up to 4 points of extra credit available. 3 Tests, 3 Quizzes, 3 Homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. She loves to pull questions from an online test bank which you can find using questions in the back of each chapter. 3 assignments are given but are easy 100's if you do the work. Encourages participation in class but no one ever shows up because it's not necessary. Guest Lecturers are important though for test questions.

You can either come to lectures or read the book and pass without a problem. Lecture notes are always posted to T-square. Offers up to 4 percentage points of extra credit. Requires just about zero effort, which is, coincidentally, how much effort the professor puts into the class.

On the poorer end of lectures, really dry and almost mind numbing. Not a hard class and his explanations are ample. The class's content itself is relatively easy and the contents per lecture can be covered in 20 min with good mathematical maturity. Wouldn't recommend on the premise of just slow & bland lectures but a good choice otherwise.

Easy exams (literally, study idk what to tell you). Not great lecturer, but the content is easy enough that you can learn it all the week before the test by reading the notes and do fine (I did this and got 100s). Really easy to get a good grade. He also doesn't require attendance. Homework takes, I kid you not, 20 minutes MAX a week.
Worst professor I've ever taken; his exams are no where near the difficult of the practice exams!

Just got done taking the hardest midterm of my life. Talked to friends in other sections whose exams where SIGNIFICANTLY easier. Has an atrocious accent. Only good thing about him is he responds to Ed posts pretty quickly

Very difficult to understand and handwriting during class is tough to decipher. Took the class based on reviews before mine but he must have changed things because the exams were nothing like the practice or lecture and ridiculously difficult. When approached about why exams were so difficult he mumbled something about "figuring it out". AVOID HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Well-organized professor, communicates class information and requirements clearly. Has written and typeset notes available after each lecture. Exams don't feel like overloaded mistake minefields, and past exams make them easy to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Administered this class incredibly well by himself (no TA). Publishes handwritten and typeset notes for each lecture. HW/exam solutions are posted promptly (even before grades are returned), and grading is generous. Clear topic lists and past exams with solutions make exams very approachable. Lectures are textbook-definition-oriented, which I like.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely take 2112 with Professor Michney. Loved this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Literally the BEST. PROFESSOR. EVER.
- Only 4 exams, entirely online, all open note.
- Up to 2 points extra credit per lecture if you comment or ask a question two times.
- Professor is obviously passionate about history and an extremely kind person! Email him with any problems at all he is so understanding!
-Honestly 10/10

Gives four asynchronous open-noted exams and thats the entire class. Final is the same. Really nice guy who cares a lot about history, but also knows Tech students have a lot of things going on so doesn't expect anything too much out of a history class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Class is made up of 4 asynchronous exams that are open note. Each exam has 5 points of extra credit available AND you can also get 10 points of extra credit to your grade if you actively participate in discussions during lecture. 2 required readings throughout the year that are tested on the exam, but overall not a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is entirely dependent on 4 exams. The exams are made up of extremely specific quotes from lectures. The notes and lecture videos posted online do not help with studying for the exams. Exams were open internet though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate about history. Grade is comprised of only 4 exams all of which are open note and asynchronous. Attendance not mandatory as all the lectures are posted online. Extra credit given for in-class participation. Highly recommend Professor Michney as he is a good professor that truly cares about his students.
Grade is composed of only 4 exams, all of which are open-note. He offers extra credit for class participation and class style is flipped. Good class to fulfill history requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade only determined by 4 tests, all asynchronous and open note. Everyone should get an A. Great lectures, you can tell he's passionate about all of the subjects. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and allows everyone to suggest or comment on the subject matter. Sweet guy. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Very kind. Grade determined by 4 tests only. Tests are asynchronous.

Michney was a great professor for American Cities. HTS3011 was the last and only history class I had to take at Georgia Tech, and I'm so glad I took it with him. He gives very thorough feedback, and most definitely knows what he's talking about. He allowed early submissions and left comments before the true deadline. Easy A if you put in the work.

He is very into his lectures in a good way, but this class is extremely tough and he is a tough grader. If historian is not your career path, I would not take this class, it's a very upper level research class.
Best prof.

Good teacher but really really rough grader on papers. Even if you have an A or B one paper could take you to a C. I would avoid this class unless you are 100% going to be a historian the rest of your life.

Grade is based off of 4 tests (25% each). Tests were online and open note. Classroom is flipped meaning you'll have to watch the 45-90 minute lectures on your own time and take notes. Offers extra credit for in class participation and dropped our lowest exam before the final.

This class is ridiculously easy if you do it right. The class is based off of 4 tests (25 percent) that are all on canvas and you can take them anytime anywhere on the test day. He will likely drop your lowest test grade before having to take the final exam (which isn't even cumulative) so you won't have to do it. There are readings but it's easy.

Final grade in this class determined by 4 exams only, each being 25% of your grade (including the final). Mainly lecture based with a couple of small readings from the textbook each week. Found myself practically copying down every word he said on the 45-70 minute long lectures. Does offer extra credit for in-class participation and bonus exam ?s.
Really loved this class and would definitely take Professor Michney again if I needed another social science!

The course was graded just on 4 midterms. Participation was not mandatory but encouraged by extra credit. Exams were hard. Keep up the reading to stay on track. Go to the lectures. Put in the work, and you will get an A.

Read and annotate his previous recordings and you are ready for the tests. 4 tests, including the final, 25% each of your grade. Not difficult if you read the material given. He gave extra credit (up to 10% of your final grade) for those who participated in class. Each test was also graded up to 125%, so there's room for error.

His class was weird. The main grading criteria was talking in class and pop quizzes. I swear he graded the pop quizzes while he was drinking because it did not seem like there was a rhyme or reason for why points were taken off of anything. He also never posted what your participation grade was, so you never knew how you were doing in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's really passionate about what he's teaching and he puts in a lot of effort to make sure his students do well. I didn't like history in high school, but I genuinely enjoyed his class. He offers extra credit after exams, and exams are fast based, not analysis based. As long as you show up to lecture and take notes, you'll get an easy A

Very hard to understand his lectures. He tries to make a point and then uses a bunch of examples to back it up. He says so much that I had to record every single lecture. He also seemed to struggle to make a good test. First one had a C average, next test had A average, next was tough again. He is very unbiased which I loved, but hard to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are so hard and have nothing to do with the lectures. Super unclear about what to study
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a fine teacher who defintiely loves what he teaches. He kind of looks like Abraham Lincoln. Some of the work we did seemed extra (he didn't test on it) but there was a LOT of reading- both in articles and books. Group project and 2 book reports due, but he gives great feedback on essays. Skimming is fine for articles. Discussion based class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You have to read for class ever day and the only homework is 5 essays. The final is a take-home paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He's hated for no reason. Gives tons of extra credit and is a very wholesome, enthusiastic, positive guy overall. He is a little soft spoken but will repeat anything you ask. Very helpful and makes the class easy.

He is really nice and cares about teaching his students well. His lectures are good, especially when supplemented with sebastian fernandez on yt. He is very clear on course expectations and gives practice problems similar to exams which are a lot easier than other sections.

Like others have said, this class is kind of a joke. You can have any professor for 2552, it doesn't really matter. Professor Tang is very quiet and can ramble on, but his tests were easier than the other sections. Make sure you have a good TA for studio and it'll be fine.

This class is a joke because you don't need to understand why anything works and you can still do amazing. He's a really nice guy but his lectures are just really over complicated when all you really need is like a select few formulas which you can just learn online. Tests are easy with extra credit as well and studio quizzes are beyond free

All professors spend too much time deriving and proving during lecture. He is very soft spoken and speaks quickly, and bad lecture notes. Studio and Sebastian Fernandez on youtube are all u need (except unit 8). He also gives extra credit on tests. Very easy math class if you pay half attention. DONT TRY TO UNDERSTAND THE CONTENT, JUST HOW TO DO IT

He's a great guy but his lectures were pretty slow and boring. He posts his notes on canvas and the TA for the studio went over everything well enough to not go to lectures. He's accessible over email and is a good guy overall, just not the best professor.
Lectures were hard to understand, so I gave up on going, but the TA went over everything in discussion. Professor cares a lot, but sometimes just makes lectures overly complex and confusing.

Super sweet guy. Very soft spoken, hard to hear. All notes on canvas. Test heavy: 17%midterms(1&2) 37%final. Most tests curved & had extra credit. Responds fast to emails. Makeups r much harder than the normal ones. Lack of practice for studying and has weird answer keys that don't have work. Exams r harder than quizzes&hw but not crazy different.

Accessible outside of class with email and office hours. Lectures were fine but could barely hear him; posted notes after class. TA graded so strict he had to curve our quiz scores to match the other sections. only gives practice problems in the textbook since he wasn't allowed to provide old exams. Seems genuine guy but wouldn't reccomend

Prof Rudchenko is a lovely lady, but sometimes is really really hard to understand. Her course wasn't the worst in terms of difficulty, and some of the excel stuff she touches on is pretty useful. Would honestly take again though not a bad learning experience

If you want to get an A in the class, take her. Open note exams that are exactly like the practice exams and I scored 100s on all. Some things to know: She has a pretty thick accent which takes a little getting used to, and her canvas page is the craziest thing in the world, really disorganized. Overall, if you take it with her, you'll get an A.

I took 2250 with her, very easy so I took 2255 asynchronous over the summer. Similar difficulty to 2050, not bad. Just learn how to do the homework and memorize the excel formulas before exams and you will do well. Dr Rudchenko is so sweet and truly cares about her students. Loves talking about AI for some reason. Take her over any other prof!
Tests were easy very similar to practice tests. There was a bit of busy work. Group project was alright she does assign groups. Overall, chill professor

Dr. Rudchenko was very passionate about the material, and she always sought to keep the class engaged. She made the lecture slides and videos easily accessible, so if we had to miss class for some reason we could still complete the excel assignment outside of class and get full credit for that day. Exams are easy if u do the hw and practice tests

Class is more work than needed. Tests are on MyLab (Pearson) and are relatively similar to practice tests and previous HW questions, so I'd recommend using those to study. If you go to class, do the HW assignments, and make a good cheat sheet based on everything in the HW, practice tests, you'll probably end with an A. Still a lot of work though.

super confusing canvas to navigate. hard to understand prof in her emails but overall very easy class. just annoying constant busywork. i would just do everything ahead of time so u dont have to submit participation every other day.

Canvas page is the most chaotic thing I've seen in my whole life... often hard to navigate. Spams emails and announcements and there's a TON of busy work with this class. Her exams are similar to practice tests- second exam was noticeably the most difficult but that could have just been me. Still pretty doable to get an A.

Love Tatiana! Easy class, but lots of busy work. There's so many assignments and parts that make up your grade that even if you miss a few, your grade is still fine. There's a participation assignment every class, but she posts videos on Canvas on what to do. 3 tests (super easy, basically same as practice test, & lowest replaced w avg of 3),.

She is a very sweet professor and the class is very easy. A lot of people complain about the amount of work but each assignment takes between 5-30 minutes so it's really not that bad. If you do the practice tests and the homework all of the tests will be really easy. Overall, not the most engaging class but it is really easy to get a good grade.

She is so sweet and a good professor, but the amount of work was ridiculous. I took the online course and things were constantly due. And it wasn't super clear what to turn in sometimes. Her forcing us to submit the excel Mon/Wed/Fri did force me to learn it though. The short essays and 5 page essay at the end were very unnecessary though.

Literally the easiest class ever. Got a 100 on every exam and homework. The AI project is extremely silly, but you get so much time to do it and it doesn't take long. A LOT of weekly homework but it's easy. She is hard to understand and a little crazy, but worth it for how easy the class is.

Easiest class of my life, but it was so filler class. Didn't really learn all that much from this class, it's like if AP stat was way more lax and some excel. The AI project she did was kinda dumb and pointless (she is so obsessed with AI it's kinda crazy, but at least you get a free Chat subscription from it), but project was easy.
It is very hard to understand her so all of your learning will mostly be on your own. Also much of the work has very little meaning so its a lot of time doing busy work

The class was very easy, but by the end its so frustrating and feels so pointless. She's very hard to understand and I feel like I learned nothing from the class. I would rather take a class from a slightly more difficult teacher to actually learn something. There is way too much busy work and homework as well.

Can't understand her accent at all. The material is easy but too much busy work. This class could be simple, but it is drawn out and as tedious as possible. The grading is not too tough. Forgot half of my assignment but she didn't take off credit. She isn't tech savvy either and felt her lectures were useless.
Insane amount of work.

shes so awesome and super funny and makes class fun, lots of homework but it all ends up being the kind of stuff on the test so in the end its helpful. exams are just like the study guide. excel heavy but pretty straightfoward. would totallllly take again
She is extremely friendly and a very kind soul.

This class is on easy material with the most work possible. Prof is really nice but she assigns so much busy work. This class could be so easy and simple, but it is drawn out and as tedious as possible. The grading is not too tough. There are lots of extra credit opportunities and dropped assignments. Overall, her class is annoying but not awful.

Take her!! Dr. Rudchenko is the sweetest and wants her students to succeed. The class is one of the easiest classes I have taken at Scheller and she makes it as stress-free as possible. There is homework but the exams are very similar to homework questions.

I did not enjoy this class at all; it was a headache. There was lots of work and assignments constantly due (some I didn't feel were necessary). They weren't difficult, but annoying. She was extremely unclear with the project guidelines. Focus on practice exams and homework to study for exams as they are similar problems to the exam.

Tatiana is a nice professor; she is caring and gives many resources for students to catch up. We have a lot of online videos to make sure we get the concept right. One thing I may add, though, is that we had Friday HW and that can be a bummer at times because its an added on assignment day submission. Do practice tests, pretty similar to tests!

There was a lot of busy work for the class, but it was nothing difficult. After the in-class, Friday asynchronous assignments, and the practice test, the exams were a breeze. All exams were on Pearson and were similar to the practice test. Rudchenko is funny, and the accent wasn't too harsh...was used to it within a week. Take her for the A.
Lots of busy work, everything is due at 10 PM but the class is extremely easy. Practice exam is literally just the exam with different numbers inputted. Professor Rudchenko is very sweet.

Class material itself is easy to comprehend especially if you have taken AP Stat in high school. There is  a lot of busy work in the class but nothing unbearable. Highly recommend doing the HWs and practice exams to be successful in this class. Overall an easy A

Honestly, she's a great professor. There is a lot of busy work, yes, but it kind of works well because if there is something you didn't understand in class you have plenty of work to figure it out. She also offered students to attend class via zoom halfway through the semester which was nice. She can be hard to understand at times but she is funny.

Dr. Rudchenko is definitely the best pick for MGT 2250 and MGT 2255! She is pretty hilarious and cares about the success of students in the class. But note that there are A LOT of assignments that you need to complete and just generally a lot of busy work. The material is not too hard as she provides detailed study guides and practice. TAKE HER!
she's hard to understand and there is SO much busywork outside of class. never learns anything in class and she doesn't even know her own excel sheets

i (& many of my peers) were baited by the positive rmp reviews for this prof, but im here to say - DO NOT TAKE. she's hard to understand and gives SO many assignments it's insane. material isn't even hard but there's sm to keep track of. i get 10+ email notifs a day from the class canvas. obsessed w chatgpt and schedules random assignments.

She is very enthusiastic, but isn't always coherent and keeps having issues with her own Excel sheets. Also weirdly obsessed with using ChatGPT for things it can't do very well (I think Tech is pushing it overall though). Exams are very easy but there's no partial credit, lost 20% due to a dumb math error that affected a multi-part question.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of easy busywork. Exams were exactly like practice tests that were also required for a grade. 3+ assignments a week, including an asynchronous friday class and many poorly made videos. Several times the class detours into hyping ChatGPT rather than the relevant content. Ruchenko is nice but hard to understand and out of touch.

The rater saying there are classes on Friday probably misunderstood the syllabus. To be fair, it does say asynchronous classes. But that just means you have homework. I'm currently taking this class and it is very easy. Exam question are taken from the practice test and homework. Be warned, there's a lot of homework, most due at 12:10 PM or 10 PM.

taking her for mgt 2255. she assigns so many assignments that it's insane. she doesn't always understand how her own excel sheets work. she assigns so many useless tasks that literally serve us no purpose. sometimes hard to understand with her accent, but that's not the main issue.

THERE IS CLASS ON FRIDAYS. It isn't shown on registrar, it's online. I just started taking the class so I have no real rating other than the fact that she likes CHAT-GPT and has a heavy accent. I can't believe this isn't on the registrar, this is ridiculous. Is this even allowed?

Easy A, but insanely annoying class. So much work outside of lecture mostly because she wastes so much time either rambling about chat-GPT or trying to figure out how her own excel sheets work, which she should know as its the only thing taught in the course. Not to mention the extra online lecture on Friday that isn't shown in registration.

You DO NOT need to read the textbook to do well. I was reading it the first two weeks, being a nerd, but it doesn't help you at all. I find her tough to understand vocally at times because of her accent, but the in-class WS's, HW's, and practice tests are all you need to know, going into test 3 with a 100% just from that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy and straightforward. The tests were very similar to the practice tests. While there was a lot of assignments and homework to submit, everything was straightforward to complete. You could even miss up to 6 classes without points being taken off. I would not take any other professor for this class.

Dr. R is so beyond awesome. She sets everything up for you to do well, and it is basically a guaranteed A. She even streams her classes on Zoom so you can attend virtually if you need to, but is also super forgiving with attendance (you can miss up to 6 in-person classwork assignments with no punishment). Would take her again any day!

This class is set up for you to do well. We primarily use excel and the formula sheets for tests give step by step directions. They are very forgiving with late work (never took off points). Dr. Rudchenko is the sweetest so I definitely recommend. I learned a lot and the class felt very low pressure.

light work class. helpful material that was taught for outside the classroom. Really improve your excel grade. Amazing teacher who gives you opportunities to get an A. Practice Test = tests essentially.

The hardest thing about this class is remembering to submit all of the assignments, but otherwise this is a very straightforward and simple class. Knowing how to do all of the homework problems is essential for the exams, but you are allowed a crib sheet for every exam. Rudchenko is very lively and energetic, so lectures are generally pretty fun.

I LOVE Dr. Rudchenko! She is so caring and absolutely hilarious. She loves what she does. Her grading criteria is extremely lenient and very clear. It is easy to succeed in this class if you do all of your assignments. I would recommend not missing class because a lot can be covered in one class, but I found the material very enjoyable and cool.

I LOVED PROFESSOR RUDCHENKO! She is the sweetest professor I have encountered at Georgia Tech and only wishes the best among her students! I scored low on my second exam and she motivated that I could still get an A and not give up! I ended with an A and highly recommend this professor for MGT 2250!

I went into this class hearing all the positive reviews and was surprised at the experience I had- very heavy with busy work. Constant homework/busy work and the Canvas is pretty disorganized. She is a sweet lady and means well and is very accessible, but I don't relate to the experience everyone else had. A little hard to understand

Rudchenko makes this class very easy! She practically shows you what to do and guides you the entire way. Her exams mimic the practice tests and classwork/homework she gives, so it's nothing out of the blue. We do have textbook pages, but you don't necessarily need to read them, as it's a very hands-on class.
Really easy class! Take her!

Was 1/2 in person 1/2 async when I took it, very clear expectations. Just attend the lectures, do HW on time and study your classwork for tests and you should be good to go. Very hard not to get an A.
This professor was very enthusiastic about what she was teaching. The homework and tests were fairly easy. If you keep up with all the assignments, you will do very well in the class.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!  "mandatory" classes but she posts everything online and does not take attendance. Tests and homework are easy if you pay attention in class. She is great at explaining what to do and gives more than enough material for you to succeed. Gives practice tests that are almost identical to the real tests. Ended with a 99.99%
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the most entertaining classes I've taken at tech. She's a little bit disorganized with her lectures but with a little extra effort, I learned a lot. She makes her expectations very clear and is a whole lot of fun to interact with.

Rudchenko is an amazing teacher, one of my favorite so far at Tech. I was awful at statistics in high school but excelled in this class. Homework are very helpful for the tests and she is very forgiving in grading.

She is nice and you can tell she cares about her students. The material is pretty easy too. Though her canvas is SO disorganized it's actually overwhelming. Nonstop canvas notifications that important stuff gets lost. There was a paper that was only mentioned in the syllabus.
Her class is easy, so you can get an A if you just submit your assignments on time.

She's really easy. You'll get a high A as long as you go to class and do the HW's. Practice tests are almost exactly the same as the exams, so do that before taking the exams. This class is a lot of busy work though, but if you took AP Stats in high school, it'll be a breeze. She has an accent but you get used to it by week 2. She loves to teach.
This class was extremely easy. The professor is super nice but doesn't speak English very well and isn't the best lecturer.

Mrs. Rudchenko is one of the best there is at Georgia Tech. Her classes can be confusing sometimes due to her strong accent, but she ensures that everyone is on the same page and understands what is going on. The tests and homeworks (you get multiple tries on homework) are pretty self-explanatory and easy.

An amazingly caring professor with wonderful TAs. You'll be very supported in this class. It's honestly an easy A and kind of basic, but I did learn useful excel skills. She's hilarious and makes everyone smile.

Dr. Rudchenko is always a solid choice. She's funny, kind, and helpful. Easy class if you just make sure you get the work done. Clear grading policy and relatively easy course. Had her for this and Management Stats, and I love her every time I take her.

Dr. Rudchenko is awesome! Shes super nice and willing to support you in any way. The class itself is very easy; If you use excel, you're good to go. Her accent is hard to understand at first, but you will get used to it pretty quickly. There are daily 'quizzes' which get annoying, but they aren't worth that much so you can miss several.

Dr. Rudchenko is the SWEETEST! She began every email by reminding us that we are welcome and supported in this class! All assignments are completed on MyLab. She posts example Excel documents and videos explaining how to do almost every problem!! This class is super easy to get an A in if you just put minimal effort in. 10/10!!

Professor Rudchenko has been the best professor I have had at tech so far. She is always available if you need help, and her lectures are well put together. If you do the homework, and study the practice tests, you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor!! Very sweet and nice. Would recommend. Also took her for MGT 2250 and it was the same level of difficultly if not less.

Spring '21 Asynchronous Professor Rudchenko is kind and sent encouraging messages throughout the entire semesters and the TAs would always leave positive messages in the homework comments. The homework has multiple attempts and she posts "study guides" for them so there's no reason to not get an A. Also the tests were open note. Practice tests ftw

(Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) Absolutely loved Dr. Rudchenko. With this being an online, async class, it wasn't too difficult, and she provides a lot of resources to get the homework and exams done. Basically, if you can use Excel, you can do this class.
Tati is hilarious. Her handouts were a ton of paper (and repetitive) but very helpful to look back at. I loved the way she taught too!

Her accent is thick, but she did alot of videos that weren't her speaking. I learned everything in that class without difficulty. I really loved how it was taught and the way homeworks/tests were done. There's a practice test for every test. She was super helpful when I wasn't sure about something. LOVE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easiest professor at the school probably. AND she's hilarious, super high energy and makes everything super clear. If you don't take her class you're doing yourself a disservice

She was hard to understand at first but after the first week it becomes easy to understand her. Accurately outlines what you need in order to make a good grade in her class. She's very understanding and super accessible outside of class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Everything comes from lecture and attendance is mandatory so you have to show up. She's very nice and cares a lot! She can be hard to understand at the beginning but it isn't that bad. If you show up pay attention and do your homework correctly the class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love professor Rudchenko! She is very sweet and cares deeply about her students. She is very expressive and positive and gives good lectures. Her tests are like the homework and make it easy to follow along in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved having Prof Rudchenko this year and she's a caring and funny teacher. It's not hard to understand her after a week or two. She's very upfront about the syllabus and grading and it's very clear how to do well. I practiced only homework for exams and got A's on all. She's strict about attendance and doesn't give much extra credit though.

Practice tests are the exact same as the real tests with numbers changed around. She follows the syllabus to the T and is unwilling to deviate from her strict rules even when common sense and leeway should prevail. The class was very easy, but then again I had a great AP Stat teacher in HS who had already taught me everything covered in this class.

She's foreign so it's hard to understand her at first. Class is exclusively excel. There is little homework, and most of it is fairly easy. To study for all tests (including the final) all you really have to do is complete the practice exams she gives. Her policy with attendance is kinda weird. She's hilarious, but generally not intentionally.

Dr. Rudchenko's class is very straight forward and easy to do well in. Tests are nearly identical to practice tests. The class is entirely based on Excel and attending class is necessary to learn how to input certain functions. There is little homework and for the most part is pretty easy. Take her class if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Her accent is a bit tough to understand but after a week it becomes second nature and you can fully understand her. The material is really easy and the tests are exactly the same as the practice test. You can use Excel for all of the tests and you get a formula sheet for every test. The class is very comparable to AP STAT with added Excel. Take it

Some may say her accent is too difficult to understand, but if you take the time to pay attention in class and do what is expected of you, you will realize she actually makes it really easy to succeed in both courses that she teaches.

I had Professor Rudchenko for MGT 2250 and 2251 and I felt like the teaching format of 2251 was much better. She has a lot of office hours if you are ever confused and the tests mostly are built off of the practice materials she provides. Overall I found her class to be fairly straightforward and much easier/less work than 2250.

Rudchenko's one of a kind. She does have an accent, so it does make it a little hard, BUT if you listen, pay attention, and show up, this class is NOT hard. Attendance is mandatory. There's take home quizzes, no homework, and fairly easy tests with conceptual questions, but regardless she gives EVERYTHING to you. Index card for a crib sheet.
She really cares about attendance and participation. You don't need a physical textbook, just the online homework/quiz platform. Homework, quizzes, practice tests, and tests are all online.

Tatiana is a great professor and really cares about the success of her students. She puts in a lot of effort to try to get everyone to understand even when the topics are difficult and she can be somewhat hard to understand. She is more than willing to meet and help anyone. Some tests and quizzes are difficult but they mostly come from the homework

She does really care about students' success in her class. She has a tough time with communicating effectively to her students, but the course material is very simple. She gives ample opportunities to meet with her and to succeed. The tests and quizzes (both online) are the same as the homework problems - answers choices and all. She's funny.

I get easily frustrated with her, just because she doesn't ever really answer questions (or understand what the questions are even asking.) She does drop the lowest test grade and curves, but the tests are hard and infuriating (though open-note) because if you are one decimal pt off, you're wrong. and she never went over it. and it's online.

Rudchenko means well, she wants to help and will do what she can to do so, but she has very poor communication skills. She, the accent is part of it, but even besides that she can make manageable concepts much more complicated. But the material itself is pretty easy.

Dr. Rudchenko, is the most helpful professor I have ever met. If you cannot make it to office hours, she will work around your schedule to help you. Her lectures are easy to follow, although she does have an accent. She provides a practice tests that are very similar to the exams.  She allows and sometimes provides long formula sheets for exams.

So glad I had him for ME2016. The class was just projects, so no homeworks, quizzes, or tests. The projects were very manageable, and the expectations were very clear. This class was a pretty easy A with him, but I heard several of my friends complaining about this class with other professors. I highly recommend taking him if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice dude. Enjoyed his lectures and the projects were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to take 2016 with Dr. Kemerli. The grade is made up of 7 small projects, nothing else. Easy A.

I dont understand the hate. An incredibly engaging professor that cares about the student success. Also we have yoga breaks between topics which is goated. If you want to learn the material with the man who wrote the textbook, I'd take 2200 with him. If you don't want to show up to class and learn everything last minute, take someone else.

Good guy tbh, he def cares about students. He sometimes cold calls on people but its chill, you can just say you don't know. He tries to learn students' names, which is nice. He explains things well in my opinion, you just have to pay attention and you'll understand.
The exams test the execution speed of your surface-level understanding as opposed to critical thinking.

Great professor, really knows what he's talking about and super approachable after class to ask questions to. Projects are super fun and I would recommend doing the EC even if you don't need it. Didn't spend more than 3 hours on any project and outside of mandatory attendance loved the class.
Not as useful as made out to be. Will help you answer coding jesus questions tho

The class needs work in two main areas: lectures and projects. Lectures are somewhat vague compared to exam/homework content. It is recommended to read the textbook (written by Ramachandran and also expensive) and attend the 3-hour weekly labs (no thanks). The projects are either very difficult or time-consuming, or both.

The course itself can be hard but not unbearable. Requiring to go to the lecture is annoying since I barely paid attention because I was working on a project that often rarely prepared for the exam. Exam questions were pretty fair but still tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I genuinely don't understand all these horrible reviews. Ramachandran clearly knows his stuff, and it shows. Most people's issue seems to be that the class is tough. I can't stand when bum students blame professors instead of putting in the work to master hard concepts. There are countless resources to help you succeed.
Coasting on tenure. Enough said. I believe Georgia Tech should consider putting competent professors on what is possibly one of the most important, fundamental courses in this major
clownshow. most important topics taught in the most horrendous way.
People will say "at least the projects are good, they teach you a lot." No they don't. They are outdated and create the illusion of learning due to the sheer amount of work.

Tests are rediculously long and time is short, rote memorization and calculations. Projects are tough along with everything else. Course is based around the txtbook which is terrible: takes too long to explain simple concepts, awkward phrasings, rambling, confusing format. Required ed discussion participation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Course needs a lot of work!

I've honestly never seen anything like it.
