They've managed to take content that's very heavy on systems-level thinking and turn it into a rote calculation frenzy.
The course quality is like something you'd see in a third-world country - hasn't been updated in 15 years, doesn't make use of new technology, emphasizes rote learning over understanding.
Tremendously difficult in the wrong ways.

I'm not sure what you're supposed to get from this course. The problems given on the test are all rote calculations, with no emphasis on systems thinking. If you're signing up for this to learn system architecture or design, you will be terribly disappointed.

Ramachandran is a good person and clearly cares about his students, but personally I find him hard to follow along with in lecture + his slides are messy. I think his book explains concepts much better.

Kishore is not a great lecturer. slides are messy, often rambles is confusing, and just uses point solutions to force students to come. Most people watch Daglis' lectures instead, which are far more coherent. 2200 is probably the hardest class I've taken at Tech, exams are difficult and they grade Ed participation to make up for no TA involvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class 2 years ago, and it was one of the hardest classes I've ever taken my whole life. The heavy low-level coding and debugging, the insane amount of concepts presented (not taught), and the super long office hour line all made the class hard. Exams were highly stressful, and TA's did not help with the assignments. Course needs revamp.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm sure Kishore means well - but that's truly not enough for a course with such heavy and important content. Lectures are meaningless as Kishore tends to come unprepared and start lecture late, go on unrelated ramblings speak extremely fast and annotate powerpoint slides in such a fashion that no one can understand what is supposed to be learned.

Students will leave the class knowing how to calculate the number of bits needed for a predefined memory scheme within 30 seconds, but will be unable to apply the important underlying concepts to other domains and industry problems. This is due to the failed teaching and emphasis on rote learning.

The concepts covered in this course are tremendously important for software engineers. Unfortunately, it's taught horrendously. The course needs to be entirely revamped, and steer far clear from the rote learning and mindless calculation path that it's currently on.

Lectures are useless, handwritten slides and diagrams are confusing and point solutions enforced. Office hours has a queue due to the mass amounts of students that need help. Even students with the best time management will struggle with this class since there are projects, homeworks, demos, and tests, with 2-3 falling on each week.  Don't take.
The professor is unaware of structured teaching, instead relying on stream-of-consciousness rambling intermingled with bizarre analogies. A thick accent amplifies the confusion.

Every single concept in this class is undeniably useful. Yet, the utterly asinine, brain-dead fixation on calculations and torturous, mind-rotting details is beyond absurd—it's a travesty, especially when AI's sitting here, rendering this nonsense obsolete with ruthless efficiency.

Good lecturer - knows his stuff and is able to communicate content effectively. His slides are kinda messy. The PointSolutions are good knowledge checks, but you have very little time. Projects are very tough - start early and visit office hours. The textbook (written by him) is extremely helpful and matches the course material.
no-bs course that will 'beat you into shape' for software engineering
You will hate the projects, but they will make you a debugging god and you will dominate all other SWEs
The course should focus on "systems and networks," which is the title. Instead it focuses on cumbersome circuit simulations
Exams don't involve much problem solving, but have extreme time pressure and lots of calculations. Indian exam style
Extremely difficult exams and little guidance on brutal projects

Extremely thick accent and rambling teaching style - knows he can't keep an audience so enforces Point Solutions to force people to attend. My advice: go to his lecture, don't pay attention, answer the participation questions and learn the content from the far-superior Daglis.

Does PointSolutions participation which is surprisingly hard to get credit on even if you're attending. Difficult tests with insane time pressure, hard to be both fast and accurate. Hardest class I've taken at GT throughout both BS and MS. Read the textbook that he wrote since lectures were incomprehensible and fast-paced. Start projects early.

His lectures are oddly difficult to follow, but he wrote the (high-quality) course textbook and you can just read that instead. Irritating exam format in which 70% of the questions are released before the exam, so exams become an exercise in regurgitating memorized solutions as fast as possible under a stressfully short time limit. Great projects!

Hard class with difficult projects and test but learned a lot about computer systems. Kishore is fair and cares about his students. Class prepares you well for distributed systems work. Highly recommend taking the class with Kishore. Definitely possible to get an A in this class if you pay attention in lecture and actually understand the content

Kishore's a sweet guy and genuinely cares about his students, but his lectures are hard to follow and slides are disorganised. Also, turning point is 3% of your grade but there's barely any time to do it. Exams are a better measure of how good you are taking a timed exam than how well you know course content. Great TAs though!

Abysmal class. Projects take over 10+ hours but count for 5%. Exams test on speed and memorized answers more than content. Even with 70% of the questions released before the exams there are countless ambiguities within. The same goes for HW. TAs are overwhelmed and often unavailable.Not enough time for attendance checks.Take with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can take the other professor, I would highly recommend it.  Kishore's slides are extremely unorganized making it almost impossible to take notes.  He also gave no time to answer the turning point questions in class.  Also participating in ed is 2% of your grade. The extra credit project was extremely hard as well. The TAs were pretty bad too

Call the 70% released questions (its 70 not 80 now) a practice exam. TAs are rude on Ed Discussion & make me not want to ask questions. Turning Point in his class is hard to do because he doesnt warn you before a question. The EC project is impossible. The Ed Discussion participation shuts down a few weeks before the final so stay on top of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Umakishore is the best! His lectures are very thorough and align closely with the textbook. I suggest reading the textbook, which is very helpful in terms of clearing the concepts taught in class! The tests and projects are fair, but make sure to start early on the projects! Great professor and great class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Learned nothing from his lectures since his voice was always muffled and his slides were handwritten and illegible. I basically just survived off of Daglis' slides. The projects were painful and drained my will to live. Extra credit project was offered but the project was basically impossible to complete. Class also had turning point participation.
Prof Rama is 2200. The course is quite difficult with a lot of work between the exams, projects, and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rama is hands down one of the best professors at Tech. The course has a lot of content, but if you read the book, you will be golden. My biggest tip is to read the book!!! everything in the lecture is based on the book, and professor Rama is the one who wrote it. The class is pretty interesting and worth doing.

The textbook will be your best friend in the class. Since he wrote the book, it's the exact same as the lectures. Honestly, I found the book MUCH more helpful because he lectures way too fast for me.

Projects are really hard and time consuming so be prepared for those. Overall was also a pretty nice dude and cared a lot.

Kishore is so passionate, but his content organization isn't the best. So, if you don't learn from watching him lecture, take someone else, as the resources provided outside of his messy slides are scarce. Also, projects take forever, and tests are weighted heavily.

Kishore is passionate about what he teaches (he wrote the textbook), but his notes are kinda unorganized, and the projects are painful. The textbook is very hard to read, and some of the concepts go unexplained in lectures, meaning you have to read the textbook too.

Kishore is very knowledgable and caring. I second the review where he is out of touch with the class - the TA team is extremely understaffed, and projects are unclear. The textbook is extremely helpful, but lectures were hard to follow. Professor Daglis had much clearer slides. I really enjoyed 2110, but was disappointed in 2200. Too much material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Homeworks are mostly short and easy, and projects help you learn but often take forever. Office hours are often crowded and lectures often ramble and are disorganized. Forsyth or Moss honestly might make a better 2200 prof. I spent hours on the memory project and only got about 50% on it. Really do not like his teaching style or exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were a pain. He would walk around the room with a mask on, and his slides are messy because he circles everything. Exams were stressful and there was never enough office hours. I know this class has a bad reputation and is worse than 2110, but Kishore makes it overly tough. One project consumed all of spring break and ruined my vacation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His course is extremely disorganized. Other reviews say it's due to the TAs, but it's not. TAs bring up issues during TA meetings and they are ignored by the professors. He is stubborn in his own way and refuses to give points even after acknowledging that the test was graded incorrectly. He also wrote the textbook, so it's just as confusing...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is hard! But that's ok. Kishore is very passionate and has great analogies, but it's easy to fall behind. Lots of people blame the disorganization of the course on him (particularly exams), but I think more of it is because of the TA team. They're so understaffed it's heartbreaking. If only the CoC payed CS TAs reasonable rates......

TA's said they would release 80% of questions before exam but changed too many on actual exam. The memory project consumed way too much time and was over spring break. Lectures are disorganized and some of his TA's are very rude and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He insists on handwriting his slides, making them difficult to read and track. He highlights half of the slides and circles on top of that, and this extreme redundancy makes it difficult to follow anything on the slide. He wears a mask, walks around the room, and is out of breath while speaking, and with a mic on top of that muffles everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the teacher is great but is very difficult at the same time

Great lecturer. His style is not for everyone, but I felt his use of lighthearted analogies and class participation kept me engaged. CS 2200 is the toughest course I've taken thus far: there are long projects, many homeworks, and difficult tests. Kishore made it more fun. (100% need to read the textbook chapters for tests, though.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Nice person, but awful professor. The exams needed 10+ clarifications to understand what the questions were even asking. Correct answers are often marked wrong. The professor is too stubborn to change even when the TAs acknowledge that they disagree with how exams are being graded/ answer keys.

Take with another teacher. Just read his book.

This professor was extremely hard to follow, and his slides were very hard to read. There was also a very annoying attendance system, and the class was super disorganized.
The projects were pretty good, and getting a good grade is achievable if you do all the work, but there is too much imo,  and  I personally learned nothing from Kishore.

2200 is a hard class but Ramachandran is an amazing professor. Weekly homeworks aren't too difficult if you reference the textbook. There are 5 total projects which are very time-consuming - start them early! For tests, 80% of the questions are released in advance for you to study and this makes for a much more pleasant testing experience.

While the class itself has many issues, they are almost all due to mismanagement from the TAs. Professor Kishore is a fantastic lecturer, a great explainer, and very passionate. The sole (albeit large) critique I have is that he moves extremely quickly, and it's easy to fall behind. Overall though, great professor for a mediocre class.

Very, very nice and wholesome. He wrote the textbook and basically created CS2200 at GT. Knows his stuff very well, and clear at explaining it. Class has complex concepts and homeworks though. Don't pair it with other hard classes in the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: While he is an ok lecturer, the grading in this class is completely dependent on how well you copy exactly what the textbook says. Regardless of if your answer is conceptually right and is correct in real life, the prof and TAs only care what the textbook says. Would avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kishore is very nice. He definitely knows how to teach. The homeworks are OK. Projects require quite some work though. Highly recommend Dr. Kishore.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had.

Although he moved pretty fast in lectures, he tried his best to offer interactions online with other students, which was nice. He was accomodating in the pandemic because he released the test questions early and allowed you to work on them with a group, and then take it proctored yourself. Also, he wrote the textbook, which was a great resource.

Professor Kishore loves the topic he teaches, but personally, I had trouble following his lectures. He handwrites on the slides before class and nothing really feels organized because of that. It's just hard to take your own notes with how much information he puts on the slides. The textbook is a life saver though; test problems are very similar

The comments about clicker trolling are accurate. After the first lecture or so, it's nigh on impossible to understand the lectures. The saving grace is the book which is more coherent. Piazza is so inactive, which is unfortunate for a difficult class like this. Most projects are in C which sucks. He was accommodating on many things, which was good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kishore's lectures were always full of interaction with the students (although a lot of us were too shy to participate lol) which made online learning much more engaging. He was very accommodating when it came to exams during COVID and was willing to listen and act on student feedback all the time.

Projects are kinda bad and very difficult but overall amazing professor with great knowledge. He was very accommodating about the tests during covid and gave us all the exam questions the weekend before the exam and let us attempt it with honorlock after we discussed the answers with our friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr Kishore was probably the most accommodating professor that I've had during the pandemic. He understood the struggles that students were going through and made a noticeable effort to make the class more engaging. 2200 is not an easy class by any means, but if I had to take it again, I wouldnt want it to be with any other professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kishore is very clearly very knowledgable of the course material, evidenced by the fact that he wrote what is in my opinion one of the better course textbooks I've used. He's always jovial and has made time for yoga breaks which is quite nice in online classes. This is by no means an easy class, but Kishore teaches quite well.

Lectures were too fast and rather hard to follow. Some of the projects were pretty tough and painful to debug, whereas the CS 2110 projects were a lot funner. Textbook readings are quite long, and practice tests are more useful for studying. Btw I don't think there are any differences in content between the free PDF version and the print textbook.

Mixed bag. A good person, IEEE Fellow, but not a great lecturer. He gives away a ton of extra points, but how is that supposed to make up for not teaching in lecture, and cracking jokes and clicker trolling instead? Also, there is a conflict of interest, as he uses his own textbook, that costs over 100 dollars, in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor. Jokes around and is jovial every day. He wrote the book, so you might as well buy it (there is a cheap knock-off version). Lots of test questions come from book examples. Lenient on project deadlines. Lots of extra credit.

Amazing professor. Had taken CS 6210 under a different professor, therefore had referred Prof Umakishore's online lecture series on Udacity. A must take course for someone who wants to be a Systems Programmer.

He is a very nice guy, and super understanding and helpful one on one. But his class is really hard and he goes through his powerpoint slides (which haven't changed since the 90s) really quickly. He doesn't understand questions in class, and always has mandatory clicker questions. TAs for this class are useless. So good luck to you.
Helpful and a great teacher
W prof. I was concerned that I wouldn't get an A by the end of the semester and I really shouldn't have mathematically, but I still did.

Dr. Utz is a very passionate professor, and I would recommend him to everyone. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He does have pop quizzes based on the books; however, they are very basic, and if you have read the text, you should do well on them. He is a bit eccentric (in a good way) and very encouraging!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: While Dr. Utz can be a bit of a handful sometimes, if you can meet him at his level, he is an incredibly intelligent, witty, and kind professor. He is a bit eccentric (which I like) but knows what he's talking about. He clearly cares about student success in and out of the classroom. Worth taking in my opinion, but not for everyone.

Holy respect on this guy. He used to be Dean of Ivan Allen and is now the assistant dean, so he has a ton of knowledge about LMC. This class is an intro to LMC class, so we get a taste of the faculty under LMC. He's lenient when it comes to grading as long as you follow ALL his instructions. Very engaging with the class, also has fun stories

This professor is the one that inspired me to get into academia. While he's introducing you to LMC he will also make room for the class to talk about a plethora of other topics you don't realize relate to the major but have interest in. Such a great and wise guy. The work in the class just requires you to be an active participant.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! He's such an easy grader. Wants everyone to succeed and is always available outside of class. You'll have an assignment due about once a month. Two solo and one group presentation. No homework, test, or quizzes. Extra credit if you activity participate. Class is "mandatory" but wont dock your grade if you don't show up.

Would make you present most projects in front of the whole class and would nitpick every detail publicly. Did make time with each student outside of class to discuss their goals in the major and gave advice. Involved a lot of lecturing and discussion.

(Taking during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) I loved this course. Dr. Utz is an amazing professor, and while this was his first time teaching this class and he taught during coronavirus, he did an amazing job. It was very literature heavy, and I wish we would have studied media and communication more, but overall, it was a great class.

Lectures are a bit slow, but he will tell you everything you need to know. Homework's are long, but well chosen and good practice. Two exams are challenging, but fair, and there are many similar practice problems available. Often extra credit problems on the exams. Matlab computer project was interesting and doable. Final can be exempted.

Lectures are honestly not the best but his class structure allows you to easily get an A. Midterms are very similar to practice so as long as you study that you'll be fine. Final can be exempted. Extra credit questions were on the midterms. There is a final project but if you do good on the midterms you don't need to put a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ueda cares a lot about his students, and his class is easy relative to the subject matter. Most people stopped going to class, but he still takes time to send many announcements and give relevant resources. HW tends to be pretty lengthy, but the tests are very similar to resources given. If you put effort in, he will definitely notice!

His lectures are pretty dry but he is very helpful outside of class and gives a lot of partial credit. Course is 6 homeworks, 2 midterms, 1 solo project (counts as 2 homeworks), and optional final that may be curved.

He is a very nice and considerate guy. Lectures were kind of dry but he was very helpful during office hours and test review sessions. If you do all the practice test problems he provides you will get an A in the class. The last HW assignment/project was pretty tough so make sure to start early on it- seriously.

He gives exam review sessions before the exams and I loved them. These help a lot, but also going to his office hours frequently also help. Sometimes I hadn't even started on the homework assignments, but just showing up to his office hours and asking him about concepts and example problems helped. Also, start the assignments early lol they're long

Ueda is a solid choice for SysD. You have to want to learn the material for the lectures to be useful b/c they are dull, but thorough. Spent ~5hrs/hw, but the proj takes a lot of time. Exam Qs very similar to HW and past Exams. 6 HW, 2 Tests w/ crib sheets (avg scores ~= 90%),1 proj, optional final. His accent was not hard to understand at all!

He's a great lecturer. He tends to give just the basics (goes on tangents) and leave the rest to you to figure out in the homework, but his class is definitely doable. You've got 2 exams, 6 semi-intensive homeworks and a very intensive computer project. I spent many late nights working on this class; start early on everything. Great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not bad if you stay on top of the work. He had optional homeworks to prepare for the biweekly quizzes, which were easy if you studied. The two midterms were slogs. Each one was 3 hours long. Study past tests. The project isn't too bad but is very, very time consuming. Final is optional. Most of his lectures were good, but some are very unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had no trouble understanding Dr. Ueda's lectures. The class was a lot of fun! Homeworks were posted with plenty of time to complete and were usually a Matlab puzzle that could be assembled by reviewing examples that were posted or covered in class. Organization of course material was perfect. Weekly time required to complete was reasonable.

Took this class online due to covid, and he gave us 3 hour long midterms. Quizzes were straightforward but the tests had material he never mentioned during lecture. Very fair grader, and a lighter work load but you'll have to work to get and A or B. Everything is asynchronous but the videos are just low quality old lectures.

The class is good, but you're gonna have to learn yourself, because Prof Ueda lacks one crucial thing: a command of the english language. It's hard to learn complex mechanics when it takes him 3 minutes to form a complete sentence. He is a kind person, though. Homeworks are helpful and help teach the subject

Dr. Ueda is a good choice for system dynamics. He knows the material well and teaches it well. It can sometimes be tough to understand him, but his slides are pretty easy to understand. Grades are based upon midterms, homework, a project, and an optional final. The class is also pretty MATLAB heavy. He also provides old exams to study from.

Pretty dull lecturer. Ended up teaching myself most of the material and was alright for the tests and projects. Tests aren't hard if you look at the practice tests he posts. Homeworks are also not too bad. Make sure you learn how to use MATLAB for the course material.
The guy has a communication problem: the english language. The course material is good though and you learn/master the fundementals of robotics.
Good Professor, many exams but learnt a lot at the end of the course.

He is a great professor, young and friendly. Never shows arrogance nor does torment you with abstract math. Although I sometimes couldn't understand his lectures due to his accent I go back and watched lectures again, which made so much sense. Prepares you well for the quizzes and exams. Expect 4 quizzes, a midterm and a final that aren't too hard.

Lecture is terribly boring, but  he teaches you everything that you need to know. Do the homeworks, study the notes and practice tests if they are available and you will do fine. Tests are very reasonable and the averages are usually in the low 80s or 70s. Easy prof, easy class, but pretty boring.

Two tests made up 72% of the grade, and the final could replace one. She frequently cancelled class for various legitimate reasons. Her online replacement classes made it a chore to learn the relatively easy textbook material needed for the exams. She clearly cares and tries to engage, but the 75-minute classes felt very long.

There is no room for making mistakes in this class. After missing an assignment deadline, I was asked to see her and was completely humiliated during the meeting. The teaching style is disorganized and not engaging at all. She is completely inconsiderate of other people's time and personal circumstances.

Professor UNR is very kind and cares for her students. It is easy to do well in her class as her grading scheme is helpful. The in-class assignments are randomly spread but are quite easy, as are quizzes and tests. Reading the definition sections of the textbook was enough for exams as they are basic applications of concepts.

She's incredibly sweet and caring for her students and you can tell she has a passion for economics. Tests reflected content learned in class, and there was very little homework. Also, there were a lot of opportunities to increase your grade, which is a huge bonus. Overall a great teacher and person too.

Prof.Nair was one of the best professors I've ever had. Great lectures. She is the most caring (genuinely asks about mental health, open to discuss it too). She did her best to give everyone in our class an A (extra credit, optional tests to replace bad grades...). She also knows the answer to ANYTHING you could ask. Love her.

Long boring lectures, so a 75 minute lecture felt like 5 hours. Was late to every single class by 10 mins. Three tests, (one dropped), last two were one week apart which was awful.The homeworks were not planned well. Claims to be approachable but when I emailed + went to office hours it just seemed like she wanted to be done as quick as possible.

One of the most approachable and caring professors I've ever had. If you ask her questions during or outside of lecture she will find a way to explain things that enhances your understanding. She often goes on tangents during her lectures, but they are almost always there intentionally to enhance your understanding of the topic at hand.
One of the most kind professors I have ever had, unfortunately she does get off topic a lot during the lectures, makes it hard to follow. First exam was hard in my opinion, found the rest to be easy.

She was a nice person but the class did not prepare me for the tests. The lectures sometimes got off track from the material. The PowerPoints and notes don't really prepare you for the exams. The exams are a huge part of your overall grade and I did not feel prepared from the lectures at all.
such a nice lady!! but the lectures nearly did me in. she is not at all an engaging teacher, and you don't need to be in class to know the material on tests.

Usha is a very sweet lady, but she really rambles on during lecture so I found lecture to be quite a drag sometimes. 4 homework assignments, 4 exams (takes 3). Topics aren't too bad, didn't study for this class too much. I'd say it's an easy A if you're looking for a free social science requirement.
The class is very easy - lots of extra credit and redos on exams. However, she is a good teacher. Basically, you can get an A and know nothing or know everything.

Sweet lady, but not the best teacher. Have four homework assignments, four test (only three count), and a few in-class assignments. Material is not too hard, but lectures are boring and makes it hard to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Nair cares about the well-being of her students and wants them to succeed, but her class is very boring. She just reads through the powerpoints that shes already posted online, and rarely gives any test-like examples. All of your practice will come from the HW. Pretty achievable A, just make Quizlet and MyEconLab your friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a very inspiring class. Exams were pretty easy (all multiple choice) but I didn't retain much.

Dr. Nair-Reichart is a good choice. She is willing to help her students. The content for the course is manageable if you read her lectures and do the homework. Tests are quite long, but they are durable.

Great professor. She does an excellent job of explaining the material. Though she has a habit of rambling on random topics, they still help you in enhancing your understanding. Super approachable and compassionate individual. Would recommend any day.

Lectures were often more confusing than helpful, but the material and tests weren't difficult if you read the book and do the homework. Attendance is mandatory because she claims to focus on class participation. Very kind and caring person, but not a great teacher. No final exam, and the lowest test of four got dropped. Overall not a high workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Her lecture slides are posted so you don't HAVE to go to class, but she does a really good job at embellishing on the material and providing examples so it's worth your time to go anyway. Exams were tricky at times but fair, just read carefully, know your vocab, and do the practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very compassionate person, but not a great professor. All slides are posted online and she reads directly off the slides during lectures, so no point in coming to class. NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS! Exams are nothing like the lectures, homework or practice questions. Don't expect an easy A (even though it's econ).
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a great professor who cares about her students grades, and well-being, while it being an online class. She did go MIA for about a month or two which led to many students paniking, but she gave us all extra credit to make up for it and the class itself (Macro) was very interesting, and enjoyable which made it not too difficult.
A great and caring professor. Responds quickly and has options for extra credit, and is always easy to work with. She has a groupme where she interacts with students and answers any questions.

Dr.U is amazing. She is such a caring and kind professor, even to students she has never met face-to-face. You have so many opportunities to do well in this class. The canvas is super well structured, instructions for assignments are very clear, and overall it is a well-organised class. Do well on HW and practice tests, and you'll ace the exams.

dr u is really understanding and very responsive. everything is online and super easy to just search up all the homeworks on quizlet/chegg. exams are the exact same as homework questions and practice exams, with a few new questions. definitely recommend!
EASIEST CLASS EVER. Everything is online, exams are online Honorlock, 5 of them. The rest is homework and other discussion stuff. It is a fully async class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. U is awesome and very easy to communicate with! She's very responsive in the GroupMe and also cares about each of her students. Also, made sure to update grades very frequently. Not difficult if you take the time to review past homeworks and quizzes.
Prof was caring, easy to reach and made the class simple and easy to stay on top of.  5 midterms but one could be dropped. 15% participation, 25% homework, 60% midterms.

Easy A, but you have to actively check Canvas for any changes because the dates change a lot. I also felt that she was not as easy to talk to as she made herself seem, since she hardly ever replied to texts. She was in our GroupMe and there were about 5 questions per day, but she chose one day like 2 days before the exam to reply to them all.
it was pretty chill but they don't really do much to relieve the stress. you have to really understand the CP, HW and PT so the rest is chill but it was really stressful in the beginning.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Communication started great then completely fell off. There were a lot of assignments, but it's doable, and everything but HW is completed. Midterms used honor lock and the questions were all from the module's assignment. The last module and final are completely optional if you did well on the other parts. Honestly an easy A
Took this class online and the tests were difficult but the exact same content as practice exams and homework so keep that in mind!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tons of homework, but it's mostly easy busy work. Just study CP, HW, and PT questions, and you're guaranteed at least an 85 on every exam. Last entire fifth module and final exam are optional, and there is extra credit available. Dr. U is a really friendly, down-to-earth professor too.
Awful. Doesnt really teach in the online videos. HWs are vague and take a lot of time. Felt like stats class. Didnt really learn much, had to self study from the textbook gto figure out the HWs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of homework but she is a great person and is always super responsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class, granted you take it online, is so easy you have to try to fail. The test questions are word for word from the homework, practice test, and class participation quizzes. Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Her organization was GREAT and HELPFUL! For this semester, 80% of the tests were based off of quizzes and homework we had beforehand. Straight-foward class with a professor who loves her job! Very lenient with deadlines and workload.

Dr. U is super caring. She really wants you to be interested in econ, and yes while there are a lot of assignments, it is not hard to receive an A or a high B in the course if you're on top of things. My class was asynch, and she really tried to make it engaging, which is difficult when asynch. Overall a lot of easy busy work. Tests aren't bad.

She was really great professor. 20 of the 25 questions on each test were on the practice tests and homework. If you do good on all the assignment and tests up to test 4, you can skip out on the last unit and the final. That was a true gem within itself! Her videos were quite interesting and fun. She makes it easy to get an A and succeed too!

Super chill! Her morning office hours are called "Online Cuppa with Dr. U", 20/25 questions on each test come straight from prac. tests/hw, and if you do every assignment thru test 4 with a satisfactory grade, you can skip all of unit 5 and the final. Learning macroeconomics for the first time, she made it manageable and textbook is informational

Professor U is an amazing professor. Her lectures can get a bit long but if you watch them fully even at double speed she never tests anything extra. Also always do at least some of the practice test, and take advantage of the the fact that you may not have to take the 5th test or the final if your average is high enough.

The class was extremely easy, and the professor is very sweet and accessible outside of class to ask any questions you may have on what was being learned this week. I took the class asynchronously and it was not too hard to add to my schedule and it was not a stressful course at all.

She is very passionate about her topic. Although it was an asynchronous class, she is very accessible at any times. She also puts an great emphasis on mental health and always pushing for students to advocate for their mental health. If you do your homework, do the practice tests, you should be fine on the exam.

Really great prof and class. It's an easy class but it did help me understand more about what global economic numbers actually mean which was my takeaway. Class being online is a good way to do HUM/SS classes, especially for older students who are taking intensive major classes. There was never a hard-to-reach deadline and I still learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. U is respectful, hilarious, and so understanding. She gives so much extra credit, and the midterms are almost identical to the practice tests. As long as you study those and do her (easy) discussion ex. credit/participation, you will get an A no problem. She also drops a midterm and exempts from the final. I recommend her to literally everyone

Dr. U is solid. She wasn't the best lecturer that I've had, but she cares for her students and makes it clear what is required in the class in order to succeed. She does give a good amount of homework though, and some of it might seem like busy work, but it's all fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. U is an okay professor. She is very understanding and tries her best to help the students. Unfortunately, her lectures aren't the best, and they can be quite boring. Also, the lectures alone won't be enough, don't expect an easy A without going out of your way. I'd say she is a solid last option.

Dr. U is a good caring professor, I think being online made things difficult for her but also she was very very adaptable for our class. After students complained she changed her tests to be way longer and easier and dropped more of our grades. She also gives extra credit. Her lectures alone won't get you an A but it's not too much work either way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I don't understand everyone other review, this woman is not good. she reads directly off of the slides, talks way too fast to let you take actual notes, and expects you to understand things in a very complex way, without giving any kind of explanation related to a complex understanding. don't take her, the class sucks and so does she

Dr. U wasn't the best lecturer, but she was very receptive to the needs of her students. If you make the efforts to communicate to her what you think you needed to succeed in the course, she would try and accommodate them to the best of her ability. Overall, she was a solid introductory econ class professor.

Asynchronous and very time-consuming (long lectures & lots of homework). But she is SO passionate and enthusiastic about what she's teaching. You might flounder on your own (not easy material & there's a lot of it), but if you go to her, she will help you tremendously. She wants you to learn. Also, EC, participation grades, and optional final exam.

Dr. Urmanbetova does a great job teaching this course and is very determined to help every student succeed. The class is not too hard but does have quite a bit of work compared to other courses. Overall, if you put in the work, you'll do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. U's class was more work than I expected, however, she was so kind and passionate about macroeconomics. I would definitely take the class again, it was easy work, yet time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a really sweet professor but I could not make a good grade on her tests to save my life. I watched all the lectures, took notes, did all of the homework, even read the textbook. Still could not make above a 70 on anything. I do not recommend her.
Amazing professor!

This class was asynchronous so this review might be a little biased, but the class was fine. Dr. U is a great lecturer and explains the economics concepts quite well, however, the class is a lot of work, and some of the async lectures are quite long and there are multiple to do in a day. It's a somewhat easy class, but a LOT of work.

Not a very good lecturer, just reads off of the slides. There is so much work assigned and almost all is busy work, especially for an asynchronous course. She was the only professor teaching this class and it was required. I wish I would have waited for another professor in another semester but what's done is done. Changes syllabus during semester
Dr. U is a great professor, she is very caring and enthusiastic. This course has LOTS of assignments and extra credit opportunities. Easy A.

Professor Aselia will give you tons of homework, activities, and assignments outside classes. Her lectures are recorded and sometimes hard to understand, however, she will teach you Macroeconomics like no one. If you are willing to understand the subject, she may be the best fit for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is decent at best. Classes are all lectures and she is not the best at actually teaching you the material. Reads straight from slides and had to teach myself most of the material. There were 5 tests and lots of small quizzes. Not too much homework. You can get by with her as a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She reads over the lecture slides super fast. I didn't learn much from her lectures, but I attended them because attendance counts towards grade. Read her power point slides (and the free online textbook at times) to succeed in this class. She gave a lot of activities that I thought were unnecessary. I personally wouldn't take her again.

Makes getting an A super easy. Lots of extra credit plus the lowest of each thing hw test etc is dropped. Optional final. I will say there are alot of components to this class so at the beginning it feels really overwhelming but it is so easy. Have to answer questions during class as attendance.

It is not exactly an easy A because you have to work for your grade. Sometimes it felt like busywork. Lectures were not really helpful for me but you have to go for participation credit. This semester(S2020) we had 5 tests but I heard she changes the class a little every semester. The class was not too bad though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were confusing and a mess overall. She tried restructuring the class the semester I took it (Fall 2019). Did not go well for many students. Tests were extremely difficult. Somewhat understanding. Provided a second-chance policy halfway through the semester because of the restructuring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. U had to restructure her class in 2019, so it was incredibly convoluted and had a ton of unnecessary busy work and exams. She is a respectable professor and genuinely cares about students. She does include a ton of bonus points so if you try you will be fine. Her lectures are very fast, so you have to work a lot on your own to learn content.

Super convoluted teaching style. Had to juggle 8 things at once constantly. I have no clue what the other ratings are saying about her. She talks way too fast during lecture, and the slides are so dense. If you're stuck with her, just do other homework in class and study later.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. U is one of the best people I have met on campus. She is very approachable outside class and makes you love macroeconomics. The negative aspect is that her slides are content heavy and sometimes she races through them. That also means, if you do not go to class, you are likely to feel left behind. The work assigned in the class is a lot as well
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. U was awesome! A little hard to understand sometimes, but she really made sure we knew the key points by going over them multiple times. Her office hours were short and hard to get, but totally worth it. She is so nice and cares a lot about all of her students!
Excited about the subject, works to make sure that students succeed. You'd have to work to fail the class.

Dr. U is extremely fair and clear about her expectations. If you read the textbook (which is free!), do homework, and review her lecture PowerPoints, the weekly quizzes really are not that bad. She offers a mid-semester feedback survey, and she changed some things up based on our responses. Super caring professor, absolutely would take her again.
Take her class, she's awesome

I really liked her, she seemed to care about her students, and the class is pretty straightforward. All her homework is online and you can look up answers on Google on Quizlet. You can also exempt the final and there are no tests! Only quizzes. It is pretty easy to make a B and if you put in the work, you can definitely make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course content is very straight forward and well explained. There are weekly quizzes, no midterms, and an optional final. She quizzes directly from her powerpoints and the hw.

I liked how you could exempt the final for this class, but not much else. However, she covers a ridiculous amount of the textbook, but thankfully, the textbook is free. For my semester, she covered 21 chapters of the book. She teaches so fast covering 2-3 chapters a week. If you want to take her, you will probably have to read the book to get an A

She cares about her students and listens to feedback. Her grading is really nice: one quiz every week. The average  85% of your grade, HW average  7.5%, participation  7.5%. If you don't like your quiz average, you can choose to take the final instead. I think maybe 3 students in my class did that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class is very manageable if you go to class and keep up with the work. There are no midterms, just weekly quizzes, and you don't have to take the final. She also offers weekly review sessions for the quizzes which help a lot. Dr. Urmanbetova cares a lot about her student for example we all failed one quiz and she let us drop an extra quiz.

You can tell Dr. Urmanbetova really cares about the quality of teaching, and she tends to bring in a lot of non-textbook examples as well. Class is primarily based on weekly quizzes (85% of grade) with final exam exempt unless you need it. Very manageable class and Dr. Urmanbetova sometimes even adjusts class structure based on feedback.

Her class is structured for her students to succeed. She gives a quiz every week on the material covered during the week, which sounds awful, but actually allows you to study in increments and you learn the material a lot better. There are 14 quizzes and 0 tests, so if you mess up badly on one quiz, its not a big deal. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Urmanbetova is pretty new to teaching and still figuring some things out but she really cares about improving her students' experience in her class and adapting to help students succeed. Quizzes every Friday worth 75% of the grade are tough but doable if you do the homework and read the book. Super nice and caring, would take again.
I really didn't learn much, but it was easy I guess.

I had Dr. U as part of the Oxford Study Abroad Program, and he was great! Most of our classes were group presentations to make it more interesting than him just lecturing to us for 2 hours. Each group had 2 presentations, and they made up a big part of our grade. He tells you exactly what to expect on the tests and makes sure you're prepared.

Doc rules! He is the funniest, most understanding, most caring choir director I've ever had. We sing lots of music each semester (I counted 34 pieces one year), and a lot of it is weird and challenging, but it's so rewarding.

Doc will not learn your name, but that doesn't mean he cares less. Very funny, very... different. Definitely not like any other choral director I've ever had before. He's a little eccentric, but I've learned so much from him. Very good professor, even if you think he's insane sometimes. ( in a good way. Love u doc
Doc is awesome
Online singing can be a definite change. But, Jerry is very fun and he writes all the music(very skilled by the way). Easy A if you show up.
He is a great choir director. He is super funny and really cares about his students.
Dr. U is great! He makes sure to engage the class and makes the topic entertaining.
Hilarious, the best, especially when in Glee club because he acts like a college kid especially with his jokes.
Doc is great! He's really funny, and Glee was the best "class" I've ever had. Plus, you get graded on showing up and trying to sing. If you do that, you get an A.

I LOVE Dr. U!!! He changed my life. I had never sang before and was very nervous. He is just such a great person to be around, he really understands people in general and he loves them too. He is hilarious and the class is just a good time.

Best guy in the world!! I had never sang before, but he is so motivating! I came to this class just to have fun, Dr. U cracks jokes the whole time. He encourages an awesome sense of community. Basically, practices are twice a week and then a final performance..if you go you get an A. this teacher is one of the most loving persons I have ever met
Doc. U is an awesome instructor.    A++++++ Instructor.  Coolest dude alive.
Dr. U is the best!
I love you
Uelzmann was very invested in the content he taught! He got to know his students personally and gave individualized feedback!

I loved him and enjoyed the class. He's very nice and clearly very knowledgable and passionate about the topic. Class wasn't super difficult, just a decent amount of reading/listening. There's a few papers and a project among other things, but it's not super time-consuming.

Uelzmann is fantastic. He's really passionate about post war literature and lectures were so engaging. He does tend to get really enthusiastic, which often leads to him speaking moderately quickly in German, just be aware of that. The whole class is taught in German, but he's super nice about explaining words you might not know. Highly recommend!

German 1002 online via VHL Central pass/fail: It was an easy free elective class (if you are taking it pass fail). I did the minimum work possible to pass. VHL is nice but kinda frustrating when you miss something like a capital letter and it docks you points. Overall laid back learning environment and easy P/F class.

Absolutely wonderful man. Clearly loves teaching and is very engaging. Loves his wife and kids, and 90s German music. Has great sense of fashion, sporting tasteful Pink Floyd and black shirts, not to mention V-necks. Classy dude all in all.

Very caring and inspiring professor

An icon.
