reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good teacher and good lectures.  Book wasn't really necessary for anything, except a couple vocab words.  Memorize the class notes and vocal terms cause that is the majority of the tests.  Also you need to know any calculation she puts on the board!

Dr. Milam is a very good lecturer and clarifies difficult concepts well. She is also a  busy lady, so it was sometimes hard to meet with her in office hours. Just make sure you understand everything very well before  each lecture bc she gives pop quizzes. There's alot of stuff to know for this class, so just stay on top of it and you'll be fine.

Milam isn't really available for consultation out of class (multiple people in class haven't gotten their tests back and today was the day of the final). She also doesn't give partial credit for minor spelling issues and will probably give you 24 on the definition of MSE even if you're in the major specific section. Take Qin instead.

Dr. Milam understands her subject very well, but she does not come across as enthusiastic in her lectures. The class was very boring, which I was very disappointed by as I truly enjoy the subject. She does not post grades nor does she post answer keys to past quizzes or tests, making it hard to study if you have lost any of them.

Yeah, okay, maybe she was a good lecturer, but that's the only thing she's got going for her. She had ONE office hour per week, and BOTH times I went(one time I contacted her beforehand) she was not there for it. She doesn't put ANY grades online, so good luck figuring out how you're doing in the class. She's also not very nice.
Never posted anything on t-square.  Made it difficult to know what grades were, but outside of that great teacher.

She's very helpful and easy to understand. Gives great notes. You have to go to class, because she gives pop quizzes. The tests aren't bad if you go to class, read what she asks you to read, and study.
Easy teacher, all you have to do is listen in class. The material is a review of high school chemistry with some additions.

She is easy to understand,helpful after class,and easy to communicate with.  However, her tests are hard, class attendence is a must because she gives test material and pop quizzes.  Dont take her unless you have to.
really good teacher.

Pretty good professor overall. The class was easy, however he kept forgetting people's names even by the last day of class and gave interesting feedback that was not necessarily helpful on assignments. Either way, he was very chill and was a funny guy. Easy class for those that have to take it.

Lectures were really enjoyable especially for a 1 credit class. Great sense of humor, assignments were fine besides the poster and learning portfolio at the end of the semester. Otherwise a very straightforward class.

He closes the clicker questions WAY too fast (basically encouraging student to use ai for quick answer), and he makes fairly simple concepts sound complicated(by shifting off to some theoretical stories). He also lacks enthusiasm in the content of these simple chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The main benefit to this class is the grade replacement from the final. Wilkinson teaches in an annoying manner, glossing over some key concepts with his popular saying of "you should have already learned this previously." The exams are pretty difficult, and he leaves no time on the iClicker. Overall though, if you put in the work you'll be fine.
Illegible handwriting, like actually. Often lectured about overly detailed things that were irrelevant to exam content. Dr. Evans >>>>, it was nice when he came in to sub a handful of times.

Lectures aren't that helpful because he spends a lot of time off topic or talking about applications of chemicals and things we don't need to know. The class has graded in-class questions and he gives very little time to do them before closing them. Chill guy I guess but maybe more suited for upper level classes.

he's fine, his grading can be randomly kind of tough but nothing crazy. the final assignment for this course is annoyingly time consuming and pointless but everything else was fine. chill dude. cool accent.
A simple course with simple assignments not graded too hard. A checkbox kinda course.

Required for chem major. He did not seem to care. Often took months to get grades back. Teaches on subjects he does not know enough about. You can learn more about these tools from a 10 minute YouTube than this 50 minute class. Guest lectures were actually helpful. Big poster and paper due at the end that he will take points off without feedback.

Dr. Wilkinson is a great professor! He really cares about the course and all his students. I found his lectures to be interesting and worthwhile, plus he is super helpful and wants his students to succeed. Would definitely recommend him for CHEM 3111 or any other course.
CHEM1212K is difficult, but not impossible. Make sure to attend lectures, lab, and do the homework and textbook reading. Exams are difficult but you can make up for bad grades later on.

Prof Wilkinson was a very good professor. If you paid attention in the lectures and did the homework, you did well in the exam. You definitely need to study, it's not an easy course, but he made the classes enjoyable. He also offered a lot of opportunities to improve your grade, such as the grade replacement policy.
A kind soul with a handsome British accent. He was sometimes a little blunt but he made the class super easy. A charming fella. PRO TIP: call him Angus Beef and he will chuckle!

Dr. Wilkinson is an excellent professor, especially if Chemistry is a novel topic to you. He is always willing to answer all questions or re-explain past concepts. His use of post-lecture quizzes allows for students to easily avoid falling behind on the subject. His exams are fair and the best way to study is to understand problem sets thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He gave a ton of room for error so missing a homework assignment (or several) was never a big deal. Tests are very fair and won't try to trick you. He is also very knowledgeable about chemistry and the impact it has on the world. He relates everything you learn to the real world and tells you exactly why it matters.

Dr. Wilkinson makes it clear that he cares about the success of his students. He's very personable & approachable, and is always happy to entertain questions during lecture. While sometimes he can get off on tangents or move a bit slow, his lectures are enjoyable. He knows the material, and his tests are 1000% fair. He's a really great professor!

Pretty nice. Each week (or two weeks) there is a chemical skill for students to learn (sometimes with different professors), so you will gain a lot. There are assignments associated with each week's skill, and a poster & a portfolio at the end of the semester, but as long as you follow instructions and turn them in on time, it's an easy A.

He's a nice dude but my semester he was gone a lot & the lady teacher pretty much took over. She made the tests and he didn't seem to know exactly what would be on them. Good guy though and I would definately take him over Schermeier- but maybe go to her class the day before tests bc she always would give them more info about what would be on tests
He's a cool dude. Pay attention and put in some work you'll be fine. He's really friendly  but never opens his eyes
He is very good at explaining chemistry concepts, but gets a little bit off topic sometimes. If you enjoy chemistry,  he is a great professor for it.

His lectures are very interesting if you are into chemistry, as he extrapolates and talks to other related things in the field every now and then. However, he doesn't spend much time on basic examples/concepts, so unless you're pretty decent at Chemistry/did AP,  you'll find him a bit hard. Very kind person though.

Maybe the best professor I have had here at Georgia Tech. My favorite part of his class was after taking a survey about his class, he took our feedback and decided to not listen to any of it. I love this teacher and he is definitely head and shoulders above the other teacher.

Love his British accent, it's awesome. He's an alright guy and lecturer, but he tends to be a bit tangential. He also did not have many office hours, and all the ones he had were during hours that I had class. Pretty average professor, would recommend Shepler more.

The lectures were good, though he tended to go off topic at times. If you can, try to get Shepler for this class; both Wilkinson and Shepler are good professors, but Shepler explained certain topics much better.

I liked Dr. Wilkinson.  He has a funny British accent that makes some of the chemistry language used interesting.  He initially explains topics well, but I think he is sometimes too smart for himself and gets caught up in his own ideas when he has to explain things in more detail.  He is still very nice and the lectures are usually helpful.

Dr. Wilkinson is great! He clearly knows chemistry very well and endeavors to answer students' questions. Answers can get confusing, so I recommend Piazza or e-mails for straightforward answers. Overall, he's a good professor that really does care. His lectures can be on the dry side, but he covers the necessary material.

He closes his eyes while lecturing and does not lecture very clearly. He seems like a nice professor; he just cannot communicate well with his students during lecture. He is very knowledgeable, but it's difficult to understand. Exams are 20 multiple choice questions. Overall, he's a decent professor.
He speaks to a higher level that someone who has never taken college chemistry before will struggle with.... alot...

Very nice professor. He knows what he is talking about, but can't really explain the material on a level students can understand. Reading the textbook and doing lots of practice problems will help in the class. Overall he is an ok chem 1211 professor.
The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests. Lectures kinda boring but powerpoint slides were helpful. Overall, pretty easy and nice professor.

If you pay attention in class and study the past exams, this class should be a breeze. If not, it's not the professor, it's that you probably should not major in anything related to chemistry... Good but somewhat boring lecturer. Never needed help, so not sure how he is in person.

This professor knew his material, but the tests were completely unfair. He used only multiple choice tests that included some of the most random bits of information. There was no room for error, even if you had a good argument. Free response questions would have been helpful. This was my first upsetting grade ever!

Pretty nice, always willing to help during office hours. His lectures are a little boring, but oh well. Tests are exactly like the practice tests--so moderate studying should give you a pretty quick A.
Horrible, horrible teacher. Very condescending. I ended up with an 79.3 after the final and he refused to bump me up even though I always went to his office hours and never missed a lecture.
He is always willing to help. You can always stop by office hours or ask him questions after class. His lecture slides help study for the course and the practice exams are a good guide for the exams.

Extremely nice professor, very helpful. Lectures are pretty boring, but if you can manage to stay focused, you'll learn a lot. Also, holds review sessions for each test, which are excellent, he really takes the time to explain everything asked. Hard tests, but I'd definitely recommend him, especially if you actually have an interest in the class.

Dr. Wilkinson is a very through lecturer, if a bit boring.  He has his moments where he captured the class during demos and slips of the tounge, but for the most part it was difficult to stay awake at 9am.  Very hard tests, harsh grader.
Very enthusiastic can good at explaining complex topics
Excellent Prof, had a bad prof but watched his lectures and got an A. Highly recommend!

Grading: 3 Midterms + 1 Final (worst midterm 15%, all others & final 20%). "Bucket point" system for the other 25% (need 70pts/120 for full credit)

Lecture: 9/10; Passion: 9/10; Communication: 10/10; Flexibility: 9/10; Test Prep: 10/10

Quirks: Bad handwriting, likes teaching 8:25 a.m. MWF

Recommendation: Would be my first choice for this course.

W professor. The class is pretty hard but if you lock in you can definitely get a good grade. I would also recommend reading through the course textbook Lay Linear Algebra since it follows the course really closely and goes into more details than the lectures have time for, and you lowkey need that for the true and false sections on the tests.

Professor Warnock was great at making Linear clear and understandable. His lectures prepared me a lot for the FRQ questions and going to office hours helped clear up a lot of my confusion over true/false questions. Make sure to do the homework and practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Example of an amazing professor. I cant say much that hasn't already be said. Just make sure you attend every lecture, especially the ones near the end of the semester.
Great lecturer and funny guy!

great professor with great lectures. explained concepts pretty clearly and has a lot of passion. i didn't pay the most attention in lectures personally, but 1554 has a canvas masterpage with recordings from old lectures and a collection of past midterm exams to practice (and more) which helped me immensely.
this man is the next Gilbert Strang.
Very chill professor. Responds to emails, very accessible and friendly

Extremely accessible outside of class. Best linear lecturer by far, took his time to clearly explain material and did not rush through the content. Provided great reviews for the tests, and clearly cares about the success of his students. If you have a different lecturer and are struggling, try to come to his instead as attendance isn't mandatory.

Cuyler is awesome! If you can get him for linear you 100% should take it with him. He takes time to really explain everything in lecture, answer everyone's questions, is easily available for office hours, and genuinely cares about the students and the subject. Plus as the course coordinator he writes the tests and sometimes would drop small hints!

Warnock is the GOAT of 1554. He's a really great lecturer and makes everything super understandable. if you go to his lecture + his office hours + studio + do the homework + do some practice tests you will get a good grade

If you get a chance to take 1554 with him, do it. He is literally a 1 of 1 Linear Algebra teacher. I cannot reiterate how simple he breaks down Linear Algebra, and tells you what you need to remember for the exams. If you don't have him, he has recordings of his past lectures, I recommend watching those lectures, he's incredible.
Good professor in general. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gives good feedback to questions. Probably the best 1554 professor.

Great professor. Linear Algebra is not the easiest course and requires studying for sure. But, hes a great professor and makes it as easy as possible to understand the material. Very accessible and personable. Definitely take if you can! Only problem, you do have to do fairly well in the class to get an A. Exams are 75% of the grade, so do good.

Warnock is an amazing math professor who is really passionate about the subject he teaches. Math 1554 is a tough math class especially for incoming freshman, but Warnock is able to put complex ideas into simple terms that make digesting the material easy. He is easily accessible outside of class through office hours and is extremely active on Piaza

Great professor, probably would've done better if I attended more lectures. He's passionate and very, very nice if you go to office hours, answering almost any question. A little bit of theory in this course, but I would say fair.

Cuyler is the GOAT for 1554. His enthusiasm for linear algebra is genuinely contagious, office hours are great. Lectures are packed with many proofs and examples, which make it easy to build a great understanding for the subject. Very caring and listens to students. You'll end up appreciating the math.

Easily the most passionate math professor I've had at GT. Cuyler's lectures are amazing, and he's a really friendly and approachable guy. Honestly even if you end up in another prof's section, just attend Cuyler's lectures, they're that good.

And stop by his office hours! He explains even better there :)
He is really good lecturer and gives great examples if you attend lecture and follow along you should be fine!

Great professor. I have him for 8 am and he is so enthusiastic about linear algebra and math, it rubs off on you. He explains concepts so well in such little time he has. Everything on Canva is useful and the past exams help a lot for prospective exams.

Professor Warnock is an excellent lecturer with some of the most clear explanations I've experienced. I've heard of other students even saying they come to our lectures instead. He also projects his voice really well. Even in the back of a 200 person lecture hall with no mic, I can hear him perfectly. I recommend him to anyone who can get him.

WARNOCK MY GOAT THE GLAZE IS REAL whoever called him the Lorax is so accurate my guy knows anything and everything about math. He is so passionate about Linear it rubs off onto you and he really tries his best in lectures to explain everything in layman's terms. Linear is hard but he makes it doable/even easy. I will miss him and his teaching sm :(

I think it's only his second semester teaching linear at GT and his first over the summer, but he did a fantastic job. Very engaging in lecture, very good at explaining concepts and finding good examples for them, knew how to pace the class well, and was very active on Piazza.
WARNOCK THE GOAT

Prof. Warnock is a nice guy who wants you to succeed. He does a great job explaining material and records lectures / posts the notes for you to review later. The class is hard as hell, but he made it passable. IMO the professor for the course doesn't matter as much as your self-willingness to study the past tests, practice, and be attentive does.

Man this guy is like the Lorax for linear algebra. Wonderful at breaking down concepts and so passionate. Struggled very much early on but brought up my grade with Dr. Warnock's help in office hours. Generous with the MQE. Test are very hard but truly mimic the practice tests. Just a hard class in general but he will be a great course coordinator.

A great prof and a great guy. His lectures are amazing (he sometimes got behind homework pacing, but go to studio and you'll learn it) and it's very obvious that he not only knows a lot about the topics, but he is genuinely interested in them too. Gives great explanations, ample office hours, and responds to emails quickly. Take him if you can.

One of the nicest professors I've met here at Tech. Super friendly and accommodating no matter your skill level, and gives really good explanations, especially at office hours! He's also very good for people that like theory - The way he talks about proofs makes me laugh every time because you can just tell he loves the subject matter so much LOL

I would highly recommend going to Dr.Warnock for linear algebra lectures even if you're not in his section. He not only explains every topic thoroughly and simply, but also is knowledgeable enough to show you full derivations and proofs on the spot. If you're confused about anything attend his office hours as this course is fast paced.

I loved the lectures and the prof, however the content in class is substantially easier than the exams. These exams were extremely difficult compared to what we were taught during the class. I think it's just calc 1 in general here is so hard. My advice is to lock in and STUDY the hell out of the concepts.

He explained concepts really well, and was very attentive to any questions asked in lectures. Also, aside from going through the theory and rules, etc., he excelled at showing how the theory applied practically, which may really help students who have a hard time remembering all the rules for the various concepts. Lectures were also recorded.

I think it was his first time teaching at Tech, and honestly, he did a pretty good job compared to the other lecturers for 1551 that same semester. He was very straight forward and good at explaining and would always pause for questions. He would also slow down if he felt that a concept wasn't explained well enough. Overall, pretty good.

Genuinely the best professor ever. He tells you what to do to succeed, and although it is a decent amount of work, it's not as bad as everyone says. Daily quizzes are annoying, but they force you to be caught up on content. Lots of extra credit opportunities which is super helpful.

he has good things and bad things about him. he does like to intimidate and show off how smart and powerful he is. also during the class he's always going off-topic and making jokes, so i learn maybe half the material in class. this guy is just doin too much.

on the other hand, i think he means well and is a pretty funny guy

The kind of prof they make movies about. Hilarious, engaging, AMAZING lectures. Yes tests are hard, but very very fair, if you put in the work an A is very achievable. Got a B because of daily quizzes- the one awful part of the class. Do NOT miss a single class. He really cares for students and teaches you what ISyE is all about.

Amazing person and teacher. Lectures are quite clear and explanations are great! Quite a hilarious teacher too. However, any absences or getting caught off guard punish your grade a lot since there are quizzes every class. Exams are also quite hard.

most difficult prof ever he makes fun of students but disguises it as "tough love" he thinks his class should be our top priority and humiliates students for not understanding concepts. if hes so committed to us learning the content why doesnt he teach it? he wastes everyones time by spending class time having side convos w his select fav students
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Having Damon as a professor my freshman year of college changed my life. Easily the best professor I have ever had at GT, made me passionate about industrial engineering and taught me that hard work will pay off. The course is pretty tough but if you follow his steps for success and put in work outside the classroom, you will do great.

Damon is quite a character, as you can see from the other ratings he is very polarizing. I thought he was great and funny but I see why some people don't like his personality. Anna the TA is great though. Daily quizzes every day, 2 midterms which were fair, do all you can to not take final, I hear its impossible. Life lessons will be dispensed.

Damon is a character. An experience. He's the kind of prof you hear stories about. His class is not for complainers. He will shape you up. Yes, his class is super hard, but you will rise to the challenge. You're gonna have probability down by the end of it. He's funny and has a lot of wisdom to share as well. TAKE HIM!

Super unprofessional and never responds to any emails or texts. Final is way too difficult and includes stuff never even covered in the class. If you do not get 92+ on both tests, you are gonna get an A. Barely learned when he was teaching, but actually learned stuff with the TA. Content is easy overall, just do not do bad on a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I do agree that some of the lectures aren't very efficient. However, Damon is a solid lecturer and the HWs provided were clutch. Going through those problems are what determine what grade you are going to deserve(Not Graded). The first two exams aren't as bad as you expect but I have done anything to have exempted the final. Anna was great too.

Damon spends basically the entire class making fun of some random kids instead of teaching the lecture. He also has no office hours and doesn't respond to emails or texts. The TA is much better. Tests are relatively simple but if you aren't able to exempt the final, you are basically guaranteed a B since the final is impossible.

Never actually learned much during class, but went for the daily quiz. Damon yaps about life, goes through a couple of pages of the notes, and tells you to learn the meat of the content by yourself. Anna, the TA, was much better at giving lectures and is incredibly helpful. The final exam is hopeless, so forget about exam replacement.

Damon is a great professor. He tells you on the first day of class what he expects from his students and how to make an A (a ton of work). Exams take the content learned in class and make you go a step further which I definitely struggled with. Overall, if you want to learn probability and how to be a better person/student, take Damon 100%.

Very difficult course, Damon is nice, but I did not love going to class every day, he is a very reasonable person though. You definitely earn the grade you get in this class. Attendance is mandatory because there are quizzes at the beginning of each class. Anna the TA is amazing though, she gives a lot of credit for the quizzes.

Daily quizzes to start the class were sometimes unfair. Spent too much time of lecture with banter. Requires LOTS of work outside of class. Kept me awake at 8 AM. Gave good life advice and good teacher if you want to spend time learning on your own and making a friend in class.

Very hilarious and engaging, knowledgeable guy. Grading was harder in the second half of the sem since people were doing well in the first half. Verbal quizzes every class were stressful, questions sometimes out of notes, sometimes randomly hard. Exams mostly fair, but the review that said they got a 98 and 99 is definitely not a norm for the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kept everybody super engaged even for an 8am. He is a tad scary and not afraid to pick on you in the name of being funny. The hardest part of the class was having a quiz every single day. The tests were VERY fair (I got a 98 and a 99 and exempt from the final with minimal effort). All homework is optional but it does help you succeed.

Damon is an amazing professor! He's entertaining and teaches the material in a way that's easy to understand. The material isn't that bad but the class is a lottt of work. Quizzes every single class but questions are taken straight off the notes or homework. Exams are similar to the homework problems too.

Amazing professor. He keeps the students engaged for a 75-minute lecture and shows how it's applicable in day-to-day life. While the test questions are harder than the example ones in class, they're not harder than the optional homework, so use that to study. Definitely take this professor if possible.

THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD IN GEORGIA TECH!!! EXAMS ARE HARD BUT YOU JUST HAVE TO PERFORM! HE IS NOT ONLY GREAT AT TEACHING HE IS ALSO GREAT AT GIVING ADVICE AND LIFE LESSONS. 
HE IS THE BEST!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There's an easy quiz every morning over the last class's topic and random extra credit. If you've had any subject on logic/sets this class is a joke with him. Tests are a random spike harder than the questions in class, but not impossible, go through past exams before the test and you'll be fine. Take this professor if you can.

Favorite professor I've had so far. Made the 8am bearable, engaged with the class, made us laugh regularly. Communication outside of class is limited to the TA's mostly, though. Exams were graded somewhat inconsistently. 100000x over, take Damon if you're able to. Any qualms with Damon pale in comparison to Foley etc. for ISyE 2027

Damon is one of the best teachers I have had so far at Georgia Tech. His lectures are engaging, and energetic, and he strives to get the best out of his students. However, in doing so he has a quiz almost every class, and tests/quizzes consist of 95% of the final grade. He also dosen't believe in curving grades. Overall he is an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this man. I had him over the summer of 2022 and he was the best thing to happen to me as an IE major here.

This professor is probably the least competent person I've ever had to deal with in academia. His test questions are incoherent, his grading is seemingly arbitrary, and his tests often have no relation to the material taught. Dealing with him outside is class is virtually impossible. He is rude, disrespectful, and does not care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor. He cares about his students - goes above and beyond to make everyone feel involved and motivated by having an insane amount of office hours, learning everyone's names (in a class of 60+), and by giving practical life lessons and even bringing in guest speakers to ensure we are successful both in and out of the classroom.

Damon is the best professor you will ever have. and he knows it. Holds so many office hours to go over questions, learns everyones names, and instills the confidence to make you feel like you can handle IE. Class is definitely hard but insanely rewarding. He makes you want to go to class and study and be successful. Make sure he knows who you are.

Damon is one of the most caring professors Ive ever had. He goes above and beyond in lectures, learning everyones names and keeping things engaging. Hes also given many small lessons to help as well, from getting ready for senior design to negotiating salaries for an internship. Definitely take his class if you ever have a chance!
By far the best professor I've had at Tech. He expects you to learn a lot, but the level of care he has for students is unmatched. If you work hard, he will make sure you get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the most caring and invested profs I've had. Tests are hard but do what he says to study and you'll be fine. Group project at the end of the semester to replace the final is not too bad, just make sure you start well in advance. No mandatory homework but do them to understand the material. Short quizzes a week, use this to boost your grade

Damon's lectures are pretty clear, and the homework helps a lot. However, there were 20 quizzes and 2 midterms over the summer, which is an obscene amount. Some of them are really hard. He is extremely fair though, which means if you put in enough work (much more than what is supposed for a 3 credit-hr class), it is possible for you to get an A.

Damon is definitely the best professor I've had at Tech. He gives you a short quiz every day, but they extra credit questions. If you read and pay attention, your quiz average will be over 100. His tests are very fair and lectures are very engaging. If you put in a little bit of effort every day, you will EASILY make an A.
Damon was one of my favorite professors at Tech. His class is a lot of work, but you will get out what you put in. Genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Damon is one of the BEST professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about the success of his students. He gives a clear outline on how to do well in the class and if you follow it you will get an A. But, Go to office hours!! He will sit down and work problems with you and answer questions until you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Damon was a really great professor who genuinely cares about his students. He gives "fun" quizzes which are pretty easy but you have to go to class. He gives clear guidelines and what you should be doing in order to do well in the class. Go to office hours and make him know your name. He does final grade replacement which saved a lot of people.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Truly has a passion for the topic and cares about the students. Most classes start with pop quizzes based on the previous lecture. There are two midterms, each worth 20%, very reasonable questions. Not hard to get an A as long as you don't skip class! Final group project is 25% of final grade, still very reasonable difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's fair, but tough. Very charismatic, but is very strict about grading. If you put in the effort (and I mean effort), then his class will be enjoyable. Beware of "Fun Quizzes" that account for a significant portion of your grade. If you go to class, study, and do the (optional) homework, then you will be fine. If you skip on on of these, you fail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Damon is one of the most caring professors that I have had at Tech. He makes you work for your grade, but he wants his students to do well. He holds office hours each week and is willing to answer questions and work with you. He always gives pop quizzes, but if you attend class and do what he says they aren't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Tech. Very understanding and caring. He definitely makes you work for your grade, but its not hard to make a good grade in the class. Hes really intense at times, so if you like to keep quiet and not participate, you should probably take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. I took him as an 8 am for the summer, and I never fell asleep in his class. However, he is a great and funny guy and incorporates that in his lectures. quizzes.

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. His test questions are weighted so that you will make a C if you miss the hardest question. His final is also weighted to be almost 70% of your grade. There are much better and more fair professors.

reviews.comment: Took him over the summer. Daily quizzes count for 25% of your class grade and many of the questions are "Wow"problems meaning that you will not be able to solve them within the time frame given. His tests are way too difficult for an introductory class. I recommend looking into other professors for this class.

reviews.comment: Daily quiz count for 25% of the grade and they are not easy. Tests are much harder than the practice tests. He talks super fast. He always calls people randomly during the class and asks questions that no one knows the answer.

By far my favorite professor in the ISyE department. Really makes you earn your grade, but he also makes you want to do well. There are tons of pop quizzes, but if you review before class you should be fine.

Coming from someone not good at accounting, he was okay. I mostly went to lecture for the note packets (not posted) since his explanations sometimes confused me (glazed over how to get some values). Graded on tests and Connect homeworks, had to put in time outside of class but an A is achievable. Lowest exam was dropped including the final.

reviews.comment: I admittedly did not put as much effort as I could have for this class. However, the class itself was not at all enjoyable. He is extremely hard to focus on and does not post his handwritten notes (only the template), so class attendance is a must. He was nice, but not sure I would take this class again.

Class is not nearly as hard as people make it out to be. You just have to study. Personally I didn't really learn well during lecture because he would run through examples, but that's just my learning style. He was really good at explaining things you didn't understand though, and very accessible outside of class.

His lectures are straightforward as long as you pay attention and his guided notes are great.  There are a fair amount of online homework assignments, but they are broken into 4 sets that are due at the day of each midterm.  Tests are usually the same level of difficulty as the material covered in class too.  Take him for a manageable A

He is a very sweet guy. It's hard to focus in his class & lectures are boring, so most ppl struggle. I heard exams used to be very similar to the HW, but not this sem. A lot of ppl in class struggled for exams, few finished them before the time ran out. If you find acct interesting and don't mind self-studying a lot outside of class, take him.

reviews.comment: Guided notes like accounting 1, its hard if u don't lock in every once in a while, he's a solid teacher

He is very sweet, but his lectures are rather boring, I find myself zoning out quite often in his class. The class structure is test heavy, with the 3 highest exam grades counting for most of your grade. Random attendance quizzes so if you miss a class you could miss out on points. Memorize formulas and review heavily to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: boring boring boring but if you do the homeworks you should be fine

I took this class in Fall 2020 (corona semester) and it was pretty simple. 4 homework assignments but they take up a lot of time. 4 exams which are medium to hard. Definitely use your resources for this class and you will be fine. 1-2 extra credits and a case study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice. straightforward teaching style. Must memorize the formulas and how to do examples from his packets, and youll do fine. Tests are almost impossible if you dont. Study hard for the tests. He curves up at the end based on natural breaks in class averages. Very nice and willing to answer questions.

Suuuuuper boring and accounting is already a hard topic to make interesting. One of the worse professors I've had but it's hard to find someone at tech who can really teach accounting well and fair, so just bite the bullet and take him if he's the only one teaching the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took accounting 2 with Dr. Kuang and really enjoyed the class. He is very friendly and approachable and definitely shows that he cares about the students in his classes and wants them to succeed. The class is mostly built around working through handouts that he provides in class that are mostly what make up the tests. Overall great professor!

Not the easiest class but everything you need to know for the tests is presented in class. He provides notes that you can fill in while following along. Tests are doable and he curves your final grade based on class performance. I had an 87.7 and still got an A

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. Lectures are very heavy, and I could not understand explanations even for topics I already knew. Grading is unusual. They expect answers to match the slides almost exactly to receive credit. Some students get good grades by copying slides into their cheat sheets rather than understanding the material.

On par for the worst class I ever took at Georgia Tech. I stopped going to lecture because I couldn't learn anything from them anyway. Terrible professor, save yourself the headache from this boring class and take anyone else or avoid the class altogether
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had in my 30 years as a student.  His exams do not correlate with his homeworks and his homeworks are nonsense.  Avoid at all costs.
Does not encourage students to excel. Do only what is required to do. Bad tests  , grading is unclear .
This professor was very confusing and difficult to follow.  He did not comprehend the appropriate level for the course, so some problems would be extremely easy, and others would be near impossible.

Easy class. Test avg in the high 80s. Clear and easy to understand. Nice and helpful when I went to get a grade corrected. Grading is strange; I got points off for deriving an equation instead of copying it off of a cheat sheet.

Very straightforward lectures, homework, and tests. Super nice professor who really cares about the well-being of his students. Heavily recommend if you're taking Accounting 2 - there is literally no better professor out there to take for this class.

He's not the most exiting lecturer, but that's par for GT accounting profs. That being said, his class is pretty straight forward and he allows you to drop your lowest test grade. DO THE HOMEWORK! The homework doesn't necessarily mimic the tests, but if you understand and can do the homework, you should make an A on the tests.

Straightforward class, attendance isn't technically mandatory, but he will randomly do class exercises at the end of class that are a completion grade. Tests are simple if you understand the homework problems assigned, and he is very nice. 4 exams, but one is dropped so if you do good on the first 3, you don't have to take the final!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kuang knows his accounting, however doesn't convey his knowledge in a way that is easy to understand. He is not very approachable for questions or for extra help outside of class. There were 4 tests however one was optional. His lectures are very monotone and not very engaging. He seemed to expect everyone to understand the material immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super sweet. Provides the packets for class and just goes through them during class. I prefer to be taught this way, but it can be a little boring. Hw is as many chances as you want before turning in. For tests you do need to pay attention to how problems are set up and in what order because that is not given to you. Loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He only grades participation and test and homework. His lectures are helpful because it is visual and you can follow along with notes. When we moved online due to the pandemic, he made us type out our math during the test but never gave us more time, which caused us to run out of time and not answer all the questions. Unfair.

Dr. Kuang was a really great professor and he makes it super easy to learn. Many others had a problem with his lecturing because it is very dry and monotonous, but if you pay attention it's really easy to ace the class. None of the material is hard and exams are super fair, but students struggle maintaining attendance and studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible lecturer! Always gives clear handouts that explain everything!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: boring lectures but easy class,fair tests but tricky material, just study lecture notes he gives us and do all hw prob he posts online, no need to buy the text, just copy the hw prob from a friend and thats how I got an A
Gives 4 test, one of which is an optional final. Goes straight by the book. Attend class regularly to receive the full 10% for participation.

Prof. Xiong is a good professor who makes lectures enjoyable. The class is straightforward, with weekly assignments due Fridays and two tests. Assignments focus on HTML, CSS, and JS for data visualization, while tests cover lecture material. Attendance is technically "required", but slides are posted online, so it's manageable if you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super chill professor, she has interesting lectures which are easy to follow, especially with the countless examples she gives. The homeworks are intriguing but not too hard and the labs are available through Git and pretty self-explanatory. Only 2 tests and the class ends before Thanksgiving. Overall would recommend.

Cindy Xiong is a good presenter. Most hws were about coding in HTML, CSS, and Javascript and working with D3. They weren't too bad but we weren't given any instruction during class on how to use D3 so you have to figure it out on your own. There are two exams, no finals. The class finishes before Thanksgiving so that is nice. Would recommend class.

Dr. Xia is caring, yes, but it can be hard to stay engaged during his lectures. I might be biased because I had lecture at Kendeda, and it was hard to understand him due to a combination of his thick accent and loud air vents in the building. The TAs were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy and good lectures, though they are long and packed with info. He is not the best at explaining concepts or helping with homework during office hours but hes genuine and is there to help. Tests are hard but he is a very generous grader which helps a lot. overall good

Shuman is an excellent choice for Statics. Lectures are done on whiteboard and are very engaging. Explains concepts really well and goes over old physics/math concepts if you need. Homework is on WileyPlus and takes 2-3 hours a week max. Exams are 88% but are very easy if you do the homeworks. TAs are also great if you even need help.

Shumans lectures were very good, he could simplify concepts into digestible ideas. I took in the summer asynchronously, 88% of grade comes from tests (2 midterms and 1 final), 12% comes from HW. HW wasn't too much, typically one HW a week through wileyPLUS. Provided practice exams and a practice final. Great professor to take statics with.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite good at lecturing. Very kind and caring. Gives you all you need to succeed and doesn't make the class too hard. If you are unsure which Statics professor to go with, Shuman is a safe bet.

Amazing professor. Made things easy to understand with examples. Make sure to do recitation problems, they're harder than test problems. Tests resembled the homework and were easier than some of the other professors tests Ive heard of. Taking statics with Xia is a fun class and easy A
Super nice and wholesome professor who is always enthusiastic about teaching
Professor Xia is really great at lecturing and made the material easy to understand. The tests are also very doable if you study.

The cutest man you will ever meet. He is so nice and is also incredibly invested in his student's success. The HW's are online and only have three attempts so be sure to be careful. The exams are generally pretty easy (good thing because they make up most of your grade). His vibes give off adorable grandpa (he is young though lol).
Overall a very good professor.

Would definitely recommend Professor Xia. His lectures had lots of examples and he explained everything very well. Gave lots of practice before the exams, and the exams were fairly easy as long as you understood all the material. Overall, Professor Xia was great!
Dr. Xia was extremely enthusiastic about the course material and gave easy homework sets (WebAssign) and exams. Lectures were clear and concise, based mostly on statics principles.

Took him for 2001 and 3001 - amazing professor, great at explaining concepts. Generous grader and he does curve. He's honestly amazing at taking a hard class like def bods and making it digestible. Best prof I've had at Tech in 2 years here. His 3001 was 100% exams (no graded HW) so make sure you're practicing consistently. Must attend in person!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the lecture was online professor Xia was very enthusiastic about the material and always willing to help out his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard course, but kind professor will help you to face and understand it. He always give a quick feedback.
Dr. Xia is a great professor and made Fracture Mechanics very interesting. I wish I could take more classes with him. He answered emails very quickly and his tests were average difficulty.
Tough course, great teacher

Super amazing teacher. Had him for statics and def bods, and he was really great for both. Everything is very manageable, he explains very clearly, and is extremely understanding and accessible outside class.
His tests are fair, and there is not a lot of homework. He grades pretty easily as well. He is a very nice guy but his lectures tend to get pretty boring since the material is a little bland.

Professor Xia makes the information very understandable and is very interested in the subject he teaches. The homeworks due are doable and good practice for the midterm and final. Both are worth around 80%, but are pretty fair. His curve at the end is pretty helpful as well. He makes cutoffs for A,B,C,D,F based on the scores at the end. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lecture are kind of boring, but that's really the only con. He makes the class super easy and slow-paced (compared to my friends in other statics classes) which is really nice.

Really good professor for statics. He went to the effort to paint a whiteboard in his house to teach us when we had to switch to online learning. Overall great professor. Do the homework and use his short study guides (has similar problems to the tests).

I took his class for statics and he was definitely easier than the other statics professors my friends had. His lectures ran over time by a couple minutes sometimes, but they were very thorough (rather dry though). Tests were lightly graded, and difficulty was reflective of the in-class examples. TLDR: Show up to lecture, study examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I have taken in Tech. Very smart guy, makes everything simple and grades generously. Always helpful and makes def bods eaaaassyyy. His problem sets have answers online from old textbook pdfs. My advice: attend every class (you actually learn) and take notes. You won't even have to study much if you do this.

Took him for summer online course. He was one of the best professors I have taken at Tech. Gave good lectures, didn't waste any time, solved example problems in class, gave fair quizzes. Not too many homework but could take some time, but he was always available to help even via email. Would recommend to everyone!
Good choice for a statics professor. Makes everything simple. Not too hard
Great guy and great class. Makes learning Def Bods bearable!
Overall an ok prof. Communication can be hard because sometimes because her native language is chinese. The lectures are very long, a lot of self study to get a good grade.

she def cares but sometimes things get lost in communication. lectures are boring and long and tend to focus too much time on things that dont matter while the important parts get looked over quickly. she is always willing to help. the tests are fair but hard. she tells u what the frq is on and the mc is just a gamble that you hope and pray on.

She's a great person, but her native language is Chinese, so she's not very good at explaining concepts in English. Sometimes kids would ask questions and she would just repeat what she said earlier. If you're fluent in Chinese, there were some kids who apparently got a lot from learning with her one-on-one. Otherwise, self-study.

This lady does NOT want to be teaching and she makes sure you know it. I don't think a single ounce of original thoughts went into her course materials. Everything is either lifted from previous semesters or from MIT. Terrible lectures and the slides barely help. The exams have no rights being as hard as they were given the teaching quality

Hardest class I've taken so far, and I had to take this class for my SEC minor. The lectures are extremely unclear, most of my learning was done in the TA office hours, which were very helpful. Exams were pretty difficult, but do-able, and consistently had averages in the 60's. The last programming assignment required in-depth C++ knowledge.
Terrible lectures and course management. Clear lack of interest in teaching or student outcomes.

Grad and undergrad sections have exactly the same hw and exams - this is a grad-level course. Prof assumes you already have extensive CS knowledge and is awful at explaining complex concepts - as a CS minor, this is the hardest class I have ever taken. If you are forced to take this class, be prepared to put in an insane amount of effort.

Expect 100% self learning. I did self-learned a lot from the programming assignment. But the material is poorly organized and not explained clearly. You can't learn anything from class because it's mostly rephrasing the slides. Take Srinivas's class if you can, you need his notes to understand the material anyway.

Very cool prof, but the course structure is terrible. Packs too much information per lecture. If you are taking many courses or have major research priorities, this course will leave you learning most things very superficially, except MPI. Programming assignments (26% of grade) are challenging & graded unnecessarily strictly (no partial credit).

Frankly confused by some of the positive ratings here... 
1. PA2 was mismanaged, where a 100 on the autograder didn't lead to 100 in the assignment (that wasn't made clear)
2. Concepts in lectures not explained rigorously, which should be expected for a class like HPC

This was the first time that I saw students get penalized for trying to answer questions on an exam. She gives partial credit if you leave the answer blank however if you try to answer it and are even slightly incorrect you get ZERO credit. Make it make sense.

Profs lectures are technical and fast-paced, so you have to absolutely lock in or else you will get lost. As such, I felt that I learned so much about HPC through this course. Projects and HWs were challenging, but not ridiculously hard. Exams easier than HW. Great prof overall, would def recommend this course with her if you are interested in HPC.

HPC is a very very difficult class. Prof. Xu had great subject knowledge and would frequently listen to student feedback, but assigned problems that I believe were more difficult than necessary to learn the course content. Overall I think she did a pretty solid job for her first semester teaching this course.

Extremely hard professor. After the final, the class average was 69% (before being curved). 70% exams, rest homeworks and projects. Normally classes with high percentage weight on exams have easier homeworks and projects. This class, the homework and projects were harder than the exams. Avoid if possible.

Not the best lecturer, but system dynamics with Dr. Zhao was a very doable and fair course. The class is graded around 7 homeworks, 2 midterms, and a final which he made optional as a CIOS incentive. Overall pretty good choice for 3017.
BAD and TOXIC professor! BORING course!
Bad professor.

Overall, Dr. Zhao was an effective and caring professor. He was a nice guy, and his lectures were easy to understand just looking at the slides. His office hours were helpful. Homeworks, projects, and exams were all fair, and not overly time-consuming. The course was very organized, timely, and well-run. Overall, a solid choice for SysD.

Lectures were not very interesting. Felt very difficult to connect the concepts to real world applications. He has a background in robotics so much of the real world connections were related to robotics. I personally don't have interest in the robotics and this class did not make me more interested in control systems.

6 HWs, 1 computer project, and 2 midterms. Made the final optional. Material itself is difficult, but he goes over several examples in class, so be sure to actually attend class or you'll be lost. Exams are long for the time given, most worked until time was called or didn't finish. HWs also took a while to complete, but can collaborate w others.

Ridiculously hard class not made any easier by the professor. Homeworks can only hurt your grade. Exams are relatively fair as he gives practice problems but even with those good luck understanding the criteria. Lectures are both boring and confusing you'd have better success teaching yourself.

The class is structured normally, 7 homework assignments, 2 midterms, and a final. The course material itself is dull but Dr Zhao tries to make the best of it. A solid choice for a questionable course.

Dr. Zhao is a solid teacher overall. His online lectures could be glitchy at times, but they properly covered all the material on tests and psets. He was also very accommodating, moving an exam when the class felt behind and making the final optional when enough people requested it. He really cared about student feedback and implemented it.

professor Zhao is very respectful of students' questions and requests. He is quite accessible through emails and after-class quick chats. The workload of this course is a bit heavy since many topics have to be covered.
Ridiculous class with hilarious professor Boring lectures, very confused Overrated
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Zhao's lecture a lot this semester. The course lecture is well organized and instructed. In particular, after the transition to the online format, he paid great attention to our feedback/questions and gave us lots of extra useful instructions to accommodate the unprecedented circumstance for the remaining of the semester.

He is a very kind instructor and takes care of students' feedback. He uses iPad and projects his handwriting note to screens. This is way more effective than using the whiteboard since we are in a large classroom. This is the first course he taught at Tech, so I am very impressed by his teaching capabilities. This is a great course.

Dr. Zhao is new to teaching but he tries to understand his students and is ready to make changes based on feedback. Very respectful towards students. His tests are not the hardest and the final is optional.

Does give pop quizzes, but out of the 7 quizzes he gave, he only graded the top 4 (the mean was 85.15). Overall, midterms test very specific details, but he allows double-sided cheat sheets, which help a ton. Exam II average was a 91. Also responds very quickly to emails and is available for help. Nice professor. Overall, not too hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: interactive lecture model sucks. barely gives any notice and expects us to make time.

Dr. Chernoff is not considerate of the fact that students have other classes and obligations. For our most recent "interactive lecture", he quizzed students on a lecture ppt that he didn't even cover in class. He wanted us to learn on our own & gave less than 2 day notice for this as well, which made it hard to manage with other committments.

His lectures are very hard to follow along with, especially since he refuses to post lecture slides until after. He gives pop quizzes that ask about very specific things. In lectures, I need to use ChatGPT just to get clarifications on half of his vague statements. When asking for clarifications, he doesn't do a good job of explaining either.

Pretty nice professor, but lectures can be very boring and are basically required. He randomly gives pop quizzes and on days he doesn't he takes attendance. Exams can be pretty difficult but he lets you bring a crib sheet. He's pretty nice and understanding with overall grades, and gives grading policies to help you get/keep your A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Chernoff is very considerate of his students and that they have things going on beyond class. However, his lectures can be rather dry and doesn't really present new information. Often we read the textbook and answer quiz questions during class time. I do not feel as though the information we need to learn is explicitly stated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was so much that I had to drop it. The material presented in class is useless without reading the textbook. Practice problems and consulting with the TA is essential. I think if I took the regular course, I would have been fine. Also, his accent can make it hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Yury is great. Yes, lectures are long and hard to follow sometimes, but you don't have to cry about it. Read the textbook actively, but let the PPT slides be your guide for quizzes/tests. Very understanding dude and lenient grader. Don't be intimidated that this is the honors section- embrace the challenge. May the force be with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was nice enough, but his lectures were relatively boring. Like many people, I did poorly on my first test, and there was no way to compensate for that throughout the class. I did much better on the last two tests. The tests are very similar to the homework though. Overall, I would not take this class with him, but if you had to you'd be alright.

reviews.comment: Very good professor and is willing to work things out with you. Very flexible, but you will need to study for the exam, I'd recommend reading the textbook and doing his recommended problems that he posts. If you put forth the effort, you'll be fine

His accent and teaching style results in a small adjustment period, but after that, the class becomes more straightforward as you start to be better able to anticipate what will be on the tests. Dr. Chernoff cares for his students and has a good sense of humor, but sometimes his lectures drag over the 75 minute period. Textbook reading recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for the first half of the Gen H lecture course. He does have a Russian accent, which made me nervous at first because I am not great at understanding accents, but I got used to it rather quickly. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Fairly heavy Russian accent makes it hard to listen through boring lectures, and not everything is one the power point he posts, but he will test over it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Chernoff was a bit difficult to understand at times, but I got used to his accent quickly. Our test averages were mid-Bs with him, he curved our homework, and took the highest of our quiz grades. He taught fairly well and made class enjoyable with his funny tangents and comments. If you went back through his lecture slides the tests were fine.

The lectures were off track, boring, and hard to understand because of his heavy accent. His tests were nothing like the recommended problems, past quizzes, or material emphasized in class. They were also difficult to finish within 1.5 hours because they were 12 pages with multiple parts. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Don't take him. His accent is so strong that it makes learning in his course almost impossible. I have no idea what he was talking about in protein bio and yet the pre-requisite for the course is BIO 1510. Also, his grading is very harsh.

I did not like him as a teacher. I had him for honors ecology, and just hated this class. He would just talk for 1.5 hours straight. Also not helpful in office hours. His accent made me not want to pay attention.

I took HTS3086, and she was genuinely so kind and understanding of her students. She posts all slides, and all quizzes and tests are open-note. There are practically seven assignments in the entire semester, all of which are very simple. Easy A class with an amazing, passionate professor!
Literally couldn't get an easier teacher. She is hilarious and lets you use open notes on tests as long as you don't use ai.

Go to the lecture before the exam, she says verbatim what is on the exam, doesn't release the topic list afterwards (exams are very straightforward). 2 major open-note exams (40% each) and two other small assignments. She is a good lecturer, and I learned quite a bit. Understanding but sets clear boundaries.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very king, wanted students to succeed. Don't worry for the open note tests, trust.

She is an engaging lecturer; however, the class is heavily determined by 2 test grades (40% each), and even though it is open note, some of the questions are pulled from left field and difficult to answer even with notes. If you do poorly on one, you are completely cooked for getting an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took SOC1101 with Dr. Yuan, and she is great! Cares for her students, does not want her class to be overly stressful, and made lectures engaging and fun. There were 2 tests and 2 papers that determined our grade, but nothing that was too difficult. Would definitely recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good good good

Dr. Yuan was honestly such a joy to have as a professor. She's funny and sweet, and she obviously cares for the subject and her students. She said herself that she wants everyone to make an A in her class. So, if you go to class and you participate in the discussions, you'll do great.

One of my favorite profs at GT. Knowledgeable, funny, and caring. Class is very interesting, and there is a reasonable amount of work. Not a lot of assignments though, so you will need to study for the tests. Would highly recommend as a Social Science elective.

Dr. Yuan is amazing. Her class is interesting and engaging and the reading she assigns is not difficult at all. She keeps track of the amount of time someone participates in a semester, but the assignments, tests, and even final project were all pretty easy and tested our understanding of the material. Loved her!!

Love Dr. Yuan! Such a great professor who was clearly passionate about the subject and honestly fun to talk to and discuss with. Tough grader, but not in a mean way, she just wants to make sure you really know the materials. Don't be fooled by the open note test policy, they're still hard!

Mr. Yavari is very passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students. If you need to miss an exam for a valid reason, he'll work with you on finding a time to take it as long as you give him enough notice. He's a bit of a harsh grader on exams but generally exams are quite simple and nearly the same as the practice exams.

One of my favorite professors yet. Very serious about teaching, to the point that you shouldn't expect him to let you sit in class all day texting or scrolling. That being said, he has an amazing way of explaining every topic and proves pretty much everything that he puts in the notes. Also, he lets you know what he expects on each exam beforehand.
Best professor I've had in my two years at GT so far. Definitely cares about teaching and will make sure that you succeed if you put in the effort.

Professor Yavari is a very kind and understanding professor, and cares about teaching. I would heavily recommend taking his class, and if you do, make sure to go to office hours. He is very helpful in office hours and also likes to chat and know more about his students. Take his class!

He is a great professor! I was initially unsure but quickly realized that I got lucky being in his class. He truly cares about teaching and wants you to really understand the material, which is more than most professors can say. He is lenient and very fair on exams because he teaches the material thoroughly. I can't recommend him enough!

Exams are really easy and all you have to do is study the one practice exam he posts. Homework and lectures can be confusing though they have significantly less impact on your final grade than the exams so do not worry if you get lost in the lecture.

Nice professor, but what he teaches in lectures doesn't translate to being able to do the homework. However, exams and the final (which are most of the grade) correlate almost exactly with practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice and caring guy. His lectures could be a little confusing, but he was very receptive to questions and posted lecture notes every week. Tests were very similar to the practices and were often very straightforward. The hardest part of the course for me was the homework.

Was initially scared reading past reviews—they are mostly untrue. He's not mean and he's actually really funny in class. Though his lectures are hard to understand, he posts lecture notes on Canvas so you can review them later. His tests are similar to practice exams, and if you read the textbook/go to class, the homework is not hard either.

Professor Yavari's course completely shocked me. I haven't met many professors who genuinely seem to care about their students understanding the content the way he does. His exams are extremely similar to his practice exams, and going to his office hours helps a ton. He's also extremely willing to work with you on your grade as long as you care.

Can be intimidating in the beginning, but over time, he cares a lot about teaching and wants you to succeed. READ textbook! Exams are similar to practice test. I would definitely take Dr. Yavari again.

attendnace at lecture is mandatory but I couldn't focus on his lectures or follow him most of the times he talks about topics as if students should already know about it, so I used the textbook and online resources to teach myself a lot of the topics there are long weekly hw that usually don't add anything to test prep, but focus on the sample exam

You should try to avoid this professor if you can because the lectures and homework are awful. He teaches a lot more complex topics than other statics classes and his lectures are very unclear. The weekly homework is evil and it takes a long time to figure it out. The only good thing about this class is that the midterms and final are super easy.

Attendance is mandatory by doesn't count towards your grade. The lectures are hard and fast paced, so reading the textbook is a must. He posts practice exams that are almost exactly the same as the actual exams, so work to understand those problems and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take him, whatever you do. You will not learn statics from him and you will be subjected to a passive-aggressive classroom environment. 90% of your grade is based on 9 questions, graded very subjectively. If you do get stuck with him, find an online statics class or an extra textbook or something so you can actually learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: May god bless your soul if you get stuck with him as a professor.

Very rude to students except the few exceptional ones. This is not the way to teach. Unfortunately not much can be done except to warn other students to avoid this professor if you want to learn statics in a non hostile environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs if you want to pass statics. Only statics professor at Tech that has a sub 3.0 GPA. Lectures don't help with homework or exams yet attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great professor and not accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yavari teaches in a bizarre way with only variables and doesn't explain in detail what he's doing, instead, he expects you to connect the dots. He's passive-aggressive, condescending, and teaches as if we've been studying this material for years. His lectures didn't help at all and most of your preparation comes from self studying. Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yavari is very smart, but the way he explains statics may not be for everyone. His tests and lectures never involve numbers (only variables) and are used to derive a solution to a general case for problems. The lecture material did not help on the homeworks. Grading scheme is also very harsh with each 3 tests having 2 questions each.

Arash is very knowledgeable and teaches this class in a distinct manner. The way he teaches, you either get it or you don't. Your entire grade is based off of 10 questions, 2 per midterm, and 6 on the final. He is very understanding, but tough. 6+ people in my class had to drop
Teach yourself the content if you have to take his class. He makes very simple concepts overly complicated.

Great professor, and will work with you if you mess up one test. My section only had three tests total and I happened to bomb the first one, but he helped me out and I did 40% higher on next. Only thing is he goes over by about 10ish minutes each lecture. Very good at explaining concepts.

Professor Yavari is a gift to us from lord! He is a real gem from heaven! His math skills are like magic. Only if he could teach more classes, I would take my whole master's program with him. He is too strict about attendance and paying attention, like the time I was texting my girlfriend during the class and he got mad at me.

He does not teach the material at all. The lecture would consist of him proving a formula you are supposed to use. In the rare instances when he would go over examples, they were way too simple to show how to handle a problem that you might actually see. According to course critique, most of the class failed or withdrew, and I got my first C ever.

I took his Def Bods class in Spring 2021. He treated office hours like a chore, and his tone was often condescending when I didn't understand something. His lectures were so packed with theory that his assigned homework was often over topics we didn't go over over until a week later. Anyone who brought this up was basically ignored.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Walks through proofs very slowly and clearly during lectures but barely covers any examples to help prepare for homeworks and exams. Will assign homeworks every week, including the weeks when you have exams. He tries to help during office hours but is kind of rude and condescending. Grades you based on improvement over time through the 4 exams.

Arash Yavari has been my favorite teach at Tech so far as I am about to enter my 3rd year as a mechanical engineer. The course was very difficult and the most rigorous class I've taken to date, however Yavari taught in a way that motivated and pushed us. Yavari is an extremely nice, understanding, and helpful teacher who truly cares for his class

Yavari was a nice guy but not the best professor. For lecture, he did proofs & example problems from the textbook that he'd often make mistakes on while writing out. The bulk of your grade comes from 2 tests & a final which contain problems that seem unrelated to the class examples & hw problems.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice guy, explains concepts clearly. Open to questions in lecture and goes through plenty examples in lectures. However, tests are pretty difficult. Final is heavily weighted in the course grade calculation. Weekly homeworks (but usually they aren't too bad). He wants you to learn and earn whatever grade you get in the class.

Personality wise, Yavari is one of my favorite professors I've had. Tbh i hated him at first but he grew on me a lot. He'll interject philosophical or other random thoughts into his lectures and theyre usually hilarious. The lectures themselves can be confusing sometimes but for the most part he works through cool example problems.

Prof. Yavari does genuinely care about his students and wants them to succeed. However, his teaching style consists almost entirely of proofs from the textbook, so you don't actually learn how to do dynamics in class. His tests are fairly easy though and you can get by with stuff you learned in phys 1 for the most part.

He really knows what he's talking about and is more concerned with teaching the subject of def bods than following the curriculum. Lecture is everything in this course as he does not follow the textbook and his tests relate directly to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Extremely unclear in grading criteria. I compared my test to a classmates; we had essentially the same thing written down and he received 40% more credit for the question. He was not helpful in office hours. I asked him steps on how to do better in the course, and he told me to solve the questions correctly. Overall, he's an arrogant man to avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Final is worth 60%, so that's stressful. Go to lecture and the tests will be easy enough, but there's a lot of material to study. Got sidetracked early on in the semester and rushed things near the end. Other professors are probably easier/clearer. He does seem to care, though, and if you get an A on the final, he'll give you an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, he cares about you passing. He will not answer your questions in class, but will happily provide help during office hours. He gives a lot of homework weekly, but his tests are fair, almost easy if you know the material. You should take him! (Pro tip: suggest a variable name 'ksi', if he asks to suggest) Beware, final is worth 60%
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Yavari is a very quiet lecturer but is there to help and answer questions.
