He gives homework every week (including test weeks) that are 4-5 questions and he supplies the questions (no need for text). His tests are more waited towards non-trivial questions, and they are 2 questions using variables and no numbers. Overall an average class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This teacher is known to have practice exams and as long as you do them you should get an A. However, fall 2025 was the first semester in 2 years that he changed the content of the tests and quizzes. This cooked me because I depended on the practice tests.

Lectures were sometimes hard to follow because of his accent. You can figure out the material by watching Sebastian Fernandez, plus diff eq is not a very hard class conceptually. The exams and quizzes were pretty easy. The TAs also grade fairly leniently. Just keep in mind that the final exam is worth a large portion of the grade at 37%.
Never went to lectures, but quizzes and exams weren't too difficult and were similar to the review problems and studio worksheets.
Nice guy, but lectures were useless. 5 quizzes 1 drop, final worth 37%. TAs were very lenient with grading/partial credit.
Chill class. Never went to lecture, just watched Sebastian youtube videos or looked at studio worksheets. Just do all the problems from studio and you're set for exams.

Lectures were not mandatory and, quite honestly, not needed. He has a strong accent, which makes him hard to understand. Studio is 1 point extra credit on your grade if you have 80%+ attendance. Grade is quiz and exam-heavy, but similar to studio practice problems. Sebastian Fernandez on YT if you need more help with the content.

Although lectures were not mandatory and only about 15% of the students showed up, he has passion for teaching and wants his students to follow through and learn. Only downside is his strong accent is hard to understand. Studio is all-or-nothing EC if you have 80%+ attendance. Final is required. Sebastian Fernandez on YT if you need more help.

Lectures are just okay. He's not a bad lecturer, it's just that his notes are really, really thorough. Notes are posted online, which is good. Regardless, I recommend that you show up at the studios because they're super helpful. Questions from studio worksheets are similar in format to those on the quizzes and exams. Grade is quiz/exam heavy.

Went to the first lecture and it was the worst thing I ever sat through, so I didn't go again. Nonetheless, stuido and practice problems are really all you need. Test were weighted heavy but not terrible to get through. Quizzes are what you need to look out for. Sebastian Fernandez is lowkey overrated and not really needed either.

Professor Chen is a very reasonable professor who does his best to make the content interesting even though honestly probably not his fault diffeq is just kind of an easy class. He's pretty accessible out of class and just generally a reasonable guy even for accommodations. Liked his class and this prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chen is a really nice person, but his lectures could be pretty hard to understand. I personally learned better from studio/Google. Tests are pretty straightforward- no difficult computation or edge cases or intentional tricks. 3 homework questions a week, extra credit for CIOS/studio attendance, but heavily weighted final so be careful.
Don't need to go to class, Seb fernandez + studio worksheets + review problems and you'll get an A in the class with ease.

This professor randomly decided to make his exams twice the length of every other 2552 section halfway through the semester. He is frankly pretty rude and unhelpful during lecture as well. Sebastian Fernandez videos are the only reason most of this class knows what is happening. Take a different section. Not too crazy of a class with a better prof.

Didn't attend many lectures, but learned almost everything through Sebastian Fernandez and studio. Chen's lecture notes were very long and hard to decipher. The 50-question review packet is really helpful, and exams were mostly very easy.
Lectures were boring and useless, but the tests were exactly like the studio worksheets. Definitely take this professor, it's probably the easiest A out of all the diff eq sections.

XYC's lectures aren't the most interesting, honestly you can learn everything from the studios. Final is worth 37% of the grade, 2 midterms worth 33%. Not too difficult of a class, but its also diff eq.

bad guy but W option for diff eq if for an A. boring lectures, kinda rude. otherwise class is free. 2 test 17% each, 37% final, 5 quiz 1drop 24%, 15 hw 2drop 5%. many pdfs of old test, quiz, final out there and don't change much each year. has practice Qs on canvas. go to studio and watch sebastian fernandez on yt. very easy, confident i got an A
lectures can be boring, but he cares about the topic. sebastian fernandez videos help
He doesn't speak English hard to understand

Professor Chen is a very dry lecturer and can come across as rude. It doesn't really matter, though, since Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube is a great teacher so there's no need to go to class. Tests and quizzes were very similar to the practice problems and were very fair.
Chen himself is an awful lecturer. Watch Sebastian Fernandez videos on YouTube instead of going to lecture. His quizzes and exams are super easy and short so I would take Diff Eq with him if you can.

SUPER EASY. Watch Sebastian Fernandez videos, no need to go to class. Quizzes and tests very fair, tests based on quizzes and studio worksheets. Final exam based on past tests and quizzes, everything very fair. Do the studio worksheets and you'll get an A.

Considering you can learn 2552 from Sebastian Fernandez, you don't need to go to lectures for diff eq. What makes XYC a good pick is just that his tests are incredibly easy for this course. Take him if you can, the material itself is not hard and XYC does nothing to make it harder.

I never went to a lecture, but the studio sections are super helpful. The TA's will teach you how to work through the problems and the quizzes are the same as the studio sheets. The exams are also exactly like the studio. Don't go to lecture unless you want to and just go to studio - the class is not hard if you lock in in studio.
Took this over summer, didn't go to most of the lectures and learned most of the content from Sebatian Fernandez and his notes. Quizzes and Tests were pretty easy.

Definitely take this class with Chen. His exams and quizzes were fairly easy, compared to the review problems we did. Lots of partial credit. He has an accent but honestly, you don't even need to go to lecture if you pay attention in studio.

Dr. Chen is a great professor. His tests and quizzes are extremely easy, and they are easier than the review problems he gives in his big packet. Sometimes he yaps in his lectures, but he is very thorough. Very kind guy.

Lectures are slow and boring and you can learn everything from the lecture slides and studios. Sudios are up to 2% extra credit if you attend. The review packet is really helpful but also way harder than anything on the quizzes/tests.

If you have a great TA, you can learn the majority of the material just in studio. Chen's lecture slides are also quite comprehensive. His tests are much easier than the studio worksheets and his review packet, although I found the final to be a bit of a curveball.

Diffeq with Chen has to be the easiest class I've ever taken at Tech. The class material is intuitive and Chen's quizzes and tests are completely free. Lectures aren't great but anything you don't understand can be found on the internet and you'll be fine. TAs will typically give the 2% EC at the end regardless of studio attendance.

Professor Chen is the most straightforward math professor I have had at Tech in terms of expectations and grading. He likes to go into detail in lecture but if you understand all his review problems you will do very well on exams. The only con I can think of is the fact that grading is done out of only 3-4 exams with minimal or no homework grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chen is perfect if you want an A and dont wanna go to lecture. His lectures are extremelely hard to pay attention to: boring, monotone, thick accent, not engaging, and waste time explaining simple algebra. He has good notes you can teach yourself with and the tests/quizzes are mega easy which is all you can ask for from a math prof a gt tbh.

The lecture is recorded and posted on Canvas so you don't have to physically attend the lecture. Quiz and Midterm problems are quite easy. The Final is very similar to the problems that appeared in midterms and quizzes. Studio attendance counts towards the final grade (maximum of 2%). You can definitely get an A in this course.

Probably one of the easiest diff eq professors. Lecture attendance is not required and all the material can be learned from TAs in studio and/or Sebastian Fernandez on Youtube. Quizzes and tests are similar to provided review problems but way easier.

Take him for diff eq. Easiest, most straight forward class. Not much variety in tests year-to-year. Never went to lecture, only went to studio. Hes not an amazing professor but the content is not tricky so you'll do fine studying with friends for exams/quizzes.

A breather compared to any other math class I've taken, but only because of Chen. Makes quizzes and exams super easy. Lecture is very long and not engaging, so watch recorded lectures at 2x speed. Sebastian Fernandez is helpful, but quizzes/test/homeworks are incredibly similar to lecture. Studio is extremely helpful.

Lectures are uninsightful, robotic, and difficult to learn from. Learn from TA/Sebastian Fernandez. Diffeq class material is easy to grasp, it's a mix of linear & calc and Chen tests us on basic calc2/integration by parts only. Final had one basic Euler's Method question, the other nine q's were a lot like ones from past quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All his questions on quizzes/exams are mild and doable

Not really difficult if you review the slides he posts on Canvas and lecture videos. Studios will give u added 2 points to your final grade which is great. He's grading criteria isn't too bad; on quizes and test he'd give you partial credit for questions.  I recommend going to studio sessions which will give u extra credit points and preparation
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not the most entertaining lecturer, but he teaches you what is needed. look at past exams for study materials and attend studio! assignments/exams are very fair and are not designed to trick you

I personally did not find this class difficult at all (scored a 100 on everything) but I also used every single resource given to me because I enjoyed it (textbook, lectures, recitations). Just show your work on quizzes/exams and make sure to follow submission guidelines for end of the semester extra credit.

Professor Chen is great because he's easy, his grading is very favorable. The content can be difficult at times but the tests and quizzes are super simple and based on the problems done in class. Also if you want extra help just look up Sebastian Fernandez on Youtube. He's can be difficult to understand but follow his slides and you're fine.

Terrible lectures, I watched Sebastian Fernandez's MATH 2552 lecture series for the whole semester and was fine. Other than that, quizzes/exams are generally straightforward. Final exam was a little harder than expected, but it was fine because all previous quizzes/midterms were pretty doable.

Professor Chen is a solid choice for this class. His lectures are a bit lack luster; reviewing his amazing slide deques and finishing his comprehensive practice problem set should be enough to do well. His exams and quizzes are easy given when I took his class in Fall 2020, he he allotted a lot of time for them and they were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Like most math professors at Tech, he doesn't really care about teaching. If you read the textbook though, you'll be fine. No need to attend lecture because he has a thick accent. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy.

Diff eq is not really hard but it was a breeze with Dr. Chen. His review packet prepares you well for quizzes/exams, being that if you understood those, the real questions would often be an easier and reduced version. Super active on Piazza, on top of things, clear grading, just take him for diff eq if you don't want a hard time.
Very fair and understanding.

Very bad at lecturing with an extremely heavy accent. Very hard to understand. Tests and quizzes aren't too bad. Heavily relied on other sources for my knowledge. Take him but don't expect to learn from him.

Doesn't know how to properly teach material to students by any means. His dull math lectures consisted of reading off of a prewritten notes sheet. I stopped going to lecture after the first week. Watch Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube and you too will never return to lecture. I would take again because of how the class is structured.

Chen is a terrible explainer. Majority of the class never attended his online synchronous lectures, but instead used YouTube videos and recitation to learn the material. He was lenient with changing the homework due date when needed! His homeworks, tests, and quizzes are pretty easy (thus why many ppl passed without learning through him).
He's extremely diligent about responding on Piazza. If you ever feel stuck, consider viewing Sebastian Fernandez's channel on YouTube.

Chen is not the best professor, but his class is the easiest class I have ever taken. Just review the lecture notes a day or so before the quizzes and tests and you'll be fine. Most of his test and quiz questions are ripped straight from his lecture notes.

Dr. Chen is a great lecturer, but you may have trouble understanding his accent. However, it should be fairly easy to understand after a few classes. The problems in the notes are fairly similar to the questions on his quizzes and exams. If you show up to all the lectures and recitations, you should not have any problems getting the A.

Chen has a little bit of a heavy accent, but you get used to it quickly. He has the entire schedule, hw problems, and lecture slides posted from day 1 which is very nice. His lectures are fast paced, but it's fine because the notes are available on his website. His quizzes and tests are very easy, and aren't meant to trip you up on old calculus.
I didn't attend a single lecture. I just watched recitations and did the worksheets and it was an easy A.

Chen is honestly a good professor. For 2552 the exams and quizzes were pretty easy but the best thing you can do for yourself in this class is look up Sebastian Fernandez on YouTube and use his videos. Did this all semester and didn't even need to go to lecture or recitation.
If we read and understand the slides he gives, then it is not hard to get an A. Quizzes and tests are pretty close to the examples in his slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was worried because I wasn't following him in class. Look up Sebastian Fernandez on youtube. He covers the entire course as an old GT TA. Lectures are useless. Homework takes no time. Tests and quizzes are extremely simple. He uses 3 different grading weights to determine what gives you the best overall grade and uses that.

Go to recitation and that's all you need to do for this class. Tests are really easy, lecture is boring. He's not the best lecturer but his notes are really well-organized and he gives a lot of review material too.
His quizzes and tests are easy overall. Lecture is not useful, recitation and online notes are all you need to do well. Easiest math class I've taken.

This was the easiest math class I have ever taken. Prof Chen's lectures are not entertaining and sometimes even confusing, but all of the quizzes and exams are a super easy. At the beginning of the semester he states that whatever final grade we get will not be curved, but you understand why when the average for the final is an A.

Didn't go to lecture after the first month, recitation and the occasional online notes are all you need. Almost always uses the same questions for exams/quizzes as previous semesters, so if you have a friend who has taken him before it really helps. Easy A but you might leave the class not feeling like you really know differential equations.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Chen is a REALLY bad lecturer, but at least his class is really easy. Tests and quizzes were not too complex. Go to recitation/studios, do some studying on your own (watch Sebastain Fernandez' Diffeq videos on YouTube) and you'll be straight.
Class is extremely boring. Go to recitation for learning the material, and you will prob get an A. The tests usually ask for basic understanding of the material

Don't even count on going to lectures. Cuz, it straight up boring. Easy math class by far, just 2 midterms and an exam. Hw set every week but just 3 questions with unlimited attempts. Textbook not needed, and recitations are a great way to learn the material fast. Easy work ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Chen is really underrated. Exams are a joke as long as you have an idea of the material. Seriously, take him if you want an A.

He got bad reviews since taking away crib sheets and assigning homework now apparently; Not best lecturer but still easiest class I've taken at Tech. He gives HW but its literally 3 webwork questions w/unlimited tries. Test questions are exactly like exam review sheets. Do HW, review sheets, and watch sebastians 2552 youtube vids (no txtbk needed).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very straight forward. Easy to understand. Lots of HW. HW gets super tough, but not mandatory. Tests are extremely simple compared to hw. If you can do the test review well, you can easily get an A. Pros: Very straight forward. Easy tests .Cons: kinda tough to approach or reach out of class.

Really poor lecturer and tough grader. No one attends his lectures and your performance in the class is completely reliant on how good your TA is. No crib sheets for any exams, including the final. Mandatory homework is also given now.

The worst professor at tech. Almost the entirety of my recitation skips lecture at this point. I wouldn't be surprised if there was a single digit number of people who go. I learned more by playing tetris in his lecture. He doesn't respond to emails, and will try to make things harder if people are doing well. Honestly, he shouldn't have his job.

He gives homework and took away the crib sheets for the tests and made them harder overall. Despite that, nobody goes to his lecture because it feels like a waste of time and most of us were taught by our TA.

Absolutely terrible lecturer. Hard to understand, boring lectures. Hardly anyone attends. Your experience in this class is completely based on your TA. (Mine was also horrible). No crib sheets anymore and tests are harder.
note to everyone, I'm in his class right now (spring 2019) and he now gives homework and no longer allows crib sheets on the exams!

His tests are relatively easy compared to his lectures; I stopped showing up to class after the second week and got through the tests pretty easily. Final is a bit harder, as can be expected. Going to recitation and knowing how to work his problems (both "assigned" and the sample ones in his lecture notes) helps a lot; homework isn't mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His notes are basically his test. He posts his notes on his website so you can go back and look at them. There is nothing but lectures in his class and they can be a bit boring but you get to learn a lot from them. If you go ask for a regrade, you generally get the points back. The posted notes and the crib sheets made this an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Xu Yan Chen knows Differential Equations very well, but he comes off as very rude during office hours. His tests and quizzes are really fair, and as long as you know the required material (on his website), you will get an A. Lecture is pretty much a waste because he will just read off of the power-points which are on his website.

Entire grade is based on tests, quizzes, and the final, so homework is unnecessary. His accent is difficult to understand at first, and honestly there's no point in trying because he's scattered and confusing anyway. Just go to recitation and you'll be fine. You get a 2 sided crib sheet on all tests and quizzes, so still a pretty easy A.

Definitely the easiest Diff eq prof. He recycles a lot of questions from the past for his tests and quizzes. Didnt go to lecture and did well. TA's are crucial though. My Ta was how I learned the material. Final was a bit of a challenge but not too bad.

Once you get used to the accent, you will learn a lot from this guy. Still, Prof Chen is a solid choice for those who are looking to pass without going to lecture. Listen to your TA, and you can get an A. However, I would recommend going to class as well.

Chen's lectures are quite boring, but diff eq is pretty boring too. He does a great job of preparing you to learn the material by doing tons of practice in class. His quizzes and tests are very very straightforward. I just took the final and it was harder than I expected for Chen, but honestly it wasn't difficult compared to other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: he explains pretty clearly what he is expecting you to know. he explains topics clearly, and there are no surprises on tests and quizzes. understand the topics and the class will be easy

Make sure you go to class and write down/take pictures of every one of his handwritten pages of notes so you don't get surprised like I did on one of his quizzes. Grading can be harsh, -30% on one quiz for small things like forgetting to simplify an answer with addition of like terms. Uploaded slides are extremely helpful. Textbook is useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 2552 is an extremely easy class. If you can easily do the worksheets given in recitation, you can get a 100% on every test and quiz. Lecture isn't necessary, as most slides are uploaded. Recitation isn't necessary either.
Tests are really easy, you don't even need to go to class to learn since the lecture slides are pretty clear. Lectures are basically just problem solving and no theory.

By far one of the easiest classes I've ever taken...I never attended lecture, but I attended all recitations for the worksheets. If you complete all the recitation worksheets and work out the practice exams (which is by far more complicated/requires more work than the actual exam), you will get an easy A. His exams and finals are a joke.
Class was really easy. Only went to recitation. Cannot understand his accent and his teaching is poor.

Dr. Chen explains things clearly in his lectures with plenty of examples. He is engaged with the material each lecture and generally explains concepts very thoroughly. The only thing that he could really improve is how he responds to questions, which he often has difficulty answering.

I loved this professor. This was the easiest class I had in a semester and I learned a ton about differential equations. He's very very good at explaining things and extremely fair in grading. Favorite math professor at tech, would recommend to anyone taking DiffEq
Tests are very easy, homework can sometimes be a little difficult and time consuming. Chen is a pretty good lecturer but it didn't seem like he really liked it when students asked questions.
Not a easy-going prof. Tests are very easy. Recommend to take the class, skip the lecture and study by yourself.

The class itself isn't terribly hard BUT Chen is EXTREMELY inaccessible and inflexible. A friend who had an excuse through the Dean was still not permitted to make up a test, for example and thus failed the class. There's only grades for Midterms (2), quizzes (4), and the final. He gives a 2% recitation bonus.

The class structure itself is very easy to pass and get a good grade in, but Chen himself is an absolutely awful, rude, and pretentious guy who is impossible to have a conversation with. If you're happy learning everything on your own, go ahead and take the class, but expect ZERO help from Chen. I really, really, disliked him.

Pretty clear in lectures but his first language wasn't English, so if you ask a question he might not understand what you mean right away. In any case, his lectures had a lot of practice problems and his tests were way easier than the homework, if you pay attention you'll do really well!

Chen's tests are easy, yet they check your abilities. It is really very easy to get an A in his class for 1552. I strongly recommend (especially if you already know a little about integrals because his accent can be a little difficult to understand). He assigns less homework compared to other profs (though the sums are hard).

good, incredibly fair professor. tests are very straightforward, quizzes are a little harder but do-able. he will drop your lowest quiz, test, or nothing (whichever gives you the highest grade). final is difficult but not ridiculous. not too friendly but respectable. lecture is boring and long but not mandatory.

He is the easiest Integral Calc teacher! He posts all of his lectures online, AND he lets you use a crib sheet on every test or quiz. Class average was 20% higher than all the other sections. His lectures were beneficial and he would crack funny jokes in class. Also, his Asian accent is very clear and was NOT a problem at all. I HIGHLY recommend!
His tests are extremely straightforward and easier than the practice tests he gives.

Take this professor!!! He allows all of your written notes for his pop quizzes and you can use one front-and-back sheet of paper for all of the tests and the final. Plus, his tests are easier than the homework his review worksheets!! This is really rare at Tech! He is not necessarily helpful but he teaches slowly in class. Go to tutoring for help.

You can tell he takes his job seriously and tries to teach so that's good.  However, you tend to learn more in recitation and on your own with homework.  The class itself isn't hard.  His tests are super simple and easy especially after you do his practice tests which are way harder than the actual tests.

Lectures aren't too useful, because he spends them going over his handwritten notes which are already online. For the most part, I learned in recitation and on my own. That said, the class is extremely easy. For each exam he posts a practice test one week before that is almost identical to the actual test. He's a very fair grader too!!
Boring lectures, thick accent, but easy tests. Just do the practice problems and you will get an A.

He is definitely knowledgeable about what he is teaching, but he has a very thick accent and he is not good at answering questions. Whenever someone asks a question, he typically repeats whatever he already said about a topic, but louder and more angrily.
He has a heavy accent and does not know how to explain things very clearly. However, his tests are VERY easy and simple. Just do the practice tests and you'll get an A.
Do yourself a favor and avoid this professor. He is rude, incomprehensible, and downright boring. You will learn NOTHING from this guy.
A pure Mathematician with a deep  understanding of the subject. He could be little more friendly/easy to talk with. Overall he is a good professor.

He likes what he does and it is a good teacher. If you want an A in the class, just do the practice tests and that is it. I have not gone to half of his classes nor recitation but with the practice tests I have managed to get an A on his first 3 tests. His homeworks are online and you can re do them to get a 100 if you do them wrong the first time.

He gave us access to a free online textbook.  There are a few random quizzes(5%) during lectures(easy). Online homework(15%), which took me 2 hours to complete each week. 4 tests(3 worth 15%; lowest 5% and a final(30%).  Chen has an accent, but if you pay attention you'll be able to understand.
He does a have a bit of an accent, not too bad. His tests are easier than other Calc 1 professors and he does a fair job at lecturing. Overall, Not bad.
Easy Class. Made a 97 in the class and I never went to class. Dont ask questions during class or he will yell at you. Take him and do the practice test that are online and you will ace the exam.
He is a very practical teacher plus he's hilarious.Do your Work and you'd get an A.I got a 94 in this class.TAKE HIM.

He's incomprehensible. His lectures are basically useless. He cracks an occasional joke but otherwise, he's very boring. He assigns outrageous homework sets which, if done legitimately, take students 5-6 hours to complete. The tests are admittedly mostly fair, but the final exam is certainly unfair and won't help your grade. Take another professor.

Never went to class. Still got an A. He gives hard study guides to prepare students for the test. get to drop one of 6 quizzes. Best score on your test weighs more into your average than your lower score.
He's hilarious. And if you go to class, there's no reason why you shouldn't do well.

The lectures are not helpful. I learned everything I know about the class through my textbook which is great! The tests are long and you'll have just enough time to complete it if you know the material very well, work fast, and don't make mistakes that need correcting.  Office visits are sometimes helpful.

Very inflexible and stubborn. If you take his class expect to do everything 100% by the book. Shows no trace of any. Might as well have taken class with a robot, except a robot would not be borderline deceptive.

Tests are very similar to the practice tests, and it is easy to do well in the class. One test had a problem not on the practice test which threw me off. He seems to change his grading policy every semester, and he is useless in lecture. I never used the book and learned everything in recitation. He is also very rude when you approach him.

I had Chen for Differential Equations. He's a decent teacher, but not great. His tests are identical to the practice tests and as such, it is very easy to do well in his class. In short, he's an easy professor, but I honestly felt that I only did well because I memorized formulas while not actually learning and understanding the material.
Hard to understand, but it is possible. I never went to lecture because I never got much out of it. He only lectures on concepts and does few problems. I think recitation was way more helpful.

Can't understand him to save your life... the only way I did well is the fact that I did my homework and the tests were exactly like the practice tests... never went to lecture and did ok in the class..

His calc II class was fun.  I sat in the back with my rfiends and made jokes during his lectures, but my friends and I still made A's in his class.  His tests are very similar to the practice tests he posts with answers before each test, and he is pretty approachable.  His english is rough, but his great notes make up for it.  VERY FUNNY.

The best thing about Dr. Chen is that he allows you to use a 'cheat sheet' on the tests, AND drops up to two tests (although the more you drop, the higher the final counts.)  I managed to fail all but one test (because I never studied), get an A on the final, and get a B in the class.  XD
He's a really good teacher but the accent's hard to follow. The practice tests are just like the real ones so if you study them, you'll do well in the class. Really funny.

If you can figure out what he's saying (foo rank matrices...), he's as funny as they get. We go slow as hell but somehow are way ahead of the other Cal IIs and where most are failing. No comment.  Anyway, he's a great guy and he'll respond to emails at two in the morning, even with a class over 200.

Accents the wrong syllables on almost all of his words, gives you a headache after being in class too long.  On the flipside, practice tests are just like real tests making the class easy, especially if you are inclined to not go to class, b/c of accent.
Practice tests are almost exactly like the real tests.  I didn't do homework for months and still got an easy A.
Practice tests are just like the real thing. He lets you scale the quizes/final to find the best average. His accent in lecture didn't bother me. Wasn't a hard A.
I couldn't understand a thing he said the whole semester!
His tests are the same concepts as the practice tests...he will give you the benefit of the doubt.  Lecture is boring....
Impossible to understand, but goes through concepts like a high school teacher
No Comments

Classes can be kind of boring but in no way hard, not a lot of assignments and she is a light grader. A lot of books are assigned but its easy to get away with not reading them. Nice person who cares about literature and their students.

She's great! Very reasonable and discusses interesting topics. There's a reflective essay, a powerpoint presentation, a group podcast, and a reflective portfolio (mandated by the ENGL department) which she prepares you well for. There's reading but you can get away with skimming here and there. Overall, high recommendation!

Great teacher. She focuses on class discussions a lot. Most of the assignments are pretty fun and creative. Only about 2 big essays to write in the class (including the final project). You also get to analyze a couple of movies towards the end (1 her pick, 1 class pick)

She was the first English teacher where I felt like I actually learned something and improved my skills as a result of the feedback the teacher provided. Very helpful and supportive, makes completing assignments very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Medina was a great professor for 1102. She was always enthusiastic and made the lectures engaging. There is quite a bit of reading, but they are overall interesting. The class discussions are in-depth and engaging. She is a reasonable grader and makes all assignments very clear. I definitely recommend Dr. Medina for English 1102.

Theme was surviving childhood. She's really nice, but a bit quiet. There's a good amount of reading, but they're pretty interesting, and you watch some movies at the end that you choose as a class. Assignments are creative and fun, some you have to work in groups. One assignment was harshly graded for some reason, but everything else wasn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's awesome, really accommodating, extremely nice and cheerful. I enjoyed the readings and the stuff we watched, so class discussions were interesting. Compared to my 1101 experience, I felt that the grading was not hard. The writing prompts are fun the last group project was a bit more work. I absolutely love the theme (food for thoughts).

Very caring and willing to give extensions. I enjoyed the readings in class and discussing them. I also appreciated her having viewing times for movies we needed to watch and even bringing themed foods.

I had her for ENGL1102. Dr. Medina is a great professor. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to learn and do well. She will give extensions on basically anything if you just ask and wants you to know that this is a low stress class. She is a fantastic person and her class is not that hard. And its about food which was pretty awesome.

Dr. Medina is extremely caring and is lenient on deadlines for assignments. There are a lot of readings, but that is normal for an 1101 class. There are projects throughout the semester that are generally easy, but require lots of time to work on outside of class. Lots of readings for participation, but you only need to give a few opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not really that hard but you do have to put in a bit more effort than u might think u need to. You actually need to partcipate in discussions to get a decent partcipation grade. If you don't say much shes gonna take some participation away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Teaches very poorly but attendance is not required so you can watch Lehmann's lectures but exams are much harder than other professors.
Tests are a fair measure of course material, boring (not helpful) lectures, but overall FYE class!
Very Tough on the grading. Tests much harder than other 2551 sections
Hard to understand
bruh i just cant. take that class at an easier school over the summer

Writes on a small whiteboard in the front of a classroom with 4 projectors (he doesn't use any of them, so it's difficult to follow his work), bad accent, makes tests impossible and unfair (first two tests had an average of 66/100, and the last one had a 61/100 average)

He doesn't run the class well and I would not recommend him.

Spring 2025. was very difficult for me even though I took it in high school. I'm not sure if I struggled so much due to poor teaching or my own stupidity. I thought he was a fine lecturer but obviously I didn't do so well in the class. He used the whiteboards instead of a projector, and it was really hard for me to see with the glare and distance.

Bad lecturer- mumbles and is quiet, only writes on whiteboard and stands in front of what he's writing. Gives less resources than others (seems that he took stuff off the syllabus when comparing with another section). Posts lecture slides, but unfinished, and we never get through them in lecture anyways, so I just watch Lehmann's videos.

He only writes on the small board at the front of the class even though there are four projectors for him to show his work, making lecture hard to follow. His tests are way harder than the slides and quizzes, and he often posts lecture slides with no solutions or methodology. He also has a big accent. First test average was 62/100.

Do not take.
Amazing professor, best multivar teacher, easy exams.
very caring, genuinely wants to see students do well, and super understanding
He's a very chill guy and the exam content is very much like the practice probelms.
Take this professor, a great guy. Tests are easy, the same as practice problems. Professor is nice and takes everyones opinions into consideration. Couldnt understand much in the lecture, but still.

Genuinely cannot understand what he is saying, I went to lecture once and never went again. Easier just to self-study this course tbh. There's plenty of online resources. Although the exams are not super difficult so he still gets a 2.

First off, I should admit that I don't go to his lecture. I'm still giving him a five star because his tests are very doable if you just do the 20-30 practice questions on the day before the test. Formula sheets were given for all exams, don't even complain. I'm glad that my tests are easier than the other 2550 professor.
He does listen to students for feedback on exam content/difficulty and does offer extra credit for studio exams. He posts all of the lecture content on Canvas and the WebWorks are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I've ever had. He barely speaks english (not joking I tried asking him something after lecture and he didn't understand me) and has the worst accent ever. He is incomprehensible that 90% of the class stop going to lecture after week 1. Also does not allow formula sheets even tho they were allowed in prev semesters

He had an accent, and brushed over concepts at a very fast pace, but his overall understanding of the material was OK. If you ask him questions outside of class or during office hour then he'll explain better.

He taught me in my first year as a professor in general, so I tried to give him some grace. However, there is only a small amount of grace I can give. He has a very noticeable and almost not understandable accent and went too fast. It got to a point where 5 people were showing up to an almost 100+ student lecture. But... he tried his best!!!

I'm not sure why his existing reviews are so bad, but his Cybersecurity of Drones course has been by far my favorite course at GT so far. The lectures were very info dense, but for me this class was a breath of fresh air compared to other classes at Tech. It is certainly different, but it taught me a ton. I would take it again in a heartbeat.

Saman is a nice guy, but a nice guy does not make a good professor. His drones class holds promise on paper but is so poorly executed that it is the worst class experience that I've had in my 5 years here. The simple and information-sparse lectures pair poorly with the time consuming assignments. If you expect to learn, you will leave frustrated.

One of the most unorganized classes I've ever taken. Assignments were run by the TAs often with vague and unhelpful instructions. Almost all of the lectures this semester were taken up by student paper presentations. As an undergrad, I learned practically nothing in this course. Overall very disappointed as I thought it would be a hands on course.

Saman cares for the students, but he really dropped the ball. The TAs managed the projects entirely, so his lectures had nothing to do with them, and we built a drone the 2nd week, but only grad students flew it once in the last class. It was an overall disappointing class for undergrads, but the paper reviews might be useful for a grad student.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Saman is a really nice Professor who wants his students to succeed. However, the class had no structure whatsoever with frequently unclear instructions and little to no guidance from the TAs. As undergraduate students, apart form building the drone in the 2nd week of class, we never flew it, or tested any of the simulated content live.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Saman is a well meaning professor, but for his cybersec. of drones course, he completely dropped the ball. Over the semester we covered 3 slide decks. Of which, Saman often played YouTube videos covering the same content. 
Overall, I learned very little from this course and honestly could have spent my time taking a different,more effective, course

Professor Zahra was not a bad professor, I would give her a 3.5 if I could. She definitely knows what she is teaching, but how much she weights participation is a little heavy. I emailed her about missing class for an excused absence and still was not able to make up for that participation. Go to class, take the practice tests, and you'll be fine.

Mgt of Health Op is discussion-based and graded only on participation (reflections), a group presentation, and easy hw where you answer questions. Prof Mobini is excellent: very knowledgeable and clearly cares about her subject + students. She does a good job of making everyone's voices heard and reads + responds to every single reflection.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: tests and homeworks are weighed the same so def easy grading scale. GO TO CLASS
ngl it's week 3 and I can not understand her majority of the time... her accent is so confusing.
test is the same thing as the practice test. take this class w her.

Had her the first semester she came to tech. Class was mostly on Pearson, but had 8am mandatory attendance. She took a point solutions participation grade, that was for accuracy, but then changed it after some feedback to completion. tests were easy and similar to practices. group project was an auto 100. really nice teacher.

It's a very straight-forward class and Prof. Mobini gives clear lectures and is very understanding. Attendance is required, but it should be because you won't understand strictly using canvas. It is very easy to do well if you just come to class and do the homework. The test mirrors the HW

Professor Mobini was great! I enjoyed being in her class and learning from her. Pearson is heavily used in the course and a substantial amount of material builds off of the management statistics course. She is extremely accessible and responds to emails very quickly. Would recommend!

I believe that this semester is her first time teaching the course. That being said, she did an amazing job and you can tell that she's very enthusiastic and wants you to get something from this class. The only pains of this class were that attendance was graded, and she made us buy a course pack for $10 that we used once. Overall, great Professor!

A very chill professor and attendance wasn't mandatory, but I still went to almost every class because he made the lectures very interesting and entertaining. Exams were straightforward and class expectations were clear. I'd take this prof again

GOAT Professor. Chill class. Lectures were there if you needed them, but otherwise his tests were very straightforward and 80% of questions came from the practice tests. Overall, very good guy and pretty funny sometimes.
u not gon learn
Super chill, good lectures. 80% of your exams come directly from practice quizzes so you should be fine.
the goat at tech
great guy so chill take him

Loved Dr. Tidler. He's funny, entertaining, and his exam questions pull directly from the practice quizzes he gives you. It's incredibly easy, but I actually just ended up attending most of the time anyway because he was funny and entertaining and got my day off to a good start. If you need this class, TAKE IT WITH HIM!!!
engaging, funny, chill, goat

Genuinely interesting class even though it's a gen ed that everyone has to take. Lectures were super interesting, Professor Tidler definitely knows what he is talking about and is interested in the topics. Enjoyed going to class, exams are copied from practice given in class, meaning they are not hard if you put in a little bit of work.

rlly recommend this class, easy A and gpa booster. practice quizzes are given for midterm and final and theyre literally the same thing so just memorize. i spent lectures doing work for other classes, but his lectures were still intriguing, hes nonchalant. most assignments were discussions boards and surveys, didnt need effort for the class at all

I am such a fan of Prof Tidler's lectures! He was very informative, but he made the content feel super interesting and fun and relatable to students in his lectures. He is forgiving with grades and offers late submissions. The only issue I had was I missed some of the in-class work, so make sure to stay on top of that if you take his class.
GOAT psyc teacher. He's very entertaining and funny, class is so easy, doesn't care about attendance. Could not ask for better prof.

Great guy, super funny, loved his class. Has a lot of passion for what he teaches and it's evident in his lectures. The workload was NOT difficult at all, and he really put in the effort to make sure that his assignments were interesting rather than busywork for the sake of assignments.

An amazing and charismatic professor! Class is structured where the in class assignments is very few, and the exams are incredibly easy and straightforward. Made lecture entertaining and interesting as well. Would highly recommend taking him for PSYC 2015

Lectures are engaging, even tho they are early. Super understanding of student struggles. Easy to reach out to. Several discussion assignments, mandatory practice quizzes, 1 midterm, and 1 final; all easy and a good balance for the class. Take Psych 1101 with him 1000%

Zach is an amazing professor who not only respects his students but has an amazing attitude. He is caring and makes his lectures very interesting. Classwork is very fun and tests are easy if you study the questions before hand. Overall, amazing professor and would take a class with him again 1000000%

While the class was easy he was difficult to deal with on attendance issues. I understand his policy but he makes no exemption for sick students even with a dean note. When trying to discuss issues he is dismissive and uncaring. I barely scrapped an A after missing a single attendance assignment but getting an A on all other assignments.

Zach would make a great youth pastor but unfortunately he's stuck doing a PHD. The unannounced in-class assignments are few and far between, but make up 10% of the grade, so be wary! Zach should consider running for office some day.

Zack was awesome. The content of the course was challenging, but the quizzes were open-internet. There were no midterms but lots of quizzes. There were also two group projects, but both were graded easily. Put in the work, and you will get an A.
Hes amazing. The easiest A at tech

Brilliant professor, the classes and lectures are super interesting and super intellectually stimulating, really love going to his classes. As for the homework and quizzes, you'll have to make proper notes and can't just pass using the lecture slides. There are weekly quizzes and 6 midterms + final so it's a bit hectic but open book and practical.

Zach Tidler is the best! If he is a prof for one of your required classes, you should definitely take him! He has a philosophy of letting people use their notes and internet for tests so I feel like that would also be available after the pandemic. Overall, he's super nice and funny. There were quizzes every week and there were 3 tests.
Rescued my dog from a burning building. Would take again
Amazing teacher! Clearly has a passion for learning and is a phenomenal teacher! He was super respectful of all students, and willing to help people out. His grading feedback was also very helpful.

If you get the chance to take a class with prof Lanterman u need to do it. Im taking gpu programming with him rn, I pester him and his TA every 2 seconds and they respond within an hour. He runs all his chats through discord, his lects are all recorded. He is the best u can get as far as a professor goes. No exams in case you are a bad test taker
Great prof, but just let me turn my hw in on canvas like every other professor pls :(

Most accessible prof ever, he will answer questions on the class discord at 2 am. Really stress-free grading style. Spends a lot of time on helpful feedback and making sure the final project is doable for everyone. Absolutely insane library of top-notch youtube video lectures.

I'm taking him online in the summer of covid and in 5 weeks he was already 2 weeks behind schedule. He knows the material and presents it well, but doesn't give any tests or quizzes, just a final project. He asks out feedback about online classes which I appreciate, but he also inserts his political views into the lectures. Just teach me signals!

Amazing prof -- he's so incredibly passionate about what he teaches and it shows in his lectures for the class and just makes you want to learn more too. Grades fairly, and a genuinely great person too (COVID-19??? Was THE most humane professor I had with how considerate he was regarding all the outside factors the pandemic introduced)
Professor made the subject material interesting and had awesome lectures.
Great professor, really into the material. Class not too organized but he's very helpful after class. It's not an easy class for me but I learned a whole lot. Favourite class so far.

This class is still really hard and requires a lot of work.  However Dr. Lanterman's enthusiasm was essential to my success.  If lecture was boring I would have never made it.  He's goofy, but in a very helpful way.  Great class!! Also there is a lot of emphasis on the lab and homework, so one bad test won't kill you.  No curve in my class.
Great professor. He has funny stories and it keeps you awake. This was a newer class, and it has much less work than the 2025 class.
Good Professor.  Very Enthusiastic!
A nice professor and a really cool guy. Just wished his lectures made more sense---you'll have to study a lot on your own to compensate for this.
No Comments

What a cool guy. I didn't get very much out of lecture but he made it fun w/ his stories. He's one crazy guy but makes class very interesting. Academically he's pretty good and he's usually available after class for help.
No Comments
No Comments

Santesso is a great professor for LMC2000! He cares a lot about his work and makes assignments feel meaningful and directly related to all the texts gone over in class. He's a tough grader, but he is also willing to give feedback and support--he truly does want you to do well. If you're an LMC major, I definitely recommend starting with him.

The material is very interesting as it's mostly focused on satires in different mediums. Overall, the class requires dedication as the essays are long. Quizzes are weighed heavy, but simply taking notes and studying is enough. His feedback on essays is insanely thorough. Dr. Santesso is funny and passionate about the subject, making the class fun.

i think someone else mentioned but hes a good professor but i just didnt really vibe with him but thats different for everbody. why did i just find out he has a wikipedia page? He tears into your paper but dont take it personally; dont think your writing is goated he'll knock you off that peg.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of people claim Santesso grades too harshly, but I disagree. I felt like all of my grades were fair, and the feedback was beneficial to becoming a better writer. I would say my only "issue" was that he did not use Canvas for grades, so you need to keep track of your own and do your own calculations. Also, participation in class matters!

most engaging professor i've ever had. genuinely loves what he's teaching. there's a LOT of assigned reading, but he goes over it well and in a way that could make a waffle house menu sound like an epic poem. very tough grader, but gives wonderful feedback and has clear expectations. class participation is a must, but you'll want to anyway.

Dr. Santesso is a great professor and clearly loves what he teaches. Lectures were also really interesting. Quizzes are very specific based on the readings, so you really have to read/watch the material he assigns. He's also a harsh grader on papers, so don't expect an easy A. Great class and professor overall though.

Mr. Santesso is a tough grader, but you can tell he's passionate about his work, he has faith in his students, and he wants his students to succeed. I was never very motivated and turned in all my work super late until he told me he saw great potential in me and invited me to an external literature seminar, which was really inspiring for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very engaging lectures but a VERY tough grader on papers. Sometimes the feedback felt subjective. Also attendance and class participation matters a lot even if he never expresses that (he doesn't). It could totally drop your grade even if you have an A.

Mandatory attendance, but unlike most classes I actually wanted to go. Lots of interaction with physical things in relation to course material (we made paper one day in class), interesting literature selection, and fantastic lectures. Tough paper grader, but fair. Helps your writing improve a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Santesso will push you to be your best! However, this felt discouraging when I received harsh grading & criticism on the essays (50% of your grade) I put a lot of time & effort into. Considering his lectures are very fascinating (& him saying B= "very very very good" but A= "exceptional"/"wow"), I recommend him to anyone wanting fun, a push or a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the second class that I've taken with Santesso and I am just obsessed with him. He is one of the most engaging professors I have ever had. That said, this course is not an "easy A" intro class that many expected. He is a rough grader and refuses to use Canvas at all for any reason. Take him if you can - it's worth the work!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with amazing lectures. A genuinely and deeply interesting class. My only problems are personal. He is slightly condescending (as most profs with a wiki page are) and WILL NOT post anything on canvas in a timely manner, if anything at all.
genuinely fun class and a great, easygoing professor! gives amazing feedback on papers, and a fun final project. absolutely take this class with him if you have the chance

He is very passionate and knowledgable on his class topics.his lectures are actually hilarious and engaging. Theres short quizzes that cover the works and lectures (but as long as you go to the lectures and listen you'll be fine) He challenges you as a writer for sure.

Professor Santesso was a great professor! His lectures and the subject matter were engaging and he really cared about each student. We had two major papers that made up half our grade and were graded harshly, but quizzes were easy if you went to class and took notes. The group project was fun and left a lot of room for creative freedom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Santesso seriously has some of the most interesting lectures I've heard. He focused our LMC 2400 class on satire in media, which was really interesting. Quizzes aren't too bad if you pay attention, some heavy reading at the beginning. Essays are graded harshly but fairly, make sure to use his feedback. 100% would take again, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Santesso is an amazing professor. His classes is very reading heavy. Pretty much every class we had a reading unless we had to watch a film or view art pieces. He seems like a tough grader but he's actually really fair. Doesn't give clear rubrics but is happy to answer questions. His lectures are also really interesting and not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Santesso's lectures are interesting and engaging. He does regular short quizzes; you need to go to class in order to do well on them. He's a harsh grader when it comes to papers, but he tells you exactly what he's looking for. His final paper is fun because he gives the option to write about whatever you want in relation to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, but I don't think an intro major class should be this hard. Didn't put any grades into Canvas, 2 papers and group project graded very harshly. He's unclear about what you'll need to know- like things he mentioned in passing in the lectures are the most important details (ex-the place a work is set in). Main details seem lost on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Santesso is one of my favorite professors. This was the second class I've taken from him because I loved the first one so much. The assigned take-home materials are a fun break from the rest of my classes and the lectures are very entertaining. Very tough grader on papers, so not a super easy A, but I feel like my writing has improved a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best! Super funny and entertaining. Not a lot of outside work. Hard grader on some things but gracious on others. Definitely attend class because you get all your notes from lectures. Definitely a must take, especially for LMC majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Santesso! He makes class interesting and is an amazing lecturer. The course load consists of a midterm short paper, a midterm, a final long paper, and a few quizzes. Definitely go to class if you can; a lot of the quizzes and midterm will have questions that we talk about in class. Overall, a really great guy and an amazing class.

Super funny guy, tells amazing stories. But you NEED to go to class, because the stuff he covers you need for quizzes, projects, and essays. He's super reluctant to give out A's on the papers, but always gives helpful feedback. Great in office hours. I really feel like I learned a lot in this class.

One of the best profs I've had. He's gotten rid of the pop quizzes and gone to announced quizzes, which are easy if you've done the reading. Really engaging lectures and discussions, and he's a hilarious guy. He's a tough grader on essays (doesn't give out A's easily) but that just makes you write better. Very fair grader on final project.

Santesso is by far the most amazing professor I have ever had. All of his lectures are entertaining and enlightening. I walk away from his classes feeling like I've learned something valuable, but I never feel like he tries to make things more difficult than they need to be. He's funny and incredibly knowledgeable!

Great professor- probably one of the best I've taken here. Makes the lectures interesting, unlike many of the LMC/humanities professors. Lots of reading, but usually skimming it is enough to do fine on the quizzes. If I needed another humanities credit, I'd take another course he taught.
Incredibly engaging, very helpful, and very funny.  Probably my favorite professor at Tech.

By far my favorite professor I've had at Tech. His lectures are interesting, and he genuinely cares about students. I've taken several of his classes, and he consistently gives about 50 pages of reading HW per class for the first half of the semester and then only assigns movies for the second half. He's a hard grader, but he wants you to succeed.

Santesso has a really fun lecture style. He's pretty current and is a funny guy. He's very clear about expectations and is really good with feedback. He is a pretty harsh grader. Forget everything you've ever learned about writing and get ready to learn how to write his way. He makes you work for your grade, but if you try you'll make an A.

I loved the structure of the class and the unified theory across multiple mediums. Dr. Santesso is excellent at keeping his class engaged during lecture, but is less deft with Q&A. He's good about responding to email if he feels it warrants a reply. Take the class, it'll make you a better scholar and you'll actually want to attend.
Awesome Professor. Makes class really fun to go to. Not very helpful emailing, but very helpful with assignment feedback. Do the work and you should do great in this class
He knows what he is talking about and makes lecture bearable. Doesn't hurt that he is hot. Recommend to anyone to take a class with him.
Best teacher ever! I really enjoyed the class. Just the right amount of difficulty and he is a very fair grader.

He kept lectures entertaining and was very enthusiastic about the class. We read about 4 or 5 Fantasy novels because of the class's topic and wrote a good bit but it was an awesome class. I loved attending every day. Definitely recommend.
He got the editor of Aqua Teen and Squidbillies to come talk to our class about villians.  He's awesome.

Professor Santesso is an excellent teacher. His lectures are entertaining (not mandatory but you should probably go to all of them because he gives pop quizzes that count as a final). Even though it's a hard class he's very helpful. I failed all the quizzes but ended up with an A. Definitely recommend.
Haiyu is a great guy, can sometimes be a tiny tiny bit cryptic but wholesome dude and course was not hard. Studied like 3 hours for each exam and got high A's on all of them

Lectures are fine, very fast-paced. Doesn't fully answer questions when you ask, just reiterates the answer he got. TA was bad, didn't explain answers to worksheets well. I failed the first midterm (hardest one) and never seemed to recover (test heavy course). Will ask you to simplify difficult fractions in a short amount of time.

Overall he was a good professor that cared about his students, but 1712 is a heafty class and the lectures were extremely detailed and in depth. The course is mainly graded on 3 Midterms and a final, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities. If you struggle with probabilities, you will find this course very difficult.

Class is very test heavy, but overall it was an easy class! Lectures jump around a bunch of different math topics and he posts the slides on Canvas if you miss them. Haiyu never hesitated to answer questions or give help if someone was confused. Make sure you go to studio, you'll get 1-2 extra credit points!
Actually the first time that I understood math! As long as you go over the midterm study guides and studio worksheets, you will most likely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly thought this class was great! You can finesse some of the exams by studying the day before if you go to studio and lecture!

i suck at math, but i loved Mr. Zou as a prof. He is funny and a very good teacher. Tests are fair and I always did better than expected (got -.6 buses on one question and covered the tests in tear stains but got an 80). the hw and studio questions def relate to exams and quizzes.

the goat for 1711 or 1712! yes the classes are hard, but he is by far the best person to take them with. He is funny and engaging in lectures and gives lots of extra credit for going to class and studio

Haiyu is a great professor for how deceptively hard 1712 is. While bad at responding to emails, he's very nice in his office hours and grades fairly. You'll need to put in more effort than you think and get extra support to do well in this class, and to accomplish that, Haiyu is a great prof. to get there.

He is a mid professor, my TA was awful which made this class more difficult than necessary. The grade inflation at the end of the semester goes crazy with homework and extra credit, so most people end with an A or B. 2 weekly homework and if you go to all the studios + lectures you get extra credit. Not the worst ever, but doable with some effort

The exams varied a lot in difficulty the first exam average score was like a B second a D and final a C. He ended up curving in the end. He provided homework assignments that could be used to add up to six points onto your final grade. Overall great guy.

Professor Zou does a great job of explaining topics in a simple and understandable way. Although, attendence isn't required (outside of quiz days), I highly recommend coming to class. Homeworks are not required, but are good for midterm practice and earn you extra credit. Quizzes are not bad and midterms are fair.

You can still succeed if math isn't your strong suit, but this class is easy for some and hard for others. Starts off fairly easy but kind of ramps up near the end. The studio worksheet problems show up on the quizzes and sometimes the exams. Partial credit given on exams, 4 extra points available for final grade. Won't respond to emails.

I have taken Zou for 1711 and 1712. I received a letter grade higher than expected both times, and I am extremely grateful (math is not my strong suit). This class is difficult, however Zou is the best teacher you can have. This class is graded by 3 exams + final, 4 quizzes, and homework. Attendance is Extra Credit.

This class was EXTREMELY difficult if you have never taken a calculus class. I went into my exam blind because of his lack of awareness of putting in grades. The syllabus quiz was given 6 weeks into the course. NEVER responds to emails in a timely manners, and also lies in emails. You will feel stupid when asking him questions.
Haiyu is amazing. I had him for a total of 2 math classes, and I would absolutely take another math class with him.

He didn't put grades in the gradebook so I never knew what my grade was (even going into the final). He would claim that he would add things to canvas and then NEVER do it or do it so late that it didn't matter anymore. He doesn't respond to emails in a timely manner. I went into the final blind bc I didn't know my grade.
Doesn't respond to emails ever

Much better at teaching this class (1711) than 1712, the lectures are much more engaging and easier to grasp. The homework is very helpful in learning the content but he often teaches it in a different way. Class gets easier as the semester goes along.

If you have previous experience with calculus you should be fine, but this class is not friendly to those who have little to no experience. Moves very quickly and his lectures are very uninteresting. Also very hard to reach outside of class, will take days or weeks to respond to emails.

Great, funny guy who understands the class is filled with non-STEM majors and teaches curriculum accordingly. Pearson homework sucked, but exams were easy if you did study guides. Goes fast during lectures, but overall relatively simple to follow. Office hours were helpful for additional questions. Attendance = extra credit.

I love him.An amazing teacher who really cares about his students understanding the material. Assigns homework pretty much every week/lecture but they really do cover the material and help you. Provides EC that is very beneficial in the end. Also really funny and goofy. if you fall asleep during his lecture, good luck.makes math fun but to a limit

His lecture style is extremely boring and unengaging. I took AP Calc / IB Math in high school and that is the main reason I understood what was going on. Studios / lectures are extra credit which helps. Def go to studio, it's a lot easier to learn content. Exams / quizzes are identical to studio worksheets and study guides. H

Easy material so easy A, but the prof frequently waited until the last minute to post homework and made mistakes on study guides- he would make a mistake, someone would point it out, he would tell them they're wrong, then they would take the test, get that question wrong, point it out to him, and he'd say "we did a problem like this in class".
Very good professor, just show up to class and take notes and the class should be an easy A.

I really enjoyed his class! The lectures were pretty engaging and easy to understand. I'd say the math wasn't that bad, but I know a lot of people who struggled with it. Quiz after every lecture for participation and homework 2x a week. Worksheets and study guides were very helpful. Great professor! (don't email, he won't answer. Go to OH lol)

Prof Zou will make you laugh in every lecture, and found a way to make probability fun. He is extremely clear, and the tests are based on the content on the study guides. Attendance is extra credit, and many tests had extra credit, or questions that wouldnt be graded. Some homework (that you pay $90 to access) but overall solid class and prof.
Professor Zou is a great professor. He has a clear voice and communication style. Just as good as watching a YouTube video and he goes through every step. I am taking him again for finite.

This course is easy if you already learned calculus in high school (AB). If you did not, it is very challenging because he goes through the material very quickly and the lectures are pretty unengaging. He is very good at answering questions and is a nice guy overall. The midterm/final was very similar to the study guides.

Haiyu is extremely kind, but his lecture style is TERRIBLE. I found his lectures boring, unclear, and hard to engage with, which sucked bc his slides are also USELESS for review as he does all of his teaching on the whiteboard. I got a B bc of youtube, textbooks, and a curve. This class is RIDICULOUSLY difficult, especially bc of how he teaches it.
You have a test every other week in the class. But his lectures are very good and he is always open for questions outside of class. He really cares about his students.

For a statistician, this guy loves to yap and seldom relies on visuals. If your class is quiet, maybe it's because nobody understands what is going on, you don't have to take it as a personal affront to you. 

If you want students to engage, make your lectures engaging. 

If you want to do well in this class, just do the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took math 1564 with him as well. By that time he was the TA for 1564. So much better than the professor. Explains concepts so much more clearer. For math 3670, he does some review every class, but you still need to go to class. He is definitely the best professor for 1564 and intro to stats/prob. Just take him, you won't regret, promise

Zou is a funny and a great caring teacher but hard. Go to class or you will definitely get behind, and homeworks and tests are graded pretty ruthlessly. I ended up with an A as he curves the class at the end, but don't pick him if you want an easy A. Definitely made statistics more interesting for me!

Haiyu is prob one of the best math professors at GT. Explains things really well. Quizzes and tests can be hard but he gives lots of resources and hws give up to 6% EC. Def listens to feedback. Early grading was very harsh but def changed after receiving feedback. Overall very enjoyable course and feel like I actually learned a lot.
He is a very good lecturer and is perfect for college students. He is incredibly intelligent and always willing to help. Just talk to him every now and then. If you try, you will do well.
Bro is just one hell of a specimen.

I love Professor Haiyu! He gives wonderful lectures, and he cares about his students(he answers all the questions you ask in class or after class). Homework is heavy but meaningful, tests are hard but fair. It's is a challenging class, but if you love math and find that Prof. Haiyu will be teaching, then TAKE IT! You'll learn more than "a lot"!

Probably the best math instructor I have ever had. MATH 1564 is hard (especially if you have never taken a proof-based math class before), but Haiyu's lectures were excellent. He is very helpful if you ask him a question after class or in office hours (maybe a little too helpful when it comes to homework).

Professor Zou is the best!! He is super enthusiastic about the subject and you can tell that he really loves teaching it. Professor Zou also cares a lot about his students and holds many office hours sessions. The class is extremely difficult and mostly proof based. Be ready to put in a lot of time studying but Professor Zou makes it worth it!

The content was difficult and moved fairly quickly, but when Haiyu says things, they just get understood. He made me actually understand the essence of math and want to take more math. He's also just a great guy and gave everyone cookies during our final.

As I wanted to know the "why"s of linear algebra, Haiyu couldn't have done a better job. He is an engaging and passionate lecturer, interjects with jokes, and clearly cares about his students. The class was rigorous and challenging, but he is fair in assessment and I've learned so much. Truly a great professor, I only wish I could take him again.

If you go to lectures and studios, it is easy to pass this class. Professor Zou was engaged with his students and responded to emails quickly. He communicates what to expect on exams. The first half of the semester was much easier than the second half of the semester. The final exam was much harder than any other quizzes or exams.

This class is definitely difficult! That being said, Haiyu is an amazing teacher. His office hours are extremely helpful and he gives some opportunities for extra credit. Going to lecture is crucial. Hws are graded easily but tests are graded harshly.

He's a great professor. All of the resources available made it hard to outright fail the class. His lectures and studio work was also helpful in learning. This class taught very surface level calc 1 2 and 3, so I get why it's hard for some people if they aren't familiar with calculus already. His study guides are exactly the same as the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned so much from Prof. Haiyu's class which allows me to see math as a completely different subject compared with what I did in HS. It is very time-consuming but no regrets here. I know I will miss this semester.

If you go to all his lectures and TAs' studios, you get 4 extra credits, almost half a letter grade. That's how much Dr. Zou wants you to pass his class. His study guides tell you EVERYTHING that will be on the exam, which is why I finished the final in less than half the alotted time. There's people complaining how hard the class is? smdh.

Words simply cannot describe how amazing this man is, you just have to take him. He's a rare professor because he is not only extremely intelligent but knows how to communicate his genius to students who I found are often quite stupid to put it frankly. If you can't crack his class you shouldn't be at Georgia Tech, try UGA.

Professor Zou has been one my favorite professors by far. I personally found his class to be easy simply by attending lectures and participating in studio, plus he gives a study guide before every examine that is almost identical to the test. Some students complained his class was too hard, but surprise surprise, I never saw them once in lecture.

Though I find this course difficult and tests can be sometimes challenging; for the first time in my life I enjoyed taking a math class. Professor Zou is an amazing lecturer with a great sense of humor. I did not skip a single lecture and note that this class was at 8am. Prof Zou is also very caring and was willing to schedule extra Office hours

The class is tough, but Professor Zou is funny and genuinely enjoys teaching his students. His lectures are worthwhile to attend, and he often interjects long and arduous proofs with humourous tales. He is always available and listens to the students' concerns. He made this semester amazing.

I wouldn't take this class if you don't truly love math; the subject matter is very hard and takes much work to comprehend. If you just need a linear algebra credit, take 1553/4, trust me. However, that is not to attack Haiyu, there is no one who could teach this topic better than he did. He is caring, personable, funny, and generous with grading.
