This is an insanely hard class but Prof Zou makes it so much better. He cares about his students, has a sense of humor, and can explain concepts simply. It will be hard to find a professor better than Haiyu.
Prof Haiyu is the GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Zou is excellent at teaching and cares about his students. This course is hard for students who did not have previous exposure to calculus. The lectures are interesting and difficult material is simplified well. Though I find the tests and quizzes to be quite challenging so I hope that the final will be doable.

Easy class. He understands that this is not stem math and makes his teaching super clear. He's really generous and flexible on midterms and quizzes. you can drop your lowest quiz. Hes a great math prof and will listen to any reccs or ideas. Also if you say like 1 think he will change half the exam to what you want.

Prof. Zou is extremely personable, and an amazing lecturer and teacher. I can't explain it, you have to take it for yourself. hands down one of the best teachers I've ever had. The class is challenging and will challenge your way of thinking, but it's so worth it and enjoyable and, dare I say, fun.
He taught difficult content very clearly and provided us with helpful resources to practice.

Don't take him if you are not ready to work. If you do decide to take him, your hard work will be rewarded. His lectures were packed with materal which made me feel that I learned a lot. I appreciate that he had his office hours right after class. I do wish he could go over more stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good person, but his grader, Aryan Mittal, was extremely difficult and had averages of F's on both exams. Half of the class dropped, so Haiyu made the second half crazy easy, which passed everyone. Haiyu himself has memorized most of the textbook, and writes the theorems on the board, and does a few examples per class, decent lecturer.

Haiyu was my TA in MATH1564 and really helped me do well in the class. I did not understand much in lectures and it was his studio sessions and practice problems that helped me grasp linear. He was the only TA in the class of like 50-60 people and he did a great job of helping everyone.

Haiyu is such a great teacher! He is super approachable and very good at explaining seemingly difficult concepts. Watching him set up problems has helped me greatly in proving things. I am glad that I signed up for the honor version of Linear Algebra as my first math course. I can't wait to see what other interesting classes Teach has to offer!

Really tough class, even though he kinda tells you what will be on the tests. His study guides are very helpful and he is pretty accessible during office hours. Online class format is a struggle but if you go to his lectures and follow through, you should do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor if you really want to learn more about prob and stats. Super logical lectures and explainations. You will even learn t-distribution and chi-square which I thought will appear in 4-level math course. Go ahead and choose him if stats is important for your career in the future! Don't choose him if you just want an easy A.

Absolutely loved him :) he's super caring and flexible about things if you talk to him.  The grades are fair and if you attend/watch all his lectures, everything is verys straight forward, but if it's not, he's super willing to answer any questions you may have.  Highly recommend

MATH 3215 was a very difficult class for me. Through it, though, Professor Zou was tremendously understanding and responsive, and made lectures not only interesting and enjoyable, but also hilarious and personable at times. Would highly recommend the professor, even though I personally disliked the subject.
Probably the hardest math class I have taken at tech. If you do all his homework and understand what you are doing, tests are quite manageable. Oh yea, for your own sanity, don't cram for his tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class started out to be hard but he realized that students weren't doing too well and changed the quizzes and tests to be more practical and in line to what we were learning. Overall, I learned a lot in this class and it wasn't too difficult. Some homework questions do pop up in the tests and quizzes so do your homework.

The first test was pretty rough. However, Hiayu made sure later tests and quizzes were more doable. You can tell he really cares about students success and he is very helpful during his office hours. Hiayu, you are a great teacher! Dont let the students bully you!

I thought he was fine, and it was also his first semester teaching this course. The first test was harder than we prepared for but he ended up curving it and gave use harder practice problems for future tests/made them easier. Our last two tests had a lot of problems we had seen before. He does do learning catalytics to check attendance.

let's start by saying that this man began a Finite Math class (one of the easiest math classes at Tech) by saying "I anticipate this class will be harder than linear algebra and differential equations" and he didn't lie. he doesn't teach well, he's boring, and if you ask him questions, he doesn't know how to explain answers

Praise the curve! This class was tough, and you have to work for your grade. Homeworks cover future material as on what you have already learned, which can make them tough. He also makes up his own problems. His lectures are high paced. He is very helpful in officehours, he also wants to help you understand the material. The class was a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: When he said the course was fast-faced in his syllabus, he was not kidding. If you do not go to class for a week, it feels like he is speaking a completely different language. His notes are very good, probably some of the best for the classes I have taken at GT. Oh, definitely go to his office hours, they are extremely helpful.

No matter who you take this is a difficult class. Haiyu (yes everyone calls him by his first name) is a very caring teacher. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. He will work out homework problems with you. If you don't understand a concept, he will explain it until it makes sense. He will answer dumb questions without making you feel dumb for asking them.

Hardest class I've taken at Tech. Haiyu provides almost no resources to help you succeed. Homeworks are very difficult, often don't correlate to the material he covers in class. His lectures are not engaging and he spends most of the time talking to the board. Test's are very proof and notation heavy, with very little partial credit awarded.
Best math teacher I have had at Tech! He goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. Go to his office hours!

Gave a lot of extra credit (20-10-10 points on the tests and final). Homeworks were pretty difficult, but the test questions were much easier. Took several test/quiz questions from homework or in-class examples. Not always the clearest lecturer, and made mistakes, but had a lot of office hours.

One of the best math teachers I've had at GT. Really accessible, friendly, and helpful (even when people take advantage of office hours to have him walk them through the homework, right before it's due).

All of his assessments were much harder than the material use to prepare. He moves very fast so it's hard to catch up if you don't understand a concept. He was very approachable and would make time to talk with you outside of class if you asked him. Very hard class in terms of a core math requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Best TA at Tech. Very patient.  He is the reason I survived the course.

This man's consistent clear explanations and niceness is the reason I am doing well in discrete math. He will sit with you and do problems even after recitation is over until you understand everything

Haiyu explained things very clearly. He was always very prepared and made going to the recitation worthwhile. He was also very funny, which kept the students awake. Hands down the best TA I have ever had so far. Good luck to you, Haiyu!
He's just beyond the average human in every way.
A very knowledgeable TA and he cares about our success. He gave too many problems in class and it can be a little overwhelming sometimes.

This class is rewarding, although difficult. The material is basically just learning how to program a GBA in C. Tests are quite difficult and graded harshly. HW5 is not for the faint of heart. The end of semester project is fun but lots of requirements, so will take up a good bit of time. For the love of god attend lecture, itll help on the HWs
bad professor

Professor Hansen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super passionate about this class and the topic is very interesting. Expect a lot of hw and labs! The tests are very hard and some might even consider harder than CS2110. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Aaron is very good and caring prof. but the materials are better taught 1v1 than in class

The best class i've ever taken, that being said, get ready to WORK. Hansen's a great lecturer and clearly passionate but the nature of the course is super difficult. At least 5 hrs a week in the first 2 months and 10-15+ after that. He's very accessible and kind to all students, but the TAs carry the course. Go to office hours and recitation!!

The HW took up my wkends and especially the last ones had me (and the whole class) going crazy. Aaron is passionate about this topic, & I respect him. The TAs are FANTASTIC and work their heads off helping and explaining every important detail to us. I wonder sometimes if 2110 would have been less stressful...The final project is fulfilling though.

all-around good guy. he knows this class is insanely difficult and time-consuming, and is trying his best to make it bearable. the TAs really carry this class on their backs; i was practically camped out in office hours every single week. class is fun, but expect it to be your heaviest workload by FAR.

Professor Hansen is a nice guy, but his class is genuinely the most time consuming and work heavy class I've ever taken in my life. Homework and Lab is due every week. I've had project based courses where I spent less time on final projects than I did on a singular homework assignment in 2261. 

Expect to spend 20+ hours of work per week.

This class was tough. There is a lab every week and and homework almost every other week. The most time consuming class I've ever had. Expect to spend 10-15+ hours on homework. Aaron is not the best and can come across arrogant. The TA's are GREAT and really carry this class. The tests are also SO hard and he asks the most random stuff on there.

This class is infamously difficult, so it was very nice to take it from a professor that cares deeply about the content. The content can sometimes be difficult to digest, but Professor Hansen is very knowledgable and cares about the content and the students. The TAs are super helpful and will go out of their way to help you with your assignments

2261 is a pretty work-heavy class. Every week you have a homework and a lab. Every other week you have a quiz. At the end of the class, you have a final project. Quizzes cover things from lecture, but they are usually timed and tricky. Despite that, Aaron and the TAs are very helpful. You definitely have to put in the time and effort to get an A.

Prof. Hansen makes the lectures entertaining and engaging even when the topic itself isn't the most fun. The assignments (homeworks and labs) aren't too hard but they require a lot of time. Working on the final project can be awesome, a lot of creative freedom given. No test, just quizzes every other week. The TAs are super helpful too.

Class attendance isn't mandatory, but it definitely makes learning a lot easier when going. Not tests, but quizzes every couple of weeks and nothing is really cumulative. Really easy to get above a 70 on the quiz and I found it doable to study the night before. Class is composed of different GBA homeworks and untimed labs! TAs were super amazing!

Prof Hansen is a great guy, you can tell he cares about his students. The material itself is not the most interesting but he makes it bearable. Best to attend lectures even thou he posts the slides, you'll do better on quizzes of you attend. Labs and HW are easy if you pay attention in lecture/recitation
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best professors I've ever had here! Knows what he's talking about and is very approachable!

Strategic Brand Management with Professor Hackett has been one of my favorite courses taken at Tech. If you show up, read the book, and do good work on the presentations, you will no doubt get an A in the class. Professor Hackett is an incredible lecturer and professor, and I cannot recommend this class enough.

Incredible guy, incredible professor. This class was extremely applicable to the real world, and it was also probably the most engaging class I've ever had. Read the book very closely to make an A on the exam, but trust that it isn't as bad as he makes it sound. Super clear grading criteria. Fair amount of work (all done in class), but worthwhile

Dr. Hackett is incredible and very knowledgeable with a great background in brand management. He really cares about students learning the content. His lectures are interesting and the class is really only focused on two projects and one exam. Definitely READ THE BOOK to do well on the exam. Definitely recommend.

I absolutely loved his class. His lectures were very engaging and he uses real life examples. The book is not your ordinary boring text - it's very interesting and easy to read/understand. I would 100% recommend taking professor Hackett. You will learn a lot.

Really caring professor and engaging lecturer. He cares a lot about student feedback and always gave us time to discuss and voice concerns/ "I wish you had done this..." about the way his assignments were structured and presented to us, after an assignment was over. Listens and implements the changes too. Loved the course, had lots of group work.
The professor is a former P&G brand guy who connects theory to application in a way that's easy to understand. My favorite class at Georgia Tech!
Majority of your grade in this class will be a project where you work closely with a company of your choosing. Class times is super interesting and really fun.

Dr. Levine is an amazing lecturer and professor. For his Stem Cell Policy & Ethics class you have to write policy memos and he is very clear on what is needed to be addressed. He critiques your policy with worthy comments so you know how to fix. He is very accessible out of class and is willing to work with you. Definitely would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Levine is an amazing professor. He's very accessible and knowledgeable, and he cares a lot for his students. He only grades by a few assignments so don't slack and you'll be fine. Final was a take home exam and major grades were group research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: please do not take this Professor. He doesn't care about all his students and he is not helpful at all when you ask him questions.

Definitely work the old tests and find those answers yourself in order to study for the tests. His tests are just as detailed as the practice tests with some of the same questions. IMO, lecture was somewhat boring, but you need the attendance grade. 3 tests. 2 papers. Attendance. Discussion section.

He's the best teacher I had at Tech. For an ethics class, he's surprisingly unbiased about... everything. This makes his lecture interesting, as he gives different perspectives on many controversial issues. There are clickers, so attend class. Difficulty level is fair, and I received an A fairly easily, even though I didn't give it my all.
Class is interesting and you don't really have to do the reading. Attendance is only necessary to do like 1 PRS questions per class. Also, he is really really attractive.

Class is very interactive which is fun. HIs grading can be weird, but is always accessible and he just wants to see students try their best. Heavy reading, but you can finesse it easily.. He's really invested in his topic which made the class more fun. Participate, put some effort, and you'll get the A. DO NOT BUY THE WOVEN TEXTBOOK FIND THE PDF.

The grades in this class are mostly projects, each project is different so it's a little more interesting than writing papers. Dr. Colton is really passionate about his subject and his feedback is really helpful. I was struggling in this class for a bit but with the chance for revisions, it helped my grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not that many grades just projects. Gives lots of feedback on your projects and you're allowed to revise one project I only got a few more points when I fixed a major issue tho. You're allowed to miss 3 classes and there's a participation grade at the end so I guess if you miss more it'll affect that. We had books but we didn't use them too much.

Unorganized, no communication it seems between her and TAs. 3 exams no drop, no extra credit offered and says she doesnt believe in curves. Unwilling to meet or answer questions at times. Exams are extremely difficult and lecture is too vague. Nothing prepares you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a horrible teacher. The way that the test are written doesn't correlate to the lectures given in class . The point distribution on the test is ridiculous (15 questions and written response the written response is 22 point! out if the 35 pt test. The way that she grade as well is completely ridiculous if your response does not match you fail.

She's great. She doesn't lecture too much, but when she does she does a fantastic job. She provides interesting videos and gives us fun group exercises. We were given everything we could need to succeed in the class. As long as you show up to class and do the online assignments, an A is attainable. I definitely recommend taking Dr. Angra.

I know that my previous review was deleted from this page, somehow. Johnson is the worst professor that I have ever had at GT. He's rude and condescending, and he's impossible to talk to about grades. He pretends to care with his "motivational" lectures, but when you try to talk to him, he is very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall an ok professor. Pop quiz on the topics he just went over in the same lecture, but they're not a big portion of the grade. While homeworks aren't mandatory, completing them will definitely help for exams. Pay attention to lectures and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson's lectures are boring and he's not lenient with grading/extensions, but he's pretty fair. Not hard to get an A if you 1) Go to lectures and write down every in-class example problem (they are re-used in quizzes and exams), and 2) Participate in lecture (he will exempt students from the FInal who have participated and have high 80s.)

content of this class is easy but the grading scheme is rather unforgiving and weighs heavily on tests. Lectures are boring but attendance is required. No homework to turn in which is nice. If you have taken AP stats this shouldn't be a hard class but 1 or 2 mistakes might drag your grade down by a lot.

The worst teacher his students would ever have, for their whole lives. He is rude, both in person and in emails. His syllabus and grade distribution is def the worst ever. If you take a course with him prepare for a C even if you are used to As.

He writes the positive review here, and it is funny that he thinks he can trick us doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad prof, that's all you need to know. He was an army general and def acts like it: extremely unforgiving. Grades are based on quizzes, and exams. He randomly decided to make Quiz 3 due at 8am instead of 11:59pm (like the first 2) and said he could do nothing about the 0's that many students received. In all interactions I had, he was very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class can easily be self-studied. Lectures are very boring but attendance is basically required. He's rude in emails.

Pros:
- clear about what is expected out of a question/exam content
- exams are re-written in-class problems and HW questions
- get to make a formula sheet
- if you do HW and attend lectures you will get an A

Cons:
- exams and attendance are a HUGE portion of the grade
- you NEED to attend lectures or you will not get a good grade
- kind of boring
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: idk how hard the class is over the fall but i took this course during the summer and it was a joke. Don't get me wrong, the course material wasn't the easiest to understand, but with 4 people so far we haven't had any real exams. Our first exam we all took together as a class and he just gave us all 100s. Do with this information what you will.

Johnson pretended to care, but it's just a facade. In every conversation, he was passive aggressive and occasionally downright rude. His lectures are awful. He doesn't teach, just works examples with no explanation. You have to answer participation questions (graded on accuracy) and pop quizzes the same day he "taught" the material. Exams are ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Your grade will definitely not reflect your knowledge of statistics. It will be the result of the quickness by which you can correctly answer newly taught topics. The tests are easy, but the grading system, with so much weight on unannounced quizzes and participation for which you are given 2 minutes if you are lucky. 

Worst syllabus ever! Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very, very, very tough grader. Barely got any partial credits at all even though some questions showed understandings of the concepts, and the participation in this class can actually determine your final average grade. He may be a great person, but he is not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most of the 5-star reviews are written by himself which is pretty funny. Attendance is mandatory so if you miss one, you could be heavily penalized for as much as 2% of your grade. The exams question are easy, one can never listen in class and get easy 100s on exams. He will waive the final if your grade is 80% and above for every section. Avoid

He writes his own reviews on here so any of the 4/5 star ratings are most likely him. There were attendance quizzes and if you got them wrong you got a 0 for your attendance. I know a student was late to 1 exam and he held that over her head the entire semester. Horrible professor and horrible human being.

Tough but fair is probably an accurate description. Speaking from personal experience, he accommodates requests within reason as long your not trying to get out of exams. Even though participation might bring your grade down, the class had a pretty good curve and rewarded those who put effort into the class. However, other sections may be easier.

ISYE 3770 with this professor was a very frustrating experience because the grading was very harsh. Even small mistakes were heavily penalized, which made it difficult to earn a good grade in the class. Unless you are willing to put in a lot of extra work and have thick skin when it comes to grading, don't take his class.

The course is fairly easy as long as students show up to class every day for clicker questions and pay attention to the lectures. Professor Johnson runs through many, many example problems very quickly during class which are very similar to what will be on the tests and quizzes. Overall, Professor Johnson seems to be a caring and respected teacher.

You have to show up to classes at 8, which is the worst thing, but otherwise, he is amazing. He explained the materials very carefully and was easy to understand. As long as you can do the problems from the book and lecture examples, you will be well prepared for a quiz. The quiz problems are fair, and the grading is also fair.

Around the first week of classes, Ron Johnson claimed to be part of the OSI board. However, upon inspection of his rate my professor page, I have found an instance on December 5th, 2019 where General Johnson tries to impersonate students to inflate his rating. Many similar phrases were used, including references to "clickers". Don't take his class

Super cool dude. You have to show up to class. He grades on turning point participation, and he sets a radius from his computer, so you have to be in class to answer the questions. Otherwise, the material in class is easy.

His lectures are quick, so you NEED to stop him when you have a question. He is caring in class, but very terrible responses on emails, so email the TA's. He has participation questions during lecture, and your grade is pretty much determined by your tests. You can exempt the final if you have an A. Teaches you what you need for the exams.

His grade distribution and how he grades participation is abysmal and completely ruined the easy A that is ISYE3770. His avg GPA is .8 below other profs and, at 2.86, is lower than the avg GPA of many notoriously difficult classes. He simply doesn't understand how to structure a class. Don't be like me, check a prof's avg GPA before it's too late.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is one of the most understanding professors Ive had here at tech, he cares for his students well being in and out of the class. He attempts to make lecture a little more interesting but at the end of the day its still math so you can only do so much.

He is not a nice professor and does not cut you any slack. He's difficult in emails and is a tough grader considering your grade is determined by a few quizzes and two tests. He's not nice in the slightest and is the farthest thing from caring. The class isn't impossible by any means but you're going to have to rely on yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: General Johnson knows his material inside and out. He teaches quickly during class, going through dozens of practice problems, but he will always stop and clarify if someone has a question. Go to class, sit in the front, and participate in calling out answers/next steps during practice problems. Exams/quizzes contain 0 extraneous material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor was the rudest and demeaning professor I have ever had in my entire life. The way he emails you back is extremely rude. He pretends like he wants students to succeed by saying encouraging things during class, but the course grade is based on two exam grades, pop quizzes, and mandatory participation. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had him in fall 2020, and I didn't enjoy going to his class to say the least. He was very rude to students during lectures if they asked questions during lecture and in emails. Taking stats with him means putting your entire grade on 2 exams and the quizzes (which are very hard to do well on bc they usually have 2-5 questions).

He's disrespectful and demeaning. He takes the power trip of running a required class too far. He makes the course complicated by not giving students marked up slides in order to encourage attendance. In short, he doesn't care if his students succeed, but if they do he takes credit cause it was in his "way". Won't plan quizzes so constant stress.

Quizzes and exams are extremely heavily weighted, miss one or do bad on one, you are guaranteed a non-A final grade. He doesn't take attendance but you will not have one single notes if you don't attend lectures. A very tough class with tough contents.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Heavily weighted on pop quizzes with 1-2 questions. No HW grade and only two exams. If you dont pay attention and fail quizzes you're done son. Could be an easy class but he makes it very difficult due to the grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of examples and is good about communication; however, he is demeaning to all students. The class is virtual so maybe he is just not good at communicating through piazza, but he is very incredibly rude. 100% would not recommend.

As a grad student, I've been taking college courses for 7 years. Prof Johnson is easily the worst/most disrespectful professor I have ever had. He makes it very clear to everyone that he has no sympathy or care in the world for the students. Quizzing students on material yet to be taught and mouthing off to students are my favorites.

Professor Johnson knows how to teach you stats. He is the best professor I have had at Tech! He is funny and really cares about his students. He gives pop quizzes and clickers, so as long as you go to class, they really help your grade and prepare you for exams.

Dr. Johnson has been my favorite professor at tech thus far! He teaches the material thoroughly, yet in an interesting way. Class is not mandatory, but he gives pop quizzes and clickers that really help your grade. The quizzes and exams are fair and based on the homework. This is definitely one of the few classes I have enjoyed going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson will teach you statistics. Many people really hate him because he is not nice to the students, almost to the point of making fun of us. However, his tests are fair and he does lots of examples, so I think he is a good teacher. He will let you skip the final if you have an A and makes you get a physical clicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Go to class each day + listen, you'll get an A. HW optional, pop quizzes. Get old exams/quizzes-he reuses them+do HW IMO: I HATED this man. He's arrogant + demeaning to students. If he's wrong or makes a mistake, he acts like he meant it + that the students are idiots for thinking he could be wrong. That said, he isn't unfair, but VERY IRRITATING
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: General Johnson is honestly the best professor I've had at Tech thus far. If you attend lecture and take good notes you'll be fine (he doesn't post annotated notes online as he writes on the board during lecture). The exams and quizzes are very fair and the hws really help you study. Take the class seriously and you'll be fine!

Honestly the best professor I've had at Tech so far. Very motivational and respects you if you work hard. Not gonna lie, this class is tough. But General Johnson tells you exactly what is required for you to get a good grade. The exams and quizzes are very fair and he never tries to trick you. Highly recommend taking his class.

Johnson is quite the character. He's a great guy but makes this class unnecessarily hard. Takes points off for technique despite getting the correct answer. His lectures are good, but it's very easy to get off task or doze off in the class. Uploaded slides don't have answers to the examples discussed. TA only met once a week for this class.

The general runs his class almost like a stats boot camp. He expects a lot from you while not always making these guidelines clear so he will take off many points for minor mistakes. Pretty much teaches from PPTs. Not friendly to students and sometimes outright demeaning. He does care a lot about the subject but I think he grew to dislike us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: General Johnson is very enthusiastic about the subject matter even though it can seem dry at times. He does grade tough, but is reasonable since he tells you what he wants you to know. Overall, one of the best professors at Tech and he allows you to exempt the final if you have an A going into it.
He's stern, but he's an amazing professor. I enjoyed his class and actually felt like taking it seriously. He sincerely is very interested in the subject and in the student's learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The General is a natural communicator and he seems like a good dude. He does like his tough-guy reputation and relishes being inflexible, so check your syllabus before you email him. He tends to jam though the technical terms too fast for you to sort through it in lecture, but the homework is usually pretty helpful.
Great professor,  but very tough
MOTIVATIONAL

Brilliant professor and clearly a top-notch academic with a lot of knowledge about the history of the field. Comes across as intimidating initially but he's very approachable in truth. You'll learn to think about things differently from taking his class, and it's nice that the tests are very straightforward.

He is really smart, knowledgable and passionate which is great if you are interested in what he is teaching. His tests are pretty much exclusively beaded off his notes and I think he does a great job of testing the important stuff as opposed to the minutia.
Dr. Ackerman is a big name in his field and teaches quite well for a Georgia Tech Psychology Professor.
No Comments

He is a great professor, he really cares about his students. HW is really heavy so it will require lots of work. The only bad thing about him is that he takes forever to grade stuff so you dont really have a way to know how you are doing in class, but in the end he gives everyone good grades just for the effort shown.

I learned a lot and I wouldn't change anything about my experiences. If you don't like the road you're on, pave a new one. Or find a different road. But I stuck with this road, meaning I didn't drop this class.
HOT. Easy enough if you pay attention, which is pretty difficult when you can't stop staring at those perfect eyes...

Starting from this semester of ECE 2020, Chatterjee made the exams be completely open-note while questions remained to be in around the same difficulty as practice exam questions. His lectures may not be a 10/10, but I still love this class!
It feels like he is not interested in teaching. He just goes by the slides and everything can be learnt directly from slides and textbooks.

Grading is 90 percent exams(3midterm 1 final) , and exams r pretty short so it's easy to mess up and get a bad grade. However exams r exactly like the practice tests so if you practice and know the content you'll be fine. Lectures were boring, I self studied most of the content. Practice tests r key cause one small mistake can cost a lot

Lecture was boring and difficult for me to focus in, as he would sometimes take a whole lecture to explain something I found a 3 minute video about on YouTube. Exams are just like the practice he gives out, but be wary, as the exams are 3-4 problems and are 20% of your grade minimum. Exam 3 in particular had very bad partial credit. HW's easy.

I like his attitude. Lectures are very laid back. 2020 content is light, so I would normally skip the lectures because I tend to zone out in class, but the online resources are so bad I had to attend lectures to learn. Tests are very close to homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very straightforward class and grading structure. There were 3 exams and a final with some homework. The exams were exactly like the practice exams, open note and homework as well. Labs are terrible. Chatterjee is a really good guy, very dull and boring but he throws in some relatable aspects and comedy. Would take again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were open notes but difficult, so you need a general understanding to pass. The only grades were a few homework assignments and tests. The topics were interesting, but Chatterjee was sometimes incredibly dull during lectures. However, he knew the content well and was okay going back over things if you ask. TA took forever fixing grade errors.

Dr. Chatterjees lectures are not very organized, and for spring 2022, we only had 4 weeks of class in person because he was ill. Not very accessible outside of class but he prepares students for tests by giving practice tests. Also homeworks are a good way to learn content without going to lecture

The tests (and final) were exactly like the homework and he even allowed open note, so it's free. His teaching is okay. If you read the materials ahead of class you will understand what he's saying and it's actually pretty fascinating how knowledgeable he is. If you expect to learn only from his lectures then you won't.

Prof Chatterjee is a good lecturer but is very unorganized and changed the syllabus course weights 3/4 through the semester. Once you understood the content and could do the homework, the exams were doable.  I would take him again, just be prepared for a lot of self teaching.

Chatterjee was a decent professor, he taught the content well. The homework was hard but the tests were easy and open note. He was unorganized but not really to the detriment of the students. Overall the class was just average, not bad but not great, an ok choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He grades on few things. But, if you do good on tests you're fine. There will be makeup lectures and all tests and the final is open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class moved very slow as we spent lots of time on lectures. Most of the course (60% for me) was based upon test scores but he allowed us to use our notes so each test was an easy 100. The HWs are simple and the labs are too, although please find a myDAQ to borrow because you don't use it enough to justify the $250 cost and get parts from the HIVE.

The class started off very slow and by the end of course I would venture to say we covered like 40-50% of course material in the last month. He leaves zero feedback on tests and homework. Chatterjee was an alright teacher and I learned a lot but I would personally recommend some of the other professors with higher ratings. Was still decent overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chatterjee taught us a 2nd year class as though it was 4th year. This might throw some people off, but I thought it was a good approach. Exams were modeled after the HW questions, so class was an easy A. Lecture content was good, but was very repetitive since a lot of students kept asking the same thing worded differently. Would recommend

He's a nice guy, but his class is completely unstructured. We were so far behind that we spent half the semester on something that should've taken a week while rushing through actual important content. Rarely answers emails promptly, lectures are a mess. Luckily, the course content is easy enough where you can study on your own and make an easy A.

He is not good at lecturing and does not care about his students at all. Takes off points on tests without any explanation. Does not have a syllabus and is probably the most disorganized professor I've had so far in college. Avoid taking him if you really want to enjoy this course.

He's a total mess. He's late to lectures half the time, and his computer isn't working the other half of the time. Loves to take off an absurd number of points on tests for the smallest things. Would avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's just not it. Most disorganized class I have ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Passionate Teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Abhijit Chatterjee has plenty of comic relief build into his lectures, he is pretty funny if your now stressing to figure out exactly what he is explaining. His class is not really difficult he just doesnt spend a lot of time explaining any particular concept. Once I found an outside source to supplement his teaching style I did fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Chatterjee showed up to class late almost every class. One time he was 15 minutes late. He rambles out a bunch of material and then you have to go back and try to decipher what he was trying to say. You really learn everything through the homework. All tests were open notes.
I've had better engineering professors at a community college. Avoid him and you will thank me later...
He's passionate. Sometimes tests are annoying but he curves.

Overall, I think he is pretty good at teaching the material. He goes over it so much that it is hard to not get an A. Plus the tests are open everything. He's just usually late and we are a few weeks behind the other classes. It's an easy A, but you may not get through all of the material. You'll know the intro stuff super well, though.

His lectures are half-decent, but can get very unorganized at times. His lectures are generally not relevant to the material covered in the exams. Also he doesn't seem to understand the concept of partial credit when grading exams.

Dr. Chattergee was most of the time late to class and there was no clear structure to the class. He told us about upcoming tests 1 or 2 weeks before. His lectures were sometimes confusing and you have to do a lot of outside studying and learning. His tests were not too bad and were similar to other ECE 2020 professor's exams.
Often comes to class late and sends out test review materials shortly before the tests.  He seems like a nice guy though.  The class overall is pretty easy.  He gives open book, open note tests.
This guy is a joke of a professor. Late to class every single day, unprepared, often cancels class. Can barley explain simple concepts.

Worst professor ever, doesn't care about the class at all. Doesn't have a syllabus, announces tests just a couple of days before. Sends solutions the same day of the tests. He is extremely bad at explaining what is supposed to be simple material. Awful prof.

Terrible professor, easily the worst I have had at Georgia Tech. I can definitely say that I have not learned a single thing and I might get a B or an A. Among other things, he misses classes and sends out homework solutions the day of tests so that we can quickly cram. Just awful. Based on the other reviews, I guess he has gone downhill.

His classes are the best. He is a very good teacher. Speaks in simple language so that everyone can understand. He assigns problems of moderate complexity which people can solve by going through the class notes.
He was fantastic, but at the end he rushed too much. I went into the final with an A and got a B out of the class. Final was awful!
Great class, great professor. Really wants you to learn the material.

Prof. Abhi's class is real fun and quite quant-heavy. He is fair in grading and really wants you to succeed. My favorite was the group homework component of the class and the interesting problems set up to solve. He encourages active participation and really cares about your learning. Would recommend for sure!
This prof had fake British accent it was hilarious to hear him speak. Aye mate.

Prof. Deshmane was a great teacher overall. He really likes class involvement/participation, and interacting will impact your grade. The vast majority of the class is graded by group projects, which act as "tests" (there are no tests). These projects have no definite answers, however, so they really test your knowledge and research capabilities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he is a pretty sold choice for multi, I think he did a good job with including a lot of visuals and simple explanations for concepts. Quizzes and tests were tough but it is not supposed to be an easy class. Use the textbook, practice a lot outside of class, and go to Professor or TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: omg do not take him; he was a new professor for multi and he originally had like a 4.8 rmp. his notes were bare and the tests were realllyyyyyyyyyyyyyy hard. he told the class that low 70s are normal for calc 3....................................

One of the better teachers for MATH2551. His exams are generally easier than other teachers, and although his lectures can be boring at times, he is lenient in terms of grading, always looking for areas to give points back. Overall, he is a good teacher. MATH2551 requires effort to grasp some of the concepts, but nonetheless I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knew what he was talking about, but tried to explain in math notation that no one understood. He didn't lecture great like Dr. Hunter, yet made his quizzes and tests very similar to his. He was very nice and answered questions, but he was not made for teaching an undergrad math class. I didn't put in too much work and still got a B.

Honestly his style could've been way worse. I think for whatever reason the class didn't do as well as he was hoping and it was partially because no one was using Dr. Lehmann's website to study, which is where he got most of our tests and quiz stuff from. He didn't want to reinvent the wheel for multi.

He's a great person, but inexperienced with teaching an underclassman course. He wrote all lecture notes from scratch with questionable handwriting, so I spent most lectures deciphering instead of understanding. He doesn't post note templates; homework content was not tested. I didn't know what I should know for exams until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tbh I learned mostly from studio, do NOT skip it if ur taking multi it's a lifesaver. Lectures could have been way worse, he's good at introducing topics but usually started losing the class during example probs. i agree that it would have been much MUCH easier if he simply copied the alr typed out notes from dr. lehmann, as his exams were similar

I do NOT recommend taking Prof. Abbrescia for Multi. He was disorganized in lectures, both in his notes as well as when explaining topics. When someone would ask a question on ed discussion, he often replied in a negative way. I do not think he was prepared to teach a gen ed class. I would recommend taking another prof.

he's not exactly the most “student” oriented prof, as i think he prefers teaching mainly upper level math majors so teaching a sophomore math gen ed didn't seem up to him. regardless i think he explained topics pretty well and dr lehman's videos could supplement any lectures you missed. wish he had more office hours tho. made tests decently fair

I see why people weren't happy with Dr. Abbrescia, but I was also able to manage an A without being exceptional or great at math. He did a lot to help us after a really bad first exam by giving us a curve and lowering grade bounds by 3 pts and his other 2 tests were pretty fair, j lots of algebra. Honestly I learned mostly from lehmans videos too

Honestly, I thought Dr. Abbrescia did a good job teaching this course. However, I stopped going to lectures both because of the extremely early time of classes and the fact that the entire class can be taught online. I feel he explains concepts well, but can be a bit abrasive on questions.

Dr.Abbrescia's a brilliant guy, but his teaching methods were just not for me. The class was so unorganized (canvas and lecture notes that were barely any notes at all). I just ended up relying on Dr.Hunter's website. If you can't teach yourself or already struggle with calc, then I wouldn't recommend taking multi with this professor.
Lecture notes are hard to follow and mostly illegible. The canvas page is rarely updated. Quiz content does not match what is stated on the canvas page. Does not give study material.

Dr. Abbrescia is not very responsive to his students and does not like to repeat himself. His lectures were so unorganized and confusing to follow, so I stopped going to them and watched the other professor's online ones. The studios never lined up with the content he was on. The first exam average was a 60...only good thing is that he curved it.

Would respond to all ED Discussion posts except for the ones regarding to practice exams, in which he would just completely ignore, so all we were given to study were studio worksheets and Lehmann's exams.

Literally the love of my life; this man changed my entire outlook on mathematics because of how good of a professor he was. Amazing lectures and was extremely caring. We had the chance to resubmit any homework for a full regrade, which helped me learn the material a lot. Exams were very reasonable. It is worth enrolling at a school just to take him

VERY VERY difficult class so prepare to study and review outside of class ALOT but he is such an awesome professor! Very understanding and accomodating of students needs. He even curved our midterm because people performed lower than expected.

What everyone has said so far is accurate. I took Analysis 1 and Analysis 2 (this class) with him, and had phenomenal experiences both times. Clearly very passionate, and nice to chat to. Very knowledgeable, but above all, extremely good at conveying that knowledge. Often draws pictures to motivate a proof before doing it rigorously, which is good.
Wonderful professor, handsome and chill.
Very clear lecturer, made sure that students understand concepts before moving on from a concept, and is sure to answer all questions succinctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10 homework's are 50% of the grade, all of them are super do-able by your self, and will let you submit twice to correct wrong answers. Replied to my emails either within the day (usually within the hour) or the next day. Very chill guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Bro at the beginning of the semester went over the syllabus, asked us if we wanted one or two midterms. We said one, so he changed it to one. The goat.

Also has HW revisions where you can get full credit.
Great Prof, if you have the chance take him!

He used a cheap microphone with a hurricane wind sound effect. Lectures felt like they were inside a wind tunnel, and the teaching style with many fragmented and repetitive sentences didn't help. All lecture notes appear to be created with an index finger and trackpad. Many students got tired of copying down random squiggles and left mid-lecture.
Difficult to understand is an understatement. His handwriting is atrocious. 100% go to a diff lecture.

Professor is hard to understand during lectures and has bad hand-writing. It's not that bad because lectures aren't attendance mandatory and you can always go to a different section, so if you have his class I would either go to another one or read through the posted lecture notes.

It's difficult to read his handwriting and even more difficult to understand what he is saying. I only attended class to get the extra credit, and I typically spent that time watching the lecture videos or reading the notes of other professors. You can succeed in his class, but only by learning the content elsewhere and paying attention in studio.

Just an awful instructor. Impossible to understand, terrible lectures and handwriting, no idea what he's doing. For 1554 I highly recommend sitting in on another professor's lecture and focus heavily on the studio, as that's likely your best bet to pass this class, not these lectures.

Neto is a really nice guy... unfortunately he just isn't the best professor for 1554. Instead of using Barone's PPTs (which every 1554 professor does) he insists on handwriting and projecting the notes - except his handwriting is unreadable. He also explains many concepts incorrectly. You'll be learning entirely with Barone's recorded lectures.

You can't understand any of his lectures. Most people stopped going to them before the third class. He would make many mistakes in class as well. I would take the class somewhere else before taking him.

There are 104 students registered in my class. For the past 2months, I am one of the only 2/3 students who show up. Don't take this professor. His accent is unintelligible, and so is his handwriting. He doesn't use the whiteboard/ppts/computer; instead, he writes on a messy piece of paper and projects that, but it is impossible to understand.

There were 105 people signed up for this class, I walked into a lecture recently and there were 2 people still showing up to class. He seems like a great and caring guy, but you LITERALLY cannot understand a word he says because of his accent. Avoid taking him, but if you do, understand you'll be watching online lectures from Barone/Mayer to learn

MATH 2552 is probably the easiest math class I've taken at Tech. However, Professor Neto's strong accent and difficulty with the technology made it difficult to understand him so I stopped attending class after the second lecture. But you can learn all of diff eq in studio

Lectures are rough because his English is not very good but he more than makes up for this by being extremely caring to students. Very consistently communicates with TA's course requirements so that recitation is all you need to do well. He's a very nice guy and he is a very good professor in the ways that are in his control.

Once he learned to speak up I could actually understand what he was saying and he actually explains things pretty well. That being said, lecture is not mandatory by any means, just go to studio. His tests are easy and his practice sets are almost exactly like the exams so you know what to expect. Genuine guy trying his best.

Prof Abdon had a rough first couple of lectures largely due to his thick accent and troubles with projecting his voice. After having come back to his lectures at the end of the semester, I can see he really improved his teaching style and speech. He is very kind and knowledgable, and his tests are fair. You can also learn everything in studio.

He is a very nice guy and I can tell he is trying his best, but he is nearly impossible to understand. The class is not hard by any means and most of the learning is done through studio anyway. Tests are very fair and not hard if you put in the work outside of lecture.

Professor Neto is by far one of the worst professors I've had at Tech. I stopped going to lectures the second week because he seemed to be a lost cause with his mumbling, general confusion, and constant mistakes. Either rely on video lectures or on the TA's. His only saving grace is that exams and quizzes are very fair.

Blud, do not take this man. Like I got respect for him, but he is impossible to understand. Class was less than 50% full on the second lecture. Class isn't hard, but when you can't hear anything it's impossible to learn.
Only writes on tiny whiteboard, uses mic wrong, cant hear him, and the words you can hear are unintelligible. Doesn't even seem to understand the content. Should not be a professor.

Attendance wasn't required for main lectures, but studios run by TAs were mandatory. The professor assigned many readings and writing-based assignments. She was very involved during lectures and explained concepts clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. But the lectures were interesting enough. I didn't get a ton of feedback up front, but her office hours were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's just rude. Like in class she seems nice but comments she leaves and emails she has ATTITUDE. Cant stand her tbh.

Mills is solid-- a good lecturer and great with offering resources. For 3127 though, attendance wasn't required for lectures but WAS for the studios w/ TAs. With how lenient she is with access to resources, you don't have to attend many lectures. Be weary of written assignments you get b/c they come up pretty often and are fairly long (1000 words).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Mills is like a breath of fresh air while at Tech. Her lectures are good, and tests are easy if you do the readings. Some of the readings are a bit long, but very helpful for the papers you will have to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Zureick is super laid back and insanely intelligent. His courses are on the unorganized side, but you will learn SO much. He is caring and wants people to learn. What I loved about this course in particular is that he reads through the code and dissects it in lecture, and then does example problems. It helped drill the concepts down.

I LOVE Dr. Zureick. He is so caring and helpful. He is very laid back and does not state due dates or a schedule. He gives 2 exams, a group project, and hw. The hw is average and he is very willing to help during office hours. The exams are a good reflection of the hw and open notes. He is willing to change lectures to what interests the class.

Homeworks in this class is pretty light, but a lot of the grade is from your exams and the research/special problem project. Lectures can be kind of boring. Class is very disorganized as you get very little instructions for expectations of the project, deadlines, etc. Midterm was easy but the final was rough imo

Absolutely insanely amazing. I do not understand how someone can teach such mature and sophisticated topics with such ease, in a way that makes the information as easy to understand as a 1000 level class. The tests are challenging, but are graded with enough lenience that if you have the right idea, you'll be fine. He is also quite funny. Take him!

People say his exams being too difficult and not related to the practice.Yes, the problems are not trivial, but you will be fine if you understand the concepts instead of memorizing the answers. If you expect to not think during the exam and only know how to solve problems you've seen before, go back to high school. You'll be replaced by AI anyway.

Ladha's CS4510 is a gem. His class will train you to think like a computer theorist and solve problems that are too abstract to find real-life parallels for. It is a crucial skill for problem-solving and becoming an actual CS thinker. HWs are very challenging but interesting, so attend office hours. He's very supportive and accessible as well.

Avoid this professor. Assignments, review material, and practice exams do not match exams, and tests have only 4–5 questions, miss one and your grade will be already at risks. 4 exams make 84% of the grade, yet practice exams are not helpful. Even TAs often can't help because the material is far more complex and different from the other professors.

This class is the essence of CS in the theoretical and "parlor-math" side. Proofs are relatively easier compared to CS 3510 and discrete, but make sure they're still sharp. Lectures important, OH for the proofs are EXTREMELY important, and reading the textbook for definitions/practice is important too. I messed up with late HWs (21 credits moment).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. However, his exam grading is really strict and a lot of points are taken on simple things. That said you will learn a lot from this class. It tends to get a bit difficult around exam 3 and exam 4. There are 4 exams worth 21 percent each and around 12 homeworks with some of them having a lot of extra credit and weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is an excellent lecturer and incredibly helpful and insightful for the right kind of student. If you are well-suited for Computer Science (especially with anything algorithm-heavy), you will thrive in this class. If you find yourself struggling in this class, take it as a sign that CS is not for you.

I enjoyed his class, but he's not for everyone. He can be overwhelming since he talks quickly. I learned a lot from his class, probably the most of any class I've taken. If you're willing to put in the work, he's a great option. Would be nice if he had short breaks during class though. Recitation and plus sessions are super helpful, esp before exam
He is the best option. Those complaining lack skills.

He talks about class content for around 20 minutes each lecture and goes off on tangents for the rest of the class. The class is almost fully test-based, and each test has like 4 questions that are worth 25% each. He was happy about a 40% class average on a midterm for the 75% of the class that didn't get a 100. Don't take this guy.

The exams take a while to get used to, but are doable if you pay attention to lectures. All lectures are on YouTube, so coming to class is very optional. Definitely a learning curve in general, but nothing too extreme. Lectures are clear and concise, tests are difficult but not impossible, and homeworks are time consuming.
Tests are hard, but he's fair
Exams are very difficult.

Ladha was appointed by Allah (Subhanahu wa ta'ala) to serve and spread light unto the students of Georgia Tech. During every lecture, you will certainly feel a divine presence. O' Allah, lead the disbelievers to the truth and they will accept Ladha (PBUH) as their prophet.

ladha is a terrible teacher. his intelligence and mastery of discrete is heavily undercut by his arrogance. his grading is arbitrary at best. his exams are extremely long and difficult, with about ~85% of the class still writing when time called on every exam.

homework takes more than 8 hours a week and doesn't prepare you for the exam at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are hard and the partial credit is unforgiving. Lectures are alright. If you're prepared to spend 6+ hours per week on the weekly homework, quiz, and staying locked, you can get a B or above. Just be prepared for a terrible time with TA's, the professor, and in general. Ladha should absolutely be your last choice.

worst class ever. don't even consider just take someone else. he clearly cannot take criticism either. either he or his tas write their own positive reviews and get negative ones taken down. you can tell the positive reviews are super short and lack nuance, unlike the negative reviews. i don't know how he still has a job at gt. avoid.

This is a decently difficult class. He is decent at lecturing, although he moves EXTREMELY quick. Tests are extremely difficult and often nothing like the practice tests, and he tries to fear monger by saying that if you use AI for help, you're cooked - which I don't believe is true. I and anyone probably could have got an A if I tried hard enough.

You can definitely learn a lot from Ladha's class. It's true that people can get lost in the lectures without prior knowledge of the content. He is highly accessible. The course is test-heavy, you'll find some exam questions very similar to practice exams or homework, while the rest are of medium difficulty problems in Leetcode.

If there was not a grade associated with this class, it would without a doubt be my favorite class I've ever taken. Ladha is a great lecturer, and the subject matter is extremely fascinating. The tests are just so. Damn. Hard. And difficult to prepare for. Sometimes studying can feel futile and impossible, but it's fun at the same time. Duality.

His lectures are actually somewhat interesting. But other than that this class stinks. The homework assignments would take me and my friends several hours each week, and are most of the time just overkill and don't prepare you for the test at all. The stuff he gives you to study for the exams are just stupidly hard compared to the exam.
Great instructor. Hands down the best one for this class.
Absolutely horrible. I legitimately think the TA's write the the 5.0 ratings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super passionate lecturer, great if you are genuinely curious about the class. not too hard either, if you go to lecture and actively participate. his textbook and lecture videos make it easy to make up class if you fall behind as well. overall very nice and understanding professor.
Brilliant teacher. Course is on the easier side, but it's been taught very thoroughly.
He is honestly the best option you could take for this class. Hands down.

Ladha himself is a good lecturer and a good person. It's his TA's that make the class a nightmare. Just because they went through hell in their semester they think it's their turn to give us hell back. HW's took 6+ hrs per week and exams had singular questions worth 5+% of your COURSE GRADE. Absolutely do not take this class under any circumstances
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are completely unrelated to homework, test review, and lectures and are worth 84% of your grade. Homework takes multiple hours and is extremely difficult. TA's are largely useless. It's sad since Ladha is a nice guy and a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Ladha is a chill guy. However, it's pretty clear that the expectations of the course don't really align with the reality. I don't think the exams are fairly written and there should be, at the very least, an exam drop for this class (like other CS2050). The TAs need less power though; they practically run the course and not in a good way.

Take if you are 100% sure that you will attend all lectures + solve all homework + all practice problems + spend a lot of time trying to combine your knowledge from the lectures with the extremely difficult practice problems, and expect even more "creative", harder questions to appear on your exam. You need to practice as if this is your only class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT! Super accessible in office hours and all his lectures are available online. In fact, the course should get more challenging.

Incredible lecturer and understands the course material extremely well. Posts all his lectures online and homeworks are pretty reasonable. Very exam heavy with 4 midterms and a final that replaces a midterm (if needed). Exams are difficult (basically 4-5 leetcode questions) but graded relatively leniantly.

This class actively regressed my knowledge of discrete mathematics and math as a whole. If God wished to give his strongest warriors a challenge, he would send students to CS2050 Office Hours to face the awful TAs for this class. Such students would emerge Navy SEALs.  Ladha is a terrible lecturer and teaches content that cater to few. Do not take.

Horrendously terrible. He clearly writes his own RMP ratings (or has someone else write them for him - check the two from 12/2/2025). Terrible lecturer, lectures way too fast, writes awful exams that don't test content well. The homework is near impossible and should not constitute adequate assessment for an introductory class. TAs are evil. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In industry, there is no autograder or project that you can flounder on for days on end until you get it right. There is time pressure, and if you aren't precise under pressure, you are axed. Having a majority of your grade come from test is totally reasonable, get used to it here before it's too late.

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

He's a nice guy, content itself isn't even really that bad, but the class structure is absolutely abysmal. Save yourself the headache and transfer in the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 84% of grade is exams. If you do minor mistake in your proof, you can loose a lot of points. Exam practice materials are a lot more difficult compared to the lectures. If exam materials included like 5 practice exams rather than just 1 practice exam + a problem set with some overkill problems, class average would probably be a lot more higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were way harder than homework and grading is incredibly harsh. Lectures are useless. Avoid at all costs.

Honestly he's a pretty good lecturer. He's very knowledgeable and uses hard examples in class so that test/HW questions don't look like something we've never seen before. I definitely don't like the 84% tests as I got shafted by one and it made it impossible to get an A, but it happens. The problem isn't him, it's the TAs who make bad test review
He writes his own rate my professor rating and deletes negative ones. that should tell you enough.

Exams are a majority of the grades for this class and he stated himself the distribution of grades is an inverse bell curve meaning half the students on every exam get well below a failing grade. On exam 2 I lost 25 points on a problem for not including the method of proof I was using. I would not recommend unless you just love the subject.

The class has gone to dumps. Ladha is a nice guy, ok lecturer….but the structure of this course is truly unforgiving.

The grading is incredibly difficult with no clear guidelines. There is a HUGE lack of communication between him and TAs. 

He admits to making exams too hard but won't do anything about it. My advice - just transfer in this class.

Absolutely ridiculous. Take someone else. Ladha's class is much harder than other teachers. Lectures are very fast and hard to follow and hw is very hard and doesn't prepare you for tests. The tests also have unbelievably harsh grading. Your grade shouldn't be this dependent on the teacher. AVOID AT ALL COSTS, YOU'VE BEEN WARNED.

Exams are deceptively easy; Ladha makes up ridiculous reasons to take points off, almost never related to the correctness of your answers.
Grading on all assignments is slow and harsh.
Lectures are painfully useless. Homework is tedious and does not prepare you for the exams.

Ladha seems to confuse ineffective teaching for rigor. Do not take.

Exams are 84 percent of our grade. Practice exams are much easier than the real exam. Exams have way too many problems for the time allotted (since the questions are very hard). Homework takes 8 hours each week, if you can even figure it out. Every assignment in this class feels like I'm rolling the dice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely splendid. People say he doesn't care about your grade, but that cannot be further from the truth. If you don't want to learn, you will absolutely fail. But if you are willing to learn, to think, and interact with him, you will do good.

Very passionate about the subject material and always made sure to explain thing in detail. I didn't have anything to compare him to but I have heard that his classes are harder than ones given by other profs.

As a professor, Ladha was a good lecturer; however, the class was structured on the assumption that students already have experience in discrete math. Lectures were fast-paced, homeworks required a lot of time and work, but weren't really great for learning, and exams were very difficult.

Professor Ladha is a funny guy at times and is pretty accessible outside of class, however his lectures rarely correlate to what's on the exams and he's much more difficult than other professors. The people who tend to like him are the traditional nerds (no judgement), and the people who don't like him typically have a life outside of their classes

Ladha and the 4510 course he led was definitely one of the greatest course I had at Tech. Lahda has the best lectures. The assignments are all amuzing and inspirational with carefully chosen materials.  Grading aren't too harsh.

It might take a bit of familiarity with proof and passion in math and theory to enjoy. But that's a fair ask.

Not for beginners. He teaches as if you already know the material, only 3 second pause for questions after a problem, and often goes on tangents. Lectures feel like a race to keep up rather than a chance to learn. He might suit advanced students, but as someone who was new to discrete math, I found him incredibly difficult and unhelpful.

Best professor I've ever had at georgia tech. Lectures go really fast and cover a lot of content but are really fascinating. Be prepared to pay attention and ask a lot of questions during lecture though

This course may be a good indication for whether or not a student has an aptitude for computer science and should stay in the field. It is the first CS course that cannot be passed through memorization and regurgitation, and requires interest and ability to do well.

The entire course is on YouTube, which I find very helpful. Not every question is answered on ED, which I guess is ok. I made some friends while taking the course, which was far more helpful than any TA/professor help. Not the worst, not the best.

Ladha is not a proffessor for the weak and disinterested. If you are interested in discrete math or CS theory, definately take him. This class is a great introduction to not only discrete math, but general proof writing, and Ladha will make sure you understand your fundamentals, even if tests can be a little bit hard than other professors.

Homework is long and difficult, generally containing problems that don't help with exams. Exams themself are very tough, and difficult to study for as there are minimal resources in the class. The lectures are face paced, and hard to follow and take notes for at the same time. Overall, more stress than there should be for this class.

Ladha is the goat, as long as you go to all the classes and do the homeworks, you will be fine in the class. He shows clear understanding of the subject, and is passionate about it. Test 3 was hard, and Test 4 was a little challenging, but the first two tests were pretty light. 100% reccommend.
Great prof, teaches concepts well. Class isn't easy but it's pretty fun

DO NOT TAKE LADHA. He is so passionate about this subject but doesn't understand that not every student can comprehend Discrete Math as much as him. He made his own exam which was way harder than other professors. For one exam I remember the TA's telling us it was so much easier than the previous one but everyone agreed that it was much harder,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The 3.3 is primarily because of 2050 reviews, I've heard thats not his priority plus he teaches quite advanced things that freshman cant handle. 

Best prof hands down for 3510, you're doing yourself a disservice not taking him. I know its hard, but if you have to take a single hard class at Tech, this is it and probably the most worth it one too.
Great guy and best class ive taken at Tech. Excited for 4510 w him.

GOAT. If you're at Tech to coast and non interested in learning he's not for you. If you want to grasp the most fundament algorithms with insane clarity then attend every single one of his lectures and annoy him in OHs with any questions, they're almost enlightening. Best prof at Tech imo. Plus content of this class helped me land a FAANG job.

Very tough class imo, but Ladha is a cool guy who is generally pretty sane. I'd recommend taking another professor if you want an easier class, but Ladha ensures that you get a good conceptual understanding of the content which I can say that I got. I didn't like how he lectured as it was super abstract and not applicable to hw/exams.

Ladha goes into more depth than the other professors, and his tests are slightly more challenging. His YouTube playlist of recorded lectures covers all of his lecture's content. His homeworks are difficult and time-consuming, but helpful in the end. He knows this subject very well, and is very willing to help and explain.

Ladha is inspirational even if you already knew about the topics beforehand. If you aren't strong in math (at least 5 Calc BC and the likes), expect to work harder. Exams requires more creativity than the other sections. Office hours are very helpful, and Ladha himself occasionally hosts in-person last minute recitations in the TA office hour room.

Don't waste your time taking Ladha. His exams are unneccesarily difficult and the homeworks are lengthy and hard. The only bright side is that there is extra credit and the CIOS does come in clutch, but everything else is terrible. Take Ronnie or Brito.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures with the catch of going at a very fast pace. The lectures go rapid fire with Ladha and he assigns a lot of homework with new topics. Important note, Ladha added on interesting topics near the end of the course for F24, but these segments were added onto the existing CS2050 work. Absolutely recommended if you are more math inclined!

Don't do it
Take Brito

Literally the greatest lecturer I've ever had. Tests were really hard though, even in comparison to other sections, but the questions were really engaging and fun to do. Everyone giving bad ratings got skill issued. Idek if I have an A but I'm manifesting for finals

Edit: I did get an A

He's a funny guy, and teaches pretty well. Lectures are optional, but they're really good for learning the content.
