I would say this class will teach you algos really well if you go to lecture esp from a math point. Tests are difficult and easy to mess up, so you have to study a lot outside of class but Ladha is accessible. TA's are decent

He's a great teacher and willing to help, but his tests are pretty difficult.

If you're looking for a chill 3510 class take ANYONE but him, if you want a challenge take Ladha.
Usually he will boost your grade by a few points at the end of year.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One thing Prof Ladha does well is teach content relevant to skills required in the workforce. Besides that, homeworks/exams were quite difficult. Little study material was given (no recorded lectures, but had a practice exam for each test and TA-transcribed notes that were okay). Would definitely take a different professor, not worth the struggle.

Algo is a mindset that you need to practice a lot over the semester in order to get into it. Ladha does a good job lecturing, but his lectures are not for everyone. He also really cares about the students. Only main issue I had with the class is partial credit was few and far between which lowered all my exams a lot--but that is mainly a TA issue.

Ladha's lectures are quite interesting, especially if you are someone who enjoys math, but beyond that it's terrible. The homeworks and exams are hard and are incredibly time consuming to study for/do. On top of that, there are literally 0 resources for studying for exams, aside from a mediocre packet written by TA's that couldn't care less.

Overall, this class was tough but definitely fair. Ladha's lectures are good, and the additional lecture notes on canvas were very helpful for homeworks. Exams weren't easy, but there was at least 3% bonus to final grade by the end of the year. 3510 will be easier if you have a leetcode/competitive programming background, but I did fine without too

The professor is clearly very passionate about the subject and topic, but he doesn't necessarily convey the course content in ways that make it easy to understand. You have to put in the time and energy to study the course content yourself. Also, the TA's don't really do much in the course - if you get how the course works you'll get an A.

He is extremely passionate about the subject matter and is clearly very smart, but his lectures often are difficult to follow if you aren't prepared. He is also super chill and very accessible - his office was open every time I was in the computing building. Exams were difficult, but doable. If you go to class and office hours, you'll be fine.

Time consuming hw, but the proofs on the hw and in the lectures are extremely similar to the ones on the exams so you will be well prepared. Ladha gets a lot of hate for structuring his class different from the other 2050s but it's really not that difficult. He's a fun and engaging prof who really wants to teach students as much as he can

Lecture could be a little bit fast but it can be very entertaining if you focus. most of the grade is dependent on 4 test and the test itself aren't too bad. The most test review are ok, but some are very bad but i think it more of a TA/logistic problem. Overall solid prof to learn from

Ladha is incredibly passionate about discrete and an excellent lecturer. He goes far beyond surface depth while also going out of his way to make sure students understand. However, his tests and homework are harder than Brito. I still got a high A and didn't have to spend much time on the class, but I would take Brito if I could go back.

The lectures were highly theoretical, fast paced, and hard to follow at times. Weekly homework was difficult and time consuming, especially if you don't have anyone to work with. If you have a good understanding of the homework and lecture notes, the exams are very manageable. Great if you're up for the challenge, if you want an easy A not so much.
The homeworks are overly difficult and the lectures aren't the most helpful. I found that the textbook and practice questions within it were useful in helping me learn and study though.

A lot of these reviews are incredibly very overblown. Ladha is very fair; he doesn't require you to attend lectures (even though i'd advise so). He also publishes the entirety of his lecture notes, so if you read those you are guaranteed to do pretty well. His HW questions are sometimes hard, but again it's definitely doable using your notes.
was clear on what it took to succeed in the class, tough content but ladha is funny and was even willing to do office hours right before the final. goat

He is very passionate about the subject, and has made me extremely interested in the material too. Other than that, the homeworks are tough and the TA's can't help, with many of them telling me to use ChatGPT to check. There's no extra credit, the exams take so long to be graded, and he teaches in a way where he expects us to understand every step.

Ladha is tough. Had a few tests where our class specifically had a little extra material to cover. But he taught comprehensively and if you want to learn and are willing to put in the work for it, you wont have a choice but to. Tough but very forgiving if you mess up or have concerns about the class. Was late to 2 tests and he let me in to test. A+

Ladha is a passionate and funny lecturer, but the homework was hard to the point where I've had multiple instances where the TAs didn't know how to do the questions. The exam reviews were ok but not the best for studying for the exam. The exams are hard as well.
It was a really difficult course do not reccomend this teacher at all

Lots of conflicting thought. Look, most 'negative' reviews are probs lazy students who didnt study, and 'positive' reviews could be overachievers/TAs. However, the disparity with other profs is HUGE. So much so that many TAs couldnt answer Ladha's HWs. Ok If you like math & genuinely want to learn properly. If not, like me, take Brito/Ronnie.

Lectures were confusing and the professor's handwriting was hard to read. Visual learners will struggle. Homework was graded harshly, exams were tough, and review materials were unhelpful. Miscommunications between the professor and TAs added to the confusion. This class was unusually hard for a 3-credit intro course. Would not take again.

It's my 2nd year here. I understand that discrete math itself is not rainbows and puppies but Ladha's lectures are not great.. especially when you have no background knowledge of any of this stuff. I've watched a YT video and learned more in 20 minutes than his 75 minute lectures. Ladha's passionate/funny, and well, that's all I can give him.

Ladha is clearly used to teaching much higher level classes. His lectures, while entertaining, are theory heavy and often don't correlate with the exams, especially past the halfway point. The class basically requires you to have at least some math theory background knowledge. If you don't, take Ronnie. Your grade will thank you. He's funny though.

Actual paid reviewers dropping 5s. You can't tell me that a class that gives out prep material 3 days before the exam, with bad TAs who don't even know what they're talking about, combined with a lecturer whose lectures are over random niche proofs rather than actual surface material that we should be going over is good in any way. Save your sanity

Professor is overly hard and every other professor is easier. Practice problems were nothing like on the actual test. Lectures are useless and not useful and he goes way too fast. Highly don't recommend.

Take Howard or brito. His homeworks and exams are much harder and HWs have completely unrelated material to the exams. TAs are completely useless and are about as knowledgeable as the average student. Ladha just thinks he's Tony Stark of discrete math or something.
Ladha's lectures and homeworks are very different from the exams and are always much harder than the other professors' exams/homeworks. Save yourself the headache and just take Ronnie if you can.

Ladha is extremely smart and knowledgable. I hear "what--is going on?" about five times a day from the collective class of students. I was never able to catch up on what he was lecturing about until I got to the HW and was finally able to understand. Exam 3 was EXTREMELY hard and is what killed my grade. Probably getting a C unless final is easier.

The worst 2050 professor you can take. His lectures are WAY too focused on theory and fast-paced, his exams are harder than other sections, and his homeworks are the worst. The exam review feels basically useless and answer keys are rarely even given out. DO NOT TAKE.

Worst professor at Tech. He wants only the 10 students who sit next to him in class to succeed. His exams are separate and super hard there are next to 0 resources provided for studying for exams. A practice problem set is provided, which is very different from his exam, and also no solutions to these practice problems are uploaded. DO NOT TAKE HIM
His test are way harder than other proffesor, his avg for exam 3 was around 70 while other classes had high B avg

He breezes through content because he assumes it is "too easy" for everyone and often skips explanations of proofs because he "doesn't wanna" explain. TAs don't know how to do the HWs, so if you were to ask for help, there is a guarantee they will not be able to help out. He said he had a psychotic episode making exam 3- that is was "hilarious" :(

Ladha's lectures are too theoretical and fast, the first 2 exams were on material we covered weeks ago so it was hard to remember. The homeworks are way harder than the exams, and the grading is also harsh, with partial credit given for certain types of mistakes, meaning you could lose almost all the points on a question from a very minor mistake.
Tests are way harder than other profs. Only take if you've done competitive math in the past.

Unless you have an EXTREMELY strong math background take anyone else. Lectures are overly theoretical. I gave up going to lectures and had to rely on Howard's lecture videos (which were only released the week before exams) to learn everything before the exams. Difficult homework that is different than other sections. Exams are graded harshly.
Do not take 2050 with Ladha. Take anyone else. His tests and homeworks are wayyy harder than every other teacher. His lectures are extremely confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he's a amazing lecturer, and he always writes elegant proofs. However, he goes very fast, so be prepared to learn a lot in short time. Overall, the class is pretty good and I learned a lot.
Lectures were excessively heavy. Wasted time covering useless material with no clear purpose. Content covered in the lecture was very different from the test, and was impossible to keep up with.

AVOID HIM. The absolute worst 2050 prof out there. Apparently a good prof for other CS classes, but his lectures don't correspond to the exams at all, are extremely confusing, and are useless as he only goes over theory-related material barely related to the course. Please, for the love of God take Ronnie Howard; his online videos are why I passed.

His lectures are too heavy on theory. While his first 2 tests are based on more other sections taught by other professors, the 3rd test was made by him for his class specifically, so it correlated more closely with his lecture, but the problem with this is you never know what to expect on a test.

Going to his lectures is pretty much useless. His lectures are fast and very easy to fall behind in. He assumes you already know a bunch of higher level things, even though this is a freshman class. I learned more just by doing the homework assignments than anything he ever taught in lecture. His handwriting is barely readable in lecture as well.

I took Ladha for both 2050 and 3510. I really like his teaching style though I know it is not for everyone. He just lectures and writes on the board and then leaves lots of time for questions. His 2050 and 3510 were probably more difficult then the other sections but is very approachable and one exam is dropped in both classes.

No textbook required (which is actually a bad thing for this class).
Lectures are fast, with unclear explanations, and harder compared to others.
TAs take long to grade, are bad at explaining and unresponsive.
Exam prep material given out extremely late. One time it was 5 days before, not joking.
You can't teach yourself through this class. AVOID.

The lectures are based on getting practical experience with more complex examples of the topics you fill face in your homeworks. Ladha doesn't simply teach for you to pass an exam/do HW, which I like a lot.
Very good at answering questions during the lectures.
Very good at explaining.
Greatest prof so far at Tech, would definitely recommend.

His lectures are complete trash. His notes don't help at all. He doesn't understand how his students feel one bit. I was so lost in all his lectures and he always gets distracted by some fringe topic that has nothing to do with the class.

This class was outstanding, thanks to Professor Ladha's incredible teaching. Despite the challenging content, his generosity in grading and crystal-clear explanations made it manageable. Truly an amazing and inspirational professor!

I loved this class and Ladha is a great professor. The content is difficult but he is generous in grading. He's also really good at explaining concepts. The best part is he records everything on YouTube, so you can go back and watch lectures you missed or didn't understand. 10/10 class.
3510 can have some tough topics and Ladha does a pretty good job of articulating the algorithms. He gives a good amount of extra credit but this class is still a grind.

If you practice study guides and rewatch his recorded lectures carefully, you should be fine for the tests. Professor Ladha also gave a lot of extra credits near the end of semester, and he was even willing to curve the final average via CIOS. He is also very reachable through email or office hours.

This man singlehandedly made me want to drop out of school because of how disorganized and useless lectures were. Almost none of the material covered in the lectures was even comparable with the homework, which was graded harshly. Please for the love of god choose anyone but him for discrete math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ladha is a respectable professor and does a great job accommodating students. However, his lectures don't fully align with test material and homeworks (first time teaching this course). I recommend doing the canvas modules and practice exams. TA office hours are helpful for homework. No $60 textbook required but instead will be replaced by quizzes.

Ladha is one of the best professors ever. He was extremely passionate, gave very clear lectures, and was dedicated to helping students on Piazza. He's also hilarious. If he is ever a 4510 professor again, please take him.

He is gonna make u think you are about to get a B in the class the entire semester. And then right at the end he fixes it. Trust the process. I didn't believe him at first either. But trust. He's got u.
This class is fantastic to reinforce/fill any gaps if you have already started leetcode/ competitive programming. If not, I suggest waiting another semester before taking.

Hearing about the other teachers, Ladha seems like the hardest one.  His tests were very conceptual and each had an extra credit problem.  Also released a bunch of leetcode type questions where if you were top of the leaderboards, you got bonus points added to your overall grade.

He is a nice professor. Our class didn't even have to by the Zybook because he thought it was unnecessary and too expensive. CS2050 is a very easy class, and I feel like Ladha would be a better professor for harder classes.

For the first few weeks I attended lecture, however most of his lecture content was more theoretical. I skipped class and started watching videos from Ronnie, which was somewhat helpful. if you have a strong math education before college, this class should be light. If you are like me, you need to put in a little extra effort.
Nice professor, but lectures are pretty high level (so they don't relate much to the exams). Exams definitely aren't unreasonable, but they're not easy.

Lectures moved at such a pace that it was either way too fast or just simply off topic trying to prove something we didn't need to know for the exam, very difficult to write notes or pay attention for over an hour unfortunately.
For 2050, he likes to yap. In general, a pretty helpful guy.

Extremely hard professor. There are 5 tests (one test is dropped), which is a lot of work for a class! Lectures are very theory-based with no examples to prepare you for homeworks or exams, which are both super challenging and time-consuming.

His TAs all will confidently lead you in the wrong direction. Don't listen to them about anything. During exams only listen to the Head TA or Ladha himself if he shows up. For homework don't post on piazza, dont use the TA office hours. Just, if u can, get a hold of Ladha (which is very difficult).
Professor Ladha is very passionate about the content he teaches. He is very clear and articulate when presenting his lectures and is very accessible outside of class for questions.

He clearly loves the content and can teach very well. However, the tests are biased heavily to people who are either very smart and can come up with creative solutions or have seen extremely similar problems before from their leetcode journey. If you have one or the other of those traits, you should be fine.

He is one of the most passionate professors that I have had at GeorgiaTech. He was enthusiastic about the content and built an environment conducive to learning.  He clearly conveyed why the concepts matters despite the abstract nature of the topics taught (this is quite a miracle, I hope to have more professors like him)

Much tougher professor compared to the other 3510 professors. Clearly very knowledgeable but not very engaging during lectures. Said in an email he expects students to come out "on their hands and knees." 1 exam every 3 weeks (4 regular exams + Final). Averages for exams were high 70s to low 80s. Homeworks are difficult and time consuming.

Ehhh, not the best lecturer, but doing his homework and preparing for his exams do help for solving interview type problems. Just read his notes (if comprehensible), do some of his practice problems, and watch relevant MIT OpenCourseWare videos

The other rmp reviews are hilarious, you will get violated, and go to hell and back from his 3510. Its a lot harder than every other section, but he is an amazing lecturer and the TA's provide amazing plus sections. By doing Ladha's class you will know how to pass an interview, his course is practical and seriously useful.

Professor Ladha is an extremely caring and charismatic lecturer for 3510. He makes sure everyone is on the same page, taking frequent question breaks during lecture that help regulate the pace. Always available to help in his office, even late at night.
I have lost hope in life due to taking this course. Before, I had dreams of becoming a successful software engineer at FAANG. Ladha put me in my place - the streets.
Lectures seem to be a presentation of his personal research interests as opposed to effective lessons. Grading for his extremely difficult homeworks and exams are all over the place.

The prof is challenging, but the course improves your skills for cs interviews. Teaching assistants often cancel their oh, and it's also difficult to get assistance from Ladha outside of class due to the lack of office hours. However, you will learn a great deal, although finding external support for this course can be particularly challenging.

Not sure why everyone's glazing. He is the hardest 3510 professor and the class genuinely ruined my confidence in myself. The practice exams are unhelpful and there is less opportunity for practice problems in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is the hardest CS 3510/11 prof. BUT he will get you a job. Here is your strat: take easy classes if you take Ladha that semester, and make this class your main grind. Apply for all the highest paying CS jobs and practice the concepts as you also do the neetcode roadmap. Don't follow the neetcode solutions, make your own based on class info.

Extremely challenging class. I heard that other professors for 3510 are way easier from classmates. 
Homeworks and exams are extremely hard and take a considerable amount of time to do well. 
Lectures are quite confusing and not helpful towards homeworks or exams. I had to use online resources to learn the curriculum.
Its insane how smart he is. Like actually. Take him, you wont regret it. Also someone please him an whiteboard eraser.

He's a cool guy but has never taught Discrete Math before. His lectures are a mess and don't really have a structured or organized format. Honestly, I've had to learn everything on my own using supplemental lectures and YouTube and the ZyBooks, he is a horrible professor for Discrete. I feel so lost and I know I'm not alone.

Idk how this class is going from a grade prospective, I think the class average in the class right now is a 74% which is kinda insane. Most kids straight up have a C in the class. The exams are incredibly hard. BUT my leetcode abilities have never been more cracked. So if you need a job take ladha. Hopefully he chills out after DP, so the GPA survi
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer but the problems really stem from how 2050 is run. Ladha doesn't know what's on the homeworks and he never goes over how to do problems in way the TAs are happy with(the TAs grade the homework). This means that even if we somewhat learn the concepts in class, we can't really apply them on the homeworks.
The TAs are extremely unhelpful on piazza and give unclear and short answers when asked about topics
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor seems like a respectable man, but his lectures are messy and disorganized. As a result, he is bound to miss key concepts and important details that other classes cover. The HW are graded by tough TAs, and his messy teaching style only makes it harder. Your best bet is to buy the ZyBook and teach yourself. Also, lots of HWs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The TAs for this course are the most unhelpful TAs I have ever experienced. During office hours they give conflicting answers and they give unthoughtful and unhelpful responses on Piazza. I cannot wait for CIOS to give this feedback so hoping this is seen before then and TAs can actually help.
Studying for tests is very important for a good grade. Lectures are very compact.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor with engaging lectures and taught very thoroughly. He was super helpful during office hours and really cares about his students. Class is 80% exams but exams are fair and have lots of extra credit. Receiving an A requires hard work but if you go to all the lectures and understand the homework, it should be relatively easy!

One of my favorite professors at GT! He really cares about his students and does all he can to help them achieve their best in the class. Great lecturer who's very good at explaining the concepts well and making this difficult material interesting. Homeworks are difficult but prepare you well for the exams which are always graded fairly. Take him!!

This guy is a G. Absolutely love his teaching style and methods. He's knowledgeable and cares a lot (even tho he doesn't show it). The content is also really crucial for CS careers and is super interesting. Take him if you get a chance; I promise you won't regret it. #loveladha

I want to share a story about why I like this professor so much. One time after lecture, I wanted to prepare for Exam 3. So, after lecture I went to his office to ask some questions. This man patiently and kindly went over all 15 questions on the practice exam with me for the next *two hours* on a random Wednesday evening. He is a treasure.

CS 3510 is a hard class but I think Ladha makes it as fair as possible. Great lectures and the tests are reasonable. A bit too much homework though (seriously, and multiple times they made a homework due only 6 days after it was assigned)

Great professor, though a little math-heavy at times (especially in the first unit). The course is made to be manageable and the TAs are open to allowing extensions on homework when needed. Though he might not be the easiest option, he is worth taking to learn the content since this is the most important class you take as a CS major.

Ladha is an amazing professor. His lectures are thoughtful and engaging, he responds to questions on Piazza almost instantly, and he listens to his students. Tests are difficult but not too bad. Going to his review session the day before helps a lot.

Excellent professor for CS 3510. Does his best to make the class manageable and to make himself accessible to students. Lecture style is great, it's clear that he's well-versed in the content and enjoys teaching it.

Look up abrahim ladha on soundcloud

Great prof. Great lecturer. Even better singing voice
Was a really good professor overall. Great and charismatic lecturer overall
It might be because he's a young lad but it makes algorithms very fun to learn.

Great course! He is definitely one of the more difficult professors for this course but you'll end up learning a lot. His exams and problem sets provide a lot of practice. Very generous with deadlines and offers a lot of extra credit on tests. Allows you to exempt the final. His lectures can be a little math heavy though.

The lectures were a bit overwhelming at the beginning, mainly because no notes were posted on Canvas. However, as the semester progressed, typed notes were added and more practice problems were released. There are also 10-15 pts of extra credit for every exam. Overall good lecturer, but sometimes he brings up topics that are too hard for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ladha is extremely intelligent and flexible. TA's are amazing and provided many resources. I didn't attend lecture since the professor taught at a level too complex for learning material for the first time, but read the book/watched Abernathy's lectures. I would recommend office hours/actively doing the HW to prepare for tests.

The prof is great overall. He makes a lot of mistakes in the lectures, but a ton of resources are provided for us to learn from. The people who hated the prof either never wanted to learn something themselves apart from the lectures or they wanted free grades. The TA team is pretty solid as well and does all they can do to support the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I never attended lectures but he posts extremely detailed notes for his lectures on his website and he follows the textbook very closely. If you are stuck on homework he releases practice problems with answer key. I always felt prepared for exams. Grading can be BS but gives 2% CIOS Bonus plus rounds grades up plus drops and exam and homework.

His lectures can be confusing and I ended up learning a lot of the later material on my own. But he has a generous grading policy and goes above and beyond to give fast feedback. He gives test grades back within two days, and will give the test itself back so you can see exactly where you lost points. You can tell he cares about his students

Ladha is fine. Not great, but not the worst either. He's impossible to follow in lecture so you'll learn pretty much 95% of the content on your own. Homeworks are really tough but they prepare you very well for the exams (plus there's generous extra credit). While he isn't the best teacher, he is very in touch with students and a chill guy.

Professor Ladha is deeply knowledgeable about the subject and the lectures are rather engaging and well-paced. He is not 100% perfect but will dedicate time outside the classroom to resolve whatever issue you might have.

Professor Ladha really cares about his students and it shows. He is extremely accessible outside class and is always ready to help students with HW. He's extremely passionate about the topic and it's fun to see new perspectives on things. Exams are pretty decent and HWs might take some time but they are fun as well.

Prof. Ladha is really interested in teaching the subject and tries to help students. The class was confusing in the beginning, but it got a lot better as the semester passed. He extends the homeworks and makes the exams decent. Overall good professor.

I am taking CS 3510 with Abrahim Ladha, and I think he's a great lecturer. He gives clear proofs and examples of the algorithms we go over in class. Abrahim is also very accessible after classes and is able to provide counterexamples and thought-provoking ideas on the fly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult. The professor almost recites the textbook in class, so if you don't understand it in class, that means you don't understand the textbook. There are no additional resources because the algorithms are taught in a specific manner with certain constraints such that outside examples have differences. Just horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think prof. Ladha is a great person -- he seems considerate, nice during social hours, and overall a cool dude. Unfortunately while Ladha is a great person, he is a terrible teacher. I try my best to follow along with lectures, but Ladha jumps all over the place and doesn't explain what he's doing. The exams/homeworks have been tough but fair.
He was a good teacher, and it wasn't really necessary to go to class. The exams are not super difficult, but the homework assignments take forever and are extremely advanced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were unengaging and by the end of the semester there were probably less than 10 people who would show up. I had to self study all the topics for the midterm and final which ended up being fine. Most of the grades came from the homework/projects so that helped a lot. He also gave us 3% extra credit added to our overall grade.

He cares about the class and is helpful if you ask, but he struggles to connect with students or make the material engaging. Lectures are long slide walkthroughs not reflected on exams. You're expected to learn SQL, Excel, and Orange on your own. Practice exams help, but most learning is self-taught, and in class content is not helpful.
Very intellectual guy, just not know how to teach a class.

Really interesting class, he is a really chill and funny guy, but lectures were dry, but you don't really need them for the assignments. Cool to see new ways to make business processes better including work with AI agents. Mainly includes group and individual assignments on various ways to improve business processes and individual work in SAP.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took him for 2210, literally so easy. i went into this class scared because of the previous rmp reviews but if you just study you'll do fine

Had Prof Gardiner for 2200 & 3745. He's a nice person, but very boring lecturer, so its hard to make yourself go to class. His exams are always tricky & require a ton of studying. He pulls from the readings for the non-coding part of exams. There is a project in 3745 as well as coding challenges and HW that help your grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dudes rude. Class is super boring

This rating is meant to help future students as well as Adrian Gardiner if he is reading this:
The teacher only taught about theory in the class, speaking at about 15 words per minute. He taught a total of about 3 classes on the technicals of excel and SQL which is OUTRAGEOUS considering the homeworks included FAR more than what we learned in class

Prof. Gardiner was a amazing professor! The lectures might be boring, but he tries his best to make it interesting! A lot of readings and memorization for the theory exams. SQL/excel exams were easy As and the homework had detailed instructions but it was more of learn it yourself. Overall, the class wasn't that difficult and there were EC

Professor Gardiner was very kind, however, kindness doesn't mean you know what you're doing. This class is very much a teach-yourself class when it comes to SQL and Excel, as the functions he taught in class were very beginner, but the functions required for homework were extremely advanced. This requires us to do most learning on our own.

The lecture videos were quite monotonous, so it was hard to focus. The slides and textbook are your best friend. Yes, you need to use both unless you're just a really good mcq test-taker. The SQL/Excel exams were doable As, but the theory exams & final were worth more and were difficult. He's willing to help with exam review. Hw was hard. No EC.

Horrible at writing exams. They are super nuanced and require absolute mastery of the material. There is often 2 or 3 correct answers. The HWs are long and complex. The lectures are dry and boring. Exams often require 15+ hours of study time. Hes just bad at writing exams. Do yourself a favor and take anyone else.

His lectures can be a little "boring snoring" (a phrase he uses) but he's a good professor and he cares if people learn and is willing to help outside of class. I feel like his class wasn't too difficult  as long as you're studying and doing the homework. I took him for 3745 (Python) and 4057 and he was pretty chill for ITM which can be intense.

If the goal of this class was to discourage the love of learning, 10/10. Professor should not be in a position to influence anyone with an impressionable mind. The plethora of Shein orders, antidepressant research, and suicide contemplation conducted by 95% of those in attendance should give any administrator pause in how this class runs. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor gardiner is truly knowledgeable and incorporates applicable and relevant content into the course. Grading criteria is fair, though there is a vast amount of content covered for the conceptual side of the course, so don't fall behind. Overall, if you put in a decent amount of work, you should do fine.

knows his stuff, but lectures are boring. do not expect him to teach anything on the homework in class. the hw is incredibly hard and you pretty much have to teach yourself, which is very annoying. and the instructions on the homework can be more confusing than helpful sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Put enough time in this class, and an A is totally achievable. Work hard on homework/assignments, and Gardiner is very helpful in answering questions so long as you're not just trying to get easy answers. To study for exams, memorizing the lecture slides and using common sense is enough. Lectures are dry, but Gardiner is super caring and helpful.

One of my favorite professors at GT. Super kind, super helpful and accessible. He's seriously underrated here.  2210 is historically the hardest class in business school, but he made it super manageable. He also is freaking hilarious without trying. Exams (60%) are a piece of cake if you study the slides. R HW is a nightmare, but only 5%. 10/10 guy
Professor Gardiner is a really good professor, I would recommend taking his class.

Professor Gardiner really cares for his students and wants you to succeed. He is quick to respond to emails and answers all queries! I would recommend taking his course to learn a lot about information systems.
Professor Gardiner is not a tough grader, but you have to get ready for the exam for sure. His lecture is kind of boring, so it was hard to focus and wake up during the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gardiner is a great professor! Very knowledgable on the topics at hand. His lecture style is more of a monologue, so it isn't for everyone, but you can tell he cares for students and wants you to succeed. Lots of homework/weekly assignments in this class but nothing too 'over-the top.' Highly recommended if you're into data analytics!

Professor Gardiner is really caring. He gave clear guidance on each homework and I learned many skills like R, Tableau, and SQL. He respond to emails fast and solves many questions. Great teachers! His lecture is not that interesting but it is his style. Recommend!

Boring lectures - I could barely stay awake in his classes. As a professor, he is very knowledgeable about SAP and friendly but just doesn't know how to engage with a class to keep everyone awake. It seems as if he is talking to himself during class, often forgets a lot of things as well. Lots of homework throughout the semester, tests are fair.

Adrian is the slowest, most boring professor at Scheller, but he knows his stuff. If you care about SAP and all that, this class will help you become well acquainted with it. However, the tests are very difficult because it is hard to gauge what he is trying to teach us in class.

I took 2 of his classes, MGT 2210 and MGT 4057. Can't speak for previous semesters, but his online class for Spring 2021 runs smoothly without technical interruptions. A really caring professor and actively tries to accommodate for many people, and will help you out if you communicate with him. Grading criteria is clear, and he is a good lecturer.

(Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) Avoid him if possible. There is so much work. Especially during a semester where we all needed extra support from professors, he just drowned us in assignments and projects. Tests were incredibly hard. He also is incredibly hard to listen to, as he's incredibly monotone. Try another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took course online in fall 2020 due to coronavirus. Gardiner had no idea how to conduct an online course. He was extremely disorganized, often not telling us about assignments until two days before they were due. Software was needed to complete the assignments and he would forget to post download instructions to Canvas. Class isn't easy either.

Professor Gardiner is a very kind person. His lectures, however, are extremely boring and it's difficult to pay attention. The homework assignments are difficult, and if you don't study intensely for the test and know many details, you won't do well.

Very nice guy, very accessible through email/office hours. Not the greatest lecturer, and does take attendance, but the homework assignments (Excel/SQL/R) aren't too bad. Tests are the hardest part of the class but even those only require a few hours of studying for a B; since nobody pays attention during lecture they require reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Das connects course material to real-world examples. She occasionally goes on tangents, drawing on her own experiences and broader scientific topics which makes the class fun. The class required significant studying. I appreciated the open-note format, though she mentioned that future offerings may be closed to internet access.

Instructor was an expert in the subject matter and taught with a lot of enthusiasm. There was lot of opportunities to score through homework, quizzes, and open exams to promote conceptual learning. However the lectures was fast pace with occasional misalignment between lectures and exams. The FRQ portion of the exams were hard.

The class was engaging and rewarding . Dr. Das's enthusiasm and emphasis on understanding the “why” behind complex pathways helped me move beyond memorization. The course felt like a meaningful exploration of metabolism pathway and strengthened my appreciation for biochemistry as I pursue medical school.
Dr. Das's class brings enthusiasm to every lecture. Its a like a morning cup of coffee. She made the first class of the day truly engaging, and she is really accessible to the students.

This class prepared me for metabolism and the TCA cycle, which is great for MCAT. Real-life examples made complex ideas fun and memorable. She didn't make us memorize TCA cycle which was a big relief.  The mechanistic approach in the class and challenging ‘what if' questions pushed my thinking. Overall, I liked the class.

Professor Das is an inspiring, and dedicated educator. She really makes you think. If you don't like critical thinking and synthesizing information then don't take the class. She truly cares about students' growth.

Dr. Das is an engaging professor who explains complex topics clearly, making learning smooth. Her class is applied, with thought-provoking exams that go beyond lectures. HWs are tough but graded easily. Extra credit helps a lot. TAs do all grading, so office hours help. Her class is structured, supportive, and manageable.

Course was reasonably organized, engaging, and intellectually stimulating. It is application-based, with problem sets and exams that emphasize critical thinking. There are also a lot of easy quizzes. The professor is supportive and creates an inclusive environment. Exams are challenging and office hours are helpful. Gets you ready for med school.

Professor Das is sweet and explains complex concepts clearly, making learning enjoyable. Her class is highly applied, with thought-provoking exams, even with open notes. She is respectful, inclusive, and genuinely cares about student success. TAs grade tough, attending office hours helps. She fosters a welcoming, supportive environment.

Exams are challenging but mildly predictable based on what she says in lecture. Application-heavy; nitpicky is a good description. Extra credit & recorded lectures are super helpful. TAs grade hw & exams so go to their office hours for help. I would recommend Dr. Das, she's very nice and knowledgable. TB not needed. Overall not stressful

GREAT slides. No textbook/external reading or work needed. Very prepared to teach. Exams are tricky and grading is kinda nitpicky (open note/slides though); little practice material given before exams. Very caring and sweet lady, she will help you / answer questions fast. Grading scheme seems scary, but so much extra cred offered it isnt too bad.

Dr. Das is a good professor who cares about her students. I do feel like the tests could be difficult because they were always much more advanced than what we talked about in class and there was no study material available besides your notes.

Best professor at GT hands down. So engaging and definitely knows his stuff. Class is pretty difficult because of how much content there is to learn, but if you put the work in, you'll see the results you want.

Decker is a nice guy but his class was harder than it needed to be. Attendance is technically not required but his slides are all images, so you need to be there to actually receive relevant info. His exams were also wildly hard in my opinion, exam averages usually hovered around a C. If you lock in and take really good lecture notes you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His ratings are high for a reason. He makes lectures for a course that is almost strictly memorization entertaining. Anatomy always ends up with the worst lecture times and locations but it is always worth going. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would strongly recommend going as he sometimes tests material not in the slides. Very caring guy too.

I was really struggling with anatomy and school/life  in general. He was the only professor that took the time with me outside of class to help me. I will forever be grateful for this man. I wish more professors on campus cared half as much as Dr. Decker did.

Hands down my favorite course at GT. I appreciated the course was very challenging and I was up for it. Dr. Decker takes difficult concepts and breaks them down in a unique way so we understand. We just finished drawing the brachial plexus and although challenging it was fun to draw along with him on the whiteboard. I can't wait for Human Pathology
Amazing lecturer, easy tests based off his slides, and overall great guy. He's also more biology-focused than the other 1040 professors if you're into that

Human Pathology was hands down the most useful class I've taken at GT in my four years. I working a summer job in a hospital in my hometown and I'm able to shadow a cardiologist. The cardiologist said, “where the hell did you learn all of this?” I simply said, “Dr. Decker at Georgia Tech.

WE LOVE DR. DECKER! Genuinely the best prof I've had at GT. Lectures are engaging, go to them! Even if you can pass the class without attending, the things he says in person will stick with you for the rest of your medical career. Exams are a bit tough, make sure you deeply understand the content and are not just memorizing. Flashcards are a must!
He has an insane amount of respect for his students and offered really cool extra credit opportunities. The lectures are kind of boring but prepare you well for the tests.

Dr. Decker was my favorite professor at Tech. He was very involved in his students' improvement and I highly recommend him for any class. The class requires memorization but after taking anatomy with him it was much easier. Physiology is a plus to have before or during this class.

Lectures aren't mandatory but contain the important information so attendance is heavily encouraged. He is very knowledgeable on the subject and genuinely wants to help students learn, an A is definitely achievable with regular attendance since his lectures are digestible and he tells you everything you need to know for exams
I'm taking human pathology with Dr. Decker.  The content is med school based, and I feel very prepared to take pathology when I get to Johns Hopkins this fall. Amazing professor!
Best anatomy and biology professor!!!!

One of the most respected professors on campus. You get out what you put into the course. It's a tough class, but taking Dr. Decker created a wonderful learning environment; even for 8 in the morning. Take any class he offers.

Dr. Decker is a great anatomy professor. He makes it engaging and interesting, which is hard to do. Weaving together personal stories, history, and facts, he makes lectures worth attending even at 8AM. Tests have a lot of content and are closed note, however, they are designed fairly. Great prep for pre-health people; I cannot recommend him more.

Amazing lecturer and tests are pretty straightforward. The resources provided outside of lectures are very lacking so make sure to attend lectures (no notes available outside of class and difficult to self study).
Anatomy has been difficult but I'm doing well. I wouldn't get behind in the course. One of my GT favorites I've taken

Favorite class yet! It was not too hard. Just study the lecture slides. It was very interesting if you are pre med. He does interesting in class demos with volunteers. He is so nice and helpful if you have questions. I had to reschedule an exam once and he made it very easy.

Dr. Decker provides amazing lectures to the students because he tells real, applicable stories during class. The course consists of a midterm (in-person), 5 quizzes (online), 3-4 case studies, and a final exam (in-person). You should attend class because he highlights and narrows down important information that will be on the assessments.

Dr. Decker's human anatomy is a tough class, but very important if you plan on going to med school. I took the course last year and plan to take his human pathology course this spring. I highly recommend his classes. He genuinely cares for his students and is very approachable.

I loved Dr. Decker. He truly wants everyone to do well in his class and gives you plenty of opportunities to succeed. Beware however, I took this class Late Summer 2024 and it moved incredibly quickly. Exams were in person and tough. Make sure you prepare!
Dr D. Was a very caring professor and mentor, the class was valuable.

I had Dr.Decker for the Ignite short summer semester and he was AMAZING. Even though there was more emphasis on tests because of the short term, tests were easy and had questions based on lectures and study guides. He is also a very caring professor who radiates good energy. Plus he gives plenty of extra credit.

Was a great lecturer and pretty funny although conversations can get sidetracked sometimes. Was very nice on the final by making it pretty easy (compared to the quizzes). Very clearly passionate about what he teaches and it makes the class very enjoyable.

Dr. Decker is a wonderful lecturer and amazing resource for pre-med students! His knowledge of medical schools (which he talks about during lectures) is insightful into the application process. He also knows how to make class both fun and engaging. The course is hard, but very doable given proper studying!

Dr. Decker is phenomenal! I have never met a professor who cares more about his students. Attendance isn't mandatory but I would highly recommend still going to classes as the quizzes do have material not on his slides. There is now an in-person final, but if you keep up with the material throughout the semester, it's very doable. Highly recommend!

Such an inspiring professor for anyone planning on going into the healthcare field. This was one of the few lectures I really looked forward to attending each week. Quizzes are online and a little difficult, but the final was in person and was pretty basic. He is funny and his lectures are super interesting. AMAZING PROFESSOR!!

Dr. Decker is very knowledgeable about anatomy and highly respected in the field. He is an awesome lecturer, and I looked forward to going to class each week. Attendance is not mandatory, but you must attend lecture to understand content because lecture slides do not provide all relevant content. Quizzes were all online. Great professor!
very nice, funny teacher. you must take the class honestly throughout its duration or you will not do well on its now in-person final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As the course just ended, I can give my honest assessment. Human Pathology with Dr. Decker was a phenomenal experience. My best friend is in his 2nd year of med school, and I showed him my course notes. He said they cover the same material. I was never prouder of Georgia Tech to hear that. This course will prepare you for sure. I love this man!

I wasn't a fan of Dr. Decker for anatomy, but he loves the pathology course and it really shows in his teaching. Classes were entertaining, engaging, and informational! Exams were tough and a lot of memorization but definitely doable!

Dr Decker is the most amazing professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech. He inspires you to learn and is so motivating and caring. If you go to lectures and take notes he tells you exactly what you need to know to succeed in this class. I plan on taking every class at Tech he offers just because of how amazing of a professor he was.

I am a second  year medical student at Vanderbilt, and it was Dr. Decker's human pathology course that helped me choose cardiothoracic surgery as my future specialty. The man is a gift and an inspiration to all who take his courses. Easily the most practical course in the GT pre-health undergraduate curriculum.

Amazing professor. Attendance isn't mandatory and all assignments are taken/turned in online, but it is absolutely worth it to go to class. His lectures are entertaining and he made me so excited to learn about the topics covered in this class. The material is easy to follow along with if you pay attention.

Great professor and a funny lecturer, he can go off track and fall behind in lectures sometimes by telling stories, but his stories are great and they are worth it. He occasionally brings in organs/bones in class for students to inspect. All quizzes are online, and our final was online. There are 7 quizzes 4 case studies and then the final.

I am in medical school and took Dr. Decker's Human Pathology course in 2021. Out of all the classes I took at GT, this class was the most applicable to what I am learning in medical school. My current pathology professor has been very impressed with my knowledge. Thank you, Dr. Decker! You are a GT treasure.

Dr. Decker is one of the greatest professors there is. His lectures are always incredible and never fail to make you laugh, and he teacesh anatomy in a way that makes it easy for anyone to learn and I couldn't imagine taking it with anyone else. If you have the opportunity to take his class, you have to do it, it's an experience you shouldn't miss.

I was recently accepted at the Emory School of Medicine. Dr. Decker, and his Human Pathology course, gave me the confidence to apply to such a great medical school. His knowledge as a human anatomist is unsurpassed. I will never forget what this man has done for me and my classmates pursuing medicine as a career. All CT is derived from mesenchyme!

Dr. Decker is a great choice for anatomy. He's so knowledgable and passionate, and never fails to make lecture engaging. It is helpful to come to class since some of the information is sometimes not listed on the slides and the slides can sometimes be disorganized. That being said though, I would definitely recommend him to anyone!
I took this class over the summer and he managed to make lectures for entertaining and easy to understand. All exams where taken over canvas at home. Great guy.

It's helpful to come to class as you may not always find everything you need on slides, but he keeps lectures very engaging and interesting. You can tell he really cares, and he's happy to help students with anything even outside of course material. You certainly need to keep up with material but the course load isn't too difficult.
I was going through a very difficult time last semester, and Dr. Decker was the only professor that took the time to listen and encourage me. I will forever be grateful. Just a great human being!
I took Dr. Decker for human pathology. Hands down the most useful pre-med course at GT. Loved every minute of it.

Decker is the best! This class was more focused towards anatomy and biology than I originally anticipated, but it was honestly pretty easy. I took it during the summer and all of our tests were online and there was no final. He's very passionate about the subject and a great person, and the class is an easy A.

Hilarious and understands that most people are there because the class is required. He makes it easy to do well in his class and the lectures are actually interesting, even if you don't care about anatomy. Also provides really cool out-of-class experiences that you normally wouldn't get as a non-science major (like holding a human heart).
I love this man!
Easy class- light work and easy exams.
Took him during summer semester and he made lectures interesting. 10/10 recommend
He's the best

Dr. Decker is as humorous as he is kind, and he's as kind as he is smart. And he is very smart. As for his lectures, they're informative and clear. You'll know what the tests assess, and if he goes on about another topic, he'll make it clear whether you need to know about it. 

Also, enjoy the day 1 icebreaker. You'll feel right at home!
He is leaving tech to teach anatomy in medical school. I took him  in 2018, during New Zealand/Australia/Fiji study abroad, and it was a great class. Thank you for everything, Dr. Decker!!

Pathology was an excellent experience. I am so glad I got to take anatomy and pathology with him. I hope it's not true, but there is a rumor he is leaving GT this year to teach at a med school out of state. He will be missed and I wish him well.

I had Prof Decker for human anatomy and have really enjoyed the course. A must if you are going to med school. he seems to have the class geared in that direction. Kind and considerate to his students.

Very passionate about anatomy and really engaging in class. Make sure to write down everything he says as his quiz questions are pulled directly from his lectures. 4 straightforward case studies and 8 or so quizzes that can trick you up if you aren't studying/paying attention to what he says in class. Overall a very cool and likeable guy

I am currently in human pathology. We covered our first case study and I found myself hanging onto every word Dr. Decker said. He actually uses students as demos which really makes the study come alive. I want to be a cardiologist, so I am excited to get to cardiac pathology.

Given the pandemic, I found out the course was modified from what is was previously, so I dont know how hell have it set up in the future. I think he mentioned all testing will be back in class, so online tests will most likely be no more. I found the course thoroughly engaging and very informative. Dr. D. has a true passion for the material.

Tests were open-note, but I still feel like I learned a tremendous amount in this class despite it being so. Don't fall behind in lecture and review the material every day, and you're guaranteed an A with him as your professor.

Dr. Decker is a great lecturer and really passionate about the course material. He'll be the first to tell you he's not super concerned about your grade in this course, he cares more about preparing you for the next phase in your education. You definitely have to work for your grade, but it's a great class.

Dr. Decker is very passionate about anatomy! The class content is generally going to be tough to learn just because it's anatomy but Dr. Decker makes it engaging and fun to learn by sharing these hilarious, relevant stories & mnemonics. Very caring & enthusiastic. I am a visual & kinematic learner so I didn't have cram/stress bc of how he taught.

I am taking human anatomy with Dr Decker and the lectures are very engaging. The man loves what he does for sure. I am definitely taking pathology in the spring. I have been on the fence between biomed engineering and medicine and he has changed my outlook. Seeing the cadavers in lab is something i am looking forward to

I took this class for the summer short session. I was loaded with other classes so I didn't attend his lecture, and was able to get an A by looking at the slides he sends out. His lectures are really interesting and diverse, so I would say go if you can, especially if you like anatomy.

Professor Decker is awesome. Lectures are super interesting and he is really fun. Tests are easy (if you take good notes) and assignments are simple. Has a delorean which he let us see which was really cool.

I had Dr. Decker for 4 classes: Anatomy, Pathology, 1040 and Cardiac Diseases. He was tough but fair. In Anatomy, dont get behind on the readings in Moores. He uses some of the book on his exams. The cadaver prosections were really cool. Holding organs was the highlight of my undergrad studies. Highly recommend him.

Dr. Decker did a great job with Human Pathology. The USLME step 1 style questions at the end of the course were difficult by doable. I am so ready for med school next year thanks to this man. He is a GT treasure.

Dr. Decker's an expert, no doubt about it. He's lecture-heavy and can be dry to listen to, but he gives an amazing foundation in Anatomy for anyone Pre-Health. He gives lots of acronyms to help you remember, and regularly reminds you not to wait til the last minute to study for his class. So, take good notes & pay attention to the little details!

I love Dr. Decker. He is very knowledgeable and good at conveying that knowledge in an engaging way. He sprinkles in lots of stories and anecdotes. I feel that I learn a lot in lecture. The tests are challenging because of the large information volume, so make sure you study.

A lot of students were screwed by the end of the semester. It is not recommended that you take him online. Maybe in person he is better when there are four exams and 1 final. He ended up dropping an exam and having the final over a small section with questions unlike any of the past tests. Seemed really inconsistent and it tricked many people.

Backloaded the entire semester and you grade through your first 3 tests is a joke. The self proclaimed most accommodating professor of the 21st century... it seems course stability is lost when too much accommodation is made and students who work very hard and get 4.0s are, by chance alone, left to get lower grades than the rest.

I love this man! Taking human anatomy online is not ideal, but he has made it actually enjoyable. Tons of information and detail, but the course is laid out perfectly and well organized. I cant wait to get back to campus and shake this professors hand. I hope I can take the human pathology course next time he offers it.
Pathology with prof Decker was an outstanding experience. I am currently a first year med student at Emory and am already using the info he taught me in path and anatomy.
He's the best! Very knowledgable and really wants his students to get the most out of the Health requirement.

Had him online for short summer session. His teaching format was powerpoints with attached audio narration on each slide. He seems very passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting and engaging. He also adds some hilarious jokes in there. Really cool. Down to earth. The assignments teaches you about yourself. Take good notes.

Dr. Decker is a laid-back professor. I had him for the summer session and he was really understanding. The lectures, although some students find them drawn out, were really interesting. He makes jokes during the lectures. Assignments are easy and tests are mildly difficult if you don't study, though I can only speak for the online version of APPH.

His assignments were very easy and his exams came straight from the lectures. He's very specific about what is going to be on the exam. Lectures can be long but some parts are pretty interesting because they're applicable to real life.

Human anatomy with Dr. Decker was a great experience. I attended his human neuroanatomy seminar he conducted for the GT neuroscience club last fall. He used real human brains and spinal cords. We were all on the edge of our seats as we learned internal brain structures. Im taking pathology when he offers it next.

I am really thankful that Dr. Decker teaches at Georgia Tech. Because it is a research school, there are not many health base classes or professors that understand that some students want to become doctors. I am just so grateful for all the work you have put into anatomy/pathology for us to further our careers as physicians.

I had Human Pathology with Prof. Decker. The course was an upper level senior course and I worked for my grade. All the content was med school based and I feel I have a good foundation for medical school. I am applying to Emory and hope this class gives me an edge. Cardiac pathology was my favorite especially all the fetal septal defects.

Dr. Decker is a great and caring professor with a thorough understanding of the content he teaches. He occasionally goes off on tangents on material that isn't of importance, but he really does a good job of preparing students for pre-health programs and future anatomy courses. Given the course is anatomy course, memorization is key.

Dr. Decker is awesome. One of the funniest professors you will ever have. This guy is brilliant, but he knows that if you're taking 1040 you most likely are there just for the credit. He understands this and makes the class as painless as possible. Take him, you won't regret it.

He came in on his own time Sunday morning to give us a review for the big joint and muscle test this week. He tests on origin, insertion, innervation and action. He knew it would be our most challenging test so far. All I can say is start studying early! I will definitely take him for Human Pathology.

Dr. Decker is one of the preeminent anatomists in Georgia. This man loves what he does and is a valuable resource if you plan on going to graduate school in any healthcare field. He presents the material in a way that makes you want to come to lecture. He is also using human prosected cadavers in anatomy lab. The whole experience is outstanding!

Dr. Decker was so much fun, especially since his content could be boring at times. He teaches a mandatory class for all students, so I'd recommend getting his if you can. He genuinely cares that students learn something helpful from his course despite it being mandatory, and I feel like I did. GO TO CLASS because he gives exam hints.

Dr. Decker is THE BEST. He is so funny. The tests can be a little specific so make sure to actually study but he does give a lot of extra credit. I took this in the summer and he always let us leave like an hour early. Super chill guy!

Human Pathology course was outstanding. He introduced USLME licensing board questions to prepare us. I feel very ready for medical school .Dr. Decker loves this stuff and always gives 110% for each lecture. Watch out for exams . Your hand will be cramping after doing 4 -5 pages of essay style questions and case studies. Excellent course,,
Not too hard of a class if you put the time in. Heavily tested on small details and diagrams. He really cares about his students and loves what he teaches, but class can get a little boring.

Super easy class- tests are 100% a memorization game. But, you'll also have a ton of fun in the class and you will actually retain the information you learn. Though I believe I still could've ended with a 98 without attending, do attend the class!! Dr. Decker is engaging and funny, he really cares about his students' success. Awesome dude!

He's just a good-natured person who genuinely cares about what he's teaching. I took it over summer short semester which was over a 2-hour class, but he knows how hard it is to sit and focus for that long so he made it fun and often gave us breaks. He made what would normally be a boring class, amazing. 10/10 would recommend. Easy material.

I had Decker on Pacific Program, and I'm actually writing this review before even finished the class. Wonderful guy, absolutely hilarious, and very straightforward with his class. First day of class he told us "This is a 2 hour class, and I will treat it like a 2 hour class." He clearly also knows A TON about the subject, and is passionate.

Dr. Decker is an awesome professor for human anatomy! He always adds clinical examples and fun tidbits to accompany the lectures which keeps me focused and interested. His tests are very detailed and get into the nitty gritty of everything he covers, but I feel like I learned a lot in his class and had fun doing it!
I took this over the summer. So much material crammed in to such little time. Was a total of 6 or 7 lectures at 3 hours each. If you can, just take it during a full semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Decker is a great lecturer and a great guy. The tests were a little difficult, though, especially for APPH 1040. But I would take the class over again just for the lectures. You can really tell that he is passionate about the subject, and it rubs off on his students.

I had Professor Decker for human anatomy. I can honestly say I walked away from the class with a greater understanding of human anatomy that I will certainly take with me to medical school. He was extremely knowledgeable, caring and went above and beyond most teachers at GT. Take Dr. Decker if you plan on going to  grad school.
Very funny, very clear. Class in general is not the most exciting but he definitely makes it better.

Professor Decker was very knowledgeable in human anatomy. He took what could have been a very dry and boring subject  and brought it to life with many clinical examples. He made the course very relevant if you are going into a health professional field, like med school.  I will be taking him for APPH 1040 when he teaches it next.

I just finished my first semester in a graduate DPT program. Dr. Decker's human anatomy course saved me. I found myself teaching others in my class. I will never forget "skunkus in my uncus" highly recommend him for any class.

I took this class in the summer and the lectures were really long. There were only 2 exams and contained a lot of information to memorize. I wished Dr. Decker would take his time to explain the material rather than skip some of the major topics that are on the exams.

Dr. Decker is an amazing anatomist. The class is so relevant if you are going to graduate school, medical, dental, PT, etc... His lectures are clear, to the point and engaging. You never want to miss class. He has been my favorite professor so far at GT. highly recommend!!

Dr. Decker is a great instructor. He teaches everything you need to know in a very clear & precise manner. You'll need the book for the online quizzes. But his tests come directly from his ppts and lectures. He makes the lectures interesting with stories and facts from his past. Attend lectures because he'll give you answers for the tests.

I did bad on my first quiz. However If u spend the whole afternoon before each test you will easily get an A. Just study from the power points and memorize them by hear. I aced the remaining tests easily. Don't even buy the book. Just buy the access code online which contains an online version of the book.
I am really enjoying Dr Decker's class so far. He has lots of student participation and everyone seems engaged. He is easy to listen to.

Class was pretty boring, but Dr. Decker has some pretty good  stories. Tests are m/c and directly from lecture slides. 3 tests, 3 online quizzes, 2 easy assignments and one essay. 5 extra credit points are available on final average

Great professor. Makes health class actually interesting. Don't have to show up, but you might want to anyways. Also, easy A as long as you study for the tests and do all the assignments, of which there are not many.

What a refreshing professor.  I just took the summer session   and have to say I really enjoyed it. Dr. Decker was engaging,funny and very knowledgeable.  I will definitely recommend his class to my friends.
He is one of the better health teachers, but don't expect like high school health. You will need to put effort into it
One of the best HPS teachers. Fairly easy and gives easy opportunities for extra credit (up to 4 points on your average). Attendance not mandatory or necessary.

Great professor. Really cares about students. I hardly ever skipped a lecture. Not that I was interested in the material, but he made lectures interesting with his enthusiasm and humor. He tells you pretty much all of the details you need to know for the tests and they aren't hard. I studied for an hour or 2 the day of the exams and did fine.
It was a very informative class. Dr. Decker made a class I thought I would dread, very good. I would definitely recommend him. He is well prepared and always seems to have a smile.

A very nie man. He joked around a lot and tried to make the class not as boring as it actually was. He told lots of interesting stories in class. He would tell you what would be on the test the class or two before the test. We had the opportunity to earn 4 bonus points on our final grade. He gave a study guide for parts of 2/3 tests we had.
Best EE professor at Georgia Tech

Professor Adibi was awesome. Had him for ECE 3025 (not listed as a code) and was one of my favorite ECE classes. Amazing lectures, covers a lot of ground but in a way that made me interested in the subject and engaged the entire period. Exams were tough but he always had review sessions outside of class plus lots of EC.

Dr. Adibi is a fantastic lecturer who is clearly very passionate about the material in this course. Participation can grant you extra credit. While the homeworks are challenging, they are graded generously and also provide opportunity for extra credit. Exams are fair so long as you understand the examples from class.
Not knowledgeable, does not teach what would help you in future; try keep students interested by giving credits, while skipping his responsibility to teach useful material

He is a great teacher. He teaches very difficult topics in a way that everybody can understand. He asks questions during the class and offers extra points for that. For his grad courses, you can easily get A. So respectful, friendly, and caring professor. One of the best teachers I have ever had during my education.

Great guy, with a great way of teaching the course. Gives you extra points for answering correctly in class. Doing all your homework can get you up to 5% extra credit. Not an exceedingly strict grader either. Very approachable and all in all, a great teacher.

Great teacher, easy grading policies - 2 grading schemes based on whether or not you want to do the homework (+5 points if you do). Wants everybody to learn alot and do well in the class. Hands out extra credit points for class participation.
This guy is great!

Ada teaches super important OS fundamentals pretty well and provides a ton of insight into how the systems we learn about have affected the world. Midterm + final are pretty difficult, and there is some ambiguity on projects, but overall one of the better classes I've taken.

I strongly believe that anyone with any passion for computing should take this class, you learn about so many foundational papers and implement some of them in very interesting papers. Only downside is the TAs are not too helpful as they all say different things and constantly grade wrong but can be rectified with a piazza post

This course has the workload of 2-3 courses and needs to be rebalanced. Though the projects are super hard, the tests (midterm + finals) make up for 50% of the grade which is unfair as not everyone tests well. I also frequently ended up watching lectures on the same subject on Udacity to understand things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ada is a great professor who is able to break down complex papers into easy to digest lectures. (while she does highly recommend actually reading the papers, I was able to get through using only lectures.) The tests and projects can be difficult, but overall I learned a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took GIOS through the online MSCS. Projects in the class were excellent & very challenging. Unfortunately, the grading is imbalanced with the midterm & final weighted 55% of the final grade. The exams are also short, poorly worded, & almost no feedback, so they dampen an otherwise excellent class. I really wish they'd rebalance the class.

Prof. Ada cares about her students. She lectures well and knows the material inside out. Grades her tests very leniently. The projects we did (DS labs) were difficult, but rewarding. The TA was also very knowledgeable. Definitely would take again!

Difficult to understand as she speeds through topics in rote fashion. Can't keep up unless you are already familiar with the material, but then what's the point of her teaching? Basically worthless if you are actually trying to learn something. You're better off studying a good textbook, otherwise, the class only serves to validate prior learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The projects are the most difficult projects I have done in the grad school. There are 46 papers to read in the entire semester. The exams were not so difficult but to prepare for the exams it takes a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome summer class! Learned so much about sensing methods and designing future devices. Assignments were engaging, and Prof. Adams was generous with guidance and resources. Put in the effort, and you'll create a project worthy of your résumé. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health sensing!

Super hands-on course with real health sensing tools like ECG, EMG, and RESP. Projects were practical and flexible, and there were no exams, just meaningful work. Alex is an amazing professor who genuinely cares and provides excellent feedback. One of the most unique and useful classes I've taken at Tech. Highly recommend!

Great intro to health sensing with hands-on use of ECG, EMG, RESP, and more. Alex is a supportive instructor who gave thoughtful one-on-one feedback and cared about our success. One of the most unique MS courses at Tech—covering biosignals, sensors, software, and many topics of your choice. No prior experience needed. Would definitely take again!

Alex is a very kind professor. I had minimal coding knowledge going into this class, and he and the TAs made sure I was supported throughout the whole course. The class emphasizes process over a perfect final project; if you show effort and growth through your work, you'll get a good grade (and likely learn some new skills, too!)

This is an enjoyable, project-based course with a strong hands-on component. Through practical labs, we learned various techniques for processing health-related signals. Professor Adams is approachable and fairly lenient with grading. He's also very supportive when it comes to helping refine the research topic for our final paper.

I really enjoyed Health Sensing and Interventions with Professor Adams. The class was interactive and project-focused, with hands-on work using real health sensing hardware. No exams, just meaningful projects that helped me apply what I learned. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health tech and biomedical applications!

I could write a dissertation about how badly Prof Adams handled this class. Opaque grading criteria, always late to class, docks grade points without explanation, barebones lectures, little to no meaningful feedback on assignments, left all the actual work to his poor TAs. I get it was the first time this class was offered, but good lord. Avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 10/10 Love this guy.

The best thing about him was he didn't read of the powerpoint and made us understand the lecture but one thing is he writes most of the stuff on white board so if you sit really back you probably wouldn't see it clearly but overall still the best one I have had at tech
Answers all questions throughly and doesn't read off a ppt. My goat
