Great teacher. Clearly passionate on what he is teaching. He explained everything really well and did a great job of creating connection between the class and real world applications.

Even without being a professor and teaching for one semester, he is the best you can get at GT: Easily understood lectures, numerous metaphors for concepts making them easy to grasp. As long as you attend lecture (they are a good time), you will get an A. He is just that good. More professors need to look towards how he teaches o7
HE CAN AUSTIN MY ADAMS I LOVE THIS MAN SO FUNNY. NOT A REAL PROFESSOR BUT HE'S THE PEOPLE'S PROF!

Got put on the spot to teach 2110 and did an amazing job with it. Super funny guy and very knowledgeable about the content, he had no problem answering any question thrown his way even if it was out of the scope of the class. Class is very project heavy (50% of grade) and content is not a walk in the park but Adams made it enjoyable and manageable.

The GOAT. Not even a real Professor, but he's a Professor in my heart. Piazza posts were fire, class was fire. Real zoomer energy, super approachable. Probably my favorite teacher this year; knows what he's talking about too, so not just a set of jokes in a trench coat but actual good educator. Wish he could teach the rest of my sysarch classes.
my heart goes out to this man
godbless his lectures and office hours
Greatest esquire.

This class has very little example and lots of derivations. He tends to repeat derivations that he already did the class before rather than doing actual examples. He's very accessible and helpful outside of class but he can be a bit condescending at times if you don't understand immediately. Overall he's pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Prof. Extremely helpful outside of class. I struggled in Defbods, but he helped me out a lot.
His lectures were really good and he posts all of his notes online. Tests were fair, study the homework and practice problems and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great at teaching the content of the class. Makes it very easy to understand.

Dr. Kumar is an incredibly kind professor, and he makes the material super easy to understand. Sometimes his lectures can be boring, but he posts all his notes later on. He was always willing to talk after class. The tests were pretty easy if you did the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome professor Biochem 2 is a p hard class. Grade is just 90% exams and 10% quizzes - quizzes are open note. Exams are straightforward for the most part but you definitely need to study for them and he provides a fair study guide and practice exam. He's really knowledgeable on the topics and good at explaining!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is knowledgeable and passionate about the content. Course is exam heavy so if you don't do well on one it may be very hard to recover but the level of difficulty is fair. Only complaint is the pacing of the semester, we spent way too much time on easy topics and flew through difficult concepts and processes. Funny & engaging otherwise.

Dr. Oyelere is an extremely educated man that KNOWS biochem but can not teach it well. This class was very poorly paced with him FLYING through the harder concepts in class. Would be better if this class was recorded and his teaching SLOWED DOWN. Near the end, I left class confused. Also he really didn't know how to use/organize Canvas rip
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams ask about small details he covers while on tangents during lecture. Uploaded notes are incomplete and surface-level; no lecture recordings are uploaded. Even though I went to class almost every single day, I still couldn't understand most of what he covered without spending hours learning it myself. The saving grace of this class was our TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were super disorganized and the slides were super unhelpful for studying. He speaks so quickly, has really poor transitions between concepts, and just does not explain things well. I probably learned 5% of this class from him and the 95% rest from YouTube. Exams were fairly easy but there was basically 0 review/prep material for them
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm guessing that the difference between current and previous semesters was the modality, but if you can take him in person, avoid it if you can. Lectures were extremely poorly paced, and tests were badly designed, which doesn't make sense for a class almost entirely graded by exams. Very little structuring or support materials, and no crib sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs for this class. Terrible lecturer, no practice or homework, and we are behind Biochem 1. Worst communication I've seen in a while. Even with GT documentation, he will not follow up for exam remakes. Class grade comprised of exams only and two random concept quizzes. Poorly paced and condescending. Tests don't reflect content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is so weird. Nothing feels to match up and exams take up so much of the grade. If you can take another class, do it!
Super bad lectures and exams. Cant understand anything he is saying and then exams are completely different.

Organic Chem is a hard class, but Professor Oyelere made it interesting and possible to learn. He is very passionate about what he teaches which inspires me to learn the material. If you read the recommended book and use his lecture notes, you can do well in his class. Only thing I'd say is he speaks relatively fast and grades on few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyelere is an amazing professor. He's very kind and wants to see his students succeed. His tests are fair and test knowledge mainly from his lectures. Best way to succeed in class is to study his lecture slides and review corresponding content from book.

Loved Dr. Oyelere. He is extremely passionate and very willing to help students understand the material. His tests are moderately hard, but he will always test what he covers. Won't be an easy A but won't be a hard A either. Fast-paced lectures; you'll get through a lot of material in a short period of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyelere was a very fair professor. His tests are moderately difficult, but nothing that you wouldn't expect. He provides sample exams and opportunities for extra points. However, lecture is sometimes hard to follow as he has a strong accent and can talk very fast. He is very approachable and is enthusiastic about Biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very enthusiastic about biochemistry and you can see that when he teaches. He made me love the subject even more despite its inherent difficulty. He will help you if you ask. Attend every lecture, pay attention and take notes and you'll be good. Accent takes getting used to but you do get used to it.
Grades incredibly harshly, test averages were in the low 60's high 50's. I took the course since many people gave him a high RMP rating, but I honestly regretted taking thermo with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steinberg is phenomenal. AE2010 thermo-fluids is an extremely difficult course, but Steinberg made the material very clear. The homeworks are hard, as are the tests, but the TAs and professor grade rather generously. The lectures are optional, but I strongly recommend going. If it is too early for you, the professor posts the lectures online.

Genuinely great professor. The course isn't easy, but Steinberg really does his best to make sure his students understand both conceptually and practically. As long you as also put in the same effort as he does, you'll do fine. Tests are open note, open book, so they can get pretty difficult

Steinberg was a great professor, and his lecture style was beneficial to my learning. He explains concepts which we then apply in the homeworks (41% of total grade), but also does a few basic examples in class to help students. Tests are extremely difficult, but open notes and textbook, and he is a very lenient grader. Would recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Steinberg is a decent professor. Early on, he mainly lectures without examples, making concepts harder to apply. However, he improves over time, balancing examples and lectures better. Homework is challenging and heavily weighted. Exams are very tough, but the class is curved, so doing well is possible if you do a LOT of practice.

He somehow made me pay attention in an 8 am lecture. His examples were great, and the slides and lectures were very informative. The grading structure is very forgiving, as is the curve at the end of the class, and he tends to be very reasonable with how much homework he assigns.

Prof Steinberg is flat out amazing. 2010 is now one of my FAVORITE courses and a huge amount of that credit goes to him. He connects the material to the real world and for me that was one of the most interesting parts of lecture. He always answers questions positively and is very caring and involved in helping his students learn.

Professor Steinberg is one of the best professors I've had at Tech so far. Along with being super knowledgeable, he's also incredibly caring: I had a panic attack before our exam, and he let me step out and take it at another time. 2010 is notoriously difficult, but if you go to the lectures and stay caught up with the material you will be fine.

Other reviews are correct in that Steinberg is very knowledgeable and knows the material well. That said, he's definitely still approachable as he really enjoys teaching and engaging with students about the material. Exams and material will push you. Exam averages were around a 65, but ~80 is an A. Overall great professor.

Exams designed to make you think and averages were ~60. However, grades are determined by HWs (worth more than exams). Steinberg is very knowledgeable about the material and is always willing to answer questions. Don't be intimidated by him, he wants you to succeed. Very approachable outside of class and go to lecture. Take him, you'll learn a lot

Prof. Steinberg's exams are awful. Problem sets can take upwards of 10 hours, and the exams have questions that could have been on the problem sets. He also uses mixed units on his test problems, that seem designed to trick you. Generally, he is accessible, and seems to want you to succeed, but is not lenient on any sort of grading whatsoever.

Prof. Steinberg might initially come across as intimidating, but he is actually a great professor and really accessible for questions. You can tell he puts effort into lectures and making you understand the topic. Going to class is my biggest tip, you'll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: During remote instruction, gave quizzes that required going to lecture AND live office hours. They were recorded with accessible notes, but this increased the time investment of this class from 3 hrs to 5 hrs. Final exam average was a 45, no curve, with an A being >80. Very difficult class with dense subject material, but you learn a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A great professor. He always tried to do a small demo at the beginning of class (particularly nice for an 8AM) and his lectures are very interesting. He clearly likes the things he teaches and is very knowledgeable about them. One things is that his tests are very hard (average between 50-60) but heavily curves them and your final grade.
Interesting lectures. He knew what he was talking about and could answer any questions. The tests are rough, averages being 50's and 40's; however the class is heavily curved.

Since the other two comments are misleading (Gesundheit), heres the truth. First Test Avg 52 after the curve, and it was big. Second Test Avg 58 after curve. The class was always dead silent. Steinberg is intimidatingly smart which I think prevented anyone from asking Qs. He cares ,maybe. In office hours,I sometimes felt belittled.
Professor Steinberg is an awesome and caring professor who wants all of his students to succeed. Gesundheit!!
He is very passionate and knowledgeable on the topics.  He is a tough grader on essays, but he gives enough opportunities with projects and participation to make up for it.
HONESTLY A HERO

Dr. Afflerbach is great. Interesting/engaging lectures. While he can be a little bit of a tough grader on some things the main thing he's looking for is effort. If he sees you're trying, you will be rewarded. Any time I needed help or had any questions his feedback was always EXTREMELY helpful. I would recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Afflerbach was an amazing English teacher! You can really tell he is passionate about teaching. Although there was a lot of reading, it was interesting and the discussions we had in class were always great. And go to office hours! He always gives very helpful feedback and seems to genuinely care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Afflerbach is the kindest and coolest professor I have had so far. His classes are very interesting, and the projects assigned are very manageable. Though there is a lot of outside reading, be sure to do it so you can participate in class. 20% of the grade is participation. Afflerbach is very responsive to your comments in class and is  helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. A is hands down one of the best teachers I've had. His class is structured as a discussion that he facilitates incredibly well. He's knowledgeable,  fair and engaging. He sincerely wants to help you succeed as long as he sees your efforts.

If I had another English class to take, I would 100% take another class Afflerbach taught. If you need help, stop by office hours. They make a huge difference. He is very responsive to emails as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Passionate professor who cares about networking and his students. Admits his mistakes clearly and works with students when they have issues. Handwriting in notes can be hard to read / understand sometimes though. Tests ended up being pretty hard (Fall 2025) but they got curved pretty hard so it ended up being fine

The professor is knowledgeable about Networking, but the course management was lacking. ALWAYS REQUEST REGRADES for homework, as TAs rely HEAVILY on the autograder. The professor's handwriting is VERY hard to read, and lectures focus on concepts while exams are calculation-heavy. The midterm had unfair conditions that the take-home didn't balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take-home midterm did not offset the unexpected technical difficulties of the original midterm, which had unfair testing conditions. Lack of feedback on HW and exams; many unanswered Ed posts. TAs/prof gave misleading info about HW/exam questions. Lectures are very conceptual while HW/exams are very computational. Prof Ahmed is pretty solid though.

Spam regrade requests on EVERYTHING! Make up any reason or else they'll never give u partial bc TAs only autograde (half can't even explain anything). Pray u don't have to talk to the prof bc he does not care. Take a diff prof, others are actually nice & don't expect u to "already know the answer" to the HW (which is why they never release answers)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a caring man. Truly understands that we are students EOD and wants us to succeed. Content was challenging but definitely an interesting class.

Incredible professor, cares a lot about his students. He knows a lot about networking as well and the lectures get pretty deep into the content. The exams are very difficult, but he applies a generous curve to accommodate for it.

Professor is super passionate about the material. Lecture notes are not great and the textbook is hard to read. Exams are super content heavy so its best to stay on top of it individually. Homeworks aren't that great of a prep resource as  hws use wireshark and terminal which aren't tested on exams. Programming Assignments are not really useful.

Solid professor all in all. He definitely understands the material and is very passionate about the field. Some lectures were hard to follow since the topics got pretty complex/abstract. But there is a textbook the lecture slides are based on which is helpful. The exams are difficult but final grades end up being  fair at the end

Professor that is clearly passionate and knowledgeable in the topics he teaches. He often tries to connect his lectures to real world events / topics. Also very sympathetic to students and doesn't try to make the class too hard (he handled the canvas test fiasco very well). 

The one bad thing I'll say is that his handwriting is horrendous

As a professor he is really nice and tries to explain everything that is relevant. You can tell he knows his material but the exams are incredibly difficult. Our class average was a 60 on the exam with the curve and we were given an optional retake that had an even lower average.

Took data center section with him. Extremely knowledge about the field and it is clear through his lectures. I would buy his data center book as soon as he finishes writing. Grading is easy as he cares much more about the students absorbing the materials. Very valuable class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is extremely knowledgeable and has a distinct interest in the topic. He's caring and tries to improve the class as he can. There was some disconnect between TAs and professor as homework/projects were poorly organized and communicated. They're working on improving.

Prof Saeed is extremely knowledgeable and eager in networking. He moves at a fast pace, hence, we covered more than the other section. There were 6 hws, 3 "quizzes", 2 labs, and a final - the "quizzes" were actually 75 minute exams and quite difficult, but he curved. Go to lectures and don't fall behind. Only complaint was the TAs were not-so-good.

Extremely easy class. The summer online class is asynch with a couple of weekly assignments. Each week, you have reading quizzes (very light) and discussion posts. The only major assignment was the final "exam", in which you had to create a presentation on one of the multiple Arabic topics learned. Overall, the class was very easy, and I recommend!

I took his class for ARBC 3501 (Men-Women in Islam) and I really enjoyed the class. Probably the easiest option for a humanities credit. Sometimes assignments could be annoying but even the slightest effort can get you an A. Also very understanding and let me turn in a lot of stuff almost a week late.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ahmed was a very helpful and respectful professor who made this class an enjoyable experience for his students. You have to show up to class and you get 3 absences before it affects your grade. The quizzes are not worth much and are easy. Just participate and you should get an A for both 1001 and 1002. Great professor and cool class!

Great professor! He does a good job of teaching Arabic basics and providing lots of different types of practice (reading, listening, speaking, etc). At first the class was intimidating since many people were already able to read Arabic, but I felt much more confident by the end of the semester. Very welcoming class environment!

Very good professor, taught a hard language in a way everyone would understand. Grading is fair and doesn't require that much time. I will 100% recommend this class to anyone that is looking for a good humanities class.
You have to show up to lectures, but he cares about his students and teaches a hard language well
Ahmed is a great teacher, being in his class was so nice I enjoyed it a lot. He's super understanding and as long as you communicate with him and do your assignments you'll do great!

Prof. Ahmed is so so kind and really caring. Sometimes the lectures are sporadic as theyre based on what students need, which was more difficult for me. No previous experience for me, so definitely had to put in work. Once we sat in the dark and just relaxed for a bit during a miserable hell week. Prof Ahmed is so sweet and it was a great class.

Dr. Ahmed has been one of the best professors I've had ever. I came into his class only knowing how to read Arabic and had no idea what a single word meant, but he taught me a lot. His lectures are interesting and he never throws so much info at you all at once. He really tries to understand what we need and what helps us learn best. 1000000/10

Literally the NICEST professor I will probably have at Tech. He's so understanding and will extend deadlines if necessary. I had his class fully online and you only have to write one response and read a chapter of the book every week. Definitely take this class if you need a humanities, it's also interesting!!!

Dr. Ahuja is an expert on aeroacoustics. His lecture slides are very organized and handy to use for whatever purpose. He doesn't go through details in lecture so after-class reading is important, even though the exams are really easy. Be intuitive and active in his class!

Prof Ahuja is your good old-fashioned professor. He goes over the material quickly, and often refers to the textbook, which you can for tables. The slides are often a mess, which requires a better understanding of the subject. However, the tests and quizzes are very doable. You can get an A in the class, just make sure not to fall behind.
His course consists of filling in the blanks in his lecture slides. It's pretty boring. Mac-PC compatibility messed the pictures up. All in All pretty good.

He is an OK professor. His tests are almost easy if you have good memory. He is very quick in teaching, doesnt explain alot. always says "I dont have time to go in detail, please refer to you textbook". Tests consists of fill in the blanks which are directly from his slides, and the rest is problems. Thermo is supposed to be hard. but it was easy!

I'm giving him +1 pity point because he comes off as a nice genuine guy. His lectures are extremely dull and dry. He took an interesting topic and made it as boring as possible. Another major flaw was that all the projects were very poorly written and outdated. Errors in those instructions probably wasted hundreds of man hours across all students.
Course was poorly designed

Dr. Ahamad's CS 6238 course is challenging, but you learn a lot. One of his strengths is his weekly office hours, where he reviews the previous week's quiz (or exam) and allows comments and differing views. This time is very valuable as it helps reinforce concepts and prepare for the midterm or final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Provides around 30-50 pages of academic journals/articles per QUIZ, on a WEEKLY basis. I've never met another professor that's asked for this much reading. The content isn't difficult (or engaging) but the quiz questions are pulled randomly from journals. Projects are much better and don't rely on readings. Drops your lowest quiz/project grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
The coursework is related to systems security so it is lecture heavy with things like TCBs, DAC, MAC, etc as you 
would expect. The Professor and TAs in general are super approachable and in fact Prof. Ahamad encourages students to drop by for office hours. Overall pretty good course and hands-on experience with core system security principles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for Secure Computer Systems and found him to be knowledgeable with great recorded lectures (online). Two exams are worth 60% of your grade, but grades on a curve based on class performance. There is a quiz each week (worst 3 are dropped) and 4 projects ranging from easy to hard (proj4, start early). I learned a lot, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most intense class I've ever taken. Stated I'd be doing about 6 - 8 hours of homework a week. I spend at least 30 hours a week (3 hours a night + entire weekend). Videos are very informative, and class structure is awesome for an online learner. I would not recommend taking two of his classes simultaneously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful in general! Your teaching yourself!

His class is pretty useless, and his lectures are dry and boring. All you do is read boring papers that you learn almost nothing from. I did learn a little bit from the projects, though. I think his grading is predeterminedno matter what you do or don't do, it seems he's already decided what he's going to give you. Avoid if possible.

This professor is unclear and not helpful. He is unaware of what he is discussing in class and forgets what he tells students. He is not consistent with his grading, and changes his standards of grading each week without telling students. He does not understand the meaning of communication. Good Luck, avoid a class with this professor if you can.
Unstructured course, extremely confusing lectures, poor quality of assignments. Utter  waste of an elective.

This professor has vague expectations.  He does not grade anything in his courses, yet claims that each assignment is crucial.  He does not teach anything, and he often invites guest faculty to lecture.  Final grades are arbitrary based on how much he likes you.  If you're an InfoSec major, good luck because this professor's courses are mandatory.
Best professor I have ever met in my life. Extremely down to earth and very knowledgeable. Highly experienced and I am gratified to be one of his students.
No Comments
I thought Prof Ahamad was very good and inspiring. He is very sharp and abreast with the research in his field. His projects focus on creativity and can be a bit openended.
Hard course, great teacher
Funny as hell

Dr. Uzer is definitely one of the best professor at Tech. He is enthusiastic and he has a great sense of humor. The class is relatively difficult, its physics, but he is a generous grader. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, you need to.
If you go to Georgia Tech, you HAVE to take a class with Uzer - you'd be missing out on so much otherwise!

Really funny guy, a warm, helpful professor who clearly loves what he does and wants nothing more than to make you understand the material. If you ever have the chance to take Uzer, you will not regret it.

Insanely difficult class, but he definitely taught me how to think more like a physicist. He will take the time to make sure you understand the material, but he'll grade you as if you're taking classical mechanics, not intro physics. Very funny and intelligent. He will likely remain one of my favorite professors.

Uzer is a really funny guy who is more than willing to sacrifice time, even during lecture, to address confusions and misunderstandings. One of my favorite professors at Tech, really helps you succeed in physics.

Professor Uzer is by far the most entertaining professor I've had a Tech. His classes are known to be extremely difficult, but he is more than willing to sit down and reexplain most anything. Do not miss out on having him as a teacher.

The class is hard, but it isn't Uzer's fault. He explains the material VERY well. The tests are REALLY difficult, but all of them are. There is a lot of homework, but it's manageable. Whatever you do, DO THE BONUS HOMEWORK. It seems like a hassle, but it is definitely worth it. Uzer knows his stuff, and he's really funny. I recommend taking him.

Fantastic teacher, definitely worth going to his lectures. Took his honors physics class and his tests were pretty much impossible to finish within an hour, though.  But he's very fair and takes time out of his day to make sure you are on the right track
Very funny and will keep you interested. The tests aren't easy but what tests at Georgia Tech are? Very good professor and always willing to help if you need it.

Very cool and funny professor. He is good at explaining key concepts that appear on the quizzes. The quizzes are tough. The multiple choice questions are meant to trick you. I suggest reading the book and doing all previous quizzes.

The class in itself was pretty much a joke, but Uzer was an awesome prof. He is the ideal "college lecturer", meaning he's great at teaching the material and keeping you interested, but he's not available outside of lecture. HILLARIOUS! If anything, go to class for his jokes. (By the way, he looks like a crazy Ben Stein). Very easy class overall.
This man is awesome. He makes Physics fun and keeps us laughing
No Comments
funny guy. strange sense of humor. does go a bit slow but covers material piece by piece.
No Comments
Nice guy, he cares about the students. I just didn't like the course material very much, nor the in class participation assignments.
He clearly cares about students and what they think of the course, responds well to feedback.
The class wasn't very interesting, I didn't learn much in lecture. It's definitely the type of class you have to teach yourself, but it doesn't require much time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Homework is just the right difficulty, enough to keep a solid grade and still learn a lot. Tests are all multiple choice, and he drops your lowest. Final is cumulative. Possible extra credit from CIOS. I don't like random attendance, especially for an easy class like this, but that is whatever. Good lecturer, you learn all you need to in class.

Great professor. Attendance is taken randomly over the semester. All material is covered in lectures, textbook is not necessary at all. All tests and final exam are all multiple choice, and they're all pretty straightforward (there will be one or two trick questions though). Overall a very fair professor. If you show up and pay attention, easy A.

Quality professor, or actually grad student. Gets grades back in an hour most of the time which was great. Good clear lectures. Fair exams. Very solid choice for an econ professor, would recommend. Only downside is random attendance checks.

Relatively enjoyable class. You get to drop your lowest test! The professor really knows and understands the material, so he is able to answer all questions clearly. His tests did sometimes have tricky or confusing questions, so read carefully.

Professor Roy is a great professor with very reasonable grading criteria and class structure. He is a solid lecturer, and I would highly recommend him to other students. As long as you keep up with the material and stay consistent, you will do fine in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Roy truly cares about his students. He is very understanding and will accommodate to his students as requested. His class is distributed by the homework, midterm, and final exam. You need to go to class and follow the textbook or you will be lost. As long as you work hard, you will get the grade you deserve. 10/10 TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Roy is incredibly understanding and cares about his students - he was one of the only professors to modify the class and communicate with us clearly when we moved to remote learning. His lectures are interesting, and the weekly assignments aren't difficult. Exams are straightforward and fair, just study the lecture notes and do the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Roy's classes and homeworks were very proof heavy, but the exams were pretty easy. He knows the material pretty well and really cares about his students. The exams often had extra credit too. He spent some time reviewing 1553/4, so there was only a little bit I had to do by myself. If you got through 1553/4 ok, this class won't be bad at all.

Worst physics professor ever. All of his tests were MULTIPLE CHOICE (i.e. no partial credit!) with SIX questions!  The questions were also highly dependent on memorizing specific formulas, since his formula sheets sucked.  DO NOT take his class if you can avoid it.  There are much better science electives.

The class itself (Intro modern) was pathetically easy and shallow. Prof Erbil, however, is an incredibly passionate guy who clearly would have loved to just teach to anyone who wanted to learn, even without requirements/grades/external motivators. Seems to me he wants to go into more depth than the course allowed. He seems like a really cool guy.

I had Erbil for Physics 3. Physics 3 is much easier than Physics 2, and unfortunately he realizes this. Unlike Physics 1 and 2 where the worst test is dropped as a buffer, in his Physics 3 class there is NO hope of redemption after a bad test grade. The final was 10 MC at 25% of your grade: one stupid math error drops your final grade 2.5 points.

A solid professor overall. Very helpful. Holds review sessions the night before a test- even if the test is on a Monday. The class requires work, and the tests are pretty tough, if not borderline unfair, but hard work will pay off in his class. I'd take him again later for physics 3 if he's teaching it.
Very easy. Almost TOO easy; anyone's that's seen electricity and magnetism in high school need not attend lecture. You'll still get an A if you remember anything. Incredibly nice guy, though.

Without a doubt the BEST professor I've had at Tech.  He is always willing to help his students, and you can tell he enjoys teaching.  His tests are very reasonable with most of the averages turning out to be in the 80s, which is very high for a class at Tech.  I really enjoyed the class and would highly recommend it.

I had Erbil for Thermodynamics.  He's a fairly easy teacher as far as grading goes; he's well-grounded in reality and insists that his students do likewise.  He's average when it comes to explaining material or fielding questions.  Erbil's big advantage is that he's very, very concerned about his students' learning.  Overall a solid teacher.

Compared with other physics classes at Tech... his was awesome.  I really enjoyed him... and yes he does talk about himself a lot, but it's all interesting... he knows a bunch of random famous scientists (or so he says).  Anyway, if you can get the old tests... you'll be golden.  Oh yeah... and an 80 is like an A... so that's nice too....
Not the clearest lecturer when compared with other phys proffs, seemed to spend a little too much time talking about himself and his MIT degree.  But overall a likable guy.
I earned an A in his class (my first one at tech!) and enjoyed it as well. He was a very good and very helpful professor, and I hope to take another class with him in the future.

Dr. Erbil rarely teaches the intro classes, but I had him for each of them, and enjoyed every bit of it.  He regularly provided help sessions, many times at the request of his students, and has a love for the material.  "Isn't that great?" h

Although Dr. Agrawal does give difficult tests, he is a great lecturer and very willing to help you during his office hours. You will learn so much in the class and taking a class with Dr. Agrawal is very worthwhile. Definitely one of the best lecturers in the chemical engineering department.

AMAZING professor. You will here stories about this class, and while he is an extremely difficult professor, he is an excellent lecturer and is extremely willing to help you out! Also, if you put in the effort, a B is atleast manageable, because he has an enormous curve (anywhere above a 65 should guarantee you atleast a B)
Worst professor ever. English is bad and he cannot hear you too. Homework grading is harsh and unreasonable. Exam is hard too.

Hard to understand. 3 exams 30 percent of the total grade, each. Group project throughout the semesters. learning environment not optimized for learning, tests feel like an interview. DO NOT MAKE THE MISTAKE of NOT TAKING NETWORKING 1

This class feels unreasonably test-heavy. There are no practice exams, and the lectures lack applicational content. It assumes students already have a strong foundation and complete understanding, while offering minimal support or guidance. Would not recommend taking it

Take this class if you think you're lucky. Professor provides NO practice exams questions, covers NO examples in lecture, and only goes over conceptual ideas. When half of the exam is applicational, good luck. There is no guidance on what to study, which makes zero sense when 60 percent of your grade is exams. assignments are easy at least.

Took this with no networking background. Don't let OMSCS reviews fool you, it's not easy. Grading differs between online (assignment-heavy) and in-person (exam-heavy). Limited resources and feedback left me confused often. Prior networking knowledge is a must.

Lecture slides only covered ~3/4 of the content, the rest you need to learn on your own via the textbook (which is well written). The TAs were pretty slow with grading and answering Ed questions. Homeworks were long but there were only a few. Exams were unnecessarily hard (avg. on exam 1 was a D), but there was seemingly a curve on final grades.

CS 3251: Lecturer is ok and classes are recorded. However, the exams/homework are EXTREMELY challenging! Both often contained content that wasn't covered in class, making it super hard. For reference, on the midterm exam, half the class got BELOW a 67! 

Luckily, the programming assignments are easy, and there's a nice curve that saved my grade.

Lectures are organized but not the most engaging. Responds to student questions and feedback well. Learnt a lot in this class. Good balance between the various assessment methods and grading was mostly fair. Beware that there are not many assignments so tanking one can harm your overall a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best courses I have taken at Tech. His teaching is engaging, and assignments are relevant. The quizzes test your understanding of the subject effectively too.

Helpful lectures, real-world content. Easy quizzes. Very doable projects, TA office hours helped for clarifying instructions. Unclear grading for assignments until after graded. Syllabus changed halfway through semester (4-> 3 quizzes), was unclear until last week of classes (despite many Piazza posts left unanswered) how much quizzes were worth.
Dr. Allegra Smith is a nice person and she is helpful, but I did not enjoy how much participation was required. I felt like being an introvert was a disadvantage in her course.

Dr. Allegra is easily the best professor I have ever had at Tech. She is so incredibly kind and her teaching is both interesting and engaging, as are the projects she assigns. She is an awesome professor overall and I can't recommend her enough!

She's a passionate teacher and very understanding! You learn skills that are truly relevant, there are weekly "responses" that are creating your own version of media (Instagram carousel, Canva flyer, etc.) and applying that to readings. At the end there's a final project with a non-profit to apply your skills that is super valuable professionally.
Dr. Allegra cares about her students and is extremely passionate about what she teaches! She cares about her students and helps you out if you ask for it.
Honestly one of the most helpful courses I have taken here. If not the most helpful. Thank you for preparing us for the future, Dr. Allegra

Hands down, one of my favorite professors at GT, so take a class with her even if you are iffy about the topic. She genuinely cares about her students and makes each of us feel respected in class. Despite being the first time she taught social media, I learned a lot and felt like my effort produced great results.

One thing I love about Prof. Allegra is that she assigns work that she knows will prepare us for our future careers. One day we had a mock interview class, for example. She prioritizes quality of learning over everything, is understanding about grades, and does a good job of building relationships of mutual respect and understanding with students.
She is super accommodating of individual differences. Thankful for her!

Dr. Allegra is the best professor I've ever had in my college career. She is enthusiastic about the content of the class and that makes it a lot more interesting. She is very responsive and accommodating when you need help. Take a class with her if you can!

Actually took her for Content Strategy but she was amazing. A lot of energy, every understanding, extremely flexible, and the class gave me opportunities to add to my portfolio. Would definitely recommend to future students.

She was very organized and enthusiastic, very nice to us (even brought us donuts TY), but grr at attendance policy because it is an elective first, and two. if you can absorb the content without doing the participation activities (which I as an introvert do no enjoy) you should not be penalized.
I found her to be splendid. I absolutely recommend her. Just READ her attendance policy because she does mark absences.
I thought she was a good professor. The class itself is boring, and kind of drags, but she was enthusiastic about it anyway. She was also super nice in office hours.
This class could be completed as a work training session. Ridiculous to have it as a whole class. I mean not like our major coursework isnt difficult enough!
Waste of time unless you are absolutely required to take it. Engineers do not need this content.
Great professor. Really cares about students and is willing to help. Make sure to pay attention to attendance policies but other than that good class.

She is extremely kind and it is a good course. Just BE SURE to read the attendance policy! This class is not hard, but I think it would make more sense if offered online or hybrid because I found that most of the participation activities had no bearing on my grasp of the content.

She is very professional and organized but she is also approachable and caring. She seems to genuinely care about her students. Her course content was expertly planned and facilitated but she is willing to accommodate extenuating circumstances without being rude or petty. Overall, she is awesome and I recommend her,
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is extremely accomodating and kind; if you need help or an extension, she's more than willing to as long as you've established a good connection (go to class, participate, be friendly in general). Lecture participation isn't hard at all, usually a fun and interesting convo with peers! Papers are fun since it's very personalizable.

Great organization and structure throughout the course. Always accessible outside of class and clearly cares a lot about students' career placement. Consistently connects what you learn in class to real-world applications, which makes the material much more meaningful. Easily the best professor in the major.

Alex does a great job in teaching Intro to Construction Management. She introduces new concepts in a way that is digestible for all students. There were a lot of valuable lessons that came out of the semester-end project that could be applied to the Building Construction world.

Alex has a lot of industry experience and really cares about you paying attention in class. It's pretty obvious that she is teaching because she wants us to actually learn something, not just lecturing to lecture. Very open to questions and assigns work that is actually relevant to the industry and what we are learning.

The professor was really engaging in lectures, but the tests are HARD. I took this Fall 2025 and got an A but for a grad level class, there were a lot of Bs and Cs in the final distribution. Expect to work hard but I enjoyed the learning experience overall and learned a lot.

Most of the heat transfer professors at Tech are terrible, Professor Menon is still difficult (it's a difficult class), but is an incredible professor. Her exams are extremely fair, homework isn't too intense, and lectures are very well made. Go to class and do all the practice she tells you, and it'll 100% pay off.

Great professor that ACTUALLY listens to her students. She has decent lectures and slides (they help when supplemented with the textbook) and is very organized. The class keeps you busy with multiple assignments but so do other ME 3345 sections. I really don't get the other comments that speak ill of Dr. Menon. Don't hate the player hate the game.
Just don't take her. Trust me. Your life will suck.

The grading was based on 3 homework assignments, 2 tests, and a final which didn't leave room for error. Don't let the fact that tests are open book make you think they're easy. The test averages were low (C's and D's) and grading was harsh. The professor was rude and often called students out for just asking questions.
Exhaustive class. A lot to learn.

You'll learn more by not attending his lectures. He doesn't curve at all, so ignore his 'don't worry about your grades you can make it up' and seriously buckle down. I highly suggest just not taking his classes, half the class got C's or below in a graduate class.  While the class topics sound appealing, teach it yourself, trust me.

She forces in class participation which is scary at first but you'll get used to it. Pacing is rough at first with the alphabets but the course load is pretty light afterwards. She grades super nicely and gives exam formats beforehand.

I had Matsushima-sensei for both JAPN 1002 & 1001. She is so incredibly accommodating to students, if you're sick and miss a quiz or exam she allows for make-ups. Very interactive lectures (expect to be called on at least once per class). I felt 1002 to be a significant difficulty jump from 1001, but matsushima-sensei made the transition easier.

Foreign languages are hard, let alone one that often uses three alphabets in the same sentence. Yes, you'll have to put in the work and you will have to memorize a lot, but Matsushima-Sensei is very clear about what she expects you to know and grow.

She makes it very easy. Great professor.

Matsushima-sensei is an amazing professor. She is very kind, makes expectations clear, and provides plenty of resources for studying and test preparation. Her lectures focus on speaking exercises. You are well-prepared for homework. Foreign languages take attending class and additional studying, but she makes the process very enjoyable. がんばって！

The Japanese language has always been on my list of languages I wanted to try out. Her classes did not disappoint, and there's lots of fun participation activities and slightly time consuming homework(They're not hard). It shouldn't be that hard as long as you put in effort. 10/10 class.

Matsushima 先生 is so sweet. Japanese was my favorite class this semester. Attendance is mandatory, but going to class never felt like a chore. There's group work too, but it's fun to get to know other classmates. This doesn't feel like a 4 credit hour class at all. There's lots of extra credit too, so I never had to worry about my grade. ありがとうございます！

I took almost all the introductory classes with her, at first I was planning to only fulfill my humanities requirements but I loved her class so much I got a major instead, went on study abroad, and met most of my friends through the Japanese department. Life changing class :)

I LOVE Matsushima Sensei! She is an absolute angel. Teaches very well and will always give reviews for any test. She is very easy to reach and you can tell she really loves and cares about her students.
She's the sweetest prof ever. Explains things so they're easy to understand, and cares a lot. I turned in a few assignments late and she takes off little to no points.
She is amazing, I enjoyed every single class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Matsushima is very kind and an amazing professor overall! No complaints here. She is very understanding and patient with students but is also clear about what she expects from them. Expect to find yourself practicing Japanese with other students in this course! There is homework, but it typically doesn't take much time.

Prof is amazing for an intro level course. Most of your grade comes from just participating in activities and doing homework. The tests and language practice is really easy, as long as you take 30 minutes to memorize the vocabulary provided. I highly recommend her classes, because she is thorough going through the material.

I had Matsushima-sensee for Fall, and she was amazing. While there were many HW assignments for practice, they were true to the types of questions asked on the tests. Practicing dialogue with every student in the class created some solid chemistry. I highly recommend learning all hiragana and katakana before this course to have the best experience!

Matsushima-sensei was my favorite professor in the semester that I had her in. Participation in class is important and the homework may be tough, but she is such a caring person and wants to see her students succeed. Definitely take her if you can.

Matsushima-sensei was great! Going to lecture and participating in class was really important. She explained grammar points very clearly. When it comes to learning characters in JAPN classes though, lectures are def not enough. You must self-study hiragana/katakana/kanji. If you grind out kana before taking 1001, you'll have a MUCH better time.

Matsushima sensei was the best! Definitely take JAPN1001 with her if you are wanting to learn Japanese. She is so kind and really helpful. The course requires that you study a lot because you're learning a new language, but she makes it fun and enjoyable. Highly recommend! It's a lot of work but it's so worth it and you learn so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Handles online classes very well. Good at encouraging participation. Fast grader and very helpful in office hours. I took JAPN 1001 and it was a lot of work but taking it with Matsushima sensei made it easier and more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking her class. She makes learning Japanese fun and is always patient. Japanese is definitely not the easiest language to learn, much less teach, but she definitely does it well!
If you want to learn Japanese. Do it with Matsushima!

She's awesome! The classes are fun and we usually got out early. Matsushima is very patient and grades fairly. I never saw her mad or raise her voice or even get upset really. She will joke around with us a little and creates a fun learning environment.

Matsushima-sensei is so nice! She is super patient and cares a lot about her students. Most of the class will be spent practicing speaking Japanese, which helps a lot with learning the language. This isnt the easiest class, and there are tons of homeworks and quizzes, but if you do the work you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you take this class, you better be prepared to spend around half of class every day practicing speaking Japanese out loud with other students. Participation is expected, and it greatly pays off.

Matsushima-sensei is my favorite teacher in the japanese department so far. She's very helpful and relaxed although I wouldn't say she's easy. She expects a lot but doesn't make you feel awful if you need help.

??????, is an amazing person. She is willing to help out as long as you go to her. The class is easy but super intensive. She makes the class fun that the 50 minutes runs out before you realize it. There are a lot of tests and quizzes,so it is difficult to fail the class. If you're thinking about taking a class with her, i'll say go for it.

Matsushima-sensei is great. Very kind and helpful and she makes the content easy to learn. Going to class is actually fun and it's a great break in your day from some of your more stressful classes. This was a fairly easy class. Just attend the class and pay attention, you'll do fine.
Best teacher ever. Flexible, helpful, and makes you wonder why American professors should be so strict if a Japanese one is so relaxed.
Super easy class, if you know Japanese beforehand. It's an easy A if you do the homework and show up for class.

Dr. Dixit's class is tough, but very close to real world experience. The amount of learning that happens is tremendous. I come from a family of carpenters and therefore had good CAD experience already. However, I learnt a whole lot more by taking his class. Two thumbs up.

The class may seem difficult at first. But as soon as you understand the expectations and ask questions. You will be fine. The professor is happy to answer all questions as long as rules are followed.

Dr. Dixit is one of the best Professors of my entire life.  He is devoted to teaching like no other. No needless Power point presentation or talking jargon. He faces the students all the times. Works with them  for all the problems. Moves around in the class and is always ready to help. A must take Professor!
Dixit is a very helpful professor who makes all assignments/project requirements clear. He is a good teacher who will take an interest in you and expects a lot of effort from you.
He super nice. In office hours he spent well over an hour making sure i understood the topic. His grading is a bit inconsistent... but overall he is very fair. He also curves very nicely.

This guy was incredibly frustrating to deal with. I would not take him. He digresses from directions, makes up his own, and then grades based on things that he doesn't tell you. He was really a bad teacher and you should not take him!

Do NOT take this professor. He does not follow a textbook, he does not teach in class at all, all of his instructions are unclear, and to top it all off his grading is very harsh and inconsistent. Though I got A's on the tests and obviously understood the material, I didn't do as well in the overall class because his projects were ridiculous.

I was not doing well in his class and went to him for help. He spent 1.5 hours trying to explain the labs when he could easily have asked me to go to a TA. No doubt he grades hard but gives curves the grades. He gave 18 exra-points for exam 1 for a very simple assignment.

I currently have this professor.  Although, his class is a bit difficult, he knows his subject matter really well. You just have to work hard and ask him questions. He is very approachable. This class is meant to be hard and this prof is one of the smartest I've had from whom you can learn the material at a very in-depth level.

“Chill guy, but not the strongest lecturer. He can be on the quieter and not always step-by-step/thorough, so expect to self-study to fully understand the material. Still, he's committed and clearly enjoys sharing fluids knowledge and real-world applications, though he's a little older and the enthusiasm is a little more subtle, than say, Torello.

I do not like to complain about professors often, but he is the worst I've ever had. In class lecture slides do not correlate to the canvas lecture slides he provides. Test heavy. Exam 2 was much harder than exam 1, and he did not use a standardized grading scheme. Homework solutions do not provide clear explanations either. do NOT take this guy
Utter waste of time
Okay. Lectures are boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A. Extremely boring lectures. Does not care about teaching. Expects you to study his reasearch.

Dr. Aidun is a decent pick for fluids. The class is hard and he goes over practice that is mostly applicable to the tests, but lectures can tend to get boring. With the proper focus, an A is very doable as the test grading is slightly on the gracious side. I took it in the spring and an A actually ended up being a 91+...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't ask questions during exam, only at beginning. No calculators. Explained concepts well in class with plenty of examples and grades generously. Curved the class down(??) Extra credit by computer project that adds 10 points onto final grade, nearly impossible to get all 10. Start early as soon as he releases, it takes more than a week to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Aidun's lectures provided us with great notes even though lectures were not always the most engaging. Your grade is basically made up of just tests. I did well by putting the notes slides in my crib sheet, but I am not sure I actually learned the concepts. The cutoffs for A, B, etc. are decided at the end of the semester (they could go up!)

Boring and slow lectures. He does not come prepared for the class at all. Exams are not based on the course material. As a midterm he wants you to do a literature review and write a review paper regarding his research. Easy A.

Idk why the high ratings. They're wrong. I made an A, but he screwed the class by making the cutoff 91% for A and 82% for B. His lectures are so boring I felt like napping every class. His HW's are just him selecting random book probs. with untaught content you have to Chegg. I did well on tests (90%) by putting slide problems on formula sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really good professor! Class was a little boring but he makes up for that by being a REALLY generous grader. Extra credit offered. The final was optional. Exams based on textbook and homework. Accessible outside of class and really cares about you making a good grade. I would know I started the semester failing lol. Best option for Fluids!
He's alright. Lectures are really boring, and don't cover anything you can't find in the textbook. If you do the practice problems and understand the homework you'll be prepared for the tests.

Great Professor. Explains everything you need to know to be successful on tests. Be prepared for tests though as the class was graded by four midterms or four midterms and a final, no other grades. Grading was fair and test problems were very similar to practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aidun is a solid choice for fluid mechanics. Grading in the class is based upon four tests with an optional final and nothing else. Lectures are somewhat dry, but important in getting a basic handle on concepts. Test questions are often similar to the optional practice problems he assigns. He also posts older recordings of lectures for review.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: HWs are not collected for a grade, and you can choose to never attend lecture and instead just watch the uploaded lecture videos at 1.5x speed. I nearly got an A by never attending lecture, and watching 8-10 hours of lecture videos the days leading up to the midterms. Exams are usually quite similar to practice problems given.

Dr. Aidun is a very kind and caring professor with very helpful office hours. He assigns many homework problems, but the solutions are always available and they are not collected for credit. The class is graded by the average of four exams, with an optional final exam that can only help you. He is a tough grader, but test content is telegraphed.

Mediocre professor. Your entire grade is exams, so it pays to do well on them. Homework is optional, so it's hard to stay motivated to do it. He posts video lectures and expects you to watch them, but his in class lectures are the exact same thing, so one of them is a waste of time. Boring class.
Great lecturer and genuinely wants students to succeed. Class is still really hard though but curves decently

Assign 30-40 pages of a term paper, single space, and only give you 1 month. Terrible teaching skills and no care about the student. Always let the student do a presentation without him put in any effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: genuinely a goated history professor. no homework, but there are required books/readings that are quizzed and tested but theyre really interesting and dont take long to read. he tells you exactly what terms will on exams which made studying easier. he also noticed that some ppl did not do well on some exams so he dropped our lowest for our class

Very caring, allowed me to do alternate assignment when I had not done the reading. Very engaging lectures, and the reading was genuinely interesting, even though there is a lot of it. Genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and I feel better off having taken the class and learned about the topics we did.
He was a really great professor who is really concerned about his students. His class is kind of difficult, but it is very enjoyable.

Prof Amsterdam was the best history instructor I have ever had. His lectures were well structured as he gave outlines for each one and his test were all from the lectures (so u gotta go to take notes cuz he doesn't post notes). Tests were very straightforward and the required readings were actually really interesting to read. Really caring

He's an amazing instructor, and even though attendance isn't mandatory, you will need to go to class in order to get a good grade since he doesn't post the lecture content on Canvas. Very chill guy, he dropped a few questions in our tests if he felt that it was confusing. He also dropped our lowest midterm. Make sure to take good notes

Lectures are not mandatory but DEFINITELY reccomended. Studying the material on your own or based off the notes makes the class so much harder than it should. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer who makes the content  engaging, concise, and easy to follow, additionally he makes it very clear what parts of lecture are important/on the exams

From what I had, you were required (and I advise you) to go to every lecture to learn the material. Even though you can get the lecture notes from others, Amsterdam's lectures are so good that you retain the information so much better. He's very caring and wants the best for everyone. Had a great time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The goat. That's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Amsterdam is actually a really good professor. He's extremely passionate about his area of teaching, but his exams can be a bit tricky since a lot of the answer choices are the same so it's important to memorize details of specific events. He's also lecture heavy and doesn't post any notes after class, so you have to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and very passionate about his lectures. If you go to lecture and listen, you will do well in the class. The tests are pretty easy (multiple choice) if you pay attention. He does not post notes or recordings for lecture so make sure to go.

Amsterdam is good at packing information in a lecture but its way too difficult for a history class at a Tech school. He also posts no lectures notes or anything and 90% of the information is based on what he says in class. The test questions have very odd answers and often have questions that are based on 1 sentence that was said in class.

If you like history, you will love this class. If you don't, prepare to have to study A LOT for the midterms and final. Mr. Amsterdam likes what he teaches and he does it well, but prepare to have to study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Amsterdam is amazing!!! His lectures are interesting and very easy to understand. You read 4 books throughout the semester with an easy 5 question quiz for each. The tests are medium difficulty I would say, as long as you pay attention to the lectures and read the take away points for the short readings you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory but I would definitely recommend going to lecture because Dr. Amsterdam is very into everything he talks about. Not many grades, a few midterms and reading quizzes. Amsterdam clearly loves what he does and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor because his lectures are engaging, loves to answer questions even in a large class setting, very straight forward to make an A. Only have midterms and 3 book quizzes. All books can be found online. I also realized he assumes that we have already had US History before.

Prof. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer, he teaches history as if it's reading a storybook. He includes plenty of details to make the material relevant to the modern day and our lives. He makes it very clear what you need to know in order to pass with an A. Very little work outside of lecture as long as you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives very long lectures that may seem to ramble  Easy class but you have to at least try and pay attention.

He will lecture all class, but is engaging and says what key words to remember for the test. I struggled on the first test because I was mixing up my facts, and asked if he could fact check my definitions after that, and he did. He is very nice, and helps you if you need it. It can be a lot of content at times, so just take good notes and study.

I would do anything for Daniel Amsterdam. Hands down my favorite HTS prof at Tech (I'm an HTS major). He's incredibly caring, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. He really cares to make the work load reasonable, and succeeds. He also legitimately wants you to learn and succeed. He managed to make "research methods" an absolute blast so props.

Dr. Amsterdam is one of my favorite profs. I was dreading this required course but he made it legitimately fun, and was an extremely caring guy with a lot of respect for us. The class was definitely a decent bit of work, but I learned more than I expected to, and an A is very achievable, especially if you ask for help. Honestly a blast, 10/10.

Very minimal work for a GT class. His lectures are outstanding and are crucial for hitting marks on exams. Amsterdam's class was a rare instance in which I enjoyed learning history. My advice is to fill out the definitions from his study guides right after each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsterdam is a super nice guy and his lectures are always enjoyable. He understands that most students at GT are STEM majors and are only taking his class for graduation purposes.

I usually despise history, but Dr. Amsterdam made the content genuinely enjoyable with his lectures. His test questions are based purely on the information he covers in class, so if you skip, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a great lecturer and a good guy. Also, the class is really easy- the only homework is 1-3 page readings for classes and 3 1-2 page "papers" throughout the semester which are essentially an automatic 100 if you do them. You have to go to class though bc notes are not posted online, but lectures are interesting and usually have a 5 min break

Dr Amsterdam cares about his students and is really passionate about the topic as well. He encourages participation even though it's a pretty big class. As long as you put some effort into the short essays and the study guide, it's a pretty easy and fun class.

Dr. Amsterdam understands most students take this class for the sake of the credit. He, therefore, makes it really interesting and the lectures are full of relevant jokes. He also has very few homework assignments. If you have a good study guide, it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely useful and if you attend class every day you will definitely succeed in the class. There's only a few assignments, but the homework is largely graded on completion and the tests are not extremely difficult. All around an amazing professor and I definitely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are genuinely Interesting and coming to class doesn't feel like a chore like some history classes do. He understands that we came to GT likely not to study history and doesn't overwhelm you with work. Generally a great professor and you should succeed if you put appropriate effort into the class.

One of my favorite teachers I have ever had. He has a plethora of knowledge on the subject and genuinely cares about the success of his students. Going to lecture is a must as his tests are word for word form his lectures. Overall a phenomenal experience and would take any course this professor offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Be sure to attend class! He gives away hints of the test and it would be impossible to study without lecture notes. He takes time to give breaks and makes jokes, so its not that boring (sometimes it gets pretty heavy though). The tests are clear cut and you know what you need to study/memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you go to lectures. In my class, notes and powerpoints were posted, but lacked any content. If you don't go to lectures you will not be able to pass the class. Tests were multiple choice, but hard. Take notes in class and study them, and you will do fine. His lectures are also pretty interesting, and worth going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You must attend the lectures to pass the class, but lectures are always interesting! The class requires a few readings here and there as well. He is truly a caring and understanding person. If you get to take his class, you are a lucky student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsterdam is great! He always makes jokes during lecture, and he often gives breaks when he sees the class dozing. He is approachable in office hours and never turns down a question. The class is very lecture heavy, and there are few graded assignments other than tests. But the tests never have surprises or trick questions. 10/10 recommend
A professor who does her job well and there is really nothing to be worried about when taking a class with her.

The class is pretty engaging overall, and she genuinely cares about her students. Best class this semester!! I used to look forward to class every week, because yes, it is THAT fun. Would take her again 100% . The exams can be challenging at first, but it's all centralized across all 1553 sections.

Overall super engaging class, she goes a little fast sometimes but takes on the somewhat complex topics in an approachable and clear way. Do not recommend skipping any lectures though as a lot of the concepts pile up on each other quickly, especially towards the end of the semester.
Sometimes goes a tiny bit fast but other than that, she is slay and had us learn a tiny bit of French for funsies. Some classes made me laugh out loud

Stockton is a kind and funny person and an alright lecturer. With the grade redemption opportunities on the test (half credit back on every question) it's hard to do poorly in this class. If you ever need extensions or help message and she is very helpful.
Very nice professor who's very engaged with the material. TAs review sessions are also a saving grace for midterms

Very knowledgable, good slides. Makes analytical easy. Prone to moving class online with little notice. Offers corrections to earn 1/2 points back on missed exam questions. Will sit with you one-on-one for hours until you understand, will help you even on the weekend or at 8pm before exam. Very passionate, can go off on tangents. No real complaints

Not a bad professor: very knowledgeable, just frustrating sometimes with poor communication (cancelling class or moving it online last minute, unclear deadlines, last minute changes in homework, doesn't really respond to emails/Teams) and going on tangents getting super far behind in lecture. She does provide a lot of resources, it's an easy class.

Nice as a person but not good at communicating. She has no office hours, says to not email her, and says to use Teams instead but doesn't even reply there. She had the TA teach the whole course basically and didn't show up most of the time. The class was easy though; just make your cribs sheets good.
Nice prof, but frustrating to have as an instructor. Says to not email her and to use Teams message but doesn't reply there either. Regularly moves class online or even cancels

this class is intense mainly due to the nature of the content. Fair warning, stockton's exams rely very much on critical thinking and synthesis of the content which was very annoying cuz there was no practice for this in class. However, there is a huge curve, idk how I made an A lmao

She changes how to class is taught a few times through the semester, and randomly would make class online with little warning. Her exams don't reflect the material learned and are extremely difficult. She is also very passive aggressive and makes the class environment very negative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class; study hard!

Dr. Stockton is one of the best professors I have had! She is hardworking, cares about her students, and wants you to succeed. She is so passionate about the material that it makes you excited to learn. Although she is busy, she tries to make time to help her students and even does online office hours. Her lecture notes are fantastic! Recommend!!!!
Genuine participation class. Lots of projects but reasonable class time is given for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Wish I had more space, but to summarize:
-Teaching style made the course's fiber arts theme surprisingly engaging
-Graded on participation points (only need 100/130 for an A)
-4 fun & easy projects with minimal writing (video, podcast, presentation, and embroidery)
-Most importantly, she is the kindest and most understanding professor I've ever had
Great teaching style, really enjoyable content and projects, easy grader.

I had a very pleasant experience taking the class. Homework mainly consisted of short readings that were to be discussed in class. The final grade was not done on a points scale and instead was about completion and shown effort over the semester, which took out a lot of stress.
It's very clear that Dr. Moore puts the student first.

Dr. Moore is a great professor! The projects we did were non-traditional, including making a podcast, a blog post, and learning a new fiber craft, which I really enjoyed. She makes it very clear exactly what we needed to do to achieve an A for each assignment, and gives great feedback. She is also flexible with deadlines and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was a wonderful professor! She cares heavily about her students and if you communicate clearly, she is always willing to listen to your situation and work with you. Attendance also has a fairly good policy! Definitley recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: some readings before class, but very doable and easy (you can also get by without doing the readings). class theme was toy stories (pretty interesting). all the assignments were either process assignments in preparation for the main artifacts or reflections on the artifacts (all easy). is boring occasionally. All the assignments are self-graded!

In mathematics, understanding concepts and processes is essential. Learning should start with simple problems, building knowledge step by step; lectures often jumped very fast to applications relying on a single method. This limited students' flexibility and made it difficult for those without math backgrounds or extra support to succeed.
She is not knowledgeable about the subject, but has a great personality.

This teacher had a great personality and was very funny, but was a poor lecturer. She consistently made mistakes during lecture that confused us all. She would need time to figure out problems as if she didn't prepare for lecture. Most of what I learned was through research online in my own time since her lectures were inadequate.
ENGH388: Instructions for all the assignments were very unclear. A very tough grader. She doesn't give extensions even there is a reasonable reason.

I took ENGH 388 at George Mason University. Worst professor ever. She deducts points for no reason and doesn't give much explanation. She doesn't help at all even when we are suffering. Doesn't reply to emails properly. Doesn't gives grades on time nor gives good grades. Best in the class was 70/100 for most assignments with an average at 52/100.
Awful professor overall. It appears she was terminated or forced out, which is suitable for a professor of this quality.
