The worst professor I have had in my entire life. She simply reads off the slides in lecture, with absolutely no interest or care. Every class you miss beyond 2 drops grade a letter grade. She does not care about students learning or grades. Unfortunate because material could be interesting otherwise. That being said, the class is pretty easy.

She did not follow the Gatech ethics (which require instructor to give timely grading and feedback). More than 80% of grade come during the last two weeks of the semester. Even a lot of student file complaint against her to coc and school, nothing has changed much.

This is the most confusing course I have had in Tech. She copy the entire syllabus from her junior design class to this Tech comm. During the semester, she keep complaining how much work she have to do and add more and more assignment during the semester (put extra assignment in a vague category in grading).
Worst professor ever. Avoid if possible!
Great professor, easy to follow lectures, very chill assignments and grading.
Words cannot describe how awful my semester with Amanda was.

TERRIBLE and UNFAIR. This was an overflow class, so I understand. I gave the messiness of the assignments and her horrible feedback the benefit of a doubt. In the last 2 weeks of the semester, she gave lousy grades for assignments that lacked direction, feedback, or a rubric. Drafts were graded after finals. Lectures were awful too.

As everyone else mentioned, absolutely avoid this Professor at all costs. She grades based on her feelings, gives 0 useful feedback, expects you to be punctual w assignments but graded everything the day before graduation. Literally the worst educator I have ever had in my entire academic career dating to preschool. Drop her class immediately

You're better off dropping out than taking this professor. The alternative is getting kicked out because she randomly accused you of plagiarism, or having to do another semester because she threw a tantrum and gave everybody a zero on an assignment, or jumping off a bridge because I'd rather end it than have to endure her lectures again.

Avoid pls. Graded all assignments day before finals (likely drunk considering insulting nature of feedback and tendency to "lecture" hungover) and attempted to fail over half the class arbitrarily in everyone's graduating semester. Mandatory attendance, 4 "free skips" but if there was an assignment she gave a 0 even if it was completed virtually.
save yourself

Can only echo the other comments on what occurred during this class, but for context, our class was exclusively graduating seniors. Completely inconsistent grading standards, unfounded accusations of plagiarism, and an almost unbelievable lack of feedback. Would spend significant parts of lecture complaining about her personal life.

NEVER take this professor. Hands down the worst professor I've ever had in my entire life. Doesn't grade most assignments until 2 weeks before graduation. Without prior feedback on drafts or proposals, gives F's on the final assignment with condescending and belittling comments. She is not suited to be teaching at a university like Georgia Tech.

One of the worst professors I have ever had in my time at Georgia Tech. Decided to screw over the entire class less than two weeks before everyone in the class was graduating. She decided to give students F's on the final assignments with one word comments that were unprofessional that dropped students grade by over 20%.

Provides unclear or down right rude feedback on assignments. That is, when she decides to grade. For example she graded the final deliverable for the course BEFORE grading the proposal for said project. When she does decide to grade, many students would say that she seemed to grade blindly, providing no justification for how the student can improve

In all my years of education, I have never had such a horrible experience in a course and felt genuine animosity towards an instructor. She is extremely aggressive, hostile, and unhelpful in her written feedback and will take every opportunity to leave condescending remarks and belittle you in the comments of your assignment.

Horrible prof. Curses in every sentence. Drinks the night before lecture then complain about it in lecture. Disrespectful and seems to hate CS majors by insulting them in class with CS stereotypes. Admits to not caring about the class or teaching yet grades very harshly for some reason.

This is the first time in my life I have witnessed such an uncaring and rude professor. Always talks about her life and how much work she has; she openly hates her job and does not want to be there. Does not communicate and is insanely condescending when she's behind a screen: she openly threatens students while assigning Fs without any criteria.

This professor lacks respect for her position and students, often condescending and bitter. Her grading is inconsistent, and she's openly discussed being hungover and drinking after class. It's disheartening to see such behavior from someone in authority.

never has a class made me want to walk across the street without looking any way. I honestly would give up government secrets if you put me in her class. This was supposed to be a class about tech communication and not once has she ever communicated about anything to do with this class. Why does she talk more about her family than class concepts???

Grades everything last minute and extremely harshly. Talks about nonsense during class yet requires attendance. Has a major ego and is very mean to students. I feel like she's a deeply unhappy person that believes everyone else should be miserable as a result. I'd take an 8am over htis class any day.

Recommending avoiding this professor if possible. Truly does not seem to care about the students regarding their coursework they learn in the class. Unable to communicate the timeline of the class and what is expected for assignments. Assignments are graded extremely late and assignments are related. Makes it hard for students to improve.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR EVER!!!! Doesn't care about the students, gives way too much assignments, grades things way too fast and without much regard to actual quality of work. The worst professor I've had at this school and I pray for all those forced to take her as part of a graduation requirement.

(CS3803) AVOID AT ALL COST. WORST professor ever. RUDE, CONDESCENDING, DISORGANIZED. Does not understand either communication or anything technical, but teaches Tech Communication. More boring jokes and her life stories in class than useful lecture material, but taking notes is required as mandatory attendance. Changes syllabus arbitrarily.

(CS 3803) Terrible professor. teaches communication but cannot communicate themselves, students are constantly confused about instructions. Randomly cancels class and expects students to do several assignments in lieu of class. Randomly chooses assignments to grade very harshly. Very disorganized. Do not take if you have a choice.

(CS 3803 TC)
I have no idea what she is trying to teach and what I am doing with course

Attendance in lecture and studio participation was mandatory as it was part of the final grade. The final and midterm cover the most random topics in class but are not difficult. Your studio TA and participation will probably make or break your final grade.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! By the time final exams had started, only 45% worth of assignments had been graded. On top of taking a long time to grade assignments, she grades harshly and on arbitrary criteria. You can adhere to the rubric all you want, but getting a good grade is near impossible. I was quite lucky to walk away with an A - take another prof!

Absolutely terrible at getting grades in on time and communicating through emails. She waits until the last day before grades are due to actually grade, so if you have weekly assignments due like weekly meeting agendas and you mess up on one, you essentially mess up on the rest of them because she doesn't give feedback on time. Hated her class.

Made this course much more difficult than it needed to be. Graded extremely harshly and did not consider historical averages for this class. Average GPA for this section was significantly lower than for other sections.

I took Amanda's class because it was at a convenient time. Brutal mistake. Grading was incredibly unclear, extremely hard to access outside of class, and the professor has literally zero technical knowledge, but seems to suggest that she does. Listen to the other reviews, take literally any other professor. To top it all off, she has quite an ego.
Lectures are easy to follow, and lecture slides are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: (CS3001) She has some weird policies including dropping students' overall grades by 10% if they miss 2 lectures. Apparently she has instructed TA's to not give students above 90% in section participation. She is also very much NOT accessible and doesn't respond to emails, citing her "busy schedule". Overall mid prof but not the greatest person.

Avoid this professor. They are condescending and do not respond well to questions, grading is confusing and done on expectations that are never conveyed, and constant busy work detracts from things of actual value. Also, they lack the technical skills and soft skills to properly instruct/lead any class. Despite an A, this was a horrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Is not qualified to teach the class, has no technical background and thus severely misgrades technical details. Grades assignments on expectations greatly beyond what is taught in class. Overall, would highly not recommend.

This is a person who literally doesn't deserve a job in academia. Do not take her if you can. I would even skip junior design if she was your only option. Every single assignment is incredibly vague and she grades super harshly. She is literally the most useless professor I've ever had.

This course itself is full of useless work, but Girard makes these assignments even more confusing. What you actually have to do is super unclear, and she is impossible to reach outside of class. She doesn't seem to care about students. They even released a final presentation / project less than a week before break with it due right as we got back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gives worthless assignments to waste your time, forces students to attend an expo she organized so it doesn't seem empty, gives vague instructions for assignments, takes off points seemingly at random, and made us give a presentation THE SAME DAY THEY TOLD US TO GIVE A PRESENTATION and much more. Literally the worst professor I've ever taken.

One of the worse professors I've had at Georgia Tech. Was incredibly rude and condescending whenever I asked a question in class. Half the lectures consisted on her complaining to the people who were present that no one was showing up (we had a class of 12) and the other half consisted of her talking about her dog or reading our assignments to us.

Terrible Teacher, she grades like she's blind, taking off points, saying we didn't submit it, when the submitted assignment is clearly in front of her face. The lectures are mandatory, and just serve to waste your time for the most part. Grades come in right before the end of the semester, such that you might not be able to get them changed. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was better this semester overall considering she had some attitude issues. Her feedbacks did improve quite a bit as well. She is a late grader so it caused us unnecessary stress during the finals week. She clearly doesn't understand how canvas submission works because she took off 10 points for "not having video link" on May 9th night!
She grades super unfairly, saying that we missed parts of our assignments and when we showed they were there she said "Um, do you want me to add a point back or something?"

On the first day, we asked politely if we could choose our teams which is how the course has worked and the next class she claimed we were rude and ranted. This set the tone for the course. You'll do lots of writing for stuff that detracts from the project and she's an unclear grader so it's rough. You won't learn a thing but you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Should be a project-focused class, but gives busy work that wastes time from the actual client project. Gives vague feedback, often takes off for minor grammatical errors but messes up hear/here they're/their/there in the SAME feedback. On top of that, she grades harshly so you're more stressed about the grade in the class than the real proj.

Absolutely awful professor. She grades extremely harshly on assignments for seemingly no reason and her feedback on them is just terrible. It feels like she is looking for ways to make the class difficult for no reason. I have learned absolutely nothing useful from this class. Avoid her at all costs if you are taking junior design.

Prof. Girard is very interesting. If you don't follow the grading criteria extremely specifically, you probably won't get perfect grades on all the assignments. The class is a lot of busywork. However, you will find that it isn't her fault, the class is just designed horribly.

Girard is the worst professor I had at GT. She was very unclear when giving instructions and took off points on assignments for seemingly no reason. Going to her for help outside of class is useless as well. Avoid Girard for junior design at all costs.

I had Girard last semester and was not a fan of her. She still is pretty cold and her grading is just as harsh. However, she was pretty accommodating during the covid crisis so that's why I gave her a 2 instead of a 1. She eliminated some assignments, graded less harshly and didn't make lecture mandatory, which I truly expected her not to do.

Girard grades unnecessarily hard and takes off points for the smallest things. She also won't really clarify why she took off those points and can come off extremely condescending both in class and during office hours. If you see her name when registering, try to avoid her.

Her grading is extremely tough and random. She will take off lots of random points on a paper and her feedback will be extremely vague. Her lectures were really aggressive and she'll remind you every lecture that he has a PhD. Would avoid at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amanda Girard is the worst instructor I have had at Georgia Tech. She lacks any compassion or care towards her students and does not grade any assignments on time. When she does grade assignments, she does not provide any feedback or grade to a rubric. She sets unrealistic expectation and does not provide feedback on drafts. Avoid her at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Taking a class with Professor Girard is a constant uphill battle. She does not clearly explain what she wants from students (she'll give you a rubric, but it's incredibly vague), will be condescending and rude when you ask for help/feedback, and has criticized students' work in front of the class to her co-professor. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Girard is the absolute worst LMC professor for junior design. Avoid her at all costs! Her grading feedback is very vague and she will take off points for absolutely NO reason. Her negative attitude, lack of awareness, and disrespect for student opinion is completely uncalled for.

One of the worst professors I have taken at Georgia Tech. Extremely slow and unreasonable grader with astronomically high expectations. She has quite the ego for an LMC professor and will not hesitate to defend herself when asked about grading. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely and unreasonably tough grader for no good reason in what's supposed to be a fairly easy A class. Gave terrible and unclear feadback on assignments and didn't really follow the grading rubrics that were given. Overall awful, one of the biggest mistakes I made at GT was taking a class with this professor. 0/10

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy was an excellent teacher. You can tell she cares both about civil and about students learning and growing in her class. Exams are graded pretty leniently and she is incredibly kind and open to meeting and talking about anything CEE. The project was fun, and isn't bad if you incrementally work on it through the semester.

Group project heavy; you work with the same group all semester. some exams, but easy if you keep up with class content. the final is the group project, which is sort of graded tough. pay attention to techniques taught in class, because this is what they are looking for

Dr. Kennedy really cares about her students. Long homeworks/tests that are graded pretty tough but the group project should help with your grade. She is so kind and responds immediately to your emails. Overall an interesting class that really teaches you a lot about sustainability and civil systems. Probably more work than it needed to be though

Dr. Kennedy is the best! She has a great personality and is highly respected in the field of Civil Engineering and Sustainability. The class has tests, a group project, and homework all weighted equally with an optional final exam. If you attend class, do the hw and practice tests, and work well with your group members, an A is very achievable.

Personally, this is one of my favorite teachers here at Georgia Tech! I am very interested in Sustainable Urban Development and although the class is called Civil Engineering Systems, it is amazing how she focuses on sustainability analysis of systems as the basis of the class. Additionally, she is the most respected in her field! So much knowledge

Although a hard class, instructor is amazing! Knows concepts and explains them clearly. Although not apparent at first, she does care for you and wants you to be success. Just keep up with the lecture material and stay on top of your group project! The group project is a lot of work and its super important you work on it throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of work. The final is optional; I was borderline so I had to take and somehow made an A. This class has readings, a group project which requires research, and homework assignments. The prof explains well enough. If you want to meet with her you have to make an appointment (she's busy). Very knowledgeable about her subject

If you're an A student who works hard for your grade, don't take her. If you only look for easy B with minimal effort, you've found your gem. Ridiculous grader (you'd get like 0.5 or 0.8 on "definition" about sustainability in an ENGINEERING class.) Does not have solution for in class problems. VERY inaccessible. Grades on project very arbitrary.

Decent professor who clearly cares about the subject. The class has easy material but you really need to work hard to do well. First test involves memorization so class average was low but the other 2 tests are math which is easy. Also, group project is tedious and there's a decent amount of homework in the class. Work hard and you'll get an A (88
Good professor, clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Lots of writing involved, as well as a massive group project.

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy is very passionate about this course but isn't the best at relating to students and student concerns.  The grading criteria is slightly strange and she expects you to do a lot for the class outside of lecture.  She is a great person and very nice but the class was just average and tedious at times.
Very willing to help anyone that has a question and very nice. She's very knowledgeable in the subject. I would recommend her!

I took this course Spring 2022. I found the lectures to be extremely dry. Prepare yourself to participate in class discussions, which are highly philosophical. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on essays. It seemed to me that if he didn't agree with your stance on a topic, you would receive an unfavorable grade for the essay and vice versa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The readings can be long at 15-25 pages on average but you will do well as long as you show up to class, participate, and complete the assignments. Discussions in class are engaging and Dr. Prasad is not heavy on lecturing. He cares a lot about students and can give a lot of guidance on the two essays (which were 50% of the class grade).

There was a lot of reading and the material was pretty dense. The class itself though was interesting and engaging and Dr. Prasad was very caring about the students. There are normally three papers and a few small assignments. It's expected you do the readings before class to participate but not required (i.e. no pop quizzes).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great Prof
No Comments
The most amazing professor I have ever had!!  Can we spell out NOBEL PRIZE

Nice guy who was always willing to help, but just reads off slides in lecture, so explanations are not that great. The lectures he "made" were clearly AI and don't really line up with the HW and Exams. TA's are great though and carry this class, making the HW, Exams, and Project which I thought were all good.

His lectures were interesting, and he is super sweet. The TAs are fine... office hours just get busy, and they also cancel a lot. The tests are not bad if you study, you will have to get review content on your own because he goes pretty fast. A ton of resources tho so its honestly not hard class. Make sure to lock in on project, helps grade a lot.
Had an unfortunate experience in this class which put me in a really bad headspace.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: fast paced class. it was like doing multiplication at the kitchen table with my dad but with coding and it's no longer socially acceptable to cry or not understand what's going on. luckily i like cs but others… goodluck! also didnt feel like the TAs and professor were on the same page half the time
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not teach. He speed-reads a slide show and then hopes you get it in time to do a coding problem at the end of class. The TA's for this class are also not nice, which makes it hard.
goated TAs
decent prof, not so decent (or nice) TAs.

Pretty average professor and class. Lectures are basically reading off of the sides so most people don't attend them anyways. However, it seems that Prof. Musaev does care about teaching and is happy to answer questions. Offers a break during lecture which is nice. Would only recommend taking this class for CS1331 if you already know Java.

He taught 1100 like it should be. He set up valuable sessions with gt alum and faculty that delivered valuable info for a first year. Not too much work outside class. dont stress if you have him for 1100

CS 1100 is a fairly pointless and annoying class. Professor Musaev does not really do anything other than introduce the speaker each week, except for the one time he tried to demo an agentic workflow and it didn't work. The homework each week is usually pointlessly long, but they are not graded harshly at all.

There were multiple lectures where he would just sit and code on the projector, but he went so fast that it was difficult to understand or replicate. It's not too hard of a class and the homeworks aren't too bad, but I found that the lectures weren't helpful at all.

I think a lot of the reviews for Prof. Musaev are overly negative, but I can understand where they're coming from. He's a decent lecturer, but neither lecture nor recitation are super informative. HWs get difficult, but they're only 1/wk. Seek help on Ed or by talking to classmates/TAs if you're stuck; they can explain in much better detail.

he was nowhere near as bad as these reviews made him out to be. the midterms/exam were made by ta's and were pretty straightforward often asking multiple questions on the same kind of edge cases. lectures were optional and the slides/recitations were what mattered. what i didn't like was that homoworks took forever and tests made/broke your grade.

Clearly cares about the subject, but lectures are dry and long. If you know how to make projects in Java, lecture is not necessary. A good performance in AP CS A is enough to do well in this class, plus a bit of studying the content later in the semester. 40% final though.

The 3 exams and the final were all easier than I expected. Participation is not mandatory but he did sometimes hint at what could be on an upcoming exam and went over live demos so I'd go, or at least look at the slides and posted code. Recitation and the TAs were super helpful, and Musaev himself is pretty passionate and willing to help as well.
Amazing Professor! Attending lectures was not difficult, I don't know what everyone is talking about.

First, the good: He was very forgiving with the grades, offering extra credit on exams, and dropped like your 7 lowest assignments. Now, the bad: if you have no coding experience outside of 1301, you're cooked. In the lectures he codes and debugs really fast, but doesn't actually teach. The weekly homeworks could take 8 hours, and they never stop.

I attended lectures for the first month and a half, as I didn't feel I was learning from his teaching style. He mostly read from slides and coded exercises without clearly explaining the concepts, which made it hard to stay engaged. However, CS 1331 is manageable with prior Java experience, and the recitations were helpful, especially before exams.

Musaev just sits back on a chair lol. The class is free if you show up, but the one time Musaev tried to actually teach us how to use Agentic Workflows, he stalled for 5 minutes and ended up using all his Claude tokens anyways, so we didn't learn anything personally from him!
Lectures were mandatory (if you missed 5 or more, you fail) and not that helpful to succeed in CS. Homework was long, unhelpful, and always required us to share documents.

I didn't go to half the lectures, but when I did, we'd usually go over some live demo, which was a breath of fresh air compared to lecture slides. Class is pretty well run, and I really liked the coding homework as it helped me learn a lot. Recitation slides were the most helpful study resource out of anything in this course.

if u generally knew what u were doing and did hws, all the exams were pretty easy imo. lectures were pretty boring + i never paid attention, but he seems like an ok dude. i learned from the internet and recitations, which were helpful. participation quizzes were annoying but there's unlimited attempts and they were helpful in recapping lectures

If you go to lecture and attend recitations/PLUS sessions, probably end with an A. Exams 1 and 2 are easy if you took CSA. Exams 3 is slightly and Final (38% grade) is much harder. Take him cause he provides lecture slides. Think he scales final but he releases grades last day and doesn't show final on Gradescope so little annoying. Decent overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I took this instead of just cheesing the advanced standing exam. this class is for the gatech LCD that got in without knowing any programming languages. boring waste of time.

if you can't pass 1331 ase you probably don't belong in gtcs. do not take this class.

hws are super heavy so start those early. i took ap csa in high school so many of the concepts were familiar and i didnt have to attend plus sessions or recitations, but if you're someone who's new to java, you'll probably have to attend those things as his lectures are kinda useless. class is very test heavy and the final is 38% of grade.

The lectures are pretty useless unless you're a cookie cutter cs major. Honestly they ask for too much in the assignments too but everything is manageable.  Don't take gt 1000 if you're taking this, you're just gonna waste your time.
Boring mandatory lectures that are unhelpful
Exam heavy, grades harshly, quiz only has a 24 hours window with no announcement, unhelpful TAs, emails are cold and unreachable, poor attitude
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a very engaging lecturer, and as a newbie to Java, lectures were very difficult to follow. The recitation and PLUS sessions were a good tool for learning the content in the class. Homeworks were long but not overly difficult. Beware of the final exam, which is a very large chunk of your grade and a step up in difficulty to the previous exams.

Lectures weren't paced great - introductions to concepts went too slow and coding examples went too fast to retain anything. I personally struggled going in unfamiliar with java. Had coding homeworks due every week that would take a few hours. Exams were also weighted very heavily that focused a lot on theory over actual coding.
If you are able to, learning content outside of class is a good way. Recitations were good to review class content.
Do not take his lecture if you don't have previous experience in Java. Tests make up so much of your grade and the homeworks take forever. Lectures are boring and don't really help.

I taught myself this class using the resources provided. I highly recommend that, if you do go to lecture, just listen and watch what he does (don't go on your computer and try and copy everything down) cause otherwise, it's hard to follow along. I liked recitation and the PLUS sessions. Update: That final... oof.

This course isnt very hard if you already knew Java (I did not). If you also dont you will have to put a lot more effort in outside of class because the lectures are not helpful at all (no elaboration on concepts, examples coded so fast you cant retain anything, etc). Just learn everything outside of class and dont waste your time going to lectures

What professor you take doesn't really matter in this course (idk if there's even multiple options). This guy seems alright though. The course itself is a decent amount of busy work and lecture attendance is required, but otherwise its chill.

I enjoyed this class the professor clearly cared about the students and how we learned in class. He was clearly knowledgeable and did helpful demos during lecture. He also did a break in the middle of class which make content easier to digest. Grading was hard but it wasn't up to him. Just go to lecture and you will do fine in the course.

Lectures are engaging, with fun brain breaks in between. Lectures are not mandatory.

In recitations leading up to exams, TAs review all material that will be covered, often using similar question formats. Recitation slides are available online if you miss.

Class was easy, and those who complain are not suited for CS. 100% would take again.
Final exam counts for 38% of grade for what

He does not care for this class. Goes on tangents about one specific idea and then takes brain breaks that last almost half an hour every lecture. Would not recommend to my worst enemy. Exams were worded poorly and TAs constantly contradicted each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good for CS1100. Lectures are a bit dry but then again, so is the class in general. You have to fill out participation notes every class and there are some required workshops/events you have to attend but overall very easy. Pretty boilerplate professor.

Took over the summer at GTE. Straightforward class with 6 mini exams and a group project with three phases. Only downside is the lectures are sometimes not as in depth as how you need to apply it in the mini exam or project so you may have to study some on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He lectured similar to how he does in 1331 for 4400. As long as you could pay attention in class you really didn't need to study outside from the lecture. He gave quizzes about every week that were testing the material from the week before. Group project for the class wasn't too difficult and he gave us a lot of time for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Always had a break in the middle. CS 1331 is a pretty standardized class, so the grading isn't really up to him. His lectures and practice were definitely the best way to learn the material.

Class felt fair and well paced as I was on par for a B+ until that 3rd exam and final. Make sure you are very familiar with Java. HWs are borderline forever to do. Idk where people get the "done in 2 hour" statements. If you're normal and new to Java like me, you'll struggle with implementation. The more you already know the better so pre-study :)

Unprofessional and Unfriendly professor. Useless and Unclear lectures, Doesn't Answer Questions ("look online"), 
Only thing I remember from this class is "I'm here to give you my opinion on Java, not to teach you guys." 
WHAT DO YOU MEAN WE CANT SEE OUR FINAL GRADE???

Lectures were very dry and didn't really leave you with anything. Just go to recitation instead or take another lecturer if possible. Usually curves final exam but otherwise not much extra credit or help if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Pros: tests don't have curveballs/very clear about what to expect, reasonable guy who seems to care about students and feedback, homework tends to be reasonable 
Cons: lectures are kinda boring, final is weighted hella
Would probably still take him over some others like stasko feel like he's more reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was quite boring and nobody went to his lectures. He didn't engage the class well enough and all of my learning came from the Recitations and PLUS sessions. I found it very strange that for the final our scores were never released and we only received a final grade. I have no idea how I did on that final.

He's a boring lecturer, ended up not going to lectures at some point. PLUS sessions were helpful, and the slides he posted were useful too. I mostly used those to study. The final was difficult for me and was weighted much heavier than the rest of the midterms, so despite good grades throughout the semester, a mid final grade put me at a B.

BS 24-hour-window participation activities are really annoying. He's also a completely useless lecturer but that's really just because the TAs in recitation or PLUS sessions outshine him in every way. You DON'T NEED TO GO TO LECTURE, JUST RECITATION. Take whatever timeslot u want with this guy bc u don't have to show up to class lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't take his job as a professor seriously- I remember him saying "I'm not here to teach you, I'm here to evaluate you." Lectures are boring and you can self-study everything better than he teaches.

Extremely dry lectures, barely goes over conceptual knowledge before coding examples. Watched a few of Landry's videos during async days and those were so much higher in quality. HWs are pretty lengthy if you have no Java experience, tests are straightforward and much easier than hw. Go to recitation- TAs explain concepts a lot better than he does.

Lectures were pretty boring tbh especially at 8 am. He also doesn't post very accessible code outside his lectures so even though attendance isn't mandatory, it would be pretty difficult to understand concepts online because it doesn't show a lot of examples.

Replaced Landry in the middle of the semester - lectures instantly became boring. He codes in front of you and doesn't go very far in depth about it. Advertised his AI side hustle in class. Like other reviews mention, had to self study the content after he took over.
Tough class, but manageable if you stay engaged. Lectures can be dry, but recitations are helpful. Definitely use unstuck study alongside the textbook for study prep.

Dr. Musaev is one of the best professors I've ever had! A very good lecturer, and I appreciated how comfortable he was with IntelliJ and Java in general - his quick typing and excellent spelling/syntax were small things that really made a difference in the course. A good intro-level course in that it truly piqued my interest for future CS courses.

Lectures not worth the time - just go to recitation. The final is worth way too much. For one of the midterms, they randomly decided to not test us on half of the content that should have been on the exam (without an announcement). May sound good, but there were basically 2x the questions of each type/concept so if you got one of those wrong...rip

God, Musaev was boring. For context, he replaced Landry after the tampon eating incident, and dear god he was so boring. Terrible teaching style for programming. Basically had to self-learn the last few weeks of content. Avoid if possible. Take Landry instead. Seriously.
Alright lecturer, mostly reads off the slides. If you have better options, take them even if it's at a worse time.

Musaev was honestly pretty good.He did a good job at explaining concepts that needed explaining. For 1331, I personally think it's much better to do the coding examples and use RECITATIONS to supplement conceptual understanding. Do the HWs early, you'll hate yourself less later. People here are prolly mad just bc they didn't give much effort lol
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He just reads slides and codes examples... except he speeds through the coding examples and calls on the same 2-3 students assuming everyone understands. After every class I would try to recall what I learned, and couldn't rmr. He's a boring lecturer, but he does tell you what will be covered on exams. Just attend recitation and you'll be fine.

Pros: Very transparent about what will/won't be on the exams, does his best to keep the class' interest, isn't unfairly tough, generally a well-meaning person.
Cons: Doesn't go into as much depth as he should on concepts, speeds through coding examples, a lot of the real learning will take place on GeeksForGeeks and similar sites.
Study for the final, it will make or break your grade!!!!!!

Biggest troll I have encountered in my ed career. Copies slides from textbook & codes demos super fast. Instead of lecture read his slides, do slide practices & read textbook if stuck. TAs are amazing for HW help & explaining concepts. Start HW early. Teaches surface level of content to have time to ask riddles & gets mad if you know the answer.
Relatively good lecturer. Test heavy class which goes super fast if you are not familiar with OOP. I would say for 1331, prof doesn't matter.

This professor is very boring, don't bother going to lectures. He doesn't really explain and expects u to already have an understanding of the material. It's mostly just exs in class but his voice is so monotone I couldn't focus at all.

Musaev is a nice professor, but I just didn't mesh with his teaching style. He took over my section's lectures after Landry's departure, and while Landry was consistently behind on content, I liked his conceptual explanations of the material more than Musaev, who usually would brush past concepts and go straight into coding. Go to recitation!!!

His lectures aren't that useful, just go to recitations, which were way clearer and more useful. The tests are pretty straight forward, but for the final keep an eye on the things Musaev reviews in class as they're really helpful for preparing. Homework takes a while so be sure to start early

Musaev is lowkey an amazing professor. He single handedly saved me from failing the final. Basically, don't attend lectures and only go to recitation for most of the class. BUT when the final hits, look at all the resources Musaev posts because his class exercises basically spoil the final.

I only had him for half a semester, was ok. Reads slides + does coding example is his lecture format. Seems nice enough, but not great at explaining or engaging. You definitely need to know Java well before taking his class, but I'd say that about 1331 in general. Not my first pick but I wouldn't take an 8 am to avoid him, if that makes sense

Most of the class was taught as if students already knew the content. Lectures were useless and was often told that we needed to learn the material outside of class. Homeworks were long and most of the class is graded by the exams and the final. Recitations clutch up, even just the slides that are uploaded are very helpful.

reviews.comment:
presentation reader.
strong russian accent.
learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Avoid him if u can. I checked how CS 1331 was graded a few years ago; it was nothing like it is now. Tests are 80% of ur grade in an intro course. On top of this, he also is a relatively bad lecturer. He will barely go over the concepts, so basically, no one will understand it the first time unless you learned Java before taking this class. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Struggles to teach effectively, skipping basics and jumping to details, leaving students confused. Relies on the same 1-2 students (already familiar with the material) to answer questions, assuming the whole class understands. Ends class late, avoids questions, and once said, "I ask questions; students don't ask me," further discouraging engagement
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a pretty mid professor, his lectures are pretty useless as he spends time doing coding examples that are hard to follow, but he posts his notes every class so you can get an A and still learn the material by never showing up. Honestly if you're stuck with him it's not the end of the world, I'd probably take him again but not very eustatically.

Prof. Musaev's course is an easy A. The tests were open notes and online. I control-f all my solutions. He might be the biggest grade inflator in the whole CS department. Def recommend if you want a GPA booster.

He was an alright professor. Nothing really stand out about him, and the lectures were kind of boring and dry at times. Most of the class was spent implementing some concept from his ppt, which was fine, but got repetitive. They were useful, but it was difficult to pay attention most of the time because of his monotone voice. Overall, he is fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've had all A's my entire life including my first year of college. I had to drop this class because he really doesn't teach much. All your learning has to be done outside of the classroom. Lectures are boring. If you don't already know Java then good luck. I already knew basic Java and it still didn't go well for me. Take literally any other Prof.

This is my second time having him. I had him for CS4400, and honestly he explained all the concepts well. No complaints. He gives tons of chances to improve your grade even though the class is extremely easy. The workload was also really fair. I'd take him if I had a chance

Good professor for this class, the "tests" were six mini-exams, each 12% of our grade with the lowest dropped. 10% pop quiz participations that were pretty easy, and 30% for a group project that wasn't bad. Would definitely recommend this professor.

If you paid attention to the lectures this class was an extremely easy A, and if you didn't and crammed the night before the tests it was a bit more difficult, but still a manageable A. The past tests he posts are really good indicators of the tests in class, and the recitations by the TAs the nights before the test were helpful.

I honestly don't understand all the bad reviews. He is a nice professor and does a good job teaching concepts. Most students tend to just blame the professor whenever they struggle lol. Go to class, ask questions, and practice and you will be good. HWs are long and suck though.
Very bad lecturer

He would say the title of the concept and jump straight into coding. There was no explanation about the data structure whatsoever. I thought I was just being dumb until I looked over his slides on my own time and found that his slides skipped over a whole topic. And when the topic does happen to be covered, there are only like two slides.
Not that bad of a professor. Might be a little difficult if you don't have previous coding knowledge though.

The lectures are extremely boring. Recitation is a godsend. Musaev assumes students know Java and just brushes over topics during lecture. Homeworks are difficult and grueling. It is always unclear what will be on the exam; always a curveball question (with no partial points) worth a decent chunk of points. Not beginner friendly. Ironic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't attend too many of his lectures because they were quite bad. He assumed you already knew Java which was fine since I did, but he skipped many details and his examples were hard to follow. Almost your entire grade is the midterms/final. Super nitpicky but that's more the class than Musaev. Homeworks and recitations are best for learning.

Awful for being an "intro" course. Everything was designed as if with experienced students in mind. Prof went thru basics quickly, and his demos in class were difficult to follow. Long HWs that may as well be called "mini-projects" were assigned weekly. Intricate details such as efficiency & security of code were graded harshly for an intro class.

He started out actually teaching the material with live demos, but halfway through he had a kid and went virtual before coming back. After that he wasn't the same prof, he was disorganized and really derogatory towards the student body. He pretty much just assumed you knew java - I would recommend him over landry, but that's not saying much.

This professor and the TA's graded pretty roughly taking as many points as they could. The professor also make no effort to provide any extra material to study outside of homework and other assignments and the lecture notes. He also refused to record lectures help students. There is also next to no extra credit for this course.

It is very difficult to prepare for tests with Dr. Musaev. He's definitely passionate, and he's not unkind, but he rambles through lectures and glazes over topics as if we're already experts on it. Students should be expected to have Java fundamental knowledge, but Musaev takes that way over the top. The tests are almost entirely trick questions.

Lectures have nothing to do with the main aspect of the class which is the group project. Expects everyone to know how to use Android Studio and GitHub to the point of requiring it without ever even giving an overview. Lectures are painfully boring and quizzes are stupidly easy.

CS 1331 is known to be a weed out class and can be hard regardless of your prof if you don't have a lot of java experience. I took him to avoid take Landry and think I dodged a bullet. He was nice and I thought he was okay at explaining thing thou I think it would be much harder to follow without a background in java thou.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He basically assumes that you know everything. All he does in class is introduce new materials and start writing codes about those without explaining the objectives of the class and niche exceptions that students might get confused. I would not recommend his class when you are a JAVA beginner (which is ironic because this class is intro to JAVA).

His lectures are so bad. He does not teach the materials and writes code 24/7 which does not help students who do not clearly know the materials, especially those who do not have any prior knowledge of java.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not good at teaching beginner.
Was terrible at explaining and teaching. No structure to lectures

Long homeworks every week, hard to balance with other classes, exams are fairly simple as long if study well, except for the final exam, which is worth 28% of your grade, it is brutal and very difficult. Don't take this class lightly and always start early on homeworks and you should be okay. TAs are also great, always go to office hours.

After reading the reviews for Landry this semester, I think I dodged a bullet by taking Musaev. The biggest problem with lecture is that Musaev kind of assumes that everyone knows Java, so if you don't know something, he'll just tell you to find out on your own. However, he does live coding and exam reviews, which prepares you for the exams well.
The class itself is very team dependent, so the level of difficulty may vary, but his other assignments (mini-assessments/quizzes) are not difficult. Class lecture is boring though.

Musaev is an amazing instructor. I was originally taking Richard Landry (who was terrible) and I switched to his lecture and my grade immediately jumped up. He is also very involved outside of the classroom with projects that he incorporates into the discussion in the class about Java! Highly recommend Musaev for CS1331.

if youre not the smartest person in a cs class, do not take him for 1331. i came in with no coding experience before 1301 and he explained next to nothing in lecture. he would gloss over the content for like 5 minutes and then launch into demos that made no sense and were way too fast to follow.

I took him for CS1331, but it was his first time teaching it. So he couldn't answer many course-related questions. But, he knows a lot about JAVA and programmed for us during class instead of just reading lecture slides. This was great because he typed fast so it wasn't boring and we got to actively learn. TAs were helpful but homework was tedious.
The lectures are boring and so is the general content of the course. However, it is super easy to get an A. All you need is a good group that puts work in. Just a stupid, but necessary, class.
Lots of work but an easy A. Useless professor though, I had to continuously convince myself throughout the semester that getting a CS degree was worth it
This is supposed to be a project based class and the project was announced with less then half a semester left. Lectures are a waste waste of time, irrelevant, and boring.

The class changed this year to let us do React projects, but this was extremely useful. Most web based engineering jobs use skills from this class's projects - developing and connecting the front end and back end together. Very useful. Prof isn't the most interesting but he's cool and nice and the class has many many bonuses to help you get an A.

The class is definitely poorly structured like other reviews mentioned, and the semester-long group project can be quite tedious. However, Musaev offers very generous amounts of extra credit throughout the semester. His lectures aren't too fun but he takes attendance through an online survey that you can just fill out at home too. An easy A.

Clutched an A due to those extra credits for milestones and having one of the best groups I've ever had made this class easy. However, the professor and overall course were very unorganized. I'm good at memory so going over hundreds of slides wasn't bad, but first exam no notes or anything but then decides to change that as the course goes on sucks

Probably the worst lecturer I've EVER seen. Besides lectures being awful, class structure is clear. You can cram the lecture material for tests the week of and you're allowed a cheat sheet now. Project demos are easy if you get the right TA. Last 2 milestones had okay extra credit. Not hard to get A. 2340 is just generally a poorly designed course.

CS 2340 is a fairly easy A as long as you finish the parts of your project on time. I think some people struggled with the first test because the curriculum is kind of weird to do with mc but as long as you go to lecture or take notes from the powerpoint, you should be fine. The prof's lectures were pretty good too imo.

More than professor Musaev, I just hated the content of the class and how he decided to grade us on the class. The class was focused on a lot of arbitrary concepts that were put on the tests and never made sense. The main point of the class which was the group project was weighted very low and was not worth the amount of effort we had to put.

Tests are weighted too heavily while most of the time spent will be on the group project. Instructions are often unclear and TAs are somewhat unresponsive on Piazza. Musaev is not mean spirited enough to want to give his students low grades, but he is also not interested in teaching the material

I stopped going to Musaev's lectures after the first couple of weeks. Unengaging and unclear, I wish I learned these topics from a diff prof because I found the topics taught in this class important to learn. His slides were unclear and TA grading criteria was much less clear. Overall this class sucks, I had to learn everything from online websites
Dr. Musaev is one of the best professors at Georgia Tech. His lectures are such a great sleep aid that he cured my insomnia!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Musaev skips half his slides & glosses over important concepts. Exams are difficult & based on memorization instead of actual design principles. Basically, if you wanna do well in this class, find a good group to do the project with & memorize the entirety of his slides/textbook. Lecture isn't helpful at all - learn everything on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take his class. The exam is a tough and useless. The professor just read ppt in his lecture and really don't care student. Less extra credit than before and the final is really really difficult projects during final week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Exam 1 was close-everything for us but all exams were open-note for previous semesters. And we were given the practice exam which was nothing related to the actual exam. This class should be project-based, but he wants to tackle us at exams.

Tests were weighted ridiculously compared to the project in the project-based class, there were always a handful of just insanely specific questions on there. The material had no hand in preparing us for actually using the frameworks we did to construct our apps. Also, insanely boring lecturer. Zero energy, zero focus on high relevance material.

In a course focused on group projects and code development, they decided to increase the weight of the tests that quiz you on a million different topics that have to be brute memorized. Lectures are not worth going to, and the professor is useless.

Words cannot express how much I hate this class, professor, and the TAs. 1) made the class harder for no reason other than "too many people getting As" 2) TAs really don't care about you except a rare few of them 3) Abbey Musaev is the most boring professor ever 4) for a project based class, 60% of our grade is based on exams that test our memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has been the worst class I have ever taken. There were a million ways this class could have been structured better but the professor chose to make a project based class more dependent on rote learning 1200 slides instead of the project which you will spend most of your time on while being 27% of the grade. Some TA's also on a power trip

This class singlehandedly ruined my mood this semester. They decided to make 2340 unfairly difficult with 60% of the project-based classes' grade on tests that expect memorization of one-bullet point info out of 6-8 powerpoints per test. You can make tests difficult while making it fair (see: CS1332, CS2110). This class missed that mark by a mile.

I usually wait for the semester to be over, but this is a special case. This professor is genuinely bad. There are instances where a student can exaggerate a professor's quality given a bad experience or a bad grade. However, this is not one of those instances. This professor has created a truly irritating and useless course.

This professor has a huge ego to go with a completely useless class. His lectures are the most boring I've ever attended, not to mention his outsized anger when anyone dares whisper in the lecture is laughable. The TAs were no help throughout the class. I would not recommend this professor, unfortunately, he is the only option.

Literally nothing good about this class. Suppose to be a project class, but you gotta memorize for the tests because apparently "we can't have too many As, so we are gonna make you guys do closed-notes instead" Both the professors and the TAs can't pretend to care. Office hours move randomly, TAs are pretty much of no help.

The course is ridiculous. The professor has a real ego problem - he thinks his course is about the industry and real world, and at the same time he prefers JavaFX and a million year old website called Catme. It's a project heavy course with 27% project grade and 60% exam grade. This course should be replaced with new materials and new professor.

"We got a lot of constructive feedback last semester about our instructional style and the content, yet we still received a large amount of As." instead of improving the lecture experience they make it close notes so the amount of As will drop. Ironically this is a class about problem solving in software development & thats how they solve problem

How can I begin to describe this class? Professor Musaev is hands-down one of the best professors I've ever laid my eyes on at Tech. I'm only 3 weeks into the course, but I've already learned so much about what I don't want to become in the future: a CS 2340 professor!

Honestly, worst professor so far. Lectures are boring and content is poorly covered. Sometimes, the material is self-contradictory. For a project class, 60% of the class is exams. Content is not hard conceptually but is boring and 100% reliant on memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Should be an easy A if you get a good group. Did not go to class after the second lecture and neither did most people. Just had to remind myself to show up for tests, which I easily studied by just reviewing the slides and creating a study guide a couple days before the class.

The class is heavily focused on a semester-long project, which is actually a decent experience. The content of the class is also fairly relevant, but it's soooo boring. Aibek really doesn't help in that department either, because he just reads off of a slide show verbatim during lecture. Tons of extra credit and open-note tests tho, so easy A

I don't think the professor is necessarily a bad lecturer or anything, but the way that content is delivered isn't... great. Lectures are boring, I stopped going after Exam 1. The project, which the course is based upon (software development, OOD, etc) feels entirely different from what we're doing in lecture aside from drawing a few diagrams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I pay Georgia Tech unfathomable sums of money to listen to this man's in-class ASMR lectures. You need to be the Hindu god of focus to pay attention in this class. Tests were medium/easy, but don't underestimate the final project. Would highly recommend studying OOD outside of class b/c it's actually useful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not caring at all. Not sure what I was expecting, but at least try and teach the material and help your students pass the class. Does not have the compassion to care about problems that his students are going through, would rather fail the entire class.
Get a good project group, you'll get an A.

Worst class taught at Georgia Tech. Grading criteria was really unclear (open-ended subject, and no benefit of the doubt given). Effort for this class is double for all of my other classes because of the group project. Group projects are only like 30% of the grade, while exams are 60%. Things may change, since Musaev did ask for feedback often.

He never considers students feeling. He would assign students in group randomly and does not think about students preference. Although he somewhat gives a survey to make sure what kind of groupmates you want, he would separate you with your chosen teammates and not admit he did this. DO NOT EXPECT A GREAT EXPERIENCE IN THIS COURSE!!!

For Spring 2021 he took away a huge chunk of the EC he used to give out, and as a result it wasn't *as* easy to get an A if you don't study/practice for the exams, which is what I came into the class thinking. TAing for 2340 is also basically the easiest/most BS TA opps to snag, and that also means some of them are on a power trip when grading.

CS2340 has some pretty boring material regardless of the professor teaching it. Museav's lectures are pretty boring since he just reads off slides but as long as you get a good group for the project and do decent on the exams and do the extra credit if you need it, this class is a pretty easy A.

The consensus is that CS 2340 is a necessary but boring class, regardless of the teacher. Musaev is pretty boring, but he's clear on what you need to do and grades easily. My heavy recommendation is to take this class with friends, because about 80% of the work comes in group projects and you pick your own teams, even across different sections.
As long as you do the reading, watch lectures, you should be able to get A on exams. Group project does require some work. Make sure you get good teammates. Not a difficult class in general

CS 2340 with Musaev is DEFINITELY not an easy class even if 85-90% of people get an A in the class. Exams are heavily weighted (55% total) relative to how other professor's weight the class. Don't come with the mentality that this class is an easy A and you'll be fine. Lecture slides are sufficient in learning the material.

Everyone is dumping on this class but the material is just boring. Musaev is a cool guy and the group project was a lot of fun. The grading criteria for the tests left a lot to be desired. However, the stuff that is taught is pretty open-ended and is kinda hard to grade. Don't be afraid of this class, it really isn't that bad.

The class material is boring, so it wasn't necessary to go to lectures. Tests were open-note and pretty easy as long as you reviewed how to make diagrams beforehand. Group projects were also fine if you got a good group. He gave extra credit in some milestones and was active on Piazza. Overall, easy class and a fine prof to take it with.

Pros: - Relatively active piazza (only 1332 was better) - group project - open note exams - no honorlock - easy to get A's on exams and projects - decent amount of extra credit Cons - Very boring/useless material - unpredictable diagram grading - group final (long, boring) - anonymous poet Musaev is a good person, but the class is a drone.

This is the worst class I've ever taken in my entire life hands down. Musaev is a nice guy but this class is just absolute garbage and to me just felt like a timesink. The material is so boring and the class is extremely disorganized, there was constant clarifications needed before exams like hours before and everything was just annoying imo.

Extremely easy course and easy A . Tests are all open note and the semester project is really easy (unless you want to put in the extra effort). Prof Musaev is a nice guy, but he is an extremely boring professor. It really isn't worth showing up to class because of how mundane lectures can be so I ended up skimming through recordings at 2x speed.

If you're like me and you want an easy A, then you should take Musaev. I'm not sure why people don't like the class; the tests range from easy to medium, the group project is simple enough, and the final is take-home. The lectures are boring (like most classes anyway), but attendance isn't mandatory anyway. Musaev is a professor I'd take any day.

This class already has the disadvantage of presenting very dry, mundane, and uninteresting material, yet the lectures somehow make them even more boring. Dr. Musaev tries to be interactive but the combination of the boring material and delivery makes the class tedious. The slides are enough for exams. However, the project is pretty good and useful.

You don't need to go to lecture. If you go, you'll be listening to an audiobook as he essentially just reads the textbook during class. Just review the slides before a test and you should be fine. This class is mostly project-based, so just stay on top of the milestones and you should get an A.

To be fair, this is the most boring material imaginable, but Musaev doesn't help make it less boring at all. He just reads off his slides that are already hard to follow. The tests are open-note, so it's possible to literally never go to class and still pass. The semester-long project is actually fun, but it has like nothing to do with lecture.

He always read straight from the textbook for lecture and made the class really hard to pay attention to. Material is important but not well taught. Didn't have a choice as he was the only professor available. The class is not hard at all, but he made me lose interest in this material.

I was so bored out of my mind that I didn't even bother showing up for the rest of the semester. It's the type of boring where you're in physical pain. Project is fine if you have a decent group and tests are ok and open book (pandemic) so its just me trying to figure out a month worth of content in an hour.

The course material isn't the most interesting, but Professor Musaev has been very kind, light-hearted, and accommodating with everything being online. Tests are open note and projects have extra credit. Overall, this class has been very fair. Note: free textbook, would look at it from time to time, but nearly everything is covered in class slides

The group project is easy to get an A on. The lectures consist of him reading off slides and are incredibly boring. The tests are poorly made and graded on a very unpredictable rubric (diagrams "require" things that are not always obvious you should add. HOWEVER, there is a lot of Extra Credit and the class is overall not too hard.

Not great. Lectures are very confusing and scattered and seem to contradict itself. Tests are graded sometimes subjectively. Definitely a class that you get what you put into it, however with Musaev it seems you have to put in extra to just comprehend whats important and what isn't.

He's a nice professor and means well but is stuck teaching a boring, borderline useless, class so the lectures are stale. The project takes a bit of time, but if you do the bare minimum you can get well a 100 on each milestone. Cram for the exams using the textbook and hope to do decent enough that the project carries you to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CS2340 is an easy class, but I still wish the lectures weren't so boring. He's a nice person, but not the best at explaining concepts. He rambles, and uses a monotone voice throughout lecture. Towards the middle of the semester, I stopped going to lectures (he posts the slides). There is a lot of extra credit and tests aren't weighted much anyway.

Group project was easy and offered lots of bonus points. I made B's on both midterms by studying the night before and the morning of. The final exam was a group assignment which was not difficult. Most people do not enjoy 2340 (this was true even before Musaev), and neither did I. The material is boring stuff that you need to know for industry.

Lectures were vague, dry, and often contradictory. The group project that made up most of the grade was fairly easy, but the exams were a mess - you'd be graded by a very specific rubric on diagrams where a lot was left open to interpretation. When questioned about the final exam rubric, he closed the class online discussion rather than explain.

He never really seemed in touch with the semester-long group projects, which were designed by the TAs. Would basically read off the lecture slides, so going to lecture wasn't really necessary if you just crammed the slides the night before the exam.

Aibek Musaev is a great guy, but a terrible lecturer, unless you have insomnia. However, it does not really matter much because the class material is easy to learn on your own. Do well on the project, learn the diagrams, and cram a few days before midterms and you won't have to go to class to do well anyways.

Even with different professors this class is known as the "focus on the project, fail exams  A" class. BUT with this professor and his weirdly written exams and poor teaching its extremely hard to get an A. Avoid this guy, he doesnt care about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This prof doesn't know what he's teaching. He straight up reads off presentation slides and gets things wrong all the time. Extremely unorganized, the syllabus laid out nothing for tests and assignments. He just doesn't know what he's doing. The class itself isn't hard but it is very irritating to have him as a professor.
Best Prof Ever. Loves elephants!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is so boring. I feel like he doesn't understand what he is teaching.

She's passionate about statics and made the class enjoyable. She genuinely wants students to succeed and is very accommodating. Tests are easy with plenty of review materials. Homework can be heavy but manageable if you stay on track. She's a bit disorganized, but it doesn't negatively affect students. Overall, a great professor worth taking.

I hate statics, but I loved Professor Antoniou's class. She's extremely caring and genuinely wants her students to enjoy learning. Pretty much all of class time is spent on practice problems, but she goes around the room and helps everyone individually. HW is a bit harder, but if you can do the HW, the tests will be easy.

The professor was amazing. The lectures were well structured and the tests reflected them really well. She gave a lot of opportunities to get help from her personally. Mini projects were fun and easy to do. Most of the content was easy if you paid attention in class. Would 100% take again.

Good at teaching content only part was that there were very few actual notes taken. Lots of practice problems but sometimes it felt like I didn't have notes to look back on as to what was happening or why. Optional final clutch

Very nice, but very busy and disorganized. I started receiving 90% of my grades for this class after the last assignment was due, so I had no idea what the grading would be like or what my grade is in the class. She and the TAs waited until the last minute to put grades in and only allowed us to see our total grade once it was final.
She's kind, and tries to break down difficult subjects for everyone to understand. I don't know why she has such a low rating.

Antoniou was sweet, but very disorganized, making it hard to follow lectures and catch up outside of class. Homework grading was often harsh, and feedback often unclear. Tests sometimes didn't match content we learned in class. I respect her effort and passion, but it was just a bit too disorganized and messy for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very caring and really strives to help. Readjusts her syllabus semesterly based on students' responses and is very understanding. Easily accessible outside of class and always willing to help. Sometimes she may seem a little intimidating, but she is indeed a great professor who is enthusiastic about the subject. Would take her class again.

Lectures are good but most classes are spent working through practice problems together. This works well and homeworks have trickier problems that do a better job of preparing you for tests with generous partial credit, and the final is optional. Dr. Antoniou is fantastic and helpful in class, as well as afterwards and in office hours.

Very good teacher. Each lecture covered the concepts briefly and then spent most of the time setting up practice problems. There are three midterms and an optional final if you aren't satisfied with your grade.

2nd time taking Antoniou and glad I did. very caring professor who will help you if you get to know her. tests are pretty reasonable and gives lots of partial credit for the more difficult ones. lectures aren't always the most clear, but taking a minute to watch some youtube videos made up for it pretty easily

She has changed the class from what was said in the older comments. The class is a flipped style which works well because she posts short videos to watch and then spends most of the class going over problems. The exams are very fair and mimic the problems done in class and homework, and the final can be exempt. She really cares about students.

Didn't teach very much, instead going over a few practice problems per class. But, made content very clear and understandable. Final was optional to improve grade. Included 2 fair midterms and a group project that took up most of homework time.

She is a genuinely caring professor who is cheerful and very accessible. Although the midterms are 35% each (70% total), they are way easier than the homeworks she assigns with some questions being on the posted prior year exam. Just understand the homework and you'll be just fine.

Not the best lecturer, but a very kind and cheerful person. She is very happy to help at her office hours and does her best to make statics interesting. The tests are fairly predictable and not too difficult, but she did take 15% off one of my tests for not showing enough work, which seemed excessive. I'm taking her again for another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To echo what was said, Professor Antoniou made an easy class, statics, unbearable. I attended all lectures, but her class examples were easy compared to irrational test questions, leaving us unprepared (exams worth 70%). Difficult to reach (states on canvas that she will not respond to emails), she left my peers and I clueless about projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: God bless this woman. The only daunting thing is that we had two exams with each being worth 35% of our grade. I went to lectures not to learn, but because I missed her cheerful attitude

Dr Antoniou's lectures were difficult to follow at times, but she was easily accessible outside of class and cared about helping students understand the material. The homework questions were much more difficult than the examples in class, but the tests were pretty fair. I recommend going to the LA office hours for help with homework.

First of all, Professor Antoniou seems like a nice person and is passionate about Statics 2001, but she's a terrible professor. Statics isn't a difficult class but was made complicated with her poor lectures, inability to explain concepts, assignments without any guidance, difficult homework, extremely simple in class examples, and harsh grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great person, can tell she cares about her students. Enthusiastic about teaching as well. However homework was not very well explained in-class (TAs helped a ton) and the final grade was heavily dependent on the final project and midterms. If you've taken Linear you're fine, if not then suffer for the first month.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has good enthusiasm but I wish she would go over a wider range of examples in class, as what we do there is not a good representation of the tests, and it is an awful representation of the homeworks. Homework took me so long. The textbook she recommends can be found for free online and it was pretty helpful for me.

Statics was relatively easy with her lectures in class. Just make sure you show up because the notes aren't posted online. We did many practice problems in pairs/groups in class, which made understanding the problems really easy. Her exams were generous, and time was only an issue if you wanted to do the extra credit and double check everything.

She is an amazing professor. Ignore the earlier on bad ratings. She has very much improved as a professor. You can tell by comparing old and new exams. Her older exams were very difficult. Instead of three exams, we have two. Also, the group project got a lot easier. She cares about her students and if you go to office hours you can get hw help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is awesome. She is accessible outside of class, is always open to questions, and creates fair tests. Homeworks can be tough, but going to office hours always helps and will prepare you for tests. She can off on tangents in class but Ive found her lectures very informative.

Not a difficult class, but the professor makes it an incredibly frustrating experience.  Most of the class is based on a couple grades at the end of the semester, most of which will not be graded before you can take the optional final.  If you have questions outside of class she is nearly impossible to reach.  Doesn't seem to care about students.
Poor instructor. Weird projects. Most of grade determined by two exams, albeit easy exams. Rest is HW which isn't bad and projects (which are a waste of time).

I'm not sure why her rating is so low, it had me worried going into this class. Shes a pretty good professor and her class isn't too difficult. My only complaint is that the homeworks are WAY harder than test material but they barely count towards your grade. She gives SO MUCH partial credit on tests so as long as you understand the basics ur OK.

You do problems in class and have them due every Friday.
