Mini Projects applying what you learned in class, two tests that were a bit tough but not worth a lot, and a final project that was an easy A if you put in the work. Be prepared to not know what is going on schedule-wise and a lot of grade uncertainty, but I would say easyish A.

Grading scheme is very confusing, last week of class is upwards of 40% of your grade, takes 2 months to grade, no lecture notes, lectures don't teach concepts, just problem solving, INACCESSIBLE outside of class (no regular office hours), lets TA's teach the hardest concepts (poorly) BUT she's passionate about the class and that shines through
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. A is a great teacher but she started letting TAs teach the class which sucks bc they can't answer questions and you don't learn She wasn't on top of grading/ material pace which made the second exam impossible. The projects are hard but grade boost. Class attendance is mandatory to get credit. Her exams are just like old ones tho

Professor doesn't teach her own class - she claims the last 1/3 of the class is the hardest, but sits in the back and lets a rotation of TA's teach the class, leading to a very incomplete and inconsistent learning experience. In addition, refuses to release lecture notes even though she has them, and doesnt give answers to inclass practice problems

She doesn't tell you what's needed or when to turn stuff in, so read everything (it's scattered so gl knowing where to find stuff). Don't let 79% of "A"s fool you. Nothing happens all semester and the last 3 weeks is 80% of your grade. No feedback, no time for improvement, no curve, no extra credit. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She likes her subject, but isn't concerned with the class all that much. She's.. too lax. If you are just taking this class for reqs, she's great for you. Seriously. If you are wanting to go into a field that uses this material, get a different teacher. They may be harder, but you are here to LEARN, not just make it through classes.

Dr. Antoniou was an awesome professor. She is extremely passionate about Def Bods and you can tell she really loves what she is teaching. Although the homeworks and projects can be time consuming, the projects are based off real world problems that make them a lot more interesting. For our semester we had oral exams which were different but good.

Shes probably the nicest teacher Ive had at tech. She is very caring and is super enthusiastic about the stuff she teaches. The HWs arent too hard and are helpful. Her lectures are usually helpful although sometimes it feels like she barely covers the topic, youll usually get it by doing the HWs though

She is super enthusiastic about Def Bods! And her love of the topic is what makes her stand out. She cares a ton about her students, and she gives partial credit on exams like crazy. However, her lectures can become strangely convoluted, sometimes glazing over some topics (and you'll have to go back and teach yourself).    Exams are long.
Very enthusiastic and helpful, and tests aren't that difficult if you do the homework

As a person shes cool and helpful. However,  shes not so good as a professor. LEctures are mostly clear, but she sometimes over-complicates a topic or does not cover it enough. Homeworks barely help for test preparation, just make sure you understand the concepts and can apply them to different types of problems. Tests are a bit long and difficult

As a person you'll probably love her she is full of energy and enthusiasm. As a lecturer she is alright at explaining things its only statics nothing to complicated. My only main complaint was the tests. I never felt as if i had enough time to complete them.  Knowing how to solve isn't enough you need to know how to solve quickly if you want A's.

Class unnecessarily made very difficult due to excessive assignments , convoluted explanations, and tests that were too difficult, meaning that the problems try to "trick" you instead of testing understanding of the concepts like they are supposed to. Take someone else
I really enjoyed this class, and I think you can succeed if you attend class and keep up with assignments.
To be honest, her lectures are fairly clear, but she does assign an amount of work. A very strict and old-fashioned professor, and always starts her at the morning. (extremely hates tardiness).

Very knowledgeable but sometimes lectures were a bit hard to follow. There were 11 homeworks that took a while to complete for each, as well as two midterms and a final exam that accounted for 85% of the grade combined.

Prof Andradottir isn't the best lecturer. The homework were mostly straight from the textbook - long and a little bit challenging but not too overwhelming or too bad (I think there were 9 homeworks the entire sem). She doesn't post practice tests or solutions to the homework on canvas (only in person). The tests were fair and you get a notecard.

She was a good professor with clear lectures that were easy to follow. The lectures were relatively easy to follow and had good examples, however they were not necessary to attend as the book had all the necessary info in it. Also gave a crip sheet  for tests which was nice altho not needed.
Didn't learn at all in lecture. Very disorganized. The textbook and HWs taught me everything in the class. Gives little to no partial points on exams.

Her lectures made concepts very straightforward to understand. Homework is longer at the start of the semester but never longer than a few hours a week. The exams are directly based on the homework and you even get a note card to write down anything you need for the exams. She is particular on grading, but she tells you how and what she grades for.

Professor Andradottir explains TERRIBLE. She has an accent when speaking and it makes it hard to understand her. Hard exams, no grade replacement so if you fail one exam you are done. Literally the class grade is based on your test performance. Beware of taking this professor unless you can teach yourself and understand the concepts perfectly.

Ms. Andradottir was a really good professor. Just show up to class and copy down the notes and you should be able to do the homework with just that information. Expect weekly homework that is going to take you a lot of time, but prepare you for the exam.

Dr Andradottir goes at a great pace in lecture for an introductory course. Slow enough for everyone to follow but  not slow enough to allow people to not listen. The exams are exactly like the homeworks, just a easier and a wider range of content. Be sure to put a few hours on homework a week, but it's not as much as a MATH or CS department class.

Really bad experience with this class. Not understanding about things at all. Practically no partial credit given on exams. IMO she made a difficult class even more difficult. Would certainly avoid and take someone else. 85% of the course is exams and the remaining 15% is homework that will take you a quite a few hours every week.
One of the worst professors at GT Arrogant ridiculous amount of work Gets pissed when people are one second late to class but goes over time every single lecture

Professor Androddotir is awesome! The homeworks are difficult but the tests are very similar to them and they really help you get the concepts down. Lectures are good and she makes it very interesting. Awesome class but dont procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sigrun is one of the best professors here at GT. I highly recommend going to office hours as she is very patient and understanding. Homeworks are very hard and time consuming. The tests are way easier in nature and are based on homework and you can use a notecard. I highly recommend to attend lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has taught at GT for 25+ years but still has her Icelandic accent - very cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a very good lecturer but the class itself is pretty difficult, with only 2 tests and the final being 30 something percent of your grade. If you work really hard, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She knows exactly what you need to succeed in her class. The homework can be a good bit of work, but it will definitely prepare you for her exams. Try not to miss class because the lectures have tons of info. Also, she is a very nice person and will help you with anything you need after class.

one of the most dedicated, prepared, dependable professors I've had at tech. she wants you to do well, but she does not curve. exams and final account for most of the grade, so be ready. she covers a lot in lecture so pay. attention. I messed up on one exam so I earned a B in the class but I'd 100% take her again. mad respect for sigrun
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class will make you work. There aren't many exams and they are worth a lot so be ready. The homeworks and practice and class will help you the most with a little bit from the textbook if you want. She doesn't curve, so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I LOVE her. She's by no means easy, but if you pay attention in lecture and do all of the homework, you'll be ok. Her office hours were very helpful in completing the homework, which prepare you well for the test. She usually lets you use a note card on the tests as well. There are only two tests and a final, so you do have to study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've had at GT so far. Sure the tests might be worth a really high percentage of your grade, but she had really clear and reasonable expectations. There was consistent and adequate homework so we had problems to practice, and it was always returned consistently on time. Lectures were straightforward and efficient.

The class has a very set amount of content, and she'll get through it, no matter what. The textbook isn't super useful but the HW is pretty much essential for studying and a lot of it is out of the book. Lectures can be boring but they're concise and have good examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sigrun is probably the best professor I've had at Tech thus far. She explains the material very well, and provides good examples. Homeworks are long and difficult but are identical to homeworks from previous years. Exams are basically your entire grade, but stem directly from homework problems and the practice exams. Lectures are a bit boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very dry professor in a very content heavy class. There is a lot of information given but it is hard to pay attention. Tests are multiple choice with some points back for corrections and extra credit for group projects. Not the best but not the worst in the world either.

She was a really good professor who cared about the students' understanding of the material. Lectures were good but a little boring and the midterms and final were not too hard. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities as well.

I appreciated how Dr. Toor was always accommodating toward the students. She's kind, patient, and clearly an expert in her field. Her enthusiasm and engaging teaching style made the content much more enjoyable.
I liked how Dr. Toor was very accommodating of the students. She is very nice and patient, and you can tell that she is an expert in her field. She was engaging and enthusiastic about the content.

not great in general. boring lectures, doesn't post videos, but not crazy hard for the class either. exams are all MC (45 questions) which makes it a little difficult to do super well but possible to succeed. posts lecture slides and offers projects for EC but the total amount they add to ur grade is tiny so i never did them. allows points back.

Weekly multiple choice homework. Structed roughly the same as most other MSE 2001 professors. She clearly cares about her students and wants to help if they need it. Very easy to talk to. The class is simply very reading and memorization heavy which is standard across all professors. All tests are about 45 questions all multiple choice.
Main project milestones were super long but not hard, lectures were okay, and grading weightings weren't bad. attendance strict tho

The main grade for the class is a semester-long project, where you conduct user research and make Figma prototypes. It isn't bad if you have a good team, but it's a lot of writing and busy work. The lectures are honestly super boring and don't cover much to complete the project, so you don't need to pay attention to them.

I'm learning literally nothing in this class, it's the epitome of stupid busy work and wasting your time.
There's so much possible stuff to learn in the field of UI but she manages to avoid all of that useful stuff and find the most boring useless things to cover.

Great UX/UI course. I learned a lot and I found the class very useful since I want to do UX/UI as a career. The entire class is centered around group work however, so CHOOSE YOUR MEMBERS CAREFULLY. There is a lot of work, but they give you lots of time to work on it. Stay organized !!! Attendance done thru turning point/point solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class only consisted of attendance, small presentation, and semester long group project. The group project is the biggest part of the class worth 75% so choose your team members wisely. She had fun lectures to listen and learn more about UI/UX. Overall I enjoyed the class.
Very supportive professor! Truly enjoyed her tech comm class. The class was themed on labor and I learned a lot.

i love dr. rathour she is literally the sweetest person ever. her class is pretty easy as long as u do the work (there's not a lot) and she's quite flexible with deadlines as well. shes also super passionate about her work and it definitely rubs off on us. TAKE HER CLASS!!

Loved the class on anticolonial rhetoric! You will learn a lot and Dr. Rathour emphasizes critical questioning. She is excellent in making you think and talk about global issues in a fair way and question your biases. I see the world in a whole new light now. Highly recommend.

I loved Dr. Rathour's teaching style. She emphasizes critical thinking and is brilliant in explaining real-world issues with nuance. I got better with research honestly. The class was chill and we had freedom to reshape an assignment if we wanted. She's intimidating at first but is a real sweetheart :)

The GOAT, fr. Everything else can wait. Take her class at all costs. If she teaches at 3 am, take it.
I have started reading more because of her infectious energy and passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Rathour's passion sets her apart from your average professor. I had no idea what a course like Rhetoric of Anticolonial Resistance would be like but I am sure that if I had not taken it, I would have regretted it my entire life. I grow as a critical thinker and writer every day. Exceptional professor. Exceptional class.

I am lucky that my college journey started with Dr. Rathour. Have never enjoyed an English class more or thought so deeply about writing and rhetoric as tools of colonial imperialism. I loved reading Discourse on Colonialism too :))

Took Dr. Rathour's class on postcolonialism before. The best English class of my life.
Her non-nonsense and passionate personality is infectious. She is caring, brilliant, and still very down-to-earth. No wonder she has a following now at tech. Take her class at all costs.
Loved Dr. Rathour! She is so good at engaging class discussions, and you can see how much she cares for all her students. She also brought us snacks and cake, so she's definitely one of my favorites.

Absolutely GOATED professor. If her class is open, dont even think about it, just take her (even if its at 3am, you'll thank yourself later). Amazing lectures, she'll get you to think about very interesting subjects you normally won't in other classes (for example i got to "lead" a church for an activity). You also get to grade yourself. Also food.
Coolest professor ever! Learned a LOT and laughed a lot. She truly cares for students' well being and learning.
First time looking forward to an English class as someone who has always preferred STEM subjects.

Took Dr. Rathour's Global Bollywood (ML 2500) class and really enjoyed it. Some essays were long to read but overall the class was very well structured. The range of assignments were fun too. If she teaches a Bollywood class again, you should register.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An antidote to imperial education models. Take her and be ready to learn. Ask her to share her chai and chicken curry recipe.
She is the GOAT. Other professors should take note.

Such a great professor. Easy going, supportive, and truly cares for her students. After learning from Dr. Rathour, I confirm that learning about colonialism should be mandatory in high school and colleges. I was blown away by the way we explored and analyzed colonial residues in visual media formats. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have taken all of Dr. Rathour's classes at GT. I have never had a teacher who could ignite the passion for decolonial learning within me. She has changed my life and my consciousness for the better and GT has no one as iconic as her. Now, I plan to sit in her classes as much as possible because my learning is impossible without her. The GOAT.

Dr. Rathour is literally my favorite person on GT campus. Professors must take notes from her on how to create a fun learning environment and not stress us out. I was always excited to be in the class and showed up 99% of time and that's saying something, y'all.
I LOVE HER!!!!!!!! A force of nature. Absolutely smashing. If y'all not taking AR's class, what are you even doing???? I have never learnt so much before.

More professors need to be like Dr. Rathour. She is an excellent teacher, cares a lot about our growth and well being, includes us as equals in assignment or syllabus planning, is flexible, let's us self grade, all the while prioritizing the goals for the semester and setting clear learning standards. Highly recommend!

I took Dr. Rathour's global bollywood class (ML 2500) this semester. Terrific human and an incredible professor.We also got to meet bollywood filmmaker Varun Grover as Dr. Rathour organized the first Hindi film screening for tech's global media event. I learned SO much and did not feel any kind of pressure. Please take her class.

I absolutely love Dr. Rathour! I have never had such an authentic, caring, and accomodating professor ever. She works with the students and is happy to modify the syllabus and assignements according to our abilities and work load. She makes it all looks easy but works very hard to make sure we are learning. Highly recommend.

AR really cares about students learning and well-being. Sassy, smart, and passionate. She creates a fun community and makes you think deeply about affects of western imperialism. I learned a LOT and her class changed my perspectives for the better. Highly recommend. Will miss her infectious energy.

Never had a professor as cool and caring like Dr. Rathour. Her class was the one thing I looked forward to every week. She brings passion, humor, and lots of expertise while making sure we are doing mentally well. Her postcolonial approach to gender and masculinity is fascinating. Definitely coming back for next semester.

Dr. Rathour is hands down one of the coolest people I have met so far at GT! She has very interesting stories and insights, and her class will definitely change your perspective on social issues. She utilizes self grading, so as long as you do the work, you will get a great grade. No one in my class got below an A on any assignment this semester.

I wonder what my life would have been if I had not taken Dr. R's class. Now I pay attention, enjoy writing, and find myself caring for the world. I cannot stop learning. She is infectiously good. And those Bollywood dance moves? Icing on the cake. Why aren't more professors like her???? Do not miss on her. GT should hire her permanently.
Her class is necessary and highly recommended. No one can explain the world to you better and with so much care. Her passion and energy is infectious. Best professor I ever had. Magical human.

Tech should have a mandatory Dr. Rathour's class. I wouldn't have become a better learner and human if it wasn't for her. Spirited, motivated, and one of the kindest professors I have come across in my life. Learn about colonialism from her and see your worldview expanding, see yourself become a better human. I want to take every class she teaches.
THE BEST! Passionate, caring, fun, smart, and humble. Drop everything and take her class. You have no idea what you are missing out. She sets the bar high.
absolute goat. just take the class and be ready to learn

Dr. Rathour has become one of my favorite people encountered on Georgia Tech's campus. She is real and raw and genuinely wants to help you through all aspects of life. She is very understanding and is always available for discussion and feedback. I couldn't recommend anyone more than I would Dr. Rathour!

Amazing professor and amazing class. Dr. Rathour is so brilliant, passionate, and funny. I will take away so much knowledge from this class. It was also not too demanding and there were plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Rathour was incredible! One of the best professors I've taken at Tech! She's truly passionate about what she teaches and provides skills that translate to the real-world when critically analyzing issues from a post-colonial perspective! After taking this class, you see the world through a new lens!

Professor Rathour's class was my favorite... she is very passionate about what she teaches. The assignments are enjoyable and you will learn a lot about the world (be prepared!). You are given the opportunity to self grade, your own assignments; as long as you do the work and be honest with what you deserve, you should be totally good!
best English prof ever

If you want an English class like no other, take this course. Her energy is incredible, you can just tell she truly cares . Her lectures are amazing, and she is extremely well educated on her course's theme. Professor Rathour also knows about the workload we have in other courses so she keeps the assignments very doable. 1000/10.

Amazing and incredibly funny professor. He was always super helpful during office hours. 3 exams, HW, quizzes, and a final. Allowed for makeup exams. Gave practice exams that were very similar to the tests. Very good professor to take multi with.
I took him a year ago and to this day say he was the best math professor ive had at GT. Take him if you can. He's super accessible at office hours too. Can't say enough good things about him.

Took him for 4107. Has to be the best math professor I've taken at tech. I would take him over any professor. Knows his stuff like the back of his hand and legitimately cares that you understand the material. Could not recommend this guy more.

LOVE HIM!! take him if you can, he is such a good professor. he knows what hes talking about, and makes the lectures make sense. he encourages office hours like no other, and when i went he was so kind and helped. dry sense of humor also. his practice exams help a bunch. pls go to his class he deserves it. slay austin!!

Professor Christian was one of the best math professors I have had! His lectures were very engaging and he made a point to learn the names of everyone who went to office hours. He would also give a study guide before each exam that would greatly help with the exam's content. Midterms were pretty easy compared to other teachers. He was worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Austin is without a doubt the best math instructor I have ever had. He does a great job at making complex topics really easy to understand. He is a very funny and approachable guy who is always willing to help you if you are struggling with the content. His tests and quizzes are very fair and similar to what he teaches. Absolute goat of a professor

Austin's always there whenever a student needs it. If you go through his notes (he posts all of them) you'll understand everything you need for his exams. His exams and homeworks are very fair and representative of what he teaches, arguably on the easier side as well. He's always understanding and reachable, If you have the chance, take his course.

Austin is definitely the best lecturer I've had at Tech and probably one of the best educators I've ever had. He does a good job simplifying complex topics while still being precise in his explanations and pretty funny. The tests are essentially the exact same as the practice tests with the numbers changed alongside generous formula sheets.

Professor Christian is an amazing lecturer. He does an excellent job of explaining difficult content and really understands his students. I have never been to office hours, but he does encourage them and seems very accessible outside of class. He also cares a lot about his students.

Professor Christian is probably the best math professor I had in my college experience, he motivates topic well, explains them in great detail, and is also hilarious. I would highly recommend going to his office hours if you just wanna talk about math in general. However the exams can be really tough!

I took Dr Christian's online class for 1552. He was great at explaining concepts and was always eager to answer questions. His office hours were super helpful too. In general, the material on tests for this class reflected the examples shared in class, so pay attention in lecture and you'll do fine.

Overall, Dr. Christian is a great professor. His lectures were slightly boring at times, but he made up for it with his humor. I would say the exams and quizzes were slightly more difficult than some of the other sections of MATH 2552, but they were fair and we were allowed to use our notes on them. The hardest part of the class was the quizzes.

Quite judgmental and the workload is heavy. Long papers and many assignments. Limited opportunities to act in front of a camera. While there is a lot to learn about acting, there is not enough time spent actually acting. It can be frustrating for those who want more hands-on experience.

I took his Music Culture and Society course online. If youre interested in the material, its a great course. I typically dont do readings for courses but Im a big fan of music and always did the readings. Even then, the quizzes were easy content wise, but difficult to complete in a short amount of time so if you dont read youre probably screwed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a fine professor, but the subject is a bit dull (the history of radio). He is willing to look at your assignments before you turn them in and give you feedback. As long as you do the reading, show up, and put in effort you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was an acting class. As an aspiring actor, I NEVER walked out of a single class feeling good about myself as an actor or even person. He was very rude, curt, and un-constructive in his comments/grading. Does not care and will not help u achieve your goals (even if they are class-related). Very subjective grader. Different opinion  lower grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He was alright as a teacher. Boring subjects, but if you do what he says, you'll get an A in the class. Do the readings, don't skip, and keep up with the syllabus and you'll do fine.

He is a horrible teacher. He has no idea how to keep his students entertained, thus making the class boring. The only reason I went is because attendance was basically mandatory. He is not a fair grader. I received a 79.8 as my final grade, and he made me get a C in the class. He's rude and filthy. Save yourself, don't take any of his courses.

He really changed his teaching stype recently due to numerous past complaints. His Performance Studies class was incredibly easy, you don't need to do the readings to get an A. Just take notes on what he says and study the day before the test. Again, his teaching style has greatly changed and he grades much more leniently now. Everyone got an A.
He is horrible.  He does not grade fairly.  His expectations on reports is unreasonable.  He is truly not a good teacher.  i advise you to take anyone other than him.  He will ruin your GPA
He is the worst teacher ever.  He is a very hard, unreasonable, grader.  His class is very boring.  He is a very dirty, nasty person who's office and body is filthy.  DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!
Boring

One of the worst professors at tech. Does NOT care about her students. So many complaints about her from my peers about rudeness, lack of empathy, and inflexibility. Made this class way harder on us than it had to be; didn't let us review our past exams and the term paper rubric was too vague.

She delivers engaging lectures, and consistently engages the class to ask our questions about the topics in question. Her tests are very fair, and a good estimate of the amount of time spent on each concept in class and the depth needed to know information. Attendance isn't mandatory, but was recommended. Very caring and understanding professor.

She was not approachable or understanding at all. Any time I had any questions or concerns she made me feel bad about not understanding something which was really discouraging. When I asked her for help she was reluctant to help me and basically told me she was not willing to put forth the effort. Do not recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Was completely unaccommodating during the COVID-19 pandemic. I had many exams, finals, and projects to worry about in other classes as well since I was graduating that semester. She was not only inconsiderate but unnecessarily rude when discussing what she wanted for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: he's a super sweet and chill prof!! he gets super happy solving problems so the examples are pretty easy to follow, almost follows the pp word for word. i got a 100 on the first exam by looking over the practice examples and the HW is pulled from the textbook. best prof for this class and probably one of the best ones at tech, take him if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, sets you up to succeed, and clearly lays out the course. Very organized, and will gladly help with any questions you have. One of the best professors at Tech!

Awesome professor! He cares about his students. Unlike many professors, he actually teaches his students. He is super organized and comes to class prepared and ready to teach. He explains concepts clearly. The PP notes are excellent, and he goes over sufficient examples to make sure we understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ladshaw's lecture is interesting if you pay attention. He is super nice and always gives extra credits.
Prof. Ladshaw is fantastic! He's incredibly caring and really wants everyone to succeed. He's also a great teacher and explains things really well and gives clear processes to solve problems.

Easily the most kind and caring professor Ive had, always making sure to let us know what to expect on exams and grades nicely. He explains concepts well, and works out lots of practice problems that are very similar to test questions. Allows for a crib sheet on tests and gives quizzes for extra credit. Occasionally throws in some humor too
Study the PT and do the HW and you will be fine. Cares for the students. Great guy.
lectures are just a class discussion since lecture videos are online, yet attendance is still mandatory. You will write way more than you ever have in any english class before.

None of the assignments were meant to reinforce the concepts covered in lecture. Assignments were just long reports for the sake of writing long reports. Like someone else mentioned, assignments did not seem to be thought out by the TA team or the professor. A lot of them seemed AI-generated. This is a busy-work class and a waste of your time.

Professor was engaging at times but wouldn't continue unless people asked questions Attendance mandatory lectures that weren't that engaging, and felt like an experiment half the time. It's an easy class if you're okay with lots of assignments and take-home exams.
Too many assignments and lectures feel kinda pointless to what the exams/assignments are. TAs and course in general was pretty unorganized. Busy work class with take home exams but okay class.
This class had bloated, AI-generated assignments that did not effectively reinforce the material and was not thought out by a human.

I liked the professor and found his lectures fun, but the course itself felt disorganized and heavily overloaded with assignments. Many took a lot of time without reinforcing the material, so the workload felt inefficient. Overall, I found the experience frustrating and not very useful. I had high hopes, but the course didn't deliver.

A few problems I had with the class:
-Lectures are mandatory and long, and he always waits for 5 questions/comments from the class
-Assignments are writing heavy
-Class is more cog-sci focused than CS focused (one programming assignment was like 300 lines of if statements)
-part of your participation points are based off talking to AI TAs

Course is well-structured and the professor supports his students. TA team is slightly inconsistent and aggressive in their approach to students (Head TA accused half the class of cheating in peer reviews). His accent makes it difficult to understand what he's saying at 1.4x speed. Overall, I liked the slow introduction to AI agents in this class.

Overbearing and uninspiring. Class is bloated with busy work and he throws a fit if you don't ask a question within 5 seconds of him asking if there are any questions. By taking this class, he will run cognitive science experiments on you as a student, which is something I definitely did not want to be a part of.
Really helpful and gives great lectures. Made me get interested into the field of AI and cognition.

I have very mixed feelings. I really like this professor, but CS7637 is the worst class I have taken yet at Georgia Tech. I learned more reading about the topics on Wikipedia than I did in lecture. This professor loves busy work too, so expect a bunch of pointless writing assignments. He just isn't a computer scientist, he's a cog psych guy.
Awesome professor if you're interested in the field of AI and cognition!
Amazing lectures and awesome professor. One of the finest lecturers I'v seen so far.
Had him for intro to cognitive science.  Great teacher!  Very interesting subject too!  Reccomended for anyone who wants to learn how people think and learn.

The professor is great; the issue is the TAs. They take over a month to grade things, and most of them don't know what they are talking about. Also, the exams are written as if whoever wrote them is not English as a first language, so as a native speaker, I find deciphering what they are trying to say pretty difficult.
Dr. Dhekne is an amazing lecturer and cares about students' understanding of the topics.

I LOVE this professor. He is passionate about the field, and this is evident in his lectures. His lectures are also interesting and easy to follow. Supplement them with the networking textbook, and you should do ok on the tests and homework. Sometimes the homework/projects were a little vague, but they were never super strict with grading.

Ngl this class is bad after the course refresh; the TA team sucks (always grading assignments late, don't reply on Piazza). Prof speaks with a heavy indian accent & it's definitely difficult to fully understand. He is very passionate tho. No structure to this course whatsoever, no communication.
Great lecturer who clearly enjoys teaching networking and isn't here to make your life painful
Make sure to take CS 3251 with him. One of the best lecturers from my time at GT. Cares deeply about learning instead of exams and grades and sharing his passion of networking
The course covers more breadth than depth, exposing students to a ton of interesting topics. The professor is engaging, inspirational, and appreciates participation.

This was a really interesting class overall. I liked the lectures, but localization was a bit confusing. We had a few group assignments that weren't too bad. The midterm was a little tricky but curved. The group project depends on what project you do. Prof is also available after class to discuss projects/ask questions.

The beginning of the semester was rough because of time-crunch quizzes and vague homework questions which required lots of clarification on piazza. However, professor Dhekne listened to student feedback and the homeworks and quizzes were adjusted to be better. Unfortunately, the projects were still fairly vague and didn't have clear instructions.
Let the students focus on their actual work, tone down the class a bit.

Avoid this professor for an intro psych class. This class is doable, but I was always annoyed how much work and I had to put into this class compared to other teachers. If you want to make an A you must memorize the entire textbook and lecture powerpoints. Tests are mc, essay question, and fill in the blank whereas other classes are mc.

Rob teaches good lectures but his progress is often slow so that you need to read textbook sections that he hasn't covered but will be on the test to prepare for tests. He is willing to help and answer students' questions yet the tests, for me, are harder than I would expect for a intro-level class. You need to memorize a lot to get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rob is a great professor and truly cares about his students. His lectures are always engaging and he makes some good jokes at times. It is really easy to do good in his class as long as you pay attention, do the readings, and finish the homework on time

This class is one that is very easy to succeed in so long as you keep up with the course material. A lot of the material that is covered on exams is talked about heavily during lectures, so even though attendance is not mandatory, it is a key factor to doing well in this class. Prof Ashwill is very understanding and I would take his class again.

I would recommend taking any other PSYC 1101 professor, you will not receive feedback on the quizzes so you will not learn from them. The grading system was disorganized and many parts changed. Grading takes a long time and all quizzes average very low 80s. The class consists of 7/9 quizzes, homework, an essay, and a group project.

Ashwill isn't a bad teacher by any means, I just think that his class takes a deceptively large amount of commitment. Don't go in thinking that this will just be a social science filler, because there's actually a decent amount of reading necessary to do well on his close-not quizzes. Lectures and content are very interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A really nice and understanding professor. His exams are NOT open book so be prepared to memorize a lot the day before your exam. I am pretty sure he curves the class because I definitely was not going to get an A with the way my exam grades turned out.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, Rob was a good professor. I took this course as a social science credit, and I ended up really having to work for an A. The exams had averages in the mid 70's, which seemed very low for an intro psych course. However, if you are very attentive, read the textbook, and study hard for the exams, you'll be able to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were meh, as this class is pretty much just straight memorization. Exams were a bit harder than I preferred for an intro psych class. Other students in the course posted their quizlets and study guides and I studied those and ended up doing fine on the exams. There is a 20 minute video presentation for the final project and a 2-page paper.

Please choose another professor. I guarantee you will 100% regret that you chose him for your INTRO psyc course. He doesn't even know what he teaches and tests are ridiculously hard. If you want to get a B or C out of an intro course, go ahead. I was taking this course as a senior, and it was even harder than my graduate-level courses.

Obscene amount of information covered on tests & closed notes. Discussions in this class don't exist because lectures always fall behind schedule. Need to know all lecture and book content. Accuracy graded HW. Few grade padding points. Too time consuming as a non major class. Not worth making space in your schedule for this section of the class...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was a fantastic teacher who clearly loved what he was talking about! There is a fair amount of homework and reading, but if you follow through with it, it's not too difficult to get an A.

He's a really chill guy, but his lectures are jam-packed with information. He speeds through sections so taking notes is difficult at times. Reading the textbook does help, and that's where I learned most of the information for the class. You'll need to put in the time to get a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are online participation activities for most lectures but they are extremely easy. There is also an online assignment package you have to buy. That being said, it's a pretty easy class, I have no complaints.

Just read the textbook and keep on top of the textbook assignments and you'll get an A. Lectures are mandatory as there are participation questions but they are interesting and it's clear Prof. Ashwill enjoys what he teaches. I'm glad I took him for Psyc 1101.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great introduction to semiconductors and very in-depth coverage of MOSFETs. Video lectures are posted on his Youtube and sometimes go more in depth than he does during lecture. Homeworks are fair and pretty much exactly based off lecture slides. Super experienced guy with lots of industry knowledge that he sprinkles into lectures.

ECE3030 with Khan is awesome. Engaging class that will help you understand semiconductors and industry trends on a deeper level. Only complaint is grading takes a long time (over a month for midterm 1), but other than that I highly recommend this course.

He's a pretty funny guy. The homework is due weekly and there aren't late submissions allowed unless the TAs are feeling nice at the end of the year. The homeworks can be very difficult or super easy, no in-between. The Midterms and Finals aren't very difficult if you pay attention. All lectures are recorded and are on youtube.

Dr. Khan teaches this course at the exact level it needs to be at. He explains many of the topics very intuitively and very clearly, leaving little for the student to have to puzzle over themselves. The homeworks are straightforward and relatively short, and they are generally a grade booster. The class content is also interesting.

Dr Khan is a great teacher! He does speak slowly, but I actually like that because it gives me time to internalize the information and take notes. He also digresses by speaking about related but non-class material in the real world, such as investors, or even what the yield of a chip is, and that's always interesting! Listen and you will learn!
Professor Asif Giga Chad Khan is very knowledgable. Tests are similar to homeworks with extra credit opportunities. Lectures are available on his youtube channel. Def would take again.

I went to go talk to him about why I scored so low on the final exam, I was on the verge of a B and needed 8 points from any exam(M1,M2,Final)to get it. He showed me that he arbitrarily takes points off for things not even mentioned in the question and says it was in lecture even though he never asked for it in the question itself. Horrible grader
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradford is a really good health policy professor! This class was not too difficult, but I learned so much! Highly suggest for anyone looking to take a public policy elective class. Each class does have pre-readings, but it isn't too bad, as you could still do well in the class without reading.
She is genuinely so good for US Health Policy. I learned so much and the exams are not too difficult.

Dr. Bradford is awesome! I was nervous to take a stats class but she is an amazing lecturer who helped explain things so well! She's also funny and pretty young, so she's very understanding! The problem sets could be tough, but she was receptive to feedback and offered many ways to boost grades. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I definitely recommend taking her as she starts teaching new classes. The class is graded by 2 tests and 4 assignments, which are hard but if you attend lectures and pay attention they are easy to get through. She is very helpful, responds to emails very quickly and is overall a fun professor to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradford is awesome. Her lectures are packed with material, but she does a great job in making sure students understand what is being taught. There are 6 total grades, 4 of which are problem sets, which can be a bit tricky. Overall, Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I would recommend her to any student.

Cancelled class day of the exam 2x so we didn't get a review session. Lectures are hard to understand. Doesn't care about her students at all. Doesn't compensate for cancelled lectures with videos like other teachers, send her students to a different lecture WITHOUT even asking that professor causing students to be kicked out of that lecture

Avoid at all costs. She is very confusing and not helpful in explanations. Take any other professor if possible to make your life easier. Going to studio and watching the videos posted on canvas saved me, stopped going to her lecture after about 2 weeks, tried going again, but was once again met with confusing lecturing.

The lectures are still informative but definitely on the boring side, so I would just learn the material by reading the assigned chapters, getting help at recitation, and watching any module videos beforehand and only go to her lectures for review if needed.

If you take her, you will often find yourself teaching all of the material to yourself, as she does not go in depth or teach it properly enough to do well on the exams. She does not exhibit expert knowledge on the topic and often leaves students more confused than when they entered the lecture. Linear can be difficult, but she makes it harder.

Very unorganized and the lectures are uninspired and unstructured. She does not go into depth on the important concepts and rather than clarifying them, she asks the students on their input (while most of us do not have familiarity). If you take her, you need to make extra effort to teach yourself or from the TAs (saved me). Take Barone if you can.
Lectures were very unstructured and the important topics seemed rushed while the smaller topics were taught in greater detail.

She's a nice person, but I stopped going through lectures halfway through the semester since it would be more efficient to learn the material on my own. The lectures are fast paced so I would have to spend time reviewing the material on my own anyway.

(I ACTUALLY TOOK HER FOR 1554) Prof. Wheeler does not give full length lectures and expects you to know all content prior to attending the lecture. She will only do two or three examples that last a matter of twenty minutes. If you have any possibility to take Barone do it, unless you intend to learn from the TA's.

I would highly not recommend taking this professor. She is a nice person, but her teaching style is awful. She makes concepts very difficult to understand. I quit going to her lectures halfway through the semester and instead watched another professor's online lectures. If you have her as a professor, prepare to be confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The midterms/quizzes for 1553 are the same for all professors, and attendance isn't mandatory. Wheeler can be difficult to relate to and hard to follow in class, so just watch Jankowski's lectures on the class page or read the textbook yourself- it's probably the only way you'll get an A in the class but isn't all that unmanageable if you enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dear god please avoid at all costs. She is a nice lady and all but I have never struggled so much in a math class. Her lectures explain very little and you have to grind outside of class to have any hope at doing well.

Dr Wheeler cares about her students and is accessible through her office hours. She can have some difficulty explaining concepts and her lectures are very fast-paced, but she's usually happy to answer questions or repeat an explanation.

My semester with her had a rocky start to say the least. As a new professor, she had some trouble in the beginning making concepts click in many of our heads. But with time she found her stride, and I never struggled with comprehending any further topics. All in all, a good professor who just needs to get comfortable with teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He teaches well but he goes too fast in class. He is willing to help in office hours. His tests and quizzes are written in a way that you are not used to seeing from the homework. Tests reflect the quizzes. Must KNOW material instead of being familiar with it. Also, USE YOUR TAs OFFICE HOURS! MATHLAB is a joke for this class, only your TA can help.
not recommeded...look for another option if possible..long tests...unsatisfactory explanation of content and extremely unapproachable

His teaching pattern is like he comes in class and does all kind of weird stuff and makes a lot of mistakes then gives a lot of hard assignment. His class is self study, if you think you will understand by reading the book, then go ahead but this professor is not recommended
This course is a great way to boost your GPA; there's not a whole lot of work and Dr. Avent-Holt makes lectures entertaining and informative.
Very good in lecture!

One of the best professors I've been lucky to have! Excellent lecturer, very clear, wants to know what the students think, and fair. You can tell he's interested in the subject matter and it's contagious. Doesn't give much homework except reading for the class (definitely do it- he likes to reference them in exams). 2 thumbs up!

Prof. Awal is always willing to help his students. He really does care about how well his students do in class. His lectures are very organized and easy to follow. There's an extra credit project he gives out near the end of the class that's fairly simple.

One of the best professors in the AE department. He has a great sense of humor and most of all, he wants you to succeed. 3531 is a tough course but taking it with him will make it worthwhile. He even got me into Blue Origin. If you have the chance to take him for anything control related, definitely do it.

Very Inspirational lecturer. I attended every office hour and did a lot of extra credit. He is the true reason why I want to become an Aerospace Engineer. He is the key connection to getting an internship

Prof. Awal is one of my favorite professors. Even though AE 1601 is meant to be an introductory class, he made it very enjoyable. He was passionate about his work and cared about all the students. Almost everyone in the class got an A as long as they did the work. God bless this man.

If you're a Challenge student, beware. She acts superior, overexplains yes/no questions, and loves to use the “threes” like “I came, I saw, I conquered” plus her favorite phrase, “By design.” Midterm questions are confusing, so the study guide is useless. Her TAs don't give feedback around her. One of the worst classes I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In a world of 1s, be a 5, not me tho
I'm sorry for her
She's so mean 😪

A concerning number of questions on her assessments do not have an objectively correct answer; they are based on her own personal beliefs. Her directions, like others have said, are poorly worded and confusing. Her grading process is also unfair and it is difficult to discern exactly what she wants from you. Do not recommend.

Major superiority complex! She grades her students based off of whether or not they agree with her on everything. She tries to push her beliefs on everyone. Whatever you do, do not disagree with her, tell her she's wrong, or speak your mind. All her class is, is an hour and a half long rant of her beliefs and how she's above everyone else.

She thinks that she is some sort of prophet and will berate you if you do not exactly agree with what she does. Her exams are poorly worded and have objective answers with zero curve (nobody got an A) and she marks you absent even if you are in class if you don't do EXACTLY what she says as soon as she says it. Do NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cocky, unfair and seems like someone trying to pretend to be intelligent/deep.
Intentionally marked absent even though I was present in class. So why should I come to class in the first place just to be marked absent?
Marked me absent even though I was present just because we were told to count the number of students in the lecture and she thought I didn't count.
This lady marked me absent for sitting in the back

I thought this class would be an interesting class to take for my first semester here at Tech. I hated this class by the second week. Her tests are so confusing. Most of the questions on her tests are horribly worded. I feel like I haven't learned anything. It also feels like that if you don't believe what she does and agree with her, you're wrong.
A very biased teacher in regards to to her opinions. Don't ask her a question or for clarification, she wont give it and will make you fell stupid in the process.

The professor is so obviously biased towards socialism that she forced us to write our final exam essays from that perspective. She cited non-peer reviewed research as fact in her lectures, which barely made sense to begin with. She was extremely argumentative and was a poor facilitator of class discussion. Does not round up decimal grades at all.
I thought she was nice, the tests are just hard to prepare for since her questions are random and strangely worded. She curves alright.
Class should be called race & racism, not sociology. Lectures and tests are written poorly, long-winded and very unclear.

Incredibly CARING and KNOWLEDGEABLE professor who has a knack for recontextualizing difficult mathematical concepts into intuitive lessons. She took the time to know all of the students in her lecture hall by name and regularly checked in with her students to make sure they were prepared. Easy to talk to!

Math 1552 was hard, but with Christina, she made it easier. She really cares about her students, she learned every single person's name in the big lecture class and made sure to check in with them to see how the class was going. The class itself is hard, and she tends to go very fast, but I would definitely recommend and would take again with her.
Pretty mid. I ended up going to Grodzinsky's lectures. She cares about students but she goes super fast and can be unclear.

Awesome professor that truly cares for each student. Was always early in class to talk to individual students, learn names, and chat. SUPER accessible outside of class. Great lectures with sufficient practice and test-application based problems. Tests are usually on the tougher side (especially multiple choice), but the optional final helps a lot.

Professor Anathasouli is amazing! Although Math 1552 is hard as a Tech class, she did an amazing job. She is always super prepared when she comes to class with slides, and she posts practice problems too. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and learned everyone's names and met them outside of class/office hours if they needed help.

She goes out of her way to remember every students' names and puts lots of effort into her lectures. I never attended since it was my 8am, but I used the online notes. I would still recommend attending. There are many ways to improve your grade and maintain an A, lots of extra study material and opportunities provided.
She is an amazing professor and has great powerpoint slides for class. She really cares about her students and is always available if you need help.
She is amazing, so caring, and learns all the names of her students. She explains concepts so well. I was not registered for her section but went to all her lectures.
Great professor and makes things very easy to understand. Participation was not necessary. The course is difficult (especially taylor series), but she made it bareable.

Calculus 2 (MATH 1552) is a hard class within itself. She was the best lecturer, and she had a TA named Yosia. She informed us she will not teach Calc 2 next semester. However I highly advise you to find Yosia and go to his recitations. Christina is very nice, and will work with you. Take her if you can, she is young and caring, makes math easy.
One of the best math teachers I have ever had. She is super caring and explains the material well. The tests are difficult, but these are standardized across all calculus classes.
Overall she was a good professor and very caring, her pacing during class was just off sometimes but she posts her notes on canvas so not a huge issue.

probably the best professor I've had at Tech so far. She explained the concepts very well and made integral calc so easy to understand. make sure to attend studio though to get a lot of practice problems to prep for tests and quizzes

No homework or textbook assigned. Lectures were absolutely phenomenal. Studios were required instead of HW by giving participation points (20% of grade). Tests were very reasonable and weekly quizzes were similar to material covered in studio. Professor was extremely accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You need to read the book to really grasp concepts and examples. He is funny and very enthusiastic but does not answer questions well. This class is just poorly run in general.

BMED 2210 is a boring and easy class. Learn it by yourself. Dr. Mantaralis isn't helpful and the TAs were sometimes clueless. However, this is not a stressful class. All materials are straightforward. You don't need to rely on professors and TAs a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a very sweet man who cares a lot about the students, but is not the best teacher. He would emphasize main points over and over instead of working through problems. Only reason I really understood the class was because of the amazing TAs. Still got an A because the TAs graded and they were lenient because they would watch him not teach us.

Attarchi is a gem of a professor. He explains concepts very well and is definitely easier on the grading than other multi professors. He explains the math very well but doesn't visualize it or apply it, so I would recommend watching youtube videos with fancy graphics throughout the semester and that helped me out a lot. Definitely recommend.
Tests are decent difficulty, nothing too hard. Cares about students and willing to make adjustments. Solid choice.

Dr Attarchi is really good at teaching. The only issue I had with him was his accent, but if you listen and pay attention, it's honestly not a big issue. He is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. He made so many adjustments for our benefit during this transition, which shows that if you put in the effort, he'll meet you halfway.

I'll be honest, I rarely paid attention in lecture and never went to office hours, but the few times I did listen to him it really paid off. There is homework due every week but it's honestly not too difficult. The online transition was pretty rough as expected for a math class, but he moved so many due dates and gave tons of extensions. Great guy!

Very good guy. His lectures are very well structured and many examples. The tests are just like the lecture problems. He gives these exam review worksheets that help a lot with the tests. Very solid choice.

He was really accesible outside of class and willing to help, but the problem is I don't think he remembers what it is like to not know the subject, and so he explains it as if we already know what's going on. the accent makes things a little difficult to understand too. He is caring when it comes to personal problems and will move a quiz if needed

Let's just start with this: there are homeworks due every Thursday at midnight. There are also weekly quizzed averaging over just a few sections of the book that you will take in either the first or last 10-15 minutes of class. NOW HERE IS THE STRUGGLE: you do well on the quizzes and the test questions look crazy, never before seen. TOTAL BS CLASS

I enjoyed his lectures and he works through a lot of examples with the class. Homework due dates vary, 1 to 2 assignments per week. I think the tests are similar to the quizzes and if you understand lecture and worksheets, you will be prepared. He is a personable professor and is always willing to answer questions in class.

He was an okay lecturer, but his test are pretty easy if you've taken calculus before. The only thing that's hard are his quizzes but he does it on purpose to help you prepare for the final. I would say just come to class and show that you care, because he really does care for his students and if you go to office hours its a big help.

Very caring teacher. Wants to see you succeed, but the tests are just so hard. Even as someone who took AP Calculus in high school, the questions asked are very difficult and unlike the questions we see in our homework. Homework is due every Thursday at midnight. Actually do the homework even if it's only a tiny percentage of your avg. It'll help.
He can be confusing, but overall I understood what he was talking about. His tests tend to be easier than some of the other calculus professors. He is always willing to help and is very nice.

I found Attarchi's lectures very difficult to follow. In retrospect, I probably would have done better skipping the class, teaching myself, and showing up to weekly quizzes. I didn't have much exposure to calculus before this class and his lectures really didn't help me grasp concepts I didn't know. He was, however, very caring and willing to help.

Overall structure of the class is super disorganized. His grading rubric wasn't clear the whole semester. Quiz almost every Tuesday and some Thursdays, pretty hard to study for them since all he says is "any previous work we've done is fair game." Practice exams are not helpful 85% of the time.
I did not enjoy this class. Lots of hard material, lectures are confusing. Prof does not explain concepts well. TA saved me. Thankfully, plenty of extra credit opportunities to get a better grade.

This is by far the hardest professor I have ever taken. Lectures consist of 50 slide powerpoints filled with words. Nothing is explained clearly. The lectures and the tests feel like completely separate courses. This is likely a weed-out class. This class tanked both my GPA and mental health. Made me question if I wanted to be in college.

Prof yaps a lot during lectures, lectures are quite disorganized and heavy with information that isn't explained thoroughly. Exams are very difficult and have questions that we have never seen examples of before. A redeeming factor is that he gives quite a bit of extra credit.

This class was very repetitive and I did not learn much. Dr. Arriaga was very nice and passionate about her research and respective work but I actually thought I was going insane with how repetitive and unnecessary lectures were. All the readings are front loaded then it's totally project based. I would take again for easy A but it was brain rot.

Prof. Arriaga is pretty disorganized (prone to typos, and rarely answers questions directly). That being said, she is very knowledgable and enthusiastic about the material, and she gives you everything you need to do well. Learned quite a bit in her grad HCI class. Especially in her grad classes, you'll be happy with your grade in the end.

Intro to Cognitive Science is a pretty dense course, but Dr. Arriaga is very organized and clear about the expectations and gives you chances to help your grade by letting students have a say in grade breakdowns and plenty of bonus opportunities. Don't skip lecture because there's random bonus and she walks you through some of the test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of quizzes that involve reading 60 page chapters. 2 essays. 3 Tests that are absurdly long. One midterm had 10 MC questions and 20 Short Answer questions. Rediculous. Lectures are worthless and she just repeats the same stuff from the first week for the whole semester. Kinda loud and rude too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Arriaga happens to be very caring and enthusiastic, but is not good at giving clear instructions. The class was Human-Computer-Interaction, and nobody had any clue what we had to do or submit most of the time. Aside from the (very) chaotic nature, the class was not a heavy workload or unmanageable. Projects were not totally unreasonable

Dr. Arriaga struggled with technical issues for weeks on end. She claims to care about students but stubbornly ignores suggestions. She also removed random things from slides and took down old lecture recordings to "make sure we went to class". Despite her experience, felt like she was a first-time professor trying to impose her will poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Its obvious she DOES care about her students BUT good intentions don't always  good results. The other critiques are fair. In an attempt to be "fair" to students she made a very convoluted grading structure that was confusing and most of class time was going over structure of the class instead of content. The syllabus was more confusing than class

No exaggeration, the worst professor I've had at Tech. Puts up a front that she cares about students, but does not listen to student feedback (refused to make a Piazza until students begged). Lots of busy work, 1 quiz/week, 2 journals/week, 1 group assignment due before the end of class/week, 6 page research paper due, & 4 page paper due + exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: By far the worst lecturer I've ever had. Her lectures are boring and repetitive, and she assigns a ton of work. Every week there was a quiz, two journal entries, and a whole chapter to read. She is extremely stubborn and does not take constructive criticism from students (forced to delete our class groupme). There were also two long papers to write
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Arriaga makes you work for your grade in UI design. The Norman book quizzes aren't too bad if you read the book and take detailed notes. For the design project (most of the semester), your group is randomly assigned, so just hope for a good group. She's an okay lecturer (boring at times), and she has a no device policy (will actually get mad).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Best class and professor I have had at Tech. Participation is required with a no-device policy, but her lectures are so amazing and engaging you won't even need your device. Cares a lot of her class and students. Flexible and understanding. Please take her if you can!

Arriaga is an enthusiastic lecturer and passionate about her field. In 3750, the first few weeks is spent reading/quizzing "The Design of Everyday Things". The next weeks are spent creating a prototype in 4 phases with a group (with somewhat early deadlines). There's a LOT of work associated with 3750, but it's an easy A. Great for UI portfolios.

She does really care about the subject, but this class is the most work I have ever had to do. There's a quiz every single week and LOTS of reading. Participation is required, and you must keep class discussion engaged. Her instructions are often confusing and she is pretty intense at times. If you're interested in this topic, take it. If not, dont
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It's encouraging to take a class in which the professor is so passionate about the topic. Professor Arriaga does research in HCI so she lives and breathes the material from this class. She knows what she's talking about and truly cares about students learning. She lays out her expectations and assignments and makes the material easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Arriaga is a great teacher who really cares if her students are learning or not.  She has a kind of confusing class structure, but gives you a lot of choices on when you want assignments due and topics for papers.  I always enjoy her class.

Really liked the professor and the class was fine and pretty interesting. Just speak up in class for your participation points. He was very considerate and would extend deadlines. He claims you need the textbook, but I would say it's not worth investing in it as we only discussed it a little bit.
Mannn to the person who said he stinks-- im taking him in the spring bruh pls dont be lying *crying emoji* , he's the only one I can take omg .

his class was easy and not difficult, but talks in circles about stuff that doesn't matter. stupid theme and provides feedback that doesn't apply. he smells and I dont personally like him. wouldn't take again but its whatever.

Hes a really kind proffesor he cares for his students and is really understanding would take again definetly. Just do the work come to class. He cares what he talks about and his class isn't boring he likes to have giant disccussions

The class was overall pretty easy. The professor is nice, but sometimes the class would get really boring. By this I mean that he would talk for a while about basically the same thing. However, overall a nice prof and will extend due date if needed.

Professor Kumar was my ENGL1101 professor for the Fall 2025 semester. He is extremely generous and kind. His course revolves a lot around 5 key projects/essays. These are honestly not hard to do and he makes it so the class is not too much of a time commitment. Would definitely love to be in his class again
Guys he brought us Lindor chocolates and Oreos on the last day of class

Professor Kumar is a very caring & understanding (gives extension whenever you ask). He is an easy grader, & 50% of essay grade is self graded. In class we watched this one movie, so we did not have any books to read. There was never really any homework except for the projects. Projects were 5-10 pages (2x spaced) & you basically choice the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is a joke. The professor and the TA just don't give s about it. I get it. As the chair, you'll be busy with who know. But if you can't afford time that you have to constantly cancel lectures 30 minutes before the class and give only four homeworks, you should've handed it to another one. What is the purpose of edDiscussion when nobody answers?
Very good professor.
Taught 2035 along with Prof Bhattacharya. He's very sweet and always checks in with us before lecture started. He explains things very well.

He reads slides word by word and assumes the students know everything already. I felt like he is always rushing and doesnt seem to care to actually explain the underlying concepts. He also misses lectures every other week!
Amazing lecturer and really cares about his students. Assignments for the class didnt make sense but he isnt the coordinator. Great professor, definitely someone Id want to take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Raychowdhury is extremely knowledgeable and a super instructor. He knows exactly where students will have difficulty understanding and makes concepts clear. I wish he traveled less, would love to take more courses with him.
Amazing professor. He really cares for his students and is an amazing lecturer. The only downside is that he misses classes a lot but the experience overall is great.
Amazing Lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Raychowdhury is an amazing lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. He provided lots of practical examples from 70s, 80s, 90, and the present times. He seems to know both the state of the art as well as the history of computing. It was an amazing learning experience. Just wish he were around more often.

He misses class and is late to class, A LOT! However, that is not to say that he is a bad professor. When he actually makes it to class he is awesome. He is great at explaining concepts and seems to truly care that the students learn. He does a great job of moving from concept to concept and provides a nice overview of where we are in the course.
Awesome professor. Excellent in explaining material. Hope he teaches more ECE classes in senior years.
A good lecturer and teacher, Dr. Raychowdhury knows the material and makes sure you do as well. Homeworks often were very difficult but were relevant to the material.

Prof Raychowdhury is a great teacher and great at explaining the course material. He convered a lot of material but always took the time to explain the concepts slowly. He also found ways to make the whole course interesting throughout the semester.

Professor Raychowdhury was an excellent lecturer. He sometimes went fast but did explain new concepts with ease and clarity. However, his course organization was frankly awful and his lack of accessibility outside class was terrible too (traveled almost every week and did not hold regular office hours). Also, the grading criteria was unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. He has taught some of the most difficult topics with such ease and coherence! I learnt so much in the class, yet never felt overburdened. He wants the students to succeed.

He explains things really well and also shows a lot of care for students. Class was curved quite a lot and he would constantly let the class know where the cutoffs were after each test. Although all his material is posted online, still highly recommend both going to class and reading his online notes, as they supplement each other quite well.

Would definitely recommend her for 2110, MUCH easier than taking it in ATL. She makes the class very fair with assignments, quizzes, and TLs. Reads off the slides from ATL, but you can tell that she knows what she's talking about. Slight language barrier that makes understanding hard sometimes, but overall a very solid prof who I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prior review was lazy & biased, didn't make it through the entire class. Extremely fair teacher & decent lecturer for her first time teaching the course. Could tell she was very knowledgeable, but language barrier hurt a bit. HW heavy, but a very very fair course compared to taking in Atlanta. Would highly recommend and I enjoyed. Also had for 2110

I was excited for CS3600, but quickly grew frustrated. The prof has no clear curriculum, comes unprepared, and answers Qs with “I don't know.” She skips key slides, gives unclear homework, and fails to relate content to AI. So far, we've done 8 graph search algorithms—none AI-related. A class w/ much potential became one I care about the least.

Respectfully, the WORST professor I've ever had in my undergraduate career. The tests were extremely poorly written, very stingy with partial credit. Often wouldn't upload the correct slides before exams. Exams are too much of the grade, the project wasn't worth enough. Please avoid at all cost… trust me any other professor will be better.

Goes by "Tuba Ketenci" on RMP too. Doesn't really know the content well enough to explain it, just reads off slides. The first exam didn't have much partial credit and two midterm exams are weighed 17.5% each so it definitely will cause major dent in your grade if you don't do well. Only take her if you've already completed a solid probstats class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are straight from the textbook and quizzes and tests are often not similar to examples from the textbook. She clearly likes teaching the course but lectures were pretty dull. The one group project was a huge boost to the grade though.
Not good. Don't take under any circumstances.
