She was the worst! Her lecture videos never fully matched what we did in the book. Made us buy WielyPlus just for quizzes. She never understood the material she was teaching and was very rude on piazza. The TAs were no help either. She graded harshly on the exams. Look at "Tuba Ketenci" for other reviews on her! DO YOUR BEST TO NOT TAKE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, the class is relatively easy, with online lectures that are mostly useless (she just reads the slides) and lots of extra credit. However, she may be the laziest teacher I've ever had. She showed up late to every exam we had and was often aggressive when responding to student questions. Her other RateMy is under "Tuba Ketenci."

Yes she doesn't teach this class. THERE ARE NO LECTURES. Its all just online videos that have a bunch of typos. But this class is fair, the questions on the test are very similar to the textbook questions. Just watch her lecture videos, and do the book problems. If you have any questions they will respond pretty fast on piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I would just like to say that though our course catalog lists ISYE 3770 as taught by "Tugba Ayer", it is not. It is actually taught by Tuba Ketenci, who at the time of writing has a 2/5 average rating on RMP. Beware.

Prof Cummings is very accommodative and kind. This class was async, it's super chill and an easy A. The weekly assignments have multiple attempts and there's tons of opportunities for extra credit. But, the only reason I didn't like the class was because I barely learnt much and there wasn't a lot of interaction with the professor.

If you're looking for an easy social science credit, I highly recommend taking this class. Tests are extremely easy and there are a lot of extra credit opportunity. Professor Cummings truly cares about her students, and is willing to make accommodations if you tell her your situation.

Literally the easiest class I have ever taken. Basically handed us the tests to study before we took them. Nearly 30 people dropped because the class SOUNDED hard on the syllabus, but it was mind-numbingly easy. The professor is nice, and the lectures are alright (you don't need to take notes), but be prepared to not learn.

I took this class Spring 2020. She was a great professor for Intro to Psychology. Her best quality is that she really makes sure that all of her students will succeed. She is lenient and understanding with your pace in this new material and with assignment milestones. Highly recommend this class for your start at Tech.

I feel like I learned nothing in this class. It is so easy that you don't have to study and you end up with an A. It is good for my grade, but looking back I learned nothing. There is a paper(15-20pg) due towards the end of the semester, but easy grades.
She was a great help to her students.

Dr. Cummings wants to see nothing but her students succeed. She was very lenient with grading and extra credit. The bulk of the grade came from group projects and a final research paper. The lectures were admittedly quite by the book, but what to expect from a Gen. Psych class. She gave very engaging activities during some lectures though.

I would definitely recommend taking Dr. Cummings for General Psychology. The first week when she goes over the syllabus it may seem like a lot of work, but do not worry. The biggest things are a few group projects which can be fun if you choose for them to be. Tests are the easiest, lectures can be a bit by the books, but Dr. Cummings really cares

Easily the best PSYC1101 professor at Tech. Lectures themselves are average, but the fact that she genuinely cares for her students really sets her apart. Tests are fair, and there are a few group projects that really aren't bad because she's very lenient with grading. She's very understanding and accommodating, as long as you communicate with her.

Professor Cummings cares so much about her students and wants to see them succeed. You can also tell she is very passionate about her subject. She is lenient with due dates too. Nothing but great things to say about her, would totally recommend.

The professor's attitude/approach to teaching were disappointing. She came across as arrogant, often implying she was intellectually beyond Georgia Tech. Her teaching style lacked clarity, enthusiasm, and genuine care for students. When concerns were raised, her justifications were often dismissive.
Very slow-paced, boring lectures. Slides are poor quality and just not very organized class.

She is actually good at teaching IFF you go to office hours in person. She didn't have office hours in person until the last 3 weeks of school. She neglected the class until the last 3 weeks. P much screwed students out of getting an A in, what should be, a super easy class. When she actually put effort towards the end, she was a really good prof.

The professor kept changing the logistics during the semester as if she does not care if this puts a hurdle on the students. The course and exam procedure are not well organized and she avoids in person office hours which are the norm for any course. She also make students feel indebted which is not nice.

Right before the first exam, she changed the policy from open notes to one crib sheet. She told us OpAmps would not be on exam1. Day before exam1 released a topic list that included OpAmps. Released incorrect topic list for exam2 causing many students to fail. She just began doing in-person office hours. Online office hours are completely useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When hearing criticism of her flawed teaching, Prof. Ansari directed the blame back onto the students who did not get the physics, and onto the other factors to justify herself. Most of the lectures either canceled or online as she fled to a corner to avoid the students!

I chose lecture heavy in my tags as there was no lecture light option. I felt like a bull in a china shop in this course where professor did not care about students. With a condescending attitude, if we raised any concern about the management and teaching style, she usedto divert it to physics and did not accept the criticism.

As an undergrad student, I pay high tuitions to get quality education and yet even post covid, the professor held classes online and disappeard from campus! This was so disappointing. Even the very few lectures that were not cancelled were taught just to put a check mark and a proof that she taught sth, not a fan of this method!
I did pretty well in this course but I stopped attending the lectures. The teaching style was lethargic and halfhearted.
People complaining about unclear teaching just didn't pay attention in physics. Professor Ansari teaches very clearly, gives fair tests, and a reasonable to low amount of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I am just glad to be done with this course today. I kept learning by reading the textbook and attending lectures taught by other professors. I attended the lectures at the beginning but I relized when I was asking questions, they were not answered properly.

I am not concerned about my grade and just finished the exam for this course. I was lost during the lectures as basics of circuit theory is covered in this course. Most of the time, the professor is just copying the derivations without providing any intuitive link between the theory and physical concept! The teaching style does not resonate well.
Comparing this course with other courses I have taken, I was less enthusiastic to attend the lecture. The lectures were dry and the fundamental concepts were not thought rigorously.
She is accessible outside class even she is very busy. The content is easy to understand, but the exams are relatively tricky. Practice more problems even you think you're prepared.

She is very inexperienced but pretends the opposite. The teaching style is not motivating at all and even herself sometimes she gets lost. For this course, I wish they could assign a really good professor to teach.
Professor ansari did a good job of explaining difficult material in lecture. The in-class worksheets were very helpful.

I did find the lectures confusing and I enjoyed more going through the textbook by myself and I learned much more effective. I believe she should not teach such a fundamental course as it kills the motivations on ECE students. Every time we tried to convey the message that we were struggling she managed to justify by saying that it is a flipped!

She did not teach in a coherent manner and it was obvious that it was her first time. Several times she lost the track of materials in the class. Assignments/projects were scattered around and the course objectives ware not clearly laid out. Also, office hours were too short.

Professor Ansari thought me circuits in her first teaching semester. Tbh, she was one of my best professors ever. Very kind and caring, wants students to learn and be rewarded. Helps you understand. Extra credit opportunities. Tests are fair. LOTS of resources and preparation material (Worksheets, HW, practice). I'd definitely recommend

Professor Ayhan is one of the best professors I have taken at Tech. She makes lectures very interesting and engaging. You leave class knowing you learned something and understand it. Attending lectures makes exams and homework very doable.

Professor Ayhan is one of my favorite professors I have taken at Tech. She makes lectures very interesting and engaging. Attending lectures makes exams and homework not very hard at all. I highly recommend taking her!

Professor Ayhan is awesome! This class is homework and test heavy, but if you go to class you will do really well in the course! Doing the practice exams and homework will also help you do well on the exams!

Full disclosure it's been a while since I had Prof Ayhan for 3232, but the fact that I still remember her as a great teacher speaks volumes. I don't remember many of my Tech profs. My own kid is in college now which is why I'm on this site. I took 3232 in 2001 and it's crazy seeing Ayhan is still teaching this course 25 years later. She's great!

Exam heavy class which is awesome! Ayhan is incredibly sweet and quite funny, but the lectures can drag on for a while. Tests include lots of partial credit. No concepts are incredibly conceptual difficult, but it does require a heavy amount of memorization of various formulae.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof.  Difficult course but she makes the content understandable and goes at a reasonable pace.  Always attend lecture if you can, as she doesn't post many materials online.  Study hard for the midterms and final: even if you're not sure where to proceed, explain your thought process and she'll give you some partial credit.  Would recommend!

Lecture, homework, and exams have very similar questions. If you memorize solutions to about 5 types of problems per exam, it's easy. The practice midterms are very helpful. The final sometimes has questions from the start of the semester and sometimes the end; so, don't rely on the practice finals, review homework.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had. Took 2027 online over the summer last year and it was such a well-structured, clearly taught class. The way she approaches concepts and introduces them should be taught to all other professors lolll. Super accessible, fair exams and HW based on lectures, very caring and helpful when I was confused.

She is one of the best professors I've had at Tech. She is very kind and genuinely cares about the success of her students. Homework could be long and tedious at times, but it helped me learn the information and prepare for the tests.

I don't understand why Dr Ayhan has a low average GPA. Her lectures are clear and her weekly homeworks cover exactly what you need on the exams. We reviewed 2027 a lot, but it was spread out throughout the semester so we learned plenty of new content even though it wasn't the hardest ISYE class.

Excellent professor, lectures were clear and examples were helpful, homeworks were weekly (but didn't take too much time) and prepared you well for the exams. Exams were very reasonable but accounted for a significant portion of the grade. Also she managed to learn the names of all the students in the class and made lectures pretty interactive.
Excellent professor who lets you know what you need to to do well. Grade consists of mainly exams, and the homework and projects. The homework and practice exams set you up well for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Now that I'm taken ISYE 3232 with another professor, I realize that she is a gem. Yes, a GEM. Her lecture is clear, her homework is not truly easy but it will not make you lose your mind. Yes, her test could be a bit harder but you will left the class without having a grudges at the professor because you know she did an excellent job as teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class due to Professor Ayhan's lecture style. She teachers using lots of examples, ties them to real-life situations, making lectures interesting. However, she does grade a little hard on homework and tests. Outside of class, she is also friendly and willing to talk about other applications of IE. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Course materials are pretty hard but her lectures are extremely clear and the examples help you understand the materials. Weekly homework can be challenging but she offers help in office hours and they are graded leniently. Exams are fair. No curveballs. You are tested on what you learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Ayhan was very knowledgeable and a good professor for 2027. She worked through a lot of examples in lecture that set you up well to complete the hw and exams were pretty similar to the examples. She understood the material well and was very fair. The workload is not bad at all with weekly homework that takes 1 hr to complete.

Eh teacher. She takes off points for the smallest things on tests even if you get the right answer she wants you to solve it her way, which doesn't really make sense. If there's a better teacher then I'd take them over her, but if not then she isn't terrible and an A is definitely doable.

I didn't know what to expect going into this class, but overall I think it was great. Dr. Ayhan is sweet, and she does a lot of examples to help you understand the material. Given that this class was online due to COVID, she tried her best to accommodate her students and get to know them! HWs and practice exams are similar to the actual exam.

Dr. Ayhan is one of the best isye profs Ive had! She made the stochastic processes class super intuitive, and I learned a lot from her lectures. Her examples in class are similar to homework problems and test questions. As long as you pay attention to her classes and understand what she teaches, youll be just fine. Really sweet and caring.

The content is challenging since it is a weed-out class and the tests are more difficult than the practice exams but doable. You basically have to go to class if you want to make above a C since she goes over lots of content and doesn't post lecture notes. No extra credit but she is very accessible if you reach out for extra help. Good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grade is based off of 10% homework, 3 tests 20% each and a final that is 30%. She said hw and practice tests were harder than the tests themselves. Dont believe this lmao. Tests were very difficult. Hw was fine. No drops, no curves. You get what you get. Great person, I just do not prefer her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor and very funny during class! Some of her homework problems can get hard, but she will help you if you go to office hours. She remembers all of her students names and really cares about her students.

A really caring professor. Don't be shy to attend office hours because she will assist you if you have any doubts. The tests are not very easy, but if you study and ask for help, you should do well in the class.

Ayhan was the best. The class is pretty tough, and she certainly doesn't let you take the easy way out, but she's super caring and helpful. She memorized everyone's name in our class, and she actually makes sure you're understanding her lectures. If you go to class and put the effort in, you'll learn a lot and get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: While this class is tough, she does a great job of explaining the material, and if you don't understand from her lectures, she's more than willing to meet with you one-on-one. She also memorized every name in our 75-person lecture, and took time to have personal conversations with students, so she cares about you a lot. Tests are very doable.
She explains very well. However, she could be very bias with students, which make it very unfair. Tests are difficult but doable. And homework could be long and sometimes hard
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, tough but does a good job of teaching the information. Fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Brilliant professor. One of the most caring professors, who could actually teach well, and gave really good feedback on homework. The class was structured really well, and definitely involved a lot of problem-solving.

Very helpful, clear lectures. She really wants the class to be engaged in what she's teaching  and will nag you until you participate, which is good because you really have to be paying attention in lecture. Would recommend her for any IE class. Tests and homeworks are difficult but fair

He's a great professor with a great sense of humor and great stories. His lectures are always engaging and up-to-date. We had a presidential election simulation, really fun and offers a lot of extra credits. Too bad he's not an official prof at GT.
Professor Azarvan is the best; super easy class and a great lecturer.

He is a very enjoyable professor and has interesting lectures if you go. I took his class at GT in the Fall of 2023. All of my exams were online and multiple choice. You also have to write 3 discussion posts (about 500 words) throughout the course on topics of your choice. This class felt like it was half a credit hour as opposed to 3. Easy A

This guy is great. Killer beard and stache should tell you everything you need to know. Funny, chill, understanding, impartial, the list goes on and on. Lectures are interesting, always relevant and intriguing topics. Participate, do the assignments, study for simple MCQ tests, and you'll do great. Multiple opportunities for extra credit. Take him.

Studying for tests and writing a few short essays is all you need to do to pass the class. Professor is very lenient and gives good lectures. Class debates and discussions are always interesting and professor is fair to both sides. Uses current events to keep things fresh and grab attention of students.
Great class, would take again. The her office hours and know she doesn't do plus or minus grades

She was fine as a professor but focused the entire class on her own interest in AI. When talking to my classmates the consensus was that the hardest part was pretending to care about AI. The entire class was about AI, she never once deviated from the subject and disregarded the fact that her students were not interested whatsoever.

Elizabeth LeRud is pompous and a horrible lecturer. Constantly tripping over her words and does not appear to be prepared. She is way too harsh of a grader. I tried super hard in her class, participated in all activities and completed all assignments on time. I don't believe I was graded fairly, and would not recommend anyone ever take her classes.

Took course in Fall 2021. Dr. LeRud was great. Class was pretty straightforward and she cares about helping you do well. Gave more than enough time for projects. Super great person to get to know outside the scope of class as well.

Dr. LeRud is an excellent English professor who respects her students. There is some reading (poems, portions of the WOVENText, and one book) and very few essays to write. She organizes her class so you complete major essays and projects over the course of a few weeks, making it digestible and not overwhelming. I would highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had. Very approachable and genuinely cares about student success.

He is an interesting figure with an interesting career but aside from that, not much recommends him as a good or even decent professor. His readings are adequate but the main problem in the class was his lack of constructive feedback, clear instruction, and preparedness. 60% of class grade was still undetermined by the last week of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take this class with P. Brecke. Dr. Best has an ego bigger than any other professor I've ever known and enjoys reminding students how much more he knows. Don't ask too many questions or send a single email, he gets petty quick. and most importantly: Do NOT have a different opinion or belief. Your grade will feel his retribution.

Listen there aren't enough characters to describe how horrendous this class was, there's 0 structure, his lectures have almost no relevancy to the ridiculous amount of readings he assigned, 50% of our grade occurred in the last 2 weeks. Don't take stia with him. Wait for a different professor. If you're going into ur last semester, stay for 4 1/2.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures were quite content-heavy, and overall I felt they mostly were tangential, focusing quite a lot on finding derivations instead of practicing concepts. He was quite accessible outside of class and very friendly and helpful to students.

PHYS 2231 (Honors Physics I) He's a super nice guy, not a super nice professor. I ended the class with a 79.4 and didn't get rounded up, but he rounded up another girl's 76 to a B. Tests were weighted pretty heavily and they were extremely difficult. Averages would be failing and he would say "I don't see any means for a curve"

Behrens is such a great professor and person. Took Phys2231 with him, and while it was an incredibly challenging class he worked hard to make sure every one of us succeeded. Put in the work to the class and he will put in the work to help you. Such a funny, earnest guy who really does care about his teaching. Got a 76 in class but rounded to a B.
He was so kind and genuinely cared about each of us. He made sure his office hours accommodated every single student. He cares so much about us and physics which made the class more enjoyable.

He felt bad when less than half of the class started showing up to lectures and genuinely asked what he could do to improve attendance. He is a very nice, student-oriented teacher and he gave us gummy bears after the final :)

He did a very good job of teaching the material and explained concepts well with good practice problems. Also is super funny and genuinely one of the most caring professors. Really wants his sections to succeeds, is super available outside of class, and frequently asks for and applies any feedback given very happily. Would definitely recommend.

The course is run by Dr Alicia, so tests are the same. There are enough online resources on canvas to self-teach this class. Bucket point system and extra credit make it not too difficult to get an A. Behrens lectures were good but sometimes a little scattered and hard to follow.

I struggled significantly in this course, but that was no fault of his. Honestly, I believe I may not have even had the chance at passing this course without him. Dr. Behrens is very kind and considerate of his students. He goes above & beyond to help his students succeed. If you have to take this course, he is by far the best professor.
Physics at tech in general is hard, but go to lecture, do all the practice given, and you'll be fine! I went to office hours a couple times typically before the tests and it was super helpful!

Loved him! Kinda bombed the final but the tests and stuff aren't up to him since it's a coordinated class. He's really funny and actual values your feedback and takes it insta consideration and moods how he lectures after it. Would recommend!!

Good lecturer and funny. Most notable thing is he really listens to feedback from students and applies it. He changed his lecturing style partway through the year based on student feedback, and it really improved his lectures
Slides were very helpful in studying for exams. Lectures pretty good to attend, he's a funny guy and explains things quite well.

Honestly, Behrens was a good teacher, but I didn't really use his resources as I didn't need it. If you're nervous about this class, just focus on learning via the GPS problems in the labs, and asking the TA's as many questions as possible. If you desperately need help, go to your prof's office hours.
Since Greco controls the class, the only difference between the professors are their lectures and office hours. I recommend Behrens because I thought his lectures were helpful and he is very kind.

I took this online during the summer fully online. The class is manageable as long as you watch the lecture videos provided (which are all taught by a different professor). Tests are tough, but fair, as he posts previous exams as study materials. Grading scale is great, and homeworks/labs are easy. Overall a great course.

I wouldn't recommend going to lectures for any Physics 2 class, as the videos and GPS practice problems teach well. But if you wanted extra clarification on subjects, Dr. Behrens was an amazing help. It's clear he cares about his students and will explain any topic you need help on, all while keeping 75-minute lectures from being sleep-inducing.

I never went to his lectures because most of the content can be learned online, but when I did, he did a great job of finding work arounds or explaining the content in new ways for the exams. The exams for our year were not difficult and many of the questions were the same as the GPS (but I think Dr. Greco did the exams) - Behrens was great though.
One of the best professors I had this semester. He is very accessible outside of class. His lectures are straightforward and based on what is on the tests.

Caring and wanted his students to succeed. Posts lecture slides before class and after class with annotations, answers questions in class, and keeps students updated on the course. At times lectures were long and monotonous but he tried to keep them interesting and covered a lot of examples. He also always stayed on pace with HW/GPS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a really good professor. His lectures are concise, and he never goes on random tangents about non-PHYS 2212 stuff. He even sent out a mid-semester feedback form and actually adjusted his lectures based on student feedback. I think this was his first semester teaching 2212, so he'll probably be even better in the future.
Dr. Behrens gives engaging and fun lectures. He actually cares about the material and the students. Doing well is totally possible and his tests are fair.

Dr. Behrens provides one of the most balanced experiences I've had in the ChBE department at Georgia Tech. I really appreciate that he creates original exams and quizzes every semester even if he is teaching the same class. He is also an ACTUALLY funny guy, which makes it that much better to be in lecture. Overall, a PHENOMENAL professor!

Dr. Behrens was a great professor! Super passionate & gave great examples of the material we studied! Material is interesting and is presented in a way that facilitates understanding. Tests are average, Homework is tedious, project is easy. He was sometimes stubborn about certain answers on assessments that didn't (& still don't) make sense.

Transport is a difficult, math intensive class, but Dr. Behrens makes it as accessible as I think it gets. He posts lecture notes, offers many office hours, and generally seems to care about students. His grading curves were 85 for A, 70 for B, and 55 for C. Projects were graded leniently- class averge of 96. Exams are fair to challenging.
If you don't get a good TA, good luck. Horrendously run class with zero room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You won't see this dude, quizzes depend on your TA. Go to class, read the manual beforehand. It's an annoying class but the TA's are helpful. You probably won't learn much from the labs but the circuits can be cool. Lab exam is fine, you'll get a study guide the week before. Just learn the book properly and YouTube the theory and you'll be fine.
Absolutely amazing would take again
The GOAT, absolutely amazing professor

He hadn't taught the class in several years, so maybe this will be a little biased, but the exams were really hard (until the final, when he deliberately made it easier). Everyone above an 89% got an A in the class. The homeworks also took a long time--they weren't graded for accuracy, but I still wanted to try and get them correct.
do not take during study abroad, he was unreasonably hard and his exams were ruthless. Most Ive ever studdied for a class and still did terrible.

This class is like ECE 3043 but improved. That being said it is still a difficult class that takes a lot of time but you learn a lot more and get a lot more out of it. There were 3 tests which were fair, a final project, and a handful of labs which all took longer than the dedicated lab time. However, Dr. Beck was very supportive throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Beck genuinely cares about his students learning the material and is good at explaining it. The course material is difficult and homework is ungraded but essential to learning. 30% each for exams 1 and 2 and 40% for the final exam. He curved the letter grade cutoffs generously. He's very patient and good at answering questions in office hours.

Tough content but Beck makes his lectures extremely clear and there is no busy work / ability to get by without actually understanding the content.  40% final and 60% over 2 midterms that are closed note but make you really know what's going on.  Overall, cool professor for a tough course. Would recommend if you want to focus on learning/problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lab quizzes will make or break your grade in this class, curve or not. Grades average out to a 3.3 GPA for your section, but that will be mostly dependent on the quizzes, which is dependent on who you have as a TA. Thien was a great TA btw, if he has a section again try to get in with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is probably the least organized at Tech. Dr. Beck himself doesn't show up to lectures as the class is run by two TAs with each section being completely different than the others. On top of that the class is only graded on 10 labs, 10 quizzes, and an all encompassing final. Overall, zero consistency from class to class makes it an avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECE 3741 has to be one of the most unorganized courses I have seen at this school. Beck, yeah he's a decent teacher but for him to allow the class to be structured so terribly is a bad reflection. Basically do labs where you learn minimal until they decide 1 week before the lab exam to give you solid material to study. Advice, take over the summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TA dependent, but here is my advice: I spent 1.5hrs to study before each lab quiz, writing down important info/eqns/diagrams into a notebook before + after each quiz. When the final rolled around, I had a nice study guide that covered the key info from each lab. Get to know your TAs, and don't be afraid to ask for help.

Dr. Beck is very caring and helpful. The only issue is the class itself sucks. The labs are do-able but the weekly quizzes, everyone bombed. This is because student shave to teach themselves course material out of a lab manual. Why do I pay 50k for that when Dr. Beck is a talented an knowledgeable instructor. The course needs to be re-designed.

Doable to get "A". Prof has 0 presence in labs (TAs). Get a good lab partner, review prior & next lab for weekly quiz & you're solid. Prof is EXTREMELY understanding. I was horribly sick the week of the final & he postponed it twice for me when I still hadn't recovered. VERY understanding, approachable (via email) person. Lot of respect for him.

Grades on a curve, once giving out a quiz comprised of problems that had never been covered because the average was too high. Get a good TA and you'll do fine, but with a poor TA labs will drag on and you'll get lost in the quizzes and eventual final.

All the stuff you love and none of the stuff you hate about 3043. No checkoffs or lab quizzes. Really good lectures. Adjusts lab time based on difficulty. Tests can still be a little rough grade-wise but prof is an amazing teacher.

Dr. Beck was my recitation professor for ECE2026. He was absolutely essential in understanding that class and made one of the harder classes at Georgia Tech an absolute breeze. He was clear, concise, and thorough in his recitation.

ECE2020 is a disaster. There is no recitation, no textbook, no good TAs, and no explanation apart from the one provided by the professor. Sadly, Beck wouldn't even post his lecture notes online, so it was tough to copy all the circuit diagrams and understand what was going on. Also, his office is not even in the GT campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beck was a very clear teacher. He gave relevant class examples and his notes were very thorough. His tests were similar to a combination of notes and homework. He was a really interesting guy who was always willing to talk. I would absolutely recommend him for ECE2020

So much work but I feel I understand thermo now! He clearly knows but explains some concepts fast! So far lots of extra credit! His slides are AMAZING and sums up his lectures. HARD exams but REGRADE after each exam IS EXTREMELY HELPFUL!

Tough course BUT he makes it very approachable! Long and HARD homeworks but his office hours are extremely useful! Helped me through internships and recommendation letters for my fellowship! He is the professor you take to understand thermodynamics!!

Probably the most difficuly professor I will ever take at TECH. Please save yourself the trouble and dont take him. Make sure to prepare for a low grade, long HWs, and exams that are nothing like the class material. Just dont take him!.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at tech. HOWEVER, Dr. Fil is the best. Very caring and great dude. I really enjoyed his lectures, he was very enthusiastic and man do I know thermo now. Fair grader. The homework was a full time job and the exams were brutally hard though.

This class was by far the most work I have ever done. The homework in this class would take around 12 hours per week, and that is not an overestimate. On the final, there were things that we had never seen before. Teaching-wise, a limited amount of foundational concepts were covered, and you were just thrown into the fire to figure it out.

Not the easiest class, but if you put in the effort you will really learn thermodynamics. The homework is long and tough, but office hours are helpful and the problems prepare you well for his exams. I finally understood thermo!!

Do the homework, attend lectures, go to office hours and you will be fine in class. I liked that homework questions were different from those in textbook and similar to what would you expect in his exams. If you get an A on his final its an A in class despite what you had earlier.

Only section that didn't have a take home final, and got the lowest avg on the 2nd exam. The hw's are long, and graded harshly and the lectures are conceptual. I helped other sections study for their finals and their review question were far easier. We got only two review questions per test. Hardest tests I've taken at GT. Caring guy.

Dr. El Fil is hands down the best lecturer I've had at GT. He makes difficult concepts intuitive, often using physical demos that really stick. The homework is heavy. Exams are hard, but if you manage your time and focus on getting partial credit, you'll be fine. This is the professor to take if you truly want to understand thermodynamics.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at Tech so far! He made thermodynamics interesting for me. It was about what I came in expecting to put in effort for this class. His exams had option of retaking the test and getting bonus points!

Personally I enjoyed each lecture specially when he can simplify abstract concepts. Exams were tough but he allows you to retake the test for bonus! This helped a lot. Very caring and always made sure we got the concept. He knows his stuff really well. Lenient grader with long HWs. Go office hours it makes a huge difference!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thermodynamics is already tough but he makes it so much smoother! Exams are tough but you can learn a lot from his HW! Super nice guy and helps you out a lot!

Expects students to have 20hrs/week set aside for this class. During exams, it was common to see people crying. The problems were unlike those we went over and were impossible to complete in the given time. Studied for the final for a week, 14hrs/day, and could not complete half of it. HW graded harshly and barely any review material. Ok to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. He's a nice guy and cares a lot but his expectations are way to high. Teaches purely conceptual in class and then expects you to learn everything on the homework, which is impossible without a software that he doesn't teach you how to use. Class is 20+ hours of work per week. Tests are abysmal and good luck finishing in time.

Definitely one of the hardest ME classes I took at GT, but I learned a ton from it. He really knows his stuff and doesn't shy away from testing you on it. The HWs and exams are tough, but there is a lot of practice to prepare you well. Grading is fair and pretty lenient. Lectures were fun, and I liked the mix of slides and board.
Tough class but learn a bunch!

Best professor ever. If you don't get an A in this class then that's 100% on you. She gives you everything you could need to succeed. I never took notes and she gives you what slides to study before the test. Just show up on the days you're told and study the slides she lists.

Professor Badura was an amazing teacher for this class. Even though the course was at 8am, she managed to keep lectures entertaining and not once did I want to skip class because of her. She is super engaging with her students and loves what she does which makes it so much easier to take the class with her overall. 10/10 would take again!
Katie really is a wonderful professor, she is a rare breed that genuinely cares about both her class and her content. I honestly wish all my professors were more like her.

I loved professor Badura! She kept lectures interesting, learned everyone's names, and brought us donuts on the second to last day. She gives you a list of what slides to study for the test, which is extremely helpful if you have a busy schedule. Would take again!

really liked her class and she's very easy to talk to. puts effort into learning everyones name and engaging people in discussion. would definitely take her class again, there's no final but each midterm (3) is 22% of the grade (tests are almost 70%). they're not difficult though, fairly easy and she posts the exact slides to study on study guides.
Great professor and enjoyable classes. Her lectures are funny and insightful. She breaks up the class into small groups towards the end to help stimulate engagement. 10/10 would take again.

GREAT PROFESSOR! She is very kind and explains concepts clearly. Gives weekly open-note quizzes and NO tests. Only one paper assignment and she gives you like 5 weeks to complete it. Hybrid format was great with her Summer 2021. 10/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: INCREDIBLE! Her fall 2020 class was excellently crafted within the hybrid framework. Every time I went to class time was used efficiently to help us apply what we learned in the online parts. 1 paper, 13 open note quizzes, 13 in-person (or online) activities. Takes feedback well, listens to and respects students. I learned a ton + love her!!! 10/10

Prof Badura is really invested in your learning. She makes absolute sure you learn what she teaches by quizzing you immediately after lecture and forcing you to recall what you learned through experiential activities or learning check-ups. None of these graded activities are difficult. Pay attention to lecture and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was extremely frustrating. She talks in the most monotone voice to show us how to use CAD, and if you don't sit in the front, it's hard to see what she does on the board. The TA will try to help but then you miss more of the lecture. Be prepared to stay after class to finish studio work later in the semester and spend hours on projects.

Professor Balic does go fast through lectures, and it can be hard to keep up and follow along. For 1070 be prepared to put in more time than you expect though. Attendance is graded but if you miss studio it'll be hard to catch up anyways. Grading wasn't too harsh but was mostly done by the TA, so it might vary from semester to semester.

After this class, I am heavily considering switching majors. Not only are her lectures extremely boring and hard-to-follow, but her feedback is unhelpful and passive-aggressive. The only reason the class itself isn't difficult is because of the lenient grading--by the TA. 
This class is a 1-credit-hour-class, but be ready to spend 4+ hrs/week.

She knows her stuff, but can be hard to follow lectures sometimes. If you miss a step, you might be confused for the next 15 min. There is very minimal feedback given on assignments, but you're likely to get a good grade anyways. If you have any questions, she is more than willing to help you. The final project was really fun and had extra credit.

Lectures could be a little dull but overall the course was well taught and very easy. Showing up to studio and paying attention was extremely important though as posted materials weren't nearly as thorough as lectures and comments made in lecture were crucial for completing assignments.

Took 1070, but it wasn't an option here... had a hard time paying attention to her lectures and ended up learning most of AutoCAD on Youtube. Very fast-paced lectures. Hard to makeup missed classwork, do not miss class. Grading was a little harsh. She'd give an assignment after lecture and leave, and the poor TA struggled to help everyone.

Dr. Balic is a very good professor up until the last portion of the class where we learn Civil3D. The labs are just copying a pdf and doing what it tells you to do and you dont learn anything. Then we have a project that requires our knowledge of civil3d and Balic is not much of a help when we ask. be prepared to learn most everything on your own.

Balic is a very good professor who knows what she's talking about. Her classes are pretty boring. She doesn't always give extensions but if she does its only a day or two at most. She does really care and want you to do well and is a very nice woman. I really enjoyed her class and enjoyed learning about the material. Labs were fairly easy.

Sweet lady + knowledgable + willing to help, but lectures put me to sleep. Class was dry, and labs were time consuming + required HW. Very time consuming, so it's an endurance game. Labs/projects being graded harshly put ppl on edge abt their grade, but it works out in the end. She gets her job done fine.

Professor Balic is great! Lectures can be a little boring, but that's just the content. The professor is very passionate about the subject, which makes her more personable. Labs are fairly easy, and instructions are clear. If you are mostly attentive and want to learn, you can get a high A.

Nice person. The classes were a bit boring but relatively easy. The first half of the semester there was no homework, just labs, which are really tedious but not difficult. The second half of the semester we had a few projects which are manageable, but make sure not to wait until the last minute because they do take a bit of time.
Love love love Professor Balic. Her lectures were very clear, her tests were fair, and the grading system was fair. She makes Statics way easier.

Dr. Balic is a nice professor, knows everything she is talking about, and really wants her students to connect with the material. The labs and the projects are the most important part of the course and take a lot of time too, so be sure to give all your effort. Lectures can be a little bit boring but they are important.

This class was very time consuming. The lectures averaged from 45 mins to an extra 30 min sometimes after class video. On top of that the labs def will take some 2-3+ hours w/ the addition of your side projects which take a lot of time on your hands. Her lab / project instructions need to be more clearer sometimes b/c I was often confused ngl.

Professor Balic is very nice and approachable w/ Q's. You're going to be sketching/doing AutoCAD which is time-consuming, so you'll have to budget your time. There's 1 lab each week and 4 projects (three that have an individual & a group portion). She wants everyone to get an A, so if you show that you're trying she will help you get a good grade.

Professor Balic's lectures are not great and the homework is very long. But if you do the homework and in class examples, nothing on any exams will be a surprise. Plus she gives a ton of partial credit on exams

Only resources are the slides she flies through in the lesson. Your best other option is the SI leader. Otherwise you're on your own. If you must take this class try hard to get a good grade in the homework and practice throughout the course of the semester, not just for exams. She makes it harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures were extremely boring and it was hard to stay awake. The projects were somewhat time consuming especially the later group projects so be prepared to spend quite a bit of time out of class on the work. Not difficult if you put in the effort to complete the projects and assignments, she is just not a great professor.

Boring lecturer, boring lectures. Includes many superfluous tasks and requirements in projects that add no real value to your learning, but rather make the course even more tedious than it already is. Pedantic grader. Not bad, but far from the best.

Her 'teaching' consists purely of reading off of slides and then solving a few example problems per topic with the students just watching. Weekly homeworks that were way harder than the example problems. We could have a cribsheet for the exams but only of formulas. Homework was worth 20%, exams 1 & 2 worth 25%, and the final was worth 30%. Hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are so boring. Outside of that, she is a caring professor and wants everyone to succeed in AutoCAD. Try to pay a little bit on attention so you have an idea of what to do in the labs and large projects. Not a hard class, but definitely time-consuming towards the end of the semester.

Dr. Balic is really good with AutoCad and Civil3D. You will know AutoCad very well by the end of the semester. Civil3D is a hard software to learn, but if you understand the labs you will be fine. Her lectures tend to be slow, and attendance is part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Balic really does want her students to pass. Lectures can be a bit boring. The class requires no CAD experience but if you have prior CAD/Civil 3D knowledge, then you will find the assignments rather easy. Class is heavy on projects, pro tip do them ahead of time. Overall, its an easy class!

The lectures were both hard to follow and quite boring. Dr. Balic was understanding in terms of answering questions or concerns. The labs would help teach the basics while the projects would leave room for creativity. Overall, the drawing and 2D CAD portions of the class were easy to learn, but the 3D Civil was confusing and difficult to learn.

Lectures are boring, but labs and projects do a decent job of teaching AutoCAD. Unfortunately the Civil 3D portion was poorly done (although it is difficult to teach such a complicated program in so little time). She is very accessible outside of class. Go to office hours if you have questions. Not hard to get an A if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lectures are very boring and project instructions can be unclear but Dr. Balic is very responsive and kind and you will do fine in the class if you manage your time well and go to Dr. Balic with any questions you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The one plus side is that she is very nice. Other than that, she is an incredible boring lecturer who makes the class unnecessarily hard. She has us working on multiple projects at the same time. She has us do a presentation which is graded very strictly even though this is not a presentation based class: absolutely do not recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is very nice, easy to talk to, knows AUTO CAD very well, but she is a terrible lecturer. She just reads off the slides and repeats herself a lot. She spends the entire time lecturing, and she often takes up the first hour of our lab to lecture. It's hard to pay attention because she is very boring. Luckily, the class is an easy A.

Always very helpful with projects and requirements during her office hours. Lectures were sort of monotonous, but very deliberate and helpful overall. Very knowledgeable and skillful with the CAD software.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is an awful teacher. Probably doesn't really understand the material herself. She reads from the slides prepared by the textbook company, and then attempts examples on the board but makes a lot of mistakes. Tests are crazy hard and nothing like what she covers in class. I worked really hard but the final felt impossible and she doesn't curve.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Balic was a great instructor! Very approachable and helpful during office hours. She is excellent at teaching AutoCAD and Civil 3D! Definitely knows her stuff. She loves teaching this class and wants you to succeed in it. The class is not hard, but the projects so require A LOT of time. Start early on them (and avoid all nighters)!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof. Balic is a nice person and easy to go to outside of class, but not necessarily willing to work with you to get your grade up. She's compassionate and cares, however I found her class to be harder than a 2 credit course should be. The tests were graded pretty toughly and the homework was insanely difficult. I had to purchase Chegg.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Balic is pretty good at teaching CAD.  She has a thick accent so if you typically have trouble with that sort of thing you should try to get another professor.  Other than that she's a fair grader and the class is really easy.  As long as you try you'll get an A.  The group projects are pretty time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class frustrated me a lot. The homework was unnecessarily long and hard. Went to office hours more than I would've liked to have to and still only got an 84% hw avg. Uses WileyPLUS. Lectures are understandable but really boring. She knows what she's doing, but its hard to pay attention and the class is more work than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr.Bhamla is very sweet and accessible outside of the class. The class is heavily about fluid mechanics, so be prepared for long and complicated math problems. Dr.Bhamla cares about his student and goes above and beyond to help. The material is difficult, so make sure you spend enough time to learn.

Professor Bhamla is the perfect example of a passionate, curious, and enthusiastic scientist. He engages the class in a way that unparalleled by any other professor I've taken a lecture from. Prof Bhamla constantly encourages audience participation and peer learning, and integrates fascinating videos showing the applications of Transport Phenomena.

I get the vibe that he doesn't actually know much thermo conceptually. He's not bad at teaching per se, though he doesn't give much explanation. Terrible at answering questions, but he does try. He likes the practical aspect more than the equations so he shows videos in class that are quite cool. Overall, 7/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thermo is concept heavy, but Dr. Bhamla's biggest strength is explaining concepts. However, he doesn't have time in class to work out many numerical problems. 2130 deserves to be 3 credit hrs. Recitation/TA office hrs are key for understanding those. He expects you to be a good critical thinker. His homeworks are tough, but his exams are fair.
Doesn't understand much Thermo and classes are a mess.

I had him in the Spring of 23 and I liked him a lot. I read through some of his previous reviews, and I thought he was fine. He's by no means an amazing lecturer, but for if you go and take some initiative and get involved in discussions, it's a good class.

I did not enjoy this course at all. I was excited to dive into OS but it almost killed my interest. He's nice and extended deadlines multiple times. However, his lectures are boring and do not help you in the labs nor the midterm. The labs were cool but hard with no feedback on the test cases. The midterm was weird since you had to rely on Google.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Lectures: not helpful & boring
Projects: very time consuming - hard to complete without office hours or help from friends
Test: felt like the lecture contents barely helped to actually answer questions - googling is much more effective

Easily the worst prof at GT. Changes grading criteria as he goes (his words). Lies to you (blatantly). Labs take 30 hours each. Autograder only gives pass/fail, no feedback. Lectures consist solely of HIM asking the CLASS questions, to which he does not give an actual answer. Just don't go to class, and read the excellent textbook instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is the most inconsistent grader. The class had one exam on it and had nothing to do with anything taught in class. The labs are mostly on your own with very little (and crappy) instruction and the TAs are not much help. Interesting course, horrible professor. Don't go to class; read the xv6 textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Two midterms, 9 HW's which are just writing 2 questions per HW problem, final is no longer optional. Polarizing professor for sure. Responds sarcastically to some questions, lectures fast, and is a tough grader. To offset her rough exams, she provides 5 bonus points via bonus assignments which she would often poorly explain and are due next class.

She is a great lecturer that knows a lot about thermodynamics, teaches her subject with energy, and clearly cares about preparing her lectures (which are both tutorial-like and self-contained). It was also cool when she answered students' questions with info she learned from her research. The classroom was also full and lively.

Professor Bassiri-Gharb is the best professor I've taken at Tech to be honest. She's extremely caring, understanding and reasonable. She's very straightforward on how to be successful in her class, and her exams are very fair based off of in-class examples, homeworks, and past exams. Made Thermo easier to understand and loved taking her section

Professor is generally caring if you reach out to her, responds very fast. Midterms are difficult but generally not bad if you take good notes in lectures and redo homeworks, homeworks are also not bad at all. Takes random participation for some lectures but has pretty good extra credit. Had a good time and learned a lot.

Rude when answering questions in class. Test grading was unfair, my first exam I got every answer but one out of 25 correct numerically and got a D. Showed my work and used the correct formulas, just in the wrong order (she stated that she doesn't use a rubric). Got the exam 2 grade back in less than 48 hours. Just doesn't care about the class.

Amazing lecturer who respects students and takes the time to make sure they understand the material. No answers immediately given for practice exams, but can easily be obtained in office hours. Exams make up a large majority of class grade, but enough practice makes them manageable.
Very good lecturer, prepares you well for exams. Good amount of bonus available. Exams were very fair.

Good lectures, homeworks were posted with answer keys when you get stuck. 2 exams with bonus points make up large portion of grade with an optional final. Respected students (even memorizing their names) but does expect you to know certain concepts. Doesn't upload lectures, but uploaded student's notes.

Dr. Bassiri is one of my favorite professors at Tech. Her exams were all take home which took away the time issue that makes so many classes hard. Her lectures are incredibly clear and I got great notes that were extremely helpful. She gives bonus points throughout the semester so make sure you get all those. She does give past exams but no solutns

Extremely knowledgeable prof whom answered questions in class very well. Gave at least 5% easy bonus opportunities added to your overall grade. Only issue I had with her was that she was very hesitant to provide solutions to past tests for review.

Took off 11% of my entire grade for misreading part of a sub problem. Wish I were making this up. Contacted her regarding this and was met with dismissal in a condescending tone. It was clear she didn't even read my email. Other than that, class is not too time intensive and lectures are decent.

Great professor for Thermo. Lectures were recorded (other than occasional software errors), grading criteria is clear. Exams are exactly how she covers in lecture/practice exams. She gives bonus homework throughout the semester; do those for sure since every point counts here. Just use your common sense, don't cut corners, and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had at Tech. She is so caring and tries her best to help students understand material, and she makes herself available to speak with outside class hours or office hours. You will need to put in work and make sure you understand the material thoroughly but the class is structured well and it's not extremely difficult to do so

Thermo isn't intuitive at first, but her lectures are AMAZING. 2 exams + final are worth 90%, but there are about 5-7 extra credit points that you can get added to your final grade. Attendance is "non-mandatory" but you won't get these points or the benefit of the lectures if you don't go. Just put effort in and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going to lecture, or getting notes from someone else, is mandatory. Exams are very reasonable, and she gives like 4 points (to your final grade) of extra credit throughout the semester. Also really funny and you can tell she cares about her students.

Her notes are good and she explains concepts clearly. She's also pretty funny and nice. I felt the 2 exams were fair and she grades them fairly too. She also gave out 5 bonus HWs throughout the semester, so if you attempted the problem at all, you got 1% added to your overall grade for each bonus HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Her lectures are organized and provide all the information that you need. I have excellent notes from this class, which really helped with studying. The homework is just the right amount to understand without getting overwhelmed. Tests are challenging but very fair. She is strict but caring and fair, gives lots of opportunities to up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Arrogant and condescending. Good luck.

She's a strict grader and expects students to derive or memorize content on the tests because she doesn't allow students to use their own formula sheets. She can be stand-offish in class and has a "stern mom" attitude with most students. I found her personable and helpful one on one and very different from in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Tech so far. She is NOT mean to students, these other reviews were definitely written by people who didn't respect her or her class. If you respect her, she will respect you. She truly cares about her students and their well being. She is also a great lecturer. Go to every class, do HW well, and you will succeed.
Mean to students. She makes me sad

Be careful asking questions in class. She will go out of her way to make you look unintelligent while avoiding the answer to the question. She also provides very few examples, especially of more complex problems.
She's not a bad teacher but uses few examples and expects you to know more than she teaches. She isn't very nice to students, especially when talking one on one. She is very unforgiving.
Dr. Biddle is a very passionate and interesting lecturer, and the class is pretty discussion-heavy.

Dr. Biddle is NOT accessible outside of class. Does not respond to emails. This sucks because each absence from his class is 2% off final grade and it's hard to communicate. However, class is relatively easy and discussion based. I've learned a lot from his class. I just wish he was more lenient to absences and more responsive. He's cool I guess.

Dr. Biddle is a chill and awesome professor. I would recommend taking his philosophy class. Participation counts and the semester is broken into 3 parts: 1. do reading before class and have discussion on Perusall & have discussions in class, 2. individual essay (some in-class time given), and 3. group essay/presentation (in-class time given).

Professor Biddle is one of the best professors that I have had so far. He cares about your grade and also cares that you are actually retaining the information. There weren't any exams and 2 papers. The class isn't necessarily difficult but will be a struggle if you don't do the work and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Biddle cares about his students, and wants his students to learn. Had to read before each class (1.5 hrs of work) to be able to do his pop quizzes and participate in class (there was no homework). However, pop quizzes are easy - they are very high level. The midterm and final were take-home, and consisted of a few essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Had daily quizzes over readings and a final project/presentation. He was a good teacher who would go over the readings in lecture and kept a very reasonable grading structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Read the assigned articles and participate a little bit. There are two papers (the midterm and the final), but they are relatively easy. As long as you actually do what he gives you, the class is an easy A. He does come off as if he thinks his opinion is the only correct one though, so if that annoys you maybe find a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My class was a discussion based class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Biddle is a great professor and his lectures are interesting and enlightening. His class consists of daily readings and lectures that clarify the author's message. The only graded assignments are weekly pop quizzes to ensure you're actually reading, and take-home essay exams for the midterm/final. Understand the material and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While I understand that he had never taught the course before, his lectures were still rough. He just copied pre-made slides from the course coordinator - I would recommend going to her if you need help instead. Handwriting was difficult to read. Seems like a great guy, but definitely does not need to teach MSE 2001.

Professor Brown moved slowly through material, leaving a full unit to learn on our own via online videos. Lectures were often unclear, but projects and test corrections were easy and boosted grades. Attendance was mainly needed for participation credit rather than understanding.
A slideshow could substitute lectures. Lots of practice exams posted. Quite a bore.

Really nice guy, but his teaching style was too slow. We sometimes weren't able to cover all the content for the day, so he would refer us to lecture videos to watch on our own time. Also, some of his explanations were difficult to understand and apply. However, there are built-in extra credit projects + corrections to boost your grade slightly.

Dr. Brown is great at explaining things. One thing that I particularly liked was the fact that when he did not know something, he would take the effort to find out and explain it. However, he is a bit slow during lectures and we didn't even get to the last unit. However, I'm going to give him a pass since it was his first time teaching the course.

The instruction is good but there is too much content to cover in this class. TA's are lifesavers with recitation and office hours. Past exams are helpful but be prepared to do a lot of self learning and outside the box thinking. Make a study group if you want to do well .Online final no partial credit was insane. You will never forget this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this in my first semester here at tech. It was very difficult at first, but there are lots of resources like past exams and your TA to help you. Prof. Juang is a very chill dude and he's pretty caring if you just reach out to him with your problems. I would say the hardest part of this class (besides attendance) is doing well on HW.
You should just ask ChatGPT to explain the content to you during lectures, since attendance is mandatory, and this guy acts smug while proceeding to say nothing of value.

Prof. knows the content of the course well, but is very bad at transferring that knowledge to his students. Lectures are hard to pay attention to, there are no materials to study for the tests that actually reflect what the test will be like, and the only time I ever learned content was in recitation and by struggling on the HW. Take anyone else.
shoutout to my glorious goat chun wei other than that expect a panic attack the night before every quiz

The only issues I had with Professor Juang were more issues with how ECE 2026 is administered as a course. It's a weed out and is designed to be a little unfair at times. I can't fault Professor Juang for any of my complaints on that, as it would be the case with any 2026 professor. Very knowledgeable and helpful if asked for help.

Overall nice professor. ECE 2026 has always been known to be difficult but just don't fall behind and you should do fine. Exams are difficult and require you to have a true understanding of the material so take some time to study and review lecture slides.
ECE 2026. Fall 2022. Exam 3. phuck u
An old man truly out of touch with students. Horrible at lecturing and unfair exams. Avoid this pathetic thing like the plague.
A truly terrible Professor for an already difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not very good at explaining anything, relates himself a lot, and doesnt seem to actually know whats going on. The second professor that taught the other section of the class did a much better job and seemed to be the only one that actually knew what was happening.

Would never take this class again. Stay away from ECE 3077. Studied for three weeks before a Test, only being able to get the professor to tell us the broad material that it will cover, and did horrible. Go from making +90 on all math and engineering course tests to failing with this class.

ECE 2026 at Tech is extremely organized and efficient. That being said, the class is very tough. I had Juang for recitation and I learned the concepts much more in there than the main lecture. Juang is very detailed and good at explaining things. He works relevant problems that are very helpful for homework and tests. I would take him again.

Concepts was easier than i expected but lots of work.Homework and lab every week. Do homework in groups or you'll be frustrated. Also use lots of office hours. For labs, do pre-lab before coming to lab. Take tests very seriously.

Pretty solid professor and class overall. The grading is pretty generous considering we have a pretty easy final project and can get up to 5% added to our final grade with extra credit. You get this ec by being in class though so attendance is required. All in all he's pretty nice and helpful and the class isn't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the better stats professors out there. He has a very generous grading policy, gifting you up to 15% free if you just show up to lecture. Tests were a bit difficult but doable if you studied. Final project can be a lot of work. However, he does random attendance checks and you need to be in class.

First sem teaching but did his best. HWs are easy, but nothing is representative of exams. Cheat sheets allowed but even then exams are difficult. 5 entire points of EC from random attendance quizzes. One group project, last exam during regular class time on the week on finals. Nice and respectful, just a wonky class structure.

HW easy and only 6. Exams were not, and the exam reviews were very different than the exams despite the professor insisting that they'll be similar (at least you can have 2 cheat sheets). Good extra credit (5 points). This was his first semester, so there was disorganization, especially with the dates of when things were due and exam dates.
For INTA 3050- very nice professor and VERY easy class but her lectures are so disorganized. she tends to ramble for the entire class with no real point. Hated going to class, but worth it for the A!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, caring teacher, amazing program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Took the course in Fall 2021. Vicki has a notorious reputation for going onto tangents but she is an incredibly caring person and will do everything she can (both inside and outside class) to get to know you and help.
She was the program lead for FYFA and while she loved to go on about tangents, she is one of the nicest people I've ever met.
Great Professor who really wants her students to learn! If your at all interested in Europe, Dr. Birchfield has the class for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She does not directly use the book she says is "required" for class, but requires students to read several pages of it for each class module. Her field trips are not always well planned. Her slides are clumsy and filled with text, and scheduling of assignments is done verbally only.
She led a study abroad I participated in during Summer 2014. She was clear, concise, and was clearly vested in making sure we all learned from the trip. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

I've had Birchfield for another class before. She can definitely be scattered and hard to follow sometimes, but overall, she's a very good professor. While she and I may not always have same or similar opinions, she's not the sort of professor to hold it against you or effect your grade. I'm looking forward to taking a third class with her.

She can't stick to her lecture at all.  She would get about 1/3 through her outline and then the whistle would blow because she spent too much time talking about pointless information.  But don't worry, you'll see it on the test.
Least organized prof I've ever had.  Brings personal politics into "lectures" (i.e. rants).  Nothing was clear, orderly, or understood in the class.
No Comments
extremely unorganized. goes off on rants during lecture. excessive, superfluous readings. tests have little to do with lecture material. lectures on abstract concepts, tests minute details.

HUGE AMOUNTS OF READING. LECTURES ARE NOT ORGANIZED AND YOU WILL BE TESTED OVER THE SMALLEST DETAIL.  NEVER FINISHES MATERIAL PLANNED FOR LECTURES, BUT YOU WILL BE TESTED ON THAT AS WELL. QUESTIONS ON THE TEST ARE DIFFICULT TO UNDERSTAND WHAT SHE WANTS.
Boring lectures and bad grader
I would not recommend taking Professor Bier's classes.

Her lectures tend to be kind of boring, but group discussions are engaging if you're caught up with all the readings. Assignments are extremely easy and tests consist of memorizing terms and writing an essay, which she grades fairly. I wouldn't recommend buying all the books, since you can get by without reading them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's super passionate about what she's teaching. Lectures can be long, but interesting. She took weeks to grade things, which was rough. Just pay attention in class and at least skim the readings and you'll get an A.

She is a nice professor. She gives out everything that is going to be on the midterm and final, so study that a lot. I thought she was going to grade easily because she is nice but she grades essays very strictly. I wish this class was more of a discussion, but instead she lectured a lot. Don't turn anything in late.

For the most part you will pass if you read and understand the textbook, which the tests are directly based on. Most classtime is devoted to lectures which ho more in-depth. The teacher is very enthusiastic about the topics she teaches.

4 textbooks barely used.dont buy. u can get by by gogling the readings. And unless you have to turn in a paper, dont bother doing the readings. Too much assigned and a complete waste of time. Ask her for her expectation on midterm papers because she is alot stricter when grading those. Class borng. she needs to learn 2 teach rather than readng ppt
Not the most exciting class but all you need to know for the tests she uploads online
needs training on how to teach and to lead discussions

Very open-minded and respectful of everyone's opinions in this discussion-based class. There is a lot of reading and writing involved, and while the material is interesting, I wish the class was more engaging. Positive attitude and willingness to listen to feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Favorite course of the semester! Classes were discussion based. The readings were extremely interesting, and our class got to vote on topics to cover for the last few weeks. Tests were based on ability to apply concepts from class, and were very similar to the short weekly responses. Professor was very kind and respectful of everyone's opinions.

I enrolled in this course as an elective but was pleasantly surprised by how engaged I became in its content, as the professor does a great job in conveying his enthusiasm. With few graded assignments, as long as you put in the expected effort, this is an easy course to succeed in. 100% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Biegalski for NRE 3112, and on multiple occasions he made it clear that he really does care about his students. Dr. Biegalski also does a good job lecturing and answering questions, as well as just being a really chill and affable professor. My only complaint is that he oftentimes is too nice and students would heavily abuse that.

I encourage you to get to know Dr. Biegalski both inside ad outside  of class.  Assuming you like him, see if you can get involved in his research.
