He send another girl from my class for a professional conference in Hawaii this past semester for her to present he research,  that would be a good GT experience,

Also ask him about fly fishing.

I took his class to graduate during Spring 2020. He is definitely in my top 5 favorite professors at Tech. He teaches the material extremely well, is interested in getting to know all of his students, and I had a ton of fun learning about nuclear reactions, reaction design, and nuclear energy. I wish he taught more classes.
One of the sweetest profs I have had. Really knows his stuff but easily gets sidetracked- Not a bad thing though. I spent maybe 1 hour per week on this class outside of lecture.

I'll be honest- I have no interest in Nuclear Engineering, and just had to take this class to graduate. However, Professor Biegalski was by far one of the best professors I had at tech. He teaches very clearly. His tests are extremely fair. He really cares about the well being of his students. I really wish I could have had him for more classes.
Best professor so far at Georgia Tech.
He makes the content more enjoyable and helps make complicated stuff easier!
One of the best professors so far! Really approachable and caring!
Caring towards students and very helpful!
Good into class. I enjoyed the lectures.
Very engaging professor and made me even more interested in nuclear engineering.

Very nice teacher who does his best to introduce the material in a lighthearted manner, although he does veer off course sometimes. Weekly homework is given and each student does a presentation to further interest in the major. Tests are similar to homework problems.

The most passionate professor I've had. Incredible guest speakers that changed my perspective on many things. Class is heavily participation-based, but I was able to get an A in participation only speaking twice all semester because I commented on Canvas group discussions and did some easy extra credit assignments. 2-3 easy essays 2pg double space

One of the best professors that I have ever had. Class is a mixture of case discussions and guest speakers. Grades are based on one test, three short essays, class participation. Prof. Todd has a wealth of industry knowledge and does a great job helping students understand healthcare. He's very lenient grader. Show up and try; you will make an A.
This was a great class with a bunch of guest lectures from people in the health care industry. I really enjoyed this class

Professor Todd really cares about his students.  I would suggest taking this class even if you are not interested in healthcare.  Straight up grades, two essay tests, case assignments, and class participation.  Professor really wants students to succeed. LOTS of guest speakers

Such an interesting course. If you have any interest in healthcare, take it. Professor Todd is the best professor! He has a discussion based class about half of the time and excellent guest speaker the other half of the time. He is genuinely interested in your success as a student. I wish I could take this class every semester!

Class was pretty easy. Just show up to class. Most of what you see on the test was said in class, so attendance is key. He's also a pretty cool guy. His stories are interesting. He has a lot of connections so he's someone you would want to know!

Hes a decently nice guy but did not care about the class. We were so behind in this class, and ECE 2020 is like the base of every ECE major so it set everyone up for failure. We covered 50% of what we were supposed to cover. The class was bearable but I was just angry that I didn't get to learn everything I should have as an ECE major.
A decent lecturer and a good guy, with not too much HW. Class was unorganized and exams covered topics not in the HW or lecture.

Professor Bloch is an extremely caring professor, who is always willing to distribute knowledge on any subject he has on hand. Signal processing, machine learning, life lessons, he has and will teach about anything. Being in this VIP course has taught me so much, even when I started from no knowledge at all.

I don't think he deserves all the hate that these reviews have been giving him. The class was fair and the exams were very similar to the homework. He is a nice person and mostly accommodating. He is very slow, but he also doesn't normally teach, and his section was only added to accommodate the influx of freshmen. This is not a deadly class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have attended 4 funerals this year and didn't shed a tear at any. I bawled after his final exam and midterms. No preparation provided except for literally nothing. This class was the definition of doom and despair and everything unfair. Matthieu Ratoslav will take your soul - do not take unless you want to cross the River Styx.

Anyone who gives this guy a review over three stars is just straight delusional. He's clearly only here for research and doesn't really care about teaching (we were wayyyy behind what we were supposed to be covering), and most your grades is the exam. If you care about learning, avoid at all costs
The class overall wasn't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute joke of a professor. Hands down one of the worst i've ever experienced at Tech. Too focused on his family responsibilities instead of his class... Not judging because I would too but maybe don't decide to take on a class and teach if you have familial responsibilities.

Please do not take Matthieu ratoslav bloch. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE HIM. The worst professor at GT hands down. Just dont. Any other ECE 2020 prof will be better. He will not teach you anything. Pleas eplease please avoid

Extremely exam-heavy, and the exams felt like the entire grade was a few problems. On top of that, it's proof-heavy in a way that didn't feel necessary for an introductory course. Just absolutely dodge this guy at all costs, 1 month behind on content, don't feel prepared for 2031 at all.

I actually do like the professor, but the pacing of the class was much slower than other sections, exam and lab dates were postponed frequently, and he wasn't great at communicating logistics with the class.

Though we only covered half of the course material, Professor Bloch is a nice and accessible teacher. Tests are relatively easy and no tricky questions, but you will probably lose amount of points on some math and theory proof questions. The final exam is worth 33% of the total course grade, so really be prepared for that.

Cool professor, fun class. Exams and homeworks were easy. Pretty chill about labs - he allowed me to use a $10 arduino uno instead of the $250 mydaq, and didn't require lengthy reports.

Pacing was slow, but it seems all the reviews complaining about it forget to mention that this was his first time teaching an intro class.

Would recommend.

He is a decent lecturer, with my main criticism being that we were a month behind on content. Normally I wouldn't care, but the content in this class is interesting and important foundationally for engineers and internships. The tests model the homework and are not that hard, and the labs are lightweight and easy.

just pray you get bhattacharya. she's the only way. bloch makes this way too harsh for an INTRO class for FRESHMAN. anyone other than her i've heard makes this class way too demanding and tedious for the so called easy ece class.

Lied to our faces about exam questions multiple times. Emphasized proof-based math questions instead of engineering/ system design ones, where the slightest error could cost you half credit. Only covered half of the material listed in the syllabus; we have to catch up now. His reviews for the graduate-level classes have the exact same complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
We got to early October's material in December. He regularly makes promises he doesn't keep.

He has described his own grading scheme as brutal. Every (lengthy) question is 2 points. If you write down anything you get 1 point. If you get the entire problem correct with no small errors at all, you get 2 points. 85% of the course grade was exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not provide practice exams, exams are EXTREMELY HARD and nothing like homework questions, he does not curve despite the low average, and he is test heavy (53% on 4 tests and 33% on final). Do NOT take his class if you want to make your life easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he great, other guy talking about his french bit is just a hater. His lectures were super engaging and in depth, I feel like I really learned why things are implemented the way they are. The homework was also very helpful and translated well to the tests. It is true that he was behind in his material, but you can tell he's just passionate

Took his ECE2020 class, and struggled heavily due to how math-heavy he was in a "System Design" class. We were over a month behind and never finished the class. He also overpromises like crazy. No practice exams; extremely test heavy; never curves despite class average; spends way to long on a single topic. All-in-all TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was his first time teaching an entry class since this section was added late. He's a good lecturer and nice guy but his pacing, approach, & grading scheme for tests were bad. We got through 1/2 the content on the sem & he has proofs on exams unlike other professors. He also grades stuff a bit late. Take him only if you like abstract questions.
He moves a little slow sometimes, but usually his lectures explain the topics quite well. We were like a month behind all semester though. His tests are extremely easy if you do the homeworks.
We were a month behind the whole semester. Explains well though.

RUN! DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY! Can't stop talking about how he's french, class is incredibly different from other ECE2020 professors, proof heavy, bad lecturer, avoid at all costs. Please take another 2020 prof like kj, rl, just anybody else.

I took Dr. Bloch's VIP for one semester, and I regret it. He does not provide a clear grading criteria and when he does not deliver something he promises on, he turns it on the students for not showing initiative. Maybe it's just his talking style, but he likes to repeat himself, and it sometimes gives the impression that he thinks we're idiots.

He often talks about the VIP being "student driven," but that stems from him being unable to properly allocate time towards it. He is also very long-winded, often repeating the same thing over and over. He attempts to connect what you do in VIP to industry which is funny cause he has no experience whatsoever in industry. Avoid this VIP at all costs

I was in his VIP and it's not letting me select that class. Dr. Bloch has poor time management skills and consistently overpromises and underdelivers. He clearly does not have enough time to conduct this VIP effectively. He consistently shows up late to meetings. Join another VIP if possible; unfortunately, I got stuck with him for three semesters.

He is quick to blame students for not studying correctly. He noted that he usually makes the midterm too hard/time constrained, so why not make it easier? If you have not taken a proofs course before I would not recommend Dr. Bloch, as he fails to provide resources on linear algebra and proofs.

Over promises literally everything, and fails to deliver. He's nice but does not prepare you at all for his exams that are twice as long as they should be. Your homework will be tangentially related to the topics in class, he'll say to come to office hours but he'll blow the entire time on the first one or two questions.

Dr. Bloch does take a while to grade things and sometimes over promised on deadlines, but I would fully recommend taking him. He's an excellent teacher and if you're willing to put in the work in the course, it'll be a good experience. If you care about the material and really want to learn it outside of just getting a grade, you'll do fine.

Many things haven't changed: late grading/proofs heavy/nice but disconnected/lots of office hours. Makes false promises about grading. Exams are based on HW but doesn't grade on time (most graded AFTER final exam). Midterm was awful, unreasonable expectations and didn't give enough time. Gave extra credit problem to compensate. Curves heavily.

There were fewer assignments than planned (6 vs 10+) with late grading feedback due to grading for 150+ students; most issues were due to him having too many responsibilities (1 y/o at home and ECE grad affairs chair). He was always communicating the situation, adjusting deadlines, and accommodating of the students. Office hours were very helpful.

Spends too long doing proofs/examples that he didn't prepare and would get stuck on. Promised min 10 HWs, but gave 6 (still due in as little as 6 days with revisions since he'd make mistakes). First test was way too long. Course didn't cover nearly as much material as promised. Class wasn't too hard but poorly taught. He's nice but disconnected.
Very hard. Very insightful. Very good educator.

Course is very challenging, and lectures were long and content heavy. Despite it being confusing most of the time, going to the lectures was important to grasp the material. Professor was very generous with grading along with an easy project grade, however he expects that you do your part in the learning process meet him halfway to be successful

I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned in class, and by the end there might have been 5 people going. Crappy Lectures. The homework wasn't too bad as you were allowed to use AI for coding, and the exams were open note(not open internet), yet this didn't really help with his slides. The project was fine. I survived but never again...

Dr. Blumling is not a great lecturer, the examples he used in class were very hard and even himself had trouble solving the problems. The tests and quizzes were very different from what we practiced in PSS and in class. The class was extremely hard for a study abroad class.

At times, the only thing that got me through this class was knowing that his actor clips existed. While working on the hours of homework that I had every week, I would turn on one of those bad boys to feel better about myself. I didn't take MATLAB before this course (since it is no longer a prerequisite) and the exams felt nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Blumling is a subpar lecturer. He likes to make material that is not just challenging but also often beyond the reach of the students. He wants to push students, but his methodology is not incremental, and it's frustrating because the class could be much more digestible and achievable if it were not made challenging for no reason.

This professor was horrible. There were no practice tests, and the only way to study for tests was by looking at Homeworks. However, there were no answer keys to Homeworks, so this class was immediately cooked. Also, BMED 2400 is supposed to be free, and he made it way harder than it needed to be. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

While a considerate person, he is not a considerate professor... Does not work through content clearly, no examples, no practice. He seems to throw everything at you and assume you are not a good student if you do not go to office hours or ask how to do something--especially if he says you did it completely wrong. His tests are an overkill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Blumling is a nice guy, but not a great professor. This easy BME class may cost me my 4.0. Tests don't reflect class material, he provides no example problems or supplemental resources, and homework answers aren't available for practice. There's also no test review, making it impossible to prepare effectively.
I feel like he does not know that students are no longer required to take Matlab before this class, so if you took 1301, you have no chance. Take anyone else for this class.

Professor Blumling completely overhauled this course into one of the most difficult in BMED. Weekly homework assignments of well over 5 hours of work a week, and tests were very unrepresentative of his lectures with awful time pressure and averages well below passing. He also assumes you are fluent in matlab (1371), and makes you code on exams.

Absolutely do not take James Blumling for biostatistics. This class is supposed to be a free A, and with any other professor it is. His tests are way to hard and the homeworks take hours to complete. It is actually unfair to students who took his class compared to any other professor with this class. He's a nice guy, but he makes it way too hard.

Homework is long and lectures don't help with completing them. The tests are poorly structured and difficult to complete. He's nice and a welcoming professor but his lectures don't help with the actual course assignments and examinations.

This course should be one of the easiest courses for BMEs and the easiest stats course at Tech. You will have hours of homework and the lectures will not help you complete it. The tests are impossible to complete based on the lectures, and you do not even have enough time to complete them. Just steer clear from his class, IYsE stats would be better

Dr. Blumling is not great at teaching the content of this course. He doesn't explain the base concepts and just kind of expects students to undertstand them, then in lecture gives the hardest possible example problem with the material. The quizzes and exams were hard to even know where to start.

its biotransport, it was never gonna be easy. For lecture, it doesnt matter who you choose because lectures are online prerecorded and profs switch off (aboulnasr has the best ones though). I had Dr. Blumling for PSS, hes very caring and easy to talk to. Hes great about explaining anything you have questions about and hes pretty laid-back too.

Blumling is a great professor for BMED 1000. He is super chill, and we normally finish lecture early. The class is a breeze. Just do your work, and you will be fine. It is group project based, so be ready to collaborate. If you get a good group, you'll be golden for this semester. Just do the weekly assignments and show up to class.

This class was literally a semester-long group project. Your TA is probably a closer resource but Dr. Blumling was always open for questions. Many opportunities and office hours to attend if you need help. Not that much work really, just a group paper a week and an essay the next week. The schedule was confusing at first but makes sense later.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made Orgo 1 so easy to understand. He's very nice and engaging in class as well, and is easy to contact for questions. So many options for extra credit. Exams were very similar to practice exams and textbook questions. Definitely have to put in work because its organic chem, but Professor Blackburn does not try to make it harder.

I was terrified to take organic chemistry this semester, but Nathan genuinely made the class interesting and less intimidating, and I ended up really enjoying a class that I'd dreaded taking my entire college career. He gives out a good bit of extra credit and is super accessible for office hours and stuff! Goated professor.

Genuinely made Orgo a breeze, you can tell he loves it and knows a lot. Flipped classroom, but the lectures really help you lock down concepts because practice is built in. He wants you to succeed and will give CIOS bonus and extra credit opportunities. Just such a nice guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I can't speak on Nathan's classroom style, as I've only had the pleasure of having him be a TA for my 2311 lecture and 2380 lab. However, I can confidently say that Nathan is an amazing teacher, and has a way of explaining and working through difficult concepts and making them significantly easier to comprehend. Take his class if given the chance.
He has a great way of making difficult concepts easy to understand and is an incredible lecturer.

Holy goat. Not particularly good at this subject and kinda fumbled on a test that cost me an A in the class, but I very much enjoyed his class. Got me a lot more interested in accounting. Not hard to lock in on this class and get an A, Professor Blunck basically gives you test blueprints. Great teacher.

Had this prof for MGT 4026, MGT 4029, and MGT 4043. His classes are straightforward with outlines and lectures videos you can refer back to. I wouldn't really recommend stacking his classes because he puts his exam dates on the same day for all of them.

Great personality and clearly wants students to succeed. Explained all topics so thoroughly that it was extremely easy to understand and cracked jokes throughout. If you have the option, CHOOSE THIS MAN.

Mythical pull of a professor. He explains the concepts well by relating them to real-world applications, and the example problems are essentially the ones seen on the tests. The tests shouldn't be too difficult if you carefully review the packets and pay attention in class. Someone here said he was like a parental figure, and I fully agree.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. He tells you every problem before the test so just review/memorize the problems from the notes and you will do fine. You don't really need to do the recommended textbook problems and he has videos on the concepts if you miss something in class.
Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

BEST PROFESSOR AT SCHELLER! If you're considering taking Accounting 2101 with anyone other than Professor Blunck, DON'T. I can't stress enough how amazing he is. He set up his class in a manner that makes it easy for all his students to succeed. Accounting is a difficult subject, but Blunck made it much more digestible.

Blunck is the most fair professor ever! He prepares you super well for each test and quiz and basically gives you the concepts you need to know for every question. If you pay attention in class, everything else is easy! 
 
Side note: This class is great to prep for interview technicals. Highly highly recommend!

Makes accounting about as engaging as it can be and explains the content very well. He is very clear about what will be on quizzes and exams, so it's easy A if you practice. HW and textbook reading is optional (and unnecessary IMO). 

If you have to take ACCT, take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very helpful

Great guy, the lectures were very informative. You could tell this guy really likes what he does and the material is presented enthusiastically almost ... hard to do for accounting. Made getting through it so much better and I definitely learned way more.

This guy is so sweet and you can tell he likes his students, likes teaching and likes the discipline and is practiced in the discipline. 

He's almost paternal in a sense, which I find endearing. 

I wish all professors were like this. Teaching is about your students learning not about you proving you are very smart or 'weeding out' students.

Prof Blunck is very knowledgable and has much to say on his subject, but he manages to keep his lectures fun and lighthearted nonetheless. I was dreading having to take a business class for my degree, but found myself looking forward to his lectures.
Fantastic professor. Tells you everything you need to know and makes accounting as intresting as he possibly can. Highly reccomend.

I took Blunck for 4026 and 4028, easily one of my favorite professors at Scheller. I am a finance concentration so I took these classes for an accounting certificate and chose to take him twice. He is incredible. His class is well structured and straightforward. It is difficult but you receive what you put into the class. He deserves the world.

The best professor I've had at Georgia Tech, genuinely caring and you can tell he loves what he does. Teaches the topic very well and will go through what general idea the quiz and test questions are going to be about the class before so you know what ideas to focus on. Very funny guy as well and made an accounting class interesting and relatable.

Professor Blunck was phenomenal, def take for accounting! The class before tests/quizzes he gives you the guidelines for every single question on the test/quiz. As long as you go to each class (attendance mandatory), you will not struggle. He also uploads the lectures if you happen to miss the class day. Lowest quiz is dropped

Professor Blunck is the best.  He may be a tiny bit boring at times, but he is an amazing guy and a great professor.  He basically tells you everything that will be on the tests so its easy to know what to study

Professor Blunck is overall a good teacher and dad-joke funny. He keeps lectures engaging although the content is inherently pretty dry. Graded on a few tests/quizzes/final with a small participation grade. Tests/quizzes are not difficult if you study ahead of time, but this class is really memorization-based and you cannot cram day before/day of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my first business class at Tech, and professor Blunck's is probably one of the few favorite classes I'm taking. He's very clear about what questions (and topics) are going to be on his quizzes & exams, and he lets you know them a lecture day in advance. He's very fair in grading & overall a great professor who's very knowledgeable.

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! Not only is he super passionate and knowledgeable, he is also very kind and understanding of students' needs. He doesn't usually try to trick you on quizzes and exams, so if you just look over your notes and practice, you'll likely do well. Very fair and sweet, he prints out lecture notes for you too.

Hes the best accounting professor ever. He is really good about explaining things and answering questions. He also gives you credit back on tests if they are graded wrong by the TA or if you made a minor mistake. His tests are manageable and he tells you exactly whats going to be on the tests.

Took him for ACCT2102 and MGT4026. Blunk is the easiest and most sensible professor I've ever had for an ACCT or FPA class. Everything you need to know is in his class handouts, so if you go to class and study those problems, it's easy to get an A (for an accounting class). He also explains what you each question on his quizzes/exams is about.

The class was a bit difficult at times, but it was very manageable even during the summer semester. Blunck is very understanding and is more than willing to help talk through any confusion. The course was a point system with 3 exams worth 100pts each and 9 quizzes worth 10pts each (lowest quiz gets dropped). It's not a bad class. Blunck was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By far, my favorite accounting class. It's complex, but Blunck makes it so easy to succeed. If you've made it this far in the accounting concentration, you've had him before and know how great his classes are. This one is certainly no exception.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: an amazing professor!! would definitely take him again!! however, the class was only graded by participation, quizzes, 3 exams and a final. he prepares you for EVERY single quiz and exam so its hard not to get a good grade on those. tries really hard to make it engaging and helpful to all of his students. definitely recommend!

While this class is difficult at times, Professor Blunck is very understanding and is an overall very good professor. We did have weekly quizzes (as this class was hybrid) but one quiz was dropped and quizzes were not super difficult. While there is going to be effort required for this class, the final was very doable and exactly like the exams.

Took him for MGT 4026, and it's the same style, but with a little more difficult concepts. Only note is that I wouldn't recommend taking 4026 and 4028 at the same time. Better to have the foundation in 4026 first.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Blunck is the only option for MGT 4026, but he's amazing at it. Lectures are informative, and he prepares you very well for exams and quizzes (make sure you review lecture notes before quizzes).

Awesome professor!!! He did a great job explaining concepts in the canvas videos, and his outlined notes were very organized and thorough so you didn't have to add much. He gave quizzes every week but was very clear on what they'd be over. Overall, as long as you take some additional notes and review the materials, you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: rly great professor. super nice & responds to emails in a timely manner. class was hybrid so there was mandatory attendance on the 1 day we met (along w in-person quiz). most of the class was taught on canvas via recorded lectures. gave an outline 4 every quiz/test & MC was hardest part. lots of partial credit for short answer Qs. would take again!

Great guy overall. Super nice and caring about his students. His lectures are great and very helpful. Only gives relevant work to do at home. Weekly quizzes are reasonable and easy if studied for. Exams are also very reasonable. The hardest part is the multiple-choice questions. Overall great experience!

Professor Blunck teaches most of the ACCT courses and is great at it. He is also one of the best introductions to college-level courses. Lectures can be boring, but he IS talking about accounting, quizzes and exams are challenging but he tells you what each question is going to test. Probably in my top 5 professors I've had, #1 is ofc Dr. Turner
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved him! He gave us handouts for each unit which were very nice. He would also tell us exactly what kind of questions we would be tested on. He was a great teacher although this class was very hard. You really need to work to get an A.

I really like this professor. I will be taking him again. 

In the lectures, he prints the outline therefore, you only have to take notes on the example problems. It is really great because you can actually pay attention in class. He does a very good job explaining things.

You have 6 quizzes but he drops 1. I didn't really use the textbook.

Probably the most inconsiderate professor I have ever taken a course from. Lectures are heavy with materials and always says he will give extra credit/assignments to boost grades,etc. but never does. I definitely would not take him ever and would steer clear from him if I were you.

His classes are an anomaly, it's harder than you'd like but easier than you'd expect just based on the content and his lectures. Professor Blunck is a pretty cool guy who is very flexible and generous with his grading and bonus points, if you put in a certain level of effort, you will do fine in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blunck is pretty cool and a chill guy, assignments are pretty straight forward, but you might get tripped on what his hints for quizzes/exams actually mean but all of the answers are in your notes or should be an extension of your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tells you what each question on quizzes/exams is going to ask for but the hints are very broad so it doesn't help since you were going to study the entire chapter(s) anyway. The hints are so broad that it can derail your studying, the exams are hard and the hints he gives does not matter, you need more outside knowledge, intuition and guesswork
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blunck was so good at teaching it felt like he practically raised me.

Best accounting professor at Georgia Tech! Take him if you can. He explains concepts very well and gives clear examples. His quizzes and tests can be challenging but are very doable if you go to lecture and do the practice problems. He is always available and can be lenient in regards to grading if you present a strong case. He's also really funny
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grade consisted of attendance, tests, and quizzes. Grading was very clear and lenient if you had a strong case. Provided notes and expanded on them during class with examples. Walked through every concept. Told you what was on each quiz/exam and which question. Definitely take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives you notes hand outs every class. Tests are based on notes, all you need are flashcards. He gives you the topic of each test question the lecture before the test. Literally easiest A, but it is attendance based (and that's how you get the notes/test questions) so show up-- and then promptly zone out. Also super sweet & sometimes funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Blazeck is tough, but a great lecturer and clearly a nice guy. No curve or crib sheet is absolutely brutal, but his exams are fair. His homework is very long.

I had him for chbe 2140 thermodynamics. He's a very nice and knowledgeable guy. I'm not sure how he put my name to my face seeing as I've never introduced myself but that shows how much he cares about his students. Definitely a difficult class with absolutely no curves. Homework is harder than the tests and graded harshly for accuracy.

No curve, longer homeworks than the other sections, reference sheet only on tests (other professors have open textbook or crib sheets), and no notes posted so attendance is "mandatory." However, he cares about his students and he has so many resources available. He prepares everyone really well for his class; I struggled but I'm glad I took him.

Blazeck was a great 2100 professor, his lectures were great and it was clear that he knew the subject well. He doesn't curve tests, but they're very do-able and lots of partial credit. He also doesn't upload his notes from lecture, so you won't pass if you don't go to class. The homework is time consuming, but you're given plenty of time to do it.

Fantastic professor. Had two TAs from his lab- one did HW, other did problem solving sessions each week (only 2100 prof with TAs to my knowledge). Made a horrendous weed out actually a class I enjoyed. Professor very caring and accessible outside of class. No curve so not much room for error but provides SO MANY resources to prepare well for exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Blazeck was a great guy. He was very relaxed and created a collaborative environment in his classroom. Just be prepared for fast-paced lectures. The tests make up the majority of the grade and they are pretty difficult. There is not much room for error either, as there is no extra credit or curves. Overall, he prepared me very well for CHBE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Blazeck is a great professor. If you ever have a chance, I would recommend taking 2100 with him. He explains things very well in class, is accessible outside of class, and gets to know his students. The class itself can be challenging, but it's definitely manageable. Do ALL the HW, don't skip class, use any resources you need, and you're golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is really hard, and his tests didn't make it better.
2100 is a pain for everyone but this guys makes it manageable. Do the homeworks and go to office hours and you'll be fine

Great choice for 2100. If he sees that you care hell go through great efforts to make sure your okay at the end. Lectures are clear and if you need more understanding his office hrs are super helpful.

Dr. Blazeck was great! I was terrified to take this class, but it wasn't bad at all with his thorough, example-based lectures. He is very receptive to feedback and overall a super caring person. Even though the class was difficult, I would 100% take it again with Blazeck!

Had a great time learning in his class. Prof. is very caring for students. Thorough lectures. Would take again without hesitation. 2100 was difficult and hard work as expected, but I feel I got a good foundation from the class.

An overall good teacher. Covers everything in class and does examples in lecture. Seeing the process worked out over and over in lecture helps to ingrain the problem solving strategy. Really nice and easy to respect.

Actually ended up really liking chbe 2100 with Blazeck. Pretty sure it was his first time teaching, but lectures were well organized and straight forward. He made it pretty clear what you need to do to succeed. Grades pretty easy relative to other teachers for 2100 and tests weren't too crazy. Would definitely recommend. Very understanding as well.
Blumenthal's lectures are good, but I couldn't enjoy them because the course was super easy. A good load of homework, but not too bad.

Blumenthal is a chill professor, his lectures may be tangential at times, but teaches everything you need to know for the tests. HW's are varying in difficulty, however, they shouldn't take too much time. Overall decent professor, especially for math. Beware that midterm and final is worth 35% and 45% respectively.
Great professor! His lectures are great and easy to follow, the homework and tests help you learn a lot. Would definitely take him again :)))

He doesnt teach from the textbook, but he moves along it. His lectures are basically his thoughts/what's on his mind. That makes it sound unprofessional, but he's actually really good at explaining things, and even better at answering questions. Very approachable, and very helpful.

I took this course in Fall 2022. Blumenthal is very knowledgeable about 1554 topics; however, he sometimes forgets that his students are not. He rushes through the course content, which made it very hard to keep up - but 1554 is simply a hard class. He is caring for his students, but could be a better communicator. Take Barone!
Lectures were clear and on-topic, and Professor Blumenthal is funny enough to keep class interesting. I had substitutes for him while he was away for a week, and I think he's the best 1554 teacher.
Best professor you could get for 1554!! Prof Blumenthal's lectures are clear and easy to understand. Best math professor I've had so far.

Great Prof! Always very well prepared for lecture and very dedicated. Even when he was seriously sick, he provided zoom classes instead of just cancelling lecture altogether.  While these virtual lectures were not as good as his in-person, they were still well structured and superior to the in-person lectures of other linear algebra professors.

Prof. Blumenthal is clearly passionate about Linear Algebra and wants his students to succeed. However, he'd often get off course during lecture which led to incomplete lectures and playing catch-up for days on end. He records lectures (when he remembers) which is helpful for review. Overall, decent (and certainly one of the better) linear profs.

Where do I even start with ol' Blue. Blumenthal is one of the better lecturers and while he may move fast, he covers everything necessary to ace the tests. Just hope he doesn't eat Twisted Taco before class and you will be alright.

Great professor and a very knowledgeable person. Professor Blumenthal makes Linear Algebra as interesting as it can be and personalizes his lectures to be intriguing. Only problem is he sometimes moves quickly or spends too long on a smaller topic in the class.
Linear is hard but Alex makes it an easy A

Just an amazing lecturer and person overall, content, homeworks, and tests were not that bad, so there is nothing bad to say. Even though he was clearly affected by Covid, he still tried to do his best for his students. Hope I will take another class with him in the future.
Absolutely amazing lectures, and really showed he was dedicated to his students. He caught COVID and despite being extremely sick and probably miserable, he held an online review for us on exam day.

Linear Algebra is about as fun as it sounds but somehow he manages to make it tolerable. He definitely tries to breathe life into the otherwise static numbers, vectors and planes. It is clear that he is passionate about math. He'll crack a few jokes here and there and is very responsive and understanding. I actually began to like math.

Professor Blumenthal is a gifted lecturer and is passionate about his teaching. Analysis isn't often a course one would think of as 'fun', yet he made it extremely fun and thrilling. The feedback provided was useful, and his office hours were 10/10. If you take his course, definitely make an effort to attend office hours. He is the GOAT of GT math.

I loved Professor Blumenthal. I will recommend him until the day I graduate! He REALLY wants you to succeed and learn the material. He completely understood when I couldn't attend class when I had a cold and gave me extensions. Amazing professor and person!

Professor Blumenthal goes fast and covers a lot of content, but he is extremely willing to help if you just ask. He tries to work with your schedule as much as he can and clearly cares about his students' success. Make sure to come with questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor's Blumenthal's proofs class was great, he clearly explained the foundations of mathematical proofs in a way that made it easy to understand. His tests were straightforward and came from the weekly homework assignments. His enthusiasm for the subject made it easy to enjoy the course. This class made me want to major in math!

Prof. Blumenthal is a great teacher, and he interacts with students a lot in class which I really enjoyed and helped me stay focused. However, there's a lot of content and his class might be too fast for students to keep up, so you would either want to read before or ask questions in class(he encourages question asking though). A lot of hw(6h/week)
The first few weeks of homework were kinda like getting forged by hellfire, but it was worth it and you learn a lot of things from a stellar professor. I would highly recommend this teacher!
Wonderful professor. His lectures are clear and entertaining and his grading is rather lenient. One of my best experiences at GT. Take him if possible!

I love watching Professor Blumenthal's recorded lectures with a sparkling energy drink in one hand and a foot long chicken melt sub in the other. With raisin cookies and chips in the middle. He explains everything in lecture, has mad jokes, and tries to accommodate us as much as possible. What more could you want in a professor!!!
I really love his structured lectures and humor.

Professor Blumenthal did an okay job of explaining concepts in class. While he is clearly well versed in the subject, he often goes at a pace that is too fast for most students to comprehend, and does not do a good job at helping struggling students keep up. As a person, he's great; as a teacher, he's just alright.

Professor Blumenthal is great! He always logs into lecture prepared with a OneNote full of notes and pre-prepared problems, so time is never waste. In addition, he knows to avoid tangents and gets everything done in class that he needs to. Despite this, he is still quick to answer any questions thoroughly. The class is tough, but he makes it great!

Dr. Blekherman is great. He is funny, insanely intelligent, and a great lecturer. His domain of knowledge stretches far beyond the course I took with him, and it shows. He is always able to answer questions I had and is highly available online and during his office hours. Great class, great professor. Would totally recommend.

His class was the hardest in my degree, but I always felt confident because I knew he was always there for us. Lectures were very good, and homework did a very good job preparing for the exams. He was also very helpful in office hours. He did have both a final project and exam, which always annoys me, but other than that, I highly recommend.

Disclaimer: I took this class dual enrollment 
I see so many people saying he was a very tough professor and that the practices were nothing like the exam. Practice exams don't have to look like the exam: they are designed to test you over the content on the exam, which they did. He was also generous with partial credit. The class had good rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class dual enrollment, and it was clear that this was his first time with the online courses. Initially the difficulty was poorly managed and there was a general lack of materials and communication, but he acclimated rather well and the difficulty became reasonable by the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took gt math year 2 with him. Very vague hw key descriptions and the TAs suck as grading. Exams have weird questions in them and are only 5 questions. Practice tests are not like real tests.

Struggles to clearly explain the material. His graders have been abysmal. They mark you wrong on every homework problem, and then when you go and ask them for explanation, they spout out some vague explanation that isn't even mathemtically correct, then ignore your requests for a regrade. Painful class to take. Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor but test difficulty was harder than quizzes and practice given in studios. I really enjoyed his teaching style, but I felt that the questions asked on the exams were not a good representation of our knowledge on the subject.

Very passionate but lectures are hard to follow. Homework is easy, quizzes are okay, but midterm difficulty is all over the place. Not bad overall, but expect to teach yourself most of the time to get an A.

Not a bad teacher, very passionate about the subject, but I did not love his teaching style. He cares about students, but I did not love the grading scheme or difficulty of scale between tests and homework. Watch Sebastian Fernandez for diff eq.

A very nice professor who cares about his students. My only qualm is that sometimes his notes are hard to follow, so you'll also need to watch the lectures in order to get the full picture (this is irrelevant for non-covid semesters). Other than that I have no complaints.

Dr. Blekherman is a great guy, and he clearly cares a lot about his students. He is very patient, his lectures are fun (he tells daily jokes), and he encourages participation but doesn't mandate it. There were weekly homeworks, which was sometimes a bit much for me, but overall they were not too hard as long as you pay attention in lectures.

Dr Blekherman is such a nice guy. He gives clear expectations of his students and gives good feedback when asked. In this class, which is an upper level math class, he gave us asynchronous attendance, which means watching a lecture and doing the quiz which he gives questions for in class. Told daily jokes which is so fun.

I don't think Dr. Blekherman was a good fit as a professor for me. Personally, his teaching style was not the most effective for my learning; it was a bit fast-paced. I also recommend not skipping class or you may fall behind.

Professor Blekherman has clear enthusiasm for the subject and he tries to make the class more fun for everyone. Lectures can go a bit fast and he does not do very many examples for each topic. However, he is easily accessible in office hours or another time.

At first I definitely thought his lectures were a bit fast-paced, but after a week or two, I got the hang of it and from then on it wasn't that bad! He would sometimes start off lecture with cheesy math jokes which was fun. He was always open to questions, and I enjoyed his class. I never read the the textbook, but it never hurts to read it.

Dr Blekherman was not a good choice for me. I found his explanations too fast-paced and his annotations in the board messy. I was always trying to write down what he talked about 5min before, and that made it hard to follow the lectures. The textbook helped a lot. Nonetheless, his lectures are entertaining and he's accessible for questions.

Blekherman is truly a funny guy. I appreciated how he injected humor into math, which is rare in my experience. The class itself is hard but Blekherman's lectures are fairly engaging. As far as 1553 goes, he is a fairly standard grader and the work is mostly the same across all professors.

I found that he was a decent lecturer, and I loved the textbook for this course! Probably one of the best textbooks I've ever had for a class, so if you have him for 1553 be sure to read the textbook in addition to going to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Explained the concepts well, was always open to questions, and prepared us well for tests. Go to lectures, read the textbook, and take the practice tests, and you should be fine in his class. Also, his tests were usually easier than the other professors. I actually enjoyed this class a lot, and it wasn't too hard. Take Blekherman!!

Lectures are very clear and he covers exactly what will be on the exams. If you do the homeworks, know the content in the textbook, and do the worksheets you will do well on the exams. He often has time in class to answer questions before tests. He also has regular office hours and additional ones around when there are tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take it with Blekherman or Janokowski they're the best 2 for linear. He's a pretty good teacher and our tests were a lot easier than the other classes. He seems like a really nice guy and offers lots of office hours but I never went.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great professor, I thought his lectures were clear and helpful and he was engaging and funny. If you know how to do all the problems on the review sheet, the tests are more than fair and straightforward. Also very helpful during office hours, held a lot of them and answers any questions.

Dr. Blekherman was okay. Didn't explain all the concepts required for exams, True/False questions torture you on HW's and exams, and voice can be boring after a while. Typically if the class average is lower than the course average, a heft curve is applied, so expect the possibility of a bump with him.

One of the best math professors I have taken. If you like proofs/theory, take his advanced classes. He is fair, but still presents challenging material and expects you to know it. His lectures are really great, and he is very helpful when responding to questions.

Really funny and cool guy and very thorough in lectures. His reviews are almost the same as his tests. The biggest downfall is that he does not give you answers to his reviews, so I recommend starting early and trying to get help in office hours if you don't understand ANYTHING in the slightest and form a study group to help check your answers!

Overall, an amazing professor. The reviews that he provides before the exams are very similar to the test questions. If you do those by yourself and understand the method behind your work you will get an A hands down. He is very professional and seems like a nice dude. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

Dr. Blekherman is great - his lectures are more clear and understandable than most at Tech. Office hours are important, and he will explain concepts even more clearly. Tests can be rough, but if you study using materials he gives, you can do well.  He also added 12% onto one of my midterm grades because it was graded too harshly.  Would recommend!

He's a huge goofball. Tests were pretty tough but he provides a lot of exam prep material and only tests on material he's covered. Office hours are helpful and he's generous with your grade as long as you're showing effort. Don't skip class, and go to recitation/office hours for extra help. Overall really solid
Engaging, funny lecturer who explains the material well. The tests were hard but fair.

Tests were not too hard, basically covering what we learned in class.  However, the final exam was all new material, nothing we had covered.  Had A's on all tests and got a 63 on the final  (class average was about 50) to end with a B.  No curve.
His voice is that of Gru from Despicable Me. He is clear.

Class is useful, learned everything there. Quizzes every week but those are basic and easy for the most part. Tests are fair, mainly solving and little theory. Homework is online but you get unlimited tries so easy 100 for that.

Seriously one of the best math profs at Tech. Lecture is useful; he does a really good job of explaining. His tests are hard though, the first test had a class avg of like a 55 so watch out. If you pay attention and study, you can definitely get an A. He replaces one test with the grade you get on the final.

Great professor.  Quizzes and homework every week, but not too time consuming.  What is explained in proofs in lecture is covered better in recitation if needed.  Gives practice problems for tests that prepare you well.  Tests are difficult but very fair!  Highly recommended!

Hilarious, very fair tests but still require you to know the material.  Office hours and practice problems were very helpful.  Ended up with a high A after a 63 and 76 on the first 2 tests because of grade replacement.  Definitely an awesome professor

This was not a bad class. He does a lot of proofs in lectures, but he never puts them on the tests. He gives you practice problems and if you do those the tests are not bad at all. Easy to make an A or B if you do the work. I would recommend him to anyone taking MATH 1502.
Class was not bad.

Great professor. He's fairly approachable, and is willing to explain concepts over and over until you understand them, whether it be during lecture or office hours. He often makes amusing jokes during lecture. Tests and quizzes are fair. He gives out practice problems before tests, and if you master them, getting an A is achievable.
Great teacher! Very clear and helpful in class!

He was really funny and clear in his lectures, his accent isn't terrible. Tests are fair! Quizzes are fairly easy, some are difficult. Homework is optional, but very necessary. He is one of the better Calc 2 professors to have. And this is coming from someone who was failing in the beginning and finished with an A, so that shows how great he is!

Pretty good teacher, but still a difficult class. He was really good about helping you if you talked to him, as well as answering questions during lecture. However, his tests/quizzes were much harder than most classes.
Best professor I've had so far. Very clear, great instructor. Tests are very fair and the class isn't so impossible to not get a good grade in. He's awesome both inside and outside of class!
Very helpful

Really helpful and funny professor. Apparently makes the fever joke across all classes haha. He would often modify his schedule at the request of students, reexplain anything, and always set reasonable expectations. Highly recommended.

He is very good. He explains the material really well, and he does so with a sense of humor. His explanations are fantastic, and he is always willing to help you. His tests are challenging, but not impossible, and there is an easy quiz every week. If you have the choice, I would definitely take his class again.

Awesome professor.  Easy to understand and he explains the material very well.  He has a pretty good sense of humor, too.  His tests are pretty tough and there is a quiz every week but they help prepare you pretty well.  As long as you do your homework and prepare for tests, there's no reason why anybody can't pull out a B at the least.

Provides pretty clear explanations, and has reasonable expectations on tests. Easy to understand and cares about doing a good job in teaching us. He's supportive and offers study guides, and quizzes each week are a great way to keep us on top of things. Also, good sense of humor... I've got a fever, and the only prescription is more Taylor Series!
Really funny, keeps class interesting, cares about students performance by providing study guides and office hours that are helpful
Awesome explanations, very funny. Great teacher.
Average at best.
He is funny.

Jacob Blevins is the GOAT. Excellent lecturer. Material isn't boring at all and he takes time on the details of the notes. Solves problems himself in class rather than just rewriting steps from notes. Homework prepare you well for the exams. Jacob Blevins is a professor that actually cares about the quality of his communication skills.
In a one on one decision between teachers, always bet on Blevins.

Dr. Jacob Blevins is not just a professor—he is an intellectual deity sent from the celestial realms to bless us mere mortals with wisdom. Grading? Fair and just like the scales of truth. Feedback? So insightful it feels like prophecy. Passion for the subject? Enough to make scholars weep. His class isn't just education—it's ascension. ⭐11/5⭐

What more can be said about the great Jacob Blevins that hasn't already been said. Much like Mithrandir in the Lord of the Rings, he is an unstoppable force for good, proliferating light and warmth to Tech Tower and beyond, a proverbial angel among men. His name can be heard spoken in the streets of Home Park, whispering of his greatness.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Blevins is hands down the best instructor for 2110. I took the 6:30 pm to 9:15 pm section but it was worth taking considering how much this man respected our hard work in the class. 2110 is hell, but he will make it WAYYY easier than the other instructors for 2110.
good professor

Jacob Barthelemew Blevins III is a wonderful man. I see him constantly sitting behind his desk located right outside the Hive (I think thats what they call it) I stop by his desk almost daily so he can put a smile on my face and put me in my place! Jacob is a kind and caring individual who deeply cares about telling you how much he loves his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blevins has a reputation for being one of the most difficult professors on campus. He really makes you work for the grade and does NOT HAND OUT As. Every point that you get is earned and NOT GIVEN. His story of growing up alone on the streets and working his way to the top of the engineering department is inspirational to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: How else can I say this.... Jacob Creed Blevins is a man of quality. An engaging lecturer with excellent knowledge of the content. 5/5 on the hot factor too which never hurts ;)
Great guy
lectures are incredibly boring but she's very very nice. If you ask her for help on a quiz she'll lowk just give you the answer and sometimes she brings in snacks and candy for the class.

She is so sweet and does her best to make people participate and learn. The phonetics unit is rough but it's an interesting class once you get past that. Tests and homework are open note but long and pretty difficult, though she gives great explanations for why you lost points. If you want an easy, mostly interesting humanities I highly recommend.

Everything is open note but exams are BRUTAL. They take hours to complete, especially the last exam, which has essay, analysis, mcq, T/F, etc basically every type of question in existence. Wish she made shorter exams or did different assignments to test all of this, instead of these long time-consuming exams. Material is kinda difficult & annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy humanities credit. My only issue was that she didn't enter grade till late in the semester.
Dr. Kim was such a nice teacher and her class was easy with a little effort. She always responds to emails and cares a lot about her students. Put in the work and it's an easy A.

Dr. Bo Kyoung Kim was an amazing professor for linguistics. Her interest in the subject made classes more interesting and engaging. Assignments were fair; all exams were online; in-class quizzes were quick and given enough notice for preparation.

Pretty interesting class and she is a lenient grader. There's translation and speaking homework every other week or so, which can be time consuming but she is flexible when turning assignments in. She gives a lot of feedback and marks what points were taken off or given back. She does tend to grade everything at the end of the semester.

This course was possibly the easiest course I have ever taken at GT. The grade is entirely based on a few exams that take a LONG time. They are extremely easy, since you are allowed to use notes. Material was not very interesting to me, but it was to others.

Dr. Kim is a great professor! Although this class was online, she did a great job at explaining the concepts through videos and was always available to be messaged if you had any questions. She is a very fair grader and an extremely nice person. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit, and great CIOS. I highly recommend taking Dr. Kim.

Dr. Kim is, by far, the best professor I've had. She was extremely caring and answered emails quickly. I asked some dumb questions, but Dr. Kim always responded nicely and with patience. There were multiple extra credit opportunities and exams weren't difficult. She made me interested in what I thought would be a boring course. 10/10 recommend!!!
The professor is really nice

Good professor but her lecture videos had bad audio, but her lecture slides are good enough to read. Quizzes are kind of difficult, tests are online (no honorlock) and time consuming but fair. Overall good class, but the beginning content can be difficult if you dont try. Put like 30% effort into the class and you'll be aces.
Clear and straightforward video lectures. She was very thorough about the grammar and topics, and she gave really great feedback on my homeworks and essays. Highly recommend her.
No complaints about this professor.

Dr. Kim's lectures are great and engaging. She always starts off the class asking how everybody is doing and genuinely cares for students. The assignments were a bit challenging but were fair. Definitely take a humanities course with Dr. Kim.
A little frustrating how lax he can be about things, especially since he's pretty behind in lectures, but the assignments and tests are all pretty fair, which is what matters to me

Dr. Botchwey is a funny guy, but he is often absent for the courses that he teaches. It seems like he's got a lot of other commitments so no shade or anything, and in 2110, it didn't end up mattering all that much but do be aware of that.
Nice guy but sometimes was a little unsure about the course content. Super responsive on microsoft teams though which is helpful.

I don't think he prepared for any of the lectures, but he was funny. He might often be not really helpful, but I would always have a good laugh (maybe my laugh point is low). There's a structure for each type of problems, you just need to practice and get used to solving them, so the prof and the book weren't that important.

He is an underrated professor. He cares about the students, but the flipped organization of this course makes people have a negative/difficult view of this course/professor. You just need to ask your questions in a straightforward manner for him.  You can get away with not reading the textbook by focusing on hw/studios.

He's not the worst professor but he's also not that great of a professor. Just be prepared to read the ENTIRE textbook if you want to do well in his class. Also, the grading criteria in this class were sooo all over the place and most of the teaching was done by the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He makes lectures interesting and is clearly very knowledgeable about biomaterials. Tests are moderately difficult, but he provides good study materials.

Dr. Botchwey is an approachable man, he cares about his students, and you can tell he is invested in the material he teaches. Unfortunately, his presence in the classroom is spotty, his instructional style is unclear and disorganized, and far too much pressure is placed on students to look to other sources for guidance or teach themselves.
He's a great teacher and really cares about his students. His passion for the course is contagious. It makes me excited to become a biomedical engineer.

if youre going to take BMED 2110 ESPECIALLY with Botchwey, you are expected to already have a foundation of knowledge before this class even started. youre suppose to already know a handful of knowledge before this class even started. id recommend anyone taking or going to take this course to start looking at old practice tests and quizzes.

Didnt know his own syllabus even though he changed it two weeks before the end of the semester. Added a whole new set of assignments worth 30% two weeks before the end of the semester and took away 50 minutes of the final on the day of even though GT policy requires to notify changes to the final at least before the drop date.

This man obviously puts in the bare minimum to teach. Started flipped class, but ran out of premade material so switched to lecture style. Lectures were rambly and I could not understand any of the points this man made. TA's made the quizzes and graded them so its obvious he just didn't respect our own time. First time I've read an entire textbook

Only way to survive the class is to read the textbook. Lectures ramble and don't really relate to what's on the quizzes. He doesn't respond to e-mails or messages consistently. It felt like the TA did all the work and he just lectured. Disrespected our time by doing lectures from his car, changing standards on a whim, and not communicating. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class format changed every 3 weeks for lecture delivery. The only solution to figuring out what was going on was to read the textbook but then each quiz for the class pulled material from other chapters and much of the material was never brought up again. He is very reasonable and willing to make changes when given feedback but oof. Rough time

Who thought a professor can be this horrible? I've cried at least 5 times a week due to him randomly and suddenly adding requirements and assignments without any planning. If you want to hate yourself, I would take his class.

Absolutely the worst professor/teacher I've had since I was born. If you want to learn what to absolutely not to do as a teacher, you should take his class. In the middle of the semester, he changed the requirement of the class, causing 3-30 min assignments more than 20% of the class. Before, I was skeptical on how bad a prof can be, but now I know

Wildly disorganized in lectures, notes and the use of his syllabus. His lectures are pulled straight from the textbook and one would save more time and energy reading the book; however, attendance is 30% of the final grade. Comical excuse for a Biomedical Engineering class - avoid Dr. Botchwey. Extremely easy class, but waste of energy.

He is a decent professor. BMED 2210 is just not a class you learn from the lecture so I didn't expect him to teach at all. But he is very approachable and nice when you ask him a question. You just have to accept the fact that you have to learn most of the stuff from your TA.

Ridiculously unorganized. We found out about assignments 2 days before they were due. TAs did most of the teaching but rarely correlate with what Botchwey was going over. He has horrible handwriting and doesn't know how to use his own technology. Poor grading system with little structure. Most test were curved because the average was below a 50.

Dr. Botchwey is terribly disorganized and you will learn very little without complete dependence on good TA/self effort. His general format for class consists of telling students to open a practice quiz and work on it in groups, later going through the problem in a disorganized if not incorrect fashion. He is regularly not present either

This class was very disorganized, and there was a general lack of communication. Dates of HW, quizzes, and tests were almost always changed. Also, these usually had to be done on paper and then uploaded to T-Square, which was confusing. However, Dr. Botchwey was frequently willing to listen and make changes. Most questions came from the book.

He was very disorganized. He has horrible hand writing and uses an iPad to hand write his notes.. a horrible combination. He is very uncleAR about his expectations for assignments and very rarely gives out an assignment sheet. Every due date usually changes.  He also is not very clear about material for tests.

Promised me a position in his lab but dropped me at the last minute after I made plans to stay on campus (900 miles from where I live).  Paid out the ass for on campus living for nothing that contributes to my resume.  His classes were disorganized and hectic.  The grades were almost random.  DO NOT TAKE HIM.  You will learn nothing

All I can assume is that he must be a stellar research professor, because he is not qualified to lead a class. His notes were ridiculously unorganized, his quizzes had little to do with the material, and he miscalculated my final grade and took an entire semester to fix the error. His TAs were equally unhelpful. Avoid.

Dr. Botchwey was very disorganized and didn't ever seem fully prepared. However, despite this, he worked well with students to make sure he wasn't taking advantage of them. He was very open for help and had generous grading in place to help those who may have felt cheated. Dr. Botchwey has great potential, but he has many problems now.
Clearly presents information and is a very good lecturer

I don't know why everyone is hating on this professor. His class is actually so funny. He is a little goofy and loves to talk about all things GT but his class is SO easy. Literally all you need to know is read the articles for the week and only write two reports the entire semester. This class is so easy and he's so funny.
Loves all things GT so loves the athletes, but all in all a good prof who cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly surprised at how someone could talk so much but convey so little actual information. I learn less from the lectures than I do if I just read the slides myself. Sounds like a kid trying to give a presentation on a topic they just learned about 10 minutes ago.
Boring professor and very arrogant, talks a lot about himself. Likes to show a lot of attention to the female students. I would not take a class from him again.

I have had Professor Myers online during a COVID semester and in-person, and his in person lectures are awesome. Very interested in the subject and cares about his students. This course is basically reading and discussing cases and articles, in addition to leading a case discussion as a group and a final presentation. Overall, a good class.

He assigns a case study every night for homeworka rather lengthy one at that. Then goes over it in class at a high level but then expects you to know such specific details on the test. Tests are essentially all he grades on which makes it a very difficult class because the tests are completely unfair and cover material that was never mentioned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Laziest professor I have ever had. Does nothing to help students learn. He posts a blank notes outline in which he covers maybe 60% of the notes through the semester. He gives very poor directions for assignments and then takes points off of things for the most meticulous reasons ans doesnt elaborate why. Dont take this professors class!

Hands down worst professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech, the professor goes on and on about random topics in class. In addition he has side conversations with individual students so it seems like he ignores half the class and it makes it super awkward. Definitely take another professors supply chain/IT elective if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind of a waste of time and money. He doesnt really teach anything practical in this MGT3510 class. He essentially just goes over a lot of case studies as you have one every night for homework. The also gives you a blank notes packet to fill out in which he hardly covers any of the notes. Then on test days he asks super specific case questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Has to be the worst professor I had at Georgia Tech. He isnt a very nice person and has very little understanding of what goes on in students lives. His lectures are ultra boring as he goes on the incoherent ramblings that are just weird and awkward for the whole class. He assigns a case study every night for homework and his tests are so unfair!

Bob is a fantastic professor and does it because he loves it. He specifically designed the Process Innovation course himself, and it is essential if you are an Ops concentration. He is straightforward and gives you plenty of heads up for pop quizzes, and the group work/simulations are fun (you even use concepts you learned in class to solve them)

He's the actual goat. Recorded lectures, relevant homework, cool projects. Explains everything really well, very responsive, and tons of extra credit. Grade distribution is forgiving, if you learn the homework well you'll be fine on exams. Take home midterm, needed a 30% on the final. You will truly learn dynamics and not stress about the grade.

Great guy with good lectures. Multiple attempts on homework. Two big group projects. Open note take-home midterm, in-person final with cheat sheets. Both had multiple attempts for partial credit. Lots of extra credit available. Overall great class, fun projects, would recommend.

a great lecturer, learned a lot in class and its very clear he cares abt the students. projects and exams all have extra credit portions, everything is graded reasonably. hw is a bit difficult but he is very helpful during office hours and it is reasonable to what we are learning in class. great guy would definitely take him again.

one of fav profs at gt, great guy, hard class but explained clearly. very fair prof. 30% 10 hw 1drop, 1exam 15%, 3project 10% each but 1st is free, 2&3 use matlab. 25% final not cumulative. bonus on tests. has zoom link for class and records. only criticism: he talks quiet. you will actually learn dynanmics here unlike patil where its a free A lol
Dr. Deng is a great lecturer and seems to care about his students. Homeworks and exams were difficult, but feel like I learned a lot as a whole through this course. Recommend taking.

The class involved weekly homework assignments worth 40% of your grade, but he takes the best 8 out of 10. There are two midterms that are take home 24 hour exams. These are worth 15% each. The final exam is 30% and takes 2.5 hours in class. The textbook "Mechanics of Materials 9th" is not required but is very useful in the class.

He's awesome, made me want to do an econ minor. I think anybody who engages with the class and asks questions should be able to get an A. While he might come off as argumentative at times, he's really trying to get the students to think about the concepts at a deeper level so that they become more comfortable with application.

He is an amazing lecturer who is also very understanding and clearly just wants you to feel good about the topic. His exams are definitely more challenging than other ECON 2106 exams because he tests on applications not just concepts, but I think you get a far better learning experience.

Easy course. Grading relies on exams heavily but they're easy as long as you do the practice exams and homeworks on time. Generous EC opportunities. Required $70ish online textbook and homework system. Great lectures and slideshows, though exams are easy enough that it won't matter even if you skip a couple of lectures.
Fairly easy course and solid lecturer. Practice tests were similar to actual tests and many questions on tests were taken from achieve.
Such a good lecturer but his tests are hard.

Chill guy, has good examples in lectures and asks class for input. Lectures can sometimes get boring but he makes the content easy to learn homework almost every week but its not hard and helped me learn the majority of the content, plenty of extra credit. Solid professor who cares about economics, practice tests are super similar to actual tests

I thought I could get away with skipping the lectures bit it was almost 9% of my grade - I would've gotten an A otherwise. The class is not hard, the homework assignments can be tedious but there is extra credit. The tests are just like the practice ones he gives and he reuses the same format and types of questions.

Prof. Harris is nice but can be argumentative, and his lectures are often boring/hard to focus on. It's a solid class but covers a lot of material. Very exam-heavy (Midterms+Final = 64% of grade). The material can be tricky, so strictly memorize the practice tests—they are your best resource.

Lowkey not a bad or hard class. Really easy if you pay attention in class, but still manageable to get a good grade if you don't. Exams are exactly like practice exams and don't seem to change year to year.
Great professor and great lectures but the tests are difficult
