Professor Harris is overall a good and caring professor who is very passionate about what he lectures. I personally thought midterms were testing on different material covered in the homeworks. You get what you put into the class. Overall, would recommend.

This class was okay. The lecture slides were extremely helpful, but the exams were hard. However, the homework and participation are weighted heavily, so it helps to boost your grade. Overall, I recommend taking this course.
Took for ECON4460. Great class and ever better professor. Make it engaging with his lectures. Especially with the pre readings we had to prepare for class. Would take a class with him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really liked professor Harris. His exams are tough, but the way his grading system works with attendance points and hw grades helps balance out exam grades. His lectures aren't the most interesting thing, but he explains everything well and expands on a lot of examples. Go to his office hours if you can- he does some good review before exams.

The material wasn't hard, but Harris overcomplicated it. Definitely do the extra credit and go to office hours if you're confused—he's more willing to help if you participate. He can be a bit sassy and likes to "argue" in class, which discouraged class discussion. However, he does reuse old test questions, so studying past exams is helpful.

Dr. Harris clearly outlines what you need to do to be successful in this course. If you're worried about your grade, I recommend doing the extra credit — he notices who does it. The tests can be on the trickier side, but he has very good practice tests accessible to everyone.

I really liked this class. HW was super chill and there is plenty of assignments to help grade. Tests are lowkey hard though so you need to study. I don't pay attention much in his lecture cause he goes off topic so much but I liked this class a lot. Note: he isn't a very approachable guy

Prof Harris is really passionate about economics and wants everyone to succeed. He tries to make lectures interesting but he speaks very monotone so its kind of hard to stay awake. Attendance isn't necessary but there are in class polls. All lectures are recorded and posted. There is extra credit and Prof Harris is very accessible outside of class.

Overall a good professor. He made microeconomics really digestible and although his tests were a bit difficult he prepared us pretty well I would say. Also, he comes off as understanding and relatable to us students. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Harris is extremely passionate about the subject. I found the lectures to be hard to follow at times, but he gave lots of extra practice to students for exams. Attendance policy is based off of accuracy on polls, so you might not get full attendance even if you show up to every class.

Not a bad professor at all, lectures are quite dry but he does genuinely care about the things he is teaching. The class gets more difficult later into the semester, but he is frequently available outside of class to answer questions. Attendance isn't taken directly but in-class electronic polls are used as participation grades. Curves most tests.

Poor attendance policy; you get points off for missing the questions, so it doesn't count for credit, which is unreasonable. But Harris really cares about his students. He gives resources for practice and offers plenty of help. Overall, nice guy and accessible. I find his tests to be a little more advanced than a principles course, so I struggled.

Great prof - clear course policies and test format. I personally found the course fairly easy but he curved the first exam and changed the weighting of the class to make it more fair for students who didn't do as well. Very nice person who seemed to actually care about his students.

Best professor I had all year.
His lectures cover the material so well, you don't have to read the textbook.
Participation and homework do reinforce material well.
Very interesting extra credit podcasts.
Asked him about some economic topic after class - an hour later he responded with well thought-out argument and a relating research paper.

wonderful prof. really cares about teaching and goes over lectures well. he changed weight of first exam because of poor scores. attendance is graded, but he gives many extra credit opportunities. very accessible-i email him questions about homeworks, and he responds with helpful detailed replies very fast. material/exams are fairly difficult

Professor Harris's lectures are really good. super engaging and explains everything at a understandable level. first exam we took was difficult but it's his first time teaching the class, so hes still learning how long to make exams. He changed the grade breakdown because a bad first exam. You can tell he really cares about teaching.

great professor, very caring, learned a lot from this class. Attendance is mandatory, but you only have to meet for like half the semester. The assignments are not too bad and are really useful. material does overlap some with ECE1100, but there is new material and she goes more in depth

All the materials have been covered in ECE1100. There is no reason for school to offer this course as required to earn students' tuition. The content taught in ECE1100 is more useful than this course btw.

They must've made this class even easier - there was only one take-home assignment and the rest were done during class. She is a very caring professor and the content is very relevant to anyone searching for internships/full-time jobs.

Extremely caring professor.  Class is the perfect difficulty for a 1 credit hour pass/fail required class.  Actually learned a lot and enjoyed every assignment.  It was perfect for what it was, and she is genuinely caring for your future as well.  Ensures you have access to her to get advise whenever and helps you without question.  Great teacher.

Professor Bourgeois is a genuine person who cares a lot about her students. She is insanely nice and wishes the best for everyone. That being said, the class was literally sitting simulator. Some cool topics and good information but there just really isn't much to it. Overall, eh class but really awesome professor.

A lot of people rag on this class because it's not engineering. They don't realize that her class teaches everything you NEED to know and probably don't know about interviewing, resumes, applying to jobs/grad programs, etc. Definitely take her class during your second year, first semester of CmpE to get a head start on internship applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is super chill and easy going. Class is an easy A if you just do your assignments on time, which are straightforward and simple.

After the first two weeks, she didn't post a single thing. The syllabus said we would have class in person, but she has been completely silent for two months now (except for one announcement). I asked friends if I was missing something because nothing happened. The GTA's are active, but absolutely no lecture or interaction with the professor.
Good teacher overall and pretty cute.
She is full of herself and believes her work and teaching are actually important.
Good prof
No Comments

I had literally no coding experience before going into class but found is really manageable. Lectures are recorded, so you don't have to go to class. I would recommend going to recitation and doing practice exams. Also there's like 2 points of extra credit added onto your grade at the end.

Very good lecturer! I can't emphasize enough how he is able to properly teach python in a way most can understand well. There are plenty of practice exams to get you through the tests and the homework helps a lot with them as well. The hardest part was figuring out how to do the webdev/robotics labs.

Although the course material itself was difficult, the lectures were very thorough. Attendance not mandatory, but sitting through lectures really helped a lot on the tests. TAs were all very knowledgeable and he was very approachable if you had any questions. Tests can be difficult but past exams were very similar. Very sweet!

rod is a great prof. he takes great care in his work, explains things very well, and is always open to questions and making sure you understand certain concepts. the only issue was the tests, which start off very difficult, but generally get easier as you become more CS competent.

I'm gonna preface by saying that I'm not good at CS, Rod was a decent teacher, he was quite passionate and funny and had pretty good lectures. For a GT requirement however, there was a lot of learning you had to do on your own that was not in the lectures, use the online textbook. Make sure you do the homeworks early and look at old exams.

Pretty good teacher!
I thought that the WebDev Lab was very useless and unrelated to the course content. I had to learn a lot of new, useless Python functions and syntax that aren't popular and used in other courses. 
The tests got a lot easier as the course progressed. 
The homeworks were good- make sure to do them!

Rod is awesome! His lectures are effective and interesting and really helped me to understand the material. He is also always willing to answer questions on homework, labs, etc. before or after lecture. Overall he is a great, caring person and does an amazing job of teaching this class.

very energetic and fun professor. the lectures aren't that difficult to follow and the homework is related to class content. personally, I felt like the lab was unrelated to class and forced me to learn a lot of syntax on my own (web dev track). exams seemed to get easier as the semester went on

Rod is a great lecturer; he makes the concepts super easy to understand. To get a good grade, go to lecture and do all the practice tests. Also, the TAs will be ur best friend in this class, so make sure to go to the helpdesk if you're struggling.

Enjoyable professor with fun lectures. Exams are similar level to the practice exams given by him. Labs were decent but they felt unrelated to the content of the class (was on web dev track). I did take this class already knowing Python, so difficulty level might not be accurate for a true intro class.

CS1301 isn't a real intro. Rod goes way too fast. Labs and TAs are awful. Never take robotics. They claim it's easier but it's hell, with async topics that don't belong in an intro. No lab help, TA helpdesk is slow and rude. Grading is sloppy, robots are disorganized. This class made me cry. Never again, made me reconsider my major as an EE.
I LOVE ROD SO MUCH. Great professor. Even as someone with no coding experience before the very first day of class, he made the content very digestable and simple. Definetly take him.

I really enjoyed this class! It is difficult to adjust to at first, but once you get into the swing of things it becomes more and more manageable. Make sure to utilize your resources in this class! There are so many opportunities to go to plus sessions or reach out to TAs, and it is totally worth it!

Rod is great. He's super funny, makes the lectures interesting, and codes with you instead of just talking and having you take notes the entire time. He is really easy to get help from and great at explaining how and why certain code does different things. Rod is the goat.
During lectures, he codes along with students for notes and has mini quizzes, which I found very helpful.

Rod was hands down one of the best teachers for 1301. He explained concepts really well and would explain it in different ways if someone didnt understand. The tests were really easy, just make sure to do the practice exams posted on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rod is so kind and really cares about all of his students! The nature of 1301 can make it difficult to get TA help in office hours, but Rod was always available to help out. There is a good bit of homework outside of class, but really helps you prepare for exams. He wants you to succeed, so contact him if you ever need it!

This class comes with a lot of work - but Rod made the concepts digestable and made the 8am worth it. The homework and labs were tedious, but they definetly help you learn and cushion your grade. I also never got A's on the midterms, but got one on the final - his TAs and recitations are great too.
What an amazing professor and an ICON!!!!! Great guy, makes everything very digestible and less overwhelming. Amazing TA team as well. THANK YOU ROD!

I came in with 0 CS knowledge, and I feel like I've learned a lot thanks to Rod! He explains topics very clearly and slowly so that it is easy to understand! Some of the homework and labs were hard but it was helpful going to the helpdesk. I also recommend taking all the practice exams to study for the actual exams!

For an introduction class, it was very fun. There is a weekly homework and around bi-weekly lab due, but everything's done on your own time away from lecture. The lectures are very straightforward and, if you like Python, rather easy to understand. Mr. Rod's a great professor to have regardless though and all the TAs are so nice.

Great professor. Interesting lectures. Maybe I'm just bad at coding, but for this class, you MUST lock in. Go to every lecture. Go to recitation. Office hours were so bad because they never had enough TAs for everyone. Sometimes I'd wait hours during office hours for a TA to help me.
He was a great professor! The class was difficult in the beginning as someone with no coding experience, but I ended up doing well in the class.

Rod managed to make his lectures entertaining and highly informative. I failed the first exam only because I didn't know how to study for the class. Doing all of the past practice exams and attending all the lectures will set you up for success. I was able to end with an A after learning how the class was structured. Also attend recitation!

Rod is a really nice and approachable professor. He was very good at explaining the beginner CS concepts in the course, and we coded alongside him in lecture. However the course is really fast paced and important to keep up with (at least for a newbie to python and CS). You should make sure to work on the homeworks early.

Borela is super enthusiastic and really nice. His 1301 course is probably one of the best ones to follow along because he really knows what he's doing. He gives all coding notes through actual python programs that you will type with him in class, which I feel does a good job at preparing you for the homeworks (helpful for tests).

I love this professor! He's great and super passionate about what he does. Very easy to talk to and is patient with you with questions. Also super engaged during lectures. Some homeworks are long but doable if you set the time aside. The TAs are also super helpful. It's definitely beginner-friendly if you've never taken Python before.

He is awesome!! His teaching style is learning by doing, and he gives good homework examples to do each week. Tests are timed, but he is accommodating and pushes you to do your best. Gives around 3 points of extra credit through relatively simple assignments. If you don't procrastinate on homework/projects and study, you'll excel in this class!

Amazing professor! Went into this class with absolutely no python experience and ended up with an A. Does a very good job of explaining concepts. If you participate in lecture and do the Hws then you will absolutely pass the class with an A. Definitley recommend taking 1301 with Rod!
Lecture was interesting, great professor and makes it easy to be successful in the class. Labs and homework were a big time commitment.

I've never taken a CS before, and he is the best professor ever. His lectures were so detailed and engaging, and the homework assignments were at an adequate level. He also provides a lot of exam resources to help you ace the class.

Rod is such a great lecturer! He's so caring and funny, and genuinely made me excited to learn CS! Homeworks and tests are a little challenging, but the past exams should get you prepared pretty well.

Rod is a great lecturer. I believe his tests are difficult and completing them in 50 minutes is har. The TA's are very helpful for help but I do reccomend going to lectures as they help you code for the most part. There are three labs, and the third one is difficult for both lab tracks.

100% recommend! He is so good at explaining himself and making sure everyone understands. There's plenty of exam prep material and review sessions, and the exams align really well with homework/in class examples. TA's were very helpful in office hours too. If you want you can skip lecture and just do the in-class quiz during that time.

Good course that gives you a nice basis on python, but I hear that it is more heavier in terms of content than the online sections, but I learned a lot. Lots of TAs but they get backed up especially during just before deadlines. Tests are all paper coding.

Great professor. You get to code along with him during class. My favorite part of the class were the labs (I had web development). You have the labs, homework's, mini quizzes in class, 3 exams, and a final. The exams and finals were just like the practice ones. The recitations were helpful but optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best 1301 professor. Very engaging in lecture and his HWs, while hard, often felt more like interesting puzzles to solve rather than terribly egregious assignments or anything like that. Definitely take this class with Rod over any other 1301 professor!

There is really no reason to not pass CS 1301 with a professor as great as Rod! He is awesome, down to earth, and personable at all times. This class was an amazing introduction to programming, and it had dynamic and unique homework/projects. Please just go to class and pay attention and you will do great! :)

Rod is just about the best professor I could have asked for! I have never taken a CS course before, but he made the material engaging and understandable. His lectures were thorough and he explained the "why" of what he was doing very well. He is also hilarious and incorporates pop culture into lecture! Take this course if you can, it was a blast!
WE LOVE ROD!!! Literally best professor for CS 1301! There are also so many extra credit opportunities, he genuinely wants his students to succeed.
Great professor! Very clear lectures with lots of walkthroughs and examples. He cares a lot about his students and it shows. Tests are a little challenging, but if you study you'll do fine.

Rod is literally the best CS1301 professor there is. If possible take him for this class! His lectures are so clear and he thoroughly explains all the concepts in great detail. He is fun and engaging and even dresses up in costumes for the exams. This was my first CS class I've ever taken and I was super worried but Rod made it easy and fun!

Really good professor. Gives good lectures and does a good job of test prep, theres a little EC too. Only thing is there are a lot of gotchas on tests and labs are a good bit of work. Homework typically is time consuming too. Best 1301 professor. TAs are also amazing for this course too.
Excellent lectures that were easy to follow and made sense. Homeworks made great use of what you learn. Extra lab sections were a fun application of concepts, but organized somewhat poorly.

Clearly understood what he was teaching, explained not just what to type, but what Python was actually doing in the background. Clearly passionate about both CS and being a professor, fun guy, not too hard of a course.
Nice guy that actually talks about how the code works instead of just telling you what to type in the file. also didn't show up much because he has extensive notes online

Best teacher ever. Very kind and understanding, especially in summer. If you're struggling to understand, try not to focus too much on note-taking but rather on the actual lecture (it can be difficult to try and keep up while understanding material). Midterms can be daunting, but if you practice well enough and know the exam layout you'll be fine!

I love Rod. He is very soft spoken and kind. He is a really good lecturer! He is always super helpful. You can definitely pass with an A if you do the work, study correctly, and go to tutoring. He's awesome!

Probably the best professor I have had so far. Very engaging and breaks things down into easy steps. Plenty of chances for extra credit as well. All the midterms were themed, which made them not as daunting.

Very funny and very kind. Lectures can be slow but works out when topics get tough. HW can sometimes take a few hours but aren't too bad if you ask for help early (help desk, TA's, friends). I thought this class was very easy and straightforward. Tests can have trick questions but have fun themes. Easy if you look at practices and go to review.
Amazing and clear lectures, homework takes a while but you learn A LOT! Really awesome intro to CS class overall.

While the professor is a very nice guy and is willing to help, the course is not great at all. Unless you are already familiar with python or a computer science major this class is NOT for you.This class unfortunately is more in favor of those students. Understand your learning style as well because his teaching style may not be your learning style

Prof Borela is a really good lecturer, as a cs beginner, going to class really helped. He's really caring to his students. The only thing that stressed me out is the robot labs. DO NOT register for small sessions because you don't want to work on robot labs for like days and hours. Start HW early because they're hard too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor, really cares about his students. Highly recommend.

The material gets piled on very quickly and although Borela is knowledgable, it can be hard to follow along during lectures. Homework assignments are often incredibly time-consuming if you don't have any prior experience with Python. The midterms themselves are usually way too long(9-14 pages) and you will struggle a lot to finish in time(50 min).

This is an intro class, and that's how he treated it. He would add lots of light hearted jokes and personal things into the code that made it more interesting, especially since I was taking it at 8:25 AM. He is a great lecturer and always posts his recorded lectures online. There is a participation grade, so go to class to ask questions.

Rod is an amazing lecturer for beginners in CS! He makes sure his students understand the material he's going over and takes time to reinforce material if needed. Definitely recommend for people for little to no CS experience!

Dr. Borela is really helpful and is very willing to help students outside of class. He broke CS 1301 down very well in a way it was easy to understand. Homework assignments were easy to do if you knew what was going on and tests were easy if you did a reasonable amount of studying and paid attention in class.
Good professor with understandable lectures and examples. Accessible after class at office and sometimes TA hours. Class is easy, just make sure to prioritize deadlines and pay attention in lecture.

Hw took a while and wasn't easy, but it is doable and is great practice for the tests, which were usually easier. Tests covered everything learned in lecture plus a few minor things, so make sure to go to recitation to fill the gaps.
Very kind and thoughtful towards students, notes are clear.

Rod is an awesome teacher, especially for a beginner CS class. SUPER thorough even on "easy" topics and loves to engage students to make sure the class completely understands. Homework can be pretty hard but really helps with your understanding of materials and TAS are accessible. The robot labs sucked though. Don't get a small section if you can.

Amazing, caring professor that has great lectures. Covers all content clearly, formats everything well, and has previous exams posted online that are extremely similar to exams in class. Great class bc Rod is an amazing person above all. Take him.

Rod was a very good and caring lecturer! He teaches pretty much everything you'll need for homework and tests. I did have some prior Python experience but this class wasn't bad at all and I would definitely take him again.

Rod is an amazing professor in lecture. He tries his best to answer whatever questions people have while there, and makes learning Python fun. The homework is much more difficult than the in-class examples, but going to recitation will help immensely. The first two labs aren't Python, but allows extra credit. Watch out for the tests.

Borela is good at teaching stuff in lecture, but the issue is that homework assignments--especially later in the semester--are more advanced than what he showed us in class, so you sometimes have to teach yourself python to do the homework. Also, make sure to register for the larger sections since he gives harder labs to the smaller one(s).

Pretty good professor for ML, he tries his best to make the complicated material easier. Lectures are pretty packed with content since it was summer. There's open note quizzes after each lecture (not too hard), a big group project which is kinda hard but he grades easy. Homeworks are kinda hard, but just start them early and you'll be okay!

Dr.Borela was a great professor, he would do hand tracing and hold live paper coding sessions for students who were confused. Make sure to stay on the deadlines of assignments and ask any questions you are confused about and you will do well.
Great guy but does really hard problems that are so difficult to understand because there isn't sufficient explanation.

Took Borela's CS1371 in Fall 2021. A great teacher who puts a lot of effort into making his lectures are effective and include plenty of examples. He really just seems like a chill and fun guy teaching MATLAB and I enjoyed just vibing through his class.

Prof borela was a really good professor. i took this course over the short summer semester, so it was kind of squeezed, but he did his best to make it work. in lectures, he traced problems and did live coding which really helped. the final was also really easy and you don't need a textbook or any extra stuff
Super nice, taught the material very well, would definitely reccomend.

Loved this professor. He's always trying to keep students engaged and he is incredibly nice. He explains a pretty hard subject in an easy to understand manner. Super helpful on homeworks too, just start early and ask questions if you're stuck. Hands down the best ML professor at Georgia Tech. Take ML with him if you can.

Borela is an amazing man and really cares for his students. As someone who finished the course with an 89, you need to prepare yourself to score high on tests so you can skip the final. Borela just does really hard problems with little to no explanation, youre better off to skip and watch Kantwon or Stalworth's lectures online. TOO MUCH HOMEWORK FR

1371 in general is a course that relies a lot of lectures and volume of homework so be prepared!
Borela as an instructor was extremely caring about his class. I was worried because hes a new professor but he took our criticisms very well and changed the format of the class to focus on practice problems instead of solely theory to prepare you for HW

All around great professor!  I saw other comments about lectures being too quick, but he always took time to go over explanations and ask us if he needed to slow down when explaining a concept.  Tests were a tad difficult, but if you go to lecture and do the practice tests, you'll be fine.  He puts in 110% and if you try, you'll get that back!

Boreal is a good guy, but he is terrible at judging student comprehension in CS1371. At times, the majority of students would be confused and he'd just keeping moving through the lecture, while other times he'd spend 15 minutes explaining a simple idea. He also makes a lot of mistakes. I know he can do better, hopefully in the future he does.

Professor is an amazing person. However, the lectures were rough. He would walk through example problems without much explanation and would use functions we hadn't used yet, trying to explain them as we navigate hard problems. The tests were graded with lots of partial credit, which was nice. However, the homework and prep for tests were hard.

Rod is very sweet and cares about his students, and he is willing to change his teaching methods based on constructive criticism. However, his lectures are hard to follow and have weird pacing, and he isn't great at explaining code examples. I highly recommend going to recitation over going to lecture.

Borela is a silly goofy fun-loving guy. His lectures are great and the kahoots he does keep people attentive. This is one of the few classes I wouldn't skip because lectures helped a lot for homework and it was fun to listen to him in class. Don't assume the tests will be super easy like me and not study, you need to prepare with reviewing old test

He was an amazing lecturer, especially for people with zero coding experience. He was very patient with students and well-organized. His post lecture notes were also really helpful for revision because of how detailed they were. Highly recommend him if you have never coded before and are looking for an intro CS class to take.

Oh man this guy is great! I was scared at first because he was new, but he made the classes so enjoyable and very easy to understand. Classes consisted of lectures and then Kahoot's at the end of class based on the last lecture so it was really fun and engaging. On Friday's the first place person would always get chocolate as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Borela is extremely caring and makes it clear exactly what you need to know to do well. Lectures are organized and easy to follow. Going to lecture and doing homework will teach you everything for exams.

Professor Borela is very passionate about making his students comfortable and making the material as clear as possible. For my part, completing the homeworks on my own and attending lectures was more than enough to succeed in the course.

Prof. Zhu is a great lecturer who does a really good job of breaking down difficult concepts. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures enjoyable, and he also offers Zoom options and recordings. The class is well structured with eight projects, a final project, and two online, open-note tests. I recommend taking his class.

Dr. Zhu is a goated professor. There are 8 straightforward programming assignments, 2 open-note take-home online quizzes, and the class overall is great. He's super knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff, if you can take him for graphics, 100% do it

This class has 8 super easy hws, 2 medium-difficult quizzes (depending on whether you studied hard or not), and a final project. I expected this class to be difficult or take a lot of my time, but it was honestly so chill. The instructions for the hws are very straight-forward and clear, and I never got stuck at all. Bho Zhu loves what he teaches.

Took undergrad AI graphics (4803) but it was identical to 8803. Probably one of the more interesting and fun classes I've taken at tech. Projects are very approachable and the course is designed really well, but brush up on pytorch and NNs before taking. GOAT Zhu and TAs are very helpful on Ed. Hope this class becomes a permanent media/intel option

One of the best professor I've had at Tech. Assignment for CS8803 CGAI where very well designed as they weren't to difficult but still allow you to really understand the subject well. 

There is a single quiz where you be good with by just reading the slides. Very active on ed discussion which makes him really approachable.
bo zhu the goat best cs prof at gatech

Honestly one of the best profs at GT. Very enthusiastic and very knowledgable about the content. Class has 8 very easy homeworks, 2 quizzes, and a final project. My only criticism is that the class is almost too easy imo. I wish it went more in-depth, especially since it's the main media class. Most content can be learned on learnopengl.

Dr. Zhu is the best professor I've ever had at Tech. He is an incredibly caring professor and genuinely passionate about his field of study, which motivated me to be passionate about it too. Grading is incredibly fair and the work matches what we learn in class. Overall a fun, inspiring, and uplifting class with the best professor ever.

I took this course in Spring 2024. It was by far my favorite class I ever took at GT. Bo Zhu was an AMAZING professor. He cared for his students and was very passionate about the topic. He was highly accessible outside of class and was genuinely wanted to get his students interested in the subject matter. I cannot recommend taking this class enough

Bo clearly cares so much about the topic and the students. He asks people to optionally post their graphics creations for each homework and then comments on and highlights the coolest features from each post. He is super supportive and makes the class as clear and easy to get an A as possible. Very accessible too, highly recommend taking his class.

Absolutely amazing - so wholesome. He is clearly passionate about the course and is incredibly kind to students and active on the class discussion forum. Exams are very helpful and the class is great, especially the lecture slides. All time professor

Great professor is very knowledgable about computer graphics and clearly cares a lot about the students. The way the course is structured means that it should almost be guaranteed to get an A in the class. He records lectures and has zoom on during lectures and sometimes it feels like he is almost teaching more to the zoom than the in personlecture
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very good professor, every single coding assignment was motivated from lecture, genuinely helped you learn, that being said - start them on time since hard to debug, but AI tools exist so pretty easy imo. active on Ed, generous with deadlines, quizzes incredibly easy with ChatGPT, so easy 100 really
Professor Zhu makes this class a lot easier than it should be. As long as you pay attention - you're good!

He is a great prof! He makes the content for this class so easy to understand. The final is a group project which was great. The HW makes up 64% of the grade which is great since the HW's are super easy. The midterms were all open note and he gives great quiz prep that helped with the exams. I was worried about this class but it turned out great.
Chill class with extra credits. Dr. Zhu is really nice and TA's office hour are helpful with clear hints for any problem. Easy in grading. 2 Quizzes are all very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Professor Bo Zhu's Computer Graphics course and it was an amazing experience. 3451 is usually known for being complex, Professor Zhu made it engaging and fun. He created an environment where students could truly learn without focusing too hard on their grade. He was always available via Piazza, so reaching out to him was not an issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is incredibly nice to students and gives kind feedback.

I have never written a review for a professor but Dr. Zhu really deserves it. This was my favorite class at Georgia Tech. He is clearly very passionate about graphics and is wonderful at explaining. He has been extremely accommodating and flexible when I needed help. Projects are alot of fun and you get great results! Take his class if you can.
Bo is an amazing professor! He is definitely the best CS professor I've had at GT. He really cares about his students and the content is very interesting.

Great professor for graphics. Projects are pretty easy and can be done in a couple of hours. Quizzes are open notes and are easy as long as you look through the practice test before hand. Projects are in C++ and OpenGL and all necessary formulas to finish the project can be found on the slides.

Bo Zhu is a wonderful professor. He's accommodating towards students and a great lecturer. He's passionate about computer graphics, and he's very kind and helpful. The homeworks are fair. Start early. The mesh subdivision homework is the hardest. For the tests, study the test review. I highly recommend him as a professor.

Appears very inviting of questions, but then calls them harsh names. 2/3 stopped attending after 1st lecture. >50% failed the first exam and the bell curve was a straight horizontal line. When approached, he got very close and said that "Other professors have a h€art atta¢k when they see me. I am the greatest statistician in the U.S."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: put a 2 instead of a 6 and lost 13 points.
He is just bad, just absolutely terrible. Just don't take him. Just don't do it. You have a life, and it was not meant to be spent listening to him. Just don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I was only here during the first week and then dropped it. The guy speaks with a really really strong Russian access, has no lecture slides or online notes. I haven't gone through a hw assignment but heard they are really hard

Do not take this unless you really need !
Take anyone else or wait. Lectures are unorganized. Provide zero resources on Canvas. Tests are graded insanely hard and assigns 10+ problems every week, oftentimes repeating problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mumbles in class with a thick accent and writes with sloppy handwriting. Never clear what chapter he's covering, and would using new notation with no explanation. Never bothered to show a worked out problem in class or give a HW solution. Only 2 midterms and a final. Other 10% is really difficult HW that rarely looked like classwork. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE. HWs are from the textbook and he assigns 20-30 problems, each usually with multiple parts. HWs were only worth 5% of grade. Only other grades were 2 exams and final. No clear grading criteria and test problems hardly match the hw problems. He claims attending lecture benefits and those who do score higher but most disagreed in my class.
Worst professor I have had at Georgia Tech. Take ANYONE else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont even try

Lectures are very confusing. The test are very hard and graded harshly. He said he would curve based on exams and the average on the first was 44% and he said there was no curve. His accent makes him hard to understand and the textbook is where I learn most of the content

This is a very peculiar class. I performed better when I stopped attending lectures and started relying solely on the textbook for information. Lectures are delivered poorly. Homeworks are graded harshly. Tests are needlessly confusing. The content of this class is fairly easy, yet this professor makes the class substantially more difficult.
DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture was hard to follow and he often dismissed questions. It wasn't uncommon for test questions to be on stuff that wasn't covered in the syllabus

Awful, awful, awful. Lectures are not a welcoming environment: he constantly belittles students that asks questions. His lecture notes and slides are like reading hieroglyphics; the only way to succeed is to read the textbook, but his homework makes that impossible to do. He also randomly moves up tests with very little notice. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to understand, and not presented in a method conducive to learning. Don't recommend at all
Terrible. Just all around terrible. Everything. Whatever you can think of.

You can get a decent grade, but you won't learn prob&stats. At the best you will get confused and stressed with the class. Terrible lectures/notes, hard to understand and rude when you ask questions. Distance learning made the experience significantly more miserable. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is horrible at explaining everything. There were topics I learned from other classes, but didn't understand how he did it. I asked questions about specific homework problems and he complained that "You're only asking questions about problems. You need to ask questions about concepts." Tests are NOTHING like homework. He's only at GT for research

Very hard to understand and terrible lecturer. Class examples do not match exam or homework. Offers little resources and gets angry when students ask questions, hindering students from attending office hours. Taking this class with him was my biggest mistake at GT so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Having to teach an online class is very difficult for this professor because he isn't exactly the best with technology. He scans his notes and just talks about it in class, but his notes are very disorganized and difficult to understand. Ended up not going to class and just reading the book, but with all the homework he assigns, its not possible.

The professor's teaching style is out of date. This should be an easy class and he makes it very hard by not being able to talk without 3-4 um's and uh's between 2 words. He is a very tough grader confirmed by course critique. The professor seems to be stuck in the USSR in mind. He might be very intelligent, but his skills in the classroom are weak

He has less respect for non-math majors. He cuts you off mid-question, rarely bothering to understand what the students question actually is. He seems not to value the students questions or interest. However, he is not heartless. A student accidentally missed the final, and he let the student retake the exam in his office.

Decent lecturer, though he does have an accent, frequently abbreviates on the board, and jumps around on topics. While not necessarily proof heavy, he also doesn't do that many actual examples either. Textbook for HW only. Tests are a bit on the easy side, but no practice tests, so also fairly unpredictable.

Seems like a good guy, but is really  bad at explaining material and is very disorganized. He interrupts you when your asking a question because he thinks he knows what your asking before your finished, so this process takes a while, by then you give up and learn nothing. Tests could be simple but not clear at what he wants you to give,  etc.

Horrible note-taking professor. He writes on the board in no particular order and then changes most of it later. Thick eastern-european accent, difficult to understand in lecture. To be fair, he was helpful when I had a problem with a test and have me a fair and deserved grade.

He speaks in Russian and writes in something that slightly resembles Chinese.  His accent is so damn thick you can't understand.  He makes jokes but no one knows what the hell he said.  Class wasn't too hard, but the final sucked ass.  But seriously... DONT GO TO LECTURE.  Oh yeah, and if you ask a question... duck... b/c you may get shot!

I took this for T&M so my experience was different, but I'd be remiss if I didn't mention how good of a lecturer he is. It's so rare for me to actually feel refreshed after lecture, but Bob knows how to talk to an audience and keep 'em engaged. If you're taking this class w/him for T&M, don't be afraid. Bob doesn't bite.
I hope I don't have to take his class again.

GREAT professor. Tests are open book and easy if you attend class and copy down exactly any notes he writes down. Lecture isn't mandatory but important to attend because examples he works are almost identical to the tests.

One of the best professors I've had at Tech. It won't be an easy class, but he keeps it interesting/amusing and is very helpful. You can easily get a B, just not the easiest class to get an A. Not really the point, he's the kind of professor you want to take for the teaching, not the grade.
Whatever class he teaches, take it. You will learn a lot and enjoy it more than any other class through college.
FUNNY

Extremely helpful and entertaining.  Easily the best professor I had in my time at Tech.  I was amazed that he was an associate professor, and knew more and could teach more than the tenured professors.  Highly recommmended.
He was the single best professor I had in my 6 years at Georgia Tech.  Loved his class.  Absolutely loved it.
Good professor--relaxed class environment, knows his stuff, willing to help, and can be pretty funny.
No Comments

An extremely interesting class that was taught incredibly well. Every lecture felt like it gave new information and the papers were extremely interesting. Just be sure to keep up with the weekly readings as some of the higher level contents are on the exams. Group project is also pretty interesting and isn't too much work.
Took her course in behavioral economics. Very direct and teaches you what you need to know. Course expectations were clear and reasonable. Learned a lot. Lectures were also fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very test heavy but easy as long as you review the lecture notes. I would recommend going to class because she wrote on the whiteboards primarily. Truly a great teacher, still consult her for advice today

Took this class with her over the summer and it was an easy A. Dr. Buser a kind and caring professor who makes the class very straightforward. I would definitely  recommend taking this class with her.
Had Dr. Buser for Summer iGniTe Macroeconomics, class was interesting and engaging. Grading was straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Buser teach ECON2105 for iGniTe, but that class wasn't available to rate for some reason. Good course that covered the basics of macroeconomics. She made the lectures fun and interesting, and the grading was very straightforward.

Dr. Buser's lectures were solid but our final grade was the average of midterm 1, midterm 2, and the final, which I thought was very harsh. This course is math heavy compared to most other econ courses. I wish there had been more example problems or practice exams but the tests were pretty fair so long as you reviewed the lecture notes/powerpoints.
Material not conveyed clearly.  Lectures do not cover what is on tests.  Seems like instructor is ego driven and expects students to read her mind.  Disconnect from lectures vs tests.
weekly quizzes and the 35% final exam are your only grades and all are very hard. very confusing compared to what you learn in the lecture. most questions are easily found on chegg or quizlet
Great class!
During lecture she just reads off 100+ slide decks. The homeworks and labs are alot. The tests were pretty difficult and she doesn't curve until the end so you have no idea what your standing is.

This was one the best classes I have ever had. I did not expect to be interested in soil, but it turned out to be really interesting. There is alot of work, though. Six homeworks, five labs, and three tests, plus a final project. 

She did not curve individual test grades, but curved final grades at the end of the semester.

Professor Burns is definitely one of the best profs I've had at Tech so far. She's very knowledgeable, breaks concepts down well, tries her best to make lectures engaging, is invested in her students, and is somewhat harsh but fair in grading (but she also curves). If you have her for 3000 expect a lot of writing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: GT needs more professors like Prof. Burns. She is tough but very straightforward in lecture and fair in grading. It is clear that her primary goal is to make sure we learn the material, and she helps in any way she can. Engineering economy is tough but SO useful and her lectures make it clear, so don't skip class. Thank you, Prof. Burns!

LOVED Dr. Buskell---always led super interesting discussions and is super funny, caring, and intellectual. The readings could get lengthy but the very flexible in-class discussions make up for it. There are no exams, simply essays and presentations which are very doable, but just take a lot of time and thought. It is very easy to do well though!

Dr. Buskell is an absolute gem. He's caring, passionate about teaching, clear on expectations, and just a great guy to be around. Reading assignments in Perusall and discussions in class, but they're never overly-lengthy. It's a laid back environment where you feel encouraged and workload is balanced perfectly. Would take ANY class with him again.

Weekly accessible + interesting Perusall readings; centered on class discussion; Prof is really approachable and genuinely cares about his students and the material; excellent and timely feedback on papers and projects that makes it easy to plan ahead and implement change for later iterations; my favorite class of the semester!!

What an amazing professor. He is the GOAT when it comes to this class. He is very knowledgable and seems to know everything. Not very accessible outside of class though, don't really ever see him. But he is great and would def take again.
Mr. Burdell is AMAZING. He can be hard to find, but he's also everywhere. Being that he graduated with every major and accomplished much more, his stories are very inspirational.
Professor Burdell is, hands down, the best professor at Tech. In fact, he was a CS major before it was cool! I hear he's also the man in the Buzz costume... GO JACKETS!!!
He's great
He's hard to find, but he's the best. He's a multi-major professor. If you are undecided take one of his classes and ask him for advice. He will be the light that will show you the way.
I would take him again anytime. I took him after hearing about him from some friends.

Had a deep understanding of the course, and if you didn't understand something during the lecture you could always go up to him after to ask questions. As long as you put in the work and show up to class then you shouldn't have a problem. He is also extremely accessible outside of class and will really try his best to answer questions.
Thought he was going to be very bad but after a couple of weeks I got used to his teaching style and he can be funny sometimes. Also very kind and accessible outside of class.

He has a deep understanding the material and is proficient at answering questions during lectures. Most people (including myself) have to watch videos from Jankowski, another GT 1553 professor, to supplement lectures. However, if you can keep up with everything he reads off, then you will probably be fine with just the lectures and studio.

He is not that bad, although you might get bored of his lectures, you can still find what was taught in class on the classroom canvas and the studios help reinforce what he taught. Obviously, it helps to come to class especially because even if you zone out of class, as long as you approach him after class, he will explain it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor read off the slides for most of the lectures, I didn't lead anything from his class.

Took Game Theory II with him the first semester it was offered. Lectures were pretty dry but taught clearly and explained the material well. Homeworks aren't graded so three tests make up most of your grade although there is a decent curve. Grades generously but the class isn't super easy and you still need to study for all the exams.

I had him twice for two separate courses; lectures can get kinda dull; weekly homework, midterm and final. Course material is kinda difficult to grasp, but he grades fairly lax; he extended deadlines a few times so he understands students' workloads; problem is sometimes book and lecture don't match and homework is from book, but again, lax grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Burkett's game theory class. He is very thoughtful and considerate and purposeful about everything he says. Very knowledgeable and good at answering students' questions. There are about 8 problem sets of homework, two midterms, and a final. The concepts can be a little hard to grasp, but an A is still possible.
Good professor overall, though the class itself was a little boring. We spent a *lot* of time defining terms to use, and that could get complex. Weekly homeworks but not too difficult or too long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Agree with other reviews. Thought some of the homework and practice problems were harder than the tests. Great prof, teaches really well. 3 extra credit surveys and extra credit on every test. Optional final. By far the easiest of the statics class while still actually learning. 100% pick Prof Bruun if he's teaching statics.
I would like him to teach every ME class at tech! The most chill professor I have ever had. 85 was an A at the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bruun was an amazing COE 2001 prof. He makes the notes easily accessible and works through lots of examples in class. The homework takes a decent bit of time, but the homework questions are very similar to exam questions
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great prof! Made it really easy to get an A because the grade cutoff was only an 85. he was super nice and posted his notes, which were super digestable and easy to read. textbook was helpful too. tests were not easy, but again only needed an 85 for an A. also offered good extra credit and would curve. loved this class!
George P Burdell is the greatest professor in all of Tech's long and storied history
The Best Professor in the ECE Department!!!!!!!! He has such a way with teaching us about C and RISC-V.

He's an incredible teacher who taught us the ways and traditions of Georgia Tech, including how to be helluva engineer. Everyone gets an A++ except business majors and u[sic]ga students but you learn so much as well. 10/10 would recommend.

I remember finding Prof. Burdell's class as a freshman, wondering if I'd made the right call coming to GT. I sat in on his class after getting lost, and was enraptured. BUZZZ BUZZZ GIRLIES!

What an amazing professor. He is the GOAT when it comes to this class. He is very knowledgable and seems to know everything. Not very accessible outside of class though, don't really ever see him. But he is great and would def take again.
Professor Burdell is a legend at GT. His THWG1001 class is a blast - lectures at 3:33 AM, learning to diss UGA in multiple languages, and ChatGPT/unstuck study to ace the course.

Walked into class and saw Dr Burdell swimming through land on his way to the lectern. About halfway through the lecture he got a call from the avengers requesting his assistance so he had to leave a bit early but it was alright because on the way out he dunked on Shaquille O' Neil from half court.

George Burrell is by far one of the BEST professors at GA Tech, if you couldn't tell by his 139 5-star ratings and 0 1-star ratings. He was my Hindi professor freshman year, I can't even begin to list everything he's done for me. He doesn't even speak Hindi but I'm fluent now. Prof Burdell is a legend in every sense of the word. If you ever get the chance, take his class.

Absolutely amazing prof! Cannot say enough good things about him - truthfully so much better after taking his class, he really showed me what it meant to be a Helluva Engineer! His feedback was always EXTREMELY helpful - Honestly a hero.

I am a better human after taking Professor Burdell's class! So is my wife! We don't have kids, but when we do, they too will be better humans because I took this class!

I have never experienced a class like this. You walk in the door, sit down, and then walk right out 1000% smarter. Opposite of that dump in Athens. 

Thank you Professor Burdell!

Good guy.  Ver imaginative.
Literally the GOAT. Should be the person of the year for sure.
An actual legend.
GT Legend.

I cant believe it, this prof single handedly raised GT as a top engineering school in the country. It is insane how much this prof knows, they are the peak representation of all of humanities finest achievements concentrated into one person.
Terrific professor, loved his class and would love to take again, tough as a whole but enjoyable nonetheless.
Prof. Burdell is literally the best professor I've had at GT. I don't know how he does it but I literally feel like a changed person. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
GPB is a light! Very hard to get a class with him but I'm glad it finally happened. He's the embodiment of what Georgia Tech is #goyackets
Very good professor. Very experienced and down to Earth. I have high respect for him and would let him sleep in my dorm.
His Lectures are usually at 3:33 am in howey 6 lecture hall. Best class I ever had
super good teacher

This man is a true legend. Absolutely iconic. Heard that he donated a kidney to one of his students.
Absolutely stellar. Best prof at Tech hands down.
Needed to do it in a group lol
I love him as more than a teacher, more than a friend. As the embodiment of Georgia Tech, I can't wait to take more classes taught by him.

Best in the game by far. He's an expert in practically every subject but humble. His lectures were exciting, funny and inspirational. I couldn't recommend him more. Bravo.
By far the best prof you will ever have- I don't care what your major is, I don't care if you don't need the class- he will change your life forever.

Burdell is out of this world. He is the ideal professor. He gives out soooo much extra credit, and the tests are take-home and very straightforward. Attendance is optional. Dr. Burdell is by far the most amazing professor I have ever had. He changed my life. What a man.

George is the best teacher I've ever had.

Dr. Burdell is awesome, don't pass up a chance to take his class.

George P. Burdell is singlehandedly the best professor- nay, person- on the Georgia Tech campus. No one else even compares. Taking a class with Burdell gives you the inside knowledge you need to get a 4.0 and steal the T off of Tech Tower. THWG!
Dr. Burdell knows everything about everything. You can't ask a question he won't give an answer to, and his explanations are always unbelievably clear.
good teacher

Love this guy. An actual superstar.
You can't make up how good this guy is.
Amazing guy. This class changed my life forever. Would take again. If you can't get his class this semester I recommend waiting, it is worth it!
Best professor.
I've had wonderful opportunity to take Burdell for CS8803, a notoriously difficult class. Burdell made it so much better, it's almost unbelievable how much of a difference he made.

Hands down the best professor to take for this class! Just study the old tests, and you'll be fine. Lectures are hilarious and prof. is very accessible outside of class for office hours. If you have the opportunity to take his class, do it!

Dr. Burdell isn't just the professor you want to take at Tech, he's the one you absolutely need to take. His lectures go beyond the subject matter to learnings about life itself. If you go through tech without having Dr. Burdell as a professor you're doing something wrong. It's a must have. A perfect balance between not being stressful but still being informative. DON'T MISS OUT
Best class at Tech. I almost felt like it was no work at all.

Mr. Burdell is just one of those dudes everybody says you gotta get. In class he's the man, cracking jokes left and right while also lecturing. Class went by so fast it was like it never happened. Leaving, I always felt a warm fuzzy feeling and a wanting to return, none of my other profs are like him. Anyways, you'll get an A, 'nough said

If there is anyone I have ever wanted to be like in my life, it's people like him that are truly making America great. A former striker for liverpool striker too! I'll never forget what you did for those orphan kids that you pulled out of a burning building my senior year. Live well professor Burdell, I love you

It's unreal how good of professor he is. 11/10. I would take him for every class if I could.

Honestly one of the best professors I have ever had the honor to take a class from. Every teacher at this school is top notch, but Burdell is truly leagues above the rest. I'm so lucky to have had the honor to take his class and I will never forget the lessons I learned from this inspirational man.

The model of brilliance at GT. By far the best professor I've ever taken.

One of the best professors I've had the pleasure of taking. Always captivating with his lectures. He's one of the most knowledgeable people I've ever known; apparently he has multiple degrees from Tech, which is pretty astounding.

Best professor I've ever had by far. Was a student here so he knows what Tech kids go through. He's crazy smart (apparently he has at least a few degrees from Tech). Very spirited and has lots of stories to share that keep things interesting. 10/10. You can do no better.
He's amazing.
Now wonder he was a leading candidate for TIME Magazine's person of the year! Best professor I have ever had.

Amazing inspiration to me. What a lovely man. He will be responsible for keeping the GT spirit going.

Great guy. I mean, when your professor is almost TIME Magazine's person of the year, he's gotta be pretty legendary.
Honestly the best professor by far here at Tech - I wish he taught all my classes!
A god among mortals, the most outstanding professor on the east coast. Almost seems impossible for him to be this great of a teacher.

Awesome prof

Dr. Burdell has been teaching since the 1930's, and is still going strong. If he ever retires, it will only be because GT shuts it's doors. Whenever I talk to a fellow GT alum, we trade stories about him.  He is simply awesome!
The greatest professor/student Tech has ever had.  He encompasses what ever student and professor should strive toward in their career here.

He hits blackjack with just one card. Superman wears George Burdell Pajamas. George checkmated Bobby Fisher, using only his king.

3/5 for the 3011 with brothers, not really for brothers as a teacher. Junior design was a lot more work than I think it should be, but there is an arguement that it's my fault for doing Junior -> senior design path. Has a lot of energy, good vibes.

Took 3011 with Brothers, this class is a lot of work but the junior design project made me feel super prepared for senior design and he is a great professor - very reasonable and likeable, and teaches the course well

Exams were take-home Canvas quizzes (40 mins, mostly MC from slides, a few short answer) with an overall curve.

He had some times where he was rather derogatory and kind of feed you to the wolves mindset, but it did pressure me to try hard and learn so it worked. The first labs were hell tho and took forever.
Tim Brothers was one of the best professors I have had. Down to earth and a great guy - the idea prof. I wish he taught more.

Extremely caring professor and gives very valuable feedback as your group works on the projects. He tried his hardest to minimalize the bloat in material. Only issue I can see with ECE3872 in general is groups are completely random and you stick with the same group the entire semester.
Dr. Brothers is very understanding and relaxed. He is engaging in class and gives very constructive feedback throughout the design project.
Bryce is the goat, great professor, easy to understand, willing to help, and truly cares about his students.

He talks like a dictionary - you cannot understand him at all and he grades unnecessarily harshly.
