reviews.comment: Shes so nice! She sometimes switched to English which is wonderful because there is a fair amount of technical jargon, but her Spanish is also very easy to understand. She made notes for each class that you just filled in the blank or made extra notes during lecture; the notes went along with the textbook, which made studying for tests easier.
Brilliant professor! Would totally recommend.

Profesora Montes-Alcala is honestly one of the best Spanish teachers I've ever had. She knows so much about the language and has class very well planned out. She makes class engaging and entertaining even if the information isn't the most interesting. I recommend taking her class whenever you get the chance because she is great!

Profa. Montes-Alcala was probably one of the best Spanish teachers, if not all-around teachers, I've had. Class is almost never a drag, and the content of the course paired with her teaching improves your Spanish-speaking abilities so much. However, make sure you understand her attendance policy. I was confused and it cost me the A I had.

Prof. Montes-Alcala is a good professor. She is very knowledgeable about linguistics and she is highly organized, so it is easy to stay on track in her class. I enjoyed this class, even though it was a little bit boring sometimes (it was an hour and a half long). But she is definitely a good professor!

She is SUPER organized, has every class planned down to the day, and never changes her plans. The class is super easy if you do the reading and pay attention. Lots of group discussion. Very interesting subject if you like Spanish. Highly recommended!!

Prof. Montes-Alcala was the best Spanish professor I've ever had. She's brilliant, highly organized, demanding but fair, funny and very attractive! I learned so much more than just Spanish in this course. Tech is lucky to have someone like her on the faculty. She accessible, very knowledgeable, speaks impeccable Spanish and is always available.Ole!

Class is very test heavy, however lots of practice tests/finals were provided. Id recommend taking him but its still a difficult class. He made it suck a little less though. He is not condescending to stupid questions and made me comfortable to ask away to my hearts content. His notes were a little strange so take your own notes.

I appreciated him. He's definitely one of the better combo professors when compared to the others. Reasonable tests and homework. Lectures are pretty good. This class was really hard though and I dont think even the best combo professor in the world can make combo a seamless experience. If you suck at math, buckle in your seat belts.

Dr. Cervantes is such a sweet professor; probably the nicest I've had at Tech. Incredibly accessible and really cares about helping his students. He makes combo reasonable; would recommend taking him 10/10.

Very caring and understanding professor. He is a good lecturer but can move slowly through some parts, though it's only because he wants everybody to truly understand the material. If you participate in class, he will be more fond of you. The homework was light and exams were fairly similar to the practice exams, and he provides 4 per exam.

Professor Cervantes was incredible. He is extremely approachable and cares immensely for his students' success in his class. If I were to critique him in any way, it would be that he moves a little slow when he does lectures, and we didn't get to all the topics we were supposed to cover. But definitely the best choice for 3012.

MATH 3012, in general, is probably one of the hardest class I've ever taken content-wise. He made this class much more bearable and showed genuine care and respect for his students. I can tell he loves teaching and I enjoyed his passion for the subject. He's definitely better than the majority of the other profs for this class.
Not especially good, but also not bad. He lectures at a comfortable pace and the class isn't difficult, so definitely worth considering.
He is not the best, but he's not the worst either. If you study hard you will get a good grade. His lectures are not very helpful but he is very good at explaining during office hours.

I'm a junior so I've taken my fair share of classes, but this guy has to be one of the most boring professors I have ever taken. If you can handle really boring lectures or you don't mind teaching yourself the material take his class because tests and HW are easy. The HW is time consuming cause it's every week. Summary boring prof, easy class.
A little jittery in lectures and jumps around a lot, but gives lots of examples so it's easy to understand.

Lectures have a political bias at times (she is a republican), and she wants to talk about current global issues/politics a lot. Grades mostly come from weekly group labs, which have unclear grading and no rubrics. Mandatory attendance but no midterm/final exams.
Politcal partisan hack

ST: Analytics Econ/Fin Value Model. Hands on class that is closer to simulating IB and financial accounting than econ. Prof doesn't delve into any of the financial concepts, instead goes on to do everything basic in micro. Course's goal is learning how to do valuation but fails by avoiding the financial accounting side. Not bad, not good, just ok.

Very poor professor. Experienced in econ but pedals weird right wing ideas. Lectures drag on with the same stories over and over. No tests only grades were weekly group question sets and Persuall. Attendance is mandatory but you can skip half the classes and get an A (zero in-class graded assignments). Very easy A but didn't learn anything at all.

Very poor lecturer and professor. Although she is a person who has had experience in the field of economics she explains this very poorly, often relying on the same stories to get her point across. By the end of the year only a handful of students attended class. Group projects are time consuming and annoying. No tests, but very annoying class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Get ready to read, honestly if you take the courses to gain culture, just buy an economy book by yourself.

Great class to take if you already know some about economics! Required readings were long but understandable. Took it online because of covid. Didn't have any midterms/finals, just group projects every week. This class leaves you with a lot of everyday background knowledge for the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: In the online class, there were no exams at all. Just reading and group assignments for the questions related to readings. So, it was really easy but the async lectures were very boring, and you basically need to study on your own. She's passionate about econ, but she barely helps when you have a question, which sucks because I wanted to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 1. Extremely reluctant to help students 2. Doesn't answer questions directly/at all, making the student feel dumb 2. Doesn't provide grading criteria/rubric: you won't know why you got those points off 3. Slow inquiry turnback time: be prepared to email, piazza, google, work with others before getting any response from her

Relied on the textbook to learn the information I needed to know to perform well on my exams. I went to the review sessions held by the TAs. Didn't have a final; had a group project (essay) instead. She gets off track & tells her life stories, but they're pretty enjoyable to listen to. She is super passionate about Economics; you'll be able to tell

Professor Ries is extremely passionate about economics, while not the best professor because she gets distracted easily, the class is definitely doable. We had an exam every week, no midterm, no final which I found to be a good setup for the class. You basically learn everything yourself and most people don't go to class but she cares/helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ries clearly presents the economic principles from the standpoint of a free-market economist herself. There are 5 exams, so the course is exam heavy while offering many opportunities to redeem your grade. The lectures are going to be based primarily on slides that present clear explanations of economic principles. Attendance is recommended.

Lectures are absolutely terrible. No point in attending, she "lectures" on the material you needed to know the night before in order to do the graded online homework (which is tedious and you usually need to read the textbook to figure out). Tests arent terrible but you actually need to study

Honestly, this class is not that hard. Although she is a pretty awful professor, the material is not difficult! Read the textbook the day before, and the tests will be easy for you. You literally can skip every lecture, read the textbook the night before, and ace the tests. The homework kind of sucks, but just do it, and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Ries structures the class so she reviews the information you should have read for homework. If you have taken AP Economics or don't mind teaching yourself, she is okay. Alternatively, if you want someone who teaches, she is not the right professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This is by far one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Ries teaches straight from the slides. There is absolutely no point in showing up to class and she does not clarify anything. There are 5 tests that count 80 percent of your grade. This class is AWFUL.

Professor Ries is awful. Exams are 80% of our final grade and none are dropped. There is no opportunity for extra credit either. Homework assignments are twice a week and can take hours to complete. This is a ridiculous amount of work for an introductory economics course.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Your grade is pretty much based on 5 exams throughout the semester. Many people skip lecture , and honestly going to it won't get you very far. The tests are difficult, and she gives little guidance, refusing to answer questions. Her lectures are not useful, and she tends to go on about her stories. Qualified professor but low quality teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I HATED THIS CLASS. GOING TO LECTURE IS USELESS BECAUSE SHE RARELY TALKS ABOUT ANYTHING BESIDES HER RANDOM ACCOMPLISHMENTS. THERE'S AN IN CLASS QUIZ EVERY CLASS BUT THEY'RE UNGRADED AND TOTALLY POINTLESS. BEWARE. THERE WILL BE A TEST EVERY OTHER WEEK WITHOUT FAIL. EVEN IF YOU'VE ONLY MET ONCE SINCE THE LAST TEST.(I LEARNED THIS THE HARD WAY).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don't ever go to lecture, just read the textbook. She's a great and qualified economist, but a HORRIBLE teacher. She does nothing but make the same hand motions over and over again without clarifying. She'll make you feel dumb for asking a question, and she is not understanding of any situations at all. Do the homework, also.

She genuinely cares and is enthusiastic about economics, evident in her copious stories of tax reform and economic advice given to countries worldwide. Those same stories, which may sound exciting, can become very boring, as they take up much time during lecture. For that reason, many people skip. The course is not too difficult, not bad overall.

Lectures are a complete joke and your grade pretty much depends on the 4 exams during the semester. Material isn't too difficult so if you take the time to read from the textbook and teach yourself everything you should be fine

The least organized class taught at Tech. Lectures are solely activity based; unfortunately, the activities rarely teach you anything, and take up all the lecture time, so you must read on your own. She makes no effort to tell students what to study for the tests; the tests feel completely different from the lecture material, since there is none.

You may as well be taking this class online for all she teaches, or rather, doesn't teach. She never effectively gauges student understanding & flat out refuses to help students who are struggling. I've taught myself all the material and am barely scraping by. Infinitely infuriating class.
Rude and wastes a lot of time

Unorganized and extremely difficult to deal with. We taught ourselves about 98% of the material via the textbook. She never lectured in class. She is no good with technology but has an opinion on everything (usually not a productive one.) I was very excited for the course until I actually got in. I cannot stand this prof. Wouldn't recommend
Her experience and knowledge in economics is without a doubt A++, but she is one of them professors that just can't teach. her organization is worse than a preschooler

All she really wished to talk about was herself and her accomplishments rather than economics.  You had to teach yourself everything, because her tests were quite hard, essays sometimes nearly impossible, and the class was all about competition with you being graded on a curve (25% of people get As, 50% Bs, and 25% C-Fs).
She seems to have a chip on her shoulder at engineering majors.  Like a lot of electives at engineering schools, it is made to be more difficult by tedious assignments.

Professor Ries is a great lecturer, very interested in the subject, and you will learn a lot.  Budget a lot of time for the class though - uses an online textbook with a lot of quizzes, in-class tests, group presentation, 2 papers due, etc.  Takes role.

ECON 2101 is abosiutely awful!! If you like ECON maybe it's ok, but if you just want to get ECON out of the way, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS OR PROFFESSOR! Pretty tough assignments and tough tests. I busted my butt for my B and I usually don't even have to work hard for my A's.

He was great! Lectures very informative and notes posted online + attendance is not mandatory. 3 midterms and final, but the final is optional to replace a midterm score. Exams were also open note, so you didn't need to memorize the formulas.
Exams were hard because there's too much algebra in time pressure, lectures were okay, lack motivation on the concepts. Not the best lecturer I had, not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mao was a nice instructor who taught beyond the scope of usual content. His exams were difficult, but his problems were insightful and interesting. I'm not sure how his grading will work out, but hopefully he curves! Not an easy class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Although he is young and not that experienced in teaching, but I can see he is trying his best to get these tough concepts to students. His homework and exams are difficult but note that he curves! Don't worry too much and your grade and only concentrate on what you have learned. Enjoy his teaching!

Content was very difficult but the professor was patient and explained things well. Going to class was not required. Lectures recordings and notes were also posted later which helped with flexibility. Final grades were on a curve so it was difficult to know your grade precisely although he updated us on the cutoffs a couple times.

This professor is amazing, absolutely love him. His content is probably the most difficult around campus, but the way he teaches and the respect for his students is immaculate. Hard class but lots of learning! He curves a lot!!

Some averages to help picture the class: Midterm 1 (23/30), Midterm 2 (24/30), Midterm 3 (17/30), Final (42/60)
Test and homework are very hard, but he curves, homework can collbarate with others. I still get A even thouth I am the lowest grade in class

Great person, he wants us students to succeed. However. His tests. I'm not that great at math/stats so that may be part of it, but holy crap his tests were hard, as were the homework at times. If you go in for help he'll help you enthusiastically. Just for a point of reference, our third exam, 16/30 was an A, 11/30 B, 7/30 C.

Cheng Mao really is awesome. He even cracks a few jokes here and there. As far as him as a professor, he is great. The content is hard, and you will have to work to do well, but he does his best to make sure you understand. Even gives extensions in stressful times and is super patient with students. If you can, take him for 3215. No regrets.

Professor Mao is very passionate about the topic and cares about his students, often extending due dates when needed. The homeworks always felt like a fair amount of work and fairly graded. However, the material is pretty hard and the tests were very difficult, but he is curving the final grades.

Passionate about the subject and compassionate for the students. Goes through plenty of example problems in lecture to help build a good foundation for statistics and build upon it through the weekly homeworks (max 9 problems). Will sometimes grant due date extensions based on how the class is doing and is always active on Piazza. Nicest guy I know

He is a caring professor that listens to student feedback. However, his biggest downfall is that he struggles to explain concepts and examples. Most students relied solely on the textbook. He is pretty clear on what to expect on tests but his homework can me be tough and very time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This semester was Cheng Mao's first-semester teaching, it definitely shows. He decided to go over twice (I'm quoting him) the amount of material other classes give but slowed down to 1.75x what the other classes gave since almost everyone was dying. To his credit, he provides video lectures and does a Q/A during class, though they haven't been help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor! You can tell how passionate he is about the subject, and I've already learned a lot in this class. He is also extremely caring and readily takes student feedback about the class. It really feels like teaching and good student outcomes is a priority to him, which is far from guaranteed here. 10/10 would take class with him again.
Great teacher that works with you to help you understand the material.
lectures are highk skippable but u have to do iclicker; 220/274 points needed for 100% on participation. she feels like she's gentle parenting lowk but its kinda wholesome
She's ok. I don't get the hype around here. The lectures/tests were fine, but lab is tedious.
Dr. Shepler makes chem II very digestible

Lectures are okay, lots of examples gone through in class and she is always willing to take time to explain anything if need be, along with this she is extremely accessible outside of class. She cares a lot about her students and is always willing to chat while walking around the class or just ask how your day is going. Exams are somewhat hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a passionate, fun, and engaging professor! Gen chem is not easy but she makes it make sense. Also, you are allowed crib sheets on each exam, including the final, so you can make an A if you just put in the effort!

One of the best professors I've ever had. She cares so much about her students' success not just in chemistry, but in academia. Super easy to reach out to and is always willing to give advice. Also offers A TON of extra credit if you're willing to put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely took a lot of work, but at the end was able to replace all three of my exams. She gave feedback after every exam, and was always available to talk about grades and course work anytime. Recommend her for sure!
Very kind and understanding. Gave great lectures. Would love to take her class again.

a professor that does the flipped classroom model correctly. office hours are good, lectures are good, and videos are good. I would recommend using the videos for cheat sheets because if it's in the vids it'll be on the test (lectures get derailed sometimes). Make sure to get all the final exam tokens. The questions are really easy. Learn sig figs

By far the best professor and the best teacher I have ever hard period. Dr. Shepler is incredibly good at explaining key concepts and is very accessible outside of class. Make use of office hours both online and in person as they are great tools.

Dr. Shepler is easily one of the most empathetic and sweet professors to roam this Earth. She structures the class with the understanding that this course is difficult. I won't lie and say the class is easy, but she definitely does everything in her power to ease the burden on her students. If you have the choice, don't take 1212 with anyone else!

Dr. Shepler is the sweetest ever! I had her a few semesters back and still remember her kindness and approachability. She personally emailed me after I did well on exams (I'm sure she subbed in names, but the gesture is super nice nonetheless). There are in class quizzes for attendance I think but it was at 8am so I didn't go much.

She obviously cares about her students. She tries her best to get everyone through the course as easily as possible. She's super understanding and offers grade improvement opportunities. She wants you to succeed.

Dr. Shepler is an extremely kind professor who knows how to teach you the most important info. I really loved her flipped classroom, which made learning much easier. Classes were usually practice, and she own often go over exam-like questions. She was also always providing extensions for everyone---very understanding!!!

Dr. Shepler is a great professor! Her pre-lecture videos are very helpful especially near the end of the course. She is also VERY caring and allows students to offer feedback/ask questions at the end of every lecture on a Canvas quiz. It was a great way to allow students to ask clarifying questions without feeling any pressure.

Dr. Shepler is the GOAT. Truly the best professor I have had at Tech. Her pre-lecture videos are clear and concise, and her in-class questions really set you up for success on her exams. She's amazing in office hours (sets up 5 in a week leading up to midterm), and you can tell she cares SO MUCH about her students. I cannot recommend her enough.

Dr. Shepler was one of the highlights of my first semester at Georgia Tech. She is very passionate about her subject and makes the class easily understandable and engaging. She is very accessible outside of class too with office hours

Honestly, I didn't go to many lectures for this class, especially later in the semester. The ones I did, however, she demonstrated clearly that she is an amazing professor and can teach with great depth. Furthermore, when I had an emergency and needed to make up a test, she was super friendly and helpful, and overall a great person. Take her class.
Really nice prof, also very good teacher. Chem 2 by nature is hard, but she does a good job at explaining, gives lots of option exam practice (DO THEM), and is very understanding. Best option by far!
She is wonderful. Yes it's a hard class but there's no one better to take it with.

In Dr. Shepler's class, students take notes before class instead of during class, using class time only for practice problems, which you think would have discouraged me from attending class because technically you aren't learning anything new, but she is such a good lecturer and teacher that I went every day even though it was at 8am!
Best chem teacher i've ever had!!

I love this professor!!! Please take her if you want amazing lectures, a kind and caring teacher, and just a great experience with CHEM1212K :) Dr. Shepler puts her lectures online in a flip classroom method but the videos are a masterpiece. They are super easy to follow and she explains everything in a clear and consice way. She is just wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's very nice but it's flipped classroom which isn't great since lectures are a brief review of content with 6 questions during class, so you won't learn much from lectures. If you took AP Chem it's just busywork, if you didn't it will require a lot of effort outside class to learn content + answer q's for hw. Great class to pay $4k for.

Carrie Shepler is a gift from God himself. Is CHEM1212 a hard course? YES. But was she an absolutely wonderful teacher? ALSO YES. 

Dr. Shepler cares. She is a great teacher in and out of the classroom. One of the best teachers I have ever had!!! She is definitely the best chem teacher you can choose at GT.

If you took AP Chem, should be pretty similar except for the last few parts of Midterm 3. Flipped classroom style video notes allow for attendance to be completely optional. 1 crib sheets allowed on each midterm, and 4 for the final. Tests are very fair and easier than the practice questions done in class. Labs kinda suck. Lots of extra credit!

Shepler is the best professor I have had at Georgia Tech. The structure of this class is great, she is readily available to help, she is great at answering questions. Shepler genuinely wants her students to do well and cares about everyone she teaches. If you have the chance, TAKE HER.

Shepler was an absolutely wonderful chemistry professor and made the class super easy to understand. The tests are very fair and cover exactly what is being taught in class. She is also very caring and is will to work with people. The grading system is set up very nice and you can get 5 points back on each exam if you do all the required work.

For people coming from AP Chem, 90% of the material is the same so the class can be easy/slow sometimes but it's for a very good reason because I learned so much! She was super nice and very passionate about the content. Makes the content very easy to understand and gives practice tests that are similar to the actual test. I highly recommend!

Dr. Shepler was incredible. I was so nervous coming in to take chemistry (my high school chem teacher was not the greatest), but Shepler made me realize that chemistry can make sense, and that I can be good at it. 10/10 no complaints and she is very accessible.

Dr. Shepler has been one of the reasons that made freshman year bearable. She makes sure that students have every opportunity to succeed, giving grade replacement opportunities as well as ample practice before tests and exams. Her flipped classroom style also allows for more flexibility when missing lectures.
The reverse classroom format made this 8am class manageable, and Professor Shepler's thorough help during office hours was a lifesaver. unstuck study was a great study tool alongside the materials.
She is so amazing, and very helpful. Answers all questions without making you feel dumb. You can tell she genuinely wants to help. Class can be hard, but just do practice tests. 10/10 recommend .

I took her class in Fall 2023. Really enjoyed the reverse classroom format, which made the class effectively async (attendance not required -- I'm grateful as a night owl w/ an 8am class). Always saw her at office hours, made a point to help students out very thoroughly. Standard chemistry attitude (extremely type A, very on top of things).

Enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and caring professor, always available outside of class and amazing, clear lectures. Tests are very similar to in-class assignments, so if you keep up with content and ask questions when needed, you will do well on the tests. Very generous grade replacement policy as well. 10/10 would take again.

Dr. Shepler goes above and beyond to help her students. She uses a flipped classroom. She gives great feedback, stating the reasons why something is incorrect. She made the course enjoyable for an 8:00 am class. Exams were rather straightforward, as Dr. Shepler gave topics to study for before the exams.

Dr. Shepler is the best! I really struggled in understanding the material but Dr Shepler was incredibly helpful in office hours and on ed. She is incredibly understanding. I struggled a lot on one of the midterm (and my grade reflected it) and she emailed me after the grades were released just to make sure I had everything I needed to be successful
Dr. Shepler wants all of her students to succeed and is very caring. Lectures were alright, fair amount of weekly assigments.

Wonderful professor! Really seems to care about the topic and her students and wants everyone to succeed. Exams are fair and you always know what will be on them. I wasn't sure I was going to like the flipped classroom, but she made it work. Great communication and clear lectures. If you're taking Chem 1212 make sure to get her.

Carrie made ~fair tests, but as a grader for her "token" system, she's extremely picky about what she wants, while not actually telling you what she wants. She's also snarky and gives mediocre feedback.Try taking a different teacher.

She is easily one of the best teachers I've ever had in my life. Her concise and clear lectures were great for understanding, and she was very clear exactly what she expected us to know for the exams by providing lots of helpful practice problems through Canvas, Achieve, and even past exams. You can tell she's really respected too, which is rare
Passionate about the topic and cares about her students

Professor Shepler is one of those professors where you can just tell she loves teaching and really cares about her students. She is always in constant communication outside of class and is always quick to answer questions. As a flipped classroom, she provides lots of resources to do well on tests and I highly recommend her.

She genuinely cares about students and wants to see us succeed.Very sweet when explaining questions. Was very open to suggestions and flexible with office hours. She did whatever was in her power to meet up with you and help you succeed in the course. Sounds like the bare minimun, but a lot of professors at Tech don't do it.

Dr. Shepler was a wonderful CHEM1212K professor. She establishes her expectations and the general layout of the course on the first day. It's a flipped classroom, but peer support is solid and her lectures cover the more confusing topics, so attending is useful. There are a lot of opportunities to get daily points and extra credit.
Mostly asynchronous class. Fairly difficult but Dr. Shepler is pretty available for help.
She was so sweet and cared about her students. Clear lectures, clear expectations, and grade remediation helps a lot.

Dr. Shepler was such an angel. She cared so much about her students and ensured everyone felt included. She is very accessible outside of class and explains topics very clearly with helpful analogies. She makes chemistry not such a bore
wonderful lecturer, good explainer, attendance not required, just do the assignments and use past exams to study for tests and you'll get an A

Dr. Shepler is an amazing professor. She is compassionate and very knowledgeable. She walks around the classroom and asks if we have any questions or concerns. If you have Dr. Shepler, even if you are bad at Chemistry, you will succeed. I do not consider myself great at chemistry, but I am confident that I will end the class with an A or B.

Dr. Shepler is one of the best professors at Georgia Tech! She genuinely cares about her students' success and is always willing to help. She uses a flipped classroom model, and her lectures break down complicated subjects effectively. Multiple things are due each class, and exams are REALLY hard, but Dr. Shepler helps make them easier to approach.

Dr. Shepler is amazing, by far one of my favorite professors. She's incredibly kind and really cares about her students. Class is bucket point system and she gives plenty of extra daily credit points. You can also replace midterm grades with the final grade. Reverse style classroom; pre-lecture videos & quizzes followed by in-class assignments.
Enjoyable class with lots of resources. Not a walk in the park, but practice exams are comprehensive and useful.

An amazing professor and cares a lot about students. Her class is bucket point style with grade replacement on the final. Studying for the exams was a lot but they felt doable given everything taught. I also liked that she had office hours that changed times throughout the week so that you could normally make them. Approachable in office hours.

Dr. Shepler is an amazing professor. She made the 8:30 AM lecture fun and entertaining, but also didn't mind changing things up to help students succeed. She is one of the best professors I've ever had, and if I could rate above five stars, I would in a heartbeat.

Dr. Shepler is such a queen and definitely an excellent choice for any chem class at Tech. She really cares about her students. The class itself is a lot of work and the tests are tricky, but she makes it so worth it. You won't regret taking Dr. Shepler's class!

Professor Shepler is awesome. We had just her lecture videos available to us, and those were awesome. She explains everything in great detail, and all the topics were a lot easier to understand because of her. In addition, she is pretty accessible on PIazza and outside of class, and she always tries her best to provide extra resources for students.

Dr. Shepler is one of those professors that you should design your whole schedule around because she is genuinely the best chem professor at Tec The workload for this class is heavy, the labs can be annoying, and the tests are hard, but study the old tests and listen to her lectures and you can do well. The best choice for Chem 1212 by far.

I wish I could take every Chem class with Dr. Shepler. She is incredibly kind and makes every effort to make students feel welcome and appreciated. Her pre-lectures and class sessions are very straightforward, and she is great about answering student questions. Her tests are very similar to the in class questions. Only second to her dog Ethyl.

Lots of points from the class are from homework, pre-lecture quizzes, and in-class assignments (you have a change to get like 450 and only need 275 though) She knows what she's doing and teaches very well. Always willing to help and is easily accessible. Will 10000% make you laugh. Tests are a little hard and may be a bit confusing, but she's great

Dr. Shepler is a good professor and explains things well, but at a fast pace. Her tests are difficult, so be prepared to study a ton! You can skip half of the daily work assignments and still get full daily work points, so that's pretty cool.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Dr. Shepler is one of the most caring professors you will ever have. So many opportunities to get full credit for assignments. Grade replacement on the final will SAVE you. Amazing through covid times and very understanding.

Dr. Shepler is a great professor, but she's tough. She gives clear grading expectations and is really good at explaining concepts, but you will have to work to do well in this course. Her tests are much harder than the practice she gives, but doing previous exam questions (which she provides) is how you can succeed. A great choice for CHEM 1211.

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Dr. Shepler is the way to go for Chem1211. She was the hands down, the best teacher I had this semester, especially with everything going on with COVID. She gives you everything you need to succeed in her class through Canvas. The material can be tricky, but shes always there to help. She CARES. She is AMAZING!

Dr. Shepler is amazing! She is very caring towards her students and did everything she could to make the online learning format easier for everyone. Expect a LOT of work (pre-lecture, in-class, and HW + lab) but it does help you learn. There is a ton of content, but Dr. Shepler makes it interesting.

Good teacher. Easy participation points. Lecture isn't really to cover material but rather practice it. Tests are harder than practice question, but she does give a ton of practice. Really nice person.
She is an amazing professor, who is extremely caring and gives great lectures. Her exams are fair, and her course is organized in a way that benefits students. Can't wait to take her for 1212!

Dr. Shepler is willing to explain any questions and clarify any topics, I would 100% take Chem with her. She will not extend deadlines or let you turn things in late, but if you attend lectures and do all your work you will do just fine. The way the class is set up allows you to miss a few assignments and still have an A.

Dr. Shepler is a good choice. She is caring, and she is willing to help her students. Lectures and assignments are easy if you watch her lectures. Contents get pretty difficult throughout the course, which means more studying. Tests are much more difficult than assignments, but there are tons of resources available.

Dr. Shepler is known as one of the best professors at Georgia Tech and there's a good reason why. She's incredibly helpful, knows what she's talking about, and extremely nice. She always tried to brighten our spirits with fun lectures. Be prepared to watch pre-lecture videos 15-50 minutes (average 30 minutes). Her tests are open note/open book.

Stupid hard class, but Shepler is the best. I had some life things going on, and she was SUPER accommodating. I had also never taken chem, so this class was a pain. I probably studied for it 10-12 hours per week at a minimum. Labs are terrible unless you have a great TA, and even so. Shepler is amazing though & knows her stuff. Go to office hours!!

Short summer session. Long pre-lecture vids taught new content. Lectures were all practice problems. Her teaching was fine, but with so much material to cover, I had to commit a LOT of my time to studying. Tests were open note, but the tradeoff is that they're all free response. She gives a ton of practice exams. Take good notes, manage time, study

Dr. Shepler is really clear and really enthusiastic. She is able to deliver new material concisely and with a lot of analogies, to help students understand. She is also really flexible and cares about her students. She is a great presenter (even online!) and adapted really well to online challenges.

-Topic videos and reading passages were sent before class to preface each lecture's material -Worksheets were handed out to each student and problems were worked through in groups -She uses a timer to keep her lesson plans on track with time for questions -Has loads of office hours + super approachable/friendly -Writes her own exams

SHE IS AMAZING. She cares so much about her students and is willing to put in extra time to help them succeed. She prepares you for tests and gives you so many resources to succeed. Take her for chem if you can!

Dr. Shepler is probably the most caring professor in GT. She makes it a pleasure to come to class every day because she is so energetic & kind. The class is very heavy with lab & requires a lot of time, but the concepts are generally easy; there is just a lot of work with hws & labs. Exams are straightforward, and she has grade-replacement w/ final

Dr. Shepler was the best professor I had during my freshman year. She explains course concepts clearly and thoroughly, and the test questions reflect what you learn. She also is always available to help, and will do so willingly. I would definitely love to have her as a professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor for 2214! It is a challenging class, but she makes lecture easy. She is a very fair grader that gives lots of partial credit. If you have extra questions, you can always reach out to her, and she will be very helpful in explaining difficult concepts. Lab is a separate component graded largely on accuracy and led by TAs.

Dr. Shepler makes Chem 1310 a VERY easy class. If you took chem in highschool, you will get an A or B without a doubt. Each test is 20 MC questions. If you do the practice tests, you will be fine. Shepler is super nice but can be a bit cringy sometimes in lecture. Just bear through it.

Great professor. Cares a lot about her students and is a great lecturer too. No complaints on her. The class is on the easier side and there is a grade replacement policy for the midterms (using the final). The only thing to be aware off is that there are clicker questions every class and they count for participation credit.
She was incredible.

She is a great professor and cares about her students a lot. Her tests are not bad but they are all multiple choice so no partial credit. Labs are interesting and not bad. The class was not bad and I still learned a lot.

Dr. Shepler has to be one of the kindest professors to walk this campus. She cares for every single student like none other and is extremely approachable outside of class. In terms of lecture, she explains everything in a way it's as if she's telling a story, and Chemistry becomes very easy to understand. If you're given a chance to taker her do it

Dr. Shepler is lecture heavy. While she does a good job explaining concepts, math problems are not always clearly explained. Exams are a really big part of the grade and there are no extra credit opportunities. The final exam offers grade replacement but I would not recommend banking on the final for grade replacement as the exam is hard.

She is a very caring person who truly wants her students to learn and wants to help them do their best. She gives good lectures explaining the material and is approachable if you have questions. By far the most caring professor Ive had so far.

Dr. Shepler is an amazing teacher, especially for your first chemistry course at Georgia Tech. Very good lecturer, with very good analogies. And let me tell you something - Fun Science Fridays - that is all I have to say about that. If you have a choice choose Dr. Shepler, you will not regret it

Dr. Shepler is an amazing teacher, especially for your first chemistry course at Georgia Tech. Very good lecturer, with very good analogies. And let me tell you something - Fun Science Fridays - that is all I have to say about that. If you have a choice choose Dr. Shepler, you will not regret it.

This course is challenging (covers a lot of materials in depth), and it is nice to take it with Dr. Shepler as she explains everything thoroughly and is clear on what will be on tests. Lab in this class is VERY TOUGH (about half of your lab grade is based on your accuracy in your labs).

Chemistry is very enjoyable and easy with Dr. Shepler. Her lecture slides are easy to follow, the class is engaging, tests are straightforward and multiple-choice, and you are allowed a crib sheet on tests. She is also very friendly and overall a great person!

Dr. Shepler is very caring and a very good professor. She is good at explaining, is a very fair professor, and genuinely seems to care for her students. If you have a choice of CHEM 1211K professors, Dr. Shepler is a very good choice!
She is very good at giving advice. One of the best professors at Georgia tech

Carrie Shepler is most certainly one of the best Gen Chem professors at GT (if not the best), and I absolutely loved her course. One of my bigger fears coming into Tech was taking Chemistry, as I had a terrible high school experience, but Dr. Shepler made Chem extremely approachable and fascinating. Her lectures were worth taking an 8 am class.
Loved lectures with Dr. Shepler (even though they were at 8am). She has great ways to teach concepts. Previewing material will really help you in this class.

Dr. Shepler is a gem. I went to quite a few office hours, and you can tell she was born to teach. She can identify students' points of confusion and really help them. This course can be hit or miss on the difficulty depending on the student. I got too confident and paid the price for it, so stay ahead and you'll do great. I never used my book.
Dr. Shepler is an outstanding professor. She is definitely one of the best teachers ever.

Truly cares for her students. Lectures are well organized and informative, with each topic receiving ample explanation. There are clicker questions, but you should already be attending anyways to take notes. You'll have to work for your grade, but it's nothing exceedingly strenuous.

Best prof for gen chem at GT. IMO gen chem is an easy A at GT no matter the prof, but Shepler is great and certainly has the best lectures. Also while she does do clicker questions, they are not required to get an A in the class (although going to class and doing them can help your grade).

Dr. Shepler was one of the best professors I have had so far at Tech. I disliked chemistry in high-school, but she found a way to make chemistry enjoyable. She explains difficult chemistry concepts in a relatively simple manner and does everything she can to help you out. She cares for all her students and is very approachable during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Shepler was really great at explaining things in lecture and making sure everyone understood it with her examples.

A true angel. Amazing teacher that will do anything for you. Good trade off for how difficult/dreadful the class is for non chem majors. Read the book & go to class & youre set! Also, go to office hours if you love yourself.
She is an enjoyable teacher and makes lectures on chemistry not terrible. She also is my best teacher this year.

She's a good teacher, which is what matters. She explains concepts well and thoroughly and helps you understand the material. She was also, however, very rude to me and unnecessarily harsh when it came to slight procedural discrepanciesto the point where it felt like she would argue with me for and only for the sake of argument.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Shepler was great! In lecture (not mandatory necessarily but there are clicker questions) she made sure the material made sense, especially for the abstract concepts. She made it clear to the class that she was able to help and posted her office hours often! The tests were difficult and tricky, but I would definitely take Shepler again!

Dr. Shepler defines it means to go above and beyond. Tests are like 20 multiple choice and fairly difficult, but her lectures are engaging and thorough. Daily work  easy, as long as you complete every hw. She is super genuine and wants you to succeed -- even offers late night sessions on Piazza! Work hard all semester and you'll likely make an A.

Must take Shepler for intro chem classes. She's extremely organized, explains things thoroughly and entertainingly, and she lays out exactly what you need to do to pass the course. If you do a couple practice exams (without looking up the answers) and make the crib sheet off her complete notes, things should be a breeze. + hw is always on chegg

Shepler was an amazing lecturer, and definitely the best choice for Chem 1211k. She used clear and helpful analogies to help students understand concepts better and was super helpful during office hours. She also gives you lots of resources to help you succeed (practice test, reading guides, extra help, etc). She really cares about her students!!

Dr. Shepler is a fantastic, hard-working professor. She truly cares about the education AND well-being of her students. While you could get by with just reading the textbook and doing practice questions, you'd truly be missing out. Her lectures are unparalleled with any others at Tech (that I've been).

CHEM1310 is a pretty heavy class, especially for those who have never taken Chem before. However, Dr. Shepler manages to make the situation better by providing solid explanation of concepts, and being a caring professor overall. It is hard to get a seat in her class sections, as she is one of the better Chem professors.

Shepler is an amazing professor! Her lectures were great, and she always made them as interesting as possible. She uses great analgies, and is great at explaining concepts especially in office hours. Really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She can sometimes get behind on material and pacing, but its not too bad.
While it was hard getting to her 8AM class, it was worth it for her lectures. She cares a lot for the students and offers plenty of office hours, especially the week of exams.

Dr. Shepler is a great lecturer and teaches everything in an understandable and basic way. I was doing just okay in the class until I attended her office hours for the 2 weeks leading up to the final, and I finished with an A. She is very accessible outside of class and will take all the time you need to explain difficult concepts.

Lectures were pretty good and she really cares about her students. Her office hours were always really crowded so I ended up going to TA office hours a lot. If you review the old tests and do a thorough review of your notes you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Highly recommend for any chem class. Lectures were rich and I would actually feel like Im missing out if I didnt go. Made a B but could have easily made an A if I took advantage of her office hours. Her humor for the most part is actually kinda entertaining. Review old tests. Don't waste too much time on online hw as they weren't really helpful
Dr. Shepler is an awesome professor! She's very approachable and wants us all to succeed. Make sure your do a bunch of work on your own for this class; it will help you get that A.

Definitely one of the best professors at tech. Very cheerful and funny during the 8 am lectures. Definitely go to office hours after each test and ask how to do all the questions you got wrong. I noticed she used very similar questions from the tests on her final.

Shepler is an amazing and intellectual chemistry professor. The only thing is she goes at a high school pace, which is more preference than anything. She is very fair though -- if you don't reach a topic in lecture, you aren't responsible for it.
Shepler is one of the best teachers I've had at Tech. Class is challenging, but she is more than willing to help you inside and outside of class. Office hours are incredibly helpful.

A lot of my friends really liked Dr. Shepler and while I have to admit that she was a good and enthusiastic lecturer, she was very unsympathetic and rude when being dealt with one-on-one outside of class, a side of her that most people did't see, but myself and a few friends saw come out big-time

Shepler's lectures are entertaining and easy to follow; her analogies are hilarious and actually make you understand. Chem 1310 is a tough class (doesn't matter who your teacher is), but Shepler made is a little more simple and easy.

Idk mixed feelings because everyone loves her, and maybe I'm just bad at chem but like her lectures didn't resonate well with me and I wasn't able to understand material from the slides well because she went through them so quickly, and the class itself requires so much outside work.

She is THE 1310 teacher to take. Most students taking this class will never use Chemistry again and she makes it as easy as possible for us. Her lectures are great as she incorporates humor and is very lively, but it's chemistry so not everyone is interested. The homework always required more than one person to do, but the exams were forgiving.

Amazing lectures! But you can't learn everything in class, of course. You will have to study hard to get an A, but the grade improvement system makes that a whole lot easier. Lab takes up a lot of time, but don't blow it off, because it is 20% of your grade. Study really hard for the final, and you can definitely get an A. I failed every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Shepler genuinely cares for the students. Office hours are very accessible, and I recommend going (even to see what others ask) especially before exams. Most in the class aren't chem-related majors, but she makes it interesting and easy to succeed (but you have to try!). Practice exams are helpful to study, and use her PPT slides to take notes.
Not too bad.  Work and you'll get an A especially if you took chem recently in highschool.

I love Dr. Shepler! Her lectures are easy to follow and she makes a lot of difficult concepts easy to understand. She will also go out of her way to provide office hours and extra help to those who need it. That being said, this class requires a lot of work, especially with the lab component added on. You have to put in a lot of effort to get an A.
She expects a lot but if you are willing to do the work, your grade will be fine. She is also excellent at teaching and explaining tough concepts.

Dr. Shepler is awesome. I had her for 1211, and I have her now for 1212. She is always willing to help you and is very supportive both academically and personally. If you go to office hours, she remembers you by name. She has comical ways of remembering tricky concepts. If you wanted to get an A in the class, you definitely could.

Dr. Shepler was an amazing teacher and I really adore her as a person in general. She's very quick to email you if you don't do so hot on an exam and is always there to help you get back on track. Her exams are super tough, but if you print out lecture notes, get help for things you need, and thoroughly cover the practice exams you'll be fine.

She's basically the Mary Poppins of chemistry. If you have the opportunity to take her as a professor - JUST DO IT. Seriously, she's there for her students and relates complex topics in easy-to-understand ways. Definitely my favorite professor for my first semester of college. I didn't get an A, but it's only because I didn't put the effort in.
Basically, you get an A if you want to. Do the practice exam questions and the A comes naturally

I did not care for her teaching. She explains things well and is there for her students, but I honestly think she has a very limited understanding of chemistry. This could explain why her class is easier because when pushed for a deeper explanation she doesn't know it. I guess that is why she only teaches freshmen courses.
Amazing professor. She teaches with a lot of enthusiasm. Many opportunities to get good grades. Go to class and to office hours if you need it. Bareable amount of homework.

Dr. Shepler is one of the most AMAZING professors I have ever had! I wish she taught all of my classes. She is so nice and super helpful and patient in office hours. Her office hours are everyday, and she is always willing to schedule meetings with you if her office hours don't work. Lectures are very interactive.  Get her if you can (SERIOUSLY!)

Tests are tough, but always fair. Homework is helpful, but the system is annoying, so make sure to plan time for homework. Really cares about students, and tries to make sure that every student taking Chem 1212 (not necessarily her classes, just that class in general) can find an office hour to get help.

Dr. Shepler  is great. She tries to make it as interesting as possible and that helped me understand better. Sometimes there will be group work during lecture. Basically you work with neighbors to answer questions. Didnt really care for that.
Definitely the best CHEM professor at GT!

Lectures are really engaging and funny. She really tries hard to make sure you're learning optimally. The best professor for 1310 by a long shot. Really helpful, sends lots of emails explaining everything. Tests are exactly what you'd expect. Cribs sheets allowed. Homework relatively optional (though REALLY helpful.)
DR. SHEPLER IS THE ONLY CHEM 1310 PROFESSOR YOU SHOULD CONSIDER. PLEASE. She is a goddess. One of the best teachers I've ever had.

Out of all the CHEM 1310 professors, Dr. Shepler is by far the most engaging. She goes at a slower pace than other professors but only because she wants everybody to learn. All classes have the same test, and I've gotten an A on every one just by reviewing the annotated lecture notes. That being said, attendance isn't mandatory but it's beneficial.
Amazing, amazing teacher. Way better than a lot of the other CHEM 1310 professors. Explains concepts very well and truly cares about you as a student. Highly recommend.

One of my favorite teachers! Lectures are clear, helpful, and informative and tests are straightforward, not hard at all if you study. She lets you write up a cheat sheet for each test including the final. Really cares about her students and majorly sparked my interest in the subject and motivated me to do well in the class. Take her!!

Fantastic teacher!  Cares about her students (but no room in the syllabus really for smudging of grades, so you get what you get) and teaches the material really well.  Go to office hours, be vocal in class (ask questions!).  She wants to help.

Great teacher! She knows her chemistry and can explain it clearly and with jokes! She doesn't get off topic that much which is good so you actually learn what will be on tests. Study and do practice problems before tests and you can make an A or B.
Awesome teacher. She will always make sure you understand and are prepared. Don't ever feel intimidated to speak to her. My favorite class, so far at Tech.

Dr. Shepler is amazing. I wasn't even in her class but I didn't learn anything my teachers (Wine first 1/2 of semester, El-Sayed second 1/2), so I started going to her lectures. She is very engaging and you can tell she is passionate about her students learning. Go to all of her lectures regardless of who you actually have.

Dr. Shepler is so fun and engaging! She always keeps class interesting. Her office hours are really helpful too! Not a necessarily easy class, but if you go to lecture and review practice problems, it is easy to do well!

Great teacher! She definitely knows what she is talking about and is really passionate about the subject. Go to class and pay attention and do the practice problems and you will do well! Read old tests for the final and you should do well!

Shepler is a really great teacher.  I went to class everyday and took notes and the only studying I needed to do for tests was to complete her practice questions.  She is very helpful and loves it when people got to office hours.

Very passionate and entertaining professor! Her lectures are easy to understand, and she's willing to help her students. BEWARN she's not an easy A professor, you MUST work hard in her class to get A. If you don't come to lectures and don't prepare for the tests, you can easily end up with a D in this class.

Dr. Shepler is very intelligent, energetic, and entertaining. All chemistry courses at GT are extremely challenging and they expect you to come in with a certain level of knowledge, but it is possible to do well if you work hard. I recommend her or Dr. Russell for Chem 1211.

Dr Shepler is an amazing professor! Her lectures are not only super helpful, but they're usually pretty fun. She starts each lecture with a random chem-related song, and is always joking around with us in class. She is very into helping her students succeed, and is GREAT about posting helpful things online. You can   do well in her class if you try

Really great teacher, she's extremely helpful if you need her. Classes aren't mandatory, but she does a great job explaining things. Just focus on studying for each test in depth and you should do great. She's honestly one of the best professors I've ever had.
Great teacher. My class is really dumb though so she has to spend a lot of time explaining like we're 5 year olds. Not her fault though. Take her or Russell if you can.
So hot I wish she didn't have a husband!
She's a really good teacher, but it doesn't really matter, because the class isn't difficult at all (assuming that you have a solid background in chemistry).

I had this class at 8am MWF and I missed about 2 classes and hated when I did. She is an absolutely GREAT teacher who loves what she does and makes it interesting and understandable for everyone else. She usually has regular weekly review sessions which are very helpful and a chat room on certain nights.I was happy I was stuck with that 8am class!

Be thankful if you get Dr. Shepler. She loves teaching and wants you to do well. WebAssign is a little tough and some questions on the tests are iffy, but overall it is a very good class. You should do very well if you take the time to study and attend class

Carrie Shepler is one of my favorite professors. She met with me whenever I needed help and is a prompt emailer. The class is really hard, but she makes it as bearable as possible. Best chem professor, hands-down.

omg!! she's really great! I know her since my professor was absent for some business. Since then, I audit her every lecture. She's really helpful, explain things so clear especially for the chapter 5,about the crystal atoms.Before audit of her class, I got only 77 out of 100 or something but as I attended her class, I hit 100 for every exam.
she is amazing amazing as hell, i beasted the class with a 97.8! if you have an option, choose her!

Dude Doctor Shepler is da bomb. She is quite possibly the best teacher I have ever had. Go to class even though she puts the note online, explains things so well. Never even crack textbook open, tests are a kinda hard, but not too terribly difficult.
She is an awesome teacher. She really wants her students to understand and teaches in a way that we can comprehend. She goes out of her way to host tons of office hours too!
She was a great teacher. Extremely entertaining, and really knew her stuff. Very approachable and willing to spend as long as it takes for you to understand the material.

She is an excellent professor, she does and excellent job at making basic chemistry seem easy. She is very eager to help students, take advantage of office hours and going to her for help. Highly recommended.
Very helpful and easy to talk to
LOVE DOC SHEP! GREAT HELP THROUGHOUT COURSE AND GREAT RESOURCE

Though she was my GT1000 prof, which she did great with that too, she helped me so much with chemistry. I felt like I was in her class. She knows her material very well and "dumbs" it down so that everyone can understand. She has lots of office hours and encourages everyone to take advantage. Overall, I recommend her 100%
Shepler is always willing to help out. She uses the PRS quizzes to try and assure attendance. Good professor for gen chem. As long as you at least try a little, an A or B is guaranteed.
LOVE HER!!!  Really helpful and amazingly sweet.  I recommend her 100%!!
She actually cares about teaching class! Her class convinced me to switch majors
Very nice and approachable in comparison to Dr. Cox who teaches it with her. Definitely cares about her students and how they do.
One of the best profs!!  Really nice, helpful, and patient.  Recommend her 100%.
Excellent teacher all around, if you have any questions go to her office she is extremely nice and will walk you through anything. Do all the extra credit at the end and the final will be a breeze.

Dr. Shepler is amazing! She posts all her notes online, and actually makes chemistry interesting. She gives analologies that are easy to remember. And, she allows a crib sheet on each test. She grades fairly and is easy to approach. If you have to take 1310, Dr. Shepler is who you want to teach it.

very good teacher. Dr. Shepler was extremely helpful with any questions and also had very good notes prepared for class every day. all of my friends came to her reviews and wished that they had her. she and Dr. cox are the best chemistry teachers in the school, and for 1310 there classes share the same tests. get one of these two teachers.

Dr. Wang is an angel on earth. He is the best prof that NRE department has and he must be protected at all cost. He covers everything that you need to know for the class/exams during his lectures. As long as you attend the lectures and take notes, you can easily get an A.
Very knowledgeable but can go off topic sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests were curved and lab reports were graded easily by the TA. Getting a A in the lab portion is easy. The midterm and final are more difficult.
Grade was based entirely on tests. Tests are curved heavily. Test were similar to homework.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Average
What's in the book is different from what he teaches in class which is different from what's on the homework. The best part? The tests have nothing to do with the other three things either!

Take Dr. Haines for Survey of Orgo!! He explained the content well, and lectures were very engaging. It was a bucket point system with lots of bonus point opportunities, so it was easy to get an A without taking the final. Midterms were carbon copies of the study guide he gives out.

What a wonderful professor! He's super good at explaining and makes everything easier to understand even though I struggled in organic chemistry. He's also really funny and keeps the class engaging. If I ever get the chance to take him again, I definitely will. He made my last semester at RVCC so much better.

An absolutely amazing professor who genuinely cared about the success of his students. He made it clear the first day of class that he wanted to work with us and offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. I would definitely take any of his classes again. 100% recommend!

Genuinley a kind hearted man. I dont think there was a class I dreaded, because even if Im not the strongest in orgo, he did his best to teach us. I would take another class of his in a heartbeat. Take his class if given an opportunity.
I will never forget how amazing this professor was, he made an almost 3 hour lecture so engaging and enjoyable. AMAZING, AWESOME, COOL and very knowledgeable.

Nicest professor I've ever had. He actually spent time going over concepts (like hybridization) that he knew we didn't remember from gen chem. Lots of extra credit opportunities and test corrections, so it was very possible to do well in his class. Extremely caring person and teacher.
Great class and professor - as someone who didn't have the best lab skills; he and his TAs SK and Brian were amazing at guiding me through this class. Learned a lot and was low stress.
This man was the best professor I've EVER had. SO CARING AND NICE AND SWEET!

Truly an amazing professor who cares deeply about his students and the course content. I was scared of chemistry from general chem 1 and 2, but he made orgo much less intimidating and understands how to explain difficult topics in easier ways. There is plenty of extra credit and the letter grading is very lenient.

Incredible lecturer, sorry to see him go but glad he was here while he was here. Ample extra credit opportunities, fair grading, and engaging lectures. All in all made the dreaded Orgo 1 feel like it wasn't going to kill me after all.

He gave us practice tests that were almost identical to the real exam, he recorded all the lectures, he gave us amazing study guides, and offered so much grade replacement. In addition, his lectures were amazing and he explained concepts very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: SUCH A GOOD ORGO 2 PROFESSOR! I dont think many people leave organic chemistry 2 with positive reviews about the class, but this professor made the class so engaging and easy to understand. I was very worried about the class, but he really cares about the students and understands that GPAs matter. If you can take this class with him, do it!

Dr. Haines is an amazing professor!!! If you have the chance to take a chem class with him, take it!! His lectures are super entertaining and informative! I was worried for Orgo 2, but Dr. Haines made it a great experience!
Chris is the best professor ever! Someone who cares about the material and his students. 10/10 would take his class again

Dr. Haines is undoubtedly the best professor I've had in my 3 years at GT. He entered every class with a passion for teaching orgo & a knack for breaking down hard concepts to make them easy to understand. He always shared what helped him most when he was a student. His humor & enthusiasm in lecture made us engaged & able to learn quickly. 11/10!

Definitely take Orgo 2 with him! He's super chill and actually cares about his students, which is hard to find at Tech! He made challenging material actually fun to learn. It's rare to leave Orgo 2 feeling like you learned something and got a good grade—but with him, it's totally possible!

The best professor Ive ever had at tech. He really cares about his students succeeding and is really fair with grades. Dr Haines. also actually taught the concepts behind orgo, instead of relying on you to read the textbook or memorize reactions. He also offered extra credit plus test remediation, and was very responsive to feedback.

this dude makes it possible to actually get an A, and he teaches in a way where you actually learn and gives you a ton of opportunities to raise your grade. also this is coming from someone who averaged 65s on exams in orgo 1, with him i averaged 85s

Best professor I've ever had, so passionate about organic chemistry but so thorough. Lectures are recorded but honestly showing up to class is better because he's hilarious and is so wonderful at explaining material. Also very understanding and genuinely wants to help you learn
He is literally the best professor at Georgia Tech. He cares so much about his students, where this is really rare to see in professors. Sad that he's leaving tho :(

Organic chem II has a lot of content but Dr. Haines makes it manageable. HE IS LITERALLY AN ANGEL. he is so funny, kind, and understanding. he made his class less stressful by providing flexible due dates and practice tests. he always puts his students first and he is my favorite professor at tech! TAKE HIM :)

He's literally the best professor I've had at GT. So caring and accessible, doesn't make you feel bad for making mistakes or not understanding material. Def recommend him 1000/10! Explains content in a very easy way and his tests are almost identical to the practice tests. So glad I took him.

very entertaining and engaging lectures. always felt bad whenever i missed a lecture, but he posts them all online. with tons of opportunity to make up your grade, such as test corrections for each test, extra credit assignments, and optional final with grade replacement. exams mirror the practice exams, so they are not bad. awesome professor!!!

He was an amazing professor! It was clear that student success was his top priority, so he worked really hard to make the class fair and provide students with opportunities to learn and improve. He responds great to feedback and all lectures are posted online.

Dr. Haines is probably one of the best professors I've had at Tech. He makes learning a very difficult class like orgo 2, actually enjoyable and really cares about his students doing well. He responds really well to feedback and his practice exams are reflective of actual exams. If you can take him for orgo 2, I definitely recommend it!

Dr. Haines was genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. He's very understanding of the load on college students, and adjusts his course accordingly. He took time to answer every question, would make additional office hours if you needed help, and was incredibly understanding when my semester was upended. He's funny and makes orgo fun.

LOVED him. He made Organic Chemistry feel really interesting and enjoyable to learn. His exams didn't throw massive curveballs and he himself is a breath of fresh air after taking Chem 1 and 2 at this school. He is my favorite professor I've ever had at GT. Take him if you can!!
Simply the goat.

best professor at tech, really funny, super cool and yeah. also he understood this was survey of orgo and the material was easy and the threshold for an A was super easy to meet without taking the final

This guy is the best professor at Tech. He is so chill and understanding. You immediately can tell he loves his job so much and is always excited to help you at literally any time. Super good at explaining complex chemical topics, definitely a super smart guy. Absolutely the most relatable and understanding guy in the chemistry department. GOAT

If you want an A in Dr. Haines class you will get one. The class is graded using point thresholds so if you get that many points you get that grade. If you did every single assignment and then got 70s on each midterm you can opt out of the final. I have never had a professor make me want to come to lecture so much let alone a chemistry lecture.

Dr. Haines is a legendary professor. He is so chill and it makes it really easy to go to him whenever you need help. Also, he is super understanding and is willing to work with you if you don't understand why something is necessary on an assignment. In lab he wont just give you the answer if you ask him, but help you come to it yourself.
he's literally just a chill guy
one of the best professors i have had so far at tech

He explains complicated concepts that I used to struggle with in a way that is easy to understand. He made orgo interesting and fun. He is also funny and a genuinely nice dude. He made his tests intentionally easy and similar to practice exams. Take his class for an easy A or B with a caring and smart professor who is fun and inspiring.

Dr. Haines was genuinely one of my favorite professors that I have had so far. This is his first year teaching and he did a phenomenal job. He made me have even more curiosity for chemistry! He is friendly and his lectures are super easy to understand. If you keep up with the practice worksheets and the practice tests you will for sure get an A.

I cannot express how amazing of a professor he is. This was the first time he taught this class and he did amazing. If you have the option to take him do it! I hate chemistry and he made it easy to learn and enjoyable. If you go to class you will succeed and get an A. His practice exams are identical to the exams.

Entire grade in the class was based on three exams and an optional final. He posted tons of resources for exams and was a very fair and sometimes even generous grader. I honestly wish I went to lecture more because I got behind and eventually stopped going. Super chill dude, take him if you can. Lectures are a little boring, but not awfully so.

Easiest and best professor ever, all tests were averaged high 90s, optional final, optional homework, notes can be a little difficult to understand, but our exam 3 was literally posted online as a resource.

He's super lenient with grading and his lectures (+ lecture notes) are pretty straightforward. The quizzes are based off the homework and he goes over stuff in class too. Scheduling a makeup quiz from being sick was also a very easy process. Overall he cares about his students! Please take him :D

Prof. Citrin is the nicest professor I've ever had. The class is typically difficult but he really wants you to succeed. Class is 100% tests/final, but he grades *SO* leniently, it'll blow you away. Finished the class with a 95+ and I get to skip the final. He's actually the goat. Take him and protect him at all costs
I would fight and die for him.

3 tests (optional final), no other grading categories. Other than that, an absolutely amazing professor with great lectures! His notes carried my studies from start to finish with enough details to cover all questions. Take this prof at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor only teaches during summers at GTE from what I know. Makes it clear he wants everyone to succeed in his class, which is notoriously challenging, while still enjoying their summer abroad. Easier quizzes, and homework's that are incredibly helpful, allow you to learn the material well whilst still receiving a high grade in a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Citrin really goes into depth during his lectures and will show you the math behind all the signals concepts. His exams are fair and the homework really helps with solidifying knowledge. He sometimes makes errors when lecturing so it can be a bit confusing but overall I feel like I learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First two units are pretty easy and test questions are pulled from old tests or homework. Lectures are pretty good and available online. Last unit is harder but test wasn't too bad. Build a buffer with the first two. Put in the effort and you'll be fine. He's a very understanding prof who gets student priorities.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: took online sync. Made groups of students present a topic, made comments on it, and that was her lecturing. Felt very low effort from her. didn't feel like she prepped you for the tests. shes alright. 3 tests + participation + 7 assignments spread out through the semester meant to be one big group project. Didn't mind the group project

I ended the class with an 89.4, which she rounded which was nice. However I still can't recommend her. Tests included material we didn't go over in class, so you'd have to read the extremely long textbook. Boring class, overly detailed tests that really could bog your grade down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class content is very interesting but the lectures are so boring. Attendance is mandatory and she calls on people randomly even if they do not raise their hand. Also makes people turn on cameras over zoom. She's a bit sassy sometimes when people don't and will call you out. Tests are not bad but are honor locked and over lots of content

When grading, she is picky about what she wants to see or hear from a presentation. Missing slight details can result in major point deductions. The exams carry a ton of weight, and keeping a high grade depends on the outcome of said exams, thus, one must rely on reading all of the required chapters of the textbook more than studying the lectures.

Despite the class being focused on attendance and group contributions, the bulk of the grade (75%) was on the three exams, which tested quite specific details from the long sections of the textbook. I was hoping to have some fun and work with my peers on the projects, but sadly most of it was stressful, spending many hours studying for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof.Citrin had the opportunity to make this class so much fun. Attendance to 3x weekly Zoom classes was required with camera on and active participation.
