It was a group project-based class, but the oddly specific tests held most of the weight in grades. Honestly, I wouldn't take this unless in a pinch, but she gets the job done if needed.

Definitely not my favorite professor. Pretty tough grader on group projects with random feedback. Tests are very specific. NO STUDY GUIDES other than the chapter numbers. She is also extremely passive aggressive and rude to students. Class content is actually interesting if you like marketing and can pay attention online.

Relies too much on the textbook, which is really long, for exams. Random tidbits from the book that were never discussed in class will be in your exams and final. Will not round grades. Thoroughly go over the book and slides, because even a single sentence can be a question in your exam. Attendance required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Boring. You basically do group work for the semester and then do a presentation that is not really related to the group work, it's just on a section/chapter of her slides. Exams are a lil too detailed and some questions didnt seem to be something she taught.

Not my favorite but was a good class to take if you can lock in for an hour online lecture each class. Work outside of class feels like busy work. She's very accessible outside of class though. Expect for her to ask where you are every class.

Lots of group work. Took her online and never went to non-mandatory attendance days bc she just read off slides. Sweet lady, but she was very adamant on everyone turning on cameras and would call people out. Tests very detail focused; don't expect 100 ever. Mostly just busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. Her lectures were brutal to sit through and completely devoid of useful information. She is condescending and doesn't explain things well. She was completely uninterested in making sure her students did well on the tests. Any other professor would be better. Took at GTL, and she wouldn't round an 89.5 to an A.

This class is based primarily on group projects and its an ongoing one at that. I really enjoyed the class even though some of the lectures and reading were kind of boring. Good class to learn a little and get a good grade.

I feel like Dr. Citrin knows a lot about marketing but missed the opportunity to make it something that was really exciting for students. When asking for help, it didn't seem like she was very interested in doing so (besides saying to read the book). I didn't love the structure of the class overall in terms of lecture style or tests.
Her lectures are actually terrible and you have no clue what she will actually test you over.

Great Professor! Attendance only mandatory when there are project workdays! otherwise she doesn't take attendance! Class very easy! Just read the book and her ppts and you will get an A in this class! She is also a very nice, caring , and sweet person!

She has a bad attitude and doesn't explain expectations clearly. Her tests are pretty easy. If your okay with getting a B, don't even bother to put any effort to the marketing project (worth only 15%, and a ton of work). Take it for your GPA , not the professor or interest in the subject.

Its a mandatory class. No one cares. She is nice enough and it's a easy A but she tries to make an incredibly easy subject more complex than it really is. If you go to class you don't even need to buy the textbook. But you will probably want to pull your hair out.
Caring teacher.  She clearly wanted students to learn and used a multitude of techniques to teach.  I enjoyed the small group sessions and video cased used to break up the lectures.
Alka just reads from Power points. Its not a hard class, its just hard to stay awake. Don't fall asleep...she will notice and call you out.

I believe Dr. Ciavatta did a good removing most of the fluff while lecturing on content that is applicable to other biology courses. He is very generous with grading and approachable when necessary. Participate in class and review learning catalytics and you should be fine.
Very hard to reach, and the grading system is only based on three tests in the entire semester. I had to email two or three times before he responded!

Dr. Ciavatta is a wonderful man but is not the ideal 2600 professor. He ran out of time on lecture almost every day and dropped an exam because the vast majority of the class failed the first one; he would release homeworks as late as a day before they're due. Upsides are he is considerate of student feedback and the class improved over time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ciavatta was nice, but he simply is not the best professor for genetics and is not the most knowledgeable on the subject. He relied on ppt slides that were pretty vague and uninformative. But, put in your best effort, do the HW and all of the LC, and read the textbook as needed, and you should be okay.
I would ignore the last 4 comments. You get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ciavatta is an expert in genetics, but unfortunately he did not teach it well. Lot of information on slides, plus you need to study textbook. First exam was too long, many did not finish, so he was forgiving with points for rest of semester. Granted that probably wont happen again and I want to write a good review but I can't after all of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures just feel like he's winging it; no clear pattern or flow from topic to topic, super monotone/boring. In class participation with learning catalytics which are just a waste of time. First exam average was a 55 and most students didn't finish. Just a really unprofessional and unprepared professor for a class that's required for most students

Has an accent but it isnt bad, lectures were pretty helpful, curves the class at the end, would say very good teacher compared to other calc 2 professors, one of the easier math classes I have taken at Tech

Antonio is a great guy and a great professor. He wants his students to do well and he's very approachable and friendly. His lectures are very thorough and comprehensive and he tries to make math interesting. You definitely have to work hard, but the assignments are fair (although in comparison, the tests were much harder than the quizzes and hw).

Had him for Calc 2 and he made a difficult subject much more manageable. 3 tests, 4 quizzes, online MML hw. 2 bonus points possible for recitation attendance. Antonio was an amazing professor and really wanted to help students succeed. Very approachable and clear with an awesome Italian accent. If you get the chance, TAKE ANTONIO!!!!

He is approachable and listens to the students. He is one of the few professors that seems to care about the students. He is fair and knows the subject well. Go to class and do the homework. The first test was the only difficult part of the class. Most of the class failed the first test, but after that the class was cake.

Great professor.  The class is not bad, just study and do the homework.  Make sure you study a lot for the first exam because it's really hard; the department made it so you don't finish it on time.  The second one is not bad, and neither is the final.
Dr. Russell is the absolute best. Definitely recommend him. He is very approachable and understanding and explains the material really well.
He is so great at explaining difficult concepts. I recommend him!
He is really good at explaining all the topics covered. His lectures are helpful and he keeps the class entertained. Tests are fair.
He is a great professor. Really cares about his students. It's a hard class but he helps out as much as he can. Explains things very well too.
Very fun, keeps the classes attention. Tests are tricky, but he's great at explaining obscure concepts.

Horribly unclear grading criteria. Asked for feedback on my project and he told me I had one thing wrong. I fixed it, submitted it, and ended up with a low grade for things that I didn't know were wrong. Advertises himself as a resource but doesn't clearly state what he's looking for. Went to him about my unhelpful case group and he blew me off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class and the professor were (are) awesome. He wants you to understand the topic, and is willing to help you get there. He also prepares you super well for the project at the end. You do have group projects throughout the semester, so be sure to pick a good group. Daily attendance questions.

Professor Clarke is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject, but still simplifies topics to make it easy to understand. He is always willing to help students with their careers, and brings in impactful guest speakers to help students find out which path is best for them. Easy 5/5
NA
Don't be tardy! He's smart, funny and oh-so-awkward. Definitely a great professor.

Lateness policy is ridiculous. He humiliates those that are even 5 min late for the rest of class and is completely unforgiving for any reason you may have for the tardiness. Grades tough without clearly telling you what he is looking for, there are no rubrics for the numerous case write-ups so you just have to hope that he'll like what you write
One of the best professors I have ever had.  You can't get any better than Clarke.  Clear, witty, insightful and connects well with students. He brings finance to life.
Great teacher
I will never forget his class.
Best professor I have ever had!
Pretty basic, straight-forward class...not very hard.
Cares whether students learn the material.
No Comments
No Comments
Good real life examples in class like baseball contracts & mergers/acquisitions.

He's a good professor and you can tell he's super into music. The course is just thick with info and hard to get into and study. Exams had multiple choice, true or false, short answer, and an essay question timed and Honorlock. The course was a lot, but he is genuinely a good guy who's really passionate about music and kind to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was great as a professor, the projects were a bit hard at times but if you start early it's fine and you should get through them. Just be expressive and make music you like and write that in the review and he will understand where you are coming from.

The lecture videos are very lighthearted and delivered well, and this is one of the few classes I've seen where the instructor is perhaps more active than the TAs. Information comes out pretty early, and there's plenty of support in online tutorials if you need help.

Class is pretty easy to get an A in, but you will have to do some work. Projects are graded based on meeting the requirements and not your musical ability, which I liked. Project 4 was pretty confusing, though. Exams were pure memorization, but class was a nice break from my other classes, and you can get creative with the projects.

If you are at all interested in jazz, take this class! Video lectures are pretty short but very thorough. I had fun going to jazz clubs with friends for the concert reports. Tons (up to ~30%) of easy extra credit. 4 online honorlock exams that are pure memorization of facts.
Easy class for humanities credit, and it is a great mind break from other classes. The only hard thing is going to concerts for the concert reports, but you will enjoy them when you are there.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class, this is without a doubt one of the kindest and most sympathetic professors I've ever had. He's very easy to reach via email and is always trying to make the experience better for the students he teaches. The video lectures are well done and help you work at your own pace which I really appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who's passionate about jazz and makes the content engaging. Since I took it in the summer, the pace felt a little intense, and there was a good amount of work, but it was manageable if you stayed organized and spread it out through the week. Definitely worth taking if you enjoy music and want a deeper understanding of jazz.

this class is not necessarily easy, but if you put in the effort an A is definitely attainable with all the extra credit. 2 reports, couples quizzes with unlimited attempts, and 4 honorlock exams. Its not an "easy A" elective because you do have to set aside time for it

MUSI3450 was pretty easy to get a good grade bc of the huge extra credit. However, be aware that the class takes effort, esp creative effort due to you creating musical compositions. It's fun, but be aware it's not a free A. Exams were straightforward, study guides are built well and really help but be aware you have listening questions

I took his MUSI 3630 class. It was overall a simple class. Four exams, two concert reports (which requires proof of going to a jazz concert), and quizzes with unlimited attempts. Provides a lot of extra credit, and he's super accomodating.
A wonderful professor who will have a lasting impact on me, in ways I may not fully realize until much later.

Musi 2013 - It isn't difficult to get a good grade in this class. Despite the substantial increase in workload compared to other classes in the program, there are plenty of opportunities to earn extra credit. The projects in this class and support from the professor validated my desire to study Music Technology.

I took MUSI 3630 (not listed) w/ Dr. Clark virtually during a short summer session. The workload can seem overwhelming at first but try not to be discouraged because there are plenty of extra credit opportunities. If you complete the assignments and at least look over all of the provided material before exams you will likely do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Music Theory with Dr. Clark was a very fun experience! However, there are tons of assignments to complete in the course that may be challenging for those without a music background. Although the content is tough, there is more than enough extra credit to pad your grade. I highly recommend taking this course!

Dr. Clark was a great lecturer! He was super charismatic, and his lectures were lots of fun. However, the lectures do not prepare you at all for the actual work load. It was ridiculously difficult stuff. Usually it focused on material not covered or barely covered in class. I took Physics 2 at the same time, and this class was much harder.
Really cool class, well done video lectures and project design.

Dr. Zeagler was a very kind and super chill professor. Lectures were mandatory but were short and concise and overall the class was not too difficult. Studio is where you need to actually interact but if you have a good group discussions are very fun. Would highly recommend.

He has amazing lectures and often tries to facilitate discussion among students. Lectures are short, but definitely informative, and he makes it abundantly clear that the class will be easy as long as you put in the work. If you do take him, make sure to participate! Most people don't, so it makes you stand out and will make lecture so much better!

Easy class; however, it entirely depends on your section TA. Some TAs legit don't care and give you a 100 for almost everything, and one in particular... is lets just say takes she takes her job too seriously.

Lectures were engaging and lasted 20-30 mins each. Tells you all the questions on the upcoming exams the class before, so you don't even need to study. 

Discussions vary based on TA, so this will be a hit or miss. Still, interesting and not difficult.

This is probably the easiest CS class you will take at Georgia Tech. 100% would take again.
Extremely good professor for this course, would 100% recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS DUDE, absolute goat. tells you what's on the test and CIOS is up to 5 points on final grade. Mandatory lectures are easy to attend, easiest class I've taken at tech. Couldn't recommend more.

I got the impression he was tired of teaching the course since not enough people engaged properly, but he taught the class well. Section was great and the TA I got did a great job of facilitating conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Very engaging professor. The readings can be very long, but you only have to skim them most of the time to be able to participate in lecture or studio. The class was interesting and I never dreaded going to lecture or studio (especially since he tells you what's on the exams). Don't procrastinate working on your term paper. CIOS bonus is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
HE IS THE GOAT I LOVE HIM!! And his CIOS incentive is great: 

75% of the class completes CIOS- 3 point addition to total grades.
85%- 4 point addition to total grades.
95%- 5 point addition to total grades.

so basically for us a 85.5 is an A

There is a lot of work for this class however. There is a lot of writing and a 10 page paper at the end.

It's unfortunate that you can tell most people aren't really engaged with this class, because Dr. Zeagler is a really enjoyable lecturer! He does a very good job of trying to spark discussion in class, while simultaneously making it as easy as possible to get an A. There is a TON of writing for this class, but none of it is graded especially harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Class wasn't too bad. Weekly readings can generally be skimmed over, there isn't an absurd amount of HW either and grading and exams are fairly easy. Dr. Zeagler tries to make class interesting and I did find the topic somewhat interesting - he was a fairly good lecturer overall. Please don't take until last minute to do the final term paper though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class isn't hard and Zeagler makes the class interesting.

I loved Dr. Zeagler's class. If you go to lecture you won't regret it, he's quite entertaining. His exams are very fair and if you've done most of the readings you'll be alright. His TAs were also great, I really enjoyed studio. People tend to stay quiet in his class so you can easily stand out as a student by answering a question once or twice.

Good professor that made it a flipped classroom. The class mainly relies on a group project that you get to choose. The midterm was a paper on a topic of your choose and the final was open note and take home. He had a attendance policy but as long as you work with your group you'll be fine. Great starting grad class and he was understanding.

Professor was a great guy who made an annoying requirement class interesting and to take. Lectures were a little dry but not really to his fault, it's just a large class with mandatory attendance where very few people are actually engaged. Some of the discussions were super interesting. Overall he was a great prof teaching a mid class.

Nice guy, and lectures although sometimes boring are pretty straightforward. Class is pretty easy, just a lot of writing. Section TA can be hit or miss. If you have a good one the class is very easy. Pretty good extra credit for doing CIOS.

super nice, chill guy! tries his best to make lectures engaging despite most people thinking the class is a joke. genuinely always looking for ways to improve and open to criticism about the structure of the course. really approachable and generally made ethics a bearable time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Zeagler is incredibly caring and understanding. He would push deadlines if they seemed a bit unreasonable. His exams are based on his lectures and are pretty simple. The hw assignments can be tedious but as long as you don't procrastinate too much, they should be fine.
Dr. Zeagler is a very enthusiastic professor who is passionate about ethics. I highly recommend taking his class.

Pretty good professor. Class wasn't too difficult, was maybe like an hour or two of work a week. Attendance was mandatory and the way it was done was a little messy.

Lectures were decently interesting. Tests were pretty easy and easy A's if you went to class
Dr. Zeagler is a pretty swell guy, though the lectures are sometimes flat. Tests were fair but not dead-easy. Tested mostly on material from slides. In-person attendance was mandatory for Fall 2022.

Do not take this course. I thought I was going to get a masters in HCI. This course killed that. Professors do not care about the course and copy/pasted assignments week to week. We rushed through "Design of Everyday things" reading 2 chapters a week only for the professors to stop showing up to lecture halfway through the semester. 

Disappointing

Took for ethics, you only need to go to recitations, lectures are not important. Nice and caring professor. Class is graded on recitation participation with TAs and a couple of papers that don't take too long to read, final was a longer paper about an area of our interests in ethics, easy A

Clint's a really mellow guy and that was translated into his teaching. He gave his students a lot of freedom and was receptive to the different approaches people took to their projects. He had a tendency to be vague at times, but he didn't mind answering lots of questions. It's obvious that he cares for his students.
I love this teacher! He really knows his stuff and he explains things in a funny way. He cares a lot about his students, too.

Wonderful lady, decent lecturer. She truly cares about you as a person, not just as a student (helped me land a research position). Exams get tougher as the semester goes on and homework can be hit or miss. Attendance is technically required (in-class clicker questions). Final project instead of exam, pretty much a guaranteed A on that.

She wasn't the best lecturer, but she cared about each student. I recommend reading the textbook because a lot of her lectures are just simplified explanations of the textbook. If you want a better explanation of what she says in class, read the textbook. She's also a nice grader and gives good explanations on your assessments, so that's a plus.
Unmatched by physics professors.

Very sweet and enthusiastic professor, but lectures were generally unhelpful. I know this class is meant to be an overview of modern physics, but it truly felt like equations were being thrown at us with little motivation. This would be fine if attendance wasn't for points which made us go to these unhelpful lectures.

This is for PHYS 2213 - she is super sweet and very enthusiastic. her teaching is very fast and you'll have to go back through the slides, but she provides great resources. Would recommend using the book, though it isn't required. the class was definitely hard, but the tests were fair and she's an easy grader

Berger's personality and vibe is great but the lectures were generally unhelpful. She went over concepts pretty quickly but the examples were sort of helpful. Labs were generally pretty good at helping you understand material. Tutoring will be your best friend. The test are absolute hell. If your taking this class, try to get Munoz.

Without having any prior physics experience, this class was very difficult for me and Professor Berger's lectures were only somewhat helpful. For the first half I found it manageable, but toward the end I found it easier to watch videos online than attempt to understand her explanations. That being said, she cared about the students deeply

Her accent at times makes it a little hard to understand what she is talking about, and her lectures are fine. Not the worst lecturer, but not the best either. The course content was manageable, but I had some background in Physics 1 knowledge already. The homework load was also relatively manageable, and the tests were fair.

She's super sweet, so asking her questions in class really helps. I would say that her lectures aren't amazing because she's really quiet and a little all over the place. However, the works level and grading was very doable.

Professor wrote on the small board at the front of the class for a lecture of over three hundred students. Instead of explaining the material she chooses to derive equations while running her class like a reverse classroom. While the only saving grace is the fact that her courses are Modern physics. Best suggestion would be listening to Munoz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Berger is not a good lecturer while the course coordinator, Professor Munoz is amazing. I did not feel ready for tests after attending Professor Berger's lectures and had to learn everything on my own. The class is structured fairly and the group work in addition to online resources are really helpful to succeed in the course.

Dr. Berger is very passionate about her lectures, but often does not focus on test-related material in a way that gives clear understanding of what is expected on exams. She works hand-in-hand with Dr. Alicea-Munoz, the course coordinator, which can make this class much more reasonable as you have access to Dr. Alicea's video lecture recordings.

Dr Berger is an amazing person and clearly loves physics a lot, however she's not the best lecturer. It is really hard to follow her lectures and she focuses on concepts that are not relevant to the exam. I probably would not have done as well in the course without the lectures from the other professor.

The only redeeming part about her class is that it's a Modern section. Comparing her to the other modern prof, Alicia-Munoz, the way Berger lectures makes no sense. The entire class is pretty much lost during every lecture, she just doesn't explain the concept or how its used. By a few weeks in half the class was watching Alicia's material instead.

Professor Berger is very accessible outside of class, which was very nice as it helped me understand a lot of the material as a third method of getting clarification (outside of lecture, edX). On the other hand, she did spend a lot of time doing derivations, and I found that you had to sit in the front as she wrote a lot on the whiteboard.

Really nice, accessible at office hours, wants her students to succeed. Not the best lecturer, goes off on derivation tangents instead of teaching important content. Variables used in equations are never fully defined with SI units and vector conventions. Stopped going to lecture ~week 4 and using EdX alone and group studying got me an A.

If you ask to meet outside of class, she'll always make time.
She genuinely cares about your learning.
She is not tech-savvy, so do not take this professor online.
French accent might make the already dense PHYS 2212 content difficult to follow, so be prepared to show up to lecture and pay attention.

Dr. Berger was extremely nice and extremely caring. The main problem is she just wasn't that great with lectures, she spent a bit too much time with derivations and unnecessary complications instead of focusing more on the broader picture. Personally I struggled to understand much through her lectures and had to turn elsewhere.

A very accessible and kind professor that is willing to work with you, though not the most effective educator. Dr. Berger tends to over-complicate even the simplest topics, and is not the most familiar with technology so her virtual lectures were often plagued with technical difficulties. I'd recommend taking physics with another professor

Berger is the sweetest person but her teaching is very confusing. She prefers to derive equations instead of explaining concepts clearly. You have to attend lectures to do clicker questions. The tests were written by her, Greco, and Alicea though so they were pretty straightforward. Definitely take a different prof if you have other options.

Her lectures are hard to follow and she overcomplicates the concepts. I used to study Professor Alicea's lecture notes because Berger's notes were all over the place. Still had to attend Berger's lecture for clicker questions.

Dr. Berger is very sweet, and I liked her quite a bit as a person, but she's a terrible professor. Her lectures were so confusing that she made the class harder! Before a test, I had to go look at the other professors' notes because Dr. Berger's were so useless. She makes this class so much harder than it has to be.
Prof berger isn't out of the world as a teacher, and her lectures vary in quality. She is, however very caring and accessible during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Does a mediocre job of teaching Physics 2. Preferably, Greco is a much better professor and has more experience teaching this course

Dr. Berger isn't the best lecturer, but she is extremely caring and is helpful outside of class. Go to her office hours - she is more than happy to help you, and is a much more effective teacher 1-on-1 than in a lecture setting. Tests are written by Greco, Berger, and Rocklin together, and aren't too bad. Study past tests to do well.

The professor is a good guy, reachable and really understands the material, but the TA Jamshid who grades all exams is very harsh, strict and unforgiving in grading, resulting in a very low average on all tests. Would be better if the Prof chooses another TA.

Prof. Di Leo is overall a pretty good professor. Homework gives you pretty good practice of concepts. However, when it comes to tests, he likes to throw you a curveball and adds concepts you might not have encountered in class or in hw. This often results in class grades on tests being low, but he will curve (I think 75% is typically an A)

Di Leo is an experience. A true force of nature. His AE 3140 notes/exams/quizzes are exactly the same as he uses for AE 6115 and the qual exams given to prospective MS students in his lab. Will it be easy? No. Will you come out of 3140 with probably the best knowledge of structures that you can get as an undergrad? I'd bet money on it.

He always displayed a condescending attitude if you have an in-person meeting with him. You can definitely feel the unwelcoming and uncomfortable learning environment! My strong advice: steer clear of this class!

Dr. Di Leo has been my fave professor thus far in my master's program at Georgia Tech. This man would still hold office hours/give lectures when he's fighting a cold. He definitely cares about his students and wants to make sure they do well. Definitely take him if you have an opportunity to.

Professor Di Leo is such a great professor, he legit responded to me in 10 minutes at 11:30pm and was able to help fix my mistakes in the lab instantly. He's also so personable and is a great lecturer. I really enjoy 2610 and he's been a HUGE part of my success!

Structures is known as one of the "hard" classes in AE, and Prof. Di Leo makes it bearable! Without a curve, we would all have failed the class, but we know from the start we get a curve. He makes the lectures interesting and makes sure the class is learning. He makes activities to help us learn. Great professor!

Although AE 2610 is mainly a lab class, his recorded and live lectures were great and very interesting, he puts a lot of effort in making them look good and flow well and it shows. He also is very accessible through email or Piazza and does a lot to make sure students are staying on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very accommodating towards students being remote. Good lectures with clear instruction on the labs and why they matter. Very approachable during lecture and over Piazza. Would have loved to do the experiments in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took 2610 online, and lab classes + online generally don't mix. CVDL and the TAs did a fantastic job transitioning to the online curriculum, and despite a fairly strict grading scheme, he makes it very clear exactly what you need to submit for a good grade. He was hilarious and passionate to boot.
He is just an awful professor. Keep away from this professor at any cost!

Di Leo took one of the harder classes in the aerospace curriculum and made it somewhat palatable. He's personable, a good lecturer, and grades fairly. Definitely my favorite professor I've had at Tech.

Structures is really hard and this was his first semester teaching, but he did really really well (even though the test averages were in the 50's, uncurved thankfully). He really knows what he's talking about and also really believes in feedback and seeing what we think about the class. He is very quality and I recommend for any class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class if you just show up (good for tests) and turn in labs on time (stupid easy with AI tools), super liberal prof (ex: data viz of israel on board and roasted it or talked about sadness post DJT election, just has that aggressive feminist energy). Voice is very shrill, but good lecturer generally speaking, easy A
A few professors teach 4460, this one isn't bad, the js assignments were a little long but the lectures were engaging.
Very easy class, and the professor gave way too many chances to get credit to make you actually learn much in the class. I ended up not even doing the final project and still getting an A.

she's nice but her lectures have little to do with the intensive coding labs. also, her exam fell in the middle of cs career fair. we asked if she could move the exam/make it up & she was like "nah. i hope you will prioritize my exam over the career fair' as if the entire point of a cs class wasn't to get a cs job but whatever. yea im still salty
She is enthusiastic and the coursework is very manageable.

This is the easiest upper-level CS course I've taken, but the course content was still interesting and practical. If you are used to taking some other threads' upper-level courses, this course should be a breeze. The coding labs are not too difficult because there's a bunch of examples online that implements what's being asked for in the lab.
Pretty fun class, coding gets a little hard later in the semester. I learned alot.

Watch the lecture videos and take notes. Use notes on midterm & quiz and easy points right there. Extra credit for showing up & participating which is awesome. The group pod helps solidify course content & is a fun way to engage with classmates. 2nd half of the semester is JS & D3 projects, tough. TA videos don't help. Turn to freecodecamp/w3school
She's a good teacher and makes a lot of jokes. Gotta know javascript to do well.
Spatial network analysis with GIS class. Lots of maps but cool software. Lectures are pretty fun and there weren't too many assignments.

Not sure where the good reviews are from. The man didnt follow the course plan and it felt like he taught whatever he wanted. Had clear favoritism to some students. Changed exam part of syllabus days before exams without letting us know + exams wernt focused on taught material. Some students would end up with higher grades because of prior classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is an amazing professor. Our class was quite small, so he could independently help each and every one of us. There was a single very difficult question he gave us on our midterm exam that messed a lot of people up, but other than that, the class wasn't too difficult. I highly recommend taking his class if you can.

Dr. Clark is a legend. His lectures are amazing and he is a funny and caring person. He loves to involve students in class and joke around with them. He makes the class very reasonable and easy to understand.

This is an amazing man and person, I'm so glad I got to meet him before he was famous. Mark my words if he didn't spend so much time in the sauna or making fun of people on reddit he would be a nobel laureate and a sub 4 miler.

Professor Robert Arthur Clark is the best professor I have had thus far at this esteemed institution. His endless love of statically determinate systems has INVIGORATED me to the point of no return, and I now find myself fantasizing about solving 3-dimensional systems of equations. I cannot wait to have him again in another, better, HARDER class!
Prof Rob Clark is too old to still be a student at Tech but he makes a great professor. He makes me too scared to get a PhD.

THE BEST PROF!! pretty test heavy, but she gives u a study guide that has actually everything u need to know on the test. as long as u participate and go to class theres actually no way u can fail. LOVE HERRR

By far the best proffesor I've had at GT. Makes the class very easy and tells exactly what will be on the test. You just have to participate and she gives multiple chances to do so. Also very nice and caring, and genuinely wants to get to know all her students.

Prof. Corales makes it VERY easy to pass this class w/ an A. You do have to participate to get points for your grade, but she gives you sooo many easy opportunities to. Her review days let you know what specifically will be on her exams. She's clearly very passionate about what she does, & she wants you to come out of class knowing your rights.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is an absolute queen.

This professor was AMAZING. My class consisted of 5 scoring portions weighted 20% each - 4 exams and 1 participation. Exams were multiple choice, 50 Qs, and her study guides/review days covered everything that would be tested. Her lectures were amazing and informative. She wants all her students to succeed and has a genuine passion for the subject.

She is truly the best professor I could have asked for. She is SO caring and wants you to succeed! She says there are no dumb questions and that we are in a safe space. She is also super funny and her exams are so easy- all MCQ and T/F. She reviews what you need to know before exams and there is barely any work outside of class. Take 2106 with her!

Dr. Coblentz is really kind and understanding. There is a lot of busy work though. Enough to the point where working on assignments for this class took longer than work for some of my Intel classes. Attendance was mandatory as well.

Very good professor and cares about her students. There is a lot of writing assignments in this course, but she gives you plenty of time to complete them and they seem decently relevant to computer science fieldwork.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is probably the worst I've taken here during my time at Tech. Attendance for this class is mandatory. The class is at 8 AM, and if you miss five classes, they will fail you. How nonsensical. This class is the epitome of "this could have been an email." If you have to make attendance mandatory, make your lectures worth my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The ratio of the amount of work for an assignment to its percentage on the final grade is insane. Get ready for writing long essays, documents, and presenting. But if you put in the work, you will get the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Too many components to your final grade. For example, a 1000 word essay is just worth 5%. Although she is lenient grader, the amount of work is a lot more than what you'd expect. However, if you like reading and writing, its an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Coblentz is super nice and cares about students. She is easily accessible outside of class for help and gives good feedback.

Dr. Coblentz is a fantastic professor and super passionate about the class. She will call on you to answer if no one speaks up, but participation is not graded harshly. She manages to sneak in real-world applications such as creating a video essay and group website/app project. She also greatly streamlines the portfolio-making process from Day 1.

Professor Comfort was great! One should know this is very much a Spanish LITERATURE class, so be prepared to read some abstract texts and discuss stuff like symbolism and metaphor. If you really want to push your Spanish comprehension abilities, then this is a great class with a wonderful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was alright and I made an A. However, the professor doubted that I was capable of writing Spanish at a high level despite having done two different study abroad programs. Moreover, she was more obsessed with how dolls perpetuate racial stereotypes and other absurd activist themes than teaching us practical uses of the Spanish language.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! You can tell she cares about her students and is so well-versed in the subject matter being taught. I feel like I learned so much and I greatly improved my Spanish skills despite being a native speaker. The readings can be a little dense but the homework is fairly easy and doesn't take long to complete.
I absolutely loved her class - she is engaging, kind, and interesting. The class is not difficult. Show up, participate, and do your work to earn an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great teacher. If you have any questions about readings or essays, go to office hours with a thesis or something and you'll leave with an exact plan for your essay. Lectures are engaging and different each day. Does require participation and presentations but kind of expected from a spanish class.
really chill and nice guy, he showed up sometimes to help in lab. gives helpful advice and labs were suuuper easy to pass and calm as well

Very laid back lab. Took with the HP/EX group and had a blast! He and my TA were amazing and always open to questions during our labs. Feedback on our assignments were exceptional and make it easy to excel in this class. I scored much higher in this than the bio lecture class, which says a lot. Overall 10/10 lab.

Although the lab was primarily led by the TAs, Dr. Harrison made an effort to show up occasionally and help out when he could. He would go around to each of the groups and ask them to walk him through what they were working on to make sure everyone had a good understanding.

Dr. Harrison's lab was actually a lot of fun, I really enjoyed that the entire semester was based on one research project and I learned a bunch of new information. There were a lot of peer review/reflection assignments, but they were never hard, just kind of tedious. He's a super caring and sweet guy, would 100% recommend his lab!

Dr. Harrison was great at teaching biology, as someone who previously had Montoya, take Harrison instead, much better. He did go off on a whole tangent about his political beliefs though, which I feel should stay out of the classroom. And I tried getting help from him outside of class and he was very inaccessible. Don't skip the IKEs/TICAs/HWs!!

The assignments for this lab were super simple and easy. The reflections after every lab took me about 5 minutes to do. The writing assignments were not that difficult, just a little tedious but definitely doable. The few times he came in to check in on us, he was very kind and answered any questions we had.

He conducts a very inclusive learning environment which is super appreciated. I thought the lectures felt a little useless at times though, especially with the "flipped classroom" thing. The lab for this course was super cool and enjoyable though (depending on TAs)! The grading scale is also very clear and makes it easier to do well w/ weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Gives lots of EC, but tests 3 and 4 are a bit more difficult with around a C average. Participation is weighted more than the final, and your best exam score is weighted more. Still gotta work for an A, especially on the latter 2 exams + final. Lot of outside homework on learning catalytics, DO ALL OF IT it's weighs a lot.

I had him for BIO1107 last semester. He's a great professor and you can tell he cares about us. In office hours he answers questions well. The tests are totally fair and shouldn't be an issue if you do the homework.

dr harrison did a good job having clear and engaging lectures that made the concepts easy to understand (but not always so easy to memorize). HOWEVER, i tried to reach him outside of class multiple times right after i experienced a specific issue early in the course, and he was surprisingly rude, dismissive, and unhelpful towards me.

Dr. Harrison is a very educated, articulate, and enthusiastic lecturer. However there were multiple sessions where he became very heated about his political views and ended up taking over the rest of class and it became awkward/uncomfortable for students. I don't think professor's politics should be coming up in class and taking over lectures.

While clearly very passionate and caring about the content and his students, the flipped classroom model makes attending lectures useless. You have to read from the (free, online) textbook before class, and the in-class questions can be accessed from anywhere, so attending is not necessary. I learned more from Khan Academy than lecture.

I took the Organismal Biology lab under Dr. Harrison and it was, all things considered, fairly easy. The only thing I would warn future students about is selecting a good group. Groups were chosen the first lab and did not change. My group was filled with slackers and I ended up basically doing the entire course myself but I still found it easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The labs are run by TAs; the actual lab itself is not bad. The only thing I would HEAVILY CRITICIZE is having peer evaluation count as a grade, because no matter how much you participate or contribute to the group, you'll have awful lab members who give you bad rating on evaluation despite giving them max scores because you were trying to be nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is already structure strangely to begin with, because he does units in an order that doesn't build off the last and also a different professor does 2 of the units. That aside Dr. Harrison does not do a good job of teaching the units he is supposed to, I learned more about his politics than biology.

Dr. Harrison's 1208 lab is mostly led by TAs, but he made a concerted effort to show up to a few sessions and showed genuine interest in our findings. Project was great and immersive-- it felt like we were actually contributing to the ATL Botanical Gardens' conservation efforts. Having a good group matters because many team assignments are graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Harrison is a great professor who wants everyone in his class to succeed. He's always open for office hours and just always do Learning Catalytics and study the way he teaches in class and tests will be easier to do. I would recommend him to everyone! Really cares for his students and passionate about biology.

Dr. Harrison is very enthusiastic about his teaching which is great, but CETL2000 is the most unnecessarily heavy class for TA prep. Weekly reflections, dumb filler assignments that last the whole semester, and unhelpful lectures. I took nothing away from the class, it felt like I was being prepped for a lot more than what I actually did as a TA

He cares about students and tries to reach out if you're struggling but has an awful class set-up and explains irrelevant details of the course which you are never tested over. He does not care if you do not understand the material even though he claims to. Maybe I am just bad at biology but I really could not enjoy the class at all

Prof Harrison is a real gem! He's super caring and accommodating, and gives plenty of extra credit opportunities which helped me a lot. the scientist spotlight assignments are pretty tedious and the tests are basically a translation of the practice exams. If you come up to him with any worries he'll be sure to talk them out with you. super chill!

I took Prof. Harrison for BIOS1107, and he was a fantastic teacher. Very personable, enthusiastic, and caring; you'll get out what you put into this class. Labs are easy but tedious, beware of Scientist Spotlights, show up for lecture even if you think you can slack, and the modules only get easier (except for the last one). Anyone can get an A!

I dislike biology and this class did nothing to change that. On the other hand, it's a manageable A in the class. Make sure to stay on top of the written assignments and just use the website links that he posts on the syllabus, and you should end the class with an A. Make sure to participate! Attendance is not necessary at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Harrison is an extremely caring teacher. He reaches out to students and cares about their mental health. Definitely provides great academic advice. The overall biology class isn't difficult. Make sure to emphasize learning the concepts on the learning objectives for the readings. Apart from that this class was never one i didn't look forward to

While this was a lab class taught primarily by lab TAs, Dr. Harrison made an effort to actually be there and support the lab. The lab was really fun, easy, and had interesting results. You'll work mostly in a group but the final research paper was on our own. I thoroughly enjoyed working with the Atlanta Botanical Gardens too!

The lectures are pretty great. He taught aside Dr. Weigel, and he held his own. The class gets easier as you go, and his sections are first, so make sure you are dialed in at the beginning. The labs are a different story, so please watch out for that. As someone who is taking two labs this semester, I have trouble managing my time for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lab was mostly led by the TAs. If you get good TAs, youre set. Dr. Harrison will stop by classes a couple times a semester, but you wont hear from him much other than that. Hes accessible outside of class if you have questions. You can tell hes a nice dude but due to online classes, I didnt get much interaction with him.
Dr. Harrison is a great instructor. He cares a lot about students and he works hard to make the classroom a good place to be. He is an engaging professor and also focuses a lot on class participation

I had him for lab part of BIOS 1107. Great guy. Will pop in a couple of times during lab. Lab is more so led by TAs, grading and teaching. This lab was taught in a hybrid manner; I would come to lab one week out of the four weeks dedicated to one lab topic. Class itself is easy, but you will have three assignments due at the same time.

Great lecturer! He was very enthusiastic during lecture and often encouraged participation. The Learning Catalytics sessions were very engaging, and at time made Biology fun to learn. He was only a co-teacher for this class however, yet his modules definitely stood out. He was also very caring about his students, was always available with open arms

BIOL 1510 is the best college course I have taken! I have learned more in this one class then I have ever learned in any science course ever before. He made all of the information interesting and applicable to real life situations. After taking this class, I want to change my major to Biology!

Amazing professor all around! Very caring and clear in lectures. Makes sure to make it clear what content will be on the exams and is always willing to help! I had him in a split lecture with Dr. Weigel and I completely lost focus after he stopped lecturing. His voice is very easy to listen to and he makes it possible for you to maintain your focus

Although many complain about the set up of this class because it is a "flipped classroom", Dr. Harrison still goes over all of the reading material in class very clearly and makes it understood what will be on the exams. He is very entertaining, kind, funny, and easy to listen to and talk to. Overall, 10/10 professor.

This class has been an absolute mess all semester. Team taught, and Dr. Harrison's half of the class was entirely flipped. Few lectures on the material even though he taught the hardest sections. He is a very nice guy and cares a lot about his students but in terms of teaching, I had to do all of the work to learn on my own.

one of the most enthusiastic & positive professors i've had at tech. he cares about his students and is constantly giving encouragement. tests are fair and there is plenty of extra credit. recommend!!

definitely not intro friendly so if you haven't taken physics before, don't take this professor. its easy to get lost in lectures and i would often find myself more confused after. physics is just hard in general so take it easy on yourself and take alicea if possible

The class is structured well, especially for a class that most of the school takes. Dr. Parker seems very knowledgeable, but often expects us to know the concepts before lecture, and spends more of lecture doing examples when a lot of us don't know the concepts. Physics at Tech is hard, and I ended up watching Dr. Munoz's lectures to study.

I took AP Physics C in hs and without that I would've been cooked. He often spent most of the lectures trying to figure out practice problems for himself and would get them wrong everyday. It really annoyed me that someone with a physics PHD couldn't even teach physics 1 well. Just watch Alicea's lectures and ignore him.

He expects you to have come into class having a background in Physics and also keeping up with the textbook readings. (note: textbook is paid). In my opinion, I thought he focused too much on ideas that didn't matter that much to the class like derivations, and wouldn't spend enough time on the bigger picture that would be important for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It would've been a 4 rating but I'm taking a point off because he wrote that alien question. Funny guy and pretty good lecturer but wouldn't recommend if this is your first time taking physics (I took physics C and physics 1 in high school and struggled to keep up with him sometimes).

I took AP Physics C1 in high school, so I may be a bit biased, but I thought Parker was a pretty good lecturer. Sometimes he would start class with a problem you hadn't learned how to solve yet, but he'd go into the lecture material after that so it wasn't a big deal. He's a really fun, good guy and I enjoyed his lectures and demos.
He didn't really cover as much material in class but focused more on demonstrations. I mostly watched Alicea's lectures, which covered all the basics, so it was much better to understand.

If you have never taken physics before getting to GT don't take him. He's not a bad professor necessarily as he tries to do a lot of practice in lecture, but he does skip over basics and doesn't write out all of his processes because he expects to you already know it. If you have to take his section just don't go to lecture and watch Aliceas videos

Parker wasn't a bad prof. probably deserving higher rating than he currently is shown. Physics is a hard subject for some, Parker definitely doesn't teach intro as much of an intro class, expecting people to know some stuff coming in. In the class your already expected to watch pre-lectures, however, which makes the actual lecture pretty useful!

Good guy with a personality. Lectures are a bit all over the place though. Partially the way physics is taught here, but the usage of the slides feels like it is assumed you already know the topics and you're just reviewing. 
Honestly lectures aren't super helpful and reviewing the slides and content on your own will likely reward a better grade.
Taught physics as a steam of consciousness and so was very confusing in lecture.

Unfortunately, didn't teach the material very well. I mostly learned outside of lectures. Tended to work on problems without explaining the formulas first. I appreciate him trying to engage the class though with rewards and demonstrations.

Very disorganized lecturer. He does not use slides or clear note structures at all. If you are in his lecture you are better off just watching Alicea's recorded lectures on canvas. He would get caught up in just doing example problems with little to no introduction to the actual topic being covered.

I really did not learn very much from this professor, however, he is so so sweet and we were his favorites in the class. He stopped me after my final to ask how it went. He likes his students that participate, and I would take his class again.

He's a nice guy & accessible in office hours, but is not a good lecturer. Not very confident in his explanations, unorganized, spends a lot of time on nuances rather than making sure students understand the big picture. Our section consistently did worse on midterms compared to the course coordinator's (understandably), so watch hers instead.

Dr. Parker's lectures seemed pointless at times, and would structure his lectures differently from the rest of the professors. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but has trouble explaining concepts to students. I ended up just watching the head professor's lecture videos during his lecture time. He for sure has potential to get better.

Parker has the potential to be a good professor but fails to live up to the expectations. He seems very smart and he definitely knows all the information, but he just can't teach it well. All the other professors use slides in class and this helps a lot. I just watched Alicea's lectures during Parker's lecture time and I am doing fine in the class.
Good professor. Explains concepts well.

Not great, not terrible. Lecture can be confusing at time, but covers most of what you need to know. Lots of homework that can be hard, long, and irrelevant to what will be on the test. Good amount of partial credit given on tests. DO THE HOMEWORK BY FRIDAY FOR THE EXTRA CREDIT. EVERY. TIME. Good enough if you ask me.

Overall a good lecturer. He explained most concepts pretty well, but he did falter a bit when it came to the rotational motion unit that was hard to follow. Fair grading: tests are weighted based on how well you do, free lab participation grades, homework extra credit. Will require a lot of practice and textbook reading, pretty tough final.

Professor Parker seemed to genuinely want everyone to do well. He was always available for office hours and hosted pseudo-review there before each test that really helped if you were willing to show up. Its a hard content class, but he explains decently, and the textbook in Wiley Plus goes into great detail. Plus, labs and HW are easy points
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He sucks at explaining fundamental concepts and gauging when students don't understand concepts and can be condescending. The tests were somewhat similar to the practice tests, but after doing many practice tests and hw, the tests were still difficult and I was always unsure of myself. Read the book before class and stay on top of the hw
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Largely test based but nothing is a surprise on the tests. I found the homework and other practice problems to be long but helpful. It was clear what you needed to know to be successful and the textbook is a great tool to help. He claims to not curve because you get some built in extra credit, but I went from a final grade of a high B to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Parker is a solid choice for physics, despite his flaws. His lectures can be a bit hard to understand at times, but if you read the textbook you should be good. Overall, he is a great guy who really cares about his students. If you put in the effort, you will excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a super caring and amazing guy but just doesn't teach the subject. Most of the lecture is spent on a small number of examples rather than actually teaching the subject, so you are forced to read the textbook to excel in the class. Homework is also way too long for what it's worth. WileyPlus is an abomination of a website.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Parker is a decent lecturer, and genuinely caring--especially if you are willing to put in the work. I would recommend you read the textbook chapters before lectures so you're somewhat familiar before. The labs are fairly easy, and the tests are very similar to the past/practice tests. This is a hard course, so be prepared to learn and work.

Parker is a good physics teacher, its just that the content is difficult. Rereading notes taken during lecture helped a lot, and I could tell he really cares about the class. Ive never taken physics before this class but managed an A! Im not sure why people thought the practice tests had no correlation to midterms when they were similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A lot of people had a hard time in this class, but if you work for it it is definitely possible to get an A. I never took physics but I did relatively well. My advice, read chapters on your own and understand it before lecture, the lectures are fast paced, so you need to know what is going on. Also, get extra credit from homework, it helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: A great loving guy that made every fiber of me hate physics, but he was nice
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was so unfair. Content from lecture and lab had nothing to do with midterms and midterms had nothing to do with the final.

You probably want to learn everything on your own because lecture will not help at all. The problems done in class and in homework do not resemble what you'll see on the final. The final was much harder than the midterms, and I mean MUCH harder. Lab quizzes and midterms made me feel like I knew what I was doing until I took that final.

Im a pre-med student and I need physics for a requirement. Taking this class seriously made me rethink my career choice, which is saying something, since Ive been dead-set on med pretty much my entire life. Thats how much I hated this class. Its possible to get an A, but only if you teach yourself. If you try to learn from him, you wont pass.

Nothing can prepare you for tests. Practice problems dont help. You think youre ready, but the truth is youre not. Everything you studied will be spun into very complex problems youve never seen before in class. This is coming from someone who went to PLUS sessions, tutoring, and did the hw. Be prepared to teach yourself. The final was brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice enough guy, but his lecture endlessly ramble on with little relevance to what we're learning. LOTS of homework that takes forever to do, practice tests aren't similar to the real test, exams are graded harshly, lab quizzes are also very hard, and the final is REALLY difficult. Definitely do bucket points because it helps your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The guy teaches something in lecture, then like a week later teaches a different concept that completely violates the entire premise of the early content. The homework is contrived and goddamn awful. There aren't enough practice tests to prepare yourself for midterms. Waking up to head to this guys lecture sucks.

Organization and coherence are the antithesis of this course. There is no connection between the homework, quizzes, lectures, and worst of all, midterms. Material can hardly be considered taught, and teaching consists of ill explained, rushed practice problems. Coming to class is a dismal affair. At least Dr. Parker has a cool middle name, I guess.

Very scatterbrained and disorganized. Vague both in lecture and in expectations. On a whole the class is more bureaucratic than academic. If you check his boxes, then you will probably get an A, regardless of comprehension. Homework is very time consuming.
Unhelpful in lecture, the homework assigned has very little overlap with tests.
Homework is terrible and barely helps you prepare for the tests. Lectures aren't much better
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: amount of hw is ridiculous but that's the way the course is structured. hard course so I'd say Dr. Parker was helpful/ accessible out of class but gets a lot of criticism due to grading. TAs were not helpful. tests were stressful and hard. final exam doesn't help your grade. make sure to do bucket points bc it does actually help

Though I wasn't a fan of his lecturing style, I enjoyed how helpful Dr. Parker was outside of the class. He truly cares about his students and is willing to break down difficult topics until you understand!
Lectures aren't mandatory but they are very helpful. He always asks the students if they understand and will go over topics again if people are confused.

Dr. Parker is one of the nicest professors that I've seen at Georgia Tech. I've had a chance to interact with him during his office hours and I could feel his willingness to teach his students more about Physics. PHYS 2211 itself could be a challenging course to a lot of people and I'm afraid that the hardness of the course overshadows his goodness

He literally said "right" 75 times in twenty-five minutes. We counted. Seems like a nice guy, but not the best lecturer at all. Also his powerpoints are hard to follow. You will have to read the book and teach yourself.

Dr. Parker's 9am lectures were bearable in that he had a very laid back and funny demeanor. However, his teaching was not bad but also not great. I relied mostly on the online assigned homework to learn, because I ended up only attending lecture to get participation points.

He teaches a lot of derivation of the formulas, but makes it difficult to understand how he gets from one step to another because he does a lot of steps in his mind. He's really smart and well meaning, but its hard for him to explain certain things because he takes certain basic knowledge for granted. He wasn't terrible, but wasn't great.

Classes are optional but if you miss it's really hard understand what's going on. She does a great job explaining the math and doing practice problems and would sometimes do review before tests. I liked her a lot and thought she was helpful, but I probably learned more from the TA and practice tests (the best way to study for tests).

Very nice teacher, I lowkey sold the grade by skipping lectures, She's very helpful during office hours from what I heard. Don't really like how she doesn't make power points she kinda just writes out the power point as she goes during lectures and her handwriting can be confusing at times.
Linear was certainly hard but Yap is a good professor and certainly passionate about her students. If you don't get Jankowski, certainly pick her. Office hours are fantastic.

Took this class as a KA pledge. It's just AP stat review. We did have 5 tests in total which sucks. Studio TA Jordan was great. Go to class + watch a kahn academy video on what she's yapping about + go to studio + copy whats on the board + take practice test + fix ur mistakes + do the Pearson homework = A in the class.

The average grade in this class tanked when Professor Yap started teaching it, if that tells you anything. It's a statistics heavy class with no calculator or formula sheet - so its just memorizing formulas & when to use them, not actually understanding the content. And if you forget 1 formula, that's ~20 points off a test. Made a simple class hard

The course covers a lot of material but it's all very interesting. Class is discussion-based so we would break out into groups to solve problems. Prof is very nice and helpful, and makes the lectures engaging. Some of the material gets really hard but its not impossible. Overall 10/10 would recommend.

This was one of my favorite classes ever. The "lectures" were discussion-based and always thorough and informative (notes were provided too but I recommend attending). Homeworks weren't easy but she was helpful if you asked. There's a lot of work including writing papers (but meaningful work and no exams), but you'll learn a ton at a deep level.

I LOVED this class. I was surprised to see old bad reviews, but her teaching style is better for math-inclined people. If you like math take this class, I learned a lot. Small class and we split into groups to solve problems. No tests! But projects and HARD homework. Also, no attendance but hw was difficult without attending.

Professor Yap CANNOT teach. The class averages for exams have been terrible due to her atrocious lecturing. Please do not take this class if you intend on preserving your GPA and keeping your scholarships, as Yap will most likely ruin both.

This course is supposed to be the "easy" math & usually has an avg GPA of around 3.6. But test averages in Corrine's section are 75-79%, and she told us she was pleased with this. Terrible lecturer. You basically have too teach yourself. The best class we've had so far was when we had a substitute. Corrine Yap is the worst teacher I've ever had.

This professor is undoubtedly the worst teacher I've ever had, including high school. Each homework problem takes way too long to do, her explanations in class are rarely clear or useful, and she does not seem to care about student feedback or their success. This class is a losing uphill battle

Moves too quickly through material and does a terrible job explaining things. We often find ourselves unprepared for the tests due to error-filled practice tests, scarce office hours, and insufficient explanations for concepts. You end up having to teach yourself in this class; avoid at all costs! Only good thing about 1711 is TA Kevin Rojas
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its like Dr Yap doesn't trust or respect students & wants you to fail. She wont share answers for studio or tests, so you can't learn from your mistakes. The only way to find out the correct answers on tests is to see her during her two hours of office time, which is a big pain. She makes learning so difficult for no reason.

Lectures are terrible. Nothing is explained well so be ready to teach yourself. She posts practice tests full of mistakes & was actually correcting errors up until the night before the exam. Tests are nothing like the practice test. First test average was in the 70s.The worst teacher I've ever had at Georgia Tech. Run.
Great prof! Very reading heavy and class was just discussion over what was read. 4 essays very light grader with good feedback.
This guy is the absolute goat ! I loved having him as a teacher and I hope everyone gets to take his class !!!!

MY FAVORITE TEACHER EVER. I am impressed every lecture with how knowledgeable he is. He is so engaging. There is a discussion post for every reading and a reading every class. 2 take home essays & a final project but he's a very very easy grader as long as you try. an A is very achievable if you are attentive and enaged during discussion.

Took Literature and Medicine with him, super cool topic and awesome professor. Very understanding and easy grader. Basically if you put a little bit of effort in and have reading comprehension skills and participate in discussion once, you'll get an A. The material was good, prof has some fun lore, sometimes a little boring but overall great lmc.

Loved Dr. Crawford's class, he is very passionate about the material and a really funny guy. Sometimes he would go on crazy and interesting tangents, which were my favorite. We had discussion posts for every class which were easy, 2 take-home essay tests, and a final project. Some readings were long, but definitely rec taking any class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Grade was determined by participation, two tests (essay style), and a final project. He's very accessible and understanding if you just email/talk to him. Sometimes he goes on boomer rants or drops insane lore, but it's really fun. He's passionate about the material and genuinely interested in our perspectives.

Dr. Crawford's class was my favorite this semester. As long as you did the readings and discussion posts, participating in class was easy (and fun!
Our discussions were so interesting).
We had two take-home essays about the class content, and one final essay about a topic of our choice. Absolutely take this class/prof if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he was so awesome! his classes were so engaging! there were a few papers sprinkled throughout the semester and discussion posts with every reading (reading every class) but he is worth it to have him as a professor. his class was fun because he cared our learning. can't wait to take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is truly so well spoken. The way he is able to talk for hours on certain topics really did amaze even with how quite our class was at times. The grading was super easy too, we had two take home essay exams, a final project, and weekly discussion postings on what we were reading! He made me very eager to learn more about our readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really a great guy and very approachable. Took him for postcolonialism and as long as you do some of the readings, keep up with the discussion posts, and don't write pure garbage for the essays, you should receive an easy A.

This man was born to be a professor. He is probably one of the best lecturers I have had at Gatech. Depending on the class, you will have to read a lot but it's 100% necessary for the tests and final project. For LMC2100, the tests were all take home essays and he was super lenient with grading as long as he sees that you understand the readings.

This is my second time having a class with Dr. Crawford and I'm so glad I did! He is very clear about class expectations, and chooses very interesting readings for both his Intro to STAC and Postcolonialism courses. He really tries to help you out if you're struggling and will give you feedback on tests that can actually help you with the next one
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gives great lectures. Very engaging, very understand, overall good guy. Amount of work required for class was very reasonable as were the tests. Pretty easy A, interesting guy to get to know.
This man. Just take him literally best decision ever. He cares about his students and tries to get everyone interested in the material he's teaching. He's also hot (lol).

Really interesting and passionate professor. As long as you do your wiki postings, write okay essays, and nail character matching on tests, you're guaranteed an A. He really tries to give you a high essay grade if your matching isn't too hot.
Probably the best teacher at Tech. The difficulty was great not too hard and not too easy. Easy A if you practice and work hard.

His content in ISyE 2027 was much more difficult than that of other professors. At the beginning of the semester I was doing horribly on quizzes and feared that I ran the risk of failing the class. Later on he started administering all of his exams and quizzes asynchronously and people obviously did better. Very disorganized but funny guy.

I know he gets a lot of slack and as such he was the last professor available for 2027. With that being said, the content is more difficult than other 2027 professors but if you look at his GPA you can see that it's actually the best professor to take. Be nice, show up to class, and he'll work with you.

Worst ISYE professor I've had so far. He doesn't use slides during his lectures, is very slow, and gets distracted easily. The average for one of the midterms was a 34. Takes a long time to respond to emails + the TA was never seen in person. He gave both an optional final exam and a final project, which he barely gave any information on. Run.

Professor Tovey is an amazing conversationalist and genuinely cares about his students, but you will have to put in a lot of effort to understand the material. His pace is pretty quick and he doesn't utilize any lecture slides. He also gives you your Midterm & Final questions in advance and is really fair with grading.

oh where to start. he is one of the most interesting professors I have ever had. he gave us all of the questions to the one midterm we had (worth 30%) before the midterm, so I memorized the answers and got a very high score. he gave us chocolate in the middle of the midterm, too. he gets ticked off by random things.

He does care a lot ab his students (invited anyone w/o a place to go to Thanksgiving). Hardest exams I've ever taken, but content is directly from homework and the practice exams. Median exam 1 was a 38, but those students did not prepare themselves for the exam, and most cheated through the prereq material during covid.

This professor really deserves one star. The teaching style is difficult to comprehend yet unwilling to change, homework was difficult, the test was lengthy and ridiculous. If you are a genius and want some fresh air, you are welcome in his class. Else, RUN.

Horrible professor. I dropped the class after the first exam (which had a median of 38 in a class of 100+ students). Avoid this professor at all costs.
