Go to class and it's an easy A. You can tell he cares about the material. However, there were so many lectures where we were just dumped with information, equations, etc. that we didn't understand. Even though AE1601 is a BS class, I could've done without all the assignments with equations that had some complicated meaning he barely touched on.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Dec is a funny guy and knows how to command a room. Even for intro level class, you could see he wanted people to be interested in the work we were doing in class. Looking to take his upper level classes at Tech.
if you like mindlessly deriving equations without any conceptual understanding of the content, take him.

Dr. Dec is mediocre at best. Lectures get boring very quickly, he writes almost non-stop, but it's mainly equations, he does very little worked examples in class. So you have to work out when, where, and how to use each equation by yourself but there is no book. He doesn't upload lecture notes or answer emails so you have to attend his lectures...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bad sense of what is fair on exams. Inconsistent responses on Piazza and unclear instructions for projects. Generally a lazy prof who does what he needs to to get by. Still would take again because lectures were clear, equations were always derived, and the material is important, so getting a decent professor is great.

It was 1601 and his first sem at Tech, so maybe I'mw wrong about this but I was really excited about the class, and after a while I didn't really care anymore. I didn't feel we were learning as much as we should have.

Dr. Dec really cares about his classes, and he cares that you succeed. He knows that 1601 is mostly a bs class, so you will earn a very easy A. Talk to him outside of class if you are interested in working in the aerospace industry. He has a lot of good tips for first years. Overall, solid choice.

Great teacher. He really wants his students to do well in class and out of the classroom. Very clear about what his tests will be on and what you need to do in order to succeed. You need to actually come to class to get the notes because he doesn't post them online. Take him if you can. Also, he's pretty funny.

Great professor, the class with Romanticism in modern media themed for my semester. Overall we did have a lot of assignments, but she let us mold the topics and theme to fit a variety of our own inputs and preferences. Definitely a great teacher, was kind, and always ready to help inside or outside of class.

the goat. super compassionate and flexible. loved the content of the class (from Taylor Swift to Hadestown to Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes to Frankenstein, super fun material to work with). definitely take ENG1102 with her if you can!

Dr. Debelius is AMAZING! end of review. 

She's really caring about students, understanding, funny, and gives you extra time on assignments + chances to redo. Just make sure you manage your time and not take advantage of her extensions. Her class is such an easy A because she makes it engaging during class time w/ minimal homework. She's great!

No other explanation is necessary - TAKE THIS CLASS! She's a very caring professor who truly wants to see her students grow. You'll actually grow as a student and person in this class and it's very easy. Just take it.
Nice, respectful, and understanding. Topic for class was Romanticism. Not exactly an easy A, but if you put in what you expect out of it, you'll get the grade you want.

Dr. Debelius is such a caring, understanding professor, and you can tell how much she wants us to succeed. Our unit was Romanticism, and I genuinely enjoyed doing the projects that we had. She is very lenient with grading and late assignments. The assigned reading can be a bit of work, but the pieces are genuinely interesting. Highly Recommend!

Dr. Debelius is a very caring and understanding professor, especially with deadlines and if you have other things going on in life. The projects weren't super heavy and she gives plenty of in class time to work on the larger ones. Also gives detailed and concrete feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: the goat, super nice and easy

Dr. D is not only a great professor, but a great person in general. It's clear that she wants her students to succeed - but not to the point where she lets you get away without doing any work. The course is designed in a way that if you put in proper effort, you are guaranteed to get the result you want.
Amazing professor, definitely take her for 1102!!

Best ENGL 1102 professor that I know of. Specializes in poems, so not too much reading for the class. As long as you show effort in your Artifacts (3 main projects for the class), then you get an A. Loved her, would take her every semester if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Debelius is a really great prof. The class has 3 main "Artifacts," and she uses specifications based grading. They're different multimedia projects and honestly aren't too much work, as she guides you through them and allows for revisions. Show up to class and do your work, but do be prepared to read quite a bit every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. D is an amazing and passionate teacher. Very clear grading criteria, easy A with a bit of effort. There's a good amount of reading though. She's very positive and understanding tho, and there's a ton of regrades and extra cred. Our class theme was "Romanticism Remixed" btw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class for iGniTe and it was extremely doable. She told us from the beginning how everything would be laid out and always offered revisions for full credit. She was very honest and upfront about everything and very compassionate. She had a textbook that we were supposed to get, but I don't think anyone read it. Great professor, easy A.

Course is actually ENGL1101. Amazing professor for a short summer course. Provided clear guidelines on all assignments and provided useful feedback on essays. Class theme was extremely fitting. All around a caring and passionate person. Would recommend to anyone taking ENGL1101 or ENGL1102.

Dr. D is a great professor, take her for English 1102. She is the most transparent professor I've had about grades ever, I was lowkey shocked by how helpful she is and how much she cares about YOU as a student. Extremely understanding and flexible about everything. You will probably get an A unless you literally don't do anything.
ez af take her if you want free credits or if you're taking difficult courses alongside 1102

Most caring professor I have ever had. Homework and projects aren't too time consuming but attendance is mostly necessary. The grades are based on complete/incomplete so if you just do the assignments, you will get an A.
Dr. D is such a fantastical professor! She is so caring and und

One of the sweetest and kindest professor at Tech. Grading criteria was clear from start and depends on a few projects thru the sem. You give yourself your final grades (yes u could give yourself a 97 if you think u deserve it) & she gives a lot of constructive feedback. No reading whole novels like other 1102 classes, a few articles only. Easy A.
Flexible grading
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Clearly really cares about the students. Very flexible. I was sick one weekend, so I emailed her that I would do/turn in the assignments Monday, and there were no problems. She will definitely work with you if you communicate with her. Great person, great teacher.

Really nice professor however she gives very long, extremely time pressured tests. However she lets you correct mistakes for half credit and replace one exam with a final exam section if it is higher. Final was around the same difficulty but not at all time pressured which made it much easier. Flipped classroom, boring lectures but lots of EC.

Dr. Deutsch was a great professor! She was very caring and really helped students to do well in the class and lab components. Extra credit was offered and exam corrections were offered as well! Class and lab were difficult, but overall was a great experience!

Dr. Deutsch is a good lecturer and really cares about her students doing well in the class. The exam questions aren't easy but the in class practice is often similar, and she is very clear about what will be on the exams. Dr. Deutsch allows students to test correct up to half of their missed points, also.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very new but was willing to improve. Tests were fairly difficult but test corrections and a final replacement were offered. Her office hours were helpful, she would go over homework problems in detail and would allow makeups for missed in class activities. Lab grades were harsher than lecture (b/c it's precision based) and frustratingly slow.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Newer professor but was understanding with the fact she was also learning too. Exams were straightforward but a little difficult. The homework was doable and she was very accessible outside of class if needed. If the exam was too difficult she usually counterbalanced it with test corrections. Grade replacement was given with the final.

Often unclear what was expected of us. It took forever to get grades back so I often didn't know where I stood in the class. There would also be mistakes in grading which was annoying. She read straight of the slides and would sometimes get confused when students asked questions. Pretty sure it was her first semester so hopefully she'll get better.

Dr. Dean has been a very pleasant professor to have! Accepts late work and is not a harsh grader/most grades are completion. Very friendly and makes it easy to participate and do the assignments without feeling forced to. She won't be like those English professors that are always looking for a specific answer.

She was very caring and sympathetic towards the fact that many students at a tech school don't care about English. The topic for my 1102 course was very interesting and our assignments were not just standard essays. Every assignment was graded on completion (as long as you met all the requirements) aside from reading checks.
super easy A, no tests, pretty much everything is pass/fail, and she accepts late work
A bit boring at times, but assignments weren't bad and she didn't grade harshly

As long as you do your work and put in a decent amount of effort, you will get a 100 in this class. She is a very easy grader and she gives excellent feedback. She also really puts an emphasis on creating an inclusive and welcoming space for all students. 10/10 would recommend her!!!

While she didn't lecture much, she was quite friendly and made herself accessible. The assignments do take a little while to complete, but grading is practically for completion, and she gives incredibly clear feedback on how to improve your projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Professor Dean blindly. She has a very interesting topics (Monsters), and she has a labor based grading system. She made attendance guidlines easier later in the sem so attendance is not too bad. She gives good feedback, and lets you redo assignments and projects. She is very understanding and helpful. Would def reccomend this English class.

Participation matters so much in this class. Don't miss any days or any assignments because she has a "labor based grading system" so even if you do the best work, you showing up determines your grade. I missed 2 days out the entire semester and received a B in the class due to me missing a workshop on one of the days I was absent. Ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Participation was a frustrating. You only get a minimum of 70% for showing up to all classes, so you have to do discussion boards & other activities to get the full credit. She wanted us to read books that I (& 99% of the class) have no time to read and expects a discussion in class. Nice professor with easy-ish hw, but lots of unnecessary work.

Overall great professor for ENGL 1101. She gives a lot of flexibility with project topics/groups and is a generous grader. Her lectures are generally framed around pop culture topics, and attendance is basically mandatory. Readings are usually long and have a pre-class quiz attached, and projects include multiple stages (outline, reflection, etc.).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She had an amazing class topic with Stranger Things and Taylor Swift, which is why I took her. Overall, she's a good professor and I had fun working with the cool topics she had. However, she is a pretty tough grader and there's a LOT of assignments every week. And every artifact has like a brainstorm, draft, final, and reflection so get ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is so nice and caring. None of the work was over the top and the class/topics were very interesting. This class was actually very fun.

Her classes aren't that interesting (to me personally) but she's very flexible with extensions (if you ask ahead of time). There is a bit of work and we had to read 2 books which we were given multiple choice (5 pt.) quizzes on but if you have a friend you can collaborate. Just figure out what she likes (ideas wise) and cater to those in your work.

Dr Ruzicka is great! I took her for the English 1101 graphic novels class which was great. She is an easy grader and her classes are interesting, they hardly feel like lectures. We had four major grades, and the hardest one was making a 20-page graphic novel. Light on the homework. DONT BUY WOVEN TEXTBOOK its a waste of money and its free on reddit

The class is a fair amount of work but she's a pretty lenient grader. Readings are heavy, typically 50 or more pages per class. Quizzes are pretty easy. Choose the subject of your essay wisely, because you're going to be spending the rest of the semester developing it. A solid choice for 1101.

Readings are normally around 70 or so pages but they're pretty interesting. The only thing I actively struggled with was the Petcha Kucha presentation, other than that the class was pretty easy. She does give pop quizzes, but they're a piece of cake if you do the readings. Her lectures are highly discussion based.

Goes far in depth about statistical and mathematical concepts, but still interesting to learn about. Projects can be done without a solid understanding in material, but it's more fulfilling to solidify your understanding of concepts. Really caring and interesting professor.

Not sure why this course gets so much hate. Dellaert is a caring professor that listens to students' concerns, and actively tries to ensure students in lecture understand the content. The content itself is quite difficult, but there's more than enough time provided to complete projects and receive full points. No in class exams reduces stress.

it takes weeks for grades to be returned to you. in addition, the criteria for the lengthy reflection portion of projects is extremely unclear, and the weight for each project in canvas is wrong, causing unnecessary stress for students. lectures were also incredibly hard to follow. don't take this class.

I've never felt so entirely lost. Unless you have a really solid stats background before starting this class, it feels like you're doomed to take away nothing. Pretty intense math/concepts and new ones every lecture. Difficult homeworks feel like "so what?" when you finish them. Entirely dissuaded me from doing robotics ever again.

Is very passionate about the topic he teaches, however completely centers his course around a textbook he wrote and a library he created. This feels less of a lecture/course and more of him flaunting his own works and forcing students to use them, even if they can be useful. Homework is long and lots of busy work. Lectures are complex but useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's an intro class, and he tries to smack in too much content for what it is. Quizzes were quite difficult with the only relief being they were untimed and open book. Explains way too fast. Projects were a decent amount, and there was a lot of math to cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible class structure and homeworks. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow. So is the book, which was written by him and not fully proofread. He is primarily a researcher and delves way too far into hard concepts that make no sense for an introductory course. Quizzes are graded easily are take home and take a while. Haven't learned anything.

The professor is caring, the topic is fun, and his contributions to it are impressive. But the class sucks. Lectures are hard to follow; projects are excessive, poorly made, and not educational; frequent quizzes have many essay questions that are a huge time drain; grading is slow and feedback is vague or missing; review material is non-existent.

I think he's trying to cover so many things in depth. It should be focused on the intro level as the course title implies.  It's impossible to understand the concepts fully, so doing quizzes and projects is like solving 1000*1000 puzzles. I feel like I'm overwhelmed...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you want to get turned off from the concept of robotics - take this class! Dull lectures, textbook, and assignments. It's probably easy to get an A, but the class is torturous to sit through. Don't think the textbook or lectures give you enough info to truly understand what you're doing

Took him for both this class and CS 3630. Has definitely improved his lectures, much easier to grasp. In fact, both them and the projects moreso served to increase your curiosity in Computer Vision than challenge your understanding of math. That said, some of the projects do drag on for a bit longer than they should.

He is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. I have 1 semester remaining for graduation. His lectures are absolute garbage which takes 1-3 hours of weekend away. I could spend that time better doing something useful. Quiz questions are nothing like he teaches in lectures. He doesn't care about his students and causes unnecessary stress.

Dr Dellaert is truly more of a researcher than a professor. He literally invented some of the concepts in the syllabus. He deviates a lot into recent research when introducing concepts in class, which I think is a good feature for an introductory class like this one. Would strongly recommend if you want to learn about current trends in robotics.
His lectures are complete garbage. His projects are a complete mess. The class with him is completely useless.

Great teacher, had great examples for lectures and made coming to class very enjoyable! The best teacher to teach law, very nice and funny. The exams are online through canvas, and quizzes online through textbook! Would take again and highly recommend.

I took TBGEN 218 with him at UWT. He knows what he's talking about in class and is very engaging and makes the class interesting. You do need to show up to class to get the extra 14 max points. Doesn't really help you with tests/quizzes if you email but will answer in class and help you out. About 10 quizzes and 3 exams all online at home.

Dhooge was passionate about the subjects he taught. He made law very interesting and easy. There is an online textbook that connects with his lectures, and his exams and quizzes were all take home, so it was easy to digest information and succeed on his assignments. He just doesn't provide barely any feedback on exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prof was really funny and made the class interesting. As long as you pay attention/take notes in lectures, then you'll be fine. Our exams were open-note and covered exactly the info that was discussed in class, so it's nothing unexpected. We also had a few days to complete the exams, so there is ample time.

Dr. Dhooge was an extremely engaging professor whose lectures were interesting on a day to day. Fair but firm grading criteria made of tests and quizzes. Assessments were open note, but not to be taken lightly, often tests stuff said only in lectures so be sure to attend. Great guy, but refused to round me 0.33% for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All tests and quizzes are taken from home, but you will struggle if you don't attend class. Information can be boring sometimes, but he tries to make it fun. He is a really cool guy, and I advise to take his class over any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a little boring, but all tests and quizzes are done online asynchronously so basically guaranteed A. Just pay attention in class and kinda interesting in class
God Tier. 100%

Dhooge is amazing. His lectures are engaging and easy to follow. The amount of reading was fair, do the reading before class it makes the material much easier to absorb during his lectures. There were two exams, a project and participation. The multiple choice exams were straight forward. Come to class and you get a 100 for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures can be tedious because they are long and the material is not always exciting, but it's worth attending. He cares so much about the subject matter and really tries to make it interesting. One of the best professors I've had at Tech. He's a gem and is happy to help you with anything you need.
Outstanding professor. While the class is content-heavy, he makes it easy for students to remember cases through the use of relevant, relatable, and interesting examples.
I really liked him. He told us a bunch of cool stories about his time as an attorney. Lectures could get boring at times but they weren't that bad. Tests were all take home, open book, open note.

Professor Dhooge is an amazing teacher who has definitely adapted to teaching online. You do need to buy a textbook(over $100) in order to submit the quizzes, but the lectures are easy to follow and funny. Participation isn't required, but if you don't go to class and take notes, you will not do well in this class.

He's super passionate, lawyer who is really knowledgable about the field. Two, forty-question test and on group project. He lets you use a cheat sheet and gives you the topics that will be covered for the test. He gave a lot of points for attendance and his lectures are a joy to be in. He's an amazing person and prof!

Professor Dhooge is such an incredible teacher. He is engaging, interesting, easy to connect to, and it's obvious how much he cares for the class. I was not expecting to like a law class, but he made it so interesting that I found myself discussing the topics with him and my fellow classmates after class every day (without fail).

One of the best professors I have had! The lectures are very entertaining and he has a lot of fun stories about his own experiences. The test are pretty easy as he gives you study guide of what is going to be on it. There are only three test but he added in some reading quizzes this year. Pay attention in class and you should be good!

Professor Dhooge is by far and away one of the best professors at Scheller. There are only 3 test so yes each is high stakes but if you read your notes and pay attention in lecture no reason you cannot earn a high A. He tells funny stories. Lecture can get boring during certain subjects but he keeps it interesting for the most part.

Your class grade is made up of 3 tests that are equally weighted, and are easy if you study and pay attention in class. His lectures are wonderful. He is funny and has wonderful stories that bring the content to life. He recommends a textbook at the beginning of the textbook, but most of my notes came from the lecture.

This guy is AMAZING. He makes every class interesting and cares about his students. Honestly one of the best professors I've EVER had. He likes to tell lots of anecdotes, and if you understand the basic concepts he teaches, the tests are common sense. The only downside is that each test is 1/3 of your grade, no participation or extra credit points.

Professor Dhooge is the best! Always willing to help and is very caring. There are only 3 tests including the final, so it leaves little room to mess up. However, if you pay attention in class and take the time to study, you can get an A. It's for sure not a class where you can just read over the notes a couple hours, it requires a deep study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love this man!!! Really good teacher! I was terrified going into the class knowing there would only be 3 tests to make up your whole grade, but I made a 100, 90, and 93 on them so it wasn't bad if you put in the work and really study. Also didn't use the textbook at all - test material really just came from lectures so try not to miss any.

He only gives 3 multiple choice tests for the entire course so each test is heavily weighted and there's not a lot of places you can mess up on. He's not flexible about changing grades, he goes by the syllabus strictly. He also recommends the textbook but from my experience, it was mostly useless and a waste of money. Hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a lawyer, so he definitely knows his stuff and is good at teaching. Tests comprise of 40 Multiple Choice, and there are only 3 tests total (including the final). Very hard to make an A. Can make a B easily if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Dhooge! He made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the tests are challenging, if you pay attention during class, you should be fine to get an A.
Good teacher but remember only 3 tests that comprise the entire grade and tests are very arbitrary. Overall, nice guy and very enjoyable class; it's easy to pass but hard to make an A.
Dhooge is a talented teacher but his tests are very tricky and since there are only 3 test grades in the class i would advise not to take.v Find professor with more grades.
Fun teacher, fun class, pretty hard tests though each test 1/3 of grade..

Good professor, very interesting, but tests were very confusing in terms of applying what was taught. Also no cheat sheets allowed, tests only consisted of 30 or so questions, so there was little room for error. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I highly advise it seeing the majority of the test was stuff he talked about in class.

Dhooge is a great professor.  Had 3 exams, which were 30 percent each, and attendance was 10 percent.  attendance consisted of him calling out your name to answer a question in class, but he stopped like 3 weeks in.  tests weren't bad, you could have a cheat sheet.  highly suggest taking him.  Easy A or B, depending on how hard you try

reviews.comment: The protocols weren't synced with our lecture material, and our TA had to teach us most of the information himself. All the labs were pass/fail and graded on a 1-5 point scale, making them really easy to fail if you didn't read the rubric properly. The protocols also often required us to create our own protocol, which was incredibly frustrating.

Labs have unclear, confusing criteria, protocol, what is expected of you to do. Material is often redundant -- such as inputting the same table into the labflow AND the report which has to be done by hand -- and I felt like I was explaining the same thing every week over and over again in the oftentimes many hours I sacrificed to this class.

Her labs are so difficult for no reason, and half the time they don't work how they should. However, she is very approachable to help if you are struggling with the lab report, and is accessible through both Ed Discussion and her office hours, and knows what she is talking about.

All of CHEM1310 labs are TA-based, so you have to get lucky to see if your TA is chill and not a harsh grader. Furthermore, all the labs are so time consuming and require a lot of work both in and out of class. The only good thing is that you only need to pass 9/11 labs to get an A in the lab section. But overall, very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really untidy labs. Dirty materials, few replacements for broken parts, and she would change the lab protocols mid-lab (not in my section but the semester after). She made labs more difficult than they needed to be. Also introduced us to Lab Flow which is very buggy and genuinely made me cry on several occasions, also was a $75 purchase I felt was unnecessary.
Do you believe in hell? If not, you will after this class. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

Santos is horrific at her job. Labs were either missing most equipment or equipment was dirty. Lab reports were lengthy and took several hours each week. Labs did not correlate with lecture. Santos didn't know what was going on and neither did the TAs. Chem lab was horrendous.

Confusing protocols. You probably won't fail but your experiment will likely not work.

The Lab TA for this class was the only thing that made it bearable... reviews.comment: dr santos is not the best professor, I will say. Professor Santos just didn't teach. I went to class every day, and it wouldn't have made a difference if I didn't go. She doesn't care about what the students need from her; she teaches in a way that is comfortable for her, which doesn't help any students. All I'm going to say is people were crying after Exam 2, and she didn't do anything about it.

The best way to describe her is rough. The class, the tests, and the lectures were rough. Everything was rough. I participated everyday and did all of the assignments and reading. She was a very nice and approachable professor but she did not teach (flipped classroom) and there were mistakes on tests. Take her if you have taken Chem before or do well learning on your own.

Santos is so obsessed with every student earning every point of their grade. She spent the entire course never admitting to any of her mistakes while believing that students couldn't make any. She doesn't round grades and doesn't really provide any grace for student mistakes because she believes we need to give everything we have to earn anything.

This course was scored out of 1000 and an 890-1000 was an A, a 790-889 was a B so when I received an 889.97, I hoped she would round up since there was no policy on rounding. However, she has an obsession with every student earning every last point of their grade and will never accept that students make mistakes that don't define their knowledge.

offers a lot of extra credit. In class questions are similar to the ones on tests.

reviews.comment: she was my lab coordinator. overall she was very organized. I am a bio major, and compared to the other lab courses I taken, this one was 100% more organized. it was easy to find everything, and she communicated what was necessary to get a good grade in the lab section.

Deborah Santos is the most unprofessional teacher I have ever had the misfortune of learning under. She neglects students needs despite complaints and prioritizes her research over teaching. Dr. Santos is by far one of the hardest chemistry professors at this school. She barely lectures in class and then refuses to give opportunities to help mediate bad grades on tests, even when the whole class does bad. Avoid her if you can

so many people are painting her out as an evil woman. She isnt.

scary, evil woman who barely gives extra credit (the CIOS was worth 0.005 points ??) and does not listen to her students when they beg her to lecture. I did not go to a single lecture after the first couple weeks because we just did nothing

Dr Santos offers so many extra credit opportunities (mini assignment worth up to 2% extra, CIOS, grade replacement, etc). Her class isnt as bad as people make it out to be:

case and point. For our final grades this semester, Mean: 83.9 and Median: 85.5.

Deborah Santos is a horrible chemistry professor. I can thank myself and myself only for doing well in this class.

a failing average was not enough her to demonstrate that the exam was either poorly designed or her course structure did not prepare us for it

Favorite instructor increase his pay to $500K. Class material was difficult for me, but studying helps, instructor is funny and very personable. If you have questions, contacting him helps out.

For any EE major taking this course, find someone in CmpE whos taken 1331 and make them your friend. Also, please have (lots of) fun in this course, especially with your projects.

Top-tier professor for sure. He really wants his students to succeed but also wants to ensure we have practical experience as well. He's down-to-earth, and his office hours are great. An A is not guaranteed, but he definitely made it very possible with how forgiving he is in grading.

He really goes above and beyond to make sure you can succeed in the course. All lecture presentations are posted onto Canvas along with recordings of lectures from past semesters. Test criteria is explained well.
If you're taking him for 2035 (or taking 2035 in general), DO THE EXTRA CREDIT ON THE PROJECTS! They REALLY do wonders for your grade!

He's an instructor who cares. I think his way of teaching just works and that his dedication to getting questions answered is cool. He's pretty funny and I think that yo ushould definitely take him if you can. In class, you'll probably struggle, but things click after class (through studying, his allowed crib-sheets, and office hours < go to those)
The goat. Take him if you get the chance

Really good lectures. The professor made sure you knew what to know for the exam. Exams were open everything except other people. Labs were well structured and easy to follow. TAs and Prof were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: pretty laid back class with lenient grading overall. 3 exams that were open everything (notes, web, ai). 5 labs scored by an autograder. tas and professor were accesible

I took 3058 online over the summer, and I loved it! Lectures were info-heavy, but digestible. Tests were not difficult and stress-free, with plenty of review. Lab/Homework was engaging. TAs were great, and incredibly helpful with assignments. Very accessible, I can tell he has a passion for the subject and cares about his students.

Overall great professor. Sometimes lectures can be dry but he provides very useful resources and is very accessible outside of class. Exams were easy. For 4180, he's been overhauling the content (transitioning from Mbed) which will make the course even better for future students. Content was directly useful for embedded HW/SW interviews.

He's clearly new and still figuring things out as a teacher—his explanations aren't always clear and lectures are dull, but he genuinely cares and wants students to succeed. He's very accessible outside of class and offers plenty of extra credit on projects. However, his final was much longer and more difficult than other professors'.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took ECE 3058 and 4180 with Diego, and both were great experiences. He's an engaging lecturer who genuinely cares. He's great at conveying information (except for APCS compliance). What I learned was directly useful in recent embedded software internship interviews. Highly recommend.
This review is for ECE 2035. Amazing professor, very chill dude. Gives good lectures and highly recommend him if you can take him. Really understanding if you come to him with problems.
Terrible grader. He did not understand the course content himself and strictly graded others. Glad I do not have to deal with him any longer. I do not understand how he is employed here.
This is for 2035. He is a great professor and teaches A LOT better than most of the more "experienced" professors at GT. He's also extremely kind and caring and responds to emails very quickly.

Goated professor, who really cares about his students. He's still young and may not be the most knowledgeable but he's aware of this. Only gripe was using Mbed but that shoudln't be a problem for future students, so this was the last sem they are using it.

Easily one of the most engaging lecturers at Georgia Tech; it really feels like he cares about students, and he's willing to do what it takes for you to succeed. Labs can take a while sometimes so be aware, but the final project is fun and engaging, and his lectures are clear and informative. 10/10
Diego himself is great, and I would recommend him to anyone. The class needs restructuring as the mbed & its libraries feel older than our grandparents. Thankfully, Diego is working on that.

He was alright. It's pretty obvious he lacks the depth of knowledge that other professors have. Exams are a hit or miss. Make sure you read the directions. Labs are boring but are meant for you to get an understanding of the different components you'll be working with for your final project. Can be annoying when answering questions.

Bad at grading. The bonus policy made no sense. It's like 85% students filling out the survey for a 0.5% boost and 90% for a 1% boost. Honestly, he should've just not mentioned it at all. Plus, he never even updated how many people filled out the survey, so who knows if it actually met the requirements or if he just didn't want to give it out.

Absolutely horrendous professor. Clearly had no idea about the subject and was routinely corrected by students during lectures. On the final project, he decided to give nearly everyone below a B pushing many grades below the threshold. His grading criteria was incredibly opaque. Diego should do us all a favor and go back to Wisconsin.

Tests are take-home, and you have 3 attempts + 24 hours to do them. Class is incredibly easy, but is dependent on which TA you end up getting, as they teach your lectures. I had Zack Brumbach, and he was great.
Dr. Fratta has a vision for the class to make it very hands on - and that did not disappoint. The labs were useful and fun, and he is excellent at responding to students. Could not recommend more!
genuinely the best professor i've had at tech. he is a goat, lectures are fun, entertaining and engaging. if you have him you're guaranteed to learn a lot imo

Fratta is a pretty decent lecturer, but he is a phenomenal teacher as he is genuinely interested in the subject and wants you to learn and succeed.  He spends so much of his own time to help you and support you to follow a project you choose and are genuinely interested in.  The class doesn't go in depth into much, but it blankets everything well.

He's teaches like the TAs that carry the hard classes with their explanations except he's actually the professor. Awesome at explaining difficult things in understandable terms and extremely comfortable environment for questions. He's very approachable and cares about your performance, easy to do good in this.

Diego is very good at explaining complex topics in simple ways. Plenty of in-class examples that you can use to study. Made a class that should've been difficult very enjoyable. The head TA was also great and her review videos helped a lot. Very fair exams and even fairer grader. Highly recommend.

Took ECE 3058 online with Diego. Super funny and had great lectures. Really enjoyed his style of teaching. 2 midterms both were very fair, and 1 final, also a very fair exam. All in all, a really great Professor and I hope he never changes!
I took ECE 3058 online over the summer term with Diego. He was such a funny and caring

TA actually teaches the class and extra videos to help with understanding. Class was honestly not bad. Exams were online with 24 hours to complete and three attempts. Homework and quizzes were pretty easy (quizzes take about 5mins). It is EXTREMELY possible to end this class with a 100.

Professor Fratta was amazing!! Take him if you have the chance. Introduced some pretty challenging content in a way that made it accessible and kept us super interested in the subject. Very caring and accessible outside of class. You can tell he has a passion for the subject. Inspired me to pursue a career in architecture/systems!
Diego was a great professor for ECE 3058. His lectures were great and were helpful in preparation for exams. He was also easily accessible at his office hours and was attentive to all students there.

He genuinely cares to teach and wants all of his students to succeed. He is very understanding when giving extensions when you need them. In office hours he is super helpful and takes the time to explain what you don't understand 10/10

Professor Diego is an amazing professor!! He is super genuine and very understanding of students. He truly means it when he says he wants everyone to do well in his class.The class itself is pretty difficult since the only things that are graded are labs and tests and the labs are pretty hard on there own, he's always super helpful in office hours.

Very easy to get full credit on homework and participation. His lectures were not very good at all, but I think if you went and tried to pay attention you could understand everything you need to. I would not take him if you care about learning proofs, but I would say it is an easy A.

I don't remember him ever laughing at anyone, contrary to what the other reviews say, but I can attest to his strictness at times. Still, the lax grading allowed me good flexibility with doing my work. Homework is based on effort and not correctness. The weekly presentations may get you grilled if you don't put in the work, but they're alright.

He is mean and disrespectful to students. He will laugh at you in front of the class if you get something wrong during a presentation. Final was ridiculously difficult and was the only exam for the entire semester.
Avoid at all cost, exam is too hard to complete on time, and final exam contains all the previous content, which is hard to review all of them.

Class was incredibly easy as if you just showed up you basically needed a 40 on the final to get an A. Biggest issue was his accent but otherwise his lectures were not as bad as people say. If you're a math major and complaining about the difficulty of this class or "how tough the grading was." Yeah these are proofs. You need to find a new major.
do not take. laughs at students proofs and is rude, and expects you to know everything.

He had weekly presentation for proofs which was kinda odd. The class did a point system where you can earn 20 points for hw, 50 for presentations and 50 on the final, so 120 points total, standard cut off. He is super strict and doesn't understand english well, takes points off for saying things in way he doesn't understand,  also very dismissive
So much harder than every other semester of Combo.
This guy is so bad. He is basically impossible to understand, his exams have no similarity to the practice materials provided like previous exams. Avoid at all costs.

Comparatively his tests are easier, but with that said and emphasis on comparatively, they're easier just because he cannot teach or answer questions or even prepare us for exams. On the last exam the average was a 65, and with that being said he refused to curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for MATH2551. Notes and explanations are very confusing, and asking questions would just get you a confusing look.  Relied on recorded lecture videos throughout the semester.

I currently have him for Math 2551, honestly he's not the best, and please try to avoid him, his lecture notes make no sense and he doesn't either. I personally did not think his first two exams the averages were around 80s but for the third exam the average was a 65, he is also really dismissive and rude in office hours.

He knows the content, but in chinese. His accent and stutter gets in the way of every understanding anything, and his lecture notes often end up looking like chicken scratch so good luck understanding what's on the board if you look away. He often glosses over questions saying that he doesn't understand and then just moves on. Tests are easy though
Had him for multivariable calclus please avoid him for ur sanity and GPA
Ding's voice makes him seem funny and friendly at first. However, he is unhelpful. His thick accent makes lectures impossible to understand. I would definitely avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very thick accent made it very hard to understand him. The class was very unforgiving since it was based on 3 exams and homework. If you can, avoid him.
I can't understand his explanations and his metaphors are weird
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Changxin was a decent choice for Applied Combinatorics. At the beginning of the semester, I had doubts as it was his first semester in Atlanta, but he did a good job teaching the information. My main gripe is that it was difficult to succeed as you are only graded on HWs, 2 midterms, and a final. But he did curve the final by 14 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only 2/3 tests count, including the final. Really clear and slow lecturer that goes over how inference tests conceptually work. She uses a random generator for attendance taking, so its a 50/50 that she'll take attendance on any given day. The lab component is also very easy and doesn't require attendance at all.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly thoughtful professor who is aware that most people have to take it because it's required, brings a warm and positive energy to the class that is very refreshing. Tests are very fair and don't try and trick you with questions and are accurate to how you understand the material
Very thorough explanation and makes difficult concepts unbelievably easy to understand! Super sweet professor too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVED Diggle! Lectures were super entertaining, but definitely talked a lot about research along with content being presented. Grade was based on 3 tests with the final being 50%, but they were take home! TA's were awesome as well. Highly recommend for BIOS 3380!

He was nice and you can tell he cared about the content but I also think he was kind of immature because he was upset people didn't come to the lecture that he made: non-mandatory, unrelated to the exam content, and was pretty boring.
So then the format and difficulty of the exams changed a lot over the course of the semester I feel like to punish.

Dr. Diggle was okay. Our grade was completely based off of 2 exams and the final, but they were all take home. This was his first time teaching the class. The exams got exponentially more difficult (the final was 4 essays in the span of 2 weeks- horrible). Lectures were interesting but not helpful. Okayish class but I didn't learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very kind and funny professor, but the grading was a bit wonky for the course. he didn't really have a rubric and graded based on how much others included in there answer - most information = highest grade. you have to read journal articles and give a review on them in class and he definitely likes to add his opinions.

I could not recommend Dr. Diggle enough! This course was very engaging and unlike any other course I've taken at Tech. He brought in guest lecturers to give great exposure into fields and split his class time between lectures and journal club presentations. Amazing professor, amazing course, if you're interested in infectious diseases, TAKE THIS !!

Diggle is a nice and interesting professor. He's very approachable and cracks a few jokes every now and then. The class itself (ecology) is easy and there's very little work outside of class, but the tests are much more difficult than what you do in class so be prepared for that. Overall a great prof and definitely recommend.

I love Dr. Diggle. He is so funny and always makes class a good time. You have about a 15 minute video to watch and take notes on before class, but then in class you usually just work through a few scenarios with him to make sure you understand it, and he gives you the answers to the tophat questions. Usually got out of class early too.

Seriously a wonderful choice for ecology, or any other class. He's hilarious and caring, and his tests are fair and usually pretty easy. Great lectures (even in flipped class format) and you can tell he loves what he teaches. I laughed in his class every day and felt like I had a really great handle on the material. 100% would recommend!!

So passionate about Ecology. Approachable and will take your questions into consideration. Sometimes he gets confused while explaining harder topics in class but will always find a way to clarify what he's teaching. Very clear expectations.
Medical microbiology, very funny, memorable lectures
Great guy and great class. Would 100% recommend taking band at Georgia Tech too

I really like BJ :) He's very caring and accepting of instrumentalists of all levels. If you did band in high school and are interested in continuing, this class was a good way for me to relieve some stress during difficult weeks. Would highly recommend

Love this man he's just so nice and accommodating. He knows my name somehow even though I sit in the back row and don't march. He treats everyone with respect. Music can be easy at times but as an engineering major I don't have much time to practice anyway so it doesn't really bother me. Take for an easy humanities if you play an instrument!
Wonderful band director! Will definitely be doing band as much as I can!

If you're thinking about taking band, definitely do! I was on the fence about joining since I'm more used to playing in an orchestra, but I'm so glad I did. He's an incredibly fun and chill guy who makes rehearsals an awesome break from school. The repertoire we play is super cool and just challenging enough to be fun for every instrument.
Great guy. Band is a great way to take a break from tough classes. Attendance based grading but pretty lenient.
Awesome guy. Teaches band really well. Wish more students actually did band.
BJ is a really cool guy, great band director and fun person to be around in general. Definitely join band if you play an instrument!
BJ is dope and makes rehearsals really fun
Really friendly guy who just wants you to enjoy some awesome music. Rehearsals are my favorite part of the week!
Great Professor!
BJ is a great guy.  Interested not only in music, but in the lives of the students he teaches.  I would definitely takes this class, just to get a break from the rigors of all your other classes.

BJ is the best! He chooses pretty interesting music to play and gives everyone A's if you come to class and performances. Band is a nice break from engineering, and BJ is one of the best and most interested conductors I've ever worked with.

B.J. is a fairly good conductor who seems like a genuinely good guy.  The class is quite easy (by design) and it only meant to be taken by those who enjoy playing their instrument with others and not take things too seriously.  The general motto for the class is: we're all engineers, lets have some fun and get a break from the hard stuff.

Enjoyed his classes much more than Donny's.  Always let you out early and tried to make the concepts easy to understand.  Never tried to overly complicate it and was never as arrogant as Donny Allen.  Interested in the subject matter and while somewhat aloof, seemed to care that students learned it.

Professor Doby is an excellent teacher and very thoughtful. He's highly accessible outside of class and actually cares about his students. For example, I had to miss a couple classes because I was ill and he granted it before I even provided documentation. Also, he knows every student's name in this class. Very impressive + kind man.

Rahnev was good. I went to his first lectures, but decided to skip the rest as he posts his slides on canvas. Quizzes can be tricky, but the lowest is dropped. Tests are pretty easy. Lots of memorization. The project is also easy, just put in a bit of effort. He is a great professor, and I would recommend his course.

Great lecturer who clearly cares about his content and students. Not a lot of work outside of class. However, this class is really test heavy and requires a great amount of memorization. Also quizzes are tricky and only 10 questions which weighed a lot which can cost you a good portion of your grade. No extra credit.

Honestly incredibly good class -- Prof Doby makes the material really interesting and engaging w/ a lot of videos and examples in class. Material is definitely easier to learn if you are interested in psyc. Quizzes were harder but 1/6 was dropped; weekly reflections were free points. Midterms/final were difficult, but not obnoxiously so

Professor Rahnev was a good lecturer and did his best to make the material engaging. My only downside is that the questions on the quizzes and exams (which make up most of your grade) are often vague/poorly worded in an attempt to trick you. Using double negatives and other literary techniques to try and fool you is a bit much imo. Not a free A.

Lot of reading. Assigned two chapters a week and were dense. Notes  + understanding a chapter took 2 hrs. Material is all memorization. For the final it took me 7 packs of index cards to write down all the terms. Even after that I got a B. Looking back I would put in less time for an 80 vs struggle for an 88. Easier if you are interested in neuro.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very sweet guy who cares about his students and the subject matter. He makes the lectures as engaging as they can be, which is great because the course content is legitimately very interesting. The assessments are fair but difficult, you definitely need to study. Would absolutely take him again.
amazing professor, kind, and cares about his subject. He also cares about his students and tells you exactly what you need to do to be prepared for tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Enjoyed this class & lectures. Quizzes can be tricky but not enough to affect your grade. The exams were very fair. He's a very engaging prof & compiled the information in an interesting and entertaining manner. My only complaint is the group project. If you get in a group where not everyone is on the same page it's a good bit of your grade.

Doby was a wonderful professor that truly cared about his students and their wellbeing. He was genuinely enthusiastic about what he was teaching and would always be willing to clarify if confusing. Was very understanding with deadline extensions and very fair with giving points where they were due. Tests can be tricky but would 100% take again

Dr. Rahnev is a great lecturer and very kind. During a few of the quizzes, he would occasionally give everyone credit for a question if it was worded weirdly. He also curved the final because it was difficult. Although the class requires a lot of memorization, an A is attainable as long as you catch up with lecture material and read the textbook.

Professor Rahnev is a very good professor. He knows the material, is enthusiastic, and cares about his students' wellbeing. He is not afraid to admit when a question was unfair on a quiz or an exam and will grade accordingly. One of the best!

Doby is a good professor and his class is fairly easy. He explains topics succinctly and makes clear the bounds of the testable information in the textbook. He takes feedback on contested quiz questions and grades the (short) term paper and project liberally. You can make an A by attending class or reading the textbook and it's not a difficult ask.

He really tried to make the quizzes and tests manageable, we had so many quiz questions that he would give the class credit for because the phrasing was confusing. The content is very interesting and he does his best to make the lectures fun and interactive. I really enjoyed this class.

Professor Doby is such a kind and caring person! I took both his PSYC3040 and PSYC4090 and lectures were super intersting and engaging. Not easy-A classes due to heavy concepts to memorize and tested on textbook. Grading is nice and you will be fine if you are really paying attention and doing some reviews after class.
yea he was chill. very accommodating, very interested in the subject. i liked him alot :)
Fun professor. He was super nice and understanding. The homeworks were fine, but definitely should read the textbooks and notes over for exams and quizzes.

Professor Rahnev is genuinely such a kind and great person! I enjoyed and looked forward to all of his lectures. It was such a nice change of pace amidst a bunch of super difficult classes this semester and the content was so interesting. He is a very engaging and well-spoken lecturer. If you're AI CS definitely take this over robotics!!

Great professor. Records lectures and has frequent online quizzes that are based off lectures. Need to read textbook and take notes on lectures to get A's but tests are online with honorlock. Really flexible and an overall easy class.

Very easy class. You still have to put in the work on reading the textbook and attending lectures, but it got to the point where I barely did either and still got solid grades. The exams are super fair & he is just a nice guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for both PSYC 3040 and PSYC 4090, and I learned an amazing amount from both. There's a lot of memorization, and he also tests on some material only covered in the book, but if pay attention in class, read the slides after, and skim the key terms from the book you should be okay. His class genuinely got me interested in his field.

Not the most engaging lecturer. But he really focused on emphasizing main points and only getting into low-level details where it was necessary or helpful. Quizzes were tough since they relied on material from both lecture and the assigned readings, and there was a lot of information in both.

Doby was an excellent S&P professor. He's caring, passionate, and very knowledgeable about the subject. He has high expectations and this will definitely not be your easy-A psych class, but if you go to lecture and read the textbook chapters you should do fine. I learned a lot, and it was the one class this semester that I never wanted to skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: she's a nice lady. not online savvy at all so beware, but extremely interesting class content and lectures honestly changed my perspective on mental health. there is a required online textbook you have to pay for, but the homework and exams are easy. all multiple-choice exams and there's only 3 of them so just make sure you read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got a 95% in this class, and I received a B for my final grade, if that tells you anything. Dr. Leader is incompetent with technology. If you can't use technology, just use Canvas and PowerPoint, and have TAs calculate final grades. But Dr. Leader does not do that, and it caused repeated issues this semester that significantly penalized students.

If you have the option, I strongly recommend NOT taking her class. She rarely responds to emails. Her exams are extremely detailed, covering material that was not addressed in lectures. I was excited to take this course because of my interest in psychological disorders, but that enthusiasm was quickly diminished by the way the class was taught.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most boring lectures ever and genuinely could never figure out how to work online lecture even after the entire semester. Not worth it to watch the lectures, just do the in-class assignments and lock in for the exams. Heavy extra credit at the end of the course bumped up grades a lot (grade replacement and lots of extra credit assignment)
Do not take this class! Dr. Leader was often late, canceled lectures, was inaccessible outside class, gave vague grading, had very difficult exams with unreviewed material.

Super chill professor, but she definitely expected way to much out of us for an "Introduction to Psychology" (and made me HATE psychology if anything). Spent 20+ hours studying for each exam (which is crazy) despite being attentive; also exam questions had lots of ambiguity, and she shot down any exam contesting. Lectures were boring asf too.
Super sweet and content was extremely interesting. Slides are self-explanatory too. Tests felt more difficult than what we covered in class, though.

Dr. Leader managed to take away all of my excitement for abnormal psych with her lectures. She was entirely inaccessible outside of class and would ghost you after asking for help. Her tests referenced things she would say once during lecture and then never mentioned again or put in her slides. Do yourself a favor, take any other psych elective.

This class was very test heavy (70%) and the tests felt so different from homework and lectures. I genuinely have nothing against the teacher, but am off put by the difficulty of tests especially for an intro class. Studying felt futile. I had a terrible experience with this class and teacher, but to each their own.

Very easy class (abnormal psychology). take notes from the textbook and study those and the lecture slides before the exam. Also, study the homework before the exam. Her exams have stuff that was not talked about in class but is in the textbook so actually READ TEXTBOOK or use chat to take notes from it.

Dr. Leader is very caring and knows abnormal psych. However, lectures are slow, and you really don't need to attend class to do well. The TA sessions before the exam (Nick) ARE AWESOME. Best study method is to just go to these. Overall, interesting class although very self taught.

Honestly....Lectures were very boring and I feel like didn't help for exams. The exams were very hard considering Psychology should be an easy subject. Textbook came in handy, but Dr. Leader would always fall behind schedule so not all material was covered before exam times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dianne Leader is confidently the worst professor I have ever had. Her lectures were very boring and a waste of time. Her tests were SO hard and had nothing to do with what she taught in class. When she  canceled class(very frequent), she would not post lectures and expect us to know the content. Save yourself, take this class with anyone but her!

Sweet older lady and the content of the class was very interesting...Those are the only good things I can say. Her lectures are VERY boring. Her tests are hard. Also whenever a teacher won't round an 89.9 to a 90, I start to dislike them because I know if I was a teacher I would have no problem giving a 0.1 boost. If able, take another professor.

Dr. Leader is a great person, but not a great professor. She isn't tech savvy, so most things related to Canvas are relegated to her TAs. You have to pay for a textbook (which isn't that useful) and their homework system (which is awful). The exams are slightly unfair, since it's all multiple choice and so many of the answers look the same.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! Dr.Leader is a somewhat sweet person, but she treats this class as if you are all doctoral students. The smallest assignments can bring your grade down, and she won't ever let you know. There is a lot of homework and assignments, and you have to pay for the stupid textbook.

Professor Leader is a very nice and caring person and she is very accessible outside of class. However, her lectures for the online class were boring and hard to take notes on. Lectures were always more than an hour and long winded. You also MUST read the textbook. Also grade is HEAVY on test grade 70%!! Please save your GPA take another class.

This class kind of relies a lot on lectures, but they were hard to attend and pay attention to because they were just so boring. What a drag! Grades are also confusing because she wants us to use an excel sheet to calculate them so you are unsure of where you really stand. The assignments were easy to complete and were grade savers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Difficult course

Unless you are majoring in psychology, DO NOT take this class. Class averages on all exams were barely passing, which gives a perspective of how difficult the exams were. Class was also extremely unorganized and the course content can be uninteresting. One positive aspect of the course is that there is EC. Save your GPA and don't take this course.

Unless you are majoring in psychology, DO NOT take this class. Class averages on all exams were barely passing, which gives a perspective of how difficult the exams are. Class was also extremely unorganized and the course content can be uninteresting. One positive aspect of the course is that there is EC. Save your GPA and don't take this course.

Overall, the class was interesting, but her lectures were boring. I stopped going at some point but still managed to maintain an A average on exams. As long as you do the homework, case studies, and review the textbook and lecture slides before exams, you will do fine in her class.

Dr. Leader is nice but she makes this class much more difficult than it needs to be. Her exams are often about topics not discussed in class. She is extremely unaccessible, as she rarely responds to emails. The TA's ended up having to fill a lot of these gaps, and they're the reason I passed the class. Take another prof!

If you are a not a psych major or don't have a vast knowledge of psychology, do not take this class. This class requires a lot of studying and sometimes it doesn't even help because the exams are on things she sometimes doesn't cover in lecture. Avoid this professor. The TAs aren't helpful because she doesn't communicate with them at all.

Dr. Leader was a very sweet and caring professor. Her lectures were more traditional, with her explaining the content on the slides to the class. Homework is done through macmillan learning which was a $100 online textbook.

Lectures were very boring and did not prepare me for the exams, which were extremely challenging. I had to self-teach the entire curriculum to myself, which was very time consuming. The only reason this review isn't worse is because your lowest test score is dropped and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

This professor is extremely boring and her tests have random questions that barely even appear in the textbook. Her lecture slides have no information and going to class will put you to sleep,the only thing that helped was her TA who had to make review videos and slides with more information than the lecture slides so we could pass. Don't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. On top of the other 2023 comments posted, her tests have very little to do with her lecture content, which has little to do with the textbook chapter, so there is no good way to prepare. Also, her homework and post-chapter practice quizzes are concept centered while the tests are application centered.

Dr. Leader is very sweet, but she speaks very softly, and her lectures are very disengaging and hard to follow. Her tests can be pretty tricky. When she uploads the PowerPoint, she won't upload the right ones. I go to class pretty often and did okay on the tests but I would find a professor that is more engaging.

Professor Leader is a very frustrating professor. Her tests are difficult and are heavily concept based. Her lecture slides are bear and have very little information on them. Her lectures are very boring and dry, and she gave a "curve" on a test, which was just adding two points to your test grade. Find an easier professor for this intro class.

Always late. Never uploads the PPT and if she does they're not the right ones. Showing up to class is the same as not going. Sitting through lectures is nearly impossible due to boredom. Tests are really hard, regardless of attendance and amount of studying. Gives extra credit to make up for the lack of material learned throughout the course.

Not awful, but not great. Regularly showed up late or notified the class that the class was canceled 15 minutes after the lecture period began. Class attendance is practically mandatory since lecture slides are barebone outlines. Tests are heavily concept based with limited practice given. She struggled with technology frequently too.

Dr. Leader is a sweet lady, but her slow-speaking, soft spoken nature makes lecture pretty disengaging and hard to pay attention during. Course has lots of extra credit built into it, but exams tended to have questions that were quite vague or were about the most insignificant little detail from the content. Relatively easy workload overall though.

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER! She is constantly late to lectures and sometimes doesn't even show up. The team teachers are better than she is and her teaching style is bland, bleak, and dreadful. This class was way more work than it should have been and I hated every minute of it, I would recommend trying to find another teacher.

She spoke kind of slowly, but that isn't even that much of a complaint. She was clearly interested and engaged in the material that she was covering. She was also quite understanding with technical issues and student stress, offering the occasional deadline change, etc. Overall a pleasant experience for an out-of-major intro class.

Worst professor I have had at tech. Took this class because I heard it was easy as everything was online. Starting this Spring semester, everything was in person. Arrives at lectures 15 min late every day, extremely unorganized, talks so slow, is awful with technology, posts important announcements after midnight. I had to study v hard for tests.
Very kind and engaging

Prof Leader was a pleasure to be taught by. Her class was an easy A in my eyes and I liked learning more about psych. It is possible to get a good grade without attending lecture, but she is a really intelligent lecturer and I would recommend listening! I would definitely recommend her class - you learn a lot and can do well with low/medium effort!
Prof Leader is such a good professor. During the pandemic, she taught me how to use Quizlet! I learned so much Quizlet from her!

She's a very sweet and caring professor who tries her best to make her lectures interesting. That said, they can be boring, but the content itself wasn't too hard. Most of the grade comes from tests, but she allowed a 1 side crib sheet. On top of that, there were many extra credit options. Overall, she's a pretty solid choice for Psyc 1101.

Professor Leader is a really incredible professor. She is extremely caring about her students and understanding when it comes to assignments. COVID posed a lot of challenges this semester, but she made sure that this class was not a burden and made it possible for us to succeed. Highly recommend taking her for any psych class!

I enjoyed Dr. Leader's Abnormal Psych class, although technology posed a challenge for her during COVID. We often spent the first 20 minutes of class troubleshooting problems, and were very behind for most of the semester and had to cut out chapters of content, which I was looking forward to learning :(. She is very caring, knowledgeable, & kind!

Definitely one of the worse professors I've had at Tech, her classes were really boring as evidenced by class attendance. Assignments were monotonous and easily found online, exams weren't an accurate indicator of what was on the textbook. She expects you to attend lecture and gives out a lot of information in lecture that isn't on her slides/text
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her lectures. She is fun to listen to (I love her accent) and she also has great guest speakers. I learned a lot in her class. I would definitely take her again.

If you have to take Abnormal Psych for pre-health, she is a fine professor to take it with. Lectures are very tedious and almost impossible to pay attention to. Content is fairly interesting. Grading is very fair, extra credit is somewhat generous and incredibly easy to knock out in a few hours. If you try you will probably get an A.

Fall 2019. 90% of grade came from tests, which weren't easy. Focused on application rather than terms/definitions (re: not an easy A). Dr. Leader is a really sweet lady, really enjoyed listening to her teach, but the grading system was pretty harsh. Good bit of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The most boring lectures I have attended, ever, I found it impossible to focus. It doesn't really make a difference as the tests are based on the book and as long as you study from there you can get an A (I actually got better grades using the book than my lecture notes). The tests are not hard and there's extra credit but prepare to read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I feel like Dr. Leader gets a lot of unnecessary hate, but I found her to be one of the best lecturers in all of my classes. Her lectures are interesting and engaging, and if you attend all classes and pay attention, there's no need to freak out about her tests. She also gives lots of extra credit opportunities!

I loved Abnormal Psych with Dr. Leader. She is very thorough and gave good insight into the disorders' cause and treatment. Her class is lecture and test heavy. Although she takes attendance every day, it was 1% of the grade. I'm a Psych major, so I really enjoyed it, but I can attest that most people that showed up were watching netflix...

She's a nice and caring professor, but she always seems to get off on tangents irrelevant to the class. Grade is composed almost solely on the test and final exam. It is essential to read the book as her lectures do not cover all the material she expects you to know for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Leader is one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech. She is so caring, her lectures are very interesting, and it's the perfect work load. She is super accessible and is literally one of the sweetest people I've ever met. She really cares for her students. Attendance is mandatory but going to class is always worth it!

I highly don't recommend taking Dr. Leader's class. She's sweet, but her class is a lecture everyday and the class is only tests. She puts information on tests that is not reviewed in class and doesn't clearly explain questions. Her class was the worst and not enjoyable at all. Seems like an easy class to pass, but it's far from that.

Dr. Leader seems like a sweet professor, but she's very dull and her lectures don't teach you anything. She skims through the tests and you're required to read the rest of the reading by yourself with no guidance. I would not recommend taking her class if you want to have a caring professor that remembers your name.

Dr. Leader is great, especially if you're pretty good at remembering what you've read. Her lectures are usually boring and kind of unnecessary, but there's a participation grade. Tip: read the chapters covered before the test, skim the notes. I got an A with that strategy and didn't struggle at all. Learned more than I expected. Great, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I had to take 5 exams. Homeworks were unbearable and very long. Reading is required but only certain, small portions of each chapter are tested (she doesn't tell her students each). Her lectures are soooo boring. She literally stands in front of the classroom and talks in a monotone voice to a powerpoint slide. Very sweet lady but I don't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Leader is a great teacher, especially for PSYC 1101. The class revolves around 4 tests (including the final), and one of them can be dropped (all multiple choice). There is tons of extra credit; if you do the homework, come to class, and review before the tests, you will get an A for the little effort you put into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures consisted of slideshows. Each test is 25% of your grade, but you have 4 (including the final) so the lowest doesn't count. The tests seemed harder than the material we learned in class. Dr. Leader is a very sweet lady, but I struggled a lot with this class despite it being an introductory course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Leader did not care about this class at all, and it was very evident. Although she may be passionate about psychology, she clearly doesn't care enough to start class at any time before 10 minutes past the supposed start time. Also, she constantly cancels class, cannot figure out the simple technology, and is dull. All I learned was from the hw.
Dr. Leader is so nice and obviously cares about her subject. She gives plenty of extra credit chances, also her test questions are straight from the book.
Grade is essentially based on tests. She will decide to change how she does her grades for whatever reason so you could potentially get screwed over at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY
