reviews.comment: Class is not hard if you aren't afraid to memorize a few terms the night before a test. I read the textbook and took notes, and I got A's on the tests, but the terms can be confusing, so studying is necessary. She offers 2% extra credit. SONA experiements required. In class, she was good at explaining things, but take notes if you want an A!

Tests are worth 75% of our grade, and there are 3 tests that count, so be mindful of that. I found that lectures were so boring that I couldn't even fall asleep if I tried. She genuinely cares about the subject matter that she's teaching, and is knowledgeable, but she fails to pass this passion on to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's sweet. Her accent is a little difficult to understand but she really cares, and her lectures are interesting.

She was such a caring, kind person, who is willing to make things fair for students. She even answered questions during the test when I was completely lost. She listens to our feedbacks. This class is definitely textbook heavy, so if you read the textbook and pay attention during lectures, getting an A is not a problem.

Genuinely passionate. Tries to make her lectures as interactive/not boring as possible. A very fair grader, and gives lots of opportunities to help your grade, so one failed test won't doom your grade. She also is very open to student feedback. If you put in the effort, you will get an A. Personally, I loved her as a prof and a person.

First, the textbook is an absolute must for this class. Dr. Leader's lectures weren't mandatory; however, she takes roll each class in case if someone asks for bonus points towards their grade she can reflect upon the roll to see your participation. The tests are heavy and she doesn't provide past exams as references, but gives study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, she really helped to communicate more difficult or complicated concepts efficiently and simply.

Her class was an easy A and quite interesting. Tests were quite easy, a lot of the questions would be easy to answer with a minimal understanding. Lecture isn't mandatory but is probably necessary if you want to guarantee an A. Homework isn't overwhelming and actually helps with understanding the material.

Ms. Leader is one of the nicest professors I've ever had, and she is also happy to help outside of class if you have any questions. However, I am not very good at memorizing and found her exams to be EXTREMELY difficult. Her exams are a mix of textbook material and lecture material, and so get ready to read lots of pages in the textbook!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Leader was a good professor who had very clear lectures and specific grading criteria for the course. If you went to lectures, she basically went over the concepts that we needed to know for the tests. However, my main gripe was that lectures were often very boring and dry which makes me not want to take another psychology course here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very clear lectures. Lectures and attendance are not necessary, but don't skip if you want participation points. Very nice professor. Lots of extra-credit opportunities. Barely any homework (around one case study per week). Easy A if you just read the text and go over outlines before exams.

Dr. Leader is amazing! She sparked my major interest in psychology. She roasts sometimes but only when people are asking for it. Very polite and tests are reasonable with a minimal amount of studying. As long as you read and show up to lecture, you'll be fine.

Dr. Leader really tries to be entertaining during her lectures. Shes obviously very passionate about what she teaches, and it shows. She takes attendance during lectures, so make sure you show up because its factored into your grade. A lot of opportunity for extra credit. Easiest A Ive received.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found the course quite easy. If you are someone who can easily retain material by reading a textbook and doing homework, take this course. Attendance is checked for end of year bumps but not graded. Extra credit opportunities abound. Tests are fair, and easy if you give any effort towards studying. Highly recommend doing the Inquizitive to study.

Good teacher who has relatively engaging lectures. A slight bit harder than the other PSYC 1101 teachers, but she makes sure you actually UNDERSTAND the material, and don't just have it memorized. As such, the tests check for comprehension, not just memorization. Also has 3% extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: No pop quizzes, so the tests are worth a huge chunk of your grade. Her lectures are usually boring and don't help much with the tests- if you read the textbook, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Leader is a good choice for PSYC 1101. Her lectures are often interesting because she often uses videos and activities, but expect a lot of PowerPoint lecturing. Tests were multiple-choice, and homework was through an online system called InQuizitive; you can always get 100% by doing enough questions (at least, when I took the class).

Loved Dr. Leader. Her South African accent makes it interesting to listen during lecture, and she wants you to do well ( but said 'she won't work harder for your grade than you'). Makes the subject interesting, and so it makes it easy to pay attention and do well. Reading helps , but I didn't find the workload to be really difficult.

I found lectures to be rather boring, and the powerpoints didn't tend to follow a logical order. Eventually I just started reading the book during lectures because I found I had to read the book on my own time anyway. However, if you read the book and study a little bit, her tests are a fair assessment of the information in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Leader for psyc 1101. Because the class was so large, I only talked to her once or twice. Easy to just read the book and get an A / high B on tests. Lectures are good for reiterating this info. Also good to know what'll be on the tests  - she didn't follow the syllabus completely. Definitely a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Maybe I'm just terrible at psychology, but this class was eh. Test questions are all application questions, so that makes it hard. Even if you memorize everything, it's hard to do well in her class.

Lectures don't include all testing materials, so make sure you at least skim the chapters in the book and do the optional activities (they're helpful and a good review for tests). Very nice and reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Leader was great. Her class wasn't a huge work load. It was a great break from tougher STEM classes and an easy A honestly. If you go to lectures and use LaunchPad before tests you'll be fine. There is also extra credit opportunities that are easy.

Thick accent, but still understandable. Lectures are useless if you want to do well on tests, just study from the book. She does not give papers, long HW's, or quizzes like other professors do, so if you don't want to have to work a lot outside of class, take her. 90% of the grade is exams though, so making an A is hard with her, so be careful.

She was kind lady. To succeed you should read the chapters and then do the homework. This will improve your recall better, so that you can succeed in the class.  Tests were not too bad; some tricky questions, made B on most of them. She gave 3 extra credit points for research experiments.

Leader is a fantastic professor, hands-down. Sure, the homework may be a bit tedious, but she has piqued my interest in both courses I've taken with her. I hope I'm able to take another one of her classes.
Very good lecturer, stimulated my interest in the subject. Class is easy if you show up and pay attention.
She's a great lecturer, but apparently has the hardest PSYC 1101 class.
She is a very nice instructor, and has many extra credit opportunities- up to 4 points on your final grade. If you study and attend class, you should be fine. I made an A.

Dr. Leader's intro psych class is interesting and made me appreciate the field a little more. She gives great examples of the concepts so they are easier to understand. She has an interesting South African accent that's fun to listen to as well. Test questions can be tricky but if you study you'll be fine! Take her class! :)

Class is more difficult than I thought, but I still got a B without putting much effort into the class. She has grad students teach a couple of the lectures. She is fair and approachable. She has an online chat the night before the test to answer questions.

Dr. Leader is not the best person when it comes to relaying understandable material. I read the book and attended every lecture, taking notes and paying attention but the tests were overwhelming and very tricky. We only had 3 tests in that class and a final to make up our grade. I wouldn't suggest taking her class unless you are great with psyc.

I found Dr. Leader to be very unorganized and she moved very quickly and did not explain the major concepts. If you have good TA I recommended seeing them a lot otherwise the class is hard and you will not understand the material well.
This teacher contradicts herself all the time and will not negotiate with you even though you work your butt off in that class.

Ok for an intro-level course I guess. She didn't seem to have the lectures planned too far in advance and didn't follow the outline on the syllabus. Multiple-choice tests are way too tricky and even if you know most of the material, you're not guaranteed an A. 4% extra credit, easily done, so do it. Pay attention in class and you should do fine.

She's a rather interesting teacher and her accent makes for interesting lectures. Make sure to take notes and READ THE BOOK. Reading the book helps a lot although it's not necessary to make the grade. She gives 4% extra credit just for doing assignments. Pay attention, do the extra credit and study and you'll be fine.

Go to class, do the work, read the book, and a good grade is easily yours. Likes to test on material from BOTH readings & lectures, so cover all the bases. Not bad lectures and likes to use examples to make it more interesting and relevant.

Teaches well, but not always what is on the test. The book is really good and explains well. Use that as he basis to study. The tests are hard, but she does lots of extra credit, and makes it definitely doable to get an A if you put in the work.

Must read the chapter summaries at the end of each chapter! I skimmed through the text and read the summaries over and over. She takes attendance. Drops lowest test or replaces lowest with final. Do the extra credit experimentrix offered. 1 hour = 1% on OVERALL AVG! up to +4%. I did all 4% and it got me an A in the class. Tests are MC but tricky

She takes attendance and it's part of your grade. The tests are kind of specific, but as long as some studying is done it isn't bad. She has an interesting accent and lecture is the most important part of the class. She offers 4% extra credit to add to final grade.
Good Teaching. Test were somewhat difficult. Go to class and you will be fine.

Took two courses w/ her.  Boring lecturer who can't adequately answer a question; didn't seem terribly knowledgeable outside of what the book told her.  Stick to reading the book and you'll be fine; extra credit is also easy to attain.
This class is an easy A. Either go to class and study your notes or skip it and read the textbook before the test. Either way, you ought to do fine on the tests.
I found the lectures enjoyable and yeah an easy A to be sure as long as you pay attention in class and go over notes before the test. text book completely unnecessary
She was an interesting lecturer and made class interesting when I decided to go. Her tests are fairly easy if you read the material. Her accent is hot too.
Nice lady, good teacher, cool accent. Study the notes she gives you online and you'll be fine.
Nice lady... As long as you study her notes from class you'll be fine on the tests.
She's a really good teacher. She also gives a lot of examples to further clarify what she's explaining. Sometimes it can get a little boring but overall it's a good class.

Not as easy as everyone says, but relatively easy compared to all the other really hard psych teachers. Anyways, she knows what she's talking about and if you study you can do well on the tests. You just have to make sure to pay attention to detail. Anyways, she's a nice lady and has a cool accent.
Great teacher, but it may have been that I loved the content.
easy but very very boring!
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Kim is a caring professor, and you can tell he is passionate about the material. However, he can be difficult to understand sometimes with some explanations especially with his accent. Previously recorded lectures are posted online and attendance isn't recorded in lectures though.

He was kind and respectable but the lectures just felt so long. Kind of east to understand but if you space out just forget about it. Supplement with Jankowski's online lectures is usually ok. I just stopped attending lecture and started doing so bad.

Extremely thick accent. Made it very hard to understand his lectures, so I stopped going after a month. He does okay at explaining concepts, it's just hard to understand him and the math at the same time.

If you are taking 1553, dont stress about the professor you get. Prof Kim is a nice guy and wants to see his students succeed but because attendance isnt mandatory numbers started to dwindle throughout the semester. Lectures are posted online and all sections have the same exams that are pretty similar to the practice exams.
Super nice guy but it was just hard to understand him. Learned from the textbook and online lecture videos, attendance is not mandatory.
nice guy but he goes really fast and could not understand much. Basically useless to go to lecture. Just watch the online videos on Canvas instead and save yourself the struggle.
He is a really nice guy, but he speaks really fast and it can be hard to understand him at times. I prefer watching online lectures

This class was more work than I expected, but it wasn't necessarily difficult. Most classes are focused on group discussions, and you will be expected to participate. I found the class to be really interesting, and you will definitely walk away with a much better idea of leadership. Stacey is such a caring professor, and I highly recommend her!

Take this if you want an easyish A. Don't take this if you're a senior who has free elective left and wants to sit in the back and bs your way to graduation. This has some good leadership lessons if you're new to it though. There's a ton of participation and you are obligated to go to class for your grades and group work. Work is not difficult.

Ms. Stacey is a wonderful professor.  She clearly presents everything well and is truly invested in your growth.  If you put effort into the class you can learn a lot and improve your leadership quite easily.  That being said if you don't put much effort in, you'll still easily get an A.  You won't learn as much as you could, but you'd still pass.
so easy, lots of easy individual assignments like one-page reflections, and then 2-3 group projects, basically graded by completion

He was definitely well informed on the topics of the in class discussions, and he is also very helpful when you ask him for ideas on structuring your assignments. There is almost no way to get a bad grade as long as you complete your assignment on time.
very cool guy

Spring 2025. Nice guy and you can tell he is intelligent and well-learned. One time he grilled each of us individually in front of the entire class about our podcast projects and maybe I'm too sensitive but I almost started crying it was so bad. I'm sure he didn't mean to be harsh and he did let up when he could tell I was panicking.

You can tell this professor really knew what he was teaching and he really seemed to care about what was taught. Though he tends to go on a ramble once in a while, he makes it clear what to complete and how to complete it. He's super flexible with deadlines (and gave us a rewrite) and as long as you try you will get an A on every single assignment.

Wonderful guy. He deeply cares about what he teaches and it is so evident. The topic was Ethnography, so it was a little hard to grasp at first, but interesting.  There is sometimes a lot of work but you will get an A if you put in effort. I loved taking Dr.Dolan's class. Only complaint is that he doesnt grade in a timely manner.

Was not a terrible class, grading was easy, but he left pretty much all of the assignments to be graded in the last 2 weeks of the semester. There's a lot of writing in the course, but it comes in bursts - half the time you have no HW, and the other half you have a lot of work to do in order to complete before any of the large projects are due.
The professor seems to genuianly want his students to learn and cares about their ideas. The class is not to difficult if you do the assignments on time.

Dolan is a really nice guy, definitely cares a lot about his work. Grading was pretty easy on us, so if you put a smidgen or more of effort you will get an A. The one feedback I have on him is that he left a lot of stuff ungraded till the end of the semester, which made it difficult to gauge progress and whether you need to change your approach.

Yaps lots but taught a really well-thought-out course. Projects were very open ended which is great if you like that, but definitely semi-unclear grading criteria. However, it seems like if you give a genuine effort to complete the assignment he gives an A. A really nice, thoughtful, and accessible guy who takes a genuine interest in your ideas.

Professor Dolan is a really nice teacher and easy grader. He can sometimes ramble, but overall, he is pretty interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but you have four absences for the whole semester, whatever the reason. Assignments are not too hard.

A pretty good class with a standard workload. Don't take if you want an ez A. Varied assignments including making a video and podcast, as well as group project. Tries to engage the class which is great, and he loves discussions (socratic seminars). Attendance is graded, but he's a very lenient grader. Wants you to succeed. Definitely recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really caring, understanding, and talks about interesting material and insight. Gives detailed feedback as well. I highly recommend :)
Very cool professor, he's flexible and cares about his students. Grading is lenient. Highly recommend.

Super chill, easy grader. He is really understanding of students and isn't too harsh on participation. Seems super passionate about what he talks about though! Classes are usually spent for class or group discussions.

Dr. Dolan is really laid back and understanding of issues. He is quick to respond to emails as well. He does take a while to grade, but his feedback is helpful. He really appreciates engagement with his questions and does a lot of group discussions. Overall, he was a good professor.

Dr. Dolan is such a nice professor. If you participate in class and complete the artifacts to the best of your ability, he recognizes that it is reflected in your grade. He understands our lives as college students and isn't there to make it more stressful. His chosen topic was also very interesting. Would totally recommend taking his class!

Dr. Dolan is awesome; he is a very laid-back professor who places a big emphasis on group discussions rather than traditional writing assignments. He is always helpful and gives very good feedback; as long as you do the work (which is not hard) and maybe get some feedback from him you're chilling with an A+. Would def recommend

Prof Yao is very kind and funny. He was easy to meet with and explained things well in a 1-1 setting. He has a little bit of an accent so his lectures were difficult for me to follow along with but his notes and slides outweighed this! I should have gotten an A in this class but honestly I was just being a slacker, would totally recommend!

(MSE6600) Honestly he is a very enjoyable teacher and is very easy to talk to. I went in knowing absolutely nothing and feel like he's very accomodating and helpful. Homework is difficult but he makes sure you understand all you need during class. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very funny, caring and respectful of students, was accessible outside of class and would extend deadlines if needed all to accommodate needs he saw. Dr. Yao is passionate about statics and made it interesting, he's also good at teaching the concepts. Not an easy class and exams could be tough but well taught and expectations outlined well.

he definitely can be hard to follow and understand and you will be teaching yourself a lot BUT he really cares about the students (often extends the homework), he is super passionate about the class, and is so open to helping however he can. The tests are harder than the practice tests though so do study.
the midterms were super easy but the final was so evil- nothing like the sample final when that's obviously what we expected given that every midterm was maybe slightly harder than the sample
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures may seem slow, but he gets through class material on pace, so it's probably just the nature of statics. Makes jokes during lecture that make him seem like a dad/uncle. Clearly values students time, and he extended all of our homeworks if we asked. Pretty much tells you what will be on exams and how to prepare

He is a very funny and enthusiastic professor. He covers material through his slides and sometimes it is not clear. He is very open to explaining further when asked, and wants you to come to office hours (it was part of participation). The exams are mostly easy and his grading policy is very fair.

He's a very caring person and likes teaching, but is just not good at it. A combination of a thick accent, trying to make jokes that don't hit (and break lecture cohesion), laughing at his jokes, and talking very slow made it hard to learn during class. His exams are easy - he gives a review guide with essentially the same problems on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Yao is a very caring and funny professor. his lectures were sometimes unclear but if you ask questions, he easily goes over the information and is always accessible in office hours. needed to self-study some information. exams more difficulty than practice exams but very similar. wants you to succeed in class. extra credit on final
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy always in a great mood to teach. Happy to help in office hours. His practice exams are similar to the midterms and final but slightly easier. He is sometimes hard to understand in lecture and you may have to self study sometimes. Grading is on the chill homeworks, attendance and mostly on exams. Two midterms and a final.

Really funny and caring guy. Prof Yao is very likeable. Lectures are sometimes unclear bc small details are skipped over but he is very helpful and patient if you ask questions.

Exams were similar to practice exams but slightly upped in difficulty.
You can tell this is what he really wants to teach. He's just having so much fun every lecture even if the students aren't.

Professor Yao is kind and helps his students thrive. Office hours were of great help in understanding the "recipe" for each problem set. Chief complaint is that lectures dragged on for long periods, but this was taken during summer. Do your HW, attend class, and remember to sum net force and moments to 0. Statics! :D

Professor Yao was a fantastic instructor, and is someone who genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He was very clear about what he wants in an answer, and his lectures were always extremely informative and helpful. He was always easy to understand, and was extremely approachable if you needed to ask questions or go back over something.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yao was a very good professor. The content on exams was very clear before hand and he always gave very helpful practice tests from the previous year. His lectures were at times confusing, and I had to spend time outside of class learning a few things. That being said, he genuinely wants you to succeed and his office hours are great. Not bad HW
BMED 1000 is a pretty annoying class so not Professor Douglas-Green's fault. Make sure to pay attention to due dates and citations in this class.

Professor Douglas-Green gave extremely detailed feedback for all assignments. Her feedback is helpful for getting better grades in the future if you take into account what feedback she gave and revised accordingly. The BMED 1000 course layout is not fun and can be confusing, so determine your due dates at the beginning of the semester.
Dr. Douglas-Green is a very kind and enthusiastic professor. She gives very constructive feedback on assignments and she seems like she really wants you to do well.
Thank you Simone Douglas-Green for helping me understand the material. I wish you the best in life. Students, you will enjoy her class.

It was clear that Dr. Douglas-Green was inexperienced as a guide and professor. While she was interested in your success, her guidance was uninformed. BMED 2250 is an easy A, but you're better off with another facilitator. I don't feel like I am a better scientist for having taken this class, and that was evident in the group presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Could genuinely tell he cared about us students. Broke the material down well but class was designated practice time. Lectures were videos we had to watch on our own time so if that's not your thing beware.

Dr white is insanely intelligent but sometimes it makes it hard to understand what he is teaching or saying because he is so smart. His assignments are super long and he's a tough grader. His exams are also super hard and impossible to finish but he curves. He expects a lot but is super nice. Just be mentally prepared lol

Flipped classroom, and the online lectures are boring. Tbh I watched the goat Jeff Hanson's lecs on youtube, way shorter and still learned everything needed for class problems. Super lenient grader, just wants you to succeed so as long as you can make yourself watch the vids you'll be good. Only downside is paying for the course but so worth it.

Dr. White's class is tough, but doing the homework, watching the videos, and going to class makes all the difference. His class is flipped, which really helped me to understand the types of questions that would be asked an how to do them. His office hours are amazing. He will sit down with you and walk you through the homework until you understand.
Really nice, 85 is an A and can drop final (over half the class did), he rounded my grade up so I could as well. Def caring and wants you to understand and do well and makes the effort to help.

Professor White really wants you to succeed in his class. The whole course is curved so that an 85 is an A, 75 is a B and so on. He also has one test drop so a lot of students did not have to take the final. All of his lectures were posted online and then in class he would work through practice problems.

Dr. White was great. His online lectures were honestly pretty dull, but he was always very responsive when asked for help and ensured each student had everything they needed to get an A. He was also very generous with grading, looking for any excuse to help a student get up a letter grade. I think his is the best section of statics at GT.

For Statics, he's incredible. Tests are generally 1-3 problems with tons of partial credit that test exactly what you study, so no theory or t/f. Homeworks are important but that's standard for any statics course. Had to pay $40 for this course but I would do it again in a heartbeat after hearing friends' horror stories. Take him if you see him.

Lectures are on the boring side and mostly made up of deriving the formulas, but he also goes over problems and information that you will need for assignments/exams, so I would still try to go to lecture. Average amount of homework and graded fairly, mostly for completion. Many exams, but the grading scheme makes it easier to get an A or B.

One of the most demanding course I have ever done. Assignments in later part of course will be 15-30 pages long. But by the end of course you can design a bridge on your know. Atleast you will know the procedure. The prof will give you very detailed feedback. Try to use as much office hour as you can.

Wayyyy too much work for 3 credit hour class. Homeworks take forever even with group members helping tackle some of the problems. He posts lots of readings and hours of lecture videos you are expected to watch because we couldn't get through the material in the normal lecture times. Very difficult exams too, but he is extremely accessible for help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Too much work. Professor is very accessible but struggles with explaining concepts clearly. Attempts to teach everything in one semester and ends up conveying nothing. Group projects during COVID is not a good idea. Overall, little is learned; lots of assignments are given; and much regret is felt for registering for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor White is very helpful when you ask him questions (always fast to respond on Piazza and email). His exams are hard, but nothing that studying can't get you through. However, he does also test conceptually, and that may have been the hardest part of the class. The homeworks are long, but design problems are generally long anyway. Good prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor- very knowledgeable and prompt to answer questions and provide feedback. Always takes the time to explain things in additional detail and helps you in any way he can.
Long, boring lectures and LONG, difficult tests with a slight curve.
If you need him, he will be there for you. Just ask..
Very good course, but very difficult. Many many many assignments which you work on, in groups, every week. Tests are very challenging and long.

Yoder absolutely cares about his students and goes out of his way to help them, either through (relatively free) bonus points on exams or granting homework extensions. Very receptive to feedback from students. Super talent lecturer and I recommend going to class even if its at 8am, you'd benefit a lot. Exams were super doable if you put in effort.

He is the absolute worst prof I've taken. Crib sheets are allowed but don't help much since he only allows formulas, no labels, no notes, no diagrams, and NO UNITS. His lectures are fairly good I guess, but they cover material beyond the textbook, and he does not cover all the textbook material you need to know, which balloons the material so much.

Genuinely cares about students. Replies fast to email and piazza.  Grades on understanding, so math errors don't count much off.  But then exam problems sometimes have a nuance or twist.  So you have to learn for a good grade.  Lectures helped me with the textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nightmare to take. His lectures don't really help with his exams which he makes extremely difficult. He allows a cheat sheet but you're only able to write formulas, no labels, no units, nothing.

2 Hr 8AM is hard enough already, but he speaks softly and gets too into the math that doesnt help understanding. Textbook is best. exam prep was a practice exam that didnt match actual; no key provided. Recitations are only good option for review. Exams are hard, with recently improved grading. Not a bad person, but his teaching didn't work for me.

Best professor I've had at since coming to Tech.  His exams are harder than average, but I think grades work out in the end.
Super clear lectures, and he can make the hard stuff make sense -- he really wants us to understand the material well, so that we can solve new problems.  Put in the work, you'll learn a lot and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yoder makes sure to make any class he teaches much more difficult than it needs to be. His exams are near impossible

Dr Yoder purposely makes any class he teaches more difficult than it needs to be. He asks for feedback and then ignores genuine advice when you give it, only responding when you give him compliments. There are many students who take his class 3 or 4 times, and they under stand the material, but Yoder's exams always get them.
The best prof I've had during my 3 years at tech. He has high expectations of students but is very willing to help. Put in the work and you'll learn a ton!

I might drop, but only cause it takes a lot of time. starts at 8:25 AM.  lectures are 2 hours long.
Not the most exciting class, but you'll learn well if you keep up with the lectures
and the textbooks.  I think he explains things well, maybe more detail than needed,  but he's pretty helpful with questions in class and piazza.

DO NOT TAKE, AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Unless you like spending hours upon hours of studying material that is as boring as paint drying then do not take this class. The homework isn't hard but it does almost nothing to prepare you for the tests. Class is 2 hours long and unbearable the whole time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor in the ECE department. Like others have said, exams are incredibly hard, he gives no test preparation materials, and the homeworks don't prepare you very well. The only "curve" is in the form of a bonus question on the exams that are so far beyond what is attempted to be taught in lecture. Do not take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prob one of the worst ECE professors in the entire department. Exams are needlessly hard, his lectures and homework are just straight ripped from the textbook, which is a chore to read. Exams are 90% of the grade so if you bomb one you're cooked. He also yaps in class about how things are done in industry. Just put the grade in the bag bro.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Always gets on his "soapbox" and talks about "how things are done in the industry" when it's clear he's been in academia most of his life - little to no grasp on how things are in the real engineering world. Insists students learn the material his way. Tests are needlessly difficult and go beyond homework/lectures. Exams are most of the grade.

Great lectures with a heavy emphasis on understanding the variables and theory at play with all derivations. Sometimes uses concepts in explanations that are beyond the scope of the course, which can be confusing, but are not mandatory to fully grasp to succeed. Sticks to the book, and provides full lecture notes prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures aren't very clear or easy to understand. All homework and most practice comes straight from the textbook, he does not prepare students for his tests well. With test making up 90% of the final grade he grades the tests very harshly with no curve. I would definitely say he is the most difficult 2040 professor.

I more or less agree with the most recent bad review before me. Lectures were effectively copied from the textbook line-by-line, and the semi-interesting material was consistently drowned out by Dr. Yoder's constant need to tie it to niche/irrelevant applications in electronics. He taught how I would if I wanted to put no effort in.

His class was made difficult almost entirely by the lack of preparation and organization on his part. He assigned problem numbers straight from the book, forcing students to buy it. Most lectures he went off on tangents specific to his background, irrelevant to the class and most attendants. Was very condescending whenever anyone asked questions.

Good and caring guy, personable and admirable. Passionate for having his students understand the material inside and out; but he's just as difficult, perhaps the most difficult 2040 professor. His grading is pretty merciless on his tests, and no curve.
A lot of homework, and tests are somewhat tough, but reasonable. Very knowledgeable instructor who is very patient with questions. If you want to understand micro, take his class.

He seems quite happy to assume everything is the students lack of effort and never stops to consider that his lectures are filled with mistakes and leave out keep pieces of information. Since there is no textbook after Ch.3 you have no idea where to find correct formulas when you finally do the test will hinge on some random trick. Bad Teacher.
Yoder is the most helpful. A tough but fair teacher. You learn the material! (which is what counts)

This was a difficult class!  My friends and I had to put in a lot of time to get good grades, because it's so much new information coming at you so quickly.  I enjoyed his lectures, and he's very patient answering questions that come up in class.

Without a doubt the worst professor I've had in my time at GT. Notes were quick, confusing, and not posted online. Frequently asked questions to the class during lecture but usually answered them himself when the class was too lost to say anything. Claims you'll be fine if you understand the concepts but tests were mostly math-based.
He's really good at explaining things, even though electromagnetics is a difficult class.
Great teacher!
terrible teacher!
I wish he would teach more classes.
He is decent for ECE 3025 but never take him for ECE 3040

The best lecturer I've had, made me much more interested in physics after taking his class as a non-physics major. Difficult course, but grading is pretty lenient with open book exams and lots of extra credit.

Super funny and always made me want to learn more. Convinced some of my non-physics major friends to take this class because I truly believe it's better than regular physics and you'll have a much better time. Only bad thing is how long the labs and lab reports were but still deserves a 5/5 nonetheless!

Dr. Sherbakov is an amazing teacher who does a great job of making the content simple and easy to understand. The tests are similar to the reviews that he gives before the exam, but the homework is quite difficult at times, so beware of that. That being said, fantastic class!
Nice lectures, cool guy. Theres quite a bit of homework but the exams are easy
Great professor. There's a lot of homework, but it is very helpful for learning the material. Show up to the exam reviews, those were always very similar to the actual exam.

My absolute physics GOAT. Fantastic lectures, tedious but interesting labs, and just great overall. You don't have to read the textbook, but it definitely helps on homeworks and exams. If he is an option for any physics class, TAKE HIM. You won't regret it one bit. Truly the best.

He is a fantastic teacher and makes hard topic easy to understand. Though the labs can be a lot of work, I would recommend honors physics 2 over regular physics 2 solely for having Scherbakov as a teacher.

Clearly passionate about teaching the class; even though I took algebra based physics 2 in high school, I still went to every lecture for him. Assigns some pretty difficult homework every week, but the answer key can be found online. Exams are exactly like the practice problems he does in class, so you should be well prepared for each of them.

Amazing professor, never hesistate to take him if you get the opportunity. Lectures are amazing and really gives you a deep understanding of the subject matter. Hw comes straight from the textbook and answer key can be found online. Very caring professor, and anyone can get an A if they put an honest effort. Take him!

amazing prof. really good lecturer and explains every step of how to derive certain equations and how they all relate. Homework is from the book but there's free pdf version and answer key. The class is hard and definitely requires lots of practice and studying, but scherby was one of the best prof's I've ever had.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Fantastic lectures, highly accessible outside of class and super helpful with questions. The material was difficult but he made it seem easy--put in the work and you'll get that A. If you're ever stuck deciding between PHYS2212 and PHYS2232 with Scherby, pick the latter and you won't regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Absolutely amazing professor. Was super helpful and very flexible with students. Has a great sense of humor too. This class is extremely hard but taking it with him makes it so much better as lectures are so instructive.

DO NOT SKIP CLASS! Even if attendance is not mandatory!

Even though he doesn't have a 5.0 he's still the absolute goat. Notice he's got over 70 5s to Marty's under 30. Not dragging Marty but I've been hearing some Dorozhkin slander and had to come support.

Was an awesome professor. Classes were fun and somewhat interactive. Some of the home work can be quite time consuming to complete, but are fun to do. He is very understanding and considerate. He often gave extensions on homework. Cannot recommend him enough.

He is an awesome and very understanding professor. He makes his assignments very doable, although some might take longer than others. If he saw that few students had turned in a homework he usually gave an extension to all his sections, which was very nice, especially during exam heavy weeks. Can't recommend him enough!

Insanely funny and chill guy, he makes some of the most annoying parts of this class fun. Workload is a lot. The TAs are nasty graders and will take off lots of points for small things. The team and individual projects are massive time sinks. But he gives you enough resources to succeed and makes lectures fun. Take him if you can.

Chill prof and very useful class. I learned almost everything through the VERY LONG hw and lab assignments, not his boring lectures. Assignments graded quite harshly, taking off for little things. Should be an easy A if you do your work with decent effort. Oh also he'll call you out in front of the class if you're late or on your phone or whatever.

There are many benefits of taking Professor Dorozhkin compared to others (access to the best project materials, has free voucher codes for ~$100 SolidWorks test certificates, more flexible for deadlines/requirements, etc.). However, his fast-paced and somewhat monotone nature made some of the important, dull topics less engaging than they could be.

Awesome prof. Not too tough but hard enough that you learn your stuff. Chill lecture style that's helpful & engaging. Accessible in office hours and happy to help if you have questions on wrangling SolidWorks into shape. Would totally recommend - made 8 am Friday lab fun.

Dorozhkin hasn't lived up to the hype. Rambles during lecture and rushes through the massive amount of content, meaning you rarely retain it. Labs aren't bad but the homework is BRUTAL: several hours a week with unclear requirements. On top of that, the TAs grade very harshly for no reason. There's also 2 projects but they're not that bad.
Lots of work but graded pretty fairly. He is pretty nice but can be a stickler from time to time. Also there is a group project for this class and he chooses groups for you, beware.

I loved Dr. D and his teaching style. He's definitely the most aura 1670 professor and tries to make the lectures more enjoyable even if its an 8am. The grading for the labs can be super harsh along with the assignments, and it can seem stressful. While it might be stressful at first, it keeps you on your toes and they aren't weighted too heavily.

I came into this class with no CAD experience and left it knowing a LOT! The lectures will seem boring, but he posts the slides after if you ever need to reference them. The labs are the most important - he walks through a CAD task and shows you all the necessary elements. It may seem fast a first, but if you need him to repeat a step, he will.

Dr. Dorozhkin is definitely the best choice for ME 1670. I've heard that Pucha gives much more work than him (and Dorozhkin already gave lots of work), and Jacobson went very slowly through the content. His lectures were a little slow, but not very long, and we stopped having to go to them closer to the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework takes a while to do, but hes a great professor and a pretty good lecturer. He seems pretty understanding.

Your grade is mostly composed of two projects (one individual and one team), but he gives you plenty of time to work on them, and he is great at answering any questions you have. Start the homework early so you can get help if needed. He is great at teaching the content, and he clearly outlines what you need to do to succeed. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If he is availble then take him.
He is understanding of other classes, so if you have midterms than he will extend deadlines. Don't talk loud in class or he will call you out.
Fun professor, definitely a manageable amount of work. Great intro to Solidworks. Take him if you can, he added 3 points for CIOS and it's an easy A.

Dorozhkin is the goat. He was an amazing professor, and as someone who knew 0 CAD before taking his class, he explained the concepts in a very fun and interesting way. Two projects are worth the majority of your grade (30% each), but he is a lenient grader. ALSO MAKE SURE TO START ON THE HOMEWORK EARLY
this class gave me such a headache. never again.

Some of the topics that are covered in ME1670 are pretty dry but Dr. Dorozhkin made everything as interesting as possible. He was pretty lenient about deadlines. Final grades are mostly based on 2 projects so don't wait until the last minute. He's a very nice, funny guy and the best professor I've had so far.

100% recommend dr d for me 1670. really chill prof but his lectures are very informative. one hw and one lab assignment almost everyweek so start doing them early. the TAs are tough graders but use their office hours, very helpful. but u cannot choose ur team for the team project. gives loads of extensions and is very understanding.

Dr. D is an amazing prof. and he teaches the subject on a very high level. He has pretty lenient grading policies to let student be creative in class and has a really fun personality to boot. I personally think that the hardest part of this class is making sure everything is perfect, because even though he is nice, a lot of the TA's are not.

This dude is one of the most chill professors I've had. He taught us how to sketch (my drawing skills were inadequate before this), and gave us a large window to explore the world of CAD. I also got my nickname of the Backscratcher kid from him :)

To succeed, I recommend starting early on HW, and practice!

Prof. Dorozhkin is awesome, but the TAs are super picky about what they take points off for. I lost so many points on homework for miniscule things, but sometimes my major errors went unnoticed. You can't choose your group for group projects. Pay attention to his lectures whenever you start learning SOLIDWORKS design drawings!

Dr. D >>> Pucha is what you'll hear. Very chill, easy grader. Some assignments were time consuming and frustrating, but that's just the nature of a CAD class. It's significantly less work than other profs. Highly recommend.
He is absolutely amazing and engaging. The content is not bad at all, and you just need to be prepared for a lot of work.

Dorozhkin is the go-to-professor for ME 1670! Light grader, great explanations. Team projects require four SolidWorks parts per person while others may require ten! Meet the requirements: easy A. Always at office hours and willingly gives advices on professional development and CAD practice. He is so funny in lectures and clearly answers questions.
Legit went to like almost all his office hours. My favorite professor by far. He's really chill and super helpful. Take him. GOAT of GOATS

Probably my favorite professor so far. Funny, engaging, and caring. Made class so much fun and, his lectures were straight to the point and easy to understand. He also frequently gave the class extra time to submit assignments for various reasons. Was very knowledgeable and gave students everything they needed to be successful in the class.
Great professor! He was very good at getting straight to the point and always made it clear what he expected.

The class is easy. Any work assigned is usually busy work. There is an individual and group project that takes time. But, he was always willing to extend the deadlines. He is very funny and develops relationships with students. Lectures are kind boring and required, but towards the end of the semester he makes them optional and cancels labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice, and frequent funny quips in lecture made it engaging and fun. There were also several points in the semester where he visibly displayed that he thought what we were working on / what he was teaching was cool, which is important for students and is much appreciated.

If gigachad was a professor, Denis Dorozhkhin would be him. Lenient homework extensions (which are super convenient for stressed out weeks), good lectures, clear explanations, and an well-round great professor. Would definitely recommend.
Great professor, always made sure we were following along in class and you can tell he cares. Also can be very lenient with you as long as you talk to him first.
Love this man.

Dr. Dorozhkin has the wit and charm that makes his powerpoint slide lectures legitimately interesting and entertaining. He gives less work than some other ME1670 professors, but you won't miss out on any important learning. The assignments are concise and useful. Plan for the team project ahead of time.
best dude ever
Great professor. Clear explanations and his jokes land. The TA can be a tough grader, but he is not harsh.
Funny professor. Attendance is mandatory but there are no quizzes or tests, just projects, labs, and hw. French TA grades pretty tough though.

Great prof, attendance sucks. Better hope you get a good team. Also avoid the French TA, he loves to give you advice on assignments, then when he grades your work he takes points off because you listened to him. What kind of kink is this?

I'm pretty sure Dr. Denis is one of the best professors I'll ever meet here in Georgia Tech. I really admire and respect him. The material was kind of difficult to me since I'm an international student in my first year, but Dr. D never hesitated to help me with anything and he will even check on you if you are not feeling good. What a great guy.

I liked Dorozhkin a lot. Nice guy, very clear with expectations. The sketching part of the class was annoying, but that's the case no matter who you take. Labs were helpful. You get your individual project printed with a fancy SLS 3D printer with him, so that's cool too.

Pay attention to lectures; they are important for projects. Turn things in time.
Think while using SolidWorks

Lectures were not interesting and hard to follow. Homework was graded to extreme specifications and credit was heavily deducted for minor errors. Corrections were not made aside from labels of 'incorrect'. Professor was not very understanding of circumstances. I received a grade of 0.25/10 on a hw for the wrong file type and could not resubmit.

He is hilarious and knowledgeable about just about everything. The class isn't too challenging, SolidWorks may be a little confusing for beginners and proper dimension sheets (last few assignments) is tedious but other than that there should be no issues for you.
Tries to be funny, and does an admiral job of it. Very lenient and kind professor, willing to make accommodations as necessary, and graded the final project incredibly lightly. Would 100% recommend.
Chill and funny professor. Very knowledgable on Solidworks and will help you out. Lenient on grading. Gets to use awesome 3D printer for one project.

Super funny guy. One of the lowest homework loads for 1670 professor options, so highly recommend taking him! He 3D prints your individual project, so you don't have to coordinate that yourself. Extra credit opportunity given. Really lenient grader on final project reports. Very accessible at office hours. Homework can be long but not too bad.
Dr. Dorozhkin is the best, and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. The workload isn't terrible as long as you don't procrastinate on the cumulative projects.
Dr. Dorozhkin is actually the GOAT.  Man is so funny and really wants students to succeed.  Feel sorry for you if you didn't have him.

Dr. D is an awesome prof. The class is relatively easy, it's just a lot of work. I really enjoyed everything about it; the lectures were fun and chill, the individual project and group project were really fun and provided valuable experience with important skills, and the lectures were entertaining. If you just produce quality work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: He likes to make jokes and he understands the room. We were right after lunch so he always read the room and ended class early if the mood was off. This class is literally just how much time you put in out of class to draw and CAD. You don't have to be good at drawing, just follow the steps and take your time.
Dr. D was consistently interesting in a class that could easily be painfully boring. He was very fair with grading and always willing to help after class.

Fun proff, learned quite a bit. Alot of assignments that take quite a bit of time but its relatively easy to get an A overall in the class. You don't really need to do the extra credit animation for the final team project unless you messed up alot of the other assignments.

Dr. Dorozhkin's ME 1770 class is hands down the most well-thought-out course I have ever taken, and arguably one of the best overall. He really knows what he's doing and will never give you a mediocre answer to a question. He has a great personality too.

Dr. D is a fantastic choice for 1770. His amazing dry humor enhances what would otherwise be a completely boring course, and he is clearly very knowledgeable when it comes to SolidWorks and engineering best practices.
Dr. D is an awesome professor and I would totally take again. Very funny and makes the class fun
Solid choice for ME 1770. The class itself sucks though.

Dr. D was very nice. He has a sense of humor which seems a bit dry but because it's dry it's hilarious. The class is a good workload. Just follow instructions for the assignments to get through the homework. The group and individual project take up a lot of your grade so make sure you do your best on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: TAs will give you bad grades. Don't fret! Give your best in your Individual and Group projects and you'll come through with an A. One of the best profs I had at GT till now!

Denis is an amazing professor! He is always energetic and brings life to what could easily be a boring class. Don't be discouraged if the TA's give you super low grades on the homework. They pretty much count for nothing compared to the 2 projects you do, which Denis will give you a very high grade on. TAKE HIM

Dr Dorozhkin was an amazing professor! His lectures were engaging and funny, the hw really helped develop CAD and drawing skills. Since the class is pretty much project-based you can do little work and get an A. I would recommend putting effort into the class to push yourself, you're gonna have more fun and learn more! TAs are also a good resource!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dorozhkin is definitely the best professor for 1770. The class has a lot of work but some other professors have more work. Basically there's 1 homework assignment a week, occasionally a lab assignment, and 2 big projects that make up most of the grade. He's a funny guy, only complaint is the lectures got pretty boring due to the material.
Dr Dorozhkin is a fantastic, caring professor. His personal stories are very entertaining; especially when he talks about casting lead in the sand. Very accessible for feedback too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely take Dr. Dorozhkin for 1770. This class was a lot of work, but I know people in 1770 with other professors had a lot more work. Pretty much there was one assignment per week and then two main projects. I procrastinated hard on both projects, causing some pretty awful weekends, but the grading was super easy. Pretty easy A if you try.
He's a nice guy but his lectures are boring. The class has a lot of work due to the homework and projects. The TAs grade the homework hard as well. However, you are able to learn a lot.

Dorozhkin is pretty lax on grading as long as all the necessary components are there. His lectures can be pretty dull but he occasionally cracks jokes that can keep it from being too boring. Has a good attitude towards the class and almost always end lab an hour early / lets you leave when ever if its a work day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take anyone except Dorozhkin for ME 1770. He's funny, good at what he does, and understanding of students. Class can be sometimes boring, but Dorozhkin's in-class attitude and humor makes up for it. Attendance is mandatory so definitely show up. The homework will be time-consuming, but put effort into it and you'll get a good grade. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is funny, relaxed, and cares for his students. Lectures reflect his chill attitude and aren't too crucial for understanding material. Assignments are simple, and help is always available if needed. They consume a lot of time, especially if you're new to drawing/modeling. The group project is a grind if you procrastinate, but is graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Dorozhkin is a really great professor for 1770 and cares a lot about his students doing well in his class. The first section of the class on engineering sketching sucks, but the CAD portion of the class is very interesting. The class is completely HW and project based, there are no tests. Getting HW and work on projects done early is essential.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. D is really funny and tells you exactly what you need to do for the course. He is respectful, though sometimes the lectures get boring. Not hard to get an A.

It has been a wonderful semester with Dr. D. He teaches just enough where the students lose neither themselves nor their drive to learn more. You can do whatever you want and can in his class. He does not impose limits on your capacities. Given that, you will still make a great grade if you show up and follow easily understood guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. D was a great professor. He makes jokes and you can tell he really understands what he's talking about. I would definitely recommend taking ME 1770 with him!

Dorozkin is a great professor, he is very relaxed and not tough on grading. He is well respected and loves Solidworks. Lectures can be a snore but he is able to make them a little entertaining with his cool personality.

Dr D. is hilarious and does his best to add life to the lecture material, which is miserably boring. The grading criteria is listed on all assignments and as long as you do what it says you will get and A. Grading on the group project is super relaxed and the final presentation was very laid back. You will never have to stay for the entire lab.

Dr. D made ME 1770 really enjoyable. Lots of drawing work at the beginning and the final group project is difficult at times, but overall really rewarding. Gives creative freedom with most assignments. He also has some good jokes, but he can be hard to hear from the back of the class. Projects took awhile to be graded. Overall fun and easy class.

Dorozhkin is the best prof. for ME 1770. The homework was time consuming, but he was an easy grader. If you show that you tried and meet all of the criteria you're basically guaranteed an A. He was funny in lecture and kept the environment light-hearted. Just take his class if you can. You won't regret it.
I loved this class and Dr. D. Super easy. All you have to do is the hw and show up. He just wants to see that you are trying. Not a super hard grader. Would definitely take him again.
Gives some random pop quizzes, so show up. Fun professor overall and not too difficult.

Dr. D is really the best ME1770 professor. The assignments are easy to get full credit if you just meet the bare minimum he requires. The group project does have some stress but you will probably get a 100 on it. As long as you put in some effort, you will get an A. There are no tests or finals, just the group project presentation as a final.

Take. Him. Do. It. He is awesome! The most chill Russian prof at Tech by far ;). He is super nice, super hilarious, super helpful, etc., etc. You do have a good bit of homework outside this class, but it is not difficult, just time consuming, but the CAD homework I really enjoyed. If you are taking ME 1770, everyone knows you gotta take Dorozhkin.

Easy class if you put in the time and effort. He's very chill, but sometimes he seems a bit apathetic about the class. He doesn't do very much to make the material interesting, so I found the lectures boring most of the time, despite having mandatory attendance . Instructions and grading are clear, and his expectations are not too high. Easy A tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dorozhkin is probably the easiest ME1770 professor. He is very chill and a very lenient grader (although the TAs grade your homework). He is also fairly humorous and incorporates some Russian humor into his lectures, but the material is still quite dry. Also, Dorozhkin may not give as much work, but the class is still fairly time consuming.

Love him. Super easy going and cares about students. Very accessible, has lots of office hours. Only complaint would be sometimes he treats you like you're dumb when asking for help. But his feedback is very helpful. Overall cool guy, and would definitely recommend.

He is a very caring teacher that presents everything in a very accurate manner. He uses a presentation format and gives plenty of chances for extra credit. He has a very dry sense of humor that many people seem to enjoy, he even roasts his students in class sometimes.

Dr. Dorozhkin made class fun with witty remarks and was very helpful with CAD... If you have experience with CAD, the lectures can be a little bit boring (I didn't really pay attention and still got an A). Most HW grades are based on your ability to follow the directions for sketching and CAD; for the individual/final project he doesn't grade harsh

Dorozhkin is AWESOME! Super funny guy, very approachable, easy class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He is super helpful with homework and assignments. Funny guy, yet lectures are pretty pointless but that is mostly due to the course material, not Dorozhkin. DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. You wont even touch it.

Great professor for 1770. No extremely difficult assignments, willing to offer help when needed. Very nice guy who leads the class well. Overall no qualms. He literally said to our class, "You're really going to have to work hard to NOT get an A in this class." Go to class and do the weekly sketching/CAD homework and the A is yours.
Dr. Dorozhkin's class is extremely straight forward. Simply participate and do the assignments and the A is yours. Very approachable and just an all-around nice guy. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Dorozhkin is super laid back and always kept class very lively with his folksy Russian jokes. Deadlines in his class are usually very flexible and he's regularly available for extra help if you need any. He's also a really lenient grader, although a lot of the grading is done by TAs who may or may not be as lenient as he is .

Hilarious Russian guy that cracks semi-lame jokes in class (which I still found funny), but also teaches the material very thoroughly and is very likely to give points back on homework assignments if you ask him about it. Awesome teacher that made a overwhelming (work load) class easier. Also did not hesitate to push due dates back if necessary.

No tests, just an individual project and a group project.  He assigns intermediate deadlines so you don't get too far behind on either.  Frequent homeworks but not that hard.  I've heard he's a lot easier than the other ME 1770 professors.  As long as you do your work and don't fall behind the class is easy.

Dr. Dorozhkin is very good at teaching and is generally a very easy grader. I definitely recommend him for anyone looking to take ME 1770. He is very approachable and is always willing to help as well.

No tests, 2 easy pop quizzes.  Attendance is 100% mandatory.  I took him his first semester here for 1770.  He has a thick Russian accent but I never have trouble understanding him.  Lots of work, but that's the nature of the course.  Pick simpler topics for projects and pray to God that your group isn't bad.  Would take again.

Pretty good lecturer in a class that could use some better structure. Most lectures were easy to follow with helpful examples. Homeworks were fair and graded very leniently. Some exam questions were hard to understand and work with, but were graded fairly. Would reccomend!

Dr. Hummel is a fantastic professor who really seems to care and be passionate about teaching ME heat transfer. He connects a lot of the course to his NRE experience which I liked because it makes the class less abstract and more applicable. Fair grader, but it's heat transfer so its just a tough course by nature, wouldn't take it with anyone else

Had Dr. Hummel for NRE 4214, and he did a decent job teaching the content. He is a bit disorganized, and seemingly randomly hand-waived a lot of theory sometimes while diving deep at others. He may not understand theory as well as he should, but he is funny and cares about his students, and he will respond to emails timely. Very lenient grader.

New professor, exams were all over the place. Sometimes open-note, sometimes not. Unclear on exam topics and refuses to give out practice exams. Claimed a curve but took it back. Overall adjusting to tech but definitely go with another heat transfer prof. until he gets settled in 3-4 years.

He's new to teaching this class, but did a solid job all things considered. Did come off as unorganized at times, but give him a semester or two and he'll definitely be one of the best at Tech. Funny guy, really personable and gives great feedback whenever you ask to go over something with him.

Dr. Hummel is a newer professor, and is still figuring out the best way to lecture to and test his students. Tests were kinda unpredictable, but he's a very good professor, and he's really funny. Give him another year or two to figure out his teaching style and I think he'll be one of the best heat transfer professors at Tech. I def recommend him.

Dr. Hummel was not the best professor I have had at Tech. I feel like with better lecture organization, test structure, and accessibility outside of class my experience would have been A LOT better. The content was presented in a nonchalant manner that sometimes made it hard to follow. He was a nice guy and even funny, but not the best
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hummel is a very good lecturer and a very kind and caring person. He grades a bit tough but is always available to go over any mistakes made in the assignments so that you better learn from them. 10/10 would take his class again.

Made the most difficult artifact (group podcast) the first one in the semester so you're kind of thrown into everything, but that means the semester gets easier as you continue. Dr. Nance is clearly very interested in the class and is always excited to talk more about topics we research for the course.
Total Karen. Not serious. Probably reads on weekends and grades like it
This professor is amazing. I had him for 1102 over the summer and I learned a lot in his class and had fun with the projects he assigned us. Definitely take him if you have the opportunity.

This professor is a D1 yapper and he would always overexplain a topic which made some things, like homework unclear. He's also very by the book when it comes to giving people grades. You have to follow the assignment requirements down to a T to get a perfect score. He does give extensions on assignments if you talk to him though.

Professor Davidovic has a good sense of humor, and is better at lecturing than many of the other E&M professors. However, he is very disorganized, forgets to assign homework, and goes extremely slowly through the course content. Our final was on 2 chapters, as this was all we sufficiently covered. Good lecturer, bad administrator, fun experience.

Overall, Professor Davidovic is one of the best professors in the physics department. Electrodynamics is a difficult class, but he is more than willing to take his time to explain difficult concepts. He also has a great sense of humor. I would recommend taking.

We were supposed to cover 6 chapters and only ended up covering 3. This is a massive problem because electrodynamics starts at chapter 7 which means you have missed 3 entire chapters and have no idea what is going on with magnetism. Avoid him especially if you have to take Electrodynamics.

I took this class in Fall 2022, and his tests were take home. However, the tests were SUPER long/hard so I would spend 8+ hours on each one. I think he said he is not doing online tests anymore. We were supposed to cover 6 chapters but we only got to 3 because he went really slow. He lectures straight from the textbook, so no need to go to class.

Professor Davidovic is one of the most caring compassionate professors I have ever had. He's extremely careful to make sure students feel comfortable in his class and extremely flexible when extenuating circumstances arise. He also usually responds to emails within minutes or seconds of being sent. Lectures and tests are reasonable, good textbook

Davidovic is a fine teacher -- nothing special but he cares about his students. The tests are usually difficult, but he gives so much partial credit that it is not difficult to get an A. Also, and 80+ is an A in PHYS3122 with him, which is a big plus.

Davidovic is constantly unprepared for his lectures and makes many mistakes which end up taking time, assuming he doesnt give up and ask you to figure it out on your own. Ive no doubt he has a good handle on the material he teaches but he can not express it to others well. Thankfully, he followed the book exactly, and the book was written well.
AMAZING if you can take him DO!!! He could teach physics to a hamster.

physics i (classical); exams are 5-6 questions multi choice, one of which is extra credit; must play your luck; questions are not bad, must have studied, understand material beforehand; easier exams than other phys profs in same course; labs are boring but easy. go to class, take notes; low attendance, but sometimes tells you what'll be on tests.

He goes into a lot of theoretical rigor and if you take the time to actually do his derivations/calculations by hand (especially in your own time), you will be beyond prepared for the exams. If you have questions go to his office hours he's pretty chill and will take time to explain. His slides are different, and I think if used well, are better.
I think out of all the professors teaching physics 2212 he's like middle of the road in terms of quality, Not the end of the world if you get him but there's better options.
Zangwill is the best physics professor if you pay attention. He is a genius and the monopole theorem is the most important thing I have learned in my life!
They took down my review but TAKE ANY OTHER PROFESSOR. Genuinely still thinking about how much I disliked this course solely because of this prof.
I've had professors before who were strict or maybe even a little unfair, but Professor Zangwill is the first professor I have ever had in my life who was genuinely mean.

Nice guy, but does not know how to lecture in a way that prioritizes what we need to know for exams the way the other professors do (his ppts are the only ones different from everyone else's too). Put simply, if you like yourself (even a little), choose any other prof. Otherwise, by all means choose him.

Ok lecturer, sometimes bad on time-management and would rush the last parts of lecture. Didn't really explain or do many practical examples in class compared to other professors. Helpful in office hours and explained the concepts well, but his style of teaching was just too theoretical and required a lot of outside practice to do well on exams.

Zangwill isn't terrible but I never felt prepared for the exams from his lectures. we seemed to be consistently behind other sections and had the lowest averages if I'm not mistaken. other profs will do much better at helping you succeed since most of us are just taking this class bc its required. I will say he's funny and has a sense of humor

He's not horrible at teaching core course material, but will often mention anecdotes about things for which he is completely ignorant/wrong. He will confidently bring up things/respond to questions on topics about which he is clearly not knowledgeable; seemingly indifferent to the fact that he is misleading a group of 100+ students.

Professor Zangwill is a very knowledgable person on E&M. Transitioning from Physics 1, which for me involved solving many practice problems, to Physics 2 with Zangwill, where we nearly always focused on theory and concepts was very hard. The class is not easy, but doable. He knows the subject very well and always willing to help.

Zangwill is a phenomenal professor. At first, I found him a little hard to follow, but as the semester went on, I got better at determining what he was attempting to convey. The key takeaways is, despite how theoretical physics 2 is, Zangwill would take time and explain grounded, real applications of the theory. I loved his class.

PHYS 2212 is standardized, so there are ~4 profs all with same exams and syllabus, and Zangwill is pretty disconnected from labs and exams. lectures are ok for conceptual understanding, but building the skills to do well on exams are done on your own. I didn't care for lecture but his office hours were very helpful for me, so 3/5

Extremely interesting lectures and clearly knowledgeable professor. Used tests to show us some upper level physics stuff that destroyed many of us. I would totally take him in the fure, just hope that he does not participate in exam writing.
Avoid this professor. He only teaches principals conceptually... the tests and homework are not conceptual. This screwed over many people in his class.

I barely showed up to his lectures, but the few I attended were good and engaging. It's clear that Zangwill is experienced and knows what he is talking about, but isn't great at judging the knowledge of students. Still, HW and labs are good learning resources, and I learned the most from the textbook. I don't understand the hate this guy gets tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is difficult to put into words my disdain for Physics II under professor Andrew Zangwill. Being the first Physics class I have taken at Georgia Tech, I found myself unprepared beyond comprehension for the absolute bombardment of difficulty found on the exams in this class, most of which are created by professor Zangwill.
Very good lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awful Professor
All around terrible please dont take him. VERY rude in office hours

Class was okay and if you paid attention you could pass. He is very rude in office hours and if he does not like you he will give you an unfair lower final grade. I emailed him for clarification on my test grade and got a very rude email back and ended up with a B even though people who I have constantly scored higher than got A. 0/10 recommend.

Dr.Z is an excellent professor and lecturer, the problem with his classes and why people don't excel is because his test aren't exams on the knowledge you would learn from the resources given to you. The homework, class notes, and book will not help you on his test even with it being open book. His test are based on intuition on what's in his head.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is the worse professor I have ever taken. He gives no partial credit on test, even for simple adding/subtracting errors. If you like going to class, memorizing what's written on the board, and blindly regurgitating it onto a test then this is the class for you. He is very rude if you go to his office. Also, he doesn't know math notation.
