Zangwill is a boring lecturer and enjoys criticizing the GT-issued textbook and teaching things "the textbook doesn't bother to mention" about physics (even though they probably won't show up on the test). In my opinion he didn't explain anything in lecture in a way that was useful on the tests.
Great professor. he is tough with students when you come see him for questions, but his teaching is clear and enthusiastic.
Wonderful at explaining material. Cares more about you actually understanding the thought behind the material than calculations. His tests were very difficult, but almost entirely qualitative.

Excellent professor, extremely enthusiastic and make your system of thought in order to think as physicist. I enjoy the class so much. Exams are analytical and open note and open book, so you should attend the class. I highly suggest to go over the material to be ready for the class. Enjoy this semester with him so much.
Excellent at explaining complex material.  Straight talker.
No Comments
No Comments
Not bad since all physics one teachers teach the same material at the same pace.  Nice guy

I took EAS 3610 - Intro to Geophysics. I really enjoyed this class. The lectures were really interesting and Dr Newman did a great job of explaining difficult concepts. The class only had a few homeworks and in-class labs. I highly recommend it.

Some of these old reviews are pretty bad but his class is much easier now! Lectures are fast paced, but Dr. Newman is super nice and good at explaining things. Grading came from weekly quizzes (open note) and labs (my TA was super helpful), so overall, not very difficult. My class was for EAS majors so class structure may be different for others.

Andy is a great guy who enjoys answering questions about anything you have. He is passionate about the material and does research related to the class. There were weekly quizzes (open notes), an optional final (open), and a ton of nice information to learn. As an atmosphere person, I didn't feel bored out of my mind, he is very easy to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was wary at first because of the bad reviews, but he was great! Class was just lectures, but he kept me interested and it's clear he really knew the material. 80% of the grade was weekly quizzes and 20% lab, and both were fairly easy. I took the honors/majors version and we went on field trips, which were super interesting. Overall 10/10

Test questions come from online quizzes at some random college. He gives extra credit quizzes that add a percentage to your grade at the end of the class. Tests account for the majority of your grade; the rest is from lab. Overall not a very strenuous class, just study for the tests. Lectures can be dry but it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tests questions literally come out of no where. The only way to do good is to memorize the book word for word or memorize past tests and hope they reuse questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Newman is an engaging lecturer, but this course covers a LOT of material. It is difficult to tell what he finds important, and some of the test questions come out of nowhere. If you like your grade after the first 3 exams, you can skip the final. Go to class! He gives pop quizzes that go toward extra credit, and it is why I could skip the final.

Newman is not very helpful to his students. Although he did provide the class with several extra credit quizzes, the tests were unreasonably hard. They don't come from lecture material or practice exams. You really need to read the text book to do well in the class.

The lectures are pretty boring but there is a lot of good stuff in it and he gives pop quizzes for extra credit. Also if you really want to do well you will need to read the book which might be the most boring thing ever. Tests aren't to bad for an EAS course even though some of his questions are really weird.

If you take EAS 2600, he's pretty fair. The tests are multiple choice, but there's a lot of material on each, so they're tough. You can't really miss lecture- he covers a chapter a day. But he's good at lecturing, and he covers everything on the tests. If you read the chapters before lecture you can kill this class. Labs are mega-easy too.

His tests were horrible!! Not closely relevant to lectures or book. You literally have to memorize every words he says in class -- including his "jokes" -- in order to do well on his tests!! DO NOT TAKE HIM

What a nightmare. I honestly hated this class. The lectures are boring, the tests are barely relevant to what went on in lecture, and he didn't really seem to care if students did well. I ended up passing, but it was painful every step of the way.

Professor Newman is helpful when you ask for help and his notes make sense, but his tests come from out of nowhere. He asked the TA's to take the tests and my TA didn't turn his in because he was embarrassed. He will treat you like a grad student so if you want a breezy easy class, I don't suggest Professor Newman. There will likely be a curve.

Great professor! Super sweet and caring. Grades reasonably, and you'll do great on assignments as long as you're creative and follow the rubric. Encourages individuality and abstract thinking. Very group work heavy, so make sure you work with people you trust! So sad she's leaving Tech, but hope everything goes well at Emory!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have to take an 8am English class, please pick this one. Dr. Williams' class is not an easy one (by common definitions of the word), but if you put in the effort you will succeed in this course. Btw she also responds to emails pretty quickly and makes efforts to help students the best she can!
Genuinely so caring and so sweet. If you have the chance to take English with her, please take it.
Very sweet and understanding.

Can't get any better than Dr. Duquette. She was simply amazing for 1102. Even though our lectures were bright and early, I was always excited to go to class. She is extremely caring and accessible outside of class if you have any questions. The projects were mainly group-based and fun to work on. I HIGHLY suggest taking Dr. Duquette, even at 8 am.

I think this English section is a little more difficult that others. She grades somewhat harshly, with averages for the Artifacts being around a 90. She learns everyones name though and always makes a welcoming environment in class.

This class overall was easy, and Dr. Williams is nice and understanding when you ask her about assignments or need help. The assignments were slightly more work than I expected to spend time on, but overall would say this is a fantastic teacher.

BEST ENGLISH PROF! Super receptive to feedback, has extremely reasonable policies, and is overall an awesome person. Assignments can be time consuming, but are typically designed well and graded with a very fair rubric. She tends to grade things as complete/incomplete so make sure you thoroughly complete assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Very caring professor, grades based on completion which is helpful for limiting the stress of the class. Gives great feedback, not an insane amount of HW.

Had her for both 1101 and 1102, and it's almost the same with her except 1102 is a bit more work (to be expected).
"Dr. D" is very caring for her students and makes her classes fun and engaging! I learned a lot and genuinely enjoyed her class. :D

I LOVE HER. she is so so kind and caring. I learned a lot while also not being super stressed. She knows that english is not the most stressful class at Tech, and tried to work around the classes with bad teachers and bad grading. I have a lot of respect for her and would take her class again.

Goat. Everything is clearly laid out and she deeply cares about each student's well-being. It's an appropriate level of work (perfect difficulty) and is interesting. Grades easy. Extremely helpful and relevant feedback. Brings treats for students' birthdays. Incorporates input from students. No flaws. Wish I could take her for all my classes.

She really was the sweetest professor. There are no surprises with her class, everything is laid out at the beginning of the semester. As long as you follow the rubrics she gives you and you go to class, you'll do great. She is very nice and very understanding.

super sweet and funny guy! really caring and personable. only gripe is the attendance policy (u will fail the class is u miss 2+ classes) but that's generalized to the class so. class itself was not very helpful if im being honest, but it's only 50 min/week. hes super accessible outside of class and will give u sm chances to makeup absences tho!
this class actually helped me get my 1st internship. he cares a lot and is willing to help at anytime. super awesome and grades lightly.

Class had no organization or structure- just a final project at the end with no rubric or grading guidelines given. I learned nothing, and received a b despite contributing to the project and attending most lectures.

Super useful class if you're looking for an internship, a lot less so if you already have one. But Dutcher is still a great professor, and the homework isn't that difficult. Like someone else said, it's heavier at the beginning of the semester and gets easier, but it all feels a bit inconvenient for just one credit hour.

I found Mr. Dutcher to be incredibly kind and knowledgeable. His best quality is his honesty when it comes to your career field, career ideations, and yourself as a person. The homework is heavy for the first half of the semester but is really light the second half. It's also all really good homework and actually relevant to your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved Prof. Dutcher, hated this course. As a graduating senior with a job, most of the course material was completely useless. Some interesting things, just wish I had freshman or sophomore year instead of wasting my time in it my last semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and truly useful class. Attendance is mandatory (-5pts off total grade every class missed). 1 assignment and 1 easy quiz every week. He/TAs will grade assignments, provide feedback, then give you the opportunity to re-submit, so there's no reason not to get an A in the class as long as you show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Michael is a great resource and a master of career development who is always willing to support and assist as you search for your ideal job. He's definitely someone you want in your corner so participate often and get to know him outside of class!

I really enjoyed taking the Career Development class with Professor Dutcher! He gave great feedback on assignments and really showed that he wanted us to do well and find our dream jobs. Highly recommend!

Really enjoyed being in Michael's career development course. He is actually a career advisor that teaches this class "on the side." He has a lot of great advice and helped me feel confident landing an internship. Just make sure to stay on top of the assignments--most are small but some take a good bit of time, so don't procrastinate.

He is new to GT and I took 3599 with him this fall. The course is fine, assignments are all doable; though some feel like busywork at times, they do provide a benefit. I learned a lot about the nuances of the job search process, and Michael (+ Stan!) were super helpful in giving me career advice as I was looking for internships. Super kind guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lovely woman. She cares about her students and wants to ensure we are learning the content. The content is not easy but she teaches it very well.

Dr. Dutta is fantastic and one of the best English teachers I've had. She is very accommodating and genuinely cares for her students. Her class was so interesting and I looked forward to going. Very discussion based, not much work outside of the few major assignments of the course. Take her class if you get the chance!

A very participation heavy class. She makes you read out loud during class, and as someone with anxiety it was a horrible class to take. I also felt that reading the texts out loud during class was a waste of time when it was our assigned reading before class. If you have anxiety choose a different teacher. If not, you'll be fine I guess.
She is a very caring and awesome professor! Loved her class. Do your work and show up for class; participate and her class isn't too hard at all.

Dr. Dutta is very sweet. You arent required to participate in discussions often but you are expected to read out loud if she calls on you. If you arent an amazing speaker and have troubles or anxieties when giving presentations, she is very understanding. She is also willing to round up your grade as long as you finish the flash writings on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring and understanding professor. I wasn't super interested in the topic at the beginning of the course but the assignments were interesting and engaging and I ended up enjoying the class. Did not take much time outside of class to complete major assignments.
Extremely caring, only a few assignments that really matter, easy grader.

Was very flexible with deadlines and patient with students. Wanted you to participate and add to daily class discussions. Did often change her mind about criteria for assignments, which could be confusing but was a pretty easy grader. Had relatively low expectations for students. Seemed to genuinely care about students' well-being.

Dutta is very nice and cares about her students. I didn't like the class topic but the class was easy. We didn't have any outside reading or assignments beyond the artifacts. Definitely take her class.
She's the best. Barely had to do any work for this class, except for the artifacts.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lane Duncan is a sweet old man who does not teach the standard way. He gave us free reign and our class was very project based. You wont know what you make in the class till it's on your transcript and he doesn't use canvas. We did some cool stuff in his class like nude figure drawing and sometimes he takes his class to piedmont park to draw.
Compared to other professors at Tech, he's at least completed a few actual construction projects; maybe a house every few years.
Really excellent. If you have a chance to take his watercoloring class, take it. It's a hard class, but he's a very good professor--excellent.

Dr. Eva Dyer moves everything too quickly without thorough explanation to machine learning algorithms. She only explained conceptual part while most homework and the exam required large coding abilities. Please do not choose this class if you do not have good foundations in machine learning, and are not willing to learn a lot by yourself

6517 is a ML class for people who already know ML. We were told at the start of class that it was actually good to not have any ML experience and that if we did not know much python, we would pick it up quickly. Neither of those are the case. Currently 5 weeks in and completely lost, Dr. Dyer does a poor job explaining and moves too quickly.

The entire class seemed to be about writing fake journal articles. She does not provide prompt feedback - still waiting on a grade for something completed 10 weeks ago. If you want to be a writer, this may be the class for you but if you want to learn machine learning, avoid the prof if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the greatest profs in the econ department. Absolutely loved him, highly recommend. Took him for ECON 2106, Fall 2025. Class was rigorous, but he was excellent.

Good professor throughout the semester but does not round ANY grades. Emailed him about being 0.03% percent from the next letter grade and he did not care. That's less than 1 extra point on any assignment so be sure to do all extra credit.

Made sure that every lecture was engaging and provided examples that connected concepts to daily life. Lots of extra credit, including for attendance, but tests counted for a large amount of your grade. As someone who had never taken econ, I found the textbook useful because some small test concepts were not explicitly mentioned in lecture.
Professor Brewer is very caring and gives great lectures in an accessible way. He builds a lot of time for questions into his classes.
super chill and gave us extra credit just for showing up. the content itself was sometimes hard to follow but you can tell he really tries to make his lectures entertaining
Lectures are hard to follow and understand.
Pretty chill guy.

Great guy, great professor. Brewer is a very relatable and caring professor while also being interesting and knowledgeable in Environmental Economics. Class was engaging. Had reasonably difficult homeworks and readings of economics papers. Very understanding if you ever needed a due date moved. Actually cared about his students. Take home tests.

Dr. Brewer is an awesome prof. I took him for Environmental Econ and moderately enjoyed the class. With lectures being 75 minutes long, I felt it got boring at times, and my attention waned as the class went on. The class is interesting enough, I like Dr. Brewer's lecture style. He's a funny guy and you can tell he has a heart. Take his class!

I really loved Dr. Brewer's class. You really learn a lot and very in-depth about how economists think about climate change. It is a very econ-heavy class and assumes you have a fair amount of knowledge of micro econ. If you find a good group of people to do the homework with and do all of the extra credit it is very feasible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literal king always does his best to put his students first and make sure they're getting the grade they deserve. Completely failed the first test and still ended with an A.

I took the grad level PUBP version of environmental econ. Only difference is the TA grades a tad harsher. Prof Brewer is a talented lecturer. He's very funny, light hearted, and welcomes questions. The midterm and final were take-home and open note, so go to class and take thorough notes. Highly recommend forming a homework group.

Failed the first test by underestimated the difficulty. Take notes and study frequently. He does everything in his power to make sure that you come out of the class with the grade you deserve. So many extra credit opportunities helped me end with an A.

Absolute GOAT, loved his lectures as he has a great personality and interacts with students a lot, even though the entire class is online. The online aspect also adds a lot of flexibility, as I could do homework earlier in the week. The homework is what I'd expect, but the class is test heavy with tricky questions, but take notes and you'll live.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer is a nice guy who cares about his students but his tests were insanely difficult for no reason. I ended with an A surprisingly with extra credit but this class is super test heavy and homework heavy. I recommend taking a different professor if u can for econ 2106!
I would not recommend taking this professor. The exams are extremely difficult, there is a lot of homework, lectures are not helpful but you only meet for 30 minutes a week.

I took this course online in Spring 2022. Although there's a mandatory meeting, you only meet once a week for a maximum of 30 minutes. Basically, this course is design where you read the textbook, do hw from the textbook, and use the mandatory meeting to ask questions and concern with the class.

Dylan Brewer is a nice professor, but this is class is extremely difficult. The two tests (midterm and final) were extremely different from the homework (sometimes containing material not even covered in class), and he is not lenient at all with grading. His classes are interesting, but this is not an easy class to get an A in.

Brewer is a good teacher and very kind, but his tests are impossible. The class was mainly graded by only two tests, which had C class averages both times. Even with all high 90-100s on homework assignments, my 2 C tests left me at a B average. If you want an A, you cant breeze by for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class consists of weekly textbook readings that accompany the homework. Online lectures are 30 minutes per week and attendance is mandatory (taken through polls). He gives two tests: midterm and final which are pretty hard (I got a B and a C on them) but he gives out plenty of extra credit so I was still able to end the class w an A. Not bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Brewer is awesome. Super funny and chill guy. This class was remote and he makes a point to keep the once-a-week mandatory lectures to 30 minutes exactly or less. We had to read one to two chapters of the textbook every week and there was both completion and graded homework. He offered plenty of extra credit. Overall great guy.

Professor Brewer's class is very chill. You do have to read the textbook by yourself and that is your "lecture". The mandatory attendance professor hosts weekly is not a lecture but more of applying what you are learning this week to the real world of the economy. 

\
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Brewer is great. Class was held virtually, where attendance was only required for one weekly session. Homeworks and tests were virtual and all open note/open internet, although some were a little challenging. You need to watch the lecture vids to succeed. Overall super nice guy, cares about his students, and super passionate. I learned a lot!

I had Brewer for online microeconomics. Every week, he had good, pre-recorded lecture videos, a learning curve assignment (graded on completion), homework (graded for accuracy), and a short online meeting. We only had a midterm and final exam which were kind of hard, but, luckily, there was lots of extra credit! He truly cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ECON 2106 with Dr. Brewer this semester was amazing. 30 minutes of synchronous class per week, and then the rest of the content could be covered at your own pace over the week. Though test heavy (60% between midterm and final), he gives out an incredible about of extra credit. Overall knowledgeable teacher, amazing guy, and chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Intro to Microeconomics with professor Brewer was a blast. Content lectures are recorded so you can watch at 2x speed. There's one mandatory meeting a week that only lasts for 30 minutes. Midterm and final are open everything and multiple choice. The final can replace the midterm! Plus there's extra credit that can boost your final grade by 3.8%.

Dr. Brewer's incredibly understanding of the fact that no one wants to be online for more than 30 minutes. The mandatory lectures once a week are never more than 30 min. The homework is open to collaboration, and all the answers are on Chegg. Tests can be difficult, tho, but are open note, book, internet. Just make sure you take the exams seriously
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor who takes class at a good pace, not a lot of material is covered, however theres tons of outside reading (which I didnt mind and found interesting). Class is easy if you understand basic calculus, and you learn a lot about how economists approach the carbon problem.

The best way to describe this class was chill. There's weekly homework but it only ends up being 2-3 hours a week in total, and we met up once a week for half an hour. The midterm + final make up like 60% of the grade, but they're open note/internet (they're still hard tho so don't be fooled).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Brewer is knowledgeable and very accessible to students to discuss class content and economics in general. Take this class if you are interested in economics and are willing to work hard.

Prof. Brewer is a good guy and very knowledgeable about the course material but I was under the impression that this class would be pretty easy and it really isn't. The tests are pretty tough and the homework varies. If you're looking to take this as an elective for an easy A, don't unless you really love economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was p a i n f u l l y easy. Dr. Brewer assumed we knew zero math or econ going into this class, which caused it to have a ridiculously slow pace. Even before covid happened I was baffled by how little content we had covered by week 10. Take him if you want a very easy A, but certainly not if you want to learn new things

At first we all did horribly on his tests, but once we asked him the best way to study, we started doing a lot better. Reading the textbook and doing the practice problems is the best way to prepare. Tests are 3 free response q's and he curves the class. He's a really nice guy, and he gives good career advice.

Too many people give this guy a bad rep. Truth is, I think it's hard to find a professor as fascinated by physics, and if approached after lecture this guy makes very interesting conversation. Yes, the tests are generally 5 questions multiple choice and one free response, but lots of them are quite common sense. Read book, do hw, you'll be fine.

His lectures are not the most helpful as far as the course goes. He often diverges from the textbook, which leads to pretty interesting lectures, but unfortunately not useful for tests. Tests are 5 questions, and they're straight from homework/book. Clickers are large part of grade, and they're often about what he's lecturing, not the book topics.

CHOOSE A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR! Truly one of the more awful physics classes I've ever had. He never actually taught in lecture. He just gave clicker questions on what you're supposed to learn reading the book. And the clicker questions count towards your grade. The only time I really learned in this class was when he left and another teacher taught.

I'd honestly avoid Conrad if at all possible. He doesn't really teach, but rather just gives clicker questions all class over material that you haven't actually learned in lecture, but are supposed to have learned through reading the book. He's not very helpful during office hours either because he doesn't know how to "dumb down" physics enough.

This professor doesn't know how to communicate the lectures very well. He goes too fast with is powerpoints and it is hard to grasp the material in class. I only when to class because there were clicker questions. To succeed you need to know every word in the book. Tests were 5 questions, so if you miss two you fail.
Heavy reliance on the book. Lectures were interesting, but not very helpful when it came down to the tests. Other than that, he's very laid back and knowledgeable on the subject.

Tough class, but enjoyed Conrad teaching it. There isn't another professor who knows as much as he does and is as laid back as he is, guaranteed. Not sure how much I really learned from lecture, but they were definately amusing.
Conrad does not care about his students or know anything about transfer equivalencies.
HOrrible, can't teach, messes up examples, lazy professor, and doesn't care about students. If you want to actually learn something get another teacheR!
No Comments

Class is structured with quizzes at the end ofevery other lecture, So you basically spend half the semester  studying for the quizzes. Also, Timko knows his subject and expects all his students to easily get, or already understand, many of the fundamentals of the subject, most of which are actually quite difficult. He's a bad lecturer.

Timko's lectures were very boring, quizzes once a week, tests typically had abysmal averages, the final was worth a large portion of your grade, and generally unfair questions, avoid for MATH 3670 or probably any class he happens to be teaching.

He had really awful lectures that didn't make much sense and didn't really translate to the studios, and I felt like he was trying to trick the class with his questions and intentionally confuse his students with the questions, when the class was already difficult.

Even the most proactive students struggle with having to teach themselves literally everything outside of class. The lectures are so disorganized and confusing that you actually feel like you've regressed with the material. Focus on problem solving.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some exam questions are not even related to class material. You are not tested on fundamentals of diff. eq. but rather some discrete topics that are not even fully covered in class. Getting a partial credit is too hard so you end up getting a 0 if you cannot find the final answer. Lectures are not even helpful, it just complicates the subject.

Stopped going to his lectures half-way though the semester since they were confusing, over-complicated, and overall pretty useless. Survived by reading the textbook multiple times and going to another professor's lectures

Everyone said differential equations would be an easy class. They were wrong. If you take it with Timko just know you're going to have to learn everything in studio or on your own. The tests were unnecessarily difficult and the quizzes were rough but I think the TA's make those. Overall I do not recommend this class.

Timko seems to care more about knowing IBP and PFD, making students do extremely hard and in depth calculation to get to answers. The tests were,,, something. Participation didn't matter, he confused me more so I stopped going. Studio was slightly more helpful. Please, please do anything you can to not take him. I wouldn't wish him upon any enemy.

His lectures do not relate to the information we are tested on. They are very proof heavy and use more complicated methods than the ones we learn in studio. I think his exams are fair and the material on them is not too difficult, but the lectures do not help in any way. He does not do a good job teaching this course.

Very frequently, the professor would spend the entire class time writing lengthy and complicated proofs to different theorems, and explaining concepts of differential equations in levels of sophistication that aren't necessary in a sophomore-level college class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hi is very unclear in how he conducts his lectures and grading seemed pretty unfair to the majority of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Leads through the pure math proofs in lectures w/o much of an explanation of how to do the actual problems, leaves you lost and unprepared.

Ask a question you'll receive an answer that, amazingly, is relevant but completely unhelpful. I once talked w/ him about the underlying concepts, told me how the symbols work together but not what they mean:/

Goes on power trips and decides its funny to give problems that we haven't learned before on midterms to make himself feel powerful. If you're reading this Timko, I hope you feel powerful. You just cost me $8000, and I need to retake this class, effectively invalidating my full time job offer. I hope the kids leave you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never been as miserable as I have been in my whole life while as a student of this professor. We spent a week before the test covering irrelevant topics that were unfairly on the test. He would not talk about test even with a D average and won't curve. He would use the worst examples in class which did not relate to our assessments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really concept heavy lectures that do not have much application to actual test material, covers arbitrary topics that no other section covers and tests the class on it, was not very open to communication most of the time, and made sure the class knew that he had no problem failing half of the students if they could not perform to his standards.

Timko clearly is very smart and knows exactly what he was doing, the issue is he spends the entire class focusing on proofs and never really gets to solving the actual equations with the methods discussed. Required extensive studying outside of class to understand the material.

Recitation was great tho, shout out Kevin.

Do not recommend. The tests are so heavily weighted in the class but the lectures were always difficult to follow. The studios are much more useful but still don't cover all of the material you need to know. Have fun teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
1) Terrible lectures:  He never engages with the class and does not externalize his reasoning process. Bad handwriting.
2) Exams do not test what is covered during studio or lectures. There are very few studying resources, the course is poorly organized. 
3) Grading is very harsh compared to all other Georgia Tech sections. 

TLDR: Do not take

Pretty good professor overall, you just have to actively listen and ask for clarification sometimes, which a lot of people here probably didn't do (mad cuz bad lol). A bit stoic and seems newer. Going to studio helps a LOT, I went every time and had no trouble with understanding lectures. He wore a cowboy hat to exams if that matters to you.

Lecture were very unclear, made concepts more difficult than they actually were. I found that I could learn more about the course by watching other lectures or online videos rather than actually going to lecture. He often found himself stuttering working through overcomplicated proofs that had loose relevance to the required coursework.
Absolutely awful. Boring lectures, complicated proofs with no relevance to the course material, sounded like he was on the verge of falling asleep.

He would use LATEX to make his slides, but he doesn't know how to use LATEX, so all the equations are unreadable. All the Lin Alg classes are unified, so you HAVE to depend on the other lecturers. Going to class actually hurt my understanding of the material because he made everything so complicated. Only take if you plan on teaching yourself.

Timko clearly is a knowledgeable, accomplished professor and a nice guy, but his teaching style left me woefully unprepared for the exams in the course. His lectures are very focused on complex proofs of routine formulas and procedures that are ultimately irrelevant to the exam content and only serve to confuse due to his lackluster explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Timko's lectures are very unhelpful but you can do well if you read the textbook and watch the online lectures/attend Barone's instead. The tests and quizzes are standardized across all sections so it doesn't really matter which professor you get as there are many other ways to learn the material.

Timko is super smart - to a fault - . He spends a lot of time trying to do proofs (while fumbling through those) that we dont need to know rather than ensuring our understanding of the material. The fact that most of my class skipped to hear lectures from other profs. should say enough about him. As someone who attended all of his lectures, dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Timko is very Smart I can assure you that. However, his teaching method doesn't go too well with the pace of the course. In fact, since the material goes by quickly, giving proof for every single formula can most often get confusing whereas it's not even required for the tests. I ended up watching the supplementary lecture videos to succeed.

He is not very good at explaining basic concepts. Spends most of the lecture teaching very confusing proofs that don't appear on test questions. Mumbles a lot and is just not a skilled lecturer. Just look at another professor's lecture recordings or the supplementary lecture videos.

Timko's a nice guy, but a terrible lecturer. If you want to gain anything out of lecture without having to have an understanding of the material beforehand, go to another professor. If you're willing to spend extra time with the book/other sources, then lecture doesn't really matter since you'll basically be self-teaching the material anyways.

(BIOS 3755) Would not recommend this professor at all for physiology. He's super monotone, never takes a break from lecturing the whole class time, and gives multiple choice tests that are annoying (all of the above or none of the above included in literally every question). GPA is low for a reason. Not accessible on Piazza, he ignores students.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (BIOS 3755)Lectures are long and boring; physio is a hard enough course without listening to monotone lectures. Most assignments are fair given course content, but exams are exceedingly confusing (he had to give back points for dropping bad questions). Most students I know are not looking at an A due to steep grading. Take a prof with a higher GPA.

Dr. Balog's lectures are so boring; he's monotone and quiet, and his slides have lots of info on them. It's so hard to stay focused in class because it's so boring. If you zone out and come back, he's probably on the same slide, so jump back in. His exams are fair, and questions are from the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Keene is a great teacher. He is very articulate, is an expert in his field, and has all his lectures well thought-out. The class is not easy?there is a lot of reading and writing. But you will definitely learn. I highly recommend his class if you are interested in the subject matter.

He's a pretty cool guy, gotta love the British accent. It's nothing but essays/papers. When you write the essays, and he says you are arguing a point, ARGUE a point. I got a mediocre grade on my first one because I did more commentary. Once I made that adjustment, I blew the other test essays and papers out of the water. Pretty easy B.

A lot of reading, but it isn't always necessary as long as you understand what he is talking about. Two papers in the class and the tests are all essays but he helps you out on those as well. Overall the class is really not that hard as far as college classes go.

Very difficult for an intro class. Chapters and chapters of reading out of the book as well as additional readings posted on WebCT were required. Only allows two absences for a MWF class. Nice guy but he talks a lot and is a tough grader.
A very articulate Oxford chap with superb teaching skills. However, don't expect any extra credit from this gent. Also he really likes word limits.

Very interesting class.  Note:  Papers ONLY.  However, a STRICT and CONSERVATIVE word count is required, making the papers very challenging.  Also, there is quite alot to read, although it is not all necessary.  It does, however, help considerably.
This guy should be cloned so future generations can benefit from his way of teaching. Hands down best professor I have had in my academic career. And he really cares about you.

Pr. Egerstedt is the closest thing you can get to a perfect professor. His teaching style is unrivaled. The course is very structured and you don't need much prerequisites. The homeworks and tests are fair and can ace them if you study well. Too bad he is now chair of ECE and no longer has time to share his genius with the students.
Best. Professor. Ever.
Great teacher, tons of enthusiasm! Very difficult. Did not seem quite as relevant in real life as ECE 6554 Optimal Control, but was a great class and I definitely learned a ton! Would recommend!
Prof. Magnus is an inspirational and a passionate lecturer. This course is an amazing opportunity to get a grasp of a an emerging control systems research area. Multi-agent network control.

fun; appropriate homework (difficulty and quantity). Great lecture! Even I already knew almost all the materials before taking this course, I still find it fun. Plus, his insight give me a different view point on this subject.
Wonderful professor, he made me revisit concepts I already knew in an original way.

If there is anything called an "Ideal Professor", then Magnus is it. Each time he explains a concept, you feel like giving him a standing ovation. He is funny,charismatic & extremely intelligent. Taking ANY course under Magnus will be the best decision of your academic career. Also, his homework & exams are based on the lectures, so no sweat....

Dr. Egerstedt did an amazing job teaching Linear Controls. His course structure was logical in its sequece, his lectures well planned and his style clear with excellent examples worked in class. Plus he's thoroughly entertaining. I thought the class was easier, but I didn't give him a 5 because he grades dumb mistakes strictly on hw and tests.

He makes sure to assign works that are both educational and interesting, so the readings are very entertaining and the projects are fun to do. His lectures are very fun and he is very caring and respectful. As long as you do all of the assignments given, you'll get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Eichel is easily the best professor I've had. Everything about the class is engaging and interesting it's hard for me to give him lower than a 5.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Eichel's class is a really fun and casual class where he works hard to give you creative projects to do that you would enjoy doing. He doesn't grade that harshly either. There is a lot of reading but it's divided up into small amounts every day and the reading is usually enjoyable and not to long for each reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Awesome professor.  If you attend class, the tests are really easy.
class test avg was always around 60, but he never gave us a curve.
By Tech's standards, I was BEASTING that class. I was consistently above the average on all tests and quizzes.I got a D.I'm retaking Calc 1. :(

I worked my BUTT off in his class. I asked questions, went to every class, went to every recitation, went to group PLUS tutoring, and went to personal Math tutoring. I was 15 to 25 points above the average on EVERY test and the FINAL!! Got a 73 in the class with the class average being 62. Got a C in the class, no curve at all.
The only thing worse than his teaching are his jokes. I went into the final 15% above the class average, got average on the final and my uncurved grade was a 66...I still managed to get a D.

He tries to be funny in class, but fails miserably. A major problem is that because he doesn't make homework mandatory, more often than not you end up not doing it... which screws you up a lot. Calc I is an easy course, but I got a D in his class.

very caring professor if you participate. some parts of the class seem a bit out of scope for a freshman english class, but theyre pretty fulfilling to complete. its a lot of work at the start of the year and gets lighter until the end of the year.  
if you go to office hours for major assignments youll get a lot of good feedback
The grades she gives out are lower than most other English 1101 professors. She is also very passive agressive and patronizing

Beware, this is a very harsh grader. Provides vague feedback that at times doesn't even apply to your work. Has unclear grading criteria. Very short turnaround time for major assignments. Gives a tiny word limit on reflection essays, then complains that it's not detailed enough. Unnecessarily difficult, don't pick her class if you want an easy A.

She may seem nice but its very fake. She always talked to me with a very passive aggressive and condescending tone. If she was a student she would be the student who peer grades your test harshly and purposely gives you a bad grade.

She shows obvious favoritism towards her students. Her grading is ridiculous and expects way too much for an eng 1 class. She grades based off favoritism so if she dislikes you, you won't get a good grade. I regret taking her course. Take any other professor if you don't want to risk getting a B or prepare to suck up to her like no other.

Really down-to-earth professor and clearly cares about each of her students. Her approach to the class was unique compared to other sections, but was still very engaging and hands-on. Gives really personal and meaningful feedback on assignments.

This class is a joke, it has nothing to do with the Health Sciences and she grades it super difficult for not reason at all. Only grade she has put in since midterm is the big Interview grade after giving out homework every single class. It is impossible to get an A in this class. For a health science class this professor does it completely wrong.

She is super nice and helps with whatever you need. Grading seemed to be really tough though. It is an easy B but the people who got an A really had to work for it. Also there are no tests or quizzes just a lot of busy work and some big projects at the end.

This woman is a joke of a professor. She thinks herself better than her students, and made that clear. Her grading rubrics are completely useless and are subject to opinion. She doesn't follow her own guidelines, yet expects students to read her mind. She assigns an unfair workload for a 3 credit hr class. Do NOT take this woman's class.

Will 100% recommend. Took the class over the summer. Lectures are very interesting. There is reading, but it's manageable. Grading is distributed almost equally over quizzes, discussion reports, and projects. Quizzes are very easy. Projects involve lots of research so don't procrastinate! She gives amazing feedback and is very approachable.

Do not recommend as a humanities. During the summer, her quizzes are easy, online, & open note, but she assigns 30 page readings and doesn't clarify instructions on big projects until 4 days before. Made everyone cram and then questions why we hadn't finished earlier. She posts lectures though; makes her class easy but boring and way too much work
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing professor
Very reasonable workload. Most papers graded by TA's who are available to contact prior to paper submission. Group projects and papers are entirety of grade.

Professor Elisa is so kind! She is very good with disability accommodations and is incredibly patient. She gives very interesting lectures and records them in case people are sick. The course work is reading-heavy (reports based on 10-20 page articles) but there's lots of time to get it done. She also gave us grace periods for every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore picked up this class from another professor and taught it very well - he clearly has tons of experience in ML. Homeworks could take a long time and were tedious, but lecture slides helped a lot. Exams were take-home/open-note and mostly conceptual.
terrible professor

Really good lecturer, the class is super hard since it is considered a weed out for electrical engineers. Homeworks are super hard but the tests are around the same level so doing good on homeworks means doing good on tests. Test 3 is really hard regardless. Supposedly the fall professors are better. Go to all lectures and recitation.

Quite difficult as expected, but if you work hard and study you can succeed.  I personally absolutely hated the seemingly random due dates (8pm on Sunday or 11pm on Friday). I am a person that likes to schedule my week ahead and this was extremely annoying and resulted in me completing assignments I couldn't turn in bc they take no late work.

Moore is a fantastic lecturer, he is entertaining and informative. Beware he is a harsh grader, and makes sure that only those who truly understand all the content do well. Nevertheless he's very friendly and approachable and makes an extremely difficult class fun and interesting despite the difficult tests and material.

Pretty good professor. The lectures were insanely fast, so if you're taking notes, you have to spend a bit of time each week outside of class to re-learn the material. Also quite a bit of homework, and the material was somewhat challenging. But overall it was still an interesting class.

Worst grading scheme I've ever seen. Only 2 exams, 25% each, and a 30% final. Exams graded in canvas separate from written work. If you get a final answer wrong, the max credit you can get back for your work is 50%. That is what killed my grade in this course. On our 2nd exam, the range of scores was from 0 to 60 out of 60, with an average of 30.

reviews.comment: This class is notoriously difficult. Professor Moore was a fine teacher; lectures tended to get fairly pedantic, and some days he was fairly condescending to students for not understanding. Other days, however, he was a funny, interesting lecturer. Very hit or miss. If you read the textbook and don't get behind, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Favorite teacher so far. The material 2026 is the hardest class in the first three semesters, but Dr. Moore makes his lectures exciting, he even gives candy to students who answer questions correctly. You should do most of the labs before lab or there isnt enough time, and go to TA office hours frequently because there is a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Elliot Moore cares more about telling jokes than actually teaching. While he is entertaining at times when lecture materials get dull, he doesn't go into enough depth when explaining anything and just glosses over certain topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Somehow makes boring material a little more interesting. Succeeds at showing which topics are more important.

Most people would say the material for this class is pretty hard, but Dr. Moore makes sure you know exactly what you need to do in order to succeed in the class. He emphasizes the important topics and explains them very clearly in a funny way. 10/10 professor and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Always an entertaining professor even when the material is a bit dry. The class as a whole is very difficult, but it's made bearable by the professors who teach it. Dr. Moore knows what he is talking about and is more than ready to share it with students who have questions. Enthusiastic, funny, knowledgeable. 10/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: goated prof. work is a bit boring and tedious but lowest grade I ever got on anything was a 98. Attendance is mandatory but class is very chill
It's a very easy class with a really nice professor. I got above 95% on all assignments. Lectures can be boring at times, but I still had a fun time in class.

awk lil guy most times. put in SOME form of effort and you'll end w an A. dont like how useless going to his classes felt w presentations every session about how to do work when we've been in school for quite awhile now... didnt LOVE the topic but also not the worst ever. dont take the 5-6:15 time you will never want to go. would retake!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is very easy with a light workload. However, I would take another section of 1102 if available. The topic is Shakespeare which got very boring and the assignments were super repetitive. But if you are just looking to get the credit this course is by no means bad. Its just that there are better/more fun options with other professors.

while his lectures got a little boring from time to time, you can tell he's really passionate about his discipline. he is an extremely nice man, and before breaks would bring little treats for the class and wish us all happy holidays. he's a very easy grader but will also provide useful feedback on projects. he's very approachable as well.

Dr. Emiliano is a great professor, very sweet and enjoys what he teaches. The class isn't difficult, but the lectures were pretty boring. The workload is extremely manageable and there were plenty of group projects throughout his course.

I would recommend Professor Gutierrez for 1102! This class was focused on Shakespeare, and while I am not a huge Shakespeare fan, the class was interesting and not hard! No exams or essays; rather, you work either independently or in group projects. He is very accessible, and he loves when people participate in class. Overall, a very chill class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very easy grader and is very lenient and accessible outside of class. It is extremely hard to not get an A if you just do the work, which isn't that time consuming anyway. Overall just a great teacher, take him for 1102.

He's AMAZING! Genuinely cares about students and easily accessible outside of class. Textbook is recommended but not required. The course is project-focused and it's very easy to get an A as long as you put in the effort.
Dr. gutierrez is a very sweet and caring professor. He genuinely cares a lot about the material and talking to students and his class is very enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy grader and a caring teacher. He loves participation in class and listening discovering new perspectives. All around, I kinda disliked his topic (Shakespeare) so be weary if you do not enjoy Shakespeare that much. I thought I liked it but I guess not to the extent of his scope. Either way, very chill guy and certainly a great person!

He genuniely cares about the course material and his students. The class is an easy A as long as you have decent quality work (won't take that much time) - I don't think anyone in my section didn't get an A. He is engaging and helpful, I asked plenty of questions and he would always be willing to help and answer me.

Dr. Gutierrez is a great English 1102 professor. If you put in the effort, you will get close to a 100 on all assignments. There are few papers, and the course focuses more on projects (group and individual). His lectures are mostly useless, but he does give you time in class to work on your assignments.

reviews.comment: He is a good professor that gives a lot of projects which are mostly essays or writing based but also some projects focused on video production and art. He also gives great feedback if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not too much work. He looks for enthusiasm and effort
Great professor! Class was pretty simple and was not too much writing as I had anticipated, rather had more projects which were interesting. Highly recommend!

Really nice guy, and a good professor. My only criticism would be that some of the lectures were a bit boring and unnesceasry, but the overall class was great. He is a really fair grader and the assignments are not too difficult. The class was overall pretty interesting and the professor does a good job giving feedback. Should be an easy A.

reviews.comment: Unconventional and interesting assignments which did not require a massive time commitment. Very approachable and flexible professor who is clearly passionate about his job. One of my favorite professors at Tech thus far (and I usually hate English).

Very kind professor and was always willing to work with students to resolve issues. Also generally a very light grader as long as work is completed on time and as specified in directions. Would absolutely take again

Lazy professor that does not take any pride in instructing this class. Makes this class hard not in the sense that the material is hard, but quizzes you on the most random facts and quotes from random people. Only picked this class because it was online asynchronous and honestly it is not worth it. Take Psych for your ethics requirement guys

This is not an easy A class. I put more effort than one of my ECE classes. If you want to do well go to office hours with TA. Test are honor lock with camera and extremely tricky even if you did the reading. It's manageable to get an A just have to do the readings with notes & the final 10 page research paper. All writings are graded very lightly.

has never answered a single email. know at least 6 people who were accused of using ai when they did not. every lecture is prerecorded from 5 years ago. quizzes cover the most unpredictable information from the 50 page readings. terrible class.
genuine balls

Possibly the laziest professor ever. She gives 40pgs of readings every week, and rarely posts a lecture from years ago she did online for other classes. Slides posted are useless and don't cover everything in the exams. She does all of that while taking home a $80k salary... I wanna be an ethics professor too
My therapist knows about this class

reviews.comment: Horrendous class. If you are not religious pick one and start praying. Quizzes cover the most random thing ever. Do not take.
actually made me cry so many times

God this has to be the WORST class I have ever taken. There should be no reason that the quizzes have to be as specific as they are. reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you care about your mental well-being. It will eat up all your time. Lectures are prerecorded and unhelpful. Idk, she kinda an opp. Chatgpt did a better job litteraly!

reviews.comment: save your sanity and do not take this class

The course itself is the issue: dense textbook, six heavy quizzes worth 60%, no extra credit. Unless you love ethics, do not take. TA's were great though, go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It seems a lot of other comments have issues with this professor surrounding AI allegations / receiving a 0 without even speaking to the student prior. I would highly advise avoiding this ethics class with no sign of ethical reasoning in sight.

This professor accuses you of using AI by using AI. You can't make this up. Reports you to OSI, and OSI is very slow in processing. Gives you a 0 before due process which is ironic for an ethics class. 6 quizzes and 3 long papers. Few lectures that are pre-recorded years before, badly organized, you pretty much read and teach yourself everything.

Genuinely horrendous class. 6 bi-weekly quizzes that you HAVE to read at least 40 pages + sometimes additional readings for each quiz. Quizzes are based on random niche things mentioned in the readings and rarely focus on principles discussed. Using AI to summarize the readings won't help you at all. 3 long papers due throughout the semester.
worst class ive EVER taken at this school. convoluted slides, biweekly quizzes that are basically midterms. dont take unless you want to dedicate full time hours to a social science credit.

Do not take this class unless you actually need to... there are better and easier social science classes to fulfill your ethics requirement. Classes are online asynchronous but the amount of readings and work you need to do is way more than a normal in-person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Only a few pre-recorded lectures from prior semester were posted, you must do all readings yourself what's the point of having a professor teach the class then? Quizzes are insanely difficult with specific questions that do not cover material but niche things random people have said. Lots of work, do not take if you are an engineer

Whole class is structured based upon readings of one textbook with few very disorganized videos. 6 bi-weekly quizzes determine 60% of your grade. Quizzes cover niche items from the textbook such as "the author used this metaphor, what does it signify" instead of actual principles. 3 long papers and multiple discussion posts. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know if it was professor or the TA. but got threatened to report to me to the student integrity council for having 30% AI detected in my paper on turnitin, (Every other AI checker online said it was 0%). Her syllabus should say that AI is not allowed at all because that is what she is treats it as.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: As stated, not an easy A class. The discussion posts and homeworks are leniently graded, but the quizzes arent too easy and need to be properly studied for. Most of the learning is just textbook reading, but I enjoyed the contents of the class. The professor was kind to give me a second chance to rewrite a paper that I got flagged for AI on.
girl literally didn't email back and just reported to office of academic integrity for something my friend was actively trying to solve with her.
Very informative course, but difficult!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class for an easy A. The grading is somewhat fair for the discussion posts and essay assignments, but the class consists of 6 quizzes each worth 10%, and a final worth 20% of your grade which asks either very easy or borderline impossible incredibly specific questions from the textbook.

If you're taking this class for an easy A, I would say don't. There is a lot of reading and the questions asked on each quiz can be either highly specific or very easy to answer. Get ready to read in between the lines and remember a lot of information. 
Watch the video lectures and try to decipher the slides (there are a lot of abbreviations). GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every week, it covers a chapter but the lectures tend to be a bit boring. The way the slides are presented are not my favorite, but as long as you actually spend some time reading, it should be fine. The "quizzes" are basically midterms, and they can contain tough questions so you have to make sure that you stay on track and understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are only 6 quizzes for the entire semester that have extremely niche questions that are almost never covered in lecture slides. Lecture slides were very basic and included weird abbreviations for words that made some slides un-readable. As an online class sometimes lectures even lacked video recordings. Boring textbook and frustrating class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As much as I enjoyed this class, I wouldn't recommend it to someone looking for an easy A. We had frequent quizzes that required close reading of a boring and dense textbook. Lectures weren't helpful for quizzes but they were enjoyable. The papers were good for raising my grade. I chose the final paper instead of an exam, which I would recommend.

I love Dr. Markley. She's really experienced when it comes to FP and she's insanely cool. Class is very discussion based (get ready extroverts) but the tests are very reading based. Be prepared to spend at least 3-4 hours per chapter (3 chapters per test). The textbook is interesting though. She's hard, but I loved her class and am taking another.

this class was set up as a discussion based test in the lectures, but most of the grade came from tests. you dont really learn much in the lectures and the tests are entirely on the material from the book, which is not covered in class

Dr Markley is one of my favorite professors. She is passionate and a great lecturer. Participation really matters she wants to have good group discussions, but ultimately she is a fair grader and a kind person.

Professor Markley was an amazing professor. She has such a wide range of experiences to pull from relating to the course that it was always really interesting to hear from her. The class was a little intensive though. Had to do about 30-40 pages of reading/notes every week to learn the material. The tests were all multiple choice but very specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most painfully boring textbook I have EVER read and you have to read about 400 pages of it. The quizzes are unbelievably specific to the point where even when you read chapters twice you will miss questions. Lectures are boring and completely useless. She knows everyone in this class just needs an ethics credit but makes it incredibly tedious.

There are 6 quizzes in the semester, each covering 50+ pages of the extremely boring textbook and sometimes additional readings. Reading is essential and even after taking notes on the readings, quizzes are difficult because the questions are very specific. Teacher is nice and class can be interesting at times, though.

Very interesting class but the quizzes are extremely difficult. You basically need to memorize the textbook chapters for each quiz. She is an incredible professor who truly cares about her students. Lecture often got off track from discussion so you had to learn a lot on your own from ppts and textbook. Option between final and research paper.

Dr. Markley is a very kind professor and her lectures are I found the content interesting. The lectures do not always cover all the material so make sure to read the textbook, its worth it. The PowerPoint slides are very helpful for the quizzes which are important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are VERY important and you'll only do good on them if you KNOW the textbook. Some questions were tricky even if you knew the material well. Overall still very kind and will answer any and all questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Markley is a good lecturer but she lets anyone ask questions in her 150 person lecture, so she never gets through the material. Just read the textbook and watch the videos she made during the pandemic to get an A. This semester she only had 1 TA, so essays took months to grade, which was annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Markley is a good, well-respected professor. Be prepared to participate in USFP because the class is primarily discussion based. This class is very reading heavy, so be prepared to read a lot. Overall, I thought that the class was pretty difficult, but not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved my INTA class with Professor Markley. While I took it asynchronously due to Covid changing course methods, she seemed to understand the difficulty of doing a class in this manner and was open if we ever needed help. Quizzes a little tricky but manageable. Overall really cool lady and hope I get to take one of her classes actually in person.

This class was very interesting. There are pop quizzes which are generally very easy and the exams are based of the textbook. Highly recommend this class, it was very informative and fun. Be ready to discuss different ethical cases.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Markley is a sweet woman who clearly cares about the class, but she relied far too heavily on discussion for a class of 250 kids. I didn't learn anything in class because she let anyone who wanted to talk, but I still had to go because attendance is monitored. Tests were exactly like the study guide, but you need to read the textbook for it.

She's really nice. She uses TurningPoint for attendance but but you don't really have to go to class. For tests, study everything on the study guide. The test questions are word for word from the textbook. Easy overall.
Great lecturer who really cares about students. go to class, read the book and youll do great

Dr. Markley is probably the nicest professor at GT. Her foreign policy class has very specific tests though. If you memorize the textbook you will be fine. If you ever need to move a test she understands. If you talk in class she will like you a lot. Try and you will make a good grade.

INTA 2030 had very few assignments but tests were weighted heavily. You had to read the book multiple times to do well on exams - forget not reading or not studying - but it wasn't too hard if you prepared. Dr. Markley is a really kind teacher and is SUPER understanding. She struggles getting through all the material but is a passionate lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Markley is so kind and a very generous grader. You dont have to go to class but you do really need to read the textbook to do well. She is passionate about the subject material and tries to make class interactive. She postpones tests when she feels we arent ready which is very helpful.

Prof Markley keeps postponing almost all her exams so much so that they conflict with every other exam. She provided lots of readings and does not teach what comes in the exam but harps on a lot of random things not even in the exam. Class is actually not important. You need to cram every corner of her book.

reviews.comment: Class is unreasonably hard, lectures a useless, relatively pointless for anyone who is not an INTA major

reviews.comment: Great prof. Tests can be hard but easy to get points back. She is really nice as a person and passionate about what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So far at Tech, Markley is the best professor I've had. I barely got an A-and only did so because she just decided to give us 2 extra points on our final grade- but I learned so much in this class. You will have to read the textbook a lot. As in, if you don't, you will not pass. Lectures weren't always on the test, but she cares about participation

Professor Markley is amazing!! If she recognizes that you make an effort in the class, you will succeed. She actually cares about her students too, and will move assignments around based on student feedback.

Loved this course. The class is primarily discussion based instead of her standing at the front and lecturing. She is also open to changing the format of the class so that everyone gets what they need. Very kind and considerate. The class is not difficult if you participate and read the textbook, which you can find for free on the internet.

Professor Markley is one of the most genuine and caring professors you will have. She assigns quite a bit of reading and expects students engage in lively discussions over them. Passionate about what she teaches and very respectful and even encouraging of challenging her narrative/view; she doesn't talk down to you. Highly recommend.

Professor Markley was by far one of the best professors I've had at GT. She begins every class by asking everyone how their days went and makes an effort to get to know everyone individually. She really understands how stressful GT can be and often tries to assign assignments around your schedule so that there's as little stress as possible.

Markley is a great INTA teacher; she really cares about course material and student success. LOTS of reading from textbook and articles can be dull, but the tests are primarily based on reading. Lectures are long and boring, but good to reinforce textbook which is vague. 1-2 pop quizzes, rest announced before hand. Debates are fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Markley encourages participation a lot in her class, and devotes a lot of time for discussion and questions. There are pop quizzes at times, as well as group discussions set up on the spot. Her lectures are somewhat confusing (bad slides), but the main focus is reading the textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class is easy as long as you stay on top of your reading. I regret not paying as much attention in lecture because Dr. Markley gave great summaries of the assigned readings and often related it to current news. Although it was easy to disengage in her class, Dr. Markley is kind and genuinely wants you to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: The lectures are pointless and are more like a platform for debating if you like such stuff. The exams are way too specific but otherwise fair in that it's almost entirely based on the textbook.

A great professor. Her lectures were informative and entertaining and she really cares about her students. She wants you to do well and if you work and put in effort on the papers you'll do fine. The quizzes are average difficulty. I would take her again.

Class is super easy but you have to do the readings. She really cares about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. Multiple choice exams make them much easier than free response questions. She wants to show you how politics are applied in the real world and hosts live debates in class. Posts slides online. Class isn't that useful.

Lectures aren't pointless. I just went because of random pop quizzes. The tests are based on many chapters and are either way too specific or opinionated. Way too much work for anyone not pursuing a government-related career.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The class is incredibly easy if you are familiar with US Government. For those who don't know many of the quirks, this class will involve lots of reading. Tests were 90% of the grade and all MC and there were occasional pop quizzes. If you have taken any civics course in high school, the class is pretty trivial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy class if you read the textbook and show up to class. Pop quizzes are common to encourage class attendance but they are pretty simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures didn't have a lot to do with the tests, but they were interesting. Plus you have to go because there are unannounced quizzes throughout the semester. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is passionate and cares about her students, but most of the class is spent on discussions that have nothing to do with what the test covers.  If you are willing to do all of the reading, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Markley is the most kind and caring professor I've had at Tech so far. Her course is hard (esp if you're not into US politics), but she wants to succeed and is willing to do anything to help you reach that end. LOTS of reading; nearly all test questions are from reading. She has few office hours, but her TAs are more than happy to help.
She is very annoying and would talk nonstop about Romania even though the class is AMERICAN government. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is a very caring teacher who does her best to make sure her students are comfortable with the material and are ready to succeed on the tests/quizzes/debates. Really tries to have discussion in class without offending anyone, has even postponed and cancelled quizzes when students didn't want it. Best class this semester.

Class was all lecture and discussion based in class, which really let students sound out their understanding of course concepts before writing our papers on similar topics. Extremely caring about student experience, always kept debates from going too far. I cannot recommend Prof. Markley highly enough

Was a very interesting professor, great sense of style too! She injects many of her Romanian experiences into her teaching. The class was extremely interesting and very debate/participation heavy. There's a lot of reading, so make sure you do all of it. She graded fairly, but sometimes her feedback was very vague.

We didn't learn that much in MSE 3025 but I don't think that's really her fault. I think she was a fine lecturer but the content was just pretty simple and I think she was aware of that bc she didn't really care if we paid attention or not and would end lectures early/cancel class more than most to not waste our time

Lectures are extremely dull, covering what feels like 20 mins of content in 75, but tests are open notes and the content is extremely straightforward. Print the notes and take them to exams and you'll do well. Very little programming in this numerical methods class, except for one (very simple) project.

Class is based on participation, 2 tests, and a final. Participation is a bucket point system, and any extra points are extra credit. Tests are very similar to the practice tests she gives to help study. She gave very good lectures that taught what you needed to know. only complaint is that I wish she used piazza, ed discussion, etc.

Dr. Hu is a great teacher! She is very kind and she truly cares about each student getting a good grade. She always has office hours and reviews exam questions during them. The class is based off of homework memorization.
