She had really good lectures often complemented with long textbook sections (optional). Her study guides did not do a great job of covering exam material, though. I also wish she was more accessible outside of lecture; it's tough reaching her, and there was no forum where students could ask questions. Not a bad professor all in all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sanders is the best option for 2016. Her lecture notes are very clear and you can probably get away with just that and the textbook, but I'd recommend going to class. Her lectures were directly related to the hw and exams (which had no matlab btw), which other 2016 profs had a problem with.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is very knowledgeable and super accessible for help. Homework can be hard, but she's ready to help if you're willing to work earnestly. Homework every week (Matlab coding) and written exams ( straight from lectures). I would take her again!

She is the best ME 2016 professor by far. While homeworks may take a little bit, office hours help a ton, and her homeworks are much more doable than other professors. Her lectures really help with the homework as well. Her tests are extremely fair and straight forward. Probably one of my easier classes this semester.

Lecture material is all there but the HW was sometimes very confusing and took minimum 6 hours weekly. Exams were fair and the practice exams helped a lot. Course itself is boring so can't blame the prof on that. 2 midterms 1 final and 10 HWs.

Dr. Weigel is a very caring and nice professor...but her style of teaching is somewhat vague and you need to know how to code (use R) for the final project even though she rarely teaches it and provides the prompts for assignments. Her test questions are also vague and the TAs are harsh graders. However, the grading scheme is fair.

She was very kind even though the content was a little boring. The grading criteria was very helpful - there's two schemes that maximize your grade! Each test had 2 parts with one being multiple choice and the other part being a "take-home" test that you can work on with a group. The final project was a lot of work so be sure to have a good group.
Amazing, kind professor. Very patient and caring, wants you to succeed. She was also my academic advisor and she went above and beyond to help me. She is a great person.

I took this course in the Fall of 2021. Professor Weigel is passionate about what she teaches. The coursework is not demanding, but does include a lab, which is where most of the work for this class will be done. If you find Biology boring, this will not be a fun class, but it will be easy. If you like it, you will love this class with Weigel

This course is online synchronous and there were two grading schemes. One was test heavy one was homework heavy which is very helpful if you are not a good test taker. There is a lot of group work during class (breakout rooms) and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed in this course.

This was one of the most pointless labs every at GATech. The instructions for the project were unclear, boring, and required WAY too much work. Does not give credit for small errors (like an extra space at the end of a word) even if everything else is perfect. Very passive aggressive to students as well and will not admit fault.

Dr. Weigel, as a lab director, is very open for communication and will respond to you promptly. That said, the structure of the Ecology lab is not great and many things are designed to force more work onto the students. Prepare to write lots of papers. It will, however, prepare you for future paper-heavy lab courses.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is strict on her policies and allows for no creative flexibility or room for failure. She expects constant attention and a passionate obsession for the subject.

She is one of the most considerate teachers i know, but her class is structured terribly. It is entirely flipped classroom and she requires you to teach yourself on your own and exams are very very difficult. This class made me switch my major.

Dr. Weigel is amazing. She not only teaches the material well, but she honestly cares about her students and tries to give them every opportunity to succeed. She's the first professor I've had that says "take care of yourselves" and tries to make it possible for you to do that.

Dr. Weigel is so caring and truly wants her students to succeed, and also provides some extra credit. The class is very content heavy so that is difficult but make sure you read the textbook and you should be fine. She's one of the kindest teachers I've ever had.

Weigel was in charge of the Ecology labs but you have a pair of TAs as your instructors so you don't ever see her in person during the semester. However, she's very responsive on Piazza and via email. Be prepared to code (R) during lab and write a LOT. You have a lab report due at the end of the semester. And she offers extra credit which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was so hard, but Dr. Weigel is an amazing professor and is so understanding if you do struggle. If you reach out for help/advice/feedback she will respond so kindly & her feedback is detailed and personalized to your own performance. She just really cares about her students. Her class will challenge you academically, but in the best ways

Lectures were amazingly informative and easy to follow. I wasn't a fan of the excessive participation and reading but it was a very structured class and everything helped build understanding and encourage students. Tests were open note but hard because of strict time constraints and LOTS of content. Don't be fooled into thinking it's an easy A.
Open note tests and your best test is weighted more. Class is listed as synchronous, but all lectures are recorded, so you can just watch whenever you want. Awesome teacher.

The textbook is free, but the units are ridiculously long and detailed. She included so much information on tests that I walked away learning less than I would have if she just taught the bare minimum. Grading depends on the TA, but be prepared to get points off for citations on papers. The class is "easy" but annoying/time-consuming for what it is
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel's class was difficult, but she cares so much about her students and goes above and beyond to make sure they understand the material. I genuinely enjoyed the material because she made me so eager to come to class every day. Dr. Weigel is seriously the best.

Dr. Weigel cares so much about her students. She makes every student feel respected even in a class of over 100. She is a great lecturer who is passionate about the material. She made me interested in the material and want to learn. Highly recommend!

She taught alongside Dr. Harrison, and I prefer her over him. Granted, the content she teaches might be easier, as they said the class gets easier as you go, but her lectures make more sense than his, and she found ways to make the class more interactive and fun in an online setting. She really cares about the well-being of all her students.
Dr. Weigel was an amazing professor. She cares about her students more than any professor Ive ever had and was more than willing to help. Really great professor.

Ecology was taught by her and another professor, her half was much better. It is clear that she wants to make the content interesting and fun (she made a whole review session themed around her cat and a kitten she found). It is possible to get an A, but you might have to work for it.

Ecology can be a tough class, because there's not always a correct answer. However, Dr. Weigel really makes this class exciting for her students. She cares a lot about you, both in and out of the classroom. She's a great lecturer and she is always coming up with new activities to engage students. She works hard to make the class interesting.

BIOS 2301 is TA-led and a difficult class overall. It involves RStudio, and if you have a background in computer science it would be very beneficial. I did not, but I managed to get through the work with help. Overall the class is very interesting and relevant, and it's helpful to learn how to write research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is super nice and a great professor. Participation in this class is important, but once you get the basics down the class isn't too bad. She'll answer any questions you have. She's also super down-to-earth and pretty chill. She dressed up as two dozen different characters during Halloween, if that gives you an idea.

She really cares about her students and she lectures really well. I didn't go to lecture often and just learned from the textbook though. Tests cover huge amounts of material, and often ask about random details you probably overlooked. The generous grading scheme with built in extra credit makes it very possible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is a great lecturer. She is clear and engaging. On top of that, she very deeply cares about her students outside of the Biology classroom as well.

This is my second time having Dr. Weigel, and she continues to amaze me. She cares a ton about her students, is extremely helpful during office hours, and is really forgiving (in terms of the grading scheme of the class). Her passion is contagious, and it's something you want to be around especially if you have to take bio but aren't a sci major.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about her students.

Dr. Weigel is an amazing person. She is a very chill professor who cares a LOT about your well being. She is a very chill person and has a grounded and funny lecture style. If you have a chance to take her I would definitely recommend it.

this class is a ton of work and if you don't need to take it specifically do not take it!! Dr Weigel really cares about her students and will help you but I can not stress how much work this is. There are a lot of boosting assignments that will boost your grade up. If you get mid Bs on exams you can for sure get an A in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is a FANTASTIC lecturer. She's always prepared for lecture and brings a tremendous level of positive energy. She's young, which also makes her seem relatable. She's one of those professors with whom you feel comfortable right off the bat. You can tell that she really cares about her students and wants the best for them. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Weigel is one of Techs gems. Shes an amazing lecturer, and the material is genuinely interesting. Shes super engaging, and although there is lots of reading, she can be approached for help both in and out of class. Not an easy A, but definitely can do well if you try. Recommend her wholeheartedly! You wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is very straightforward about what is required for this class. They do require that you do the lecture's reading before attending class; however, she then goes through it thoroughly in class. She also provides a practice test because she really does want you to succeed. Some modules are detail-heavy, but they don't make it too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: flipped class so lots of reading and self-learning. First two tests are pretty difficult, but after that the class gets a lot easier. Grading is extremely fair, and even despite the content being quite difficult, a lot of people consider the class easier than other intro sciences. Certainly requires work, but it's more than possible to do very well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel knows a lot about biology and you can tell she's passionate about what she's teaching. The class required a lot of reading, but all of the participation assignments were graded for participation. Tests were fairly easy and matched the structure of the practice tests pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class has been a mess all semester, but Dr. Weigel has by far exceeded the other prof. She understands what she's talking about and is patient and very accessible. Tests are extremely fair and the class grading is not bad. Lots of reading because it is a flipped format. She will be a great prof when she understands how to run a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students and always helps out in office hours. Some of the material is challenging, but always go to offie hours right before the test!

The course was flipped format, which I didn't like, and there was no textbook, but if you memorize/understand the material presented in class you'll do well. Dr. Weigel was nice and seemed to care. The final was made mostly of questions from the midterms, and there was grade replacement, so in the end everything worked out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Her ecology class wasn't too bad, and she really wants the students to learn the material, so there are a lot of extra credit and grade replacements.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor she actually cares about what you say and will make adjustments based on your needs. Really engages with the material to help you understand it not just memorize it. There are only two tests but final grade replacement was used in our class.

She clearly cares about her students and about the subject matter. Her lectures engage the class and she really makes an effort to talk about things that are interesting to us. One of my favorite professors so far!

Dr. Weigel made the best out of an otherwise annoying class. Criteria for the tests was always very clear, and she was responsive to the concerns of the class. Take her if you can; she's very laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel is an incredibly witty professor and makes for a very good lecturer. Her tests are reasonable. Go to recitation. Attendance not mandatory, but keep up with the Learning Catalytics.
Weigel is the clearest professor about her exam criteria and make up. If you go by her given learning objectives, go to recitation, and do her IKE and TICAs, you've got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Weigel taught the latter half of general ecology which honestly saved my grade from the first professor. Her lectures and expectations are incredibly clear and comprehensible. She is an overall friendly and approachable, as well as knowledgeable, professor who cares a lot about student progress and feedback. 10/10 would recommend.

Out of the 3 biology professors that taught BIOL1510 for fall 2016 (Choi, Kerr & Weigel), her test was the most straight forward. Like her test was my first A, my first decent test score. Her lectures are pretty cool too. I feel like they probably planned this on purpose to give us hope that we might have a chance in the class or something.

Professor Stas is a very entertaining and enthusiastic lecturer. He has a harsh style of lecturing and even harsher tests. However, he truly does care about the class and does want to see everyone succeed in their own ways.

I can't recommend him enough. He's explains complicated concepts very well holds engaging lectures. He's VERY flexible with due dates and is very down-to-earth with what he expects from students. Exams are very reasonable and can easily be studied for by reviewing HWs and previous exams.

Best professor I've had at Tech so far. Extremely effective lectures and is very accessible outside of class. Class is set up so that you don't have to stress about grades. Assignments and exams are very reasonable. Provides A LOT of resources.

Awesome professor, he knows the concepts and cares about students. One time when I didn't submit a homework assignment, he emailed me to check that everything was alright. He has a great brand of humor and makes concepts interesting and intuitive. Tests are average difficulty, as it homework. He has great availability for office hours.

Dr. Endert is a great lecturer and very caring professor. Topics were relevant and I learned a lot, even though I usually don't pay attention in "memorization-based" classes. That being said, the beginning is a little boring but it gets more interesting later, and the final project can be fun if you have a good group. Exams and HWs are easy.

Good choice for an easy elective. Endert is a good lecturer and is engaging to listen to. He is also in general a friendly guy and makes himself pretty accessible. Homework assignments were very straightforward, and so were the exams if you just attended/watched the lectures. The bulk of the class is the group project, so just pick good teammates.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required. Unfortunately the lecture content is very boring, but not difficult. There are also coding labs that progressively get harder in Javascript D3, and you need to learn it yourself since lectures don't cover it.
Exams aren't too bad, labs get harder as semester goes on. Records the lectures so you can go back and review even if you miss class.

Professor Endert doesn't really teach in this class, instead every class is led by a difficult student group who lead a presentation on an assigned paper and the class discusses. Class ended early every time but the discussions and topics were interesting. The assignments were graded easily and not very time consuming.

This course is structured with one paper each class, all culminating in a group project. The assignments were moderately time consuming but interesting and ultimately easier than other classes.

He is a great lecturer and has great command over the topics, and the class interactions were quite interesting.

The class was meh, he taught well but it was definitely a lot of content which made it hard to follow especially because you have to know so much for the exams just for half it to not be there. Make sure you start the labs early because they can catch up to you. Always use the TAs and other students in the class cause they'll be your life support.

6730 with Endert is a great class to take. He is super knowledgeable and tries to keep lectures engaging. Basically, if you just pay attention in class and keep up with the group project, you'll be all set. Homework assignments are not very time consuming, exam material comes straight from lectures, and everything is graded pretty leniently

You learn nothing useful from lectures. You have to learn all coding stuffs by yourself with a provided source that is not clear. Test contents are ridiculous and tedious. You need to memory over 300 slides for each exam. You might get a high score but this is the most boring course I took in GT.

Memorization of lists, taxonomies, etc. Not hard per se, but annoying. The labs have nothing to do with the lectures, and the recitation just covers what's in the labs. Just a strangely organized course, imo. The labs are super easy, and the material is too. I just don't feel like the structure fosters a very exciting or productive experience.

He's the typical average professor you get. Not the best, not the worst. The info viz class specifically is pretty heavy memorization and paying attention in his boring lectures only helps for the exams. Class says you don't need to know javascript but the programming labs are worth 40% and lectures / TAs are pretty useless for it.

Professor's teaching was alright. However I can't condone his behavior and unprofessionalism. This one time I went up to him after class to ask him about a question I got wrong on my exam, and he got all angry at me. How dare I even question the grade I got? All I wanted was to ask why I got it wrong since the grading didn't show me why..

Info Viz with Endert was pretty solid. He is passionate about the subject, however, a bit on the dry end in terms of lecture. The midterm is mostly memorization of slides and the homework and prog assignments were not challenging. He did mention that future semesters will have a lab component so it might be more work than previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ensley was a blast of a professor. One of the single nicest professors I've ever met. The class involved a lot of reading different books and passages as well as discussions about them, but Dr. Ensley made sure that engagement was interesting and worthwhile. Fully recommend for any class you have to take with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr Ensley was my Introduction to British Literature professor. She is incredibly kind and caring. Her lectures were always enjoyable and interesting, and class was never boring. One of my favorite professors. Highly recommend taking a course (or multiple) from her if you have the opportunity.

Very fun class. Most of the readings were interesting. Lots of class discussion. The grade is primarily in a few projects, which are graded generously. I asked for time extensions on nearly all of the projects, and Dr. Ensley was always happy to give them, even though I didn't give much of a reason (basically I had quizzes in other classes).

Best professor ever. She's so sweet and actually cares about courseload and your life unlike a lot of other professors. Getting an A is just making sure you do your work. Much better than the professor I took for 1101! Highly recommended.

Take her! She's a wonderful prof and was extremely considerate that I took her class from a totally different timezone (12 hrs ahead). Gave extensions as needed. Very clear with feedback and helped me with non-class writing for a personal project. Great person, wish I could have taken the class in-person with her.

Dr. Ensley is by far the best English professor I've ever had. Initially, the course topic ("What is English?") seemed boring, but the readings and projects she assigned made it a lot more interesting. While her grading is strict to the rubric, she gives great feedback and is flexible (especially during COVID). Great choice for ENGL overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ensley is super sweet and caring, especially during COVID. She cares a lot about the class material, although I did not find it to be that interesting. She grades fairly and gives a lot of feedback, although some of the homeworks and assignments feel unnecessary and like a waste of time. Decent choice as a prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Ensley is super passionate about the topics she teaches, and I had a great time in her class this semester. She also really cares for her students, and is always very understanding and helpful.

I loved Dr. Ensley's class! The theme was the supernatural in early english literature (which I had little interest in prior), but Dr. Ensley was engaging and very passionate. She did not take the class too seriously, but was serious enough (her expectations were clear and fair).
She is so sweet and kind, always willing to help you. As long as you put effort in your work, you will do well. She grades participation, so you should participate.

Dr. Ensley is great!! She is super understanding and willing to give extensions if you ask in advance. She grades fairly and gives you the opportunity to revise a project/essay if you get below an 85. I definitely recommend!

She is a fairly good grader, and I really hope I get her for ENGL 1102 next semester. She's passionate about what she teaches, and many of her homework assignments are completion grades. Very few graded projects for accuracy. So glad I had this professor. Love you Mimi!!

I had Engman for Math 2551 - I went to class three times and got an A on every test and a 97% on the final. He's not a great teacher (the voice is hilarious), but he's a kind grader and fair at the end of the class! I would suggest him for multivariable if you have a strong math/ calc background.
If I hadn't already taken calc in high school, this would have been terrible. Super confusing to listen to but not too much work overall.

He's a super nice guy, but not good at all at explaining things. He gets distracted during lecture, which makes it hard to know what to study. Lectures are dull and confusing. He also has to change the schedule a lot because of getting distracted in lecture and not covering the material. Go to recitation, it helps.
Not a great professor for a low level math class, just hope that your TA is good and can explain it to you. Honestly though you can pretty much get an A by just doing the problems he sets out

I had background in AP Calc, so this class wasn't terrible, but lectures were really boring and unclear. I felt like the lectures were more complicated than tests. Recitation was helpful and HW assignments were pretty easy. Tests were not difficult, often times we were given similar questions in recitation before the exam. I would take it again.

Marty is so boring and hard to understand (he mumbles a lot and sounds like he smokes a pack a day). His handwriting is terrible, and if you are confused and try to ask questions, he is not helpful. By the end of the semester his lectures were almost empty. The only way I learned was by teaching myself or at recitation. DO NOT take him.

Prof. Engman was extremely poor at communicating what he was teaching. He would just write illegibly on the board and not be clear about what he was writing or saying. The tests were fairly straightforward and similar to the practice tests, but I wouldn't take him again.

Mumbles a lot and talks into the board during lecture as he writes on the chalkboard. Tests seemed fair enough, but he does not curve and calculates your grade by just adding everything so its out of 500 or something. Homework was 3 mymathlab assignments and 3 written ones from textbook (not sure why we even had to use mymathlab with 3 homeworks).

A cool guy, helpful during office hours and obviously very smart, but the grading is harsh. He expects you to memorize everything but only tests a few things, so I always felt like I was wasting my study time. A lot of the homework is optional, but if you don't do at least most of it your grade will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Test are reasonable but if you make a few small mistakes, it can easily drop your grade. He is against curving the class and has a set grading scale. If you make  below an 80 on 1 test, it is very difficult to bring it up to an A. It is easy to learn from the book and in recitation. He has really bad handwriting and is difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I found him really difficult to understand so lectures weren't helpful, and I relied on the book.  He has very few things he grades on (6 hws and 3 test + final) and there is absolutely no curve on anything.  He gives a recommended hw list  and you should absolutely do it.  Tests are pretty straight forward but some discontinuity in grading.

Marty is pretty cool, especially if you go talk to him in his office. All of his test questions are straightforward except the last one which will always be a challenging problem. It can be difficult to follow along with lectures. Make sure you do extra problems in addition to the homework, because it won't cover everything  you need to know.

Marty is an awesome person and is very entertaining to listen too. He is pretty good at explaining the calculus stuff, but not as good at explaining the linear algebra. His tests were EXTREMELY difficult. We got extra credit on the first test, but only on the first test. The averages were all C's or failing, but he doesn't curve AT ALL.

Marty is a really cool guy, and I really liked him as a person, but as a teacher...His tests were difficult and he DOES NOT curve. He grades on a weird scale by adding up total points. I attended every lecture and I ended up only a few points from a B, because the third test and the final were both terrible (really bad averages!).

While he was pretty nice as a person, his class was unnecessarily hard (fill in the blank TESTS & quizzes). You should attend class b.c he drops your lowest test grade, but I missed out on that. Do the extra credit, or you're SOL. I got an A, & he went over things you really should know in gen psych, but don't take this if you don't have to.

While he is not a bad teacher, I would say his class just isn't worth the difficulty level. His tests do not test critical thinking but instead require you to remember random vocabulary words that could have appeared only once before. I do not feel that his assessment style is fair to students, and he doesn't grade on a curve.
Great teacher, interesting lectures, but weekly quizzes mean you must keep up with the reading or you are screwed.

awesome lectures. very good instructor. supposed to be the hardest section of psych 1101, but the class is very interesting and by the end of the semester he knows everyone's name which is really awesome (you dont see this a lot at tech). great teacher overall. i would reccommend to any psych major.

Supposedly the hardest section for Psych 1101 but he did a great job in not making the lectures dull as hell, which they shouldn't be but somehow other teachers can make them that way. The quizzes are sometimes very detailed and tricky though.
Great!  Goes out of his way, compared to 99% of the teachers at Tech.

Not bad, but not outstanding. If you don't like proofing as much as I do, I was OK in class skipping lecture most days and going to studio with a fantastic TA. Homework is a decent amount of effort. The complexity of the material increases by a large margin.I had a hard time comprehending what she was saying and thought the lectures to be useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not bad, not great. Really proof heavy, so if you don't like that like me, I was fine in the class skipping lecture most days and attending studio with a great TA. Homework is pretty reasonable. Material increases in difficulty by a pretty significant margin, so start off the first couple midterms well.
Her exams are just like what she taught us in class. She is super kind and she even wrote me an email when I missed a quiz on accident.

Professor Steinbart is a great lecturer and know the material very well. Homeworks are reasonable (1 every week). Tests were difficult but fair, we were given a practice exam with similar questions. Definitely recommend taking her for 2551 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She teaches well. We had tech issues for a bit but its good now. She is by far the best multi option. PROFESSORS MATTER FOR MULTI (things arent standardized). Her tests were pretty straightforward and quizzes exactly like homework (but no partial credit on quizzes due to MML). *note this was a COVID class so tests/quizzes may be different format

So, if you're just learning Calculus for the first time, I can't say how this will go for you. I took Calculus in high school, and this class was a breeze. Just make sure you understand the material, DO ALL THE HOMEWORK, and go to lecture. You'll be fine doing those things - her class shouldn't be that hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had a very hard time understanding what she taught, and found the lectures unhelpful. Highly recommend taking a different teacher if you haven't taken the content before

Gives a lot of work. She's very approachable and sweet, but she makes every student work hard for their grades. Recommend attending lectures and making sure you understand the material in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The mic always broke so nobody could hear her, and she wasn't good at explaining concepts anyway. If you get a good TA it might be different, but mine was only interested in showing off his own knowledge. I learned everything on my own on the online homework. No crib sheet, so lots of memorizing formulas. Take someone else if you can.

Ok so she is a really nice person, but her class is tough. I lost a lot of points because she had weekly quizzes which were worth 25% of the grade in the end. I would say make sure to give you all from the beginning because she doesn't curve or give any extra credit. Other proffs had huge curves with similar grades, so I wish I had someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've had at Tech.

Prof Steinbart is extremely sweet and caring. Her lectures are proof heavy, which I'm not the biggest fan of, but she understands the concepts very well. There are weekly quizzes (get harder) and only 2 midterms but I found that more helpful. I personally learned a lot of the material on my own but she is extremely sweet and open to questions.
Good professor. Lectures are long but she has good examples. Homework and tests are straightforward.

Her lectures were extremely important. It didn't always make sense because she did teach a lot in terms of variables but she made up for it by including examples and provides realistic practice problems. She was a great teacher and was really trying to get feedback from students and help them based on the feedback. Tests are straightforward.
Lectures are long but useful, and homework is relatively easy. Dr. Steinbart is really responsive to feedback. She makes a lot of typos and writing errors, but otherwise she's great

Professor Steinbart is a great professor. Although sometimes what she says can be a little bit hard to understand simply because sometimes her terminology gets a little messed up, she is very willing to help you. Her tests are really easy and very fair. Also, she really cares about our feedback. She has lots of proof based lectures which I enjoyed.
I really liked the way she taught the class; her lectures were pretty engaging for a math class. Grading is super fair, and as long as you pay attention the class is manageable.

Lectures are long but worth going to, just be ready for lots of proofs that you won't be expected to know. She works lots of examples that are similar to what you'll see on a test. She's very approachable and wants to help her students. Tests are manageable. Only get 3 tries on MyMathLab homework questions.

Dr. Steinbart is a great instructor. She is well prepared every lecture. She will provide worksheets and chapter outlines. She will clarify  topics and concepts before moving on. Very approachable. Also the class is fairly easy provided you READ the chapter and take good notes. Using logic and proofs is a must for this class. Overall, you'll learn.

For Linear Algebra I highly recommend her. If you do your homework, pay attention, read the book, and not fall behind, you'll be fine, she's not cruel in her exams, and she tests in stuff that was covered.

Her class is tough but fair. Lecture can be confusing at times with all the proofs she does, but you're not tested on them. The exams don't throw curveballs at you but will really see if you know the material. The final was tougher than the regular exams but I passed it and got a B in the class (she says the class isn't curved, but I think it was).

Take her! She explains things well and gives handouts to make the lectures more bearable. She's helpful outside of class and cares. It's a lot of material, so the course moves quickly, but she covers everything well. Weekly quizzes, some graded homework, 3 tests and a final to check that you're keeping up. So keep up and you'll be fine.

Take her! She explains things well and provides handouts to help make the lectures more bearable. It's easy to talk to her outside of class and she seems to care about the students. It's a lot of material, but she only asks that you learn it -- some graded homework, easy weekly quizzes, 3 tests, and an exam.

Ok teacher but does nothing but proofs during lecture and makes things more difficult than they appear.  She does not curve at ALL!!  i made all B's on the tests and the class average was always in the 60's or 50's and there was no curve!!
HATE HER. does not curve

She loves to ask too much proof on her exam problems. If she asks you to prove that the integral of a certain function within a closed contour is a certain value, she also expects you (implicitly!) to find out what if the function is outside the contour, or she takes out points from your answer! Come on!

She flew through the material. Explained concepts clearly but did very few example problem. Seemed bothered when students asked questions in class. If you can learn from a book this prof. is for you. You better have a good TA thats all I have to say.

If you do not know what polar coordinates are or you have not taken calculus, then you do not belong in this class. Period. If you want to learn Complex Analysis at a brisk clip, then take this class. There is plenty of homework, the tests follow from it, and grading is fair. Leave plenty of time to take this course, as the workload is constant.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

uh...don't take her. She goes way too fast, have quiz every week (which counts for significan't % of ur mark) exams are hard, lecture is boring and uses ****ty book written by one of her colleagues, (gatech prof) which is impossible to understand...
No Comments
Had him this semester for the leadership version of GT1000, really kind guy. You should take him if you have the opportunity!

Does not have a lot of teaching but WOW, very good prof. I heard great things about him in the past and I specifically took his section. I had a great time in his class and I would definitely take it again.
He's very informative about the school and is always willing to help and share his knowledge.
Legend.
He is very helpful and im so thankful to him
I specifically liked the activity we did which involved strengthsQuest. It gave me a great insight to my individual strengths and I was interested and read a lot into it.

Profesor Erik Johnson is a very charismatic and caring professor. He is very accesible and his lectures are really fun and interactive. I would 100% recommend taking this class with Profesor Erik Johnson.

Amazing CS professor. The final for our class (fall 2025) WAS MANDATORY. But I think he curved - idk? But I ended up getting the A. Dont forget to do quizzes. Do homework, and study those for taking your tests. Vigoda is a fair professor and is a great guy. Love him, and he made 130A my favorite CS class I had so far!
Simply the goat
All I know are black boxes. If anyone asks me how dijkstra's algorithm works I'm cooked.

Professor Vigoda is amazing. He's a bit of a character, and his lectures can be a bit all over the place, but he structures the course really well, and actually teaches us algorithms through the lens of famous, important and practically useful algorithms in computer science. Low emphasis on rigorous proofs or on writing code.
Amazing lectures. he gives clear examples and step by step explanations. Take notes during his lectures, they help. Accomodating of personal emergencies.
He is a great professor that knows what he is talking about. Good lectures and explains concepts thoroughly. Homework and grading is clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pretty thorough lectures, although he speeds through them and they're sometimes hard to follow. His video supplements were the biggest help for me in learning concepts. He was very intimidating during office hours, especially with simple questions. Tests were very fair and he will reward improved grades with altered weighting of assignments.

Vigoda did it again! 
Great professor. He makes the difficult topics presented in 130A/B simple. 
Homeworks and quizzes are a direct reflection of the questions you will see on the midterms. 
Final is optional for those with an A or A-. Great policy!

His lectures could get a bit confusing at times when going over proofs, but overall he is a great teacher. Hws and quizzes help and reflect lecture material and exam content. My only complaint is that there were 2 midterms and a final that result In 75% of the grade, but he is very flexible and will weight the tests different to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I saw the other good reviews about him and was excited to take his class but people that have had him in the past say that something has changed in him. He speed runs every lecture in a super unclear way. When people are left with questions he throws childish tantrums and refuses to answer basic questions. If you don't have to take him, don't.
Professor Vigoda is the absolute best. He is kind, cares about his students, and is super passionate about what he teaches. Highly recommend 130A and 130B.
Good professor who teaches well. Grading is reasonable, though midterm and final heavy. Lectures are all available online and you can learn everything just from the textbook alone.

Nice & pretty great at explaining things but sassy when talking 1-on-1. I got a lot of "you should know this already" from him at genuine questions. Stay ON TOP of quizzes, it's a slippery slope if you slack on them. Project 1 was INSANELY hard but project 2 was easy. Class is sorta easy but moves fast so you have to REALLY concentrate to get an A.

Vigoda, more like ViGOATa!

He is in the top-2 CS professors I've had here at UCSB. 

Short, 3-5 question quizzes after each lecture, which are very easy if you pay attention. Homework was easy-medium in difficulty. Midterm only covered material from quizzes or homework. No trick questions.

Final was optional for those w/ an A or A-.

He taught the class in a way that it is easy and clear to understand what is being taught. Super clear lecture notes and hw/programming assignments were very doable. Overall one of my favorite CS classes I've taken

Lectures are really fun and engaging. 130B comes with a lot of difficult concepts but this professor does a great job at explaining them. Homework and quizzes were relevant and useful for the exams. Overall great professor.

Took him at UCSB - lectures quickly, topics are hard to understand when you see them for the first time but he assigns quizzes based on lecture content which force you to learn/understand the material. Fun professor, would regularly bribe us with Starbucks gift cards. CS projects are all-or-nothing, start on them quickly, but they're not too hard.

This is for CS130B at UCSB. No programming assignments, so if that’s what you like learning with, this isn’t the class for you. This class is 80% exams, so study well and you’ll be able to get a good grade. Pretty good lecturer. Very clear grading/curving options
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vigoda is a great lecturer, his explanations were fast but had a very logical pattern which made them easier to follow. Attendance wasn't mandatory and you could watch pre-recorded lectures, but the lectures were great, and along with homework, were enough to be very prepared for the exams. I took this class Fall 2019.

He's definitely my favorite lecturer out of all the professors at Tech. I would sometimes zone out during lecture but he had a Udacity course with recorded lectures of the same topics. If you actually pay attention during lecture, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer, but speaks at light speed. He is pretty clear about what you need to know for the exams. You learn 5 main concepts in the class and have four exams besides the final, so the tests are pretty individualized. Curved & A/B means you can skip final. Homework gives you a good idea on what will be in the tests. Lecture vids online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A good lecturer, although tests can be difficult. Make sure understand the homework; they're extremely helpful. Posts lecture notes and homework/solutions online, which is helpful. Sadly no practice tests, although those can be found elsewhere.

I loved Eric as a lecturer. He moved very quickly, but was super into the material. He would give an outline of the types of problems to expect on exams, which were always of comparable difficulty to the homework assignments. There was a pretty decent curve at the end of the class and the final was optional, so a decent number of people got an A.

Dr. Shen is a very passionate professor, willing to sit down and be accessible outside of class. You can tell he loves to apply chemistry to real world application. Even better, he loves to learn! He asks his students to share facts for extra credit and he will even bring in guest lecturers to explain his less experienced topics.

Eric Shen is a very engaging lecturer and a caring professor. He liked to include real world applications for every new concept to make it more digestible/interesting. The lecture content and in-class questions reflect the material on the exams well.

The pookiest teacher there ever was. Eric did a great job in lectures and his practice problems prepared us great for the exams. The content wasn't exactly easy, but he did a great job of breaking it down for anyone who asked!
Super nice guy, okay lecturer. Practice and patterns are key with his course (and generally ochem). Not a lot of work, but studying takes some time. Lots of chances for extra credit.

This dude is great. He gave so many extra credit/regrade opportunities, which made something as terrible as Organic Chemistry so much more bearable. He's open to feedback, and will always slow down if you ask! He's also really interested in the subject and it shows- he encourages you to ask questions if your curious, and is really nice overall.

Great class to take if you need to fulfil the Organic Chemistry requirement without a year of it. Class is points-based with extra credit and grade replacement-- he rewards effort as well as accuracy, which is especially nice since Organic Chemistry is a hard subject. Class is livestreamed, and there are weekly in class assignments and hw's.

He is very knowledgeable about chemistry and makes us excited about it as well. I love his TA team, they're all amazing and you can tell he cares for all of them. Although lectures can be dense, he is very accessible outside of class. Lectures can also be very sporadic but I think you just need to get used to his lecturing style and then its great!
so nice and makes a really hard class understandable. grading criteria was pretty easy too

Of course it's not "easy" because it's orgo, but homeworks are pretty light (usually only 5-10 questions) and his tests are very fair. Graded on a bucket point system so an A is attainable if you do well on the three midterms. He's always got good energy and takes time to entertain student questions. Very approachable and open to feedback.

I hated this class. Prof would talk to us like we were chem grad students, and talk about his research and advanced topics. This is supposed to be a survey class for non-chem majors! Lectures are recorded. Thankfully there is a point based system for grades.

He's amazing! He's really humorous and knowledgeable. He always tries his best to make the class easier for the students (lowest CIOS rate I know). The class policy seems incredibly accommodating to me (can bring the grade for 1st exam up by going to office hours, final is for grade improvement). He also records his lectures and uploads the slides.

Amazing professor teaching a difficult class. He is a caring professor, and a decent lecturer, although it personally took me a second to find a good method of taking notes in his class. Tests are quite difficult, but grade-replacement policies will help you out. Will recommend, especially if his class is needed for a major requirement.

I LOVE DR SHEN!!! he is so nice and amazing and makes a lot of concepts really clear, and is very straightforward about what's going to be tested. for exams, just do all the practice/past exams he provides and you will be good to go. the grading scheme in the class allows for a lot of room for improvement and he provides a ton of extra credit.
Dr. Shen is really good at lecturing and really cares for his students. He gives a lot of opportunities to raise your grade with extra credits.
Cares a lot about his students, and tries his best to simplify hard topics.

he is a fantastic teacher! he is so pookie, the way he teaches is very engaging and he truly cares about the class. he makes me want to go to lecture, and makes a very feared and difficult class easier to understand. if you need to take chem 1315, take this professor!

Had him as a Co-Teacher for Fall 2023. Really good teacher as demonstrated during Review Sessions, and always accessible on Piazza for assistance. Also, designed Quizzes/Tests, which were definitely fair (with Bonus points) and overall, his bubbly personality was very contagious, showing his very deep passion for Organic Chemistry in class.

Great guy. Felt that the homework was super manageable and directly connected to what we learned so it was reinforcing & not soul sucking. I do recommend further self practice to succeed, but the textbook he used was also great and had many questions to work with. Super accessible and kind, waived final if >85 before the final. HW and CW points!
Great professor, tests are straightforward, homework is simple as long as you watch/pay attention to lectures

Eric is a fantastic teacher! He genuinely wants people to learn and is extremely receptive to student feedback. He is very accessible outside of class, accommodating, and very kind. Orgo is tough, but he tries his absolute hardest to help and lectures very well. Tests are open note & an A is an 85. If you get the chance to take his class, do it!

Taking Organic Chemistry with Shen was an absolute pleasure. Lectures are in-person but he records on Zoom as well, I showed up because I genuinely enjoyed his teaching style. Shen keeps students engaged and is very accessible outside of class. His humor often made my day.

Dr. Shen was truly the best professor I could have asked for. Organic chem is notoriously a hard course. He makes it manageable with digestible lectures and easy homeworks. The tests are open note too! Grading is generous (an 85 is an A) and he truly cares about the kids. You will need to put in a lot of work outside of class to succeed!

Amazing professor, genuinely cares about the students and what they're interested in. Very responsive to emails and in office hours and wants people to learn. One of the best professors I've had at Tech for sure! Would reccomend him to anyone that need to take Survey of Orgo

He is very very considerate! He takes any feedback he receives to heart and will adjust accordingly. The class is tough but he offers all the resources he can to alleviate some of the stress. I love him. My king.

Professor Shen was one of the best professors I ever had.  He focused lectures on what students would likely need to know in the future and was very responsive to the students.  If he didn't finish teaching or students were still confused, he would review the next day.  An A was an 85, exams were open note, and final could be exempt.

Eric was one of the best professors I have ever taken.  In a historically difficult class, he helped make the class much more manageable.  He focused topics on what students would most likely need in the future instead of following units right out of a textbook.  He also adjusted the class pace to match what students needed.  Exams were open notes.

PSYC 3000 (Science of Happiness) One of the best grading systems I have seen at Tech. The class requires a bit of reading, but it is very manageable and so worth it. I learned a lot from the assigned readings and loved discussing with others on the discussion platforms. Overall, I would recommend taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There were weekly 6-8 question quizzes on each chapter which you had to read ~100 pages of the textbook to prepare for. Textbook readings were a lot and very frequent but kinda interesting. Quizzes end up having 1-2 confusing questions that drop your quiz grade a lot if you miss them (20% of grade, 1 drop). Tests all FRQ, but grading was lenient.

Would not recommend taking this class if you are taking as an elective. Exams are worth 70% and in my opinion were graded too harshly. The quizzes were also difficult and the averages were often mid  to low 70s. Lectures were boring. There was a chance to get up to 3.5% extra credit but if you haven't done well on exams and quizzes , expect a C.

No homework, 3 tests and a paper. Pretty lenient grader but the tests are bit difficult if you haven't kept up with lecture or read the textbook. Professor seems nice and like he cares about students.

If u want an A, u HAVE to work for it. skim the textbook &pay attention to lecture material/study guide topics to do well on the exams. Research paper can bring ur grade up if you write a decent one, and As are manageable on exams if you make time to study and actually digest the info. 3.5% EC opportunity & mandatory research hours. Nice prof/class

Schumacher is a very competent instructor, but there are 3 tests and one research essay that makeup 25% each. This makes it harder than expected to earn an A, especially since the tests are rather difficult despite the content being deceptively easy. However, there are a lot of extra credit opportunities which helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you want an A, if you don't care about psyc and want to spend more for your other classes, this one is okay. No weekly homeworks except a paper so almost 0 time commitment. Seriously study for exams because they are actually kind of hard and define your grade. 0 margin for error. He is a decent lecturer.

Only graded by 3 exams (no cumulative final) and a research paper; don't let that scare you though because he is an amazing lecturer and makes psych very intriguing. He always tries to make each lecture memorable and have practical and applicable information. One of the best psych professors there is! Highly recommend and would take again!!

Grade is very test heavy and you go into exams pretty much blind. There are no homeworks or quizzes to give you an idea of what is expected. The exam "study guide" that Schumacher provides is a list of over 200 terms. The entire grade is made up of 3 tests and a research paper. He's a decently interesting lecturer but that's about it.

He expects too much for people taking an intro to psych course. He often used terms I wouldn't understand mid-lecture and had assignments like research paper on psych which was 25% of my grade. The entire grade is based off 3 tests and 1 research paper. Unless youre a god at psych, this class gonna be super hard. Definitely wouldn't take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This man does not know how to explain concepts

Super nice and tried to make lectures more fun by showing videos and telling stories. The class was graded by only three exams and a research paper. Tests were fair and average difficulty (you'll definitely need to study if you want a good grade though). Textbook is provided by him for free. The content was a bit boring but that's not his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting lecture. Charismatic. Tests are not hard. Need to read the textbook a little bit sometimes for reference but not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: DO NOT take his class, he teaches off lecture powerpoints that are not available before the class. Expected students to memorize over 150 words for recall on a fill in the blank test that counts as 30% percent of your grade. Some of the words weren't available in the notes or the textbook. He seems like a nice guy but expectations were unreasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Schumacher is a decent lecturer but comes across as though he is disinterested, possibly as a result of his personality rather than lecturing ability. Gives test questions ahead of time (in the graduate course) and material heavily based on the numerous articles read in class. Tests based on more rote memorization than critical thinking.
He is the BEST! I loved this class and would recommend it to anyone needing an A. He is very nice and very helpful!
He is the BEST psyc teacher!! So helpful and nice. His class is an easy A and the book is not needed. Definitely recommend him!
No Comments

This man cares about his students, and his enthusiasm for the material and life in general makes the class a great way to get your education. His class was the breath of fresh air I needed in my first semester here!

He really cares about the class and is always around to answer questions. He's really great at seeing how different students approach a question and going from there to help us identify where we made a mistake. Has the enthusiasm of a teacher who has not yet lost hope for mankind. Dresses like a huge nerd but he pulls it off

He's an awesome guy. His teaching is ok, a bit disorganized but decent. Class is mostly solving problems. He has a great sense of humor and is very friendly. The homework is horrible sometimes because one mistake and you've messed up the entire 10 step truss problem. He holds review sessions to help students. He cares a lot and asks for feedback.

Prof. Hilton was a fantastic statics professor. He's hilarious and a bit on the derpy side, but that makes an otherwise dry class enjoyable. He is very passionate about teaching as well. The workload was pretty light and the tests were very manageable.
*Fantastic* professor. Excellent at commanding attention in large lectures and is incredibly helpful during PSS sessions. If you take 3310, take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ethier is a demanding prof, but also an amazing instructor who is deeply passionate about the course material. Biotransport is definitely a tough course, but Dr. Ethier makes the course worthwhile. Study hard, do lots of practice problems, ask for help, and you should be fine.

Probably the most difficult class you will take. He is brutal when it comes to grading, but very friendly during class and group sessions. Many times, he asks questions without much structure, but expects answers with complete structure. I recommend skipping his notes altogether and reading the book for topics he covers in his notes.

honestly an not a great professor all around. not engaging when she lectures, rude, does not reply to emails ever which makes it impossible to have your attendance corrected when you miss class. attendance is mandatory and you lose points if you come in >5 mins late, which is unfortunate when i'm the one PAYING for these courses.
She doesn't even answer emails and the final grade calculation wasn't even right.

graded by too many things when clearly some grade categories are not even necessary for the class. has article quizzes which tests on the specific content of a research paper, so it's irrelevant from the topics learned in class. the supposed "homeworks" are just writing practice questions for the article quizzes. she makes the class impractical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Was overall an okay class since the content is not that hard, but giving this rating because she seems to nervous laugh a lot and when I brought up personal mental issues for accommodation, she let out a random chuckle when it was a serious topic. Just not an enjoyable person to talk to outside of class.

The professor is honestly not bad but her lecture slides can be sort of confusing to look at. But she does try her best to teach by providing practices and study guides. The course content is pretty easy to grasp as long as you're willing to put extra time. Did not attend most of the lecture/lab but ended with an A, so it is definitely doable.

i'm sure she's a great person, but she was one of the least engaging professors i've ever had. in-class activities were inconsistently weighted so get ready to either sit through every lecture or watch the canvas uploads like a hawk. she does post exam study guides, though, and the content wasn't too hard. watch out for research article quizzes.

I took this course in Summer 2024. Kim was an effective communicator, but if felt pretty obvious that she didn't want to be teaching this class virtually. Group sessions were used to complete small, easy assignments. You, with your group were responsible for writing a research paper over the course of the semester. Class was easy but uninspiring

Prof is clearly an intelligent person but that does not make her a great teacher. She does not teach the basics of the concepts we learn in class well. You will have to teach yourself most of the material. The lectures do not really help unless you already have a proper understanding of statistics. She definitely makes the class harder than needed.

I feel slightly bad that she was thrown in as the lecturer for PSYC 2020 last minute with little preparation. It's also clear that she knows the content very well as she constantly talks about advanced topics without establishing the basics. If you take the class with little to no stats knowledge, you'll have to learn a lot outside class.

Eunbee is definitely a victim of being thrown into a course without enough time to prepare. While she listened to feedback and adjusted her lectures upon receiving complaints, she focuses primarily on conceptual and abstract material, which is weird for a math class. I made an A by teaching myself the information. Not super hard but not worth it.

Exams were pretty tough in this class, but he offers a lot of extra credit and weights the journal entries and group projects pretty heavily, which are essentially free A's if you do them. Easy to make an A in this class if you do the prep work and extra credit and participate in class. Good class and professor overall.
He is extremely caring and a nice guy. There are a lot of group presentations and there is a paper due after each lecture. The course content is easy to understand, and his lectures are good.

There are two group projects but both are very manageable. His lectures were easy to understand and I found them pretty engaging. You either have to complete a 1 page journal or memo for every class but considering there is no other homework it's very manageable. He cares about students and wants them to succeed.

pretty boring class but overall the assignments were super easy and you'll get a good grade as long as you do them as instructed. he wasn't the most entertaining professor but he was very easy to take

As someone that dislikes group projects, I didn't feel like I was being pulled down by them. It felt pretty balanced between individual work and projects. He is a very understanding professor and wants his students to succeed. Taking this class means being prepared to write a lot, but it was engaging and less commitment than I expected.

The best features of this course were journals and memos that allowed me to reflect on what I learned each week. His lectures were easy to understand and the projects made me utilize out understanding of the material effectively. Professor Kim was very supportive and encouraged my team to be creative in group work and presentations.

The projects and cases were genuinely interesting and thought-provoking. The greatest strength of this instructor was his ability to be available for questions at any time and to make lessons about Human Resources applicable to my day-to-day life. The syllabus could be more clear with the due dates!

There is some busywork (written reflections of what we've learned after each class session), but it's fairly simple. There were several group presentation projects, but they aren't very difficult. There are opportunities for extra credit (5-pg analysis of certain articles). You can find the textbook online for free (read it! it will help a lot)

I did enjoy his class much. There is a lot of busywork at the start and end of each class which is useless in my opinion. There is also a lot of group work and your experience will depend on the quality of your group. No tests throughout the semester except there is a final which makes no sense. Very boring class but you can survive it.

First off, get ready for some projects as there are a lot of them. Show up to class, humor him with his busywork, and you'll be in a good spot. For such a project heavy class, the problem is when it is possible to have a 95 going into the final, get a B on it, and end with a 89 in the class with no bump. Similar situation happened to like 7 of us.

Way too many projects and too much busy work. Feedback on grades is vague or non-existent. Language barrier. With all of that said, anyone with a pulse should make an A in the class -- that vague grading system is super lenient, as virtually all grades on group projects are between 90 and 95.

Easy A.  About 40% of your grade is from group projects, but he's a VERY light grader, so, as long as you don't completely BOTCH it (i.e. present on donuts and elephants or something), you'll do fine.  Oh, also, 10 PAGE FINAL EXAM CRIB SHEET.  He has weekly memos and journals, which can be a little tedious, but it's a small price to pay.  Take him.

Dr. Kim keeps Org Behavior interesting and does a great job of teaching the class in different ways from movie clips, to articles, to class discussion. The class is completely group based and the only formal test is the final (where you can use 5 pages front and back of crib notes). The class isn't too difficult and you will learn a lot as well.
Took Phys 4321 with him. He's very flexible and accommodating.  Cares about the students and is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. I was dreading this class but Dr. Murray never made me feel like I was overwhelmed at all. Like others said the class structure isn't great (flipped classroom) -- he's a great teacher that unfortunately has to comply with unsavory department rules. Great at answering questions and helping me understand the mess that is physics!

While he didn't lecture traditionally, his questions and explanations in class covered all the material as far as I could tell. He explained most things well in my opinion. Labs were pretty worthless. Half were worksheets and they happened before the material was covered so we mostly followed the procedure blindly.

He is one of the worst professors I have ever had in my life. I have never learned less in a class and the entire class was too much effort. I put in a lot of work and by test day it didn't matter because it was very difficult because you ended up learning nothing conceptual.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Murray knows his stuff, but he refuses to teach in lectures. You MUST read the pre-reading material before class and do the turning point questions for participation points (which counts to ur final grade btw). It was a lot of work for me to keep up with his tests even though I'd already taken the class before and got a high A. Take Murray ATYR
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Murray really knows classical physics. My biggest complaint is that, as the class is read first and proceed to have clicker questions throughout the lecture that are graded, Murray seems to not care whether students succeed or not in his class--just that they learn. There is definitely a place for that which is not introductory physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not care about teaching physics. You have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Did you take physics in high school? Don't worry this man will still try his absolute hardest to confuse you and make you fail the course. If you didn't take physics in high school take literally anyone else because Eric Murray does NOT lecture. Instead, he makes you learn all of the material on your own and insults his students' intelligence.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If I could sum up Eric's teaching ability in one word: horrible. He is not a nice person either. He expects students to learn the material on their own and then when we get something wrong in class he calls our answers "embarrassing". Tough exams and really just not an enjoyable course. If you have to take him for your major, I'm sorry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Murray is an average prof , but I think that has more to do with the how the class is set up, rather than his teaching ability. He is a good person who certainly knows his stuff, but the flipped classroom is just terrible. Lots of HW.

The grading scheme is pretty lenient and there are ways to receive extra credit. However, "lecture" is just a bunch of clicker questions, so be prepared. He also responds pretty snarkily to students at times, which I don't appreciate much. Nonetheless, the rest of class is okay, but be prepared for studios AND labs in addition to the lecture.

I enjoyed taking Dr. Murray, but be prepared to read the textbook if you aren't familiar with physics. All his lectures are structured around practice questions rather than directly going over the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is completely terrible. He has no concept of how to teach physics and how much his students understand concepts. His entire class is based on clicker questions and he expects all students to master physics off of a textbook. I actually can't believe he is a professor in this school and I can only attest to my decent grade to previous classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Unpopular opinion: I do not really mind his clicker-q heavy lectures all that much. Although they are mandatory, I do truly think they help me get better at physics. However, he generally rude and condescending to other students when they try to ask him questions, and is generally not flexible with other students' schedules.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're paying to read the textbook and the class is entire clicker questions that don't help me learn at all. Do not take Murray. Take anyone else.

I loved Dr. Murray's class. I came into it not having taken an advanced physics class before but was able to get the hang of it. Before every lecture, you read the textbook and then during class, you answer questions on the material. There are a lot of leniencies with grading. He is also a funny guy who cares about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class time consisted of reading problems and clicker questions. The easiest way to do well is simply to show up to every class having done the reading, and actively participate in the clicker questions. Professor Murray is a caring dude who will answer everyone's questions and makes himself available outside of class for help.

Personally didn't enjoy the teaching style. You have to read and teach yourself and basically go to class to practice (clicker questions - they count for correctness). Would 10/10 recommend going to PLUS sessions - where you really get a taste of how the test questions are.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: EVERY CLASS is CLIKER Qs ONLY. If large majority gets a Q wrong, he'll explain it, but other than that, no lectures at all. Expects you to read then just do clicker Qs (on which your attendance matters and you get less pts if you're wrong). I find mechanics relatively easy so I was alright with not going to class much. Do HW early for extra credit.

I felt like he put too much on our plate as students. His lecture is taught in the format of clicker questions, which means you have to read the TB before every class to understand the lecture. Overall I found this class taxing especially when we had labs, four HWs, recitation problems, and tests to study for on the following Monday.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Murray was an awesome professor and was excited to teach us, and I found it to be a fair class. It's a flipped classroom model which is kinda weird. If you've taken physics before/feel like you're good at physics, you'll probably be fine. Just read the textbook, do the homeworks, and take the practice tests. Lots of ways to boost your grade.

Although his lectures are pretty clicker question heavy, he was always happy to clarify something if someone didn't get it. Also, he was the most accessible professor i had this semester. He's in his office a lot and you can just walk in for some help, which definitely helped me ewith some of the tougher hw questions. Overall a solid choice.

Unfortunately doesn't do much lecturing because of the 'flipped classroom' model. So ends up just doing a ton of clicker questions and explaining as he goes; which can be helpful (if you learn with concrete examples rather than abstractly!)
This class is just rough in general. Professor murray is nice but you need to sit close so you can hear him. Lots of clickers and definitely need to learn things before you go to class.

Dr. Murray is a wonderful professor. His lectures are very enjoyable, and he's a very nice person. My only complaint is that lecture was clicker-question heavy. The course is fairly difficult, but it's still very possible to succeed if you do the pre-lecture readings, go to class, attend PLUS sessions, and take the exams from previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Murray wasn't bad by any means, and for a 150+ person lecture you can't expect too much from your professor. He was easily accessible during office hours. The class was taught in a reverse classroom style, where we were supposed to do the reading before class, and then in class we would answer reading questions using TurningPoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Murray is a good prof for a bad class. Lots of homework and clicker questions that don't do much to help you learn the material. Do practice exams to prepare for tests. Make sure to go to lab and lecture for attendance. Overall this is a weed-out class and is just a lot of busy work which makes a potentially simple class require a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You need to keep up with this class. Lectures are not supremely helpful but necessary for participation grade and reading question grades. Study old tests thoroughly as it appears to be the best way to prepare for tests.

Honestly ruined my interest in EM. Came into the class really, really wanting to learn more about physics, but it soon became obvious that we have to teach ourselves everything. He never actually lectured, only just gave clicker questions to make sure we taught ourselves right. Not an easy A at all, so not good for people just wanting to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are good - not the most entertaining, but I was never very bored. He explains things well and is clear about expectations.

Lectures are useless, because all he does are clicker questions. Unfortunately you need to attend all of the lectures to get participation points. 3 homework sets a week on web assign. Labs are a waste of time considering half of them are just worksheets. Expect to do all of your learning in recitiation and doing practice tests.

Dr. Murray is energetic, eloquent, and hilarious! He does a great job of explaining concepts and often prepares fun demonstrations for lecture. The exams in this course are fairly difficult, but if you keep up with the assigned reading and homework and work through some of the past exams, you'll be prepared.

Dr. Murray is great. You just have to adjust your expectations from a typical class because he does the flipped classroom thing. He does teach in lecture (and with a very positive attitude); it is just through the explanations of his clicker questions. Do the short homework assignment and textbook reading before class and you will succeed.

You have to read the course material from the (surprisingly unhelpful) textbook because the lecture is spent answering clicker questions.  Murray is enthusiastic and kind and will some explanation in class, so lecture isn't a total loss. The clicker questions may show up as MC on the test. If you can do the homework, you can get a A on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK
