reviews.comment: This is one of the hardest classes I've taken so far and Murray makes it somewhat bearable.  He is very good at explaining abstract concepts and is a fair grader.  However, his tests are reallllly hard and the homework sucks.  Try to get him though because just about every other professor will leave you confused.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to read the book or else you won't understand. He gives really good feedback when you ask him questions. If you don't understand something just  ask him. You can walk into his office whenever you want and he'll let you in as long as he isn't busy. I asked him a question after every lecture and he gave me very clear answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Murray is okay, but he doesn't really teach concepts in lecture. He just assumes that you come to class understanding the reading assigned so you can answer the clicker questions. You definitely should go to lecture to get the clicker points, but it's pretty boring. Tests were hard, but if you can do the homework problems on your own you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Murray's class is flawed but so is every GaTech intro PHYS class. Nothing is taught in lecture (all you do is clicker questions), but you have to go because attendance is taken (and you need the clicker points). Therefore, you're going to have to read the textbook before every lecture to do well.
Seems very knowledgeable but his lectures are just him asking questions via clicker the entire time. His tests are very easy as long as you read the chapter before.

Dr. Murray does not teach. The class is based on you reading the textbook and then coming into "lecture" to answer clicker questions. The clicker questions included material that wasn't explicitly covered. I went to office hours once, but I didn't find it helpful because he did not explain concepts thoroughly and acted as if it were obvious.

Go to class! The clicker questions are part of the grade (and about the difficulty of the test MC part), and it will matter if you are boarder-line. He covers all material through clicker questions, so it is not a traditional note-taking lecture. DO THE HOMEWORK. There is a bonus percentage, but it won't help if you do not do the review practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Go to class for the clicker questions and make sure that you read the sections before the class. Professor Murray starts class with clicker questions and then explains the answer afterwords. Class is more a practice for the tests than a lecture. Very clear professor, and he is very good at explaining the material.

If you are a smart student who can master electromagnetism just by reading the book this is the right professor for you. There is no "lecture", labs are rudimentary and the homework is straightforward. You can get a decent grade by memorizing old exams. Find another professor if you are really interested in the subject.

I find Professor Murray to be really efficient. However, you must read the book in order to do well. I recommend anyone taking Classical Physics to actually study a week before every test from the test bank. Make sure you know how to do every single problem. This class might be hard, but it's doable. The final was easier compared to the other exams

Not even Chuck Norris himself could conquer this class. There is no known cure for this class. The only things that help remedy any pain you will experience all semester come from taking extensive notes from reading the book and praying to the Physics Gods.

Dr. Murray does not teach. The class is literally go learn physics on your own. The only thing he does in lecture is clicker questions. The quizzes and final are tricky, and he likes to keep the averages in the 60s. On top of all of this, he does not even curve the final grades. You get what you get. Do not take this class unless you have to.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. I go to all of the lectures, labs, and recitations and I still have yet to pass a single one of his tests. He is confusing and a smart ass. He doesn't lecture he just asks questions and expects us to understand the class by reading the text book. Do not choose him if you can avoid it!!

He's hard, and not helpful.  Very sarcastic and can be arrogant at times.  All you do in class is clicker questions, literally, I didn't learn a thing this whole semester. Tests go from easy to extremely hard.

Absolutely terrible if you want to actually learn physics, but wonderful if you just want to get through the class. Only did PRS questions through lecture, and I was left having to teach myself out of a different textbook than what he uses. Definitely going to be very behind when I go to take E&M.

I have never seen any tricky professor like him. He will make you learn physics. It's definitely very hard to get A in his class. The best way to get A is to do all the MS physics HW without taking help from google, Reading book, understanding every prs quiz question. He is very helpful. He provides enough out of class help.

His class is easy if you go to lecture, read the book, and do practice problems. He does a good job explaining topics and uses the PRS to show tricky things that will inevitably be on the exams. His test can be hard with some of the tricky multiple choice questions but if you read the book it will help. Also, go to recitation, it'll help.

Murray was a fairly good teacher, but I really thought the course was planned well.  The book he used was a life saver, and I could always refer to it if I did not understand lecture.  Very approachable and willing to help!  Take his class!!!

Murray is a smarty guy but he is terrible at explaining ideas. Instead of lecturing he only uses the PRS to quiz students. If I'm supposed to learn the whole class by reading the book in order to answer the PRS questions, what's the point of having a lecture at all?
Ummm hard and ridiculous describe him at best.  There shouldn't be a class where a student HONESTLY tries and GOES to tutoring and still has a hard time passing. It's just RIDICULOUS!

Best Physics teacher/professor I've ever had. If you do the readings, goto class, and even half pay-attention then his class isn't all that difficult. This past summer, NO ONE who came to class 90%+ of the time failed. That's BEFORE a curve was applied, mind you. If at ALL possible, take his class... chances are you won't regret it.

He is a smart man... but his lectures are AWFUL! doesn't care about failing half the class - however if you do want a good grade he will do his best to work wtih you - really does try very hard - but he can be arrogent - take someone else if you can
Great lecturer.  Tests are difficult, but once you learn the type of questions he asks they are not as hard.  One of my few classes where I looked forward to attending lecture.

Great lecturer, with difficult tests.  Very approachable and eager to help his students in help sessions and during class.  Encourages asking questions in class.  Very clear, but you'll still have to study a lot.
teaches phys II, speaks english, but give no curve and isn't lenient at bumping grades even if close. GPA is low rangin from 1.8-2.2
Slightly arrogant, but very good, approachable, and friendly.
No Comments
No Comments
Teaches well, but hard tests/terrible curves.Takeonlyif department makes tests.

Sohn was a great and sweet professor. Her teaching style is great, however, her tests are unfairly difficult. Much of the test material was not covered in class and the multiple-choice answers were very similar. You need to study, however, she is definitely the better professor option for Strategy.

2 mini exams worth 5% each and one cumulative midterm worth 20%. There were 2 group projects, one of which is the final project worth 30%. Drill the practice questions on connect for the exams. Attendance & participation mandatory. Gave great feedback for the final project and met with me multiple times. Project was pretty cool. EC varies.

If you put in moderate effort, do all of the assignments, and show up to class, you'll get an A. She does have an attendance and participation grade, but it's easy to get full points. Lectures are pretty boring. Study slides for her exams. When I took this class, our presentation got moved online, so that was straightforward as well.

I honestly loved this class, she made it very interesting with discussions and even her style of lecturing. However I will say that the midterm exam is very difficult and not comparable to the difficulty of her other two mini exams. She does allow cheat sheets for these exams however and the group project helps your grade a lot.
Hm Mh

The professor is nice and approachable. She allows cheat sheets on exams and have an easy group project. However, she also checks participation in class. Overall, a good professor to take a class with.

This class is very straight forward. The grading is made up of two mini exams, a midterm, and a project. As long as you pay attention in class/read the textbook, an A is extremely manageable. She is also very willing to help students out and answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Generous 4. Good, fair prof, and class had interesting material that could've been presented in a more exciting way. Projects were really cool to work on and have actual applications, but some of the test questions were definitely intentionally tricky. You get a cheat sheet though so it's all good-overall a solid prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Midterms were a bit tough but you can make up for it in the group project. Likes to have discussions in class, uses a lot of real world cases which is interesting. Nice professor.

Terrible classroom manager: disorganized, Canvas gradebook is a mess, never revealed final grade cutoffs, allowed an argument about religion to break out between 2 students during presentation Q&A, got in a shouting contest with a student during the final. Exams are stupidly simple if you read the text; lectures have nothing to do with the exams.

He can be quite condescending because he knows a lot about the material but doesn't take into account that students aren't as knowledgeable. I think he sure find a softer and more compassionate approach when criticizing students work.

Was not a fan of this professor. He is very rude and condescending. From the few conversations I have had with him, I've left feeling like my intelligence was insulted. He will question everything you do if he doesn't agree with it and thinks you're always wrong. Skip the headache don't take him...

He is really caring & funny, and is always willing to help & give you feedback on your project. BMED3110 is all about learning a skill set that Essy is a pro in. He has so much more knowledge & you can feel like an idiot when he starts asking about your project just because of how much more he knows about scientific studies. Overall a good choice.

He is rarely in the lab after the first month. He just sits in his office on the first floor. Half the time, the TAs don't know what is going on and one of us will have to go visit his office to ask him how to get stuff to work. Assignments are fairly low effort, and if your group members each do their part it should be an easy A..

Not enough characters to express how awful this class is
You won't hear from him, only TAs on disc. board
Expect 50+ hours per project (due every 2 wks)
Minimal info on what autograder expects, waste hours fighting with it every week bc they changed how they want image center calculated from FLOOR to ROUND without telling anyone
AVOID AT ALL COSTS

I took both CP and CV "with" him. At least he's the one giving the lectures in CP, in CV its a diff guy who I will admit is pretty good but doesn't even work at GT anymore. The only involvement the prof had with our CV class was a post in the discussion board asking for feedback about the course, all of which was (justifiably) negative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible video lectures for Computational Photography class in OMSCS CS6475. Just basic concepts shown in lectures and then ZERO involvement with the class with a token apology at the end of the semester. TA's are quite awful and give so many ridiculous clues instead of clearing basics, I suspect a psychic would do well in this course

THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN - DO NOT, I REPEAT, DO NOT TAKE! It's a graduate course (CS6475) cross-listed as an undergrad course and it is the worst. TAs are condescending and short, often making students feel dumb for asking a question. There are no 1-1 meetings as a policy, and assignments take 30-40 hours to complete. 0/10

DO NOT TAKE! STAY AWAY! This is cross listed with a masters class but they make no adjustments in grading or assignment difficulty. I have taken cross listed classes with masters students but there was always ways they made it more on the undergrad level. Professor is disconnected with class(basically run by TAs, who arent that helpful tbh).

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. RUN. GET OUT. SAVE YOURSELF. This course is a graduate class crosslisted with an undergraduate class, but Mr. Essa is the worst and makes no adjustments for undergrads. If that wasn't bad enough, he doesn't provide office hours to help with code and neither do the TA's. They literally do not meet with you 1 on 1. Stay away!!
Poor lecturer, explains concepts very vaguely. Tests are much harder than examples given in class. You need to read the textbook yourself to understand concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor: super nice, and cares about her students success/understanding of the material. For me her office hours were very valuable: she is eager to explain things again/more detailed than in class (which helped me a lot).

She is so very nice and caring about students. Plenty of resources to learn from and practice for tests and quizzes. At times she may confuse students with complex topics from the course, but she will try her best to fix it. She is not the best lecturer but she knows the material well and is willing to explain it in multiple ways.

The most caring professor I have encountered at Tech. That being said, lectures were disorganized, often incomprehensible, and I often found myself reading the textbook in class. One thing to note- while she is not the best lecturer, she is much better during office hours. The midterms are not difficult, and neither is the final. Just read the book

Her lectures were often hard to follow, so I ended up teaching myself using the online textbook and homeworks, or looking things up in general. Recitations are crucial, my TA helped a lot. Quizzes were not bad, but I really had to study for the tests, linear algebra is sort of the worst. She curved the grades though, anything above 85% was an A.

Laura Eslava is clearly very caring and kind. She makes it clear to her students that she cares about their well being and their grades. However, caring does not make up for her complete inability to teach linear algebra and her incoherent lectures. If you have no prior knowledge to linear algebra be ready to read, a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Eslava is caring. If you're confused, be sure to ask her after the lecture and she will explain the concept more thoroughly. However, the lecture itself is really confusing. Since English is probably not her first language, sometimes she doesn't know how to explain the concepts. Attendance matters, but I just read the book during lectures

I came into this class with no prior knowledge on Linear Algebra. Dr. Eslava is really sweet, but I can't understand most of her lectures. I would skip lectures, but she gives random participation so I don't want to miss that. I have to do a lot of self-studying in order to do well in her exams.

If you already know linear algebra, this class will be easy for you but if you are coming in with no knowledge, it'll be very difficult to learn. Lectures are typically very confusing and surface level. She teaches the easier parts of the material and even then she constantly makes mistakes, doesn't answer questions, and gets off track.

I can tell she is at least somewhat knowledgeable in the field, but I learn absolutely nothing from her lectures. Almost none of my classmates have a clue what happens every lecture. The class isn't hard, but lectures are just wastes of time. If you read the textbook for 20min, you should learn more than one of her 1hr15min lectures.

Dr. Eslava really cares about her students well being, and she is always willing to help outside of class. That being said, she struggled to explain a lot of the concepts. Even though her exams were reasonable, a lot of students struggled to do well because they didn't understand, and I found it was best to learn from my TA or the book many times

Prof. Eslava can be slightly confusing during lecture, but her willingness and desire for her students to succeed more than makes up for any shortcomings as a lecturer. She is a really kind professor, and defies the notion of a "weed out" class by actually doing her best to give her students fair assessments and grades. Would definitely take again.

I had never taken or been exposed to linear algebra before this class. Professor Eslava is a decent lecturer. Not fantastic and not terrible. Sometimes, she can be a little confusing but if you're paying attention and actively taking notes you can get the main concepts. Her tests and quizzes are pretty easy, and she's a super nice person.

Absolutely one of the worst professors I have ever had. She does not know how to teach, and she doesn't even realize it. You will learn better if you look at her slides by yourself than you listening to she explaining them. Her quizzes and exams aren't hard, but most students do bad because they didn't learn anything from her.

Her lectures aren't really that helpful but she gives you a lot of resources in order to do well in the class. She doesn't collect homework; however, what she assigns gives insight into what will be on the test. I wouldn't suggest her class if you aren't willing to self-study because you won't pass by just going to lecture.

She provides a lot for you - on her website there are course notes, lecture notes, homework, practice midterms and practice solutions. Her lectures are tough to understand, but the sheer amount of resources she makes available does make the class doable.
Hard tests!

In her comparative politics class now...she is a great teacher and handles some pretty inane questions from vapid students with patience and clarity. The material itself is super dry, but she is enthusiastic and extremely helpful. Terrific prof, and she's pretty hot too.

Great Professor, demands a lot from her students, but I guarantee that no matter how hard you are working, she's working harder.  She really cares about what she is teaching and it shows in the enthusiasm she brings to every class.  If you dont put a lot in from day one, and speak up in class, your going to get frustrated and do poorly, so work!

Not a good professor. Not helpful, uninspiring, acts condescendingly towards students.  Has an awfully unpleasant demeanor when the class does not answer questions according to her liking.  I DO NOT recommend taking this class, the grade is absolutely not worth the effort she requires for it, especially a 1000 level elective.
Do your reading, study hard for the tests. I really enjoyed this class- the debates made it very interesting. She encourages disagreement as long as it is logical. Hard work pays off.
Skelley is a great teacher. She cares about her students and loves what she teaches. Go to lecture and READ and you will get an A. She is also the hottest teacher at Tech!

She sticks mainly to the book, and the tests are pretty easy. Her lectures are very clear too. However, I didn't know what to expect come test-time, and rather than expanding on the material read, she basically reiterated and graded us depending on if we could answer more specific questions. Overall an okay professor. Just be sure to READ.

She was an alright professor, the lectures where amusing and the quizzes and tests where insanely easy. I did almost none of the reading for the class, opened my book MAYBE 5 times and still got a B+. Attendance isn't necessary but the lectures are really helpful. Just read the lecture notes before each test and you can pull a solid B, A = more wor

Good professor.  She's new, but really cares about the students.  Stayed after each class for questions, as well as scheduled office appointments.  I thought the class itself was hard because it covers 3 subjects - Empirical Methods, Statistics, and SPSS software.  There is a research project, literature review, and the usual in-class presentation.

This is the most ridiculous class I have ever taken. Not only was it taught in the most boring and uninspiring way possible, but she demanded waaaay too much for a 2000 level class. Let's just say I worked my ass off and it went unnoticed. Apparently your research project doesn't matter, just the homework which has nothing to do with the class.

Extremely helpful professor. Explains things very clearly and knows his stuff. Homeworks are representative of exams. Everything feels fair, he curved/tossed out unfair questions on some midterms. Available during office hours and willing to make time outside of them for students. Absolute gem of the AE department. Didn't have to take final.
He was nice and approachable during class. He was open about how tests were graded and was good at making sure that content was consistent through homework and tests.

I thought that he is a good instructor. The form of the class was not the best. It was almost entirely student led. He could put some more effort in and give more lectures. I would have liked to learn more about the material. Easy class, so I can't complain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Harrison is one of those professors that makes coming to class very easy. Homework is fairly challenging, but he is very easy to access during office hours for questions and homeworks are good preparation for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: GO TO CLASS IF YOU WANT AN A. The handwriting on the notes is hard to understand. Cutoffs will be applied to your letter grade so don't be too stressed. She is nice with students and good at explaining. However, there are too many obscure proofs in the class which will drive you drowsy. Do practice exam and understand your assignment.

If you really like math, then she is the best option. She is caring and enthusiastic in this class. Tons of proofs will be done but they are not exam materials. Final is very similar to practice in structure, which helped a lot. HOWEVER, the written notes are hard to figure out most of times, so you better go to the course. Her course is not easy.

This class is challenging enough. It was very frustrating going to lecture because thery were mostly proofs that weren't very helpful and rarely abided by the textbook. Very difficult tests with very harsh grading and few resources to prepare with, low averages prove so.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a challenging course, and the way it is taught makes it even more difficult. Assignments are brutal and very few resources are given to students the complete them. Lectures consist of long-winded proofs and concepts that only vaguely relate to the content of the exams, making them hard to study for and resulting in low test averages.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only section open and now I wish I took this another semester. Frustrating experiences with everything in the class. Applied Combinatorics but spends half the class on proofs no one will probably use. I'd rather learn more concrete examples and some T/F questions on the tests are tricky.

I'm finding it almost impossible to succeed in this class. The hw is VERY difficult, and she doesn't provide any additional resources to help. Exams feel unfair as the questions are tricky and test obscure concepts instead of central ones. Too much material & no way to prep besides a practice test which was completely different from the real one.

just finished the second test and feel myself stupid. I got over full credits on the first test. However, in the second one, I just recalled days in my stupid Chinese high school. The test is incredibly difficult and I almost felt numb. When a test is difficult beyond your imagination, you will feel funny instead of nervous and disappointed.

I really don't have anything bad to say except that the difficulty of the exams are harder than most classes. As long as you are hoping to learn something from the class and don't really care about your grade, you will enjoy Dr. Evelyne's lectures.

This class was quite an adventure. The second midterm threw most of us off, and the final wasn't easy either. However, the class was really enjoyable with interesting lectures and concepts learned, and most of the problems she gave out were thought-provoking. If you want to take MATH 4022, Evelyne was a great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic, nice, and very smart professor. I took her for MATH 4022; she cares a lot about the class and the content. Lectures covered content from the textbook/proofs, but she took her time to explain questions. Exams are hard but very fair, and the feedback given is detailed and helpful. I don't understand why there are so many bad reviews.

One of my favorite courses/instructors ever, mostly because she did an excellent job of explaining difficult concepts and provided high-quality lecture notes instead of just reading off slides. Not deserving of all of the poor reviews. Never had points taken off unless I was completely clueless. Difficult midterms, but the final saved my grade.

She provided detailed lecture notes and would like to give examples to some abstract concept. Exams and HWs are fairly easy as long as you attend lecture/review her notes. She would like to listen to students' advice and make changes correspondingly. An easy class where you can learn a lot. She is definitely the best professor for MATH 3012

Her lectures were very straightforward, and her notes were very concise. We only had homework once every 1-2 weeks (about 3-5 problems). She also provided exam study guides and practice problems a week prior to the exams, which were very representative. As long as you keep up with lectures and do the homework, you'll succeed in this class.

Professor Smith-Roberge is a great lecturer. Her lectures are easy to follow. She makes detailed notes which allow you to keep up with the class even if you choose not to attend. Very helpful on assignments, which are not too many. She is a tough grader though, and it is easy to lose points, especially on tests. But overall, an amazing professor.

Lectures were well taught and the notes she posted for each lesson were easy to follow even if you didn't attend class. People complaining about low test grades fail to realize that this class is supposed to be hard. Other sections with different professors had similar grade distributions after she curved the class which she explained many times

Pros
-No mandatory attendance
-Detailed lecture notes are posted
-Short homeworks, quizzes are generally free

Cons
-Final is30-40%
-Distribution is still lower than the average of other classes based on lite stats despite promises
-Notes are hand written and take effort to read
-Difficult tests

TLDR: Doesn't require a lot of effort, but difficult

Roberge clearly has a great understanding of the material; the class is lecture-heavy but she explains concepts well and clears up misunderstandings if you ask questions. She posts extremely detailed notes from lecture that make it easy to catch up on missed material. Though exam averages were low, final grades were curved to match other sections.

I had a great time in this class. Others are correct that she doesn't follow a text book, but everything you need to know will be in her lecture notes. Don't take this before CS 2050 or Math 2106.

She gives you a list of definitions and techniques as a study guide before every exam. If you learn everything on the study guide, then you'll be fine.

Greatest teacher @ GT, so great that exam averages are consistently failing. Course is called "Applied" Combinatorics, always lecturing difficult and detailed proofs. Extremely harsh and seemingly arbitrary grading, often takes off half points for small mistake (ex: make a statement that is not completely true, receive 2/3 (66%) on quiz).

Obviously there is a reason why her rating is so abysmal. Absurd grading and tests, teaches arbitrary content, completely laughable teaching "skills." It is possible to get a good grade in her "class", just do not mess up on tests/finals which had averages around ~60 (which she thought was fine).

First year teaching, exam averages below a D every time. Graded by very few things, tests are nothing like homework assignments. Despite having no proofs/discrete prereq, gave a difficult proof question on final. 

**Somehow manages to cover less content than the other sections** despite all this, truly an amazing accomplishment
The tests are really hard and long. There isn't enough time to complete everything. The assignments and practice problems are nothing like test. Lectures were useless.
Very difficult grader. Practice problems look nothing like exam questions. I did all the practice but still failed the exams. Lectures are okay but very all over the place and a bit unorganized.

Lectures are walls of text, and seem randomly thought of. No clear structure, as she doesn't use the textbook. Tests are extremely difficult and the problems don't properly reflect what was taught in class/was on the study guides. Do no take.

The professor is decent at lecturing; she hand-writes everything and notes are available afterwards. But she's extremely strict on grading and problems are very arbitrary. She'll take more points off for a small mistake than give partial credit for. This was her first semester teaching at GT so she assumed we already knew a lot of prior stuff.

The class was especially challenging because she doesn't use the textbook at all and arbitrarily decides what she will teach. She expects homeworks are written like an English class and was inflexible and even rude given a personal situation I approached her with. The class itself is challenging, but she makes it impossible.

Please listen to the other reviews and do not take this class. This professor is far and beyond the worst in the math department. The test averages were both below a D and they are not curved. There is no way to know where you stand in the class until after grades are released when she will curve the final grades.

A very tough grader. Exams can be lengthy for the amount of time given and exams take up to a month to be graded. If the class failed a certain question, she won't curve the exam. The average on exam 1 and 2 were bellow the passing average (D). Quiz and assignments fairly easy. Doesn't follow a text book as well and no TAs made this class harder.

Never used the textbook and the class is taught from arbitrary material. Does not follow the normal Math 3012 curriculum and instead comes up with her own ideas and topics to be taught. Only information provided are her lecture notes in which no outside sources are any help.

1212K, online TB, flipped classroom, informative with engaging lectures. Make sure to watch the prep videos before each lecture. TB reading is supplemental, best for getting a visual of the big ideas for kinetics, acid-base, and electrochemistry units. Final exam has 4 sub-sections, which can replace your performance on the first 3 exams if better!

I really liked chemistry with Dr. Evans. He was accessible outside of class and had interesting lectures. His class requires lots of work before each lecture, but this does encourage mastery of content. His tests can be challenging, however, he does have a good grade improvement policy with the final exam that many students take advantage of.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Evans is an entertaining lecturer but doing well in the class is tough. About 22.5% of the course grade comes from lab and another 22.5% comes from homework, which are both very easy to get full credit for. However, the midterms and final are extremely unfair in comparison and he does not curve grades (but there is grade replacement on the final).
Best of the chem 1211 lecturers

Horrible teacher who makes the final exam almost inpossible with many trick questions. Doesnt test my knowledge of chemistry even, just uses stupid weird units or confusing wording. Hes very obnoxious and has a huge ego. Super unhelpful in office hours. I worked MY ASS OFF for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The test are nothing like the homework or classwork. Even though the test may have easy problems on them  if you don't study the examples he go over fast then you wont get a 100. He writes small and ugly so if you can't see so good then i wouldn't take him.

His lectures are boring and not at all necessary if you have a good recitation TA. However, if you do the practice homework his tests don't usually have too much unexpected stuff. The quizzes are insanely easy since you can use a calculator. He doesn't assign much homework for a grade either. Not an insanely hard class but it's easy to bomb a test.

He would start problems and then halfway through them realize he didn't know how to solve them. His lectures were long and frustrating. Many of his directions were not clear and he would skip from topic to topic during lecture.  My TA was the only bearable part of this class, and I ended up going to her office hours for help instead of him.

Evans can be rough around the edges, and a lot of students give him a hard time. He saved me on more than one occasion, though, and I really respect him for that. One day I overslept and missed an exam for his class, but he let me take it the next day. I ended with an 89.3% but he gave me an A in the class because I did well on the final.
Straight forward. Do the homework
Evans is a very straight forward, nice professor. Do the homework problems and you will do fine on the test. It wasn't an easy class, but much easier than calc 2.

You could probably read the book and do problems on your own and do fine in the class. Evans teaches straight from the book. Sometimes he stops the class to read directly from the textbook. The professor is literally the textbook.

Evans is a great teacher who understands the student perspective. He doesn't spend time going over proofs or showing off, he's very clear and concise in lecture and stays enthusiastic the whole semester. All of the homework is optional, but he tests you on questions from it. Read the book and and do all the homework problems and you can make an A.

If you show initiative and show that you want to exceed in his class, he will go out of his way to help you. I highly recommend taking him. HW is not mandatory and the test and quizzes were manageable. You can easily make a B in his class. I did grade replacement and went from a D last semester to a B , both with prior experience.

Tests were reasonable and based on what we learned in class. Can be a bit confrontational if you ask him something that he already covered in class, so if you have a good TA it might be better to take your questions to recitation. His handwriting is kind of hard to read so you might have to sit close to the front.

He was very easy to understand, his lectures were very dry but very easy to understand and follow. Tests were straight-forward: no curve balls, no sudden "we didn't cover this in class" moments. If you do the homework (it's not mandatory, but do at least some. Trust me, some word problems...). He was always nice to me when i came to office hours.

May seem intimidating on the first day, but he's pretty nice and funny. Homework is not mandatory, but test questions are very similar to the homework. You rarely use a calculator, but he lets you use a unit circle on every test.
Great calc professor! Probably one of the best I've had. As long as you do work you'll get a good grade

Not a bad professor, but could have explained some things better.  Lectures straight from textbook examples. Tests are not bad, but there is usually one advanced/difficult question per test. RARELY lets you use a calculator on assessments, so be aware of that!
Final exam was straight from the tests he gave throughout the semester.

Dr Evans is a straightfoward, Georgia Tech professor, not easy, not impossible if you are willing to put in the time. Difficult to get off on the right foot if you have never had calc before, or have taken a break since high school, but the secret is in doing at least 75% of the homework and past tests, which are avaliable online.

This guy is a good calc professor.  He is straight-forward and will teach the material in a smooth, organized manner.  Practice tests are online, and all are from previous years.  They are very helpful. Tests are simple if u study the correct homework problems and previous exams.  My second time taking it, but he was MUCH easier than Tudorascu.
Hard class! No curve at all...I had a B heading into the final...got a C on the final...got a C in the class. I would not recomming taking Evans.

I had an A in calc 1 in high school... Repeated it with evans for a D.  No calculators, no formula sheets, tests much more difficult than homework, tests long, hard, graded hard, learned material - but didnt get the grade i deserved, studied intensely and still got D. No Curve. HARD CLASS.

Very dry sense of humor, but a good professor. If you pay attention in lecture and do the assigned homework you will have no problem. Tests are relatively easy...but he can drop a couple bombs every here and there.
Material is moderately hard. Tests are strait off practice testes
Final exam reflects tests from the semester. Good TA will contribute to your grade being higher.
LONG TEST, HARD TO FINISH IN TIME ALLOWED. DRY SENSE OF HUMOR IF YOU COULD CALL NEVER SMILING FUNNY.
Great teacher.  Funny to boot

Dude's pretty good. We had 6 tests and dropped one.  His first 2 were moderately hard,next 2 were extremely easy and last 2 were really hard.  If you plan well for the tests, you'll have a good grade.
nice guy, actually speaks english. Tests are very reasonable and final consists entirely of old test questions most of which have the same numbers! Class average will likely be 3.0 or better.
probably one of easiest calc teachers here
This guy cant teach well at all.

Not a good teacher at all. I thought I had worst professors, but she definitely is the worst one ever. She shows her prewritten Matlab codes as examples, but doesn't fully understand the Matlab functions itself. Clearly, it looks like someone else wrote them. I don't think she knows how to code or teach. Don't know why she's teaching at all.

I heard from my friends that she was good, but honestly after taking this class last spring 2018, I didnt learn anything from her. Shes rude outside of class and thinks shes all that. She likes to talk about how smart she is during class and skims over the slides. We need a textbook, not her informative slides.
A dull class. She's too self involved with herself. Talks too much about her life outside of the classroom and not the material in class.
Lots of proofs rather than application of methods. He also doesn't arrive to class on time and he's skipped class before. Would not take again.
he is tough but learned a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Theodorou focused heavily on the derivations of formulas rather than their applications. Take detailed notes on derivations in class because 75% of exam content is deriving formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can tell he really loves teaching this course and is super understanding. Take him if you have the chance!

professor fan is absolutely amazing. one of the kindest professors i've ever had. he is so responsive to emails/questions and gives great feedback. makes the content extremely digestible and easy to learn. he also grades very generously, and i would 1000% definitely take another class with him if i could. also, there's not many assignments & exams!

Insanely good professor. Very patient, kind, and inspiring. He goes out of his way to assist students, e.g., responding to emails at 2AM. He structures the class clearly, creating a seamless, positive learning environment. Choose your group partners carefully, as projects are divided into several submissions. He wants students to LEARN efficiently.

Dr Fan is very dedicated to making the Bus Analytics Practicum a great experience for students and companies. The course is very well organized with checkpoints built in to ensure success. His accent is a little tricky, but he records lectures so you can review and see the transcript. Very generous grader who always provides valuable feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a kind guy. He is always willing to help. I love the way the course is structured, with short weekly quizzes and open note exams. There are checkpoints for the group project, so it's hard to get behind. His lectures are insightful and he always thoroughly answers questions, even if it is hard to interact over Zoom. Cannot go wrong with him!

Decent amount of homework but not anything above the standard for a GT chem class, is a very good lecturer, goes into details, goes through examples, draws things out but occasionally goes off topic and gets behind. Nice guy who is accessible out of class. Does in class questions to encourage attendance.

He's kind but his lectures are genuinely a whirlwind. He loves chemistry so I feel like he goes on tangents and the things we learn in class are NOTHING like the exam. The TAs and lab TAs also lowkey have no idea what they're doing. I think CHEM1211 is just a dumpster fire no matter what.

His teaching style is ok but the lecture content is easier than the exams which makes the class difficult. It is a point system so exams do not count as much and he allows the final to replace past midterm grades.

I took him for 1211 and I have him for 1212 at the moment of writing. He's a good dude, funny guy with an obsession with Ke$ha (yes the singer). However, the tests are a little difficult and he likes to test if you actually understand why you are doing the things you are doing and not just doing them. Overall, good prof if you rly apply yourself.

he was just ok. a lot of his classes got off topic and js ended up being confusing since they're also fast paced, but he had extra credit which was nice. the tests also felt a lot harder than the practice, but the grade replacement at the end was a W

honestly your grade will depend entirely on you so don't procrastinate. lots of homework and free points. iclicker questions in class counts so just go to lecture even if you're not going to pay attention. he was funny and nice and always super cheerful so that helped. exams will get you if you don't study. thermodynamics absolutely destroyed me
Dr. Evans truly cares for his students and their struggles. He is very approachable and accessible; definitely go to office hours consistently and establish a relationship early on.

He is very passionate about the class material and seems to genuinely enjoy teaching. He sometimes brought fun demonstrations which were engaging and I think he's pretty easy to understand. The flipped classroom dynamic at the end of the year did not help though.

I think the way the class was graded makes it easy to succeed (grade replacement on the final + labs and homework are a large portion) and tests were pretty fair. I thought Evans was a pretty good lecturer at the beginning of the semester, but by the end I completely tuned him out and only went for iClickers

Evans is clearly a passionate professor and makes lectures interesting and engaging. However, exams are so much more difficult than the practice exams provided. The lab portion of this class felt like such a waste of time. The final exam grade replacement saved me. Ended with an 89.2 and got a B :( But it was a good class! DONT PROCRASTINATE.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, engaging lectures, funny guy, and active on Ed Discussion to answer questions. Attending lecture is highly recommended for participation points and learning the content in general. I personally thought tests were a bit hard, but for the most part are representative of what is on practice tests and on the homework.

I have two main issues with this class. First, the practice exam questions are nothing like the exam questions. I would be getting 90s on my practice exams just to get a 60-70 on the real exam. Second, labs take too long, and the weekly lab reports are too much work. DO NOT take this class with another lab class! I did and you can see the result.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Moves through lectures very quickly, but is very accessible and helpful during office hours, tests are pretty fair, and he makes jokes during class. Overall, a pretty easy A.

He cannot teach, and his tests are almost nothing like the practice problems that we do in the textbook, homework, and class. There was literally a test that covered a topic that was neither in the textbook, nor on the lecture slides, and the only way to know the answer was if you want to the Plus Session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For context i got a 98% so this isnt cope. But i cant stand evans as a prof. Stupid flipped class structure forces you to self-teach. then in-class iclickers to track attendance. worthless to attend class. will not take feedback, intentionally designs tests to trip people up. easy grading structure makes class easy but this guy is a bad professor.

you will spend a great deal of your time working on labs that make about 20% of your grade. these labs don't sync up with class content and will feel like a significant waste of your time. his lectures are okay but he rambles. he has iclicker questions for class participation, but he often reveals the answers. final has grade replacement.

Dr. Evans made no effort to coordinate labs with the timeline of the course content, having us apply concepts and formulae we had no exposure to. Combining this with unclear lab grading criteria made lab way more of a headache than it should have been. 90% of my chemistry effort was lab, which shouldn't be the case for a supplementary component.

very nice guy and its apparent he loves chem, but talks in circles about nothing. BS questions on the exams bc they know you dont know the answer. a lot of material to digest if you've never seen it before take someone else if you can, but its not the end of the world.

Let's be clear, I already had credit for this course going in. I wanted to refresh my memory in prepertaion for organic chem. This was one of the lowest quality classes you can take here, next to computer science. I have yet to see incompetence at this scale, and I work with the general public. If you have credit from chemistry, move along.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For most of all the lectures he spends half the time rambling about things we don't need to know or things we only need to know if taking classes like orgo. He goes through the in-class problems expecting us to know how to do half the steps already.

Dr. Evans seems kind and is ready to help students. However the content we learn in class and that is on the assigned homework is SO MUCH easier than the tests. The tests are insanely difficult that it feels rigged, especially the final. Don't expect a grade bump either and no extra credit in the test category.

He is constantly losing his train of thought in class and getting things wrong, which confuses everyone else. Ruined my ability to like chemistry. Three exams that are sort of fair, but then an exhausting, outlandish final. Save your GPA, as he ruined mine. He's knowledgeable, but an awful teacher, and isn't empathetic.

It is unfortunate that this is the best professor for gen chem at ga tech. He is an amazing lecturer and really makes concepts digestible but his exams are extremely difficult and NOTHING like the practice exams. No matter how much time i put into the class my grades barley reflected it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Evans is a terrific professor. He is very passionate about chemistry and clearly wants to see his students succeed. I thought his analogies for explaining things were helpful and memorable. His tests are hard, but fair (and very doable if you watch the pre-lecture videos and do HW).
The tests are HARD but Dr. Evans is a nice professor and is very helpful in office hours. I wish the tests weren't so different from the homework and in class questions.

Terrible professor, 25% comes from homework. He teaches the concepts basically, then uses difficult applications on tests that haven't been seen before. Rude and unprofessional. Refused to accommodate disability accommodations.
He's super chill and the lectures are engaging. He's lowk a lil weird sometimes icl but it makes the class engaging and lowk fun. Take him ‼️‼️
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is a good lecturer and knows what he is talking about. The tests are very unlike the practice exams, however, and time is an issue. He is very active on Ed Discussion which is nice, but you never know what to expect on his exams other than the fact that they are very difficult.

I only had him as a course coordinator, so I cannot comment on his picturing abilities. I can comment on the assessments he creates for the classes he coordinated. Each of the tests he has created are poorly thought out and seem like they take him about twenty minutes to make. Spelling errors and common and embarrassing for someone in his position.

Honestly, I got my A right on the cut. Not a bad prof, but enjoys the material so much that it gets confusing a LOT of times with his "analogies". Love the grade improvement plan policy though. Beware of FRQs in 1212k. You CANNOT slack in this course AT ALL!!!!!

Solid chem professor, although he does go on tangents sometimes and makes analogies that sometimes we don't understand. Nonetheless, he's passionate about what he does and it shows in his lectures. Exams were mostly fair. Bucket points for prep-quizzes, in-class questions, and homeworks.

Dr. Evans is a decent lecturer, and it's easy enough to keep up in class if you watch the videos beforehand. Class is a completely flipped format, so in person classes focus on solving problems. Attendance taken through iClicker questions, tests have had typos/errors that threw me off on the rest of the exam. Exams are usually harder than expected.

Evans has a clear passion for chemistry and wants students to do their best/succeed. 3 midterms w/grade replacement final. Bucket points = weekly homework, prep quizzes, point solutions. Last unit = flipped format - video lectures before class and questions during class. Lecture = week behind the labs - get a later lab to get early lab advice

He explains concepts pretty well and his lectures are relatively entertaining. I will say though, the exams are not great. 75 points are from multiple choice with no partial credit and usually each question is weighted pretty heavily (5 points each) so your exam grade can plummet just with a few questions missed.

Dr. Evans is super knowledgeable about what he teaches, but his tests are difficult and lectures are often fast-paced. He is very approachable outside of class and makes learning fun during lectures. Going to lecture is the best way to be successful, as he goes through example problems and shows the solutions.

While I can't comment on his abilities as a lecturer, he is an awful exam writer. Questions on the exams go for up to 5 points (even multiple choice) with no partial credit and there have been typos on the last 2 exams that have costed time from the confusion. Is it too much effort to read over the exams before handing them out?

One of the worst course coordinators I've had. On our second exam, he made multiple mistakes with the exam format, one of which cost me 7 pts  which he did not give back, because there were "too many exams to go through." An educator who doesn't take the time t to support his students and rectify HIS OWN MISTAKES should find a new profession.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Personally I loved Evans as a chem teacher. He is definitely better for those coming in with a chemistry background. Loved his humor and how much he cares about chemistry!

DO NOT TAKE EVANS!!! Stay far away from him and his class. His lectures are not even helpful for exams and he made the content A LOT harder than it really was. He seems like a nice guy but he is not good at his job. The exams test things not covered in lecture or in the textbook. If you care about your GPA, don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans will outline several ways for you to succeed in this class if you ask. There are daily textbook readings, but he has his own prerecorded videos for each lecture that you can use instead if you prefer. The grade replacement policy for each section of the final is generous, though the final is about as difficult as the midterms. Funny guy!

you have to work really hard aside the lecture to understand the material. Exams are fairly harsh, but his grade substitution policy can save you in the final IF you put in the work, cuz the final was still not really that easy. He deffo knows what he is doing, but for this class, u need to rlly use all side resources available (eg. chem help desk)

he's a great guy but ngl the exams ARE very tough -- i took chem through dual enrollment in high school and the exams were still hard for me mind you. however, he is very accessible and the grading/way it's balanced is very fair (imo). you j gotta keep up with the work

Dr. Evans is an excellent professor to have for a beginner course in Chemistry. He loves the science and it shows in his lectures. However, you can't just glide through his class. It takes a lot of studying outside of the classroom to pass the exams, simply because the tests themselves are a bit more difficult than the material in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a professor who clearly explains exam concepts, this isn't the one. For an intro course, his teaching quality is disappointing. Success depends heavily on good lab mates and a helpful TA since his lectures often lack clarity. He rants off-topic, and key topics like nomenclature weren't even on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His lectures are enjoyable and easy to understand! All the tests felt fair if a little short on time. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but part of your daily work grade is answering questions in class so if you never show up it will affect your grade. He's a really nice guy and I felt like I learned a lot in his class.

Dr. Evans is the best professor in the Chemistry department. While he is known to have difficult exams, he is extremely fair in every course he teaches and offers several ways for students to pass his classes. While most people probably won't get an A, you will walk away with a better grasp on the content he teaches than from any other professor.

Dr. Evans is amazing. He explains concepts in a way that just make chemistry so much easier to understand. He uses lecture slides, but annotates them as he goes to make concepts even more clear. He is very understanding and easily accessible outside of class. I would suggest doing the textbook readings, it will make your life easier!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take if pre-med; topics incude way more mcat topics compared to other lectures and super trivial to get a B. Harder to get an A compared to most courses (for me). Great for folks who 'just need to pass the class.' Nice guy, would recommend for anyone who has to take chem 2312

Dr. Evans is greatand I would reccommend taking him for orgo 2 if you have the chance. He pretty much guarantees that you will get at least a B if you do the bare minimum with his specifications grading stuff. The tests can be hard, but if you work for it they arent that bad and an A is definitely doable. Much easier than others for orgo 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would advise against taking Evans for Orgo 2 if you want an A. You have a guaranteed B, but an A is near impossible. His tests are hard, and he doesn't offer any grade forgiveness (CIOS or replacement). You learn mainly through his Youtube videos. His lectures are just examples, very fast, and difficult to follow. Also, he uses a class Discord???

His grading scheme is great, and it basically guarantees you a B in the class. However, getting an A is nearly impossible. Even after putting in tons of effort, it is really hard to earn an A because the tests are very hard. Also, his lectures are pretty unhelpful because he really only goes through example problems- he doesn't teach the concepts.

While his class does offer a lenient system for falling back for a B, the assignments for that option and exams are pretty hard once you fall behind. And falling behind is pretty easy, since he only goes over examples and harder concepts in class; he mostly expects us to learn through videos assigned. A LOT of self-studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were detailed, however he went off on tangents a lot trying to make analogies that didn't really help most of the time, so I would just get confused. He also isn't super helpful for resources; when I asked for extra help with concepts he told me to watch crash course. Had very rude comment over mic in an exam cussing out a student

Mevans is great for orgo 2. the spec grading essentially guarantees you can get a B, but getting an A is a lot more work. He teaches off of videos that only cover the relevant material (no textbook reading needed). Super accessible via discord (late night, weekends, etc) and easy to ask questions to. Best orgo / genchem prof, no competition.

Took the course with the specifications grading system. If you don't know, that means that your grade comes from the maximum of [weekly quizzes] OR [exams, hw]. It sounds pointless and horrible at first, but the weekly quizzes are very representative of exam questions and helped a lot. By the end of the semester I thought it was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Personally, I love him. I'm in 1212 right now and miss his lectures so much. I find him relatable and funny, and his lectures are really engaging. Some people will say he's kinda mean, and I could understand but his outburst unfortunately made me laugh because people do ask stupid questions sometimes. team mevans

Evans has a funny personality, and his style of teaching is really helpful art helping the content get stuck in your head. The reason the review is a 4 and not a 5 is one instance where he screamed at a student during the midterm on the loud mic.

Besides that, he clearly has a passion for the content, and is willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Evans makes a lot of questionable jokes, is weird, and lectures are boring. In fact, he had a breakdown during class and called some person an idiot. He also admitted to making his tests harder than other professors. However, I would take his class again because unfortunately, he may be the best 1211K professor.

Best professor out of all CHEM 1211k professors! Chem is not an easy subject, but the way he takes his time annotating each slide and providing in-class questions makes it a lot more manageable. You can definitely tell he understands chem and knows how to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans gives very engaging lectures. The grading criteria is clearly laid out in the syllabus, and there are several opportunities for grade improvement during the semester. I made appts to meet with Dr. Evans before exams, and he always answered my questions throughly. Very enthusiastic. Read the textbook. Make crib sheets. Do practice problems

Dr. Evans is extremely passionate about the content and explains concepts in a clear, elementary manner. But, lectures often do not even begin to cover the complexities of the material, so make sure to read the textbook and do the homework. Exams can be tricky but crib sheets are a life saver. I was able to put in minimal effort and get an A.

Attendance not mandatory, but in order to get daily work points you have to sign into PointSolutions and answer questions at random points throughout the lecture (you can get the code/answers from your friend if you can't come) Good lecturer, just confusing content to me. If I studied harder I could've gotten a B, but was not instructor's fault.
He tends to go on many tangents during the lectures. Exam questions are usually nothing similar to the practice tests. No opportunity for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's okay. I can tell he is very passionate about chemistry. He tends to go on tangents and talks about the bare minimum in lectures. Get ready to go to office hours/ form study groups cause you basically learn everything yourself. The only reason why I would retake him is because he's basically the only good teacher in the chemistry department.

You can clearly tell that Dr. Evans loves chemistry! He does go off on tangents sometimes, but I feel like that's related to his passion for the course. Unfortunately, he asks very tricks questions on tests and makes so it's difficult to prepare for exams.
Makes class expectations very clear. He does a great job explaining lectures and is very passionate about what he is teaching. I would definitely take him again!

Dr. Evans made learning chemistry very enjoyable and understandable. There is a lot of content to cover in this course and he does a good job at getting through all of it. Sometimes his lectures contain a lot of "fluff" material so it can be overwhelming, but he is really helpful during his office hours if you have specific questions.

I have Evans for CHEM 1211k, and I would highly recommend to take him. He presented chemical concepts in an understandable way and clearly was passionate about his teaching. He makes classes enjoyable, and the other assignments are simple and go well with the course content.

Dr. Evans does not care much for the Student's grades. Our exam averages would go as low as 35%, which is just unfair to the students who are working hard for their grades. He cares about the content but not about how well his students are actually picking it up/how fair the exams are of a reflection on our knowledge.

Mevans was an amazing CHEM 2312 LS professor. I think he gets a bad rep because orgo 2 is hard, regardless of how good your professor is. The class is A LOT of work, and there is so much content to learn. Mevans makes learning orgo very, very achievable. His grading scheme also made it very easy for you to do well, as long as you put in effort.

Dr. Evans taught Orgo 1 during a summer session. His flipped classroom model worked, even though Organic Chemistry was a tough pill to swallow. But hey, I put in the hours and passed. You know the drill: it's about drive... put in the work... but remember to ask questions IMMEDIATELY after a confusing lecture! Office hours also helped me a lot!

The "flipped classroom" model of this course makes it extremely difficult to succeed in this course. Tests are much harder than the practice/ are worded unclearly. Outside of class, Dr. Evans is very approachable and seems like a super nice guy, but its hard to succeed in his class unless you put in 200% effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Evans knows what he is talking about and does a good job teaching orgo 2. This class will take a lot of effort (lecture videos and homework are time consuming), and tests are difficult. However that is to be expected with the difficult material. Funny guy and lectures are engaging. I love his grading style as well, lots of room for redemption.

Dr. Evans is a great professor and truely cares about his students. He is always making good jokes and makes class fun. He's also really good at helping you understand topics you are confused about and is always accessible. The class for 1212 is a flipped class where you take the notes from videos and the textbook and then come in and do questions.

It's orgo2 so it kind of is what it is, but getting a B in the class is pretty trivial. There are 10 quizzes which if you pass all of you get a B and you get three attempts, but getting an A is a lot of work. He obviously loves orgo so he somtimes makes esoteric test questions which are confusing, but he is available over discord and office hours.

Orgo 2 is going to be hard no matter what. I thought he taught the class okay, good to watch his videos and lectures. He has specifications grading, where he has one grade that is points based (541+ pts = A, 481+ = B) and another grade based on pass/fail quizzes(pass all 10 and you get B, good fallback). Whichever grade is higher, you earn.

Dr. Evans is extremely knowledgable in the field of chemistry. However, his lectures can be a bit confusing as he uses advanced terminology. Dr. Evans also has a tendency to enjoy tricky questions (compare Shepler's grades to Evans's). Although I enjoy his personality this man may single handedly prevent me from being able to attend medical school.

Spring 2023, Dr. Evans did a flipped-model classroom. This required more time reading the textbook and watching his lecture videos which was brutal. This class is conceptually not the worst but definitely harder that 1211K. He is not a bad prof, but his exams are low-key unfair. He likes to have select all that apply questions have only one answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Evans does his absolute best to make a hard course bearable. He is very understanding of his students and tries to give everyone the best opportunities to succeed.

I loved Dr. Evans. Super kind and understanding if you tell him about any difficulties and will try finding ways to help you out as much as possible. He made orgo 2 such a fun course and his prelecture videos helped a lot. Ik I'll definitely use those when I review for the MCAT. Grading system is amazing.

Evans is definitely a challenging professor. However, you can tell that he really loves the class and he works hard to make it interesting and interactive for his students. The class had a flipped classroom model so you do have to stay on top of the material outside of class, but overall I would say that Evans is a great professor.

Exam 2 average was a 35%. All the material is expected to be learned outside of class, and lectures are useless. There are too many videos for each lecture, and each video takes forever because he predraws the structures so you have to pause every few seconds... at first I was optimistic about this class but it quickly became a nightmare.

I enjoyed this course and it made for a fairly smooth transition into college. The courseload can seem a bit overwhelming but it follows a regular schedule and expectations are outlined clearly from day 1. By far the most accessible professor I've had yet, he's always available for help on discord and piazza.

Didn't have him as my professor but he handles everything for the course. He is accessible but the exams are ridiculously difficult. They are nothing like the practice exams and he doesn't really explain the distribution of the material on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Let me tell you that the grade replacement for the final was the holy grail of this class. His lectures are pretty thorough so as long as you have a deep and thorough understanding of the content, you'll be fine on the tests. Labs were very laborious since they include a pre-lab, notebook pages, and a post-lab so I'd just be prepared for that.

Dr. Evans is a great professor in comparison to other professors grading this course. He is VERY accessible outside of class, however when asking for assistance he gives very cocky responses. You really have to understand material and know how to apply it to succeed in this course. If you took AP Chemistry before, this course is that times 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Do yourself a favor and take his course (1211k and 1212k) because he sets the pace, makes the tests, and runs the course. Not to mention fabulous note taker! He uses an ipad to allow himself to engage with students, has clear handwriting, color coded notes, before slides and annotated slides always posted.

Super easygoing about accommodations.

Dr. Evans is an overall great professor. Clear explanations, answers questions without judgement, provides exam/regular practice problems in lectures, and very accessible for questions. Exams are very difficult, but he's happy to give feedback/review. Extensive rubrics & lifesaving grade replacement policies. Studying & overpreparing is critical!

Dr. Evans is a great professor! This class moves kinda fast, but its definitely managable. His lectures are great and you can tell he is truly passionate about this subject, which makes it much easier to learn. Make sure to learn the concepts, and not memorize facts because the tests are much more application based than just knowing what was taught

This class is one that moves very quickly. Dr. Evans uses a model of teaching where you are expected to have already looked over the material that is being covered in class that day, which makes the workload for this class a large one. However, if you keep up with the material, it is not difficult to do well in this class.

Dr. Evans was very encouraging and supportive of his students, but he often went on tangents and skipped through a lot of the problems. He would start it, but not fill in many of middle steps. I have very shallow understanding of orgo as he dismissed more complicated steps as something we would learn later. There is a lot of independent learning.

Professor Evans is really caring and supportive of his students. He makes himself very approachable and available and wants his students to succeed and enjoy chemistry. However, he is too smart for his own good because he sometimes does not explain things very well or goes off on a tangent about modern chemistry. He is caring but confusing.

Honestly would not really recommend. He is hard to contact, there is a lot of homework, and the class is harder than it really needs to be. The grading scheme for the class is forgiving, but that's really needed for the way most things are graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom, practice problems in class were essential to study for the exams. The exams always had stuff more advanced than what we did in class or on the HW. Everyone did poorly on the exams, but the semester-long project was a grade saver, and it was graded leniently. Very enthusiastic in class, and he really loves chemistry.

I loved Professor Evan's teaching style; please note that it is a *flipped classroom*. If you do not watch the videos and just go to lecture, you will fail. I missed a chunk of videos in the middle and it brought my grade down significantly. If you are not willing to watch the videos don't take the class.

This class was considerably complex and very fast paced, however doing well is still possible by putting in the work and being organized with deadlines. Get benzo-coins early so as not to struggle later. Lectures were sometimes cut and restarted on the next day due to time limits. Preparing the class and using the resources available is a must!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CHEM 1211K with Professor Evans was an interesting course which although well paced and interesting, required a considerable amount of effort to succeed in it. Between prep-quizzes, homework, lecture and lab be prepared for a considerable time investment. However by putting in the work and using the resources students have, doing well is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Labs for 1211k are a real pain but 1212k labs are much shorter and the reports are usually just filling out a table or two until the full reports towards the end of semester. His online lectures are a lifesaver for tests. He has a strong mastery of chemistry and loves to help students. BEWARE Prelab quizzes are absolute torture and take so long.

Overall the class is manageable but the exams are hard and Dr. Evans doesn't provide much feedback and isn't responsive to feedback from students. His lectures can be entertaining, but he doesn't work through the majority of the math is problems and wasn't willing to despite numerous students asking him to. You'll have to teach yourself a lot.

Dr Evans assigned homework and test material that was way beyond the needs of the course (Survey of Organic Chemistry) and refused to curve the extremely difficult tests even though every class average was in the 60s. Surprisingly was a lot more forgiving when grading written work though. Easily accessible through the class discord.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is for 1315 since it isn't listed. Literally came up with organic chemistry concepts we haven't seen before on the tests. Homeworks are long and tedious but tests are even worse since they don't mirror anything we learn in class. I have cried a total of 7 times this semester because of him.

He seems to have no regard for his students' wellbeing in and outside of his class. His grade distribution with lab and lecture is actually pretty fair and the grade replacement on the final is nice but his tests are absurdly hard and frequently did not line up with what was emphasized in lecture. I only did well because I took AP Chem in hs

Have him for chem 1315. This class is supposed to be a survey class but it's harder than actual orgo 1. He gets so caught up on exceptions and always tests you on it. He makes the practice exams incredibly easy but the actual exam might as well be written in Chinese. Its almost like he purposefully wants to trip students up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This guy is evil. Straight up. Survey of Orgo 1315 isn't listed on here but by god does he make it so much harder than it needs to be. Like I wonder if he likes seeing students suffer. The average score on the last test was a 66 and he flat out refused to curve score. The only way to do the homework properly is to go to office hours and ask the TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher who makes the final exam almost impossible with many trick questions. Doesnt test my knowledge of chemistry even, just uses stupid weird units or confusing wording. Hes very obnoxious and has a huge ego. Super unhelpful in office hours. I worked MY butt OFF for this class

Dr. Evans is not the worst professor you will have at Tech, but he is far from the best. While he truly understands the concepts he is teaching, he gets off track, and is distracted often by simulations that will not matter in the long run. His test are tough, so read the text book. It's passable, this might be the first F or D on a test you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not care about students. Not invested at all in 1310. Its not that hard to do well in his lab, but he interacted minimally with students and was fairly obstinate.

Dr. Evans is a very helpful professor. He is clear and helpful in his lectures. The material can be difficult and the exams are hard if you don't know the content but there are tons of opportunities for practice. He is always active on discord and piazza to answer your questions. Half your grade is hw and lab, and final can replace all midterms.

Dr. Evans is very accessible because he has multiple office hour times and is active on discord to answer questions you may have. The exams are very difficult however and its easy to miss questions if you are not careful or dont understand a concept well enough to apply it. Still, Dr. Evans tries his best to help and is pleasant to chat with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You get what you put in with this class its difficult for an intro course, but the grade distribution is fair (half of it was easy to get daily points and lab, not to mention grade replacement). Evans is a fun lecturer, ridiculously easy to get in contact with, and has pretty helpful Youtube videos too! Makes it less stressful :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things
