reviews.comment: His tests are very easy to lose points on and the questions are extremely specific, you have to really know the concepts to understand how to apply them in the way he words the questions on the exams. Definitely a passable class, just takes a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is a great professor and lecturer. He's engaging, incredibly accessible, and is genuinely passionate about the material he teaches. Although he does have his shortcomings, particularly with his tests. I never felt like my knowledge from the textbook and lecture ever transferred to the tests, always leaving me confused on how to even study
Alright at lecture, but his tests are the absolute worst. Tons of tricks and not representative of the course material. Do your homework and labs because they will save you from the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures are alright, but only does the bare minimum GT requires him to do so.
Dr. Evans is usually really excited during lecture, which makes them enjoyable, but you will have to work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Makes things way harder than necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Evans is literally adorable. He goes to great lengths to help students with lab reports and general chem questions. He does a great job of explaining things to a basic level of understanding. The textbook and practice problems are your best friend and I can't stress that enough. The lab is most time-consuming so don't procrastinate on the reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: After reading some of the reviews on him, I was a little scared, but he is actually pretty good! Just do the textbook reading before class and he will go over powerpoint slides in class and answer questions. Pretty good dude. Tests were slightly more difficult than what we learn but homework/ quiz grades make up for it.

He's in charge of the lab sections. really easy to contact; you can email or ask in discord and he'll answer your questions, though sometimes it feels like his explanations are too complex and he teaches things way beyond 1211K. Attendance is mandatory but that's because it's lab. My lab TA was the best, but my friend's is tough, so its a hit or mi
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans handles the lab sections of undergraduate chemistry classes, and he is without a doubt one of the kindest professors here. He's extremely accessible outside of class, either by email or Discord. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!! He will give out answers for lab reports. He genuinely cares about his students' success, and it shows.
I think Dr. Evans is a great teacher, but you do have to work for your grades. The class is mainly from the power points and the only way to do well is to do practice problems.

Doctor Evans does not care about you. Not that you'll meet him in person anyway. The class is taught by a TA as you would expect so the in lab component is fine and can honestly be pretty interesting if the TA is engaging. So what's wrong with Doctor Evans? As stated above he does not care about you. He is unwilling to compromise or help students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a high-level, well-respected professor; but this is the course that he clearly doesn't care about. He's a nice person, but the course's design is ineffective, considering we are mostly learning from the pre-made YouTube videos of ANOTHER PROFESSOR. People who rate him highly for this course are just thankful that they barely got an A.
Tests were extremely hard, the class averages were usual high Fs or low Ds. Was not helpful at all and did not seem to care that his students were failing. If possible avoid taking chem with Evans.

Worst professor I have ever had. Not understanding of anything and writes tests in order to purposefully fail students. Class averages were consistently in the mid 50s to mid 60s range. If you want to have a required general elective be a bad grade on your transcript, take Dr Evans.
The content was ok but his exams never reflect what had learned. They're always so much harder than the practice exams he gave us.

Literally during the pandemic, you were still required to be on campus. I already made arrangements to be off campus since it was not a problem, but he still said, "too bad, you have to come". I had to buy a rushed ticket which cost a ton of money. I can only imagine what the students who went oversees to go home must go through with him.

Dr. Evans lectures do not prepare for his exams as they are much more difficult than any practice exams. He also gives busy work that does not help in understanding the material or preparing for the exams. Chem 1310 is tough but with Dr. Evans its unreasonable. Would highly recommend not taking him for Chem 1310, especially if its online.

Dr. Evans is a really caring professor and is very willing to assist his students. The lectures are mostly working out problems, so most of the learning is done on your own. However, I will say that the exams are excruciatingly hard and have traps intended to trip students up. Overall, Dr. Evans is a great professor but makes very difficult exams.

My main issue with this class is that it is taught with an emphasis on memorization, but the tests are VERY calculation heavy. While lectures do go over calculations, they're not nearly the level of difficulty that the exams are. And, with the online, auto-graded format, there isn't nearly enough partial credit, so questions are often 0 or 5 points

Dr. Evans is not the choice to go with for 1310. His lectures are not very helpful and his exams are nothing like the practice exams or anything he has covered in class. 1310 is difficult in general but it is impossible when this guy makes the tests for every section. My lab grade is almost perfect and I know how to do the work. Exams from Mars.

CHEM 1310 is a relatively difficult class no matter who you have. Evans does an alright job though. His lectures were not that helpful for me, but he is more than willing to work with you outside of class. The exams, from what I've experienced, are harder than the practice, but just put in the work, and you'll do relatively alright.

Dr. Evans is a solid choice for 1310. His lectures are very informative and he answers any and all questions very enthusiastically. The "lectures" are more problem solving, so they are not necessarily required. The tests have been fairly difficult thus far, but not impossible. As an online class, tests are harder due to open notes. SOLID CHOICE THO

Dr. Evans has handled the transition to online learning better than any other professor I've had. It's clear he loves teaching and that he really cares about the students. He's very approachable and willing to help if you ask for it. His class is a lot of work but if you do it you will learn a lot.

Dr. Evans is a great professor who is approachable and cares for his students. His grading is very lenient, but organic chemistry is hard anyway. He will add many extra credits at the end ( around 40 for us on a 1000 grading curve). However, his lecture is not useful for the exam, but more like materials expand beyond what we need to know.
Go to lecture for the point solutions EC. Do your HW and exam practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2312 with Fahrni was the hardest class I've ever taken at GT. I read the textbook and reviewed lecture slides before class and STILL found exams to be very difficult. Lectures were rushed and it was unclear which mechanisms were needed for exams. I always had to rely on YouTube to teach myself which was very time consuming.

Just take another professor instead. Don't let the "85 for an A" fool you. Very little partial credit on the exam's synthesis and mechanism questions. He writes new homework every semester and they can be absurdly long and difficult, if you want good grades on them you basically have to go to TA office hours. The exams averages hover in the low 60s

Do NOT take Dr. Fahrni. He's really sweet, but lectures like you have a phD in chemistry. Going to class is useless, the textbook is a lot more helpful. Exams are either really easy or really hard. All the HW is accuracy and graded harsh. Exam avg is usually a 65-70. 85-100 is an A, but it's still hard to get even w an exam and HW drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo 2 is a difficult class. For Dr. Fahrni, an 85 is an A and 72 is a B; extra points on exams + lowest exam of 4 dropped. Some topics covered in lecture are not mentioned in the textbook, but everything is recorded. Multiple last-minute review sessions and Dr. Fahrni answers questions, explains his thought process, and is kind and understanding!

I understand this is a difficult course, but Fahrni made it 100x harder than it had to be. I learned mostly through the textbook and Youtube. He assigns LONG readings, and then he criticizes the textbook. I spent countless hours in office hours because I could never do the homework based on lecture. I only went to lecture for attendance points.

Orgo 2 is expected to be a difficult class; however, Professor Fahrni made it undoubtedly harder. He assigns textbook readings and then teaches the exact opposite in class. When you go up to him to ask a question, he answers in the most roundabout way and does not explain anything. Would not recommend. Left his exams in tears!

Dr. Fahrni explains mechanisms well, but it's challenging when he often disagrees with the textbook. 
The textbook is much easier to understand, and the examples are more applicable to the course than those in his notes. Everything is graded for accuracy, and some topics tested on seem to be niche, based on their coverage in class and the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CHEM 2312 is a hard class in itself. However, it was pretty hard to find stuff to stick too with Dr. Fahrni. He loved to have the students read the textbook but actively disagreed with what the textbook says. There were times where he says this reaction was wrong because he says so. Other than that he's pretty kind and goes on fun tangents.

First: no matter what, 2312 is a difficult class. I read all textbook sections before each class, and Dr. Fahrni still moved at a pace I thought was too fast. About half the homework problems are based off in-class slides, the rest required non-textbook resources. I respect his effort, but I wound up learning most of 2312's material outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clicker questions are 10% of the grade. This class is very easy to do well in if you pay attention and keep up with the material, each test is only on 1-2 topics (5 tests and a final).

He's brilliant and good at explaining things but he moves way too fast. He writes while he speaks and theres no way to process the information or get it all in your notes. He missed 2 weeks of class for a conference and someone else covered lecture. Of course, the average for that exam was several points better than it had been in the past.
Fahrni's tests are either very difficult or very easy. Nice teacher knows what he is talking about but sometimes does not explain intuition well. Need to do a lot of outside referencing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Many people find Dr. Farhni's class to be very hard, but the reality however is that it is very doable. His teaching is exemplary, and he is by far one of the most talented in his field, but he doesn't spoon feed. This course has a lot riding on SELF DISCIPLINE. If you read and take a lot of personal notes and make flashcards, you'll do amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fahrni gives decent lectures with long winded explanations of mechanisms that aren't required. He doesn't do much to bolster chemical intuition, which is required in organic chemistry. He is accessible outside of class and is willing to give points back on tests if you explain your thought process for a wrong answer.

Dr. Fahrni is extremely intelligent and an amazing lecturer. He cares about his students, but makes it clear that the grade is a reflection on the student, not him. Tests typically had a 5 point curve, and the averages were 65-70. Attend every class as there are clickers. Homework is straightforward. Use word for tests as questions are similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: HIs lectures are important to go to, but not very helpful. He focuses a lot on mechanisms, which aren't worth many points on the tests. He manages to make multiple choice questions that are harder than his free response. He does a lot of things to help your grade, but that doesn't do much when each test is too hard for most of the class to pass

By far the best 1311 prof. He is tough and thorough, but he scales and curves a little. The texts are useless, so take REALLY good notes, or find someone who does. With good notes, and a fundamental understanding of the practice tests and HW, you can make at least a B. PS even though lecture seems pointless and above you, GO!

Need general chemistry textbook for reading in this class! Fahrni is a VERY nice guy; however, sometimes he just doesnt get the point across. There are four problem sets (homeworks) and 4 tests of which the top 3 grades are taken. Practice tests tell you what will be on the tests and you basically need to learn it all yourself if you want to do wel
He's the smartest man alive.  His tests are fair and he really teaches his stuff well.  He's always on top of everything.  I know my inorganic really well now because of him.

Compared to the options, he's really not that bad of a professor, he's the best that teaches this course.  Although he can be a bit over my head at times, is tests are fair and you can judge by the practice tests what will be on them.  He gives plenty of examples in class although he can be arrogent

Professor Farvez gives intense lectures. He's very vocal, and his oral skills are through the roof. I've never been so satisfied in such a long, hard semester, but he's honestly the best. I spent a lot of time in one-on-one office hours. Despite the tight deadlines, he encourages hard work with rigid schedules and stiff grading.

Professor Farvez was an extraordinary teacher. He reached above and beyond what should be expected from a professor, and always offered up advice or just a friendly face to talk to whenever his students needed it. Ask him about his youtube channel!
In these trying times, Professor Farvez was honestly a bright spot in a difficult semester. Despite his intimidating accomplishments, he's a humble and nice instructor who truly wants you to succeed.
Professor Farvez really makes you work hark in this class, but you learn so much! One of the best professors and best classes I've had and taken at Tech. Truly lifechanging.
Been a few years since I took his class, but I still think about how great he was to this day.
Not his student, but an old peer of his that's been admiring from afar. Good job bro, keep up the amazing work. You're truly a legend.
After the wild end of the Spring 2020 semester, Professor Farvez was incredibly understanding and made the awkward transition from physical to online lectures seamless. Truly a class act.
Amazing lecturer!
Amazing professor. I don't think I'd take this class with anyone else.
This is one those professors where you know you would talk to again even after completing the course. Attendance was mandatory but his excellent explanations make it mandatory. What a guy
Great person, learned everything I need to know about life from him. Really appreciated guy!
very good. very nice. very yes

I haven't gotten a chance to take any of his real classes yet but I hear he's an overall nice guy. Not too strict and knows Tech students go through a lot so tries to be understanding and lenient with grading. Likes to uplift lectures by sharing memes. Actually not a professor yet but maybe one day.
Take another professor. Readings were way too much, so make sure to study for the exam. Also only graded by a few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i used to like her in the beginning of the semester, but the readings were just way too much. also, she does not put grades in until the end of the semester so you never really know where you stand. she does not like when you use the computer in class for some reason? even if it just means taking notes. however, the lectures were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is really interesting and the professor is the nicest person I've ever met. The one test we had was pretty difficult, but it was mainly memorization. Very reading-heavy, but interesting ones. There was a group project that was pretty easy to do and a final essay/project that was decently designed.

Dr. Farooq is one of those teachers that you simply have to take at GT and she is genuinely one of the kindest and best professors I have ever had. Note to future students though, she does not post grades so make sure to keep in mind the breakdown of grades from the syllabus. Participation is key and can make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Farooq is the nicest woman on Earth. She truly cares for the mental health of her students, so don't be afraid to reach out. She teaches Intro to Social Justice in a unique way by viewing it through multiple lenses like technology or law. I learned so much! Love her.
The most amazing professor ever! I am going to try very hard to take a class with her again. 11/10 would recommend.

Very few professors connect with students the way Dr. Farooq does. She assigns a lot of reading but it's not impossible to keep up with it and most are interesting reads. If you show interest in the class and reach out to her if you're having difficulty, she will help in any way she can. She's incredible and I encourage anyone to take her classes.

Amazing lecturer, maybe not the greatest class for students without an interest in reading and writing, but I loved it! She is incredibly eloquent and smart in everything she has to say. Very funny too, joked and got along with all of the class.

She's a very nice lady and is very clear, a wonderful professor, just I did not click with the class.  It requires a lot of writing and reading.  There is about a novel to read every week and a half.  She encourages in class discussion and is willing to help and is very encouraging.  Her class is for only a few people, but she is a great professor.

Professor Farooq is a very nice woman, her class requires alot of outside reading. Your grade basically consists of your participation and writing. Basically if you can write well this class is for you. She is very enthusiastic about meeting with you to help you out if you need help. I recommend this class.

American culture was actually American lit, have to buy 14!!! books!! presentations,3 absense=lose a letter grade. DONT TAKE!!unless you want to read a novel a week. crazy insane ammount of work with a strict teacher. AVOID!!!!

Dr. Sulejmani is by far the best prof I've ever had. I had her for 2310 and 3410, and her lectures in both were easy to follow. She is super approachable and very funny, and she cares deeply about her students' success. If you need advice in pretty much anything related to BME, go to her office hours!!!

Dr. Sulejmani does at good job at helping you think through problems. Compared to alot of professors at Tech I feel like she actually wants to see students succeed and always makes time for students in office hours and answering questions outside of class. She is very responsive and explains things in detail.
she is a bad teacher and not helpful at all
She is passionate and explains the content very clearly while asking good questions to stimulate our learning. She makes it super easy to understand
Very accessible during office hours. Good at pushing students to do the best they possibly can.
Professor Sulejmani is one of the best professors I've had at Tech. It's clear she cares about her students and wants to see them succeed, even in a tough class.

Dr. Sulejmani is great! Biomechanics is not as bad as people say it is, especially if you have her for PSS. Her PSS mini-lectures and the fact that she would walk through each PSS problem step-by-step helped a lot. She also holds extra office hours during busier weeks which is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best BME professors at Tech. She is very approachable and wants students to enjoy the class. She provides excellent feedback and guides students through the design process extremely well. Definitely the goat.
Dr. Sulejmani is approachable and wants to help, go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I ever had. Insightful feedback, extremely knowledgeable about statistical testing and the FDA evaluation process in general. She was easy to talk to during and after class about classwork or other classes.

Teacher grades quite harshly and very specifically (with group projects). She holds her students to an extremely high standard which isn't good for students who are trying to learn the material thoroughly. It can be very stressful experience when taking any classes with this professor even your best work might not be good enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was unclear what she wanted you to include in your assignments. She loves telling people they are wrong, and she does it with a smile on her face. Her grades did not reflect how much effort and understanding you put in the class.

Dr. Sulejmani is by far the best prof that I have had a tech. She is patient and kind, and incredibly smart. Great balance of problem solving and lectures. As long as you study and put in the work, you will be fine. Biomechanics is a hard class but she made it so much easier. If you ever get the chance to have her for any class, take it.

Dr. Sulejmani is the GOAT. I had her for BME statistics, but she also teaches biomechanics some semesters. She is super understanding, a great communicator, and super accessible outside class. Go to her office hours!

I can't really speak too much on Dr. Siddiqua as I did not really go to her lectures often enough to critique her teaching. What I can say is that she was very difficult to understand and I felt that it was one of the reasons why I did so poorly in this class. I'm not going to put all of the blame on her though, there was also lots of blame on me.

She has an accent but not such a heavy one that you can't understand anything she's saying. Teaches straight from the slides but she has her own notes that helped a lot more than just taking notes from the slides. Will answer questions but her answers can be a little confusing. Lecture before tests is just her reviewing/answering last minute q's.

I can kind of understand what she is trying to explain but she doesn't really explain things in a clear, concise way. I can't really say much though because I only went to lecture the first 2 weeks of class. My studio TA taught well though so I did just fine by only going to studio.
A lot of people say she's bad, but I feel like she's OK. The course is very easy. As long as you attend every class, you should be fine.
Just watch the online lectures of another prof instead. lectures are straight garbage

It was honestly quite hard to understand her during lecture, and the topics oftentimes didn't really make sense from her explanations. The tests are quite difficult, but that is from the course coordinator and not her. Avoid taking if you want clear explanations.

I don't think she's a horrible prof by any means. Her explanations when she's working through problems are clear, but I did end up going to Sal Barone's lectures instead. The exams for 1554 give like no partial credit and are also out of 50 points so if you forget a minus sign say goodbye to 16 points
Dr. Siddiqua is a great professor, she goes through a lot of examples in class and uploads a lot of resources. Tougher class, but she makes sure you understand content before moving on too quickly.

Other reviews have some valid criticisms like the accent but I found that for 1552 the guidelines and expectations for exams are very clear online. Not saying 1552 is an easy course but realistically it is very possible to get an A. No real issues with this professor other than mandatory lecture. Study hard and you'll be fine.

Dr. Siddiqua is very nice. However, she has a strong accent, which made it hard to learn math specifically. Other than that, she was okay as a professor. She always encouraged us to reach out for help and check her extra materials. She is just okay.

Bruh, I gave up listening to her after the first exam. If the lectures weren't mandatory, I would forget what she looked like from never showing up. Thankfully, all the professors share a canvas page and post all their notes, so I used others to help, but tbh just watch YouTube videos. Stay safe y'all ❤️

I took her because she was the only one that fit in my schedule. She was hard to understand because she would talk too fast and low key scream in the mic so it would reverberate throughout the room. I didn't really pay attention in lecture, but if you put in the work outside of class you'll be fine. Put in the workout outside class, you'll be fine.

If you take this professor, be prepared to learn from any other source but her. Her lectures are impossibly difficult to understand. The only saving grace were the online videos on her page made by other professors.

If I'm being honest, if you have no choice but to take this teacher. Good luck. The first few weeks of 1554, I couldn't understand anything she said, and I mean that literally. I was only able to learn thanks to the online videos in the first few weeks until I started lecture hopping to better teachers for more guidance.

Although the source was a bit demanding at the times, I enjoyed the course and the instructor teachings. It is a probabilistic approach to machine learning. Very different from other ML classes I took.
Lectures were fine the slides were a bit confusing though
I had it in my summer term in 2024. Very Knowledgeable professor. Very caring to students.
I enjoyed his lectures in spring 2024. Great teacher.

The negative reviews of this course are grossly inaccurate and unfair. He is an outstanding lecturer with clarity. Homeworks are relatively hard but he prepares the class with his insightful explanations. Prof. Fekri has a high reputation for his other classes such as ECE6605, which I also took.

I don't think this course/professor is anywhere near as bad as some of the reviews here make them out to be. The class was four homeworks (25% each). We had three weeks to do each and they allowed collaboration. It was difficult, but Fekri was upfront about the amount of work required in this class on day 1. He was pretty good at explaining stuff.
He doesn't really spend enough time for the lectures. Many slides and the homeworks are glued from others' and the load is way too heavy.
never take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very bad experience. He is not able to explain concepts well. Homeworks are too harsh.
Cannot explain concepts clearly. Very difficult to understand his slides.
A rubbish course. Very poor teaching skills. Homeworks are heavy and copy from other schools. TAs often have ridiculous requirements for homework before the deadline.

I'm in GA Tech's online master's program. I took this class b/c of weekly office hours held over Blue Jeans in the evenings. Halfway through, almost all of the office hours sessions were cancelled. It took at least 4 weeks to get feedback on homework and tests. Communication was poor and often condescending. Save your money and take another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He spends 10-15 minutes in lecture trying to get a trivial point across, so there is no time for examples in class, just concepts. Homework assignments are effective, but exam averages are pretty low, and exam is much harder than classwork or practice exam. Class is boring, he doesn't do anything to keep our interest in pretty dull material.

I had Prof. Fekri as a recitation professor for 2026, and from what I heard, he was the best recitation professor the semester I took this course.  He moves quickly and is somewhat impatient if you do not remember material , but he will review concepts, and you will learn a lot.  His practice problems also prepare you well for the tests.
Very unclear instructor with unorganized lectures

Also took INTA 4331 (Chinese Politics) with Professor Wang, amazing guy and genuinely is so knowledgeable and friendly. 1110 is larger so it's more test based, but if you attend lectures and especially read the textbook it's completely fine. If it's a more specialized class, there might be essays instead of tests, and he's super accommodating.

Dr. Wang is amazing. He tends to ramble but is very passionate about China politics and government. He has lots of cool stories. The workload is not heavy at all--it's pretty light. Dr. Wang is very easy-going and kind. Show up to class because he takes attendance and keep up with the content. A 10/10 class. Highly recommended.

Don't listen to people who say this guy is bad. I can't imagine a world in which he isn't an amazing professor. Definitely take INTA 1050 if you want an easy A. The only thing you need to do is show up to class and study a little (like a couple hours) before the exam.

Every class was an hour and 15 minutes of lecture, sometimes interesting, sometimes not. Participation - 20%, 3 midterms - 60% and a group project - 20%. Questions on midterms are very specific but exactly like the textbook. Attend lecture for participation but really all you need to know is in the textbook. Funny and interesting guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going to class is pointless. He will yap and go on tangents that are completely irrelevant to the tests. Some questions in the exams were never mentioned either in the lectures or the textbook. If u have connections that have previous exam answers, you're fine, if not, you're cooked. He also says controversial things and gets facts wrong. Funny guy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice and funny teacher. However, the class only had 3 tests. The only other buffers were the attendance which was a small weight, and the optional group presentation extra credit you can do at the end of the semester. Tests follow the textbook chapters VERY closely. Expect to read everything to get an A. Don't rely on lectures only.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was very interesting to listen to and is a silly guy. The class is only graded by three tests and is based off of both lectures and a textbook. Super lecture heavy but not that boring

Professor Wang is one of the funniest & most entertaining professor's I've had, but his class is not easy. He gives slides and textbook pages, but test questions are a toss up between content from each - so you need to read both. That being said, having a good study group makes the class breezy. One big group project with semi-tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor! Just lots of reading and lots of information to take in... What was frustrating was that even if I read the proper chapters and took detailed notes, the test has very specific questions which could easily slip my mind on the test. Other than that, he's a very good professor who cares about his current and previous students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly has so many interesting life stories when dealing with China and the CCP. Quite literally an expert in his field- there were multiple times when he was on the news in the morning, and later I would see him in class. Highly recommend you take any of his classes on the topic of China.

only two tests and group project. the tests he claims are based entirely on the textbook but even having read it and attended all lectures, they are difficult and contain material that felt unfamiliar. loved him as a person! very funny and very nice, but not an overall engaging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you take prof. Wang, you will definitely have to purchase the textbook. He is very test heavy we only had 2 tests and a group project, these 3 things are your only grades. The tests are extremely difficult even if you did read the textbook, studying definitely requires using other resources online in order to even pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang has a great sense of humor and wants his students to succeed. However, I definitely had a difficult time understanding him over BlueJeans lectures, which impacted my test grades. Make sure you pay close attention in lectures to help prepare yourself for the tests. Try to do well on those two tests and one project.

He was really funny and nice but exams were just 50 questions where you regurgitate random facts from the textbook. No critical thinking which is frustrating for some upper level students. Basically, read the textbook in depth and you'll be ok, but it takes forever and you have to memorize everything. Only 3 exams for the grade + participation.
He is just a great guy and makes you look at the world differently

took his class during the summer. You really have to read the textbook if want to do well on the test. More memorization than understanding concepts. Professor is enthusiastic and willing to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wang is an amusing lecturer and he tends to give you all the information you need for the tests. The books are "required" but the lectures are almost enough on their own. You have to show up and participate, but if you do so there shouldn't be that much work outside of class.

I took the Inta intro class, we had 2 textbooks and about 1,000 total pages to read over the semester. It's almost possible to keep up, and not all material is covered in lecture, but he reuses tests from previous years. He rambles off topic in lectures and is difficult to understand at times, but he's kind and funny and easygoing. TA grades work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students. Every time he sees me out of class he checks on me, not just math-wise but just making sure I'm ok. Willing to hold office hours multiple times a week at your leisure. I am honored to be among his first students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sebastian really knows the material and really cares that we also know the material. He wants us to succeed.
The greatest TA Georgia Tech has ever seen.
The best!

Sebastian is the greatest Diff Eq TA on the planet! He made a massive video series to help his students succeed. He explains things so well, that when he is your TA, you will likely skip regular lecture. He hosted a 3 hour review session for all students. He won Georgia Tech TA of the year. He is literal perfection.

Honestly, he is the most caring human being I have ever met. Not just for his class, but he will put you above everything. He will make sure his class doesn't stress you out. That being said, you probably wont learn much in his class. He covers less than half the actual content of the course. But you will learn that half of the content REALLY well.

He is just an amazing guy. He has a big personality that shines through and may come off the wrong way sometimes. He assigns alot of work, but also goes over example problems in lecture, making the homework very 'do-able'.

Such a fun personality. The class content was very scattered, but very interesting subject matter. He was very passionate about what he spoke about. A good bit of homework assignments, but very very flexible with turning them in. Will miss him!

This guy is hilarious. The midterm everyone got a 100 b/c he had the answers show up on the unlimited attempt test lol. He grades based on vibes and is super chill and funny. He may have class outside. I would say he's great to get statistics out of the way idk if id take him for something I actually wanted to learn really well.

Dr. Fedele is such a nice professor, but I can't say I learned much. We had 1 midterm, 1 final, & ~ 10 HW assignments. The professor was VERY caring about the students' wellbeing, but his lectures were disorganized & I didn't learn very much (except about art). If you do the HWs, study the solutions, & show you tried, you'll do well in the class.

With him, I took an advanced course on Fluid Mechanics, and he started with "What is a derivative?"..!!! He went on and explained many complex topics with the same degree of clarity. He really cares about his students and put SO MUCH effort into teaching. The assignments were very helpful too. He even postponed deadlines to help us out!

Fedele is a caring and flexible professor. He's very willing to extend homework due dates and help students. Each homework problem is either sourced directly from lectures or very similar, which is nice. Homework is a completion grade. Lectures don't keep my attention, and he focuses mostly on fundamentals of calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Many days, you will leave class not knowing what you learned during the whole two hour lecture. Lectures highly disorganized. Free flowing lecture from the whiteboard. Will tend to sway away from the concepts to talk about the fundamentals proofs and concepts of calculus. Despite that, professor is nice and hopes for every student to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fedele's lectures are very disorganized. He focused a lot on how to use calculus, but not so much on fluids. If you put forth any effort whatsoever, you'll get an A (everyone got either a 100 or an 80 on the midterms). Since I need to use fluids in other classes, I'm now very behind. He is a nice and funny person, but I didn't learn anything.

tbh i dont know what I was supposed to learn in fluid mechanics. I defeinetly learned new stuff taking fluids with fedele but overall it wasnt much content. He does a good job of explaining stuff and the theory behind it, even if he often repeats lecture content a lot. his lectures are pretty enertaining and he grades nicely
Easy A professor. He does goes of topics some times. Funny. He doesn't check HW. I don't feel like i learned a lot from him. He does curve a lot. Just take him if you need and easy A for your GPA.

You won't really learn anything from Fedele, so if you need 3084 for a future class take someone else. If you just want the A though, then sign up for him immediately because he doesn't check HW, uses the same exams every semester, and curves like crazy at the end of the class. You can put no work into the class and still get a 100. Nice and funny.
Very caring professor. He brought great resources in for the GT1000 class.

Attending his lectures help. They're super clear, & I had a thorough understanding of the material just attending his classes. The assignments do take time, characteristic of any grad course. Super friendly & caring guy, with a sprightly sense of humor. Doing the previous year exams he gives is all the prep I needed to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The goat of Dynamics. By far the best teacher I have had at Georgia Tech. Super clear lectures followed by example driven classes to help you understand the topic. Super friendly guy and answers questions clearly. Love Dr.Ferri.

if ur hearing good things, it's all true. he's really funny and good at making dyn easy for u. his exams seem extremely scary when ur taking them but he is such a lenient grader that if u try to maximize points, you're completely set. offers around 3 full points of extra credit total if you use every opportunity (DO ALL HW QUESTIONS) take ferri!!

He clearly cares about teaching and it makes showing up to lectures rewarding. He clearly prepared his lectures to make them clear and understandable. Homework can be difficult, and unfortunately does not count towards much of the grade. Exams are 90% of class grade but he gives plenty to prepare for them, and they are not unreasonable.

Fantastic professor. Class can be hard, but that is just the nature of a masters level dynamics course. He is super accessible and a great lecturer. The homeworks are really helpful and he includes the final answer to make sure you are on the right track. The tests are very similar to the homework but don't require a ton of actual math.
Great lecturer, I love him so much. I want to be him. Exams are pretty easy if you're doing HW and going to class, there won't really be many curveballs.
Good lecturer that emphasizes the basics. Class is extremely hard though. He is lenient with his grading on the exams.

Dr. Ferri is an incredible professor and lecturer. Instead of using slides, he writes out on the board. This creates for engaging lectures, but does mean that if you miss a lecture you will fall behind. So don't skip class. Dr. Ferri assigns about 5 homework questions each week, and the grading schemes on tests are generous.

Dr. Ferri's GT 1000 class was easily my favorite class of the semester. GT 1000 in general is a very simple class and there's almost no way you can't get an A. Dr. Ferri is very knowledgeable about Mechanical Engineering at GT and you can tell he has a passion for what he does. He's well respected and has been doing this for a while now.

Professor Ferri is amazing. He's a fantastic lecturer and really passionate about the subject. The homeworks can be a decent amount of work, but they are usually closely related to in-class examples which he demonstrates to completion, so they're definitely manageable if you go to lecture. Overall, 10/10.

Took at GTL but his lectures were solid and homework answers were given; he wanted us to show to work to that answer. Tests were 25%, 25%, and 35%, and the 35% final was TOUGH with some material we may not have explicitly seen (only downside to the course)

Dr. Ferri taught def bods for the first time and, while not as good at dynamics, still was overall an effective teacher. The class consists of 2 tests, a final, and weekly homework and is manageable for time and grades. His understanding of the class is probably not the best at GT, but his teaching skills and clarity make up for it.

Prof. Feri was amazing for dynamics. He knew exactly how to structure the curriculum and explained concepts in a simple and clear way. He is a lenient grader and it is very feasible to get an A provided you show up. Tests make up a high percent of your grade so study carefully! Homework is essentially completion.

If you take dynamics in the spring, 100% take it with Ferri.  As other comments have said, it's a hard class but he makes succeeding very reasonable with extra credit and reasonable partial credit on tests.  If you put in the work and go to class, you'll not only do well but end up being super good at dynamics.

Super caring and understanding professor. It's a hard class and he doesn't water it down, but he does the absolute most to try and make sure to get and understand the content. Super awesome class and would def recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I had at tech. Great at explaining and also clearly a good person. Class was the appropriate level of difficulty.
Even though I only had him for a ME specific section of GT1000, you can still tell his brilliance and passion for students and engineering.
One of the best profs at Tech. This was one of my favorite classes at Tech, yet it was also one of the hardest.

Great guy, great professor. Just make sure you never get comfortable because that's when your grade will tank. Be diligent about the homework and studying. Always make sure you do the homework even if you don't know what's going on. They were very lenient on grading homework this semester.

Tough class, but Dr. Ferri made it really enjoyable to learn dynamics.  The guy knows the material like the back of his hand.  Top 3 professors I have had at Tech for sure.  Really awesome guy outside of class.  I've heard he's an important figure in the ME school, as well.

My best teacher in undergrad/grad, hands down.  Very helpful, knowledgeable, and clear in teaching.  Respects students, and students respect him.  However, homeworks take time, and it is not an easy class.  However, he gives you all of the tools you need (as is always helpful during office hrs) to succeed.
Great professor for dynamics, very clear and helpful, and very straightforward lectures. Tests were average difficulty.
Very good professor ... exams are not TOO bad but they are quite lengthy so time is the only issue for that .. but all in all i definitely recommend him
Brilliant man. Good communicator. For GT, light on homework. Makes material interesting. Goes beyond what is required to help you understand the material, even in other classes.
Fenton is a very good, super sweet lector who really cares for his students. Fenton consistently had the highest exam average and the highest final average.
He's a great, caring professor. Yes the class curriculum is standardized and he only lectures for the class, but his impact on your learning is worth waking up for and helped me succeed.

Fenton was awesome. As mentioned, his section had the highest averages scores on midterms and the final. His lecture slideshows are accessible outside of class and the problems are usually representative of what will be on exams. While he sometimes speaks a bit fast, he is understable and very, very caring. Do the work and you'll do great.

Amazing professor. All PHYS2211 classes are the same overseen by the course coordinator but Fenton consistently had the highest averages on midterms and the final. Lectures were a good mix of content and practice problems with a few interesting experiments thrown in. His accent was not bad at all and he made an effort to make sure he was understood
His accent is very hard to understand and he tends to speed through the material. He focuses more on the practice problems than the facts/hard information.

he's a really sweet man who cares a lot about his students. the class is a bit of work, but it's not too bad. we had 6 mini-tests and a final. the problems were very similar to the practice problems, so if you study them, you should be fine. there's homework and take home labs in addition to group problem solving sessions during lab time.

Professor Fenton is an amazing professor. Sometimes he can be a little disorganized or hard to understand, but he has great powerpoints and helpful lectures. I recommend doing the optional textbook reading and practicing for the tests with past test questions. Tests are difficult but have lots of partial credit, so you end up doing okay.
Very good professor and lectures are structured well, as long as you practice before exams you should definitely do well.

It's hard to accurately rate Prof. Fenton by himself - I took him with Prof. Alicea-Munoz as the course coordinator, so everything outside of lectures was her.  As for lectures though, Prof. Fenton was great.  Made class interesting with practical demonstrations of physics concepts and made some decent jokes.  Take him if you can!

Took sync. I personally did not enjoy his lectures. He is disorganized and has a heavy accent. The ppt slides were cluttered and his handwriting was difficult to read. The class itself is structured pretty well though, so it's not so hard (easy labs, weighted tests). Take Dr. Alicea if you can instead; her videos were what I mostly used to study.
He is a very good teacher, but he has a heavy accent so if you struggle with that don't choose him.
super nice but can be a bit scatter brained and disorganized with his lectures. if you have the option between him or Dr. Alicea, I would choose Alicea.
nicest prof known to man, sincere. tests can be hard, but easy A in class since labs are peer graded.

Professor Fenton is the sweetest man on this earth. Words cannot describe how much I love him. Cares so so much about his students and makes his class so fun and makes physics easy. He will never make you feel bad about not understanding and is so gentle with his explanations. He is a blessing to this school. Wish him nothing but the best.
Dr. Fenton is a really nice person and he always made sure to answer everyone's questions.

he's really passionate about physics and it shows, wish I put more effort into his class cause he's a good guy. took him for Physics Modern, which I would recommend since the labs are easy and the tests aren't as hard as they are in Classic.

Professor Fenton is the best choice for Physics 2211... it all comes down to this: his lectures are very helpful (as long as you pay attention, but that's on you, not him), he is always ready to answer any questions you have, and he always explains topics that are pertinent to the class :)

Fenton is a decently good lecturer, but he answers every question asked in his 450 person class, which makes class move slowly. His co-professor, Dr. Alicea, is really good at teaching, so watch her videos to learn in-depth for the tests. If youve already taken AP Physics 1 in high school, this class is the exact same, so its easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is extremely nice and tries to help every student he can. Sometimes he would help too many people and it would take forever to get through the material. The weights for grading was set up to make it easy to get an A or at least boost your grade a lot.

Dr. Fenton is great, he has memes posted in all of his lectures and really focuses on student understanding. He stops lecture to answer questions and is one of the most attentive professors I had. The class itself is set up to be manageable. Definitely go to GPS and collaborate with classmates and be sure to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I cannot stress enough to take this man. The best and most caring professor I've had at Tech. Tests are weighted differently based off how well you do, and labs are peer-graded. He genuinely wants you to do well, and is easily accessible for office hours. He stays at the end of each class for questions. Least painful physics experience @ GT.

Professor Fenton was the best professor I've had at Tech so far. Luckily it was not my first time dealing with a lot of the concepts involved in the course, but he put a new light on them and helped me form a deeper understanding of the material. I would do everything in your power to take him for Physics, you won't regret it!

Dr. Fenton was a great, caring, and conscious professor throughout the semester. Even though our class had 500+ students he made us feel like he knew each one of us and really wanted us to succeed. He was very accessible outside of class and made lectures funny and understandable. Definitely recommend his class if it's your 1st time taking physics.

Dr. Fenton makes physics 1 a very enjoyable course. His lectures are very helpful and definitely enhance learning. On top of that, the memes in his classes are very funny and helped keep me engaged during class. I highly recommend taking his class.

Physics is a hard class with anyone, but Dr. Fenton did a great job of trying to minimize the difficulty. The mini-test system wasn't bad difficulty wise, but it did lead to a ton of work with alternating weeks of lab and tests. Dr. Fenton is great at explaining concepts and is hilarious during lecture. A fantastic choice for Physics 2211.

A truly caring professor. I really love his philosophy around how to teach this course by sticking close to the fundamental principles. He adapted his class to an online format very well during covid. The memes during lecture are great too.

Dr. Fenton does a great job of working through a variety of examples through clickers and answers every question during lecture. I found Dr. Fenton's explanations to be clear and helpful. Overall, he really enjoys teaching Physics and cares about students' understanding and interest in the material. He also shares fun videos related to the topic.

One of my favorite professors so far. He has an accent and messy handwriting that can make understanding a little difficult at times, but he will always clarify what was said/ written if asked. There are so many opportunities to get a good grade in this class and he cares a lot about his students. Great memes too, love this man.

If you have the chance definitely take this class there are tons of opportunities to get an A. Much less work than classical and much easier to do well as well. I also feel like I learned just as much. There is basically no coding either they give you templates and you plug and play.

Flavio is such a gem as a teacher. He truly cares about each and every one of his students. He uses fun examples and tries to make the lectures interesting. He and Dr. Alicea are easily accessible for office hours. Grading is easy, had an exam that had a 101 average this year and as long as you do homework you're set.

He is truly an amazing professor. He cares so much about his students and really makes sure to make lectures engaging and interesting. Tests were very fair. The only thing I would say is that sometimes, it was a bit difficult to follow his writing in an online setting and I wish I was able to have this class in person! Amazing regardless!

Fenton is a great PHYS 2211 professor. He made tests very fair, and they were always what was covered in class. He is very accessible outside of class, and takes the time to answer questions in class. highly recommend :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fenton is the best physics professor out there. He cares so much about his students and even went the extra mile to have review sessions before every physics exam. His office hours were super helpful and before the final, GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS/office hours because he will usually give a breakdown of the types of questions to expect on exams.
Fenton is the GOAT! Even though his class was hard, he was always very accessible and truly wanted us to do well in his class. Going to his office hours helped a ton. Take him if you can

He is honestly one of the kindest, most caring professors at Georgia Tech. He truly wants you to do well and he directly tells you what to expect on tests. He made physics very enjoyable and easy! I 100% recommend him!
He genuinely cares about how students perform and is so patient and understanding during office hours. Great teacher and brings many examples to class to help us learn better.
Great class. Great professor who is very understanding of students. Get him or Greco for 2211 if you can!

Prof. Fenton is a great guy and a good professor. He really cares about his students. Encourages office hours (definitely go). Don't expect his class, or any Modern Physics class, to be easy: homework levels are excessive and the material itself is not always straight-forward. Fenton is also hard to understand at times with his Spanish accent.
Good Teacher, cares about students. Brings a lot of examples to class.

Lectures were very boring, and I ended up just reading the textbook. Homework was sparse (4 total) and was difficult, mainly because the class is difficult. Exams were also difficult, but were take-home with 48 hours to complete (I didn't finish either of the midterms). Takes a very long time to respond on piazza, which is frustrating during exams.
Will curve even if the class average is 90% (not sure why). But easily the easiest A of my life and everybody else in the class.

lectures are not the greatest, but cares a lot about your grade and curved the exam when the average was an 85. also made the final easier because the last exam was hard. very kind and nice and attended lectures for that reason. very passionate about niche topics.

2nd linear - lectures are very proof-heavy (but still interesting), while homeworks and exams are completely application based and don't really have much to do with lectures (this makes it difficult). Very nice guy, but if you are not already good at teaching yourself material and doing abstract applications don't take this professor.
Lectures weren't the greatest but super nice guy. All tests were curved even when the average was like and 85. Took recommendations, good listener.

Dr. Bonetto is not a great lecturer and I almost never attended them for that reason. However, at least for 2552, his tests and quizzes were more than reasonable and the grading was very lenient with frequent extra points. Do not take his class if you expect to learn in lecture. I learned everything from studio and the textbook.

Lectures and notes are hard to follow. Exam was take home with 2 day period to complete, but very difficult. Homework from textbooks did not always align with the exams. Overall, he's a very nice professor and a caring guy but his exams are crazy hard.

Lectures were impossible to understand. Exams were take home (a good thing), but so impossibly difficult and exhausting - most questions were beyond the scope of the textbook and covered incredibly niche topics. He fixed many mistakes during exams without saying what he changed, and he made asking questions uncomfortable. I learned very little.

I took Dr. Bonetto for 3235 and 3236. I felt like I learned a lot from his classes and quite enjoyed them. The graded assignments were quite manageable in both classes, 5 HWs and 3 take home exams. Not the best lecturer ever, but I still went to class and felt like I got something out of it. He's also a very nice guy, overall highly reccomend!

I liked Bonetto because he was a nice guy, and he graded his tests leniently for this class, but I stopped to going to lecture in January because it was pointless. He basically teaches in a stream of consciousness and its impossible to take notes. I learned solely from the textbook and did fine. Don't take him if you expect to need a lot of help.
One of those classes where the exams are WAY harder than the homework and the lectures. Would NOT take again.

Professor Bonetto clearly knew the material being covered in class, but he was not very good at explaining it. I was lucky to have a helpful TA who helped explain more abstract concepts and who taught us the math. If Prof. Bonetto is your only choice, it won't be the end of the world, but try to get into another section.
Be prepared to learn everything on your own. Sometimes, going to his lectures makes it more confusing, but it is risky to skip because he does random attendance polls. Avoid him at all costs.

Every lecture was pure, unadulterated pain that I got nothing out of but couldn't skip because attendance was sometimes recorded. He just read off the powerpoint (not even very clearly, and he interrupted every other sentence by coughing). Luckily the textbook is free online and just for this class. The final was really hard.

Nice guy, but he can't teach for the life of him. Attending lecture is useless, but 5% of the grade was based off attendance, so I went to class to just sit... Never learned anything from lecture, virtually taught everything myself

I had him for 1553. The lectures were e x t r e m e l y boring. He often just reads off the slides and spends too much time explaining things that don't matter. I learned almost entirely from PLUS sessions, my TA, and my friends. Choose someone else if you want to actually learn when you come to class.

Coming to lecture felt useless sometimes. He basically just reads off the slides he posts which are basically just summaries of the online textbook. Additionally, he will solve simple examples that don't really matter in terms of the tests and quizzes. Basically, you're going to learn the content on your own.

He literally just read off the powerpoints during lecture. He is a nice person, but not a very good teacher. I learned everything in recitation. If you read the powerpoints and the online textbook, and do the practice midterms, you'll be fine.

This is an easy class if you find his website and practice ALL the previous exams from that site. The exams range from 2004 to 2018. He gives questions mostly from those exams and even if its outside of them the concept is exactly the same so you can still score a 100. I ended up passing this class with a really high A despite all bad reviews!!!!

Going to class is pointless. Sometimes I felt anxiety about how much time and energy I was wasting by GOING to class rather than skipping. The homework is ridiculous and he assigns way too much for you to have time to learn it and do it properly without chegg. The only lectures worth going to are the ones preceding tests because he gives sample Qs
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He teaches the statistics at a very fundamental level.  His flow is very poor, the homework problems are awful, and you won't learn how to do anything in the lectures.

Homework takes forever and is 20% of grade. A Must have is a Solution Manual. Tests are impossible but everyone fails so the curve is huge. The average is curved to a B so just stay in the middle on test and Ace the homework, should be fine. Your not gonna learn much, unless going elsewhere.

Around 15 hours of HW bi weekly that had no bearing on test material. Tests were hard and full of typos. Lectures were useless, only did ok by seeking help elsewhere. Office hours non existent and contacting prof outside of class was difficult. On top of it all he showed up 5-10 min late nearly ever lecture.

Hard to understand.  He knows his stuff but fails to communicate it appropriately to students.  Lecture attendance was poor because he simply went over proofs, which weren't on tests anyway.  Find yourself a tutor early, it helps a lot.
Just a word of caution if you have him...the final will be IMPOSSIBLE.  so don't even study.
He was no help what-so-ever. His tests were impossible and he was terrible at explaining things

Lectures were boring and useless to the understanding of the subject. He talks way too much about proofs and he stumbles over his own words. His tests weren't too terrible, but the final was ridiculous. The only redeeming thing about having him was the large curve at the end.)

Horrible teacher. If you get him, transfer out of his class. tests on obscure content and has a way of writing the tests that makes them foreign. I think he enjoys failing students. One day he will get whats coming to him

Useless teacher. Lectures are worthless, consisting of him stumbling over proofs and tripping on his words. Tests are like coming up to bat and getting a curve ball, you can be an amazing hitter and still miss. That said, the tests are not impossible, yet grading is harsh. He does provide a curve after he has beaten the life out of people...

Heavy accent..but really isn't terrible. I didn't go to lecture at ALL--everything I learned I learned from recitation. Lecture is a lot of proofing, but the tests aren't. His tests aren't bad (usually) and if they are he realizes it and will curve them accordingly.

It's surprising that he taught many different classes before, but he taught most classes only once. According to my experience with his real analysis class, his lecture is horrible, just keep twisting his tongue. He's not too mean in grading, but I could not learn much from his lecture, I have to read the book and learn by myself.

I rated him before, but it seems to have disappeared. I thought he was a terrible teacher. His accent is rather heavy. He held office hours after class, but he was usually in a hurry to go somewhere. His tests were very hard. He has a big curve at the end, but unfortunately you don't learn much.
It makes it hard. I got my first "c" in his class which I never get in my college life.
Worst teacher i've ever had

He was extremely longwinded but got very little points across. His bi-weekly homeworks had nothing to do with what he taught and took around 20 hours each. The tests were very difficult. He was alway between 5 and 10 minutes late for class.

For some reason, the engineering schools have decided that the way they teach technical writing should be within Dr Fennell's purview. Her approach to this task is flawed and ineffective. The class is all about "reducing the cognitive load" your reader experiences. All I learned was how to talk to a fictional 45-year-old client like they're seven.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am SURE she is a great English professor, but avoid anything engineering related with her at all costs. We spent the entire class dealing with a fake client Julie (165k, Married, 1 kid, MBA, General Anxiety Disorder) and the whole thing make me want to blow my brains out. Too high of a COGNITIVE LOAD!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jill Fennell (Goes by Ursula in lectures) is a great language arts professor, who has recently moved into the jiggler-engineering space. She helps us learn to read and write, which are skills which she assumes we are not able to do upon entering the class.

Gives really good lecturers and actually made Junior Design enjoyable. She did a great job of explaining all deliverable requirements and clearly knew a great deal about rhetorical composition. Also, she's not a tough grader. Would highly recommend her for Junior Design.

Short summer semester: The topic of fantasy was really interesting. There were lots of participation activities and really extensive projects so it was a huge time commitment. It was scary knowing that she doesn't accept late work. However, she gives extensions and is quite a lenient grader despite all the expectations. Great teacher overall!

Dr. Fennell was an excellent teacher. While, there were moments when instructions werent very clear, she was always very easily accessible and helpful when I had questions. She didnt give that much work but assignments were long and extensive. Her class was very interesting and enjoyable and she graded fairly as long as you followed her rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graduate Seminar is insanely easy, just be sure to keep up to date when the AE Seminars are because we didn't have any for the first half of the semester and had to rush to attend enough for the class requirement. Overall meaningless for returning students from undergrad as we've been here and know how to use the library.
Dr. Feigh is a brilliant and caring professor (she was smart enough to marry Dr. German after all). Lots of reading but super interesting class.
need too much work outside of class. Materials in class sometimes can be vague and outdated.

Dr. Feigh is pretty good, she really knows what she's talking about in the field of autonomy and always has examples and stories to back up her very detailed lectures. A lot of the time though, her expectations as to what students should be able to know/do for homeworks and quizzes are too high, though it seems like she's getting better about that.

When teaching to the whole class she was a bit vague and left you in the dark, but if you talked to her individually Dr. Feigh was very helpful. That being said, she also assumed everyone knew more than we actually did and assigned homework without telling us how to do it then didn't go over it too in depth during class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Feigh was generally pretty helpful and understanding. That being said, her labs were usually pretty confusing and they often required a significant investment of time outside of class. Since most a lot of assignments are turned in at the end of class, attendance is absolutely 100% mandatory. Miss one class and you're down to a B.

This professor is great. She definitely knows what she's talking about and is more than willing to help her students out. The class is definitely challening, but as long as you pay attention you should do fine.

Nice guy but very disorganized class. Everything was posted late and he was frequently late to class at 2pm. Slides were just screenshots of the textbook. Sometimes made concepts more confusing than they had to be, but had a good sense of humor and lectures were somewhat enjoyable. Homeworks were very long.

Excellent and kind professor, extremely hard class. The course material is definitely not easy for a freshman. Be ready to read the textbook and spend a long time studying on weekends. But he curves a lot for us, so even though you get a low grade on exams, you still have a high chance of getting an A.

First is a great teacher. Great sense of humor, clear explanations, and friendly. Homework was heavy and tests varied in difficulty, but mostly hard. I took 2 classes with him and would take more. To the posters below: This might be because he had to teach intro physics to you...
The professor was not really helpful but the class was not hard. Attendance optional.
Dude is brutal. I received a zero for being late on a paper. Avoid at all costs . Had to consult the Dean just to avoid an F

workload is very fair, it assesses/challenges your understanding. teaching is awful. youtube was my teacher. He's a PhD student that is only teaching the class bc he has to. Has a good understanding of material, but uses notes from other lecturers, so he is with you trying to understand their notes, wasting a lot of time. Emotionless, boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take someone else, he has little experience as a teacher which isn't really his fault, but he doesn't make an effort to improve. His grading is strict to an unreasonable degree. The max grade in my class was a 90.7%, and half the class dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The secret to getting good grades in his class is to really understand his lectures. He's not much helpful other than that. And his tests/homework are based on lecture material. Otherwise, he's not a very caring professor and doesn't really care about helping out when you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Proof heavy, but probably a good choice if you're CS theory thread or a Math major since you'll be doing a lot of proofs anyway. Textbook for the class was never used other than for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Don't take him. Lectures are not helpful and his tests are not good measurements of your knowledge.

His lectures are not very complete or competent, and the grades received by the class reflect this. Ridiculous curve at the end brought my C to an A, so I suppose that's a plus. Did not learn much, and would not take again.

Fairly nice guy but lectures are all based on his notes and he seems lost when the answer on the board doesn't match the one in his notes. Covers all the material he puts on tests, which is good. Lectures are definitely catered to those who HAVE TAKEN Calculus before, though that may just be a GT thing. Wouldn't recommend but his class is do-able.

Tests and final were nothing like homework and quizzes. Homework was different and much more complex than things gone over in class. After the first test i knew there wasn't much hope for this class, but the course-wide curve bumped up my grade in the mid 60s to a B.

So he is a really nice guy but the test were not like the quizzes nor the homework. He also does not give practice exams. I would do practice exams for other classes but still not do good on his exam.  I spoke with a lot of people in my class and to be blunt, a lot were failing.   Some kids are passing/ have As but I would not take him again.
Gives out graded quizzes/worksheets every Friday which he doesn't include in his syllabus
Prof. Finn is a super sweet and whimsy guy, but his lectures are pretty hard to follow and the content is difficult. He's too good at chem to be teaching undergrad.

Super knowledgeable on ochem to the point where it was detrimental. He felt way over qualified to teach an 1000 course and I didn't learn from his lectures. He's a really nice guy though, super accessible and caring, gave a lot of extra credit.
He is very good at his work but personally I felt he's too smart. It's not a  bad thing but for people with not much recollection of chem, the beginning will be real rough
So enthusiastic about teaching, and very knowledgeable about organic chemistry.

Professor Finn shows respect towards his students and he was very knowledgable about organic chemistry! I will say the class is difficult if you get behind as his slides can be hard to understand. 

He offers office hours and is always available to answering questions. He also offered several extra credit opportunities, which saved my grade!

Professor Finn is clearly very knowledgeable in organic chemistry and wants his students to do well. His lecture slides are sometimes unorganized and hard to follow and the homework feels near impossible to complete without office hours, but he makes sure he is available to answer questions and offers great extra credit opportunities.
Lovely professor, very fair, and absolutely adores Jazz.

I love Dr. Finn so tenderly and listening to his jazz music before class every morning really got me in the mood to learn chemistry. Probably the closest thing this school has to a Nobel Prize winner. His research dates back to the 70s. Caring and funny. Sometimes his lectures can be hard to follow, but he's good at supplementing with readings.

The curves in this class make getting anything but an A very easy. M.G as a person is super cool. His lectures are fine, but he often goes off on tangents about unrelated topics. Tests are 75% problem-solving; if you know how to BS you can likely get fine grades. Be prepared to not know what you are looking at when you open test.

Literally one of the best professors I've had at Tech. So caring and really wants you both to learn and to succeed. Grading scale and extra credit opportunities make it super possible to get an A, and lectures aren't required but I highly recommend showing up -- Dr. Finn is SUCH a cool guy and has some of the best lectures I've ever had at GT.

Great professor, empathetic, and fun to learn from. Any amount of work put in will earn you a B. A lot of work will earn you an A. He is most concerned that the students come out of the class having learned something new. You may be worried about your grade throughout the semester, but his extra credit project can bump you up a letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Finn is an okay professor. He gets confused during lectures, and he tends to make mistakes on the in-class problems. He is a super caring professor, but it can be confusing to follow his train of thought. The class itself isn't super difficult, and there is a lot of room for error. The textbook, which is required, is super helpful!

He doesnt even write his own exams. He left it to Dr. Evans who is horrible. If MG wrote the exams this class would be better. He often went on a tangent and I wasted my time taking notes on useless information

Dr. Finn's lectures were enjoyable to attend, however, they did not go much further past the book reading. To be successful and understand the material fully, you must keep up with the textbook reading and do the practice problems before the test. Whenever there was confusion on the material, he was very open to questions before and after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I went to majority of lectures, but felt as though the slides had gaps of key information. Therefore, I did read the textbook as the primary method of teaching myself the material. That being said, Professor Finn was always open to answering any questions that we had, and I felt as though he did care about the success of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Take him if you can

Professor Finn was okay. I rarely went to lecture (they were recorded and posted online so attendance wasn't mandatory), I found the textbook a lot more clear and helpful. Professor Evans is the one that runs the class as a whole anyways (all intro chem sections), so I didn't feel like the content that Finn covered was completely tracking with him.

I took Finn for CHEM 1211K and he was a fine teacher. Sometimes I felt he would explain the concepts in a weird way, and the textbook was always a little more descriptive. He is always responsive to questions and has good office hours, and with some extra work into the concepts, it should be an easy B or A.

Professor Finn is a great prof!! The class was already tough enough considering that a different prof came up with the exams, and I haven't taken chem since sophomore year of hs, but he really did make chemistry interesting, implementing real-life examples that fascinated me and played some jazz music before lectures, which I always enjoyed.
Accessible, entertaining but doesn't really know what's on exams because he doesn't write the exam.
Gives you all information needed in annotated lectures to pass.
