Lectures are vague and I think it's really hard to understand unless you read the textbook. But you can tell that he really enjoys chemistry and wants his students to learn and retain information for later chem classes, not just memorize and pass the tests. I don't go to lecture anymore though, I only read the textbook and do great on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Finn cares a lot about his students' success. His lectures are tolerable, even at 8:25 AM. Sometimes, he'll get tripped up and display the wrong answer, but he'll always post corrections after class. Going to class every day is the easiest way to get a lot of the participation/daily work points, which is the biggest factor of your grade.

Finn is super nice and wants his students to actually understand the material instead of just memorizing it for the test. The class is difficult and tests are hard, but he tries his best to make it manageable. He lectures while Dr. Evans does the lab portion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: M.G Finn is the absolute best. Orgo is obv a hard class but he really puts effort into helping his students, and gives generous curve for each test. If you grind the hw you can get drop last test and still get an A.

His lectures are a lot, but he posts slides ahead of time. HW is impossible... go to his office hours and TA office hours to get it accomplished. He seems scary in lecture, but is really nice and approachable during office hours. Also, do the extra credit papers.

He's a really caring professor, but the content for this course is just insanely difficult. He provides so many different ways for you to succeed, though. (the extra-credit option and a dropped exam is a life-saver). I definitely recommend using the textbook bc it helps with the basics behind a lot of the stuff discussed in lecture

Finn is a great professor; he can get super excited about the topics and really tries to help you understand stuff if you need help. But the homeworks take forever to do and are a good chunk of your grade. 3 exams, your lowest is dropped which is such a gift. Good extra credit if you need. Loved Finn, but had to spend A LOT of time on this course

Super cool guy, but the class is literally so hard. Homework takes many many hours to do and involves a super deep understanding. Would definitely recommend going to office hours. There's three exams and the final, but one exam gets dropped which is amazing. There's also an extra credit project worth a TON of points, huge grade boost

Easily one of the best profs at tech - Finn is really approachable, and he's always willing to help, both during and outside of office hours. The class isn't easy and homework can be time consuming, but there is a generous extra credit project at the end of the course and the grading is scaled according to the difficult of the midterms

He goes fast in lectures, so it is worth it to do read/skim the textbook before class. His exams/homeworks are a lot of work, often more than is technically required for the course, but Finn takes that into account with different grade cut-offs. I always felt like I had learned something after every class and Finn was very accessible. Great course.

For the head of the chemistry department, Dr. Finn was remarkably chill and caring about his students. He offered a lot of extra credit, scaled grades according to performance, and held a lot of very helpful office hours. His lectures were a bit disorganized, which made it difficult to follow at times. Read the book in advance & it'll go a long way

He might be knowledgeable in chemistry, but he is the worst professor I have ever had. He teaches this class at a PhD level, and it was so hard where chemistry majors who have completed orgo 1/2 could not explain what we were learning. The TAs were so terrible and rude. There is opportunity for extra credit, but it was graded harshly. DONTTAKEFINN.

He truly cares about his students learning the chemistry of real world rather than just memorizing naming-schemes and data. The homeworks and exams are rather difficult, but he generously curves, so if you work hard, you can earn an A. And he offers many add. opportunities to learn (OH, PLUS, TA OH, Recitation, etc) so you master it if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, but class is pretty difficult, especially for survey of organic chem. But if you go to office hours and do the homeworks ahead of time, this class is definitely manageable. Finn is really passionate about what he does, which makes lecture interesting - hands down one of the best profs I've had so far at tech

Dr. Finn really loves chemistry and it definiatly shows in lecture. Sometimes the lectures can be hard to follow and I was left scratching my head after some lectures. However, if you go to his office hours, he is super helpful and gives really good feedback. Tests were pretty tough so make sure to do lots of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is obviously knowledgeable and enthusiastic about chemistry; however, his intelligence actually gets in the way of his teaching. He skips over basic concepts, making it difficult to understand the rest of the chapter. He does provide complete notes which is a plus.

He's very qualified and enthusiastic, but I couldn't help but feel that he made his lectures way too abstract for 1212. He would forget to turn slides and go on a tangent only to tell you that the whole lecture was not going to be on the exam while the stuff he briefed over was. After I stopped going to lectures, my grades rose dramatically.

Very entertaining, but very informational lectures. You learn about extra, practical applications for concepts and you won't even mind -- you might even ENJOY it. Highly recommend. He doesn't emphasize the 'algebra' of chemistry, which WILL be emphasized on the exam, so make sure to review the problems that he sometimes skips.

M.G. Finn--Georgia Tech's best shot at having a nobel prize-winner on staff. A 'B' in this class is effortless...but if you want an 'A', review O.chem relentlessly and expect this class to consume your life. Don't need to memorize anything, but expect to predict reactions you've never seen before on the exam. An ability to bull#### is crucial.

The absolute worst professor I have had so far in my three years at Tech. I took her freshman year in 2017, and on a whim decided to see how much her score had dropped since I took it. Seems like it went up, so I'm just doing my part here to bring fix it lest other students make the same mistake I did. Too much reading, boring lecturer and topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesn't seem to understand that assigning work that necessitates, at times, up to 10-12 hours outside of class in an introductory English class to freshmen who are taking mostly STEM courses should not be standard operating procedure. That said, if you complete the work you will likely get an A. But expect many long nights if you take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Enjoyed her class. No essays but projects (I liked this, but depends on the student). She gives plenty of time to work on projects if you manage your time properly (a month to do a big proj). Organized. Gives you a syllabus of the assignments a month in advance. Yes lots of reading, but skimming is fine - she's looking for an engaging discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Fitz's class was a lot of work, more than I would have expected from a 3 credit hour freshman English course. The projects that are assigned are not crazy difficult, but are extremely time consuming. She gives good feedback, and is not too tough a grade, but be prepared to really work if you take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. The workload is absurd compared to other English courses. Every project and reading is rushed, she has no concept of time when assigning deadlines and the grading is unpredictable. Class attendance is mandatory and the class will consist of a "discussion" of a reading no one had time to complete or reading a project rubric.

Easy class on the topic of Lists. Although the subject itself was lackluster, the 3 projects (2 group projects, 1 self project) took up little time for a good grade. As long as you occasionally say something during discussions, she'll give you a good grade in participation.

DO NOT TAKE THIS WOMEN'S CLASS. I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. SHE DOESNT REALIZE THAT WE ARE NOT ENGLISH MAJORS BUT ENGINEERING MAJORS. SHE DOESNT CARE THAT AN ENGLISH AT A TECH SCHOOL SHOULD BE THE LEAST OF OUR WORRIES BUT ALL SHE CARES ABOUT IS THAT SHE HAS THIS OPPORTUNITY TO TEACH. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I REPEAT DO NOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Fair grader, good discussions, lots of group work. Class was enjoyable. Not much writing at all. The projects were interesting and not too hard. Make sure to speak in class. Overall I had a great experience with Dr. Fitzsimmons. Would recommend.

Dr. Fitz gets a bad rap on this site... but her class really wasn't bad at all. There are three main projects (2 are group). She is very caring and understanding of her students and has very clear criteria for what she wants in projects. The class is usually a discussion and she does a good job of keeping it interesting. Make sure to participate!
Took class on YA Dystopias for 1102 and was probably the biggest mistake I ever made. Insane amount of reading each night and the topic not worth amount of work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's a nice person but her class is probably my least favorite so far mostly because of the crazy amount of reading she requires. her assignments are unnecessarily detailed in the wrong way with tedious requirements. also not to mention you have to use twitter which incredibly annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She assigned projects, readings and book assignments with absurd deadlines. The reading is incredibly time consuming and you need to read it to participate in discussion. Participation grade is huge and you have to talk in class. The class was rushed and there was never a lull in material or an off day. Readings could go from 40 - 130 pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of my least favorite classes. Not only are you supposed to read a million things, but we were required to tweet at least 5 things a week about what we are working on as a part of our participation grade. Very annoying and tedious assignments. Grades very very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr Fitzsimmons is a nice person, but her course for ENGL 1101 was frustrating. There is an obscene amount of reading required for the class. 20-40 pages of outside reading per day required, not including the WOVEN text. Lots of reading. Lots of reading. Lots of forums. The topic, how Millennials age into adulthood, was extraordinarily unremarkable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Marty is awesome. If your not into exploring issues of gender and sexuality do not take their class, but if you don't mind, get ready for some awesome discussion and readings about transgender and other non-conforming bodies in media. Marty is really about you exploring how approach assignments and is therefore a really forgiving marker.I recommend
I would take anything she teaches!11

Marty is by far the best professor I've had at Tech so far! They are not there to make you fail. It is a class built around participation and interest, and I changed my perspective on a lot of things after taking their class. They are challenging the structure and values of academics at Tech, and I hope Tech continues hiring such rad professors!
I loved being in Marty's class. The topic is very specific, but honestly incredibly important. If nothing else, you'll learn how to approach and think critically about queer issues.

Professor Fink truly cares about their students and wants to help everyone succeed. Unlike a lot of classes at Georgia Tech, it is possible to get an A in their class. Just turn in your assignments and come to class and you will be fine.
Florian is just awesome. His class made me love linear algebra so much, and he's such a chill, reasonable person. He understands how to motivate today's students.

Florian is a great professor. Lectures are great, he is great at explaining concepts. Homeworks are very difficult but definitely help learn the material and are graded very leniently. Highly recommend taking his class

This was Dr. Schaefer's first time teaching MATH/CSE 6643. Some of the HWs were very demanding despite having 2 weeks to complete. Grading done by the TAs was very lenient. Went into the class very unprepared so took a lot of extra effort but well worth it as I learned a ton. He is responsive to student feedback and generally brilliant with math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Fletcher is a very engaging lecturer though his slides are a lot of data tables. The slides do not always present the important information from studies, so it is best to attend lecture and listen. There were a few written assignments and a group project, but they were broken up throughout the semester which was nice.

The lectures were interesting because Dr. Fletcher was easygoing and fun. However, be prepared as there are lots of trivial assignments that take a lot of time. The final exam consisted of 159 questions. Overall the class is of good quality, but it took me more time than expected.
Decent lecturer. Lots of assignments. Exams were composed of trivial multiple-choice questions. The final exam consisted of 159 questions. Be prepared as this class takes much time.
My favorite professor I've had at Tech. I was not that interested in personality before taking this class, but he is very engaging and makes even boring topics entertaining.

Though I already enjoyed psychology, his class heightened my interest. He warns students at the beginning of the semester that his tests are difficult he is right. If you study a week in advance and pay attention during lectures, you'll be fine! He is a super nice guy, is easily accessible, and makes class fun!

Dr. Fletcher is an entertaining professor. The class is pretty straightforward if you attend lecture. Study the material covered in lecture, and you will get an A. The final is mostly old exams (he clearly states that he is a lazy test maker). As a psych major, the class was pretty repetitive and didn't delve that deep into personality.

(Take during COVID-19 Spring 2021.) Definitely would not take again. Class taught in flipped format, so we taught ourselves EVERYTHING. Class time used for group projects EVERY WEEK with random groups that often would not work together. Major grades were only midterm and final. Definitely take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fletcher is that one awesome professor that you look forward to seeing. His lectures are entertaining as he is sarcastic and hilarious. He is passionate about psych and that inspired me to like psych even more. His lectures are very easy to follow. Tests can be a bit difficult but if you start studying a week before, you're guaranteed an A
Really enjoyed this class. Attending lectures are super important. There are a lot of assignments but they are not difficult to complete.

Dr. Fletcher is awesome, his lectures are really interesting & entertaining. Students were always so engaged in class and there was a lot of participation which he encouraged. Tests are not bad ad long as you go to class. Take notes on all the examples he gives in class, they're super helpful for studying. Highly recommend.

Amazing professor and class!! It's super lectury and he goes really fast but he makes it interesting. Also definitely go to office hours because even though the tests can be hard I've done well on all of them by going and getting extra help. Lots of papers but really easy grading that help bring up your average if you do bad on tests

Dr. Fletcher clearly loves teaching Psychology. He's young so it is easy for him to relate to students and come up with relevant examples in order to make material more understandable. Tests are hard but there are lots of fluff points. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, will answer any questions. Also, review the midterm, half the final is verbatim from midterm.

Super funny guy, and one of the kindest profs I've had. Go to office hours & be honest, he wants to see you succeed. Lectures are important, and there's a weekly participation grade. Grades are very spread out, so it's easy to recover from any bad marks. Tests can be difficult, definitely focus on making examples, not just studying definitions.

Very relatable. Tests based on textbook but he knows that most people won't read so if you take notes in class you'll be fine, unless he specifically says to read a certain chapter. Weekly assignments as a grade buffer. Make sure to review the midterm for the final. Class not mandatory but he does random graded attendance checks often.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are usually pretty engaging and he really knows what he's talking about. There is usually two or more 10 point assignments a week, there are a lot of buffer points. His tests are pretty challenging, but if you understand the material you can do well. There is also small extra credit assignments throughout the semester.

An amazing lecturer with a sharp wit. Tests are fair and not difficult if you prepare, but may not be as easy as you expect. That being said, there's lots of "fluffy" points, so getting a good grade in this class is not difficult. Grades aside, I left this class with a much greater appreciation for psychology. And I never once got bored in class.
Take this class. I didn't even look at the textbook once. Very easy class with a fun lecture. He gives a lot of extra credit.

Keaton Fletcher is a fantastic lecturer. Classroom discussion is always very interesting and engaging. Attendance is not mandatory per se, but there are in class assignments that are only accessible during lecture which can impact your grade if missed. He offers ample opportunities for grade improvement via extra credit.

(asynchronous class) his lectures and homework do not correlate at all. All he does is read the slides word by word and provides a few examples that probably won't help. Tests are pretty hard, very weirdly worded questions. Homeworks are just way too hard for their weight. lots of assignments.

The homework and tests aren't hard if you pay attention in class and actually try understanding the concepts he makes you apply in assignments. Excel is used for everything and the skills you learn will probably prepare you for excel use is ANY other class. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I wish every prof I had is like him: respectful, knowledgeable, funny.

A really knowledgable professor. I wasn't able to take advantage of his office hours but I still managed to get an A with low B's on both of my exam grades. Just do well on the homeworks, in-class clicker questions, and extra credit which is all manageable. He prints all the slides out and his exams are from the slides basically.
Pretty great professor. His test were pretty tough, but if you knew your material well, then you can succeed! Don't take all the extra credit and points you get from clicker questions for granted.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class itself is on the tougher-side as you learn a lot of information in such a short period of time. However, he really helps you understand the material and leave feeling like you have an IT minor. Overall Florin rocks and he really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed! His office hours are incredibly helpful! he rocks!

Go to class, pay attention, do the clicker questions..... You will pass if you do all of these things. Do not be afraid of a bad score on the first test. I scored a 60% on the first test and because of the grading scheme I was able to end the class with a 96% overall. Definitely  a great teacher to take if you're interested in the subject area.

I like Niculescu more than I care to admit. He is a great guy and super helpful. I thought he was extremely clear.  You really can't do badly in this class unless you just don't try. He covers a lot of info and if you actually care about IT you really can learn a lot.

Take him. He's a very, very good professor and lecturer. His class is so well structured to the point where it's not difficult to get an A, but you still learn the subject material easily. This is one of the best courses taught at Tech, trust me. You don't need the textbooks, just read the slides and you'll be fine. He's extremely helpful and nice.
He's a great professor, very knowledgeable and approachable. Very young, fresh and energetic.
It's a pretty easy class. As long as you understand his lecture notes, you will do well. Just go to class, pay attention (somewhat), and answer the PRS questions and you will do fine!

Flowers is by far my favorite professor at Tech. He doesn't care if you show up, but I always got up early to go to his class because he does an incredible job of teaching and introducing architecture (history and philosophy) to his students and is respected by all faculty and arch kids.

this was the best class ever. attendance wasnt even counted but it was still the only class i was always actually excited about going to. benji turns architecture and art into this deep philosophical class wide discussion and its so awesome and i would take it 100 times if i could

I actually enjoyed coming to class to hear Benji's lectures. He made everything interesting, and really reminded me why I picked my major. There aren't too many assignments, and the tests are all memorization (and based off lectures). He'll make the class as enjoyable as possible, even if it is just about buildings.

Benji is simply the GOAT. He gives the best lectures, and even though they are not mandatory, everyone shows up. The tests are a lot of memorization, but nothing too bad. He will keep you engaged for the whole semester and he has the best stories.

Extremely engaging lectures! The best professor i have had at Tech so far. However the tests and quizzes are 98% based on lectures so just make sure to show up and pay attention. He also says he requires books however i never opened any of them so my recommendation is don't get them if you plan on showing up to class.

Benjy is awesome! His lectures and assignments are a bit "off the wall", but are really interesting and designed to make you think. He really cares about what you learn, not grades, so he tries to do everything he can to make the class not about grades. There was only 3 easy assignments including the final, so make sure to do your best on each one.
Benji Flowers is without a doubt one of the best. He has an ability to make the concepts very easy to understand; he has a great passion for architecture. He wont let you fail

Best best best professor ever!  Although attendance isn't mandatory, I'd definitely recommend attending lectures just because the way he delivers the course materials is very interesting & enjoyable, u'll learn more than just architecture.  He's an easy grader, so long as you memorize what he tells you to study, you'll pass with an A.

Hands down the best professor I had.  Attendance is not mandatory for this class, but Professor Flowers' lectures are definitely worth to attend. Your grade for this class consisted of 3 quiz, 2 test, a digital journal assignment and a final. He drops 1 lowest quiz grade and students are allow to exempt out of the final.
He is the best professor I've ever had. Incredibly passionate and candid about architecture and also just hilarious. He's one of the main reasons I haven't dropped my major yet.

Benji is the best! His lectures are so informative and are super interesting. He will make you think about doors and windows and everyday objects in completely new ways. The class content is always enjoyable and the readings aren't bad at all. 10/10 would recommend.

Benjy is a truly fantastic prof. His lectures are informative, relevant, and interesting. He does not have an attendance policy, but everyone still comes to class because his lectures are so amazing. The projects do not require a lot of time, but they do require a substantial amount of thought.

Entertaining, funny, informative lectures (PPT's only). Be ready to memorize the names, dates, locations, styles, etc. of literally hundreds of buildings/paintings. Essay portions of tests are surprisingly difficult. Beware this class takes up a ton of time. He posts online what to study for the final, but will test you partly on other material.

Amazing professor, its a shame he's retiring this year but if he's bluffing and decides to teach another year, I'm leaving a review so the future students can take him. Lecture was optional but I went to almost every one of them.

I took this course online in Summer 2023. The course was unremarkable, but easy. Tests were fair. Flamming gave pretty dry lectures, but some of the content was interesting. Most are taking this as a Social Science requirement. It is not a bad choice, but I would say only take this class if US history interests you. You will be bored otherwise.

Before talking about the class, I just want to note how caring and respectful of a person Professor Flamming is. At the start of every lecture, he would take a moment to ask how we all are doing and at the end, would inquire about any events or activities he should come to support us the coming week. Class is very very easy, he teaches very well.
Class was very easy.  Grade was based on a couple tests (which were fairy easy) and he gave extra credit.
This class was very interesting and easy. The course is only graded by 3 tests so it is very test heavy. The textbook and lectures were useful and helped me understand the content better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flamming is an amazing professor. His lectures may be a little slow paced so I ended up studying mostly off the textbook. 2 midterms (25 questions, 80 minutes) and a final (25 questions, 4 hours (ik even I didnt believe it). Extremely easy with grading assignments. The first two tests can be found online if you look at papers from the past
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: pretty decent prof, took him over summer and everything was online open note. graded on 3 exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took it online over summer, 2 exams, 1 not cumulative final and 3 assignments. Tests have 25 questions and are heavily based off his lecture slides + textbook pages. It was an online summer class so it was open note. Around 80 minutes for each exam. Prof was very nice and understanding. You definitely will need to read the book and his ppt slides
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class for summer 2023. We were graded on 3 exams. Final not culminative. If you keep the textbook open and watch his lectures it'll be very easy. Questions were basically directly from his notes and the textbook. He posts lots of resources for you to look at and is very understanding. Tests are open for a 3-4 day window and last for 80min
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is an absolute legend. You will have to read a lot but his tests are absolutely easy. His tests are open book and open note. Search up old test and you will have similar/same questions. Assignments are easy and the rubric is perfectly laid out. I would take his class again for sure.

super easy A, nice and understanding, half the tests come from the textbook and you don't know which ones. Super chill and gets excited when people actually come to class. take this if you need SS credit.

Your grade is determined by three midterms, but you're able do well on them if you know the vocab words for each chapter and attend lecture, since 50% of the test questions are from information that he only gives in class. Flamming is a great professor and is passionate about what he teaches. It is very possible to finish this class with an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flamming is an interesting professor & person! He actively attempts to keep students engaged in class through jokes and explanations. Your grade is based on only 3 exams (33.3% of grade & 50 questions each). You will NEED to study for them. As with any non-stem class, your grade completely depends on memorizing the correct topics/facts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just like any other History course, the tests do not represent the content well (only 3 grades). Most of the questions are about specifics, like dates, things the professor said during class, or something unrelated to the topic. If you're going to take 2112, prepare for a memorization game that is not fun. Flamming is quite the character though :D

I attended maybe 2 lectures because of my own disdain for waking up early and history and I paid for it. BUT the few I attended were great, he's incredibly enthusiastic and makes the lectures fun and entertaining. I suffered for not attending the lectures and probably would've thrived if I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would like to take the course again
Solid and caring prof, exams aren't bad at all and lots of resources to help you succeed

Dr. Flamming is an incredible lecturer and a gem of a person. His tests are 50-50 between content from lectures and the textbook. If you pay attention to his lectures (and it'll be hard not to), and read the terms from the study guide, it's an easy A.

Flamming is an amazing professor! In his lectures, he cracks jokes and helps to keep students engaged in class. Your grade is based only on average of 3 exams (final included, all weigh equal), easy, but you still need to study for them. There are extra credit opportunities that add a couple points on top of average. Definitely would retake!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had during my time at Tech so far. Dr. Flamming is an extremely genuine, caring person. Definitely take it if you need the Constitution credit and you can get a seat in his class.

Very friendly guy. Super chill class and can tell he cares. Lectures may be a little boring but an hour+ lecture about history isn't supposed to be a thrill ride. Only negative is your course grade entirely relies on only three exams (includes final). But he does offer extra credit, bumps the test grades a bit, and the tests are very easy. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Flamming is probably one of the easiest professors to take a class with. Take HIST 2112 class with him. since it is hard to not get an A in the class. There are enough resources online like quizlets that you can use to practice the materials. Read through the book, listen to his lectures and collaborate for notes  - they are more than enough!

Dr. D is literally my favorite professor at Tech. He's a passionate historian and a great source of knowledge, but his class is relaxed and enjoyable. He's funny and caring and approachable, and his lectures are on par with the best audiobooks. If you're reading this because you're considering taking his class, please do it!
Great lecturer, easy on his students, very kind, and overall a great guy.
10/10 professor. Will take every class of his that I am able. One of my favorites ever
Professor Flamming is one of my favorite professors I've had at Tech. His lectures are interesting, and he really cares for his students.

Dr. Flamming is an awesome professor. He's very passionate about what he teaches and every lecture is like he's telling one big story about history. Your grade is based off of 3 midterms, but they aren't too bad and are very straight forward. I highly recommend him for anyone who needs to take History.
Very fun class with 3 very straightforward exams. I highly recommend taking Dr. Flamming's course.

The best professor I had at Tech! Class was so much fun, even though the online version consists only of voice over powerpoints. Dr. D gets explains clearly and in great detail the thinkers of the time, providing great historical context. Lectures and assignments are easy and thoughtful. Very attentive when meeting 1-1 and always available.

Took this class online due to the pandemic. Tests are ridiculously easy if you watch the lectures and do the study guide from the textbook. He was super caring and sweet and lectures are long but fun to watch!

Professor Flamming is awesome. His lectures are amazing. They may be really long, but I would still recommend. He talks with detail, drawing on anecdotes from his personal life, and it really brings the history to life. He's pretty accessible and loves to discuss history. The class is also pretty easy, and it isn't hard to get an A in the class.

Professor Flamming is great. Keep up with the readings and you will be golden. He is kind and an interesting lecturer. He does speak pretty slowly but if you take him online just bump up the speed. Took this for the ethics credit and would recommend it 100%
Professor is absolutely amazing! He actually sang a song in class once, super fun and caring. The course is literally rote memorization though, so be careful

Flamming is the bomb! I didn't know I could be so interested in American history, but his lectures are genuinely great, and he speaks about some super interesting stuff in the course. The tests are easy, so as long as you read the textbook terms and watch the lectures you'll be good.

Dr. Flamming is amazing! He really cares about his students and his lectures are super easy to follow. The course is only graded on tests, BUT they are all multiple choice and very easy if you go to lecture and read the book. Great guy and I can not recommend him enough.
He is a great professor! He is the best professor in Georgia Tech.

Best professor I've had so far at Tech. Extremely well-spoken, and moves through topics at a perfect pace. Clearly knows what he is teaching, so everything is just taught perfectly. Not a complaint but he talks slow, so 1.75x speed lectures are great if you are taking the class online with recorded lectures. Tests aren't hard, but I learned a lot.

Dr. Flamming is a true king. His lectures are SO good, and he really cares about his students as human beings. The class is straightforward, and as long as you come to lectures and take good notes there shouldn't be any curveballs. Cried a little bit at his last lecture, not gonna lie. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Flamming is truly one of the best professors at Tech. I took him for Hist 2112 and it was actually enjoyable to learn about US history. He handled the transition from the physical classroom to online learning (COVID) amazingly and really helped us out. 2 tests and final, all MC. Just show up to class and take notes it will be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Flamming is one of the few professors at GT who actually care about the success of his students while wanting them to learn SOMETHING. It is incredibly easy to do well in his class if you just show up, pay attention, and do the textbook terms he gives you.

Such a wonderful professor and person in general. Lectures were fun and inspirational, and you can tell that he cares deeply about his students. He is hilarious and kind, and very uncharacteristic of a GT professor in the way that he wants you to succeed and not feel stressed out. Go to lecture and read chapters before exams, and you'll get an A

Lectures are organized and worth listening to. Grades are just the average of three multiple choice exam scores, and the exams are pretty detailed so you need to read textbook carefully and pay attention to his lectures. Has about 3% of possible extra credit, which makes it easier to get an A.

He is a very respectful professor and loves his students but there are only 3 exams for the whole course. If you don't go to lectures you wont be successful in the class. He gives a few extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester. He is very test and lecture heavy. But he is very sweet and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is not just a great professor but an awesome person as well. He was always asking us how we were doing or what events were going on that weekend. One day he even gave us a huge speech about how people think our generation is lazy but he believes in every single one of us and stay strong through finals. Easy class, great guy, take him.

Flamming is one of the best professors at Tech. His lectures are amazing, his tests are straightforward, and he is a super caring guy. If you have to take history, I would say stick to Flamming. He's the best in the department!!
Best Prof ever!
He's an awesome guy, super nice and funny. His class should be an easy A if you look over words on the study guide he posts and attend lecture.

He was an awesome professor. It was very clear what was going to be on tests. He was very open and fair in terms of going through tests and regrading. Just a top of the notch good guy who cared about his topic matter and the students. Super inspirational. Our last day of class he gave like a mini speech encouraging the class...I shed a few tears

Dr. Flamming is one of the teachers who will always have a place in my heart. His story telling and excellent sketches made the class interesting (history was my least favorite so well done), and he always dressed up sharp!

3 Tests, each 33% of your grade, each test is 50% lecture material and 50% textbook memorization. Textbook notes are easy, lecture notes are from his lectures obviously, and Prof. Flamming is hilarious and engaging so the lectures are worth going to. Amazing teacher for (likely) your last history class.

Prof. Flamming is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is a fantastic storyteller and brings history to life in his lectures. I looked forward to going to his lectures every week. He is also very encouraging and believes in his students. His class is really easy, as your grade is just based on three easy MC tests, but you will learn alot.
Flamming is the best teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Enough Said

Flamming is a passionate and funny professor. He makes lectures interesting and tells funny stories. If you show up to most lectures and pay some level of attention you will do fine. 3 tests, including 1 non cumulative final. 50 MC questions, half from book half from lecture. Study guide includes all terms from book so no need to read whole chapt
Really passionate and caring professor. Tests are really easy.

Flamming is a great guy and terrific storyteller with history. Stays relatively on topic and you'll learn a lot. Tests are multiple choice, half on textbook half on lecture. Only hw is the textbook readings which are long but you can scan for the list of terms he gives you (and review them before test). Very easy test and then gave extra credit.

If you have to take history, definitely take it with Flamming! His lectures were always great and he told so many funny stories throughout the semester. There are only 3 tests but as long as you do the reading and go to each lecture, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Flamming is passionate about history, extremely knowledgeable, entertaining (you'll hear a few great stories), & loves teaching us. He also believes in his students. Three exams are 50% lecture and 50% book (reading isn't that bad, and he gives a list of terms that are fair game). So if you missed APUSH credit, don't fret - this class is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A for American students who have always been studying this same history.  Otherwise, you'll still get an A because it's just memorize the terms.

Great Professor, gives great lectures and a lot of extra credit opportunities to help you do well. Only downside is that the class was only three tests, each a third of your grade, so you have to make sure you do well on them. Favorite professor at Tech so far though, you will do well in his class if you show up to lectures.
If you actually manage to slip into his class, you wont be dissapointed.

Extremely funny and actually made history enjoyable, which allowed me to learn a lot more. Tests were all multiple choice, with half on textbook terms on assigned reading, half on his lectures. Pretty easy, and definitely fun.

Lectures are 50% of the tests while the textbook is the other. The lectures were amazing. I was never a fan of history but he made me actually want to go to lecture. He made everything clear cut and entertaining,  and you could see his enthusiasm for the class. The tests were very clear cut. I'd take this class again if I could.

Best professor I've had at Tech thus far. Definitely going to take another class of his if possible. Very straight-forward; 3 tests each worth 1/3 of grade (50% lecture material & 50% textbook material). Textbook material is all from a study guide too. Lectures are actually interesting- he's pretty funny and actually cares about his students.

Great teacher, really into the subject. Hilarious and an awesome guy. This class should be easy as long as you do it right. He gives a list of textbook study guide words and half of every test is only on those (so if you just read the textbook sections on these you should be fine). Other half of each test is on his lectures. 3 tests each 1/3 grade.
What a legend. The class is easy if you take textbook notes ahead of time. Be sure to attend lecture; the powerpoint slides are useless without his accompanying comments. 10/10 would smang
He is an awesome professor who actually cares about his students, and he makes the class interesting and easy.  He's everything you would want in a professor

Probably the best professor on campus.  Turned what many feel is a boring subject into something really interesting.  Only gives 3 exams so you do need to make sure you at least go through the book to get an A, but doing so should be easy.  You don't have to attend lectures to get an A, but you won't want to miss any of his lectures.

Dr. Flamming is a captivating and hilarious lecturer. I never really understood US history before taking his Post-Reconstruction American History overview, but now I feel like I have a comprehensive understanding of how America got to where it is today. The whole grade is based on 3 multiple choice, 50 question tests.
Great guy - great professor. Makes class interesting and memorable. HIGHLY recommend. But don't skip out on class because he makes lectures worthwhile.

Prof. Flamming is a genuinely hilarious guy.  His lectures are long, but you can't learn anything from just looking at the posted slides. Tests are easy multiple choice, 50% lecture and 50% text. I just read the text and paid some attention in class and I got an A. The 1 project is mild research and 3 easy paragraphs.
Great Professor, fair exams,  interesting material.

loved him. favorite professor at tech so far. I'm a big history fan, but he made every lecture great. funny guy, really knows his stuff. doesnt make it to hard on you, just really loves what hes doing. id recommend anybody take him, you will enjoy the class
Dr. Flamming is an absolutely stellar professor. When one is disappointed when class is cancelled, that means a professor is doing something right.

SO NICE. Loves his students and wants to get to know them so introduce yourself. Such a great contact. Go to class to learn answers to the test. 1/2 test on lecture 1/2 test on book. 3 newspaper article summaries. Gives a study guide which outlines what book questions will be on the test

best teacher i've had at tech.  if you have the opportunity to take this class, do so by all means.  class is focused on the significance of history, so it is not focused on memorizing facts. the class is very interesting and fun, and flamming always includes life lessons in his lectures.
Great professor.  Fair class that is easy to get an A in if you do the work.  A pleasure to be around.  Good sense of humor.
If you ever get the chance, take one of his classes. He is an amazing professor.

PLEASE TAKE THIS GUY! Great teacher, makes history interesting and fun. Funny guy keeps the class awake. Took him over the summer and it was easy A but i also learned alot. Go to class and do the study guides and you'll get an A

Great teacher. I hated history before, but really enjoyed his class. 3 papers, easy to write on old newspaper articles. Tests are half book def'ns, which he gives you ahead of time, and half lecture. funny and intriguing.
Good, easy teacher. Funny too.

He is a good teacher. He gives three research papers to write and they are really easy to get  an A on if you have any kind of writing skills. I would definitely recommend taking him over others. He has 2 test and a final. he drops your lowest grade which is awesome. I enjoyed his class and pulled out an A.

He is a good teacher. He gives three research papers to write and they are really easy to get  an A on if you have any kind of writing skills. I would definitely recommend taking him over others. He has 2 test and a final. he drops your lowest grade which is awesome. I enjoyed his class and pulled out an A.

One of the best teachers at Tech. I normally hate history, but I had to take his class as a requirement, and I ended up taking another one of his classes as a free elective just because I loved his class. Really easy too, and I'll take all the A's I can get here.
He's a very good teacher and a nice guy.
No Comments
No Comments
Great Teacher, funny, open, lot of knowledge
I love her so much shes so cool and so awesome, best professor to start my college career with

Dr. Fontenot was kind and understanding. To get an A, you do the assignments and do 3 A-level ones that are not difficult. You have a helpful peer review. All the assignments you do make your final assignment easy to do. There are group projects. There is a fun presentation of projects later on in the semester. Would definitely recommend her class!

Dr. Fontenot is very caring and wants the best out of her students. She's accommodating to extensions if you ask for them, and she made the class a fun place to learn from classmates. The class itself is easy because you can get a B by doing the major projects and an A with a little more work.

Dr. Fontenot has been my favorite professor so far at GT! She is always accessible and is clearly passionate about her class. Being a bio major (not premed), I absolutely loved the topic she chose for our class, interspecial entanglements. To get an A on projects, a little extra work is required, but it's worth it to have Dr. Fontenot as your prof!

He's a great guy, and class is usually really relaxed and fun. The way he teaches can be slow sometimes but you can just work on homework. Medium amount of homework, not hard, just quite a bit. Attendance is mandatory and grading is very easy. Final was literally optional if your grade was good enough.

Class is fun and you'll learn a lot, as long as you're willing to put in the work and pay attention in class. Homework is fairly time consuming but helps you study for the quizzes. As long as you spend the time on the work, you'll likely get an A.
Amazing professor, great knowledge of material and willing to work with students on related extracurricular interests.

Going to class is really important, but if you miss a class, then he's super understanding and will let you do make-up. Attendance is heavily suggested. Will call on you in class, but not critical of mistakes & genuinely wants you to understand the material. Really funny as well, makes the classes entertaining. Very easy to understand the grading.

This professor was... interesting. She's old, simply put. She speaks in sentence fragments and is slightly senile. Her entire class is graded on the 4 exams and 1 other assignments. As long as you quote word for word what she says in class, you will pass.

Does not use Canvas to enter grades so be ready for the surprise at the end of the semester (even though you can probably gauge). Less than interesting lectures and extremely hard to grasp onto a word uttered.

Attendance not mandatory but you will not pass if you don't go. She tests on EXACTLY what she says in class so I recommend recording the lectures. My biggest struggle with the class is that she provides no rubric or real expectations for the seminars and is such a tough grader on them. Grade is 20% for 4 tests and 20% for a seminar you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During class, write down VERBATIM what she says, then regurgitate it VERBATIM (examples and all) on the test. When you feel like zoning out, don't or you'll miss writing something. Easy grader if you write down her exact words. I underlined things for emphasis on the tests (whatever she rly emphasized in class), i think that helped my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she is clearly very respected in her field and has lots of published works, but she simply should not teach this class anymore. She often mumbles and it is hard to follow her line of reasoning, which makes tests difficult since they are almost word-for-word what she says in lectures, and are each 25% of your final grade. Take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fox gives a one-slide outline per lecture so you have to attend and take notes on EVERYTHING. I recommend using voice memos so you can go back and listen b/c exams go over exactly what she says in class. Took me a while to adjust to her style but overall learned a lot and enjoyed her enthusiasm!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fox treats this class like a graduate-level course. The reading load is insane, but if you show up to every lecture and take note of every single word she says, you can get an A on the tests. She is enthusiastic about the material and encourages respectful discussion. Seems like a sweet woman, but would not take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was not my favorite class, but Dr. Fox was very enthusiastic about the material which made going to class easier. She assigns a lot of reading, but I didn't read any of it since most of it was reviewed in class. It is important to show up to class since she phrases information a certain way which is key to succeeding on her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In-class lectures are really important. Take the chalkboard outline as gospel and make sure you know all of the prongs. Each answer needs to constitute a separate category/classification. Answers should be sufficient; she prefers quality over quantity. Be straightforward and talk in class.
Very unorganized course; no clear grading criteria whatsoever. She never updates grades and rarely returns papers. 75% of grade is based on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: boring and talks irrelvant topics

I lectures are hard to pay attention to, and the information is directly pulled from the textbook. The TA's were remarkably disorganized. 
Textbook is genuinely great and not hard to stay engaged with. 
The best advice I can give for this course is the read the chapters before doing any projects, and if you read them you'll be ok for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Forsyth is clearly very passionate about the subject. However, he has the MOST boring lectures ever. All my learning came from lab and reading the textbook

forsyth... whatever. he's fine. him being good or bad won't affect your grade. the TAs on the other hand sucked this semester. there were 3 that were actually helpful in lab and office hours, the rest were rude af and really not helpful

Okayish professor. Seems to enjoy the content and has passion. The lectures can be a bit dense but videos are posted so it's workable. The TAs drag the rating down; they're a step down from the 2110 TA group, and the four "quizzes" are worth 60% of your grade and tend to have somewhat arcane questions.

Overall ok. His teaching style is not for me. Lectures are dense and sometimes hard to follow. However, he is knowledgeable and does care about the class. Rely on the textbook. There was a lack of communication between professor and TAs at the start but it got better. Homeworks and projects can be difficult so getting started early is key.

The class is hard, trust me. But Prof. Forsyth is the best part of it. So long as you communicate to him when you're struggling and show up during lectures, he'll care about you. That's something not a lot of teachers do. He knows what it's like to be a struggling GT student, and is there for advice when you need it. A gem of a professor who cares.

Ignore prev years. Not sure why they got rid of open-note exams, they were clearly designed to be like this but they decide change that this semester. Too many random stuff to memorize and lectures were a snooze-fest; he would just read off the slides (which had a lot of errors too). Mandatory lab attendance was also annoying. Do better please
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I could not engage with a single lecture he gave as he mumbles quite a bit. I liked the projects in this class and I learned more from those than lecture. My lab TAs were great. I wish quizzes were open internet, like previous semesters. They likely changed it due to LLMs and could maybe allow a cheat sheet. Last project gave 4 pts EC.

Had Forsyth for both 2110 and 2200; he's a good lecturer who clearly knows and cares a lot about the content! He does lecture pretty slow though and it's kind of boring at times. For 2200 I'd definitely recommend reading the textbook as the slides are based directly on it, and it may help fill in any gaps from lecture. Also the TAs were great!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are 60% of the grade, and nothing was released beforehand like in past years. They made the tests more difficult, if not the same. Many heavily weighted questions come from obscure slide mentioned once in the slides. I liked the topics, but the exams feel unreasonable. Use the textbook, not just slides. Terrible tests

I see posts saying the TAs were bad but I always went to my lab TAs OH and they both were great. They stayed after the lab til 8:30 and reviewed HW questions and helped us debugging projects. Maybe I was lucky to get good TAs like that

The class content was nightmare tho, I hope I can secure an A but im not sure... good luck future students lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He was a good lecturer and condensed the textbook chapters pretty well. But a some of the exam questions were a test of niche knowledge. The multiple choice questions are 4 or 5 points (get 2-3 wrong and you get 1.5 points knocked off your entire grade). Multiple choice questions should max be 2 points. A lot of TAs never show up to OH either

I think Professor Forsyth is a great lecturer and his lectures make the dense textbook much easier to understand even if he rambles a little. HOWEVER, the TA team is terrible. They are frankly not good at lab, VERY slow at grading assignments, slow to respond, etc. The students who want to be TAs in edstem probably respond more than the actual TAs.

We are only 4 days away from final exam, yet no information has been posted, no practice material, no topic list, nothing. We don't know our grades as almost nothing is graded on time. ED discussion posts are left unanswered. Overall, this class has been run very poorly this semester, and at this point I'm just glad it will be over in few days.

This class is run by horrible TAs. The tests are pure memorization and are effectively trivia questions. It is clear that the tests were designed based on prior years, when they were open notes. Homeworks and projects are busy work and provide very little learning since TAs refuse to grade homework and projects on time.

Reads off a powerpoint that is filled with errors. Cool. I'll just go to office hours. TAs don't even show up to office hours most of the time. I wait 45 minutes for a TA in queue. TA says idk just read the book. Great. Open notes also got removed so there is lots of memorization of weird information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dan is very knowledgeable but that's about it. This semester's TA team was BAD. Answers on Ed were rude if they ever bothered to answer. Practice material came right before exams with no answers, and a TA set a 6:00AM demo, if he thought that was funny, it wasn't. Projects are long, help is rare, and the course can feel like it sets you up to fail.

He was incredibly difficult as a professor and I found I didn't learn much of anything in class. The lectures were very boring (his attitude didn't help) and the content was infuriating at times. It was very clear that Dan did not particularly care about the structure of his class or how poorly his teaching style meshed with the content.

I found Prof Forsyth's lectures difficult to follow, especially since he would often go off topic. I usually learned the content through attending lab or by doing the homeworks instead. However, he definitely is passionate about the course content and was always trying to come up with ways to provide more hepl and resources for students.

Homework every week plus projects that span 3-4 weeks. Project content not taught until week before due but told to start early. Lectures are a bore, just read the textbook, they cover the exact same thing. Expect to not get help from TAs, you will wait for hours in OH just for them to not be able to answer your question. Not impossible, but hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The workload is insane and help is rare. You will wait 4 hours to get 5 mins of a TA's time on a VERY time consuming and vague project. You will have to do long homeworks every week and forget about fall break - you will be expected to study over it for the test immediately following it. The class is made unnecessarily difficult for little reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Please ignore all the previous good reviews, the course is no longer structured the way it used to be. Projects are now worth 5% each and are extremely time consuming. Quizzes are now worth over half the grade with very little practice material. Professor makes the TAs do everything, and the current TAs are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible work load. You have a project and homework constantly running every week along with quizzes that test knowledge that hasn't even been taught it. He yaps about random history and falls behind in lecture constantly. The TAs do a terrible job also helping prepare for quizzes/answering questions while Dr. Forsyth is completely oblivious.

Update on Course: Quizzes are no longer open notes and are worth 60% of the grade. Labs are manditory and lectures have participation quizzes. Projects are difficult and homeworks are not always simple. Professor is always behind in lecture content, thus you must read the textbook. Many TA's don't understand the content and grading takes weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tells way too many stories during his boring lecture. As a result, he ends up falling behind schedule and having to delay the homework/projects. But the main complaint: TAs are really incompetent. Homeworks/projects aren't clear and have pesky grading criteria, they will fight you for regrade requests, and don't answer any questions on Edstem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of conflicting and incomplete information this semester. Also, took away open notes, making the class more about rote memorization than actually learning anything. Students are left asking for clarifications on Ed Discussion, which often go unanswered for a while. Quiz prep/practice quizzes weren't posted until a few days before the quiz.

Professor Forsyth is a super caring guy whose always available during office hours and always great to chat with. Lectures aren't mandatory and most people learn the material from the labs and end up skipping class, and the grade is heavily homework-based, with lots of quizzes and timed coding assignments instead of exams, would take again

Prof. Forsyth is everything you want in a CS teacher: he communicates clearly, editorializes to make information more comprehensible, and shares even his tacit knowledge throughout his lectures.

CS 2110 was easy to get an A in if you did the homework as timed labs are just homeworks and quizzes just test if you've read your notes once or twice.
Prof. Forsyth has a wealth of knowledge on the topic and his lectures are worth going to.

Dr. Forsyth is one of the most compassionate professors I have had at Georgia Tech thus far. After completely failing the first exam, I set up a meeting with him for advice on how to proceed in the class. Lectures are really interesting, and the new AI model we experimented with was super useful for studying for exams. Overall, great professor!
Good professor. Class really teaches you the intricacies of computers and how they work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Didn't really go to lecture. Read slides and textbook. Nice professor, but 8am classes killed my motivation to go to the class. Exams were open note and were very reasonable.
Really cool professor, super knowledgeable and lectures were in depth. The only problem is they're a little long and boring so you might fall asleep. Assignments are hard but you learn a lot.
Amazing Prof who really knows his stuff, very kind as well. Wish he taught my networking class this semester

I found it a little hard to follow along with his lectures but watching the recorded ones at 2x speed was much easier. Clearly cares a lot about the class and his students, and he's so nice. Grades were clear, open internet exams, no real reason not to get an A. Take him for this class!

Take my grade as a warning for staying on top of the class. I think Prof. Forsyth is a really good lecturer and his passion for the subject definitely shows in lectures. However, do know that this class covers a lot of topics and it's very easy to fall behind. Start projects early and read the textbook and work through the examples to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is easily the best professor I have had. He makes everything so accessible. People get mad because you have to read a lot for the course, but the prof is so passionate and really does teach you a whole ton. I think this was the most useful and interesting course I have taken to date... and would 100% take it again with Dr. Forsyth.
class is annoying, just read the textbook
this guy is an absolute snoozer. the way he presents information is weird. he's passionate about the topic though
Easy exams, difficult projects but very doable to get full points on all of them. Boring lectures but textbook is very good and exams are open internet.

Loved this guy and his lectures. Wish he talked a little faster though, sometimes I would watch the recordings at 2x when I was in a rush. Worth noting that the difficulty of 2110 was way overhyped, but be ready to grind homework a fair amount. Quizzes were easy and low-stress, exam was weighted heavily but not super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Forsyth was very caring, helpful, and engaging! He also respected each student as a responsible adult and allowed everyone to join virtually if they wanted. I appreciated his insightful lectures and in-class demonstrations. :D

I loved Forsyth's class a lot. He is incredibly kind and you can tell he really cares about his students. Very knowledgeable as he has been in the field for a really long time, he has lots of experience with every topic and is super passionate about explaining it. Highly recommend!

Class is alot of work but if you read the textbook and start projects early you should be fine. Tests being open internet is great but I felt it caused there to be a lesser incentive to actually learn the content and more incentive to get good at Ctrl+F through the textbook.
Allows for internet during tests, including the final. The lectures are good.
Extremely knowledgeable lecturer who ran the course very fairly. This class is a lot of work but if you take the time to do all of it it is not hard to get a good grade.

This professor was pretty good, but the class itself was pretty difficult: if you messed up on one or two exams (which were difficult), it could bring you a whole letter grade down. Lots of projects and hw, and exams are difficult whilst being open note. Make sure to read the textbook and go to office hours for help a week in advance. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Forsyth is an incredibly caring, humble, and inspirational professor who you can tell genuinely cares about his students and their well-being. 2200 is a difficult course, but do not hesitate to reach out to him for help and support. His lectures were awesome and having them recorded for review was very helpful as well.

He's a great professor. The class is tough content-wise but the grading scheme is fair and the A is very attainable. He really cares about his students, and the TA's are extremely helpful. The tests are very fair, but the projects are very difficult, especially to debug. Be prepared to WORK for this class.

He's a great lecturer but the course material is hard, especially the projects that take a while and are a pain to debug. Prof is still willing to help you though. However, the best part of this class is TA office hours and lab, where you can get basically all your confusions sorted out because the TAs are absoluted goated.

Lectures are entertaining but do not use the lecture or lab slides as your only notes for tests. Textbook is very dense, but taking detailed notes on it will help a ton with exams. Quality of TAs and lab sections will vary greatly. Projects can be hard to approach and debug, but office hours will usually help considerably.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: He speaks slowly, so I watch the videos sped up or hop in Zoom and do other things while the lecture is going on. Exams are fair and open-note. Overall it's an easy course. You should read the textbook and then watch the lectures as a review. Projects can be tough, but again, nothing is unreasonable. Easy as long as you do the work.

Definitely one of the best professors I've had. Forsyth is extremely knowledgeable, and has clearly seen a thing or two in the CS space. He knows about both the history and current state of class topics, and has many personal experiences which reinforce the topics and demonstrate their real-world applications.

Honestly I enjoy his lectures more than the actual content. He has decades of experience in the field and has a way of explaining things that just makes sense to me. The actual class itself is of moderate-hard difficulty, but it is somewhat standardized across semesters.
great lecturer

While you can definitely tell that Professor Forsyth cares for his students and wants them to succeed, his lectures seemed to be neverending and were very monotonous. This lead me to watch Kantwon's lectures instead of going to class, but I know many people who went to every class and got an A as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures well and down to the point. The class overall is very well organized and predictable.
Lecture is extremely dry and boring but you must attend! Explains things with very little detail, slides are OK to self learn from.
Detailed lectures. Lots of homework and projects to preprare for quizzes.
Cold hearted

Dr. Forsyth is an excellent professor, and I would definitely recommend taking his course. Despite not being particularly interested in 2200, he made the course a very good learning experience. The work load in the course is very heavy with extensive homeworks, projects and exams.
This class was hard, but I thought professor Forsyth was a really great professor. He cares about his students and has a passion for the subject. I recommend taking him for 2200.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are recorded for this class and are really helpful for understanding the material. The slides, homework, and tests are almost completely based off the textbook, which is also helpful. There is a lot of work in the class but it normally follows the lecture material.

I am currently enrolling in CS 2220 at Fall 2022 in Georgia Tech. I have admitted that he is a very good professor with funny & vivid lectures using lecture slides. Moreover, TAs are best to help. This course have a little bit hard understanding on concepts (but it is easier as you take CS 2110). When choosing sections, choose him & enjoy!

Took both CS 2110 and CS 2200 from Professor Forsyth. The material itself is hard for most students, so other than the difficulty itself, the professor is lenient on extending deadlines on projects, gives generous curves when average exam grades are lower than expected.

He maybe not the most engaging lecturer, but really experienced, clearly loves the content and is a great person. CS2110 is a hard class, so mostly giving advices here. Start early to do the homeworks (you save so much stress) and actually do them. Books are easy to read and Labs and TAs are the best thing ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher who is obviously very knowledgeable about the content, and excited to share is knowledge with the class. Difficult content but he teaches it well.

Lectures were pretty nice, though I probably learned more through recitations. Points were explained pretty well and he was responsive to questions. I enjoyed his class and feel like I learned a solid amount.

Professor Forsyth is a great choice for this class. From all the homeworks to the large projects, his class is definitely a lot of work. His exams can be difficult given their format where each question is all or nothing and is worth a lot, but he's a great teacher and is very knowledgeable. You'll come out having learned a lot from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Forsyth enjoys teaching the material, although I personally didn't like this material and found lectures to be bland. Weekly homeworks, roughly biweekly projects, and 3-week exams made this course very time-intensive which I found to be the most annoying part. Textbook was useful for HW and especially during the open note exams.
Dan was a great professor and really knowledgeable about this class and good at explaining topics. This was a hard class but I learned a lot.

Professor Forsyth isn't the greatest lecturer, but he explains the difficult material well and overall is a great choice. Lectures weren't terrible, though I'd recommend supplementing with textbook, because the 2200 book is genuinely one of the good ones. I learned a lot and he was accommodating and fair.

It is easy to see that Dr. Forsyth loves his job. He knows the source material very well and even though much of it is hard to grasp by the nature of the course, he does a goo job explaining it. It is a huge advantage to read the textbook in this class, so I'd definitely recommend buying or renting a physical copy

Clearly enjoyed teaching CS 2110, making lectures more fun than they should've been. The course is difficult, but if you take each homework seriously, the tests will be much easier as everything is open note. I never read the textbook but I've heard it's useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dan is a wonderful man. He clearly cares a lot about the content and that his students learn and understand the material. He gave his personal phone number for if there were any specific questions or class-related emergencies. My only gripe was that his lectures were a little on the bland side sometimes.

He is very kind and understanding, but sadly, quite boring and monotonous as a lecturer. The professor doesn't really make a difference in the course though, as most material can be learned by yourself.

His lectures are really informative but his voice is a little too soothing. Very nice professor, he is understanding and caring. 2200 is a class you have to work for but if you attend the lectures and read the textbook you're pretty much set.

A very caring professor, although his lectures are a bit boring. That's fine thou, because the textbook is very good. You can watch the recorded kishore lectures if you don't like reading. Tests are reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mr. Forsyth is one of the most caring professors I've taken at Tech. He wants you to learn and expects you to work for a good grade, but at the same time if you're struggling or having unexpected issues arise he will do everything he can to help you and make sure you don't get punished for things outside of your control.

Dr. Forsyth's lectures were always solid, and I came away from the course with a great understanding of the material. But where Dr. Forsyth really shines through is how caring for students he was during this unprecedented semester. He was a great communicatior, and he really seemed to take student feedback seriously. Great guy, would 100% recommend

Professor Forsyth is a pretty good professor. He goes through the material outlined in the book, does example questions, and keeps everything very straightforward. I always read the book, but I still think he does a pretty good job explaining things. Tests are straightforward. Would recommend!

The worst lecturer you can imagine; very few people shows up. He also has the audacity of saying that the final is cumulative is nonsense. The previous professor 's finals were not. If it weren't for professor Rama's lecture videos, I would've dropped the class. But since Tech has been unfocused on teaching, this is not surprising.

Most people didn't go to his lectures. He takes a lot of time to fix simple syntax mistakes. The class is very standardized so it doesn't really matter if you go to his specific lecture. Overall I would not recommend you take him, but if you can't get into Kantwon's class, don't stress about it.

Forsyth is a great professor. He cares so much about his students and their performance and gives very clear lectures. He also is extremely willing to make time for his students outside of class and is willing to work with them until they are comfortable. He is a nice person and a great professor and I highly recommend him for CS1371
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't get why Mr. Forsyth receives so much negative feedback here. He is one of the best professors I have ever had at GT. His lectures were very clear, his examples were thoughtful, he was always friendly, accessible and caring towards students. He is also very knowledgeable, having worked with Computer Science for ages.
His lectures really are ramblings and hard to understand sometimes, and sometimes just taught about super tangential topics so that was ass. But the TA's can be a life-saver.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but boring and tedious lectures. Will ask a lot of "everyone should know this" questions when everyone clearly does not know (me included). Lecture is not taught to emphasize the important details of each topic which makes the quizzes really difficult; it's hard to decipher what the important takeaways are.

His first semester teaching this course, which is intro to computer architecture. He often mumbles on in class without writing anything out and it's really hard to follow. He also talks to us as if we already know the basics of computer architecture, even though that's what this class is for. He's pretty condescending, too, when you ask a question.

He was behind the other classes which hurt us during the quizzes and blamed the students for not studying enough.
