He also refused to get a microphone for a large lecture hall (in the instructional center) even after we gave him the link to request a mic. I do not recommend him, as he is a bit arrogant.

Readings assigned for each class but not required. Participation and attendance was a percentage of the grade but as long as you say something each class you'll be fine. Great professor and very understanding of students schedule. The late policy was nice and only 4 assignments for the whole semester. Overall a great and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fong is great! She genuinely cares about her students' well-being and wants them to learn. The class had a lot of readings (about 95% of which I did), but you can definitely do well without reading everything. She is very straightforward in her grading and wants her students to succeed.

I absolutely love Dr. Fong. This class was incredible, had super interesting readings, and was well supplemented by interesting lectures. Dr. Fong knows her stuff, and is hands down the most compassionate, flexible, and understanding prof I've ever had. Very generous late policy. Assignments are fun and not too difficult. 10/10, an absolute joy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I didn't feel like I learned anything in this class; over half of the essentially mandatory lectures were student-led discussions. The grading is pretty easy if you put in the effort. There was a lot of reading that we were supposed to discuss but barely did.

I love her as a person but she gave out sooooo much work for this class it was unnecessary. She always gives you a quiz everyday for the first 10 minutes over what you read. Sometimes I read and still didn't know the answer. The project are very long and irritating how much work it is. This class is a lot of work. a lot. more than some of my stem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Forsthoefel is the greatest. She is so passionate about what she does, she is ALWAYS willing to help, and her class/grading is not too hard. It is a lot of reading and quizzes but it's nothing too bad. She is a prime example of showing that things do not have to be difficult to learn.
She was a great teacher and I'm glad to have had her for English.

Dr. Forsthoefel is the best. If you go in for help, she tells you exactly what you need to do. There is a decent amount of work involved but if you do it then it is not a hard A. She is very passionate about what she teaches but I can honestly say I learned a lot in this class and she made me a better writer!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Forsthoefel is awesome. I learned a lot in her class. Shes pretty hot too.

Dr. Forsthoefel can be very challenging but the way she leads the class and the time she gives you to do the projects and papers really give you a great advantage in organizing yourself and use your time effectively. She is very innovative and creative with the material chosen for the course. I would definitely take her again as my professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment:
I only survived this class because of my AMAZING Studio TA. 

The prof is not great at explaining concepts simply and mostly just reads from notes, and his handwriting is very hard to read. Sometimes he didn't even know answers to questions I asked.

His lectures are super unhelpful. His notes are almost impossible to read, he makes frequent mistakes so the information he gives isn't always reliable. He also doesn't demonstrate much willingness to work with students and refused to give out practice exams. Get acquainted with your studio TA if you want to do well in the class.

Lectures were an unhelpful recap of the pre-lecture videos. I didn't have any issues with his accent. He always spent the first 5-15 minutes of every lecture complaining about how the class did not ask enough questions (in an 8:25am section). He was always falling behind and would catch up on weeks of content the lecture before the exam.

Heavy accent and goes through content super fast during lectures. His notes are also super messy so lectures are pretty useless. 2 exams, a final, and 5 quizzes are basically your whole grade but if you put in the time and learn outside of class (do the worksheets), exams/quizzes aren't too bad and an A is definitely realistic.

He could barely communicate and use words he wanted so he got mad at the class a lot. You cannot read his writing and notes so lectures were pointless. He also makes his section more rigorous than others.

Thick accent, terrible handwriting, and mumbles. Decent guy, but not a good prof. My studio TA CARRIED me through this course. Not a standardized class between sections and his exams/curriculum were miles more difficult than other sections. If you can take anyone else, do it. If you can't, go to studio and watch Sebastian Fernandez's videos.

Take another professor for Diff EQ. His lectures are hard to follow due to a combination of a thick accent and poor teaching style. If you do take his class, go to studio as it's the most effective tool for learning in this class.

Avoid taking him for diff eq if you can. Awful lectures. Exams are VERY difficult compared to other sections (the class average on his exam 2 was failing). The curriculum also feels more rigorous than the other sections, as many niche topics were covered in studio that many of my peers in other sections did not go over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Accent hard to understand. Professor makes tests harder than they need to be. Professor makes quizzes grading scheme unrepresentative of understanding (obscure true-false question worth 5/25 points on quiz over modeling differential equations)
Awful experience. Did not understand lecture at all and his exams were much harder compared to other sections.
He cant communicate well partially because of his thick accent but also he gets frustrated at the class often. Overall a bad experience and I would definitely not take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Looks like he can be a chill guy out of the classroom, but not necessarily the best teacher. Avoid him if you can
DONT TAKE THIS GUY!

I would not recommend taking this instructor. The lectures are essentially just a less effective recap of the pre-class videos, offering little added value. Communication sucks due to a very strong accent and a noticeable lack of flexibility when it comes to supporting students. Overall, it's been more of a challenge than a learning experience.
Nice guy, can't teach for his life. Run

Dr.Fragkos is a nice guy, but he has a ways to go as a lecturer and teacher. He hasn't mastered pacing in his classes yet. If he were working on a detailed problem towards the end of class, saying time was running out, he would start rushing through the problem. His handwriting is also difficult to read. I had to teach myself.

It's just CALCII. I have my qualms because I think that there is an unnecessary amount of work. Fragkos is not a very good lecturer. Hard to understand, not because of his accent, but because he explains new concepts with mathematical terms and theories that we don't understand. His handwriting is also terrible. I ended up going to Ms. G's lectures

Very difficult to understand and his handwriting is even harder to read. I feel like most of the material he covered wasn't helpful for the exams. Lectures were not helpful for any of the exams...much less for the final itself.

Hard to follow lectures at times because of his accent and he was just not the easiest to pay attention to. I learned the most during studio with a TA and on my own through homework. The guided notes from all other professors in this course were also posted to canvas so it was nice to be able to look through different notes.
He has a think accent that makes lectures a bit difficult to hear. He uses guided notes that get uploaded to canvas after so you only need to go to studio.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fun guy, cares a lot about what he teaches. Reading will be heavy and necessary to pass, as well as lecture notes. He won't allow any cell phone/laptop/tablets in class. He comes across abrasive, but he does care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is an old school lecture professor. He assigned four biographies and two textbooks to read over the semester. The reading isn't bad if you keep up with it, but you can't skip a lecture or reading if you want a good grade. He offers four extra credit papers based on the biographies. Do them. Recently, attendance became mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I only took this class because I had to, it was repeat information from high school but more thorough. I spent 20+ hours reading and studying for each test, and there is a lot of content he expects you to know. Attending class and taking notes is necessary. He offers extra credit for each test if you're a few points short of an A, but that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster's enthusiasm for teaching history was clear, although his lectures can be quite a drag sometimes. But show up to class, read the books he assigns and you have an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Always do the extra credit for each unit! You have to read the books anyway for the test and they can make a difference in letter grade. Its not enough to read the material, you have to review the readings, too. If you do really bad but then improve drastically, he'll drop your lowest test. Lectures are boring but try to stay awake and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you have to end up taking his class, start with the essay exam. Don't waste your time with the multiple choice tests. I gave him a negative rating because after seeing him multiple times during office hours asking him for advice throughout the semester on how to improve on tests he still failed me.

Professor Foster's lectures are really boring, monotonous, and sleep-inducing (even front row). He convinced me to take his class during the first week, and it has been my biggest regret since I've came to Tech. If you don't like to read historical books don't take this class. If you didn't like history before this class you will not like it after.

I took his class since I'm in a studio-based major and didn't really want to take anything too rigorous. The class itself is pretty easy, and the professor genuinely wants you to succeed. Do the readings and go to class (though if you miss class you can email him for an audio recording of the lecture) and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved his passion for the subject. It clearly permeated through to me, and hopefully other students as well. Workload is heavy; it includes lots of reading, but if you enjoy history it won't be a chore as the books he chooses are interesting on their own. His final project turned out to be my fav assignment in college so far!

Dr. Foster is a great professor! Lots of reading but very doable. If you read the material properly and understand it (DONT SKIM) then easy A. Tests are essay format and aren't bad at all. Attendance is mandatory with 5 absences being the max, but he is lenient if you have a valid excuse (sickness, etc.). 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can tell he really cares about the topics he teaches, which makes his class enjoyable even if the lectures are large. Attendance is mandatory (can miss 5 days), but that only serves to help you, and reading is a must if you want to pass the class, but if you put in a little effort, you should be very fine.

This class is almost entirely based in the readings and the lectures. The only things that go towards your grade are the tests and the extra credit, so you HAVE to do the assigned reading if you want to pass. Foster offers 2 different versions of the test, a multiple choice version and a essay version, so pick whichever you're most comfortable with

Professor Foster is really passionate about history and about appealing to the interests of his students. Lectures were extremely long and boring, but take detailed notes and do the readings (there are a lot). Also, do the extra credit assignments and he will be very generous with your grade. I got an 87 which he rounded to an A. Would take again.

Excellent professor! Has a passion for the subject and really cares about his students. Assigns a lot of reading so he may not be the best option for someone just looking to satisfy their history requirement. Definitely take the essay version rather than the multiple choice version of the test. It focuses on major ideas rather than minor details.

Very good teacher. Lectures are pertinent to the test. Take notes and do the readings and a light review is all thats needed before each test to get an A. He is very helpful and wants you to succeed. Didn't like history before his class

He's a great teacher. Interested in what he is teaching and getting students to understand. His lectures are wonderful. He focuses on the social and cultural aspects of history which I personally find more interesting. If you're taking the multiple choice tests, just read the textbooks really, really well. Even small, useless details.

Dr. Foster's class was an easy A if you do the readings. The readings, both the textbook and the other books he assigns, are very required in order to do well. Lecture is also crucial, and definitely take notes. If you read the books and go to class you're gonna get a high B or A on the tests. Final isn't cumulative. Would recommend.

His lectures are pretty boring but if you put in the effort to take notes, you'll have to study considerably less. He passes around an attendance sheet, so try to go to class. Also, if you keep up with the reading your life will be much easier. I took everyone's advice and opted for free response tests and did better than friends who took MC.
Lots of reading. Also, lectures are pretty dry, but most of the material is covered in the reading anyway.

I'm in his summer class right now and am having an amazing time. In high school, I used to hate American History because I was bad at it and it wasn't interesting to me. Dr. Foster has completely changed that! I have always been excited to go to class and to listen to his lectures. He is so passionate for the subject and I admire that. Brilliant!
Best teacher in my last semester.

Professor Foster is a sweet and helpful guy. He assigns a lot of reading and makes his tests pretty hard, but he really works with you if you want extra help. When I took the class, he had a policy of dropping your lowest test as long as it was 10 points below your other tests. Also, take the essay format- much easier than the multiple choice.
Tons of reading, extremely boring lectures, recieved a 79.5 in the class and he wouldn't make it a B

I have no interest in history whatsoever, and because of that, i got a D on the first test. But he allows you to take an essay portion,which i strongly recommend(so much easier) and i end up having to study for about 20 hours for each test, but that usually guarantees me an A. very nice guy, but his voice can be monotonous->sleep-inducing.

Do not take if you have a heavy course load. I personally had to spend more time for his class than my more important major classes. He assigns a ridiculous amount of reading. However, if you do it, you ace the exam.

Go to class and read the book. He takes attendance personally, and assigns a TON of reading, but if you keep up with lectures and reading assignments you'll be fine. He gives an option for free response or multiple choice tests; if you've read the chapters the MC are pretty easy. His class is most I've ever learned from a history class before.

Dr. Foster is incredible. While there is a lot of reading, it's easily manageable. He is also the most helpful and accommodating prof I've ever had. And take the free response exams- there easy to get an A on.

A lot of suggested reading but overall attending class is the most important factor. If you pay attention to his lectures and take good notes you should get a grade that reflects your efforts. He is very interesting but can be a tad boring during class.

Summer. Summer is the best time to take this class because it focuses equally on class lectures and assigned readings. There is a lot of reading, but he makes straight-forward tests and there are actually pretty neat essay questions. I took this class over the summer, used internet videos to cover major topics and did very well in the class.

For some people it was incredibly hard, for others it's easy. I got a 74 on the first test, high B on the second and A's on the last two. He dropped my first test as a result of my improvement, so he's merciful. I recommend taking all Free Response. But I had a friend who skipped every class, took all multiple choice and still got an A. Up to you.

Hardest class I've taken at tech, and that's saying a lot.  There is sooooo much reading, it's so unrealistic.  We had six textbooks and reading and remembering every detail of them was mandatory to do well on exams.  Would definitely recommend taking a different, easier professor for basic history requirements!

Class has a lot of reading involved. If you go to class and listen to lecture and skim the book you will get an A. Tests can be tricky but nothing too hard. Class is mandatory but usually you can get someone to sign you in if you don't want to go. Overall an easy teacher with reasonable tests.

Take the essay exams not the multiple choice. I took the multip;le choice the first time and failed.  Then on the next three tests I took essay and made A+s. He dropped my first grade and I ended up with an A+ in the class.  Skimmed the book, but if you listen in class and take thorough notes, you will ace the essay exams.

There is so much reading in this class. And you really can't do well without doing the reading. Also, he spends most of the class talking about one subject and saying "but we'll get to that later..." and then he never talks about it again because we run out of time.

Terrible professor. He spends half of his lecture complaining or talking about things that have nothing to do with history, but yells at you if you try to use the time productively by reading the text. The amount of reading is ridiculous for a class that really people only take because they have to. He's awful and pretentious.
A lot of reading, but as long as you do the reading the class is not hard at all.

I got an A+ without reading anything. To do this, you have to know how to study and take what you need from the textbooks. Most of the tests come from the books. If you really listen to his lectures, they're actually very good and REALLY help for the test. I def. recommend him.
Very interested in his teaching.  A ton of reading but most of it is interesting.  Definitely a worthwhile elective.

He assigns a lot of reading. His lectures are very boring. He rarely gets to his points, although he really gets into history. Take the essay exams, they are much easier than his multiple choice exam.

The challnege with him is the substantial amount of reading he assigns. I am an international student thus I am not interested in American history yet his lectures are sort of interesting so this helps. He is always willing to help you with any problem you have and as long as you keep up with the reading you should be fine. The tests are kinda hard

Dr. Foster is an incredibly cool teacher. He was always available whenever I needed him. his lectures are somewhat interesting and his tests are fairly easy if you do the reading. I would definently recommend this guy to anyone.
No Comments

Wonderful teacher!  Super interested in the material and more than willing to assist students - very apporoachable.  The tests are challenging, but as long as you keep up with the readings, you should easily get an A or B.
Excellent professor...he gets really excited about the material, so it's easy to find it interesting.

Lots of reading for this class, and the lectures are somewhat interesting.  You can choose to take a multiple choice test or an essay test.  Multiple choice tests can be difficult, especially without doing the reading.

There is no doubt that this is a difficult class, but you can tell Dr. France cares about his students. He's highly accessible after class, during his online office hours, and he hosts review sessions for every exam. His lectures can be confusing, but if you utlize all of the materials he gives you to practice with for the exams you should be fine.

Dr. France is a solid option for Orgo 2. Yes, exam averages are low, but he is very accommodating, and it's the TAs that are harsh, not Dr. France. Regrade request. He's very available- stays for 30-40 mins after class answering questions, responds to emails the night before the exam, and promptly; he's kind, lighthearted, and cares. Lots of EC.

I honestly do not get why Dr. France has such bad reviews. He makes himself available very frequently for help and shows he really cares about his students. I agree that his lectures could be improved, as he does not do much practice in class. However, his grading scheme is generous; 87.5 = A and you drop the lowest exam and double the highest!

What ever you do, DO NOT take him! Every single exam had an average of 60% and over half of the class dropped. He crams material into lectures, and skips over major topics that ends up on the exams. Grading takes weeks, and everything is graded for correctness. You will teach yourself 95%+ of the course.

Don't take - lectures are vague and incomplete, but detail is expected on the exam. Every exam average was 60%, and half the class dropped. He crams too much material into each lecture, skips over topics that end up on the exams, and takes 4 weeks to grade. It's impossible to learn from his lectures. You have to teach yourself 95% of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the most painful classes I've ever had to sit through. Dr. France just reads off the slides. His grading criteria are unclear, and he waits until the end of the semester to input anything. The only things I learned in this course were because I read the textbook.

Extremely lazy lecturer, just reads off the ppt for an hour. Same stuff you see in the text. No practice problems, which you need in orgo. Polar opposite orgo professor compared to Pollet. Skip all the lectures and read the book, do practice problems, your grade will be the same as if you had 100% attendance. Avoid at all costs.

Don't take this professor if you can avoid him. Boring, unhelpful lectures. Very hard to make an A or B. Don't go to class and read the textbook if you want to be successful. Midterms are incredibly hard, and  the final exam included material that we did not learn. Doesn't respond to emails, didn't show up for one of our midterms, late to the final

- lectures were not engaging and I had to rely on the textbook to learn
 - a large part of your grade comes from homework which is graded for accuracy, and not completion like most other chem classes
 - the difficulty of homework and exams did not reflect what was taught in class
 - most of my friends ended up dropping the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took him in the Spring of 24 and would recommend to avoid if possible. If you go to class he will stand there and talk over the slides for the entire time and won't write anything down or go over examples (lazy teacher). Stay home and read the slides and go through the textbook. Get used to teaching yourself for the entire course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bro is the king of reading off the slides for 50 minutes straight. Does not solve problems or show examples during lectures, literally just regurgitates what you already saw in the reading. A harsh change of pace if you had the pleasure of taking orgo I with Pollet. Good luck teaching yourself all the material with the book.

If you have the option to not take this class, DO NOT. It was not it. Dr. France was not very helpful and refused to help. I worked so hard in this class and it was not enough to get me the grade I wanted. He also only curved the class to make sure that he had enough people to look good as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OCHEM 2 is already a very hard class and I feel like Dr. France made it harder than it needed to be. He's very passionate about chem and would often go off on tangents about material not on the exams and would have to rush through actual material. It was very hard to grasp information this way. Handwriting is also terrible and hard to understand.

This class is really really hard, but Dr. France tries to make it as straightforward as possible. Tests are curved very reasonably, as is the class as a whole. He is very easy to reach via office hours and the TA/PLUS leaders are both good at explaining concepts. However, his handwriting on the annotated notes are terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are fast-paced, but reading assigned readings and the textbook section that coincides with the topics helps a TON. Also, you MUST do through the practice questions that are within the textbook because his lectures dont cover the small things. With him, I had a better "feel" for the material, so I killed the Orgo section of the MCAT.

Dr. France is great, I've learned A LOT in this class, but that learning comes with a lot of effort so be prepared for the grind. I'll probably end up taking another prof for orgo 2 just because of the average GPA difference, but if you don't have any other options for orgo, Dr. France isn't a bad choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is obviously very smart but can' teach. Do your self a favor and don't take orgo with him even if it means delaying graduation or being behind. Man just reads off slides and makes us do readings and present the readings the next day. He just regurgitates the info. Pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. France is extremely knowledgable in organic chemistry, however that doesn't make his class easy. This was a very difficult class, and if you struggle with organic chemistry I would suggest a different professor if you could. That being said lectures are very knowledgable and interesting.

Lectures are fine but extremely fast, so you have to constantly catch up by reading the textbook. He provides a lot of past exams, but the actual tests are WAY HARDER than the practice ones. Final was IMPOSSIBLE. The average was around 60%. I decided to switch out of chemistry major after taking this class.

For reference I got an easy A in orgo 1. This was the hardest class ever and he is not lenient with grading at all. I will never take another class with him. I scraped by with a B (legit by .1%). This sucked

worst semester of my life I hate this man. The final average was a D and he wont curve. All regrade requests are denied. Unless youre a god at orgo prepare for a B or C. Also, final was 24 pages and most of the class didnt finish it (hence the 61% final average score).

It's orgo 2 after all, you're going to have to work for it. Make sure you read the textbook and pay attention in class, having him during the virtual semester was very tough but he is a great professor and really knows what he is doing. He holds review sessions using his own time and you have access to so much material to study with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. France. Don't mix up the difficulty of orgo 2 and the ability of the professor to teach. The only drawback was that his lectures tended to go really fast, especially during the online lecture. I would highly recommend him though. Tests are hard but test what you know. Homeworks are helpful. Oh, and his co-professor Meghan was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: France definitely knows his stuff, and he's a great professor! Don't let other reviews fool you--France is great at what he does and teaches organic in a very clear way, but organic is just hard period. Don't confuse a hard subject with a bad professor. France is also pretty accessible outside of class, and he was helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor at all. Lectures are good but not mandatory. Be ready to read the book and study a lot outside of class. It is orgo after all

Orgo 1 is hard, but this prof gets you through it with as much help as possible. he gives you everything you need to know for the exams and you leave the class prepared for orgo 2. He will help you in his office or after class. Lots of extra credit and can exempt final. He keeps it interesting and fun in class. I enjoyed it.

I understand why people dont like the class. however, I think people should take the bad reviews with a grain of salt. Orgo 1 is hard no matter who you take. France takes you through everything and guides you through every detail. The tests are hard but he provides plenty of material to help you prepare. There is also lots of Xtra credit.

Please try to switch out if you're looking for a teacher. Going to lectures does NOT help you prepare for his usually unreasonable tests. He uses powerpoint slides and try to read/explain stuff from there without giving practice problems or specific examples. If you know how to teach yourself, you'll be fine. Otherwise, you're better off switching.

This class isn't too difficult if you understand the material &do the hwk& practice probs. In other words the tests aren't filled w/ trick probs that even if you studied are difficult to get. However, this professor doesn't teach orgo well at all; he simply reads off slides that he borrowed from a coworker. The class requires alot of self teaching.

The class wasn't necessarily difficult if you know how to teach yourself, but if you're looking for someone to teach you, I recommend another professor.  His notes are copied out of the book, his tests have problems that are not even explained by him or the book, and he is not very enthusiastic.  I only learned by delving into my own textbook.

If there is an alternative, take that professor instead! His notes are just summarizations of the text and most of his classroom examples are easy (most don't prepare you for the homework). If you have to take this class, then always go to the help desk or the TA's. Not knowing a material can hurt you since the lessons are related to each other.

Was an interesting lecturer but the class is way too difficult for an elective class, be prepared to put STEM level effort into a non-STEM class. He doesn't post lecture materials or notes and moves through his notes pretty fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Fuentes class, the lectures were fascinating; I learned tons. He's a fair grader. Just be ready to take detailed notes if you want to succeed. Readings are assigned 2x a week. Quizzes are on the readings, so take good reading notes too. Exams are bit difficult, but multiple extra credit opportunities at the end. True difficulty: 3.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fuentes is great. His lectures are interesting, he's clearly passionate about the course material, and grades are diversified among reading quizzes, worksheets, and exams. I really enjoyed INTA 2050 and highly recommend taking his class.
Professor Fuentes was very engaging and made the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class grading is 60% tests and 40% daily works. His lectures are very informative, and I didn't think they were boring, as he is very passionate. I'm not an INTA major and just took this class for "fun." There is definitely some reading but nothing too, too much. Cool guy!

Fuentes is great. Lectures are in-depth and thoughtful. He cares about what he is teaching and he's good at it. You actually have to do the reading assignments and attend class to complete the in-class worksheets. Exams are 60% lecture material, 40% readings, but it all really works together. Similar difficulty to an AP history class.

Dr. Fuentes is a great professor-- one of the best I have had at Tech. The work I had to put into to succeeding in this class was worth it since lectures were valuable. I left with so much more knowledge. I really appreciated the readings quizzes at the start of each class because it meant everyone was doing the work and made for a better class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Fuentes! His class, Intro to Global Development, was perhaps my favorite class last semester and his lectures are fantastic. The reading material he pulls for each topic are in-depth and thought-provoking and I thought him to be a fair grader and a sympathetic professor, especially with COVID times. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is reading heavy, which can be a lot at times. His grading can also be weird and inconsistent, but overall the class was enjoyable. As long as you do your work, read, and attend class, you'll do good in the class.
Professor Fuentes' 2050 class was very interesting. The class is reading heavy, and you must attend class to succeed, but if you do the work an A is both enjoyably and easily attained.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class has so many assignments so there is a lot of leeways. Dr. Fuente's lectures summarized the readings for the weeks & he gave the students a chance to ask questions about the assignments and readings. Readings could be a lot, depending on the week, but each assignment is due on a different day. Great professor & interesting material!

With online, his grading was simple, 11 worksheets and 11 discussion posts where you can drop the lowest of the two. Two different essays and a final that was two more essays but they're all 3 page double space. Video lectures are helpful. Worksheets get LONG and you need to read the articles he gives but they were straightforward which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Funk is okay. His class is 75% tests, and the tests are not very easy. Lectures are not great, but attendance is optional anyways.

He's a very chill and nice professor. His lectures are a little hard to get through because they were so long.. But he's a very forgiving grader. Exams are pretty simple and even use lecture problems. Overall, this class was way less stressful than the prerequiste Thermo.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor, would help out if you talked to him about any problems. Lectures were really boring and he would just read off the slides he posted so most people didn't go. Took forever to grade HWs, but they were graded very nicely. Exams were ok, provides topics overview and would give PLUS TA some of the problems ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's an 8am, but he's alright.

Lectures are very boring and sometimes he can be a bit confusing, but he doesn't assign a lot of homework and his tests aren't too difficult. He is also a fair grader and very approachable during his office hours.
Final project was creating a short horror film which was a fun little experience. Other assignments were also fun and somewhat of a break from a tech school.

I like the idea of teaching English/communication skills through the lens of horror. Class was interesting and engaging because of small size and interesting topics. Projects were mostly done in class and graded on completion. She cares about the student and the subject matter. Attendance mandatory.
Theme for her class was horror which was very interesting. Easy class, everything for participation. Great professor and very passionate.
Awesome professor! Cared deeply about students and Dr. Fuller is very down to earth. Definitely take Dr. Fuller!!
Easy A, very nice professor. High reccomend
Such an awesome prof who cares about what she teaches despite it being the main prereq at a STEM heavy school. The content was very fun and engaging.
Easy grader

If possible, take any class with any other professor than Fung. He is the least caring professor I have ever had. He does not respect his students and has fallen asleep during every students presentations. If he does fall asleep, he will dock points from you for what he missed during his in-class nap. I hope he is better for his future students.

Had Dr. Fung for CX4010, and it was an awful experience. His lectures are pre-recorded and contain lots of information, and there a sometimes multiple recorded lectures a day. Grading is incredibly strict, and this makes coding the easiest part of this class when compared to its regular quizzes and essays. I learned a lot, but did not enjoy it.

The course was mostly unrelated to the assignments. The grading of assignments and course project were not bad, it was even worse; as it was done based what a few favoured students wrote in their answers or had in their projects.

The grading scheme was never told and total course was graded on the end day of the semester giving no chance of improv

Dr. Furst has to be one of my favorite professor. The lectures can become very in-depth and theory heavy but he was able to explain everything really well. Homework can be a little challenging but if you put in the time it should be no problem. Super caring professor overall and the best TA team I had so far, thank you for the great semester :)

Dr. Furst is a very interesting professor who distills the class so you understand the essence of the material over asking you to memorize his lectures. Very generous on grading- if you can show you know it, you will do well, and he doesn't want you to be stressed. Highly recommend. Super interesting person too- stories will not disappoint.

Furst clearly cares a lot about his students- he cancelled the one midterm we had because he didn't think it would help us and would only create unnecessary stress for us. He allows for homework regrades which I thought was really helpful for mastering the content better, especially since I didn't completely understand his lectures all the time.

If you are taking algorithms at Georgia Tech, this is the probably the easiest professor you can hope to get. Dr. Furst gives no tests (instead we have a final project, and most grades are from homeworks that one can redo at any time). Despite this, you will learn a lot, even if due to his unique teaching style, each lecture feels empty.

Super interesting course which changed the way I think about the world. Different in that grades are not emphasized (almost everyone will get an A), and instead the focus is on learning. If you have room in your schedule, this class is worthwhile.

Hands down the best professor I have had at tech, absolutely incredible teacher, super caring, and unbelievably knowledgeable.  Absolutely the number 1 teacher you could ever have for CS2701.  You should take this course and he should be your Furst pick.

The lectures themselves can be really in-depth and much more information than the average student needs, but the lecture notes taken by the TA's for each lecture are really clear and useful. The professor cares about people success by allowing regrades for full credit. As long as you try and get help, you can always get an A with regrades.

Not bad but I'd only take Furst for the hw regrades tbh. Lectures were hard to follow and often behind the hw. There seemed to be a disconnect between Furst and the TAs. Furst would say one thing, TAs the opposite. HWs are hard, but can be regraded. Write hw algorithms in plain English instead of pseudocode if possible, TAs are less picky then.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take this class - you don't learn much because the professor goes on tangents and all of a sudden, you're spending 7 lectures on FFT and 1 on DP. TAs are  inconsistent at grading and there's an equal chance you get a 50 or 100 on HWs due to how radically different each TA grades - and the prof does nothing about it. He has no control.

Professor Furst cares a lot about the success of students, and would answer any questions and provided a lot of insight. The course was somewhat too easy due to the regrading policy, but I still learned a lot.
Dr. Furst truly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. The class is designed in a way to promote growth and doesn't have any high stakes assignments.
Great lecturer. Innovative class policy allowing for all exams & homework to be regraded. Attend office hours regularly and you'll master the material.

Dr. Furst is very caring and wants everyone to do well in the class. He offered regrades on every homework assignment, and even on the riduloulsy difficult midterm exam we had. There was no final exam- instead we had to answer a few reflective questions. Though it's an easy A, I didn't really learn anything. If you want to learn, take someone else.

Grading is easy. It just felt like such a waste of time, each homework is a long assignment that have you regurgitate some algorithms. There is no real thinking involved. Grading criteria is also very ambiguous, not even the TAs seem to know how the class is graded. TAs seem to purposely grade harshly knowing you can do corrections.
Dude, this guy is awesome. Just take him, you won't regret it.

Professor Furst is an amazing person and professor. His class structure was way different than I was used to(homework and participation were 75% of the grade) but it was very beneficial. 

He is willing to help anyone learn if they are willing to put forth the effort. If you are confused in class, you can ask him to clarify further and he will.

im very conflicted about this class. the grading structure is very easy, but lectures are super useless and irrelevant to the homework. This is a class that is actually supposed to teach you important concepts: DP, NP, greedy algo, but we barely even touched those concepts. If u want an easy A then take it but other profs are easy and teach you

Furst wants you to get an A in this class, you can regrade all assignments for full credit. Besides the grading he gives some of the most interesting lectures I have been in, they are not mandatory and you can get a good grade in the class without them but if you are interested in really understanding algorithms I strongly recommend Furst.

The homework are hard. However, he let us redo them for full credit afterwards. Our grades were based entirely on homework and participation, so it was super easy to get an A. Personally, I wasn't a fan of his lecturing, but a lot of other people enjoyed his class. His very sympathetic to students and helpful in office hours. Really cool guy.

He is incredibly nice, funny, and interesting. His lectures are great, and the course overall was awesome. My only complaint is that he went very slowly at the beginning, so we didn't have as much time to cover the very interesting material.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Always very helpful and did his best to make sure that everybody understood the points he made. Very open to feedback and willing to be lenient on the exams. If you show up to class, pay attention, and do the homework, you shouldn't have any problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great introduction to the art of algorithm. Although attendance is not required, Furst's lecture is very helpful, and teaches things that cannot be explained in a textbook. He makes sure to explain the process of inspirationally generate a new algorithm as well as the concrete proof of the algorithm. I will recommend this course to others.

Ok professor. The class was very easy, but once you get done with the drawing portion of the class, lectures are practically useless to anyone who isn't interested in manufacturing, not great for someone who has to take ME 231 for credit in another major, but an extremely easy class.
Lol! One of the worst teachers. Doesnt teach anything
She is really nice and someone I highly recommend. She is passionate about what she teaches and is always accessible during office hours or if you make an appointment.
Dr. Fu is amazing! She genuinely cares about her students and is incredibly accommodating. Easily the best professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Fu is amazing! So long as you get your assignments done by the due dates posted and try on your final group project, you will finish with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fu really is a great teacher she doesn't overburden her students with too much work like other ME1770 teachers typically do. It is important to come to lecture because of attendance, and she gives constant reminders for work due. She is reasonable on her due dates. Go to office hours she will help you ALOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Fu is a really caring person and the class is really simple. Just go to the class and don't leave off things to the last minute and you will be fine.

Really kind professor for ME1770. Has a bit of an industrial design bias in the class (the art section is a bit heavy) but if youre not good at sketches it wont hurt your grade. As with other sections of this class, major group work. **Deadlines are flexible**

Good and nice professor. Her research was the real reason I took her class, she's always willing to take on a good student for design and engineering research. The class isn't hard as long as you stay ahead and do your work.

She is an okay professor. Most class periods nothing is accomplished but attendance is mandatory. Mostly sketching in the beginning and CAD in the end. Work hard on the projects and do not get behind. Su (the TA) is great for help! Not a tough grader but has high expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Pretty simple class. Just watch the required videos and pay attention in class you'll do fine. Lectures are aimed at relating concepts to industry. If you have any issue just go to TA office hours. Master Su is awesome!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is barely available to help, never shows up to labs and cancels office hours pretty much every week. Her grading criteria isn't always clear so she will often take point off for things you didn't know were required. Most classes you won't do anything but attendance is required. She gets the job done but is not amazing.

Dr. Fuller is a great professor. I would take him for any chemical engineering course, no questions asked. I learned a lot in his class. Stay on top of studying and attending lectures to maximize understanding of the material because his exams really test if you know the topic well or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor relative to the others in the CHBE department. Clear with his grading and very accessible out of class. The course is super manageable if on top of your work.
Great professor. Assignments weren't too bad as long as you stayed on top of the course material.

I took EAS 3110, not PUBP, but I regret not reading these reviews beforehand. He really does hoot/holler a lot- the most I learned in this class was from the guest lecturers. It's an easy class for anyone looking to just get a science credit done, but I wouldn't recommend it for EAS majors; "preaching to a room of climate deniers" is 100% accurate.

He's a good professor a little over the place while lecturing but if you really talk to him and listen to what he says he's quite knowledgeable and the most passionate person about the environment you will ever meet. Work is easy and I took notes in class and was barely called on (just don't let him catch you off guard and you will be fine)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class should've been interesting but he has a talent for talking in circles while saying very little of value. It's like he's preaching to a room of climate deniers, not students capable of critical thought. Assignments were poorly paced: we had few until the very end when we were bombarded with papers and presentations with no time to give.

Dr. Garcia is an okay professor. He is prone to getting off topic and rambling, but he eventually covers the material in the lecture slides. Slides are posted in Canvas, and exams are open-note. Be prepared to be randomly called on! He likes to call on people who don't appear to be paying attention to the lecture. Overall, not good, not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
CP2233!
His class was the part of my week I dreaded the most. This guy yaps about absolutely nothing-giant waste of time. Randomly calls on people when he's mad w/ bad questions and terrible attitude. Only positive is that tests are open note. Learned nothing. Completely ruined a class that could have been really interesting and taught very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He literally just stands up there hootin and hollerin and it's very apparent that he has no clue what he's talking about
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She took attendance sometimes in-class and sometimes using inclass activities which due the same day. Takes a long time period to get back term-test results. The final was cancelled near the end of the semester, so basically the grade will be based on only in-class activities and projects.

The course, as taught, isn't super difficult. Grading is really generous, and tests are mostly based on stuff from the slides. But it's often difficult to follow lectures because things move so fast and so much stuff gets skimmed past. Dr. Garten is very knowledgeable but difficult to reach outside of class.

lectures felt confusing and just like a bunch of info thrown with no coherency or good explanations, when a guest lecturer was teaching with the slides, they said the same thing. Also lecture slides and HW answer keys were not made available until significantly later, grades/exams not given back until pretty late as well.

Sometimes the lectures do not cover everything that you need to know. She rushes through concepts which makes it hard to understand all the material. The class scheme is very simple and you just need to put in extra effort.

25% HW and class clickers, 25% for two midterms and a final each. Tests are all multiple-choice, and the content is relatively easy to get. Good choice for knocking out this course, but make sure you don't fall behind, Units 1 and 2 are much easier conceptually than Unit 3, and the final tripped a lot of people up.

Extremely unorganized. Complete waste of a class. You learn how to do HIS problems, and walk away with no general real world knowledge. ALWAYS is referencing undefined variables, theres like a thousand sloppy PDFs on canvas that you have to search through. The textbook he says to read isn't what he references. Chill dude but needs to lock in so bad

I think he's actually a reasonable dude and nothing on tests were curveballs at all. The class as a whole did bad over the summer since half the students had less than 2 hours of watch time on the asynchronous lectures according to him. It's an easier class than the GPA reflects. The students who did bad probably didn't try enough

He is able to teach, just not well. Seemed so disinterested in every lecture. Beyond the occasional uGA joke or whatever, lecture are boring and the hw was never similar. Tests were not ridiculous but he could have done better preparing us for particular types of problems. They are open note, which is okay, but you get no feedback on tests or hw.

He lectures in a very disinterested voice which makes it difficult to be invested in what is being taught and is pretty unforgiving about grades even if the majority of the class doesn't do well on assessments. If you take his class, make sure to review the RQ examples and practice problems with a timer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are SO hard to study for, many questions are just completely out of nowhere. I never knew what an exam would look like going into it. Class is infrequent, and you're cooked if you miss it or zone out during lecture. A lot of the stuff he does and tells you is incorrect. Don't take him if you want a fair class, or if you want to learn a lot.

Gaines is kind and accessible: regrades are easy, exams mimic homework, and all lectures are posted online. But he cancels class last-minute, often swaps live lectures for videos, rushes through material, omits topics, and makes frequent errors in notes, HW, and exams. Choose him for a relaxed term; pick Alpha if you want a rigorous,in-depth course

Would not recommend. Lectures are mostly rambling and he doesn't post notes. He also cancelled class last-minute very often.

He provides you with a 34 page long formula sheet, which somehow manages to not define any relevant formulas.

He also requires a $150 purchase for McGraw to submit homework, which takes forever and is mostly auto-graded.

Gaines is one of the most unqualified and incompetent professors at Tech. He cancels over 60% of classes and can't answer basic questions. His homework requires a $150 online fee, which you'll waste 10+ hours on because it isn't tested. He refuses to post lecture notes and moves fast. The only thing in your favor is that his exams are open-note.
Don't take him he doesnt really teach but just reads over his hand writing in class... no communication... moves too fast in class... lots of filler words with no real meaning

If you want to learn do not take this professor. He is the definition of unprepared and unqualified. He spends lecture rambling about teaching instead of actually teaching. If you ask a question expect filler words and phrases and no answer. I am embarrassed that gatech thought having this professor teach a 3000 level class was acceptable.

If she's your senior design examiner, GOOD LUCK. She was extremely difficult all semester and fixated on a minor, irrelevant detail that even the other examiners knew wasn't an issue. Despite repeated explanations, she never understood and scored us low. She would berate us after presentations, but she wouldn't even let us answer her questions!

You can tell that she's really trying to give good feedback and be fair, but she misses the mark. There's not much you can do if you take senior design with her, but I would caution against using cutting-edge/novel methods. We tried to use a recently published method and she disapproved because she wasn't familiar with it. Avoid if possible.
Probably one of the worst teachers I have ever taken a class with at Georgia tech, genuinely needs to retire.

DONT TAKE. I came in thinking this was going to be an easy elective and was proven very wrong. she gives out grades arbitrarily and gives extremely vague feedback (usually the same feedback for everyone in the class). attendance is mandatory which is tough because lectures are extremely boring and she notices if you're doing something else.
DONT take any class for her, RUN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

She teaches little to no useful content and its expected that you answer and complete all the projects with little context or guidance. She arbitrarily grades assignments and gives the same comments to every group. Absolutely the worst, most uncaring professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech. PLEASE AVOID

Her lectures are kind of boring but she clearly states what it takes to do well in the class. Also, her tests are very hard to finish on time so study hard and be prepared. Her notes are not usually available elsewhere so try not to miss lecture. There's a group project at the end - get started early.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is only graded by 4 short multiple-choice tests, no homework or any grade buffers. In-class lecturing is very tangential and off-topic. Buying the textbook and reading it was better than sitting in class. Exam dates were only announced in-class, and were not present elsewhere. No canvas course either.

Avoid this professor no matter what, she is genuinely not worth it!! . No slides, no canvas. The only grades are the four exams and the final. The date of the four exams are not given to you, she doesn't lecture about test material just about her life, and she's made multiple inappropriate comments during class. trying to report her as we speak.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These reviews can go over a decade back. Nothing has changed. 1.5 hours of waste. Often incomprehensible, barely talks on actual material, goes on about her personal life and is fine belittling questions. 4 20 multiple choice exams are the entire grade. She was both late and didn't have our final on the final exam day. Textbook is the only way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't expect to learn anything from the lectures. She only talks about what's in the news (which isn't on the exams) and her opinion on current events and politicians as well as her personal life. Expect a lot of side tangents. She doesn't take attendance and she doesn't have a Canvas page. Your whole grade is 4 exams (20 questions multiple choice)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lectures are near worthless and are mostly just stories (just talking, no slides). There's a textbook to go with that may help, but it's way too expensive.
If you already know your stuff, this may or may not be free. If not, look elsewhere.
No homework, but there are only a few tests with not enough questions. Miss just a few? Goodbye, A.

Worst professor. Don't take her. Spends the entire class talking about her own life and problems, talks nothing about the textbook or anything we are supposed to know for the class. No homework, your grade is 4 exams, had no clue what the exams would be like bc she doesn't cover any material. Study the textbook if you want to understand anything.

Lectures are a waste of time, prof waffles about nothing for 1.5 hrs. ZERO resources given (no notes, study guides, powerpoints, nothing), prof couldn't even activate Piazza. Only four 20-question MCQ exams total, read every detail of the textbook to do well. Only reason I would take her again is for another free period lol she's terrible.

Attending lectures are a complete waste of time. Every class she will open the book, explain 1 or 2 sentences, stay on topic for 3 secs before she goes off on her personal life and her controversial opinions. The only thing you do in the class is take 4 exams. So either understand gov, or just take notes on the book before the exam and you're fine.
Very easy class-just show up and there were a few take home exams. Lectures aren't very helpful, I didn't feel like I learned any material and she talks about her personal life most of the time.

I NEVER showed up to lecture, but when I did she was very funny & definitely kept you interested. She didn't really teach she just talked about what we were learning about was like & shared anecdotes. I just read the chapters the tests were on a couple days ahead of time & I nearly got a 100%. Plus she lets you work on the group project from day 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: As a graduating senior I can say that this was my least favorite course/professor while in college. The teacher does ramble (as mentioned in other comments) and often talks about her personal life. Additionally, (in my opinion) she humiliated a student in class for asking an on topic question.
I attended almost all the lectures, despite them being useless. Did well on the tests, mainly because I read the chapters carefully. Getting the book and reading the chapters will be most rewarding.
Really liberal and opinionated. Tends to ramble.
Do yourself a favor and never ever take this class. You will not learn anything worthwhile. Three tests and a paper with no directions and no guidance on anything. Absolutely useless.

what a waste of my life. Spent like $180 on textbooks which we read maybe 1/5 of. TEacher literally taught me NOTHING. Just talked about her life for 1.5 hours twice a week. Democrat and very biased. 2 multiple choice tests, detail specific. 1 project/paper. Multiple choice final. Teacher is nice person but bad teacher. do not take her

what a miserable waste of my life. Spent like $180 on textbooks which we read maybe 1/5 of. TEacher literally taught me NOTHING. Just talked about her life for 1.5 hours twice a week. Democrat and very biased. 2 multiple choice tests, detail specific. 1 project/paper. Multiple choice final. Teacher is nice person but bad teacher. do not take her

most useless lecture ever, basically just get the textbook, read every detail for the test, no powerpoint slides not notes given, easy class if u just read the textbooks and bring ur laptop to lecture unless u want to listen to her gossip all day
really wants you to get better at the language so lots of speaking involved. theres a good deal of work to do outside of class but not too much or difficult to deal with.

Dra. Geary is an amazing professor! She communicates deadlines clearly and is very responsive over email if you ever have any questions. The online mini classes and TalkAbroads are not graded harshly and really helped me get better at speaking Spanish. The online textbook is mandatory for weekly assignments (costs $50 I think).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. She actually cares about her students in and out of the classroom. The class isn't hard, if you care about learning you'll thrive in her class. Very available for help/email, and has a genuine desire to help her students succeed. Definitely recommend her as a professor, very positive energy

Sra. G was amazing! This class was super fun - I practiced my Spanish in a chill, encouraging environment. I loved the telenova, group convos, and video calls with native speakers. Heads up- some of the class materials cost money (~$110). If you're nervous abt speaking broken Spanish, take this class, it will really help you solidify and practice!

Sooo much good conversation practice! Never graded for accuracy, just for putting in genuine effort. Had opportunities to speak with native speakers and also watched a show in Spanish- very fun!! A good bit of work outside class but nothing too hard. She can sometimes treat students like children but cares a lot and is looking out for us.

Take Dr. Geary if fluency is your goal. There is a good bit of homework, but it's all speaking Spanish and is graded on participation, which allows you to frequently practice speaking without fear of taking a GPA hit. You'll also watch a show as HW and discuss it in class. Dr. Geary is super passionate, kind, and wants you to succeed.

I absolutely loved my Spanish class with Dr. Geary! It is clear that she loves teaching and loves seeing her students grow and do well. Through her class I have now learned ways that I am excited to continue improving my Spanish and am sad that I can't just take her course again.

Dr. Geary is so sweet and 3101 made me SO much more confident and proficient in Spanish. She's a great professor and the class is incredibly helpful and engaging. It's a pretty easy course and she's an easy grader, but there is a decent amount of work expected for it (all oral/conversation based assignments). Made me add a double major in Spanish!

Dr. Geary was a great professor! Her class had a fair amount of time consuming assignments but all were graded kindly and were important to the class. In general, her grading was generous and she wanted us to succeed. My Spanish improved so much with her class and I would happily take her class again!

SPAN2001, not 1001. But i LOVED this teacher! She was so sweet and always engaging us. She made me fall in love with Spanish again. Attendance was mandatory, but you could miss 3 before it mattered. Either way, lectures were important but they were also fun and i never missed one because I always wanted to go! The best teacher. Very clear lectures

Best Spanish professor I've ever had. Extremely caring and wants her students to succeed. Grades based on effort, not success. If you can, take SPAN 3151. She only teaches it every few semesters and it's a lot of work, but it's worth it.
Class was async, but felt actually helpful. She gave excellent feedback on online submissions.

We had "class" but it was just a small group you were assigned to for reviewing the weekly lesson. "Class" was laid back since we were all trying to learn. Never did I feel judged for my Spanish. Prof and classmates were great. Turn in everything on time and you will love learning Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Geary has been my favorite Spanish professor I've taken at GT. She is very respected and genuine, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. There is quite a bit of homework in the first half of the class, but she cut back on the work during the second half of the class. This class was completely synchronous by the way.

Had for both 1001/1002. Really nice, and genuinely cares about her students. It's online, but she's always available- I've messaged her at 10 pm before and she's responded within 30 mins. There's a ton of homework, but most of it's pretty easy and can be done an hour or two before it's due. Just skim the textbook before quizzes and you'll be fine.

There's lots of homework, but it is so easy that it can all be done literally an hour before it is due. You meet up with your partner every other week and if it is a friend or you get paired up with a cool person, it's actually a lot of fun. Just do slightly above average for the A. She is also readily available.

She may just be the best teacher I have throughout my GT career. Guys, she is so awesome and a pretty lenient grader (although some may not agree). She really does care about everyone and always tries to make the class engaging. The epitome of a good professor!

GREAT teacher! Had for both 1101/1102. She's extremely interested in how her students are doing in classes as well as everyday life. Uses book a lot but also has supplemental materials which she uses to make sure students fully grasp the concepts taught. Best Spanish teacher ever!

Lectures are not about the material that will be tested on your exams-- the prof. just kind of rambles about w/e. You will have to buy an expensive Pearson textbook bc it isn't available anywhere for free. Your final grade will be the average of like 3 or 4 exams, each 20 mult choice questions. Prof. is very disorganized and unaccommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Persons is very knowledgeable but is not cut out to teach. Lectured on current events, vaguely mentioned course material and provided no resources to prepare for the exam. Grade consisted of 4 exams with the final exam being cancelled, she printed out 60 syllabuses instead of the exam. Provided no extra credit or grade improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: real poopoo
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Persons is very intelligent and full of experience in politics. However, she does not know how to teach. The lectures are boring and not helpful, but she is quite witty and has funny moments. The syllabus is super vague, and your grade is determined by 3 or 4 exams, all multiple-choice. If you care about the subject, take a different professor.

Dr. Persons, while having amazing experience and background, was a very frustrating teacher. The syllabus had only tentative assignments and dates. We were supposed to have 2 tests, a paper, and assignments; we only had one midterm and a final paper. She refused to use canvas despite petition and would cancel class on a whim.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Lectures were pretty boring, but slides were really good to study off of separately. HWs were long but not too hard, we also only did 3. Course is split into aeronautics and aerospace halves. The exams and HWs for the aerospace half are much easier. Exam grading was kind of harsh, also grading for HW and exams took forever.

Prof. German is a really nice guy, and his lectures are super understandable. That said, he can drone during lectures which makes them a bit boring as he goes through slide decks. Homework was infrequent which made preparing for tests and quizzes difficult (2 test + 2 quiz = 80% of the course grade). Would recommend over other 3330 profs for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely nice, and great professor to go to lectures for. I didn't and still ended up with a B in the class, but an A is definitely an easy thing to get if you put in the work. Horrible at responding to emails/canvas messages/piazza though.

German is a great professor for vpro. His lectures felt very easy to follow and understand. Probably the most well spoken professor I've ever had. HWs closely model what the tests/quizzes look like so it's easy to prepare for those. The class does focus more on aeronautics than spacecraft, but overall worth taking regardless of which you prefer.

It is clear that German is vey passionate and excited to be teaching vpro. He tends to drag out lectures but is very clear and enjoys expanding on things not covered by the slides. Exams are very fair but homework often involves a scavenger hunt. He is super nice, caring, and will answer any/all questions. He is such a girl dad and girl boss
One of the best profs I've had at GT. Clear and concise on course content and expectations. Has passion for course content and instructing. Will be taking his AE option next semester.

German is legit my FAVORITE professor at this school. He is absolutely the nicest person you will ever meet, and he lectures like he's babying the class, NOT in a demeaning way but in a charming way. The homeworks are very straightforward and tests are IDENTICAL to homeworks (literally just apply eqns!). Low stress but you'll still learn a ton!

Very understanding. I got sick multiple times and he allowed me proper extensions (I had documentation). Very clear lectures, teaches well. Tests fairly and hws are useful to prepare for tests. Students like him a lot. I've taken 3330 with Dec as well, German is the clear option for me. Shares his lecture notes (ppt). Not much practice besides hw.
Brian German is the biggest teddy bear and best professor at Georgia Tech within the aerospace department. Take his class if you can, become his friend if you can.

Had him for an options and I love the class. The passion for this material is quite evident in his teaching style. Dr. German is also very accommodating with the course structure, and it is clear that he just wants his students to learn and share this passion. He makes this class feel easy but at the same time I have learned so much!

The reason that Dr. German is so good is because he's really passionate about the material he teaches, and that translates to being able to teach it well. The things he expects us to learn are very structured (mostly Powerpoint based lectures) and he always backs them up with the wealth of practical knowledge he's accumulated.
Class was pretty easy just have to come to class and take notes

Very generous professor that genuinely cares about his students. The material is pretty difficult, so studying is definitely a must. I'd recommend this teacher to anyone, though. He's got to be one of the best on the campus.

Truly inspirational guy, he knows his stuff. Get a general idea of the knowledge from the slides and you're most likely going to get an A on the tests because of the INSANE curve. Concerts were fun and knowledgeable. Great story teller and could probably teach with his eyes closed. We went out with him after the program ended and was fun asf.

He is a good professor and is very lenient to your needs. Overall the class was very enjoyable and we learned a lot about the history of music. I took the class on the travel portion of a study abroad program, and he left you plenty of time to explore and have fun. If you'd like to learn about music I would take him.

Great dude, he knows his stuff, and is a very talented musician. It was very fun to spend the summer with him. His tests are hard, but he curves them very heavily, so if you think you failed, don't freak out. Overall, a fun class and a cool dude.

Oxford: copengagen/france. Study hard for test that's 3 days in. be on time for every class. memorize the classical songs that have long names for tests. He will curve test to give top 50% a 100, so if a test is impossible and u studied a lot don't freak out. you can get full credit on late hw. not a fun class.

Prof. Gholami is incredibly kind and is a great instructor. Her class is centered around 3 group projects which are graded VERY easily. She understands that most people are at Georgia Tech for STEM degrees and tries to incorporate aspects of communication and writing that would apply that in her class.

If you got Dr. Gholami you are so unbelievably lucky. She is so unbelievably kind and patient and also FUNNY! This entire class is group work, so be prepared for that, but she creates an amazing environment to allow you to express your concerns and voice opinions. 10/10 would recommend. She is so sweet and probably changed my brain chemistry!!!!!!!
All the assignments were basically completion grades. You won't get a lot out of the class, but you'll get an A.
I had this professor for 1102, and she was really sweet and caring towards us! Honestly this is your standard English class, and if you just do the work, you should be fine.

Very easy class as it felt like everything was a completion grade. Projects are very open ended and almost all were group projects. Very lenient with deadlines and will take late work. Allows you to skip 4 times without affecting your attendance grade. Overall very caring and nice person and easy class. Highly recommend.

I absolutely love Professor Gholami. I took her for English 1101 and 1102. She is sweet and caring. She grades on an objective basis, so as long as you do the assignment according to the expected criteria, you will do well in her class. Her class is basically entirely group work so be prepared to work with others! I 10000% would take her again!

had her for english 1102 and would 100% recommend. as long as you show up (attendance is graded)  and turn in your work you should get an A. she is very sweet and passionate about her job. the only thing I disliked was that all projects were group projects, but you can get them done during class time. great professor for a required class!

Prof. Gholami was very caring and kind, but her class got pretty dry at times; the projects were super open-ended and 2/3 were group projects. They didn't feel particularly rigorous, pretty much graded on completion with relatively little feedback on how to improve, which I think would have been nice.

Such a super super sweet professor! She is a really lenient grader and is not tough on her students at all. I would highly recommend you take her because her class is very fun to be in sometimes as well.( btw we only used the textbook like three times in the beginning of the year  so don't bother buying it. )
Greatest professor of all time. She is super nice and accepts certain excuses. I promise you won't regret taking her classes.
Best English Teacher Definitely should take her class!!!!!!!!!!
GOAT

She is a very kind and considerate professor. Class MWF for 50 min. She tells you you get 6 absences max for the sem but then extends it more as the semester progresses. Only 3 big assignments for the sem and a kind grader. Just show up to class and do the assignments and your good. It can get difficult to show up every class.

Please don't let the other rates dissuade you. She is extremely passionate about material science and it is reflected in her lectures. She is very bubbly and upbeat in her lectures. They are at high-level but she will help explain any topics to you in office hours. Probably one of the kindest and most helpful professors at Tech!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I've ever had at Tech. Her lectures are incomprehensible, and her entire course is disorganized. Homeworks had nothing to do with the lectures, and tests had nothing to do with the homeworks. Take MSE 2001 at a later semester if she is the only professor you can get.
