Possibly one of the worst organized classes ever. DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST!!! Even if u have to, just take it another semester with another prof. Firstly lectures were awful and not useful at all as she just read off slides, HW and exams were also extremely horrible and were not at all helpful. Barely any extra credit it the course.AVOID AT ALL COST

Lectures are like eating rocks, impossible to chew on, and even more impossible to digest. She loves to go on tangents about unrelated topics. Doesn't seem to understand that this is an intro level course and will never elaborate on important definitions. On top of this shes terribly disorganized and openly disrespects TAs in class. Big NO!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She clearly cares about the subject, but as a result the lectures devolve into irrelevant, far too in-depth content which distracts from relevant info for the exam content. All material in the Canvas course is arranged horrifically; a different textbook for every topic, mismatched exam solutions, etc.. Nice person, inexcusably disorganized.

was clear she likes the subject but just doesn't know how to lecture. very boring lectures where it was very hard to keep track of what she was saying. there were 2 tests and a final(not cumulative) and a bit of extra credit but i basically taught myself the course. if u get her, focus on the sample exams.
Does not provide valuable lectures, test content is barely covered, course material is very poor.
Just stay away.

Run away. She runs the class on invited speakers and does not teach. Our group final project wasn't even graded by her. It was based on surveys that non presenting people could fill out (often not, not mandatory and because no one payed attention in her class). You will not gain a intro to mse. u will gain a coinflip grade and reading assignmts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Taking this class in covid times, and its a disaster. Lectures are a grab bag of chaos. Hw is fine, but graded so late you can't fix issues. Group projects hinge upon the quality of your group, with vague instructions.

Like others have said, she did go off on tangents at some points, but she was generally pretty good. Tests (3 + final) were pretty much exactly like the practice tests, so they weren't that bad.. Even if you don't go to class, I'd DEFINITELY recommend going to her review sessions. I'd also recommend using the textbook to supplement lectures.

Deciphering lecture content is a crucial skill, as the material going on the whiteboard is important but sometimes cluttered and not explained too well. Exams are tough, but not impossible to get high marks in with enough studying. Rely heavily on the sample exams. Lots of homework, but it actually ensures you understand some of the material.

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever seen. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Her material makes zero sense and she loves going off on random ass tangents that make no sense. If you take this class basically you teach yourself. Also this semester she started doing Turning Point questions so heads up.

Assigns WAY too much homework, not a clear teacher, and only teaches about her own research and discoveries. avoid at all costs...... she spends lectures talking about how hard things were when she was in school and not teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is enthusiastic about her subject but doesn't know how to teach. She throws equations and definitions and then assumes we know what they are for. Half of the homework has no relation to the lecture, and the tests are impossible without doing the sample exams first.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I had her for MSE 1111, and it was bad. The grading was vague and arbitrary, and your entire grade hung on homework and attendance. On top of that, the assignments had nothing to do with topics discussed in class. Also she rambles about useless stuff to fill up time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: she doesn't provide any way to rewatch or review lectures, does not lecture well, is all over the place and does not explain well, has powerpoint up but uses white board for most of the notes (so you cannot review this material later), HW does not help you learn because it gives you no feedback,

Lectures are scatter-brained and unclear. Gerhardt presents material and equations in a seemingly random way without explaining what the variables are or how they work. Online homework was a joke and not helpful at all. I learned more from the textbook than from her.
Resources for you to study with? Don't make me laugh. Even the online homework is often wrong and her materials she does give are 10 years old and for an outdated curriculum.
she throws so much informations at you without explaining it in detail. She has extra help sessions and right before tests. Fairly easy if you attend all review sessions...
Dr. Gerhardt is a great professor. She is enthusiastic about the subject and really wants students to succeed. I really recommend taking her.
Best class on macroeconomics through so many daily life examples.
Although attendance was not mandatory, I never missed her class. Her teaching is a lot of learning.
Amazing lecturer and class. Easy A, but learned a good amount of econ. TAKE HER!!

She does talk alot while teaching the lectures but if you pay attention you'll be fine. She gives a hour for homework assignment; there were 12 HW's but she'll take your TOP 10 assignments and get rid of the other 2 bad scores. We got to use a crib sheet for the midterm and the final was super easy since it MIRRORED the homework TOOK ME 5 MINUTES.

Prof. Archana is an amazing teacher. She teaches economics concepts with so many examples and learning is just above any textbook. Very less homework but lot of explanation in the class. It was helpful to me specially because I am not a Econ major.

This class was fine if you want an easy A, but I didn't end up learning that much about economics. The HW questions are easy and there are "games" throughout the semester, which IMO did not help reinforce understanding. She gave extra credit a couple of times to help us succeed. However, I did not need to watch any of the lectures to get an A.

Professor Ghodeswar was a wonderful professor! She is extremely energetic, caring, and knowledgeable. She really wants everyone in the class to succeed and provides a lot of opportunities to do well and improve your grade if need be. Loved her!

Archana was an absolute gem! I came in to econ not really wanting to do it at all, and while I still didn't really care much for the material it was clear she really, really wanted us to enjoy it. In addition, when I had several special circumstances she bent over backwards to make sure I had a fair chance to turn in homeworks.
Archana is very knowledgeable on the subject. She did a great job relating it to real life current situations! She cares about her students and wants to make sure everyone does well! Would recommend
She is energetic and positive!

A nice professor, however did not understand the material at all. Grading policies are lenient, so I did most (all) of the learning though Trotter's online materials. I would recommend if you don't care about the material at all and just need an easy A
very good teacher

Lectures were pretty useless, very hard to follow. The majority of what I "learned" in this class was a result of hours spent with the textbook or KahnAcademy. Tests were absolute bombshells, which included failing class averages. Weekly quizzes were a T/F nightmare. Only plus was he'd give some test questions at office hours and he curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very casual and unrigid manner of teaching made for an environment that let me learn far more effectively. Dro pping the lowest exam and lowest quiz made it so that I could relax and do my best to learn at my own leisure, not at the proverbial gunpoint past classes have had me at.
Dropped lowest quiz and test (only had 3 of each). Tests on the material he teaches so no surprises. 87% is an A. Nuff said.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT OFFERED

reviews.comment: Lecture slides were posted to Canvas and were well-organized, while I did not attend class Dr. Ghiaasiaan made previous lecture recordings available. Average amount of homework for an ME class, grade mostly based on 2 open-note midterms and an optional open-note final, as well as a MATLAB computer project.

Grade was just homework (20%), 2 exams (40%), and a final (40%) so not the best structure. homework was from the textbook. exams were very hard and not similar to past material at all - average was a 50% on both exams - and the final was even harder. He's a boring lecturer and just reads off slides. I personally did not like his class at all.
It's course I'm never willing to take again and please avoid this course!

Too much workload, especially lots of mechanical applications in calculation actually does harm to the ful understanding of the field knowledge, and affects the energy input to other more valuable places.

7 homeworks, one midterm exam, one final exam, three projects
This is the heaviest workload I have ever experienced in a graduate level course and this large amount of work does not seem to be helpful. Too much homework and exmas are gererally not proper for graduates.

Dr. Ghiaassiaan is a solid teacher with clear lectures that exhaustively covers all the material on exams. There are a lot of problem sets for homework, but they prepare you for exams well too. He was fairly accommodating and made the final optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He just sit there and deliver his lectures but if you listen carefully you can actually learn. He uses his own text book. There are around 5-6 home works for the class plus one mid term and one final exam. He is flexible and very lineant in grading as well.

His lectures were a little fast-paced, but he got through all the material with good explanations. I really liked his character and his grading structure (2 tests, 2 quizzes, computing project, hw for completion). He is pretty lenient on your grade at the end of the semester if you ask and showed that you tried.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of HW, and problems get LONG. Two quizzes, two tests that count fora lot. Computer project that was like two homework problems but with coding. Problems on the tests and quizzes were Nothing like in class examples or anything in homework which is why I wouldnt take him again. Opted out of final but you dont know your grade until the very end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures dont help very much - youll get more out of reading the textbook and going through his slides as in his lectures he really just reads off slides but in a calmimg yet anxiety inducing way. Homeworks every week from the textbook - they are difficult you will need chegg. Exams are sooo difficult - study at least a week in advance.

Test are long and most likely wont be over anything you went over in lecture or homework. If you ask him a question hell either ignore you or forward it to the TA - who by the way enjoys taking off an incredible amount of points for the smallest mistakes. Lectures are not helpful and I could probably be learning more from YouTube

Ghiaasiaan is without a doubt the worst professor I have taken. Zero feedback on tests, it all gets forwarded to the TA's. The exam solutions are lines of computer code and his lectures are just him reading the slides. No concern for his students whatsoever. Avoid this man at all costs.
Ghiaasiaan does not know how to teach an online class whatsoever. He may be good in person tho.

Definitely don't recommend this guy. I think Georgia Tech students deserve a better professor for ME 3322. His Thermodynamics is EASIER than you think, But he tends to make it impossible to pass. Tests are heavy, you might need 2 hours to finish it (but he gives you 1). His TA's are unfair when grading your test, they take off points for everything

A nice, but blunt guy. His lectures consist of writing notes from the textbook, but I taught myself the material from the textbook instead of going to the lectures. 4 tests worth 25% each (1 final included). He decided to drop the lowest test. Confusing wording on tests make them harder for no reason. Not good at explaining concepts. Hard to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Doesn't answer back to emails or piazza, and rarely answers students' questions. Lectures are very long and unhelpful, I heavily depended on textbook notes. Grades by percentiles, and your grade is based on 3 difficult quizzes and the final (each worth 25%). Inadequate amount of time to complete 3 questions, 5 parts each
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For our section we were never given online grades, so my grade was "N/A" for the whole semester. He also ranks the class for the final grade so you may do well but below the average and get a lower grade. Tests include problems that weren't on homework or taught in class, so you have to truly understand the material to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ghiaasiaan is a good lecturer, and let's you use book/crib sheets on exams. Do all of the homework, and use old practice exams to study. The issue with this class is that the final is worth 45% of the grade and your grade is based entirely off of your peers. The tests are loooong, so prepare well and you'll be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heat transfer is a hard class, no way around that. He makes it easier by allowing textbook+crib sheets on exams. Homework is helpful for exams, and there's not too much of it (5 problems a week.) Lectures are hella boring though.

The lectures are very informative, but all the proofs make the lectures extremely long. Your grade is almost 100% based on tests, luckily the tests aren't too difficult. Unfortunately, TA's for the course are weird at grading tests and count off for dumb busy work stuff even when you get the answers correct. Overall, a great and helpful teacher!

Do the homework-not a lot only about 5probs a week. Study the practice tests he provides come test time. I'm not sure why the tests averages were so low (60's). I always walked out thinking the test was child'splay. Granted, I did the homework and understood it. An A isn't hard to get with some good ole tech hard work.
His lectures were pretty boring, but he is very knowledgeable and willing to help students.  His tests are very easy as long as you study the materials provided.
He is a very boring professor, but he is kind and willing to help you. His tests and assignments are very fair, and he provides adequate test material for the tests. Study hard and you will do fine.

He is definitely not the most interesting or effective professor in the world, but his tests and assignments are very fair. If you use the text book and study practice tests an A isn't too difficult isn't to achieve.

Dr. Garcia's the GOAT - one of the best professors I've had. Lectures were taught very well, exams were fair (crib sheets allowed too), he's really knowledgeable and patiently helps students. HW can be hard initially but if you start early and go to office hours it's fine and it prepares you for exams. Super interesting class and highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Course content was fun and the homework/tests were fair. We were also offered a crib sheet.

He was honestly such a good professor — you could tell he really cared about the students and made the material really easy to understand/straightforward. Crib sheets allowed on exams and always willing to stay after class to answer questions.

Lectures were great, he also live-streams/records his lectures for days you don't want to walk to class. Homeworks are long and hard but allows you to be familiar with the material. Exams are also pretty long but straightforward. Not sure where the other reviews calling him flirtatious are coming from - he's just a friendly guy that's a bit awkward
Coffee up for his lectures. Long lectures. The course demands a serious effort and isn't something you can breeze through. He can come across as flirtatious at times. Find a competent TA.
i can stay awake in his classes. course isn't taken lightly. he's flirtatious. if your TA is decent enough, you will be able to easily receive an A grade
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: effective lecturer, but class can seem long haha. he gives many extra credit opportunities, gives partial credit, & genuinely seems to want u to succeed. hws can be hard and long, but office hours seem to help others. u can zoom into class. midterm 1 is hard, but midterm 2 is fine. would totally recommend taking him. best professor i had this sem!

One of the best professors that I have had a Tech so far. He was engaging and really knowledgeable about the subject. If you put in effort he really wants you to succeed so he gives a lot of extra credit to those that deserve it. Learned a lot and might have been one of the most applicable classes I have taken yet.

If you're looking for an easy A and a kind, understanding professor, I highly recommend her. She knows this class isn't a top priority for many students and is flexible with deadlines. You can miss up to 6 lectures without penalty. Do all the work, and you'll likely finish with an A or even a 100.

Easy class if you are looking for an A. Practically forces you to participate, and if you do not discuss, she will probably sit there and look at you awkwardly until you do. busy work just to teach you something you alr know. passive sometimes with ambiguous expectations. Just take her if you need a class you do not wanna stress about.

Easy class, boring topic. Felt like she gave a lot of busy work but everything was essentially a completion grade. Great if you're looking for an easy A. She is pretty flexible with project topics so you can try and make the class what you want.

She is a really good professor. As long as you do the work you should get a 100. She is also super understanding and will allow you to get an extension on assignments without needing a reason she will just give you it if you ask.
Grades by completion. Very easy class, just kind of boring. Very kind and caring, allowing extensions sometimes

Passionate about his lectures but can come across as condescending and passive aggressive at times. Made comments that felt unnecessary and even rude. Would chastise students for missing lecture or for submitting assignments close to the deadline. Lectures were interesting though.

Gibson is unlike most bio profs - there is no memorization. We learn some concepts, but read a lot of current papers in the genetics field and discuss them. This class is all about changing the way you think. You write paper critiques and learn mostly how to think like a scientist. He expects a lot but if you but in the work, it's rewarding
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gibson is a kind professor who aims to give most students As and Bs. It's obvious he actually cares about lectures, and he teaches pretty well. I think he does teach the class more like a graduate level class, but it's not too bad. You don't have to try to hard to get an A.
Amazing and enthusiastic guy. Always enjoyed his lectures and his infinite help in office hours.
Scott is a great professor. He cares about his students. When you talk with him, you can see his genuine passion for teaching this course.
Great professor! He's funny in the sense that he's a big nerd, best type of guy. Great class, learned a lot. Would take again and recommend Scott heartily.

Decent professor! This class mixed a bit of stat-ish and linear (matrices and stuff) and every unit was confusing for me but she made it bearable. Her lectures are boring and from the textbook but they were useful on the tests. Homework worksheets are done in studio so there isn't any work to do outside of class. Questions are answered thru piazza

While Christina's lectures were not the most helpful and were sometimes confusing, her office hours were very helpful and her exams were straightforward for the most part. She is a very caring person but at times, she did make this course harder than it needed to be with her quizzes. But she is not a bad professor nor was the class  difficult.

Her lecture style was straightforward and followed the textbook very closely. Most of the weekly homework questions are done in studio so if you go, there isn't much work outside of class. Exams are fair and there's an assignment to get extra credit on all of them. Overall was a good professor that cared about her students.
Class is very easy if you pay attention. Three tests, highest exam weighted the most. Do not need to worry about this class as long as you put the time in.

While she is a great person, the bottom line is she makes an easy class hard. Lectures are confusing and unclear, and answer keys or work are sometimes wrong. It was a disorganized course (TAs never knew what was happening), and the exams aren't too bad, but the quizzes can tank your grade. If you can wait and take it with a different prof, do.

Not accessible outside of class at all because she claimed that she "can't tutor students one-on-one." Her own answer keys for her own practice sheets would be wrong, & TAs didn't even know what they were doing sometimes too. There's barely support for this class with PLUS or Math Lab sessions. Would never take her class again, terrible professor.

While she is a nice person, she's not the best teacher. She somehow makes the concepts ten times more difficult than they need to be. Her lectures are long and straight out of the textbook. She is not very accessible outside of class either.
Taking Prof. Giannitsi was like a breath of fresh air. She's happy to explain concepts several times and she's always clear about what will be on the exams.

Christina really cares about her students, and it is shown through how she is always willing to make time for them. I also enjoy her lectures because she doesn't go too fast and always tries to make sure that what she is saying is comprehensible. If you have to take this course, I'd recommend Christina.
Doesn't give overly difficult exams, HW reflects exam content

Dr. Gilman is a great teacher. She is very understanding, gives great feedback, and tries to set you up for success throughout the semester. I tend to ask a lot of questions and she was more than happy to help. If you are looking for a good intro level teacher, Danielle Gilman is the way to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilman was easily one of my favorite English educators I've had. She is deeply caring and gives incredible feedback for how you could grow as a communicator. The class topic was over Archival Narratives but her choice of artifacts still made it fun and engaging.

Dr. Gilman is, by far, one of the most caring professors at GT. All of her assignments have very clear rubrics, and she always provides feedback on why she docked certain points. The three artifact projects can be completed the day of if you devote all your time to it. Will grant one extension on a major project. Very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor so far at Tech. She's very engaging and an amazing lecturer. Be sure to participate in class, never skip discussion posts, and just do your assignments on time and you'll be perfectly fine! Projects (3 in total) weren't hard at all and I absolutely loved doing them.

I kinda breezed through the class without learning much of anything. Nothing was ever hard, it was just time-consuming. I will say that Dr. Gilman is a stickler for proper MLA formatting and I got a few points docked a couple of times because of that. Since the class was online, I never met her but I got through it, so all is well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very good choice for ENGL 1102. She is passionate for her topic and is a reasonable grader and understands that English is not the top priority for many students here. Once again, a very good choice.

Dr. Gilman is a fantastic English professor! I had her for both English 1101 and 1102, and the class is a little more difficult in 1102. She grades pretty tough on assignments, but all assignments come with extensive feedback, so you will definitely improve. Overall, she is a very considerate professor who gives very interesting assignments.

Dr. Gilman is an awesome English professor! She does not overwork her students and ensures that students have sufficient time to complete assignments and projects. Dr. Gilman has adjusted to online teaching well, I recommend taking her class to any student!
Loved this class!! Not a ton of work and we didn't have to write traditional essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilman was a fantastic English 1101 professor! Although there are quite a few assignments, they're spaced out well, and the artifacts/projects themselves are much more engaging than your standard essay. In addition, the selection of readings was diverse, and overall, it is a very different English class, especially compared to high school.

SO many papers and no feedback given. Takes forever to put grades on canvas. The class was in person for the first few weeks and then transitioned to online-only after she got sick and then broke her leg. I felt bad for her but she should have had a TA or something.

Very inaccessible and has no clear set of instructions for assignments. You do get to revise after but she is super slow at grading so you basically have to wait till the very end to revise. Her grading is very random and hard to justify, seems like she doesn't even read the assignments you submit. Class is easy though.

Very inaccessible. Took the class online (asyncrohous) and I had to email her several times before she responded. No rubrics for assignment, just a sheet explaining what you should do. Makes it hard to know what her expectations are. Long readings that you get quizzed on.

Solid teacher but the class is very assignment heavy. There is a set of readings and an easy quiz most weeks. Additionally, there is basically an assignment every week. The assignments are graded tough, but there is opportunity for revision, and the grades of the quizzes balance it out.
Does not give clear directions for assignments and is inaccessible. Would not recommend.

Writing heavy. The textbook is barely used. Easy A's on homework. She likes to give feedback & answer questions to help. As long as you put in effort, you'll most likely get an A/B. Class time is used for activities, peer review, and individual work time. She allows deadline extensions. Pretty laidback, especially during the online transition.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gignac is really great at teaching and emphasizes understanding the material, not just memorizing formulas. I learned a lot in his class, more so than in other math classes I've taken at Tech. He gives lots of practice problems and practice tests, but his tests are still very difficult. He gives lots of MyMathLab assignments.

People complain about how difficult Dr. Gignac's class is but in reality his tests are pretty easy and straight forward if you just do his practice tests. Gignac is an amazing lecturer, the best I've had in my three semesters at Tech. If you just take the time to actually understand the material getting an A is very doable.

Dr. Gignac is an excellent lecturer. He gives a great basis for topics and brings really good examples to class. He is also very engaging. However, the level of difficulty and student expectations he has are very inconsistent. He definitely made the class a touch more difficult than I imagined. Would recommend if you're willing to put in some work.
Most thoroughly engaging teacher I have had. Truly cares about student success.

He does speak English which is rare and definitely a plus for math teachers at tech. His lectures are pretty good, but his haughty comments get annoying. Tests are unfairly difficult in the fact that he gives practice tests which are worlds of a difference easier than the real ones and then gets  mad that students didn't do well.

He is very passionate about his teaching and wants you to learn. However, it is a difficult course and his lectures can be confusing at times. There's homework, just like any other math class. His tests are difficult, so study lots. Also, there is a quiz every week, which in some ways is good because you don't forget the material.
Great professor and was extremely clear and thorough. please do all the homework and extra homework! would take again.

He really cares about his students and is by far the best math professor I've ever had. You have the know and understand the material if you wanna do well on his tests and quizzes. They aren't easy but if you study, there's no reason why you can't make an A. He gives really good lectures so make sure you come to class!!

This (Fall2014) was Prof. Gignac's 1st semester at Tech. His lectures were extremely clear and thorough and he made the subject interesting. Would definitely recommend him as one of the the most enjoyable and impressive instructors I've had thus far at Tech.

Gignac is a really nice guy and gives good lectures for an 8 AM time slot. That being said, when most of the class made an A on his first test he got upset because he didn't have a good distribution and made all of the following tests about 5 times harder. He did curve the class at the end though, which I guess sort of made up for it.

Rigor can be described as a lot for a humanities course, but it is a good option if you are already interested in linguistics. Sometimes struggles to keep class quiet but is always open to feedback. Mandatory attendance for weekly quizzes. Very kind + relatable for younger students! Would reccommend
She's very open to changing course structure based on student feedback. Clearly passionate about the topic and is open to improving the course to help students as a whole.
If I went to Stanford for my PhD to only make 90k I'd make the course dreadful for the students too. She expects us to memorize 400 slides per test, piquing on the littlest of details. DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amount of effort required for a humanities elective is insane. Also the content is unintuitive and the class feels overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Too much work for a humanities class.

Im being real: if you're taking this just to fill a humanities requirement, don't. If you want a chill A, this isn't it. Expect ~1 hr of homework, strict on-time attendance (she starts immediately), and quizzes. It's linguistics at a STEM school but not easy only take it if you're ready to put in real work for an A. Plan accordingly and manage time

I was a happy girl before taking this class. If you are not religious, pick one and pray for your sanity. I used to love to speak languages and communicate with my peers, but after taking this course with Professor glass, i went mute.

She was super nice and genuinely passionate about the subject. You don't have to go to class except once a week for quizzes so make sure to attend for those. Homework takes a long time, but there aren't very many. The exams are straightforward, and the portfolios boost your grade. There is no cumulative final exam."

Professor Glass is overall a fine professor. However, beware of the class. Each tests covers 200-275 slides of information and all of it is expected to be memorized, sometimes very specific questions are asked about very subtle points hidden somewhere in the slides. 1-2 hours per homework, 6 hr study for test = A. Topics range beyond linguistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear syllabus with grading criteria. Textbook was optional. Weekly in class quizzes---not too hard. Usually weekly homework, not too bad. If you use the study guides she provides, the exams are straightforward, no surprises. Good prof, answers emails and in-class questions.

Good at explaining, but not a good professor personally. Harshly grades/treats students she does not really like. During office hour, I asked for advice for homework, but she responded pretty rudely that I should put whatever I think is plausible. Secured a fair grade by overworking. It was a nightmare, and I will def avoid her in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took LING 4813, studying semantics and pragmatics. She does a wonderful job of distilling all the knowledge from the textbook into easily read handouts, and has a wonderful setup for the final paper as well. Each day I looked forward to learning some new tidbit about language that I had known about but never known the name of. Great class!

Really interesting subject mater. Dr. Glass is kinda all over the place in her lectures but the weekly quizzes are easy and self graded. The HW and tests are also pretty straight forward. I would take this class again and would recommend it to anyone else as an easy humanities.

In terms of HW, expect to spend 1-2 hours. Lenient with deadlines so just submit before grading starts. Very relaxed, we stop working on quiz if most people are finished, then we start grading our own quizzes. Sometimes we do in-class activities, which could be fun. Lectures can be confusing as she speakers fast. To enjoy the class, participate.
Dr. Glass is obviously very passionate about linguistics, and will teach you a lot if you are willing to learn. Very understanding with the online structure!

Highly accessible and gave very clear and helpful feedback. Willing to work with students to make the assignments doable and engaging. The class had unusually low enrollment, but I'm very glad I didn't drop it. There were many assignments, but they ended up being very fun and covered a wide range of fields and topics in which to apply linguistics.

Dr. Glass makes EAS 1600 a breeze. You don't learn any lecture material in class, but instead watch videos online that cover the content. You do two projects, one on Exoplanets and another on Wikipedia in class, but everything is really easy. No tests and one easy lecture quiz a week with no time limit. 

Amazing professor and amazing person.

Dr. Glass cares a great deal about the content and does her best to make the lectures engaging and interesting with activities and participation assignments. The course is very easy and the assignments can be completed while sitting in lecture, since attendance is required. The EAS/Honors section was project based but the projects were very short.

Dr. Glass will be very happy with you if you are enjoying the course and are participating. I was in the Majors/Honors section, so I was with people who wanted to be there. The class overall is easy with a weekly quiz and two interesting solo projects during the year. Both projects were fun and felt satisfying to do. Answer questions when she asks!

I love Dr. Glass! You can tell she really cares about the topics discussed and loves what she does. I would highly recommend this class if you like Earth science. There were no exams, only asynchronous lectures to watch outside of class and discuss with activities in class .

Dr. Glass is overall a great teacher. The class is not that difficult to earn an A in, and you end up learning a lot about environmental science in the process. Very accessible outside of class and ample opportunities for extra credit. Lectures are pretty good, and the grading criteria is very clear. Would recommend.

Boring lectures but very easy class. Only 100 clicker questions are required and you dont have to physically be in class to answer them (you can answer online from anywhere). Tests questions are taken from previous tests and study guide questions. The video project was fair, just start early. LOTS of extra credit opportunities for an easy A.

Decent lecturer for EAS & a really nice woman. Provided her previous exams from the last time she taught the course; your exams often have the exact same questions. You can exempt the final! If you take the final, it's mainly the most missed q's from midterms. She held a review session for the final where she basically told us what was on it.

Fluid Mechanics is a difficult class, but Dr. Glezer's lectures are helpful and include plenty of relevant examples. The 45 min exams are stressful, but not overly complex. Grading scheme is extremely friendly, allowing you to drop the two lowest test scores (can exempt final). Homework solutions are posted with the assignment. Would recommend.

Handwriting was actually atrocious, we spend most of each class asking him what things say. His tests have too short of a time limit just so he can spend 10 minutes lecturing after we finish the test, you could go into the test feeling good and walk out confused if you even know the subject, Better than some professors friends had so ig worth it

Despite Dr. Glezer's incredibly stressful 30-minute exams, you can't help but like him thanks to his clear and interactive lectures, and great sense of humor. His fluids course is far from easy, but you will definitely learn and enjoy it.

really fast lecturer, but lectures are well organized and lots of content covered every lecture. he has horrible handwriting though so be prepared for 5 minutes of every class dedicated to questions of what a word on the screen is. exams are difficult, but similar enough to hw. doing hw and studying lecture examples is key to the class

He is a fast, smart teacher but he knows his stuff. He is kind of mean towards students, but his lectures are structured pretty well. His tests are tough, and are one prob worth 70 points and T/F. I would not have passed this class without the TA who is leaving after this year. Take with caution but his class is manageable if you put in the work.

Fluid Mechanics is a tough class. Dr. Glezers lecures are at times very helpful and interesting, but other times are very hard to follow. 2 Exams and a Finals make up the vast majority of the class grade which can be tough. Pop quizzes are not too hard. Homework can only hurt your grade.

Dr. Glezer is very knowledgeable professor and a good lecturer. However, his grading system is based only on 6 quizzes which are 20 minutes. The quizzes are often tricky and difficult to complete in the allotted time. He also assigns homework that can only hurt your grade. Aside from that, he is one of the better fluids professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fluids is one of the toughest classes at Tech. Dr. Glezer teaches fluids every fall, and he is good lecturer. He has a great understanding of fluid mechanics as it is the primary focus of his research. He can assume that students know more about fluids before taking this class. He can also be condescending about not getting concepts immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Glezer is one of the best professors I have had at Tech. Let me be clear: Fluids is HARD. Plain and simple. Dr. Glezer focuses his teaching on the concepts behind fluid mechanics, which makes his class difficult. But he is extremely clear in his lectures on what will be tested.
His tests were pretty annoying. You had to memorize many terms for the group of SDGs that were being tested on. Hopefully he changes that soon. Very woke class

Class is not super hard, however it is very tedious. Lots of homework, study guides, and projects, and lectures can be very boring. However, I will say taking the class brings a sense of community amongst your peers and after each long project you always leave satisfied with your work. Dr. G always listens to student feedback. Great professor.

GT2803 is quite a bit of work for an elective course, but Dr. Gleason does his very best to make it manageable for students. He regularly asked for feedback and was very lenient when it came to late work. It is important to study for tests, but with much of the grade based on the Grant Proposal, as long as you put in work, you can make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gleason is a nice guy, but his lectures are hard to sit through. If your major isnt BME, its hard to feel at all connected to the material. The tests are hard and based on niche facts, but there are other grades to balance it out. Most of the class is based on writing a grant proposal, so its important to have a good group and actually try.

Everything on the tests/final was from his recorded videos rather than class lectures. The amount of work is more than it should be for an elective class. The group projects make up most of the grade, but we did not get any feedback on how the grades were calculated. The thing I liked was the people.

Mr. Gleason is an okay teacher. His lectures can be dry, but there's plenty of resources to get through the work. There is a lot of work though and the group projects can be frustrating because if you've got bad teammates, there's nothing you can do. Other than that, the class was fairly easy and okay.

This professor's class was boring and difficult to stay awake in. He gives so much homework it's insane. Not one topic in the course is actually interesting or useful for any degree at tech. DO NOT DO GLOBAL LEADERSHIP or this course. He sucks at lecturing and clearly has a "white savior" complex. He seems like he's trying to fix the third world.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, and gives good vibes.

Dr. Gleason taught this course with Dr. Ethier and they switched off. You learn the material by watching his pre recorded lectures outside of class and in class you do problem solving sets. His lecture videos were very clear and the PSS reinforced the material well. You have a final project as well that buffers your grade

You will do A LOT of work in his class. We spent the first few weeks analyzing this 10-page grant some students last year wrote, and then we were organized into groups of 3-4 where we ALSO wrote  a 10-page grant doing our OWN unguided research. Not very "leadershippy" but whatever. If you do the work expect a difficult but guaranteed A or high B.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. G is a great professor and an even more excellent human being. If you do go into the LLC, be prepared for a lot of work for this class, but nothing is graded very harshly. On most assignments, the lowest grades are 85-88 and if you turn in all your deliverables on time, you should get an A. Classes can get boring, but nothing terrible.
Rudy gets a bad rap but he is a great teacher. He is understanding and gave my class many extensions. There is a lot of writing though.

AVOID!!!  Class taken as an elective and is anything but that. If thinking about doing global leadership DO NOT, the housing is not worth the agony and pointless suffering that this class causes. Goes into the center of the classroom because he has no control. Worst class ever. I sob every time I think about rotting in this class or doing its work

GT2803 it's supposed to be a free class where everybody can get A's but it actually isn't. you will get more homework in this class than any other class that you will take in freshman year. I spent more time doing work in this class than physics and linear algebra combined. He has insane white savior complex and the lecture quizzes are impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unclear assignments with unclear grading criteria. Unnecessary amounts of busy work. Going to this class makes me want to drop out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Gleason is the best.

It was his first time teaching this course, and it wasn't organized at all. We never got through all the SDGs due to the lack of organization. The grant project could have been beneficial, but he didn't give any feedback, relying on peer reviews to grade the overall project. The grant itself was a lot of work.

Honestly, just do the extra credit and don't attend the exam. He had an "algorithm" to assess our grants, which basically meant he took our peer review grades and spat them back out, and a lot of the reviews were meaningless evaluations.  

He's a nice guy but I just don't think he has time to teach or actually mark a 120 person class.

*took GT2803* Great guy and was willing to work with us when changing deadlines. Group projects were a bit of a pain, mainly because of the content we had to research & write on. Then we would have to read at least 3 other grants and review them. Lectures could be a bit dry sometimes, but I'm glad I took the class. I learned something new everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rudy sucks, he will test you on the hardest 5% of every topic and you will leave the class wondering why your brain no longer works, only to realize that it was his awful teaching that made you feel inferior. Furthermore, he's the most unorganized man not only at tech, but probably in the greater Atlanta metropolitan area.
On tests lots of points were taken off for slight mistakes. The amount of homework he gives out is not fit for a two credit class and is very difficult. He also does not respond to emails often.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Gives hard homework, his test problems are often different from what you see in his lectures. He really tries to stretch your understanding of the subject. He curves the overall grade. Thought I had a solid B, surprisingly came out with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Super nice guy but the class is extremely unorganized and has essentially no resources other than class notes. If you have him you better have chegg. He spent an entire class period attempting to go over the answer to a homework problem and still hadn't figured it out by the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall not terrible, but points taken off on homework will wreck your grade, in addition to getting tons of points off for slight mistakes on tests. Went into the final with around an 80% meaning no chance of getting an A, but I guess I did well enough on it that he still gave me an A. Won't respond to your emails. Doesn't post lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class covered diverse energy-centered topics. If you are interested in the subject - it gives a nice overview of technologies and  practical perspectives. Professor is nice and enthusiastic. Quite knowledgeable too. Highly recommended.

Some  of the guest lecturers were truly excellent, but the course overall was very poorly designed. Dr. Yushin's part was weak in comparison to those of the other professors who taught. The course had important material but I could not give it a higher rating because the main professor (Yushin) was not organized and taught poorly.

Dr. Yushin is very knowledgeable in various aspects of electrical, magnetic, and optical properties. Very enthusiastic about the topic and connected everything to practical applications. Good sense of humor. But I wish we spent less time spent on the Schrödinger equation. Quizzes and tests were also very hard... But I enjoyed the class a lot!
Really fun class (the best I've taken so far). But tests and quizzes are not easy. Grades are fair. An optional movie project was most enjoyable to work on.
He is an alright  professor.  Tests are hard, but he holds review sessions and gives out study guides that are really helpful. READ THE TEXTBOOK.
great examples on each topic
a good one
Fair & cool
among the best young teachers @ Georgia Tech
very very reasonable curves. if you go to the review sessions you're almost guaranteed an A in the class

He's one of the better profs for MSE2001.  He really knows his stuff, and he's generally very approachable.  He grades very fairly (with very reasonable curves). He really helps you prepare for tests by holding review sessions and giving out a study guide/tips before each test that basically tell you exactly what's on the test.Read the book though!
interested in the subject, available for Q/A, one of the better profs
Really poor lectures and the professor gets upset when students ask him questions. Likes to talk about himself a lot. Learned very little from his class.
probably the worst professor at Tech. Makes mistakes during the lecture, contradicts himself, and usually has trouble answering questions. I got an A in the class but did so by reading the book.

Prof. Rix teaches lots of examples and he is very clear in what he teaches and what he expects from his students. I really enjoyed his class.  HW problems are great for test preparation. He is always available for questions. I wish I had more professors like him!

I learn by solving examples, so this class was perfect for me. The entire class is basically solving different examples. He understands the material and makes sure you do to. One of my favorite teachers.
Does lots of examples.  The tests are very fair, but not easy.

Prof. Gopal is brilliant and caring. Lectures are fast, but the content is great and grading is simple: HW (20% - layup), Project (30%), 1/2 tests (25%), Cases (20% - layup), Participation (5%). Tests allow a 1-sided cheat sheet. Outside work is needed for the pace, but material isn't hard. Highly recommend her!
Her lectures are very fast-paced. Her quizzes are hard but she lets you use a cheat sheet. The group project is a little difficult. Overall, not too bad if you try.

Very interesting class. Fast lecturer, and content is often on long (50-100 slide) powerpoints. However, the structure of the class makes it easily manageable. There are 2 tests, only graded on your highest, and can have a 1 page cheat sheet. Group project and report is 35% of your grade, but it is basically a check the boxes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I dont think that the class is structured very well, the stuff we learn in class doesnt build on top of each other and is very disconnected from the group project that we have to work on throughout the entire semester. Class feels like a grad class based solely on what she wants from you but doesnt give the notes or lectures to justify her demands.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gopal has no type of direction to her class. quizzes are over 6-7 poweporints & the smallest things in 200 slide powerpoints. only had one thing our grade book for the whole semester which made me think my grade was fine. She put everything in at once 3 days before finals day and my grade dropped 10 points. Had no idea I was doing bad.

the grading is convoluted, she breaks down participation into like three different parts with qualifications for each one, shes not a bad person but a bad professor, the lectures are a drag and studying for quizzes makes you feel so helpless because she doesn't tell you what we can expect despite the study material spanning 200+ slides...

Does not grade anything, my grade has been the same since the 3rd week of classes despite there being only 3 weeks until the course is over, hard to estimate what my grade possibly could be and if I could get points off on certain assignments because she does not post anything. Take her post 2025, she's new at this so it's not good to take her now.

Quizzes are based on 200+ PPT slides, review quizzes are misleading & based on pre-existing finance know-how than what is taught in-class, which made it hard for my non-finance major friends. No guidance on the term project just a "you should have started your projects by now," no check points as other professors who assign term projects might do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are really boring and honestly don't help. class is extremely fast paced so i would recommend doing A LOT of work outside of class. he just recycles hw, learning catalytics, and textbook questions for the tests so they're pretty predictable
Highly recommend not taking the class with Goodisman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr.Goodisman is a not good at explaining in lectures. He talks and talks about stuff ,but never points them out on the slides and never give examples of the concept to help us . Exams is content heavy. He never answers emails . He goes straight to the LC in one slide. Expect you to know everything by heart. He is very passionate about this class.
He is just hard for no ready, exams are so long and hard, he is a nice professor but he take his class so seriously

Incredible professor. The B+ was mostly due to not enough time spent reviewing concepts. Do well on the tests (shouldn't be too hard with his excellent lectures, ESPECIALLY comparatively) and you're set.

Professor Mayer provided a lot of methods for students to learn from. Linear Algebra is quite a tough class, especially if you are not strong in math. he's actually based

reviews.comment: I had Professor Mayer for 1554 and now 2552, he is by far the best professor I have ever had. Super caring about his students and is a great lecturer. The content is difficult but he makes is easy to understand. Grading is always pretty generous if you try your best. As long as you keep up with the content, he makes the class a relatively easy A.

Guys I dont know what else to say, tell your friends all about this prof or keep it a secret. This will be one of the best math professors you can find at GT. Ensure you have a slot before telling your friends, dont want to get waitlisted for this course.

Surprisingly this was the easiest math course I have ever taken
Very good class overall

He is an amazing professor and will give you what you need to make an A. Solid 10/10 professor who made learning math fun even online.

This was one of my favorite teachers. Teacher was helpful and caring. Make sure to read the textbook or it will be much harder to understand things. Quizzes and tests weren't too bad though. Overall an enjoyable class.
Do yourself a favor and take Dr. Mayer for Diff Eq.

Professor Mayer is a true Gem, would recommend any math class with him simply because he really cares about what and who he is teaching. Mayer was an ok prof but the class was very tough + most of the material had to be learned through the supplement videos. The tests were brutal, but I recommend going through the textbook and attending studio (the practice exams were way easier than the real tests). Some of the negative criticism in here can be justifiable, though, none of them impede your ability to learn; rather, I think the grade people got pushed them to giving a 1. Mayer is a great teacher: kind, caring, and a knowledgeable communicator. I had him in Spring 2020 when we had to transition to online. He was a very caring professor and great lecturer both in person and online. MATH 1554 can be a challenging course for many new students. Mayer does a decent job at helping everyone get adjusted. reviews.comment: Unarguably the best teacher I've had in my life. This man is so dedicated. You can tell he's really passionate about what he does and cares about the students. He's not there to catch you off guard, but rather he does anything to see his students succeed. My first college professor experience and I love it!
Best professor ever! He even spends time helping students at odd hours like midnight on Piazza or even discords!

Took the summer online diff eq course, and Dr. Mayer's lectures were super easy to follow. He's really responsive to emails and piazza posts, too! Going to his office hours helped me understand a lot, and he's just a genuinely caring and funny professor. Take him if you can!

Linear algebra is hard and boring but this man is great. I took his 8AM so ended up missing alot of the classes. Prof Mayer posts his notes online so you will never be too pressured to attend the class. Overall a great guy!

I love this man with all my heart. Best math professor I've ever had. He made the class fun and entertaining even as an 8am (totally worth it). I would highly recommend him. He is also the coordinator for this course (as of Spring 2020) so he always knows what's up. Very caring too.

Greg is a caring and hardworking professor. That said, he makes quite a few mistakes during his lectures, but he always finds a way to correct himself later. His test are of medium difficulty, but are similar to the previous exams he gives you for practice. Would highly recommend him over any other linear prof!

He was one of the best lecturers I've ever had and truly cares about the subject a lot. That being said, the tests were pretty hard and usually had C averages but he ended up lowering grade boundaries by 9 points (81 was an A, 71 was a B and so on) so most people's grades turned out fine.

Dr. Mayer actually cares about his student's success in linear algebra. I found his lectures to be very informative and didn't really need to use the textbook to do well in the class (though I know people who used the textbook a lot). The exams were not too hard and were relatively similar to practice exams given before. Plus he's hilarious.

I had him for MATH 1554. Dr. Mayer is a great and kindhearted professor, but I didn't personally like the style of his lectures. You can't go wrong with Dr. Mayer.

I had a great time in this class, and didn't really have to learn a bunch of content outside of class. I found the review sheets and practice problems to be really helpful, since they are pretty much exactly the same as the tests. Great professor, fun class!

I basically never went to class or recitation and taught myself the class through mymathlab practice and youtube and it worked fine for me, but your mileage may vary. There are in person and online office hours so if you have questions he's super easy to reach.

reviews.comment: Solid choice for a teacher -- much better then other available options when I had to take classes. Good teacher, gets ideas across pretty well. Wants students to succeed. Great prof for linear algebra. Lectures are good but recitation and piazza are more useful in my opinion. Understand the concepts and you will be fine. Tests are predictable. He stays up late to answer questions on piazza.

I took this class as a Distance Student. Dr. Mayer is very entertaining and cares a lot. I watched all the lectures, did the worksheets in recitation, did the homework and practice tests and had an easy A. At first, I found the class difficult, but you'll realize that the tests are fairly predictable if you just attend class and do the work.

Dr. Mayer definitely care and felt accessible. The homework is very reasonable, usually didn't take longer than half an hour per assignment. Tests did get harder towards the end of the course. But he is more than willing to give partial credit. He gives a "sample midterm" before each test, which is very similar to what the test will be like. 8AM.
I freaking love Dr. Mayer; he is the funniest prof I've had in a while and is so caring! :)

He is a pretty easy grader and usually gives partial credit on tests. He's also pretty nice and if you ever forgot to do homework on time, you can email him and he'll probably reopen the assignment for a day or two. His lectures are pretty dry and not super interesting, but worth going to if you don't want to learn the material on your own.

Dr. Mayer is pretty awesome, easily the nicest professors I've had thus far. The test difficulties varied greatly (90 on one test and 50ish on another- even though I studied hard for both and felt I was prepared). He does some participation stuff throughout the semester. The quizzes are pretty short and straight forward.

Very nice, caring professor. He was often available for extra help and to regrade tests if you requested and was generous about giving points back. Homework wasn't too overwhelming and he would give extensions if you asked. Lectures weren't super dry; he makes some offhand comments that are entertaining but he mostly stays on task

I took his linear algebra class online, and I definitely recommend him! Dr. Mayer is a fun and extremely nice person. If his lectures aren't clear enough, he's always willing to help students outside of class, and will stay up late answering Piazza questions. If you understand the homework and practice test, you should be fine.

I love Greg. His lectures weren't always the best, but he was super helpful and nice if you ever asked him for any assistance. He is also rather hilarious. The tests were very easy. There were 4 regular tests, and a noncumulative final. I would highly recommend taking a class with Greg if you can.

Dr. Greg Mayer is a hilarious, well-respected, and incredibly kind guy. He teaches very well and at an appropriate pace, and though the course content may be difficult, he makes it reasonably easy to follow. He is highly accessible during office hours AND VERY HELPFUL IN THEM, and the tests are EXACTLY like the lecture and homework. He's very nice!

He is a light hearted professor who is dedicated to his students. He explains topics fairly well and he is very available to his students. He even does extra study sessions. However, he does make a lot of mistakes in class. The class has homework but its not unbearable. The tests are fairly easy. If you can take the distance learning section.

Dr. Mayer is a good professor who makes it easy to succeed. The lecture slides are easy to follow, especially if you print them out beforehand. There's a decent amount of online homework, but he understands if you submit something late. The only downside perhaps is that there are only four quizzes before the final, though they aren't terribly hard.

Dr. Greco is a not a reat professor. He goes on so many tangents and never finishes the lectures slides. They basically made attendance mandatory last semester, so it was such a waste of time to go to lecture. I ended up having to watch Alicia's lectures on my own time to get all the content.

Greco cares deeply about student feedback, but his lectures barely cover the course content and include plenty of jokes and sample problems. You will need to do a substantial amount of external learning to be prepared for tests. Some extra credit is helpful,     but he is not super accessible by email.

Grading: 3 Tests + Final (best test 20%, middle 15%, worst 5%, final 25%), 25% lab, 10% misc (attendance is 6%). Lecture: 6/10; Passion: 10/10; Communication: 9/10; Flexibility: 9/10; Test Prep: 9/10 Quirks: Bad handwriting, tangents, poor slides. Recommendation: Go to lecture to do clicker questions for practice, but get notes from elsewhere.

PHYS2212 is a difficult yet doable class. No matter who you take, you will get the same boring lectures that end up going off topic. Greco tries his best to make lectures "fun", but his definition of "fun" is not really fun. The only true way to learn in this class is to watch Alicea's videos and to do as many practice exams as possible.

He needs to change the way Physics 2 is taught at GT. Attendance should NOT be mandatory if you're gonna be such a picky professor for test rubrics. Really you can fully understand a concept and still be unable to produce much work on a test that counts for credit. DONT TAKE HERE TAKE SOMEWHERE ELSE

He plays a very fun game where he will improve his style later on in the semester, but if you already fell behind, good luck. He is however half-decent at showcasing multivariable topics for physics. If you want a serious and fun treatment of E&M, take PHYS 2232. If you want a basic treatment of E&M, take another professor!

SAY NO TO GRECO!! Georgia Tech literally made him apologize for how badly he was handling our physics 2 section this semester. I learned way more watching Alicea's videos, but it sucks because lectures were 1hr 15 minutes with mandatory attendance. I only missed point solutions about 4 times and lost out on a part of my grade. Save urself.

Cant slime him out because both of us could have done better. I feel as if I had to put 3x as much work in compared to my friends who are "good" at physics, and Dr. Greco didn't exactly make the feeling much easier. His lectures were pretty good tangents or not but I still feel like they were boring/uninteractive to the pt where I j gave up midsem

Greco is the LeBron of physics 2. Everyone giving him bad reviews because of tangents or the great AWS incident (which made me mad too) just need to lock in harder ✌️😭. This guy is the goat and made my first semester fun.
Course coordinator for 2212 so knows what's going on. Decent lecturer and funny guy but did a lot of learning on my own

I used to be a physics major, then I took this class and changed asap. The lectures were messy, there are about 200 students per section, and the outside of class work is insane. Expect homework, labs, homework previews, GPS problems, and an insane amount of studying. Teaching yourself won't cut it, you have to know everything inside and out. :/

Dr. Greco is not for everyone, as he goes on a lot of tangents. I found him to be extremely effective, where he would introduce tough concepts and then work through a LOT of problems in class. Dr. Greco also announced to all sections the specific topics each exam covered and held extra review sessions for a month before the final. Amazing professor

Watch Alicea's lectures if you don't usually get physics first try. Greco dances around the most fundamental concepts and then acts shocked when we did bad on tests. Honestly this class would be 10x better if it wasn't such a big lecture size. Imho physics is a subject everyone learns differently, and everyone here doesn't want to acknowledge it.

physics at georgia tech obviously caters to students who are good at physics and are engineers. if you are not in that category, well, good luck. dr greco did not make it any easier, tests are complicated and designed in such a way that for each problem either you get it or you don't. no in between. feels like a class designed against students

try to get at least 100 on one of the tests, it will save ur grade. other than that dr greco is a fine lecturer, but i learned much more from aliceas vids and it sucked bc attendance still matters thru clickers. giving him grace bc I know i could've tried harder but this so called gen ed requires a lot of work if ur bad at physics, be warned. sucks
literally could care less about him going off topic, in fact it was decently nice to see a professor with humor. alicea
He was a good lecturer even though he went off topic a lot.

Pretty good lecturer, he went off topic often but made lecture intersting. The tests while some of them were hard had good partial credit that made them fair. Also all the people complaining about him not rescheduling the exam after the canvas outage are idiots. All the review materials were literally posted on Ed and there was no problem studying

Fun lecture. Won't stay on topic. Doesn't seem to care much about students: slow response on edStem + refused to move midterm for phys2212 when AWS (canvas) was down the day BEFORE and OF the test...ridiculous. When the test's average was low, they didn't slow down for test 3, it was ridiculously hard too!

Pretty bad lecturer and goes off topic quite often. Also does not explain any of the basic, fundamental concepts in class. He also takes a while to respond on ed for questions related to soon due dates. Makes the tests unnecessarily difficult and openly admits this to students. Very unorganized in terms of what is taught and what is tested on.

I took Greco in the Spring of 2025. He wasn't the greatest lecturer but he was a fair professor. He never asked for anything that would be unfair to his students, and I respected that he would show up 30+ minutes early to his lectures to have remedial lessons for his students that struggled with the 2212 concepts. All the hate seems undeserved.

My comment that I originally did seems to have disappeared, weird. Anyway, didn't hear any of the student out when canvas shut down the day before the test. He makes the tests extremely difficult. Then he scraps as little as possible to make the class for an exam average at a C. I dont understand why he is trying his hardest to make students fail?
Awful lecturer, does not explain concepts clearly and does not stay on topic.

He is actively deleting negative RMP comments. Inequitable reaction to global AWS outage despite every other major class moving their midterm. Ignored hours of requests for clarity on exam status, leaving many emotionally distressed.
So hype. What a guy. No notes.

Spent more time talking about bequeathing his skull and how he skipped class in undergrad and still got As than he did on teaching content. Also, he petitions negative reviews on RMP to get them taken down, so the rating you see is not an accurate representation of students' experiences.

I was preparing to write a poor review of Dr. Greco earlier this semester. However, after a few weeks, Dr. Greco switched to high gear. Following our first exam, he came one hour early every lecture and went over problems, an invaluable resource. Also, he held a final review session on a Sunday night. Many of the reviews on here are unfair.

Earlier this semester, I left a poor review of Greco. I've completely changed my mind about him. I've NEVER seen a professor put in effort like he did for our final review session. He also came into lecture an hour before, every single day, to help students. I thought he didn't care about students earlier on, but I couldn't have been more wrong.

Lectures weren't always on topic the whole time, but we didn't have any issues covering all the material. The tests are fair if you understand the material and the grading scheme is pretty forgiving. He really cares about his students doing well and is available a lot outside/before and after class.
Greco is a great lecturer, and makes sure everyone is always engaged. Physics 2 is a difficult class so to do well you have to lock in, and people hating on him need to lock in harder.

I'll be honest. There are things that Greco could do better (e.g. not go on tangents so often in class, make more detailed slides with greater material focus instead of history focused, etc.), but he did care about our success. He was helpful in office hours, email, and review sessions. If you make an effort to learn, you can at least get a B.

I took physics two this semester and was optimistic at first due to the grading scheme. However, I was wrong because Greco has review sessions only for his students, makes tests unreasonably hard with questions from researchers, and does not even give study materials like study guides to help us out. What a waste of time.

Greco did 2-3 practice problems through the full 16-week semester. He spent a lot of time on topics such as bequeathing his skull or how he got all As without studying in his undergrad rather than covering exam content, which leaves you wholly unprepared for his exams. He also posts incorrect GPS solutions & makes careless logistical errors. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I recommend skipping his class (getting point solutions code from friend in class) and learning from another professor's notes (Sachdev had incredible lecture notes). Greco is a funny guy but he yaps a ton so his lectures are not good.

Dr.Greco lectures well and is always excited to teach us. He truly cares about the performance of his students, so much so that he began to do practice sessions at 8 AM before lecture for students who need extra help. He's very helpful during office hours and is the professor you want to take physics 2 with.

Reviews of professor are unfair. Exams made by all of the professors, so that isnt just him. He isnt the best lecturer and he rambles a lot. He certainty isn't terrible, and I feel that the occasional ramble is helpful to break up the long lectures. He also is willing to show up early for struggling students, so I wouldnt call him lazy. Solid Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Funny guy, but his lectures don't always do a great job of explaining the content. The main concern would be that during lecture, nobody will have any questions, often because nobody knows what to even ask, but he will stare at the group for 5 minutes while nobody asks anything. Mostly reliant on topical videos to learn.

Professor Greco keeps the class engaging, but his tests can be tricky. The lectures aren't always the most helpful, so using resources like Unstuck ai for study prep is key. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course.
AVOID HIM AT ALL COST

Greco is an incredible physics professor. He's funny, knowledgable, and caring for his students. The exams can be hard, but I don't think he's doing it on purpose to intentionally make people fail. Labs were a joke but could help with understanding of the content. The grading scheme is very forgiving.

Edwin Greco is a terrible individual. His tests for Fall 2024 is extremely difficult comparing with other semesters. He gave excuses that you should be responsible for difficult exams with bad grades, although everyone did bad on exams. No curves given. He doesn't care about your grade or whether you can be successful in his class.

Do not take 2212 if greco is the coordinator (his name will show up on canvas as one of the instructors). Unbelievably difficult class and each exam got progressively more unfair. laughed off our frustrations with every single exam until one when our averages were so low that it was massively curved. Wait till Alicea is coordinator to take 2212.

Pros: Genuinely wants you to learn, accommodating, and passionate about Physics. Attendance is part of your grade, BUT you can replace it with other stuff.
Cons: Unreasonably difficult (relative to prior years), doesn't handle criticism well, and uses a very glitchy website for labs.

You can get an A, but be prepared to fight for your life for it.

He was the course coordinator for physics 2 this year and did a terrible job, imo. The tests were intentionally harder than in past years, with many questions unrepresentative to what we learned in lectures or GPS. The class was extremely discouraging to me and my friends taking the class. He was also rude when answering questions in Ed discussion.

He was the course administrator for Physics II this semester, and it was not a fun time. He would be very unclear or ignore comments in the EdDiscussion, and the tests this semester were incredibly difficult.

If I'm being blunt, worst teacher and administrator I've ever seen. Teaches nothing, rude and uncaring about the students, and tries his hardest the make the class the hardest on campus. The exams were a joke, as in they were impossible to complete, and his handling of the other course administrators is laughable. If you can skip this class, do it.

Very narcissistic individual that can't seem to admit things are his fault such as the lab submissions going down before the due date making it impossible to submit labs. Puts the burden on students for his own incompetence and will purposely make problems harder, require more work just to drive home a point.

Thought he would be great from this site, but he was just unfocused and rude in lectures. He would get really mad at people for not talking in the back of lecture, even though he has people participating in the front. Also, he would write exam problems that were intentionally unlike anything we had done, so no one understood them.

He obviously is very good at what he does and really knowledgable about anything physics related. Outside of that, can have an extremely off putting attitude and make a lot of sarcastic comments that can come off pretty rude. He has way too many students to manage that he could care less about you as an individual.
Professional Yapper.

He's an okay professor. He does yap a lot and gets off track at times, but it's probably needed for an early class. I recommend doing the practice tests a lot since exams are a good chunk of the grade. Labs are as easy as it gets here.

He was a good professor but there are too may students in the class for him to get to everyone's questions. Personally I felt like the practice exams helped the most for that class rather than the lectures.

Great lecturer. Sometimes goes off topic and gets behind other sections but still covers all the material in great detail and makes sure every student understands the content. Cares about the students and takes meaningful action to improve the class from post-exam/lecture feedback. Exams can be difficult but are collectively written by all profs.
Very good understanding of the course material and of his presence in the classroom; wanted to benefit students in the long run as much as possible.

He cares about his students a lot and encourages participation in the lecture. He made an effort to learn as many names as possible in the huge lecture which I thought was nice. Attendance isn't strictly mandatory but you get bucket points for answering clicker questions.

He is extremely entertaining and loves physics, but he also loves ensuring that students are enjoying it and being successful at it.
