Best thing he did was to go into an example in-depth and allow people to ask questions which was extremely helpful for specifics. The class had interesting video report labs but they could be annoying too. Easy class.

Do not take this class with Greco if you're not a physics buff. Spring 2023 session, all of his lectures were 90% useless - he would go off on tangents and waste a lot of time, putting his sections behind all of the others (subsequently, making HW more difficult, as the content was not covered before the due date). Tests *disproportionately* hard.

He literally could not care less about you. Your house could be on fire and he would still require you to go to recitation because it is not an illness or "family emergency". Take Alicea if you can because Greco is unorganized and annoying. The best way to study is past tests because the homeworks, labs, and lectures are no help whatsoever.
Actually ridiculous that this class wants 3x attendance and 1 useless lab a week

Goes off topic a lot and lectures tend to feel unhelpful, but honestly students don't give him enough credit of how familiar he is with the course. Tests are very difficult, but graders are generous so it evens out. Study and keep up with homework and it works out in the end.

Tests are difficult and had to somehow "know" something ON test day that wasn't mentioned before. Prof. Greco was helpful when I reached out to him outside of class, and he was EXTREMELY caring when it comes to accommodating students. He told me that he goes off class topics to grab the attention of students that zone out. Overall great professor.

Lectures were often irrelevant to the week's topic or we were behind by about two weeks worth of content from the homework. Lectures do not help with homework content. I pretty much just used my Physics 1 knowledge from high school to get by. Lab times are wasted on practice problems instead of actual labs. This class really sucks.

Horrible lectures, goes on irrelevant tangents, extremely disorganized class. I did not learn anything as I already took AP physics 1 in high school. Says he is available outside of class but never responds. Take physics 1 outside of this school, if possible.

One of the worst professors that I have ever had. He is not a good lecturer, often going on rants or tangents about unrelated topics. The exams and final are unreasonably difficult and are not at all based off the examples provided in class/GPS sessions. Avoid this professor at all cost.
Horrible lectures and ridiculous assignments

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SPRING. DO ANY OTHER SEMESTER BECAUSE ALICEA WILL BE THERE. She is the only good professor. BUT still, the tests do NOT match up to class examples, GPS's and any other practice they give. Studied for 4 days straight for the final, 9am-midnight, and I sat there befuzzled. Unless you are a dweeb, this class is impossible.

Greco would consistently fall behind compared to the other classes because he would get distracted and waste so much time. I found myself watching Alicea's videos to actually learn the material because Greco just simple does not cover all the content in lecture. I have heard that he is helpful in office hours though.
Greco is a hilarious teacher. He can get off-topic sometimes, but his lectures are pretty useful. The weekly assignments aren't bad, but the tests can get quite difficult.

Only people rating him high are the people that come to class knowing everything and just wanna have fun in class. Half of the session is him talking about stuff not related to the course and making jokes. I get it he's funny but his exams are not funny so just explain!!

If you learn the content before attending his lectures, this professor is for you. If not, you will have a hard time understanding on what he's doing since he also goes on tangents. So avoid this professor if you don't want to learn the content before attending his lectures.

Dr. Greco is an enthusiastic and caring professor. He will try his best to understand the issues of each student and is prepared to guide them every step of the way. He gives out enough practice material such that I felt confident with the learning topics, and he tailors the learning experience for each student. Overall, one of the best profs.

Taken as a hybrid course. Greco cares so much about students, but Physics 2 is gonna be hard no matter what. Taught as a reverse classroom, physics videos were posted and the lecture was focused on answering questions and working through problems. He has a tendency to veer off topic, but most of your grade is from tests/quizzes/labs so that's ok.
Really great and entertaining lectures, I had this as a 9:30 and didn't fall asleep even when it was online. Tests are HARD and when he says study STUDY. Office hours are super super helpful.

Labs are easy to finesse, old test problems are your friend, and gps was actually kind of helpful. First two tests are doable and very formulaic; I did not attend lecture but did watch edx videos and did the old test problems and I did fine. Overall not very hard but does require some effort to get an A. Pretty hard not to get a B.

I had a really bad experience with this class (Greco was not my prof but ran the course), so I reached out to him and shared how I felt after a certain interaction with an individual and he got back to me and was very kind. In a semester where I felt shut down in that class, he made me feel like I could finish strong and like I was supported.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Greco is very entertaining and knowledgeable! If you keep up with the class, the grading scale works in your favor. Old practice tests prepare you for the exams. Lab class, but the video lap reports were not too time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult but Greco made it better due to his informative lectures and helpful resources
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Makes physics fun to listen to. Pretty clear explanations. It is a lab course, so it takes some time, but it helps you learn if you put effort into all of it. He's also very receptive to feedback and accessible outside class. Physics is still hard, but he's one of the best you'll ever get.
Dr. Greco is a very knowledgeable professor who is very passionate about physics. However, his exams are quite tough and are definitely challenging compared to the homework.

Read the textbook before class on what is being covered, laid out in the syllabus. Take time and do the homework because it links to the relevant textbook section if you don't understand. It is a hard class but if you put in the time, study in groups, and go to the PLUS sessions you will be fine. Greco is better than most at keeping class engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Guy really seems to understand the feelings of students. Lectures are straight forward and fun. Greco is a funny guy and a good teacher. Felt there was too much work for lab reports, but it's a 4 credit class.

Greco is awesome, but his tests are tough. Review the material you just learned after every lecture to solidify it in your brain. The homework, labs, and other bucket activities are easy, but the tests are where it counts most.

Greco is great but taking physics at Tech in general kind of is the worst. Liked him a lot more than the professor I had for 2211. If taking 2212 online you'll have weekly mini-tests and a lot of the activities have you make a video. Great guy who does his best for students but is honest about the difficulty level and holds you to a high standard.

He's a pretty funny and caring dude, which is great. You'll get your standard introductory physics experience with him, including: *clicker questions *labs (not terrible) *group solving time *tests (weighted favorably) Overall, I'm very glad he was my physics professor, definitely recommend.

I took the SOAP class over the summer and believe an A in the class is achievable if you put in the work for the labs, look over the old exams and actually read the textbook. Theres a lot of presenting, which might seem weird at first but you will get the hang if it through out the semester. Having prior physics knowledge makes this class easier
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor for a hard class at Tech. During the whole COVID crisis, things got crazy but he always seemed concerned for our well-being and tried to make exams as fair and straightforward as possible.

I do not know how he is with his normal in person classes during the school year, but do NOT take his Summer online class (SOUP), he doesn't even teach it is a flipped class room set up where you learn everything on your own from the textbook and videos and then meet with your break out group once a week. both tests avg were in low 70s, rough class

I wasn't in his section, but I sat in his lecture because he's a great lecturer. He's dynamic and explains things well, although in a distance format his time management is horrible. He clearly loves physics. Wonderful personality in person, but when it came to digital communication sometimes the way he would respond to things wasn't constructive.

I know Greco is one of the beloved professors her, but I just do not get it. From snarky comments to random lectures I found him off-putting to say the least. He didnt make physics more engaging for me, like others say. The class is very challenging, so its not all his fault, but do not necessarily expect him to be as great as some make him seem.

Had him for both PHYS2211 and PHYS2212. Really cares about students and tries to make opportunities to help us out. The content for PHYS 2, I just found a lot harder than PHYS 1 but he was fair on the tests and I think the final was overall a bit easier than the midterms. Uses weighted grading where best test worth more than your worst

Dr. Greco is a great professor. He uses fun demonstrations to make lecture more interesting, and he really develops a friendship with people who participate regularly in class. Lecture would sometimes get ahead of HW, which was a bit frustrating but manageable. The content is difficult and Dr. Greco works to make it fun nonetheless.

While his lectures were a little random at times, he was always willing to meet outside of class to explain concepts and homework problems. Extremely understanding and is willing to help. Energetic during lectures

Lectures are entertaining and exams are very reasonable. Make sure to do previous exams and extra practice problems at the end of book chapters on Wiley because he often gives exam questions that are the same/very similar to those.

This man loves Physics, and he wants you to love it to. His lectures are super entertaining, and he goes over the really difficult problems in class because he WILL put them on the test. The homework assignments get a little repetitive at times and aren't particularly similar to the questions he likes to give on tests though.
This man is the best physics professor Ive ever taken. He is hilarious and genuinely cares for his students. His class is really hard and I spent many all nighters for it though.
The physics GOD. This is the best physics teacher I have ever had. Can explain concepts really well. The key to succeed in his class is going to lecture and actively paying attention.

Actually helped me learn. Very willing to spend an extra day going over material. Homework was a fair load but extra credit was available to do it early. Dr. Greco is super caring and has given his number out for if we need anything. Funny and good at breaking down hard concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really made me care about the material.

I don't think Greco had a hard time staying on topic, a lot of his "tangents" are planned and help explain the material in an interesting way. He's very clear about how to succeed in the class, and it's hard, but Greco's teaching is very intuitive and much better than the physics i learned in HS. Would 100% recommend, he makes physics less awful
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Didn't learn much in lecture. Spent a lot of time in TA office hours struggling to learn the material. Some of the labs/hws are so hard people will use chegg for the answers. Not sure if final was easy or I eventually learned. Greco made me laugh when he compared current to harambe sitting on a wire counting counting moving charges. Would not rec.

Greco was a great professor. His lectures were clear and funny. He did sometimes go off-topic, but he got better at staying on-topic as the semester progressed. He is very available and enthusiastic about teaching physics. The combination of doing your homework, going to lecture, and reading the book will help you succeed in the course.

Greco's a hilarious professor. His lectures could be a little more helpful when it comes to learning the material but theyre still helpful (and entertaining) enough that theyre worth going to. Its not an easy class but it helps if you do the homework and start it early, not only for extra credit but also to give you plenty of time to understand it
Great professor
Prof. Greco is awesome! His lectures are fantastic and he makes class really interesting. You can tell how passionate he is about physics and its contagious. He also cares alot about his students.

Greco is a great guy and a great professor. At times he can get off track during lecture because of a joke he comes up with or a story he remembers, but other than that he really works to make sure the students understand the material. As long as you do the homework and the practice tests, you should do fine on the tests. not a cake class
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Loved my boy Greco, definitely made physics fun. Lectures weren't the most useful, but if you just read the textbook, do all the hw early and complete the practice tests, you'll get an A.

Greco is a horrible lecturer, but a funny guy. I stopped attending lectures because he would ramble about unrelated topics for a huge part of the class period in which I would rather be doing HW and understanding concepts alone. If you can do the HW and understand the concepts, it won't be too hard to make an A in this class tbh.

Decent guy, horrible professor. Nothing we ever did in lecture was related to the exams, and he would often spend the entire time on one problem which he would end up doing wrong and would later post the solution to t-square. I didn't learn a single thing from him, but I had two years of physics in high school so I was fine.

I don't know, everyone loves Greco because he's funny, but I thought he was pretty 'meh.' When he actually taught it was awesome but a lot of classes he would just joke around and do some problem he made up on the spot that wasn't really like the stuff we were expected to know how to do on the exam. Just study a lot and go to PLUS sessions.

Terrible lectures. Attended every course, did the homework, read the textbook, still made C's. He does not help you learn the topics at all. My best advice: hope to have taken a good physics course in high school. Everyone just pulls from their previous knowledge.

I never felt like I thoroughly understood physics, but I still did well because he tries to help you out as much as he can. Not a great lecturer but awesome in office hours. Do the homework early, do and re-do and re-do again the practice tests and take advantage of any extra credit opportunities. Lab is pretty easy but also a waste of time.
Not an easy class and you have to study to understand physics - because physics. But doable. Would recommend with this teacher; he is hilarious, teaches well, and is accessible to ask questions.
Classes bored me. Luckily got an A through extra credit from points gathered throughout the year. Would Take Again.

Go to lectures, especially just before the tests and even on test days. Tests are hard but not impossible, lab is easy. Do the homework FOR SURE, and the practice tests. Get all those bucket points, they make a difference. Greco is hilarious, surprisingly awake for 9am, and always helpful. Great teacher :)

One word: JOLLY. This man is probably one of the happiest professors I've had. Really makes the class fun and tries to keep the class engaged. He knows his stuff and is really willing to help if you show effort and go to office hours. Make sure you know how to do the homework and do the all the readings and practice tests and you will get an A.

Greco is absolutely hilarious and does a fair amount of examples in lecture. Definitely go to lecture and do all the reading and homework. Tests are ok, so make sure you keep up with the material and do the practice problems provided. This is a modern physics course, and I found the coding aspect to be really simple and a nice test problem.

Physics is not an easy subject, but Greco makes it enjoyable. He emphasizes understanding the subject rather than just memorizing formulas. He goes out of his way to make himself accessible to student, but he is not always the best at explaining things. The tests are difficult, but Greco tries to give you as much credit as he can.

The best part about Greco is that he wants students to appreciate Physics, rather than cram formulas or trick students, which makes him the one of the best professors I have had the privilege of having.
Dr. Greco is fun and really cares about students. He is the best for lectures in the intro Physics classes... i've had the opportunity to be lectured by all three. You won't regret taking Greco
Tough class but he made it enjoyable. Dresses up for Halloween and gives prizes that day!

If you're into learning things through the textbook and practice assignments then take Greco. The lectures are funny but can be all over the place and don't go as in depth as they should. Tests weren't bad as long as you get the key concepts.

Tests suck, final is easy, keep up to date with the information and know that everything builds on the basics. His lectures are all over the place, but if you ask questions he does a pretty good job at explaining everything.

Most of Greco's lectures are spent listening to his jokes and maybe watching him work a couple of practice problems. Really nice guy but not a very good teacher and comes off as somewhat unapproachable. Tests were pretty hard and he didn't curve. Wouldn't recommend. I barely made a B and I had to work ridiculously hard for it.

Dr. Greco is a really nice guy, however he gets off topic a lot. I self taught myself a lot by just using the textbook and working problems from there. You don't have to go to class, but there is clickers for a very small percentage of grade.

I really don't see what others saw in his past classes. Greco clearly knows his stuff, but he is inept at teaching. Completing one problem in an hour class period was an achievement. He explains almost nothing thoroughly. Wastes too much time in class on jokes rather than actually achieving any useful level of instruction. Would not recommend.
Funny and enthusiastic. Makes class fun. Dresses up for Halloween

Most of what you learn is from the textbook. He NEVER teaches substantially in class. I really liked physics but after going through this class I dread it. Sets assignments on topics he hasn't covered. Didn't enjoy this class at all….

Most of the professors at Tech can teach fairly well but Greco is an exception. He is one of the worst teachers I've ever had and cannot stay on topic for more than 30 seconds. Not a terribly hard class but if you take him prepare to teach the class to yourself!
Great Professor, will keep you interested the entire semster

Great teacher, but goes on tangents often. I didn't go to class very often, so I used the textbook to do Webassign a lot. The tests are written by the department, so just because he's a funny teacher doesn't mean the tests will be easy. A very approachable person

Greco is a very entertaining professor, but rarely teaches what is actually relevant to the assignments. Tests are very challenging, because he doesn't look at the homeworks. But he is very understanding and curves the class. Favors the front row people, though.

Dr. Greco is a great professor and very entertaining for his students. I found myself always enjoying going to his class. However, his goofy sense of humor and tendency to get off track might make the actual physics aspect of the course more challenging for those who struggle with physics as a subject.

Dr. Greco is a very good professor, but he has a tendency to go off topic. He's very passionate about physics and he tries hard to make it interesting to the students. I had a hard time really learning anything in his lectures, but he's approachable during his office hours. If you read the book and look at old tests/quizzes, you'll get an A.

Excellent Professor. Funny and Entertaining, though he gets off topic a lot in class. Tests are very challenging, but fair. . Go over old tests/quizzes, practice a little each night, understand the material, and you should be able to pull at least a B. Greco is sort of approachable, just have good questions to ask him and don't waste his time.
Very entertaining and incredibly helpful

He is very helpful, and willing to work with you until you understand it. He has a great personality and always keeps class interesting. He does not allow laptop use in the front of the class. If you want to use a laptop or electronic device you must sit in the back (laptop ally). His classes can be interactive, and he always posts the PowerPoints.

Very entertaining lecturer.  Knows what he's talking about and the tests will always have something that you've seen somewhere before or a variation of something.  Seems like a very approachable person, but acts very cold and impatient when approached personally. Does not curve, but doesn't need to.

He's pretty good at explaining the concepts. He jokes a lot which are funny, but sometimes the whole class gets really distracted..and half of the time I can't concentrate on lecture. The tests are hard..but they are from homeworks and lectures so i can't really complain.

An extremely talented teacher and a very well-run class. Modern Physics teaches you the fundamentals and I feel like I really understand things, instead of just memorizing formulas. Tests are extremely hard but fair, and he doesn't curve. Overall, if I could have him again for Physics II I would definitely do it. I wish more profs could be like him
Physics 2 at GT sucks. Tests are awful. HW takes a lot of time. Weekly Lab Quizzes suck. Compared to other Physics professors, Greco is helpful and fun.

Makes class fun and teaches the basics. Goes on alot of tangents. PRS counts, therefore you need to attend every class. Test are HARD and you will need to study for them. They are nothing like the homework. Online Homework. Need to purchase the book. No Curve. Not easy teacher but fairly decent teacher.

I thought this class was fairly easy, and as such, have missed several classes, but the classes I have attended are essentially an explanation of the material in the book, but with examples worked out on the board. The only thing I dislike about this class is the daily homework, which while helpful seems juvenile and unnecessary in a college class.
Very helpful and a good teacher.  HW is easy webassign; tests are much harder than the HW, but he is good at explaining the basics.
Good, helpful professor teaching one of the hardest intro classes at Georgia Tech. Notes are on ppt slides. Test are very hard, hw is pretty much daily online.

Easily the most fun class I've had at Tech, he makes lecture enjoyable even though it can be pretty dry sometimes.  Very easy to approach, and he always has a joke to lighten the mood.  Makes me want to take more physics

Dr. Greco is awesome. He loves to help his students, and understands that physics is a tough subject for many students. Tests are hard, but that's not because of Dr. Greco; the physics teachers as a whole make one test for all of the classes. He's also a really cool guy to be around. For Halloween he lectured in a penguin costume.

Professor Griendling is an amazing teacher who truly wants students to succeed. The rocket project report and glider video are time-consuming, so start early, but otherwise homework is minimal. Her guidance and enthusiasm make her classes very rewarding.

She was amazing at introducing us to AE! She has industry and research backgrounds and has lots of insight. She was very accessible via email or office hours, and she was quite understanding. We had 2 group projects, so several lectures ended up being work periods.

Professor's lectures are clear and she posts the notes. She's really easy to find outside of class and she'll also make sure everyone gets a good overview of what aerospace is. Class is not attendance mandatory but there are in-class group assignments that are for credit. Most things that will be covered in classes are posted beforehand.
Dr. Griendling was amazing. She is super knowledgeable about the field, but is extremely accessible and open if you have any questions at all. She exudes enthusiasm for aerospace that is contagious.

shes awesome. 2611 is an easy class already but shes a nice person overall and does her best to help you learn. she genuinly enjoys teaching. i had friends who took her for 1601 and said the same. im taking her again for 3330 this semester. highly recommended
Extremely easy class, basically business professionalism for aerospace, and she does absolutely nothing to make it harder. Also very fun professor to be around.
Easy class. Make sure to show up.

She gave great lectures and gave a good effort to get the students excited about aerospace engineering, which is sorta the whole purpose of the class. There's honestly way too many assignments for a 1 credit hour class, but it is pretty fun and interesting.
She clearly cares about her students and will make rational accommodations for you / the class if needed. She tries to make sure that everyone's on the same page and is always willing to help you.

Amazing Professor! Our section had consistently higher grades than other courses because she took the time to walk us through assignments. 1601 can be a heavy class, but she made it very manageable. I hope that I take her again.

Amazing Professor! Loved in class detailed examples, plus gracious policies (Open-Note, Take home quizzes). This is a low-stress class, through which you definitely learn A LOT throughout the semester 12/10 would recommend taking her for a solid course in Statics!

The class was graded on attendance, homework, and take-home quizzes (no midterms or finals!). If you pay attention and go to class it is very easy to follow along and get an A in the class. Dr. Griendling's lectures are engaging and she is always willing to help if you don't understand something.

I've had Griendling for both COE2001 and 3531 and both times she's been fantastic! She's extremely friendly and knowledgeable, and really brings passion to the course content. There are no traditional tests or final, just homeworks and open-note, very easy quizzes, so the class is very low-stress if you manage your time (but you also learn a ton)!

Professor Griendling is the best. If she is an option for a class, then you're gonna to want to take her. If you pay attention, the class should be straight forward. She is very reachable, and will be fast to help out and accommodate any issue that you may have, big or small. Seriously though she's the best.
Dr. Griendling is a very caring professor who clearly explains what it takes to get an A in her class. Her AE 1601 class made me excited to be an ae.

I take Dr. Griendling's courses by default. She respects feedback and lectures well. As for this class in particular, keep in mind that it is homework heavy because there are no midterms (only a low value final reflection. And you can choose to take a longer final to replace a homework grade with that test.)

Class is split into 6 easy quizzes with 1 retake allowed (35%), 7 homeworks (35%), final project (15%), and the rest is lecture videos and in class work. Class is flipped so it has lecture videos. In class you just do examples. Significantly easier and less work than other sections. You won't learn much but it's statics so it doesn't matter.

Awesome and passionate teacher, good class structure. Weekly quizzes (no midterms), open note/open book online with one retake and a homework drop. Can exempt the final with a 97. Material isn't bad at all; you're pretty much done with statics if you know how to draw FBDs, sum forces, and take moments.

Dr. Griendling is the best professor I've had so far. The examples in class and homework cover everything you need to know, and there are biweekly quizzes with no midterms in COE 2001. The quizzes are very easy compared to class practice problems and homework, and her lectures are all you need to get a high A in this class.
Dr. Griendling is a great professor. AE 1601 was a super easy class, but I had a ton of fun. She made the assignments interesting. If I get the chance, I will definitely take her classes again.

Five homeworks for the semester, but they're all pretty long. Tests are fair and an optional project replaces a midterm. Dr. Griendling's lectures are pretty good, but her personality and care for students make her a stellar educator. She gives extensions for legitimate reasons and is usually willing to meet us halfway. I'd recommend her.

One of the best professors Ive had at Tech. She is so understanding with the workload she gives for the class and always listens to extension requests to accommodate students. Shes an amazing lecturer and can make even the most advanced concepts seem simple. I would definitely recommend Dr. Griendling for any course.
This class was an easy class, but she made it a lot more fun and helped me reassure to myself that I enjoy aerospace engineering

Dr. Greindling is a very caring and stellar COE 2001 professor especially if you're an AE. The way she organizes this class with asynchronous concept lectures and then live in person solving examples was incredibly effective. Homework does take a considerable amount of time but I found that I had mastery of the material upon completing it.

The projects in this class are straight forward, and she guides you step by step on how to do them. She's a good lecturer; most lectures were asynchronous and the information was presented in a fine manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. She works lots of problems in class and keeps the material interesting and relevant. Quizzes and homework every week, but they are super easy. She is available outside of class and has lots of office hours or posts extra example problems. Averages on all the quizzes were high and there were never any surprises.

I would 100% recommend Dr. Griendling. She is very good at explaining concepts. Going to her office hours is also super helpful for the homework! If you show up to class, you'll probably get a great grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Griendling is a solid choice for statics. She uses real-world examples to make the class more interesting. Her class is VERY easy, but you still learn a lot. Take her, especially if you are an AE.

Dr. Griendling makes such an effort to keep everyone engaged in lectures and gives clear instructions on projects and grading criteria. She is by far one of the most caring professors I've had. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor Ive had so far. She is very caring about her students and has a genuine interest in making sure students learn the material. Gives very reasonable problems on the tests. Show up to class, pay attention, and do the practice problems to succeed.

Very clear lecturer, and adds in relevant, real-world information. Most of the content in this class is really easy, but the rare hard stuff is pretty hard. In-class activities are really helpful for test-prep, and she drops 6 (so you can miss 6 free classes). Grading scheme is pretty test-heavy, but the tests are all written so grading is fair.

Class is very lecture heavy and very boring. The exams are nitty gritty and she doesn't seem like she understands what her own exams are asking for when you ask her to explain. Sometimes she is difficult to talk because she responds in a slightly condecending manner. Overall I did not like the class and it sucks that it's a required course.

Dr. Green is awesome, she clearly cares about the lecture content and wants student to succeed. That doesn't mean the class is always easy - but she's very willing to answer questions and explains concepts well. Grading is usually more than fair as well, with plenty of partial credit.

I found lectures difficult to keep up with at times, just because of the sheer amount of content covered each class. However, the learning objectives provided are very helpful as the tests are written based on them. Dr. Green is also very friendly and approachable if you feel you need additional help in the course.
Shes slick funny. Solid lecturer and the grading isn't too harsh

Dr. Green was a wonderful professor. She's very caring an understanding, and wants you to succeed. The class itself was pretty test heavy with no extra credit or curve. However, the grading scheme is pretty good (6% for the lowest midterm). You will have to put a good amount of effort into this class to get an A, but it's definitely achievable.

Very BORING LECTURESSS!!! felt like there was some melatonin every time I attended lectures. Go by the Learning objectives for exams; they will be your BFF. Not a hard class, but gets hard to follow through when lectures are almost mandatory bcs of TICAS and unbearable.

we had in class assignments that were previously online, but oftentimes when Dr. Green would teach she would randomly do them on paper. It made attendance matter more and was often super annoying, especially since they used to be fully online previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of busy work and attendance is mandatory tracked by in class assignments. the practice exams are no where like the exams and the exams start off easy and get harder. lecture are kinda boring and tedious and learning objectives (which she lives by) dont really cover all you're supposed to know
Lots of reading and content, which can be extremely overwhelming especially before midterms. Dr Green is approachable and happy to help if you have questions though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: pretty bad lecturer, not very helpful. bios 1108 average gpa dropped 0.18 (5%) as soon as her and robbie richards starting teaching.

Extremely helpful in office hours. Class used online free textbook. Attendance was technically taken through a short participation quiz meant to be answered during lecture time but it always closed at 5pm so you could just take notes from the textbook and posted slides if you wanted to skip lecture. Also, the lab component was very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Green was the worse, she was very rude and unhelpful throughout the year, along with this she really does note care about if a student is doing good. The exams are not terrible if you study and go to class but if not they may be hard because there is a LOT of content. But as a professor would not recommend taking her if there is another option.
Her slides and lecture were kind of vague and not very helpful. However, she was very kind and happy to help. The class was textbook/content heavy, but the tests and final exam were easy.

Very kind. Tests are not open note anymore, but are very representative of practice exams and online textbook's learning objectives. ***A lot*** of information for each exam, but start memorizing relatively early and youll be fine. Free 40% of grade from writing assignments and online participation. Final was the easiest exam.

Dr. Green is kind and willing to help students. Though I had limited interactions with her, she made me feel valued as a student in her classroom. Clear lectures. Very passionate about material. This is a memorization-heavy class, so stay on top of material and read the textbook.

I had Dr. Green for BIOS 1108. While I liked her personality, the class relied heavily on Learning Catalytics, which I found unhelpful. Her lectures often missed key content in the learning objectives, leaving me to teach myself after class. The learning objectives were the most helpful part, guiding my focus on relevant material outside of class.

I took BIOS 4803 and she was honestly great. The class was mainly split up by little lectures and in class exercises worked as a group or paper discussions. Participate and do the readings and you'll do fine. The class is a very manageable workload and she is very flexible with due dates. 10/10 class, my favorite class I've taken at Tech so far.

Dr. Green is very caring of her students but does make the class overly difficult imo for what a lab science credit for most people. I spent more time on this class than all my other classes and finished with a 90.01. Interesting class for sure, but be aware of the workload when signing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Green! She's a real sweetheart and her lectures are interesting because she's so passionate about the subject. There were a lot of unnecessary worksheets and way too much group projects, but if you work hard to learn the material, you will do well.

The design of the course was not to my liking-- it's a half-flipped classroom, with lots of worksheets and small group activities and only "mini-lectures", which wasn't particularly helpful for me. Expect a lot of time studying on your own to do well on tests. That said, Dr. Green was helpful and approachable and offered plenty of extra credit.
Super hard class, but the professor is really nice and willing to help you out. Lots of extra-credit opportunities. This will probably be your most all-consuming class, but it's somewhat interesting.

The worksheets during class are not helpful at all and waste precious class time. Her PowerPoint presentations are not detailed enough for you to study those alone. I would recommend taking notes in class along side the printed-out PowerPoint slides and then reading the book as well. MC is really hard, but the short-answer isn't graded too hard.

Really great teacher who provides a lot of resources to help you learn and succeed in the course. If you utilize all of her resources and do as much participation activities as you can (going to class not even that necessary), you can easily succeed in this course. The only bad parts of the class are the lab portion (useless) and the group video.
She gave out some pointless worksheets and did not make the class very interesting. If you're doing this for your lab requirement, I would not recommend.

This class, though interesting at times, was EXTREMELY difficult (and I'm a bio major). She does a lot of pointless worksheets in class, and the amount of reading and studying you will do will be enormous. Don't take this class if you want to get an A in it.
Lectures were great, but tests were very difficult. Studying and reading the book is required if you want an A.

Cool class, cool professor. You can tell by her lectures that she's interested in her subject. Most of the time I didn't have to bother withe the book b/c her teaching was clear & thorough. I'd easily recommend her for your professor.

Dr. Turk is an amazing lecturer. He covers really interesting material and explains concepts clearly. Lecture notes are handwritten and not posted online. There are 4 major projects and 2 open-note multiple-choice exams. A portion of each project grade is based on effort which was very vaguely defined.

Prof. Turk is a great professor who clearly explains course material and expectations. Lectures aren't posted online, but they're easy to follow if you attend. The class is mostly project-based with clear requirements, making an A very doable. Assignments are mostly completion, and open-note tests reflect lecture content. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Turk is the best, he is very passionate about Computer Graphics. This has been my favorite course so far at Tech. The class is 5 projects and open-note midterm and final. The projects aren't super hard, but definitely time consuming. Very manageable if you start early. 

Only complaint is that the TAs were very unresponsive on Piazza.

Project-based course (Procedural Content Generation) with beautiful projects that students write from scratch using Unity. Lectures are lovely but proceed at a geriatric pace due to his insistence on writing detailed slides (including helpful pseudocode!) by hand as he speaks. Exams are open-note and ultra easy.

Fantastic graphics professor. Appeals to intuition, clear, insightful and does not shy away from details. Humble and not afraid to tell you he's not an expert on something. 

Projects are are all in Processing and/or GLSL and are very fun and learned a lot from them. I would take him again if I see him teaching another course.
He has good handwriting and drawing skills.

Turk is a really nice guy and his lectures are very clear and easy to follow along with. Each project counts for about 15% of your grade, so get started on them early. Exams are open-notes so as long as you follow along with prof during lecture you'll do fine. Overall, a good lecturer and an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Greg is pretty amazing! The special topics class I took is "Procedural Content Generation for Games" which is a very cool class if you've ever wondered about techniques for...well...procedurally generating things.

He's the best professor for graphics so if you are here to find who to take for CS3451, he's the guy. His programming projects are using Processing with p5js which can get very tricky and require lots of TA OH visits. Exams are hard not because of content but bc of how he words the questions and answers.

Greg is an amazing professor. His lectures are super clear and detailed. The class is mostly based on interesting homework, so it is easy to get the work done. Overall, put in about 10 hours a week (including lecture) and you will have a good time. 10/10 professor

I took the class during the Online semesters. That being said, the lectures were always clear and focused. The class was very interesting and the material progressed logically. The grading was almost solely on the projects, which was great, because the projects were really fun to do. The professor is also a very chill dude.

Graphics is known to be one of the harder CS classes but Turk made it pretty manageable. V passionate and gives fair assessments. HW are pretty hard, especially ones after the animation hw, but def doable if you start really early and go to TA hours. Also copy lecture notes verbatim since test material comes straight from it (open note tests).

Very knowledgeable professor Make sure you go to class! If you don't understand something, just write it down and go to his or TA office hours . Def cares about his students This is just for graphics: there was a big disconnect between the lectures and the homeworks. Make sure you go to the TAs for the secret sauce for the homeworks. They have it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The best you can take for graphics. Only thing were that homeworks needed to be started at least like 3-4 days before the due date. They were pretty dense. TA office hours are extremely helpful though. His midterm/final is open book, open note. I dropped graphics the semester before with a different prof and found turk way more manageable this sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Turk is an engaging lecturer and really cares about students. As long as you start your projects early and go to office hours if you need help, it's a very manageable class (also check piazza!). His exams are open note, so as long as you go to lectures and review your notes the night before the exam, you're almost guaranteed an A on exams.

If you start the projects early, this class is entirely manageable. Professor Turk is a truly caring man who wants you to actually learn the topics. He spent an hour after class every class period to assist with any questions. I would definitely take him again.

Projects are insanely hard. Don't wait until the last minute like I did to begin them. Probably one of the hardest classes I've had. But he's a great lecturer and he's the best professor at Tech for graphics. He's very approachable. If you work hard, you will do okay. Don't be afraid to ask for help.
I literally never went to class or read any of the assigned reading and got an A. TBH it depends on the TA you get for studio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Didn't attend a single lecture, just 2 quizzes which were easy and then some writing assignments for homework. Discussions were very chill, usually around 30 minutes and just had to speak a couple times to get 100 (this depends on ur TA tho). Very low-commitment easy class.

I won't lie I didn't attend a single lecture for this course. Grades were just through papers and weekly mandatory studios which can be painful depending on how willing your studio is to participate. Pretty standard class nothing outstanding.

Great Professor. Quizzes weekly are easy and papers are long but simple. Lectures are not required, but weekly studio sessions are. Depending on your TA, you may have to stay for the entire studio period, which is the only reason I gave difficulty a 2. A very easy course with a caring professor, highly recommend.

Dr. Grinter is a very respectable professor. Overall the class isn't too difficult, just weekly quizzes, homework, and discussion participation. I also really liked the idea of the term paper and giving us checkpoints such as initial proposal and outline to do before the final paper which I think is super helpful as someone who procrastinate a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof Grinter was a good lecturer and made the class low stakes enough for it to be a true learning environment. Learnt some pretty neat stuff. Easy A.

She's a good speaker and enjoyable lecturer, but since the lectures generally mirror the online/textbook content anyway, many students stopped going to lecture pretty quickly. Rigor was much lower than what I'd expect for a 3 credit hour course. Assignments and course structure are easy to follow.

3001 is a very easy course, and getting a good grade just comes down to doing the busywork. Beki is a good lecturer but there is no reason to actually go since you are never tested on the content. The only real work is a couple of assignments surrounding the term paper, but the deadlines are even more generous than the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The prof is a very easy going person who really just wants you to pass the class. Lectures are optional but not needed, because everything is online. Grade is determined by weekly discussion and quizzes, plus a very easy final paper. Just remember to do the busy work, and you are pretty much guaranteed to get an A. The prof is also willing to help.
Very easy class. Complete the assignments on time, and put in the effort and you'll be fine. Never went to lecture and ended with a 98+.
Ask your TA!

People were confused about course logistics and she was quite harsh about it. Gave blunt and vague answers, and always acted like she was in the right. She is very no nonsense and cold during lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her class was online Fall 2022. Watched like 2 lectures in the beginning, then didn't bother. Just read the readings and participate during discussion and you're all set. Discussions usually lasted like 40 mins even though they're supposed to be 2 hours. "Pop quizzes" were extremely easy and the final term paper is easy to BS.

Loved this ethics class. Prof. Grinter was very understanding and wanted everyone to learn. The class was online and we could either watch a recording or watch it live. Weekly quizzes for the readings.There is a discussion with TAs but I guess how that goes depends on how your TAs requirements are.
super easy

He is really nice, helpful guy with a lot of experience! For the first 5 weeks of the class, it's just about NEPA policy, must pay attention and read to do well on the exam. Two big group projects, very interesting, but suck if you have bad group members. The TA is chill with grading. If you're interested in the topic, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Nice + knowledgable but lowkey intimidating. Class is notoriously time-consuming. 
Don't read the NEPA book. Prof goes over everything you need from the book during the lecture. Type notes + CTRL-F during exams = did not use book ONCE. 
Projects are a royal pain & info is overwhelming + unorganized. Start early and pray for a good group.

Extremely heavy on reading and group projects. Summer semester has 3 weeks to read the entire textbook, 5 for regular. Make sure to annotate everything. Exams are open-note but exhaustive. Feels like a grad class. Lectures and projects are poorly structured. Very time demanding. Do not combine with a lab class if you're bad at writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is half easy half hard with two time consuming projects. I found him to be knowledgeable yet arrogant as he wants you to use his research on his projects. He is very meticulous about rubrics and guidelines so read everything extremely carefully.

Super knowledgable, experienced in the area and has a ton of incredible things to share with you. Tons of reading, most of it necessary to do well on the tests. There are also two huge projects that take a lot of time. Half class is easy, half not. He was super understanding and accommodating with a personal situation. Great professor, great mentor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and approachable. Took his Special Topics course on sidewalk and I would strongly recommend taking it. The content is interesting an the bulk of the class consists of a project that provides a good understanding of all the behind the scenes stuff that goes on in infrastructure projects.

He gives good lectures but expects you to really think. His projects are challenging & will force you to ask him questions. He is always available in his office and willing to help. His tests are all written and include 1 or 2 five-paragraph essays. He tends to be late to class and gives tons of partial credit. Read or you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Horrendous lectures, can't stay on topic at all. Do not take. Idk who gave this guy a 5 star rating.

I read the review that gave him five stars and I'm genuinely convinced he wrote that. I've never written a review before but this prof is so bad I feel obligated to make this. He is Joe Biden. He drones on about absolutely nothing in the most sleep inducing way possible. Our grade breakdown was 10% HW, 50% two exams, 40% final.
He is a very caring and smart professor, and also very knowledgeable about warehousing. He is a great inspiration to his students.

You know how Tech tower was the tallest building when it was built in 18-whatever? Pretty sure this guy was teaching when they finished it. Out of all the professors I've had, this guy puts all of the yappers to shame, and the way the course is taught is absolutely horrible. Expect 4-5 hours 4x a semester to learn the material day before each exam.
I went 3 years at Georgia Tech and never dropped a course even when the classes got really difficult. I dropped this course because the teaching was just that bad. Avoid this professor if you can.

Teacher makes the course feel like its a 3 hour class when its a 1 hour. Content is a mess in canvas, just wait for the other econ teacher to get credit for this 1 hour course. Whole grade is just 4 tests, would've been good if you could drop one, but if you bomb one you're basically not getting an A anymore.

Not a hard class but had to teach myself. Prof. Sharp spent lectures discussing his takes on conspiracy theories and also occasionally making fun of students. Incomprehensible is the right word for him. I don't know the last class that I gave up on lectures because the professor just wouldn't stay on topic (any topic). For your sake don't take him.
Prof Sharp is the most incomprehensible professor I've had at this school, but it doesn't matter because all of the content is on clear pre-recorded videos and practice exams.
You know, I asked my uncle once how someone would know when it was time to stop. You know what he said? "The youngsters will tell ya"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too much material in a mess folder and lectures are not clear

Sharp is terrible. he teaches like he is going senile and his slides make about as much sense. your grade is 4 tests. Also attempts to teach what is clearly 3 credit hours in a 1 hour class and has no clue what he is doing. He somehow both fails so start and finish teaching questions properly, instead just giving the middle and then stopping.

The most boring professor I've ever had. He seemed like he had no idea what was going on, and his grading scheme was absolutely insane. The entire class was made up of 100 points, so every point you missed on a homework was 1% off your final grade, and there was no partial credit. I pulled an A but it was extremely stressful.

Is very slow, and I don't think understands half of what is going on around him. Had to downgrade his new laptop to Windows XP and uses Excel 2003, probably because that is all he knows how to use. I don't understand how he hasn't been fired. Taking him was the biggest mistake I made in enrolling in classes at Tech. Avoid at all costs.

One hour class was a cake walk. Students watch video lectures online and can optionally attend class to ask questions and go over homework answers (though homework is not graded). You can skip class and still get an easy A. Gives 4 exams throughout semester and no final.

Possibly the worst structured class I've ever taken. HW/Group Projects are 50% of grade, but are not very well defined and very time consuming. There is one midterm 20%, and a final exam 30%. The exams are structured like old practice tests. Lectures are very dry. It is hard to pay attention in class. It is more useful to self-teach the material.
Poor lecturer. Class is unorganized and homework is difficult to maneuver from lack of clarity/structure

Difficult but very interesting course. Lectures are great and Dr Gunter is friendly and helpful. Homework will take lots of time, and exams are fair but difficult. Be prepared for lots of coding and troubleshooting. The material constantly builds on top of itself, so make sure to thoughouly understand the fundamentals so you don't get left behind.

Dr. Gunter is personally one of my favorite professors. This class is definitely difficult, but if you're able to keep up, it is very worth it. Now, I will emphasize, I took multiple other classes at the same time, and I spent 95% of my time on this class. HW is super long, 3 midterms, and a final project is brutal but I loved the class.

Note, this is for AE 6357: Satellite Orbit Determination. 
Dr. Gunter is an amazing lecturer, and you learn a lot in his class, that you won't learn otherwise. However, the structure of this class is very grueling, with 6 very hard homeworks, 3 midterms, and one final project, which made it an absurd workload, even for a graduate class.

This SHL class was disappointing. There was a disconnect in communication between the TA (who was present for the labs) and the professor (who was often nowhere to be found). If one group included something in the report (that wasn't even on the rubric) another did not, then the group that had less got a worse grade. It was a competitive class.

He did not have any interest in the class. Was often not present. Did not explain any of the material and tested on obscure material that was not covered. He was not very lenient. Seemed to not know what was going on in lab when he did show up. I do not think should be teaching, should stick to other work.

Great professor and very passionate about the courses he teaches! Homeworks and tests can be hard but they really help you understand the material. Occasionally pushed back deadlines to give more time for assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Have taken him time and time again for my graduate AE courses at GT.
I wouldn't recommend taking with him.

Condescending responses to questions/clarifications. Reads right off the slides without further explaining concepts. Mistakes on homework solutions that were never corrected or announced to the class. Completely unclear grading, does not give ANY feedback on exams for what was missed, only a score. Final weighted 52%.

I've never felt such burning hatred for a prof before Waldo. Misleading questions on tests. 52% weight final. Condescending attitude to student questions WHILE giving wrong answers. Reads off of overcomplicated lecture slides. Wrong answers on HW. 1:1 tutor with GT remotely saved me, but even she said she hadn't seen some of my content before.

Dr. Antoine Guitton is a nice person; however his teaching methods combined with the course structure are very bad. 3 tests worth 16% each and 1 final worth 52%. No other grades. The tests are 20% T/F and the rest are FRQ problems similar to the HW. The problem is, he hardly, if ever, goes over those problems in class. Basically a slides only prof.
An amazing lecturer. His OHs are pretty helpful too. Definitely take CS 6290 with him if you have the chance.

I took this course in Fall 2023 while Gupta was a Phd student under Conte. It was his first time teaching the course, so I am sure it has improved since then. Sometimes, his lectures would start to become confusing, and he never really stopped to clarify anything. No laptop/tablet policy, so prepare to take notes by hand. Overall "meh" experience.

Pulkit did a great job co-lecturing 6290. His lectures were very informative and well laid out. If anything he just writes faster than Conte. He also did an amazing job leading the projects and trying to make the instructions as informative as possible. This class is lots of work and will keep you busy but is very rewarding.
Controlled by prof T C.

For a first time teacher, Pulkit did a pretty good job getting through the class. This class is by no means easy, and sometimes lecturers turned into rambles but he cares about the class and tries his best.
It was his first time teacher so it was a little unorganized, but hes a good teacher for this decently hard class.

After the passing of the beloved Professor Caleb Southern, Pulkit stepped up to teach this class even as a PhD student. He makes it very clear that he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He moves through lectures fast, but for the topics being covered I think he's doing a good job. He's also pretty funny. Update: ABSOLUTE GOAT.
Pulkit is the GOAT WE LOVE YOU
-1 for poor artistic abilities but overall chill

ME2110 is a hard class, but he will help you and give good advice if you take incitive and reach out. Schedule zoom meetings instead of emailing a wall of questions as he is more helpful in a live conversion (in my experience). He is a very tough grader and will tear up your reports, so meet with him before submitting to clarify expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Will scare you on the first day. The course is definitely hard and taxing, Dr. Helms is an awesome professor that will guide you through it if you let him.

Really good professor. Yes he is tough, yes me 2110 is hard, but Dr. Helms really helped carry the weight off of his student's shoulders. From giving extra-time when needed to allowing/reccomending projects to be started early, he makes the class easier for his students. Make sure to listen to his feedback, its very useful and its how he grades.

Dr. Helms truly did not teach anything. He would spend all of lecture yapping about some random information that was not helpful one bit rather than lecture content. He would then give assignments purely based on the information he didn't teach at all. Horrible professor, horrible grader, waste of a class. Avoid at all costs.

Please avoid this class at all cost. If you are taking this class with Professor Helms, you should rethink about this. This course is a class that contain so much busy work. 
1. lecture (60-120 minutes every week) before class
2. Read articles, have 3 exams, have group project.
3. the professor just talks whatever he feels like during class time.

Don't take this class. This class should not be this hard or this amount of work. A lot of assignments are ambiguous and his grading style is unambiguous. He is not merciless. He give 3 tests and group project. Also, you need to read article every week, do weekly assignment, and also watch the lecture. He expects you to do it.

ME 2110 is a difficult class because it's time consuming (a well known fact at Tech). Dr. Helms frankly didn't seem to care. The main issue I had is that he grades super tough but provides no rubric, and even if you follow the feedback he gives to a t, you probably still won't get the grade you want/expect.

His grading is very tough and often feels subjective or unfair, but he did give a nice curve. He doesn't give rubrics for his grading, so you learn what he is looking for by failing and getting a LOT of comments.
Really great professor, it is a lot of work however at the end you will realize he was hard on you for a reason.

Get ready for a bunch of group projects! This class is different from anything else I've taken. The projects are vague so it leaves you with a lot of creative room - it's annoying at first but it grew on me. If you need help, go to his office hours, he explains things a lot more when you meet him in person. A fun class if you enjoy psyc!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Frequently changed class structure which made it confusing what was going on and what to turn in. Cog psych is supposed to be one of those interesting courses but I didnt learn anything meaningful or impactful from him. Half of grade is group project but grading for the project is ambiguous and random. Tests were a little on the tough side

She is probably the best professor for the class. She's a good lecturer but not always the most understanding when you ask a question. Frequently called out students in lecture for quietly whispering, and will NOT round up- I ended with an 89.5 and she refused to make it an A. Overall not the kindest person, but explains concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably best teacher for the class
Very good lecturer, very test heavy but partial credit is reasonably given.

Her lectures are super great, and if you miss something she posts her notes from that class online every day pretty quickly after the class. She stays after class to answer questions if you go up and ask, and is super accessible outside too.

This class is absolutely one of the hardest I've taken at GT, but Prof. Grodzinsky is an absolutely amazing lecturer and can give you so much additional support if you just ask. If you have the time to study Calculus for an hour or two per day, you could really end up passing with an easy A/B. Would 100% recommend taking her if you can!!

Mrs. G is an amazing professor! Lectures aren't mandatory, but are really great for learning the content. She's accessible outside of class and very accommodating of different circumstances. Definitely take her if you can!

Mrs G's lectures are really helpful at introducing topics and the studios are great at solidifying the ideas taught. She's been doing this a long time and you can tell she knows what she is doing. Lectures aren't attendance-based, but are actually worth your time. Tests are also not too hard and outside of like 7 packets, there is no real homework.
Take calc 2 with ms g, her lectures make the concepts pretty easy to understand and have the base knowledge to apply in studios.

Ms. G is known to be the best professor for calc 2 here. She is organized, explains content well, answers questions, and is accessible. The study guides prepared you very well for the test. Would recommend.

Prof. G is awesome. She is super nice and gives simple but detailed and helpful notes/instruction. There are a good bit of worksheets but you cover most of the questions in studio or class. Really easy to get help from and is super willing to answer questions during class and try and explain things in different ways.

She is the absolute goat! I went to her bc my lecturer was terrible and my grades immediately improved with her teaching. She explains things in away that is both simple and detailed. 100% the best Calc 2 professor at Georgia Tech.

A great professor. If you do the review, you will do well on the exam. I recommend going to the lectures and studios. You get the answers for the packet assignments and up to 2 pts extra credit if you attend all studios. Beware, she is a little strict about behavior during lectures. She does not allow open laptops and will call you out for talking.
Very sweet lady and a pretty good lecturer. She is passionate about what she teaches. She is kind of hard of hearing tho

Mrs. Grodzinsky is an excellent teacher and she does a great job explaining difficult topics. Tests are not built to trick you and they accurately reflect what we learned it class. It is also clear with her attitude that she wants her students to succeed and is always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was very good at lecturing for the 1st half of the semester, but kind of fell off for the 2nd half. She knows her stuff, just the 2nd half wasn't structured as well. There is grade replacement, but don't rely on it too much. There is a decent amount of extra credit and she does a CIOS bonus which helps. Definitely can get an A.

There's a decent amount of work for her Math 1552 class between mandatory lectures, studios, videos, and homework assignments, but she's an amazing teacher who offers lots of outside help and extra credit. You can genuinely tell how much she cares about being a good professor and her students and I could not recommend her more.

Dr.Grodzinsky is an absolute must for 1552. Her lectures literally couldn't be any better. She is very caring and accessible for questions during OH. The workload was average, and the tests were very appropriate with the resources given to us. ALWAYS ALWAYS do the midterm reviews, those are going to be the best resource for preparing for midterms.
No other words, she is a must take professor.
Very sweet and very effective professor. Her class is very structured and you know what to expect on graded homeworks and her exams. Best professor to take for this class!

Prof. Gordzinsky is so enthusiastic about teaching math and is very good at explaining the content. Every one of her lectures was packed with important content, and her office hours are also extremely helpful if you have concerns or are struggling with the material. If you can get her as a professor, take her section!

Klara is a great and caring professor. It can be a tiny bit annoying if you already know the topics, cause attendance counts towards final grade and she can be really repetitive in lectures. But other than that she is really clear and makes things easy to understand. Definitely easy A+ if you want to get an A.

Prof G's lectures are superb - she really breaks down the tough content. The workload is heavy, but using unstuckstudy and the mandatory studios helped me ace this class. Definitely worth taking if you're willing to put in the effort.
Awesome professor, made sure there are lots of resources available to be successful. If you attend lecture and studio and take advantage of help available the exams and course are relatively easy.

I came into this class after barely scraping through Calc 1 through sheer memorization, but despite Calc 2's difficulty, Grodzinsky helped me to make it to the end of the semester with a B! Go to her office hours - She's incredibly willing to help you if you're struggling, and will remember you if you come regularly!

I took AP Calc BC before this which was difficult for me but she made everything so easy to understand while also explaining the reasoning behind everything. 4 midterms, homework's, pre lecture videos, studios, and an optional final. She really helped me enjoy math through this class. One weird rule she has is no laptops in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very glad to take Integral with Mrs. G. She is the head of the department, and it is clear why.

Head of math department so knows what she's doing. Posts notes by the end of the day - other teachers use her slides for notes. Very detailed note-taker, does a lot of examples, very clear and concise lectures. Made concepts very easy to understand and always took pauses during her lecture to make sure she didn't go over a concept too fast

Mrs. G is the best professor ever! She explains everything super well and doesn't leave anything out. Never was there something on an exam that she didn't teach in lecture. Provides notes and example problems to follow along with during her lectures. Gives study guide before each exam and tests are never harder than practice problems.

Easily the best math teacher/prof I have ever had. I never thought i would be able to enjoy a math class until I took Linear Algebra with her. She is genuinely one of the best lecturers I have ever had, and I don't have enough good things to say about her. I wish she taught every class here

best prof for 1552! made integral calc so easy to understand and she's really caring and accessible as well. use her office hours if you need but the tests are pretty straight forward and usually come from studio or the study sheet. optional final to improve grade + attendance and hw points asw
I took this course in Spring 2022. This class is hard. Grodzinsky makes it easier. She works with students' grades and will help you when you are in a rut. Great choice for a Calculus 2 professor.
She was very sweet and understanding. I took it this class in the summer and she made it pretty easy.

She's such an amazing professor. Her lectures are clear, she provides lots of examples, and exams are very similar to the exam review. You have 4 skips but I ended up going to majority of the lectures because she's such a good lecturer. As long as you do the test review and examples in class, it's a pretty easy A. (though it's lots of memorization)

I did bad in the class because of the content. It was SUCH a hard class. But Klara was great! She was the only reason I didn't fail tbh. She was very clear about what was needed to do well in the class and her lectures were VERY helpful. She was not strict, just cares a lot about us taking her class seriously. Hate calc, love Klara

She's enthusiastic in every lecture. I like how she pays great attention to and repeatedly remind us of important stuff. She also demonstrates a lot of examples. Test review sessions for all sections in the morning of the exam days are super helpful if you have last minute questions. We have 4 midterms, and the final exam is optional.

After completing my first year at Georgia Tech, I can confidently say Mrs. Grokinzy was the best teacher I've had so far. Her lectures are good and her notes are very comprehensive. The final exam for the class is very lenient as it is optional and can ONLY improve your grade. If you did good in calc 1, you'll do good with calc 2 with Grodkinzy.

didnt have her class, but i watched her online lectures instead of going to my professor's lecture. she explained concepts very clearly and made it easy to understand. her office hours are great too. exams are reasonable, and the review guides they give u for exams help immensely. make sure to know how to thoroughly do each question.

Mrs. G is the best 1552 professor you can take at GT. I'm not in her section but went to her lectures everyday as she explained everything in a way that was easy to understand. This class has a LOT of content but Mrs. G does a very good job of making sure that you can get through the work and exams.

Dr. Grodzinsky is an amazing lecturer who makes content very clear and easy to understand. She also is very accessible for questions and answers them easily, clearing any misconceptions. Tests were pretty fair and indicative of what we had practiced in studio and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this professor! She is so sweet and caring and passionate about the subject. Attending her lectures really helps clarify the content. I learned a lot from her.

It is important to go to lectures because there is so much content in this class, but her lectures are great! I took AP Calc BC and really struggled with some of the Calc 2 topics, but Mrs. G had taught them in such a clear way that has really helped me understand them. She's the best!

Professor Grodzinsky is one of the best math professors I have ever had. She's incredibly knowledgeable, amazing at answering questions, goes over difficult concepts several times, and is always available for help. The class is difficult but she explains content very clearly. Would 100 percent recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Prof. G 3 semesters in a row (all diff classes) if that tells you anything. She's incredible! Exams reflect material learned (old exams, lecture examples, studio wksts) and her lectures will usually absolve any confusions you could have. Never had to use supplementary material to learn. Her office hours are pure gold. Go to OH before exams!

I personally found her lectures to be fairly slow and boring, but certainly not intolerable. Expect to spend a minute on homework, especially if you use WeBWork over MML. In my experience, the most helpful component of this class is the mandatory studios, I would pay most attention there. Still overall a very kind and helpful lecturer

Klara is the best math teacher I have ever had. She is so sweet and cares about her students. She is also very understanding. Once a TA graded my test very poorly and I got 10 points back after meeting with her. She is my queen :) her tests are pretty tricky tho so its def a class you can't not study for

Amazing lecturer, very helpful pre-lecture videos, tests accurately reflected material, non-mandatory attendance.  What more could you want? I'm very happy that I was able to take her this fall. 10/10

honestly, dont pick this class. First F I have ever gotten in my life and I have gotten all As in my life till now. She is the first math professor on earth who writes faster than she speaks. Anyways, good luck and I hope you get through it and get a C or higher :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor. She makes the course easy to understand, and it's a very challenging course. She makes sure to go through plenty of examples in class so you aren't surprised by anything in the homework. I wasn't registered for her section, but I attended her lectures.
Do yourself a favor and register to Mrs G's class. Great lecturer and really cares about students.
Great professor and delivers extremely fair assignments based on the lectures. Amazing person and cares about what she is doing.

Dr. Grodzinsky was an amazing professor who constantly provided opportunities for us to ask her questions and feedback. Her lectures were amazing, and for 1553 that I took over the summer, she provided lecture recordings & notes, and for 1552 that I took in a normal semester, she provided lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Grodzinsky was able to teach a course that is notoriously very complicated in a very simple manner. Her teaching style was great and was very helpful.

Dr. G has been one of my favorite professors to date - she's a joy to listen to in class, and her grading scale is designed to work in your favor. She enjoy linear algebra a lot, and it shows in her lectures and enthusiasm while teaching. A stellar introduction to linear algebra that left me wanting to learn more - she's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Grodzinsky is overall a good professor. She explained the concepts well; I just don't understand calc. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended. She posts the notes from class, but they can be hard to follow without her explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Grodzinsky was amazing. She explained every single concept so well. I attended her office hours several times and they were the most helpful office hours I've ever been to. She gives you all the tools you need to succeed in this class. She's also in charge of the TAs which is helpful.
she's an absolute angel! the only reason i was able to pull a B in calculus 2 after nearly failing calculus 1. so so sweet, amazing at detailed explanations.
