Professor Grodzinsky is probably one of the best math teachers that I have had. 1552 is challenging, but if you put in the time, I think you should succeed in the class. Her lectures are very informative, and clear. The tests are hard, but if you follow exactly what she teaches in class, you should do fine. Also just go to class it helps a lot.

Klara is definitely one of the best math teachers I've ever had and I would 100% recommend taking her class. The class itself is hard but she makes it easier to understand. The 4 tests are worth 80% of your grade, but the problems on exams are easier than what is covered in class and on the homework.

Klara is genuinely one of the best math teachers I've ever had. The class material itself is definitely difficult but she makes it less daunting by explaining concepts very well in class. The 4 midterms are worth 80% of your grade, but the level of difficulty of the exams is less than what you do in class, making it attainable to do well.
This professor is a good lecturer, and the class is fairly easy. There is not too much homework, and the test review packets are helpful for the test.

Really nice lady.  Not a great lecturer.  She is the only math professor I have ever seen who writes faster than they speak (and then moves on before students can even process anything).  I never went to lecture bc it was too frustrating, and I got 100's on every exam by studying class notes.  Weekly packets are 5x harder than exams.  Good overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great professor! Very organized and made the class very simple so that it was almost impossible to not get an A as long as you attended lecture and completed work. She is very caring and sweet.

She is very organized and provide lots of practice to succeed on the exams. If you attend lecture and studio, and do the homework and review packets, you will have a guaranteed A in the class. She is clear and concise while lecturing and is always available outside of class. She is very caring towards her students and wants us to succeed.

Professor Grodzinsky has been the best professor I have had at Tech. She is very clear with her details and explains concepts vey well. Hands down the best, and I would gladly choose her as a professor again. Take her class!
Excellent lectures, though not mandatory. Studio is required and has weekly quizzes. Make sure to do the homework and practice problems, and you'll be prepared for the test.

Prof. G is SO amazing! She makes the pre-lecture videos for all of the Math 1552 classes; explains concepts thoroughly and is always available to answer any more questions we come up with. Hw checks, quizzes, and final are same for entire department; practice each week (use Paul's Online Math Notes). HIGHLY recommend taking Prof. G! She's the best!

I highly recommend taking Professor Grodzinsky for Math 1552 if you are not very confident in your calculus skills. Her grading provides much favor to her students and her lectures are very thorough. Go to lecture, practice problems on study guide, go to studio, and attend OH if needed.

Mrs. Grodzinsky was always caring and calm. She really reminded me of a grand mother. She always kept her students informed on what they needed to do to succeed. Also, taking this course felt like you were learning math from somebody you knew personally, who also knew plenty about what they were teaching.

Grodzinsky was the best professor I have had and she is the best professor anyone will have at Georgia Tech and that is a straight fact. She is amazing and kind and makes the tests and the course enjoyable. If you do the homework, and go to lecture, you will succeed in this class for sure. Klara Grodzinsky is awesome and I will miss her class.
She's really sweet and I really enjoyed learning from her!

As someone who is generally intimidated by math (I know, weird for a Tech student), I honestly couldn't have asked for a better professor/course organizer. Her lectures are clear, she posts recordings and notes after class, she's highly accessible out of lecture, and is super sweet/understanding. I was able to do well in Calc 2 thanks to her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The sweetest professor at Tech! Clear lecturer and grader. Content isn't too difficult and there are many other assignments to help boost your grade if tests/quizzes aren't your thing. I definitely recommend her for calc 2.
Dr. G has been the best math teacher I've ever had. her lectures are amazing and she gives enough examples to make the homework doable and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's so sweet but knows her stuff. Her lectures are well structured and organized and she teaches at a comfortable pace, you rly get the most out of it without getting overwhelmed. Homework is basically the notes you can use to study for the final and minimum work so you don't feel like you're wasting effort. If you suck at math, take her.

Loved having her for integral!! She is so kind and organized! She had worksheets for every class (great study materials), let us submit photos of our pets for Pet of The Day and even organized optional meet n greets the day after tests! Could not possibly have been more caring or accommodating. If you get the chance to take her class, do!!

Grodzinsky was the only math professor I've had that I liked. She was so sweet, explained things well, and was always willing to help. Lecture was not mandatory, but studio attendance was. There was a weekly quiz that was exactly like a homework question (notes allowed) Notes were allowed on all tests actually!

Professor Grodzinsky is one of the best lecturers at Gatech. The material was a bit tough but she made it simple enough to allow everyone to understand. Along with that shes very caring and empathetic. If you have the chance to take Grodzinsky please take it!

I used dual enrollment credit for Calc1, and I didnt have a solid foundation in math. My struggles in this class werent due to Mrs. Gs teaching. She was helpful, encouraging, and often met with me to discuss my grades and specific problems. She even included me in a small group of similarly challenged students to work with her.

I cannot express just how much I respect Professor G... She is WONDERFUL! Her Homeworks are to the point and helpful -not excessive, she genuinely cares about her students and is very helpful inside and outside of class. Her lectures are AMAZING... probably the best online lecturer I have had yet. Such a smart and awesome professor, a 10/10 tbh.

She is very caring when it comes to students and always wants the best for them. Her lectures are good and she is open to any questions! Incredibly lucky to have the course managed by her and be in her section.

Literally amazing. There's really nothing to say about her that hasn't already been said, but she is hands-down one of the top 3 professors that I've had at Tech so far. Informational & engaging lectures, reasonable exams and quizzes, and suuuper caring. She's so approachable which makes going to office hours likeable(and super helpful)! 10/10!

Excellent professor. Easily accessible outside and explains things well in class and office hours. besides homework and studio worksheets, i did not have to do anything more and got an A. Go to class and if you're still confused, go to office hours and you will succeed. she was also amazing and accommodating during this pandemic!! TAKE HER!

Prof. Grodzinsky is one of the best at Tech. Made a slightly difficult class quite manageable with her brilliant explanations. Super empathetic and supportive of students too. Tests are not too hard, and going to studio helps if you're new to Calculus.

Would absolutely recommend Grodzinsky for Calc 2. Explains things very thoroughly and is very approachable in office hours. Even though the class is hard, she explains all concepts and practical calculations extremely well.

I can say that this class is unpleasant in terms of its content, but Prof. Grodzinsky truly cares about her students and wants them to understand. Especially as we transitioned online, she was so helpful and accessible to help. Definitely a great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I struggled some with the class, but that is because I find integral kind of difficult and didnt have a good ta. However, Grodzinsky was a good lecturer and did a lot of example problems. She was extremely nice and helpful when I reached out to her, and she genuinely cares about her students. Also, she doesnt allow laptops in class fyi.

Professor Grodzinksy is one of the best professors at Tech. She thoroughly explains the concepts in class and explains the concepts as well as works through problems. She's accessible outside of class with plenty of office hours. She also prepares many resources like handouts, formula sheets, charts etc. Totally recommend her for Calc 2.
Dr. Grodzinsky makes calc II very very easy. The course with her is a smooth ride. Her lectures are great and if you attend all of them you shall do very well in this class.

Dr Grodzinsky is the best professor I had so far at Tech! Her lectures are so good that there's no need to read the book. Since she has +20 years teaching this class every content is clearly presented. What I did to study was attend lectures, recitation, do hw, and practice exams bf tests, and it worked really well. Do not miss her lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor for Calc 2. The lectures were good, and the studios with a TA were really helpful.
She is the pinnacle of what a math professor should be. Her best quality is how much she cares for her students, and it shows in her lectures, communication, and everything in between.

She writes color coded notes in class for lecture and uses really good examples. She's also very approachable and just nice in general. Tests aren't curved even though it seems like they should be sometimes (we had a test avg in the 60's). Final grades are curved on an individual basis for borderline grades.
GODzinsky. Amazing professor, very clear in lectures and always made sure everyone understood everything. Take her for Calc 2 if you can.
Her lectures are awesome. Overall great professor.
I'm not gonna say that this is an easy class. But the professor is amazing for her teaching methods.

Her lectures consist of slides AND her own handwritten notes on another screen. She shows all her steps and color codes everything to make it clear and easy to understand. She explains concepts very well and is very organized in her style of teaching. Definitely try to get her as a professor.

Dr. Grodzinsky' s lectures are very effective - her slides and handout sheets are awesome. She answers questions in Piazza really quickly and with detail. She manages the recitation TAs well. She is clear about grading and gives opportunities for struggling students to improve their grades. She changed my view of Math at GT. 5/5

She's a very sweet, caring professor. She's great at explaining concepts and makes sure to give a good number of practice examples. This class is a VERY manageable A if you do the review packets before each test (questions basically get pulled from this with the numbers changed). I highly recommend her!!

Professor Grodzinsky is THE professor to take for Calc II. If you listen during lectures and go to recitation, you'll be more than ok. The worksheets in recitation are hard, but the tests are generally pretty easy. The only people I know who struggled in this class didn't show up to class. She has a lot of office hours, which are also helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Klara is a gem. She's so enthusiastic about teaching math, and she really cares about her students. Her office hours are super helpful, and she'll really take the time to sit down and work on a problem 1 on 1. Always there to help. But don't miss class because there's a lot of material she has to cover so she moves fast.
If you put the work in you will do well. Go to lecture and succeed

Professor Grodzinsky is really good at explaining concepts and working through problems in class. Far and away the best math teacher I've ever had. Weekly quizzes are difficult but if you can do well on those and on the worksheets, you'll be fine for the tests.

She truly is the best pick for a Calc 2 teacher at Georgia Tech. Everyone convinced me that I would fail Calc 2 at Tech because it's considered the hardest of the pre-req maths, but I ended with a high A in this class because of her. She really cares about her students and wants to help you. You have to put in the effort, but an A is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great professor, probably the best you can get for integral calc here. Her lectures are great and she really does care about her students.

She seems to be the solid pick for Calc 2. If you are taking this class, then this is the teacher to take. All of her recitation worksheets are as difficult or harder than the tests/quizzes, so as long as you understand the material in class, then you're fine. She is also a nice person and has copious amounts of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome

Mrs. G is one of the best professors at this school. She is always so caring and able to contacted outside of class. Granted, she teaches one of the hardest lower level classes, Calc 2. However, she is truly a caring professor that is passionate about what she teaches.  It is inspiring to see a professor so passionate about their field. 10/10

Klara was a great professor. Her lectures were very engaging and she explained difficult concepts clearly. Participation in lectures and recitation counts toward your grade. It is a small percentage but it is definitely worth it to  show up and get the points. Office hours are very helpful as well and there is a bonus question on every test.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall a great teacher. There are quizzes every single week which is pretty stressful and you have to really study for them because you only get 15 minutes and they are only 2 questions. Good teacher but content of the subject is difficult. Be ready to study and do lots of extra practice outside of class.

Klara is the embodiment of an ideal professor. She is unique at Tech in that she teaches by solving real hw and test problems rather than pointlessly outlining theory. She took her personal time to give me extra help when my grades started to slip. It's really hard to find a seat in her classes, so consider yourself extremely lucky if you nab one.

great teacher, really cares about students, explains things well, doesn't leave anything out, many opportunities for good grade, easy quizzes and tests if you try or i you're just a huge nerd/really smart

I took her in the late short summer session, and that was a mistake. I am not great at math, but I always make an A - except for this class. I was very fast paced. She is very vague about what is going to be on the tests/quizzes. There is a lot of homework to boost your grade. She does give partial credit. Her lectures are not helpful.

Professor Grodzinsky is great. Her lectures are clear and are all accompanied by helpful powerpoints, which she then posts online. She provides comprehensive review sheets before all of her tests. I took her for Math 1552 and then again for 1553 - scheduling all of my other classes around hers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Klara is a solid calc teacher. She explains things well, but she requires your undivided attention. If you have taken Calc AB or BC and you didn't receive credit, then MATH 1551 will be a breeze. Go to her office hours if you don't understand and she will be glad to help.

Grodzinsky was very enthusiastic professor. I did poorly on one test and that brought my average down, so make sure you dont screw up on one test cause there are only 3. She gave weekly quizzes on Fridays, which was very annoying, so I couldnt party on Thursday nights. Turn in HW on Fridays also so Thursday nights were busy.

Grodzinsky is one of the shimmering diamonds of Tech's math department. She's an amazing lecturer. She was more than willing to help me when I was struggling and brought to an A. She gives lots of great examples. Worksheets and quizzes really hit home concepts. If you can get a seat in her class, TAKE IT!!! Don't be tempted to skip LinAlg lecture..

Took her for 1552. Really sweet lady and good prof. She cares about her students. I honestly got a C in her class (not a math person...) but I still enjoyed having her. She was pretty clear and a good lecturer. Also regarding textbook use: never used the textbook but used Math Lab all the time, considering all the hw is on there.
By far the best teacher for 1552. She has extra review sessions before tests and extends/adjusts office hours where necessary. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.
Provides additional recitations as well as office hours. Explanations are clear and, if not, she will take the time to continue explaining outside of class until you understand it.
She is seriously one of the nicest people ever. She's very lenient but most of the class is online and sometimes she doesn't explain topics very well. Other than that, everything was pretty easy.

She is very nice and helpful. She wants you to learn... all it takes is going to class, taking notes, and doing the homework. Go to class and recitation because it counts towards your grade and helps you learn! There's quite a bit of homework, tests, and quizzes. She's one of the best math professors at tech, so definitely take her class!

She is probably the best professor I have had yet here at Tech. Lectures were super clear and she had great examples of everything. I never cracked open the book and got an A. It's not too difficult and that is nice.  If you don't get an A something is wrong.
She gives tests and quizzes and curves at the end. Highly suggest her!

After the series and sequences bit, the class was a cakewalk. all homework is on an online textbook thing, so that's why it is kinda important. never looked at the book itself unless I missed a class. Clear, easy, explains well.

Grodzinsky is the type who would have baked all 200 of us cookies before the final if she had a big enough oven. She really wants her students to understand calculus and make a good grade- she's not trying to trick you. That being said, I still had to work to get an A. I studied like crazy, made average grades on the tests and an A on the final.

She's always willing to help out and is very patient with you if you go to her with a problem. Attending lecture is mandatory and not going will cost you some points, but honestly with her explaining everything  you'll get a lot out of the lectures.

Best math teacher ever. Explains math very clearly and with crazy good examples. Never had as good a math teacher. Tests very similar to in class exercises. She doesn't make her tests unrealistically harder than practise questions. Just amazing.

I got a 100.23 in the class. Her assignments are very similar to the tests, and she's very clear. She posts practice problems for the exams, and if you can do those, then you will be fine in the class.

The easiest A I've gotten at Tech (102%). If you took AP Calc BC or IB Math HL you are gonna have a really easy time with her. I never met someone that could explain math that well. Definitely take her. Her tests are similar to the practice exams. The final was really easy. I got over 100 with minimum studying. Take her over any professors.

Grodzinsky is awesome! Her lectures were always well attended because they were clear and helpful. Her tests were reasonable if you reviewed the recitation worksheets and practice tests she puts online. She is always willing to help and is very approachable. Not a super easy class - you'll have to work for an A - but she makes an A possible!

Very understanding and sympathetic, always willing to help students. She cares a lot about her students. She's not easy A, you have to work for your grade! You'll do fine on the tests ONLY when you study recitation problems and review guides. She's one of the best professors you can get at Tech, take her!!
Great teacher. Very clear and helpful. Has great homework assignments that are actually helpful instead of busy work. Tests are fair.
Very good professor that cares a lot about her class and her students. Tests are fair and she is very clear when she explains material
I love her! She is the best Calc I teacher ever!

Tests are easy as long as you study recitation problems and know how to do them. No tricky problems. Give out at most 4 points at the end for perfect attendance and homework completion and replaces lowest test grade with final. Basically usually more than half of the class ends with an A

Wonderful professor. Does everything she can to boost your grades. Tests are based off of homework, lecture, & recitation problems, so if you can do those then tests should be easy. She's willing to help anyone both online and in person. Be happy if you get her!

Professor Grodzinsky was an amazing professor. I learned a lot in her class, despite already being pretty familiar with Calculus. Her tests weren't easy, but not too difficult if you put in the effort of doing homework and studying. She really cares about her students. Wish I could have her for Calc II.

Mrs. G. truly is a blessing. She was always eager to answer questions and work with her students. Her tests became increasingly harder, but if you go to class, do the online homework, and do the review problems when she provides them you'll be fine! I'm not even a strong math student and I pulled of a B. :)
This woman is a gem. She's extremely helpful and truly cares about her students. As long as you study hard for the tests you will do fine as they are very fair. I would HIGHLY recommend her.

She is so sweet and a GREAT teacher, but the tests are still very difficult. You have to be more than just comfortable with the material. You have to be an expert to do great...and thats given with almost any math class at tech.

Incredibly nice professor. She really cares about her students and the class is pretty easy. If you go to recitation and lecture, do the weekly homework, and study old tests, you'll do great. Also, final exemption if you have a 92%

Highly recommended. I struggled through the class but she grades very fairly and indeed does care about the students.  very approachable, easy to understand, would recommend her against many other 1502 professors.

Mrs. G. is fantastic. She made one of the "weed out" classes at Tech interesting and informative. Her grading policy is very forgiving since I had a 60% test/quiz average and still got a B in the class. Recommend her 100%

She is the nicest and one of the best math teachers at TECH! Her teaching of Calc 1 helped me throughout Calc 2 as well. Very nice and approachable and cares about her students and their performance! TAKE HER!!!

Klara Grodzinsky is a light at the end of a dark tunnel here at Tech. There are too many professors that only care about their research, but Klara puts her students ahead of everything else. If you can get her, I highly recommend it. Her lectures are clear as day and tests are fair if you put forth the effort.

Grodzinsky could teach calculus 2 to a kindergardener. She took the most failed class at Georgia Tech and made it very easy, understandable, and interesting. The tests are very fair, and so is the final (I ended up with a 102 average for the class- the class average was an 80). My advice is to do whatever it takes to get Grodzinsky for calculus 2.
This professor was very helpful in class and had clear explainations of the concepts she was teaching.  She also grades quite liberally and does not make passing difficult at all.

She's a good instructor.  Her policies are very fair and she is generous in grading and dropping some bad grades.  At midterm I had a mid-C, and I ended up with a very high A. Apply yourself!  Finally, a Tech class where hard work pays off.

Nice guy who was helpful the 1-2 times I went to his office hours, but lectures were difficult to understand and he wouldn't always make it all the way through them. But, you can just watch the online lectures or find another professor to go to so professor doesn't really matter in here. Whole class takes the same exams so really doesn't matter
Very hard to understand with accent.

Great guy, truly cares about his students and knows topics well. However he uses lots of jargon which makes learning hard and he has a very monotone voice. He also has a slight accent but after a week or two is no problem.
He overcomplicates simple topics and the accent makes it hard to understand sometimes. Just watch the online video lectures that are available to everyone and you'll be fine.
Nice guy and willing to explain if you have questions, but lectures are dry and boring, making it hard to pay attention.

at first his accent can be sort of confusing to understand, but you get used to it pretty quick. his lectures are a bit dry and monotone, but the concepts and material are explained well. however, sometimes he uses confusing notation. he answered students questions very well, and the tests are easy to prepare for with the library of past tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
I have never before encountered, much less been taught by, a professor who is so exceedingly skillful at convoluting the most basic concepts.
Professor He uses lots of jargon. After a while, I stopped going to lectures and had to watch the head pfr.'s online videos. It is not his accent that makes him mediocre.
His accent is very hard to understand and he uses very lofty math terms instead of explaining the concepts in a relatable way.

His lectures were a bit monotone and hard to follow, but the lecture notes were perfect for his tests and quizzes. Handwriting can be a bit confusing but you can get used to it pretty quick. The tests were not hard and are easy to prepare for using the notes.

I had him for both 1553 and 2552, and I can tell he improved a lot after his first semester. Lectures were good, tests were reasonable, and overall nice guy. I didn't perform very well on the midterms (not b/c they were hard) but I got an A on the final and was at an 89, but he rounded my final grade to an A b/c he could tell how hard I worked.
This might have been a math class, but its clear the prof never went to his teaching classes. Lectures were a mix of accent-heavy mumbled jargon, with scribbled notes to match. Avoid at all costs.

His lectures were great. He explained everything thoroughly and doesn't have the accent people claim he does. As long as you pay attention, its a good class. The quizzes made sense and followed the lecture notes.

He does not have a heavy accent like the other ratings suggest, I promise. He is a pretty normal lecturer, not the best, not bad. His tests for Differential Equations are very reasonable. The quizzes are reasonable too. Solid class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor He is nice and knowledgeable, but doesn't present very well. His handwriting is pretty difficult to understand, but you eventually can read it. It can be a struggle with his boring, monotone lectures (especially 8am), but if you do notes after class its pretty easy with his uploaded notes. He also writes easy tests comparatively.

I signed up specifically for Dan Margalit, who was replaced by Prof. He the first day of class. Extremely frustrating. His accent wasn't hard to understand, but his handwriting was awful and he went way too fast for us. Lecture was spent frantically writing instead of learning...less than 10 people were coming to class by the end. Do not recommend.

He's a new professor. Accent heavy, mumbles, bad handwriting, doesn't understand student questions... He was late to our final exam as well... I wouldn't take him unless he's a desperate last resort. I wish I watched the head professor's videos to actually get a better grade...

You can definitely tell he's a new professor... His accent and handwriting makes it really hard to follow along in class (I stopped showing up and watched Jankowski's videos). Instead of learning, it feels like you're just trying to follow his train of thought.

Very clearly a new professor. Accent and bad handwriting made his lectures hard to follow, often wasn't able to cover all the material required in the class period. Most stopped going and watched Jankowski's videos or took notes off posted powerpoint slides (that he does not use). Showed up late to his own final. Hoping he adjusts for the future.

He's not the best teacher, and he doesn't explain things that well. However, attendance is not mandatory, and everyone in the class just ended up watching Jankowski's lecture videos. He does have good style though.

Terrible prof. His lectures were useless. He had a thick accent, terrible handwriting, and was very monotone so the entire lecture you would just be struggling to follow what he was trying to say as opposed to actually learning the course.Just watch Jankowski's recorded lectures and you will be fine.

Professor Chicas is easily one of the best lecturers at Scheller. His classes are highly engaging and often involve interactive activities. As far as homework goes, he assigns short readings and occasional quizzes that supplement the topics that he teaches in class. The exams are easy and the group project at the end of the year is pretty cool too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was chill, allowed technology to be used. Material was not difficult, even if you crammed a night before. There are exams and a group project, so be aware. Threw us a pizza party at the end. You can tell he cares about the material a lot and tries to engage the class however he could. His lectures can go on for long, but I know ppl who liked it

Very enthusiastic in every lecture, brought great energy. Study sessions in class for big tests (2) which are all multiple choice. Uses good examples and activities when needed, makes lectures interesting and engaging. Cared about students' success and is available in email. Definitely recommend as a professor
Great teacher and laidback class. Take him for OB!
He's awesome, liked him and his class.
Professor Chicas is an amazing professor who cares a lot about what he teaches. Take him for an easy A, the group project is super fun!
Take him for an easy A. Great guy

These comments are tripping. He's a great teacher and a great dude. He gave several "mental health days", he engages the class in lectures, he brought pizza on the last lecture day. I guess he didn't used to allow devices but he does now. Favorite professor for sure. Take him.

Professor Chicas is very passionate about what he teaches, though lectures can be a little long. He tries his best to engage his students and make the information interesting. 2 exams, including the final, which are fair as long as you keep up with the readings and lecture material and group project worth 30%

Mandatory attendance, no technology, and group activities lowk forces you to pay attention to his lectures that he really tries to make engaging. So then the tests and projects aren't hard since you were forced to pay attention. Really nice and cares too much. The IP address thing was funny imo. If you don't show up, tests still easy if you study.

Acts as though he is caring but doesn't even respond to one of my emails explaining my situation with absences. Tests are worth way too much but not overly difficult. Very energetic and passionate about what he teaches but again I found him to be very unprofessional for just ignoring me. Would not take him again.

Prof Chicas is not flexible AT ALL and the requirements and rules for this class were absolutely ridiculous. No technology policy and he checked attendance through QR codes. On the last day of class, he announced he had been tracking IP addresses for the codes-  felt like a huge power trip to the students.

Awesome guy, very passionate and cares a lot about his students. Lectures were mostly engaging and some had in class activities. He has a no technology rule, but allowed iPads for notes. The exams really aren't hard if you pay attention in class, and he offered extra credit. Would definitely take again.

I think he has great intentions; I understand that he is very passionate about teaching bc he's new, however this class is supposed to be simple and easy and it is not. His lectures are mind-numbing and no technology, so you have to just sit there. He also weights the 2 exams as 50% of your grade and they're not really simple. Have to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy but very extra. He's a new teacher so  makes it a lot harder than it needs to be. One midterm, one final, and a video project basically determine your grade. Attendance is also mandatory, and he checks ip address on the QR code submission. Would take a professor who is more chill and does not require midterms tbh, cool guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, lectures are attendance required and taken by qr code. He insists on no technology period, either take paper notes or just sit and listen. Gives short reading quizzes throughout semester but only 2 tests and a group project. Wish more grades could help better reflect my understanding of material. Again, cool guy but idk if I'd take again
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor, but his lectures are very lengthy. No technology and attendance and participation is mandatory. He does attendance QR codes and can see the location of where you filled it out. There are 2 tests, weighing 30% each. I think he made the class a lot harder than it needed to be. Take a professor who doesn't give midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really knows his stuff and inspires passion for the subject, lectures are not boring. He talks about his research a lot, and it's a good real-life example (plus it's pretty cool). He makes the content seem easy, but the class is definitely hard. Read the textbook anytime you don't understand something, and don't get behind on content.

I loved Professor Hester. He can explain things in a way that makes it make sense. Highly, highly recommend taking it with him if given the opportunity. The class was difficult and concept-heavy, but he works really hard to make it more digestible for students while also being really funny and personable.

2 exams, 4 hws, 2 programming assignments. read the textbook, was way more useful for exams than the lectures. his teaching style gives the impression that this is an easy A class. lectures are kinda boring. hws and programming assignments are easy, just put some effort into the exams. final exam was really hard but we got 20 point curve

Toshi is hands down the most caring professor I've had. He is passionate about teaching and sharing insight on actual missions he has worked on. Attending lectures/office hours is strongly reccomended, HW can be challenging but he is accessible and willing to help. He knew everyone by name and is 100% invested in his students' learning and success.

I would highly recommend Toshi for 4361. He truly cares about what he teaches and would often ask students for feedback on assignments and tests. In class quizzes are more of an attendance grade than a quiz grade. He made AE 4361 my favorite class by far even though HW was tough. However, his office hours are a great source of help for HW.

The review of May 2024 was from the professor's first offer of the course, so there were naturally some bugs to be squashed. The homeworks are tough but serve well to teach you the course content, and the lectures prove helpful. The midterm was subpar, but he fixed the issue later: the final exam was much more fair. Overall a good course.

Avoid at all costs

Almost managed to make an easy class difficult 

Hws often took 6-10 hrs and required outside material (old notes, google)

Questions on the forum answered unhelpfully (usually just: "please refer to xxx")

Hw worth 10% while the 15 min quizzes worth 20%

Tests tested review lecture attendance not actual knowledge
He clearly cares greatly about students' understanding of material and is happy to dedicate time helping you work through issues. Great professor.

Chill dude with engaging lectures, especially if you're interested in the subject. Only work is weekly reflections, simple midterm, and a long but easy final essay; keep up with the readings and pay attention in class and you'll be fine (he's an easy grader). Doesn't post slides so take notes and try not to miss class. Be prepared to talk in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Very well-read and an excellent orator. However, I wish he posted slides. I would take again!!

Overall, average INTA class. Lots of lecturing on slides. The material was enlightening, but I did not personally learn more than I came in with. The midterm was easy, very easy. The final paper was tedious, but also pretty easy. He is a nice professor.

Great class, & you learn great foundational concepts. Not many assignments, just weekly reflections, midterm, and final paper. A lot of reading, but they are for your benefit. Midterm and final-you will be thankful that you took notes on the readings and during class. Very understanding professor, but take notes in class. He does not post slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his class online. We had quizzes each week material was very hard he gave a lot of material. He did not teach and when asked for assignments to improve grade he agreed until the end of the semester he will not give it to you. He does not care about his students.
Don't take this class. Worst class I have taken at Tech.

This guy does not know his stuff at all when it comes to the basic biology we covered.  He failed at explaining both basic genetics and evolution -- couldn't draw a punnett's square and confused Darwinian evolution with Lamarckian evolution during lecture.

Exams are super hard!! Not even reading the book would help that much!! The class is also designed to not give a fair A!! If have an 100 on everything (pop quizzes, hw, assignments), you still have to make an 85 average on the test to get an A and averages are like in 72s and 75s. If you want a fair A, don't take this class.

I found his exams to be kinda hard since you basically have to read the book cover to cover in order to do well. He's really nice though! Powerpoints can be interesting, but please make sure you read the book!
Young, amiable guy. Engaging lecture; simple, non-cumulative exams. Detailed reading is recommended.
A pretty nice professor. Exams & quizzes are not too hard if you read the textbook and PowerPoints. Extra credit points are given for participating in experiments.

I did not expect general psychology to be so difficult. The tests are way harder than the quizzes. YOU MUST READ THE BOOK WORD FOR WORD!!! I like the teacher just fine, but his tests are killing me and he doesn't even give you insight as to what will be on the exams.

Really informative and a great professor. It is easy to do well on tests, but you HAVE to read the book, which isn't difficult at all. There are quizzes but they are pretty easy. SHOW UP TO CLASS! Definitely worth taking if you can.
interesting, young, keeps the class entertaining and informative

Wasn't thrilled at first but she's actually very nice, energetic and passionate, and I appreciate that she actually shows up during labs (even 8am's) when many professors would just leave it all to TAs.

She seemed very nice at first but has been shown to repeatedly understate the class difficulty. She said that it's an easy class and nearly everyone gets an A but her gpa is a 3.3 and I know I'm not the only one who found the reports to be extremely harshly graded (and also be very unclear in criteria)
Awesome teacher.
Lab reports were very long, but labs themselves were fun and informative. Lectures were clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Labs and lecture were run well, but reports were insanely long and disorganized.
great move by Georgia Tech. great professor and chill guy. he makes stat fun and understandable. take him

He was an awesome professor. Very understanding of students needs and was very accessible for office hours when needed. A lot of students did not perform well on one exam so he made an optional take home R exam to replace exam grades.

Mark is incredibly knowledgable and very passionate about statistics! He lectures effectively and is very thorough in responding to questions. This class was not difficult (and attendance is not required), though I can see it being challenging if you were to skip too many in-person lectures. The accompanying lab is largely self-directed.

There's good, there's great, then there's Dr. Himmelstein (Mark). A genuine dude, statistics extraordinaire, and a true diamond in the psych department at GT. He's one of the best professors I've had at Tech, and it's clear that he really cares about his students. 1000/10, take him

I took this course in Fall 2023. This class was an easy A. As long as you did the assignments, you are almost guaranteed to get a good grade. Hibbard was lenient with due dates and was accessible outside of class. Attendance was mandatory, so make sure you come to lecture or letter grades will start coming off quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hibbard is one of the best professors that you could take. If you have the opportunity to take him, please do! The class discussions are very engaging. The class was mandatory but he cared about the well-being of his students, so communication was all he asked for.

Goated professor. He was very lenient with what you could submit for the 3 main projects in the class, and gave 100s as long as you followed the rubric well. He also structured his class very well while assigning minimal unnecessary work, and clearly cared about the well-being of the students. His lectures also focused on relevant modern-day topics
Great professor! Super accessible and understanding, very willing to work with students. I highly recommend his Apocalypse course.
I absolutely recommend Professor Hibbard. He was very laid back and really looked at his students as human beings. His class was enjoyable, and easy as long as you do your work.

I think Dr. Hibbard was an amazing professor. First of all, the section of the apocalypse was very interesting. Some of my things we did were learn about the Zelda Timeline, make a zombie survival plan, and play Plague Inc as a class. Dr. Hibbard was very understanding and a fair grader. You should take him if you can.
Super cool person. The class was very interesting, and the lectures were super engaging. Was very clear with grading criteria, and also had an extra credit assignment.

There was a good amount of homework and assignments, but they were more opportunities to raise your grade. She was very forgiving of late submissions. She was very funny and made the class enjoyable to attend.
I love Dr Wu!! She truly cares about all of her students and is highly accessible after class
Great professor, fostered a really welcoming environment and a delight!
Loved her! My favorite professor at Tech
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very informative and very creative class - awesome speakers coming to class to visit and also just interesting content. as an engineer I was very skeptical of taking the class, but it turned out to be one of my favorites in all of my degree

Dr. Wu's Chinese Society, History, and Culture class was very interesting. She would talk in depth about the concepts in an engaging manner. There are lots of assignments with presentations, quizzes, tests, student comments, and a final exam. As long as you do the work, it's an easy A though. However, it's crucial that you keep up!

Pretty easy humanities credit. The class was six week late short summer course, so it was alot of work. About 4-5 assignments each week that take about an hour each. There is a quiz each week that takes about an hour. There are two group projects and one podcast which adds to the workload. I took four summer classes but it was managable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her class is really easy! Quizzes are open note but all you need are lecture slides and the textbook so you don't even really need to take notes if you don't want to. She's very nice when you ask for help on quizzes. No final exam but 3 tests that you take remotely with 5 attempts!

Not only is she a great teacher but she is funny, caring, fair, and flexible. All assignments are very doable/fair. She gives one homework and quiz per week. There is one small podcast project and one small presentation and you will get a good grade just for doing them. Three tests plus final. My favorite professor Ive had at Tech. I recommend!!!!

LING3100 with Professor Wu is a great choice for a humanities credit. Most of the class was based on low-pressure presentations on research papers and were mainly for the purpose of encouraging class discussions. I feel like I learned a lot from this class and the workload was very manageable. As a person, she is extremely kind and caring.

Most of the grade is concentrated in a few assignments but they arent too difficult, and deadlines are very reasonable. Dr. Wu did a good job teaching the material and keeping the class engaged, but it does move slow at times (with the benefit of giving us time to read research papers). Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's super nice, and clearly is passionate about linguistics, and lectures are interesting! The complaint most have is that there's too much work, but I think the homeworks are the only thing in this class that take > 1 hour to do. Exams and quizzes are straight up from the slides, and not too difficult if you skim the slides beforehand.

Dr. Wu is really nice but the assignments are so time consuming, the quizzes and tests aren't that hard but there is a lot of content to learn, the homework is really long and there are so many other time consuming assignments, I wouldn't take it again because the assignments are so time consuming

Dr. Wu is very kind and accessible, but the grading in this class is extremely pedantic. I understood the lectures, but I would always be surprised by my grades on exams and quizzes. Luckily, the course is structured so that you should still be able to get an A (projects, etc.) even with the insane grading on tests. Class is A LOT of work.

Professor Wu is easily approachable and accessible. Plus, her lectures are super entertaining (but thankfully she doesn't seem to care much if you do other stuff on your computer as long as you're in class). Overall she's a great professor! Her main downsides are that she gives lots of hours' worth of homework and exam grading is VERY meticulous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wu was very caring and wanted everyone to succeed. This class was not very difficult, but it was a lot of work. There were frequent quizzes, homeworks, and readings as well as mandatory attendance. Not Professor Wu's fault, but I still struggled to be interested in the material despite her enthusiasm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: a lot of people sign up for linguistics expecting to do literally no work because it's a humanities course. professor wu is so sweet and clearly so passionate about the field and our learning, and she always tries her hardest to find a way for us to get enthusiastic about the content. hws can be time intensive, but really nothing bad for gt.

Do not take this class in person, especially if you are looking for an easy A. Professor assigns homework that takes hours a week and is a very significant part of your grade. Homework  and a project was even assigned during spring break with a test being the first day back from break. Lectures are very vague and not well put together.

Great class taught by a great professor.  Very reasonable grading and a fair amount of work.  Don't expect to do nothing in this class and get an A, but also don't expect to put a lot of effort in either.  Lectures are interesting, homeworks add to the lectures, and tests cover material from both.  Two projects that are pretty fun

Grading: 3 Midterms + 1 Final (noncumulative) (all 25% and multiple choice). Lecture: 6/10; Passion: 8/10; Communication: 4/10; Flexibility: 10/10; Test Prep: 8/10 Quirks: very quiet, gives plenty of extra credit, knowledgeable. Recommendation: Skip every lecture and cram 1 week before tests for easy A. Sit in the front row if you want to hear him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor to take for History.
Graded by 4 tests. One of the four is a written test that covers a book. All four tests are very straightforward. Very chill professor and I enjoyed his lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's genuinely the sweetest and definitely knows what hes talking about. in the beginning of the year its a little hard to get the rhythm of how he lectures but eventually in the 1st 2 weeks you get the hang of it. He gives so much easy extra credit for tests; like sometimes when not many people showed up, he just gives out extra credit if ur there
While his lecturing can be a bit boring at times, it is clear he knows the content very well. The exams are difficult but he gives many resources to get you prepared, and the content is digestible.

Grade is based on 3 MCQ exams and a written exam on the Cherokee Removal book; gives 5% extra credit for writing essays. Shouldn't be hard if it's not your first time learning US history. However I do wish that Prof. Hild's lectures are more engaging, sometimes it's very easy to lose track of what he's talking about and hear everything clearly.
Computer wasn't working one day, cancelled class and gave everyone 5% extra credit on the next exam just because. Love this guy

I absolutely love Professor Hild! While his lectures didn't strike much interest with me, he gave everything you needed to succeed. The class has four tests, one being a straightforward forward book test. All other tests, including the final, were fifty multiple-choice questions. Reading the textbook chapters is useful, but not required to pass.
Hild is super chill, understanding, and makes it easy to get a good grade. Lectures can sometimes feel a little long, but the tests aren't hard at all.

Chill dude, but his lectures can be pretty boring sometimes. You can get an A in his class by cramming a few days before each exam. The entire class was 4 exams, one of which was open book. Overall nice, but I wish the lectures were more interesting, as I gradually found going to class to be increasingly inexpedient.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Test heavy but can be studied just through the test study guides. Very little effort actually needed except day before exams. Attendance isn't necessary at all.

He is very knowledgeable and understanding of the students' situations. Grade consists of 4 tests, each worth 25% of your grade, but it really isn't that difficult and has enough extra credit for you to do well.

I took this course in Spring 2022. This course was easy as long as you paid attention in lecture. Hild is a bit of a dry lecturer. The grade is based off of 3 exams and a hand-written essay done in class. They are simple if you engage in the material.

I took this course in the Fall of 2021. The entirety of the grade was made up of 3 exams and an essay that was written in class on paper. The exams were easy if you paid attention to the lectures, otherwise, they WILL be challenging. Go to lecture, pay attention, and this will be an easy A.

Excellent professor and easy class. Your entire grade is 3 tests and they are pretty simple long as you study for them. The study guide is your best friend and you have the option for 5 bonus points on each test. Make sure you try and study for tests and its an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring about students needs and makes the class very easy. Only assignments were exams but if you study and do the extra credit then you'll be more than fine. Sometimes I would zone out when he was lecturing but I think that was more because of my lack of interest lol. He also very pretty funny and uploaded all his PowerPoints.

Grade depends on tests but if you show up to class the tests wont be that difficult. He is willing to answer questions and his lectures are long but engaging.

Took class online and it was easy as long as you read the textbook or watch the lectures. Lot of reading but attendance isn't mandatory and professor is very good!

Dr. Hild is a great professor! The course has 4 exams and all are super straightforward. I highly recommend taking his class!

Dr. Hild was a great professor. His class is very straight forward and easy. He makes it clear what you will need to study for the exams. Professor Hild is the man. I took this class during a 5 week period and loved the class. We had 3 tests and he gave us a study guide for each test (test study guides). I studied a few days in advance, went out the night before and made high 90s on every test. I didnt read the text book but read another required book. Loved this class

Professor Hild is such a good professor. Although the course is entirely exam based, he always provides study guides that follow the exam exactly, and as long as you show up to lecture or read the textbook, you'll do fine. His class is very easy as long as you've had some exposure to American history in the past.
I wasn't looking forward to taking this class, but Prof. Hild made it pretty interesting. Only 4 exams, but he offers extra credit too.

love professor hild!!! nice guy, clear lectures (monotone voice tho, be careful not to zone out), some funny jokes. just take good notes in lecture + if u miss one fill in the gaps w/ notes from textbook + study the night before the test  easy a. fully multiple choice, gives decent study guides, doesn't take attendance, lots of extra credit.

This class was easy and most of the tests you could figure out if you've lived in America for ten + years. He was pretty dreadfully boring sometimes, but overall his tests were easy enough that you could prepare for them in a few hours the night before and make close to a perfect score.
Pretty easy to follow, funny at times, made U.S. History enjoyable.
Took him for a five-week New South class in the summer. There were two books but you only had to read one. If you read that one and come to class it is not a difficult A.

Had Hild over the summer and never really showed up for lectures. I would recommend going to the lectures before the tests. I would fill out the study guide he gives and memorize everything on it. If you do that, you'll get an A on the test. The final was the least stressful thing I have ever done at Tech. I loved Prof. Hild.

I had Hild during the summer semester as a summer freshman, and his lecture was overall boring. It's hard to focus when 1, it's content you've already known and 2, he tends to go off on a tangent. His spiels do relate to the content, but they tend to get boring very quickly. He does have easy extra credit opportunities though. It's not a hard class

Dr. Hild is great! He can be monotone a lot, but he is extremely clear. You will always know what will be on the test if you pay attention and at least skim the textbook (just read what he doesn't cover) and you'll be set. Also, he makes jokes, but if you zone out you miss them (trust me, they're good)

Solid pick for a social science/GA History requirement. Test were easy. Did not use textbook. Showed up to a third of the classes. Half of the final exam was open book. Made a comfortable A in the class. Keep in mind that his short summer classes are easier than fall/spring since the summer exams are multiple choice.

Hild's a really nice guy and a great professor. He's not the intimidating professor that first year students might expect. If you read (time consuminng), pay attention in class, and do the study guides you should make a high A with no problems. He also shows a documentary and if you write a short essay you get 5 extra credit points on your test.
