reviews.comment: Professor Hild is one of the best professors I've had so far. He is passionate about what he is teaching, gives students all the material they need to be successful, and offers opportunities for extra credit. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to lectures so you don't have to read the textbook, and do the study guide and extra credit papers. Easy A if you take decent notes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hild is an incredible History professor who obviously knows his stuff. He gives a study guide before each test and the tests are pretty much identical to the study guides. You don't have to come to class, just come for the extra credit movie review, and the study guide and you'll do fine. DO NOT buy the biography book, use SparkNotes instead.

Hild is a great teacher. I enjoyed going to his class even though history can be boring. Pay attention in class, do the study guide, and extra credit papers and you will get an A. The textbook isn't bad, but I didn't use it after the first test.

Dr. Hild, while endearingly awkward, was an amazing lecturer with a real knowledge of history.  He truly loved what he taught and tried so hard to make students see the same way. While lecture isn't necessary b/c he posts them online, it's worth going if only b/c I felt guilty not to due to the effort he put into them.

I took him over the summer and LOVED HIM!!! He's adorably quirky and funny, and I really enjoyed his lectures. He is really passionate about history and gets into telling stories about stuff (sometimes related/unrelated to the curriculum). Over summer we just had 3 tests, all very simple and straight from either the book or lecture.

This is an amazing teacher. I took him over the summer for my U.S. Perspective requirement and he used power points and videos to teach history. Lecture were extremely helpful but students who skipped class and read the book could still make As on his test. I got an 97, 103, and a 84 in the final and I left the class with a 94. Easy if you read.

This class is not as easy as it is made out to be. A lot of the test questions are tricky. There are only 50 per test too, so it is pretty hard to get an A. The Georgia Odyssey paper is also graded somewhat stringently. I finished with a B. For each test, he does give a study guide and a 5 point extra credit paper. He has a good sense of humor too.

I enjoyed HIST 2112 with Hild.  He joked in lecture and made US history as interesting as could be.  Exams are fair, containing about 80% power point material, 10% textbook material and 10% Georgia Odyssey questions.  The Georgia Odyssey was open book and should be an easy 100.

Attendance is not mandatory which is good. His lecture is extremely boring and hard to hear if you sit in the back. He requires you to buy one textbook and one novel like book called Georgia Ody. DO NOT buy the textbook, just buy  GA odys and make sure to completely read it. His tests are reasonable, study key terms and memorize GA Ody.

Really easy class to get an A in. Not too interesting, and he kinda drones on sometimes, but its so easy. Just write a 600 word extra credit paper about some movie prior to each test for 5 extra points. And read Georgia Odyssey for 3 or so questions per test.

The class is providing me a wealth of knowledge about my heritage.  I laughed, and got intellectually sweet on him, when I got into the foreword of his book and read "regionally unique undemocratic character" to describe the state of southern politics in the late 19th c.  If you're a Georgia native, check him out.  I'm loving it.

Super easy! Great teacher! Class was really boring, but it was an easy A, for sure! I'm terrible in History, but I got an A! Georgia Odyssey is a MUST READ to do excellent on his tests! Also, the extra credit paper definitely helps and takes a total of 5 minutes!

This man is awesome. He teaches history with a sense of humor. His test are extremely easy and you can get an A on them by just taking notes. He gives 5 points of extra credit on test for writing a paper on a movie viewed the day before the test. Read Georgia Odyssey and ABSORB it. It's interesting and some questions on the exam are from the book.
Yes bro, yes.

The best thing about his class is that you don't have to go! He gives you a list of terms to memorize before the test and tests you only on that. Also gives you 5% for writing a movie review before each test. I went for 10 classes the whole semester and made an A. Tests were sometimes tricky though. Needed to answer tricky questions to get an A.

I love Hild! He re-uses 2/3's of the questions on his tests so if you study from past tests, as well as any additional study guide, you'll be good to go. He offers 5 points extra credit on each test simply for writing a movie review. I've also been to his office hours where he has been extremely helpful. Take his class!
His lectures are pretty straightforward, if you go to class and take notes and read the textbook then the exams are pretty easy.

Yes, as the poster below noted, you do have to read the book to do well in class, but I never have any problems following his lectures.  He writes all the important stuff on the board during his lectures anyway.  And he was very helpful when I went to his office with the study guide before the exam--he spent over half an hour helping me review.

he's a nice guy but you cant really hear him well when he talks because he mumbles, his lecture isn't that informative. he gives you terms for the test before it, but when the test comes around there are a good amount of questions you needed to have read the book for. some questions he didn't talk about so the tests were kind of hard.

He is an awesome professor, he is pretty funny and he really knows his stuff when it comes to history. Text book was helpful for studying, but if you take good notes and pay attention you will be fine. His tests weren't too difficult either.

I agree with the comments posted in the review below, but would add that he does require a written review of an assigned book in his classes at Tech. It's not a difficult assignment though, and he even lets you submit a rough draft and get his feedback on it if you turn it in early enough.

I took his US History class at Georgia State. Awesome teacher. Funny. Really knows his stuff when it comes to history. Doesn't care about attendence. Take notes and you should be fine. His test aren't too hard and he gives study guides and an extra credit opportunity before each test. No research papers or essays. Test are all multiple choice.
Pretty funny teacher, doesn't require knowledge of dates, only chronology
Funny, gives good study guides, shows interesting films.  Definitely recommended!

The class is awesome. He's funny and interested in the topics he talks about. You can tell he knows alot about it and if you want to learn you definately can. The tests aren't bad if you actually show up to class.
Awesome teacher, not too hard, but if you had the desire to learn you could learn a lot.
No Comments
Seems like a nice guy, funny when he wants to be, plus he curved the grades on our first exam!
get ready to learn chinese buddy

If you memorize the vocab she gives you then it's really chill to get an A. You might have a hard time if you don't know some Chinese words beforehand because they will be put on the test. Sometimes she puts traditional words in the simplified version of the test. Hard to calculate final grade bc she gives letter grades. Class is rlly funny tho

The classes can be challenging, especially because of the sheer number of vocabs. Exams could be slightly difficult as well, but there's a lot of extra credit opportunities to make up for it. 何老师 is very caring, and loves her students.

何老师 is a great teacher and has a very engaging class time. Class size is small, and she is very chill and converses normally with students. Exercises and pre-readings can sometimes feel like a lot of work but were honestly not too bad. Heritage focuses on reading/writing/grammar so it would be hard if your speaking/comprehension were weaker.
The homework can be seen as heavy if you're not already somewhat proficient in Mandarin, but it's do-able. 何老师 is a great teacher for lectures though. She really engages with her students.

何老师很好笑, but this class is WAYY harder than I anticipated. Lots of work that she honestly doesn't prepare for you (essays, dictation, presentations) You're going to be spending a lot of time outside of class if your Chinese isn't great. I don't recommend taking heritage if your speaking is weak. She's very funny and helpful though!

So she is a good lecturer. The reason for the low rating is that on midterms, there are some vocab that you didn't learn in the textbook making it hard to answer some questions when lacking context because of the missing knowledge of some vocab. This happened on every test. Additionally, she does tend to get off topic a lot. She is funny at times

I really liked the class with 何老师. There are usually two synchronous lectures every week where we go through the lessons and do breakout room activities. Exam wise I feel it's pretty fair with tests and a final. There are also homework exercises for every chapter that are due roughly every two weeks. Overall really great class, 100% recommend!!

Funny professor, clearly passionate about teaching Chinese. The class has fast pacing, definitely requires some previous knowledge of Chinese. Course requires a decent amount of memorization. Overall really good class, honestly might be my fav class in my entire college career. 我爱学中文！
I love her class, she can really tell a joke. There's a lot of homework, but she's not a tough grader. Instead, she'll give feedback. The midterm and final are pretty difficult though.

Class was hybrid with an in person debate. If your spoken chinese isn't good, prepare to get grilled by your peers. HW/Essays are the bulk of your grade, and she makes you hand write the hw problems. Quiz/test have honorlock and were kinda difficult, especially the midterm/final. Overall enjoyed the class and encouraged me to improve my Chinese.
Funny professor, pretty lenient grading.
Answered questions clearly and would sometimes hint to what we needed to know for exams. However, topics weren't always explained clearly, so watching Warnock's lectures might be necessary.

1554 is a pretty standardized class, difficult for sure but doable if you study right. Make sure to take several practice exams before a midterm, I underestimated how helpful they are. Prof Hozumi is pretty good, but I would watch Prof Warnock's videos regardless of whether I attended class or not and found them a good supplement.

I was initially worried because of the low ratings, but his lectures were very good and he was always open to answering questions. He sometimes made mistakes but they generally didn't affect learning. I would suggest reading the textbook before class since his lectures really help to reinforce it, and definitely do the practice exams.

Lectures aren't mandatory, but I did like going to them because he writes notes by hand (even though he makes small mistakes). Class is pretty standardized, so it barely matters what professor you have. Take frequent practice tests and do the WebWorks, and you can get an A even if you don't go to class.

I think this professor is fine. He messes up some times with small numbers on the math, but it is because he does not use PowerPoints and writes the notes by hand with you (which I like). It does not really make it harder to understand/learn concepts. Overall just read the textbook and do the practice tests before the exams and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a very great teacher... messed up a lot in class... had to use YouTube to learn most of the concepts...
Messes up sometimes but overall teaches the concepts well, just do the practice tests and you'll be fine.

Like other reviews said, does make mistakes from time to time while lecturing and other students had to point out his mistakes/correct them. Good at lecturing but I felt I only internalized the concepts he taught when I was in studio.

Made mistakes in the very first examples during first week of class... 
Made your choice guys.

Prof. Hozumi can make a lot of mistakes in lecture and at times confuses himself, which can interfere with learning. But, he is usually good at breaking the concepts down and tells you exactly what you need to know for exams. If you do the practice exams you will do well. Hozumi is also very understanding and always helped me with my grade requests

Great explanations of concepts in class, extremely clear because he just explains and does examples right there with you. You do need to put in time outside of class just because the material takes time to understand, but Hozumi is definitely the best lecturer for this class.

I don't know why people trash about him in 1553... In 1552, he is super funny and clear about concepts. His examples in class align with test questions. Before a test, he lists the order of integral tests that you need to find convergence in order, so I'd say that he is pretty good. Also very caring. Asked for a homework extension and he gave one.

I went to class before the first midterm and realized I was better off watching Jankowski's videos. He often got confused over conceptual stuff and would make computational errors. Watch lecture videos and use the textbook. Tests were similar to practice.

Despite it being his first time teaching, he did really well with all the material. He definitely improved as the semester went on, so people who were only there in the beginning and left weren't able to see him improve. He genuinely wanted us to understand where the topics we were doing came from so he would show us some derivations.
Didn't teach the concepts in depth. I was better off not going to class.

I went to lecture but the textbook was by far the most useful resource. He often got himself confused or made computational/definitional errors that he would have to go back over. Tbh the exams were very similar to the practices so the textbook and online lectures were sufficient to figure things out. Nice enough guy and will probably improve.
He was fine, I stopped going and watched Jankowski's lecture. He was knowledgeable but I believe it was his first time teaching the course so he would get things mixed up. Not much to say about him

Stopped going to class after 3 weeks and just used the online resources given by the main guy, Jankowski. Started talking about the definition of a derivative in linear. Save your time, don't go to class.
he is not good at explaining concepts at all.

no solutions for anything (old tests, exam reviews, homeworks, etc) + 2 questions of each homework are graded so its extremely difficult to know if anything is right. i went to office hours, study groups, and tutoring and it wasnt enough, i had no clue if my thought processes were right. not designed for people who dont have experience w proofs imo

Fantastic for 2106. Brilliant, great lecturer, accessible for questions. Two tough midterms worth 20% each. Biweekly quizzes (2 problems straight off HW). Straightforward final (30%). Isn't great about giving feedback on your work, but happy to provide if asked. Extra credit for typing HW in LaTeX. Great professor if you hope to learn the material
pretty useful class. The test was easy most of the time.

She is a great lecturer, and clearly cares very much about her students. Harsh grader though. The only negative I had about this course is that the exams always covered a lot of material while being closed-note, which made the memorization of theorems and results the primary stressor, rather than actually learning and applying the techniques taught
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good professor that knows what she's talking about and knows how to teach. The tests are decently hard but fair; the first test is light and the second and third tests are much harder (but you'll be able to do well if you study). She gives weekly homework assignments that take a couple of hours, but aren't too bad. Overall, would take again.

Really good at explaining concepts, extremely helpful and nice during office hours. Class is pretty challenging, especially if this your first time doing proofs. Tests are hard, but graded very fairly.

Professor Hom is amazing. She's absolutely brilliant and is a thorough lecturer. Lots of homework due once a week (4% extra credit if typed in LaTeX). Every exam is composed of the hardest example from each topic. The class and material itself are very difficult, so it requires a lot of work to understand. Can't wait to take 4107 with her next sem.

Type homeworks in LaTeX for 10% extra credit. Exam 1 is easy but 2 and 3 are much harder, no final for this class. Very good at explaining proof in an intuitive way, useful office hours. The class isn't easy of hard. Took Fall 2020 (COVID & Online)

Super caring professor. This class was just really different from any math class I've ever taken, so I struggled a lot, but Prof. Hom is super willing to help during office hrs. 3 exams counted for 60% of our grade. We had a week to do each HW. No final exam, just a portfolio of proofs
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's so nice!!! Just go to office hours if you have an issue and she'll explain everything. She really cares and knows a lot. If you can, please take math2106 with hom it was literally a godsend. The tests are okay (2nd one is harder) and the homework is long but just find a study group and itll be ok.

She's very enthusiastic and helpful, but she tended to make assumptions about what students would understand and not explain things fully. She was really good about answering questions. Office hours and study groups are a must to survive the homework, which often used uncommon proof techniques that weren't discussed in class. Grading was very fair.

Very passionate and teaches you everything you need to know for the exam. Lectures based off textbooks, but go to class for a better explanation. Test average from first test to second dropped from a B to an F, so stay on top of the material. She's very helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Weekly homework with 10% extra credit each for typing up your solutions. Tests can be difficult, but fair. Attendance quizzes (graded on completion) on Friday. My only gripe with professor Hom is that she doesn't post the solutions to the practice tests online (you have to go to office hours/in-class for solutions). Besides that, amazing professor.

ONLY take him if you're willing to lock in the first half & attend every class. If you attend almost every class you can exempt the final. The midterm is extremely harder than necessary but doable if you pay attention and do ALL the chapter readings. Don't skimp on the chapter notes & studying. I made a C on the midterm, exempted final & got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It's easy to get an A in this class if you just attend lectures (lets you exempt the final) and lock in for the midterm. Classes aren't super interesting, and they're lowkey kinda awkward, but the assignments are pretty easy. Probably the best option for interational business, and he's got some unique experience which adds a little to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: hes one of those proffesors who really care. This was the most interesting class I had while the textbook material was boring I actually enjoyed hearing about international relations. Take the class only if you can come to class almost everyday because it has huge perks. if you do that then you should be good.

Prof Hoadley was entertaining and has a lot of real world experience esp in Asia that he leverages to make this class meaningful. The midterm was somewhat hard, but the essay project is easy - just be careful about citations. He offers extra credit. If attendance is good, he waives the final exam, so go to class. Def the best teacher for 3660.

This class is very lecture heavy by nature, but Hoadley is very passionate about the topics which makes it interesting. He allows the final exam to be waived if you have very good attendance. There is one midterm that can be a little difficult, but not too bad. Textbook is only important for the online, remote quizzes.

Attendance not mandatory, but if 70% of class attends 70% of the classes, then no final. This probably won't happen, but if you miss 2 classes or less, final is exempt. take home quizzes 25% of grade. lots of extra credit on tests. 1 midterm. one paper. really quirky and awkward but a sweet guy. extra credit if you listen to his podcast.

He's a teacher that definitely likes what he does, but his lectures are boring and kinda useless. The book helps the most. attendence is not mandatory, but if you dont miss any you get to exempt the final. EC available. test are a huge portion of grade: midterm + final is 55% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very sweet guy, knows 3660 is boring so tells dad jokes. I thought they were funny, but most people zone out. We have 3 ChatGPT exercises - super chill, not much work. One midterm, you need to lock in for it if you've been zoning out, not bad though. Final is optional if you attend 75% of lectures. Also have home canvas quizzes before class- easy.

Easy biweekly open everything quizzes, 3 ChatGPT exercises that were a nuisance but not hard, and 1 closed everything midterm. Midterm was tough (you kinda just have to memorize everything), but final is optional based on personal attendance. Lectures were boring, but attendance is mandatory. Don't need textbook, and there's plenty of extra credit.

Professor Hoadley made this class very interesting and engaging, even though it was at 9:30. Grades came from chapter readings, a midterm, a final, and an essay analyzing an essay generated by ChatGPT (fall 2023).  He offered extra credit opportunities and attendance could lead to an optional final. I loved this class and would recommend it.

Pretty good professor, the work isn't really that difficult to actually do the work but your gonna be reading a lot to do the assignments. Lectures are pretty nice to listen to and he's a fun guy to talk too. Plus, if you go to most lectures, you get to exempt  the final( Fall 2023)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class overall, but it is important to show up to classes so you can exempt the final. Tests are basic and from the slides, be prepared for tons of jokes that do not land.
Hes a good professor if you keep up with the work and reading. Not to mention he exempts you for the final if you come to around 90% of his classes (stated Fall 2023)
The quizzes were easy, and many of the quiz questions were on the test. There wasn't much homework other than the quizzes. There was one project, but it was pretty easy.
He makes lectures interesting with really bad dad jokes. quizzes are easy, tests are just quizzes, plus some lecture notes and textbook notes. super easy and fun.

Nothing is really communicated until a couple days before assignments/exams are due so be ready for anything. Tests are easy, quizzes are easy, but everything else feels like a chore and a waste of time.

Grading is unclear, assignment directions are unclear, test questions can range from anything on the quizzes to whatever the hell he wants you to quiz you on regardless of past experience or familiarity. He had lectures whenever he felt like it, could only find out after waiting 10+ minutes in bluejeans if he didnt show up

Syllabus is a mess, you don't know when assignments are due until a week or at most 2 weeks before they are due so you can't plan ahead. Tests are secular and just repeat the questions on his quizzes. Assignments are 100% meaningless and extra credit opportunities are just you listening to self-promotional material by him. Take him online.

The homework he gives is largely pointless, just look up all the questions online. There's a midterm, and if you get at least a B you can exempt the final. There is a debate group project you must do that he grades very leniently. He's a very funny guy who's class is kind of boring. If he notices people don't come to class he'll take attendance.

Pretty average: nothing too stellar but nothing to complain about. Lectures are pretty boring, and tests come straight out of the book. Content starts very easy but gets more advanced as the semester progresses. Gives several weekly homeworks that he pulls the test questions directly from. Two tests and one project make up most of your grade.
Great professor

Very responsive and attentive to all matters related to the project. He has great and valuable international experience. This class should be a core class specially for those students that have never been outside the US.
Unclear grading which leaves a large amount of your grade arbitrary.
Smart prof has lots to teach if you can keep up
The course is kinda hard so I'm sure it doesn't work for everyone but he's a very nice prof, nice to everyone in the class. I don't know what he did in the past but it can't be that bad.

Expected better communication and overall teaching skills from past reviews but overall this professor and introductory class have only taught me to not trust that beginners are welcome. Everything is rushed and not explained as thoroughly as presumed, I am hoping to learn coding on my own as this was just a waste of time and money.

I took the online CS 504 class. Lectures were posted every week and there was a mandatory participation quiz. If you took the quiz (you could get them all wrong) you got full credit. HW assignments are lengthy but only had about 5 due every 3 weeks. Overall if you watched the lectures and asked questions you will do fine.

This guy straight up skips your private posts on Piazza when you ask for help. He reads every single posts yet does not respond to any, I don't know if he understands TAs are not the only one who can respond and they have classes too. Avoid this guy if you want to actually learn and get help outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures don't have any flow and are very confusing. He doesn't have any course presentation and teaches by typing on the screen. It is very difficult to follow what he is talking about.

He's alright. Seems like a nice guy outside of class, but his lectures are mediocre at best and confusing at worst. Mostly used outside resources to learn the material. On the plus side, he was very generous with the extra credit and the class was pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazingly organized and clear. Ive tried to learn ML so many times before but this course made it understandable and applicable. The projects are very long but not impossible if you start early. He is also very considerate when it comes to extending deadlines for your situation or to account for heavy course loads overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, low-key loved this class. Hrolenok was a cool guy. It was his first time teaching so there were some hic-ups, but honestly he curved the class really well and gave lots of extra credit on exams so I thought it was great!

Awful lectures. Even poorer assignments. Office hours are constantly filled with 30+ students trying to understand what the assignment is asking us to do. Lectures consist of him speaking for 75 minutes straight off of busy looking slides full of incomprehensible math equations and graphs. Natural talent for being a poor teacher.

Real nice guy, can be kind of boring but the material is great. He has a really good way of explaining complex/abstract topics in an easy-to-understand manner. Made me much more interested in the class. Definitely would take again
She was very understanding and wants everyone to do well. The textbook matters a lot but if you read it you should do well in the class.

Prof. Liao is a caring professor who understands your situation and allows you to postpone assignments/tests if needed. However, her tests are difficult, because they are based on the textbook and the wording is quite hard to understand sometimes. If you are taking Psych of Aging like me, beware of the quizzes/tests.

Dr.Liao's lectures were poorly organized and her slides were generally vague. The questions on quizzes and tests were almost always pulled VERBATIM from the textbook, so if you don't read the textbook, this class might be a bit difficult. She does offer extra credit and a lot of easy assignments to boost your grade. Also, LOTS OF ESSAYS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was very knowledgeable about the topics, but I feel the class was very reliant on the textbook. Some of the questions could only be found in the textbooks. There is a not a clear outline of what would be on quizzes, so it was a hit or miss, but there was information about what to study for the tests.

Dr. Liao is very knowledgable, accommodating, and caring. The course is extremely textbook and reading heavy; some exam questions can be found in one line of the textbook. The exams are decently difficult for being a PSYC class. Many students do not get above a C on the exams. Great lectures and interesting, but definitely not an "easy A" class.

She is a tough grader on assignments, does't respond to emails, and tests on things not covered in class but are found in the textbook. She's also not an engaging lecturer and I had to teach myself because her slides are really vague. The only redeeming quality is that she offers a few extra credit opportunities. Sucks cause I liked the material.

reviews.comment: This course has the opportunity of being really interesting and fun, but just isn't. The professor is not really engaging and is really quiet/ hard to understand. The tests cover things not discussed in class and mainly covers random details from the textbook. This is a classic teach it yourself kind of class. It should be easier but just isn't.

reviews.comment: He just read off slides and did not explain well. But a lot content with details showed in exams. Didn't give very useful resources to prepare for exams and the content from lectures did not fully cover content in final.
weartsydfuiohl

reviews.comment: Reads off slides and does not teach well. Does not give any resources to prepare for exams and lots of assignments.
Don't take this class if he is teaching.
Learned nothing from him. Don't take the class if you expect to come out of the course with any knowledge.

There was not a single practice problem or helpful example done the entire class, or posted online so the average grade of the final was a 56. He is a terribly boring lecturer and does not stick to the topics of his class. Terrible class, would not recommend

Professor Hsu is a cool guy, he was very passionate about his research and it sounded very interesting when he talked about it. That being said, he didn't really know much about how to teach this class (tbf, it was his first time teaching it). You are graded on 2 tests and 4 hws, and he doesn't release practice tests. Class wasn't too hard though.

reviews.comment: Great teacher, nothing else to be said.
Love this dude honestly. His course isn't too bad as long as you pay attention and do your work.
these people leaving the reviews are crazy, this guy was a great genuine dude, who loves what he does.
One of my favorite professors at GT
horrible professor, lectures are 10 questions, 10 points each. Horrible questions too. He is nice as a person, but hard to get a good grade tbh

All the nice reviews are spam and written on the same day by children, go and read them. The class would be 100x easier if he did the bare minimum and released answer keys and work for practice problems. The class is difficult and the slides are horrendous and not helpful at all. He's definitely a chill guy but he's just so so so bad at teaching.

Cool guy but genuinely worst teacher ever. Won't give answer keys to practice problems or show work and his slides are so bad you literally don't know what you're doing. I have never called a teacher bad before until him. He does curve the class but thats bc if he didn't everyone would fail because he's so bad at teaching.

He is really smart and a solid guy but is genuinely so bad at teaching. He just yaps about math and starts examples before finishing others and is inconsistent with what he calls terms so you end up being so lost. While I do like him he is by far the worst teacher and worst class ive had in my life. The midterm and final are 10 multiple choice qs
He is not a good teacher and is not good at communicating with students.
Do not take if you want to learn something.

Amazing Teacher
Great guy. Good personality
Favorite professor I've had.
Thank you. I dont know why so much hate. Genuine Christian man.
Amazing Professor. Nothing else really needed to say..
Great Teacher.
One of the best professors I have ever had in my college career. Great Guy.
He was an amazing professor and was really kind. Great teacher
I loved this class and it was amazing. Great teacher, I hear his son is good at soccer too.

No point in going to lectures. 65% of your grade is two tests with little to no provided practice. Lecture notes are super vague and barely help if you weren't there for context. Class is curved and easy to pass, but I wouldn't recommend it if you truly want to learn corporate finance. He's a chill guy though

One midterm and one final which make up 65% of the grade. I personally dislike the heavy emphasis on exam grade considering this is an introductory finance course for non-majors. Lecture wise I feel Prof. Hsu is fine but some lectures do go a little tangential off topics and I feel like some topics we spent too much time on and some not enough.

He seems like a decent person but he isn't a good professor. Projects were not pretty easy but they did involve quite a bit of self study. He used slack and told us that he would always answer in a timely manner, yet he went MIA two weeks before the final. The final slides were useless but if you need to take the class, you'll probably pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly good. Don't know what all the bad reviews are about. Like pretty chill tbh I like the guy he enjoys teaching.

Showing up to the lecture is worth the same as not going at all. He likes to talk about things that are barely related to the class. He is invested in the content, but he forgets that this class is for non-business majors. His practice questions for exams are useless because he barely includes questions about the concepts he actually tested us on.

reviews.comment: I learned nothing. The were only 4 homework assignments and 2 exams (a midterm and a final). The midterm was 10 multiple choice questions, online, no partial credit. The final was also only 10 questions. His lectures are scattered, seemingly talking about things that have nothing to do with the homework material. Inaccessible outside of class.

reviews.comment: The professor rambles all class about unrelated math interpretations, very boring lectures. Tests are very hard and have very few questions so it is easy to mess up. Very few examples in class to help learn. Homework is also not helpful to prepare for exams.

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend the professor as hes poor at consultation and doesn't answer questions for practice midterms and finals or in general. Overall, don't take him.

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher. This course was a handful, but I'm happy I learnt a lot. Teaches from his slides, no textbook needed. Gave us 4 projects involving digital design of various components like cache, and other stuff in Verilog.

Well, I disagree some of the rating above. I think Prof. Lee's 6100 is one of the greatest courses offered at Georgia Tech, and you will be lucky if he will be teaching it again. In particular, I enjoyed working on his projects and learning many industries' perspective from his lecture.

I regret taking ECE6100 with him. It was more software-oriented than hardware-oriented! C'mon, why is it called Computer Architecture BTW? Those projects were too hard-core, and those macros are way too draconian-stupid and hard to grasp (BTW who programs C/C++ with macros? That's too outdated.) And beware, he has a pet BULLDAWG! (not GT-friendly!)
Excellent professor with difficult exams.  Be prepared, go to class and take notes from his examples, that is where his questions come from.
charismatic, well prepared and organized lectures, watch out his exams.
A cool guy with encyclopedic knowledge in microprocessor designs.  The projects were brutal, but really learned a lot.

Dr. Huang is super sweet. It is a flipped classroom style, but you don't actually need to watch the video lectures. Every class has a problem set that are kind of annoying but easy enough. The labs are fun, but the reports are so time consuming (10-12 hours each including data analysis) and the grading is really picky.

I think Dr.Huang was one of the best professors I've had. There are no exams, and she helps with worksheets in class, but labs are graded pretty tediously. She makes learning about environmental engineering very interesting, brings in other professors for talks, and takes you on a field trip at the end of the sem. Interesting class, amazing prof.

I enjoyed this class. It's a flipped class, watch the recorded lectures and then work on worksheets with our lab partners during the class time. Dr. Huang would answer any questions and check our answers - guaranteeing a good grade if you do it in time. The labs were easy and not long. 6 modules - 6 lab reports. No tests. Field trip to F Wayne Hill

Very nice professor and is accommodating to students. Lab reports are extremely reasonable and homeworks are easy. No exams, quizzes, or final. Labs are fun and informative. Prof is very willing to help with any questions on the homework

Her slides are great, give lots of homework + examples. Grading criteria are not very clear. Sometimes she changed her problems answers which is very confusing. Exams are long and require A LOT of calculating.

If you can, take another professor. It would make sense if there was a rubric or an outline to follow. This professor does not have one. He has a mysterious grading system, and feedback is so vague. He won't even answer emails, and is extremely rude during office hours. If you are a POC student, avoid.

Dr. Hussey explores interesting topics (e.g. Cyberpunk), but his lectures are all over the place and very hard to follow. His assignments are totally unclear, and he changes them several times. He also expects everyone to read way too many pages before each class. He would be a better prof. if he were more organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hussey has extemely unclear grading criteria, expects students to read hundreds of pages a week, and is really tough with grading. If you have an option, take another professor. On the other hand,  readings were interesting and he does care about the stuff he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hussey is a good professor, he includes video games in his teaching! He grades participation assignments (like the portfolio and the blog) based on effort but grades harder on essays and the group project. He is funny and learns everyone's name pretty quickly. He also allowed an essay revision at the end of the semester to raise your grade.

Hussey is a very fair professor. There's no mystery as to what is required of you (very organized class website and he updates it regularly). He'll only grade you tough if it's clear that you didn't put effort in (we all know English as a whole sucks but everyone has to take it so just do the work so you can get your A).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Doesn't give clear instructions on essays and projects and assigns lots of reading, but drives interesting discussion in class. Pretty funny guy and agrees to look over stuff if you don't like your grade. An easy A if you don't half-ass it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I am not totally stupid. I know that in life hard work doesn't pay off, but I thought that in this English class at an Engineering school we could all pretend that fictional hope was real if only for one last fleeting moment. That didn't seem like the case. The class was reasonably enjoyable, but the grading was not fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This is Georgia Tech, so don't expect an easy class - even for English. The least you can hope for is a class that's interesting enough, and Hussey delivers. Tough grader on essays, but you will improve your writing from it. He's enthusiastic and considerate of our workload. Sometimes flexible. Genuinely cares about his students and how they learn.

He does not give clear guidelines for all the essays, so essentially you're going to have to make up a prompt and answer it. He reads aloud to us in class a lot. Does not drive compelling discussion in class. Our set of literature is not interesting either, and we rarely played video games. Please consider another professor
Teacher assigns way more work than you'd care to do at an engineering school. Arbitrary grader. Don't be fooled by the topic of "video games," it's not fun in any way.
Overall great professor and the class was easy

Only downside is the early morning class time. Jeff likes to do live demos instead of reading off a Powerpoint. Assignments were easy and taught useful and interesting topics. Always a fun time guessing which soda he was gonna drink during class.

Super amazing guy. Professor Hurley is very caring and went out of his way to make sure students received good grades on labs and had enough time to do them. The labs themselves were tedious and took time. They were pretty cool but the setting up of them could make you lose hair by the minute. Overall, loved the course and the professor!

I learned a lot from the class, but it took so many hours. Some weeks I spent days straight just working on one lab. That being said tho, the labs were amazing and hella fun (after you banged your head against the wall for 20 hours to get the library set up and functioning). Slightly dated libraries, but fun experience. Just be prepared to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you can, take his class. Your ability to program anything before and after this class will be night and day.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I actually took him a year ago before I graduated. Everything he teaches has been relevant for my field. He definitely carries the ECE department.

Dr. Hurley is clear and straightforward when it comes to writing assignments and grading. He often gives out extra credit opportunities, which is especially helpful for students who may be struggling with the class. He also will extend deadlines if students seem to be having difficulties with assignments. Very fair and reasonable professor.

ECE 4122 exposes you to a lot of different interesting and advanced topics. The class is all project-based and you get tons of hands-on experience programming C++. Lectures-wise, they were pretty good but seemed a bit too early for most of the students. He and the TAs were very fair in grading and very helpful when you get stuck with some code.
One of the best classes I have taken and it is largely because of how Dr. Hurley handled the class. Learned a lot and at a good pace without any stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice professor and little workload

Hurley was great for an online class. He was super chill and was very clear about what the tests would cover so they are very easy. Go over the study guides he gives out and past exams they are almost 100% the same as the real one. The homeworks can be tricky because sometimes he finds them online without knowing a solution to them.

One of the best professors at Georgia Tech! He is extremely understanding and caring towards the wellbeing/progress of his students. He will literally look at your code and try to work it out with you no matter how long it takes while being extremely patient and nice.
Gives 10 hw problems per week that take more than 5 hours to do but only grades 3 random problems. It seems like he just wants to give us work because he can.

Class was impossible after restructuring. Exam every other week, 6 total, and the hw would take 8-10 hrs. I would spend 1.5 hrs a day just to do the hw comprehensively because they graded that hard, too. No partial credit for proofs except for the 1 on exam 5. A TA who wrote a bijection proof hw problem didn't even know how to do it, it was graded.
"Former highschool teacher" - don't be intimidated by any theatrics. Ron, tone it down.

my gripe with ronnie was that he made the class unreasonably challenging in the beginning. due to my trajectory in the start of the semester, I wrote this class off for the rest of the semester. 

in reality, the class gets easier and id suggest not giving up on an A. i wish he had been a bit more forgiving at the start. 

amazing lectures imo

So many exams its impossible to breathe or keep pace in the class. Homework is nothing like the exams and is graded extremely critically. Tests aren't terribly difficult but are so much work in so little time and graded harshly with little partial credit. Professor doesn't care if students are failing and offers little additional help.

Solid lectures, tons of online resources available to prep for exams. Homeworks are long and much harder than exams. Exams consist of only content discussed in lecture. if you go to lecture or read the lecture notes + do the practice exam then each exam is a breeze. I enjoyed the 6 exam format, gives you more room for mistakes.

Ronnie is the easier professor compared to Ladha, but if you actually want to learn any discrete math at all for ur future career, DEFINITELY take Ladha. Ronnie's (and I'm assuming Britto's too) content is on the simplest level and I legit fall asleep in the lectures every time. He is not an interesting lecturer.

Ronnie Howard used to be a fantastic professor but how has adopted the"Georgia tech mindset" instead of making learning an intuitive process, he decided to make everything unnecessarily difficult in the name of students getting B's. I don't know why teachers want their students to fail like this, it's unproductive

For disability accommodations, he especially took on a "Fairness mindset" which made it incredibly uncomfortable to ask for ODS approved accommodations. Overall, he seemed like he was trying too hard to be a "Georgia Tech Professor" than to actually be a good teacher. Maybe he'll grow into one later, but for now if you can avoid him: avoid him.

Not sure why he decided to make it 6 exams instead of 4 exams this semster, you have almost no time to breathe in this class. I dont see the point of going through the content so quick (including stuff thats not even tested) and then testing your knowledge of thta content a couple of weeks later when we are 2 units ahead. Very dissapointed.

Ronnie is still an amazing professor. His lectures were really engaging and provided a great introduction to the topic. Homeworks were long and brutal but really helped you digest the content. The tests were difficult but were consistent with what was taught in class. Easy final project that boosts your grade if done correctly.

Got an A on every single exam lmao the 6 exam policy is really not bad. Pretty forgiving if you bomb one of them- and no cumulative exam. HW is quite long but Ronnie is a good prof. I would show up to lecture even though not mandatory. Tons of people didnt show up to lecture (>1/2 of section) and are complaining about not scoring well
do not take w him. unless youre alr super proficient in python then this is a good refresher. if youre like the majority of students, youll need to learn it on your own.
Ronnie's the goat for this class with awesome lectures and plenty of practice material for exams. Everyone who says otherwise is just trying to cope with the fact that they're brainless baboons.

This class was just awful. Six exams with really time-consuming homework. Ronnie said he'll be continuing this six exam policy into next semester where classes are 75 minutes, so be ready for lecture and an exam if you plan on taking him. Avoid if possible

Ronnie is 100% the best professor for 2050. Due to the syllabus changing from previous semesters, this semester was a roller coaster of emotions, but if you put the effort in and study, you will do good in the class. That being said, it is definitely harder than it needs to be.

2050 is a tough course, but Ronnie is prob the best of the bunch. He's a caring guy, and his lectures are pretty amazing. That said, this course is much tougher than you'd assume - 6 exams worth 84% of your grade is brutal, and it feels like there's no break from exams. Weekly HWs take hours. If you're willing to put in the work, you'll be alright.

this class was a lot harder than it should've been. the exams were always harder than the practice and there was a lot of self studying involved. the homeworks are really hard and there are a lot of them. pls take it w a different prof if possible! ronnie was funny but funny doesn't get u As
If u want an easy A, choose Ronnie and you won't be upset as long as you don't upset urself by not studying.

Ronnie's lectures are efficient and full of happiness. Really easy to get an A if you do spent time learning the course, exams are close to teaching materials.I think the 6 exams schedule make you focus on one chapter a time and it's super easy to ACE it! Ronnie seems to be tough but is offering so many extra credit cards.

Felt like he didn't really care if we learned. Exams didn't correlate to past exams and were much harder than what we went over in class. Hws took so long in the beginning of the semester. Class and hws got less intense as sem went on which was nice. TA's were kind, but this class was overall much harder than it shldve been. LOTS of self studying

CS 2050 is an insanely hard class and is gonna be difficult with any prof but TAKE IT WITH HIM. His lectures were amazing and he was always trying to find ways to help his students. Tests were relatively straightforward with partial credit but there are 6 exams and are work 84% of your grade.

Exams weigh 84% of your course grade, which seems a bit much compared to other computer science courses and mathematics courses at Georgia Tech. Open-ended questions on exams are all or nothing - - you won't get any partial credit.

they changed the syllabus from previous semesters which made the first half of the class difficult. They listened to feedback and made it much more forgiving for the second half tho. Ronnie is still the best lecturer for discrete. Homeworks are very long tho and are basically weekly. Basically an exam every two weeks too which made things hectic

This class was very manageable, especially if you did well in 1301 or have a solid foundation in Python. Ronnie isn't the most engaging lecturer, and it can get boring at times, but in gneneral lectures were solid. Exams were tougher this semester and weighed more but the final project was pretty easy. You learn some useful things so pay attention!

I nearly dropped this class after exam 3 - The beginning and end of this class are doable, but the middle section of this class, with subpar study materials (which they did improve on), incredibly long homeworks, and difficult exams back to back drained me. Very much a timesink, but may be better next semester if feedback is taken into account.

Contrary to the other reviews, I don't think this class was bad. Prof Howard is a good lecturer and most of the exams seem fair enough as long you study. Homeworks are long and graded :(. 6 exams a semester which is a lot but at least studying for them isnt bad because there is less content for each and there is usually decent study material.

CS 2316 with Ronnie will NOT be an easy class to take, but he is a very knowledgeable professor and you will come out of this class much smarter/well-versed in Python, SQL, and other computing concepts than when you started out. I put a lot of work into this class and my grade reflects that, but if you half-try, you will not succeed at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: way too much work this semester for just a 3 credit class

The fact that he went from a 4.6 to a 3.9 in a single semester should be enough proof of just how terrible of a professor he is. Incredibly dry an inconsiderate towards students who teaches as though this is the only class students are taking. I don't know how he had such high rankings before, but be wary, he is not the good professor he used to be
Terrible terrible

Before Fall 25, this class used to have 4 exams, which changed to now being 6 per term. Study guides and practice exams dont prepare you enough for the real thing, and sometimes there isnt an answer key for you to check. The homework takes an insane amount of time to complete and is graded super harshly. theres no curving to the class whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a really hard class and he told us he was going to make it harder. There is so much work for this class and if you don't dedicate 100% of your attention to this class, it hard to succeed. He's very strict about AI and will send people to OSI very easily. I just think there is way too much work for this class for it to be 3 credits.

Much better than Prof. Ladha for Fall 2025. The tests are genuinely easy as long as you prepare using the practice material given. There are no tricky questions on exams and are super straightforward as long as you looked at the lecture notes at least once.

Definitely easier than any of the high school math courses I've taken like Calc AB/BC.

Ronnie is a nice and genuine guy but the structure of the class is just unreasonable with tests every other week and extremely long HW. Someone here said it is pathetic for a top CS program to go easy... I agree, and have no problem with hard classes, but I do have a problem with ones that take a disproportionate amount of time for no reason.
He goes very fast in class. The course is based off a few tests and one final project. He increased the weightage of the tests just for this semester. Do not take him.

Easily the worst course I've taken at this school so far, not in terms of difficulty, that's whatever, but in terms of structure. The sheer amount of exams that have been given in this class has caused me great stress, there is almost no real break you end up getting from them. Thus, I'm quite burnt out now.

Great professor, terrible class design. 6 Midterms, lots of homework, hard grading, its a stressful course. Howard does a great job explaining in lecture, and is enthusiastic about the content and helping his students succeed. He also makes it beneficial for those who actually show up to lecture by dropping hints and tips for exams.
anyone complaining should reconsider this major or even attending GT. The class is not that difficult and dr Howard has been clear. FR, asking a top cs program to go easy is insane and pathetic.

do not take w him. removed crib sheets because they're for "lazy people" even though they were always provided in the past. goes very fast in class, doesn't really explain the code, just writes it down for us to copy. hw's take FOREVER and are tough. class content doesn't prep you for exams or hws. exams are not like prev tests & are much harder
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Crazy how one class can ruin your semester. This class is extremely unmanageable for a 3 credit class. With tough homework and exams every other week, you can easily spend 15+ hours a week to get by. When he sees people struggling, he offers no support and puts blame on the students. TA's vary in answers, which makes office hours useless. Not good.

Not half as bad as everyone says. Show up to lecture, study... Most of peoples' grievances are the TAs' faults, not the lecturer's fault. His exams are known to be easier than the other profs. He literally made our last exam easier bc of everyone complaining. His exams are very fair game and much easier than the homework.
bum class dont take if u want an A
Worst class of oat. Take if u hate yourself

There is no clear grading criteria. It depends who is grading your paper, and if they are having a good day or not. Homework assignments take forever to do and the TAs can barely even help. Lectures and homework are on 2 different levels, and going to office hours doesn't even help because every TA says something different.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 6 exams, one every other week. They're generally fair, but NO partial credit given, study guide answer keys not given, and you have less than a week to study for them, making it hard to really understand the material and succeed. Homework doesn't help, is very long, and the averages are awful. Is he trying to make the entire class fail?

The only positive thing about this course is that Dr. Howard is a good lecturer. Unfortunately, the restructuring of this course has made it incredibly challenging for anyone to succeed. Do not let the first two exams fool you. The homework quickly becomes irrelevant and does not prepare you for the stressful and unforgiving exams.
Poorly structured class. No one i know enjoys this class at all
dont wanna waste any more time than ive already done w/ this bs class and teacher so just read all the other reviews for his cs2050 fall 25 class

Ronnie as a professor for 2050 is eh. His lectures are really boring, only saved by the fact that it's just 50 minutes compared to an hour and 45. Other lecturers are just better at teaching imo (Like Ladha, tho Ladha is tougher). His homework is pretty long and tedious, and they started hiding answers. His tests I would say are decently fair.

Ronnie teaches well, but sometimes goes too fast. There are 6 exams, each is 50 minutes. The problem really lies in the class structure; six exams with heavy math content requires more time to practice, which is hard to do with exams being every other week(not to mention having other classes to study for).VERY HARSH grading, no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my first time submitting a rating, as I await for my exam in 30 minutes. I am terrified, I have studied everything, yet nothing helps. The prof does not care if we fail, the exams are hard, nothing like the study guide. He needs to consider curving...

To be very honest, Ronnie is great at lecturing and explaining things and keeps you engaged (sometimes goes too fast). However the course is horribly designed:
1) He changed to 6 exam format, thus one every other week. However he kept the prior pace of content so you start a new unit the week of or before the exam and are always "behind".
(pt 1)

This class is exhausting, very long hw every week. 6 exams is not for the weak, plus harsh grading where you dont get partial points and its 84% of your grade. now they arent releasing the answers for practice test so we dont even know if we are right. Despite Ronnie being a great lecturer and teaches very well, the class structure is horrible

6 exams. Most of the class got below a 50 on last exam so for this exam he states it will be by far the hardest exam and decided to make a practice exam and refuses to give the answer key to check if we are even right. Good professor in the past, but his GPA and ratings are going down for a reason... Like who flexes that 25% of his summer got an F.

Always heard he was a good professor.
Took his class

- 8 question homework is taking over 5 hours (11 pages)
- Exams have no partial credit whatsoever and graded very very strictly. Missing any part of a body of a proof even with 15/20 part of the question correct leads to a 0/20 on the question.

I like Ronnie, and I also do find the content interesting. HOWEVER, he has changed the structure A LOT, and with that it has made the class 10x harder and really unmanageable especially if you're taking a lot of other classes/hard classes. There are 6 exams that seem a lot harder than the past years, and the grading seems a lot harder too.

This class is one of the most unreasonable classes I have taken in Tech. There's HW every week that takes an average of 7-8 hours (it's like a part-time job), which some of the questions the TAs couldn't even solve! Practice materials don't even prepare you for the test. Prof jokes about the exam avg not being as low as he HOPED.

The structure of this class is simply absurd, with 6 exams accounting for 84% of your grade, making it hard to catch your breath and catch up in the class. Has the mentality of "if students are struggling that their fault" and almost revels in the fact that students are struggling (literally bragged about how 1/4 of his students failed last sem

Overwhelming course format with a multitude of fast paced lectures followed by exams every other week, with limited time to truly digest information learnt. Homeworks given every week, which take an average of 6 hours. Professor offers no lenience in grading/curves even when noticing a large percentage of student's struggling. Brags about failing..
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this professor. he's basically trying to fail you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ronnie is a good lecturer, but the new structure is awful. Exams every other week + homework that is graded extremely objectively/harshly that takes a lot of time. Ronnie isn't the nicest guy, and was happy to see 1/4 of his class fail over summer. Treats it as if you are only taking his class which is unfortunate because I find it very interesting
Terrible professor. Doesn't explain everything and gives the stupidest homeworks of all time. They take so long for no reason and this guy doesn't care and doesn't even do them himself.

Amazing professor, but the way the course is structure now is some bs. Take this class somewhere else meaning a different school. Exam every other week, and strict homework and test grading. It makes no sense to make the course harder after having 1/4 of the class failing the previous semester.

Ronnie is a great teacher, however this course has gotten unreasonably hard within the last semester or so. There are 6 exams (exams every other week) and the homework and exams are significantly difficult. 1/4th of the class failed last semester and he was proud of that. im not sure if this is a prof problem or a class problem.

Truly the GOAT. Was my first programming class ever, and he explained concepts so clearly. Gave lots of opportunities for extra credit. He is hilarious and a super down to earth guy. Only negative thing I can say about him is that he tends to laugh before answering questions if he thinks its a dumb question..comes off as slightly passive aggressive

Ronnie is a great lecturer. I took this class over the summer and I can't lie, I didn't take this class as seriously as I should, but I still passed. For someone who's never coded before, Ronnie is very good at breaking down concepts, just make sure you go to the lecture, please. Missing a lecture for this class will genuinely not help you.
Great lectures, lots of homework and outside assignments but its nothing too difficult if you attend class.
Took his CS1301 over Ignite. Amazing class, put in effort, get an A. Lowest test grade I got was an 88. Would 100% recommend anytake take his class for Ignite.

Howard is nice, good at answering questions and has fun with the themed exams and the homework. However, the lectures themselves get pretty dry and you can honestly get by doing just the zybooks and homework.

Took the class in a late summer session, only 6 weeks long, with little prior coding experience. He made the lectures really interesting and to-the-point, and I was never confused. The class was extremely difficult because of the speed, but with his good lectures and extra credit, I was able to get an A+. He posts previous exams before new exams.
cool guy. make sure you stay on top of homework and projects. Course content sounds harder then it actually is, just keep an open mind and follow along with the code.

i enjoyed his lectures. i had literally zero prior knowledge of anything programming related and he made it way easier than i thought it would be and actually enjoyed it. lectures are long but he has a dry sense of humor that made it better (sometimes). tests were decent. labs and homework took a while but not bad.

Ronnie is my king. Someone once told me you must take him before you graduate and I agree. Super funny chill dude. Will miss him. If you have no programming experience 1301 (j programming in general) will be a bit of a learning curve but with his help and the TA's help everything was light. Lectures are very long though get some snacks lol

Nice and funny guy but class was pretty hard. Got rid of crib sheets for tests which sucked. Tests were fair, TAs are quite helpful. Homeworks were brutal though, very strict on cheating or sharing homeworks (lot of people sent to OSI), don't procrastinate on the project. Heard tests are going to be weighted more in the future (from 45% to 60%).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was fine as a person. Worse as a lecturer, he went pretty fast. But it's the homeworks that SUCKED. Lots of tears went into this course tryna pass the autograder. He seems to be a good upper level CS prof, he should stick to his forte, this was his first time teaching CS2316. Beware of keeping your code unique, he sent half our class to OSI.

:( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean :( mean

Homework can sometimes be heavy but Howard is a great teacher who understands the materials. Lectures can sometimes be a little dry because he moves slow, but he clearly cares for the students and class and tries to explain every concept as simply as possible. Exams are not that bad also, and there are a lot of study materials for it.

Ronnie is a fun and interesting lecturer. Regarding 2316 this semester, they did not let us have a crib sheet, even though it was allowed in all previous semesters. Heard this class was going to become more test-heavy in future semesters (60 %+ weightage). But as a professor, Ronnie is great and I would recommend :)

Overall amazing prof. I did not like the unset due dates for homeworks and they could be tricky to keep up with, especially when some were more difficult than others. The TAs were incredible. Exams were very fair and doing practice and the review sessions helped loads. The final project was also really well explained and organized properly.

He's a wonderful prof! Few lectures felt a bit fast at times, but overall great. Exams and homework could be difficult sometimes, but going to office hours always helped, and if you stay on top of the class, everything is very manageable (grading scheme likely to change a bit in the future tho). Final project was also very doable. Amazing TA team!

Howard makes his lectures super straightforward and his expectations for students' abilities with regards to HWs/exams are very clear. If you go to class, do the homework, and do some studying for exams, I think you'll find the class enjoyable.

Ronnie was hilarious and caring - sadly rare qualities among his colleagues in the COC. Class was well organized and accessible. FANTASTIC team of TAs who were eager to help and know their stuff very well. Grading is reasonable and tests are generally fair. Final Project is well explained and very manageable.
Professor Howard was very good at explaining concepts and and was always open to questions. The class can seem like a lot but is manageable. The TA team was very helpful as well.

This professor followed Melina Mcdaniel's syllabus for his class, and sometimes rushed through content. Luckily the content of the class wasn't very difficult so it wasn't a big deal. This was the first semester where crib sheets were not allowed so the exams were a tad difficult, and the final project is great for your resume.

Great, funny guy. Mostly easy class, j takes a while to get used to. Hws can be hard, but hw recitations are so useful def go to those. I recommend going to lecture but it's not mandatory + he posts video lectures a week before tests (I only watched vid lectures for the 4th exam and I think it went well). No cumulative final, just a 4th midterm!

Ronnie is great. He is funny during lectures, but covers all the content needed for exams. He has completed notes on OneNote available for students, so going to lecture is not necessarily required. I would highly suggest taking him for any class that he is teaching. I would absolutely choose to take 2050 with Ronnie again given the chance.

He is unbearable for junior design. In demos does not give teams the benefit of the doubt or seek to work with students but is difficult to deal with and does not listen to understand, only to hear his own voice. Upon seeing a group of 6 guys he said "this is why we need more girls in cs"... come on. Neither a kind person nor a fair professor.
Ronnie is a great teacher and makes the class so fun. He posts video lectures before every exam which are very helpful for studying or refreshing topics you're rusty with.

The whole first semester of Junior Design is a little silly, with only a bit of real work getting done, but Ronnie minimizes wasted time. He doesn't ramble in lectures and doesn't assign a tremendous amount of busywork. If I had to teach this class while satisfying the GT administration, I can't say I'd have done much differently.

Ronnie has been teaching this class for years, and it shows. Lectures are well-practiced and easy to understand. Homeworks are pretty easy, especially if you have any experience with proof writing, and they're excellent preparation for the exams. Although the class is large, Ronnie is kind and cares about students.

such an amazing professor. truly cares about students, his lectures are easy to understand and prepare you for the homeworks. imo not a hard class at all, and he is definitely the best professor. Also, if you ever struggle on the hws, GO TO OFFICE HOURS. seriously - they walk you through the questions if you just ask for help. favorite professor.

I took this class in Spring 2024. Ronnie is an amazing lecturer. He knows what he is doing and is absolutely hilarious when giving lecture. Your experience in this class will come down to your group. You can count on Ronnie to be a great lecturer and not to be the cause of any problems you face in this course. Course was well organized and easy!

I took this course in Fall 2022. Ronnie is an amazing lecturer. He knows what he is doing and is absolutely hilarious when giving lecture. The course content is hard, but I don't think I would take the course with any other lecturer. I highly recommend taking him if you can. Beware of homework and difficult tests - but that will happen in any 2050.

Made the exams straightforward and the homeworks weren't too bad compared to other sections. Can definitely self study from his slides and he posts videos before the exams. Review material is very good.

Easy class and chill guy. However he didn't really seem to care about this class and all of the assignments had unclear instructions which allowed the TAs to take off points for things we weren't even expected to do. At least you only need a 70 in the class to pass since it's pass/fail.

Your professor for 1100 doesn't matter, you're pretty much guaranteed to pass if you just show up, but if you can get him, Howard is the man. Super laid back guy, really chill on grading/late work, and I even watched his lectures for CS2050 instead of my own prof's because he's so good, felt like I had to give him a 5 somewhere.
Took Ronnie for a few classes, you won't regret taking his class if you can get into one!! hilarious and caring :))

Ronnie is a great prof to take Project Implementation with. He is very helpful, a nice grader, and cares about his students. Just for the class make sure to have a solid group with decent communication, otherwise it will suck.
One of the best teachers I've had

I rarely went to class because I wouldn't be able to follow the random problems he did. I succeeded through this class with TAs and homeworks (which are long but really helpful when studying for tests). Overall, good class but wish more prep was given for tests. I switched out of Brito for Ronnie but I don't think that was necessary.
Difficult homeworks and somewhat difficult tests. Fine lecturer.

Project Design is similar no matter with which Prof you take it, but Ronnie is a great choice. He is funny, gives clear instructions, and tries to help as much as you let him. If you put in the work and communicate with your team and client, you will succeed in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The HWs are tough, but manageable and fair. His lectures are good, especially the online videos, but he does tend to make mistakes while teaching in person. The ONLY reason he gets a 2.0 from me instead of a 4.0 or higher is Exam 3. The exam was unfair and did not reflect the practice exam, past exams, or topic list. One bad test grade can sink you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just avg. Not good not bad. Lectures only cover basic stuff and don't prepare you for HW. Lots of mistakes in videos and doesn't bother fixing them. HW's are very hard but prepare you for tests. However if you mess up on one test your grade is screwed. I had high 90's up until exam 3 and then got a 78 which dropped my grade to a B. TA's are great

I loved Ronnie's class a lot. He is the goat and the amount of resources to help you are immense. The HW is not as tough as everyone says they are, although it could occasionally be challenging. However, if you can understand the notes and the homework, you will do great. As most of it is online, I only had to really attend class twice in August.

Incredibly understanding. Lectures show both his passion and sense of humor. Class itself is fairly easy since he gives a ton of examples. Midterms are VERY fair. Overall goat professor and enjoyable class.
man is THE GOAT

Good class. This semester was hybrid- online lectures and meeting once a week to review and do practice problems. Homeworks are a pain and difficult but are fair and prepare you well for the exams. Overall, good professor and not a very difficult class.

Lectures were basic but fine. HWs are very long and can be very hard. His responses on Ed are absurd. If you ask a question, he'll give you a yes or no, wont expand at all. Had to visit OH frequently. Last HW was autograded so no partial cred. Easier tests but mult. choice questions are worth too many points. Said his TAs know more than him.

Quite test and effort heavy. Ronnie does a good job of teaching most of the time. The assignments are harder than the tests and do a great job in preparing you for the exams. TAs are extremely helpful; always go to OH for HW help. Majority of your learning will be self-teaching through the homeworks. Do practice problems and you'll be fine.

Unprofessional lecture videos that frequently had mistakes. Does not seem to know or care how to cut and edit videos. Lectures have background noise and are beyond low effort. Also tends to write very snarky low effort responses to questions online. Frequently makes mistakes in class as well as on video. Admits to not knowing the material himself.

Effort it took to learn this course was way too much. To survive this course without spending 20 hours on a single homework, you need to have a large group of friends to rely on. I did this course without friends and my grades, self esteem, and mental health have been largely negatively affected by it. Recitation was helpful when you ask questions.
if you love your grade dont take him. If you love getting a blue test version and LOVE having impossible questions your gonna love him. one bad test RUINS your grade. Puts your grade in SHAMBLES.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He makes the concepts easy to understand and fun to do. The homeworks were great for practicing for tests since they tend to be long and even harder than test questions.

Prof Howard is humorous and responsible! He could explain new knowledge pretty well with lots of vivid examples. Always upload notes after class and is willing to answer questions about homework! TAs are not that helpful so be prepared to ask Ronnie himself! He is the GOAT of this class.

Ronnie is awesome. 70% of the class was tests (4 exams no final), which can seem daunting, but I found each of the exams to be very fair. If you do the HW (which are harder than the exams imo) and go to recitation and do the practice test without looking at the answers you will get an A or B. Attend lectures and your life will be easier.

He's funny and knowledgeable, so it is definitely worth attending his lectures. Even though the homework was tough, Ronnie is a great teacher so you'll learn everything you need for it in lecture. Best professor I've had so far.

Ronnie is the best prof for CS 2050. I found the homeworks to be difficult at times, but the tests are pretty fair. While attendance is not required, I highly suggest going to his lectures. His lectures are always full. I got a B because I missed a lot of lectures and because I was stressed about other classes.
