There is simply nothing wrong with this man. He does everything perfectly. Lectures are spectacular, homeworks are difficult but very fair (as well as exams), and he's very accessible outside of class. By far the best professor I've had yet at my time at Tech. Also, never forget Zybooks...

Take Ronnie and if you don't have Ronnie attend Ronnie for discrete!! He is a very funny guy and is able to take the most complicated topic and simplify it. Only class i've taken which was full till the very last day. If you show up and do the HWs (which are based entirely on the lecture), you are guaranteed an A!

Overall great class! Very time consuming homework so definitely get into study group. Tests are fair and are typically easier than homework's but be prepared to practice a lot of problems if you've never seen any of the course topics before. Lectures are good and very applicable to homework and tests. Very clear grading. Very difficult homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Howard will tell you exactly what the class will be like on the first day and will not stray far from that. To summarize: super organized, great lectures, and hard homework. If you can do the homework, the tests will be light. The TAs are also amazing. Plus, he'll teach you about some heavy metal and his shed he built.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing prof, very engaging and helpful TAs. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: By far, the best choice for 2050. Interesting lectures, clear and solid preparation for exams. Can't go wrong.

Ronnie explains the course material in an easily comprehensible way. If you ask him a hard question, the TAs will probably know more than him. However, he does a good job with what he has to teach and is quite funny in class. If you attend class and do the homeworks (which are much harder than the class questions), it should be an easy A.

Ronnie is a very dedicated and funny professor who truly cares about his students. The exams are a majority of the grade but are generally easier than the homework assignments that are assigned. I highly recommend taking his course - it was an absolute blast!
Literally one of the best professors at GT. He's funny, his lectures are clear and concise, and he cares a lot about his students and this course

Fantastic professor with excellent TAs, everybody genuinely cared about the class and gave great feedback/help. Homework was time-consuming (not super difficult) but the tests were almost always easier than the homework so if you were super comfortable with the homework you'd ace the tests.

Ronnie is genuinely such a great professor! There are weekly homeworks with 2.5 points of extra credit if you turn it in on time and the TAs and Ronnie are really helpful during office hours. The lectures are great! The tests were completely fair and he teaches very well and in an understandable manner. Don't fall behind and you'll be good!

Ronnie is one of the best professors I've had at Tech. His lectures are enjoyable and he really makes the class manageable. The homeworks can be a bit tricky, but there's resources to help you with them. Tests are generally easier than the homework, so as long as you understand the homework you should be fine.

Ronnie is a really great guy and teaches really well. The class was difficult at first but became easier as the semester went on. If you pay attention during class and do the homework, the exams should be pretty easy.

The absolute GOAT of CS 2050. Ronnie has been teaching this class for a while; he knows how to teach each concept amazingly well. Lectures are straightforward and clear, and tests are always fair. Homeworks and in-class problems are much harder than the test. He gives great feedback on Ed or in office hours, and cares immensely about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, easy to follow, and cares a lot about questions and confusion. Don't miss his lectures tho.
The goat. Homeworks are typically much harder than what appears on the tests, so as long as youre good with the homeworks, you should be good for exams, etc
Really funny and engaging professor! Has been amazing so far, homeworks can be very time consuming but they are much harder than the exams. Exams are easier than both lectures and HW.

Ronnie is the most down to earth professor I have had at Tech, very straightforward.Homeworks and exams are not easy, but he wants you to succeed more than any professor I have had at Tech these past two years.  I improved my exam grade by over thirty points between two exams w/ class resources, overall great learning experience- highly recommend!
Ronnie is one of the best lecturers I've had at Tech. His enthusiasm and jokes make the class truly enjoyable. The tests are fair, and preparation material is really helpful.
I had a lot of fun learning discrete from Ronnie. The homework is super helpful and if you go to office hours they will help you understand!

There is a lot of material but his lectures are very straightforward and easy to follow. Homework can be hard, start early and if you struggle, go to OH they saved me. Exams are fair but definitely take note of the things he says in class (if he says it's important, IT'S ON THE EXAM, AND STUDY IT HARD). Amazing TAs and amazing prof.

I really enjoyed his class. His lecture are very helpful and straight forward including the recitations. His homework could take a little time but you get a whole week for each homework. The exams were quite straightforward if you reviewed the lecture notes and hw. Final was the easiest exam! He's very fun and upbeat would defiantly take again.

Really cool and chill dude. Class structure is very straightforward. Weekly homework and 4 exams. There is generally a lot of material in the class though, which makes lectures a little fast. However, he is very approachable and provides lots of examples to make it easier. HW takes a bit of time so start earlier in the week if possible.

Ronnie is a great lecturer with very fair exams. If you study his lecture slides and understand the homework problems, you will do great on the exams because the exam problems are generally easier than what is discussed in class/on homework. Exams do make up a large portion of your grade though, so make sure to prepare for them and you'll do great.

If you want to do great in this class make sure to attend lectures to understand his notes. Professor Howard is one of the best  at GT. I enjoyed every single one of his lectures. The exams were not out of this world and if you studied you will do good. There are a lot of weekly HW but they prepare you very well for the exams. Take him ;)

Professor Howard is extremely kind and funny! He is a great lecturer, and attending class is extremely helpful. The HW's and recitation worksheets also prepare you for the exams. Some of the TA's may tell you the wrong concepts/steps, so make sure you find a knowledgable TA for HW help. Great class and prof!
Blueprint of a great teacher. Knowledgable, easy-going, teaches well, reasonable, and even good-looking what more can you ask for.

Great professor! His lectures are clear, and he takes you through a lot of examples. Follow everything he says in lecture and you will do well on the exams. However, he sometimes skip steps whenever he goes through an example, so be careful of that. I lost a points on a homework bc I missed out on a couple of words. Exams were also pretty fair.

Pretty good lecturer, just a boring class. MC on his tests is difficult/tricky sometimes but the FRQ's are straightforward. The homework is harder than the tests. Recitations are 100% worth going to, you just need to find a good TA. The help lab is not. I only went once and it was very disorganized and unhelpful.

Ronnie is a pretty good lecturer.  His notes in class clearly lay out what is tested.  There is a lot of repetition throughout the semester though as we do many proofs that seem to be the same, but train you on what the homework and exams are on.  The homework can be a lot sometimes, but they do prepare for the generally fair tests.

Ronnie isn't that passionate about math. If you ask him something outside the scope of the course, he probably won't know. That being said, very fair, very knowledgable, and nice. Homeworks are sometimes frustrating but not because they're difficult. Tests are reasonable, predictable, and fair.

Going to be honest, the only thing I really have to complain about in this class is that the homeworks are due Friday night. But they are very realistic. Beyond that, everything you need to know really is covered quite precisely in lecture. Ronnie speaks with a casualness that really helps build rapport with students. He's kinda just a funny dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Greatest strength is definitely his ability to deliver sound lectures and explain problems in a very simple and easy to follow manner. Homeworks were time consuming and at times beyond the scope of what was covered in lecture. Exams were fair however. Overall great professor who I strongly encourage you take if given the opportunity.

He is a very good dude and professor. Cares a lot about his students and tries his best to make lectures entertaining. Overall one of the best professors I've had at Tech. There is a fair amount of homework that's designed to be more difficult than the actual exams but it's doable.
The best professor I've had at Gatech till now.
Tests were 70%, so make sure you study for tests. Overall, he is a nice teacher :)

Ronnie is one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech. There are 4 exams and no final, and all of the tests were super fair. Practice exams and HWs prepare you well for the tests. Ronnie is also a really good lecturer, he broke down concepts in a super easy-to-understand way.
His lectures are a little boring but hes a good professor. Very fair tests and felt like he did a great job of explaining the material. Very fair. Would recommend

Professor Howard was great; his lectures and explanations were well done, and the homework assignments while challenging helped prepare people for the exams. Overall, he's a very nice guy, and I would recommend taking his classes.

The professor is amazing and his lectures are engaging and interesting. However, it isn't even necessary to go to class because of how easy the tests (and homeworks) are. All you need to do to get an A is study the lecture notes before the tests and you'll be fine.

Ronnie was a great lecturer. He made the concepts clear and doable, and he made sure to give homeworks that matched the exams. With that said, do the homeworks, and you are essentially guaranteed an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ronnie is a fantastic professor. He clearly tells you what and what not to do on the exams and how to do the problems. The problems in lecture and on the homework assignments are very similar to the exams. He's also a super genuine guy and I'm really glad my first math class was with him. Can't say enough about Ronnie, I highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pay attention in lectures, do the homework, do the recitation worksheets and you'll do great on the tests (which have extra credit!). Put in a little more effort to really understand the material and you'll find yourself getting very high As on tests. Ronnie's a fun professor who's pretty self-aware. Somehow this class made proofs fun.

Ronnie's such a great professor who understands the material and is able to teach it in an easy manner. He's understanding and very friendly. One thing may be that he class is a bit dull, but that can be more due to the course material and not the professor himself. Would definitely take again.
Ronnie is a great professor, you cannot go wrong. Took him for CS 2050 and makes some difficult proofs seem easy. Really enjoyed his lectures and this class.
Super easy going professor and well, fair content taught and given in tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and he made the class really fair. Going to recitation helped a lot with the homework and the exams weren't too bad. If you go to lectures and solve problems the way he wants you to, you'll be fine.

Great prof! He explains things well and goes over many examples during lecture, so pay attention in class. Going to lecture + recitation were two main reasons I passed. A lot of people found the homework difficult and tedious but tbh if you just watch the TAs do recitation problems its basically the same thing. He's chill + tests easy if you study.

Prof. Haiying cares very much about her students. She is VERY accommodating. 
Her course was one of my heaviest-- and it was only 2 credits! You WILL LEARN in her class whether you want to or not. 
The homework was tedious, but you had 5 attempts. And the pop quizzes are basically for participation. Exams are tricky only because of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice person, but bad lecturer. She has you try to do problems in class after minimal lecturing and doesn't explain how she does them. Homework is extremely difficult and time consuming, but if you are able to figure out and understand homework you will do well on a large portion of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a fantastic person, but not a good teacher. She explains poorly straight from textbook, and then has you immediately do practice problems instead of her doing practice problems. Attendance is random based on participation "pop quizzes." Homeworks are lengthy and difficult. Her tests are easy homework problems. She grades tests quite easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Avoid this Professor at all cost. Although she is caring, she is not the best professor for someone who does not know Statics already. She just restates information from the textbook and does not actually teach the concepts in class. However, I can say her exams are just problems from the textbook and she is more lenient during grading.

No attendance, but random quizzes in class. She can't teach and homework is on chegg. YOU WILL NOT LEARN IN CLASS. The light grading I've read on RMP is hit or miss. She would grade bad for me, but super well for my friends so beware. Doesn't explain anything, just follows slides, ridiculous for a class that requires a lot of written work shown.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: terrible lectures, super hard homework but graded tests SUPER nicely. homework are available on Chegg and thats what everyone did to finish them. But even just setting up problems on tests and attempting to solve would get you 80% of the points. If you're looking for an easy A and not learn anything, she's great.

As usual at Tech, a nice person but a bad professor. You WILL use chegg to solve the homework problems because what she 'covers' in class is never adequate. What examples she does 'cover' in class is LITERALLY already in the book. Test multiple choice is hit or miss, written portions are intro problems or homework. Avoid her, if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Generally, I don't care what professors I get, but I would recommend against her. She is a very nice person, yes.  However, she did not teach this course well. The homework was heavy and unforgiving, the exams didn't reflect well on what was expected of us, and we were expected to know, and tested on material that other sections were not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a very nice professor, but her entire teaching style was bad. She would use Mathematica instead of actually solving problems. Exam results had no feedback, didn't know how to solve her own problems during office hours, and gave lots of time cosuming homeworks that never really helped
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It might be a struggle if you aren't familiar with physics before taking this class. Her lectures were quite slow, and most of the time she was just reworking examples from the textbook rather than teaching the material itself. She was also very hard to reach outside of class and not that accommodating to students with ODS testing accommodations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All the people I met say statics is easy. Not with her. Her CIOS fall 23 is gonna be bad, and I hope she knows why.

Dr. Huang is caring and nice, but not the best professor for Statics. The class is slow, resulting in lectures that don't prepare you for the homework (WileyPlus). You'll have to self-learn if you want to do well in this class. Exams are not representative of what you're expected to have learned. She's generous with partial credit, but still.

Not an awful professor, but if you want to do well, you'll need to be proactive in learning and studying outside of her lectures and the assigned homework. Get started on the problem sets early; if you can do them correctly without assistance using hand calculations, you'll do fine on the tests.

For a core engineering requirement, she sure does not know what she's doing. Homework does not reflect example problems from lecture, midterms are a completely different subset of questions, does not give practice exams/problems or even communicates remotely clearly what a test comprises of. For your sake, don't take her for statics.

She skipped through practice problems without teaching any concepts. Didn't explain anything in class. Used Mathematica to solve problems instead of by hand making it confusing to follow. No structure in the course and test grading criteria was unclear. Grade is based on lots of time-consuming and difficult homework with 2 tests and a final.

Dr. Huang really isn't who you should take for one of your first important engineering classes. She doesn't clearly specify what it takes to succeed in the course and is not understanding nor accommodating. She doesn't teach how to solve, she teaches to use Mathematica, which is not helpful. I really really advise you to take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is based off 3 tests (including final), you only receive 3 attempts at each homework problem, and the she goes over very few difficult examples in class leaving you confused on the homework. The professor also uses Mathematica a lot and does not go through how to complete the problem. Save yourself the frustration and take someone else.

disregarded ODS requirements, was IMPOSSIBLE to reach outside of class (said we should not expect her to respond to emails because she is busy), could not be worse at lecturing if she tried. Uses mathematica to teach no one understood her code so in class problems were useless. can do well if you teach yourself but this woman is awful at her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is really nice, but doesn't go over a lot of material. She crammed the last 3 chapters (of 6) into the last 2 weeks and it was all there was on the final exam. Homeworks and exams come directly from WileyPlus. Most people used Chegg. If you do not have a good base on this topic don't expect to learn from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Huang is an extremely kind person but her class was equally as difficult. I personally spent 23 hours on the Bonus Homework assignment. Exams are made to make you feel like you failed so be prepared for that. She is opposed to practice exams. You WILL get more partial credit than you think which is a blessing but exams send a major hit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While a nice lady outside of the classroom, she is not fit for teaching this course. She only uses Mathematica to teach how to do problems and won't teach how to do problems by hand. Lectures focus on examples, not concepts. Uses Wiley for EVERYTHING. Grading criteria are unclear as far as partial credit goes. Takes almost a month to grade exams.

Great professor, teaches very well. Homeworks are tough, but they also account for a big portion of the grade, so be prepared to work on it. Tests are easy if you understand what's being covered in class and do the homoework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very approachable outside the class and if you can't make her office hours she is flexible to meet at other times. Will guide students when they ask for help and is patient. Don't wait to ask for help, the class starts out easy but the coursework (HW worth 20%) is A LOT. Keep asking your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Huang is such a kind and caring teacher. She did multiple things over the semester that showed her kindness. We didn't really learn that much material in class, but rather worked on practice problems. There were pop extra credit quizzes. The homework is very difficult, but tests much more reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Flipped-course, meaning she teaches nothing/you watch the pre-recorded lectures and read the lecture slides on your own to answer weekly problem sets, but she can check your answers if you ask. Partner work, but could mean you do everything. 5 full lab reports and 1 data analysis w/ presenting 1 lab report at the end. No exams. Easy A if you work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was so so caring and very willing to help you outside of class if you're having trouble. The hw takes a lot of time though and is usually a lot more difficult than test questions, but the lecture examples were helpful and she gives pop quizzes sometimes so definitely go to class!!

caring, personal, and understanding. the class is pretty straightforward in nature. try not to skip class as she gives out extra credit. pacing was weird as we spent 3/4 of the semester covering 1/3 of the material and then crammed the last bit in the last month and change. HW takes a lot of time but if you understand how to do it youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable professor. Nice and patient.

Make sure to attend all of her lectures because she checks attendance for a grade. HW is longer + harder than any questions you'll see on her tests. If you study example problems from lecture and do okay on the HW, her tests shouldn't be a problem. Make sure to read the intro slides because she likes having multiple choice q's based on theory
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her lectures are essentially just her solving problems without much explanation of the theory behind her problem solving or really any non-numerical physics. (The class is exclusively solving problems numerically.)
She's a fairly good grader, but you only have two Midterms and an Exam. The homework is difficult and takes a long time to complete, so start early. She's pretty straightforward in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor. Grades well, teaches the concepts thoroughly. Very open to questions and has a very helpful attitude when it comes to students who are confused with the subject. She likes using matlab/mathematica in class for calculations so if you like CS her section is probably one of the better ones for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The course is very difficult, but it isn't difficult to get a decent grade. I feel like I've learnt the most in Dr. Manh Khang's class, and still, there is so much more I didn't master. The lectures are recorded, but the attendance is taken. Prof. is very helpful-- I think he understands the confusing questions students ask very well.

Probably easiest A you can get for your stats requirement. He releases 95% of the midterms ahead of time, so it's almost a guaranteed A on the midterms if you spend a couple hours the night before memorizing what he gave. The homeworks were eh, they could be long and confusing but you can cheese them pretty easy.

Prof Khang's greatest sin is that he is 100% truly abysmal at teaching. He's very prone to going on useless tangents about math concepts that often muddle the actual course content. His homework assignments might as well be written in hieroglyphics since he never teaches the material you need to understand them. Course was a total waste of time.

3 tests, take-home final, 1 weekly homework. Horrible lectures. Powertrips over the smallest things and is very difficult to work with. Decent amount of extra credit built into syllabus. Be prepared to teach yourself everything.

Passionate but lacking teaching style. Lectures are inefficient; he frequently stops to wait for students to figure out proofs, saying "anyone?" on repeat, wasting time. Some may find him rude. Difficulty is moderate, but class is frustrating at times.

He has potential to be a great professor, but needs realistic expectations and time management.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Im convinced every positive review on here was done by him. He laughs at people when they get things wrong, even though he sits there and begs us to interact with him. His lectures are awful and uninformative. He pretends like he wants us to get excited about math but clearly is just teaching this course as a power trip.

If you really like math, you can't get a better professor than him. Amazing lecturer whop genuinely cares about the student. He has the class together prove every major result, which is great for student learning and pacing. Gives so much extra credit because he cares about the student learning and pushing themselves, not giving them bad grades.
difficult, attendance required

Truly extraordinary talents are often misjudged by the normal eye.

Took MATH 4320. Dr. Huynh's lecture is very enlightening. Instead of blindly follow slides he improvises around the topic and dives very deep into the math fundamentals, asking questions that'd elevate your understanding to a whole new level.

Tremendous guy. If you know you know.

Honestly horrible. Did not follow the suggested course textbook, and I really did not learn a thing looking back. The structure and pace quite literally created numerous gaps that he says to avoid. Smart guy, should not be teaching. Reviewing everything with Stat 110 now as I have classes where the ideas here are critical.

The lectures are awful. Huynh regularly laughs at students when they get questions wrong. However, it is still worth it to go to lecture because you can get a 3% bonus for attending all lectures and more bonus points for participation. If taking this class, find a good group of classmates to do the homework with and to prepare for the tests.

Math 3215

He is clearly very smart but his teaching is pretty poor.

His explanations are unclear.

He releases 4 of the 5 exam problems ahead so you can get through with almost no mathematical thinking.
He gives a lot of extra credit and makes the final exam take home.

Pretty much, if you show up you will get an A even if you don't learn much.
Not that accessible outside of class. Not a good lecturer either. Many people just went to other lectures because the course was standardized.

I took 3215 btw. His class is very difficult, but he gives loads of EC for participation, attendance, bonus tests for doing nothing, and CIOS. He also releases most of the test questions beforehand with an extra, usually impossible, mystery question at the end. This all makes up for the difficulty. Yes the class is super hard but you will be fine

Incredibly incredibly intelligent guy. Would not trust him to teach anything though. Horrible at communicating ideas, goes on tangents (the amount of time I've heard quantum mechanics is mind-numbing and we're not even 3 weeks in), disrupts people when they ask questions. MATH 3215 btw.

Learned from reviewing slides/textbook. Lectures were recorded. Released partial previews that revealed VERY similar questions to exam, with one mystery question. Allowed collaborations on HW. Can exempt final and can collaborate on take-home exam.

Very difficult professor for a very difficult class. Would NOT recommend. TAs basically carried me through this course. Professor is difficult to follow as he will often go on tangents based on questions he asks, but only accepting answers if they are worded exactly how he is thinking, no variation allowed. I stopped attending lectures very fast.
Khang clearly actually cares about teaching. That's pretty much all that kept me from giving him a 1.
Just cause youre knowledgeable doesnt mean you can teach it well.
Very smart man, terrible at communicating information. Started attending Barone's lectures after the 2nd exam and regretted not switching during the first week of classes. Do not recommend.

If you are passionate about math, he will be a great professor. Otherwise, maybe not as much. He is extremely qualified and makes a genuine effort to help all students. He rewards participation and attendance as extra credit. The content of the class is doable with enough effort. He releases exams as Take-Home to compensate for their difficulty.

I had this professor for MATH 2552 and he was not great. He was unable to answer students' questions and had illegible handwriting. His tests were very straightforward and followed the practice exams exactly. I would take him again but would not recommend wasting time going to his lectures.

Khang can sometimes be hard to understand and lectures are not important at all. His notes are sometimes difficult to read but are useful. My TA was the one who really taught me 90% of this course so I recommend attending studio. Quizzes and tests are exactly like the review problems he gives, so the class could overall be a lot worse.
W professor

Lectures are essentially useless. Difficult to understand what he is saying and writing. Doesn't explain concepts clearly. I learned 99% of the material from my TA. Tests and quizzes aren't all that hard because he gives review problems that are essentially the same at the test questions. Be prepared to learn everything in studio or on your own.
Quizzes matter the most so be ready to study a lot. Not much time in between them so do your best. The group project is great if you need to get your grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture isn't terrible but his quizzes are. Grading scheme: 7 quizzes, 70% & 20% final project which is advertised to have only a few A's. Each quiz will always have a question which you did not learn about unless you rigorously go through each example problem and learn it yourself. If you have the time to study, it's fine but if not expect a B.

3340 in general is a tough class. Dr Hu makes it bearable and I came out the other side of his class with a good idea of whats going on. Graded on 7 quizzes at 10% each, a constant slow burn that kept us sharp but took a lot of work. Lectures engaging, most helpful with prior reading. Do & understand the homework, read the textbook, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems mostly knowledgeable about what he's teaching, but does not use time effectively in lectures - practice problems have poor explanations if any, and he leaves most of the answering to the students (not helpful if we know nothing;). The vast majority of your grade is 8 tests and a project, both of which are graded harshly. Awful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are ok but 2-3 before quizzes is not enough. Class had 8 quizzes, completion hws, and final project. Quizzes always have twist that makes them very hard but graded generously so that average ends up as C+/B-. Project has no guidance, on bell curve around 85, and will hurt you. Only 13% got A in class. Not good but might be least bad fluids

There are 7 very hard quizzes taking up 60% of the grade, but there are a lot of partial credits. The course project is given early, but it's fairly vague in instructions. He doesn't curve grade, I ended with an 89.xx% and still got a B, which is fair, but keep that in mind if you're looking for an easy professor that spares you some points

Fluids is a difficult subject but it felt like he made the class harder than it needed to be. 60% of the class was 8 bimonthly quizzes which were harder than the practice given. 20% of the grade was a project, which was graded very arbitrarily. Very accessible outside of class but makes his expectations for classwork unclear, will not round grades.

Had a quiz every other week - average an A on these to maybe get an A overall. Quizzes are hard, you won't be prepared no matter what you do. Start early on the group project, put too much effort into it and maybe you'll get a B (on a bell curve). He's a mid lecturer, very tough grader, and won't help students out a lot. Don't take him if you can.

Fluids is hard, but he is definitely the best/easiest fluids professor. I highly recommend. Quiz about every other week, group project along, homeworks for participation (they are textbook problems with an answer key). The project can go on a resume but was not a fan of the bell curve. He has a ton of office hours and is very kind. Probably get B.

Dr. Hu is probably the best option for Fluids. His use of seven exams and optional final makes the class very manageable as long as you stay on top of your work. Exams were very fair and similar to homeworks. Dr. Hu is very respectful towards his students and is really enthusiastic about his applications of Fluids in his research.

The textbook is not mandatory, but that doesn't mean you won't need it. If your class does well because he is a decent lecturer, he will purposefully make your quizzes ridiculously hard. If you want partial credit back on your quiz make sure everything else is right otherwise he'll take off points for other mistakes. Group project is on bell curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Hu Special Topics minimester (a 1 credit 5-wk class) on biomechanics/animal motion. It was discussion based with 10 people on his book on the topic. He's a great person and this setting of class suits his personality really well. I would highly recommend taking it if ur interested in the topic, even though it may not count for your degree.

Dr. Hu is a nice guy. His classes are nice and he cracks jokes in between the class. But he will make you work for your grades. The course is graded based on 7 quizzes and an optional final. He drops the lowest quiz grade. There is also a class project. He will consider curving your grade up if you are in the border.

Not the best lecturer, but entertaining. 7 quizzes (80%) and a group proj. (20%). Accessible, only if you are willing to wait an hour in line to speak to him, usually to clear up his jumbled homework solutions. Project is vague and graded harshly on an unfair distribution. Final (hard!) can replace course grade, but no curve outside of that.

Took him for Fluids. He was a terrible lecturer who would attempt one warm-up problem per class which ended up consuming the entire lecture b/c all the students had to ask questions. Grading was 7 quizzes and a project, which had very little criteria but was graded 1/3 A's, 1/3 B's, and 1/3 C's. Really pathetic he isn't the worst fluids prof at GT.

This class is the hardest class I've ever had at Tech. He expects only about 20% of the students to receive an A. His lectures are a bit disorganized so you might have to spend a lot of time studying on your own. However, he might be one of the best choices for this course since other professors seem to be worse than him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hu is a well respected scientist and researcher. Unfortunately, he is not a good teacher at all. Lectures are heavily disorganized and he goes on random tangents that distract from the material. Weekly quizzes vary in difficulty with some being easier and others being unreasonably hard and are 80% of your grade. I do not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures were mostly going over problems from the optional homework. He explains the material well but can be disorganized about it. If you do the homework problems and understand how to do the homework problems, you'll be fine. He's really funny and friendly, someone you want to listen to. Fluids is hard but he makes it very manageable.

Best professor I have had at tech. Funny and personable. The 7 quizzes are not very difficult if you do the HW and extra problems. Final is optional and he lets you use it as a grade replacement. But compared to the quizzes it is pretty hard so avoid having to take it. Overall great class and professor. Definitely recommend.

Very disorganized lecture. He doesn't even know how to solve his own hw question if you have question about it and if you want an A, then read the textbook and do all the problem in the textbook (I mean like everyone of them). On the plus side, textbook is not difficult to understand but thats about it. Self teaching course if you must.

Hu is easily the worst professor I've taken at Tech. He changed his grading scheme for an important project halfway through the semester. Was told mine was an A quality, he actually gave me a C. He is a jackass, plain and simple.  I had to email him at least 5 times before he would respond once. During class it seemed like he had no idea what to do

Nice guy but awful organization. He would assign homework that he didn't have the solutions for and more often than not, he'd be unable to solve them when we had questions. If he did have solutions, you'd have to go to his office and copy them by hand (there's usually a line)? There's also a poorly defined final project in lieu of the final exam.
I love Dr. Hwang!! Her class is a lot of work outside of class, but she really cares about her students and it's not hard to do well. She's also the funniest prof I've had yet.

I had Hwang over the summer and her class was super easy grade booster. Attendance is mandatory but if you show up and do the work (which there isn't that much of), you'll definitely get an A. She's a lenient grader and a really fun person to talk to!

For my class specifically besides the intro video we had 2 group projects and an individual project that were all pretty fun. She's an easy grader. Super nice and laid back. We had to read 2 books and had quizzes on them but I read summaries and got 100s on the quizzes. Please take her if you have to take english. You won't regret it.
Great teacher who really cares for the class. The work was a bit much at times, but as long as you put in the effort, it is rather an easy class. She's a very casual and relatable teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Set-up different from a usual college English class. Two group projects (video/audio) plus one individual writing (all interesting). Get well with group members (peer review). Nice and easy grader with feedback if you show a bit of work. Literally the easiest English prof you can get at Tech (another:Rose). Beware of reading quiz so do the reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great teacher! The work is different from a normal English class but its definitely way easier for a STEM student. Shes very caring and understanding and a very lenient grader! Shes hilarious as well! Would definitely recommend.

She was an amazing professor. Attendance was mandatory, but as long as you show up and do your work with some interest, you will get an A in the class. She will make you interact with everyone in class and I made new friends in the class as well. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Joo facilitates a really great classroom environment with student discussion every day. Student presentations are held every week. Get ready to read papers each week to understand research. Course content is 10/10 super interesting. Highly recommend.

Take Dr. Joo. She is a positive-spirited and down to earth professor with a clear passion for teaching. I had her for crossing borders and she made me want to class while also giving flexibility for other, more strenuous courses. I love her and will be taking next semester.

Probably the best professor I've had at Tech so far. She really cares about her students and gives really good constructive feedback on how to improve. If you're thinking about taking her class, you should do it!

She is a great professor and genuinely cares about her students and their learning. Great lecturer though her classes are mostly practice instead of lectures. Definitely one of my best professors yet!

Dr. Joo is the best!! She is super caring, and gives a lot of great feedback. Also very flexible with deadlines. I have absolutely no criticisms of Dr. Joo. She's great. The class is not hard, as long as you genuinely care about the language.

Professor Kim was an amazing professor. She had organized lecture slides, plenty of practice problems during Studio, and she gave clear expectations concerning grading and quality of work. Solid MATH 2552 professor, would take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and teacher! She is very accesible outside of class and does a great job at mixing lectures and practice problems. Only downside is that exams and quizzes are slightly above average difficulty and make you think, but luckily she drops the lowest quiz and the homeworks and CIOS bonus help out.
Use her office hours if you don't understand something from lecture. She is very helpful one on one. Quizzes and tests often are similar to in class examples, so practice those when studying.

When it comes to making quizzes and tests Kim makes them much harder than anything she has shown in class or assigned for homework. She quizzes on things she never fully taught in lecture and expects us to do problems in the same amount of time as she can. Avoid taking if possible. Hard study abroad teacher.
Cool professor.

This class was the biggest disappointment I've had at Tech. This class has so much potential to be interesting, but the way it was taught by Prof. Kim left a lot to be desired. Instead of learning about processor design, you learn about obscure intricacies of FPGAs, and do homework that is graded at the end of the semester. Easy A, though.

Honestly one of the worst classes I have taken at GT. Completely disorganized, homeworks were completely unrelated to everything else, and in projects we were blindly following instructions and learned very little.

Professor Kim was very understanding of some of the circumstances that popped up for me because of online teaching, and the whole COVID year. She allowed leniency and in the end I got a much better grade than I feel most would have allowed me to get. The projects are sometimes unclear, but the course is established and she works well with her TAs.

The assignments weren't always clear on what it wanted students to do, but luckily the grading was very lenient. It can also be hard to understand her lectures sometimes because she is so quiet. I also appreciated not being forced to buy a 300$ fpga board for assignments (during online covid). The research project or final exam option was also nice
Gives extra credit opportunities so an A is definitely possible
Great lectures that incorporate topics into Atlanta case studies

Class with Prof. Hyde was a blast. HTS 3008 is a pretty introductory-level overview of a lot of topics and he did a great job of making this wide range of subjects accessible, interesting, and relevant. Participation is important, but low-key. He's a great dude who really cares about his students' opinions as well as their learning and success.
This course gets its strength more from discussion than from lecture, although he isn't a bad lecturer.

Dr. Hyde is an absolutely fantastic professor. He understood how stressful COVID was for us and tried his best to make the class as forgiving as he could. He's a good lecturer and incredibly knowledgeable, and his papers are usually interesting. He gives great feedback but also doesn't grade too harshly. If you get the chance to take him, do it.
Really nice and understanding. Class had only two essays and 5 document reading questions and one project. Also no tests. He grades pretty easily.

Professor Hyde is a great guy. His class was more about helping impact the community rather than focusing on tests or quizzes. In our class, we interviewed residents of a local community about topics like gentrification, affordable housing, etc. We only had a few assignments. Attendance matters for the participation grade, but he is a fair grader.

Dr. Shin was a very kind and helpful professor. He was very good about making sure everyone understood everything as he takes the time to answer students' questions. Workload was reasonable and manageable. I would definitely recommend Dr. Shin!

Awesome professor! At first I was doubting him, but he turned out to be a very nice and cool professor! His lectures are clear, concise, and straightforward. Do the optional homeworks and past exams, and you can get that easy A.  Go to his office hours when you can; he's very helpful!

Prof Shin turned out to be very nice and approachable and laid back. He is willing to take the time to talk to you and help you. He makes linear algebra concepts very clear. Tests were copies of practice exams and homework. I wouldn't say I was particularly challenged. Average test scores were usually A's.

Amazing professor, was very clear and really just wanted to make sure his students understood the material. I wouldn't recommend anyone above him. Do the work, and his tests are very fair and you can get an A just fine :)

Based on what I've heard from people with different Calc teachers, Shin is one of the best. He was very fair with grading and didn't put anything on tests that we weren't prepared for. As long as you keep up with the online homework, go to class, do his practice tests, and study all the material for tests you'll be fine. Highly recommend him.
GOAT !! Would take this class, pretty good grading scheme. A project was a large part of the class grade, wasn't too hard to do well on the project.

Dr. krout did a good job revamping the course. it wasn't a free class but wasn't super difficult. fair amount of work outside the class (no busy work). very accessible outside the classroom; I worked with him over the summer to accommodate switching sections, and he was very responsive and helpful. exams are fair, and slides are good.

Absolute KING - he did a great job revamping 3002 to make it accessible and manageable this Fall. While there were a few hiccups earlier in the semester, especially around the first exam, he takes feedback with grace and is a wonderful professor to work with. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Krout was a great teacher for a difficult class. 3002 was a heavy group project class with a semester long project but he graded everything really fairly. The exams are really difficult despite being open note (but thats lowkey just this class) but he grades fair and gives extra credit/points back if he thinks its deserved.

one of my favorite professors i've had at tech. he cares a lot about students and is very open to making adjustments to the course based on feedback from the class. very accessible and easy to reach. things are not graded harshly and it's easy to get an A if you just put in a little bit of effort. would def take him again.

His teaching style was MUCH better than Dr.Holder's (co lecturer). He moves through content very quickly, but he explains concepts clearly and in an interesting way. He's also friendly and is great about helping you out if you don't understand something.

He was a co-lecturer for this class with Dr. Holder. The only con I have would be that he goes through the slides super quickly so it was difficult for me and many others to write down notes. However, he was such a friendly and respectful professor who knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Krout did pretty great. His lectures were a little fast but if there was anything that wasn't clear he usually stays after for a bit to answer questions. Honestly, he's a very friendly professor if you just reach out to him.

He speaks quite fast in lecture but is about a million times better than Dr. Holder who is the co-lecturer in the class. He is also a great person to ask questions and advice about for the class (UNLIKE Dr. Holder).

He taught the class with Dr. Holder, his lecture style is her opposite. He flies through lectures which makes it hard to absorb material and take notes (slides aren't given out before class), but he knows his stuff and is decently interesting.

Her order of presenting information is pretty messed up. Be ready to spend 1/3 of the time listening to words that are not elaborated, 1/3 afterwards to actually start learning things, and the last 1/3 to link the two parts and try to make sense of them.

Professor Mary's CS1332 online course is amazing. Clear lecture videos with lots of examples and amazing accessibility through office hours. Exams were a bit difficult (particularly the coding), but hey, it's CS1332. Besides that, I would highly recommend.

Lectures aren't very helpful. Her videos are pretty good and the TAs are very helpful. Basically very TA led. Faulkner taught our class once and he was pretty good, take him instead. Exams aren't too bad and similar to past exams but grades were very test heavy.

The online class. Would recommend if you are comfortable with online pacing. The recorded content is pretty close to what is on the exam and isn't significantly out of date. Just make sure to keep up with the recorded content prior to the exams. Loved the sections on additional topics in theory that wasn't present in the online CS1331 class.

Class is taught completely virtual. Didn't meet the professor until the day of the final exam. Lecture videos are helpful, but reality checks seem out of date with exam difficulty/questions. Demos were a new thing added to the class, which I think was unnecessary due to the fact that we have no projects in this course and the class is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a lecturer, she doesn't get through all of the content, makes mistakes, and frequently misses class. However her videos are very good quality and there are tons of resources online, so putting in the effort to making sure you stay caught up with the curriculum is a must and will get you a good grade. Dont go to class and just watch the videos
Super easy class; pretty easy lectures. Wish she engaged a lot more with the class. Also, the lectures were really slow. Take Faulkner

Important class. Very good lecturer for the portion of the class she teaches. Attend class. Very good and accessible TA's, take advantage of them. You need to stay on top of homework and understanding to do well. Grading is harsh on tests, and the material on them seems more complicated and abstract than you would expect from a core understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. HB had amazing lecture videos and was a great person. CS 1332 was a bit more difficult than CS 1331 but there were plenty of resources to help one succeed on everything. Tons of extra credit administered throughout the year as well (about 7 bonus points towards exams + CIOS bonus).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the most caring professor I've ever had. She wants her students to not only succeed in this class but in your life and career. Her course is tough, but she explains topics well and although I never went to her Office Hours, she seems like the type of professor that would do whatever it took to help you out.
O K HI BYE O K

honestly this class was pretty difficult, only because there are very few things this class is graded by. not to mention you have to have a passing exam average to pass the class. i get it, there are probably reasons why but as someone who had a hard time understanding things, it did not make it any easier that i didn't have any saving graces.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the online section of this class and Dr. HB has amazing lecture videos that are incredibly helpful and well done! the exams are pretty difficult, but fair enough if you know the content. She's also really understanding, I had to take an emergency absence and she waived any late points I had on the HWs. I would definitely recommend!
She literally has no idea what she is talking about. This course is run by incompetent people and makes GT look like a laughing stock

HB is a decent lecturer; the course is just a bit tough for someone with little prior knowledge on the topics. I know people who claim to have bad experiences with her based on her character, but I have had no issues with her.

She made these ridiculously high-quality lecture videos that are clear, concise, and easy to follow along. Discovering them made studying for exams so much easier. Do not take this class for granted, please just do the homeworks on time and study for the exams and you'll get an A.

Dr. HB's CS1332 class is one of my all-time favorites at GT, due in large part to how diverse the amount of learning materials there are. You can watch the module videos if you're more visual, use the vistool if you're more hands-on, or read from the slides if you prefer text-answers. The tests can be tricky, but are quite fair. Best CS course @GT.

Very difficult to reach professor rarely responds to emails and is very last minute about updates like when the final is. Awful class with some of the worst test on knowledge I've seen just avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this course 3 times before I passed. There is an annoying test grade policy that makes it to where you can pass, but are still forced to retake the class. All things aside, HB is a great professor. She is caring for her students and is very involved. 1332 is simply a challenging course for those who are not ahead in their CS education.

I learned a lot in this class, and it was low stress. The grading is very fair, and she even lets you exempt the final if you do well on the three exams. Exam content is easier than HWs and is similar to the practice exams on canvas. Lecture attendance wasn't required. Definitely recommend.

Professor Hudachek-Buswell's 1332 class is challenging but rewarding. Her video lectures are clear, and tools like Unstuck study can help supplement your learning. Exams test your grasp of concepts, so stay on top of the material.

Good lecturer, clear explanations. Do not hesitate to ask questions anytime you have a doubt - she will answer your question thoroughly. I had the hybrid section, and her prerecorded videos are a solid resource. Well-organized course as well.

Took this class during the summer. At the beginning, she seemed like she would be a scary teacher, but by the end of the semester it was clear that she was cared a lot about her students and the material she taught. Exams were based exactly on the homeworks and there were plenty of extra credit opportunities.

I took 1332 over the summer, meaning that the time constraints changed the way the course was structured. Professor Hudacheck-Buswell was a great professor that constantly worked towards accounting for the needs of the students. Lectures were only once a week, so I had to make the most of her pre-recorded videos and TA team in order to do well.
Very good lecture videos. Exams were full of gotchas but overall class does a goos job at improving your coding skills and knowledge for later classes.

Great online videos that make attending class irrelevant. Content is very digestible and reflective of the exams. My main qualm with HB is her lack of respect for students that I felt she showed very regularly. Not only to students, but also her TAs. As of right now, there really aren't any bad options for 1332, but keep the module videos in mind.

does not explain concepts well and is passive aggressive. does not care about students. class is very hard and focuses a lot on memorization. exams are difficult and grading structure of the class is awful.

Very slow talker (had to watch all videos on 2x speed...)). Exams are overly difficult and there is a huge emphasis on memorizing time complexity and straight up CODE from the homework. This course has been nothing but a huge waste of time for me; I did not learn much useful stuff. Please revise course structure. Minimum 70 exam average to pass :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall the class was just hard.  You need to get a good grasp on the concepts in order to get a good grade.  They post helpful videos so rewatch them if you want a good grade.  Also do the hw since the coding on the tests are based on the hws

Took the async version over summer. The videos were well produced and being able to watch them over and over again was convenient. Coding assignments felt fair, grading was kind of harsh with all of the edge case testing but that's more my fault. Fair professor.
Test are very difficult and should be studied for.

Took the hybrid version and don't recommend it. Nearly all learning is from pre-recorded videos. The videos are well produced and have nice visuals though. Exams + final make 85% of your grade and homeworks can take a while. Felt like there's a lot of emphasis on memorizing rather than fully understanding and being able to synthesize from content.

I think HP is ok I just had her during the first attempt of hybrid in an 8am lecture and when she was facing some health problems. The lectures do NOT teach you material rather it focused more on showing examples from material you should've learned beforehand. Overall it was okay, but the hybrid section will probably get more organized with time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the hybrid version of this class and can't say that I recommend it. It makes it a lot harder to learn the material if you're trying to do it all from the module videos. If you take the hybrid option, please go to the in-person lectures anyways, it helps out a lot. Otherwise, the class is very straightforward and you know what is expected.

This professor was outstanding - easily one of the best professors at Tech!  Her class made me wish I was in CS - I'm CompE.  Moreover, she was very caring - my registration time once fell during one of the exams, so she let me take the exam with an earlier section so that I could register at the earliest.  Highly recommend!

Overall terrible course structure (3 exams + 1 final and they account for 85% of your grade, w/ 70% minimum exam average policy). Little to no time on the exams (50 mins to do MC, diagramming, and 2 coding questions).Too much emphasis placed on useless memorization; course designed by someone in Academia with zero work experience outside academia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found this subject very easy, but I could see how one might struggle in this class. She's not very good at teaching and really makes me wonder if she understands the material herself sometimes. It's hard to believe that at one of the greatest CS schools in the world, she's the one teaching the most important (i think) class. very mediocre
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures and very in depth, go to office hours if needed the TAs are amazing resources. Course is really difficult but arguably the most important class of all CS major. Start Leetcoding right after taking this class.
I really liked her haha

CS 1332 is organized really well by efforts of Prof HB. They provide all the necessary materials on Canvas so it's even ok if you don't attend lectures. Online videos provide more information than taught in lectures. Homework and exams are manageable thanks to all the materials and helpful TAs.

I took the online section, and the lectures left a lot to be desired compared to how involved and rigorous the in-person sections were. You can definitely do well in the course if you apply yourself a lot and really hammer home the concepts, but there is a lot of material to learn.

I took the in-person section, and the lectures were very helpful. HB takes time to go over the tough concepts, but leaves the easier memorization to do on your own. The TAs are good, and office hours are a great resource for the homework which is challenging but  prepares you for the tests. HB usually gives hints about what to study before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to class for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hands down the best class I've taken so far. The course is super well run, thanks to HB herself and the TA team. Her pacing may be slightly slow, but I think it's alright since she spends a lot of time making sure that students understand the concepts. Her module videos are very good as well. 10/10 class.
HB is a good professor. Her lectures are a bit boring but useful. The homework and assignments are easy in my opinion. There are plenty of resources online to help you succeed.

Unlike most professors, she handwrites her notes - which is SUPER helpful for diagramming, an integral part of each exam. By attending class and taking notes with her, you're actively learning the content. Practice exams are provided before each exam, and they do not stray format-wise from those practice exams. There are a ton of online resources

Took the asynchronous section so wasn't in direct contact with HB. Overall her videos and resources posted online are extraordinary and really prepare you for both the exams and homework. TAs are very helpful for the course and are easy to ask questions. Exams are applications of learned data structures. Maybe the most organized class at Tech.

Amazing lectures! The in depth explanation of data structures and algorithms and diagramming helps learners of different types to all learn the concepts well. The homework and tests were fair and TA's and Professor are accessible, caring, and very helpful in general! Great motivations, resources, lectures, and help! Probably the best class I've had

She was a good professor. She takes time, and writes down materials, gives examples, and goes over the materials. The TAs are the best! Everyone is very knowledgeable, understanding, and helpful. The tests are difficult if not practiced. ALWAYS attend all questions, there are partial credit. If you do all the non-coding question, you will get a B.

HB's in-person lectures were okay, and I did not like how she gave us an exam after break due to GT "changing" their scheduling. However, the resources and recorded lectures for this class were extraordinary! The TA's are also great, and recitation was a great review of the material.

I learned a lot from HB, she has great lecture videos that cover all the content so you don't need to go to lecture in-person if you don't want to. The homework was coding data structures and the tests were a good challenge. HB also cares about her students and she's funny sometimes

Lecture videos very dry but covers content well. Had to use restroom before final, and was not let back into room by TAs despite test not even starting. On another occasion, HB was very condescending and rude over a simple question. Teaching is very average quality, at BEST.

HB is a good professor - she cares about her students and her TA team is really awesome. Her lectures do become quite dry, but she has created an exceptional module system for 1332- you can learn pretty much everything through her module videos, which are concise and teach the concepts really well.

HB was an amazing professor to have, and while the content can be tough at times, there are plenty of resources available to students, and she always picks amazing TAs! Tests can be a little long for some people, especially with a 50 min time limit, but overall she's great!
Overall course very well structured. I appreciate how many different resources there are in addition to lecture, and I wish other courses would be more like hers
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is awesome. She is kind and caring but also strict when it comes to grading sometimes. But overall very fair. I wish we had more professors like HB!

Great professor. Notes during class were easy to follow, and she thoroughly goes through every example making sure we understand. TAs were amazing as well. The amount of resources they provide is crazy. She gives us the entire online class modules for us to use. They give you all the things you need to succeed, make good use of them to do well.

HB cares. She puts effort into her craft, and it shows. 1332 is a challenging class, but you'll never feel like you've been duped because you're given so many resources to succeed. I wish more professors focused on students' success/imparting knowledge like HB vs crafting tricky problems to show you... how clever they are, I guess?

Very nice professor teaching me CS 1332 in Summer 2022.
Full of easy-to-understand lecture records help me a lot in both time-saving and well-understanding.

Her modules are awesome, she is an amazing lecturer and offers an insane amount of resources. Her TA's are probably the most useful TA's I have ever had. BUT SHE -AS WELL AS HER TA's- CAN NOT WRITE. The test questions for the multiple-choice sections and her socrative polls are worded so poorly that only the writer knows what is being asked.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IN SUMMER. Other than that, the TAs were really nice and helpful. The tests were more like memorization test but there were a lot of partial credits. This class should not be hard during a full semester because you need time to absorb the new materials.

-Grading breakdown: 50% quizzes (5 worth 10% each), 25% final, 20% HW, 5% participation
-Course is leacture-heavy, so attendance is strongly recommended
-Quizzes and HW were fairly easy
-HW often done in class with help
-Prof was personable and caring
-Learning curve is steep if you've never taken CS before, but it gets a lot easier

All tests are cumulative, so each test just becomes straight memorization of too many topics and is ineffective at best. She crams so many topics into each test and the timing is awful. Grading can be lenient sometimes but good luck getting a regrade. Homeworks are excessive and u have to memorize them for the test. Exams are not well made at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her async class over the summer and had too many problems. If u r off campus during the summer, good luck. Async class but has tests in person, i had to email the dean for remote TA office hours and that still took weeks to implement and TA's didnt show up sometimes, and shes a stubborn pain in the ***. Cant admit when she/TA's are wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took an online async version of this course and I really enjoyed the format. The modules online consisted of well-made videos that taught the content really well. I did not interact much with the professor but I did enjoy the class. Grading can feel a bit harsh at the start but there are lots of resources + TAs are very helpful with explanations.

The online lectures that were available were high quality and did a great job of explaining the course material thoroughly. If you wish to succeed in this class, take advantage of the material that is offered along with the TAs. Done well, you have most of the tools necessary to succeed in many other aspects of tech.

Lectures were sometimes hard to learn from since she handwrites notes. But this is made up for by the excellent quality of the online lecture module videos which thoroughly cover all course material in a succinct way. This is a very well organized class with amazing TAs and plenty of resources and a must have for anyone entering the tech field.

Dr. HB is overall a great choice for CS 1332. The in-person option that she offers is a little tougher than the online CS 1332 section since you have to memorize everything for the in-person exams, but her lectures walk through all the content you need to know. Homeworks are clear and reflect the test content accurately. Overall, great teacher!

Above average professor, lectures are really really optional (I went, but know so many who didn't and still did well). So much extra material to learn the stuff. TAs are amazing. So basically do the homeworks, study for the exams, and you should be good.

Decent lecturer, great TAs, and she's very nice but is decently strict. The class is clearly exam focused as the 3 exams and final are 84% of your course grade, and they are moderately difficult. Exams are fair, but the timing isn't too great, forcing you to learn the material thoroughly. However, there's a ridiculous amount of helpful resources.

Really great professor! Kind, knowledgeable, and available. Her lectures get a bit boring and she was absent for quite a few of them, but a great (and really big) TA staff filled in the gaps. This course is pretty heavily dominated by homework, so don't overload yourself on courses and don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. HB really cares about her students and their success.  The TAs in this course are amazing and help her make this course manageable.  There is a lot of work in this course, but it is very relevant to the job sphere, so it is good to learn the material.  There are bunches of resources to help you succeed supplied by her and the TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. HB says it on the first day: DO THE HOMEWORKS TO DO WELL! She provides a bunch of resources on canvas to supplement her lectures (or replace them). If you genuinely put in the effort to do the assignments, you'll be fine. Very fair in the sense that she'll only ask coding questions on material that has been graded. No dropped HWs or exams, tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the module videos went over a lot of concepts very thoroughly and there were a lot of good resources provided, some aspects of this class were just unfair and too much. The professor tries to cram every single topic from the unit into the tests and gives us no time to even finish them, and then the amount of homework is just excessive.

Harder than other professors, but this is the one class as a CS student you want that. She did seem strict at times, have heard stories of kids getting in trouble for code similarity on hws so be careful. Online lecture modules are the clearest and best presented lectures I've ever seen. While strict, she did seem to care about her students

The class is definitely difficult, and HB can be a bit strict making it a bit harder than it should be. The exams are decently difficult but there are more than enough resources for you to study and feel prepared. While the class is tough HB's lectures are some of the best in the business, and will help you fully understand and learn the material.
The recorded lectures were one of the best I have seen for any course. The class is graded mostly on exams and no exams or homework are dropped so be prepared to work hard for this class

Dr. HB is a fantastic teacher but she can be tough. She teaches the material very effectively and goes slow enough for everyone to gain a solid understanding. Her tests are difficult but fair and will require you to invest a significant amount of time studying. As a teacher, HB is awesome but just be prepared to work hard.
TA's are a godsend. HB i feel like is kind of strict for no reason and I feel like the tests aren't really written fairly.

This class was miserable. I'm not sure if it's always this way at Tech, but the college of computing makes this class an awful experience, which stinks because the material is really cool and HB lectures well. The exams in this class are the worst part. Too much material, not enough time. Doable, but painful. The memorization is ridiculous. Avoid.

The vast amount of resources that HB provides for this class is the main reason I would advise you to take her section. There are lecture videos, lecture slides, TA slides, recitation slides, visualization tools, extension resources and so much more. Having all these resources at your disposal for such an essential CS course is a great help.
She's a decent professor, but quite inflexible and not super understanding at times. I still think she's a solid choice, but the way she structures her class is kind of annoying.

Really enjoyed the class! Professor makes sure that people understand and is willing to spend time going through examples and answering questions. The pace is relatively fast, but as long as you review the content and study well, the tests aren't too bad. The videos are amazing! Honestly, one of the best teachers I have ever had.

Provides great videos with many example problems/walkthroughs. Lots of study material and very clear on expectations and what to know. Exams are reasonable and direct, with no silly trivia or gotcha type questions. If you study with the material given, you will do well.
Take CS1332 asynch! The videos are clear, concise, and well done. HW's can be hard and time consuming.

Honestly, not bad. Lecture was pretty boring tbh, but the course offers so much study material that it doesn't really matter. Hudachek is very clear on her expectations for what will be on and how to do assignments/tests, and the TAs for this class are probably the best out of any CS course.

This class was a reasonable amount of work. I was so nervous about the CS requirement and I had never taken CS before, but HB did not make it hard to earn an A. I kind of enjoyed her class, and the TAs were great too. She's also very kind and understanding and was flexible with deadlines when I really needed it.

Really good professor. The class content is really organized and Professor gives you all the tools to do great. Homeworks are really challenging and you learn a lot from them. The grade is mostly made up of Midterm and Final so you should do great. The best CS class I have taken so far in my life.

She spends more time talking about her dog than actually teaching. For an intro cs class, it's really hard to follow with 0 previous knowledge. The TAs def carry her class but if they aren't teaching the lecture, you can teach yourself just as much as she would but in less than half the time. Also there's no way to put recorded lectures on 2x speed

This is one of the most comprehensive, well-constructed courses I've ever taken at Georgia Tech. Class has a ton of TA's with a lot of support outside of class. Homeworks are really good challenges that are super helpful in preparing for the exams. Class grade is dominated by midterms/final, so you do need to perform. High effort  you will succeed

lectures aren't mandatory but they are amazing for understanding the material, which helps a lot since the course is test heavy. The professor provides a ton of material that is super helpful for homework and test review! If you attend lecture and work through all the material provided you will do fantastic! best class i've taken at ga tech

This course was designed very well. There were always multiple ways to learn the content whether it be through lectures, professionally produced videos, or well planned recitations by the TAs. I really enjoyed taking this course, and I always felt the the expectations and grading were fair and understanding.

Her lectures are pretty dry if she doesn't tell you about her day or what happened in her life but her homework, practice worksheets, and practice modules/quizzes are very close to what you get asked on the actual quizzes so if you just care about getting a good grade and moving on from CS, Dr. HB is pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The program you use is easy to grasp but the way she shows how to code in-class is too advanced for non-CS students to catch on and replicate on homework and quizzes consistently so I don't recommend taking her unless you are already pretty experienced with various coding interfaces.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 1 Final  25% 5 Quizzes  50% 8 Homeworks  20% 42 Mini-Completion based Quizzes  5% Despite it being an intro class and one of the easiest CS courses at GT, don't take it unless you are already familiar with CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. HB was ok. The lectures were a bit dry and I stopped going about a month in. However, the amount of material available for the class is crazy and if you put in the work, you're guaranteed an A.
