HB is very caring about her students and TAs provide valuable feedback and recitations (GO!). Lots of resources available in the class - the onus is on you to succeed. There is a wide breadth of knowledge, but the course doesn't try to put you down (i.e. exams are very fair and not nit-picky ahem 1331, etc.).

Very passionate about what she teaches and an excellent lecturer! The online videos are professionally developed and of extremely high quality. This course covers a lot of content and you will need to study a ton of material for exams, but HB gives you so many resources that you will undoubtedly be successful as long as you put in the work.

Class has a lot of resources you need to succeed - you don't really need to take notes during lecture (recitation and doing practice before the exams is adequate). Lectures are mediocre and exams are heavily weighted but not that hard if you study.

Dr. HB is by far one of the best professors I've had here at Tech. She truly cares about the success of her students and is always available/very helpful in office hours. She is also very understanding. This is a tough class with a lot of weight on exams, but if you do the homework and ask for help when you don't understand then you will do well!

Well, it's data structures and you have to work and study a decent amount to get an A. TAs are great. Understand each data structure with fine details since the exams (especially the MC) will test you on your ability to synthesize that knowledge. The coding portion is always the scary part of the test. Just gotta grind and memorize the code.

Dr. HB knows what she is doing! Her exams are easy if you study and do the 10 coding HWs. Her exam questions come directly from the lectures, recitations, and HWs. This class is very easy content-wise! And the Final Exam is even easier than the 3 regular Exams, which is a plus because the Final Exam weighs more than the regular Exams and HWs!

HB has very helpful instructional videos and organized materials to help students learn. That being said, the exams are very difficult to complete within the given time frame and they're weighted so heavily-which is strange because you'll spend most of the time in this class doing homework. I highly recommend a different 1332 professor if you can.

I really, really did not like HB. I felt that she was disrespectful to her students and not at all caring or flexible in regards to our well-being. Additionally, if you do badly on even one of the tests, it is extremely hard to make up for it because the class is so dependent on test grades and not on actual coding work.
HB is such a boring lecturer and the modules for this class are also super boring and unhelpful. Would not take again and I just want to get this class over with.

HB isn't a bad lecturer, but she can be dry and often is just reading off her slides. She wants students to do well and learn, though, and is willing to help if you ask for it. Exams are heavily based off the homework and slides, so spend time on those (recitation TAs are also super helpful).

Hate the grading structure of this class. I believe exams account for 84% of your grade. Project work should be rewarded a lot more. With respect to HB module videos, they are pretty boring and you really do learn a lot more from the TAs and other students. Would take it again only because Piazza was very active and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: HB was such a kind, caring professor. Her class was not easy (in my opinion). The class was VERY test heavy, which can be a problem if you mess up even one of them. However, her module videos were clear/concise, TAs were always ready to help, and she answered many questions in class. I enjoyed 1332 a lot content-wise, and HB made it even better.

People are very hard on HB. She cares so much and teaches the course in such a clear way. I think she is a great professor and I think people get intimidated by her but she is a nice person, she just is short with you. Get over it, she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't know how anyone could complain about the online section? The modules are clear and concise and any confusion could be solved through office hours and recitations. A bit harder to do that in the corona semesters but I would say the class is fair

Slow lecturer, and the lectures are pretty boring. You will learn mostly from the TA's, they are a godsend. Exams make up like 80%+ of the grade, but the class is still HW heavy (although they count for like 10% of the grade). If you do the work, I feel like this class is fine.

I rarely ever interacted with Dr. HB as I took the online version of 1332, but the lecture videos were very effective in learning the material. Plus 1332 has a great group of TAs and lots of support materials, so overall a pretty easy class. As others have mentioned, take the online version.

The modules used for the online vers of this class were organized, concise, and useful. Dr. HB was incredibly sweet every time I had the chance to email/talk to her, and the TA's were the best. I don't know why theres so many negative reviews for her, but I would opt for the online version if I could. One of the best classes I've taken at GT so far

Took the SOUP version in the summer. It was pretty organised and curated (I've heard it's better than the in-person version). The exams were pretty easy (median for the 2nd one was 90) but I always got slammed in the homeworks. The exams account for most (84%) of the grade so just be careful with that.

Class material-wise, Dr. HB was decent in organizing the material. I took the online version. You'll do fine in assignments watching the lectures. The class is hard not necessarily because of material, but because of the exams. If exams didn't turn open book because of COVID-19, I would've had to memorize homework code to get As (was getting B-'s).

I'm surprised HB has such a low rating. I think she is my favorite professor I've taken at GT so far, but others don't feel the same. I found her lectures to be very helpful, despite her hand writing her code, it gives time to follow what shes saying. She's the most caring professor I've ever had and genuinely cares for her students.
HB is a great professor who knows her content really well, and really cares about her students too. Not to mention, the TAs are super helpful!

Professor HB was an okay lecturer, but most of the learning I did happened outside of class; homework, extension materials, and recitation really helped. She also posts the video lectures she makes for the online section of 1332, which are A LOT more concise and straightforward than the in-person lectures. Use them for sure.

Very passionate, kind and intelligent professor. Excellent TA team who genuinely cares about solving your doubts. The comments they give on the homework are super detailed and you sort of understand why you lose certain points. Exams are semi-tough, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: she really knows her stuff and on top of that she can reallllly teach very well. go to class and struggle through the homeworks and youll get an A/B atleast. Tests are very hard but she gives you everything needed to prepare adequately for them.

Not a CS major and not great at CS and absolutely loved 1332 (1332 NOT 1371) with Dr. HB. Thought the lectures were well laid out and definitely helped with homework and visualization. Lots of great resources, tests are a time crunch. Again, not great at CS, but the weekly HW took me days to finish. Loved Dr. HB, would take again; definitely cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not as bad as other reviews say she is. Dr. HB lectures well, although she does tend to take longer than necessary. Dr. HB's class was probably the best transition to online classes I had. The one main gripe I have is that coding assignments only count as 13% of the final grade, which imo is a bit too little.

Dr. HB has an amazing personality, and she is one of the best lecturers I've ever had at Tech. She puts effort in going over material in every lecture, and she always encourages students to work hard for her class. My problem with her is that she expect a little much of her students, but this is why Georgia Tech education is not a walk in a park.
She really is an amazing person, but a TERRIBLE teacher. The course is hard enough imo. STAY AWAY!
The teacher was really strict, but was contactable outside of class. The lectures were pretty average.

1332 is a tough course at Tech, and HB's lectures are absolutely mind numbing. However, she's the only one who has taught the course for the past couple of semesters so you may have to deal with it. Get started early on the HW's and study the notes and you should get an A or B, but she's not a good lecturer at all.

This is a review for her Junior Design Part 1 class. She was actually not that bad. She tells it how it is and for the work you'll do in Junior design, I respected that. She's not too tough of a grader but other profs might be a bit more lenient. Def not an easy A unlike other JD professors but not the end of the world if you take her.

The tests given were very fair, and the class itself is set up ridiculously well: you are provided with an insane amount of great resources. However, attending lectures is largely a waste as the material is covered more concisely in the online videos. She also started showing up late to each class around halfway through the semester. Take online.

She is a great teacher! She really explains the topics well and even gives you the code for your homeworks! Plus, the tests are extremely straight forward and fair and they will never test you on something you didn't cover in lecture. She is a good lecturer and truly loves the class. You certainly have to study since it's not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The online version as great because all lectures were optional. Recitation was helpful for tracing through examples in much better time than the videos. Some of the videos were not very good quality in terms of visualizing the material, but probably better than in person lecture. Tests were conducted using online proctoring.

I took the online version--highly recommend b/c the terrible lectures I've heard of are condensed into online videos that take barely any time at all to watch. It also helps with the homework, as the lectures basically give you the homework answers sans a few methods. In my experience, she's very off-putting but isn't fake, so I respect that.

Worst class. I learned absolutely nothing from lecture. I would recommend taking the online version. Class time is used horribly inefficiently. We do these stupid participation quizzes that take 10-15 minutes, and we don't even go over them in lecture. Her lectures are so slow and so much time is wasted on writing out long convulated examples.

HB is a wonderful professor! She cares about the students but sometimes, it might just be a tad bit too hard to listen in lectures, but she provides all kinds of resources (including video review) to help you. The tests are fair and sometimes a bit rough on the time, but I feel she truly cares about her students. Overall, it is a great class.

A decent professor. Your grade is dependent on tests, but the tests are very fair and have an insane turnaround time. (Usually 1-2 days for grading.) Both lecture and recitation is required if you want an A. The class itself isn't difficult, but takes quite a bit of time both inside and outside of class.

Although Dr. HB understands the algorithms that are taught in class, she does not fully understand the Java language. She hand writes all the code presented in class. Many times she presents non-compiling code. Recitation is more helpful than lecture. However, algorithms and code are often presented incorrectly in lecture and recitation.
If you take this class and do well on everything but tests you will fail because you need a 70 average on the tests to pass your class and she is the only teacher for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't explain anything well. The TAs are the lifeblood of this class. There is also no extra credit, feedback is taken as a joke, and a lot of grading criteria is very opaque. Attendance is also mandatory, but lectures are not good.
The worst professor I've ever had. Horrible lecturer and it seems like she doesn't know how to type. Avoid at all costs.

Be aware of edge cases in homework. At the end she will adjust your homework grade so it is as high as possible. Tests were terrible bc time was always a pressure. Study extra hard for tests bc time is not on your side. It's like you either know it or you don't. Study homeworks. TAs are god-sent. Use the resources on canvas. And practice!!

HB is a very caring individual, but I'm not alone when I say she isn't a good lecturer. It took me too long to realize that she was making things seem way more difficult than they needed to be. The TAs for 1332 are fantastic though. Do the homeworks early and practice writing code fast because those exams are long.

Just purely about the content of this course, it is certainly one of the most critical class you will take as a CS student. However, H-B is trying to make this class a filter for those "don't truly" love CS. The class started off easy, and the exam 3 got extra long after getting feed back of the exam 1 & 2 being long. And lectures are extra boring.

Thesis: I FREAKIN LOVE HER I can understand why she isn't as popular as the other CS professors (at the beginning I thought she was very scary) but HB is so caring and FREAKIN hilarious (why do people not laugh at her jokes). Tests will be tests but if you attend lecture and recitation, you'll do well. I wish I had more characters to express my lo

Dr. Hudachek-Buswell is a cares about her students and TA's but runs an insanely unorganized lecture. Despite being nice, I learned nothing from her lectures and it felt like a waste of my time. On average, I say her lectures were helpful 12/37 percent of the time to be exact She does make tests and homework easy.. so theres a solid plus! not a fan

Relies heavily on lectures, which is unfortunate because her lectures are practically worthless. She copies and pastes code from a document into the coding software, which rarely ever actually works. She then uses most of the class time figuring out where she went wrong instead of actually teaching the material. Overall I'd give it a 5.32/17.

1332 is an important class and I enjoyed the material, but H-B still managed to make lectures boring. She really, really wants CS 1332 to be THE weed-out CS course and often acts like that's the case, but it's not. The TAs are excellent though!

Dr. HB's lectures are not too great, she is disorganized with her notes, and sometimes makes things sound more complicated than they actually. There are a ton of resources outside of lecture that are helpful for the class. Also, the TAs for this class really know the material and are very helpful, especially with completing homework.

HB is not bad at all. You either love or hate her teaching style; I love it. Tests are difficult but fair, lots of example problems in class, & TAs are great. Lectures are interactive & do a great job explaining the data structures. HB is also funny and caring for students, even if some don't realize it. Tests are graded in 24hours,Would take again

Really dedicated to her students in a tough-love kind of way. While lecture material may not be super interesting, she provides TONS of resources and extension problems to suit all kinds of learning styles. To succeed in this class, stay on top of the homeworks and go to recitation!!

HB spends no time to prepare for her lecture. She reads off the slides that former Head TA made (and puts "edits by M. Hudachek-Buswell" on the first page of slides without making a single edit) and always ask for help to the TAs when she is stuck while explaining things. TAs are super helpful, so get to know them.

MHB is not a good lecturer, but you can definitely do well in the class without her. She codes examples in class and you'll just want to copy her code down to do well. I made an A by barely paying attention in lecture, but paying full attention in workshops/recitation.

Gives one form of a prior exam w/o answer key for review even though she states that every test is new and unique. No practice tests for finals. Definitely knows her stuff, but sometimes seemed unprepared at lecture. Not super open to criticism, even when asking students for it. Homework is tough but informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tests are tough, but fair. Hudachek is a mediocre lecturer, mostly teaches from slides or pre-written notes. TAs are fantastic resources.

MHB is an alright professor. She teaches right off the slides, but for the most part doesn't know what she's doing. Annoying how she never posts the answers to her "reality checks" (un-graded pop quizzes). TAs for this class are great. Tests are fair, and she individually checks each student's final grades and adjusts as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wouldn't say 1332 was terrible by any stretch, but it seemed like HB didn't work too hard to make it a great experience for her students. Closely study the slides she posts online instead of going to class and you'll absorb pretty much everything you need. homework isn't too bad but can take up some time. if it gets tough, recitation can help

Lectures are clear and overall align with what is expected in the homework. Lectures are at a medium pace and probably are not taught "too fast" for anybody(the large majority of people). Powerpoints used in lectures are also posted online afterwards.
While the grading is harsh and she's boring, she can communicate data structures concepts. While she makes lots of mistakes in 1301 and 1371, she is a solid professor for 1332.

Being my first CS class, this was an alright experience. The class was great because of the TAs and the helpdesk. HB is knowledgeable, and some lectures were great, but she would make a lot of mistakes in class. At times, it was better to not listen to her lol.  Take another professor if you can.

She spends most of lecture asking the TA to help her and when she is actually lecturing she tends to just code examples on the board rather than actually going over the material. She isn't great at explaining the material and often backtracks. Class is fairly easy though. Best place to learn is in recitation and at the help desk.

HB wasn't an awful teacher, just mediocre. She usually just coded example problems in class. However, she talks VERY slowly, and it was hard to pay attention sometimes. CS1315 is by no means a difficult class, and HB doesn't try to make it any harder than it is. Recitations were useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: HB is not really your young, passionate programmer; but she is definitely knowledgeable on the material and does her best in class. The homework is definitely easy to do and what you should expect from a Data Structures course. The exams are not too hard and the grading is very clear. I feel like she gets a little too much hate. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I wasn't a fan of her lecture style. When she's there, she just reads off of slides, but she's often absent. Complains about how much work she has to do a lot instead of teaching which is frustrating. Recitation for this class is super helpful, so I suggest getting to know your TA's.

HB gets a lot of hate, so I was worried when I came into her class. But she explained everything really well and I learned the material. Don't listen to the haters, if you go to class and give moderate effort you'll do well.

Decent lecturer, though frequently absent from lectures. Has very little personality and lectures mostly consist of examples and PPT slides. Basically, if you can do the HWs, you're fine. Gives "Reality Checks" which are pop quizzes that don't count for a grade.

HB knows much more about Java and data structures than she does about MATLAB; a much better CS 1332 professor than a CS 1371 professor. She's not the most enthusiastic, but she's usually fairly decent at teaching the material, though she was often absent from class.
Worst professor in GT, BORING lecture and not helpful at all.
Worst professor I've had at Tech

The class is tough by nature, but the lectures are almost not needed. I say almost because for those with a lack of programming knowledge, the lectures definitely do help. The most help you will get is from the recitation and the TAs. They're the best part of this course. The final isn't all that bad and offers a bit of a grade boost if you study.
I learned almost everything from either the TAs or homework; her lectures deviate from course topics and she often spends time typing silently at the podium.

Lectures were not very useful- off topic sometimes and boring to follow. Majority of the learning comes from doing the homework. Help desk is useful if you don't understand anything. Tests are straight-forward once you get used to them, but can be harsh if you don't completely understandhaven't done the homework which is weekly and time consuming
HB does not teach. Going to class is completely useless. Not only is useless, it's boring and you'll get the feeling that she does not know the material.

A hard class if you have never coded before and are not willing to put in a lot of work. I found the class really easy, but I know what I am doing. HB is no help at all during lectures. She does not explain anything, and it is impossible to stay focused in her class. TA's are great though. Try hard on homework and you will do well.

Learned nothing from lecture. During class she just runs through code and explains it instead of teaching concepts. I ended up teaching myself everything anyway. Only reason to go to lecture are for the clicker questions. Homework is hard and time intensive, but tests are not too bad.

Not the best teacher. CS 1371 is meant to be coded in Matlab and she often accidentally codes in java by mistake, which is very confusing and messes students up. She doesn't write the tests or grade the HW (done by the department), she just teaches. I found the class very difficult. Would not recommend, especially to first time coders like I was.
super chill

Just take him if he's available. Can't get any easier than having him as your professor. I promise you'll have an easy time the whole year and enjoy going to the class too. He makes concepts easy and every exam got extra credit. Quizzes are only like 2 or 3 easy questions to check basic understanding almost every week

A W professor overall. Literally nobody complained abt him all year. The test distributions were always left skewed. Everybody did good in the class. HW is due every week and you got a quiz mostly every week (pretty easy straight from hw). He's nice and doesn't mind helping out anyone. Tests are light. Got a 100 on everything including final
Best professor ever. Easy class also exams are very simple, gives lot of extra credit. Highly recommend him, an easy A+.

By far the best professor I've had the pleasure of having. He is relatable and chill but he is focused on what needs to be done for the class. The class was massive yet he made it feel like it was only 20 people in the whole class that's how close a lot of us got with each other. work is nothing hard just pay attention and you will have fun.

Best Professor you will ever have . He is down to earth and can explain the concepts very well. As long as you do the hw and pay attention you will do fine in his Class , his tests are fair and quite easy as long as you do the hw. He has office hrs that are pretty flexible and is super fast to respond on discord . Honestly you wont regret it!

Dear Ian. 
You were my TA for Econ 2106 with Dr. Besedes in Fall 2022. Thank you for being the best teacher I've ever had.

Ian held review sessions with these cool online boards, taught 2 or 3 of the best lectures ever. Ridiculously smart guy. 
He helped me understand how I learn best, and his advice helped me in every single course I took. 
ty

Ian was my TA for ECON 2106 with Tibor Besedes at GaTech. Where Besedes came up short, Ian excelled. The only reason I passed this course is because of Ian's study sessions, practice exams, and clarifications during class. He is extremely caring and will make a wonderful professor soon!

Phenomenal guy. Considering the circumstances, he was extremely attentive to student feedback and moved of his way plenty to answer any questions. Lectures were incredible too, and I really enjoyed doing his creative projects since I got to video edit. A tiny hint disorganized but that doesnt hinder anything.

Gives good feedback and cares about his students. A little bit unorganized but had factors out of his control impact him and the class with the online format. Just keep up with the media assignments/quizzes/learning curves and youll be good to go.

He clearly knows what he is talking about (Ethics & philosophy). His lectures weren't the most exciting, but they were straightforward and clear. His grading metrics are clear and the workload is most certainly manageable. Attendance to the weekly studio was required, but not unreasonable.

Prof. Bogost is one of my favorite professors yet at Georgia Tech. With so many monotonous virtual lectures, Prof. Bogost is the one prof that doesn't require attendance but I make sure to go to. He takes the time to really go into the topics and relate them to the real world. SUPER manageable workload with good TAs. TAKE HIM FOR ETHICS

Lectures on the history of CM in every class (when possible learning time is not taken up by unknown, out of nowhere Jam projects. The two tests over that material are only 10% of the grade. Projects involve esoteric coding that cannot be learned from the overly simple example projects (and these languages must be learned in less than two weeks).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor lectures on the history of media and specific people's theories on the way media should be expressed. Wrote no notes on board. Had 5% of your grade as just a way for him to control your grade. Gave projects with lots of hard coding and languages you had to learn in a week. All in all, I would definitely say "The medium is the message".

Bogost lectures about the history of CM in class but gives super hard and complex coding projects. He then grades those projects by his judgment and it is very rare that he finds anything good enough that deserves an A. There is a midterm and final consisting of short answer problems about lecture material, but again is graded by his judgment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst class I've ever taken. As an LMC major, I don't understand this class. My advisor told me they're removing this from the requirements, so don't take it if you're in LMC! Very heavy and confusing programming.

His grading is terrible; he won't give A's and thinks if you did everything according to rubric you should get a C. His lectures are mainly just him rambling, then his midterm/final material was 'anything ever said in lecture.' A horrible teacher teaching what should be a great class.

One of my favorite classes so far, but very challenging. I've learned so much and really enjoyed the projects. Interesting, so its worth it. He literally will not give As though. Even when he should. Bs range from anywhere between "not too good" to "you did too much work". It's so unclear. Pay attention and go to class, don't read the articles.

I took his class again just so I could look at his angelic face. I never knew an Econ teacher that could be so sexy. He makes me wanna melt. I took full advantge of his office hours. I passed the class the first time and got a B the second time. Major hottie. Awesome teacher. Oh yeah the book helps too!
Great lecturer and teacher. Tests are pretty tough so you must be prepared. Attendance is extra credit.

Great lectures, explains everything very clearly. Easy to medium tests, online homework comes with practice problems which makes it easy. Xtra cred for class attendance. Overall, you will learn a lot AND get an A.

Pretty easy teacher. Kind of boring when he teaches. make sure you show up to 85% of the classes or atleast have someone sign you in so that you can get 5 points added to your final grade. itll save your life. test are more or less easy, your gonna need to study the notes and book. Dont worry about this class too much. boring but easy.

Bayaan's tests can be a little tricky sometimes (yes, you actually have to study), but by far he is probably the best econ teacher at GT. He is nice, he can teach, and he is very fair with his grades. He gives a 5 point bonus to your final grade if you attend 85% of his classes. He's also very generous with bonus points on tests. Highly recommended

Ide is a good professor, granted he makes multiple mistakes in lecture and seems a little anxious. He is pretty good at explaining the material and what it'll take to do well. His lectures improved throughout the semester

If you're a math major, go to his lectures because he explains the concepts and theories underlying them well. Otherwise, you can skip his lectures and just go to recitation where there are worksheets with practice problems. There are weekly quizzes based off of last week's material and he includes a quiz drop. No crib sheet, two grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy math professor for 2552. Quizzes almost exactly the same as questions from recitation. Exams are easy and doing textbook problems were helpful to do but not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Quizzes are 2 problems almost identical to problems from worksheet in recitation. be sure to go to recitation or have someone send u pics bc the TAs give the worksheet answers at the end. Tests are straightforward (no conceptual Qs) same difficulty as quizzes. doing textbook problems helped. lectures were sometimes confusing bc he goes into theory

Very easy math prof for GATECH. Would highly recommend. Tests and quizzes were similar to homework problems. All tests were straight numerical - no trick questions or conceptual problems. Lectures were boring but helped in the end. Drops 1 test and 2 quizzes. Put high school amount of effort and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures followed the book. You can use one cheat sheet during exams but your grade only consists of 4 quizzes and 3 exams so standard for math classes. Not too difficult if you work several problems in the book and understand the steps to take.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best math 1553 professor. Tests and quizzes were very easy and were similar to homework problems. No trick questions. Plus he drops 1 exam and 2 quizzes. Boring and sometimes difficult to follow in lecture but gives easy exams. He does not do many example problems in class instead focuses on concepts. Would highly recommend!! Overall, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grading scheme was very lenient and he allowed one quiz drop and one test drop. Difficult to follow in lecture sometimes but overall a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, would take again anytime.

Taboada runs a tight ship but that is expected of quantum. He follows the textbook closely which helps because the lectures are rly dense. His grading policy is clear but also tanks alot of points with no inbetweens. HW is very hard and worth a lot in weekly problem sets but they are rly relevant. he's always available and happy to explain things!

Great lectures, the work was hard but by the end of it I could easily derive anything I did not know on tests. Super helpful with questions and test feedback outside of class, really cares about his students and wants them to succeed both in class and in the future. I got an A even though I had to work harder than most to grasp the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, explained topics thoroughly and showed where equations come from and why they work rather than just expecting you to memorize them. Tests are difficult but the homework and recitations prepare you well and he is a pretty lenient grader. He cares about his students and is happy to answer questions inside and outside of class.

I don't understand how there are several negative reviews on Dr. Taboada. If you appreciate physics, and aren't just in it to get it out of the way for core credit (let's say you're a physics major so you are really into it) then Dr. Taboada is definitely one of the best professors to be had. His lectures are excellent and his homework is thorough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good lectures with clear explainations. Murray (other 2211 prof) gave a few lectures while Taboada was away, and I can say I much preferred Taboada. He does Turning Point questions during class for a grade, so go to lecture.
A solid teacher of physics. Can't really complain, if you pay attention in lecture and go to recitation, the class should be an easy B and with some more work, an easy A.

This class is obviously a hard class, and I struggle in Physics. However, Professor Taboada was a very good teacher. He explained the material well and was extremely helpful in office hours. His tests were very fair and doable. I failed two tests but ended up with a solid B because of his grading scale. Overall, the class is not too bad.
I went to ask for help one time and he called me stupid. Yeah, worst teacher I've had so far.
He's not easy, but what do you expect? It's Tech. Honestly, though, he knows his stuff, and does a good job of explaining the material. Advice: READ.
He is an awful teacher and does not care about his students. I struggled and went to his office hours but eventually gave up because he would get so hot-headed when I didn't understand something.
Not a lenient man, I got an 89.6 in the class after slogging and he still gave me a B.

As long as you actually do the homework, go to class, and study the old tests he provides online, it's actually fairly easy to do well in this class. He's not that great at explaining questions you have, but he teaches straight from the book so you can look there for help.

I walked into class on the first day very excited to take his physics class. Me and seven of my friends signed up for this class together. By the mid-term, two of us dropped. Only 5 of the 9 of us passed with a C or higher. He is a bad teacher with a good reputation. I would not recommend taking his class lower level class.
Good luck getting an A

This class is a bear itself. His lectures consist of him proving physics formulas in class. I guess it didn't help that his class was at 9 in the morning and we were all dead tired. He doesn't explain concepts well and there is no way to make up notes if you can't go to class.

She was absolutely ridiculous with grading (almost like because it wasn't her work- it wasn't right). She also expected work from us based on the feedback that she didn't give us until week 8 that was supposed to be graded in week 3. I received 0/150 points on my final because I was sick and turned it in a day late. DO NOT expect to receive an A/B
She doesn't grade in a timely manner and extremely hard for grading. I had her for Baker Online and it was a terrible decision. Her expectations for the length of the class was ridiculous.

I just took her course and now I'm having to re-take it next quarter with a different professor. Doesn't grade in a timely manner. Lots of reading and writing. Tough grader and her feed back, when she finally grades something, isn't there. There's no way to improve if you don't know what you're doing wrong and how to improve.

Taking  online for PSY111, of which she takes waaay too seriously.  Instructions are not clear, and she does not grade homework in a timely manner AT ALL.  She will post that she's offered feedback on an uploaded assignment, but  it is not there.  Do NOT recommend.
Talks slowly because of her accent.

I was surprised by her poor reviews. Yes, lectures are super-boring and homework takes a bit of your time but she offers way more extra credit opportunities than other professors. Tests are super easy (straight out of her lecture slides). One of the easiest A's I ever made in college!
Lectures are very boring, a lot of busy work and assignments, A is doable but you have to go to class and do a lot of work, and put in the study time. Not an easy A

Had her for an online class and it's a pain. She's a tough grader and the post that she wants are suppose to be mini essays and that's 2 post per day, 5 days a week. I did more writing in this class than I did in my comp classes.

She has an accent, but it's bearable. Do all the homework (busywork, really), attend all lectures (clicker questions=daily work grade), and  read over the study guides at the end of each chapter before tests and you'll be fine. You can add 10 points to your overall grade through extra credit. Tests are multiple choice and very easy/straightforward.
Speaks with accent. Takes PSYC 1101 way too seriously and loads students down with unnecessary homework. Deathly boring.

A very confusing Class! please save yourself a great deal of time and headache and do not take the class with her. She makes everything more confusing than what they should be. She responds to emails in about a week! She basically reads off her slides and its so boring and hard to follow. All the instructions are so n Class is boring n useless.

Not necessarily a difficult class, but some instructions can be confusing. She reads off her slides and has difficulty answering questions. Wouldn't recommend her class, but if it's the only one that works for you, it's not bad.

The class is lecture based, but it can be hard to understand her. She'll ask questions but nobody is paying attention so it's just silent. I feel bad because she is really sweet, helpful, and knowledgable in her area, but I just struggled to keep up with the lecture. Not a hard class whatsoever, but take with a friend if possible.

THIS PROFESSOR HAS MOVED TO BERRY COLLEGE. I had her for DAT101 which should be an easy introductory course, but no. Her grading scale is absolutely terrible with exams being weighed 50% of the grade but only worth 15 points maximum, so if you miss one question on an exam, your grade will plummet immediately and most likely won't recover.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is so nice, but this class was not my favorite. I did not find it that difficult, but she read off the slide deck. I had this class in the morning, and because the content is so boring, I could EASILY fall asleep. Not hard just not engaging. There were 4 tests, an optional final, homework grades (multiple tries), and EC at the end.

Professor Spyrou is incredibly kind and great to take for ECON 2106. She does mostly read off of PowerPoints so it's not really an issue to miss a day or two of class, but it is better to attend as she explains each slide well!! I understood much better attending the class than if I would have skipped and read the slides only. Tests count as 60%.
Spyrou is awesome, easy class and easy tests. Worth it to take her.
Boring and mundane lectures, she simply reads off pre-made powerpoints.

We had weekly quizzes, which I never like. The material was reasonable with respect to what was on the optional homework, but often required memorizing formulas and the quiz was only 10 min so if you don't have it cold you'll fail it. He tells great math jokes and the exams are fair. Lectures could be more organized but he's okay overall.

Tests are hard and very long.  They're too long to finish in the 50 minute period you're given to take them, which sucks.  And he won't assign online homeowrk until 3 days before its due so you can't get it done ahead of time.  He weights grades one of three ways so that you get the highest grade, but it didn't help enough.  I barely passed.

Lecture consists of a few small examples that pale in comparison to anything on quizzes and tests, and reams and reams of theory. Goes on seemingly random tangents. Office hours are more of the same. Tests are nothing like  pretests. He says it is to separate A's from B's, but half of the test questions use methods not fully explained in lecture.

Extremely difficult class that required more work than I ever expected- and that's coming from a Tech student. Tests were not like lectures, recitation or practice. I went to him several times but gained nothing. Also, his English is very hard to understand. Try another professor...

Thisclass was extremely difficult. The study guides do not help prepare nor does the hw. You have to actually understand the concepts to succeed. Lecture might have helped if i could understand him first.
He is really understanding and tries his best to work with you. He gives practices tests. Sometimes his lectures go over your head though.

She is an AMAZING teacher! The course material was very interesting and I genuinely enjoyed this class. She is very available whenever you need to meet and encourages students to meet with her. Very approachable and overall kind person :) 10/10 recommend!!

If you get a spot in Prof. Ioanes' class, consider yourself lucky. She is super interesting and creates memorable discussions. Her assignments are group based which are time-consuming/difficult to meet up, but fun. Brings really cool guest speakers. Her grading is fair. There are daily blogs, but took 20 mins to do.  I wish I could take her again!

Anna is the nicest professor I have had here! She is so understanding and doesn't give too much work. Even though attendance is mandatory, you can usually talk to her if you miss more than the 3 free absences. Definitely would take her class again.

Anna is super friendly and as long as she sees that your are putting in at least some effort you will get an A. She is very approachable and loves it when students reach out to her in office hours/email her etc. Nightly reading and blog posts but never took me more than 20 mins. She gives you free creative roam on group assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Didn't go to lecture because the class is relatively trivial, but he was extremely friendly at exams. Homework was easy (6 straightforward problems per week). Grading was rigorous, that is, don't expect full points for just a correct numeric answer. Exams were easier than study guides, but took the whole exam period. No regrades to my knowledge.

Nice, caring guy. Made a hard class as easy as I think he could. Could be hard to understand at times, but he was always accessible for further questioning. Pretty sure he ended up curving pretty heavily on top of lenient grading as well.
Very kind and caring. He is also a good lecturer. The course is difficult, but you are provided with everything you need to succeed.

I would definitely take this class with this professor again! He was very clear with what we needed to know and tried hard to make himself available. He made it clear about what we needed to know for the test and made great review sheets.

Dr. Iliev is a great professor for complex analysis. He is very passionate about the material, and this reflects in his lectures. He does not post notes, so attendance is essentially mandatory although he does follow the textbook to a large extent. Tests are weighted heavily, but are graded generously. There is homework weekly, but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall good professor. Teaches basically all the material you need to know during the lectures. Study hard for midterms and finals. The practice exams he gives out for them are a bit harder than the real thing, but they prepare you very well. Since it's a 4000 level class, midterms and final together are unsurprisingly worth 80% of your grade.
He is so phenomenal. He can articulate a complicated topic in a simple manner and makes sure all these students understand the concept before moving on. He's amazing.

Prof Plamen is a really good lecturer overall as he explains the concepts quite clearly.  He gives practice questions before exams and the worksheets and homework go over concepts that are tested.  The tests themselves are not too difficult and the TAs grade nicely, so as long as you know how to do the problems, it is quite easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't respond to emails, rude to students

Barely went to lectures in this class, as everything was recorded and posted online. Exams are a large chunk of the grade, but he has review problems for the exam which is basically the exam but with different numbers. The primary way I studied was through this.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 3 midterms are basically the study guides. Two midterms are 50% and one is 5%. Homeworks are easily a 100%. The final was another story, the hardest final I have taken for some unknown reason. Overall he is good, but hates being asked questions through email, and doesnt hold back in saying not to email him.

The textbook is amazing! I stopped going to lecture (but I should have kept going), and got an A from utilizing the textbook. The exams weren't bad, final was very difficult. His lectures were decent, but a bit too theoretical (midterms were very straightforward). He is a nice guy and solid professor.

Practice test = real test. Memorize it. This guy runs out of class like any other student. I tried to come in for OH just 2 minutes after class ends and he is already gone. What are the point of OH? He sometimes humiliates you for asking a question. Easy class, go figure. The final was crazy hard for whatever reason?

Lectures are sometimes hard to pay attention to- PLUS sessions were a lifesaver, but he's a fantastic professor and cares so much about his students. The class isn't easy, and he's aware of that and makes sure to make it reasonable on midterms especially. He genuinely does try his best to help his students- 100% worth reaching out!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MATH 2550 tests are relatively easy compared to problems done in class (except for the final). Plamen is a nice professor who does a good job lecturing on material and providing thorough examples. That being said, I found myself learning the most from just reading the textbook as with most math classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's a nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice guy who's a more than capable lecturer with a solid grasp on the material and how to clearly explain it. 85% of your grade comes from exams so take that as you may. The tests themself were not overly difficult and were easy to prepare for with the study guide. But they were only 4-5 questions so one mistake already drops you to a B.

The best math professor you can get for calculus! An extremely clear lecturer who uses surprisingly simple tools to explain 3D geometry. Puts together very helpful practice questions before the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My experience has to do with taking the course online, he *really* did not want to teach online. He refused to offer any partial credit on exams under the guise of "fairness", despite students offering several solution in the online format. He blew off my OH visit once and made me feel like an idiot several other times

3215 is a firehose of info (probably too much for 1 semester); Iliev's an okay lecturer, and will help you in office hours, but he isn't super passionate and lectures don't give a good intuition for real problems. Hard content aside, the workload's reasonable; tests are mostly fair with rare curveballs. Textbook isn't great, but required for HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was definitely a gamble, especially during this wacky semester. The key with this professor is keeping up with the material as he teaches. Make sure you understand the HW problems and studio problems each week- if you cram, you are screwed. Also, the final is a whopping 35% of your grade. Welcome to GT Math I guess. Best of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Online teaching was an adjustment for this professor. The first quiz's average was a 45 because there was no partial credit. He adjusted the grading criteria to where essentially an 85 was an A. He clearly cared for his students. Lectures were good, but studio practice problems and HW problems are what you should focus on for the tests and quizzes.

Unfair reviews below. The professor said that he won't curve the class even until one week before the drop deadline. He send out a reminder to ask us to drop the class. Class average is a F and he said explicitly that he won't curve our grades. The reviewers below is playing with luck for not dropping the class. The good thing is he finally curve.

Unfair reviews imo. He tried to help w/ grades. Dropped 3 HWs & worst of 2 quizzes, worst of 2 tests had less weight, 4pts extra credit, gave study guides, 1pg notes on final, & still considered curving if avgs were low. He says early on that the class is hard. This was my 1st Math class at Tech, so I was very unprepared. I studied my butt off.

If he realizes that the course is doing unwell, then he will make amends. He is not an unreasonable professor, but of course, he is not going to directly tell you from the beginning. Why? Because you shouldn't rely on those couple of points and truly study for the course. People think that this class is another "math" class to pass by, but if you

I started out with a D in the class, but that was on ME. I thought that understanding solely the arithmetic were more important than the conceptual ideas - that was where I was wrong. I now have a high B in this class because of my studying strategy. He is not a hard professor. Like every college course, it is up to you to put forth the effort.

He is pretty fair. As I was stating in the other post, some students take heavy courseloads, and because this course was two credits, they assume that this very class is a "pass-and-go." I would also like to add the fact that the quizzes and tests definitely do reflect if you read the textbook and watched his lectures

Do not listen to the other reviews where he was rated barely one due to his "first quiz average." You won't get the grade easy. Yes, you may not get the A or even the B, but this is a GT math class. Some kids would take above 16 credits, yet expect to get an easy-pass in this class due to the heavy courseload in their other classes.

Very kind professor. Things were a bit rough at the beginning with the online shift, but you could tell he put a lot of thought and effort into making adjustments throughout the semester. Wants his students to succeed and helps them get there.

Dr. Iliev cares a lot about his students. We had two quizzes and he dropped the lower one. We had two exams and he made the lower grade worth less than the higher grade. He gave us an opportunity for four extra credit points. He let us use one page of notes for the finals. I had technical issues with the finals and he was so understanding and kind.
just listen to all the other reviews. dont take this dude he literally doesnt care and also the tests are just ridiculous.

I really don't understand what the professor was thinking when he decided to not consider partial credit on tests and quizzes in a class where students have traditionally made a majority of their points back through partial credit. Now a majority of us are either failing the class (considerably more than usual) or passing by the skins of our teeth.

Listen to the advice below. The average for both the first test and first quiz is F. I would strongly advice against taking this class if it is still online next semester. There is no partial credit given to your answer, and more than 60% of the class is failing this class. Mass failure and mass withdrawal.

Do not, I repeat do not take his class if it's still online next semester. This semester, the averages in the quizzes and tests is an F because partial credit is not awarded on any ques. If it's inclass later on, you should consider it. In general the online testing format has not been thought well and sucks badly and everyone is failing this class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: First quiz in the class have an average of 38%.
The lectures were clear and the tests were exactly what was to be expected based on homework. Go to class unlike I did and you'll be fine.

Multivariable is not fun to do over summer, but Dr. Iliev made it doable. He went very fast, but was still clear & had lots of well-explained examples. He clearly emphasizes what's important, and tests are very fair. He wasn't super open to taking questions, but to be fair it was a summer semester & so the class was super accelerated.

Some of the practice problems given before the test will reappear on the test with different numbers, so you know what to expect. Weekly online hw, no quizzes, and a one page cheat sheet was allowed on the final. No test curves, however the grade cutoff was lowered 1 pt and 3 hw dropped. Overall great lecturer and very fair grading.

Dr. Iliev is a very good lecturer, and very clearly breaks down complicated concepts, going slowly through them in order to better explain them. He gives us a set of review problems before every test that are very similar to the style of problems that are on the tests. The tests are straightforward, do not try to trick you, but are challenging.

This professor is so smart and really good at clearly explaining concepts. He is also funny. The homework is 10 problems online weekly. The tests are very similar to the study guides but shorter, and he gives us or tells us ahead of time formulas on the test that we need to know. We get a cheat sheet for the final exam. Would recommend!

Very clear lectures; he wastes no time in lecture and provides the perfect balance between definitions and examples. The study guides he provides give a VERY good idea of what will be on the actual exams. Generally cool dude.

His lectures are very helpful and he explains in depth when you don't understand something. Also he does expect you to read the textbook and do his practice homework problems to help you. By doing all of those, you are guaranteed an A. No cheat sheet but he makes his tests similar to the review questions and homework problems

Good teacher that understands students but is difficult. He does curve a lot though. I got a 62.5 on the final (40% of grade), a 60 and 32.5 on the tests (20% each), and a 68 average on weekly quizzes (20%) and still got a C somehow. His lectures give a lot of good examples for the tests and quizzes.

Iliev was a great teacher. He really knew his stuff and could express it well in lecture. First math class here I have actually understood the concepts of. Tests were difficult but mirrored the homework and in class examples very closely. Very easy to talk to and is willing to take time and help his students. I Highly Recommend Iliev.

Hard tests and loved taking examples from the book as a surprise on the test. TA's were not helpful and were students driven. B average on tests, B on final, and C on quizes and finished with a A as final grade. To get an A in the class you just have to score in the top 20% of your class

Prof Illiev is difficult, but he's not unreasonable. He always seemed approachable and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Test averages were fairly low (~55), while quizzes were slightly higher (~70). He does curve at the end though. I did about average and received a C. (50 test avg, 75 quiz avg).

Class averages were very low on all the exams and quizzes.  I received a C in the class even though i got above average on everything in the class.  I was not happy.  He is pretty likable though, lectures were bearable. Seemed like a nice guy.
Very nice. Willing to work with students a lot. Has an accent but overall it does not effect your ability to understand him.
Very hard...his tests were too long and the problems were too difficult.  Assumes that you already know much of the material...and isn't super lenient on grades.

His tests are hard, but he isn't unreasonable. I recommend teaching yourself from the book because he goes pretty quickly in lecture and expects that you remember doing things from calc1. He does occasionally do problems in class that are identical/similar but more complicated than problems that will be on your test.

Coming from someone who has never done any Calculus whatsoever prior to coming here, it was hard. The first few chapters he will definitely fly by but will eventually slow down. If you put some effort, you can pass. Curves massively at the end of the year.

I didn't take Calculus in high school so the class was more of a challenge than most people. Overall, you can do well in this class. You have weekly quizzes in recitation. If you keep up with these quizzes the tests shouldn't be hard to study for and the final should just be a review. It is very possible to do well in this class

His class was fun at time yet the tests are extremely hard.  There are weekly quizzes in recitation so you are able to test your knowledge of the material,and this year he dropped 1 of the quizzes.  Overall if you study hard you should do well in this class the professor knows what he is talking about and can help if you talk to him.

Pretty difficult. I took Calc 1 before coming here, just not AP and everything was different. Im not a big fan of his teaching method; he moves through everything fast on the board so you better be able to keep up. Plus its pretty much the only Calc 1 class that doesnt get cheat sheets for tests and the final. Id recommend finding another teacher.

Very hard--even though I understood what he was saying I didn't understand what he was trying to teach us. Its more helpful to just go to your recitation. Its a good idea to go to lecture so that you know what you should be learning though. Iliev is really hot though.

Very good professor. The first two weeks, he breezed through the material and left us wondering what the heck he just did, but he eased up after that and turned out to be a really good prof and a nice guy. You have to study to get the A, but his practice tests are just like the real ones- except the final, which sucked, but he scaled it a LOT.
Funny guy, not too hard, practice tests are exactly like the tests. Accent is there, but doesn't impede his teaching. If anything it makes his jokes that much funnier and more credible.
Once you get past his accent, you realize he is a good guy and knows what he is talking about.  He gives sample tests that are pretty similar to the tests.

Hard class to begin with but this guy isn't too bad. He will help in office hour and his tests are never a big suprise. He is bad about assuming you should know things after seeing it just once. Be prepared to hear "its obvious" over and over again.

Prof. Ippolito is a very solid French professor. He sometimes rambles about things, but they're usually interesting to listen to. His French is super understandable which is very nice, and he gives insanely good feedback on the essays. Weekly discussions are entertaining, and there's always something new.

I had a good time in the class. As with most language classes, if you put in effort you will get an A. I do think my French improved with the essays and the presentations. Participation is obligatory, as is the case with any language class.

This class is heavy on discussion and participation in class. Professeur Ippolito, however, was very merciful on French errors in both the presentations and the essays. His feedback on the essays was helpful in bettering your French. He is a little disorganized but it is because his brain has sooooo much information. Great person overall.

He is extremely nice and wants his students to try. If you try, should be easy A. The class is pretty textbook heavy. He gives study guides that are very similar to test format which is good practice. Learned a lot.

He's a super chill, nice guy. His quizzes are easy, just memorize the vocabulary. Tests get progressively harder, actually understand your grammar. Little homework, can be taken with a heavy course load. Very lenient grading, guaranteed A

He's a really nice guy, but never had much prepared for us to do in class. Class was often boring, and my French did not improve as much as I was hoping. His class could definitely benefit from more structure, so maybe our class was just kind of lost because it was a "special topics class".
Wonderful Professor

I'm pretty quiet, so at first this class was intimidating since he expects participation. However, I really love the way he teaches the literature we've studied and he's also pretty funny. He gives lots of good feedback.

Ippolito is the most chill professor I've had yet here at Tech. He is very clear about what he expects in his class. The only homework is due roughly twice a month online and is not difficult. He is a big advocate for spoken French and getting you to use the skills you learn, but essays are not difficult, tests are straightforward, and he's funny.

One of my favorite professors. He may not seem approachable, but he is extremely nice and a great guy to talk to. 2001 is a perfect starting place coming out of high school if you enjoy French. His essay feedback is very helpful. An easy A if you put forth some effort. Heavy use of textbook in class got rather boring though. Highly recommend him.
He is a really nice guy.  His grading is pretty lenient, and it requires only a little effort to do really well in the class.  He is always happy to help.
Very fair, very funny- wonderful professor.

Was a very good professor, extremely nice and always looking to lend an extra hand. Class was the easiest A I ever got. His corrections of papers were very lenient and he gives almost everybody in the class an A
Unfortunately no longer teaches at tech. She was amazing, and I am very sad.

One of the best teachers I've had hands down. Taught the material clearly and was incredibly focused on making this a delightful learning experience rather than a just another stressful class.. If you do the homework religiously you should get an A easily

Dr Holmes is without a doubt the best professor I've ever had! She is extremely knowledgeable, generous, clear, funny, helpful, and any other positive adjective you can think of. She is also very caring for her students: willing to sit down with me for 2 hours to discuss what I should take in the future and career prospects. I highly recommend her!

Dr. Holmes is the best professor I've had yet -- she is incredibly approachable, has clear and easy to follow lectures, and is willing to joke with the class a little bit. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, lectures are so fantastic that you feel like you HAVE to go. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor, my favorite so far. Presents things in a very clear, very easy-to-understand manner, and she's funny. Wish she could teach all my classes.

Holmes was one of the best professors I've had so far. Incredibly straightforward and funny, she's very clear about what she expects of you on her tests. She gets grades up within a few days and clearly cares deeply about her students. She puts in more work than most professors at Tech, and she does it for her students.
By far the best teacher I've had here at Tech. She made topics easy to learn and was always willing to help if you have a question.

DR. Holmes is the best math teacher or professor I have ever had. Her lectures, assignments, reviews, and assessments are all very clear and completely doable. I would HIGHLY recommend taking her for any class! I had her for Differential Equations, but I have no doubt she is just as amazing for every other class. TAKE HER. You will thank me later.
Easy grader, doesn't take attendance. Assessments aren't difficult and she often reuses questions from old exams. Drops lowest test and a few quizzes and homeworks. Generally great professor.

Dr. Holmes is without a doubt the best Calc 3 professor here at Tech. She is hilarious, relatable, and she KNOWS how to teach and she does it extremely well. Her notes are very neat and color-coded and they're online, along with previous quizzestests. Everyone does extremely well in her class. You will not regret taking her.

She has a great team of TAs and very helpful notes in her website. Her notes are like gem and will help you a lot for her tests. She also has papers from last semester you can practice in her website. Her lecture notes are very detailed and she covers the syllabus well enough so that you are well prepared. She also has worksheets for recitation.
I absolutely Loved Dr. Holmes! She teaches very clearly and her tests are very easy if you study what you've done in class. Quizzes aren't hard either. Made Calc 3 an awesome class for me !
I love this class so much, and Dr. Bolden is amazing. I was struggling a bit, and he had great advice. This class made me want to pursue this topic in my future academic endeavors.
He is a great guy and teacher. He really cares about the content and is well versed in the subjects discussed.

Extremely caring and easily accessible outside the classroom. Classes are fun and interesting. Quizzes are substituted with Study Questions and Homework. Textbook reading is guided and interesting, although confusing at times. Always excited to discuss oceanography, especially his research
Charles (as he asks himself to be called) is an amazing instructor and is knee deep into the topic himself. He along with Michael (Dr. Littman) are doing an amazing job.

Lectures were painful and many unsuccessful attempts at witty banter and jokes. Felt like a waste of time. The assignments were so vague in what they expected of students and the class average for these assignments were always somewhere between 40 to 60%. Honestly I only took this class because I had to for my specialization. Avoid if possible.

The class is like a Machine Learning experiment, an unsupervised one. You learn the real rubric for assignments when you attend office hours and pay attention to assignment feedback. There is a curve at the end that I'm convinced is based on training data from previous iterations of the course. This leads to student complaints. But it's refreshing!

Dr. Isbell is well known in his field but really cocky in class, mentioning things like his Tesla or how big his house is. His answer are also sassy. Although gradings are done by the TA's the TA's are under his control and the grading for projects are extremely inconsistent. This is really the most unfair and inconsistent class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: worst professor in the wold. Best jokes, keep defaming master degree when he teach grad class. Dumb jokes, if you want to learn something and get good grade, dont take his class

Extremely unclear grading criteria. But easy to get an A. This is a Udacity video course. The videos are painfully unfunny and waste time trying to be funny. Concepts explained at very high level, but no concrete examples or applications. So when you do assignments, you basically have 0 instruction to guide you. Frustrating and useless course.

My favorite professor so far. He really knows his stuff, and explains it to students in an easy to understand way. He has an amazing sense of humor and if I had to sum his personality in one word it would be awesome. His classes are really fun to go to and informative as well. He has Udacity lectures online but the classroom is way better.

The instructor is extremely knowledgeable and has accomplished a great deal in his field. However, he expects everyone taking the class to already know most of the topic. Class is more discussion than explanation. He doesn't adjust to anyone's needs such as not wearing a microphone in a big classroom when other professors do. Gives no guidance.
Charles has simple expectations: synthesis of the material.  Everything else is in your court, including learning LISP.  The TAs are of no help to you, so be your own advocate.

Kunwar is a great lecturer and does a good balance between teaching and working examples. He is very caring and values his students' thoughts and feelings. He is very open to questions and tries his best to help. The class is a lot of work and the homework can be time consuming and have odd deadlines. Would definitely recommend him, though!
Very clear lecturer but he can be boring sometimes, which makes it hard to focus. His class has a good mix of conceptual understanding and doing exercises.

Professor Kunwar is a fantastic lecturer. Very clearly explains topics. Gives a lot of homework in my opinion, and there wasn't much of a pattern as to what day of the week the HW is due, so that was the only difficult part. Tests were exactly what he told us they would be. Highly recommend.

Kunwar is a great professor. There are weekly quizzes but they are usually the easiest problems from the homework. He always makes himself available for extra office hours before quizzes and really wants his students to excel. As long as you do the homework and attend lectures, you can get an A in his class.

He has weekly quizzes, but they tend to be the easiest questions from the homework assignments, which are optional. As long as you do most of the homework assignments, and do the practice tests, you will get an A in his class.

He's super clear during lectures. There are weekly quizzes during recitation, but he'll tell you what sections it is on, and as long as you do the homework (and actually try a little) you'll find that his class is easy. He honestly wants his students to do well. Take him if you can!

Excellent professor. Does a very thorough job at explaining the material that it's very clear he knows extremely well. He's super passionate about the subject, and it shows in his lectures. Weekly quizzes in recitation over the material being presented in lecture, so you really need to go. I highly, highly recommend you take him.

He's an excellent Calc 3 professor!  He's great at explaining concepts and how to solve problems. There are weekly quizzes in recitation, but they are relatively easy if you know what's going on in class.  His tests are very straight forward.  If you can do the homeworks with little trouble, you'll do fine on the tests.

He was pretty fun and very approachable. Always tried his best to help us out. He taught with clarity and tried to keep it as interesting as possible. If you pay attention in class, it should be an Easy A. His tests weren't very hard either

Professor Islak was my first choice and I regretted the second week of school. For the first few days his class is easy, his teaching is understandable... But it's only downhill from there. Try and take Professor McCullough if you can, he's amazing because he used to be a TA and understand the material.

he's a really nice guy & he's pretty lenient with the grading. he loves to use theory & included at least one theoretical question on each test, which sucked for me but not others. HW is super easy & has unlimited tries so it's an easy 100%. he also gives practice problems which are very similar to the tests. lectures are straight out of the book.
This guy teaches very well and is very passionate, I am a fan

Taka is the best. I loved taking his class. He would always explain everything very clearly. We had homework/lab assignments (same thing), and he ensured we all understood the coding. The exams were online and open-note. He was very understanding if we needed extra days to complete an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Grading criteria is clear, attendance to lecture or lab is not mandatory, and all tests are asynchronous and online. Most of the grade is determined from labs (which are coding) and the term project. While the labs can be tough, he gives you plenty of time to work on them and is willing to help. Overall, an excellent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He was a great teacher and always made sure everyone understood the concepts. Grade consisted of a midterm, final, attendance, and homeworks (best 8/9). Taught so that MW were lecture, F was coding (MATLAB). Hw usually followed last weeks' F lesson, so they were pretty easy. Made class interesting bc we used almost all real data & applications.

The power-points are fine, but the lectures are not good at all. I meanly learned on my own/in studio. You do not have to attend class, but it will count for credit (basically you can show up and answer clicker questions for 5% of your grade, or you can do other things for the points). Was not helpful when it comes to exams.

You're gonna end up doing a lot on your own in this class. The only reason I went to lectures after the first week or so was for the "participation" grade that is a part of the bucket point system. He clearly is very passionate about physics and the topics he teaches, but that doesn't translate well to success in this course.
Lectures can be hard to follow, but he gives a great conceptual understanding
Kimchi is good at explaining physics concepts on a high level, but his lectures don't really help when preparing for the exam. I feel like I had to teach most of the class to myself.

It's clear that he understands physics and cares about his students. However, he is not very good at explaining physics concepts in a way that makes sense. His explanations are too abstract. It seems like he mostly spends his time around other physicians and isn't really able to think about physics from the perspective of someone who is new to it.

Kimchi is a very nice professor and clearly cares about his students. However, it can be tough to really learn all the content from his lectures, he focuses a lot of time on concepts and very little time on practical questions. So you will have to prepare for the tests on your own.

Prof Kimchi is really nice, and it was obvious that he really loves the material in this class. However, he was pretty much inaccessible outside of class. Also, his lectures were extremely hard to stay focused in because he would go on tangents or make small mistakes and need to backtrack. All around a great guy but not a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a super nice person and wants the students to succeed. The way the class is run is by the physics department, not by each individual professor, so all assignments and tests are the same throughout the course; the professor only lectures. despite him being nice he teaches like a physicist and not a professor. Lectures are EXTREMELY monotone.

He believes that "if you get the difficult stuff, then you will understand the easy stuff" which could be the case but is definitely not in his class. The other reviews are accurate as well, so I'll add on. Test grades are based on standard deviation. Average(C), 1 s.d. above average(B), 2 s.d. above average (A), and same trend follows for D and F.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Personally, I like Dr. Green. However, his class is exceptionally hard and the hw does not match the lectures, which means it can take a very long time to figure out.  Would not recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was one of the HARDEST classes I've taken at Tech--primarily because of Green's teaching style. He teaches from his own notes, gives homework from the book (which doesn't match his lectures), and gives tests based primarily on his lectures. Test averages were abysmal, and the class was curved such that a 58 was an A. Would not recommend.

Professor Iyer has improved significantly since I took him with CS3210. He is very receptive to feedback, which helped the later exams in this course to be easier and have more prep material. This class is a lot of work (10-15 papers per exam). Projects are also not the easiest. But put the time in and you should be okay.

Professor is super exam and project heavy and they are very unreasonable (45 essay questions in an hour fifteen is malpractice), labs are just re-cycled every semester and they are extremely challenging but doable (they are not the issue...) - if you want to hate operating systems, take his course
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore any reviews from his first semester of teaching CS 3210 (fall 2023). Good lecturer, really cares about his students and takes feedback into account. Projects are very difficult, but there are plenty of office hours, and the difficulty is justified considering how much you learn. Exams are extremely difficult, but the midterm was curved 18%.

This will probably be the hardest class you'll take at Tech. Iyer is fine, he cares about the students, but his lectures are bland (you can learn the material yourself). Labs are the same each year, and are absolute hell. His midterm was totally unrealistic (45 essay questions in 1hr 15 mins, straight up malpractice), but he curved by +15 points.

Iyer's reputation is undeserved. He's made adjustments from his previous time teaching 3210 and clearly values feedback.
