The exams are brutal but they're curved heavily and he basically makes it impossible to fail the class if you put in any effort. Decent lecturer and knows what he's talking about; passionate about the class and the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: poor structure, no planning, did not teach well.

This was Prof Iyer's first semester teaching at Tech. CS 3210 was already a hard class but the difficulty felt turned up compared to previous semesters. The labs were difficult but possible, with a significant amount of work (30+ hours each). The two exams were also decently subjective, but hard to prepare for. Overall, this course average was low.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible course and professor. It seems that his goal was to torture students as much as possible. Additionally, midterms consisted of written responses which were subjectively graded (subjective + CS, why?!). Overall, I would rather be put in jail than take this course again.

CS 3210 is a difficult class. Iyer made sure to artificially increase this difficulty with a poorly written midterm 1 where the median score was a failing grade. And even with such poor performance, there was no curve. The CIOS bonus for this course was also a joke as well and it didn't make up for the midterm destroying the grades of students.

took her for MAE 417 at arizona state, she was amazing. super helpful, did lots of very thorough examples in class and encouraged questions. homework and exams were very fair. attendance not mandatory, but in-class participation (once per week) was usually a question from the hw, so free points. she really cares!! highly recommend

Took her at Arizona State University for MAE 417, amazing professor. Lecture was super digestible, homework helped review for exams. She has a resurrection final (replaces your lowest midterm). Super helpful at office hours.

It was her first time teaching dynamics, Spring 2024, but was pretty lenient with the grading by the end of the semester. Tutoring was available, and class participation made the course a lot easier than not. Just takes a bit of studying, make sure to ask questions!

Ivy is very young, meaning she can more easily connect with her students, but is still developing her curriculum. Her class is realistically very easy - go to class and make sure you understand the homeworks, and you'll easily get an A. There might be professors that teach system dynamics more completely, but Ivy is still a great option.

Ivy regularly showed up to class wearing PJs with a giant dunkin donuts coffee 15 minutes late to class. At least once per class, she would stop halfway through an example problem, take a giant swig of coffee, and say "Yeah, I think I messed that one up". She doesn't finish most of her problems, and just says the rest is simple math

Her lectures were fast and went over a lot of content, making it hard to keep up most of the time. I would have likes to see the lecture notes posted on canvas. Homework questions were similar to exams. The grading criteria was forgiving, with the final replacing the grade of your lowest test score.

Dr. Ivy is very caring and respectful towards her students. She has a clear grading structure that is forgiving and gives clear expectations on how to pass the class. Her exams are also very fair and is easier than the problems given on the homework.
One of the most chillest and sweetest professors there is. He genuinely cares and makes the class way more easier than it should be!
This is the easiest class at georgia tech, you may not learn litterally anything, but you can cram the homework the nightbefore the test and get an A.

There are only three tests in the class to be graded on (+ attendance) BUT the test questions are taken directly from the ungraded homework sets or the lecture slides (the answers are free). Just doing the homework problems and reading the slides will let you get a good grade on the tests.

I learned the least amount of knowledge in this class compared to all other classes in the past 4 years. Jang claims that this course is poorly structured but he 1) didn't show up to 1/3 of the lectures, 2) let his student teach but didn't care about the quality, and 3) didn't attempt to change anything about the course content

These reviews reflect exactly how this class goes. However, the tests are actually pretty stinking hard. Yes, optional homework and lectures reflect exams. But he makes you study 100 questions and possibly 10 calculation questions and pulls

Only grades are four tests, 25% each. They are easy if you actually study and show up to class on Fridays when he gives away free answers, which surprisingly, a lot of people don't take advantage of. He's a funny and knowledgeable guy.

Dr. Jang is an amazing professor. He's funny, cares about his students, and is extremely knowledgeable about the topics in the class. You learn a lot and the tests are questions straight from the homework. Take this class with Dr. Jang!!!

As a non-MSE major, I was hesitant to take this for my engineering elective but it was probably the lowest stress class I took all semester. Your entire grade is based on 4 exams for which he basically gives you homework identical to it and other than that, he's just such a friendly and funny person. Definitely recommend!
easiest class I've ever taken at tech - he explains the concepts really well and exam questions are directly from the homework. show up to class and you'll get an easy A

Prof. Jang is a very welcoming professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. The lectures will take some effort, as he presents a lot of information, but the engaged student should find this class an easy and informative experience.

Very knowledgeable and clearly cares about both the content and his students. It is nice to take a class with a professor who is genuinely invested in what he teaches, he's clearly always thinking about stat mech. Office hours are especially helpful. He'll start from the beginning and walk through concepts step by step.

Very knowledgable and accessible. The material for PCHEM is definitely challenging and you'll want to have a strong chem foundation before you start, but I found it easy to stay engaged and interested. He was always willing to answer questions and schedule extra office hours. Clearly explained what was on exams and I always had plenty of time.

He's really nice, but the material in this class is super hard. If you're an engineering student; I would not recommend it as it is extremely concept heavy and not really that pertinent to actual engineering. However, he was always attentive at office hours, scheduled extra when asked, and was very understanding about test dates and moving them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've ever had. No bad in lectures but gives insanely hard homework assignments and when you go to his office to ask for help, he will refuse and then laugh in your face. Office hours are not helpful either. Everyone does so badly that 50% is passing, and many people still won't make the cut. It's a miracle I passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best teacher at Georgia Tech. He really cares for you as a student he makes sure that you understand the content. He is very accommodating and wants you to succeed at GT highly recommend.
He is amazing. Two open note exams with a study guide he provides. Cases which he does cold call on people but very nice. He was honestly the goat.
Dude is goated. Trust. Exams open note and ez

One of the best professors I have had. Although lectures may sometimes be a bit boring, he explains things very clearly and posts all the lecture slides. Tests are open notes and you only have to do 10 homework assignments total, with 30ish homework opportunities. Final is optional if you go to every class after the second midterm. GOATED.

Professor Liu is genuinely the best teacher I have ever had. He is so kind, caring, and accommodating with his students. He is also very passionate about law and tries his best to engage the class. Only 2 midterms, both are open note, and the an option of extra time. I would 100% take his class again. Literally cannot emphasize how amazing he is.

Seriously one of the best professors GT has. 2 tests, open note (he also provides notes you can bring). Optional final exam that can't hurt your grade. He seriously cares for his students, like if you are swamped with exams in a week just let him know and he will let you reschedule your exam for another date. 10/10 prof, TAKE HIM YOU WONT REGRET IT

Great guy! Minimal effort required on your part, provided the notes to use for all open note exams. The in class participation was getting called on one time to explain the case study you did (they were barely a page long). Tried to accommodate everyone, answered any questions even at 2am! Final was optional if you went to class in the last weeks

Brilliant professor! Professor Liu is one of those professors Tech is lucky to have. His expertise and knowledge of law truly shows he could be anywhere else. The structure of the course is amazing and even though overall attendance is not really mandatory, I still went to almost every lecture because I just enjoyed everything about the course!

SWEETEST PROF EVER! take him for legal! super passionate abt law and caring for students. no time limit on exams, exams are open-note, and attendance not mandatory (can join via zoom). very nice cool guy as well.
Professor Liu is one of the most engaging professors I've taken so far. Class is very easy, just lots of reading for assigned cases and pre-exam review. Lectures are very engaging and fun.

Genuinely the best prof at Tech! He actually cares about his students. There are 2 exams, 10 in-class assignments (graded by completion), 10 pre-class assignments (also completion), and an optional final. Exams are open note and unlimited time.

Jerry Liu is the best professor at GT! He allows notes on exams and provides a detailed study guide. He is also always accessible and provides help. His lectures are entertaining and engaging. Attendance is not required until after the second exam, if you'd like to skip the final. Overall, a great professor and person!
Very helpful and clear on what needs to be done, and allows notes on exams

Jerry Liu is the best Legal Aspects professor at GT! His lectures are content-heavy but broken up with group assignments. You write 10 case briefs (AI collaboration allowed), exams are straight forward with generous study guides, and you can skip the final if you do well on the first two. Highly recommend!

Jerry Liu is literally my GOAT. By far my favorite professor I've had in college—and honestly one of my top teachers ever. His lectures are great thanks to his expertise, and his personality makes them kinda funny. From attendance to exams to student interactions, it's clear he truly cares. Wish I had more space to yap abt why I like this guy sm.

Professor Liu was a very fun teacher. He loves to talk with his students and really engage them in the lectures overall. There are a certain amount of required assignments throughout the semester so class attendance is highly encouraged. You can also exempt your final if your attendance is strong enough. Make sure to understand the study guide.

She assigns readings to look over for about every other class, but you only have to skim them and pay attention in lecture to have an understanding of what's going on. Assignment requirements are communicated clearly and the TA's and Roberts give good feedback, so it's easy to do well on assignments and get an A in the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If I am being honest, the class was okay. I wasn't always excited, but she was very nice and clear with grading. A lot of unnecessary reading. I never read any of the readings and did fine. I would recommend that you all take her if you want an A. The group project wasn't too bad, but you wont be able to just coast your way through.
Prof Roberts is very reasonable and kind. Class reqs are very straightforward and as long as you do your work, you will be fine.

I expected it to have lighter work than it did but honestly it is worth it for a chill CS class. Lectures are a bit dull but there were a few class activities that I enjoyed. The class is mostly a semester long project that you work alongside a team. There is one midterm and a presentation of the project.

The class itself isn't difficult, but she is an incredibly dry lecturer and it's difficult to pay attention to how she rambles in monotone. Also, grading criteria is not clear at all; despite how easy the homeworks are, it's equally easy to lose points on something not previously mentioned in the directions. Would suggest the other Ed Tech prof.
Pretty solid class, engaging lecturer. Not much to say, you just do a group project about designing an educational technology.

Prof Roberts's Ed Tech class was wonderful. You'll learn a lot during lecture, and she really engages students. The class is what you make of it—if you apply yourself and are passionate about the group project topic, then you will really enjoy it. There is a good bit of writing, which is to be expected. Great class overall!

Teaching-wise, she is great. Very driven and motivated about ed tech. The structure of the class however wasn't ideal and kinda messy.  We would have weekly assignments and not get grades back for months which was frustrating especially since grp projects build off each other. Also this class did not need mandatory attendance smh. super easy tho!!!

Professor Roberts is passionate about her work and her lectures are engaging, but she gives grades for assignments so late that due date for the next assignment has long passed. I and some of my friends have gotten 70s and 80s on assignments with 3-5 words of feedback, but this might depend on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Roberts is one of my fav profs I've ever had. She is kind, respected, and respectful. Her class does require some long paper/essays but they're never TOO difficult, and we never had exams! She makes class engaging and interactive, which I liked a lot. She loves this course and teaching; I would definitely recommend her.

Professor Roberts is a wonderful and inspirational professor. I would definitely take her class again! She really cares about ed tech and her passion for the field really shines through her teaching. If you can take a class with her, do it! You wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jeff is great. Grand Challenges is really easy as a course but he's really approachable. Tuesday is usually lecture day and Thursday is team meeting day. The lecture days can be really boring but he has a lot of wisdom to share. As a freshman, he's the professor that knew me best and wrote my recommendation letter.
Jeff is so nice! He really is passionate about GC and is rooting for your team.
He was really nice and gave pretty food feedback. His lectures were kind of boring and long but other than that everything was pretty easy.
Very caring and understanding, class is not mandatory but if you attend he won't forgot your name because he's so nice. Projects are very long depending on how many bugs you have though.

Genuinely might be the best professor I have ever had. He offers great feedback on the labs and presents the content of the class in an interesting manor. The labs can be a little tough but there are plenty of resources to help you get through them, there is also a bit a leniency in the deadlines. Highly recommend taking 2036 with Dr. Davis.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Favorite professor I've had at GT. Very apparent in his passion for this subject and teaching. Very understanding for projects and gave extensions if needed. The projects were also fun and were effective at teaching class content. Exams were tough and few so it is admittedly difficult to do well in the class, but I thoroughly enjoyed the class.

Professor Davis cares a lot about his students and is the most understanding professor I have had. He always gives students more than enough time to complete the labs, releases a lot of practice tests for each exam, and has a youtube playlist with condensed lectures so you don't have to actually go to class. Just communicate well with him!

Really nice professor who cares about his students' wellbeing and responds really quickly to emails. Got sick before a project was due and he gave an extension after I explained my situation. Really appreciate having him as my teacher, would take his class again.

Professor Davis is great. His lectures are clear and focus on examples and code instead of reading off powerpoint. The lab assignments are relevant to the course and always introduced something interesting. He definitely cares about students and tries to be understanding of circumstances.
Took him for his Grand Challenges class, gives good feedback, clear and concise in his advice. Would recommened.

I've taken Davis, and he is one of the toughest professor I've met. He doesn't curve the tests. I studied 1 week and a half in advance for the test, and final exam but still couldn't make it. 2 tests, 1st one is 20% and end one is 25%. He does provide old tests but they don't help much. No quizzes. 6 challenging coding projects. Not recommended.

There's so much work for this class. He will set you up for success later in your degree. His grading seems harsh, but note that 30-40% of the class will end up with an A with points back. Understand the homework, the test questions are very similar. Not as mean as in 2611. Take him to learn.
dude doesnt understand what 1 credit means

Please just don't. He fully yells at students for not finding their groups within -0.00002 seconds. He nitpicks every single point on rubrics, and grades strictly enough that this class can take 5+ hours a week. 2611 isn't supposed to be hard, he makes it a complete pain and time sink. Take with someone else, I beg of thee.

He can be a little scary in class because he calls you out for little things. I don't enjoy going to class because he gets mad at people when they're late and highlights people's errors in front of the whole class, but attendance is mandatory (and he will figure out if you're missing it). The class is at least very easy.

Not lenient or understanding at all, rude and will call you out for the smallest things in front of the entire class. Would've been a straightforward and enjoyable class, if he wasn't teaching it. Super nitpicky, will find something wrong with your work for even the simplest assignments.
rude, will call people out in front of entire class

Too much work for a one credit hour class. Yells at students. You can never do anything right type of professor. Will always find an issue with something you're doing and loudly announce it. You will learn, and he's effective at making his students learn. But you will not enjoy taking his class.

I took Professor Seitzman during Summer 2025. One of the best professor's I've taken at Tech. AE 4451 is not an easy course to take in 5 weeks, and his homeworks are tough and challenging, but his style of teaching is awesome. I suggest for anyone who wants to go into propulsion, to take him.

Dr. Seitzman is the most intelligent and quick-witted professor I have ever met. He has transformed my engineering intuition for the better and I am grateful to have had a class with him. Although sassy, he wants to help you understand the concepts. Homework and exams are tough but if you put in the effort to go to office hours, you will be fine.

Seitzman is a fantastic professor! His lectures were very clear, helpful, and engaging. He gets that AE 2010 is a hard class, and he is happy to re-explain concepts as many times and as many ways as you need so that you get a better understanding both during class and outside of it.

Took his 4451 class over the summer in Limerick and it was one of the hardest classes I've taken. That said, if you like Jet Propulsion there is no class at Tech that will give you a better foundation in it than Seitzman's class. Study up and buddy up for the homeworks, and give yourself time to do the final project. It's hard but valuable.

Probably the best class I've taken. Seitzman is a very good lecturer, but has high expectations, as the homeworks and tests are difficult. If you aren't interested in the subject and just want an easy A, do not take Seitzman, but if you want to learn he's probably the best professor in the department. Go to office hours, hardass about extensions.

The content of the course was not very difficult but Dr. Seitzman's harsh grading forces us to put triple the effort in mastering the content compared to other grad courses. This is not the typical course where you can get an A and come out still not knowing concepts, our final was like a summer packet covering every single conceptual question.

The subject matter is tough, there's no getting around that and Professor Seitzman holds his students to high standards. At the same time, he really cares about his students' understanding and is willing to put in the effort to help anyone who is willing to learn. One of the best taught classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures were 2 hours and I was locked in the whole time. Can't recommend him enough if you actually care about the content.

Dr. Seitzman is one of the best professors at Tech, and his classes are extremely challenging. I struggled on some of the homeworks, and he actually EMAILED ME and encouraged me to ask him for help if needed. I've never had a professor in college go out of their way to do that. It will be hard, but I recommend taking him if you get the chance.

The hardest class I've taken at Tech, but the one I've learned the most from. I did this during the Limerick program, so it was a lot of information and tough homework with short turnaround. The homework took up most of my weekdays, but Dr. Seitzman is a great teacher who will really help you get all the theory and math through your head.

Professor Seitzman might be the smartest person alive. He will not go easy on you but you will for sure learn the material. I recommend taking Jet Pro with him for anybody who wishes to go into propulsion. There will be a lot of work and struggling but the lessons are invaluable. Make sure you go into jet pro with adequate thermo knowledge.

Took AE4451 with Seitzman abroad in 5 weeks, and although tough like his AE2010 class, he sets clear expectations for success and is an outstanding lecturer. He is flexible when scheduling meetings outside class and does a good job of guiding you to answers. High effort yields excellent learning, and I highly recommend taking any AE class with him.

Class once a week for 50 minutes. Spent 1hr on hw a week. In-class assignments are easy, however, there were a lot of them and you have to keep track as each one counts for your final grade. Just complete your assignments, 15 min a piece, and you will get an A. A good professor who gives good advice, although he can be blunt sometimes. Recommended.

Dr. Seitzman is clearly very smart and knows what he's doing. However, he took this 1-credit class way too seriously, and would yell at and sometimes even bark (woof woof) at students. Especially at the start of the year, the grading was very harsh, and it made this class so much more work than it should've been.

Seitzman not a good professor. He consistently yelled at his students and even barked at them a couple times in an effort to get them quiet. He gave too many assignments for a one-credit course. He would put students into groups during class then yell at them when they couldn't find their group even though it was a 200 person lecture.

Prof. Seitzman is not easy. Going to lecture is not required, but not attending only hurts you because Seitzman usually gives important comments that go along with his lecture slides. Ditto other comments on the homework sets: they are long, difficult, and intended for you use notes. Seitzman will challenge you and hammer in concepts.

This course is super interesting, especially due to Dr. Seitzman's expertise and enthusiasm. Seitzman's method involves absolutely hammering the course material into your brain with difficult homework sets; you can expect to spend around eight hours on each of them (around 5 problems). Beyond this, exams are difficult, but open-book/notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seitzman does not have set office hours, creates extremely hard homeworks that even upperclass student tutors cannot solve, is somewhat degrading when questions are asked or when offering help. Homeworks are not graded in a timely manner and solutions to past homeworks arent given on time before each exam. Please avoid this professor.

Professor Seitzman gives relatively good lectures. He asks lots of questions and is sympathetic toward students. However, his homework is incredibly challenging and does not include values students need to solve the problems (it is assumed we will look this up) with class hw averages around a C.

Professor Seitzman is the best professor I have had at Tech. He understands what it's like to be completely confused and is extremely patient. He asks many questions in lecture to keep you engaged. GO TO OA for topics you are struggling with. Trust me. He will grill you, but toughen up because you will leave a smarter person and a better engineer.

Taking Dr. Seitzman for AE 2010 turned out to be a HUGE mistake. Toward the end of the semester, I had a family emergency arise & to say that Dr. Seitzman was unaccommodating is a huge understatement. Challenging classes & professors are expected at Tech, but I have never had a prof who didn't publish exam keys & whose feedback on tests & HW was NA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor! He will really challenge you and make sure you know your stuff. If you don't he will really nail it home. Definitely makes you work for an A but it is well worth the effort.

2611 is a stupid easy class. Go to lecture, do the assignments, get the A. Seitzman doesn't complicate it, and does present the material in a more enjoyable manner than most prof would. I appreciated his simplicity and the laid back approach to the class.

Dr. Seitzman has very high expectations for his students. He is very particular and makes sure that everything you say is precisely true. He requires a thorough understanding of concepts and assumptions. He was a very valuable teacher for putting you in a solid engineering mindset. Not an easy A, but possible with hard work.

Dr. Seitzman is by far my favorite professor at Tech. I've taken him for a couple of classes, most recently 6450. His lectures are interesting and relevant, and he tries (and succeeds) to make the material really applicable to the real world. His homeworks are time consuming but helpful, and tests are not easy, but straightforward.

Seitzman is a great professor, he is very knowledgeable and great at conveying information in a way students can understand and learn. He can badger you sometimes, especially in office hours, but he does a good job at breaking down the concepts and is very helpful during office hours. Homework are very insightful and greatly facilitate learning
Great professor. Popcorns a bit in class and can come across as intimidating, but very helpful and accessible. Good lectures, fair homework, fun class.   Great hottiness.

Seitzman is heavily involved administratively, academically, and and professionally (through research) with the AE department. Will guide students, but won't hold their hand. Be prepared to show you are working hard and creatively. Straightforeward, accessible, and a little intimidating.
Good

Dr. Sietzman is very enthusiastic. Be prepared to interact because he's big on participation. If you don't read this class will suck. You also NEED to have the pre-recs otherwise you won't be able to understand what's going on. His exams are heavily weighted on conceptual knowledge learned through homeworks. Be prepared to work 40hrs/wk.

Seitzman is a great professor. He's excited about the material and genuinely wants his students to understand the material. Homeworks are time intensive (about 40 hours a week) but the class is great! If you put in the effort you'll know your stuff for sure. Exams are based on conceptual knowledge of coursework and hw.
Not helpful for me at all.
Whenever you have a chance take Dr.Seitzman, do it! He's really amazing, like him so much!
His class isn't super-easy, but he's very helpful, particularly if you drop by his office to ask questions.

Dr. Seitzman is an amazing! He really tries to make students grasp the concept and develops an intuition on the subject which is very essential in eng. He is a good sense of humor. He is very helpful during his office hours and don't be scared to ask question in class. Try to understand every concept he teaches in class and exams should be fair.
Good professor who has a heavy emphasis on class participation. Homeworks are difficult, but cover material in the lectures. Midterm and final were fair.
He is a great lecturer. Teaches things very well. He makes you work hard but he wants you to succeed. He does not want you to suffer.

Dr. Luo was a great fluids professor. Lectures are a bit boring, but he explains the content well and does plenty of examples. He basically tells you the exact questions that will be tested, and they are very similar to the example problems. You get a one-sided crib sheets on exams. Homework is on Wileyplus, so it's easy to get full credit.

He was a really good professor. As long as you show up to class and take the notes you'll get a good grade. No surprises on exams and always similar to the practice exam or homework questions, wants you to get a good grade. A lot of people say to take Fritz over him but Luo explains the content way more and is just as lenient of a grader.

Took his Porous Media class. He is a very nice professor and helps you learn the material very well. Some lectures were a bit confusing along with the topics, but that's always normal. No exams which was a plus and the final project was easy, but also actually helped you learn many concepts.

Lectures were really straight forward and easy to follow. He explains stuff well so as long as you pay attention in class and understand the homework you won't have a problem. The grade is 90% exams but the exams are very fair and he prepares you for them. The final is optional if you're okay with your three midterm grades.

Hes okay not great not bad. It is 90% tests and he only grades out of 30 points so one messup on each problem (3) puts you at a 90. The material is hard but he does a decent job at explaining. Also the final is optional
Online fluid flow through porous media class. Not worth the time.

The other professor (fritz) is an easier grader but this guy does a better job at explaining. CEE3040 is quite easy. Exams aren't too bad except 4 the occasional trick question. He does practice problems in class and his reviews can be helpful. You'll fall asleep in class if you dont pay attention. He gives proofs of the theorems if u're interested

If you go to lecture and follow his example problems you'll be fine. At the beginning of lecture he reviews the important parts from the previous lecture which is helpful. Tests aren't super easy but his curve is so generous that it doesn't matter too much. Overall a very reasonable professor! Need a WileyPLUS account, that's the only downside

Favorite teacher at Tech so far. Extremely straightforward, very streamlined class. Lecture was super structured and always useful. Every lecture he reviews last class, explains new theory, and works a couple examples that are just like the homework. The tests are very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lecture examples are very similar to his exam questions. Won't give you or teach you ridiculously challenging things that you probably won't use in the future. He pretty much teach you everything, the basics of them, that you need out of this class. Tests are a little hard if you don't study his lecture examples, since there's no sample test.

The guy does have a thick accent but he explains very well. Also he reviews everything that he teaches the class after he explains a topic. He curves, which makes it easier to get a good grade in a test. He is a good teacher. If you do the homework, you will be fine.
Very thick accent, hard to understand. His grading system gives the top 50% an A or B, but the hard subject matter is not taught very well.

I absolutely loved taking this class, I learned so much and Dr. Jordan made the class very interesting and engaging. The readings are quite long and pretty dense. The final exam was take home and there was a simulation at the end of the semester. I would 100% take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Jordan and this class! She cares so much about her students and is always willing to work with you if you need help. 100% recommend!

One of the most caring professors I've had here. As a STEM major, I was still super interested in her lectures and she did her best to make them that way. She does assign a ton of reading, at least compared to all the engineering classes, so don't slack on reading. Also does grade on participation, but as long as you come to class you're fine.
She's amazing

Dr. Jordan is super cool. She is very knowledgable and passionate, but heavy on the readings. However, I almost never read and still was successful in the class. This class was very lecture heavy. Almost everyday was show up and take notes based off her PowerPoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love her - so fun, so knowledgable, and so cool. Definitely knows her stuff. However, there are a ton of readings that she expects you to have understood passionately and there are like 6 grades for the whole semester. Overall, love her but her class has been a stress monster.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Jordan ROCKS. Her lectures are so interesting and I am not even an inta major! Try to do the reading as much as possible, but she normally drops hints the class before she gives a "pop" quiz. Her tests are not very difficult as long as you pay attention in class. Also if you need to skip you definitely can because she posts the powerpoint online.

She thinks that everyone who takes her classes are INTA majors and caters her lectures only to them. The lectures are long and boring and directly read from ppt slides. Expect several readings before every class. Tests are very challenging and cover very nit picky details from the readings and movies. Don't takeif you are looking for an easy A/B/C

LOVE her. She's hilarious and has engaging lectures. I'm not at all interested in the topic but I thoroughly enjoyed the class due to her teaching. Tests are easy but studying for each can be overwhelming because there is A LOT of info for each (only 2 tests, each covering copious amounts of info). She's very understanding. I would take this again.

She's funny and her lectures are interesting. Tests are easy if you study the powerpoints and do the readings. Does pop quizzes on readings at the beginning of class so go to class. Super-easy grader on the paper.

Loved this class! However, it is pretty tough for an introductory course. Read all readings thoroughly as she gives random reading quizzes. Tests and quizzes can be pretty detail-oriented. Dr. Jordan is probably one of the best teachers at Tech! She knows the material very well and her lectures are always interesting! Plus she has killer style.

She gives tough tests and can sometimes assign a lot of reading. However, Dr. Jordan is extremely knowledgeable (especially in terrorism!) and really makes sure you know the stuff. She's a fairly good lecturer. Also, she is SO cool outside of class. I would make sure to talk to her beforeafter class and go to office hours so she gets to know you.

Engaging lectures, attendance isn't required but there are pop quizzes and you'll need to take good notes to get an A.  She's not the best at designing tests but they aren't too difficult and it's easy to do well if you put the time in.

Dr. Jordan is very engaging lecturer. The class really isn't that hard. There are 2 tests and you get study guides for them. Study the study guides and you'll be fine. There is a lot of reading, but it's interesting reading, so its not so bad. Also, there are a few reading quizzes, so make sure you at least skim the reading  assignments.

There wasn't a day when I didn't look forward to her class. It was entertaining, enlightening, and just hard enough to ensure that you had to do some studying. Right  in the sweet spot between easy A and working for your A. Would definitely take her class again, and will be taking her higher level classes in the future.

She's truly is a great teacher. Sometimes there's really long readings assigned, but as long as you get the main idea you'll be fine. She is really passionate about what she teaches and has a great personality. Easy to talk to, too!

She's amazing and you can tell that she knows what she's talking about. She's super nice and an expert in her field as well. A lot engineers at GT hate on her because they hate anything non-relating to STEM (and she assigns readings relating to International Affairs which obv. isn't STEM) so be sure to evaluate the criticism through that lens.

After changing my major, I was skeptical about whether I chose correctly. Her intro class made me realize I made the right choice. She is so very helpful and her lectures are very informative. There is a handful of reading, but as long as you read and go to class, this class will be a lot of fun. Again, she's freaking awesome.

While I was unsure of my major heading into this class, her teaching and the subject as a whole convinced me to actually head into the subject. He teaching was incredibly helpful, and the class was interesting and easy enough if you complete the assigned readings and pay attention at all in class.

Interesting subject and professor is very enthusiastic. However, there is a lot of reading involved and you have to read for random quizzes she gives during class. Only take the class if you enjoy INTA-related subjects/topics.
Professor Jordan is awesome, and she really cares about the subject, and you can tell that she enjoys teaching. She was extremely helpful and accessible.
Her class was amazing! There's a lot of reading but it is usually interesting and lectures are part lecture/part discussion. We just had a midterm, final, and group project. Great class so far !

Class is very fast paced and you can fall behind very easily. Doesn't post lecture videos for whatever reason (even though attendance is mandatory?). Her grading and syllabus are harsh, but she cares about students and is willing to help if you go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Big time commitment for this class but it is not insanely difficult. If you go to class it is very manageable and any questions can be answered in office hours. Class is five big software assignments with a final group project/presentation that is very simple. Do not fall behind otherwise you will struggle to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wen does not respond to emails asking for help, not flexible with students, lectures on exercises loosely related to the assignment but does not provide instructions on how to repeat the work. Class and grading overall can be frustrating because instructors will say something in class and then directly contradict that statement when grading.

The professor was friendly towards students and accessible. Lecture content straight from the textbook, so I ended up skipping almost all the classes. Homework & Exam questions from the textbook. The only problem was the grader, who would deduct points for solutions that were more descriptive than those in the textbook. Curves median (74) to B.

The course was quite challenging at first, and at times I couldn't fully understand. However, the professor's office hours were quite helpful. He was effective at breaking down questions and explaining concepts clearly, which genuinely increased my interest in the subject. He was also supportive to students, and grading was fair and generous.

Decent professor but reads straight from the textbook (Axler) during lectures. Doesn't really provide ample motivation for the reasons behind proofs which makes the lectures extremely dry. Goes at a decently fast pace which doesn't help either as the demotivating portions are essential to the interesting segments.

Professor essentially just read off textbook to us(Axler). There isn't much you'd get from lecture you couldn't get from reading the textbook.Grading felt unreasonable as I never recieved any feedback as to why I lost points.

His first time teaching the class. The content was quite hard and abstract, as was the homework. But after taking his course, I feel that I've learned how to self-study proofs and have improved my mathematical proof-writing.

Professor is not the most experienced lecturer, sometimes skipping over crucial topics and proofs for sake of time, as well as sometimes creating a enviroment that is not conducive to learning. Grading is fair and straight forward, though tests account for 75% of the grade. Overall just an ehh professor, nothing too notable.

Lectures were ok, he went slow enough for students to understand concepts, but in general sometimes hes not that good at explaining things. When you ask him outside of class about a problem, theres a high chance you might still not understand. But he's nice and going to recitation will help you understand what happened in class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her online 3401 class (couldn't select). She will take off points if you say a wrong fact in essays and hw, so you result in saying less. She assigns 6-20 page readings before each class. I'm very glad we had 0 tests. Lectures can be boring but also fun at times as she is very into what she is teaching. Overall I'm glad I took the class.

She is super kind and cares about her students. One of the few professors who actually goes through homework and gives feedback. Do the readings and you'll be fine. She values class participation and will call on you in class to share your homework responses if she likes your insight. Overall she is sweet professor who is passionate about teaching.

DO NOT take her any class. She's so mean and very intuitive grading style. Every time you had to read a lot for hw before the class, and she pretty likes to extend the class time for like around 15min. IF you take hers class, get ready for worrying about your letter grade every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
She's amazing!! So kind and caring. Prepare to be called on, I usually got called on around 5-10x per class, but it really made me more comfortable speaking in Chinese. As long as you're passionate and willing to put in work, you will do absolutely fine with her. 

I took CHIN 1002, but I couldn't figure out how to click a different class code.
Do not take this course with her

Very caring professor - relaxed some essay requirements due to COVID Is pretty chill in class, but not afraid to ROAST you (or well I guess challenge your beliefs in class discussion) very knowledgeable, you can tell she loves to learn every day not too much homework! Can't believe I can say that for a class here at Tech... I recommend.

Professor Liu is an amazing lecturer, always enthusiastic and ready to challenge you with the course material. Also always down to roast a student so be prepared for some razor sharp wit. If you have the chance to take a class with her, don't hesitate.
Really kind and knowledgeable professor!

Best professor I have had at GT. Period. Classes are interesting, she's cute as a button, and always more than willing to work with you after class. Not too much homework per unit, and I actually come out of it for the better having learnt something. If you're taking Chinese at GT DEFINITELY choose Liu Laoshi.

There's not a lot of homework and they are pretty easy. Her tests are very fair, so it is not hard to get an A if you show up and pay attention. Her lectures can pretty boring, but she posts slides and attendance isn't mandatory.

A great professor who made statistics fun. Grading is mainly 3 midterm exams (non cumulative) 25% each, all multiple choice and a final project (20%). Also weekly HW. You're allowed to bring formula sheets. Very helpful practice tests and HW questions. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and it was very very easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, easy A. Do not have to go to lecture to understand what is going on. All tests are multiple choice.
Slurs his words and goes too fast, and the content is paced horribly. He seems nice and passionate about what he teaches, but sacrifices clarity for it.

Josh is overall a great teacher. He's super helpful, but his explainations of this can be a little rushed and sometimes not make sense, but just ask to clarify and he'll be glad to help. Only issue with this class is the grading scheme. 30% for each test and 10% for homework, so one bad test means you're likely to get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take this class if you have a friend who has already taken it, very similar semester to semester. You are allowed a cheat sheet front and back for each exam and 3 cheat sheets for the final. Lectures don't help and randomly hard questions on exam. Put practice questions on your cheat sheet and you will be fine. Homework is fine, 5 questions each.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this professor. He claims exams mirror practice problems, yet the exams have harder integrals and methodologies than all of my math classes. Cheat sheets are nice, but you have no clue what is coming for the exam since the practice is nothing like it, so they end up not helping. Take a different professor or tank your gpa.

Overall monotone, boring class where you don't learn much. Fairly difficult exams and super fast paced lectures where only 1 type of every question is taught. In the end you have to know how to do so many types of problems. Only saving grace were the cheat sheets. An A will take significant effort. Take harry sharp if you can instead.

Josh cares very deeply about his syllabus. He talks too fast; I can't imagine taking this class as a non-native English speaker because of how much he slurs his words. 90% exams, no remediation opportunities. Course was managed inefficiently; less than 15 students attending lectures halfway thru;  Josh would make passive aggressive comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 exams, 10 HW's, and a final. He's super nice, always willing to answer questions after class and very helpful during office hours. Lectures can be a bit boring as he just reads off of slides. Very light class, 1 HW a week that takes 2-3 hours. Pay attention in lecture, do the HW, and study the weekend before the exam and you'll do great.

Super black and white class, no way around it. Tests are mirrored from in class examples. HW's are easy. Felt like high school class with weekly hw, big tests, and simple teaching. Do a bit of work and you'll get an A. Not difficult but not free

Pretty straightforward class, tests were predictable and basically mirrored in class examples, but with different values/functions. Lectures were just reading off slides, but he tells you what specific examples will show up on the test, as compared to the basic announcement he makes on Canvas. Overall solid professor, gives good partial credit.

Very straightforward professor and class - no secrets. Similar to a high school class, weekly homeworks, pretty simple, boring material to get through. Exams are pretty easy and just based on the homework/practice problems. Class doesn't take much time in general and lectures aren't worth attending - he more or less just reads the slides.

Nice guy, but really just reads off lecture slides. Lectures are pretty tedious, especially for an 8 AM section. Class is pretty straightforward, do HW and read up on your notes, a B should be guaranteed. An A will take more work outside of classwork, but he gives out practice exams and examples generously.

Very nice and caring professor! Lectures were boring and confusing at times, but he is very responsive over email if you have questions. Exams are 90% of grade, so that is stressful but he provides lots of extra practice problems.

Josh is a person who cares about what he teaches and his students. On the flip side, he talks too fast to where it's hard to understand him at times and his class can be passed essentially by self-teaching yourself the material via the notes he uploads. The class is test heavy (3 tests - 90% total), and his lectures were monotonous and boring imo.
talks very very fast, reads straight off of old slides, a bit hard to understand. however, he is very caring and answers questions very well. tests are also each 30%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a CS major with a really tough course load, this class was very doable. The tests were worth most of your grade, but the test format, questions, and grading were all very fair. He's also easy to reach and pretty understanding which I really appreciated.

His lectures were really thorough because he always provided examples alongside the formulas which really helped with homework and tests. Homeworks were assigned weekly, and they were based off of lecture notes so that was nice. Exams made up 90% of your grade, but they weren't too bad as long as you studied and were familiar with lecture material.

^^^ agreed with previous comment Prof. McDonald is the definition of a homie Pretty easy class if you show up to lecture and take good notes take advantage of cheat sheets because this class heavily relies on applying formulas josh is super accessible via email and i always got the vibe that he was happy to help with any questions <3

Josh is a goat. He's super chill with the class and treats his students with respect. His tests were fairly easy and felt like AP stats. I highly recommend this prof for any CS majors trying to get that stats credit.
great professor. be prepared to put a lot of work in.

Dr. Lau is very nice and he is very strict about lateness. His class is easy and he does not throughly critique your work. It was hard to care by the end of the semester because I had a high A. Just do the work and you'll be fine

Dr. Lau is a very caring professor. He wants you to succeed. He wants you to learn something from 2310 that will help you in a future internship or class. Sometimes, he can put forward ideas that are outside the scope of the class, but he wants you to benefit and grow. He is strict about attendance.

Dr. Lau is a super nice and helpful teacher. He really cares about students. He is a stickler about few things so just show up to class on time and put in effort and thats all he cares about. The class can be annoying but do the work and its a good experience.

No matter which professor you're with, I think that BMED 1000 is stressful, especially as a 1 cr. class. However, Dr. Lau made it easier to know what we were doing and WHY we were doing it. Taking his course was an enlightening experience, as he possesses extensive knowledge in the subject matter and a passion for teaching that is truly inspiring.

Opened class with dad jokes, overall made the lectures very light-hearted and enjoyable. Explanation of content was fantastic, exams were of reasonable difficulty, and homework was not overbearing. Very easy to balance with other courses.

Amazing teacher, starts classes with jokes to ease you in and good at lecturing. Tests resemble homework closely and plenty of study resources are available. Heavy emphasis on tests, but standard for a gt math class

really funny guy, and really good professor. his notes were really helpful and his lectures even more so. took him for math 2551, and was really easy. if you see him in oscar, try to get him as a prof
Good professor who explained things well. He had the class decide on what QED symbol to use in class every lecture which was fun.

Great math professor. Exams are standardized but he prepares you well. He really cares about each of his students and wants them to reach out for help. He always has flexible office hours to make sure everyone can access him.

Stucky is the GOAT. I failed calculus 3 times before I took his class. He helped me work through the deficiencies in my mathematical skills and helped me learn to become better student. He would always answer emails from me and other students and genuinely cares about the people he teaches. His jokes make lectures fun. Thanks Stucky!

Dr. Stucky made Integral Calculus much less difficult to get through with his dad jokes and humorous personality.  For the most part he explains everything pretty well, although he would skip through a good bit of algebra related steps which I found annoying.  Overall Dr. Stucky is a great teacher to take 1552 with

Integral calculus will always be difficult. Took this course my first semester of college and it was definitely a struggle. Stucky made it super easy to learn and follow; lectures consisted of lots of practice problems. Tests questions were a step harder than practice examples, but study hard and you will manage to do well. Just put in the effort.

Dr. Stucky is a fantastic lecturer! He is very knowledgeable in math, and it shows through his explanations of challenging problems. Integral calculus is a challenging class, and you will struggle. HOWEVER, Dr. Stucky helps alleviate the pain of this class with in-depth solutions and guided notes. Plus, you get daily jokes!

Dr. Stucky is a nice guy overall and he tries to make lectures fun with jokes. However, he tends to skip through steps during problems which can be difficult for students who have a certain way of thinking. He is hard to get ahold of through email especially if it is regarding exams. I had to email the course coordinator because he never answered.
Reminds me of my absent father:)

Dr. Stucky is a funny guy and his dad jokes make lectures fun. His lectures can be difficult to follow because he skips many algebra and precalc steps in his problem solving. He's a nice guy and lecturer, but I did find myself watching the recorded course-coordinator lectures to understand important concepts.

Stucky is the kind of professor who says "I was just testing you" every time he makes a mistake. The course at GT is limiting to people with accommodations (must get special permission to take exams at testing center, no excused absences even for religious reasons, etc) but there's room in the syllabus for error so it doesn't affect your grade much

He's nice and the dad jokes definitely make lectures more entertaining, but he consistently skips steps when solving problems in class. Which can get pretty confusing very quickly. If you're confident in your algebra and pre-calc knowledge then you'll be fine, but if not you should take someone else.

Chill Prof. Says lots of dad jokes during lectures and always try to get his students to laugh. He is honestly a really respectful and down to earth guy that will never hesitate to help you out. The tests are extremely fair, never any curve balls or tricks so long as you study. 10/10 would take again with Stucky.

He also asked very insightful questions like "How do I do Subtraction" and made bold statements when you would try to correct his mistakes like "I have one more PHD than you, so you can shut up." He is awesome.

I took Mr. Stucky at another school. He was without a doubt the best professor that I ever had. No other Professor would admit to his students "I do the math wrong quite often" or "I'm the instructor; I'm always right." He also gave great life advice like "become ungovernable." Yes, he said these things but that made the class awesome.

There isn't enough words to describe just how influential and amazing of a professor Stucky is. He genuinely cares about every students and has a way of teaching that not only makes perfect sense, but is also entertaining.
