reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty boring but the content is interesting. If you memorize the testing slides you will do well.

Grading consists entirely of 5 tests that require you to have memorized some art slides on her presentations. Lectures are SOOOO boring, mind-numbingly boring, make me want to gouge my eyes out boring, but as long as you take some notes you'll pass with flying colors.

suuuper easy. lectures are fairly interesting if you like art, but definitely a bit repetitive & very monotonous. make a quizlet the night before each test, memorize like 15 art pieces by name, artist, year, and movement w/ correct spelling, and an easy a. she's nice - 5 tests, none during finals week.

Easy A class. Dr. Medina gives powerpoint lecture slides of what will be on exams. Study these and you'll pass. It's not an exciting class, and honestly pretty boring, but a good choice for an easy elective.
Literally just memorization. The material is boring but she makes it interesting. If you make a quizlet and go over it repeatedly the day of the test, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her culture of objects class was interesting. The class isn't as easy as chairs or hist of art but it's very doable and straightforward. Your grade consists of 2 take home tests, 2 presentations, weekly homework assignments and participation. Definitely take her homeworks seriously as she'll deduct a lot of points if done incorrectly or lazily.
Lectures aren't that boring if you're genuinely interested in art. Take notes and review them before the test. Tests are entirely memorization, so as long as you study, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her Lectures are so boring, I took it online in the summer & only paid attention when the paintings or sculptures that were going to possibly be on the test. She grades based off of spelling so if you miss spell the word even by one letter then its -2. But her tests are pretty much memorization. remember the name the artist the type of art,location
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: easy A class if you can sit through her lectures. She is incredibly boring but the only grades in the class are tests and attendance. tests are memorization of products/architecture

I thought the content was interesting but friends (sometimes me) would sleep throughout the 2.5 hour lecture. Attendance is mandatory but you could use it as time to catch up on other hw. Tests are straight up rote memorization and easy. Would study two hours the night before and and an hour before the test and easily get an A. (Summer 2017)
Easy A if you show up and are good at memorizing. The content is interesting even though her lectures are monotonous. Overall I would take it again.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at tech. The content is interesting if you have an artistic side, and the tests are easy 100s provided you known "key terms" and memorize the slides she puts up of the important architecture, which isn't hard to do if you give yourself a little time to look over them.

Yes, this class is boring but it is such an easy A that it is totally worth it. Professor Medina is very nice but she does drone on during lecture. Honestly though, you do not need to pay attention (show up for lecture though as attendance counts). Just study the slides the night before and you're pretty much guaranteed at least a B on the test.

She is so easy. It's ridiculous. You don't have to pay attention at all, just show up for attendance and study the test slides she uploads. Just make some flashchards the day before the test. Easiest A ever. It's the best. She's the best.

She is so boring. Just memorize what she tells you to and you'll get an A for sure. The book is a waste of money even at $14. This class is so painful, but worth it for the A. But the way she sets up the class, you have to do well on all the tests to get an A, so don't slack off. Just memorize the monuments.
Awesome teacher!  She is kinda monotone but so much so that its entertaining.  Really good at getting the material across.

Medina was very repetitive, but for a reason: it was on the test.  She's a great professor.  The material is interesting.  She has a monotone voice, but it's better than not being able to understand her.  If you get Word for the exams from a fraternity/soroity, it's a VERY easy A.  Definetly a must take.

I took history of ID for an easy A, but it turned out to be one of the more helpful classes I've taken at Tech. I think any ARCH major who is taking Architecture history 2 should take this class at the same time b/c it is the perfect complement to the curriculum.
I agree with two of the above comments. She repeats the same thing over and over again but easy A class. You can't even sleep because the class is so congested.
VERY EASY CLASS!!! Take if you need an easy A!!! Basic goal get an A on the paper and at least two of the 4 tests and you'll pretty much get an A in the class.

Medina is very repetitive in everything she teaches. The only way to get through her classes without falling asleep is to play Bingo, but instead of numbers, you use her store of phrases: "Phallic reference," "Dynamism," "Linear Perspective," etc.

contrary to what other people say, i really liked and enjoyed her lectures. i think it all depends on if you are actually interested in art history...a lot of people take it as a free elective because they think it's easy.
Boring, repetetive lectures. Tracks attendance; otherwise nobody would show up. Checks spelling on test answers. Grades depend primarily on students' rote-memorization ability.

Definitely not for those trying to learn Arabic. Paced lectures in a way that only heritage speakers understood. Randomly called people out and if you struggled to answer (like most people learning a language), your grade suffered. Had an attitude most of the time. I knew I had to drop the class when I had an anxiety attack before lecture :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Must have experience with arabic in some form or fashion in order to succeed in this class. She was not afraid to call out specific students, and didn't give many resources to actually learn. Textbook was mandatory. She went incredibly fast and it was hard to keep up. She was very passive aggressive when we didn't understand the content.
She was great. The class was online and that made it tough, but she as an instructor was very good and worked with us as we tried to figure out how the class worked
Prof Rupar is a very nice lady, and you can tell she wants her students to do well in her class. She's caring and all of the other reviews are pretty accurate; would def take her again

Professor Rupar was an amazing teacher. Her lectures and Homeworks were educational. Attendence and participation was mandatory since its graded and it is recommended to understand the content. The test were a little challenging but as long as you are comfortable with the homework you will be fine. She provides practice exams to prepare for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really great professor, though accounting can be challenging in general. I finished with a high B, but she rounded it up to an A! Dr. Wang truly cares, so I recommend being active in class, attending her office hours, and seeking help whenever needed to succeed in the course.

She is good at breaking down the concepts, but accounting is a hard class tbh. Her test are MC + FRQ style and get harder as u go. You'll probably feel lost during the first few weeks and this is when it's crucial to study. Really just study after every lecture and it all builds so u should be fine. Build your grade up before the final bc its hard.
Done an amazing job lecturing. The test has lots of extra credits and she's always there if you have any questions. Would recommend her!

She's a very knowledgeable professor, and you can tell she cares about her students doing well in the course. She was always very open to people asking questions during class and was very available for office hours. This course is very complex, and she moves very quickly in class, therefore, it's really easy to fall behind.

Prof Wang is such a kind and caring professor! She really wants everyone in her class to do well. She learns everyone's names and lets us take breaks during her lectures. She always drops at least one question if not more on her exams if she thinks it was unfair. Genuinely cares about her students and would 100% recommend her!

If you are having trouble with something, she will help. She's clear about deadlines but lenient if you have a good reason.. Her projects and homework are very straightforward, but there are a lot of terms that can be difficult to remember. She'll help you either way if you're struggling though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring professor who wants everyone to succeed. If a lot of people miss questions on the exams, she takes those questions out and gives points back. She learns students' names and happily answers all questions. Lectures were kinda heavy but she would give us breaks in between with clips of a TV show. Also gives in class time for the project.

Great professor! Takes the time to learn everyone's name & tries to explain accounting in the easiest way possible. We are given a monopoly project in place of one exam, the project isn't structured the best, but its manageable. Very caring, and wants you to understand the subject. Love that she records extra lectures in case you miss.
Lectures are very fast paced but she is a very caring professor who takes care of her students
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy to manage class, there was a group project to supplement midterm grades and a lot of extra credit on exams. She prints out all of the slides which was a lot of paper and could get annoying to keep track of.
She is extremely caring and passionate. The class itself is difficult, but there are many things to balance your grade and she does want to help you succeed.

Professor Rupar is passionate about what she does and accessible outside of class. The class is not too bad at the beginning but does get more difficult. Stay on top of the content and the homework. Take MGT 3000 instead if you're IE.

Rupar is an awesome professor. I initially struggled in her course (no accounting background), but she does such a great job in lectures and always check to ensure all questions are answered. She is super helpful in office hours as well. Take the time to understand the why behind concepts. If you don't do well on exam 1, get a 1:1 tutoring appt.

She teaches really well, but she speeds through, which makes it hard for someone who has never been exposed to accounting (me). Her tests are difficult, and there are only 2 exams excluding the final. The group project was stressful but she gives really good feedback. She definitely wants you to succeed and takes time to know her students.

This is by far the hardest class I have ever taken and she didn't make it any easier. All she does is read off printed slides during class and speed through the content like we're supposed to know accounting already. She doesn't explain things well at all for a first level class. Take a different teacher if you can, it'll make your life much easier

This is by far one of the best professors you will have. Super nice and kind, definitely wants students to succeed in the course. The course itself is difficult but she definitely makes it a lot easier. The group project really helps your grade and as long as you do the homework and the one off online quizzes you will be just fine.

Great professor! Decent amount of homework/quizzes, 2midterms, 1project and 1final. Explains concepts clearly and includes multiple examples. Drops questions on exams if the average on that question is low and goes over it. Would recommend

Class wasn't difficult, she walked you through every type of problem, and printed out the notes for every lecture. Quizzes, homework, test and projects balance out the grade. She couldn't be nicer or more willing to answer any question.

Dr. Rupar was always very engaged with the class and seemed very passionate about what she was talking about and cared about her students. Homework, 4 quizzes, 3 exams, and a nicely graded group project make up the grade. Accounting is, by nature, a difficult class, but she makes it a little easier. Practice and pay attention and you'll get the A.

The class was more difficult than I expected it to be, but not because of the lecturer. She is very passionate about what she does and clearly cares a lot about her students. I would definitely recommend taking her!
She is really good and had a great time in the class. Accounting is a hard class in general but she makes it very good. Favorite teacher by far
Dr. Rupar is a great professor. She really cares about her students and is a great lecturer. Def take her for 2101. You won't regret it.

She was pretty cool, exams were fair and did not have any curveballs. Lectures are fine but if you want an A or is an accounting student I suggest reviewing the classwork and/or example(s) in the notes after the lecture since accounting processes and concepts can only be so easily understood by watching someone else do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She definitely makes you work for your grade. Lectures are okay, but goes really fast. To study for tests, go through textbook chapters and take notes, because her practice test she releases for each exam isn't indicative of the actual exam. Final exam had a really low average, but she threw out some questions. A solid choice for ACCT 2101.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked her. She cares a lot about her students and tries to make accounting as easy as possible to understand. The homework is pretty easy and you have 3 attempts on each. She drops your lowest quiz and homework which is nice but they're all easy to get 100s on. Exams are kinda difficult but she does give practice exams.

Awesome professor. I've never taken any sort of business- or accounting-related classes before this one, and she made the content easy to comprehend and enjoyable to learn. You can tell that she cares about her students & wants them to really understand what she teaches. You get a lot of time to complete your homeworks.

Her lectures are so helpful and she actually prints the slides for everyone to take notes on since it's much easier to do that than take separate notes. She is an amazing professor and she's so sweet and fun to listen to! I really struggled with accounting (it's MUCH harder than you think) but I would 100% take her again.
Gives very informative lectures. will learn a lot. prints slides and stuff -- take notes on them -- keep em neat good study resources
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super sweet and great with communication. Clear grading criteria. Super passionate and in-class participation are relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: she def cares and is very accessible for help outside of the class. she does truly want her students to succeed and structures 3003 highly around getting feedback. good lecturer, boring topic. the tests in this course are a bit tough but the grading scheme allows for leniency. can average B on tests and a B on the term paper for an A.

Dr. McCann is by far one of the best professors I have ever had at this school. She is kind, knowledgeable, & very passionate about what she teaches!! I would take as many courses as I could with this professor since I not only feel like I learned a significant amount, but also enjoyed this course so much! Also I took 3003 with her, not 3001.
Very caring professor who really cares about you. Tests can be tricky if you don't come to class and pay attention to what she verbally says. Also, I took 3003 with her not 3001.

Very kind and understanding, I had her for 2001 and 3003 - she teaches well and seems to genuinely care. Class structures for both were Not The Best, but I dont think that's on her. Out of any of the neuro teachers she co-taught with, she explained things the best, if not a little fast though. Highly recommend taking her classes.

there were readings before EVERY CLASS and major assignments due the same week as major exams. She co-teaches with Holder so she's better in comparison to her but the class can be very heavy and the tests are sometimes unnecessarily difficult with very particular grading. She wants her students to succeed (i think..). No final, term paper instead.

Out of the 3 NEUR 2001 professors, she was the best. Her lectures were engaging and interesting and she made sure that we understood all of the information. The unit 3 midterm (the unit she taught) was extremely straightforward and easy, especially compared to the other 2 tests. Overall amazing professor.

He was a pretty good professor overall, and I think I could've done much better in his class if I hadn't been so burnt out the semester I took it. Tests are a large part of your grade, but he is great at explaining concepts. His tests are fair, and I overall recommend taking his class.

His lectures were good since we did multiple examples and it was easy to get how to do the problems. His tests and quizzes were very fair and the sample questions that he gives you are very similar to the test/quiz questions. Most of your grade is the midterms, quizzes, and the final so if you lock in for those it shouldn't be hard to secure the A.

Absolute saint of a human. His lectures are great, he's one of those profs who doesn't overload us with unnecessary info outside the scope of the class. And fwiw I did hear he's really kind about allowing makeup tests/quizzes. Funny guy too

Very dull and extensive lectures, I honestly skipped his lectures. He records videos which is nice to look back on during studying. Honestly, underrated professor. I wish I went to more lectures. Dry humor kind of guy. Talked to him the first time the day before my final and he was great at explaining stuff. Very fair tests, just prepare well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: help why'd someone say his voice is annoying 😭 anyways he's a really good lecturer and does a LOT of examples and there's studio + sen fernandez. there's plenty of study material for the class and the examples on tests are like 90% similar to them. beware tho the grading scheme is like 95% quizzes and tests o don't fall off too hard but yea ur gud

i know u hear these reviews telling u not to go to class, which is fair, he does post the vids. but dude is actually funny in lectures and suupperr chill. he's honest about what's on tests and it's great that he cares more abt u learning diffeq than a letter grade. BUT this is prolly the most important sophomore gen ed for engineers so LOCK-IN TWIN

sometimes his voice gets on my nerves but his attendance is the most optional shi ever because he posts everything online in videos. lowk slept in every day of his class. fire tho because he is a great lecturer.

The quizzes and exams are SO much easier compared to other professors. Karthik made sure all of the integration was easy and every problem was familiar. I would recommend pirating the textbook for extra practice problems, as homework is only 3 problems a week. The final exam is worth 37% of the grade but doesn't include any hard concepts.
Dr. Karthik has a very straightforward class. Homeworks, few quizzes, and a few exams is all you need to worry about. Questions are fair and based off lecture material and practice resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very chill professor. his lectures are clear and thorough so you walk away with a great understanding of the material. the practice given in and out of class sets you up really well for the quizzes and midterms. he also does well with communication and stays accessible even out of class. i would strongly recommend taking him.

there was a lot of partial credit given, which was very saving. he literally tells you the exact type of question on exams/quizzes at least a week before. i needed to take my exam another day and he understood my reason without doubting me. really understanding professor, made this class so much more easier to understand!
Wouldn't take again, bit of a jerk

Lectures were good and sample material/quizzes/worksheets were great preparation for exams. Assessments were straightforward and super representative of material given. Professor worked hard to make the course engaging and applicable.
Best name of all time

Quizzes: 24% (5, 6% each, drop lowest); Tests: 34% (2, 17% each); Final: 37%; HW: 5% (15, drop two lowest). Lecture was 8 a.m. Was monotone, repetitive, and not interesting. Notes are clear, quizzes and tests are INCREDIBILY easy. He releases a statement a week before each quiz/test about the exact questions that will be on them. Take again? Yeah..

Lecture videos posted on Canvas, tests are very similar to practice exams, and overall the tests are really fair. Lots of additional office hours around exam times, along with 2% extra credit for attending studios and 85% participation rate on CIOS.
posts lecture videos, light homework, gives what the questions will be about before quizzes and tests, 2% extra credit (1% for going to studio, 1% for CIOS).

Really nice guy, very considerate about students. Lectures are basically all you need, he explains everything in detail. Exams and quizzes are similar to past years and theres one quiz drop and 2 hw drops. Take him

Mamillapalle lectures the material really well. Took in the summer, had 5 quizzes, lowest of which is dropped, 2 exams, and 1 final. extra credit CIOS and if you attend enough recitations. HW through webwork. Mamillapalle is incredibly responsive and cares for his students, I had an injury during his class and he worked with me as much as he could.

Suuuper free. Everything in this class can be learned from Sebastian Fernandez's Youtube videos. The homework are super short and worth 5% of your grade with 2 dropped, the quizzes were usually very easy (one dropped), and the exams were much easier than other professors. Only thing is the final is worth 37%, which is a little annoying.

posts all lecture videos which was really helpful bc it was an 8am and i went to like 30% of class. 2552 is difficult when you first start but his lectures are great. he offered 2 full points of extra credit, plus dropped 2 homeworks and ur lowest quiz. only 3 exams total but not too difficult to succeed in his class, and ur given lots of chances
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really really loved him as a teacher. I found his style of teaching/lecture really effective as he worked through many examples and often checked for understanding. He posts videos of the lectures and the exams were not bad if you understood the practice exams. The class is very exam heavy but again if you do practice its not too bad.
About as good as it gets

The course was very straightforward, and exams and quizzes were fair. Lectures were generally dry but were spiced up by the occasional proof or joke. I would take this course again in a heartbeat, highly recommended

Dr. Karthik, is a FANTASTIC professor with awesome, funny, and useful lectures. Before exams, he posts an announcement outlining the types of problems, which is incredibly helpful. If you review lectures, complete homework, and practice old assessments, you'll find the course VERY easy. Easily the best MATH2552 professor.

Tests are very similar to practice exams he posts, straight forward for test material and gives the topics you will be tested on. Lectures and studio are not attendance mandatory, but he goes over all material needed for the test. Final was weighted 37%.

I enjoyed this class, I expected it to be harder than it actually was. Lectures can be a bit boring, but they cover everything you need to know. Tests and quizzes accurately reflected the material. Prof is approachable and helpful.

This guy is a pretty great lecturer, and he posts them all on Canvas. Tests were fair and studios were helpful. He moves very quickly through the material though so you have to pay attention, but there is a lot of content to cover. Got funnier during the lecture as the semester went on.

This guy is my goat. I'd take his lecture for every class if I could. Goes through proofs for equations so we know why the application works. Not a day went by where I didn't enjoy the content or lecture. Studios were very helpful and the tests and quizzes were extremely easy. Gives practice exams that are very similar to the exams in class.

Organized, recorded lectures, good about uploading completed lecture notes, responds to emails. Sometimes adds a bit of humor to the lecture which is always appreciated. Although it was sometimes boring and almost felt like a waste of time, it was really helpful that he frequently did review at the beginning of each class.

Terrible lecturer. Like horrible, but he's great apart from that. Tests are super easy and similar to practice ones, and he gave a ton of extensions when the computer system would break. Also he would be available all hours of the day. I was honestly a little worried for him, like leave work at work my guy, but also it was nice.

Amazing lectures that covered every edge case for every concept, no curveballs on quizzes/exams. All lectures recorded and posted in Canvas. Funny and charismatic professor who cares about his students and never hesitates to answer questions. Fast replies on Piazza. Would love to take another class with him, or even TA/do research. Sign up for him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kim was an amazing professor for 1102. If you need to take this class for credit, she is definitely the professor to take. I think this was the first time she taught 1102 this spring, but she was amazing. She's very easy to talk to, very lenient with deadlines and grading, and makes sure to catch you up in class material.
She was a very nice professor. She also had a pretty interesting focus for ENGL 1101 (age) which helped make the course a little easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is the kindest and sweetest professor I had this semester! I loved her so much I'm trying to take her for 1102 next semester! She gives great feedback on assignments to ensure your trajectory is smooth throughout the course and all the assignments are simple and engaging. The class topic was age in media which I thought was interesting!
She is the sweetest person ever and is extremely approachable if you ever need help!
Dr. Kim is awesome! She is really nice, caring and available outside of class. As long as you show up to class you will be ready for assignments and the Artifacts will be easy peasy.
Awsome teacher, she grades well, gives good feedback, and she is just awsome!

Kirkman has good intentions, but people don't pay too much attention to the lectures. TA's grade extremely differently. Some give out lots of points on assignments; some are very lenient. Not a super interesting class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives very broad instructions on weekly writing assignments, so he is able to grade harshly and say its not what he was looking for. Seems to grade a little personally and will take off points if I say something I believe and he doesn't agree with (politics, etc). Lectures are just him talking straight to you. Weird grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nobody is excited to attend an Ethics course, however Kirkman does a great job making his lectures interesting. Writing isn't too hard and neither are the exams. Overall a solid ethics class
Should be a free class but makes it way harder then it should be. His grading scale made no sense.

Only grades for the semester are weekly essays and a final project. He gives lots of feedback on the essays which sometimes is super harsh. Classes were him talking about the assigned readings with no slides or other material, he just talks at you for 75 minutes. He was very friendly and the class didn't demand too much, overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives you a lot to read, a lot to write, and can sometimes feel like he's harping with his feedback and unwilling to just say "Good job". But he does actually care- if you talk to him just a bit outside of class, do all of your work (as tedious as it may be), and take his feedback seriously, you can almost guarantee an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: 3109 online meets MW for 50 minutes, discussing ethical topics, these meetings are not bad and you don't have to participate.  Friday discussions are on case studies where you can discuss and debate an ethical dilemma from an engineer.  If you get a good TA, this class can be great
Very unclear expectations of the final project, basically just lectures the whole entire class with no slide show, so he's just talking at you the whole class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I hated participating in this class as his responses to any thoughts were usually critical. Grading is extremely unclear, leaving you unsure of where you stand in the class. Very tough grader when it came to the weekly commentaries.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class GPA is high, I feel like it would be easy to get an A if you put in the effort he asks. That being said, the final project effectively determines your grade, and this is frustrating because you need a perfect score (no partial credit) and everyone knows how bad group projects are at Tech. Easy class but stressful if you don't like risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkman talked a lot during lecture. He was clearly passionate about the subject (and a lot of other subjects too), but in an 8 am class it was kind of grating. Definitely agree with a lot of others here about unclear expectations regarding grading and what the final project even was. LOTS of reading, but overall it's fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkman is incredibly knowledgeable and leads great conversations. But the course design and structure is imprecise. He does "ungrading", which alleviates stress, but makes the grading criteria unclear. The learning outcomes are vague, and he does not hold back on feedback, but he does care and is open to criticism.

Dr. Kirkman is a great choice for this course. This semester he operated on a principle of self tracking your progress throughout the course and then discussing with him at the end of the semester what grade you think you deserve based on participation, what you learned, etc. Don't know if it will always be like this, but it was this semester.

I took 3109 with Prof. Kirkman in the summer. In this class you need: 1. Use 4050 minutes read the materials that he asks for, write a short essay (about 300 words is enough) every week. 2. post three discussions ( pretty simple and easy) every week. 3. A friendly final project. Hes a nice grader overall and class is easy for CS and Engi student
Grading criteria purposefully confusing. Take a different humanities if you can. You can get a good grade, but you won't learn anything and you'll leave with a bad taste in your mouth.

Kirkman is hard but fair.  The readings and weekly assignments can become cumbersome if you have a lot going on.  Great attendance isn't a necessity, but you can get a lot out of the lectures if you do attend regularly and pay attention.
Weekly Writing assignments get to be a bore.  He grades hard, TAs grade easy.  Attendance is not necessary.

Preaches about how much he hates "death by powerpoint" and then lectures directly from slides posted online. Easy B. Really really difficult A. Just hope that he doesn't grade any of your tests or papers and lets the TA's do it.

Easy class. Rather dry lectures. Attendance is NOT necessary at all. Midterm exam and final exam are literally same format, same weight, same grading scale. TA's grade most papers and grade really easily. If he grades your paper, watch out, he'll tear it up and ruin your chance at an A.

Amazing lecturer who takes time to go through concepts and examples with precision as to leave no confusion. Accessible outside of class and gives plenty of prep material before exams. Tests are not bad and are standardized.

His lectures weren't the best, but you can always watch Jankowski's lectures online. Tests are the same across professors, so it really doesn't matter who you get for linear. Way more conceptual than I expected (multiple choice and T/F were hardest parts of the test). Definitely felt like more effort than a 2 credit class, but overall it's fine.

The class was very manageable if you take the time to go to class and learn the material in the homework. The quizzes were based off the online homework assignments. Professor Kim is very dull, he sometimes forgets things or explains things confusingly. Overall boring but not bad.

Professor Kim was okay. He is good at explaining the math concepts if you ask for extra help but he is a bit dull during lecture. He likes to put students in groups during class to complete assigned problems.

Prof. Kim was fine, but a bit dull at times. You really have to enjoy linear to be able to pay attention. Lectures are definitely skippable because he posts Prof. Jankowski's videos to Canvas. The class is pretty hard, especially if you take it your first semester like I did, but if you're willing to put in the time to study, an A is attainable.

Decent prof. Lectures are a bit dry and you can pretty much just read the slides to be successful. I always skipped lecture during busy weeks which was nice.

I loved this man when I went to lecture; however, I only did this about 20% of the time. Reading the textbook is arguably a more effective way of learning the material, so you get to choose if you want to go to lecture or read.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Klimenko and his TAs are really disorganized with testing and grading. He reads off his slides in lecture, and lecture is really not necessary to be successful. The homework isn't bad, but the tests have questions that seem unnecessarily tricky. Definitely go to the TAs' review sessions for some test tips.

He does a good job of relating what we learn to real life, although sometimes he does that so much we fall behind. Class is graded entirely on a curve so basically 1/3 get As, 1/3 get Bs, and 1/3 get Cs. There was a lot of homework, and the practice tests are almost exactly like the test. He makes you buy a $140 textbook.

I took Prof Klimenko for Global Economy. I don't think his lectures could have been more boring or inefficient. He literally just goes over powerpoint slides each and every time... they're really unbearable. If you do all the homeworks and practice problems thoroughly, it's not too tough tho. Still would not recommend

He was very passionate and covered all material during lecture, however, the lecture slides were taken directly from the textbook. I found the textbook very helpful, so I typically worked on homework during class. Homework is very helpful. Tests were somewhat difficult, but they had huge curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Klimenko is such an iconic teacher. Though his lectures can get a little monotonic, his examples using Delta, Hartsville-Jackson Airport, and Sally's Ice Cream Cones never get old. Tests are difficult, but you can get an A with one or two grind days per exam.
It's super hard, but you learn a lot. I had to study for 9-12 hours for each midterm to skip the final and just make an A after getting almost 100s on each homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor spends at least 45 minutes per lecture ranting about something that he never ties back to the subject. More than half the class is either sleeping, doing other work, or not there during a lecture.

Klimenko is a very knowledgeable professor and has very specific examples that he will continuously reuse to the point that they become a meme-- most often, the use of Delta Airlines as an example of a monopoly. That being said, lectures are not required and don't add much to the published slides and textbook.
He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject and genuinely cares about his students. Although his lectures can be sleep inducing at times.

His lectures are kind of boring but he gives interesting and realistic examples based on the topic. Test prep sessions are helpful. Homeworks are easy with 3 tries per question. Study extra practice questions and tests get a lot easier.

He uses the same examples for everything, which makes it hard to tell apart situations. His tests are super long and full of confusing MCQs. His class slides are average at best. Sticking to the textbook and homework would be your best course of action.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and willing to help, but lecture is the most boring thing I have ever sat through and I really enjoy economics.  He posts all of the slides that he reads straight from in class, so there's not much of a point going.  Tests are very difficult, but he heavily curves and it's impossible to fail his class if you show up to the exams.

Lectures were really long and hard to stay focused in. He was really knowledgeable about the topics and open to questions in lecture. He lets you skip the final if you are happy with your grade after the first three tests, but the tests are really hard. He curves all of them, but you need to take the homework seriously if you want a good grade.

He is very knowledgeable, and gives a lot of examples to explain concepts. I would not skip classes. He lets you skip the final. I got an A in this course because I did the homework and read the book. His tests are hard (would not recommend taking him unless you really like the topics). You will learn a lot more in this class than ECON2100/2105/etc

His lectures are very long and boring, there's no point in really going to class. He posts all the slides online and just study the slides and follow along in the book (if you really want to understand material) to pass the tests. The homeworks are of varying lengths and help you understand. Just do homeworks and slides and you'll be fine.
Klimenko is good. He really understands the material. He puts the slides online, so you can follow along. Sometimes its hard to stay focused during his lectures.

I promise, unless you are doing well-above average on his tests, you will not know what your overall grade is until right before the final, which is optional. I only went to lecture a few times and it wasn't that helpful. He is smart, but there is nothing you need to know beyond the book.
not a bad professor. lectures were boring. not mandatory. big curve is very helpful. tests not that bad if you know the material. hw is long but not too difficult.

ok teacher. Lectures are really boring...he basically reads the textbook to you off powerpoint slides. It is not attendance based. If you go and do the homework you don't need to read the textbook. Online HW. Doing the HW helps prepare for the test! Never posts test grades for at least a week after. Curves the class. 20% As, 60% Bs & Cs, 20% Ds& Fs

He is a very interesting professor, open to your  ideas and presents his lectures very well. Although his class usually has over 200 people only about 30 of them show up each time. Tests are medium hard, but if you read your material and attend the lectures you should be good.

Under no circumstances would I ever recommend taking this course. The quizzes are nothing short of insanely hard because of the sheer volume of information covered and more than 50% is not even touched on in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I am purely curious about the people who gave him a 5. He definitely is smart but he doesn't know how to teach. He expects students to know everything before he teaches and skips a lot of techniques such as Kruskal's algorithm and such. He gives quizzes with ridiculous difficulties and doesn't care about the students. Also the TA doesn't know too.

Brutally difficult, but worth it if you want to get a serious, in depth understanding of logistics. Very knowledgeable and kind, he'll go the extra mile to help you understand, but won't ever dumb down the material. Demands a lot of reading (20-30 pages per week), and tests are usually graded on 2-3 problems worth a lot of points. Curves (80+ = A)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cares more about emphasizing his own understanding then creating it within his students.
Very heavy workload, exams don't test relevant knowledge,
Take his class if you want a message to stick with you.

Kleywegt is tough but I still enjoyed his class. I learned more in his class than most other upper-level ISYE classes at Tech. He was always willing to answer questions and have discussions about class applications to current events & problems. He is super knowledgeable & has high expectations so don't take him unless you're willing to do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Poorly made slides, and no textbook to reference. Relatively apathetic professor, with no connection to actual industry practices. Extremely difficult grader (over a third of quizzes with <50% average). Does not disclose dates / requirements in the syllabus. Find a way to avoid this class if possible.
Difficult quizzes with little warning and no examples beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tests you on things you've never seen examples of. Grades insanely hard.
The course is not all good and he is the worst professor in ISYE. The course is very badly organized and the exams are really hard. No point in taking this course.

Such an absurd amount of work. Tough grader. Makes you feel like an idiot in front of the class. So much reading. Homeworks are nearly impossible. He curves, but still gives out mostly C's. Don't take him unless you're prepared to do massive amounts of work. The class overall is very interesting though, probably the only reason I stuck through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Class participation is a must. We had  to read a book called 'The Box'. It seems to be unnecessary but in the end it bumped up points on the test for those who missed out on problems.

this professor cares way more about the material than he does his students. your biggest danger is losing your pulse and dying from boredom/exhaustion, because he literally just shows up for 3 hours to yap. But if you can tolerate that, his grading/teaching is relatively easy.

The lectures themselves were interesting, but the organization of this class was a nightmare. There was no clear grading criteria, nothing was graded until the day of the final, and I have never had a professor that was more inaccessible. I don't think he responded to single email the entire semester from any student.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He did not upload our grades for THREE papers until the day before final exam. And he uploaded them all at the same time. No grading criteria/rubrics. Graded participation based on vibes, and the highest grade was a 95. Did not respond to a single email all semester. His lectures are interesting, but horribly unorganized course and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF! He discussed pornography unnecessarily - made students uncomfortable. I did not learn anything about internet law. He does not grade anything until the end of the semester and assigns long memos without rubric or clear instructions and grades based on "feelings". He is biased and unprofessional and doesn't respond to emails.

Class meant to be 630-915 pm. He decided (after W deadline) to shift it to 6-845 pm. This should include the 15 min institute-mandated break. Instead, we now begin early and stay late. There has not been a class that didn't extend from 6 pm to 9:30 at least, usually without break. Att. is req; missing more than once is -5 on your course grade.
Great teacher, graded heavily on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are weekly readings in this class, but the lecture covers all of the material needed for the quizzes. The quiz banks are also posted and quizlet has the quiz questions as well. There is a "studio" where you sit in a group and talk about the readings. 2 papers count as 50% of your grade and the TAs can grade harshly if you write a bad paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Klein himself is a great lecturer, and honestly, I learned and reflected a lot in this class. However, there are so few assignments. 

Don't just brush it off as an easy A class and make sure to put in effort from the beginning. .

The work is really easy and you'll get a good grade as long as you pay attention in lectures, you lowkey don't even need to do any of the readings. He is very passionate about the subject and really makes you reflect on yourself. I'm ngl this class might make you entirely change the course of your life, I would highly recommend.

Dr. Klein takes a topic that many engineering students do not have interest in and keeps them attentive enough to introduce them to ideas and topics that make them think in ways they may not have before. The lectures are interesting, the readings are interesting but optional, and the classes are easily worth the little time they require.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: really easy class and the prof is great. i was dreading this class bc philosophy isn't my thing but he actually made it pretty interesting. highly recommend for ethics credit.
Good lectures and light workload. Klein is funny and clearly cares about what he teaches

Good class, heavily participation based. Do the readings, you won't regret it. That is probably all you have to do to ace the quizzes. Great lectures, can become a class pushed to the side as there is not much work but I thoroughly enjoyed it. Do yourself a favor and put quizzes on your calendar because he doesn't remind you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor made a grading curve, not the good kind. He claims that his TAs were giving out too many A's so he came up with 1/3 A, 1/2 B, and the rest C or below. There was a lot of readings. The quizzes/exams were 10 multiple choice and based on lecture material and readings. He unlocked the paper prompts about 2-3 weeks it was due.5 page length
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading was fair (but based on only a few assignments) and the first few weeks of class were interesting, but Dr. Klein is truly a deranged man. He seemed to be coming up with the class as he taught and spent more time ranting about technical difficulties and foreign policy takes straight out of RT or China Daily than talking about internet policy.

Professor Klein was a good teacher lecture could sometimes go off topic but he was usually pretty interesting. TA was helpful and although he didn't have much grading criteria it was not hard to make a decent grade.
You go into quizzes completely unaware of what is going to be on it. Not to mention you are told last minute about them. There is no set syllabus.
Class is very unorganized. He springs quizzes and papers last minute with little to no instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Klein has been a fantastic professor for Philosophy. He's a great lecturer and is clearly passionate about the material he teaches. Keeping up with the readings is definitely important in the class when it comes to quizzes, and he will at times spring extra readings on you from current events, but it's not unmanageable in any sense.

I did enjoy Dr. Klein's lectures. His lectures make philosophy very interesting and makes you think. A lot of books are covered in this class, but you don't have to read these books as long as you familiarize yourself with them. His quizzes are straight from his lectures, but there are 2 essays worth 40% combined that make it hard to get an A.

Dr. Klein is nice and his class is easy as long as you participate in discussions and keep up with the readings. I had this course completely online due to COVID, so it was extremely disorganized. This was pretty frustrating at times and he kind of changed the grading scheme. Overall, if you want a chill class I would recommend, but it's hectic.

I loved Dr. Klein! A lot of students did not like him during the online semester, but I enjoyed his lectures and class format. Many students who did not watch the lectures were upset that they would be penalized for this. If you put in the effort, you should do well. The two papers were a bit stressful, but he is very gracious with extensions.

Dr. Klein was extremely hard to work with during COVID. The problems from this class include, but are not limited to: not posting lectures on time, not posting the final, changing the syllabus the last day of class in favor of hurting student grades, never being available/responding to emails, and being the least accommodating professor ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The topic was interesting, and the quizzes were easy as long as you did the quiz bank before. My TA was Ollie, and he was awesome. He was a fair grader and led interesting discussions. I would definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Klein makes his PHIL 3127 class interesting. doesnt have much to do with ethics but the readings make you think critically about the information we are exposed to in our day to day lives and his lectures are a good analysis of it. mainly graded on papers and quizzes but quizzes ask fair questions and paper is graded fairly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were super interesting and fair because no one was actually going into philosophy. We would watch movies sometimes and he made them apply to current events. Mandatory attendance and lots of reading, but quizzes were easy and there was no final. My TA was a hardcore liberal by the professor was moderate. This was a great course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredible professor. Made the material very interesting and lectures were pretty chill.

Quizzes are easy, as they're from previous ones, which are on quizlet. Can only miss 2 lectures, or points are deducted. Participation and paper grades come from TA's, so they vary, but my TA, Meg, was one of the worst and most of us still got A's. Overall easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures can get boring and tedious, but he does his best to make it enjoyable.  He is understanding and realizes the majority of students are not extremely passionate about philosophy.  Half of your grade is two papers which are graded by your TA, so the grade disparity between sections can be pretty drastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Just study past quizzes on quizlet for the 5 quizzes you will have. One quiz gets dropped which is really nice. Papers are kind of annoying but the TA's usually grade them fairly. Klein is a very enthusiastic lecturer and has some really interesting points.
Presented material in an interesting way, smooth lecturing, and helpful TAs.
Great professor and has an awesome way of presenting information.  Very clear in bringing forth the lectures. Study the slides!

Great professor, has been doing this for a long time. The class is very interesting, but there is a part where it becomes boring. Overall great class and great professor. Show up to class and should have no problems when taking the test.Just go through the slides and also read the material he sends through email.2 papers, not a problem.

Amazing teacher. I learned so much. His class was based on the Matrix. It is an ethics course, it was all about prison of the mind. I found the class really interesting. His test are super easy. You just need to study a little and do fine. I scored 100 on most. There are two papers, which arent too bad. Lost points after missing 2 days of class.

I'm taking him online in the covid summer. He records lectures and has office hours. He explains the material well and is super helpful with the homework. He's super funny so the lectures aren't boring. He knows emag really well and I can tell he enjoys teaching it. Tests are pretty easy and he keeps the average a high B. Great guy, 10/10 recommend

The best professor in the ECE department in my opinion. Very clear lectures and is really good at explaining tough concepts. Has homework every week and lets us ask questions about them before it's due. Tests are fair and grades with a curve of keeping the class average a high B. All in all, great.
Good professor. Material is clear and helps with the homeworks in class.

Klein is one of the best ECE professors at GT. Wrote a book for the class online that is very understandable and used as a basis for lectures. Encourages questions and loves answering them no matter how hard they are. If you get stuck on HW problems he will show the solution in class. Tests are easy if you get previous exams but doesn't curve much.

Pretty straightforward course. Show up and pay attention to the material and you will be fine. Also, exams are open book/notes, so if you bring everything that was covered in the class you are good to go.

She seemed like a nice prof when she lectured but when you approach her in person she is cold and seems like she really doesn't care about you or how well you do in the course. I thought the tests were going to be a breeze but turned out to be harder than they needed to be. Overall a fairly easy course, but is unnecessarily hard at times.

Go to class to complete case studies, pay attention in class and do the extra credit. do all of it and an A is practically guaranteed. Study a little for the tests and you should be making A's and B's pretty easily.

This class makes me feel like i am in highschool again. Just do the assignments she gives(they are not hard at all). I studied for the tests the day off the test and still ended up with a 97.9 in the class. I took the short summer session also which was 5 weeks long. This class is not hard at all if you somewhat apply effort.

This class was one of the easiest courses I've ever taken at GT. The homework was very simple and often beneficial. The tests were super easy (just read the powerpoint slides and study guide before the test). She gives out plenty of extra credit, so not getting an A is almost impossible. She also makes class very interesting.

She posts all powerpoints and lecture notes. Study them the night before the exams, and you will do fine. I never used the textbook, it was a waste of $. Do all the free extra credit and you should be able to pull off an easy A.

Take the class seriously.  Attending class, minding due dates and studying will make an A very easy.  She is extremely fair.  Don't expect to talk your way into an A.  She offers a lot of extra credit.  Take advantage of it.

It's definitely possible to get an A in this class. Just take studying for the three tests seriously - they're 70% of your grade so if you mess up one, you'll likely get a B. Also, take assignment and extra credit due dates seriously. She will not accept them late.

She is super not helpful. Every time a question is asked, she treats you like you're an idiot. She's sassy in class and does nothing but read off of her powerpoint. Although she's focused on the big picture, her tests are very difficult. I'm not even sure if reading the book helps. it's just an unnecessarily difficult class that's boring and not fu
I really enjoyed this class.  It was a welcome intellectual diversion from all the engineering classes I've been wading through.

definitely responsive and adds to her powerpoint slides. she's not exactly your easy A but if you put in the effort i.e. read the book before classes and review the slides before the exams, then you are good. also don't forget to do small assignments. a plus for her tests is that she doesn't nitpick statistics - she's after the big picture/concept.
Tests aren't online anymore. Class is kind of hard but doable, lots of extra-credit opportunities. She keeps the class interesting/not-boring enough to keep you awake

Class is very dificult as a whole, but she at least has online tests.  Although timed, it is still an advantage to have unlimited resources for tests.  There are also assignments throughout the course which count as small percentages of the final grade.  Out of the selection of instructors, I would definitely recommend her.

The class is harder than its supposed to be, but still this is an easy A. If you get anything else then your just lazy or stupid. Tests are all online so you can use anything you want. They are timed however so you cant take your time. Class is really boring since all she does is read the notes that she puts up on her website Class Should be easy A

"She teaches this class as if we were all pre med students. Although the teests are online she makes it too hard for a basic health class. There is much more workload than there should be in a required class thats suppossed to be an easy A" I agree with that comment 100%
No Comments
She is a terrible teacher....to not to get her at all costs

Don't get her if you can. She reads off her notes and her tests are way too hard for a class that should be an easy A. I don't go to class anymore because all she does is read off her notes.
One of the top 3 professors I've taken at tech. 350 words is not enough to glaze this man. He is goated. Take him.

Whoever gives this guy below a 5 is tripping. Best professor I have ever had in college by FAR. Makes a very complicated topic very understandable, and even very fun, as long as you go to class and put in the normal amount of effort. Exams can be a bit tough, but they are completely reasonable because you can re-do parts of it for extra credit.

One of the best professors in the ME school. Really clear lectures that explain the underlying concepts without getting bogged down in the math. He very clearly cares about the class and genuinely wants everyone to learn and understand the application of the material. Tests are hard but you are guaranteed ~20% back on them so As are very obtainable

Best prof at GT. Shreyas was able to teach the content and explain things so well that you could come to his office hours a week before the exam knowing very little and leave having a strong grasp on the material. Exams were hard but with corrections, so you learn the material even better without fear of too harsh of a grade penalty.

Shreyas is my goat. Genuinely one of the most engaging, funny, and knowledgeable professors I've had in my time at Tech. He's a capable lecturer, his homework is fun, his tests are hard but test corrections go CRAZY. He's extremely fun to be around and wears bucket hats and shorts to class. He's the epitome of "I'm just a guy." I love him so much.

I got into the class because people said  he was a great professo, but apparently he changed his whole syllabus/curriculunce since his GPA was very high. lots of homework. His final is NOT optional compared to other professors. regret it,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Shreyas was very enthusiastic about everything he taught. It kept me engaged. He also took out some of the stressful elements of the class by formatting it differently making it more learning focused. If you can take systems with him, do it! This was my favorite class at Georgia Tech. He is the best option for this class by a landslide.

He's amazing, one of the best profs I've had here. Passionate about what he teaches and is enthusiastic each day. Optional final with no grade risk. His 2 tests had a 70% average, but he let you correct up to 20-25% afterwards, shifting the average to an A. His HW's are every 2 weeks, kinda time consuming but fun to do and encourage collaboration.
Professor Kousik was an incredibly professional yet personable lecturer. He made system dynamics fun and a breeze to learn. I highly recommend taking his course
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, great guy, very knowledgeable and has a informative perspective of the topic.

Prof. Koposov's lectures are full of insight into European history. A majority of the work you will do for this class is pretty dense reading in addition to 2 essays. Prof. is a super friendly guy who is always willing to answer any questions you have and is a relatively easy grader. Highly recommend it if you like history!

reviews.comment: Quiet and maybe hard to understand during lectures but a great professor and very forgiving grader.

reviews.comment: Funny and engaging lectures. only three graded assignments, though class participation is necessary. you need something like 9 comments per semester.

reviews.comment: Despite being 80% lectures this class was so entertaining. Grading is based on 3-4 projects but each is straightforward and you're given a lot of freedom. If you have any interest at all in history take one of Dr. Koposov's classes!

His lectures are interesting, but impossible to focus on unless you're in the seat right in front of him. It's easy to get an A in the class, but there are only 4 grades-- presentation, midterm paper, final paper, and participation. There are no set guidelines for the participation grade; just pray.

Far and away the best lecturer I've ever had.
If you want a course serious in content and reasonable in workload, this is a great option.
And if you want your politics and worldview challenged in discussions about real history, this might be your BEST option, unless you can get into a graduate seminar.
Cannot recommend this professor enough.

reviews.comment: Koposov? More like, KopoKing ��. This man is a great professor. The midterm and final papers are a bit of work but are fairly short compared to other HTS profs.

Dr. Koposov's course, while interesting material, was at best "meh". He's a very nice man, but his teaching style is almost completely lectures that matter almost nothing to your grade. Annoying grades on only three assignments.

reviews.comment: Grade in my experience was based on 3 essays with a lot of prep work needed for each essay. mostly easy A tho

reviews.comment: Professor Koposov is not only a renowned historian, but a marvelous professor. This class was remarkably fascinating not only because of the nature of the content and discussions, but because professor Koposov's lectures were always riveting. The class consists of heavy reading and graded participation, so if you read and participate you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He makes the otherwise difficult material easier to understand. He's humorous and a genuinely good lecturer.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He provides all lectures as printed, fillable pamphlets and is a very good lecturer. Homework follows lecture content and is harder than exams. Grading is done quickly and very fairly. I always wanted to go to lecture because he was very funny.

Absolutely named Dan GOATlyar, one of the best professors I have had. I would definitely take another course with him. All notes were very structured and the homework was challenging, but followed them closely and he was easily accessible for questions or office hours.

The class is hard and daunting and its easy to get lost, but: Homework is very representative of the lectures, lecture notes are clear and concise, and Kotlyar is genuinely interested in what he's teaching and is good at it. You will need to stay focused in class, but he's generous in grading and his tests are the most fair I've seen at Tech.

Had Dr. Kotlyar for NRE 4210. He is easily my favorite professor in the NRE department. He is able to clearly explain complex subjects with ease, and his lectures are full of useful diagrams and equations to support the theory. He made the class a bit too easy this semester, but it was still incredibly informative. GT is lucky to have Dr. Kotlyar.

Kotlyar is a really good lecturer. Your issue will not be with him but with the course material. There is a textbook but he's expecting you to learn his notes (which he hands out via paper in lecture), so if you ever get confused with his lectures, read the textbook for the concepts, and go to office hours to do the assignments

Kotlyar is by far the best NRE prof. 10/10 Amazing lectures. HWs (32%) start easy but get progressively harder until they are very very difficult. Tests and Final are hard but fair. He grades generously. Know ALL homework problems by heart (including derivations). Coding project (13%) is a long derivation and some basic python. He gives most of it.
Dr. Koros is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors I have ever had at Georgia Tech. His lectures are easy to understand and his homework is great practice
I took this class as a transfer student; he was the best. He really helped with chbe2100

Very passionate professor who is willing to do anything to help his students. The tests are challenging but if you keep on track with the homework and lecture, you will be fine. Highly recommend taking him if he is teaching the course.
Very helpful professor and an excellent teacher too. Tests are fairly hard but if you work, you'll do well. I highly recommend this guy.
very helpful and passionate, good guy
Really passionate professor

Basically AP Stats except you can use Excel to do the formulas for you. Weekly videos + notes take 1-2 hours max weekly. Tests have formula sheets provided and use questions nearly identical to practice problems from Pearson. Homeworks have infinite tries, plus you learn a lot of useful Excel skills.

This class was exactly like AP stats. Weekly assignments are pretty easy to get through. 3 midterms and your lowest grade gets averaged out by the other 2. If you do well enough on the midterms you can exempt the final! You can also choose to take the tests virtually with honor lock or in person. The tests are like the pearson practice tests.
Great Professor. Lectures are clear, Tests are like practice tests, and homeworks on pearson have infinite tries. Responds quickly by email.

Super chill professor 10/10. each week is just a homework assignment and a check in that you read lecture. Exams are based off the practice exams and homework so as long as you do them its easy. Nice guy will always text you after an exam saying good job on your last exam and also replies within a min. Textbook for the class is paid.

Professor Rajavi was a sweet professor. After each test, he would reach out about your performance and help move forward toward the next exam. He makes things very clear for when they need to be completed and frequently sends reminders about what needs to be done. MGT2250 was basically AP Stat in Excel and his class made it easily understandible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really easy class. Async on Pearson. You have to submit ur notes on his videos every Sunday. Review of AP stat. practice tests are super helpful. you can complete all of the semester homework early and just not worry about it. he exempts ur final if you have a 95% average on the tests basically meaning a 98 in the class, so it's not that helpful.

Took the hybrid course which allows you to watch video lectures and go to an optional lecture once a week.  Really good at explaining concepts and how to work excel. The 3 midterms are relatively easy as long as you study and you also get a cheat sheet.  Homework assignments aren't overwhelming either. Great professor for an easy A

He is amazing- def take 2250 w/ him! This class is virtual; his videos are clear, and he does examples in Excel. You have to purchase an online Pearson textbook to do the weekly assignment and the exams, but the coursework is very minimal, and it's clear that he wants you to succeed! Exams are super similar to the homework- easy A! 10/10 prof!

This is an asynchronous class with homework/notes due every week (super easy, unlimited attempts), 3 midterms with the lowest getting replaced with the average of the other two, and a final. midterms were exactly like the homework/practice exams, a very easy A in the class. you do have to buy pearson to do the hws. but definitely recommend !!!

Very good teacher and loved his class. I had the asynchronous version so I you would just watch videos and do hw. Very easy class and you will succeded especially if you have taken ap stat in highschool. Good guy and practice exams are literally the same as the exam.

Homework once a week (unlimited attempts), summary over material due weekly (gives many different options on how you can do it), three midterms (lowest grade gets replaced with average of highest two), attendance only mandatory on test days, and practice tests are almost identical to real tests. Responds to emails within ten minutes.

Rajavi is a great professor and makes this class very informative and easy. All attendance is optional other than the days there are tests (3 days a semester). The practice tests he gives out are exactly like the tests and all the homework has unlimited attempts (free 100). On top of all that he is really caring and encouraging.

Entirely optional attendance with one class per week and in-person exams. His lectures were always useful and he made sure to provide plenty of practice questions similar to the material on the exams. Having a weekly summary and HW assignment did make this class a fair amount of work, but not bad at all. Great choice for MGT 2250.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are very easy to understand and he is a phenomenal teacher. If you have the option to, pls take him, really really wont regret it. I know sometimes a new teacher with low ratings can be hard to pick - don't think twice about this prof. His hybrid course is amazing and super informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall, a very time-consuming and difficult class was made significantly harder than it had to be. Probably the harshest teacher for this class. Take literally anyone else. BRUTAL at 8 am.
Sometimes not prepared enough and impolite.

She prepared us for the final competition extremely well, but she also had extremely high expectations. She gives much more explicit guidance for the reports, which is nice, but also leaves much less room for error and the grades she gives reflect that. Taking her will make you a better engineer because she challenges you to earn every point.

If you want to learn the most from ME2110, take Mrs. Mahaffey. She is a detailed grader, but she teaches you how to become a professional in the realm of engineering. Although she expects a lot, She also cares for her students, and after taking her class, it is evident that she takes time to personally connect with every student.

Mrs. Mehaffey grades toughly but fairly and gives great feedback (office hours are SO HELPFUL). She truly cares and teaches very well-the best advice is to be attentive to all lectures and be cautious in reports and assignments. Pick a strategic team playing to each member's strengths. Working early in studio is THE KEY to performing well!

Kristi is a very tough grader on reports which make up a majority of your grade, but she gives great feedback so you should get a good grade on the final report. Guidance on robots also helps teams do well at competition. Kristi is very kind and cares about her students. She curves at the end, so if you work hard you should get an A or B easily.

Pretty tough grader compared to other professors, but this class is rough no matter who you have. She is very caring and wants her students to do well. Her section usually preforms well in the competition because she prepares you very well. Just beware the written reports. Its nearly impossible to get an A on them. She does curve at the end.
Study hard from the beginning if you want to pass this class and attend office hours; he is very helpful.

A great professor. Homeworks are weekly and graded mostly for participation. Exams are graded brutally and require mastery of the content for a grade better than a C. However, he genuinely cares about the content and the students, so I think it was a fantastic course.

Not the best but a good professor, nonetheless. His lectures are ok, but he is very accessible and always willing to help. Not as familiar with the material as the main professor for the course, but he does a decent job. Definitely caring about his students.
Good, clear lectures. Explained practice problems and was super helpful at explaining things 1:1.

Kretchmer is an OK lecturer, he explains and works through the in-class questions clearly. In the flipped lecture model, the lecture videos don't go as in-depth into the material as I would like, and you do end up spending a lot of your time reading the textbook to understand the material. Tests are hard, but grade improvement helps.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kretchmer didn't really do much as his class was a flipped-classroom model and the lectures just repeated the pre-lecture content (which sucked)- I recommend just skipping the lecture if you're disciplined enough to do the work outside of class. Tests were BRUTAL- averages usually in the 60s. Reading the textbook is the best way to succeed.

Read the textbook if you want to do well. Nice guy, standard, organized, and straightforward lectures. Only thing was the the lab portion took way too much time. Tests were hit or miss because no partial credit. Final was hard, but grade replacement policy helps a lot of people.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not the worst teacher, but his lectures were mostly him reading info to us from a slide and less explaining of the info. The tests were okay, and if you know the info you'll be fine, but it was easy to make a few mistakes, and there is no partial credit. The in-class questions give you a good chance to get your grade up tho.

Frustrating class. He only did the lectures, which were fine. Tests were predatory. A-level understanding could yield an A or a failing grade. Tests felt like Russian roulette. The lecture and lab material did not sync, making them excruciatingly time-consuming as you had to self-teach. Spent ~60% of total time on the 1-hour lab.
Kretchmer is a OK lecturer, class is difficult but he could be more engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: L class

Took ML co-design section with Tushar. Clearly very knowledgeable about the domain and the lecture contents are well-thought out covering both hardware, software and theory. -1 for being in Boston half the time and having subpar guest speakers instead, and the TAs literally not grading anything until the final month
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Krishna is a very nice guy and I found his lectures pretty engaging; however the workload with the labs can be brutal sometimes. Luckily there's a boatload of extra credit; I didn't use it but I totally should have. Exams are difficult.

I heard from many sources that Krishna is a great lecturer and prof, but I have yet to experience this. He is consistently 15 to 20 minutes late to class, cancels, or has his TAs run the lectures. All of the great things I have heard about him could be true if he only made hosting class a priority. I truly hope this is just an off-semester for him.

The professor is amazing, caring, and knowledgeable. You would definitely learn a lot about the on-chip network through the course and labs. The lab is based on the GarNet (Part of GEM5), which is used a lot in research papers and other organizations including both industry and academia. Also suggesting going through slides before class -> helpful!

Interesting and fun class that prepares you well for computer engineering. He is caring, gives a lot of extra credit, and definitely prepares his lectures, which go by very quickly. TAs are awesome as well. Labs take a lot of time but solidifies your understanding on the material. Only thing is he often shows up late and then rushes the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable man, but he goes through lecture super fast and hard to follow sometimes. Tough labs and fair exams. Lots of extra credit opportunity.
