Dr. Tushar is very kind and knowledgeable. Lectures are fast paced, and the lab assignments are very time consuming. Tests are fair, and there is plenty of extra credit opportunities on the labs and exams.

Professor Krishna is definitely caring towards his students and wants everyone to succeed. Lab assignments and exams can be pretty difficult, but they are fair and there are lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall really liked him as a professor but oftentimes arrived to class late and goes through slides super fast.

Tushar cares a lot about his students. His lectures are sometimes a bit difficult to keep up with as he goes so fast, but they are very helpful. The homework and exams are extremely difficult, but fair. This is the hardest class I've taken, but it taught me a ton.

It can be really hard to keep up with the pace of his class. He keeps rushing and skipping through chapters a lot. His lecture slides can be very inconsistent and often gets him confused during the lectures.

He is a great guy, but he simply cannot teach! He is fickle-minded and is always rushing through the lectures so much. He assumes that the students have already read everything beforehand, which can be very frustrating. I think he would be fine teaching lower-level classes, but not classes like these where you have to be very meticulous.

Really great prof who cares a lot for his students and their education. Does not want to tank student's grades and often curves scores. Lectures are informative and prof goes gives real-world examples which help to make the class feel like you're actually learning something relevant. Labs can be challenging but extra credit opportunities help.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A good professor who prepares the class carefully. His lecture is clear and very useful. But there are 5 labs, 3 quiz and 1 final exam.
Fantastic professor and human being!
I loved this guy. He made me love learning again!

Best professor I have had at Tech. The homeworks and exams may be a little tough but he always takes time to explain the answers in detail. It really shows that he cares about his students learning and not just passing the class. 100% take him if you can

Prof Kretzmer is a teacher who cares. His class in my opinion was a bit more difficult than other the other teachers who teach this section but i believe that to be for good reason. He doesnt just teach to try and get you to pass the class, He teaches in the hopes that you actually learn and apply the skills in the real world.
I cannot overstate the positive impact that this man has had on my life.
You can tell this guy cares about his students. He is always flexible with how he teaches. Honestly the best professor I've had at my time at tech
I was blown away by how effective Professor Kretzmer's lectures were. I highly recommend him, if you can get his class, do it.
Dr. Krishna is a caring prof but I really did not enjoy a class with her. The material itself was easy but the test were unnecessarily confusing and did not really test the knowledge of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was really boring and had some technology issues during her lectures often. If you've never had a stats class before you'll probably find her class hard but if you did, you'll already know a lot of the content. The studio session I had was a complete joke and I skipped it every week, dude was rude and not helpful.

she is so nice and cares so much about her students. very easy to get good grades bc homework has unlimited tries and you get to do revisions on all quizzes. the only issue is that the tests can be hard

Your grade is made up from 50% quizzes/HW and 50% tests. You get unlimited tries on HW and 2 tries on quizzes, these are very easy assignments and are basically directly what we covered in lecture. Unfortunately, the tests are very difficult and often have problems we barely discussed in class. So be aware of many curve balls on tests.

Although the class itself was not too difficult, her teaching style definitely made it rough. Throughout the semester it felt as if she was actively trying to work against us instead of helping us through. Sometimes it even seemed like she herself wasnt familiar with the course material which was frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's very sweet and class is sorta fun. She cares about students but can be pretty out of touch - grading criteria is very unclear, poor communication and class is on Discord (she doesn't use Canvas). You don't have to pay attention in lecture. It's all blog posts, projects, & papers so you don't have to read. You have to keep your camera on.

BEWARE: will center class around children's games/stories/development regardless of listing. Lots of group projects and expects creative physical artifacts with paper to support design decisions based on theory she's taught. Great about providing slides, readings, and resources. Super understanding, flexible, and approachable for help!
Assignments were useless. Didn't learn anything. Avoid taking her if you can. I had her for two classes in one semester and regretted it so hard
There was a lot of work that went into the projects, but she is very open to communicating if you are having trouble understanding things.
Do not waste your time with this class. Not only are there extremely long lectures but 4 individual projects and 2 group projects. That require hours of research and time.
Talks a lot about where he has previously worked. Impressive but makes lectures boring. Very interesting seeing how to learn the foundations of engineering.

Lectures are mandatory at 8 AM, and missing two costs a letter grade. His lectures can be shorten as most of it felt useless and time-consuming. He will go on and on about his experience and working at BMW so make sure your laptop is charge for his lectures, it will get boring. Overall, learned nothing in his lectures compared to the lab.

Only downside is that the class is mandatory and was 8 am in Scheller. But Kurfess was a chill lecturer. It felt like he cared about the students, especially right before the comp and after. Yes he talks about himself and his experience, he will repeat the same thing for every class, but its chill. And he doesn't grade you.

Overall good professor. Yes the lectures are at 8am, but no he doesn't pick or want that either. Clear criteria and description of projects and super friendly/accessible after classes. Pay attention to class when he discusses the report tables(eval matrix, HOQ, etc.). Given the class time, he was a great professor.

Most useless lecture ever. Attendance mandatory for an 8am where we did nothing. Only benefit is he doesn't affect your grade at all other than attendance so you can go, and ignore him, and do other work. Absolutely massive ego. He doesn't seem like a bad person he is just extremely boring, not well prepared for class (slideshows wrong), and vain.

Genuinely such a terrible professor for ME2110. Made attendance mandatory for his 8AM section, where if we missed more than 2 lectures, we got dropped a letter grade. The lectures were the worst. I couldn't tell you a single thing from them, they were so painfully unhelpful. He didn't affect grades for the course, but I hated him so much.

He's just the lecturing prof. so he doesn't have anything to do with grading but man is he boring to listen to. Constantly talking about his glory days and how he used to work for BMW and went to the pentagon once. His attendance policy is also way to strict (especially for an 8 am lecture that teaches you literaly nothing).

Kurfess was the lecture professor and the class is graded my lab Professor and TAs so Kurfess doesn't really do anything. His lectures are incredibly boring and he spends the entire time glazing himself and talking about how great he is and how he worked for BMW. he updated the attendance policy to be an absolute back breaker.
I had Kurfess for the 2110 lecture, meaning he had nothing to do with the grading. He was merely there to give notes on what the reports would be on and talk about how he used to work for BMW.

Dr. Kurfess is excellent. His lectures are very engaging, interesting and inspirational. I think he is very thorough with explanations and he offers so much professional perspective. The assignments really offered fun and effective ways to learn. I wish there were more classes available to take with him

Kurfess is just the overall ME 2110 professor which is one of the most time consuming, difficult, and stressful classes you'll ever take in your life (40+ hrs a week). His lectures teach you some things, but also consist alot of him talking about what he does in life which is sorta interesting. Your grade depends on your TA and lab instructor.
good professor, but the video presentations that he makes you do instead of the normal in person presentations that other sections do take a lot of time to make.

She literally doesn't teach anything. Half the class involves students presenting projects, and the other half involves a mix of random guest speakers or summarizing random articles. It's an easy class but so boring.

Literally don't learn anything in class. I had to write an essay where it asked to "make connections with things we learned in class" and I had so much difficulty since the professor doesn't teach anything.
The most boring class I've ever taken at both GT and in my life.

The class is extremely boring. The lecturer just yaps nonstop for over an hour and no one learns anything meaningful. She has a strict no-laptop policy and also seems passive-aggressive for no reason.
I really enjoy Neha's varied approach to the subject matter. She brought many new concepts, papers, and discussions into my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kumar's class was very eye-opening. She is really great at facilitating discussion, holding space for many viewpoints, and getting you to think critically. She also sees students as whole people and is very supportive and helpful if you are seeking ways to get involved in research or other avenues for responsible computing work.
Dr. Kumar's class is great! There's a bit of reading but that's basically the hardest part of her courses!
This professor truly cares about her students. I learned a lot this semester, as well as to prioritize teamwork and participation. I would absolutely recommend taking this course with Dr. Kumar.

Do not take this lecturer, they were demeaning to myself and two other students repeatedly. They were unorganised and blame shift onto students who don't agree with their views in class. I lost a lot of respect for the school and I reported the lecturer for harassing us in and out of class. Not sure anything was done. AVOID.

Firstly, she is too partial towards select viewpoints (e.g. Not Israel). Disinterested in class - hates that she has large class sizes and kept complaining she wants smaller class (unprofessional). Disorganized - asking large groups of students to present in short times. I haven't had a Professor who turned me off a subject before but she did.

She does not teach. Do not take her. She is extremely unprofessional and inappropriate. She lacks empathy and will basically spend time berating and cornering you in class. Classes were super boring and useless discussions where if you don't agree with her she will dislike you and it will reflect on your grade.

Her class was so heavy in participation. The class format was almost entirely discussion based on the books from class. Therefore, there were only 5 people who talked all class period. Her own biases made her disagree and shame those who did not believe the same things as her. I would not take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Firstly, she is too partial towards select students. Very disinterested in class - hates that she has 60+ students and keeps complaining she wants smaller class (puts us off). Very, very disorganized - asking groups of 13+ students to present in 15 minutes (when remote). I haven't hated a Professor before - but she is a first.

Neha Kumar is one of the best professors I've ever had. She really knows her stuff, encourages deep discussion, questions, and different ways of relating to the material, respects her students and sees them as whole human beings.
Prof Kumar is very friendly and forgiving to students situations. Theres a decent amount of reading and writing, but its overall a pretty easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's a wonderful professor who is passionate about the subject and that comes through in her lectures. She inspires her students to rethink their approach to CS, and understand social aspects of it. One of the most eye-opening courses I've taken at Tech!

Best discussion-based class I've been in. She moderates the talks really well. Lots of assigned readings (about 7 chapters each from 7 different books), but you can get by with lectures. Three papers and a group project: straight forward and simple. Great breather class & learn a lot! Highly suggest Prof Kumar!
She didn't even teach the class - the students literally did presentations all semester and taught themselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Neha is an incredible person and professor. Her class is designed to make you think about how technology impacts the world on a global scale. If you actually like to THINK instead of just showing up to lecture and going through the boring motions, then I would recommend taking Neha as her discussions make you ask deep and important questions!

Everything all of the other reviews have said is accurate.  I want to add the fact that I think the grading scheme is also particularly bad.  The reading and in-class quizzes make up way too much of the grade (like 45% combined I believe), usually only cover half of what she claims will be on them, and are graded with practically no partial credit.

Her lectures are dry and slow, slides are disorganized and messy, she does very little prep before class. She talks as though she knows what she's saying, but severely neglects to explain it at all for us struggling to learn it. Get ready to read the book, quizzes are 75% of your grade, the big projects are only 25%. Do NOT take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the first day, she admitted that she wouldn't teach us the material and would rather us teach ourselves from MIT OpenCourseWare and the textbook (Ross). For her Canvas files and lecture sheets that she writes on, it couldn't have be more disorganized and jumbled, plus her project requirements are a bit unclear. Very disappointing professor.
Just don't take her ever. She literally doesn't want to be there and admits that she gives MIT Open courseware, so she can just do examples in class.

Shoutout to MIT OpenCourseWare because they're the ones who really teach this class. Kuske doesn't do anything but example problems in class, and relies on students to self-teach new concepts via assigned recorded MIT lectures. She does not care much about students, so if you need help the TA is your best hope. At least she makes it an easy class.

The course straight up doesn't have a structure. She gives links to MIT courses (4000 dollars to take this course btw) that are too complex or unrelated to the course objectives, or use confusing notation. The HW's are completely unrelated to tests and the lectures fail too highlight important info, and she couldn't possibly have less enthusiasm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: NEVER take. Doesn't care about students. Makes you watch recorded MIT lectures outside of class and quizzes on them. Lectures are so unorganized, she is so scatterbrained about delivering notes, and is wrong about her own notes more often than not. Also, is just outright cut-throat over a relatively simple class. Don't take if you want a good grade

The class time is all discussion about the week's (long) readings, and participation in these discussions is 35% of the grade, so make sure you read. The few assignments we had were writing based, and while he did grade harshly there were draft stages & time for revision before the due date if you utilized it. I took as a freshman, don't do that
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Easy class if you keep up with the lectures and reading.
You have to be a pretty solid MC test taker to do well in this class. He is nice and accessible outside of class, but lectures do feel heavy and long sometimes. Overall, it was a good intro class.

Dalton is the best! Cares so much for his students and you can tell hes really passionate about what he teaches. There are many chances for extra credit, usually through class participation and an optional essay at the end of the course. His lectures are a little fast, but they follow the textbook closely so you can always refer back to it

Professor Lin cares about his students and encourages participation in his class, which counts for 20% of your final grade. Likes to give extra credit for this though. Tests are content to test apart from long answers which require some application of the material. The policy analysis is clutch here. Can miss lectures but I liked to go.

This is for the ME Satish Kumar, not the MSE (they seemed to combine their RMPs). Lecture was a bit boring, but thorough and easy to understand. The class was well-run and seamlessly organized. Very standard, fair, typical ME class. Solid option for heat transfer - it won't be a cake walk, but it will be fair, and your grade will be earned.

This professor is very kind and his tests are very fair. He actually made me like heat transfer. Go through his slides and take all his advices regarding testing seriously. Apart from that if you put in decent work, the class should be good.

Not sure why his rating is so low. He's passionate about his field and it definitely shows in his lectures. They're always fun and his smile reminds me of a chipmunk in the best possible way. The exams my semester (Fall 21) were based largely on the quizzes, which in turn were based on the homework which makes the class relatively easy too.

I was nervous to take Kumar after reading the other reviews, but he was a GREAT instructor... Gave excellent organized notes and he was flexible w/ deadlines! Class is manageable and was the easiest to comprehend out of thermo & fluids (IMO) but radiation was confusing. You will be smooth sailing w/ Kumar. My only complaint is he was a bit dull.

Easy A, Professor Kumar was a great teacher and super passionate about polymers and carbon fiber. It's hard to learn the content, but tests were basically HW questions so it's an easy A. Definitely started an interest for me in materials

Kumar is good for your gpa but not for your understanding. Kumar's tests and final are straight from the hw. The hw is released before the test so the class is an easy A. Kumar is also very enthusiastic about materials. Although his lectures arnt great and he can be a poor communicator. If you want an easy A but may not learn much, take kumar
Very good Prof. Extremely enthusiastic about MSE and cares about his students.

His lectures are easily one of the most boring things I have ever listened to. Test are very easy and based on the homework (which is optional but do it!!!) I wish this class was more interesting in lecture as it makes it a struggle to find the motivation to attend class.

Dr. Kumar is honestly such a nice guy. He is very passionate about the subject and always is fair with grading and assignments. To do well in his class, you just need to read the book and do the homework. If you do that, it is an easy A. I just wish his lectures were more helpful. He would only partially respond to people's questions.

Kumar is tough and not super personable, but he does care. It's hard to understand his lectures sometimes though. I ended up learning a lot on my own from the textbook, but his tests are definitely fair. And homework is not bad since he gives you the answers (numeric, not like the whole solution), so you can check your work.

Some people call it the hardest class ever taken just because of lack of introduction to the materials (pun intended) taught. Choose Kumar just to get the class over with and not stress too much. Exams are similar to homework, so cram those. Kinda boring lectures but his infectious enthusiasm about carbon fibers and MSE gets to you eventually.
All he wants its his students to do well and be engaged with the material. His tests are just like the homework, which its not mandatory.

He's a good professor. Homework is not taken up, and it's just to help you with the topics. Study the homework for the tests. His lecture slides are available when he starts the chapter, but going to class is a good idea. He has clicker questions and quizzes in class, but you can talk to people and look up answers. No crib sheets on tests.

Really enthusiastic about the subject. Uses powerpoint for lectures are and they are posted online. No mandatory attendance but this will change for his next class as less than a third of the class would regularly show up. 4 tests which are similar to the homework. Read the book and you'll be fine. The final is a copy and paste of the 4 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Really enthusiastic about MSE and teaching in general. Tests are pretty specific but you can do well in the class if you want, I was just lazy. Tests are like homeworks. Final was exactly like previous tests. Only 4 tests and the final so it sucks if you do bad on one.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: There are two Satish Kumars at tech. The one that teaches MSE 2001 is aweseome. He just wants us get us excited about the material and doesn't make us memorize details or do calculations. Tests are just like the homework and there are review sessions before each test that are really helpful.

Dr. Kumar talks and transcribes the text book on the white board for the entirety of class.  When you ask questions to clarify projects or homeworks his responses are beyond vague and only add to any confusion you may have already had.  He was did display lenience on a few project and HW deadlines but that is because the class begged for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He does not give good explanations  and his lectures are very dull. He has no enthusiasm for teaching and also  teaches word-for-word from the book. Going to his office hours does not help, as I often leave more confused than when I entered.  Avoid at all cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really boring professor. Teaches straight from the book and you have to attend lecture or else you will fail the class as there is mandatory attendance. Tests are pretty easy and straight forward although the averages were in the 60's. Projects are difficult and he barely gives you enough time to finish them. Tough grader.
Boring. He teaches exactly what is on the book and assigns hard projects. Does not give you enough time to complete projects.

Dr. Kumar is a very great teacher. He tries to make the material more understandable by talking about his research,  demonstrations, and practical applications. His class is fairly easy if you do the homework and the practice tests he posts online. He is very approachable in his office hours and even after class. You'll learn a lot from his class.

Very flexible and understanding. Has a very clear and reasonable scheduling of exams/homework, so it's easy for students to keep track of the course. Not very tech savvy but I've personally never had a problem regarding that. Be prepared to participate!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've taken multiple Japanese classes with her. Assignments are always easy and she's generous with late assignments/partial credit. If you finish every assignment and go to class you will get an A even if you don't put much effort into assignments. She is eager to help and gets to know students on an individual level. Feedback is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, one of my favorites here. I really admire how much feedback she gives on each and every homework assignment. She really wants you to succeed.

Taken over the summer, 3 hour lectures are never fun. She removed one whole section from the LING curriculum so I would strongly advise taking this class over the summer. The long lectures every day make it easy and necessary to stay on top of the work. Just get things done and study the day before and you can get an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Alright professor, very nice. Whole semester is planned out (homeworks and tests) which is nice. In class, she calls on people to answer questions alone but will help you if you don't know how to answer it. Not the best in-class grammar explanations.

Took this legend for both 2020 and 6133 and I can definitively say that I did in fact get hired at AMD.

Also, if you take his 2020 it will be the hardest version of 2020, but well worth the headaches.
Quite possibly the best professor I've ever had -- so passionate about the subject material and teaching in general!!!

I took his class a few years ago and felt obligated to come back and leave a review because his lectures were phenomenal and really sparked my interest in EE. His exams were memorably tough but they were honestly fun.
I absolutely loved having Sung Kyu. Probably the best professor. His lectures were extremely helpful (the most any lecture has ever been for me).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are good but he teaches you things that are unnecessarily complicated and ECE trivia essentially. Basically anything designed to trick you up.

I had a rough year outside of class and had absolutely no desire to go to any of my classes, but this man's ability to lecture made me actually want to go to class. I've never once had a prof. were I've enjoyed the lectures quite like his. He is beyond passionate and caring about his students.

While this class is very hard, the professor is amazing. He is much harder than the other professors for the subject but he is so passionate about the topic and can make it fun. Office hours are a huge life saver so please take advantage. Every exam has a curve and even though it was hard and challenging, I am happy that I had him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class can be considered a "weed-out" class. It's super rough if you miss one class. The exams were not always the same as the problems the professor went over in class, which sucked. I recommend getting a study group to complete the homework assignments together. He's super passionate about what he teaches and super helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lim is incredibly energetic and is very thorough with his lectures. His exams can be very tough, but will prepare you super well for upper-level ECE courses.

His exams are difficult because his lectures are superficial. He constantly makes mistakes and goes off-topic all the time. I have never seen a prof care so less about his students(try asking him questions after class, but the TA was great). Make sure to check everything from attendance to grades, cause later on he will blame it on you! AVOID!!!!

Best prof at Tech so far! Lectures breeze by very quickly the way he engages the interesting material with the students. Grading is heavily determined by tests - be ready to take up the challenge to make yourself work for your grade, but you will learn LOTS. Dr. Lim is super knowledgeable about what he's talking about. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures, homework and tests slightly on the tougher side, but the grades are curved. Definitely recommended.

Lectures can be fun if you can excuse his constant fickle-mindedness and laziness. He will say that we won't cover this topic, only to cover it at the last moment for a few minutes and then have a very difficult exam question on that topic. Very unorganized and takes multiple weeks to grade. You won't know your grade till final grades are posted.

He is an amazing lecturer and explains it in a way that is easy to understand, so make sure you go to and engage with every lecture. Exams can be quite difficult compared to the material gone over in class, but everything is curved relative to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Funny and cares about his students. Pretty good at lecturing and ensuring that all his students understand what's going on. Tests can be short and difficult, but he curves so that most of them have around a mid B average. Only downside is he sometimes doesn't go into enough detail on certain topics, which is a little annoying as an ECE major.

Pros: - Very engaging Lectures - Curves every exam Cons: - He'll teach you the most basic concepts, while his exams are VERY difficult - Very unorganized (Posts assignments at the last minute, Changes exam dates multiple times, Grading often takes multiple weeks, etc.) You will be fine if you study a lot outside the class and way ahead of time.
One of the best profs I've ever had!

Takes the time to explain the material. Even if the class is online just watch his lectures or attend his lectures and you will need almost everything to do your assignments and get good results in your tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: By far the hardest professor I have taken but also one of my favorite lecturers. ECE2020 is typically an easy class but the engaging Lim really emphasizes optimization and certain topics more, which makes it harder but better understanding. Take if you want to master but are ready to struggle (for easy A, take Raychoud or Kev).Lim curves everything
Take him if you can! His lectures are so engaging and you will learning a lot of fun stuff. Definitely the best for ECE 2020

I really loved Prof Lim's lectures and how he's passionate about answering student questions and giving them a glimpse into real world applications. However (at least for me) his tests are extremely hard and are weighted extremely heavily. Also, the tests and final are graded on a curve so you won't know what grade you have until the very end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fully explains every concept so that the subject matter becomes intuitive. The exams combine concepts or relate current material to old material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Attendance doesnt count for much but the lectures are much more useful than just the slides. His lectures are entertaining and has the whole class laughing. I definitely enjoyed taking the class.
Make sure you understand EVERYTHING on his slides. He makes you work for your grade. It's that simple. You have to give it your best to pass this class. Getting a C will be harder than you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor.

Lim is a good prof, who is easy to pass, but hard to get an A /B in. He curves down if grades are too high, but most tests will fall in the B/A range. You have to study a lot outside of class to keep up with other students, but Lim does a great job teaching. HW can be bad if you don't check with others, so form a study group. Better than Schimmell.
The best 2020 professor available. Fantastic lecturer and knows every ounce of material. This is his only none graduate level class right now so if you have the opportunity take him.

Dr. Lim is awesome, but challenging.  I'm sure 2020 is not the hardest class, but he made it pretty difficult.  His lectures are very clear, but his tests are hard.  He expects you to be able to expand on what you have learned to solve problems that you have definitely not been over.  Probably an effective challenge but a challenge nonetheless.

I really liked Dr. Lim. He is really good at explaining and he always had a positive attitude. That being said, do not expect an easy A or even B with him. The material for 2020 is not terribly challenging, but his exams are very difficult and they will not be what you will expect.  I understood the material but still made a C in his class.
Explains concepts well and goes over practice tests before the exams, but be prepared for some curveballs

No textbook required for this class. Teaches very clearly but makes test extremely difficult. If people do well on test he will tell you he will make them harder and does. Test are nothing like example exams he provides
Great professor. He can teach the material pretty well. However, he can make the tests more challenging than necessary.

The course was easy and interesting. But he is not a very consistent grader. Just gives out A's to people who do the project instead of taking the final exam (even if results are wrong). Gives out poor grades to students who missed out the average by a fraction of a point/students who got below average in the midterm.  That's just painful.
Lectures are always very clear and well-paced. You will get a lot out of his class, which is important as this material crops up time and time again throughout ECE.
Drop everything your doing and take this guy's class! This guy will teach it well and you'll know the material.

Excellent prof all around. Approachable, explains well, nice guy. Course is sometimes hard but he makes it very clear what he expects you to know. He also does good to make sure you do learn the material. He'll feed you if you fill out the course survey!

She is such an amazing lecturer! She explains concepts very well in 3100 that made certain topics just stick better in my mind compared to when the other professors taught. She is also very caring and challenges students to believe that they know a lot more than they think in PSS.

She taught in combination with Michelle LaPlaca (who was terrible) but Professor Ross was super nice and accomodating. She was interested in the well-being of her students. BME 3100 is a super hard class though so like beware anyway, but she was the better lecturer of the two.

I'm surprised there aren't more ratings for her on here. She's hands down the best professor I've had! She's super engaging, she uses core concepts and takes several checkpoints through the lecture to make sure everyone's on board, and she's very encouraging. Attendance is optional but counts toward your grade. Final can replace lowest test grade.

Really great professor. Lectures are really good but she also has good recorded lectures for every concept. Some HWs are hard but the grading isn't bad. The tests were graded really nicely but there are 4 exams besides the optional final which was a big annoying. Also final exam could only replace all exams, so it would become 80% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lectures that really helped understand concepts. Would bring in physical models to help demonstrate different beam elements. Homework was graded by completion, and final was optional if you scored a 92 average on midterm exams.

She was an excellent lecturer; she'd explain everything step by step, even topics from previous classes like statics. I would say stay on top of homeworks; in my semester, they were graded for completion so I slacked off a bit and would panic and cram before exams. But the exams were always easier than the homeworks. The final can also be dropped.

The only bad things about Dr. Stewart is that she makes homework due at 5 PM and that the class is very homework dense. Aside from that she is a VERY good lecturer, and makes everything make a lot of sense. Just attend the lectures, do the homework yourself, and you'll most likely leave with an 'A' and a very good understanding of defbods.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, the origami portion of it at least. The project part of the class seemed to only vaguely connect to the actual class and was more work than the origami part. Professor Stewart was great as a lecturer but I wish we could have done more origami.
Gave practice exams/study guide very similar to exams, always reviewed before exams and prepared us well. Exams weren't bad, she told you exactly what would be on it.

Oe of the best lecturers I've had at Tech! Dr. Stewart is great at explaining core concepts and has awesome handwriting (often uncommon in math-heavy classes at GT). She posts helpful review videos on Canvas, and her exams are very fair.

She was so unorganized. Super condescending and rude towards students. Unengaginf lectures. quizzes were a lot of memorization. 

If possible take Dr Dai not Stewart

Dr. Stewart was an okay professor, I just think that this class didn't give much opportunity to teach. It was really cool to learn origami principles, but lectures felt unnecessary and disorganized at times. Still a really easy class though, and all 3 professors were chill. Recommend taking despite it being slightly insufferable for 3 hours.

Doctor Stewart was a very kind professor who wanted you to succeed in the class. The homeworks were a lot more difficult than the test and class material. Tests were very fair and she made sure you were well prepared. Would curve if the class average was too low. Posted really helpful review videos on Canvas.
Tests were fair and followed the practice tests and review packets. Homework was fair in amount and difficulty. Lectures were good.

Really great professor, but the labs are extremely difficult. They're very writing-heavy, you do them individually, and it's due after a week at noon. Lab reports get several points off for minor mistakes (graded by TAs). Quizzes (tests) are straightforward and mostly memorization. DO NOT COMBINE WITH ANOTHER LAB CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Stewart is a caring & adaptable prof. She taught 3020 bc the original professor wasn't available, & she did a great job preparing each lecture. She looped in her own interesting research into lectures, & listened to our feedback. The reports take ~10 hours each week, but the labs are fun! Follow the report guidelines, START EARLY, & proofread!
Very good at teaching and the concepts seemed quite easy as a result. Class had weekly HWs, 2 midterms, and a final. Great professor, take her if you can.

One of my favorite professors at Tech. She is a very fair grader on exams as long as you know what you are doing. Her extra credits are based on HW, and she has practice exams for each exams. The exams are quite fair, if you understand the practice exam, you'll do well. Just make sure to study 1-2 weeks ahead of time for the Final Exams.

Dr. Stewart is a great lecturer & provides many resources for her students to succeed (extra practice exams & pre-recorded lectures). Her exams tested my knowledge appropriately and on top of that she is a fair grader. The only difficult part of this class was the homework; some questions couldn't be answered without extra help from the TAs.

Dr. Stewart is very respectable. She uploads previous tests before each exam. She also has tons of videos online for covering each topic which is very helpful. Odd questions can pop up on exams, but her grading is very reasonable.

Stewart is a great choice for DefBods. Her lectures were always pretty informative and engaging for an 8 am class. She also posts her virtual lecture videos online if you don't feel like going to class, which are just as good. She makes sure to go over how to tackle each type of problem, which helped a ton for tests. No complaints from me.
Great at teaching. She even managed to keep me awake for most of the classes despite it being an 8am.

Dr. Stewart's lectures were always pleasant. Her course is very organized and informative. There is weekly HW with bonus opportunities, but I never looked at them after submitting-- Her notes and practice exams were sufficient for studying. If you don't enough time to complete an exam prob, write down the steps you would take to solve. Kind grader!
Super clear and well delivered lectures, and there are recordings from pervious years. Dr. Stewart makes it as easy as possible to succeed. Very fair HW and tests.

I was excited to take a class with her but was left kind of disappointed. She had potential to be my favorite professor but at least for the grad level course, she took forever to grade things and give feedback for improvements. It was hard to reach her for questions and communication in general in the class was a mess.
Really great online lectures. Super easy to follow and understand. She makes her expectations really clear and helps to make equations sheets with precise criteria for what exams will cover.

I think it's fair to say Dr. Stewart has been my best professor at Tech. Her lectures are very clear and concise. The class is not difficult because she teaches you a general process for each type of question that could be asked. The homework questions come from the textbook, but she does provide the questions so textbook is an additional resource.

Professor Stewart was absolutely amazing; her attention to detail, compassion, and overall ability was unparalleled. She gave it her all, exhausting every effort to make this class as understandable as possible which is VERY hard. Her tests are very fair; her easygoing yet understanding nature commands respect from everyone. Would do it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Stewart has definitely been one of my best professors I've had at tech. Her lectures are incredibly helpful in understanding the course material. She is clear on what she expects on exams and homework. Definitely take her for def bods if you can.

Dr. Stewart is one of the nicest and most approachable professors I've had at Tech. She is very organized and her assignments are reasonable. There are quizzes instead of traditional midterm exams and you have several chances to retake them and get 100%. She is fantastic; take her for anything you can.

One of my favorite teachers during my time at Georgia Tech. Great at explaining concepts, provides excellent material to prepare for exams, gives fairly clear and easy tests, and is just an amazing person in general. Also holds coffee hours to just talk about things to get to know her; One of the nicest human beings you'll meet.
Very clear lectures with a lot of passion. Dr. Steimle is the GOAT.
Spectacular professor, probably the strongest I have had so far. Dr. Steimle has a lot of passion and breaks down difficult concepts clearly.

I have never enjoyed a class as much as I enjoyed this one. Her class was incredibly enjoyable and the weekly study sessions she hosted were beneficial. If you have the opportunity to take this class, you should hope she is your professor.

Best professor I've had at GT. Lectures are thorough and make concepts easy to grasp if you put in the work. Homework is hard but great exam prep. Exams are heavily weighted; midterms were easy, final was difficult (I suspect they apply a curve - they dont give us the final back). Group simulations were boring and time-consuming with random groups

Dr. Steimle is one of the best professors at Georgia Tech. Her lectures are exceptional and she provides plenty of help resources as well as very interactive office hours. The class itself wasn't hard at all, but you just need to make sure you don't get lost and she makes sure to put enough resources for that to be totally on you. Take her class!!!
Genuinely the best professor you will have at Tech.
Incredible course, she is super interesting and well organized. Great lecturer, gives really helpful examples and makes it easy to succeed.
Very engaging and interesting class. Makes stochastics really interesting and teaches the subject matter in very engaging ways.
Absolute GOAT of a professor, highly recommend.
Very knowledgable professor who is great at presenting the information in the course! Homework is super heavy but she was available during office hours to work on it.

Dr. Steimle's 3232 class is one of my favorite classes I've taken at Tech. She clearly cares a lot about the content of the course, and she literally gets a smile on her face whenever students ask a question. Really great lectures, building up concepts from the ground level so that the intuition behind everything covered is very clear.

Steimle's slides are easy to follow, and her homework is fairly representative of her exams. she is available outside of class and answers questions patiently and with kindness. it is clear that she cares about the well-being and success of her students, and she is easily one of the best profs i've had at tech!

Dr. Steimle is one of the best professors in the IE department. She is clearly very interested in the topic, and makes the class easy to understand and engaging. Despite being a difficult course, Steimle makes it clear what you will be tested on and is a fair grader. Unsure where the poor reviews are coming from.

Great professor. Easy to understand. Available for questions outside of class. Exams are tough but fair. It is true that she will report people to the academic integrity office if they are caught cheating on exams, so if you want someone who will let you get away with cheating, take this class from someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very bad professor! You can be sure that she will do anything in her power to make you uncomfortable.

Prof. Steimle was a great professor! I felt that she cared about the class content and was extremely well prepared in terms of the lectures and I love that she provided lecture video recordings. Exams were challenging but if you understand class content well, it's good. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: What she lacks in empathy she makes up for in her lack of understanding. Definitely would not recommend taking if you have the option to. She instills a bad class room environment.

She is the worst professor that someone can take. She does not care about her student's well being and will do anything to prove that she is superior. She does not care about the student voice or opinion, it is very hard to discuss with her and you can be sure that will show you no availability for you. Honestly do not take her !

Phenomenal professor.  I can see how the workload can be challenging, but tests/assignments are fair and lectures are very helpful for learning the material.  Clearly caring and goes the extra mile for her students, as long as you're willing to put in a reasonable amount of effort :P

as mentioned in other reviews, she just lacks any empathy and understanding towards students. She doesn't accommodate students at all and seems to believe that her rules should take absolute precedence over a student's well being and ability to succeed.

I felt that there was a lack of understanding and support for students. The communication and feedback were not as clear as I would have liked, and I believe that more empathy and responsiveness to students' concerns would enhance the learning experience. This is by far the worst professor I had in my life and I would never advice to anyone.

Easy to follow lectures due to her delivery. She would give out online quizzes after the lectures to make sure you're keeping up with the content, but they're only a small portion of your grade. She also drops a handful of those end-of-class quizzes, so doing them feels very rewarding. Homework might be tedious, but they're helpful for the tests.

Steimle is one of the best ISYE professors I've had at Tech. Lectures are great, and up to 2% of extra credit is added to your final grade if you complete most extra credit assignments. Tests are fair, and as long as you pay attention in lectures and keep track of class material, it should be a fairly easy class.

Steimle was a great professor for stochastics. Great lectures with lots of examples and pretty straightfoward to follow. She was very prepared and organized as well. Lots of homeworks and assignments for this class, but she offers extra credit too. Exams were challenging but manageable if you prepare well, and TAs were great during office hours.

Accessible. Invites Qs/class participation. Does practice Qs & study sessions. Understanding of circumstances. Weekly HW relevant to tests. Has online "quiz", 1-5 Qs abt lecture (attendance).  Allowed 8 drops. Gives video recordings/stream. HIGHLY recommend. Taught in organised way, content makes sense/industry applicable. Knows how to teach WELL.

Steimle really cares about us learning the material. She goes at a good pace so lectures are digestible. Lecture slides are great & if you take notes along with her in class you're golden. There was lots of homework in the beginning, but if you stay ahead of it and go to study sessions it's manageable. Tests are tricky but not totally unwarranted.

Would also put Lots of Homework and Caring, Professor Steimle was an excellent professor. Followed syllabus, homework was structured like most 2027 classes but easier and with a drop. Online lecture quizzes were short and easy and effectively counted as "attendance". Lectures clearly explained course concepts + lots of application to industry.

Caring professor who is genuinely interested in the material. She was a bit heavy-handed with assignments early in the semester, but that changed after receiving feedback. I took ISYE 3232 earlier with a different professor and I had to drop it. Luckily, Professor Steimle made the material much more clear, and I did much better this time!

One of the best professors I've had at Tech! She really cares about her students and wants everyone in her class to succeed. You get tons away from her lectures and you pretty much understand most of the topics after them. She does leave a lot of homework that is quite difficult but her tests are fair and she is very helpful at her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professor I've had at Tech who really cares about students and wants everybody to do well. Her lectures are very clear and you can understand most stuff after the lecture. There's a quiz after each class but they are pretty easy. Homework can be challenging, but she offers help during office hours. Exams are extremely fair.

BMED1000 is very easy but prof was unreasonable and not accommodating, unclear instructions in class and largely group dependent. Attendance mandatory and large part of grade. You do not get to choose your groups and the organization of this course is not good

Dr. Christian provides an amazing overview into cell physiology and the "micro" scale of medicine. From great, recorded lectures to providing fair tests and HW Assignments, BMED 3600 is slightly easier than other BME classes, but still allows you to learn a lot. Loved the in-class Project and Poster Presentation bolstering Gene Therapy knowledge

BMED 1000 is generally a very boring class. Dr. Christian taught all of the content that needed to be taught, but kind of guided you along in the semester-long project rather than giving real feedback.

Took the early short version, so it was a lot crammed into 5 weeks. Go to lecture, as there is both a lot of content covered and a participation grade. Weekly quizzes were also a little hard, but there was also a final research paper that balanced out the grade. 

Dr. Christian is the best lecturer in the BME department, and made a hard class fun!

Prof Stendig is a lovely guy. His lectures were interesting if you listened a good bit, they were interactive (he's running up and down the stairs of Howey like he's 30, he's pushing 70) and the course was very interesting and organized. Would take again 100%

Rambles and doesn't keep track of time. Disorganized and doesn't communicate assignment grading criteria or expectations. Honestly it just comes down to if he likes you or not, which stems from entertaining his ego. The canvas is a mess, we barely use the textbook. Pop tests - he doesn't put assignment deadlines in the syllabus. Really out of touch

He made sure he recieved feedback and used it to become a better professor. Very willing to help students get credit back on assignments and did test corrections for exams. Also just entertaining in class. He had attendence as extra credit. Overall made the class enjoyable

He cares a lot and takes feedback which he reacts to quickly.  Had a couple knowledgeable entrepreneurs, investors, and lawyers talk to us.  Did a class project giving us experience in pitching and coming up with problems/solutions.  Provided great resources for us to learn ourselves.  Easy class teaching new perspective, not much knowledge tho.
Really interesting class, and does his best to keep things contemporary when possible. Absolutely recommend taking, if you have the choice.
If you read the textbooks and do the homework all the tests are very easy.

Prof. Stendig is a great guy, he definitely cares about his students. I didn't really love his lecture style, so I did most of my learning from the textbook which was pretty effective. Offers lots of Extra Credit opportunities (atendance is extra credit) and test corrections, which I highly recommend doing.

His lectures didn't vibe with me. I ended up textbook grinding the class since the lectures didn't help me with the class. Overall, the copious amounts of extra credit and help he provides to excel in the course make up for the somewhat lacking lectures. I overall enjoyed the class and think he was a great guy but the topic for me was just bad.
He is a phenomenal Professor, deeply cares about his students, is very passionate about economics, and is frankly hilarious. Gives a lot of extra credit and second chances too. 10/10

He cares about his students, is a very funny guy. He is older and likes older music which he plays at the strat of every class. The class itself is easy, if you have taken any econ class before. Only two test which were worth 45% of final grade. the other 55% is from easy assignments every week that actually help. Definitely recommend taking.

This professor cares very much for his students and offers as much extra credit and help as he can. The class itself was more difficult than it needed to be because there were only 2 tests and they were very heavily weighted which is what made the final grading stressful and difficult. Overall an amazing teacher.

Absolutely take English with Professor Lee. He is such a caring and sweet professor, and he is so passionate about what he does. As long as you follow his rubric and complete every assignment, you will get full points and will enjoy the class. Lots of fun group projects are assigned and the classroom environment feels very enjoyable.

If you have the opportunity to take him for 1102 do it. Professor Lee is extremely nice and cares about his students. He is very considerate in all aspects of the course and understands that students have busy lives outside of the class. If you every have a problem with the class reach out to him and he will help you make accommodations.

Dr. Lee is the sweetest professor ever. Lectures did move a bit slow, but he provided a lot of in class work time. I barely had much work for this class aside from major assignments. He is also an easy grader, as long as you follow his feedback, you get 100. I highly recommend him for ENG 1102.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's one of the best professors you could ask for, very sweet and genuinely cares about students being able to understand what he's teaching. Fair workload and is very considerate of your time by providing grace periods for assignments. Cares about input from students and is very passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Lee is an amazing teacher!! He is one of the most caring and sweetest professors. He is always willing to help his students. He is a very lenient grader and doesn't assign much work. Everyone should take him!!
Sweetest professor ever, extremely caring and kind to his students. Fair coarse load, lots of group work, fun class. You want him!!
Very accomodating professor, work is easy and doesn't take much time. One of the sweetest professors, go to him if you have any questions or concerns. Recommend taking him for LMC 3403!
Seungho was an amazing and engaging lecturer. This class was super easy and helpful for areas such as resumes and public speaking.

Mike was a good professor and great guy. He meets all of his students where they are and especially for an English class, he does a pretty decent job to not make the lectures too boring. I would def take him again tho. Tough grader fs but if u try a little bit you'll get the A

I think it is impossible not to get an A in the class, as long as you turn everything in. Was generous on grading especially participation (just let us grade ourselves for that). Was easy going and responsive whenn questions were asked outside of class

If you show up to class and make an effort to get feedback from him, it shouldn't be hard to get a good grade in the class. He gives some readings but some are videos or other sources, so it's not that bad. The group projects can be a bit tough but he's a fair grader, and he's flexible with deadlines. The attendance policy is also pretty lenient.

He was a pretty chill teacher. No tests, but 4 major project grades, and 2 of them are group projects. Lots of reading had to be done outside of the class though and around 5-6 discussion posts throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lacey was a very poor lecturer, most of his lectures I didn't gain much. Essentially you teach yourself to get a good grade and he relies heavily on you reading the textbook front to back before each lecture. He also makes mistakes here and there in the lectures, overall underwhelming.

class was not too bad, he's a good teacher. just make sure you understand the hw problems well and youll be good for the exams. there is an in class assignment everyday but it is a participation grade

Overall, I had a lot of fun in this class! The tests are worth a lot and are not the easiest I've taken, but you have a lot of resources available (textbooks, officer hours, etc) and he's always happy to talk and offer help or discuss random math things. We love Dr. Lacey he's the goat - would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lacey is an amazing professor! The class isn't a walk in the park, but if you put in the effort, you'll get the results you want! Always open to talking with students and helping them whenever necessary.

I kind of had a hard time following him at times so I definitely had to do a lot more studying outside of class. However, I think he was a pretty lenient and generous grader. I thought the stories he shares about his life experiences were interesting. He gave a lot of homework but also it was useful for studying. Attendance is part of the grade!!!
Lectures can be hard to follow. Otherwise, happy to help if it is sought, and is a very generous grader, with less emphasis on minutia than understanding.
Great Professor. Tests are weighted heavily but you will do well if you study for them and he is a generous grader. Would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests determine 85% of the grade. Tests are hard, and lectures are not useful.
Only depended on exams, 85% of the grades are exams. Making intro level math class extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 3 exams (2 22.5% midterms, 1 35% final) make up 80% of the grade, so it'd be hard to recover. His teaching of the content was fine as he knows his stuff. He often made small mistakes; he doesn't like being called out on said mistakes. Very light on homeworks and is a generous exam grader- all things considered, keep up and you'll be fine!
He acts like he is on tenure. 10% off of hw if you do it completely wrong. Easy A as long as you can do a course without needing a professor.

Very little feedback, homework completion based but does not give back answers, does not like when you point out errors in class, exams much harder than practice, light grader but don't expect to actually learn anything in his class.

Professor Lacey cares about the success of individual students! He is one of the nicest professors I have ever had at GT, and his course gives a rigorous understanding of real analysis. I initially failed this course, and finally got a C, and he still told me I'm a wonderful student at the end of it all.

Very nice and understanding, attendance is not mandatory and all lectures livestreamed, he also records review videos afterwards, however, lectures can be a bit dry and it feels he doesn't explain concepts/intuition for a few things taught in class. Tests are easy as long as you have done the homework.

Look if you're good at math, take him. If not, avoid. He pulls numbers out of thin air, makes lots of mistakes, doesn't really teach concepts. I had to basically teach myself the entire course, without knowing where to even begin or what the concepts even were. Never took stats in high school, so I was just lost for the entire semester.

While he clearly wants students to succeed, Lacey can be a very dry lecturer and didn't do a great job at getting the intuition for linear algebra across (mostly power points about how to perform calculations). Grade was exam-heavy; exams were fair, but make sure to do lots of practice problems.
I enjoyed the class. I had to study quite a bit but it was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's an ok lecturer, the lectures will teach you how to do problems but the concepts require reading the book (midterms are concept heavy). Your grade is basically your 3 midterms (tests worth 70% total). I ended missing the A border by 1 question on the midterm which sucks. He did not bump my grade up, which is respectable (fairness).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dual Enrollment student taking first ever college class. And, quite literally, the worst class ive EVER taken. Did not teach/explain anything well, took lectures straight out of the textbook (which wouldnt be bad IF he took time to actually read it), and often confused himself working his own problems and asks you, the confused student for help.

Expect the following in each lecture: 1. "Oops! Did I make a mistake?" 2. "How many minutes do I have left? I don't think I can finish this example." And yet in his own words, he is "a leading expert in Fourier series." Year in, year out, despite constant critiques, Lacey never attempted any improvement - always coming unprepared for the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He messes up in examples and confused me right from the start. To do well, read the textbook, do the MML hw, and the TAs are usually amazing. I pretty much never went to a single lecture, but watched many of the recitations. This class is one I definitely struggled in because it was basically self taught. Good, nice guy though. Tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Oof worst math class Ive ever taken and I like math

Lectures were awful. It was extremely difficult to get the important points out of his lecturing. He often wasted 10 min at the beginning of class talking about irrelevant info such as hurricanes, voting, etc. Then he would complain that we didnt have enough time to finish that section in the chapter. He rarely went back to finish them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He doesn't really go too much into details in his lectures.

Dr. Lacey is funny and cares about his students but his lectures were difficult to understand. If you zone out for one second youve lost the topic. Sometimes he would start a question get excited start another problem and never finish the first problem.
Sometimes during lectures he'd solve the example questions wrong, and just say "I forgot how to do it" or he'd just rush through it and not finish the question Seems nice tho!

Lacey is in general a good guy and I believe he does genuinely care about his students, however teaching just isnt his thing. There were times when he would be going through example problems and he would get stuck in the middle of them, give up, and move on. We missed a lot of important concepts this way. I pretty much taught myself using mathlab.

Decently good lecturer, and he cares a lot about his students. Exams weren't hard. I'd venture to say that 1554 with Lacey is easier and less work than several 1553 sections... only downside is that he tends to teach at 8 am

I took this class as a distance student, so I might not have had the full experience as a campus student. Lacey in general, is very thorough on some concepts while at the same time skips over some important concepts. This was the first year he made a final, and it was EXTREMELY hard. However, he is a kind and understanding teacher, and compensated.

Take what I say with a grain of salt. The course constantly changes. First off, he's a great person. Tests are fair (the sample tests are representative of the actual thing), homeworks do help, and Piazza is amazing. Ask for help early, and you won't have to later. Biggest regret? Not asking for help early on. Lacey is an amazing person.

I am still in his linear algebra class. He has these awkward moments where he asks the class a question and nobody responds. He's a nice guy and he fully understands the content and he can convey the content well. He does a good job of conveying the definitions of terms and how to solve problems. Also check his wikipedia page. Yes. He has one.
The class is easy you can self study and not attend lecture and still get a good grade.
Really dry, only talks about theory and never really applies any of the ideas
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Lacey really does care about his students. He is not the best lecturer, but is really helpful in answering questions. Practice quizzes were a big help for actual quiz questions.

Prof. Lacey is one of the best professor I had at Tech. He is a great man and an extremely knowledgable professor. Unlike other ratings said, he explains the material well, and really motivates you to explore further. His 4 midterms partitioned the classes to 4 sections which is actually a really good set up.

Dr. Lacey is a great man; he genuinely tries to improve the lives of students as well as helping to fix the racial and gender divide in mathematics. Unfortunately, he can't lecture very well, but the class is easy enough to get an A if you just read the textbook.

Michael Lacey is one of those teachers who knows his stuff, but has trouble getting it across to his students. That being said, his tests are so easy, if you know how to do the practice quizzes, you will do well on the real thing. Final exam for us was literally just another of 5 quizzes, and it wasn't cumulative. He can be unintentionally funny.

Not the most vivacious guy out there, but his lectures got across the material well enough to me. If you are math savvy, you should do fine in his class. If you have struggled in the past with college math, you will probably do poor in his class. Seek a different professor if you need a really good lecturer to learn math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: not very good at lecturing which makes material that should be very easy feel much more difficult
He isn't a good lecturer, the tests are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bad lecturer - don't take his class

He's not the best lecturer, but he does genuinely care about the students. He is there if you ask for help, and he does his best to help when you do ask. His lectures often had some sort of participation such as in class assignments, so attendance was mandatory. Otherwise, his tests are a tad on the tough side, though he does curve if necessary.

He is very smart, and i'm sure makes a wonderful researcher, but is rather lacking as a professor. His lectures were confusing, and his tests were impossible, but the quizzes were easy, and on occaision quizzes were based soley on attendence.
Not the best way to start at Tech.  While this class is hard regardless, I would recommend looking for another section.

This techer is by far the worst that i have had in a while. His lectures confused me even though i have done the stuff before. I definately do not recommend Prof. Lacey to anybody...Had a really good TA though...Leslie Myles.

I've taken calc before and I got totally lost in this class. Homework, lectures and tests are like three different classes, none relevant to each other. The test questions are the hardest possible questions he could ask. Does not collect homework.

This is probably the worst calc 1 teacher at GT. It seems as if he prides himself on failing incoming freshman. He cannot teach at all and is the very definition of a researcher/HORRIBLE teacher. His lectures are often so complex that half the students do not even attend them anymore. I definitely DO NOT recommend.
You're definitely better off studying by yourself. Just hope for a good TA (for recitation)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pray to god you have a good Recitation TA, because the explanations coming from him leave you more confused than when you started. No idea why he chose to teach if he simply just restates stuff on slides and acts like each class is review and not actual learning. Take anyone else, or simply take 2026 when you have a very light sem is my advice.

2026 is a difficult class. You have to put a ton of time into it regardless of the professor but he just makes it worse, it sucks. Like someone said lectures are very unproductive and shallowly go over things rather than explaining. The structure of the class is bad, tests are mostly bad and pedantic, and he makes it no better! Get ready

His lectures have to be the worst I've ever experienced. This course is on the harder side, but Dr. Lee can't explain a single concept clearly; all of his lectures feel like a review session, and he teaches like you already know everything about the topics. Might as well read the whole textbook. He cares about students, but absolutely can't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I just took his class and got a C average. I could have done better by working harder to understand the course, but I might as well not have even attended the lectures. His teaching style really doesn't communicate concepts or expectations well. You'll succeed best if you treat it like a self-study. Overall, I would recommend exploring other profs.
I feel bad giving him just a 3, because he really does care about his students but he cannot teach well at all. Hopefully you have a good TA .

His class is hard, but he will always take time to meet with you and discuss course concepts. He emails back within the hour and always has time for his students. He teaches a hard course so his reviews are low.

Going to lectures wont really help you, most material is learned from TA recitation. Lee would make his tests super long to a point where it is impossible to finish on time. Make sure to do all Hw and labs as it will help your grade. Be ready to learn the material by yourself when taking this class.

His lectures aren't that helpful and the tests were very difficult. How much you learn is pretty dependent on your TA. He also kind of insulted us after the entire class did poorly on one of our exams saying we just needed to use our brains and not our calculators.

The difficulty of his 2026 class comes less from the conceptual aspects, but instead from the disorganization of the lectures and the unclear explanations. Be ready to self teach concepts and try to make sense of things on your own. Also, tests are very time based, so train yourself on speed above all else.

You will read the entire text book in this class cover to cover. The labs are time consuming but not difficult with a solid understanding of matlab. His lectures are not very exciting, he is somewhat monotoned. However, he is very accomplished an offers a wealth of knowledge. This course is the perfect example where practice makes perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Your succes in this class depends on who your professor and recitation prof is. Prof Lee seems to be a nice guy but can't explain a darn thing!  Even when asked a direct question to clarify a topic he was not able to give a direct answer. If you are the type of learner that needs to understand what is actually happening behind the scenes its a NO!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You NEED to attend recitation to pass this class. He can actually be really funny, but for the love of God GO TO RECITATION!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don't read too much into difficulty as he has the same tests, labs, and HW as every other professor who teaches the class. As far as lectures go his accent is very thick and he talks very slow. He missed class a few times and Clements came in and was much clearer (and he writes the tests). Lee does his best to help and offer it, but he's not good.

The class is known to be difficult and requires a lot of work, so it may not be entirely his fault. There were homework and labs every week, often on topics we would cover after homework was due. The homework was extremely helpful for tests, and the class was curved in the end. Lecture seemed to gloss over topics.

Professor Lin is very helpful and he wants you to do well in his classes. Attendance isn't mandatory, but lectures are entertaining and he takes note if you participate, which can help your grade. All you need to do well in his class is learn the slides and read the textbook.

One of the most caring professors I've had. Tests are not particularly difficult, you mostly need to know what he goes over in lectures and also take notes on the readings. 2 Midterms and final weigh pretty heavy on the class, but there are extra credit opportunities, he curves, and final replacement. Amazing, kind, and funny person as well!

Really nice, funny professor. Enjoyed learning about IR in his class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but make sure to read the slides for the tests. Weekly quizzes are easy and tests aren't impossible, but definitely require a lot of studying. Recommend taking him!

I enjoyed every class-- even though lectures were online due to COVID. He is such a caring professor and is available to go over tests. He wants everyone to succeed and if you work hard, go to class, read the textbook, and study, you will!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is nice, understanding, and willing to work with you. He gives extra credit if you participate in discussions on some of the readings. If he curves a test, then he is likely to discuss with the class what they think is fair (within reason). I took one of his classes during COVID and he offered another time to go over class if your wifi was out.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Lin is an amazing lecturer. His lectures are straight from the slides but he explains the material well. His tests aren't tricky, but they are very specific so you need to study a lot. He's a great person, accessible outside of class, and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students. Also one of the best online transitions I had!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely enjoyed his charismatic personality. He showed genuine interested in the subject, and his lectures were pretty solid (went over what was necessary, good for note and tests). He didn't just make it all lecture, he incorporated new articles, videos, guest speakers, etc. Easy class, no homework. Just take the tests seriously.

This professor is so cute with his jokes and asking the class how to pronounce words. But basically the class is just lecture and the whole grade is only three tests. The tests are SO SPECIFIC. He will put something on there that a random guy asked a random question about a month ago. You go in feeling prepared and are torn apart, but made a B.
Not 1102. 3403 was enjoyable :)
Loved this class! The atmosphere is super easy going, which makes it easier to stay engaged. There were a log of group projects, but they were manageable.
He was an extremely easy grader, and was forgiving when it came to assignments. Only had one major indidivual assignment, the rest group projects. The readings were simple too.
Was overall a fun class, graded mostly on group projects, ways for extra credit
I had Dr. Lehman for an online course. He gave really good feedback for my research proposal.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class and the humor. He kept it entertaining for 8am.
