not a hard class but def my least favorite english class I've ever taken. no assignment was difficult, but most things he would grade for completion until he randomly gave an 80 on an assignment worth 20% of your grade. I think pretty much everyone gets an a since he is generous with participation and portfolio grades.

I would recommend Dr. Lehman. I had him for thesis writing, and he provided good feedback to help get it polished before submission to my advisors. Was also really flexible with deadlines if you email before the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class. As long as you turn everything, it's an essay A b/c there are a lot of assignment graded for completion.

Assignments are typical for an English class, but many of the instructions for larger projects can be too vague and "open ended" leading to confusion and lower grades. Feedback is not good and inaccurate, and when asked about it he can be very condescending and counterproductive. Depends on his mood sometimes but got an A so its not impossible

assignments are pretty lengthy but have extremely ambiguous grading criteria, overall chill but tedious class. However, talking to him was like talking to a brick wall. impossible to get clear feedback and he regurgitates buzz words in a circle. Tanked a 60 because I was so fed up trying to talk to him. Not the worst but heavily recommend diff prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lot of work, typical for ENGL 1102. Sometimes had vague and overly specific grading criteria/standards, but it wasn't bad in the end. Make sure you participate as it's 15% of your total grade. No pop quizzes. Make sure you look at the course theme to see if you'll like it. He is helpful and nice outside of class during office hours as well.

Pretty tough grader and gave extremely vague assignments with confusing feedback. A lot of assignments are randomly graded for completion so its very possible to get an A but he'll make you sweat for it.

He was a pretty chill teacher. No tests, but 4 major project grades, and 2 of them are group projects. Had a neck from Appalachia in our group, but turned out ok once he stopped talking about it all the time.

He really tried to make the class readings and material interesting. He was interested in what I did outside of class and understood that we weren't expecting to do a lot since it was a non-major class.

I was not a fan of this professor. Academically, he felt very disconnected from the material. He grades rather harshly, and does not offer great feedback. He wants every assignment to be done in "his way", whatever that may be. He does grade for participation in class! Also, look at the course theme of the class.

The workload was manageable. Individual project at the beginning of the semester, then group projects the 2nd half of the semester. He was was easygoing, and kept the atmosphere in class light. I wish there was less group work, but I get it with the amount of students in the class.
Was early morning class, but enjoyable. Discussion based so make sure to participate. Rarely lectures, maybe once or twice all semester. I messed up a major assignment, but he let me make it up.

The topic was interesting to me. I liked the creativity allowed for the individual and group projects. Peer review and feedback on discussion posts were helpful. A lot of the work was group, which was fine except some people in my group were lazy.

Dr. Lehman gives rather monotonous and repetitive lectures and assignments. We had to write far too many canvas discussion posts which was rather draining. He gives vague instructions, but overall, if you put in the effort, this will be a fairly easy class. Also, be aware of the topic for the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Unnecessary, repetitive workload; Delayed feedback + grading; Unclear directions; Boring lectures; Says he's available outside of class if needed; Bulk of grade dependent on group work; Kind of goofy; If you submit + try on everything, you'll probably get an A, but he'll make you sweat for it
Boss level
I visited during office hours through the semester, which was really helpful. In person, he gives useful feedback on how to revise assignments. I liked the course.

Just finished the course. Was pissed I had to take a comp class, but ended up enjoying it. Major assignments were group projects which we had total (maybe too much) freedom on. If you turn everything in, he is generous with the final grade.

1102 is very structured at Tech with many small projects that preach "WOVEN" communications into a final project. However, Lehman loads students with unnecessary paragraphs and readings. His projects have absolutely no direction-- only to be graded harshly by Lehman who discredits any work not done in the exact way he would have done it.

Really nice professor! The class does have homework basically every day, but its nothing too impossible. He knows that his class is not most people #1 priority, but still expects you to participate. He grades a lot of things for participation, so just do your homework and put in a moderate amount of effort and you should get an A.

A way more difficult class than expected for no reason. Lots of reading, pretty harsh grader with vague feedback and assignment framework. Generally a nice guy and very responsive though, ask for clarification and help so you know exactly what he wants and don't get a bad grade. Definitely had to work really hard for a good grade.

Dude is literally the worst English teacher I've had at Tech. Class was dreadful. If he was in a bad mood, class was awful and he was mean. Rarely in a good mood. Was a really hard grader and gave very vague and unhelpful feedback. Very awkward guy. Often took over projects to make them how he wanted them.

I hesitantly took this class in Spring 2022. Honestly, it was a breather to other courses. I had fun with the group projects (lot of them) and enjoyed class discussions. Mike was great, but he asked us all to give him bad reviews so that he could potentially have less students (hard for me to do). Anyways, at times, super weird but made me laugh.
He has an odd sense of humor, but overall was an enjoyable class. Glad I took it.

Professor Lehman was fantastic. I took this class Spring 2022. I was originally dreading having to take an English class at an engineering college, but it was actually super fun. There were lots of projects and stuff that we had a good bit of freedom on. Attendance was mandatory, but you do get to miss up to 9 classes.

Good professor. Had him Fall 2021. Lots of reading to do, but not many quizzes on the reading. It was more for discussion. Outside projects are what the class mainly consisted of. Be sure to do your essays before they are due. He does sometimes give extensions. Very considerate as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading early on, but just make sure to participate in class and give a solid effort and he should be pretty lenient on the grades.

He was a cool person and really enjoyed talking with the students (make sure to talk when he asks questions though because he does get annoyed at a lack of participation). He grades mostly on completion except for the big projects. You can snag an easy A by participating and putting in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super down to earth and chill. He assigns a lot of reading and a good amount of assignments early on in the semester but is really lenient with grading if you at least put in the effort. Overall a great professor.

She is amazing. Clear grading and extra credit opportunities & regrading missed questions. Makes the lecture fun and her energy is amazing. Absolute legend, and will help you anytime to understand concepts if you drop by office. Has a cool gecko and brings examples to class. I don't have enough space to say all the nice things possible, take her.

The goat. She's very passionate and energetic about both MSE and teaching. Puts a lot of effort into making sure we learn the concepts well. The class itself is very memorization-heavy. Exams are fair if you have your stuff memorized. Gives points back on the midterms, and has extra credit group projects available. Take her if you can!
Such an awesome teacher. She clearly loves her job and actually makes the class interesting! She is also so caring and really one of the nicest teachers at tech, take her if you can!

She's young and enthusiastic. You can tell she loves MSE and cares about her students. I enjoyed her class. It definitely reminded me of high school, being taught off of slides, memorization-heavy, and multiple choice homework/tests.

Professor Turaski is simply wonderful. She wants you to succeed in her class, provides you with all the tools and extra credit to do it, but more importantly is just an amazing human being. She helped me (a disabled student) with lots of things regarding my accommodations and genuinely cared about my wellbeing. Take her if at all possible!

Turaski is an amazing professor. Her lectures are extremely engaging and she even sometimes does demos during class. She even makes sure to connect MSE topics with other areas of engineering, which is pretty nice. Weekly HW is easy and there's fun mini-projects for extra credit. Highly recommend!

Take her class if you can! She is an incredible lecturer who makes it easy to understand the content. Unlike other MSE 2001 professors, she offers the chance to correct missed test questions and get some points back, and she also had 3 optional mini-projects for extra credit. She wants you to succeed, and she gives you all the tools to do it! 12/10

Best teacher for MSE2001 by far! The content for MSE2001 can be boring at times, but Turaski is always engaging and makes the class fun by doing mini demos of certain topics. In addition, she was the only teacher to give extra credit on exams by doing test corrections. In addition, there are optional mini-projects that act as extra credit too!
Tests are all multiple choice from the slideshows with plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Lectures are pretty engaging with some interesting demos.

Prof Turaski is a great lecture that is truly passionate about what she does! She cares about her student and easy to approach. She is very accommodating and is open to helping students. She is also open to diving into topics more and always encourages learning. She gives me hope that there are truly good and caring professors here at GT. 100/10 :)

Really passionate and loves her job, straightforward teaching, posted notes and recorded lectures, do have to attend ~50% of class for participation pts. Take her, her love for the subject does make the class better, you learn a lot
Turaski is a great professor who makes the class incredibly interesting.
Prof Turaski is amazing. The most passionate and caring professor I have ever encountered.

As an ME student I was expecting to find MSE very boring but Ms. Turaski made the course very interesting with engaging slides and in class demos. Homework load was very reasonable and midterms were also reasonable with a moderate amount of studying. Also lots of extra credit projects that are an easy way to improve your grade if needed.

Great professor who does a good job keeping students engaged and explaining course concepts. Grading is pretty lenient, but fair. Out of all the classes I've taken here, I've easily learned the most from this one and use the information regularly. She's pretty young, so it's very easy for her to connect with her students. Would highly recommend!
I really enjoyed this professor. She is really good.

This is one of my favorite teachers of Spring 2024, as she inspired me to almost go for an MSE minor! Turaski does a good job at applying the concepts of MSE to the real world with live demos and even just applications towards every field! 10/10 would recommend her class. 

As for the class, if you struggle feel free to ask for help, and practice!

During my year Professor Turaski was sick quite a bit and we had a lot of other MSE teachers as subs. Safe to say that she is the best MSE professor at Tech. There are three exams, 2 midterms, and a final (all weighed 25% each), which have some challenging questions and require you to really know the content, but overall manageable
Amazing prof. Tests were all multiple choice and had questions similar to the practice test and homework. Super enthusiastic and caring. Gives lots of examples and practice. GOAT, take her.
She's super nice and will help you a lot in office hours. Her tests aren't that difficult and the workload is not that bad. Lectures are not mandatory but very helpful if you go.
Test are formatted very easy, turaski herself is a very hard-working, passionate and friendly teacher that also shows us fun demos throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Even though this is an intro class, she actually cares and tries to be a better teacher. Like one time she polled the class over whether we wanted more practice exams, and she wrote MULTIPLE exams just so we could practice more. Tests are multiple choice, and straight from ppt, easy A if you study for a bit.
Great professor, definitely better at teaching and more passionate than other profs.
She's really great. She obviously really cares about her students and goes out of her way to make class interesting. Highly recommend!

Prof. Turaski is a really awesome lecturer. She is clearly very passionate about material science. I highly recommend taking her class. She frequently does demos in class, which is cool. Homework and exams are all multiple choice, so they're pretty easy as long as you pay attention in class.

She was a really great professor, probably the best for MSE 2001, so definitely take her class. I'm really bad at chemistry and is probably why I received a B as the final grade. This class involves a lot of chemistry. I'm also more of a mathematical minded person and this class is more memorization than it is math. For me it was difficult.

You can tell she's passionate about teaching MSE. She was new, but she implements student feedback and improved a lot in terms of structure and resources. She records her lectures, and exams reflect the homework. She does participation points, so you do have to go to class, but the grading system is very lenient if you miss lectures or homework.
Great professor for MSE 2001, cares about lectures and teaches content well. Tests are moderately difficult but she gives plenty of material to prepare.

I had a different professor, but she still helped me a ton, especially on my exam days. I would go to her office hours and no lie, I learned more in her office hours than I did in any of my lectures. I didn't even have her, but I still regard her as one of the best professors to ever teach. GOAT
Very good professor, had many practical project that seriously had me considering to switch majors
Her in class demonstrations helped make more complex topics make sense. Her grading scale was great, and she taught an otherwise harder subject in a way that made it seem not as hard.

She is super knowledgeable and passionate about material science, and all of her materials are well organized and accessible. The tests are multiple choice but will require some studying because questions can get really specific. She made the class a lot more enjoyable than it otherwise would have been, highly recommend taking her class :)

I really enjoyed having Dr Turaski! I felt like the content was interesting and she explained the concepts, even the tough ones, in a very digestible way. I would definitely recommend taking this class with her!

She was really good at explaining difficult concepts in a way that was easy to understand, and she also used a lot of real-world examples to show the usefulness of the content. Professor Turaski was also very open to questions and tried her best to make everyone succeed. Take her class!
Very good lectures, makes difficult content really easy to understand

Take her and you will not regret. She makes the tricky content very easy to understand. Her office hours are great for asking questions. She is really a caring and passionate professor. If you go to classes and do you homework, you will be just fine. You really never see a professor like her these days. Best professor for MSE 2001. 100% recommend.

Professor Turaski is an amazing professor! Lots of visuals which makes things easy to understand. Lectures are very engaging and you can learn everything to get an A by just attending. Take MSE 2001 with her!

The course itself is pretty difficult and just full of memorization, but her lectures are really good and helpful. There are two online textbooks that she provides but those are not necessary to succeed in the class. Just watch the recorded videos. Clicker questions and homework are great resources for exams.

If I recall correctly, this is professor Turaski's first year teaching and she's done great! Great at explaining stuff in lectures, has demonstrations. You can get up to 20% of your grade from mini projects, hw and clicker Qs. Different grading styles for best final course grade. HWs and practice exams are good study. Most lectures recorded!

Dr. Lieberman isn't the most engaging lecturer, but her lecture videos get all the information you need across and her tests were very easy and fair. The flipped classroom is not as bad as the other comments say. Other professors might be better, but if you take it with Lieberman you have nothing to worry about.

flipped classroom is terrible. you have to learn everything alone and the videos offered are so terrible. I had to watch another random professor on youtube to learn anything. she sounds so uninterested in what she is teaching and sounds like she wants to be there less than you want to be. DO NOT RECOMMEND BIOCHEM WITH HER!!! TAKE WITH SOMEONE ELSE

Dr. Lieberman is an amazing professor! She's funny and knowledgeable. Bchem-I is hard to grasp and master, but her flipped classroom helped take time to learn content outside class and address all concerns in class. You also see real life application in class through group activities. If you put in effort, you will get so much out of this class!

Was not considerate and many times showed video lectures of herself during in-person lectures rather than teach. On the rare occasion that she taught, she was condescending to students who asked questions about course material. Her exams were fair, except for the 3rd exam that was made more difficult because too many people were doing well.

The tests are fairly difficult but you can pass if you really study. The homework though almost had nothing to do with the test. Also she was also not very considerate of students who were struggling in the class and she was not lenient if any problems arose even technical difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had at tech. Does not know how to use technology. Her test are too difficult for the time given. Would not recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Lieberman is amazing! She is humorous and fun and makes class exciting. The only drawback is that some of her tests may be difficult, but the lowest test grade is dropped :)

Dr. Lieberman is the quintessential example of a professor who is only here for research. She does not really care about the students and does not lecture well. Lectures often focus on topics nothing to do with exams, and homework covers topics not discussed in lecture. To survive you must memorize the textbook. Worst class I've taken at Tech. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She assigns a lot of in-class busy work/small assignments, and didn't always spend much lecture time teaching/explaining actual content. Her tone can be a bit off-putting at time, especially if she thinks it's something you SHOULD know (i.e. doesn't consider that you might've forgotten things you learned in other classes).

Her tests and quizzes are decent if you study really well, though there were some questions that came out of nowhere. She's kind of condescending in office hours and so was the TA (both unhelpful) so find a good study group. Overall good course, informative, interesting lectures. Don't slack, study hard, and this course will be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her tests and quizzes aren't bad, as long as you study and understand the material. I liked her lectures, not the most boring professor. However, she does have an attitude when she feels challenged by students. So don't use your phone or turn over a test or quiz paper unless you want to be scolded in front of the whole class. You've been warned.

Professor Liang is over hated considering the fact that he is a good professor. The only real problem in this class is the grading system with 60% of the class getting an A or B and with Cios 70%. The exams aren't too bad as all the formulas are from the slides and you are allowed a double-sided crib sheet, so you have plenty of space.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: First off, Dr. Liang is a good hearted guy that loves to answer questions. However, professors will usually frame their exams around the course material, and the homeworks around the exams. His seem almost random. Be ready for long crib sheets trying to get every equation you can because you dont know whats going to appear

Coerces you to buy a $300+ textbook by not giving you the homework problems. Forces class attendance through pop quizzes and incomplete lecture slides. Test material does not match lecture or homework. This has gotten so bad that my class has quite literally unionized against him. Avoid at all costs, do not waste your tuition dollars on this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The reviews from the past 9 years make it clear he does not care to improve his class. Everything has already been said and it impresses me that nothing has changed after so long. I know these reviews are filled with butthurt students, but yeah do yourself a favor and wait a semester to take a different section. I will say, his lectures were good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liang is very passionate about his work and the manufacturing field, but his class felt disorganized. I took this class online over a summer, so the overall structure made it harder, but the grading consisted of 2 midterms, a final, and a couple homeworks. Curve is huge at the end, but the exam content is pretty unclear. Very specific questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My issue is with his exams; they constitute a large portion of the overall grade, and grading criteria is defined in the syllabus but they aren't followed consistently. I once had to email him some calculations to show that I deserved 2 more points for a problem; after many stubborn refusals he said my proof was right but only returned 1 point.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Tests on nothing covered in the lectures. Literally received exams that didn't use a single formula or concept from the lectures. Will redact slides from the lectures, so if you aren't there, you don't know what was taught. Wrote 35 pages of notes by hand and none of it actually showed up on any exam that was given to us.

You'll have to use Chegg.
this guy kinda blows
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall I found him to be a really good and interesting professor. To prepare for his exams, just be aware of every formula that you have covered in lecture and you will be fine. I also found him to be quite kind and just very entertaining during lecture, but maybe that's just my style
bad guy
Relies on rote learning. Extremely unhelpful during office hours. Testing criteria is unclear.
Very challenging class, and Prof Liang was unhelpful throughout.
Class with him was so tough because he moves at too rapid a pace and doesn't care about whether students are absorbing the material
Expects you to spend your entire semester memorizing. Is confrontational if you ask him questions. Stay away for sanity.

Absolute worst professor that I've ever come across. Throws volumes and volumes of material for rote learning and eventual compression into a tiny crib sheet, provides absolutely NO partial credit, and whenever approached to discuss incorrectly graded homeworks or exams is hostile and dismissive. Faculty should reconsider letting him teach, IMO.

This is definitely a class I don't think I learned anything in. For what it's worth, no one will get an F in the course and there's a CIOS thing where you're basically guaranteed to get a C if 85% do it. Tough exams though especially with the time constraint. Would recommend if you absolutely want to get out of this class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring lecturer, but a relaxed and sometimes funny guy. Attendance is mandatory if you value the 8% of your grade from four pop quizzes. Tests closely resemble his example test and historical tests from past years, and problems within lecture notes. 35% get A's and 35% B's if 85% of the class completes the CIOS, regardless of your numerical avg.

Maybe my least favorite professor. He is not clear whatsoever, and the class is based solely on your ability to have all the formulas on your cribsheet, and to fill in the lecture slide blanks. You have to show up to class to copy slides and for pop quizzes, but you won't learn anything. What a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Liang is a bad lecturers. On any given PowerPoint slide he will spend between 5 to 25 minutes rambling on the slide's content no matter how much content is on the slide. 20% percent of each of his test are on random things from the textbook too so watch out for that. He's also super strict about turning in hw. He makes funny jokes though
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Liang for some reason has a non-announced HW policy so students frequently don't even know a HW was assigned. He seems to have little respect for students time and does not seem concerned about making his class effective.

Multiple choice is 60% of your final grade and anything that is in the book (yes even weird side notes and those strange 'today in industry' even though the book is 15 years old..), spoken by him in lecture or not, and what is on your notes that he may and or may not complete is viable testing material. Completely unfair and unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most disjointed,  confusing classes I've ever taken. Lectures are all over the place and they don't follow the equations in the book which makes it even harder to understand what's happening. The average on the first test was a 34% (not kidding). Although I had one of the highest grades I'd never want to take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes are given. Homework is graded half on completion and half on accuracy. Tests are hard. Class is graded completely on a curve (30% A's 30% B's 30% C's 10% D's.) Lectures are kind of all over the place. Not the easiest to follow, so you will end up having to figure things out on your own with the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are all over the place. The questions on the tests were from things we may have covered once or twice or from a small sections from the book. If you do the CIOS, top 25% get As, next 30% Bs, next 30% Cs, and last 15% Ds. Pop quizzes over previous lectures. Fill in PPT lectures. Prove your hard work and he'll help you out.

He is or was when I had him all over the place. He's lectures were okay but he went of topic a lot. I had a one on one to go over a few points he got angry and told me I want trying. Wish I could drop his class.

one of the worst professors I have ever had. Disorganized, confusing lecture style; many mistakes in lecture that make HW very difficult (seeing as he does not post notes online). Too busy to be an effect professor
He is very smart, and his lectures are very interesting. If you pay attention and do the homework, you will make an A

Was a great industry oriented class with enough physical modeling. If you want to learn about machine tool, you should take this class. Midterm and final were hard when I took the class, but the professor gave A to almost 70% of the class. He is nice and very smart, he got a huge experience in  industry and give a lot of example from his experience

He is a decent professor that is nice will listen to whatever questions you may have. He is very fair with his grading policy. The class test averages were very low when I took him, he compensated by making the final much easier. He has pop quizzes and assigns homework as well, which he grades very leniently.

Really cool guy who genuinely cares for his students, lectures are okay, while textbook is used, he only makes tests based off what he gets through in lecture, will cut out stuff from the course if he can't get to it. Slightly hard to access outside of class but is always willing to answer questions in class. Tests are fine as well.
Prof. was great. Just read the textbook before class and show up to lectures because he sometimes takes attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Lloyd was very nice and caring. His class was more difficult than other psych sections I talked to. Some exams (including the final) had essays. He would sometimes brush over material/get sidetracked and go very fast. You HAVE to read the textbook to succeed. Has in-class assignments on random days that we have to be there for, so show up.

His lectures were a boring but not entirely useless. Read the textbook and you'll be fine but he does have some questions from lectures which he does emphasize. There are random in class assignment that you have to be in class for. Due dates were Fridays at 4pm so def keep track of that. Overall not very difficult as long as you read the textbook.
Overall this was an enjoyable class and work was manageable. Make sure to check due dates, for Professor Lloyd does not always emphasize when assignments are due. Class attendance is also helpful.
He's a good person, but his lectures sometimes get side tracked. Whatever was tested was just the textbook. PLEASE READ THE TEXTBOOK!
Lectures were good and he was very clear about what we were going to be tested on. The class and the tests were very straight forward. I would recommend!

Even if you attend all the lectures and take notes, it is impossible to do well if you do not read the textbook (the lectures are next to useless), and the chapters aren't short. There were also THIRTEEN CHAPTERS that we didn't get to in class, but were also on the final. My advice is to read other psych professor reviews and TAKE SOMEONE ELSE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty nice professor. IDK if just me but his British accent+crappy mic+big lecture hall made it sounds like he was rambling during lecture.Lecture doesn't cover everything. Expect to read a lot textbook. Exam MCQ are not striaght forward.Drops 1/4 exam and extra credit. Attendance not mand. but there are inclass assignment.Go take someone else imo

Pretty nice guy but I just found his lectures to be hard to understand. It might just be a me thing but I felt like he would ramble and his british accent was slightly hard to follow. Either way his lectures didn't cover enough and you have to read + buy textbook. Tests were fair if u read textbook, in-test essays are easy but very little time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall solid professor. Lectures were good and as engaging as they could be. Tests were all multiple choice with one test having a written essay, but lowest of four gets dropped. A few precents of extra credit here and there. There are in-class assignments every now and again which test your attendance.

Professor Lloyd is really straightforward and there for you under any circumstance. While class isn't mandatory, its a good way to meet other people, hear nuanced questions, and stay alert for additional assignments. His exams are a lot to memorize and learn but are overall logical. His lectures are monotone, but keep the pace and you'll be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Lloyd is a very straightforward professor and gives you all the tools needed to succeed. His study guides are extremely representative of test material. The tests themselves do require some decent study time, but its nothing unreasonable. He spot checks attendance every few weeks. The homework is easy. Overall had a great time in his class.

Amazing psych class, but it was a bit more difficult than I thought. Honestly a fair amount of work and a good learning experience overall, just be prepared its not anywhere close to a free course. Homework due at 5pm on fridays which was weirdly difficult for me to remember and really hurt my grade but prof is extremely caring & worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Lloyd is nice. However, his class is harder than I've seen in other psych 1101 classes. You just read the book and teach yourself most of the content. The class is very test-heavy which also have essay questions. There is not much homework but the tests can be hard and our averages were around 70-80s. He does give extra-credit here and there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor, made the lectures engaging and worth attending. Although attendance is not required. Textbook was required, and alot of reading may be necessary. But if you attend lectures you will be fine. He made office hours accessible especially after tests. I would definitely take his class again.

He's a great teacher. Didn't find any reviews when I signed up for his class but pleasantly surprised. Lectures are engaging and you can tell he loves the subject. You don't NEED to show up to do well but I would highly recommend since it makes studying seem like review. Homework is really straightforward, as are tests. No BS.

Great lecturer and super easygoing. Lectures are great for going over the text and going more in-depth. Have to buy access to the textbook which has all of the homework (which there isn't that much of). Also, he's British and his accent is quite lovely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: stopped going to lectures after a few weeks, they honestly confused me more. learned through studio, ta was very good at teaching and quizzes were pretty much like the previous studio. had a c but the final had extra points that bumped me to an a (not sure why there were extra points). sometimes the syntax would switch and make questions confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy my experience in this class at all. While the professor was knowledgeable, the lectures did not reflect that very well at all. The lectures typically felt very scattered and conceptual. The concepts did not get broken down at all, and thus the lectures lacked a purpose. Studios were great, and tests and quizzes used studio questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I can't tell if he actually cares about his students because he often claims to care, but regardless he's very condescending, even during lecture. Not very approachable, and terrible lecturer. Midterms were much harder than they needed to be, and grading was harsh, ex: takes off points for messiness. TA was good though. Be ready to self-teach.

This professor is horrible. He is really hard to understand, has very unorganized lectures and you will walk out of lecture understanding nothing. Please take another prof. Going to studio and Plus Sessions will help, but you are better off teaching yourself diff eqs on youtube.

Take anyone else. His lectures are completely useless. You are 10x better off just reading the textbook during normal class hours. You're forced to go every Tuesday though for the quiz, but I highly recommend leaving after the quiz (if you're unfortunate enough to be in his class). Pretty nice guy, but terribly disorganized. Also no crib sheet.

Worst professor I've had at Tech - prof doesn't even know what he is teaching and HW and Canvas announcements very unorganized/vague. Weekly quiz to force attendance but lecture is a waste of time - you need to self study book and homework. No crib sheet on tests, have to memorize formulas but if you took AP Stat the course is easy enough.

I would say take someone else for diff eq if you can. The man loves his students and really wants them to succeed, but the book for this class is terrible, and frankly, his teaching is not much better. He will go through an alright explanation of a topic, have 50 minutes of lecture left, but still only get through one example problem. Class Curved
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Sit in the front of the class or you won't be able to hear him.  Has a little bit of an accent.  Tests are tough but there is a nice curve at the end of the semester.  Weekly quizzes in recitation.  Had him for diff eq.  Nice guy.

Grading for the homeworks is completely arbitrary. Despite increased effort each time + starting to include include extra figures and analysis in my homeworks, I ALWAYS get the average score (87) with no feedback on how to improve. There are 5 homeworks, a group project, and a final. Wont grade the project proposal (been a month) and its due soon
No rhyme or reason to grading. No rubrics. No feedback. Syllabus changed in the middle of the semester. No explanation ever as to what grade you received. Most frustrating class I have ever taken.

There are no rubrics, no explanation as to why you lost points. Grades are based off of vibes strictly. I asked for feedback, she replied weeks later and said I lost points for not including something that wasn't listed as a requirement and was told it's common sense to include it.

The teaching style made the material difficult to follow, and assignment directions and rubrics were often unclear and contained several typos. Grading relies heavily on the Turnitin AI detector without room for discussion, which made the class super stressful.
No rubric for grading. Never get feedback on why you lost points. Changes policies and syllabus in the middle of semester. Will flag you for AI without you ever using AI.

You would think a CS professor would understand how AI and LLM models work. Kept getting docked for 'using AI' when I did not and all online AI checkers show less than 10%  AI detection. She did not care and said she only trusts Canvas' AI detector and that her decision is final no matter what. Stopped replying to emails and discussion posts.

Extremely rude to students when providing criticism. It's like tough love with no love. Grades are seemingly arbitrary and she can just decide that a student's contribution to a group project doesn't matter. Everything in this class is essentially just up to the professor's whim / a quick skim of materials rather than any specific rubric.

Lectures basically teach nothing, yet attendance is mandatory. The homework rubric is unclear, hasn't been updated since the millennium with bunch outdated links, but it's still the course's best part. The group project and description are a total mess. Only she knows the real rubric, which changes with every announcement. She is rude to students

Professor has really high standards for written homeworks and the final project. There is a weekly writing assignment with really high standards, adding a dose of stress to all of your Fridays.
The grading criteria is extremely vague. There's no rubric, which makes it feel just down to her personal opinion.
She is also extremely rude to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course felt like a bunch of nothing information. Every lecture was equivalent to a simple google search that could have given me all the content I needed. The professor was also difficult to listen to, and I don't believe that she was a great lecturer despite making attendance mandatory.

Not recommended, especially if you want proper feedback on grades. No rubrics. You get peer reviews on essays, but no reasoning for how grades are given. Same for projects. Sent an announcement stating all grades will be released but never happened. You get overall letter grades despite numerous missing graded items.

Good, friendly professor; cares for students and is accessible outside of class. We had to do some biweekly projects which were centered around some technologies like web crawlers, caching/optimization, etc. No final exam but you get a 10-15pg paper which is pretty easy, and a team project (your choice of topic).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Students are expected to behave like mindless drones, and instructed to drop the course when they seek guidance. If they do manage to appease her TA lackeys, they will find their minds deformed by the same delusions Ling Liu holds, their thinking fixated on a zero sum game, long detached from any spirit of collaboration or semblance of humility.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst course, worst professor I've ever seen. This course has nothing to do with Big Data. Reading and Writing is heavy, come with a solid essay writing skill, or you will get negative attendance points even because low HWs/Final grades. The project workload is also the heaviest I've ever been through. Not to mention how rude she is to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Used profanity words to comment on students' work. Public humiliation for times. TA and professor only reply to Ed post when they want to, most of the posts were ignored. Grading rubrics is arbitrary, you only see your entire semester long project grade at the end of the semester. Grades automatically curved around 85. Don't waste your time here.

Extremely rude to students, poor lecture content and delivery. Assignments and course syllabus is mostly outdated. Note that the course name is misleading, and is not a course related to handling of big data.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: absolutely the worst professor I've ever had at Tech in all of 5 years. not a single other comes close at how genuinely rude and uncaring she is. class topics are essentially chosen at random and are unrelated to the course. during project demos, she would interrupt groups and publicly humiliate them. stay away from this course if she's the prof

Genuinely a crashout, rude, grades hard for the projects and has a huge final paper. Haven't finished yet, but I've heard the curve is huge because of this. Most of this wouldn't be too bad if she wasn't extremely rude too.

This professor is extremely rude. Her grading guidelines make no sense. She speaks far too quietly during class, and even the course material is terribly structured. Although, she does curve a lot, so there's that.

This is not a Systems course. This is rather a collection of topics the instructors is excited about. The same is reflected in the assignments, project-topics, and the review subjects. This class felt more ML and LLMs heavy than Systems heavy.

Also, lectures felt very vague, and most of the learning happened during the assignments and projects.

I have been in GT CS for 5 years and this is THE worst of all the ones I have taken. The instructor is knowledgeable about the content she teaches. However, she is extremely rude to students and makes the course overly arbitrary. The rubrics for assignments are vague and the workload is too heavy for the final paper. Time wasted.
Using public humiliation as a form of motivation is not valid. I don't need to know that another student is doing poorly in the class or is going through "family issues"

The CS6220 course experience is one of the worst at GT CS. TAs are non-existent. Homework is poorly designed with little instruction on what to do. Grading is quite random as well with no clear standard. However, if you just need an easy A and don't care about course experience, this course might actually be pretty nice.
Rude, too much paper writing, a lot of work expected on the group project and then another paper on top of that.  Barely teaches anything and invites lecturers only to question them herself.

Dr. Liu is extremely passionate and knowledable about the content. However, while the content of the class is useful, there's no practical application assignments which help you understand if the content has truly been learned. Also, the course load of is heavy, which includes the homeworks and the final paper which is 15-20 pages long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ling Liu is a mediocre professor that is further hindered by her lack of effort. Homeworks aren't graded by her but by other students. We are also assigned a ridiculous 15-20 page essay which adds nothing to the class except extra stress and work for no reason or learning purpose whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course topics are incredibly disjointed. The project, final exam, and participation grades are not given by the end of the semester, and the TAs and prof do not respond to these complaints on EdStem. The homework is tedious, and the grades are artificially curved to give most people 80-90. The participation requirements are  convoluted.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible teaching. She speaks random stuff in class which is not at all connected and doesn't make sense.

Dr. Liu knows the content of the course and is actually very passionate about the content she teaches; however, I can confidently say that this was one of the weaker classes I've taken at Tech - especially in the info thread. The grading is completely unclear, it's hard to find correct information about assignments, and the assignments are too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is really passionate about the lecture content and extremely knowledgeable. That said, the grading criteria are extremely unclear and hard to follow yet worth so much of our grade. The class has been backloaded where ~70% of the class grades come from the last 1.5 weeks of the semester. The final is a 15-20 single-spaced paper.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is very enthusiastic and knowledgable on the subject taught. You can learn a ton from programming assignment if you pay time and efforts. I hate to say this but the workload is extremely heavy unless you like writing papers. The final paper is a 1015 pages single spaced paper which is 3x more than other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Aweful
Awesome!

Such an amazing professor! He is very passionate and makes lectures engaging with real-world examples. There are creative projects and case studies, including Tableau assignments using data. The workload is manageable, and grading is clear. If you stay on top of assignments, you can do well.

he's objectively a great guy. fun to talk to, EXTREMELY passionate about the subject, but that just made me feel bad that i absolutely hated this class. he's really trying his best to get a bunch of gt stem kids to care about creative data visualizations and he's doing as well as anybody could

Yanni is a great professor who really cares about his students. He was accommodating and understanding during COVID. We had a lot of critique sessions where we would give other students feedback. Had a few assignments with a partner and learned how to use Tableau. Great class with work you can use on a portfolio. Would recommend taking with Yanni!!

Expected this class to be awful, and actually wasn't that bad. Just go to class. Professor is an approachable guy. The projects suck, and the grading is harsh, but if you make the effort you will get a decent grade.
easy class if you just show up. Don't even have to do the readings, projects are relatively simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Loukissas is the most confusing and difficult professor I have ever had. This is an intro class and he expects you to learn a new coding language every other week and create an incredible project every time. It's as if he thinks we don't have other classes. Lectures have nothing to do with projects so you're on your own in learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: just avoid

Not the best lecturer... unclear about his expectations until kids acted up but he is passionate about his field of study and that's what motivated me to try harder in his class. He tried and changed things up so the class felt more interesting. Easy A, daily readings but give it a chance and you might get more out of it than you thought
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grading is subjective. They "grade on how much a project wows" them (direct quote from TA in class). Lectures have nothing to do with projects. There's a project in a new coding language every two weeks. Know java or die.  If you go to office hours, Dr. Loukissas is will gladly give you feedback before turning in a project. He really does care.

Maybe it was just this class, but it was so hard especially if you don't have coding experien. There are like 5/6 projects and you have 2 weeks to learn a coding language and then make an amazing project. Grading was rather subjective, which was kinda annoying tbh. It is really hard to get an A. Be prepared to work really hard. Average work is a C.

This is one of if not the best professor at GT. 
He's always available after class, explains concepts in a clearly, and has engaging lectures. He goes over problems in class in a hands-on way, he has a sense of humor even when the class isn't responding and he writes clearly for people taking pictures. He's just genuinely a great guy.

Great prof, useless class. 13 untimed module quizzes with 2 attempts and unlimited time, which you can easily get a 100 on with 30 minutes of studying. 20% each for Midterm and Final. No one shows up to lecture as the lecture notes are on Canvas and are great. You can easily shove this 1 credit hour class anywhere in your schedule.

Had Dr. Lowe in the spring for simulation and he was a great professor! Very caring and easy to talk to, accessible through office hours as well. Clear lectures with well explanations and as long as you pay attention in class you'll do good. Would def take again!
Super amazing professor! Professor Lowe was extremely kind and really straightforward with his policies. The project is as tough as you make it be. Show up to class and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All around good prof.  You'll need to learn VBA and Simio in this course, but Dr. Lowe goes at a reasonable pace and explains concepts well.  What sets him apart is that he really, really cares about his students - if you're struggling or need help, reach out to him early and he'll work with you through it.  Great professor, an even nicer guy!

only grades are 13 module quizzes, midterm, and final. module quizzes are open notes & no timer. easy af class and u just need to study the day before the midterm/final to get an A. would def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lowe clearly cares about his students. Very personable and accessible, but if you don't put in the effort or don't respect him or his class, he'll be unwilling to move an inch for you. As for the class, attendance was optional and grading was based on a few tests. Easy A if you put in the work and show up for class (or study before exams).

The class itself is mostly just learning formulas, finding out when to apply them, and punching in numbers. If you go to lecture, he is very funny and more than happy to answer any of your questions. Only word of caution I would say is to not take his class rules lightly, especially when it comes to his pretty strict exam procedures.
Professor Lowe is fantastic. He is super organized and walks through the material thoroughly so everyone understands. Would definitely take again!

I took him for Simulation and Eng Econ. Hes all about teaching what is practical in ISYE and avoiding heavy theory. His tests are really fair, but make you think which is good honestly. He jokes around a bit too which is fun. Id take him again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've had at tech. This is my second course with him, and he's great in lectures. Show up and do the work, and you will get an A. He teaches what he's going to put on the test, very straightforward.

Professor Le Lostec was an amazing professor. Class was asynchronous with homework/lecture due every MWF. Exams were not that difficult and overall I enjoyed the class. I feel prepared enough where I would take 2001 if I had the room in my schedule.

Fall 2024. Mostly VHL. At home tests on word documents via honor code. Encouraged scheduling meetings with her online to help with speaking (I did not utilize this very well). 2 group projects: my group members from the first project ghosted me for the second one so she let me do it alone.

Prof. Le Lostec is clearly competent and a kind person. She was very helpful through the entire course. Not an easy-A course but frankly I didn't study at all and still got a B so, not complaining. Would definitely take her again if I had to take another language course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took her French 1002 class online. She is an AMAZING french teacher. If you really want to learn the language, Professor Le Lostec is the best. She has office hours everyday to practice speaking. Homework is due 3x a week. There are 6 unit tests. She is a hard grader, but this is so helpful in learning a language. She is fair and understanding.

Dr. Le Lostec was a very nice teacher and was really helpful and accessible outside of class hours but did definitely have high expectations for students. If you utilize all of her resources and office hours and practice times, getting an A can be easy but you will definitely have to put in the work and effort.

I suffered through this course because I didn't keep up with weekly schedule setup. I really appreciated the effort the professor put in to support thorough, she is super accessible outside of class. This course isn't an easy A, but it's definitely possible. It is test-heavy with 6 quizzes for each unit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Madame Le Lostec is a very nice woman, and is very accessible outside of class to practice or review with you. Aside from that, this class is way too difficult because of her. For introductory French that many take for their humanities credits, she grades very harsh and expects you to be a lot more fluent than 3 months of experience would warrant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a very nice lady but expects a lot from students. Definitely one of the hardest professors I've encountered. If you utilize office hours, study groups, and outside resources you can manage to get an A but it is a lot for a humanities requirement. Super understanding but also has high standards and does not budge.

I first registered for the course just to satisfy my humanities requirement for my major, but quickly found out that you can't just BS a language class. You definitely need to set aside time to practice the language, not just reading the textbook. It's a difficult class for sure, but can be done.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a very nice lady, but she makes her class much harder than it should be. She is always available to help you out. She does not give clear instructions and acts like you should know things she never taught you. If you are very good at French and have lots of free time you will do fine. If French is not super easy to you the class will be bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I absolutely adored Madame Le Lostec, would love to take another class from her. She would get mad when people wouldn't learn the vocab, but she is still a very patient woman. She grades kind of strictly during the tests but gives so much partial credit I never worried about losing my A. Just try your best and participate!

Frau Le Lostec is a very kind woman. It is apparent that she wants her students to excel; she is willing to meet outside of class. Expect additional homework (beyond VHL) due every class. She is an extremely strict grader with little tolerance for grammar mistakes (even those not being tested). No test corrections like other professors.

Professor Lobnik's class was nothing short of an amazing opportunity to delve into the art of literature. In addition to inspiring such unique & eye opening perspectives on various texts, Lobnik was truly a strong source of encouragement in guiding student towards textual analysis & self expression. I would take this course a thousand times over.

Dr. Lobnik is one of the kindest professors I've ever had. She cares very deeply about her students and the texts she is presenting to her students. She is very willing to meet your needs and accommodate you. Utilize her feedback and attend office hours if you need any kind of help.

I took English with Dr. Lobnik at Agnes Scott. She is so sweet and caring. If you do the bare minimum, you'll do well -- just keep up with the readings and talk a bit in class. If your goal is becoming a strong writer, she will help you if you put in the work and effort! You won't regret taking her class unless you hate reading :-)

Really sweet and approachable professor, albeit an awkward start to the semester. She's passionate about her expertise and utilizes many different learning approaches so that everyone has fair chances to participate. Lectures can be a drag, but interesting once discussion picks up. Helpful feedback and was SUPER accommodating when I fell behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Lobnik taught an ENG101 course at Emory in the spring, and was hands down one of the best English teachers I've ever had. She was incredibly approachable, helpful, and constructive. Class discussions were sometimes a little boring, but given the subject material it can be difficult to make reading discussions engaging if not interested.

Very very sweet teacher. If you participate and attend class, you'll do well. She really wants you to learn and succeed. Going to her before assignments are due and using her feedback will definitely help your grade. If you don't participate in class or attend, you will not do as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lobnik ensured that each of the students were equally well informed of the themese that were covered and focused intensively on making sure that everything in class felt relevant.
Dr. Lobnik is a really great teacher! The class discussions are always engaging and pushes you to think about things in new ways. You should definitely take her!

Anyone interested in taking a challenging and rewarding literary course should take a class with Professor Lobnik. She is organized, easily accessible and makes guidelines very clear. Because of her class I have truly become a stronger critical reader, writer and thinker. Would strongly recommend!

The class material is thought-provoking, as Dr. Lobnik is very passionate and knowledgeable about her field of expertise, and is subsequently an engaging orator. Participation is key in this class, and going to office hoursworking with Dr. Lobnik's suggestions is incredibly advantageous. The syllabus is straightforward and informative.

Dr. Lobnik is a great professor, she's excited about what she teaches and she really cares about her students' success. Sometimes assignments instructions were confusing, but she was happy to clarify. This class was challenging and a lot of work, but Dr. Lobnik grades fairly and is always willing to help.
Great professor! Always ready to help students during office hours. Very fair in terms of grading, but clear work ethic needs to be shown. I'm taking her again next semester!

Dr. Lobnik is a great English professor. She is extremely helpful when myself and other students have questions regarding assignments and her expectations are clear-cut and realistic. The time commitment to this class is normal and her grading is very fair. Her classroom discussions are also very interesting. Definitely would recommend!

This class isn't difficult if you put forth the effort and participate. If you don't like to talk just try because she is really good about helping you form your ideas while you participate. The syllabus is clear about expectations and she's a fair grader. No tests or quizzes and she's willing to help on projects if you need it.

This class has a lot of assignments. But the instructions were clear & the deadlines were reasonable. The professor was very responsive to my emails even on weekends. The virtual help sessions were especially helpful. I learned a lot. I would recommend his class to others.
His class is very well-organized and straightforward. You learn what you need. He is a good person.
Tests and homework are based on the textbook and what you learned in class. Dr. Louie is a caring professor. If you're having trouble with something, he is there to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible experience. Unfair grading, no clear rubric, and refuses to communicate. Shows favoritism in class and lacks real teaching ability. Lab promises were fake—no funding, no progress, just wasted time. Avoid his class and lab if you value your education and time.

Exam I - 95.5, Exam II -86, Exam III - 103.5. Average adjusted to 70%  - 66.5. Seminar (30%) -15. Total score 81.5. Grade: BForgive me for speaking frankly, this professor is racist and foolish. I don't know why my average exam score is 94 but my total score is only 81.

He does cool research and this is basically a class where you learn about the latest research and biology. The class is really lecture heavy but they are interesting lectures. The exams are very difficult but he wants students to do well so go to office hours and chat with him. It's hard work but worth it especially if you want to be a scientist.

Great professor and TA (Alex Costa) for the 4590 research project. Their focus is on molecular genetics, so it can get a little overwhelming if you aren't interested in that field. A couple very simple quizzes/notebook checks, grade is mainly from participation as they really just want to see what you've learned over the semester.

The sweetest professor I've ever had. He cares so much about students' well-being and made the class so fun by trying to adapt to us as we learn. I had the privilege of taking both his available classes, and he worked one-on-one with you whenever he could.

I adored this professor. He made his class so engaging that it is by far my favorite class I have taken. An amazing lecturer and human. The class completely relies on your group project (so do it well!). Coming up with an idea is the hardest part imo. It feels like he needs to like it for it to be a good idea.

Hands down the BEST lecturer I've had at Tech so far. He cares so much about his students and puts a lot of energy into learning real applications of the material. He grades tough and project is worth 80% but worth it. Try to tell a story during the presentation rather than copying example slide formats or the rubric. You pick groups in 1st class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure to take this class with some friends. It'll be one of the most fun classes that you take, and you get to work on a project the entire time. Lowe is amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about his students and oftentimes expends his own resources (money, time, connections) to support our education. Probably spent around $1,000 on each class out of his own pocket to teach us lessons about market fluctuations, trading, and marketing tactics. I learned a lot more than I expected to. Thank you Mike!

One of the most caring, knowledgeable, and hardworking professors I've ever taken. Although the group project is worth most of your grade, he does required check ins and truly cares about how your group progress and research is going. Lectures are extremely entertaining and useful. Would take him for every class

70-90% of ur grade is the project. Make friends with classmates and teammates bc they grade you. Grade urself 100. really nice but tough grader. won't give you good feedback in ur periodic meetings (he'll just tell you it's good) and after the presentation he will roast it. We got an A bc he made a rash promise to us while we were abroad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AWESOME teacher. actually knows the stuff and is super open to help and meet with you and your group at any time. the final project is 80% of ur grade so make sure you take the class with some people you trust to get work done or choose a good group on day 1!!! overall, he was so fun and made this class enjoyable.
Very caring professor, engaging lectures and fun group project. The project is the majority of your grade so really pour into it and you'll pass for sure
My favorite professor ever! He is very helpful, gives great lectures, and genuinely cares about his students.
awesomeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

Professor Lowe is great! We barely had any coursework, and if we did, it was useful for the final project that you have to complete at the end of the semester. He is kind and truly cares about his students. I would definitely recommend taking him.

Dr. Lowe is super awesome, always understanding, and a great teacher. This class is almost entirely determined by a group project that runs all semester long, so if you get stuck with a dud group it is just a miserable class. Wish there were clearer grading guidelines, though, as often it felt more like shooting in the dark than anything.

Professor Lowe is one of the best educators I have ever had. He's super passionate and makes lectures interesting and helps you learn through real world examples rather than textbooks. The class is very project focused and your grade will mostly depend on that. Absolutely take one of his classes if you can!
Amazing all around class, great professor!

Dr. Lowe is absolutely HILARIOUS and so down-to-earth. Half the classes he brings in food that he spends his own money on, and he's so chill. I found the quizzes to be really hard and really hard to study for, so that's why I got a B, but I put in a ton of effort for my group project(s) just because I felt inspired to by him (and got great grades).

Genuinely invested in his students' success. Offers tremendous support and is always available to answer questions and provide feedback. Personable and outgoing. Semester-long project with an actual client. Different schedules cause issues because we don't have class during the semester. He can be spontaneous at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting class and the professor is a cool guy. I think his quizzes were unnecessarily hard. He also gave out extra credit randomly to students which I thought was unfair. He also threw out his money randomly to students which seemed like a weird attempt to get good reviews.

Michael is a cool guy. There is a project during the semester, and it might affect your final grade.
Quizzes can be a little tricky, but it was not bad.

A teally great professor! His lectures are really easy to follow and we did lots of fun activities like trading breakfast food for a cluster analysis. He offered a lot of support and really great feedback throughout the group project. Also a very caring prof, was lenient with extensions and always available for meetings. The grades are v chill too
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Completely unfair that the teacher uses peer graded projects to justify your final project grade in the class when students who grade your project are t required to watch/attend your presentation (aka give random grades)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Accused me on multiple occasions of not watching the lectures for no reason when I provided multiple pieces of evidence against that claim (for reference I am a straight A student and never missed a day of class in my life). He was condescending and rude for no reason. Puts on a false facade.

WARNING, HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOUR GRADE OR SUCCESS!!! Only is trying to reach a quota with grade cutoffs and doesnt want a lot of people getting an A. If you get an 89.999999 you will receive a B even though the syllabus says 89. Will not offer a curve or any leniency. Seems nice in class but actually could not care less about your grade!!!

One of my favorite professors I've had here. He's an awesome dude and cares a lot about his students. This semester the lectures were pre recorded which sucked but he made them really interesting. Quizzes and your group project are the only grades in his course. Easy grader on the group project assignments though and provides good feedback.

Great professor! Very enthusiastic about marketing. Lectures are super entertaining. Quizzes can be a struggle if you don't thoroughly read the books. Semester-long group project. Definitely would take him again!

(Take during COVID-19 Spring 2021.) Made the most out of online class. Super approachable and helpful with semester group project. Incredibly funny and interesting recorded lectures. I learned SO MUCh from this class, and I would take this professor again in a heartbeat. Definitely take Dr. Lowe for Marketing Management.

Super funny and engaging professor. He clearly has a passion for the subject he is teaching and gives great feedback on assignments and projects. He is eager and willing to meet with students outside of class. He grades pretty easily and is clear with what he is looking for. His class has made me heavily consider a marketing concentration.

Michael Lowe is one of the best professors at Tech! As long as you put a speck of care into the class, you will pass with flying colors. His lectures are amazing and genuinely super enjoyable. Additionally, you can tell that he really cares about his students through his actions and feedback.

Dr. Lowe's class is very straightforward. There are no tests and entire class is based on the marketing project. His lectures are amazing, and he is great at making the content relatable and interesting. He is happy to help out with the project (which I highly recommend as he gives great feedback). Definitely recommend

Easily my favorite prof in two years at Tech. Super approachable and genuinely cares about each of his students. On top of that he's hysterical-he writes raps and even bought a girl a $120 pair of shoes to demonstrate a course concept. Super passionate about what he does, take his class!!!

Professor Lowe makes marketing interesting and fun by having entertaining lectures with occasional games. Theres a group project that you work on all semester long, but Professor Lowe is always there for guidance. We had to read two novels, but they arent bad. He also cancelled 3 in class quizzes that he originally planned on giving!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Lowe is one of the most energetic and caring teachers I've ever had. He really just wants all students to walk away with more knowledge and is realistic in assignments. The marketing project is heavily weighted though and doing well on that is critical. If you do what you're supposed to, this class should be very straightforward and really fun.

Very different kind of class. No tests/quizzes... all project/participation based. His grading is pretty subjective and the final class grade is on a curve: there were "too many As" my semester, so he bumped people DOWN to Bs. Overall though, he is pretty nice and his classes are pretty engaging. He once bought a girl Nike shoes.

There are two book readings, a few online Instagram posts, and one end of semester project. SUPER EASY CLASS. he really cares and just show up and pretend to participle and you will almost be guaranteed an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I found this class very effective. He put A LOT of effort (and a bit of money too) into the powerpoints and lectures, and was always considerate of student concerns/deadline issues, although not a pushover, so don't get too carried away. Easy A, but the charisma/pride he took in his work goes beyond the grade.

GREAT lecturer, very engaging and funny. Lowe is very knowledgable and brought in several outstanding guest speakers. No tests, but group project instead. Weekly quizzes ensure he is getting the info across well, but isn't too heavily weighted-- show up and pay attention and you'll be just fine. Highly recommended!

Literally my favorite professor in Scheller. Super funny, helpful, and intelligent. Plus, there are no exams, and he makes his syllabus really flexible. The biggest part of the class is a group project, which is doable. Just an overall great experience and great professor!!

Great teacher, very entertaining. Sometimes can ramble about a derivation you'll never need to know, but just toon it out. The class itself can be tough, but he's a kind grader. You need to actually know what you're doing to do well on tests, so go to lecture and give the hws a legitimate attempt (even though they aren't graded).

Classes are very proof and symbolic based. Only online posted material is a practice exam and homework, no solutions to either. Syllabus is 3 midterms 20% each and a final 40%. He does grade on a different scale which makes it easier though. If you are a good test taker and know how to study and prepare on your own then you'll probably get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he was actually a really good professor. Clearly knew the information he was teaching and was good at explaining concepts when asked in class. Tests were difficult, but it is supposed to be a challenging course so I thought they were fair. I felt that he wanted to create good engineers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He reads off directly from the textbook, but you're better off reading it yourself. Test average was 60, and you don't get any resources. Gave us an old test to study with no answers. He doesn't care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors in ME. This class was so proof-heavy that he spent no time explaining why or how anything mattered or applied in real life. He simply proved theorems, spent no time explaining their significance, and moved on. Reading the textbook was more educational than going to class. By the end, only 5/50 people showed up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a pretty bad teacher. He definitely felt like he was only here to teach grad students and he was confused that we didn't understand him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would NOT advise taking him. Hes obviously here for research and teaches to the smartest kid in the class. If you ask a question, he often makes you feel stupid for asking something. If you ask for extra help, he word for word responds with read the textbook everytime. Has alot of pride but alot of his notes are wrong and he hates being corrected

He gives the digital version of the textbook for free. The biggest problem is that his lectures just go through the text book almost verbatim with very few examples that represent homework or exams. His exams and homework are both difficult and graded tough, but there is a significant curve at the END of the class. 
He's ok and clearly very smart.

Ok so this guy might seem a little rough around the edges, but he wants you to learn fluids and he gets through the material. I always left the class feeling overwhelmed trying to understand the material but by the end of it, I got a good grasp of fluids. Tests are hard but fair and require critical thinking. Prepared me for later ME Classes.
