Lectures pretty much just went through the textbook, but he does point out some errors in the book, and derivations that were omitted. Homeworks are rather long/hard but are graded very leniently, tests are decently hard (mean of 60-65) but he curves at the end.
Not covid friendly. Makes people go to on campus class despite risks.

Took him for Thermo summer 2017 semester. He was always willing to help in his office hours and after class. His first exam took me by surprise and I worked for it the rest of the semester. There was a high standard of deviation for all the exams which boded well for the curve. The exams weren't so difficult in retrospect, time was the issue.

This is the worst professor I've ever had. He makes his homework and exams impossibly hard just for fun. Doesn't show up to appointments. If you ask a question or are struggling at all he's condescending and rude. (He literally cheered when I told him that his homework was so hard even the tutors couldn't figure it out.) He barely gives examples.

Professor Wessels is a very kind and passionate professor who is willing to help you out. The class is standardized and has very difficult exams, though. Professor Wessels, however, is very well-spoken and open to questions.

Wessels is a very passionate professor and I really appreciate him for showing his love for calculus. Make sure to attend lectures, fully do the homework, and learn to not make silly mistakes in exams. Also, just because you took calculus in high school doesn't mean you should brush the class off because it will get back at you.

Prof. Wessels is an amazing and enthusiastic teacher. I did not do well in the class as I did not study well and skipped many lectures, although my C+ got curved to a B- at the end. However, I guarantee that going to lectures and PLUS sessions will give you a great shot at an A grade. Prof. Wessels is very passionate about math and it really shows.

He is a good professor, I enjoyed the lectures. 1551 is standardized so professor doesn't matter so much but he is willing to help his students. He spoke clear and cares about his students. I took calc 1 in high school and still found 1551 not easy, so don't take it lightly and it wont be bad.

good prof, but calc is just a hard subject. these exams are made to fail you and there's no getting around it. better than most of the other professors and would def take him again. GO TO CLASS please please please go. it will just be even harder and confusing if you dont. sit in the front and go to office hours.

Professor Wessels was not helpful when asked questions. The lectures were not very encouraging or thorough. He is nice overall, but I did not gain much from his lectures. I found myself watching videos for further explanation on class topics. I would not recommend professor Wessels if you are looking for a more engaging professor.
I rarely went to class but he seemed invested in the material. I would say the lectures were pretty straightforward and his teaching was clear and easy to follow. I also hate linear algebra so...

Prof. Wessels is alright. His lectures often left me feeling a bit confused. I had a really great TA though, which helped me tremendously. The course material is hard, so I don't fault him for that. Just be prepared to learn half in class, half in studio.

Linear algebra can be a tough topic to understand, but he was good at explaining the concepts. This is a standardized course, so the content layout is the same for each section. I enjoyed how he would explain the examples in the notes, and I found that very helpful when trying to understand what was going on. He's a solid option overall!

Honestly the best prof I've ever had at tech. Lectures were always clear and engaging so I looked forward to going to his class at 8am. He's even better at his office hours or after class; he makes sure his students understand how to modify their approaches for strategizing. He was amazing and always very transparent, so tests were predictable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Linear Algebra is super hard (I learned that the hard way unfortunately). I didn't attend lecture too much and pretty much only showed up on exam days. But, when I did go to lecture, he was pretty enjoyable and gave some detailed lectures on the content (I wish I went more). Linear Algebra is standardized so the structure itself isn't his choice.

professor is good at conveying linear algebra on a very technical sense. if you need a really in depth understanding of mathematics to really get it, i would go to the textbook or office hours where you can get it really explained more but ngl it was fairly easy.

He cares for his students and wants us to do well, but he is very bad at lecturing. He only says what he writes and barely explains what or why he is doing certain things. Linear algebra is already a hard concept, and his minimal elaborations did not help that. I ended up skipping lectures and watching another professor's recorded lectures online.

Mr. Wessels is a great professor! I thought his lectures were clear and pretty easy to understand (for Linear lectures). I watched some Jankowski videos but honestly they didn't seem dramatically better to me? Maybe unpopular opinion but I really liked Wessels and would definitely take his class again.

if you're looking for a linear professor, just watch jankowski's lectures. while wessels is fine, the online lectures are so easy and digestable and things make more sense. Not worth attending in person in any sense of the word.

Mr. Wessels' class was okay, good for the subject he taught. I thought he was an okay teacher. His handwriting is not that bad in my opinion, but to be fair, I exclusively write in cursive. Out of all the teachers that teach this subject, Mr. Wessels is the norm and he's not bad at teaching.
Don't get why his rating is so low. He explains concepts proficiently and the only downside is his below average (for a teacher) handwriting.

I was nervous to take Dr. Wessels for calc 1 due to the reviews on here, but I am glad I have. He is a great lecturer and an even better person. He is very caring and encourages students to see math outside of the classroom.

Professor Wessels is a nice person, but definitely not a good professor. I ended up teaching myself multivariable calculus through other professors at GT and YouTube. His notes, lectures, and studios only made me more confused. For a period, he changed his office hours to during our studio time- when studio attendance was a part of our grade.

This class was absolutely awful and you should choose any other professor. He goes through at least 3 sections per lecture with no proper explanations. He reads what he writes as lecture goes on and spends zero time on actually explaining the material. His teaching method for math involves no explanation which basically leaves you against a wall.

Wessels is a really bad lecturer. He does not understand how to explain math. After the first couple of weeks, I started attending another professor's lectures so I would understand what was going on. At the same time, our quizzes our consistently harder than those of the other sections. He means well and is nice but is not a good teacher.

Dr. Wessels is a decent professor. He is very nice and helpful. He answers every single Piazza question himself and is available at office hours every week. His lectures contain a lot of notes, so it feels overwhelming but the notes are available online as well. Dr. Wessels' handwriting isn't the best, and he goes too fast at times, but is not bad.

Dr. Wessels is nice and caring, and he responds to Piazza/emails fast. His 2551 section was in loose coordination with others, but his exams/quizzes were considerably more difficult (+ very little partial credit out of very few points). He also moves fast during lectures with hard to read handwriting. Getting an A is difficult with him.

Moves at the speed of light. He takes around 20 minutes of a lecture to teach some of the hardest and most complex topics in multi. Hard to understand. Awful handwriting. I taught myself every topic in multi through watching YouTube videos. Did not learn anything from his lectures and I went to every single one. Never recommend.

Amazing Professor. As a non-math major, I was extremely intimidated by the advanced vector spaces for this class, but was glad that Dr. Loss was there to help! Go to office hours and TA Studios! They really make or break your content understanding. Lot of outside reading, but enforced by lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really caring professor and teaches linear algebra so well. Proofs are explained very clearly and prof is easily accessible. HW, tests, and quizzes are all super fair. Take him if you can

Loss loves linear algebra a lot. The problem is sometimes he loves it a little too much, and goes on crazy tangents proving unrelated theorems which, while interesting, mean we had to rush some of the actual course content. Two tests and one final basically determine your whole grade, so clutch up. Entertaining professor, but difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's clear he cares a lot more about making sure we're getting something out of the course rather than just teaching us what we need to know to pass the class. If you want to get more out of linear algebra than what you'd get from 1554, take 1564 with Professor Loss, you won't regret it :)

Extremely chill professor, he drops the lowest homework. The lectures were sometimes intimidating and I feel he went quite deep in some topics and even covered topics that were not on the exam, but the tests and final were reasonable. He is also caring and helpful in office hours but sometimes goes too fast in lectures. Would definitely recommend.

The greatest professor I've ever had. Has an immense understanding of the topic and gives really good lectures. Posts lecture videos and notes online. Will redo a proof as many times as needed for students to understand and makes quizzes/tests very easy compared to what they could be. I seriously hope I can take him again in the future.

While linear algebra may not be easy for everyone right at the beginning (I was in the same boat too), Loss's way of teaching fundamental concepts in such an easy way make it "intuitive" at the end. He ensures students understand whatever he teaches. His quizzes and HWs every alternate week make sure you don't fall behind and get enough practice.

Professor Loss embodies the ideal math professor. He thoroughly derives and proves concepts in class. But what stood out most was how he connected linear algebra to other fields like differential equations, calculus, and physics. While much of this is supplementary and not tested, it's a valuable bonus for anyone eager to learn more.

Loss has a great way of making everything seem so natural and simple without ever actually oversimplifying it; lectures tend to delve into more complex topics so you feel like you're being pushed to learn, but tests stay on the pretty easy side which makes grades less stressful. Very intelligent person with a light, positive attitude.

Loss is probably the best math professor I've had at Tech so far. He clearly enjoys teaching the subject, and wants to make sure everyone understands key concepts from linear algebra that are important in other fields. Provides practice tests, and gives really great lectures.

Linear algebra is one of those fields that isn't really intuitive until it "clicks" and everything comes together. Loss does a really good job of teaching the material in a very fundamental way so that everything eventually clicks. He is a really caring professor; drops your lowest midterm and really wants you to understand the topics well.

Awesome professor! He seemed really kind and you can tell he's interested in the topic. Dropped our lowest hw/test. I didn't really understand linear well conceptually when I took 1554, but he steps through everything nicely and makes sure you understand everything at a base level.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Loss's lectures were the only one I went to consistently this semester. He is a great lecturer with clear notes and explanations. Very helpful in office hours. Homework and tests were not too hard.

A great lecturer. Cares deeply about his students and their well being (we had several on-to-one checkups throughout the semester to see how we were holding up with the covid situation). Lecture material and homeworks could get a bit difficult, but the tests were easy.

Dr. Loss cares about his students and went out of the way to set up meetings with us individually to check our progress in the class. Analysis is very difficult but he makes it bearable. He's responsive to feedback and implements most suggestions that students ask. The two midterms also had extra credit which was nice. Lots of work though.
Teaches the material very clearly, and is always making sure we understand what is going on. Very caring -- he held a few brief one-on-one meetings throughout the semester to check up on us.
Just take it, the best math professor I have ever had in Georgia Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wow. One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares whether you understand it and he will explain it until you do.
Lectures can cover fairly difficult content, and homeworks are usually a bit of work, but the tests and grading scheme are easy. Tons of practice tests available, which is nice.

Dr. Loss's grading and assignments are pretty clear cut. While the class took effort, you can do well if you do the homework and the practice tests. His lectures are pretty good, though the class has 1 hour and 45 minute periods which is pretty rough.

Prof. Loss's lectures may not be the most engaging but if you can filter out the important information they are pretty helpful. Quizzes and tests were straightforward, nothing unexpected. The final is hard, but that was expected since the course materials can be difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Loss is an excellent professor and overall a cool guy to talk to. The content of Calc 3 is difficult, but if you put in effort, it's not hard to get an A. There are quizzes every week, two exams and a final. Quizzes and exams were fair, final was hard. Everything on quiz and exam you've seen before. Do practice textbook problems to study.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's not the most engaging lecturer. He mostly works examples on the board while facing it, which makes him hard to understand. That being said, his tests and quizzes are fair and you get two dropped quizzes at the end of the semester.

Professor Loss is a really cool dude. He's very approachable and friendly, and his lectures are actually quite helpful. His assignments and exams are all very reasonable, and he supplies practice exams and topic review sheets, so you pretty much know what to expect. Good class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: He takes his time to explain each concept thoroughly to you. The class is very textbook based. If you read the chapter, then homework and exam practice is straightforward. To prepare for exams, don't only depend on practice exam. Instead, focus on the topics list he gives you. The exams are straight off of the topics list.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Loss used to be hard, but he was paired with Morley to increase the percentage of kids getting As. As a result, the class is very doable, with extra credit on every exam. And I want to make it clear that it is VERY POSSIBLE TO PLACE OUT OF THE FINAL EXAM! I think about 50% of the class is able to. Highly recommend loss.

Funny guy, makes lots of jokes during class, the material really isn't too difficult. The class is very dry other than the jokes, not much there to hold anyones interest. He goes through lots of examples and sample tests during class. There are pop quizzes in recitation and overall grading is really clear. He doesn't put up with BS so don't try it.
Cool dude. If you go to office hours he'll go into depth on a topic from lecture. If you like math then he's the guy for you.

I thought that he did a great job presenting and explaining the material. However, it is imperative to attend class both for the explanation of the material and for the pop quizzes on recitation days.

This is not the easiest A, however the tests are fair. Everything on the test will be something you have seen in class before. He posts old tests on his website before the test so you will have something to study with. You can get extra credit on tests if you get the extra credit question. Overall good professor, very helpful but requires some work

I enjoyed this class. It isn't always easy, but he provides you with the tools you need to succeed. He had three old tests posted on his website for each section to practice (and 2 old final exams), but also gave out another practice or two before each test- pretty similar to actual test. If you like math, do the work, and study, you can do great.

Loss is a genius and he makes sure his students know that. Coming from high school his class was rough because he speeds through large amounts of material in one lecture. Getting a B is his class isn't hard but getting an A is. I got an A but I had to study around 15 hours each test to get an A. His class is definitely tough but it's doable.

If you are very good at math and teaching yourself then you might get a good grade. However, he is very hard to understand and does not really curve. I had a friend who got an 89 and ended up with a B. Our averages were always around a 55-65.

I didn't have Loss as a teacher, but I attended his lectures after a friend recommended his class. I loved his style of teaching. He can be hard to follow but if you like math, you will like the class.

Not an easy teacher to understand in lectures. He curves his first couple of tests but after that you are on your own. His tests are very hard but he does provide practice tests. Your TA will be a life saver.

Loss was very likeable and was very willing to help in office hours. However, his grading is pretty rough. He drops one test, and if you have a low grade (f/d/c), you will get a decent curve. If you have a B though, you're screwed. I had an 88 without a curve and didn't get an A, even though the average of the five test averages was like a 60-63

He was understandable and really knows the subject. He also posted old tests online that were helpful. Sometimes he goes the extra mile and somewhat complicatyes problems, but that stuff never ahows up on tests. Overall very straight forward and likable guy.

At first I had a really hard time following him in lecture, but eventually I got used to his teaching style and he became my favorite professor. He does stress theory a lot, but he relates it to application. Very good professor

I struggled with the way taught the subject. Coming from Calc BC in highschool, I expected to know how to do some of the problems already, but he emphasizes logic and does a lot of proofs, so I spent most of my time trying to learn the math from his perspective. If you can understand his practice tests and u go to his review sessions you will b ok.

He definitely knows his stuff. He's very approachable and genuinely nice. His lectures are a bit hard to understand and his handwriting isn't great either. His exams and quizzes however are very straight forward and easy(no tricks). As long as you keep up with the textbook, attending lectures aren't a necessity. Overall he's a good professor.

Knows his stuff, willing to help the individual, very approachable. Lots of material to be covered and he does a decent job at going over most of it, but you'll have to do your part as well if you want a good grade. He does curve at the end of the year but don't count on it to help you get a great grade.
Great professor overall. The material itself is very tough but he does a great job explaining it. There are always practice tests online that are very helpful. Curves slightly at the end of the year.

He is a very helpful professor and incredibly fair on the tests. He provides online practice tests and old tests with solutions and will go over the practice tests in a review session prior to each test. Lectures are fast but good. HW optional but helpful. Overall a great prof but not an easy A.
Great teacher; he would always go back and explain something if a single person in the class didn't understand. Homework is optional, but very useful for studying for tests (which still aren't easy).
Good teacher who really knows his stuff. He is pretty funny and you can understand him perfectly, but he can go fast in lecture. His tests are very fair though.
He is an amazing professor who is incredibly passionate about his work and his students.

Lukas is one of my favorite ECE professors I have ever had. He is so passionate in his lectures and takes student feedback very seriously! He clearly communicated what we need to do to succeed in the class, leaving no surprises. He is very accessible by office hours and email and is a very reasonable professor in general. 10/10 recommend

Pretty average professor. He legitimately enjoys teaching students and is one of the few professors to hold in person. The in class examples are easy, but homework is hard. He's available to help, but I often had to look in the book or interpret the question because its not clear. His exams are much easier than the homework and the average is high.
I don't know how his tests are yet, but I love his lectures and his passion about the content of the subject. He really cares for his students and is super accessible outside class.
You use all sorts of media, from movies to graphic novels. If you want an engaging English class that isn't just writing papers, take him.

Dr. Rodewald is the most supportive English teacher/professor I've ever had. He gave humongous amount of feedbacks that are very helpful, detailed, and encouraging. His lectures was energetic and fun. The workload was reasonable and did not take more than 3 hours per week. Overall, he's amazing and I am already taking him again.

He is very relatable, and doing the bare minimum you can still get a B. He gives some extra credit to people who read his emails and is very lenient on grading. Make sure you do the readings, especially the ones that have quizzes and you'll do fine in the class :3

Dr.Rodewald couldn't have been a better professor. He has successfully made an English class enjoyable and thought-provoking. He is extremely caring of his students and accessible outside of class. His grading criteria are clear and realistic. He also allows for 3 extension passes, so use those wisely! I highly recommend taking him for ENGL 1101.

He tries to make class as interesting as possible, and he usually succeeds. He doesn't give huge chunks of reading to do usually, and if there is a longer reading he won't give any homework to get done during that time. He is willing to give extensions if you email ahead of time.
He is supe friendly and funny and gets along with the students however sometimes his feedback/lectures can be a bit cryptic and hard to understand.

Dave is generally liked by ID students because he's just like an old nice guy. The class isn't that hard, you can get an A. The assignments are time consuming and difficult, should not be a 1 credit class. Stay on top of your work and you will be fine

Dave is a nice guy. He's pretty funny, and he's got a good personality. He comes late to every lecture by at least half an hour, but will deduct points from students for being 6 minutes late. He seldom grades, and leaves almost all lecturing to TAs. Any amount of money at GT pays him, is an overpayment for the amount of work he does.

Dave is an Awesome prof. He has really good lectures and clear criteria for assignments. However, when you ask questions he is not very clear and will sometimes say something to improve and then grade the opposite way. He's very nice and caring but ask lots of questions so you know whats up. Also he very kind and supportive of peopled work.

He is very kind and passionate about his field, especially car design. He is a harsh but honest grader. His biggest fault is just that it takes him a very long time to grade assignments which can lead to your grade being a mystery until the very last second.

Dave is a super kind and bubbly professor. His grading can be harsh at times but he gives good feedback. A homework assignment or project is assigned every week and the following class starts with a class critique of that assignment. Don't underestimate the amount of time you'll have to spend on this class. If you try your best you should do fine.

Although he can be a tough grader, he gives great feedback in a class-wide discussion. This way all students benefit from each others critiques and lessons. He also is very personable so he is easy to talk to if you need some one on one help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She tries to teach a liberal arts class at a tech school. It's not working. Wouldn't recommend!
I dislike her teaching for pedagogical reasons. Iykyk

Ah, Professor Dombrowski, what a delight. First-time teaching and it shows—vague instructions, harsh grading, unrelated readings, and stellar irony (she reads slides while telling us not to). Communication skills? Top-notch, if making students cry counts. Would love to avoid this class, but it's required for MS-HCI. Lucky us, right?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable. Sometimes went off on tangents that were hard to follow but generally interesting. Need to pay attention in class because test questions are from the lecture, but most is not on the slides. Had weekly readings + podcasts for a grade, two big projects. She is engaging and not too hard of a grader. Wants you to care. Overall 10/10.

Shes super knowledgeable and if you want to learn, ask questions about her experiences. She was easy to listen to and kinda funny. However, she assigns podcast and reading reflections every week which took me probably 4 hours on average to complete. Shes a fair grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lynn is really nice and clearly knows her stuff, but the online/distance format of COVID really hurt her. She's not the most organized/best at using online resources, which can make understanding assignment expectations and deadlines frustrating at times. The class is meant to be discussion based, and would have been much better if taken in person.

Dr. Brown is a tough grader but is REALLY helpful. She's always willing to spend time giving you feedback. However, I felt like she was a bit unclear about what she expected for each assignment the from time to time. She gives plenty of time for each assignment, including classes for peer reviewing. Overall, it was a tough class but enjoyable.
Dr. Brown is smart and passionate about what she teaches. She is a tough grader, but willing to help.

Dr. Brown is a fantastic professor. She gives a workshop day, sometimes with peer review, for every assignment. She makes time to give guidance on bigger projects, and is super helpful. There is a lot of work outside of class, but is definitely manageable.

She has a heavy curve and gives extra credit. Make sure you write down the answers to the clicker questions; studying them is a good way to prepare for exams. Her class is boring, but she explains things well. Clicker questions are part of the grade. She explicitly states she doesn't test on anything she doesn't talk about in lecture.
Nice professor with genuine interest in the class.  Easy to learn from.
Provides insight from research interest.

What a boring class.... I bombed the first 2 tests, 60 and 47. Got a 71 on the final (not cumulative). Those are each weighted 20%. Lab is 30% (has used same labs for like 10+ yrs) and attendance/clicker is 10%. Extra credit assignment add 4 points to your overall grade. My grade ended up being 79, which was a "B." An "A" ended up being an 84.
Amazing teacher. Dedicated to making you feel at ease with the material and able to walk you through a potentially terrible course. Consider yourself lucky if you get him!

Fantastic teacher. Class is mostly discussing older papers from the literature. Very forgiving grader. There's usually a tangent during class, but its generally educational or actually funny. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you won't be able to pass the test without it.
Absolutely AMAZING professor! The Lab and class are both challenging but he makes it fun and very interesting

He is a really cool and quirky guy. He really enjoys chemistry, and he rolls to class everyday on a RAZOR. Lectures are optional, but he does such a good job explaining the lecture notes, that if you attend class, you should be able to pull out with a B. He is very good at explaining chemistry. Not a hard class if you attend lectures.
Greatest English Teacher of all time. Simply sensational

Absolute goat and the most underrated English teacher. Extremely chill grader, thoughtful, and cares about her students (will give an extension, help, etc if needed). The workload is low and you will get an A if you just submit everything. Trust me, take this teacher

Easy and chill class. As long as you know how to write and pay attention for most of the class, you should have no problem getting an A. Professor Mann is very kind and super understanding, so her class should be the last thing you have to stress about. There is some reading, but most of the work is done in class and it's not that hard anyway.

Dr. Mann is an amazing professor! She is super nice and caring and wants you to succeed in her class. Her course theme follows bioethics and scientific experimentation which was extremely interesting to learn about. Overall, I really enjoyed her class and definitely recommend her. Just do your work and participate in class and you will get an A.

I attended nearly every lecture and found them to be very helpful to succeeding in the course. He's also a funny teacher, and provides lots of resources (like practice tests which very closely reflect what's on the exams).

Compared to the four credit MATH 2551, MATH 2550 taught by Dorian is more difficult. However, his exams closely resemble his practice exams in format and question type. He is a hilarious lecturer and loves talking about his random life experiences. While slightly more difficult than expected, I would highly recommend. He's a great and funny guy.

Everyone below me complaining about test difficulty is lying or stupid. His exams follow the practice exams he gives out, and he tells you in lecture what will be on the exam. Entertaining professor who genuinely cares for students' grades. MML homework feels like busy work, but if you just watch all the lectures and pay attention, it's an easy A.

Doron is a funny person but a bit disorganized and bad with technology. He's a tough grader and his exams are not exactly a walk in the park. The biggest thing is, for a 2 credit class, this class is trickier than seems fair imho.
Barley teaches the content just gives us notes with formulas and some examples and expects us to understand. Also tests are very hard and not like the practice exams.
I love Doron!!! He's such a funny lecturer and his materials are very accessible on Canvas. Practice tests are basically the real exam. Take 2550 with him!
Amazing lecturer, very entertaining and engaging. Lectures are a bit fast paced but he records them so you can go back and watch them later. Exams are basically just like the practice exams.
Very hilarious person! Thought his lectures were a bit fast but he recorded them which was good for me since it was a 8 am class.
Doron is hilarious

Very easy class, notes are detailed and contain everything you need to learn and know for the test. The test itself is very easy, easier than the questions given in the course files usually. The professor is also really chill, and grading is very lenient. They give way more credit than you probably deserve.

Good lectures, nice person as long as it's not related to exams/grades. A large portion of my section missed a weekly quiz (not an exam) because it was not on Canvas calendar, worth 1.25% total, and he refused to show us any mercy. Very similar to the whole Math department at this school, absolute harvesters of toil. God forbid they help a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty sure I'm on track to get an A, because he's a very good teacher. He's also really funny and engaging. I like that the lectures can be held on zoom, so I don't have to walk on the opposite side of campus. Keep up with the homeworks and quizzes and lectures and everything should be good.
good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lubinsky is an engaging lecturer who makes complex topics digestible. While tests are challenging, attending studio and using resources like unstuck AI can help. Overall, a worthwhile course if you're willing to put in the work.

Dr. Lubinsky is a great professor. His classes are instructive and entertaining, and I find myself wanting to go to his classes.  He is very fair in grading, and is knowledgeable in the subject. He breaks down confusing concepts into steps, and it's very helpful. I would definitely take this class again, and further classes with Dr. Lubinsky.

Dr. Lubinsky is one of the best professors I've ever had at Georgia Tech. He's very particular with steps, and he's genuinely funny. HIs grading criteria, while somewhat strict, is extremely fair and you can tell he knows what he's doing, even if he goofs every now and then. Overall, highly recommend you take a class with Dr. Lubinsky if you can.

Lubinsky is a great lecturer, adds humor to lectures & is a great guy. Expectations & material are clear, HW & take-home quizzes are very reasonable. If you attend studio & do the practice tests, you'll be fine. Tests are similar to practice tests, not actually much harder, just kind of annoying derivatives/integrals. Cheat sheet on the final!

Tests are very hard and make up the majority of your grade. Practice tests are given, but their difficulty does not match that of the real exams. We also got no formula sheets on any midterms, when several other 2551 professors provided their students with formula sheets for all 3 exams. Would not recommend.

Lubinsky is a good lecturer. However, there were lots of needlessly difficult integrals. I was very pressed for time on tests; my peers in other sections didn't have this same issue. There's lots of homework and weekly online quizzes that are only worth a quarter of your grade. Be prepared for the bulk of your grade to come from difficult tests.

Professor Lubinsky is an OK lecturer. He goes on random tangents sometimes, wasting class time and disrupting the flow of the lecture. His quizzes are like child's play compared to what you get on exams. His exams are much harder than the practice test that he gives out, and so far none of the exams have been curved despite the averages being a C.

He is an okay lecturer, that's it. If you are going to be a mediocre lecturer then you better make exams doable. The exams are very difficult and make up most of your grade. He also goes on random tangents that distract from the material being taught. Unnecessarily difficult.

Lubinsky is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had in my life. His lecture style is incredible, and he's a very fun and engaging professor. He also gives some of the clearest notes ever, and explains complex math in a way that feels digestible instead of overwhelming. I cannot recommend him enough.
Taught the subject matter well and his lectures were good. Recorded his lectures as well. The tests were hard compared to the homework given.

He's very good at lecturing, but the tests can be pretty difficult in comparison to the practice tests and studio worksheets sometimes. He's still probably the best multi option because he keeps class pretty entertaining, records all his lectures, and is good at explaining things.

Lubinsky does move very fast in his lectures, but all lectures are also recorded. His exams are harder than other 2551 classes, but he also goes into more depth and I felt that I came out with a better understanding of multivariable calculus than some of my other peers who took other profs.

Dr. Lubinsky is a great person but goes very quickly. Homework was twice a week and a quiz once a week. Tests were really hard as they contained some pretty heinous derivatives and integrals at times. Practice tests were very similar to real tests. He is a solid teacher, but I wish I would have taken someone with easier tests. This class was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In my opinion, he is a harder professor than some of the other ones because he goes extremely fast. He also does not really motivate his lessons, so its more memorization based. He does it make it clear what the tests are like and does a good job on lecture notes. Not terrible, but overrated based on other rate my professor reviews.

He was a great professor that made the wealth of information covered in Math 2551 lectures enjoyable, with a great sense of humor. His grading was fair and the guidelines were clear, and whenever I had a question or an issue arose, he was very quick to answer and provide helpful guidance/feedback. Highly recommend!

His lectures explained the material really well. He also posts his handwritten lectures + recorded lectures + typed notes for each chapter on canvas. Did all my homework (MyLab) and went to studios so found it pretty easy. Stopped going to lecture about halfway because he was kinda rude and made some questionable jokes, some jokes were funny though

Professor Lubinsky was a really funny and engaging lecturer and I learned a lot in his course. He was super organized too and his notes were detailed, comprehensive, and posted on Canvas. The first two tests weren't bad but the third test and final were hard, so beware
Professor Lubinsky is a good professor his lectures are clear and concise, he's a fantastic grader and very fair. The class and content is difficult but he makes the content digestible.

Professor Lubinsky is one of the most amazing professors I've had at Tech. Very lecture heavy, but a fair grader, and if you come to class and do the homework, you should be fine. He's also very light-hearted and loves to tell small stories and joke in class but never goes off on tangents.
This guy has a cute and funny accent. Don't let that distract you though... This class requires much work. Do the homework without cheating and you'll be okay. Cheat if you want to, it will be fine.

Dr. Lubinsky is an entertaining yet informative lecturer. Definitely feels like a 4-hour class as it can seem pretty heavy with concepts at times. He does a good job at breaking everything down, even though he may work a bit fast-paced. You can tell he cares for the students though.

LOVE Lubinsky! I took Multi in high school but decided to take it again and it was worth it. The class was easy to me but I already had a foundation. Lubinsky is hilarious and has so many fun stories. Please engage with him, you won't regret it

Professor Lubinsky's multi class was a good 4 credit hour course. The homework takes a while, and the class requires a diligent effort, but it is very clear was is required for an A. I would sign up for him again in a heartbeat due to his inspirational nature and witty math jokes!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very funny but also more or less effective instructor. Hard exams. Long and frustrating homeworks but multiple attempts allowed so ultimately easy points.

lectures are very old school but amazing. prepare to do a lot of homework, but expected for a 4 credit class. his midterms are very similar to the practice tests he posts and reviews. pay attention in class and you will be fine.

Professor Lubinsky is a great lecturer who throws in mostly funny jokes whenever he can. Although there is lots of homework, it is great preparation for the tests and (open note) quizzes, and it allows you to keep a good grade while not having to get all As on tests. He is one of my favorite professors at Tech so far.

Funny, kind-hearted professor who is very knowledgeable on the subject matter. Lectures and homework can be long but lead to success in the course. Homework and easy quizzes leave some room to get an A even if you aren't stellar on the tests. Favorite professor at Georgia Tech so far!
A+ when it comes to lectures, C- when it comes to communication. Sit in the front and laugh at his jokes, even when they're really really bad, it makes him more approachable.

Lubinsky is a funny and knowledgable lecturer, but he's also a grumpy old man. His jokes are often pretty abrasive and he projects an attitude of indifference towards us students. That being said, the tests are fair (and quizzes are open note) so as long as you do the homework it's not hard to do well. Beware though, TONS of MyMathLab homework

The funniest professor I've had so far, and one of my best experiences at GT! His jokes keep me incredibly engaged throughout the lecture which already contains thought provoking and interesting concepts.

The class is not really demanding, you really only need to study for tests and do MML. I think an A is definitely manageable since his practice exams do prepare you well as they closely are formatted exactly like the tests just harder algebra I would say. He also drops the lowest of the three midterms.

Professor Lubinsky is great. He teaches by explaining and writing notes by hand at the same time, and then he uploads them as well. His lectures are great, and I would highly recommend attending them. Watch the lectures and do all the homework to the best of your abilities. The class may not be the easiest, but an A is still manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures were very engaging and he provided a lot of examples for every subject, making sure we always understood the material correctly. Whenever I had an issue, I would just email professor Lubinsky; and he was always helpful, taking care of our metal health at all times.

I love the jokes, but I think the online format makes it difficult to understand the material if you're new to it. The questions on piazza aren't thoroughly answered and he sometimes goes fast in the lectures. I stopped attending the lectures within a month- just studied from the textbook and youtube. But it's an easy class if you put the effort.

I barely attended lectures. I think the online format made it hard for me to grasp info when he was just copying notes from a set of pre-written notes. Ngl, he's a fun guy, but I don't get the popularity. But he's probably better in person. Luckily, 2550 isn't too hard. I sometimes watch youtube/read the textbook and the MML hw forces me to study.

MATH 2551 was the most brutal class I've ever taken at Tech, so I suppose I was lucky to take it with professor Lubinsky. While he was frustratingly uncompromising as the world transitioned to COVID life, he was always quite funny and a great, if not very fast lecturer. This course will be tough either way, so you may as well take it with the best
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The material is fair, but Prof. Lubinsky has absolutely no idea how the online homework system works and does not care to give students any wiggle room, whatsoever. If you reach out to him for help, his response will lack so much substance that you'll be left more frustrated than if you hadn't emailed. Good teacher, pathetic communicator.

Prof. Lubinksy is the best math professor I've taken at Tech so far. Somehow he makes writing with a bic pen on a white piece of paper work better than any professor does. He's also very funny. Definitely do take him if you can.
Very difficult class, but completely worth it for his witty jokes and amazing personality!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lubinsky is a great lecturer and thorough note taker. Class is engaging, but he does post notes on each lecture outside of class, and it's even better than the textbook. The switch to online classes caused some changes, but the most difficult aspect of the class is that it's only homework, midterms, and the final.

Lubinsky truly makes lectures worth it. He is funny, light-hearted, and great at conveying the material. The concepts he teaches are not hard to understand, but the calculations he makes you perform on tests can be very rigorous.

You are GEORGIA TECH students, you go to **BIG** school! Will miss hearing this :(. The tests can be tough, (especially w/o partial credit when online), but there is a reason why everyone wants to be in his section. This level of difficulty is to be expected as we do not go the 'The Okefenokee School for Wayward Boys and Girls'.

Lubinsky made the 8AM worth it, and tests weren't too bad if you work through the practice exams and hw problems. However, sometimes his piazza answers (when he did answer) were kinda rude, but he was definitely the best at explaining concepts for this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was an amazing lecturer for multi. The class is very tough, but he made lectures enjoyable by telling funny stories about his dog. The tests are very fair if you do the practice tests, and he lets you drop your lowest exam. No quizzes. So much respect for him as he deals with a lot of crap from dual enrollment kids on piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lubinsky's teaches well, and is clear on what will be on the test. His first three tests are fine (mirrors the practice test), but the fourth (online due to the pandemic) is challenging since there's no partial credit. However, he is not so helpful when you have questions (does not respond to piazza posts with care).

Lubinsky genuinely could care less about you as a student in his class. Emails to him are responded to with rude remarks that make you feel stupid and don't answer your questions. Exams are weighted at 90% of your grade and MyMathLab that takes forever is only 10%. Went to office hours -he ate his lunch the whole time and didn't answer my question.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lubinsky is by far the best professor I've had so far at Tech. Lectures are fast paced, but he does an excellent job dissecting a difficult subject into exactly what you need to know. He also includes hilarious stories and comments in his lectures that make it worth the 8 am. Lots of tough homework, but our lowest test was dropped. Hard final.

Great professor. Funny dude. Always willing to help when you show up at his office but has NO clue how Math Lab works so keep that in mind. Posts lecture notes. If you want to do really well Id read up on that one sad dog movie because it seems to be his favorite film, lol. Final is HARD, try have a solid grade beforehand.
Class is very difficult and has no leniency when it comes to the quite long homework assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Lubinsky manages to make one of the harder and dryer math classes bearable and at times enjoyable. Midterms are not too bad as you are able to drop your lowest one. In my case I did really well on three and absolutely bombed the other one. The Practices midterms are helpful. The Final is very hard so try to come in with a high grade.

Lubinsky is worth the 8 am; his jokes make waking up early bearable. He is great at explaining material, and he also posts his notes which are VERY helpful. Exams are generally fair, but the final is difficult! Overall, he's a solid choice for Multi.

Lubinsky's lectures are usually worth going to, but he does post lecture notes online for every class, so don't stress if you miss. Tests are pretty fair, but the final is definitely a lot tougher than the midterms. Homework is online through My Math Lab and pretty helpful for studying. Definitely a good teacher and an interesting dude. Worth it!

Lubinsky really works to make sure students understand the "motivation" behind the concepts, not just the formulas, and that makes the class much more enjoyable. Hegenuinely cares about students and will help you if you ask. The final is difficult so study hard and do as well as you can on th emidterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful choice for MATH 2551. So caring and explains tough concepts well. Never feel bored in this class because of he jokes all time, though not everyone gets it. MML Homework is long; tests (4 midterm + 1 final) make up 90%, but with lowest dropped. Careful, do well on midterms (90+ possible if study) not to sweat on the final (really tough).

Lubs was legendary; tough class (lots of hw and crazy hard tests), but you'll do well if you go to lecture and do the recitation worksheets. Easily the funniest professor too; I personally never read the textbook, but many do. He's also always willing to help if you need it. All around 5.

Professor Lubinsky was absolutely amazing at teaching. Its a lot of material to cover, but he made every topic seem like a breeze. He stays upbeat and energetic throughout the entire lecture and never made me want to fall asleep, even at 8am. 100s on midterms was definitely doable if u study. hw is a bit tricky and the final was truly devastating

Dr. Lubinsky is super knowledgeable about the material in MV Calc. His lectures are great, but the material of the course is tough especially the second half. The practice tests are almost exactly like the real ones. Do the homework to understand everything better, and try to have a high grade before the final because the final was really tough.
It would be better if the class weren't at 8 A.M. Lectures were good, but I was always tired especially at the end. The final had a lot of new material on it that brought my grade down.

Lubinsky is an all around incredible professor. He explains concepts extremely clearly and is very specific about the expectations for the class. He also keeps lectures interesting with personal anecdotes and occasional self degradation. His tests are rather difficult, especially the final, so be prepared to study hard.
He made the class (which felt like drinking from a fire hydrant, btw), be manageable. He made it make sense. A great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do WHATEVER you have to do to be in Lubinskys class! He really knows whats hes talking about. Hes super organized and makes 2551 relatively easy. His practice tests are basically exactly what his tests are. I promise its definitely worth getting up even though its an 8 am class. Plus hes pretty funny.

MyMathLab homeworks take up an entire sunday. Lecture is decent but recitation matters more. My TA could barely speak english so I had to teach myself with uploaded notes. Skip all the theory, he doesnt test on it. Drop lowest of the 4 tests, which was the weirdly confusing test 3. Final was the hardest test I've ever taken.. 75% on v new material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: hilarious professor. i love his sense of humor and it was the only thing motivating me to get up at 8am to go to his classes. his lectures are incredibly easy to follow and useful. homework can be tedious and the written portion of the final is difficult but tests are easy as long as you can do the practice tests

Great professor with humor. The class was 8am everyday so I didnt go that much but it didnt hurt me because he posted the notes online. Study the practice tests and you'll do fine on the test. He drops 1 of the tests but he intentionally makes one of them hard bc test 3 had a very low average. Final was one of the hardest things I've done at Tech.

Lubinsky is a great professor. I would recommend him to anyone who needs to take 2551. I took this class as a 5 day a week 8am lecture and do not regret it at all. It was worth the 8am. However, if you don't feel like going to lecture, you don't even have to because he uploads his lectures online! Tests are very similar to the practice tests!

I took the class as a distance student, and Professor Lubinksy was really great! He jokes much about "Okeefenokee college" or something like that.. but he really teached the material well, and I felt well prepared for the tests! Just do the homework, and you will be fine..

Lubinksy is honestly pretty good. I definitely learned a lot in class. The tests were pretty difficult and long. When I was struggling to finish tests, I reached out to him for help, but found him to be very unhelpful. However class is kept engaging through his humor. Not a bad teacher, just really difficult.

Took this as a distance class last semester. The guy is an amazing lecturer, and the class is fairly easy. Print out typed notes, follow along with lectures and study the night before tests and you'll get an A. He did say there would be a curve, but it ended up being something like a tenth of a point, so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hilarious professor and great lecturer. Explains concepts clearly with sufficient practice problems. His typed notes are also a big help and very detailed.

Amazing professor. His lectures are very informative and enjoyable - I only wish I had attended more of them.   Honestly, go to class, listen to this awesome professor. His analogies and stories are very high class, and if you do the assigned work too (yup, there's online homework), you will be fine.  After all, we are Georgia Tech students. :)

This is a difficult class, but Professor Lubinsky manages to make it fun and engaging. Tests are straightforward if you do the homework and go over practice exams. Definitely try to take him if possible!

Awesome professor that teaches the material very well. His tests are fair and if you do the homework you will be fine. However, his office hours are useless. He was more focused on the cricket match on the TV in his office than helping us (well he is from South Africa)

He taught the material well while managing to be funny at the same time. He was very clear about the material on the test, and the examples in class were representative of the types questions asked on the exams.

This man is a memelord. Be ready to hear "You're going to Georgia Tech" or "This isn't the Outer Okefenokee Swamp Community College for Wayward Boys and Girls." This class was an 8AM but he was funny and engaging enough to make that okay. I originally didnt watch any of the lectures, but when I did the class was substantially easier.
Fantastic professor. Class was very enjoyable because of his lectures. Prepared us well for the tests with the combination of lecture and the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class was very enjoyable, because he taught the material in a very clear and concise manner, made it clear what was necessary to succeed in his class, and was funny throughout the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: As long as you pay attention in lecture and you do the homework, you'll do great. His lectures are very clear and easy to understand and he's funny which helped make it more interesting for an 8am. The only complaint is that he is hard to talk to outside of class, but he is a great lecturer.

I took MATH 2552 online by watching Doron's lectures and he was great. His lectures are very helpful and he posts notes to each one on T-Square. Tests were not very hard. Just do the homework and you'll be fine.
I found the course challenging.  He gets sidetracked often.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, lectures are very helpful and interesting since Lubinsky is a pretty funny professor. Tests and homework are fair if you understand the material. The only downside is that every time I'd visit his office hours to ask him a question about an assignment it seemed like he was kind of annoyed that I was there.

He is an okay teacher, but his lectures were relatively confusing. The material is extremely hard to understand sometimes, and he isn't very helpful when questions are asked. Always compare your graded tests with friends because sometimes he takes off different point values for the same mistake.

He was a great teacher and made the class very interesting with his sense of humor. The class material is very difficult and it is hard to catch up if you miss a class, though the pop quiz dates are usually pretty predictable. He gives a moderate amount of homework. He says he is making tests harder next year.

This man is the bomb dot com. He is pretty clear and helpful. His reviews are nice. Go through Piazza if you have questions. His South African accent and stories kept the class pretty interesting. Expect to hear either "You're Georgia Tech students!" or "This isn't the Outer Okefenokee School for Wayward Boys and Girls" during every lecture.
Don't bother emailing him asking for help because his responses are not helpful and are often one word answers. Lectures can be disorganized and he speeds through the material so pay attention.

he can be a stubborn old man when he wants to, but he is funny, and he is a decent professor. he does not care much for his students, and trying to show up for office hours multiple times proved futile. I would not take another class with him, but i respect him, and his southafrican accent made things entertaining.

Phenomenal professor! He delivers well-organized, coherent lectures with plenty of examples and just the right amount of theory, plus he's absolutely hysterical. His class is a lot of work, and his final exam is extremely difficult, but I feel like I know the material extremely well. He is a MUST HAVE for Calc II!!

Professor Lubinsky is one of the best professors I ever had. His lectures are very comprehensive and he is very thorough and helpful. I actually ended up learning a lot in his class and really enjoyed it as well. I would highly recommend him.

He was the best math teacher I've had. He was amazingly clear about the content, gave plenty of examples so that new topics were easily understood, provides practices tests that are 90% of the actual tests and he keeps you entertained throughout the class while still teaching effectively. If you have the opportunity to take his class, DO IT!!!

Great Professor. Teaches concepts as best as they can be taught, so it's practice that makes it stick. Tests are hard. Written homework assignments, which are graded, are harder, so if you do the homework before each test you should be fine for the tests. Definitely possible to get an A if you try.
great professor. Knows what he is teaching. Like to have him on my next  course

Get Lubinsky for Calc 2!  He is a very good(albeit fast)teacher and he's even pretty entertaining.  This class will not be a walk in the park by any means, but you get to drop one of your tests, which is extremely valuable.  Long homework packets, but I'd absolutely take his class again.
Very good professor, with a great personality (and accent). The class is still hard though

Lubinsky was an absolutely awesome professor. I had him for Calc II in Spring 2012. The material is really difficult, but I feel that he did an excellent job of conveying the methods necessary to solve the problems. It is evident that he has a deep understanding of the curriculum and is more than capable of teaching it.
He is really good at teaching. His homework is original worksheets, not from the book. They are the most difficult. I rarely went to class, but got an A because I made a 114/125 on his final.
Great Professor! Try to get him no matter what!

He is definitely my favorite calculus professor at Georgia Tech so far. His notes in class are very easy to follow and he has practice homework and tests online which are the exact format as the homework and tests. The homework was a little challenging at first but this class overall was very good. I would definitely recommend Lubinsky's class.

One of the best professors in gatech in terms of lecture quality. He delivers one of the clearest and most well-organized lectures. However, don't expect this class to be an easy class. The tests and homeworks are not easy, and you have to put some efforts in it.
He is so adorable, he worked examples in class and gave practice test that were almost the same as the test we would take. Homework counted for more than the test itself did.

BEST TEACHER AT GEORGIA TECH HANDS DOWN. I learned a lot from him. Throws jokes out during class while teaching. Do anything to take him, or just sit in on his lectures. Do the previous practice exams, they will help with the exams. Awesome professor!

Really enjoy going to class even if the lecture notes are online. Homework is tough but it really prepares you for the tests. Previous exams are available and most times resemble the tests. Highly recommend taking it. (can't say yet for the final as I am currently taking his class)
Great professor. Was always entertaining and could explain the material really well. One of my favorites. You HAVE to get him for Calc 2!
Very good notes and easy tests (except for the final which is the hardest test I have ever taken).
GREAT TEACHER, funniest teacher of all time...very easy and interesting if you plan on taking calc 2 he's your man

TAKE THIS CLASS. If you are considering taking calc 2, no one tops Lubinsky. His lectures are clear and detailed and you'll actually understand it. Tests and homework are fair and resembles the previous terms' and are all online.. same with notes. One of Tech's finest.

Awesome professor and a great teacher.  Explains things very well and provides many examples which can be found helpful for preparing for the tests.  Also, tests are similar to old tests, which he posts online.  Would recommend highly for any class he instructs.

MUST GET THIS PROFFESOR. You can actually understand him. He tells jokes during class and makes class actually fun. Attendance is not mandatory because he gives the notes online, but i recommend going. Very helpful, does many many examples in class. Tests are more problem based. He post old tests that are similar to his own. Very Good Teacher.

Easy to get an A with. What you get from his class depends on you. Tests and exams are not challenging at all and you can get by without knowing much (this is my personal opinion). But I do think that he does a good job. Lots of examples are offered for you to grasp the concept. BUT I MUST EMPHASIZE YOU CAN GET BY WITHOUT LEARNING MUCH.

Great teacher! He makes calc 2 simple b/c he doesn't go so deep into theory like most other calc teachers do. The class is straight forward; he works lots of examples and tests are almost exactly like practice tests. A little awkward one on one, but oh well.

I seriously love this man. I had him for one of the hardest classes at Tech (in my first semester no less), and he made it easy and interesting, and I feel like I learned a lot. I never missed his lectures because they were just too funny. Thank you Professor Lubinsky!

Awesome teacher. Online notes, clear and thorough teaching, tests and homework are very similar to previous years. Makes math very entertaining! Very easy to get an A, as you can drop lowest test score. VERY Highly recommended.

Easy, funny, and excellent teacher. Very rare at Tech. No need for the textbook. All notes are online. Gives you a month to do homework, which is almost exactly like previous homework online. Study and do the old tests a night or two before the test and you'll do fine. The final is beastly long, but not that difficult. Bottom line: I love this man.

His lectures are entertaining. He explains the subject very well and he was one of the first math teachers I've had that I could actually understand through their accent. Old homeworks and tests are pretty much all you need to do his new homeworks and tests. Definitely take him
Awesome professor. He's funny and entertaining yet he's thorough and easy to understand. Highly recommended.

Great prof, his tests are exactly like his old ones which he posts online. He also provides typed notes which are very useful. Prob the best prof Ive had so far at tech. Just study his old exams and youll get an A for sure.

He is a very good teacher. Unlike most Tech teachers, he actually TEACHES! He explains the topics well and provides you with notes so good that you won't even have to touch your textbook. He posts previous exams online that are just like the tests he'll give you in class. He's one of the fairest teachers I've had at Tech. Highly recommended.
His lectures and exams are very straight forward. As long as you go to class and recitations and spend some time studying before exams, you should be fine.
FABULOUS teacher. Practice exams are almost exactly like his tests. HE explains everything clearly and grades fairly. One of the best teachers that i had at Tech my freshman year

He did a great job at explaining the material and he was always very willing to explain things in such a way that were easy to understand. His tests are extreamly fair!  One of the fairest teachers here at tech.  He did an amazing job at teaching the course, I feel that I learned something.
He's a good prof even though his jokes can send one off to sleep. He knows his subject well and is very helpful outside class also.

The professor did not give helpful comments to class presentations- often having expectations that he did not clarify prior to class, and overall was rude and unaware of his brashness in class. Students often felt like they could not raise questions in class becuase of way responded to them.  He was also dismissive of topics he wasn't aware about.

GREAT lectures. Opennote quizzes use NotebookLM. 10% Extra Credit, no exams. Big final essay. Random attendance quizzes. Assignment guidelines are unclear at times. AI usage allowed for everything (literally), say "how" for essays. TAs are very disorganized; they copy-paste entire (yes, entire) student submissions into random online "AI detectors."
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: No exams—just a couple Canvas quizzes each week and one paper. Lectures were engaging, and while grading criteria could be a bit vague at times, the course was straightforward. AI use is allowed (just cite it in the paper). Random attendance quizzes, plus lots of extra credit. Highly recommend.

Probably the most fascinating lectures and readings I've seen. He's difficult to keep up with at times, but he's an expert in his field and it shows. He gives you enough extra credit opportunities and easy-A's (open-note quizzes btw) to succeed as long as you put in effort once a week. Only 4-5 attendance quizzes, but you'll want to show up anyway!

echoing reviews below, the class isn't hard but the prof and tas are so disorganized. instructions/grade weighting/assignments are constantly changing, and we never had idea exactly what was needed to get good grades on the paper. terribly coordinated class, and slow answers on ed discussion. random participation quizzes. THEY CHECK FOR AI!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures r boring and repetitive, but easy class. Grading is done by different TAs and they seem to use different criteria. AI allowed for all assignments as long as you cite it and write an appendix on how you used it, even on the term paper, which is very clutch. No tests, just easy open-note take-home quizzes, and the semester-long term paper.

McGreggor is super nice and a great professor, but his class is not organized. Each TA grades a batch of students' work and each of their grading criteria are different. You have to dig through Ed Discussion to find really important stuff about assignments. They push notetaking for credit, but the slides go fast and are mostly pictures. Mid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: overall this class is not bad, but i really hated the professor and TAs. it's fairly easy to get a good grade, but assignment instructions are vague and TAs give conflicting information. they would take off points for things that weren't specified in assignment instructions and give horrible feedback. this class was just not well run or coordinated

Easily my favorite lecturer at Georgia tech. Class is super engaging and makes me want to participate. Be aware for A LOT of quizzes and reading, but he assigns a 20 page literature review which if done correctly is fascinating and I think a great application of what we learn in class

The best lectures I've experienced at GT. Lectures have interesting material and discussion, and he presents them in a way that makes me look forward to attending class. My only gripe is that the term paper had somewhat vague and conflicting instructions, and questions about them were never clearly nor timely answered. However, grading is lenient.

Professor McGreggor's lectures are very interesting so it feels natural to participate in the discussion. The final is the 12 page paper but the writing is spread out over the course of the semester and he's lenient with late work. He also doesn't mind the use of AI as long as its cited properly which is a life saver for the papers.

The class relies on participation points (attendance and online discussion) and the research paper. The feedback on assignments is very slim and they give a lot of low-As so whether you get an A or B really comes down to whether you got participation points. If you come to lecture 5 times and post online once a week you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: weekly quizzes and participation matters, 12 page paper in the end. take if you like psych but if you do its a guaranteed A
Probably the easiest cs class here

He's a wonderful and caring professor and a great lecturer who's very passionate about the subject. There's a research paper and weekly open note quizzes over the content. Participation and attendance are required with random participation checks. It's a very easy and fun class that has fascinating content. I highly recommend taking it from him.

3790 is a great class. It's not super relevant to CS (most of the CS concepts are taught in other classes), but it's a very interesting psych class. The assignments are all easy, and the papers leave lots of room for creativity and are graded fairly. Take this class if you can, it's not super hard and it's fun.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Textbook/lecture-based class. No exams, just biweekly open-note (yours and others' uploaded) quizzes and a final paper. Mandatory attendance, but only through a word-of-the-day you can get from a friend. My only critique is that the quizzes were pretty unclearly worded so that you would only recognize it straight out of lecture. Easiest class.

Hated lecture because he would talk nonstop about what seemed like nonsense. He made attendance required but he only checked attendance by having you submit a word of the day to canvas, so if you have a friend who goes to lecture and can send you the word you never actually have to go. Quizzes were open-note but still difficult.
Goes a bit fast in lecture, but teaches the content well. Provides the class with research opportunities and an assignment, and is fun and organized. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Clear and fair. Grading criteria sticks to what's in the syllabus.

Lectures and office hours were the key for this class. She was awesome in office hours and broke concepts & practice questions down very well. The tests were kinda difficult, so redo the problem sets while changing information given. Group project was really interesting as well! Dr. McNamara is easily one of the best professors I've had at Tech!

Dr. McNamara is an amazing lecturerer. She comes to class prepared and really knows the content. Her problem sets can be difficult. Use the TA for help with them. Her exams are also a little tough sometimes but she curved them to be a B average minimum.
Took her for a minimester. Easy class. She explains everything clearly and the quizzes are simple if you pay any sort of attention. No real complaints.

I took her half semester health course and while it was lecture and assignment heavy she is super nice and clarifies exactly what we need to. Assignments are easy and powerpoints are posted online. I think we had two or three quiz including written responses but as long as you study the modules and PP and practice quizzes it's an easy A.

She is so kind and caring, the lectures were really long but she gave us breaks and was really lenient if you emailed her about having to miss class. She makes you do some work outside of class but APPH is so easy content-wise that anything never took more than 10 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She managed to make three hour minimester courses very engaging! Not a lot of people can do that. Super simple class, and there is a ton of extra credit.

Genuinely a great teacher. The class is very easy and I thought it would be silly, but I enjoyed being in class even though it was 3 hours on Friday (definitely take the MINI-MESTER not the full class).

I mean this class just isn't hard, and she knows that. She isn't trying to make your life miserable, and the class is not too much work other than the final project (which requires some activity logging and a bit of reflection, five hours total maybe)
TAKE HER! THE GOAT!

Had more fun in this class than I expected. She kept lectures engaging, and provided more than enough extra credit opportunities so there is no reason to not get an A. Just complete the assignments/hw on time and put a decent amount of effort into the final project and you will be fine. Mostly did other work during class.

Just show up to class and do other work. As long as you set aside 1.5 hours for each homework assignment, 3 hours for project, and do decent on the take-home quizzes, your grade in this class should be a fairly easy A. My friends who took online lecture said their class was easier, still an easy A either way, however.

Although lectures were mandatory, we all just did work for other classes/ played Clash etc. She knows we all don't take this class extremely seriously, so she makes her lectures very fun and social. I made some new friends. Extremely chill professor who truly cares about her students, she even goes as far as trying to get to know all of us!
Great teacher and easy class overall. Just a few online quizzes, assignments, and projects but overall, a light class. Attendance is mandatory though, only downfall. Very kind teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is an obstacle to one's education. Not because the class is in any way difficult, but because that is all the class serves as. She could very well cut the filler and give students lectures and quizzes every so often, instead she decides to be a nuisance and treat her students like a kindergarten class.

Super easy. You have weeks to do short assignments, the only quiz wasn't even honorlocked, etc. She offers EC but you won't need it. The lectures are a little tedious, but it's a great time to do homework for another class. Plus, she's really nice and clearly cares about her students. Easy A.
Assignments were not difficult, and the course was heavily focused on the final wellness project. Lectures were lengthy and involved small activities, but helped student socialize with one another.

She was super passionate, I took it over the summer so it was super chill and we had like 5 assignments. The lectures were really long since it's condensed, but it was easy and she gave us a 15 minute break and small little discussion breakouts every so often.
Very chill professor, made getting an A as easy and stress-free as it should be in a 2 credit class like APPH 1050

Queen. Lectures are long but it's not like she's holding you accountable to complete every single activity so you can still meet and talk with friends but really it's a chill class that answers a lot of your first questions when you arrive at Tech :)
She's so sweet, her lectures were extremely long and felt like a waste of time, but she cares for her students and is passionate about what she does highly recommend.

She's a really nice lady, but the amount of assignments and the content in them are just unnecessary. You don't have to pay attention much, though, so I guess it's a nice GPA booster. That being said, she was really easy to contact and was helpful with clearing up any questions.

Takes a 2 credit hour health class way too seriously. Plus the assignments are so unhelpful and simplified. Getting treated like a toddler for 50 minutes twice a week for a class where your attendance is graded is actually horrendous. You'll probably get an A though, I guess.

Only two/three easy quizzes and two big projects that SEEM daunting but are really not if you just follow the instructions. Come to every class to get your participation. Participation is like 95% of your grade so I would not miss any classes. Many extra credit opportunities provided.
Really easy class, Prof McBurse is sweet and caring, I liked her. Only downside is required attendance.
literally took APPH wayy too seriously. like i could have used my time so much better if i didnt have to be treated like a kindergardener for 50 minutes twice a week
Very simple class, attendance is mandatory, but not much work. She's pretty lenient with grading and offers a lot of extra credit.
