It's APPH so not much to expect. Based on what I heard from the other teacher, McBurse did generally seem better. She was nice and deadlines were very chill. It is pretty easy to get an A in this class as long as you put in the minimum amount of work needed. Lectures could be a little boring at times but again, it's APPH
Grade is heavily determined by participation. easy A as long as you attend class, and the assignments are easy. little class material that is very easy to remember, and only two quizzes

very kind prof and she cares for students. attendance was mandatory but it wasn't that bad. assignments make up the bulk of the grade but as long as you follow the rubric, its very easy to get an A. chances for extra credit as well and very accessible outside class. take her for apph!

Sasha actively embodied everything she taught us. She made sure everyone in the room felt comfortable. Super easy class, but make sure to go to lectures to get the participation point at the end. If I had to give one piece of advice though, you really don't need to read the assigned book. There were maybe three test questions on it all semester.

Great professor. Assignments are very easy. Cared a lot for the students. Attendance is mandatory because of the participation grade. A lot of extra credit options. Easy grader. No tests and only 2 quizzes. Don't need more than 30 mins a week. Give more than enough time to complete assignments.
There's no reason to not take her it's an easy A. There's busy work but it's so easy, and most of it can be done during lecture. Also you don't really need to buy or read the books she gives

Excellent professor, clear cut class, and quality information. This class is one of those mandatory things that you have to take, but she made it very enjoyable and worth investing into. It's a pretty easy A, but there is dozens of points for extra credit and many ways to get back participation. She teaches for you learn, not to strictly grade.

Professor McBurse is so caring and passionate about her lectures. She is a great lecturer; particular about assignments but if you just follow her very specific instructions it is an easy A. I probably attended about 85% of lectures and completed all hw on time and got an A without any extra credit. She cares about you and the material. Great!

Very easy class as long as you do your work/attend most of the classes. There are no tests, just 2 big quizzes, so you do not have to pay that much attention to her during lectures. She is very nice and obviously likes what she does. There is also 1 big group project during the 2nd half of the semester that counts for a good chunk of your grade.

I LOVED HER CLASS!! Honestly, everyone else saying it's busy work is right but it's not her fault; APPH is required for ALL GT students so she can't really do anything about that. Her exams were all at home, and open notes, just don't use AI and all the answers are in her lecture slides anyways!! She also don't have a final either!! Super easy A fr
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super caring and nice! Loved her and definitely recommend her!
Easy class with a caring professor.  The class was boring due to content that I'm not very interested in, but that is not really her fault.

super easy class, only thing is that attendance is mandatory which can be annoying but still easy. quizzes were also easy she literally highlights the answers on the ppts so its easy to study for, assignments werent too much each one took less than an hour.

She's a super nice cool lady who really cares and takes the time to get to know students. Lecture can get boring, and the required reading is very annoying (I never read it), but I would recommend her section over others.
Dr. McBurse is very sweet and caring. Her class is quite easy with quizzes being online. Make sure you show up to class as participation is a good chunk of your grade.

Great prof. Only downside is participation is "mandatory" but barely worth anything in your grade. Just go to class and shes great. Work is very easy, you can get an A in the class with little to no effort.

This class has been amazing. Professor McBurse is extremely caring and passionate about her job. She always lets students know she is available if they have any issues outside of class. She is also a great lecturer with very lenient, clear, and fair grading criteria. HW, quizzes, and projects will also not require a significant amount of time.
Mrs. Sasha made me actually want to attend my 9:30AMs. It's refreshing to see someone so passionate about teaching doing what they love

Some of these reviews are harsh. Attendance is required, and the lectures can at times be simple, but this class is an easy A. I didn't find the rubrics too tough to understand or any of the assignments overly difficult. The quizzes are based on the slideshows, so not too hard. And you can tell she cares about the content in each lecture.

For a required health course, it wasn't that bad. Tests were online, and projects were easy. Pretty clear rubrics, but missing points add up fast. Uses a website to check attendance at a random time & does NOT allow people into class late due to this. I would recommend her for this course, just do your work on time and get the attendance points
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory to get check-in points, but good teacher! To the point, seems happy with the job she has, and it was a pretty self-explanatory subject for the most part but I wasn't bored out of my mind. Extra credit opportunities if you miss out on an assignment on accident, my only complaint is that they're REALLY heavy for a few points.

You'll be fine; It's just an annoying class. She says nothing is busy work, but it all is. Content is boring and I didn't learn anything helpful. Grading criteria is unnecessarily strict for random assignments (why does it HAVE to be green?). It's nice that she cares about her job, but it's a gen ed, and GT students are stressed as it is.

Attendance is strictly required. A lot of homework is busywork. Other than habit forming and stress management, her class is so dumbed down it's barely useful in real life. The nutrition, chronic disease, and finance units are comically simplified. You will spend hours listening to these boring lectures and then doing barely related assignments.

If you can avoid taking her class please do lol. Attendance is required-ok, but this course has an unnecessary amount of work. The assignments are pointless, and almost just seem like busy work. She also has these very specific ways just to complete what should be a simple assignment. If you have to take her though, it should be fine, just annoying

I think 14 lectures, attendance is 17% of grade and she checks attendance different every time. She is not clear about how much work it takes to get an A on an assignment, and given examples are inconsistent with her grading. Lectures are lame and her exams include material not covered in class so you have to read textbook (for a 2credit class!).
Attendance was graded even though the lectures were kind of pointless and unnecessary. She also would like yell at people in front of the entire class if they came in late which was kind of extreme.

Professor McBurse is amazing! She really cares about her students and gives lots of extra credit. Her lectures were interesting and I was impressed by how good she was at remembering our names. 1050 has an activity session as well as the lecture but I really enjoyed this part of the class. Very easy class and great professor!

As most are only taking this class because they have to, I appreciate McBurse making it ridiculously easy. There is barely any homework, points are easy to earn, and there's lots of extra credit opportunities. It would take skill to score any lower than an A. Her lectures were almost two hours long and very unengaging. Attendance is mandatory.

Poor lecturer; goes deep on the wrong content and gives actively problematic assignments. Take her class if you're okay with location-verified attendance, taking photos of all your meals, and writing research papers where 16 peer-reviewed journal articles receives half marks on the rubric. TL;DR - You'll get an A, but at what emotional cost?

Mrs. McBurse is a very passionate instructor who cares for her students. If you have problems, you can email her and she'll respond fairly quickly. She gives us plenty of extra credit opportunities so there's no reason to fail. She also has a grace period for late work.

LSS Green Belt: Students should expect inconsistency in grading and feedback. Comments sometimes reference expectations not clearly stated in instructions, making revisions difficult. The level of engagement and feedback can feel uneven across students. Those preferring clear, consistent criteria may find the course frustrating.

Lectures are boring. He gives you blank notes, but hardly covers them in class. He assigns two long HBR cases ranging from 15-30 pages every week and barely covers them yet expects you to nearly memorize the cases. For the test, you are expected to know the notes and HBR cases. Tests are very unfair for how poorly the material is covered in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Myers is hands down the best professor I've had at Tech. I took him for both MGT 4360 and MGT 4803 Process Innovation. He cares. He's super engaging. Attendance and participation is 30% of your final grade in 4360. He brings in several guest speakers that are on topic and interesting. Take this professor! You will enjoy going to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have had him for two classes so far, and he is one of my favorite professors. He is excited about the material and makes sure his students understand everything. This class was completely project and participation based. He frequently lets class out 30-45 minutes early.

He might be a bit boring, but he's very nice and cares a lot for his students. He is willing to answer any questions and lenient with extending deadlines. Online notes are awesome and make it clear what needs to be studied for each exam. Coding hw is in python, but tests are mostly math based and not cumulative. Final is basically a really long hw.
He's a good professor and cares about you learning the content. Posts his notes which are good and mimic content for homework's and exams.

Menon is a great professor. No final exam but rather a project. The project does take a long time to complete though and is extensive. Homework is very long too but makes up the majority of the class grade making exams less stressful despite their difficulty. Menon is always willing to answer questions in depth and even offered EC several times.

Extremely comprehensive lecture notes available after-class that are up-to-date. If you understand what's on these notes, you will get an A. Relatively easy class for core ME curriculum. NOTE: HE TEACHES IT IN PYTHON, which imo was a great move. It's not hard to learn if you know matlab.

Great professor-cares and will help with anything, regardless of how lost or basic your questions are 100/10. Shows a genuine interest in material and makes fun connections between the computing techniques described in class and their use in the real world.

For his first time teaching this course he certainly did a great job. I learned a lot about numerical methods and especially applications for them. He has quite a bit of homework. His tests were a good mix of theory and application, but I heard future sections will not have tests and instead be heavy on projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Python section) Homeworks are tedious, but he gives a clear rubric and start code to help. Really shows that he cares about his students. He posts his lecture notes online and provides a lot of practice problems for tests, which are very helpful. If you take the time to go to class, lock in, and do the homework well, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: good info if ur looking to create a startup. 20% is attendance (do without it), just make sure you go over the lecture material and tests are straightforward. Test have identifiable mcq answers if you just study an okay amount (2 days before exam and I was fine). No presentations, just deliverables. Decent guy. Hybrid class, online on wednesdays.

Lectures are useless but there are in class assignments. Test questions are mostly from self-check quizzes on canvas so they are not bad. Homework is time-consuming and the professor expects you to use A.I. If you do the self check quizzes and go to class you will get a B minimum

Class was very straight-forward. Professor Smith literally sets you up for success and is very passionate about the subject. Loved when he told us about tech news. Homeworks and exams are not difficult at all, all the bad reviews are from people expecting this course to be one where you are able to get an A with no effort. You get what you put in.
Such an underrated professor. Is he an easy class? No. But it is one you can earn an easy A in if you try hard enough

He definitely gets very off topic and you don't learn much from lectures. HW is strenuous but overall easy if you follow instructions and use AI to explain how to do things. Exams aren't too bad though just do the SCQ's and you'll end the class with a minimum B.

This man is insufferable. He rambles on in lectures about stuff that makes no sense. That said, it is not difficult to get an A in the class. He posts practice quizzes for each module, and if you do them over and over, you will get a good grade. Just tune him out in lecture and you will be fine - some people just keep their headphones in.

He acts strict, but his teaching is terrible. Never replies to emails.He is the law. If he makes a mistake, he apologizes, but if you make a mistake, you get a zero. He is the definition of a toxic professor. he is the worst professor in history. Let's hope his parenting style helps his children become the next Einstein. Let's see, maybe he's right
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took MGT 2200 in Summer 2025. Class is tough but doable. There are 5 tests + 5 HWs. HWs take ~3hrs each, tests are ~55 Qs in 75mins, but many repeats from SCQs (do SCQs 10x). Grading: 20% HW, 60% tests, 20% final or test avg. Meets with students if you email him. Not my top choice, but he's fair. Either he's improved or RMP is too harsh.

The worst professor of my entire college experience at Tech. He doesn't care for students nor their circumstances. He does not try to be accessible to students via email despite it being explicitly stated on his syllabus that it is the ONLY way to communicate with him. He is rude, goes out of his way to embarrass students and disparage their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures often go off-topic into unrelated history, and grading is harsh without clear feedback. Difficult to understand expectations or improve performance. Gives 75% for no reason on assignments and lectures on random history channel episodes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I receive a 95 in this course last semester, but was the worst course I took at Georgia Tech. He just rambles about AI and teaches rudimentary ways of how to prompt AI "skillfully" ... If you know how to use ChatGPT well then he will give you an A. Test questions are given beforehand through self check quizzes so 0 effort is needed for the class

Prof smith's classes consists of an occasional piece of information that might be on a test coupled with continuous rambling about random bits of history that have nothing to do with his class. He also random gives everyone in the class a 75 on particular assignments in order to lower his gpa.
This guy just rambles about AI, this class is a complete waste of time. I would not recommend taking this at all, he is very dull and doesn't understand what he is talking about.

Lectures are ok, you learn somewhat from them, but what prepares you best for the tests is going over the slides and especially grinding the self-check quizzes. If you do the self-check quizzes enough times, you'll see quite a few of those questions on the test, but without them you might struggle so they're probably your best friend

Not good at all. You must self-learn all material if you want to understand. Other than that, the class was manageable since all tests were based on SCQ. Tip: Do each SCQ a minimum of 10 times in order to memorize the answers.
dude is terrible. if u need him for 2210, take another professor. he emphasizes getting everything done on time but then takes like 2 years to grade homework.
Can't properly connect or teach his students. Bad grading structure, takes forever to grade homework. Do not take this professor.

Tests are sometimes similar to practice tests, but this man was not kind at all. Never responded to email (intentionally ignored) and took forever to grade homework. Showed little mercy and did not teach at all for lecture. Ranted about random stuff. Homework was so difficult and he gave no context on how to do it. 5 exams and optional final.

It honestly baffles me how these guys are still allowed to teach at Georgia Tech. Not a good professor. Lacks basic communication skills. Lacks basic respect. Lacks the ability to teach or grade assignments on time. Is great at making students stressed and messing up their grade though!

Doesn't teach, you will teach yourself 100%. Tests were okay and based largely on slides % self check questions. Dont expect to learn anything valuable while in class, but you had to come for in class assignments. Tough grader & not a nice guy to want to get to know better. Has a "tough sh*t* attitude. Made me switch out of ITM. Expected to use AI?
Not a good professor. At all.

extremely hard to communicate with. as a professor he has a complete lack of respect for students. takes months to grade homework assignments, which barely cover what we even studied for in class. acts like he supports or works with students when he does the bare minimum as a professor. maybe he needs to go back to school and learn how to teach.

Read off slides and told us to use AI for assignments. Exams were based on practice questions, making them doable. However, homework was very difficult and time-consuming. He didn't teach SQL, Excel, or Python well, and his notes were generic. Homework wasn't graded until the end, which hurt my grade. Honestly not a good teacher.

Never responds to any sort of communication. There is a large difference between following the rules as a professor and just being a downright terrible, unsupportive teacher. This guy is the latter. Homework assignments are nearly impossible to do. Don't know why this guy is still teaching at tech

Very picky on who he likes and dislikes right on the first day, and it doesn't change at all. He doesn't care if you get hurt and can't make it to class. My friend fractured his wrist on the way to class, and he didn't care that he got hurt and still gave him a 0 even when he showed proof and volunteered to do extra work. terrible guy overall.

an unrespectable human being. theres only three homework assignments, but they each take you an insane number of hours, and when he finally gets to grading them at the very, very end of the semester, he grades it so unbelievably harsh and critiques every minute detail. this guy has no right to be a professor at georgia tech.

Both the homework and in-class assignments were busy work and did not teach us anything at all as we were told to use AI models to help us with coding language problems. All the tests had the same format and were easy to prepare for, until they weren't but then we would get tested on entirely different material than what we were told to prepare.

test questions all come from the practice quizzes, so do each practice quiz at least 5 times and youll do fine on the tests and get at least an 85. homework hardest part of this class. only had 3 homework assignments, but each one is very long and complicated. he assumes ur gonna use chatgpt (which you will cuz theyre so damn hard) for the hw
yeah so just never expect an email answer to anything even if you follow up 5x
Doesn't respect his students, doesn't actually teach. Just yaps then gives you HW he hasn't taught.

overall not as bad as ive heard. he's pretty inaccessible outside of class (doesnt rly respond to emails) but the class material itself really isnt terrible. you just need to be proactive with keeping up with it. hw only weighted 10%, tests 30% but they're basically 85% the exact same as practice questions on canvas. overall pretty handsoff
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For Project Management, Smith was a pretty good teacher, although only read off the slides every class. Because of this, his teaching style was pretty impersonal. There are 3 tests, one is optional. There is a large group project that lasts all semester. There are about 2 easy homework/readings per week.

Michael Smith really teaches a really engaging class about intro to ITM - he made me really interested in the content and you can tell he really cares about it and wants his students to understand how valuable it is. I still view his class as one of the most valuable at Scheller to this day, even though he ignores his emails lol

Parts of MGT 2210 are pretty dumb but Prof. Smith does as much as he can to make it interesting and useful.  Be prepared to do some work outside of class and memorize some vocab words (from the textbook, not just his lectures) and you'll get an easy A. Don't be surprised when you put no effort into the class and come back with a low grade.

One of the best choices for a GT2000 Professor. His class were better than other sections due to the various tours of different parts of campus and his in-depth knowledge of Georgia Tech. He can be inflexible, and the class is maybe 10-20% harder than other sections (still an easy A), but you learn more and do more in return.

he had informative lecture videos and provided us with helpful self-check quizzes but was a terrible professor to take as he did not upload the material for the class in a timely manner - he often would upload the entire unit the week before the exam and also uploaded the homework less than a week before it was due nearly every time

Mr. Smith is highly motivated about teaching his course and also mentions many interesting insights he knows and shares his own prior experiences from prior jobs. The knowledge is really important if you consider to work in any IS area after. 

However, grading is hard and additional work is required to learn knowledge tested not done in class.

This course was extremely challenging, and the workload was heavy. The professor did not provide much guidance in class, and it constantly felt like we were teaching ourselves. He was unresponsive to emails and seemed disinterested in helping students. While the professor was knowledgeable about the subject, they did not communicate it effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Passionate about the course material and shares many real-world examples. His spontaneity can cause confusion. He's receptive to feedback, comes to class with a positive attitude. Exams are challenging, and the language used can be difficult to understand. Sometimes the exams don't always relate to the lectures

I mainly relied on the textbook. His lectures do show up slightly on exams, but he tends to go on many tangents about his life. Just be prepared to self-learn. There is not much homework, but each homework is quite lengthy and can be challenging, as you might have to search things up and learn it by yourself.
Definitely one of the harder professors in this subject. You have to teach everything yourself, and he genuinely doesn't seem to care for his students. Do not recommend whatsoever!
Tough class with lots of content that you'll have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were okay. A lot of useful and relevant info, but a bit boring. Super clear grading criteria and, if you put in the work, not too hard to get an A on all of the HW/projects. The tests are based on his lectures (so go to class) and textbook notes. Not a lot of everyday HW, though. Overall, you have to try to get an A, but not bad.

For starters, he does not respond to emails. The majority of this course is self-taught and his responses in discussion boards are rude and not helpful. He expects a lot out of his students and teaches valuable skills, but spends lecture time reminiscing about his time in a fraternity at Tech.

You teach yourself everything. DO NOT TAKE AS A FIRST YEAR. Smith is a great guy and seems like he really loves what he does and cares for students, but he is tough and you WILL struggle as a first year.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class to build resume-worthy skills!!! Professor Smith is challenging, but motivating, and makes you actually want to deeply understand the material to be able to succeed. It does require some learning on your own outside of class but that is expected of many harder classes at Tech. This has been the most rewarding class I have taken so far.

Half of the class is on learning information systems (Excel, SQL, R, Tableau), and you have to do it all by yourself. He throws hours of pre-recorded videos on you and says have fun while teaching none of it in class. What he does teach in class is useless. The test is 10% what he teaches in class, 40% textbook, and 50% self-taught info systems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All the software platforms we had to learn, we had to completely teach ourselves. He also does not respond to emails and took days to reply to my comments in canvas. I participated in class often, did all the work and readings, and still struggled. Also everything was graded for accuracy even if hadn't learned it yet

One of the hardest classes I took online + the hardest business class I've ever taken. This really should be a 4000 level class considering the workload and course material. He refused to give me an extension when I had covid and was rude and not accommodating and his test questions were extremely hard, even reading the entire textbook was no

He's very passionate about his class, but the structure is strange. All the tests are based off of the textbook reading and stuff that isn't taught AT ALL in class. Lectures are completely disconnected to the homework and tests so you basically self study 100%. However, he is very helpful in his office hours and cares about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy but a TERRIBLE professor. He doesn't teach you anything all semester and instead expects you to learn everything through boring online videos made by someone else. When the time comes for exams, you have almost no idea what to study/expect for the exam. There is also a semester-long group project that he grades extremely tough. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am taking his class during the pandemic and he seems not care about the amount of work that he is giving his students. Tons of reading and lectures to watch, and on top of that he gives other large homework assignments that take up a lot of time. He definitely cares about the topic he teaches, but unfortunately makes it very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took his class during the pandemic, and let me just say it has been the worst experience I've had at this school. His assigned projects take hours of pre-learning before you can even start, and there is absolutely no fun in anything. Would 100% avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you like homework then this is the class for you. If you don't like homework then don't take this class unless you have to. So, to sum up, don't take his class

I absolutely loved this class. You learn so much from lectures, homeworks, and quizzes. As long as you do your reading, take the quizzes, go to lecture, and start early on the homework, there is no reason you can't make a high grade (just work on your time management). It's hard work and he doesn't babysit you through anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: do NOT take Mike Smith under ANY circumstances. unless you are available outside of class to go to his office hours at LEAST 2 days a week, you will not succeed in his class. this is because he does not teach about half of the content, and he expects you to learn hard programming platforms like "R", SQL, and Gephi COMPLETELY on your own.

absolute WORST professor i've taken in college. avoid him like the plague. he only teaches about half of the material and expects you to learn the other half on your own--material not covered in the textbook either. had to get a tutor, so much wasted time and money. never felt more disrespected in my life.

Guy knows what he's talking about but does go off on unnecessary tangents; tests are hard and designed to confuse you (especially with the wording) so be prepared to study long hours to grasp the concepts and potentially under-perform on the exams because of how trippy the questions can be
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is unnecessarily difficult. Lots of reading quizzes and homework which take so much time since he does not teach the concepts. Test are super hard. Try to get another prof for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Way too hard for an intro undergrad class. He should be teaching strategy, not IT, because he doesn't teach the topics covered in the homework and expects you to learn it on your own. Very difficult. Only take him if you have no other choice.

Professor Michael Smith really cares about his students and is very engaging in his lectures. If you are taking Smith be prepared to work hard and many hours on homework, take weekly online quizzes that are timed and are based on the reading (2-3 minutes to answer 6 Q's). Tests are very hard, but he is available outside for help.

I learned a lot from this class. Great professor. Definitely knowing what he is talking about. The class has lots of homework (Excel, R, SQL, Gephi) which definitely expands my skill sets but they are tough. Also attendance is important because there are clicker questions and it's 10% of the grade. Tests are fine (I averaged a B+) if you study.

Dr. Smith's class is very difficult. While he an amazing lecturer, he assigns a lot of homework. There are weekly readings (with short online quizzes) and labs/homework (Excel, R, SQL...). Tests are also really hard. Attendance is required, and he does clicker questions based on lecture that count for your grade. Definitely tough to make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Had him for emerging tech and always looked forward to his class. His test are only 25 questions though and designed to trick you so study up.

Goes on unnecessary tangents during class. Quizzes, tests and homework were hard. When contacted for help, he does not respond. If you go in for office hours, he will say he cannot help, and that it is your problem to figure it out. Overall not a good teacher. Avoid him as a professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a charismatic man, but you probably still won't focus in lecture, mainly because it's not needed to do well in the class. I like that he updated his schedule to give a lecture on blockchain, as that shows that he wants his students to learn the newest technological advancements. Only downside is that some test questions are quite misleading.
Disorganized teacher. Class and tests were unnecessarily hard. Harsh and subjective grader. Would not recommend taking him for any course.
lol what is this guy overcompensating for
Great prof, very interesting lecturer. This semester he taught a "preparing for consulting" section. I would fully recommend this class to anyone interested in this career path!

Attendance/participation is 40% of your grade. Other than that, he's a strong professor. Jokes just the right amount and is very understanding (provided there is documentation of illness). Very considerate professor and teaches well. Clear choice.
great professor and very reasonable. interesting class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great guy and a very interesting class.
So amazing . Great grading scale . I barley went to lecture . Take this dude
Hands down best discreet math prof. Truly, seem like he care. Pay attention in class. It might be seem boring but it worth it

I love this man, absolute GOAT. Made Discrete Math easy and accessible. Has 3 grading scales that you get to choose so you get the highest grade possible. Either the 3 midterms or the homeworks can be worth up to 55%. No final. Lectures were kind of boring but there are random pop quizzes (infinite tries on canvas) for attendance. Highly recommend.

Discrete math with Professor Tao was the easiest class that I have taken at Georgia tech. His grading allows you to make 30 minute weekly homework assignments up to 55% of your grade. Boring lecturer, but tests were very easy. I didn't walk a way feeling like I had a very solid knowledge of discrete however.

Professor Molei Tao was amazing!!! His math class was my fav class this semester and math is not usually my fav class. He made math 2603 very understandable and less scary. His lectures were very good and informative and pretty enjoyable as well. The exams are exactly like what we learned in class. I would 100% recommend taking him for math 2603.

AMAZING professor! He made discrete so simple to understand and his lectures were always amazing (and were also exactly what the exams covered). He was a very kind and understanding professor as well. I normally don't post reviews on Rate My Professor but made sure to write this for him because he is one of the best professors I've had at Tech!

Professor Tao is the best ever! His class was the easiest class I've ever taken at Tech and I learned so much during lecture and studio. Please take him! He genuinely cares so much for his students and he crakes a few jokes during lecture too. I would 100000% take him again!

Tao is a great professor! I would def recommend taking 2603 with him if possible. The class was designed for students to get an A. Exams are straightforward, just make sure to pay attention in class and review the textbook because a lot of the questions come from lecture or the textbook.

He has the sweetest soul ever. It's clear he really wants his students to succeed. His lectures/notes aren't posted anywhere. He doesn't provide practice tests but they don't include any curveballs and are most of the times examples from class. He always welcomes feedback and works with the students to make the class better. He's amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: amazing professor. his lectures were perfect, there are 3 possible distributions for your grade, and they use the highest distribution. hes very open to feedback and actually uses it. hes super thorough and everything he teaches has a purpose. exams were reasonable and you are allowed a page (front and back) crib sheet perfect prof i love molei tao

Great teacher, really cares about his students. Lecture can be confusing at times as he tends to do practice problems with concepts before formally introducing those concepts; however the tests are pretty easy and homework is light as well. Would recommend.

Professor Tao was by far the best instructor I've had at Tech. You have to attend lectures to get the notes as he doesn't post them on canvas, but I enjoyed his class a great deal. Exams were easier than most homework questions, and his grading modes made getting an A very possible. 
Amazingly dry sense of humor.

Lectures ineffective, but a very well designed course, with interesting material, homework, and exams. Accessible outside of class, and a genuinely nice and understanding guy. Homework is 60% of the grade, and the difficulty was high but manageable, as there was plenty of time between due dates with multiple office hours sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy A. Class in general is very easy/reasonable. Two midterms of four questions each. Allowed one crib sheet front and back. Does not throw any curve balls. Definitely one of the easiest professors at the school. Would definitely recommend.

Molei Tao is by far one of my favorite professors thus far at Tech. He gives you so many options to succeed and cares about his students and learning a lot. His lectures are informative, and the tests were very simple. Overall, a great guy, and I highly recommend.

This class has the most forgiving grading criteria and easiest tests I've had at tech. You get a full page for a crib sheet and the tests are right from the HW, which is 55% of your grade. Lectures are fairly boring and right out of the book, but not attending can mean you miss some important stuff.

The class is easy as long as you don't expect to show up and pass. The exams and quizzes are fair, straightforward and even easy if you do your work. He explains the concepts well and is very respectful towards students.

This is a great prof, He cares about the students a lot. Even though his cutoff point for A is 93, but the test and quizes are not hard at all and the class average is around 90. Definitely recommend this prof, choose him if you can.

Professor Tao is a blessing.  He cares about his students and their learning so much that he will often over explain things to make sure you get it. Class consists of  4 quizes and 3 tests,  the syllabus says you need a 93 for an A, but the average for everything is around a 90 and you also get a cheat sheet for everything. He is Awesome. Take him

Very nice and respectful to students, cares about his teaching.  Class consisted of 6 HW's and a final, none of which were too difficult.  Test and HW's were representative of what we learned in class.   Would definitely recommend.

Class is split up into 2 lectures and 2 labs every week, with lab attendance being mandatory. I personally enjoyed Moss's lectures, although he could definitely take a while to get tot he point. Would say where Moss is really helpful is during office hours, which he's easily accessible for. But since lab does get ahead of lecture, TA's matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You learn most of the content in your lab so hope you have good TAs. Moss was very engaging in the lectures but could sometimes make the most random analogies when teaching content. Lots of projects, exams were a bit rough near the end as we had 2 exams, 2 quizzes, homework and a project due in the span of 2 weeks. Interesting course tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: class is entirely dependent on ur TAs and its pretty hit or miss. i recommend scoping out ur TAs first week and then switching sections if needed. moss lowk isn't great at lecturing since he takes a long time to get to a point and makes confusing connections. i stopped going and just read the textbook. relatively low difficulty till assembly unit.

class is heavily dependent on how good ur TAs are and thats completely hit or miss. i recommend scoping out ur TA in the first week then switching sections if needed. mark is lowk not a good lecturer since he takes a long time to get to his point and sometimes makes confusing connections. i just started reading the textbook and skipped lectures

Moss is a very good lecturer, it does take him a bit to get to the point sometimes but he's very enthusiastic and engaging with what he teaches. He also posts all his lectures to Canvas. Labs were essentially just mandatory recitations were never on-pace with the course (as in they were almost always ahead), making them a drag to go to biweekly.

overall he's a kind and chill teacher. he does have a hard time getting to the point in his lectures but other than that he's a great prof. unfortunately, i got the worst TAs possible which makes the class more challenging than it was supposed to be. they're incredibly unhelpful, rude, and straight up ruins the class. other than that good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CS2110 has been my favorite class I've taken at tech so far. I think the course is designed very well and you have a lot of resources to get help. Moss himself is really nice, but his lectures are a bit long winded and he does tend to go on rants sometimes about only adjacently related topics.

Great lecturer, answers questions, and generally just knows what he's talking about. Uses Microsoft Whiteboard, which I prefer over PPT. 

In fall 2025, the class was project-heavy (45% of grade), but you're guaranteed 100% on projects if you keep up with the content and work hard.

He's a great lecturer, breaking things down simply and traces through examples. The hardest part is unfamiliar content, but review and find a TA during OHs for project help early and you'll be set. I'm taking him in the fall with projects weighing ~60% of your total grade, so you can afford to struggle with the quizzes like I did.

Such a great lecturer; really cares about his students. Lecture is important but lab is even more important, so keep going to lab if you want to do well on your projects in this class. For preparing for quizzes, you're better off reviewing project work and homework.

Moss lowkey does too much in his lectures but clearly cares for students/the subject. TA labs are very helpful and most people would just go to those if attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures. Projects are light and quizzes can be slightly difficult but honestly are not that bad.

Honestly, I am just dropping a rating here for the TAs. Moss is such a boring lecturer in my opinion (have zoned out in basically EVERY lecture), but the TAs make it all worth it. I would genuinely describe office hours as a religious experience. I have learned weeks of content within just a few hours!!
Easily the worst OMSCS professor I've had the displeasure of working with. Not accommodating, very unreasonable, would not recommend taking a course under his instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Class was not easy, but it was project-based for fall 2024 session. Lots of projects, had a final as well. Just go to lectures and focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Moss was a good lecturer for what can easily be a very boring and difficult subject. Homework can sometimes take a long time, so start early, but he did his best to keep our class engaged in his lectures.

Moss is a good lecturer that understands and cares about the material, but I found that he wasn't the most engaging; the last half of the semester I just watched Forsyth's recorded lectures instead. Moss was always very available and adept when I asked him followup Qs after class. I like the 2110 Quiz/TL format better than a couple midterms.
Very caring and respectable professor - downside was that lectures weren't that engaging.

Don't get me wrong you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, but I found his lectures to be incredibly boring. It lacks a lot of depth and he often goes over things not ever covered in the quizzes. I stopped going to lecture and solely learned everything from lab/textbook. As long as you do those two things, you should get at least a B

I;m an ME major minoring in CS. This is a hard class, but Moss does an excellent job teaching it. This is my favorite class I've taken so far. You cover so much content, but his lectures make it very digestable, and they are very relevant to the exams and homework.Would reccomend to everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were alright. It doesn't go as much in depth, but it's still pretty important to go as sort of a direction. Labs are where it's mostly at. Do NOT fall behind, as they cover a lot of material. I was behind 1 lecture and it took me almost a week to get back up to speed. Homeworks were really interesting and online lectures vids HELP A TON!

Professor Moss is a decent engaging professor, but he makes really simple concepts seem confusing and difficult with how he explains them. His notes system is atrocious and makes learning more difficult as he spreads his notes throughout Canvas modules instead of just using files. It's hard to retain the things you learn in this class.
Good lectures, very well structured course overall, gives good career advice

Moss is a good prof that knows what he's talking about and knows how to teach it. Class this semester was graded on 5 projects, 8 homework, 4 quizzes and a final. The content is pretty easy to figure out if you look on YouTube or read the textbook, so lectures aren't really needed. It's still helpful to attend or go to recitation if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good professor regarding notes and introducing the Topics. Lab sections were actually very good to help you on projects. Projects had an autograder that didn't have any hidden cases. Quizzes were fair as well. All your turned-in work...should be your work... as circuit sim used for project 1 & 2 has really good cheat detection.

Class is pretty easy, lectures are just him reading out of the textbook and elaborating. Projects don't take more than an hour or two each, quizzes are easy as long as you did the project. Very passionate and will answer any questions you have, but this class is standardized so it doesn't matter who you take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CS2110 in general is a well set-up class. Projects (take-home homework) accounts for 50% of the grade, and it uses autograders, so it's basically free 100s.  Moss is a good lecturer overall, but goes on tangents sometimes and has the occasional tendency to overexplain ("do you guys know what linked lists are?")

I took this course in Fall 2023. Moss was a great professor who broke down database topics very well for those new to the subject matter. There was a semester-long group project, so make sure you get a good group and don't get randomly assigned. Tests were difficult if you aren't great at SQL, but they were fair. Worst test grade was dropped.

2110 was a great class. There were 4 small quizzes instead of any exams, which were fair and closely matched content covered in class. The projects are simple, but one of them requires you to meet with a TA for a "demo".

Moss is a thoughtful and enthusiastic prof but, you learn the most stuff in lab, projects, and hw. Projects are autograded and 50% of grade -sweet. hw 20% and not bad. Ask questions and pay attention in lab, study the practice quizzes they provide, and start projects early and you won't stress. Very interesting and important class, learned a lot.

Honestly, I don't think it matters what professor you get for this course. Mark Moss was fine but don't know many people that went to his lectures. The labs and office hours will teach you everything you need to know. I would highly choosing a lab that you can consistently go to.

Kind of terrible at teaching. Maybe 5% of whatever he yaps about in lecture is actually useful for homeworks/projects/exams. Basically self-taught myself the entire course from the textbook which was effective but required me to invest so much extra time.

Not bad, but certainly not good. Lectures are dull and very surface level. Doesn't cover the material that will be on the exam or hws at all. Enthusiastic about the subject but can't really teach it, thus no one shows up to lecture. Lab and OH is where you will actually learn the material, so the professor doesn't really do anything at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's one of the best, most detail oriented professors I've had. He explained SQL so patiently and thoroughly when I was struggling with the content that by the end I felt very comfortable with the language even though I had 0 experience with it in the beginning. 10/10 recommend his class

I literally never leave comments on rmp but Dr. Moss is one of my favorite professors!! I will say that a lot of his lecture content doesn't have much to do with the exams, but if you look at HB's videos they help a lot with that. His lectures focus more on real world connections which is helpful for internships

I see why they call the course "SAD" now. This class isn't that hard once you learn to just wait for other students to slowly decipher his arcane instructions on this discussion board. I think the Zodiac Killer gave more clear instructions than this guy.

Very dry lecturer that had way too much fluff. Quizzes were easy but easy to mess up if you got a few wrong. Project phases are easy if you have a good group but otherwise are an absolute nightmare. Felt like I learned more from the project than actual class.

Moss is a great lecturer and keeps you interested in whatever topic is being lecturer about. The class setup feels fair as a student, and gives a lot of leniency by allowing half of the mini-exams to be replaced by the final.

Just an all around good guy.  Very caring and accessible to students.  Intuitive material coupled with understanding instructors (3 of 6 mini-exams can be replaced by an optional final) helps significantly for doing well in this course.  If you don't do well in CS4400 with Dr. Moss, it's most definitely your own fault.

I really liked the lecture style given by Professor Moss where he is able to teach materials by either having us follow along or presenting examples without merely reading off the slides. The course is graded by 6 mini exams and 3 project phases but he does provide a lot of resources for you to study. Overall, a very chill and respected professor.

Moss gives you an absurdly large amount of resources to learn and prep from + his lectures are very effective. The only way you fail this course is if you don't use one of the countless practice exams/problems he gives out before every exam. Group project is good chunk of grade so be warned

amazing professor, either do final project or final exam will replace your lowest assignment score. Although sometimes he's not in his office hours, he's pretty easy going and can explain things pretty well

Moss is a great lecturer and makes all course content very understandable by walking you through all of the concepts. 90% of the grade is based on 6 mini-exams and 3 projects, the lowest of those can be replaced by taking the final or doing the 4th project. For the mini-exams, the corresponding practice exam is exactly like the mini-exam.

Moss is a decent professor that makes his class interesting. Unfortunately, the class is not a very well-structured course. It spends too much time teaching SQL and not enough time teaching actual theory for databases. I still have many questions about databases after taking this course and I wish I would have had them answered.

I was really looking forward to this class, but unfortunately the structure made it quite annoying. The group project was where I learned everything. Thankfully I had some SQL experience, so it wasn't too hard. The TAs were really hit or miss. Communication was poor, and a deadline for one of the project phases was changed the day before it was due

Organisation lacking at start, but overall structure was clear. Go to class, figure out what is graded and HOW, and it's pretty manageable to get an A. If you start the project phases on time, you're solid. TAs are helpful. Make yourself accountable and it's doable to get an "A". Tests are EXACTLY like practice sessions. I slacked off and got a B.

I had Moss for 4400 and I thought he was good, so I chose him over Forsyth. This was a mistake. I have no disdain for Moss, but the course is organized extremely poorly. Assignments were released late, tests and projects took months to be graded, and the "living" schedule we were given never aligned with what we were doing. It's just not run well.

He's a nice guy but this class is designed poorly. My main problem is that he leaves a lot of the Piazza, OH, Project related things up to the TAs and they're horrible. I mean these TAs don't show up for Office Hours half the time and when they do it's useless. Dr. Moss usually steers important questions to the TAs amplifying their ineptitude.

Very poorly organized class. Project requirements change on due dates. TAs rarely show up to office hours and when they do don't know what they are talking about. Quizzes take the average of 7 attempts which prevents students from practicing. Unanswered Piazza posts. All in all one of the worst classes I've taken at Tech

Doesn't respect students. Very unclear grading policy. The project is designed with tons of mistakes and wrong data.
Update project right before due day and give no extension
He's amazing, but you knew this already.

Mark Moss is a great professor. He provides ungraded practice material for all the concepts covered in class so you can adjust the amount of time you put in based on how much practice you need. I was brand new to SQL before taking his CS4400 class and now it is the programming language I use most frequently in my career.
Difficult class but one of the best for probably the most important class as a computer science major.

I felt guilty for missing lectures. His lectures were boring sometimes but most of the time it was interesting and tied in real-world applications and examples. Mini-exams were the first I've ever encountered here at GT and grew to like them. Prof Moss would often end class early. This his last year teaching 1332 he told my spring class personal.

Good professor! He's very organized on Canvas & has lots of helpful resources. Obviously knows his stuff and makes analogies in lecture to help you understand material. Lectures are a bit boring,& grading was slow, so it was hard to know how much effort to put in for studying & on the group project. Take with friends to help with the group project.

Genuinely do not think it's possible to fail this class under Moss. Open note exams (EVEN THE FINAL), 2 weeks for homework, and a dropped HW and exam. Absolutely cracked. Recitation rly helped (I went every week), TAs are awesome. I do wish we had less pseudocode and more forced understanding. His lectures could have also been more straightforward.

The class is laid out poorly. The canvas page is a mess. Your grade is made up of a project, 3 mini-exams, and a final. The project was ok. The 2 mini-exams and final have widespread cheating. The 3rd mini exam is a demo with limited time and confusing directions. If you screw it up, you will not get an A. The TAs were awful, but Mark is nice.

I preferred the recitation slides and lectures a bit more bc they were clearer and more simplified. While moss is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, his lectures can get a bit convoluted and draw away from the main points imo. HW was pretty rough and time-consuming to me but they're lenient with curves. Overall would take 1332 with moss!
Really such a nice guy and a great teacher. I'm probably going to get a B in the class, just because of my own failures, but I would still take him again.

The course itself does not force you to understand the material in any way (major gripe). Homeworks were very uninspired. TA recitations were awesome. Moss himself is a passionate and knowledgable guy. Goes above and beyond in his lectures. Moss does have the potential to be rude at times though.

He did well with a class that has admittedly quite dry content, speaking with energy and clarity, as well as trying to paint a broader picture of why these things were important and some relevant examples of where they might be used, such as in OS and database applications. Homeworks and tests were all very realistic and fair.

Nice professor, explains concepts well, if you already know SQL will be a little boring at times. Tests decently easy and open note. Group project is tough at times if not already pretty good with SQL

I love Mark Moss so much. Hes a really good lecturer and makes hard concepts understandable. The only thing is that he has mini exams every other week and the other weeks where you dont have exams, hw is due. So it is a lot of work but its manageable and really fun. Tests were hard in the beginning but got easier as the semester went on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Moss is such a nice chill guy, and this class was never stressful. The exams were exactly like the practice exams, so if you sufficiently studied practice tests, the actual exams weren't bad. The group project phases were not too difficult but could be time consuming. He has a relaxing nature and really cares about his students! Take him!

Professor Moss is a great choice for this class. His lectures are good but slow; I'd recommend watching their recordings on 2x speed. The quizzes are easy if you use the practice quizzes, but the group project phases should ideally be started as early as possible. Also, the optional final phase is a lot of work but graded liently.

Moss' lectures do not reflect the exams at all, which are much more difficult. Make sure to take the practice quizzes and find a good group because it is impossible to switch. Not as easy as previous semesters, but it is super easy to get a B, so it does not take much to get an A. TAs are so flaky so do not wait last minute on exam/project help.

Good lecturer, although class can sometimes drag because he strives to answer all the student questions (which is a good thing). As long as you watch lectures and start the projects on time, it's impossible to not get an A.

His lectures move very slowly, I could not follow them. However, the homework and lecture slides are enough to learn from. I probably learned more in this class than any other this semester. His tests were not honorlocked. Overall a very manageable and effective course.

Last semester was the darkest period in my life, but I really enjoyed this class and felt that I learned a lot. Moss is a robust lecturer and cares about his students. Lecture prepares you well for the exams. The final group project where you write complex SQL is genuinely tough but you get ample time to do it, and it won't kill your grade.

He is such a solid dude. It's obvious that he cares for his students and knows his stuff. He goes above and beyond to make sure you understand the content. The exams are very similar to practice exams.
The lectures are amazing. Homework is the best resource for you to understand course concepts and do well in exams.

Professor Moss is passionate about the subject, willing to help outside of class, and is a good lecturer. Manages to teach the material in a clear and understanding way. However, do note that he goes quite slow during lectures. There is no mandatory homework, just quizzes, and a group project. Find a good group for the project.

Easy class to get an A in if you show up and pay attention. Mini exams are easy and the lowest one is dropped. They often come from practice exams so you wont be surprised. The group project is manageable as long as you plan and start in time. Overall, very nice class even if lectures can be a bit boring. Moss clearly cares about the subject!

Dr. Moss is the best. Do two things, and you'll do fine in this course: attend and listen to lectures, and DO THE HOMEWORKS. The homeworks are the real key to much of this class, they let you know the data structure in and out.

You have to go to lecture - most practice problems are done in lecture and it's really helpful. He talks pretty slow, so be prepared for that. A great professor though and you can easily get an A if you do the practice quizzes before the tests. Project can be tough at the end of the semester, but the beginning it's easy

Professor Moss is a really great professor! He is really clear during lectures and goes through problems step by step so they are easy to understand. Even with online lectures, he made a clear effort to engage with the students in chat. There is also a ton of practice material and resources for this course so everyone should be able to understand.
CS 4400 is a very difficult class but Professor Moss makes what would be an awful experience considerably more bearable. He is a strong lecturer, and is very passionate about what he teaches.

CS 1332 with Dr. Moss was a great class. My one big problem with Dr. Moss is that he tended to get distracted at times during lectures, but he makes up for it by having very intuitive lectures. He is also very considerate, moving exams based on student circumstances. Homework and exams are the standard affair for an introductory CS class.

Dr. Moss is overall a fantastic lecturer. He gets distracted at times during lectures, but he more than makes up for it by really explaining a large majority of the concepts in 1332 really well, especially for someone who has never encountered this material before. Homework and exams are standard difficulty for an intro CS class.

Professor Moss is super nice and his class taken online is very easy because the tests are open-note. The homework grading is sometimes pedantic but start early and make sure you don't make any easy mistakes and you're good.

Dr. Moss is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. His tests were super reasonable and based off the HW, he'd clearly flag what we should study, and he was very willing to answer any questions students had. He was overall a good lecturer but occasionally bungled an explanation. Lots of projects; read the textbook for help, which is fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: 1332 with Moss is great cause his lectures are much more engaging than Dr. HB's. Other than that the course is functionally the same. HW is time consuming but never overly difficult. Tests can be hard but the 1332 team gives tons of resources to prepare. Moss is a great professor but tbh wasn't too involved with the course besides lectures.

Professor Moss is a great lecturer and explains the concepts well. He is also very upfront with what is tested - in our semester, we had 6 mini-exams and the lowest was dropped, along with the usual group projects. He cares a lot about his students and knows what he's doing.

The tests are very doable if you read the slides. Don't bother with the textbook. The only annoying thing is the project. It's a lot of work. Other than that, not a bad class. Not much work for most weeks, until you get into project crunch-time. I studied for the tests the day before every time, and made an A.

Prof Moss is chill. He is very funny and passionate about lecturing and genuinely cares about his students by giving out extra credit on every test. Just review exactly what he tells you before the test and you will get good grades. Make sure to get into a good group for the project, haha.

Dr. Moss is so kind and easygoing. He gives extra credit on every test so the averages are usually pretty high. If you read over the slides and go to office hours for the group project, you're set up to make an A.

Lectures are extremely slow but he does explain things well, and you can just read the slides and practice exams to study. Exams can be a lil tough but are curved by 13 points so it's not too hard to get an A. The final project was not too difficult if you've done fullstack but just very long, and you may just want to take the final exam instead.

He's a friendly guy that really cares about the well-being of his students. Unfortunately, his teaching style was super disorganized & unhelpful so I mostly skipped class and read the powerpoints on my own time. 3 midterms were hard, easy, and average difficulty respectively. Final project was cool and really reinforced the course content.

He is a really sweet professor and his class isn't bad. The first exam is pretty hard always so don't let that get you down. Definitely would recommend doing Phase 4 instead of the final especially if you have a CS major in your project group so that you have one less final to study for. Overall, just study well for tests and have a good group.

CS 2340 is an absolute joke of a class. It focuses on a big group project that is very easy, and there are 2 mostly MC tests that are almost verbatim from the PowerPoints. Moss is a solid professor, and attendance is absolutely not a prerequisite to do well in this class.

Dr. Moss is a very fair professor. Guidelines to the class were clear, due dates and assignments were always fair, and he is 100% a nice guy. Lectures were also good- He is a funny guy, Georgia Tech just seems to be a tough audience. Textbooks referenced were good and free for Georgia Tech students. Only awful thing was the grade turnaround time.

This class was mostly based around an extended group project, which was challenging but had clear guidelines. Lectures are not really important, but you do have to understand the material from the textbooks to get a good grade on the tests/projects. Dr. Moss is a really sweet guy, too. Easy to get help in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just an overall really good dude. Cares a lot about his students, very easy to approach, not intimidating to ask questions to, he's a baller. He also really knows what he is talking about and can explain it in an easily understood way.

Moss is a great guy. Super nice and funny. I would say that as an IE major myself, this class was pretty easy. Kinda touches on the end of CS2316 stuff. The last project (I did the heavy weight GUI in Python Flask) was challenging, but I had a solid team with half CS and half IE members so we got through it well. Highly recommend Moss!

Excellent lectures, ton of extra points. Quizzes are easy, but the final project implementation was flat out unreasonably hard. Luckily, this implementation was only 5% for lightweight, but it can be very time consuming anyway and TAs themselves didn't know how to do some of it. Easy A but not a pushover class anymore just because of the project.

Professor Moss truly cares that the students learn the material. He is extremely open to questions and spends quality time answering relevant ones in class. He is respectful of his students and his lectures are clear and all information is relevant.
Listens to students concerns and tries to rectify them accordingly. Encourages and gives a lot of tips to students when they are feeling bad about their grades.
Good professor, listens to feedback, really wants students to learn. Makes it tough, but fair (most of the time). Really challenges you.
The best class I took at GT.
holy goat. ts professor is the funniest french guy ever.

He is genuinely invested and enthusiastic for his class (and does funny jokes too), but just not the professor for me. I found his explaining really hard to follow, as he rambled about things that were not covered by the course in many ocassions. I ended up learning most of the content through Alicea's recordings.
Great professor. Lectures are engaging and I felt the content was explained in a clear way. The only class I had this semester where I looked forward to the lectures.

Mourigal cracks jokes and is funny. Lectures: he writes everything down on a whiteboard (no slides), so pay attention to his drawings/key concepts when he writes them. He doesn't cover new material super efficiently during lecture, but the next day, he'll do "review" of the previous lecture, clears up confusion. Expect exams to be pretty difficult.

Physics is a slug at GaTech because they make you do a lot of work and the coordinator makes the tests really hard. Through all this though Martin is a great teacher! Hes funny and engaging, if there is one thing I wish he used slides for notes instead of just using the board as it is hard to follow later. That nitpick though, Martin is the goat.

Mourigal is actually one of the best professors I have had. His lectures make even the most difficult physics concepts really easy to understand. There are also a lot of jokes and asides thrown around which make for a really good time. I felt very prepared for the exams because of his explanations and ways of thinking of certain concepts. TAKE HIM.
He's awesome! Super nice, funny, good lecturer. Really helpful and really enjoy his class. Thanks professor!

Easily the best lecturer I have had in the physics department. Homeworks were challenging, but they were graded on completion and worth 40% of the final grade. The tests were quite hard. Average grades for the 2 midterms was a 70%, similar results for the final. Definately a challenging class, but would take it again with Mourigal in a heartbeat.

Prof. Mourigal is the GOAT. This is the hardest course I have ever taken at Tech, but he makes this course as fun and clear as he can. Exams and homework are difficult, but you can use everything but electronics during exams, and his office hour is very helpful for doing homework and preparing for exams. Just take his course and you won't regret.
Hardest class I've taken, but amazing lectures and character.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Mourigal is an amazing professor and a briliant man. He knows the material and presents it in lecture well with lots of examples. He's got a lot of great jokes that keep the lecture interesting and he legitimately enjoys teaching students. Homework is just like class examples, except much much harder, but he's always avilable to help with it.

Dr. Mourigal is a real gem. He's a fantastic lecturer, very funny and approachable. He was always willing to help in office hours with even dumb-seeming questions. His homeworks are hard, and his tests are harder; he expects a lot out of you but is not unreasonable with his grading. Take him if you can! You won't regret it.

Dr. Mourigal is by far the best professor that I've had at Tech. He clearly cares about his students and the subject that he's teaching. His office hours are incredibly useful, as he works with the group in the interaction zone to show us how to work through the homework problems. Also, his constant jokes make lecture so much more enjoyable.

Professor Mourigal is a great professor and I would definitely take this class with him again. He's got some great french/france related humor and teaches the class in a very fun way. Regardless, This is a HARD class and you will have to work hard and read the book if you hope to do well. This is no fault of his but rather of the material itself.

He's super helpful and approachable. If you show an interest in the subject manner he'll definitely be there to help you out and have a discussion with you. Even if you don't understand what's going on he's willing to give extra help if you seek it.

He is excellent at explaining what is one of the hardest subjects at Tech. Had the best lecture notes I've ever gotten from a teacher and he was pretty good about posting them after each class. Those notes were a life saver during homework and while studying. Keeps class interesting and is pretty funny

Prof. Mourigal is a great lecturer, he clearly is very interested in the subject matter and engages his students. That being said, classical Physics 2 is one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken. Expect to work in this class.

Dr. Mourigal is a great professor, he was excellent at teaching, fun, and he really cares about the success of his students. The difficulty of the class is due to the physics department, not to him personally, and he really tries to help you learn the material. Overall, he's a great professor and my favorite I've had after a year at Tech.

Professor is a nice person and very helpful. However, be prepared for a heavy workload—there are weekly assignments that you cannot skip. Cryptography itself is a very challenging subject, especially if your math/CS foundation isn't the strongest. It's a tough course, but you'll learn a lot if you put in the effort.

Professor Mooney designs challenging courses which will prepare you for the real workforce.
I've taken nearly every hardware security course and computer architecture course via Professor Mooney.
The content is incredibly in-depth and applicable to "real-world" and "life-after-college".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mooney is a great person but lacks in teaching capabilities. The materials are not organized, nor is his teaching style. The slides lack in content, clarity, and so does the verbal lectures. The lectures may be recorded, but they are not very useful. Homework is assigned every week too so be prepared for that.
Pointless, let the students focus on their actual work which they came to this school for.

This class is boring and thats because of the content. My only problem is that the focus of the class is getting a job but she won't give you an excuse for college fairs or interviews. It deducts from the four allowed unexcused absences for the semester. I think thats some bs

Really approachable and caring. Not much to say about the class because it wasn't something I was super interested in coming into it, but I actually enjoyed some of the projects and I think it helped me with my writing.
Clear instructions, caring and funny. themes are decently interesting

Dr. Musick was a great professor who cared about her students. Lectures started with a 10 - 20 minute session of reading off a PowerPoint leading into a reading or analysis of a particular topic for the day. Some sessions felt very long and dragged out. Great professor, I would recommend them to others.
Great professor and great class! She cares about her student's well being and is very relaxed. Best professor for 1101!

Dr. Musick really cares about her students' success. That being said, her class is really easy, but class sessions can be very long and boring. Most of the time, they start off with her reading slides word for word for 20 minutes, and then eventually we look at other assignments.

Focused almost exclusively on AI sector in class discussions/readings submissions did not receive feedback. Little coverage of course concepts in class with tests being incredibly specific to textbook. Test questions confusingly worded and harshly graded. Disorganized assignment of projects, made to do work over fall break. Hard to succeed.

Grades were exam-heavy (28% and 30%) with multiple group projects, yet almost no real teaching. Under 10% of class covered actual material; the rest was pointless case discussions with zero feedback. Massive disconnect between lectures and exams. Would never take again.

Grade was broken down into 2 tests worth 28 & 30%, 3 group projects worth 4% each, a larger group project worth 20%, and participation worth 10%. Tests were out of the book. Fewer than 10% of the lectures were spent on lectures regarding course material. Remaining 90% of lecture time was mostly spent on smaller cases we never received feedback on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Outdated dinosaur.

Extremely Unclear Grading Criteria. 

Does not respond well to criticism, frequently threatens to have students kicked out of the University when he is challenged or provided constructive feedback.
Harsh grader. I didn't enjoy this class much.

This professor is awful! I could not NOT recommend him more! He goes on about rants unrelated to the lecture but expects you to know the material for tests. I had to go to the dean about this class. Take any other professor.

This professor is amazing. He has so much of his content readily available online, and it is very concise and to the point. His lectures are interesting and very informative. I would 100% retake this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Mueller for PUBP 3020. It's not hard to get an A in the class if you attend lectures (not mandatory) and read the textbooks (provided online). He's intimidating at times and sometimes says out of pocket stuff but overall a good lecturer and gives good suggestions and questions.
He was so bad, I wanted to give him a zero. But thats not possible. So, I gave him a 1.
Professor Mueller is very good at facilitating conversation in class. He's a tough grader, though. Make sure to get clarification on assignment requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Classes like his are the reason I took GA Tech's online course curriculum. Homework load was perfect, class content was well tailored, and his lectures are phenomenally concise. I will take this instructor again.

Dr. Murty is an extraordinarily good instructor. His lectures are engaging stories that reaffirm his expertise in the field and his dedication to learning. Transforming difficult material to an attractive medium is difficult, but Dr. Murty does so with ease and full of energy. Attending classes
is a weekly treat. Take courses taught by Dr. Murty!!

Such an amazing and interesting class. Mainly lectures with a semester long group project on a NeuroAI topic. Also includes tutorials on how to build your own AI models which were very intersting. Overall a very cool class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Murty's enthusiasm is truly contagious, making the class an engaging and enjoyable experience. I found myself looking forward to each lecture, eager to see what exciting insights he would share next.
