His passion for teaching, combined with his exceptional skills, has made him one of the best professors I've ever had.

By far one of my favorite professors since coming to Georgia Tech. You can tell he really cares about his students and wants everyone to understand the concepts. He was also fast at responding to emails. He is a great addition to the faculty at Georgia Tech and I cannot wait to see the courses he offers in the future.

Very difficult A due to being very test-heavy (and the content is hard!). However, he is the best lecturer I could ask for, and I felt like he set us up for success. Exam and quiz questions are very similar to his curated lecture notes. The HW wasn't helpful for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really good professor especially for an intro-level class. The content is pretty challenigng but you can tell that he cares about his students enough to make it the most undestandable for them. The class is basically graded on quizzes and tests (and a few easy assignemnts), which makes it kind of hard to get an A, but he's a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I ended up dropping the class because of a major switch. The material for this course is known to be hard. Professor Mukherjee is a great professor though. He is willing to talk with you and explain everything. If you're ISyE or CS, it's a course requirement. There's no 'easy' professor to take, but I highly recommend Prof. Mukherjee.

The best professor I've had at Georgia Tech so far. His lectures are simply amazing! He is very accessible outside of class and very helpful in office hours. The grade is based on 2 midterms, quizzes, hw and a final (35%). But the practice questions he gives and lecture examples prepare you to do very well! Cannot recommend him enough. TAKE HIM!!!!
By far the best 2027 professor.
The best lecturer I've ever had, very well spoken. The class is very test-heavy so definitely use his textbook pdf and DO the practice problems. Would 100% take again
He has an amazing set of lecture notes he created himself that I used the whole semester. The exams are worth a LOT so really use his past exams and practice problem sets to get the most out of them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Really nice and caring. Explains concepts extremely well and from the ground up. Attendance not mandatory but helpful. Class is test heavy (tests/midterms are 55% and final is 35%), but they aren't hard (definitely easier than HWs and they don't try to trick you). Prof also has a fantastic set of lecture notes that he shares.
Dr. Mukherjee is one of the best professors at Georgia Tech. Anyone who says otherwise must not have gone to lecture because he explains everything perfectly.

Dr. Mukherjee is the best. His lectures are amazing, so definitely go to them and the class should be an easy A. Tests are relatively difficult but he prepares you very well. Incredible professor overall.

His lectures are very informative. GO TO CLASS and I swear it will pay off. Focus on the extra practice problems that he gives every week (usually between 5-9 problems) and it will help you to be successful on the tests.
One of the better teachers at GT. Tough and heavy course, but worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests were very very difficult and no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Mukherjee was a very good lecturer and his lecture notes are very high-quality and useful for upper level IE courses. Midterms and Final were worth a large portion of your grade, but homeworks in-class examples do a good job preparing you for them.

Solid choice. Unrelenting to change test timings with different time zones (thanks Covid), but very in-depth, clear, example-filled lectures & fair in his tests. Has plenty of grading criteria & answers questions properly. Had I studied a little bit more, would have made an A. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He explains concepts very clearly in the class and gives useful and interesting examples. There are a lot of tests but they are easy. Homework are difficult but helps learning a lot.

Worst professor I've ever had at Tech. He got feedback that first test was "too easy" so he gave no partial credit for remainder of the semester. The final was worth 40% and had no partial credit either despite being mostly word problems. More students got Ds in my section than Cs. Bad lecturer, hard to understand, would recommend anyone else.

Amazing teacher. Knows the content really well and is very open to explaining concepts again. Highly recommend taking ISYE 2027 with Mukherjee. Class is heavily based on the final (40%), so try to do well on the first two midterms and set yourself up well. An A in the class is very doable if you attend class and do the HW+Practice Problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives really good lectures for those who go to class + puts really good lecture notes on Canvas for those who skip. The first midterm was incredibly easy, but the class gets a lot harder halfway through and a lot of people (and me) failed the second one. He explains concepts really well and the tests were fair as long as you read the lecture notes.

Good teacher, very knowledgeable about the subject and explains it clearly. Course isn't too hard if you've taken AP Stat, and by doing the homework and making sure you know everything in the textbook's "Summary" sections, the tests and quizzes aren't insanely hard. Skip class and you will probably be confused, he explains better than the textbook.

Lectures are centered on weekly readings for which you have to also write reflections. The readings were super interesting, on a variety of topics in sociology, and internet computing. There is a semester long project. There's also 3 assignments, with increasing levels of coding. The prof is very knowledgeable & makes the lectures interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is generally chill and some topics are somewhat interesting. There are a few papers you need to write, however they aren't that much work. Class was "mandatory" depending on your TA

Her lectures make it very easy to understand the class content & prepares you well for recitation. You have reading to complete before coming to class, but you'll be able to understand the lecture content without the readings. 

Attendance for recitations are apart of your grade. This course has a lot of reading, writing, and discussion components.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are super boring, and the lecture slides have barely any content. Some slides are just the name of the topic so even if lecture slides are "posted", you get nothing from it. But lecture content is mostly useless. Show up to mandatory recitation, do the homework assignments/paper, and you're set.

Students can't ask questions on Piazza, and when someone brought it up, the professor was sarcastic and rude about it. She said she couldnt do anything about it and it "hopefully will be fixed soon" by Piazza, which is working fine elsewhere. It's now one month since a student has posted. Lab attendance mandatory. All assignments graded by your TA

Professor de Choudhury was a decent professor. She was a very enthusiastic, but slightly dry lecturer, and the dryness made it a little hard to pay attention in class. There's also a slightly excessive amount of homework, especially near the end of the term. However, the material in the class is interesting. Overall, its an average class.

Three things to know if you want to excel in this course: 1. Reading research papers 2. Technical writing 3. Coding for assignments and group project Since the reading and assignments progressively become more involved, you do get time to adapt and improve (based on the feedback of the prof and the TAs). The lectures are thoroughly enjoyable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring, but attendance wasn't mandator (but there were 5 pop quizzes over the semester, which were difficult). Attendance mandatory during recitation. I did only one of the readings assigned throughout the semester, and otherwise only relied on her slides: I still got an A. The homework and term paper are essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: We read two or three papers before each class, and then discuss them in class. One big group project which wasn't too bad. Very interesting topic, and we debated some of her papers in the class too which was neat. She was good at facilitating discussion and picked interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly a really boring class with poor structure and too many papers. It feels like taking a high school class with mandatory attendance and pop quizzes (she puts them on days she thinks people will skip like before and after spring break). She also loaded the end of the year with assignments, and she released the specs for the assignments late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extremely well organized class, great prof! The class is built like a discussion, do readings and write posts on the readings, then come to class and discuss the topics. Assignments are a little bit of coding, focusing beyond just coding, into deeper social topics and reasoning behind technologies. Absolutely loved this prof and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took this class for a humanities credit; don't take her unless absolutely necessary. She assigns lots of reading and her participation quizzes are very difficult. The grade is NOT worth the effort. She assumes everyone is an architecture major, and that you have preexisting knowledge of architecture. Cannot recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about the course. If you like art history, she's great to listen to. The lectures are pretty straight forward, but she goes at a fast pace. The reading notes are very long but not really "needed," so you can just download the overall chapter reviews if you don't want to write down notes. You'll be good if you stay proactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken. She gives a study sheet which is bone dry in info. Only other resource is textbook, which is just dense jargon most of which is useless info. Take notes in class if you want a good grade (hard to do, slides have no notes only PICTURES). Attendance quizzes are pop quizzes. Semester project is dumb and uselessly complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is abysmal for an introduction course. Her lecture slides only contain pictures, and no notes, so be prepared for that. She gives out attendance quizzes every lecture, which she opens for only 5 minutes at the end of class. Questions are very specific and not possible to find on slides. Would STRONGLY advice any non-arch major to avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are informative, but the delivery is painful and boring. Monotone voice with no engagement. She's very hard to reach outside of the lecture, and it usually takes a week to even get an email response back. 8 AM class. This is a required class for Architecture majors, like me, but if you are just looking for an elective, DO NOT TAKE THIS.

Lectures for this class are terrible. The professor stands there and reads from her slides with no emotion. Slides have no information and are just pictures. Attendance is mandatory with no way of getting around it. Exams are open note but still impossible since the questions are specific. Grading is very inconsistent and projects take forever.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. She has an extremely stoic personality. During class she reads over slides and seems to have very little knowledge about what she is actually talking about. The slides have no information on them (just pictures). Attendance is mandatory. Grading is pretty inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor just lectures the whole entire time. Lecture slides provide no relevant information and only contain pictures. Attendance is mandatory and is truly a waste of time. If you are not an arch major, do not take this class. This is not an easy class and grading is very inconsistent.

Lectures are boring and grading is hard. The assignments have unclear guidelines and if you even THINK about citing something wrong or having a small grammatical error, say goodbye to your A. The combination it being an 8 am and her lack of enthusiasm makes it had to stay awake. Her slides have nothing on them so prepare to take a lot of notes.

her lectures are extremely boring and attendance policy is brutal so you can't get out of them. the class is made up of pointless assignments that don't add to learning at all. she's bitter and unsympathetic - only care about legitimizing her class by making it as tedious as possible. the worst professor ive ever had here and that's saying a lot.

I think she was a poor lecturer, often giving boring lectures. And many of the assignments had unclear guidelines on what they were looking for, and couple that with surprisingly particular grading, this was difficult. I am also not an architecture major, and maybe that's just how they roll. The professor is definitely knowledgeable, though.

Lots of writing for this class, but overall interesting if you like history. The final project is a lot of work, but if you keep up with the benchmarks you should be ok. Only notes given are slides with pictures, so come prepared to take a lot of notes yourself, but the material is very easy

Very unclear and inconsistent grading criteria - I would submit something that I thought was pretty good and get a C, then submit something mediocre and get an A. Lectures were not engaging, but the content is interesting enough to make up for it. Tests are open note, and relatively easy.

Dr. Mamoli is a respectable professor who is very knowledgeab in her field. Lectures were rather unclear to take notes on, but notetaking isn't too important for this class. The study guides are perfect notes for the tests, plus most of your grade will come from the large projects throughout the semester. Not an easy A, but a rewarding class.

Terrible lectures, attendance quizzes each class, doesn't respond to emails OR Ed Discussion oftentimes, doesn't care about student success, no communication between her and TA's, can only study for midterms via study sheets she produces, DONT read textbook (useless), TA's office hours are SUPER helpful pls take advantage, take a better humanities!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't take her class. The communication between her and the TA's was terrible, the grading was ridiculous and non-consistent. The lectures are extremely boring and very hard to make notes on, it just seems that she is not passionate about teaching. that's all. She never responds to emails and overall is very hard to approach. Expects way too much.

Natasha is funny, kind, and she's been teaching Russian for 20 years, so she really knows what she's doing. Since Russian is a difficult language, there's lots of work to do, but Natasha makes it fun. The class is an easy A if you study.

Don't let the idea of taking Russian scare you because Natasha is one of the best profs at Tech. She cares so much about her students and it's very easy to learn and do well in her class with little effort. If you don't do well on an assignment, she will let you turn it in or redo it the next day. The tests are fair and not at all difficult. 10/10

Natasha (first name basis oh yeah) is just amazing, she's so kind & understanding & has been teaching for like 20 years so she's very good at getting points across. If you don't come to class, it's okay because she will ask if you were sick. With assignments & oral quizzes, you can ask to do them for next lecture if you didn't have time to do it.

This was my favorite class I've taken at Tech. She is super sweet, helpful and really funny as well. She gives extra credit opportunities and is always willing to help. There's homework, but it isn't bad and really helps you learn the material. She's a pretty easy grader, but if you don't try, you won't do well. I would absolutely take her again.
The only thing is that Natasha is a non-native English speaker so sometimes it is hard to understand what she wants from an assignment. Otherwise she's great!

Natasha is beautiful, sweet, and one of the best professors I've had at Tech. the class is super small so you will personally get to know her. she's very interesting and divulges you in Russian culture. The class is not difficult at all, but you will have to work for an A.

I love Natasha! She is very interested in ensuring her students are learning Russian, but she is not a very strict grader because this is an elementary course. She goes over exactly what will be on each test and gives you examples for your oral quiz monologues. Also, she is very approachable, funny, and sweet.

Dr. Nezafati is a GOAT! He is a very understanding and caring professor who takes time to make sure his students understand the concepts of class, not just a pattern for problems. PSS was very helpful, and his lectures reinforced material well. The homework was time consuming and quizzes were hard, but by the exams you were good and an 83 was an A.

Dr. Nezafati cares a lot about his students and if you're going to take bmed2110 definitely take it with him. The class itself is a lot of work but if you take the time to watch the lecture videos and understand the homework, the quizzes and tests aren't terrible.

Great teacher! 3 exams (1 was the final) - each one was based on what we had learned since the previous exam so nothing cumulative and each one had 3 attempts (with grades averaged). Explained everything very well. Rounded my high B up to an A (I went to every class and did every assignment) and I'm very thankful. Very manageable class!

Big emphasis on group work and applicable skills (real life data studies, academic writing and review, etc.). Go to class because the slides are heavily abbreviated and only make sense in the context of his lecture. About 1 HW/week

Dr. Nezafati was very enthusiastic about the material. He explained everything very well and was very helpful when asked questions. He emphasized the small details, which are very important for this difficult course. He also made the online lectures this semester which were great. Definitely wouldn't want to take this class with anyone else.

Dr. Nezafati has been a great 2110 professor, especially with learning such different concepts than normal classes. He has always been very open to questions and helping outside of class. He seems to really enjoy the material and makes the class a lot more interesting. There is a lot of homework but TA hours are always really helpful (PAUL!!!)

He is a very kind professor but is not a great lecturer. His lectures are not very informative, and they are often disorganized. You have to go to class because Point Solutions tracks your location, but they are not super helpful. YouTube will be your best friend; StatQuest with Josh Starmer is much clearer for conceptual stuff.

BMED 2110 is a difficult and intense course. However, Professor Nezafati made it as manageable as possible and fun. He is by far the best professor for this class and makes complex topics understandable. He also makes his lectures very engaging and fun. I love him, he's one of the best professors at GT
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, very enthusiastic about the material, easy exams. Awful group project, long-winded explanations. Take Shu Jia instead if possible.

Really nice professor, explains concepts really well, and most experienced 2110 instructor. Really cares about his students, the structure of the course, and the BME program in general. Goes on long tangents sometimes.

This class is the weed-out and is naturally hard. Don't stress about it too much. Nezafati is a great prof, but I didn't like how the instructional team was 3 profs. It made the content more confusing than it already was. I would recommend asking questions early on if you get stuck. Falling behind in this class is easy to do, and you will get lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Nezafati's first priority is to his students. Although the weekly homework problems are difficult, he makes practice available every week, and his office hours are also of great help, both in-person and on MS Teams. If it were my call, he'd teach every single demo session too! Great teacher, great guy!

Class is hard, but he explains concepts very well. Super approachable outside of class, I asked him stuff after almost every class period and he didn't get annoyed and helped me understand the concepts. Similar to COE 2001 and CHBE 2100 since 1-2 equations are used to solve problems. Also, an 83 is an A, so you can't complain about tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was very helpful inside of class and always told you what you needed to know before an exam. Some parts of the class were harder than others, but there is a lot of slack given. Do what they tell you to and you will probably get an A. He can be a bit long-winded at times, but he does so to make sure everyone knows what is going on.

He is one of the most genuinely caring professors you'll ever meet. He always made the effort to be as accessible as possible to accommodate his students. 2210 isn't easy and it's very work heavy but Nezafati gives very fair quizzes and tests. All around great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, but overcomplicates things a little. Very particular about how you should do certain problems. That being said, the way he teaches you to approach problems is very methodical, which I like. Starts to get difficult during energy section. 83 is an A. Can potentially drop a hw and a quiz. Tests/quizzes are fair.

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I've had at Tech. He is accessible outside of class for several hours every day, highly responsive via email and wants his students to succeed. reviews.comment: Professor Nezafati is always willing to help, he truly cares about his students. He is very clear of what is expected of students and provides plenty of material for practice.

The tests are extremely fair, but working with others to understand the material in this class is the key to succeeding. Would definitely take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice, really caring, and really clear. Wants you to do well, you just have to meet him halfway.

Dr. Nezafati was an excellent professor. He is incredibly passionate about the subject as well as his students and wants to see you do well. He has a clear outline of what he is looking for on tests/quizzes/hw and grades according to that. Make sure you do all the hw, it takes forever, but it is the best practice for tests/quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures of 2210 will be divided between several prof. Dr. Nezafati was happily in charge of teaching the energy balance section. Go to office hours of prof and TAs. reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Nezafati truly cares about the success of his students. Yes, BME 2210 is a difficult class, but Nezafati encourages you to set up appointments outside of office hours and email him with questions. His English is okay but you will do well in this class by practicing problems, not by simply listening to Nezafati talk.

The class itself is very difficult but he doesn't make it any easier. He is still learning english so it would be very hard to understand what he was saying or meant to say. I would be afraid to ask him questions because he can be very defensive (since you didn't understand him to begin with) and doesn't explain it very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this course in Fall 2021. As expected, this class was difficult. However, in hindsight, this class is so much easier than the calculus and MATH courses that follow. Professor Gupta is very caring and strives to help her students understand the fundamentals of calculus.

Wow. Some of these reviews are sexist af. She is incredible. Knows exactly what she is talking about. I struggled at the beginning and was basically failing. Her super detailed feedback on quizzes and tests saved my ass. 20% of the course grade is a "portfolio" you submit. She made this hard class an awesome experience. Would take again and again.

She's a very, very harsh grader. Your quiz and exam may be deducted for various subtle details. And her expectations for students are particularly high, especially in a mathematics class teaching proof and logic. She will teach you pages of new and complicated proofs and concepts in the first class, and make you fail miserably in quiz after a day.

Actively looks only for one correct way to answer a question which is very detrimental for the class. Not great for this course. Might be ok for a basic level math class. Definitely lot of room for improvement.

Surprised to see the ratings. Maybe good for basic math classes but bad for this course. Accent is little different and though she takes time in office hours etc no one knows what answer she expects in hw/ quiz.
Horrible. Bad grading criteria
She is super nice and her class is super easy to understand.

I found her to be an excellent professor. Her lectures are great but, while they were not mandatory for my class, they were the only way to learn the content. Make sure todo the homework and all practice problems you can to prepare for exams, though.
Great at giving strategies on approaching hard problems. Makes sure that you understand every concept especially when you ask a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love her to death. If you are struggling, reach out to her. I did after a D on the first test and she gave me a bunch of extremely useful advice. I'm ending with an A! I'd take her over and over again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

Best professor I've ever had

This pandemic has been rough and online classes suck. But Neha made it so much better everytime we had class. Her class is not easy, but I've learned a ton. And I'm grateful for her relentless optimism and the help she gave me when I was in a tough spot earlier in the semester. A real gem.

The Professor seems dismissive and belittling in most interactions. Too much work for a two-credit course. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is such a nice and sweet person, but that is where the good ends. If you did not take calc in high school you are screwed. She is disorganized and instead of teaching the concepts, she just does examples. Which can be okay, but not great for application. Quizzes literally had trick questions on them and tests were too long for short time given.

She's the sweetest person ever. Also really good at explaining calculus. She constantly pauses in class to ask if anyone doesn't understand or has questions and she will explain things in a way that makes math actually easy to understand. One of the best math professors I've had ever.

I absolutely loved her. Her course was not easy, but her personality kept motivating me to keep pushing and learning. The material was heavy, but she explains everything really well and wants her students to understand. ASK QUESTIONS WHEN IN CLASS, she loves it. Must take!

Dr. Gupta is amazing. She gives out a lot of extra credit and is really clear about what she expects from students. Get ready to do a lot of homework. Everything on the tests is covered in lectures and recitations. Don't miss recitations. Make sure you go to office hours and ask a lot of questions. Study hard for the final.
Dr. Gupta is always in a pleasant mood for class. She enjoys interacting with her students and lectures well too.

Dr. Gupta is one of the best professors I have had. I am not a math person, but Dr. Gupta really made me enjoy calculus. She is super accessible outside of class and was really helpful during office hours.

Dr. Gupta is super sweet and really cares about her students. She wants you to do well in her class. She is also very enthusiastic about what she teaches and has a lovable, light-hearted personality. I really enjoyed attending lectures. Homework was a little tough but doable. Tests are fair. 10/10 very much recommend.

Dr. Gupta is one of the most amazing and caring individuals I've met at GT. She is super accessible outside of class and even encourages you to attend her office hrs, even if it's just to stop by and say hi. She explains concepts VERY well. Not going to lie, I will miss being in her class.
She was very helpful and encouraged her students every lecture.
She was a solid choice.

For someone who does not love math, Gupta makes it SO HARD to not enjoy her class. She literally made my day every time I saw her, no matter how miserable I was in her class. She is very accessible for office hours and wants to help her students. Best math professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you are taking Differential Calculus at Georgia Tech, Dr. Gupta is the best choice for you. Lectures are quite interesting relative to the material taught. She is very nice and caring, she will help you if you need it and make an effort. If you can choose her, I would definitely do so. It will significantly help you in your future mathematics

If you are taking Differential Calculus at Georgia Tech, Dr. Gupta is the best choice for you. Lectures are quite interesting relative to the material taught. The class itself is pretty annoying because, if you're like me and already know all the content from HS you expect it to be super easy, but they're looking for very specific things and I think the aim is to trick you on tests and quizzes. HOWEVER professor gupta is so enthusiastic and cares SO much about her students, really great and engaging prof

Neha is by far the best math professor I have ever had. She will work tirelessly to help you and really cares about your success and happiness in general. I emailed her the night before a test once because I was anxious, and she sent me a huge email with encouragement and kind words and talked me out of my stress. An INCREDIBLE human being.
Best Calc 1 Prof!!!

Great professor. Super enthusiastic and fun. You HAVE to go to lecture, because she goes over super difficult problems in class that show up on the tests. She always releases a big problem bank before each exam, and if you master all the problems on the bank you'll do great on the tests. She's super nice and helpful during office hours.

reviews.comment: Dr. Gupta was an absolute gem. She really cares for her students and lecture was always engaging. I never went to office hours bc it was so crowded, but if you do the homework, a little extra practice, and go to recitation you'll be fine. Brush up on precalc bc they do optional tests which adds five points to your final grade if you score 87+!!

Bruh Tech's differential calc courses are all jokes. It should've been a walk in the park but it was like swimming through a gasoline ocean on fire. She's the best in the department and it still sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Its Calculus 1 so its kinda of difficult. She tries her best to present the material. The quizzes, hw and participation grades are easy As. Her bundles of energy and high enthusiasm made lectures more tolerable, and her lectures are well structured and easy to follow along. She lets you know exactly what's going to be on the exam and provides enough material to prepare.
Very very sweet professor. Willing to listen to students and provide feedback. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Gupta is the most caring and understanding professor I've met at ga tech. I highly recommend going to her office hours! She takes the time to get to know each student. Dr. Gupta is great! She really cares about her students and makes lectures interesting and engaging. If you are unclear about a topic, she will go out of her way to make sure you understand, going as far as meeting one on one and buying Starbucks!
SHES AMAZING

Dr. Gupta is the sweetest woman ever! Her class is the easiest a STEM class at tech can be, so still hard but she is a really good teacher. She makes it easier to understand hard information and really cares about her students

reviews.comment: So good. Can't recommend enough.

reviews.comment: The MOST caring professor I ever had. Her lectures are clear and interesting. Real GEM!
Super nice teacher. Tests and quizzes are just like the problems you do in class

Neha is literally the sweetest teacher I have ever had. She genuinely cares about her students and tries her hardest to help every student succeed. I never went to office hours but she offers a lot of opportunities to get extra help. She gives out packets which are helpful when reviewing for tests. Might be more difficult without a Calc background.

Shes just a really nice person. It's a hard class, but the most important thing is to just work on the test bank cuz most of the problems come from that and if you can do all of those problems you can get A's on the test pretty easily. I recommend going to office hours because she definitely notices and probably helped my grade because of it.

Quizzes and exams are what you expect and she sets you up with a problem bank beforehand to study. Going to class is important, she does a learning catalytics every day.

She's clear, engaging, and enjoys class participation. Learned a lot without being that focused. She really cares and is sooo helpful. One of the best, definitely take her. She gives packets to take notes; they make sense even if you don't listen in class. If you study for quizzes, they're easy. Tests are medium difficulty. True to 2 credit hours.

Neha is a literal saint, she's so unendingly nice and happy and optimistic. She genuinely cares about every student, and really wants you to succeed. Brings you candy, gives good lectures, gives very clear and accurate study guides, will help you outside and after class all the time. She's ridiculously nice, take this class with her.
Relentlessly optimistic - but a little too much so.

I was not great at calc in high school and was concerned about math at tech, but Neha really cares about the well-being and the understanding of her students and created an inviting classroom environment. I learned so so much even though I still found the tests and quizzes challenging and am really glad I took the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Neha is one of the nicest and most caring professors I ever had, and is always cheerful. She genuinely wants every student to succeed. She gives plenty of opportunities to ask questions in class, and she is super helpful in office hours. Also, she brought us candy for Halloween.

Overall a really great teacher. Calculus is something that I am not very good at, but Neha really goes in the extra mile during lectures to provide the simplest and clearest explanations to her students. There will be 4 quizzes and 3 midterms overall for this course. Make sure you study the midterm practice problems she gives you, as it will help!

Really, all you need for this class is your pencil, your self, and some elbow grease (even if you've done calc before!) She makes it easy on you by providing worksheets, but tests are heavy on building the theories and not discrete. so learn your stuff. She's super supportive and goes out of her way to ensure you're doing well in class w/ feedback.
Super nice and caring. If you can take her definitely do it.
Neha is super nice and friendly as well as being a great teacher. Her office hours are super helpful and she is such a genuinely nice person.

I took him Spring 2020. He's a good lecturer but the exams were absolutely horrid. He was so bad that the math department fired him the semester after I withdrew. Thank god he got fired. I hope he never is allowed to teach again.

Gosh, the worst prof I've ever had. Not bc he doesn't know what he's talking about, but because he treats his students so poorly. reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is easily one of the most fair profs I've taken from at Tech. His lectures can be hard to understand, but if you actually show up or just read his notes and the textbook, you should be completely fine. His grading is super straightforward and so is the homework/tests, they're just like the notes but harder.

VERY fair prof. As everyone else has been saying, hw can be really long and difficult but helps sm for exams. if you can do the hw the exams are a breeze for the most part. cares a lot about the class. great choice for 2100 and I think our section was by far the easiest. so glad I took Liu and would 100% take him again.

Professor Liu genuinely cares about his students and wants us to succeed. The homework was tough but office hours were helpful and he kept the tests pretty light. He never threw curveballs and was very straight forward about what's expected in his class. His notes are also really clear and its easy to catch up if you miss a class.

Great guy and incredibly understanding. Homework's take a really long time. Exam's are hard but lenient on partial credit as long as your approach is right. Don't take the non-exam components of the course lightly because they add up (homework, quizzes, rig project).

He is an amazing lecturer. He has clear notes, which are uploaded right after class and are very helpful. He gives lots of HW which takes a lot of time, but it's just the nature of this class. Exams are easier than HW so just redoing the lecture problems and HW would prepare you for the exam.

Dr. Liu is not the best lecturer, but is very approachable and also very smart. He is almost always willing to answer questions for us, and tries not to overload us with unnecessary amounts of work. He listens to feedback from his students. A lot of homework, but tests are similar to homework problems so make sure you can do the homework yourself

Dr. Liu was a great professor. Past reviews had me nervous to take him, but after this semester I was pleasantly surprised. He cares about his students and makes accommodations. Reviews might rate him low because the class itself is hard, but he is a good professor. Homework does take a significant amount of time, but it helps for the exams.

Tough class but great professor. Lectures can go pretty fast sometimes and they focus a lot on problem-solving, but all notes/worked-out problems are posted right after class. Always willing to answer questions during and after lectures. Homework takes a very long time but he often makes the more time-consuming/less relevant sections optional.

Hes a nice enough man, but hes not great at explaining or answering questions. Extremely tough homework that takes hours and hours. Im talking 10 hours a week on just homework. Tests are very difficult too. Partial credit is given, but not enough. No multiple choice and tests have questions that arent similar to anything done in class or on hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is difficult in general. I wouldn't say Liu is a great lecturer, but he is very willing to compromise with student and will listen to any suggestions. Very reasonable. The textbook is confusing and not helpful. Right amount of homework for 2 credits, but the concepts require studying
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu does not have an effective teaching style, but he is extremely smart with the material. If there's another instructor teaching, go for it because the chances are you will almost learn nothing in class. You will have to really on the textbook and outside resources to learn the material. His tests are hard, office hours are advised!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, very accessible especially with trouble shooting. I found this course to be a lot, and had no background in coding so I felt lost. At moments I felt talked down to when I did not know something. However he does genuinely care, and clearly loves what he does. At times though I did feel as if he was a bit overqualified.

He makes it extremely clear what it takes to succeed in his class. He is exceedingly caring and accommodating to his students. He is truly enthusiastic and made me genuinely enjoy the course so much. He is very accessible in office hours to ask questions to but doesn't spoon food the answers to his students. Amazing professor.

This class really helped me be a better industrial designer. The professor was enthusiastic, very helpful on our projects, and super knowledgeable. The studio can definitely be challenging, and I might hesitate to take it if you've got a bunch of other really time intensive classes, but otherwise, I highly recommend.

Extremely easy class. Take her if you want an A, but not if you want to learn French. She's unorganized and her syllabus is not clear. She does give accommodations for students though. By the end of the semester, only 5 people would come to class consistently except for when there was an exam.
Extremely absentminded, often had to remind her what we did in the previous class. Two grades the whole semester, I don't think she actually graded them though, everyone got an A.
Take her if you want the easiest A of your life. Don't take her if you actually want to improve your french.
Prof. CF is a very energetic and fun teacher. I enjoyed her teaching and discussion methods to review literature and learned a lot in her class. Would recommend 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor. Just do your work and you'll be good. She is so sweet and one of my favorite professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and so kind. I love taking all French classes with her. She grades pretty easy. You work hard for the first half of the semester, but she makes it easier toward the end because she knows this is Tech and we have a ton of other exams too. Shes so funny also.

I took him for complex analysis and as a non-math major it was extremely difficult for me. Everyone else thought it was really easy though and I could tell he was a good lecturer I just couldn't comprehend what was going on. He answered all my questions and graded my answers fairly.

He is a great guy and a good teacher. His lectures are straightforward and he works out examples in class, not just focusing on theory. His quizzes and tests are fair. Make yourself present during office hrs and ask questions, he is super helpful and will remember you when it comes time to assign final grades!

He is very interested in his students' success. Class is not necessary since he uploads all of his materials online. The homeworks are very useful for practice and the quizzes are easy. He gives practice problems and a review for each exam, so if you can do them, you'll do well on the exams. All in all, a great professor and a great class.

He presents the material clearly during lecture, but the material can be difficult and if you fall behind it easy to get lost because he moves quickly.  There is a quiz every week, but the majority of your grade is three tests and the final.  He teaches to the test, but make sure you go to recitation.

The class can be very confusing at first but Northington makes you develop the right thought process for solving all kinds of problems. Very clear and understandable lectures, never had to check the textbook once because he taught it so well in class. quizzes and tests never threw any curveball questions at you. Very nice guy, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He was pretty great linear algebra professor. His office hours were great and his lectures were super useful. The content was difficult but he made it easy. I would recommend to do really well on the first two units (a lot of  high test averages) because unit 3 & unit 4 (on the final) was difficult for most of us. Take him if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Went to office hours once before the final and had a one-on-one Q&A over the last unit with him for an hour, incredibly helpful. He is a solid lecturer and a down-to-earth guy, seemed to genuinely care about students and adapted the final to exclude material we couldn't cover in lecture due to a tornado the week or so before. 88+A

All around great professor. Lectures got progressively better throughout the semester, and tests got progressively harder. Recitation quizzes were easy, especially if you did the homework beforehand. Make sure you study hard for the first and second tests because they will turn out to be the easiest in hindsight. Very achievable A if you work hard.

I liked Dr. Northington's style of notes. The weekly recitation quizzes were really easy, so make sure to always go! He explains the concepts clearly and goes over examples in class that were helpful. The tests weren't that hard either.

You'll do fine as long as you show up to class. Lectures consist of example problems with questions. The quizzes are easy, so you need to go to recitation. The tests are not bad at all. The professor is a cool guy and knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear and well paced, tests were straightforward.

This is Northington's first time teaching but he's done a great job for his class - he's very friendly and forthright with students, grades fairly, and his tests/HW are fair and not a huge amount of work. It's not an easy A for the class, but he assigns an amount of work that is more than reasonable. Great prof.

First time teacher this year and was ehh at first but definitely improved by a large margin towards the end. Provides great notes and resources, is especially good outside of class.  Would recommend going to office hours when possible. Professor is not necessarily hard but the subject can be.

Professor Northington is highly passionate about the subject and his students. He is always available for office hours. His tests can be easy, but there is a huge margin of error that can cause you to easily fail. There are no grade replacements, dropped tests/quizzes, or extra credit. He drops a homework, which is kinda pointless bc they're easy.
Solid professor. Knows lots about the subject and is always willing to help outside of class.
Best teacher I have at Tech so far. Had him on Pacific Program in New Zealand. Great guy and really cares that you actually learn something. Definitely take one of his classes!
very good professor.  tells you what you need to know and nothing else.  Also the day of the first test i was late by 45 min and he let me take it right then and there. very understandable

He was a wonderful teacher, very approachable, and an interesting lecturer.  I took one of his M-C tests, which had a few tricky questions, but he curved it to make up for them.  I took all the other tests in essay form and got straight A's the rest of the term.  I would take him again any day!

M-C tests aren't that hard (got all 50 questions right on one of them), but he puts some random questions on there sometimes that don't come from reading or lectures. You have to read a whole lot, and he shows his liberal bias too much (but that's typical among all of the History professors).

Restored my faith in the history department! Absolutely fabulous lecturer. Gives the option for essay or multiple choice test. TAKE THE ESSAY TEST! Gives extra credit! Exceptionally organized, posts all lecture outlines and extra documents online. Would take again in a heartbeat!
Great professor would highly recommend!
Why was he kind of mean and unflexible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Didn't really enjoy the class because it was textbook heavy and a flipped classroom setting, would've preferred a lecture setting instead. But there are test correction opportunities for essay questions, which helped me. Overall, his outline for what we were expected to know seemed a little vague and unorganized. Honestly, wouldn't take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: not a great prof. he's one of those ppl who only care ab their research rather than teaching. he was abrasive when i was having a very tough time (personal issue), and his TAs for the NEUR2001 lab aren't great either. that said, his lecture TAs are a lot better and i'd highly recommend going to their recitations! only reason i did well lol

He taught the 2nd unit of NEUR 2001. His lectures are always interesting for sure, but you HAVE to listen to what he says because a lot of important info is NOT on the lecture slides. He's a very nice and chill guy and clearly cares about each of the students. Just beware the 2nd unit of NEUR-2001 is the hardest (as of spring 2024).

Loved Professor Oettl's strategic management class despite being worried to take it as it was my first ever strategy class at Scheller. Lectures were engaging and Oettl did a great job of relating case readings to current events. His grading was fair and it's clear that he cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well. Take him!

Lectures not worth going to since tests are literally out of the book. He is the only Professor I had that actually took "class participation" seriously for a grade. and the extra credit dint even help. So make sure you talk in his class even though attendance is not mandatory. Tests were also hard, no curve even though class avg was low on 2 test
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Oettl's "strategy" in explaining business and corporate strategy isn't the best.  He might have done a better job in explaining the fundamental aspects. Rushing through a 120 slide  presentation in three days isn't the way to do it. This leaves us confused about what is important and how all come together to get a high level understanding.

He bases a large portion of your grade on your strategy's outcome (performance) instead of the thought process behind your strategy. For instance, your final exam grade is based largely on your performance. Also, he is very unclear on the guidelines of the case write-ups; in his syllabus there was a one sentence description.
He definitely cares about teaching and is very passionate about the material. CFD is very math-heavy, especially for an online course... But, he did a good job trying to make it interesting.

Professor Oefelein was a great thermo professor. The majority of lectures are working example problems. Homeworks were difficult and took a lot of time, but tests were only slightly more difficult than homework. All lecture notes, homework solutions, and test solutions were made available to students.
One of the best professor in the AE department. Dr Oefelein has great sense of humor and most of all, he wants you to succeed. 2010 is a tough course but taking it with him will make it worthwhile.

If you have the chance to take Dr. Oefelein for anything thermo related definitely do it. He posts all of his lecture notes, homeworks are hard-ish but straightforward, and tests are easier than hw problems but still very straightforward if you study. 2nd midterm was takehome as well. To top it all off he's a great guy with a decent sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There are so many things I want to say but not enough words in the English language to describe how goated she is. All I will say is she has never given a student below an A in her entire history of this course and she gave out max score on every assignment as long as you did it. Goated person and goated course.
One of the best professors at GT! She is quite caring and provides great feedback on assignments. This was an overall easy class but engaging.

I took KOR3415 online with her. The best professor ive had at tech, she is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. she is very understanding, and her feedback on assignments is so kind. best prof ever
I don't usually leave reviews but I had to for her. She is absolutely the best. Simply take her if you're still deciding. She is so kind, understanding, and thoughtful. 사랑해요 선생님!
The kindest professor I've ever had. She is the absolute best and cares deeply for her students. Please take a course with her, she's amazing.

I can not even begin to describe how amazing of a teacher Mrs. Oh is. She is caring, kind, funny, and a great teacher. She always has a smile and never makes anyone feel left out of the class. She wants you to succeed and asks how you are doing even outside of class. 100/10 teacher and would take again if I could!
Very sweet professor; and took time and made sure that every student individually understood the content without being condescending.
Best teacher I've had in my 4 years at college. Great lectures, very funny and easy to understand. Also brings snacks for students.

Professor Oh was incredibly kind, funny, and helpful. She made the class fun with plenty of games and snacks. We moved pretty quickly in lecture but homework was graded easily, so it was easy to make an A in the class if you studied. There was less emphasis on speaking and practice, but she provided office hours for those looking to talk.

Professor Oh is the best! This is my second semester taking Korean with her and I wouldn't change her for anyone else. She's so caring both inside and outside of class; very understanding if you're having trouble/miss class; lectures are interesting. If you're deciding on taking Korean, make sure you take it with her.

Learning is always hard, but SSN Oh puts more focus on our actual learning and understanding over our grades. She's extremely caring and a very light grader. She's very available for help and often holds in class sessions and gives us snacks. I'm retaking her for 1002 and she's continued to be passionate about teaching.

Professor Oh is an amazing teacher! Her classes are always very engaging and she's always available to help students when they need. Despite being an online course, she encouraged us to come to her office hours and her in-person classes for extra help. She's an easy grader and provides great feedback on every assignment, and is overall encouraging.

Dr. Oh is such a warm-hearted, kind, and caring professor. She is dedicated to teaching and encouraging her students. I have never met someone with such a kind heart. I had her during COVID (2020) and she still remembers me personally! That's just the kind of person she is. I'd take all my courses with her if I could. 1,000,000/10.
Great class! I took Korean only to satisfy my humanity's requirement but this class was unexpectedly awesome. She even remember's and celebrates everyone's birthday.
She's really sweet and the makes the course pretty easy to do well in. It's an easy A if you are willing to do the assignments and put in a little time into learning the material.

She is the most caring and understanding professor I've ever had. I always feel comforted and welcome in class! She is also very accessible by phone number or office hours. Getting a good grade is easy in this class bevause she gives you opportunities to make up homework or even get extra credit after the final.
Korean class feeds me.

She was extremely fun and enthusiastic about learning Korean. All of her activities were fun and she went above-and-beyond to make sure we understood Korean and Korean culture. She was extremely accesible and went out of her way to help if you wanted it.

I don't even know where to start! She's absolutely amazing and super caring! She makes learning Korean so much fun, and the way she engages the class is really nice. She is super accommodating and you can tell that she really cares about you and your progress. If I could take her for my other Korean classes I would!

Professor Oh is by far the kindest most enthusiastic lecturers you will meet at Tech. She genuinely cares about her students and dedicates so much time outside of class (even during school breaks!) to help students practice Korean. She is so wholesome and is incredibly flexible. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Oh SSN is an amazing, charismatic person. She cares so much for her students and is encouraging and bright at every step. She is so kind and she really wants you to not only succeed, but really get a feel for the Korean language and culture. Definitely take her.

Professor Oh is so sweet and amazing. She truly cares about each and every student. I definitely recommend taking intro Korean classes with her. If you need help, she replies to emails very quickly and will help. She is very positive and wants all of her students to succeed.
Continues to be the best prof I've had at Tech, and one of the kindest people I've ever met
The kindest professor at Georgia Tech. Takes the time to write out personal emails to each student about test scores. Fun class and relatively easy if you do the homework

The nicest person I have met at Georgia Tech, maybe ever. Korean is a tough language, but Oh SSN really goes above and beyond to not only make it easy, but fun too. Lectures are interactive & enjoyable, and tests mirror HW. There's a ton of vocab quizzes, but only worth 10% of the grade. She cares deeply about her students & wants you to succeed.

Fun class. Professor is always excited to teach students Korean. Lots of vocab quizzes, but they're straight forward and easy. Tests are not difficult and if you're ever struggling, she is more than happy to help. Easy A. Homework is given often as well, but graded very generously.
Professor Oh might be my favorite person ever. She is extremely helpful and makes learning Korean really fun. I can't wait until next semester with her.

Obviously, with this being a language class you'll have homework but the textbook and workbook are cheap.  Professor Oh is great!  Vocab quizzes are often but easy.  Tests are more about application of the language.  There's also a recitation session.  There are a couple of simple projects. Overall, a great GPA boosting class.
Professor Oh made me love Korean! She's amazing! She is super helpful and really does everything to help you learn the language!

Great teacher. Definitely knows his stuff. Entertaining lecturer and lectures are very important. Tests make up 80% of grade and they are never curved so be prepared on test days. Overall very reasonable and makes the class enjoyable.

Pierron was not good for dynamics. It was his 2nd semester teaching it, 90% of grade is from exams (2 midterms, 1 final) and 10% is from HW. HW is just write 2 questions about the problem. Spent too much time deriving equations, attempted examples, didn't finish them and sometimes was wrong. Class attendance dropped so much after a few weeks.

Avoid if bad at physics, otherwise you'll be fine. 2 midterms + 1 final = 90% of grade (9 problems total). Takes off a lot of points for messing up the math, but also gives 70% for just showing you know the process. 
Depends how you look at it, for me it made the tests more stressful and that didn't go well with my other classes.

His lectures were clear and well structured, and the homework was a breeze. However, 90% of the grade was from the exams (40% midterms and 50% final exam), so you absolutely must do well on them. Fortunately, all of the problems are from the textbook, so pracitce well and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pierron is a great professor. While the class itself can present difficult problems, Dr. Pierron's lecture style involves working through a variety of different scenarios using a game plan that can be applied to any statics problem! 90% of your grade is from tests, but he's a fair grader and you know what to expect each time. Caring guy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, eager to help. Prepares you for exams well
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has this annoying thing where he makes you put two "questions" you have on your homework. I forgot to put them on the first HW and got a zero, which was annoying and made me get a B in the class. He's not a bad teacher, his exam questions are usually straight from the textbook so just do all of the textbook problems and its an easy 100 in the class
Love this man. I like how he teaches and he's pretty funny. The tests were fair and he gives plenty of study material.
I did not understand what he was saying, but his heart was in the right place.

the goat. defo take him if you can. such a cool person and an even better professor. class is not too difficult either if u listen to lectures and study material that he highlights in class. TB is a waste of time, only do past papers and HW and you will be absolutely fine

Great option for thermo. HW is an automatic 100 as long as you do it and tests make up 90% of your grade (lowest one dropped). Not much time/work if you understand the material well and can do well on the tests. Baguette/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homeworks are an easy 100%. However, 90% of your grade are the exam problems, so if you think that you don't have to practice, think again. But he is forgiving and gives you 70% credit just for proving that you understand how to solve the problem, 30% doing the math behind the solution. But don't miss lecture, he usually doesn't upload notes often.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great option for this class. You know exactly what kinds of problems are on each exam, and he even gives you a sheet reminding you the steps to take. The sheet also breaks down percentages as to how many points each part of the question is worth. Good lectures as well. Don't sleep on homework or exam review, but a great professor all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Lectures are super informative and he has a sense of humor. Homework assignments are completion, and the two exams + final are most of the grade. Very accessible through office hours.

The class itself is kind of weird, you have to solve problems using 1-2 equations. For people who've taken CHBE 2100 or BMED 2110 this class is a lot like that.

Professor Pierron is the absolute best, ever! I do not say that lightly. Yes it's hard, but he gives you all the tool you need to understand the material well. Don't skip class because the textbook isn't half as helpful as he is. If you have a question, ask after class or in office hours because he will work with you till you understand. 11/10 prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: 90% tests meaning one bad test and little chance for an A. really informative lecture though
One of the best professors I've taken at Tech hands down. Amazing person, clear grading criteria, no surprises on tests, basically all the good stuff here and you can't go wrong taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class seems hard if you have no prior knowledge, but the lectures cover everything you need to know for the test. If you listen well and follow along with the practice problems in class, you could get a good grade without studying for the midterm since he teaches the content very thoroughly. Office hours are helpful if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great guy, but average professor - Though, most find him to be a good professor. He knew the material very well but sometimes had a hard time explaining the easier topics because of his deep understanding of the subject.

Honestly, one of the best professors I've had this semester. He is incredibly understanding and explains the material in a way you would understand. If you email him for help, he will set up an appointment immediately to address your concerns. Be careful on the exams as they are weighted heavily on your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He was honestly a blessing this semester despite what was going on. He is super understanding toward his students, even giving 24hrs to do all exams. He is pretty good at explaining things and takes the time to go through multiple practice problems during class, and fields all questions. Only complaint is that the exams are very heavily weighted.
Super understanding, funny, and lenient grader. He is one of the best professors I've ever had!

He has been great during COVID. His lectures are straightforward, and we have 24 hours to work on each exam. You just have to pay attention during lectures, and actually do the homework(he gives you solutions for the homework, he wants you to attempt them and submit any questions for a grade). Class grade based off 2 exams + final (90%) and HW(10%)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy and professor! Lectures have a lot of examples and less theory, which worked really well for me. Notes can get kind of messy, but nothing horrible. Gives a lot of practice problems for students during class, which makes some lectures more of a recitation. In person attendance during COVID. HW submit and pass, exams very chill. Recommended

Really really nice, funny and caring. Homework super easy, gives 100 if you just submit it. Exams kinda hard but it would be an understatement if I said he grades fairly. He helps you, gives credit to everything, somehow makes you get a good grade. Lectures a little boring but even though thermodynamics is hard, he will make it easy for you.
Prof pierron is the best. He goes through the material very well and gives logical steps for how to work out each type of problem. Tests aren't horrible if you pay attention in class and do the hw.

Professor Pierron explains complex thermodynamics in accessible and understandable ways. He is accessible outside of class and cares about his students. Gives a Word for test prep and tests are reasonable. Thermo takes a lot of work, but if you put in the hours of study and homework you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are good at mechanical physics, then this class is perfect for you. There were few graded assignments (7 HW's worth 10% total, Exam 1+2 worth 25% each, & Final Exam 40%) so if you can learn the material, you'll easily make an A with little work. However, if you struggle with the material or are a bad test taker do not take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a good professor who makes lectures entertaining. I really like that he engages the class and makes jokes along the way.
Great prof. Great at explaining material. Test takes most people the whole class to finish and abut challenging but overall learn a lot and also make funny comment as well

Definitely one of the best teachers at GT. I joined late GT and I had hard time to adapt, I didn't had much time to do my homework. He gave me a lot of advices and was interested in my situation. Rather than this, I will add if you are interested in understanding fatigue at a grad level, you should definitely take this class without hesitation.
Best teacher I've had at tech. Very organized and tests are easy if you do the hw. You can make do without a textbook in thermo.

Probably the best teacher I have had at Tech so far.  Great at explaining the material.  Cool, funny guy as well.  If you ever have questions, go talk to him.  Not too much homework and the tests are easy if you pay attention and go to class.  Definitely recommend.
Great class. Explains material clearly and is willing to help students.

Easy A. Just do the extra credit, pay attention during class to do the homework, and decent on the 4 exams. You can also replace an exam with the optional final. Professor Remick is a very funny, kind, and caring professor who is always willing to help you. Very accessible and a solid choice.

Super easy A! There are 4 tests which are all online and open note and open book. Theres also some extra credit for doing the practice tests. And she has a 5th test which serves as a way to replace your grade on a poorer test grade. Super easy, totally recommend her and its an easy A.
Did lots of in-class Excel worksheets and a little bit of homework. Tests are open Excel and open notes so just take good notes and pay attention to the formulas and you will have no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: All of her tests are open book/open note/open chegg/ open google, but you still need to understand what you are doing to do well. As long as you understand the homework you will be fine. She is also funny and makes a lot of jokes in lecture, but you really don't need to attend every class to do well.

I have never taken statistics before but I learn a lot from this course. My first test is not good, but after that everything is better. Do the homework and keep reviewing them. Also, do practice chapters, so the test will not be hard.

Remick is definitely quirky as professors go. If you took AP Stat/similar in HS, this class will go really well for you. Otherwise, don't worry! The tests are open book/note/printed off lecture slides/old hw questions/whatever u want. Plenty of exercises + HW so you could miss a few, but never too much work outside of class that it's overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you are good at stats or have taken it before, take her. Test is SO much harder than homework and practice test, but she uses questions from the practice section. Do those. She literally uses the same questions. 3% extra credit earned by practice test. She rounded up my grade by a whole point to next letter. Go to office hours, ask questions.

Reads off slides, class is insanely hard to pay attention to. Doesn't require attendance and there's no motivation to go since everyone pretty much self teaches themselves everything. Tests are not very easy and material gets difficult by the third one. She's helpful in office hours-- guaranteed B, A onlyif you've taken stat before/work like crazy.

Lectures are pretty useless unless you're the kind of person that material will stick in your head after you hear it said and worked out. Whiteboard handwriting is terrible, honestly. Tests are straight forward and basically straight from the homework. Do all the homework and minimal class participation is required for credit.

You must read for this class, and it's also helpful to have basic Econ knowledge beforehand. I found that her tests didn't always match up with the book, but overall her class wasn't terrible. You get participation points by asking questions 8 times in class. Once you do that, you really don't have to go to class if you study the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the most boring lecturers I've ever had. Your grade comes from 3 tests, so you have the option of not taking the final.. but it's still not worth taking her class. take a professor who is more helpful than the textbook! you won't regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy class. Lectures are a tad boring, but her in-class explanations and examples make the content easy to understand. You need to participate in class 8 times or do an in-class presentation to get full participation points. Tests are easy if you do the practice exams. Drops lowest test score. Adds 2% to total average if you get an A on 12 of HWs.

She requires participation from students, but I got the credit pretty easily because she'll ask simple questions and takes lots of answers. There's an optional group presentation as an alternative. I went to lecture because it makes the class easier, she's pretty good at explaining. Tests are easier compared to homework, and the final is optional

Incredibly boring lectures, pretty much just reads off the slides. You have to participate in at least 8 lectures in the semester to get the full participation points, but she makes it pretty easy. Her tests arent that bad as long as you do the practice tests she gives out. If youve taken Econ classes before youll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy class. Lectures are boring but if you show up and half pay attention you get an A. Lots of chances to get bonus points and even one exam is dropped.

Dr. Shemyakina was a great professor. She had a firm teaching style, but was still nice (especially if you were one of the people that came to most lectures). She's a little quiet, but really knowledgeable and gave great examples. She liked to have the class participate throughout the lectures. It wasn't incredibly easy, but it wasn't hard.

She's very picky and has incredibly boring lectures. Her tests are very arbitrary. She doesn't really care about her students and more so just herself and she doesn't care if you fail or pass- you can tell that she is just here for her job of reading off of a projector and nothing more.

Able to drop one test, lots of wiggle room on homework completion, etc. Basically there's no excuse to not get an A. Lectures are pretty much her reading from a powerpoint, but material is straightforward and tests are accurate reflections of the slides and practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super easy A in a boring class.  Just spend a bit of time (an hour) reading each chapter, and the tests are SO easy to get an A on.  If you go ahead and get your 5 participation points early, you don't have to go to class really.  Knock out all the homeworks (they're so easy too) early and get the extra credit.

Very fair teacher. Teaches whats on the test, tests on what she teaches. If you study you will get an A. She has an accent that you can understand what she is saying but difficult to stay awake for unless you enjoy the subject. Many opportunities to boost your grade up a few points in the year.

Very average.  She has a thick accent but for me it wasn't too hard to understand.  However, her class is so boring that I just teach myself.  There are also not a lot of grades at all, so its really important to do well on every test.

This class was horrible. I could barely understand her accent and the fact that she doesn't speak loud doesn't help the situation either. Attendance is pretty mandatory because she gives extra credit for being there sometimes. Homework is online and some of them are dropped. If you want to get a good grade, do not take OLGA!

Good prof.  She knows what shes teaching and rewards you for doing the course work with reasonable exams.  She only grades the top 50% for your hw so if you get stuck it sometimes doesn't effect your grade.

She is an OK professor, but can be difficult to understand. Class is not particularly interesting but generally gets out about 5 min early. Weekly HW assignments aren't too difficult, but there are a fair amount of them. PPT slides are made available online.

Not a very great professor at all. The class is supposed to be easy, but she overloads you with Aplia homework assignments and her tests are nothing like what she goes over in class. Her lectures are boring and her accent is way too strong. It didn't help to have this class in the morning, either. Try a different professor for Microeconomics.
Class was graded on a couple of tests and no study tools are given. Professor Oliver is very nice and caring apart from this.

Phenomenal lectures! One of the best professors I've had at Tech and constantly keeps lectures interesting. Only quips are that the 3 exams weigh 75% of the grade (20, 20, 35) and the online slides lack solutions to example problems. However, if you pull up to lectures and do the homework, I think you'll find the course to be enjoyable :)

Exams are very heavily weighted on your final grade. 2 midterms 20% each, with the final exam being worth 35%. He doesn't round grades at all and does not curve exams. Lectures are very boring and uneventful. HW is online and isn't too bad, just time-consuming. The only good thing about his class is that he doesn't take attendance.

Our class was weird because it was only 7 people and our classroom had some issues, but Oliver didn't really help the case.
