He admitted the course was really hard when he made (countless) mistakes in lectures, but didn't cut us any slack on our hw or tests. Wish the course had some curve. Tough class, tougher professor.

Dr. Oliver's tough grading and hypocrisy create a frustrating learning environment. There is a significant gap between the high standards he demands from students and the numerous mistakes he made himself, which were often overlooked or ignored. Approach with caution.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fair professor, class expectations are clearly laid out, grading is heavily test dependent - 20% for each test (2) and 35% for the final exam. Do the work to learn the material over time rather than cramming it, he doesn't look to trick you, but the exams are fairly challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Oliver gives amazing lectures. He has clear grading criteria, and if you put in a decent amount of effort, you will understand the material and do well. He gets off-topic sometimes, but it keeps the course interesting. Overall, Professor Oliver is an exceptional professor and it is well worth attending his lectures and paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Oliver delivers detailed and clear lectures, though they can sometimes lean a little towards the dry side (not a huge issue overall). The homeworks and tests cover the course material very directly, so there are no surprises. There is one group paper that functions a literature review, and he does have a fair way of assigning group credit.

Professor Oliver is a great lecturer and would definitely be great in an in-person setting, but watching his lectures asynchronously was also good. Grade in class is very heavily weighted on the one midterm and final, which are not too bad. Quizzes basically come straight from lectures so make sure you take good notes. A great choice for ECON 2106.

Dr. Oliver was entertaining and clear in his lectures. You do have to buy the 100 dollar online textbook access though to do the assignments. Don't procrastinate the graded homework since he doesn't take it up until the end of the semester. Attendance isnt mandatory but quizzes and extra credit are during class so it basically is to pass.

Good teacher but he didn't seem like he had a lot of time to care about the class he was teaching. Stopped giving us homework halfway into the semester because he didn't have time to make them and most of our lectures he came up with the night before. I don't feel like I learned anything but at least the course was easy. There's a group paper...

I really enjoyed Dr. Oliver's class, and as a result I decided to become an Econ major. His class does require a good chunk of time outside of class, but his grading is fair, and I managed to obtain an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is lecture heavy!!! If you show up and pay attention, you will be fine. He is always willing to hold extra office hours to help you understand the material.
Took summer microeconomics with him and found him to be a very good teacher. Lectures are long, but he makes them as interesting as he can
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fun, engaging professor who has a passion for economics and conveys that well. I screwed up on the final exam, so that was why I got a B, but overall, it is a fairly easy class. Pay attention during his lectures and do the assigned homework. He is easily accessible- take advantage of that. Great guy in general, you'll want to be friends with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance wasnt mandatory but he gave extra credit for showing up. Gave really good examples to explain the topics covered in the textbook

He was a pretty cool guy who always had his slides posted online to go over again. I didn't always pay attention in his classes but the course was easy enough that just going over the online homeworks again was usually enough to be prepared for a quiz. The finals took more studying but not a really considerable amount.

Matt was cool and he really likes Justin Timberlake. He was good at explaining and lecture slides were always posted, but attendance was helpful bc there was extra credit points given if the class had good attendance. The weekly homework helped your grade a lot and helped prepare you for the weekly quizzes in class. Barely any tests though (2).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I love Professor Oliver despite the fact that I am not interested in the course (environmental econ). He's great. 2 exams, which he gives the possible essay questions for them a month prior. About 6 HWs. One group paper that is a pain, but given the entirety of the course, not too bad. Easy A.

The way Oliver's course worked, at least for ECON2106 in the summer, attendance wasn't mandatory, but there were benefits that came with attending lecture every day. He isn't as strict as he will seem from the syllabus, and in class he is actually very fun. He likes to talk about his family, but he doesn't get so off track that he forgets to teach.

Your grade is just homework, weekly quizzes, the midterm, and the final, so make sure to do the homework because it boosts your grade up. Overall, the class wasn't hard, but the midterm was a good bit tougher than the final. His lectures were interesting at the beginning when the material was easy. As the material got harder, the book was necessary
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The only reason you need the textbook is for the online access code for the homework. The best part is attendance is not mandatory - especially if you took AP Microeconomics before this class. I didn't attend a single class and still made an A. Just make sure you do the homework to review, and read his PowerPoints that are online and you'll do fine

Dr. Oliver is great! Econ has always been hard for me, but Dr. Oliver does a great job of explaining everything. He's also a funny guy and inserts jokes in between his lectures to make the hour and half class not so brutal. Makes it clear what it takes to get a good grade in his class and even says he gives out a lot of As. Attendance is mandatory.
Great professor. Tests are similar to homework and lectures are insightful. Very nice attitude toward teaching as well.

Dr. Oliver was a great teacher! Although the lectures aren't mandatory, definitely go to them. He'll sometimes give out easy extra credit during class and tell you what to memorize for the test. He does go off on rants sometimes (mainly about politics) but I found them pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very enjoyable professor. He teaches what he loves and he does it well. It's possible to skip lectures and pass but don't do it. He gives extra credit to those who show up regularly. Left-leaning but respectful to all views (I am conservative and I was fine). Does not curve. 9.5/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Funny guy, fair grader. Drops a lot of quizzes and homeworks and stuff. Super liberal and goes on a lot of rants.
Lectures are useless but the class is very easy.  He preaches about politics a lot, so steer clear if you find that annoying.

Professor Oliver is engaging during lectures and passionate about his field and wants his students to feel the same. He was available to talk to and ask questions even during non-office hours. He was a fair grader and all grading assessments were fair as well. You generally knew what to expect. Don't buy the textbook, just the online access.

Super clear about how to get an A. His lectures are pretty good. I was able to fully concentrate  around 85-90% of time. He gave my class 2 pts & 4 pts for the midterm & final respectively. He drops the lowest quiz grade & several homework grades. As long as you study & do the online practice problems, you good. (Don't buy book, it's all online.)
He is a very good professor, and really knows the material. Even of you can't make his set office hours, he is usually able to make time for you.

Super easy class. Attendance checks are random, easy quizzes every friday, and he is super clear about what you need to know to do well on the tests. Not much homework. He is super passionate about economics and will answer any questions you have. Easy A if you study. Would highly recommend

Took this class for the chili pepper. Update: he doesn't deserve the chili.  But seriously, if you go to class and pay attention, you'll be fine and won't need the book. He's a cool guy, definitely loves Econ, but didn't make me love the subject or anything.

I loved Professor Oliver! He used to be in a band and has a ton of tattoos and an overall awesome personality. He really knows his stuff with Econ, and teaches with powerpoint slides that he posts online. If you go to class (occasional attendance checks) and study the power points, you will do just fine. Also gives weekly quizzes, but no big deal.

Took him for environmental econ (small class) and it was the best experience. Minus the research paper, his class was easy and he's super passionate about it. He's always available to help even outside office hours. He also gives you the questions for the midterm and final, so it's nearly impossible to fail. Also has some solid stories
Lectures are useless and there is no order on the board. Math reasoning is far from clear in class but he still requires you to be clear in your demos
DO NOT take this professor. His lectures are so confusing and not helpful for his insanely difficult tests. Only reason I passed was because I had an awesome TA. Nice guy, but bad teacher.
Not a bad professor, had good curves on the tests, but the final is heavily weighted.  Managed to end up with a B in the class after getting As on all the tests and a high B on the final.y
Awful professor, exam was unnecessarily difficult, lectures are pointless. Do not take this class with him.

I took ML 2500 Intro to Cross Cultural Studies. She's super sweet, caring, and enthusiastic. She brings German snacks sometimes. The workload can be a bit more than one would expect if you're taking this for a humanities or free elective requirement. There's a lot of reading, writing, collaboration, and creativity required.

I took ML2500 (NOT GRMN 2001) with Dr. Orich. She was understanding and gave extensions if needed. I thought the class would be a bit easier, but there was A LOT of reading and an assignment every week based off of the readings. There was also a semester long project based off a book. I would avoid taking this class if you just want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: It was a great time being in GRMN 4813 with Dr. Orich. She was always accessible over Teams, and the conversations we had in class were thought-provoking to say the least. Make sure to be engaged in class and you will be fine. She usually assigns a podcast/group assignment, so look out for that. Overall, it was a great semester in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely great professor, very dedicated and very good at teaching German. She is very easy to talk to in and outside of class, and genuinely enjoys teaching. There is a decent amount of homework, but that is to be expected from a language class. She just makes sure you are actually dedicated to learning german.

Dr. Orich was my first German professor at Georgia Tech and she really is an amazing soul. She cares a lot about us as students and takes the time to ask about our lives and what we're doing. 100000% would recommend.
Dr. Orich is a very great teacher and helps the entire class learn. However, be prepared to work very hard in her class.
Really cared about her students and how they are doing both in and outside the classroom. After a while she understands your weakness and focus on improving them. SOLID choice

Took this class over the summer in Metz. 6 lectures, easy attendance quizzes (she'd tell us exactly what to prepare ahead of time and they were j participation based). She's very kind and you could tell that she cared about the wellbeing of her students. Had a local guide as guest lecturer, so you would learn more in-depth! 10/10- super sweet prof!

Very intersting class to learn about Europe and the local city of Metz. The class is her and a guest lecturer with quizzes to check for attendance and one photo essay as the big assignment. Only complaint is that the first part of class can be redundant as she goes over the assignment several times.

Kind of a rant for a course this professor rarely teaches but she for sure has an attitude so be warned. She went on a whole rant to a class of 200 about how we were being disrespectful because we didn't fully understand the implications of the French-German wars/relations? Definitely made some nasty remarks which didn't make anyone respect her.

You don't actually learn all that much from the class content, but you go on awesome adventures with her in 3234 and learn a lot from that.  Including museums, tours, and a free meal, it was an awesome experience that I wouldn't have been able to receive any other way.  Awesome teacher, great feedback, and just genuine and down to Earth.

*GTE class
Started with 3 weeks of class outings around Metz which were all interesting and informative. The outings covered war history in France, Roman history, and a paid-for restaurant meal. After that, the lectures were all pretty boring, but the assignments were all very clear and easy to do well on. 2 free absences allowed. Easy to get an A.

English is a crappy subject in general but she is a great teacher. She respects the fact that most of her students are just taking her class for credit. All you need to do is put a decent effort forward and you will get a good grade.

Professor Orth-Veillon is a really helpful and sweet professor. It's also really easy to get an A in her class with next to no effort. She assigned a lot of reading, but that was balanced out by very few other assignments. Definitely ask her to look over your rough draft before turning it in. She also lets you resubmit essays for a higher grade.

Dr. OV is awesome. She will revise an essay for you and let you resubmit it. The quizzes are easy if you have read, and always have bonus questions. It is easy to get an A even if you put in minimal effort.

Awesome professor! Easy A if you come to class and complete the assignments. She is easy to talk to and extremely helpful. She lets you revise graded essays and resubmit them. I would highly recommend her!

I found the class very easy, and as long as you do your homework and show effort she is very helpful. I recommend when you have an essay giving her a rough draft to revise for you it will help you get a better grade on the final draft. She is very helpful and willing to work with you if you show effort in her class.

Do not take this, professor. Save yourself the trouble. The exams look nothing like the lectures, and then she expects us to pass. not worth it; you'd have to end up teaching yourself everything after class.

Math 2551: Lectures were very hard to understand and very boring. Mainly read off from the textbook without explanations. As a result, l often left the lecture very confused on the content. Tests and homework were also very hard. The only reason I passed was due to the TA, who was absoluetly amazing at explaining all of the topics.

I had her for 2551, her lectures were pretty bad, and it is very hard to understand her. Recitation is very good and kept the class afloat, and the material was not too bad. Reading the textbook is a cheat code.

Do not take this course, I repeat, stay away from it! Dr. Herscovici strictly copies problems from the textbook with little to no explanation as to what she is doing. I found that not going to class and instead of studying the textbook on my own is more effective. I highly recommend that you do not take this course.

This class did not work for me. Dr. Herscovici spends more time deriving the theorems than explaining their use or giving examples. The lectures consists of an exact translation of the book to a notebook that doesnt help at all your learning. You loose so many points for anything in both HW and exams.

She was very kind and did her best to make the class reasonable. The first test was really hard but she gave tons of EC and made the other tests much easier. Lots of HW, but it counted so little that it was barely worth trying on (except it was the best way to learn). I rarely went to lectures, did HWs using the textbook and did well in the class.

The course is lecture-based and has very few assignments so it's very much up to you to attend class. I srsly bombed the first midterm (50%) but the professor is pretty nice and gave out super generous extra credit and incentives so if you put effort into doing the homework (and honestly I only finished like 80% of the hw), you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor was unresponsive outside of class and when she did respond the answers were incredibly unhelpful. The grading criteria is a joke. A homework is assigned every 5 days and they take hours to complete (12-15hrs/week) and they are only worth 5% of the grade. If you do not perform well under time constraint you will struggle to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Orli was an OK professor. She is a good person, and lectures definitely improved by the end of the semester. But, especially at the start of the semester, the class felt very disorganized. Homework is extremely excessive, and exams are rather difficult. Overall, a subpar experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has notes written which are mostly definitions and problems straight from the textbook and just recites them in class. The homework is long and difficult, and it's hard to find resources online to help you learn the material yourself. You're not going to get a good understanding of the content but will just have to figure how to do problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Copies the textbook chapter into her slides, reads through the slides in lecture, that's about it. Lectures are extremely dry and have no intuitive explanations behind anything. Almost never answers student questions fully. Reasonable to get a good grade, near impossible to actually understand the material for the future.

As others have noted, vague unclear assignments. Unclear grading criteria. No opportunities to gain meaningful feedback by asking questions due to fear of violating the honor code. This makes it very difficult to gain insights into concepts that are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very terrible professor especially for the level of quality that is expected from Georgia Tech. Assignments were vaguely cryptic and had multiple inconsistencies. His grading was very stringent and non-transparent.

Professor Orso's unresponsiveness, delegation of non-grading tasks to TA's, and poorly designed grading scheme with vague instructions were concerning. Additionally, the multiple spelling and grammar mistakes in lectures and assignments hindered understanding and overall learning. Improvement is essential to enhance the quality of instruction.

ME 3410 - Thermodynamics Held out until after withdrawal date to give first exam. Did not return any homework until end of semester. Test averages: 45, 60, idk Curves like a sob Not very nurturing, but funny.  Lectures are long and convoluted. Reads directly from slides. Lends historical insight during lecture. STUDY GUIDES ARE IDENTITICAL TO TESTS

He is very heavy on derivations. He treats lectures more like history lessons, and spent three consecutive lectures deriving a single equation, then immediately moved onto deriving another. Very few example problems done in class. Very boring and dry lectures, he reads through slides of derivation steps

At first, a bad impression.  However, after you give him some time, you realize he's actually pretty effective; especially when compared to any other Tech prof's.  In the end, he's more like a grandpa than a teacher.  Also, his tests are very good and effective at giving a thorough evaluation.
A little bit dry but generally reasonable.  Go to his office hours and ask him about his patents - you'll be bored for 20 minutes or so but then he will love you.

Takes a lot of time to prepare his lectures. Always available for office hours. In his other classes he teaches with powerpoint which I do not particularly care for, but he make them available which makes up for it.
Most frustrating experience ever. Semester long project, on top of poorly timed homeworks and tests. Doesn't really teach as much as he "regurgitates"

Don't think his lectures were very easy to follow just because he goes so fast but the class still was fine. HWs are 50 percent of grade and they're very doable. Would recommend taking it with a friend because sometimes the homeworks can be challenging

I had him for Summer '21, after spending a year here I can still say he's one of my favorite professors. The homework questions were original and interesting, and the material was covered very clearly.

The lectures go pretty fast, but he does a lot of examples. He gave a ton of extra credit on Homework (which was 50% of the grade) and on the midterm. He is super nice and approachable! Responds to emails and Piazza quickly. Recorded lectures.
An amazing professor who is always ready to help. His lectures are pretty amazing as well and his homework isn't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very Understanding professor, grades fairly, gives extra credit. Would take again!

The class was very basic and oriented around the textbook. I personally didn't like the professor that much as she called someone out for not doing hw during the add/ drop week, which I thought was unnecessary since we were all still deciding what classes to keep. She'd treat you like you know German already so just be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She gives out a study guide before every test and quiz, so you know what you need to know in order to do well. She does a lot of out-loud activities in front of the class, and she won't hesitate to make an example out of you (not that it makes the class any less enjoyable). She also tells stories often that are really easy to follow along to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Frau Oswalt comes off a bit strict and tough, but she's really funny and a great teacher. There is a lot of memorization and you need to do the homework before class. The class was an easy A though and it was pretty fun. Tests and quizzes are also easy if you read the checklists and pay attention in class.

She has a "hard workreach your goals" mentality. Her life is very interesting, and she tells stories. I just wish we had more time to hear more. She's funny and intimidating. I really appreciated her class and would definitely take her again. She tells you exactly what will be on the tests and quizzes. She calls on everybody, so be ready
Really cares about students' learning experience. Preparedness for class and class participation are crucial. lots of homework, but you will learn German. overall a great professor

She is a great professor. Participation is very important because she will randomly call on students. Ateendence is also imprtant. I missed one class and I felt so behind. The textbook is used in every class besides test days. She is not the easiest professor but she is very helpful. I can definitely say my German has improved.

She is a very good teacher and cares about each student. This is one of the few classes I actually look forward to. Regular homework, essays, quizzes and tests are assigned, however this is necessary to learn the language.

Her class is very easy. The homework was mandatory but helps you out in the long-run. She is very lenient when it comes to make-up exams/ quizzes. She is very nice and very concerned about your grade. I highly recommend taking her if you need a humanities elective.

I came in having not really cared about German to actually enjoying it and understanding it after taking her class. It's a lot of work and very tough. I will get a B in there having worked really hard, but the fruits of my labor are my understanding and my ability to use German outside of the classroom, not necessarily my grade.

The class is very basic. If you study, you will do well. She teaches the language with a strict focus on the textbook. Homework workbook pages are mandatory and a hassle..There is one test and one quiz per chapter. We also did two short presentations about relevant topics of our choice in german which accounts for a speech grade. Class was akward
She seemed strict at first, but she's a great teacher.
Pushes hard, but you are so much better off for it - she's awesome, and very easy on the eyes, which is a plus.
She was a good teacher and was lenient about grades. She may seem tough at first but she is a really good teacher and her class is easy.
Explains well. Makes class fun and exciting. You have to work hard, but you can make a good grade if you do the work.
Amazing professor! He's very open to questions and very responsive, and his tests and quizzes are fair.

I took him for CS 4001, which is an ethics class, so this might not apply to his engineering classes, but he was great. Lectures were fun and very engaging. He made his expectations for tests and assignments very clear. Great class.

he is a very good professor. he is good at explaining the concepts and clearing doubts. his tests are completely based on what he goes over in class and the papers on the ECE 2030 website.he is excellent
Great, engaging professor. Gives feedback on assignments and you have the option to improve two out of four major assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is more time-consuming that a lot of other classes because of the readings and assignments, but the material fits in well with the course topic.  Professor Cantrell is generally nice but the class requires a lot of work to be put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: More had an issue with the man-splainy-ness of the books we read. Hated nearly every book. BUT, teacher did a good job of putting content we learned in context of modern politics and news events.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic about the class topic. Be prepared to participate in discussions. Gives weekly reading quizzes that are very easy. Majority of the grade comes from assignments which will be completed outside of class, mostly in groupwork. Fair grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Cantrell is one of the better ENGL 1102 Profs out there. His readings are long and sometimes dull, but he directs discussions well, and creates an engaging class environment. Projects can be tricky, but if you go into office hours he will help you out really well. Pretty easy grader; put in decent effort and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cantrell is a solid choice for 1101. You'll do a lot of reading (100 pages a night) but a quick skim will get you through. He's a fairly easy grader, so if you can deal with a boring class topic, you can get an A.

Dr. Cantrell is a good teacher. He understands that this is a Tech school and no one is here to be an English scholar. He makes the class interesting with good readings and lots of technological projects. Not too many essays. Had him for 2 semesters. Not difficult as long as you participate and read occasionally. Lots of reading though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Cantrell is a good professor. His projects are challenging because they aren't typical English assignments, but they are fun. Classes are not super exciting, mostly small group discussion. However, Dr. Cantrell is really funny and likes to keep things interesting. Not an easy A, but not a harsh grader either.

There's a lot of reading, but it's actually quite interesting, and he's not nitpicky and only cares about (and quizzes on) the main points. His projects are a bit long, he allows you to revise if you do bad. REALLY helpful during office hours. Very caring overall, very interesting topics, and a great prof overall. Would recommend anyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I came into the class with a weak foundation in English. I spoke to him about it and that was the best talk ever. Not only have I matured in English, I have also gained some critical thinking skills. You read a lot, yes. But this is an English class. I suggest picking a class in which you would read, and learn useful skills applicable outside class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cantrell assigns a LOT of reading (200 - 300 pages / week) and expects you to have it finished. However, you can skim through the reading and finish around 100 pages in 2 hours and still actually learn the content.  However, this is still significantly more work than any other English teacher. On the plus side, he does give out good grades.
Otte is a great professor for 2211, given that I already took AP Physics C: Mechanics, in high school.  He has good lectures and demonstrations, solid prof nothing to complain about.

Great teacher overall, however, he likes to take most of the lectures deriving equations mathematically. Which is not the learning style for me. Great guys, funny, easygoing, passionate, show you cool demos.
Okay lecturer, but difficult tests.

Physics 1 prof DOES NOT MATTER. We all have the same tests. Lectures did not help much and were not very organized. I learned the course by looking at aliceas lecture slides which are amazing. As for Otte, he's funny and engaging but not very good lectures, I stopped going after first month. Grading for tests is extremely lenient you should be fine

Very mid professor overall. His lectures were ok, they didn't really teach you the material they were just supplementary. Overall the recorded lectures from the head prof Dr. Alicea-Munoz and the weekly preview videos were much more helpful than his lectures. He was pretty nice tho if you went to office hours ever.

Professor Otte is very knowledgeable about physics and I liked when he talked about his research a bit during lecture. He is also very encouraging about coming to office hours and asking questions during class. His lectures are not bad, but I thought Dr. Alicea was better at explaining so I recommend watching her lecture recordings.

Incredibly boring and seems incapable of putting together a clear powerpoint presentation. In theory covers everything you need to know but is very fond of longwinded in class examples. Is probably nice and cares about students but I learned very little from him. Watch Dr. Alicea lectures and you're fine.

He's a solid professor but he sometime does too much. Like he talks about advanced physics topics when it's not necessary. No matter what professor you decide to take, you will end up watching Alicias lecture videos so it doesn't really matter. He's funny though I'll give him that.

This class is very difficult and very time consuming, but Otte does a great job explaining concepts and working through problems. If you need extra help he is always willing to spend extra time on his students, and his jokes were good. I would still try to get modern over classical, but Otte does a great job for the curriculum he's forced to teach.

Very funny guy & he cares about his students. His lectures are entertaining, and attendance is on point solutions. There's Extra Credit for doing homework early. 4 midterms and a final. First few test are usually curved. Very time consuming, but an A is possible. Do the practice tests before the midterms! Very accessible during office hours.

This class is incredibly difficult to pass if you don't have previous physics knowledge. During his lectures, Otte simply goes through example problems without explaining the concepts behind them. I spent about 60% of my time on this class and it was incredibly frustrating teaching myself all these concepts that he should've done.

Class itself is very difficult but I believe Otte did a good job with how fast paced and heavy the class is. Taking notes inside and outside class is a must. Otte always made time to meet with me when I was struggling (like failing every exam struggling) so dont be afraid to ask for his help because he truly does care.

Professor Otte is a very nice person and a decent lecturer. He can keep things fairly interesting and I enjoyed taking his class. It is important that you keep up with the homework, they play it off as being optional in the beginning but it will absolutely make a letter grade difference in the long run. The class itself is very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a hard class and very time consuming, but that's physics. For sure go to office hours because Dr. Otte is very patient and helpful. It may not always seem like it in lectures be he cares a lot about his students, especially if you show that you care about the course.

To preface, I am a 4th-year CS major who is taking this class at the very end before I graduate. Taking that into perspective, if I took this class as a first or second year, I would admit that it would be very difficult. However, after taking similar yet harder classes, this is pretty much the same level of difficulty as upper-level courses.
Hard class and harder prof
Made class impossible if you haven't take physics c in high school
Avoid at all costs. Unclear lectures and you are teaching yourself through the textbook. He just goes over examples in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I kind of feel sorry for him. He feels like an average teacher to me, except I hated the for-credit in-class questions and the occasional remarks about how he feels like he's not a good teacher (because it feels a little bit true).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Out of the available PHYS 2211 professors, Otte was the best. His humor makes the class a little more tolerable, he does care about the students, but the lectures aren't the most helpful. Far too much homework, and the exams are extremely hard and don't align with previous semesters exams. If you can, skip classical all together and take modern.
At all costs do not take Professor Otte.  Take modern physics and make your life infinitely better, or if you have to do classical, take a different professor.

The lectures, lab, homework, and tests in this class never seemed to align. They were always in different content at any given time. The lectures themselves were scattered and hit/miss. You get credit for attending lectures IF you answer TRICK questions BEFORE he goes over them. Can make up for it with other grades. Hard tests made by other teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He clearly cares about the subject and his students, but he's not the best lecturer. I've been skipping because I learn way more from the textbook and Mastering Physics. In class, he just does a lot of examples and his sense of humor is a little condescending, idk why people get a kick out of it. Lots of homework, hard tests.

I started this class with physics as my favorite subject, and after taking it with Dr.Otte he has ruined my passion for physics. Dr.Otte's lectures are completely useless, he often goes on rants that are unhelpful and unrelated to the topic we are learning. Be prepared to teach yourself. He is also rude to his students when the get questions wrong.

Otte consistently fails to deliver concepts in a way that is understandable to students. He uses random experiments that usually do not work as intended and reads from a sheet he does not explain. The class wouldn't be so bad if attendance wasn't mandatory as the textbook and homework are helpful, but required attendance makes the class a pain.

This class would be much more effective if less homework was given and attendance was not mandatory! I'm not fully there during the lectures many times and having recorded lectures would greatly boost my ability to concentrate if need be.

Professor Otte is likely one of the worst professors at Tech. As a hardworking student, you can expect 8 hours per week of homework and to be unprepared for the biweekly exams. His lectures are undedicated to learning and he often spends time laughing at wrong answers. He is rude to students asking for regrades. If you can, avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is hard. Professor Otte is funny and he cares for his students, but the tests are super hard and the resources available to students don't prepare you at all. Otte tries to make the lectures interesting with experiments, but this takes time away from explaining things that could help solve problems for the tests. Caused lots of stress.

He is a very good professor that explains concepts clearly. He is also very fair in grading. The only bad thing is that he will do a lot of experiments that take up a lot of time, when the time would be better spent doing practice problems. I would be prepared to read the textbook because he does not cover all the concepts in class.

Otte is a superb lecturer with subtle humor, and he's flexible not only about attendance but also scheduling--he'll push an exam back if you ask him and nobody objects. He expects you to know the math for the homework (straight from book), but exams are basically conceptual in nature. Expect to write paragraphs, not proofs.
He's a good professor and has a good sense of humor. He brought in his daughter one day for the lecture concerning the conservation of angular momentum. It was great

Otte is a great CLASSICAL Physics professor. He knows what he's doing, keeps the style of the class from getting to the condescending lectures that make you just want to skip, and is open to help students if they try to ask questions. Also, tests are matched between classes, so he gives the same tests as any other Physics 1 prof.

With 2211, the tests don't depend on your prof, so who you take doesn't make a huge difference. I would say Otte is pretty entertaining, but not the greatest at explaining. The book is helpful, the practice tests are essential. The time you need to invest for an A depends on who you are, but I studied a lot less than the other reviewer and got an A

It is an extremely difficult course. That said, it isn't too unfair (like Chem1310). I studied for 5 days straight before a test for 10 hours a day. I got a 100 on that test (the only 100!). So even if it's completely unreasonable how much work is required, it is possible. The following test I only studied for 15 hours total, so I got ~83.

Good Teacher, good class. Only qualm I have is that there's one midterm which is worth a significant portion of your grade, so you NEED to do well on it. Studying for it though isn't too hard, just make a study guide for the outlined material (ALL OF IT) and you should be ok. Overall though, an interesting class, with a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: MGT 6059 - Emerging Technologies was one of the best courses I ever took; and it was indeed because of the way the professor taught it. He is an inspirational figure when it comes to teaching methodology and creates immersive classroom experience and discusses latest & relevant case studies which really gets you hooked.

Professor Overby was a great teacher and I really enjoyed Emerging Tech with him. He does an excellent job of educating the class on technological and market trends and is very knowledgeable on the material. Lectures can sometimes get a little slow, but ones with debate-style discussions are really interesting. Talking in class really helps!
Professor Overby is an amazing professor and an even better lecturer. His class is highly relevant to modern technology and trends. Highly, highly recommend taking one of his classes.
Not a great lecturer.
During class all he did was read from his slide deck, which was made up of screenshots of the free online textbook. I was so confused throughout the entire semester.

Professor Ozdemir is very smart, so he sometimes skips steps. But if you ask him to explain a step, he will do it well. He's quiet, so sit near the front. The homework can be challenging and is assigned weekly, but he's willing to extend the deadline if needed. Lectures are important and seem to include material not in the textbook, so don't skip.

Confusing lesson structure where he only explained the new content after doing examples, though when he eventually got to his explanation it was always incomprehensible. Take someone else.

The textbook is online/free and was the only reason I knew what was going on. You are better off teaching yourself.
Really just not a great lecturer. Especially for a class like this.

I went to his lectures the first weeks but they were terrible. It seemed as if he didn't know the content and would never answer questions in a straightforward manner. I ended up relying heavily on the book and going to another professor's lectures. If you can't find another teacher don't take this class or make sure you can go to another lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ozdemir tried to teach, but his online lectures were incomprehensible and his physical ones were bland and went too fast. Watch another professors lectures if youre stuck with him (Jankowski or Margalit)
You're screwed. Stick to the book and find a tutor fast.

I feel really bad giving Dr. Ozdemir this poor of a rating because he seems like a really nice person, but he obviously doesn't know how to teach. He doesn't explain concepts in a comprehendible way, and if it weren't for my awesome TA, I don't know how I would have survived this class. If you do take his class, expect to teach yourself everything.

Doesn't teach well. Learn more from the textbook or you will suffer on the quizzes and exams. Rely on other material/professors if you can. If you can, take a better prof. The tests are not made by him and are centralized, so you will suffer from bad teaching.
Super smart and nice guy, but often struggles to get his point across.

Professor Ozdemir seemed like a really nice person, but it was really difficult to understand the content in his lectures. Half-way through the semester, I ended up just watching the lectures from another professor.

Professor Ozdemir is a super nice guy and knows his stuff. He struggles sometimes getting his point across but he was thrown into an unfortunate situation with this semester being his first teaching and it being all online. Always accessible and responds quickly (much better one on one). Book is super good, if you read and do practice youre good..

I would highly suggest preferencing other teachers over him. Unable to communicate sufficiently. I remember for our first quiz, this professor never even told us we had a quiz. Like he never mentioned there was a quiz or what it was over. He cannot explain concepts at all and is very boring. Take somee one else trust me
horrible job explaining conpects and lectures are as boring as they come. Take any other professor
Professor Padukka is incredibly nice and cares about her students. However, her teaching style isn't super engaging, and you would probably be better served watching Alicea's lectures.

Phys 2211 is very hard  (at least for me) and considered a weed out still but Dr. Padukka truly cares about her students and wants you to pass. Her office hours are helpful and she will even ask in lecture of hundreds of students how she can improve her teaching to help students to better on tests

The availability of Padukka was frankly incredible. The semester I took her, she had a zoom meeting you could join that ran along side the in person lecture. Padukka lectures were also very good. She covered content at a good pace and always allowed opportunities to ask questions. Always willing to help students, even if they needed extra help.

Great lecturer, kind, and always ready to answer any questions. She also streams her lectures if you can't (or don't want to) be there. Make sure to look at the GPS and homework when studying for exams

Dr. Padukka is such a kind and caring professor. Really makes an effort to help her students understand the material. Also understands physics really well! Do the homework and GPS problems (just do as many practice problems as you can), they really help with the exams.

Pretty straight forward physics class. She is absolutely amazing and super kind. Attendance is part of bucket points so you don't have to show up. Notes for her section and all other sections are posted online. Labs are super annoying, but online and peer graded. Also pretty good late policy.

Super nice! :) She answers all the questions students have in class or during office hours and even offered extra supplemental classes for those who have never done physics before. She does go through problems super fast, sometimes it was hard to keep up. All lectures are streamed online, but it's physics, so go to class or you'll fall behind.
Nice professor, pretty approachable if you have questions during/after lecture and lectures are filled with examples. Lectures are also streamed and uploaded online.

She's very kind and lectures are straightforward and full of examples. If you've taken physics in high school (algebra based even) this class is a breeze. Attendance can count towards bucket points but isn't required to get full credit in the category. Lectures are streamed online so you don't have to go in person.

Padukka is a great lecturer! She is good at explaining concepts and providing examples; however, the class is usually behind and we hardly finished each topic from every lecture. With that being said, she really cares about the success of students and goes out of her way to help!

Physics is notoriously difficult at GaTech. However, Padukka did give some good detailed examples in the lecture that helped greatly. The rating I gave is not her fault, but the fault of how this course is set up. I am simply not a fan.

Very good. Accessible, lectures are broadcasted recorded and the lecture notes are posted after every lesson, and approaches us like she actually wants us to do well in the class. All you can really ask for to be honest
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: streams her lectures so her lectures are super accessible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. I'm not great at physics but she made this class much better. She was always happy to answer questions after class and clearly cares about her students. Her lectures are also recorded in case you can't go.

Professor Padukka has immense respect for her student's. She is always willing to answer questions and makes sure that the lecture material is understood without spending too much time on one topic from the goals of that day. Yes physics is hard, but she did her job well and made it bearable.

unorganized + needs a writing class since he's bad at writing coherently and without grammatical/phrasal errors making it harder to answer basic questions. When questions arise during exams, he wastes precious time by simply reading the question again. I also have eyes. That is unhelpful.

He is approachable one-on-one outside of class, but grading is very strict and can feel snarky. Assignments often lack clear guidance, yet points are deducted for minor errors like spelling. The class may feel discouraging, but students can improve by adapting to his expectations.
Snarky and rude. Picky comments and feedback on work. Could/should have shown more kindness towards students. Don't take his class if you're looking for respect.

Excellent professor and a very easy class. Take-home exams were all very straightforward and had questions directly from the slides. 

The course content didn't especially interest me sometimes, but Professor Perullo presented it in a cool way every time I went to class.

Jerry is one of the most knowledgeable people in the space of Enterprise Cyber, and it shows through his class. It is a fun, easy class where you will learn a lot, and, if you want, you can thoroughly engage in conversation in class or with the live panels. The tests are not too bad, just few questions making up a good portion of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly the easiest class I have ever taken, but also surprisingly high quality. Kinda wish I went to more than just the first lecture – you'll get out of this class what you put in. He's a great speaker and a chill guy. Budget about 10 hours in the semester for an A.

Knows a lot about cybersecurity in industry. Creates a course that is manageable along with 3 other hard CS courses, which is good for MS CS. He takes time to engage with students, and his class is well structured. Tests were open note open book and had ample time to complete.

Prof.Perullo is an amazing lecturer and cares about students. The class (now it has a new course number CS 6239) is fairly easy. Participation is required, but discussion on the course slack channel also counts as attendance. Overall a great course if you are interested in how cybersecurity is handled in industry.

This class gives an overview on Cybersecurity Risk Management in enterprises. It's a pretty easy class with only 3 open note exams and 2 case studies for MS students. The professor's lectures are interesting if you're into cybersecurity. Good class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Though attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are so fun that it makes me want to attend voluntarily. Super flexible with grading and assignments. Super funny also.

pay attention to the lectures because virtually all of the exams are based solely on the lectures - his powerpoints are a little confusing to follow. exams are very easy (open note, not proctored, at home). you can tell he's very passionate about his work and psychology which is refreshing for a college course. very nice and easy to talk to.

Dr. V. was very caring and genuinely wanted us to learn how to meditate and practice mindfulness. The class was very easy going. Lectures consisted of meditation and learning about different techniques. Assignments included weekly reflections, a term paper, and two open-note exams. He also offers extra credit and is very responsive via email.

Verhaegen is an excellent lecturer who loves the subject and has really fun lectures. The class is dead easy: do your diary every week (takes 5 minutes), do your experiment credit for free points, and the tests are open internet, async and unproctored, so good luck NOT getting an A. Extremely easy, extremely fun, highly, highly recommend him.

Dr. Verheghen was a breath of fresh air among the profs I've had so far, every lecture was engaging and funny, I would go for the enjoyment of it. He incorporates activities that actually help teach the topics learned. Tests are very straightforward and applys the concepts from lecture.

Professor Verhaeghen is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. He has a kind and welcoming personality, his class is designed to encourage participation and minimize stress while still being incredibly educational, and I always looked forward to attending his lectures. He very clearly cares about his students and loves what he does.
Dr. Verhaeghen is a wonderful professor who makes his content very interesting and very evidently cares about students. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to his lectures are definitely worth it

Dr. Verhaeghen is one of the coolest professors I've ever had. He has very interesting lectures and makes you want to go to class. Exams are online and open note and there are only 2 exams and a final paper that is reflection based. As long as you participate and show effort, you can do well in his class.
Dr. Verhaeghen clearly loves what he does and has a fun time lecturing and including personal tangents. He is super kind on grading and if you just do the work you'll do well.

Dr. Verhaeghen is very caring and interesting as a professor. He always apologizes for possibly mispronouncing my name but he actually reads it right. He uses fun anecdotes and activities to make the lectures engaging and helps us focus even if its remote. Would definitely take his class again if there were options.

Excellent, funny professor that does his best to make online lectures engaging. Very knowledgeable on the topics discussed and usually has anecdotes to tie into lecture topics. Definitely wants his students to succeed and comes off as very caring. I took away a lot from this class and would take him as a professor again if possible.
Dr. Verhaeghen made each lecture fabulous to attend, and he managed the task of making online lectures with no one to bounce off of engaging. I was always excited to learn in his class.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a great professor and fantastic person. You get a lot more out of the class if you attend lectures, and he makes psychology really accessible. I am sad that I didn't take a course with him earlier.

Probably one of the coolest people I have ever gotten to meet. Incredibly laid back - just wants you to understand the material and have a good time. He is one of my favorite lecturers but is extremely humble. The tests are good at measuring your understanding and there's few unnecessary assignments. Would take him for every class ever

Dr. Verhaeghen is so kind and caring about his students. He understands how stressful Tech is and does his best to structure his class to alleviate that stress. If you put in the work, you will get an A!

No textbook is used for this course and exams are entirely based on lecture/slides. This can be a bit on an adjustment if you have more of a reading-based learning style, but Dr. V is a really talented and engaging lecturer.

Dr. Verhaeghen is so caring about his students and about psychology itself. There's no textbook for his class - it's all based on his lectures, so you gotta go. But he's a super engaging lecturer. Tons of real-world examples about psych, and occasionally walks us through an experiment on ourselves. Tests are fair and come straight from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful and funny teacher, really cares about his students and always has something interesting to share.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a sweetheart and is very knowledgable about psychology. He is good at lecturing but his powerpoints are so long (like 200+ slides) which makes them really hard to go through. Grade is mostly comprised of 3 exams w/ essays and a final project; exams are somewhat challenging & require application of concepts (some stuff not in ppt)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3012 Intro to Cognitive Psych - Very knowledgeable, approachable, down to earth professor - Lectures are amazing, very engaging and lots of fun demos! -He cares about students (he was always checking in on us during the coronavirus transition to online), allows a double-sided crib sheet for exams to reduce anxiety
He is amazing !

Verhaegen is very funny. Most of the lecture time is spent telling stories, most are funny, a few aren't. The class is graded on 3 midterms and a final (1101). Tests are just fine if you attend lecture and read your notes the night before

I took his Mindfulness and Meditation GT1000 and it was one of the best choices I made first semester. He is extremely caring, knowledgable, and a really cool guy. I would definitely recommend him for this class. If you show up with and open mind and participate, you are basically guaranteed an A.
Really great funny guy I always forget to do my diary entry though because it's due saturday night.

enjoyed lectures -- he's very funny (but a little quiet sometimes) basically only grades are weekly diary (free 100%), tests, and end of semester project study slides and go to class  tests will be very easy for you
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pay attention during class and take notes. Tests are very easy. Enjoy the class and you'll be fine. Don't forget to do your weekly journal entries (basically a guaranteed 100% in the gradebook).

The course material is fascinating, but Dr. Verhaeghen brings even more fun to the lecture with his quirky personality. Just show up to lecture and do your crib sheet, and you'll be set for the tests.

Dr. Verhaeghen is a very sweet man who wants to make sure his students learn. His lectures can be pretty boring. His powerpoints are slightly annoying, they don't have much "structure" so they can be hard to follow when reviewing. Tests can be detailed sometimes.  He allows crib sheets for every single test, and they could be front-and-back.

Awesome professor who is extremely enthusiastic and understanding. The lectures were always fascinating. The class wasn't extremely demanding, you didn't have to write thousands of papers; although the tests did cover a lot of material. Really enjoyed this professor.
This professor is awesome! His lectures are always so interesting and he makes complex content seem so simple! I definitely want him as a professor again!

Agree with below- project heavy, participation heavy, and an overall great class. His experience in the field makes the classes and content that much more engaging. It is difficult, but this course will definitely teach you about privacy tech policy law.

Actually took 4725 -- class was informative and I loved Swire as a professor. Project descriptions are ambiguous and he just expects you to infer, but there are Q & A's and office hours.. take full advantage. Do not assume you know. Grades things personally which I appreciate, strict grader. I'd recommend, great incredibly accomplished professor.

Swire is an amazing professor. He'll conduct weekly discussions about cyber security and explain in ways where anyone can understand. Due to his status, he was able to give valuable insight, and bring top of the line professionals to give the class insight into the working world. You will improve on communication and research. Grading is tough.

Great presenter. Extremely knowledgeable about the material and quite funny. Shines extra bright during Q&A. Can recommend any class with him. The staff grades pretty tough on the fairly ambiguous projects. One point off for giving advices in direct conflict with other TAs or instructors several times during the semester.

Prof. Swire has to be one of the best Professors I have seen at Georgia Tech. This is the one man that can make policy interesting to tech folks at 9 PM on Monday and Tuesday nights. During your time at Tech, if you get a chance to listen to Prof. Swire deliver ANY lecture, make sure you attend it.

Prof. Swire is an extraordinary lecturer. He is very engaging, knowledgeable, and well-spoken. He's also great at explaining difficult concepts. This class is project-heavy, and the grading criteria are not always clear. However, being able to learn about data privacy from him is a very rewarding experience. You will learn so much from this course.

Dr. Swire's video lectures are some of the best overviews of privacy policy I've seen yet. He literally wrote the book for IAPP. Although he only has two tests the entire semester, they are worth a MASSIVE amount of your grade. Otherwise, his class was pretty easy. The other assignments were quarter page summaries of something you read weekly.

I took him for LMC 2700 the course overall is okay he did not teach us how to use p5.js it was mainly the two TA that "taught" us how to code and graded everything. Didn't really felt like a professor but he comes to class sometimes to explain things. Overall, chill professor and taught us his career journey. Mainly a self-learn course java coding.

Expected to hammer down on visual design fundamentals, instead got dragged along on his DIY ink plotter passion project. Grading was inconsistent with no explanation, AI was overly-encouraged. Phelps was passive aggressive toward quieter students. I don't usually review profs, but not what was advertised at all and would not recommend anyone take.

I loved this class! It can be difficult at times (especially if you have no prior experience w/ Adobe Suite) but he's very kind & accommodating and gives great feedback. You have a project due every 2-ish weeks at the beginning of the semester & then more often towards the end, but it's very doable as long as you stay on top of things.

i genuinely love him, he gives the best feedback and I've genuinely seen how my work reflects my progress as I learn and take his feedback into account. however, i felt extremely unprepared at times because i didn't come into class knowing how to use the adobe design suite already. the tutorials take hours each week, so i ended up winging it.

Nice guy, passionate & knowledgable, assigns open-ended projects. He won't teach you how to use the software, so watch the optional videos if you aren't versed w/ it. What drove me crazy is that he'd ALWAYS go overtime on critique days. After a while it seemed like he j didn't have respect/awareness for our time. I'm ADHD too but figure it out man.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: such a nice, approachable guy and gives the best feedback on assignments. he can come across as picky, but no project is perfect and you can tell he genuinely cares about wanting our work to be the best it can be. super accessible outside of class, workload is relatively chill, and pretty open-ended final project. highly recommend !!

Had an awesome time in his class. You won't learn how to use the tools and software but you will learn how those tools will help you make compelling work. Very personable guy and his critiques definitely help you get to a more refined finished product which overall helps your grade in future projects. The work makes great portfolio pieces as well.

(Taking during COVID-19 Spring 2021.) Great professor but an aríst to say the least. Things must live up to a certain expectation. Also, do not take this class with the intention of learning Adobe products. He's teaching methods and background, not software. Know them before coming in and work SUPER HARD on every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had no experience with design software, so for the first half of the class the learning curve is steep. You complete a project every couple of weeks using various Adobe programs -- be prepared for him to roast them in class. If you bust your butt watching LYNDA tutorials and figuring out the software, you should get some good portfolio pieces.
His lectures are very boring, and he doesnt upload any content whatsoever onto canvas so it is very hard to continue learning outside of the classroom

First test wasn't too bad, but the class kind of bombed it, so he made the second test and final so much easier with extra credit. He gave out so much extra credit, so as long as you go to class and somewhat understand physics 1, you'll probably be fine.

Prof. Suryanaryana is a really solid professor. it's only my first sem. at Tech and considering he's my only real "engineering" class take this with a grain of salt. As other's have said, he goes off of textbooks, but doesn't post his lectures online: VERY lenient grader on tests, and utilize TA for hw's cuz its free 25%, do textbook problems

If you understand his lectures, you will do fine on his tests. The homeworks are the hardest part but only because you can work with other people. Clear lectures, and approachable guy if you ever need anything clarified.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Suryanarayana was my best professor this semester. Lectures were clear and helpful; I always left feeling like I had learned a lot. Some of the homework questions were a little tricky, but the tests were much less difficult. Overall, I would definitely recommend taking Dr. Suryanarayana for statics; he is a very effective professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are tough and will take your ego down a notch. Very kind and helpful and is open to advice from students. Difficult content but a very effective teacher. Overall best class I've had at Tech in terms of how effective he is.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Skip lectures if you want. Just study textbook or notes you will be fine. Grading will be very easy. Professor will make the final easy if he sees everyone struggling in the class. HW are directly from TB.

He is an average professor to have while online. You could honestly get through the class and not learn anything since the lectures were dry and boring, homeworks are straight from the textbook and the tests are curved. Would have preferred a more engaging teacher. Minimal effort will probably get you a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches straight out of the textbook. So lectures aren't that great or helpful. But he does grade pretty fairly in my opinion, he bases it on the average of the class with each test. Minimal effort can get you a B.

His lectures are entirely from the textbook, and the examples he does in class are the ones already solved in the book. Don't really need to go to class. Homework is straight out of the book. Tests are not too bad if you understand the examples and homework problems. Final exam was much harder than any test. WARNING: he grades on a bell curve.
Absolutely amazing professor! Very understanding and available outside class, best physics 1 professor imo

Professor Yunker is absolute AMAZING. He is one of the best physics professors I have ever had. His lectures are super informative and he is a very easy person to ask questions to. He always makes his lectures very engaging and clearly wants his students to thrive.

I'm a CS major who had to take physics to graduate. I hate physics in general, but Prof. Yunker made it interesting and fun. He's a very engaging and interactive professor -- far from monotone. He breaks complex physics topics down into a way that is easy to understand. Overall, just seems like a good guy who wants his students to succeed.

Lectures were great and informational, perhaps a tad repetitive or boring at times, but very easy to understand and with good explanation and interaction with the class. Notes being posted after was also a bonus
Always willing to answer question and take time for his students. Lectures can be a little bit dry but he teaches you exactly what you will need to know for the exam.

Yunker is the goat. He does a great job of answering questions during lecture and also provides an virtual option for lecture. While sometimes he moves a little fast, he makes all of the slideshows available after class for review. The class is hard in itself, but Yunker tries his best to support his students and ensure that they succeed in class.

Dr. Yunker is very nice, he is always on top of the students asking if people have questions. The lecture is given with the same PPT presentation as all other lecturers which is kind of general and just goes by problems. A lot of clicker questions. The TA's usually go over the material more in depth.

All the other reviews have it right. Professor Yunker is so caring and respectful of mental health even. I was really struggling through the class and even though he didn't see the email from the Dean about my situation, he didn't hesitate to give me advice and empathize with me. I almost failed this class but I made it through. Physics II is hard.

I loved Yunker for Modern Physics! I was nervous, especially after struggling in Physics 1 with Murray but Yunker truly cares about his students and is very knowledgable. Just beware that 2 other professors helps write the exams and tend to make it harder than Yunker would like. Yunker wants to help his students thrive, very uncommon in physics.

Professor Yunker is a great person and he had amazing lectures. To do well on the exams do all the practice exams. I expected physics 2 to be hard, but I enjoyed it a lot. If you enjoy physics this is the class for you. I truely loved it.

Prof. Yunker is the teacher to take for Modern PHYS 2! He explains the content really well, is very accessible out of class, and answers all the questions posed to him if time permits (after class, through email, office hours, etc). Yunker also is transparent on what to expect on our exams. Highly-highly recommend him.

Prof Yunker was amazing! He's super accommodating and will take time to sit with you if you ask him to (office hours etc.). PHYS 2212 is always hard, so make sure to do as much extra credit as you can (caps at 10 pts, just attend all lectures and do all hw). The dept was all really nice. Use all the resources they provide and you'll be fine.

This class made me cry often, but that was not Dr. Yunker's fault. His lectures were pretty good (not out of the ordinary, but made it usually worth going), but the class is just pretty hard to get a grasp on and the structure could be improved upon. I recommend Dr. Yunker, but if you can take physics somewhere that isn't GT, you should do that.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Yunker does a good job at managing the class as a whole.  Physics in general has a lot of activities to do, and it can be relatively hard to manage.  Lecture has clicker questions that are graded for participation.  It is pretty difficult to know how well you are doing in the class due to the number of assignments and a lot are peer-reviewed.

Although the material is difficult, he's very caring and will go out of his way to help his students if they are struggling. As long as you do and actually understand the solutions for the homework, GPS problems, and practice exams, you will be fine for the exams.

Professor Yunker is a very funny guy and I really enjoyed his lectures. He often got sidetracked and off topic but I didnt mind since we manage to cover the material anyways. Labs were run by Greco but reasonable. Grading for the class was fairly forgiving and the tests were straightforward (difficult but fair).

Aside from the complicated course structure, prof is a good lecturer and a nice guy in general. Too bad the lectures are mostly useless thanks to prelecture videos, but sometimes they have nice practice problems (which sometimes then show up on tests).

2212 is still super tough, but Professor Yunker is just more proof that the Physics department at Tech is GOATed. Clearly cares that students thoroughly understand the course material, and is open to questions and concerns.

Yunker was super cool. Very funny and a solid professor too. you can tell he really cares about students (hard to do in 500 person class). However the class structure is a bit ridiculous. 6 midterms and a lab every other week doesnt leave much time to not do any physics, however the grading structure is very lenient

Physics 2 is hard no matter who you get, but Yunker definitely tries his best to make it as painless as possible. Always stops to answer questions and makes sure they are explained fully. Cares about his students and is willing to work with them. Overall very genuine guy and down to earth.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: More reasonable on tests than other professors in the physics department

Professor Yunker is honestly one of the most genuine professors out there. He's very empathetic and really cares about how well his students are and do. He's also very helpful if you need anything. Tests could be medium to hard, but I'm not sure if he sets them. At any rate, if you put in the work, watch lectures, do HW, you should do great.
He was great a lecturing and really explained the material well. My advice? Go to office hours and do the HW.

I was terrible at physics in high school, so I definitely thought I wouldn't do well in this class. Luckily, Dr. Yunker is an amazing lecturer and extremely helpful. Thanks to him, I finally understand things that never made sense to me in high school. If you can take Physics with him, absolutely do it.

Yunker is the best modern physics teacher there is at Tech. His lectures are very clear and he sometimes hints on test questions. He's very friendly and keeps a lively attitude during lectures. I use to suck at physics in HS but his lectures allowed me to better understand the concepts and I did better than I would have thought.

One of my favorite professors. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to really get the material. Asking a question isn't intimidating at all because he always says "great question!" Really great with interacting with students and wanting the best for them. I'm glad that he could care for all 200 students in lecture. Really great

Yunker is great at explaining concepts, answering questions, and assessing feedback. However, he uses slides for lectures, which is not a great idea for physics, and there's a crap ton of WebAssign homework (you don't have to do all of it, but you should at least do some). Tests are straightforward and easy (although very conceptual)

Dr. Yunker presents material very effectively. The class takes up a good bit of time, but Yunker makes it much less painless. He does example problems similar to what shows up on exams and is so kind during office hours. He really wants everyone to do well.
Better do all the WebAssign homework if you want to do well. 40ish problems a week. Physics at Tech is hard. Take it elsewhere if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is a very good professor. Watches out for students, good at explaining. Mumbles a little and gets so excited by physics that he gets distracted by other physics, but makes sure students understand information. Very willing to answer questions and help out. Also gives useful hints about what will be on the tests.

Hands down my favorite professor at Tech. He teaches the material extremely well, his lectures aren't boring and are very clear and concise, but beyond his lecturing skills he makes physics fun and genuinely cares about all his students, whether it be their understanding of physics or their mental wellbeing.

My favorite professor at Tech thus far. He's amazingly patient, kind, and cares a lot about his students. His lectures are easy to follow, and tests are exactly as he said they would be. I highly recommend taking him, one of the best decisions I made to take physics I with him!
Teaches the topics very well. If you pay attention, you'll learn a lot.  Even though the exams are not that easy, he makes sure students are prepared before each one. Shows a passion for physics.
Explains the subject matter well, and is good at responding to any questions. He even gave us the exact 8 types of problems that would be on the final, making studying easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sometimes confusing, just look at his examples and the recitations. Textbook helps clear things up though. Generous grader, no hw, you should be fine.

A breeze. He was a little hard to understand in person, but the textbook could typically clear up any confusion. He was also very willing to meet with you. The only grades were quizzes and tests, both of which are very straightforward and sometimes had extra credit. They mimicked recitation exercises or lecture examples. A great non-linear curve
He is not the greatest at explaining things, but he makes the class insanely easy.  Best curve I have ever seen in a course.  Easy tests, all of which contain extra credit.

This had to be the easiest linear class at tech. The midterm averages were generally in the 90s and the final avg. was an 84.4. He uses a non-linear curve that dramatically increases your grade. He is not always the most clear lecturer, but the textbook and recitation were helpful.

Absolutely insane curve, if you attempt each question and get an answer and vaguely know what you are doing, automatic 90+. Lectures are essentially useless besides the examples he does, don't pay attention to theorems or proofs. Attend Recitation, definitely more helpful

Very kind professor at GTL that does his best to make sure his students succeed. His lectures can be a little confusing sometimes but his grading is extremely generous. I highly recommend studying with external resources (i.e textbook and online videos) for assessments, but the exams are all very fair and only cover the material learned in class.
Dr. Benge is my "goat." BAAAAA. He is hilarious and inspirational and caring and he spans everyone's heart.

Loved the class. Wasn't a fan of teaching style at first, but I grew to like it. Not the usual super organized lecture notes; You learn as you go, but I like that. Handwriting isn't unreadable, as other reviews here might suggest. Definitely the best math teacher I've had in a while. If you read this Dr. Benge, thank you!
Best math teacher Ive ever have
