reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Imagine getting up every morning at 8 and go to class and see him scribble hieroglyphics on the board. Well, not exactly hieroglyphics but his handwriting is so bad, you will need to consult every student sitting in your row what some characters on the board are. He is not bad at explanation, but as a note taker his class was hell for me.
I learned a lot from him, and I wish there were more professors like him. He wasn't easy, but I worked for it and it payed off. I would recommend this guy if you really want to learn the material.

I got a 41 on the first test I took in Philip's class and worked hard to get A's on the other tests and got an A in the class. He gives a lot of supplemental homework, which is pretty necessary to succeed in the class. He also posts practice tests which are similar to the exams he gave us. Take advantage of office hours for clarification!

Benge was a great professor! I very much enjoyed his class and sense of humor. He was always willing to re-explain a concept or help you work through a problem. This course was dependent on your work ethic. Supplemental hw is major. I also found office hours (Benge's and TA's) and other tutoring sources to help tremendously.

Tests are really hard but if you study and do all of the supplmental homework you can get A's on them. As long as you put in A LOT of hard work the class is totally doable but don't expect it to be as easy as the other calc 2 courses.

Professor Benge is by far the best math professor I have had. His tests are hard and the class is very theory based, but you come out with a really strong understanding of the material. The tests are usually very similar to the practice exam andor the supplemental homework, so actually do the supplemental homework. There is a small curve.

Tests are really hard so averages are low, but he's a very engaged teacher. Good sense of humor. Lectures are really fast paced and a lot of material at once so recitation is where I learned the most.

I had Philip for his first semester of teaching and he did a really good job. That being said, his class was not easy at all and I personally struggled a lot with the first half of the semester (more calculus based). He is always eager to answer questions, but his explanations were sometimes almost "too smart."
Very enthusiastic

I loved Bengey! He is a really fun and likeable guy and is genuinely enthusiastic about what he teaches which makes it that much easier to learn from him. He's absolutely brilliant himself which can lead to him getting a little high-minded with his students but he is always willing to take questions and help you understand. Challenging but fair.

He is an extremely likable guy for the most part. He keeps class entertaining with his quirky analogies and jokes, but don't let that fool you, his tests are NOT EASY. He is in love with theory and proofs so expect that on his tests. There are weekly quizzes.  Other classes get crib sheets and lots of bonus. Don't expect that, but there is a curve.

If you want good grades, you have to make sure you complete assignments beforehand and review them with her during office hours before it's due. She gives good feedback (but I mostly think it's because she wants everything analyzed/written about in a certain way) to get better grades on your work. It doesn't help you become a better writer though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's really easy to talk to and very likeable, but she's not an easy grader. If you pay attention and seek help in office hours, you can figure out what she wants out of you after a little. In my class, we studied television shows and movies which is 100000 times better than reading pointless books like the rest of the classes.
Very tough grader. Would not recommend.

She will tell you on the first day of class that she doesn't care about your GPA and that she is a tough grader. If you aren't passionate about feminism and racism I wouldn't take the class. Workload isn't too much but some assignments are annoying. I would take someone else if you aren't an LMC major.
Nice person in general but extremely tough grader. Few assignments in the course. If you're not a really strong writer, don't take her. Seriously.

Dr. Bronstein will work with you to improve your writing and grade if you talk to her. I was on the fringe of falling down a grade level and she helped me to get the grade I needed to keep my letter. She is very outgoing and passionate, an all around great professor.   I will say, beware her grading. She is not easy and tears apart shoddy writing.

Dr. Bronstein is a really good professor for English. It was one of my favorites for that semester. She is a very tough grader but at the same time super helpful. If you show enough effort, she is always willing to help you out. I would recommend her class very much. However if you are looking for an easy A, look elsewhere.

She is very nice and if you are interested in pop culture and has very strong writing skill you will survive. However, if you are not so good with writing this will be brutal. You can get B with effort but not A without talent.

Has no idea what he is talking about.  Quotes heard in class: "I am not really sure what that slides means, so we are going to skip it" "A salted password is the little RSA token you wear around your neck" He is argumentative with anyone who asks questions.   Beware.

Over all not that great of a teacher. It was an easy class, however, I did did not benefit from his lectures. I had an overall 96% in the class and received a B, simply because I had a 2% attendance rate. I had to get this re-corrected the semester afterwards, because attendance wasn't even in the grading portion of the class stated  the syllabus.

Good professor overall, but has to teach a hard class (I believe most of the difficulty issues are not his fault). Doesn't do live code in class, instead completes it ahead of time and steps you through it line by line.
While an easy A, Phillips's lectures may have a negative effect on your understanding of programming. If you are placed in his class, make recitation your primary source of knowledge.

Most of your grade comes from exams which are based on the lecture materials, so it's important to take good notes. There's lots of opportunities for easy extra credit, take them it will make you less stressed at the end of the semester.

Exams are worth 60% of the overall grade, but many of the problems are very similar to the problem sets so if you complete the problem set you will be fine. The lectures can be a little confusing at times, but Prof. Pineda Torres does a good job of conveying information in an understandable way. There are also several opportunities for extra credit

Dr. Pineda-Torres is incredibly cohesive, articulate, and nuanced when discussing concepts. She values the theoretical as well as empirical sides, which gives realistic insight into economic research and its applications. If you do as expected in the syllabus and speak relatively frequently in class, the course should be very manageable.

New professor, huge busy-work assignment every few weeks. Professor over-emphasized her concern for academic dishonesty and seems to actively hunt students who cheat. Easy A if you do the work, don't take the class for granted just because it's easy. You'll need to show up to class for quizzes and be prepared for busy work out of the textbook.

Honestly, I've never talked to him, but that's probably because he seems to only care about his research and teaching intro chem is his side job, makes sense. One thing to note is that his handwriting is practically illegible, but he won't be mad if you ask him to clarify. Test are all multiple choice but not too hard. Lectures are above average.

I think La Pierre is super knowledgeable, but not in a way that translates well into freshman chemistry. His handwriting is impossible, and he often lectures like he's talking to another professor, not a student. The textbook was personally more helpful for me. I thought the tests were unnecessarily difficult and had a lot of confusing mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had a B in the class until the final, which could grade replace all previous exams. Tests are tricky, but not too bad as long as you review all the previous exams on the website. Ended up with an A partly because I went to office hours, where he teaches much better than in lecture. Also, Pierre has bad handwriting, but it is manageable.

Please go to lectures! Good professor, though I didn't get to know him well. Know's what he's doing, but his handwriting is barely legible, which makes note taking in class difficult. Tests are challenging and tricky, so be sure to study.

Professor La Pierre is an extremely knowledgeable individual, and possibly one of the most knowledgeable professors I have had. However, his use of high level Chemistry vocabulary can sometimes leave you feeling lost in class, as Chem 1212 is an intro level course. This was the first C I have ever had, and I can say I really tried hard.

A good lecturer for chemistry! You should pay attention in classes, but the textbook is actually very good as well, and I read it to do well in the class. His handwriting is atrocious, and he flips way too quickly between slides as soon as he finishes writing. The final replaces test grades if you do better. Clicker questions every class.

Yeah, his handwriting sucks but that's not a huge deal. His lectures are long and boring, but well-organized and if you pay attention they are good preparation for the tests. Overall he's a competent teacher but he spends a lot of time talking about things that don't matter.

This class is very similar to AP Chem. If you attend the lecture, do the homework, and attend the PLUS sessions an A is easy. The only negative is Dr. La Pierre's handwriting, and sometimes he is inaudible, so you zone out of class. His jokes can be a turn off too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a good person, but is not a good lecturer. His handwriting is not so good so you would have no idea what he writes on the board. His lectures can get confusing (especially in the transition metal chapter, which is, ironically, what he specializes in). But as long as you devote enough time into the class, you should be fine.

Fairly good lecturer, few problems with handwriting. My biggest gripe would be how he rushes through content that he specializes in (ironically). However, the lecture slides are always available online from the beginning of the semester. Plenty of opportunities for grade bumps / replacement (final overrides low midterms).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a good, easy to follow lecturer, although his handwriting can at times be illegible. The tests are the same for every CHEM 1212 class, so the difficulty will be the same no matter who you take.

His hand writing is by far the worst i have ever seen in my life. He doesnt say what he is writing and moves slides before you can write the information down. He also does not explain examples or clicker questions. If you ask a question, his answer will likely leave you more confused than you were before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: if you challenge him, he gives you grade insight into the Germans
goat

Pilipp might be my favorite teacher at Tech so far. He is absolutely hilarious and is quirky in his own German way. He appreciates participation in class and truly cares that you learn the material. The best way to describe him is as a happy guy. If you keep up with the vocab list in the textbook and do the short hw then it is easy to make an A.
His course was fairly easy and I learned a lot. He was accessible if you needed help out of class and was pretty funny and entertaining.

He really wanted his students to learn the material and pushed them, but the class was not overly difficult. There are daily assignments, but he usually does not check them and the tests are pretty fair. He managed to make the class interesting and I honestly looked forward to going it.
He was proficient in German, but he was a terrible teacher and did not treat his students with kindness. He was on of the meanest teachers I've had at Tech.

Extremely nice professor teaching a very easy class. Although it is very much an easy-A class, that is only true if you put in the work and do every online assignment. But although some are harder than others, all assignments are easy. Very caring & forgiving, genuinely wants everyone to do well, and is very understanding under all circumstances
Awesome professor. She is so ready to help the students. There is a lot of homework but when you get in a rhythm is easy to follow and there are some fun activities throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the class was online, she made sure that everyone was aware what was due, and there were a lot of opportunities for speaking. She was a pretty easy grader. As long as you did the assignment, you'd likely get full points. She was very accessible via email and very accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Love this woman. Her syllabus is much scarier than she is, she is very forgiving with deadlines and absences as long as you have a legit excuse. Her work is fun and engaging, make time for this class. If you do you will learn alot. If you don't have the time you will still get the A. Amazing class, amazing lectures.

This class was a blast and it is easy to talk with the professor. You have nothing to worry about as long as you do your work and stay on top of things. She is really understanding and accepts late work. Overall great class and professor

Professor Pilkington was a great teacher she is caring about the class and enthusiastic about the course. There was a good amount of homework but it was never difficult. She is really lenient and adaptable if you just talk to her. Just do the work and go to class and you'll get an A. Really enjoyable and stress free class.

She was really caring and thoughtful about our well being. Make sure you devote some time to do the projects, and everything will go great in this class. The class may seem daunting based on the syllabus, but it is actually really easy. It may take time to give the necessary instructions on projects, though. Overall, she is a wonderful teacher.

Professor Pilkington is very caring and always has a smile on her face! She is a great Spanish teacher and wants everyone to do well. Group activities help you get used to speaking the language instead of just writing or doing grammar. The activities are relatively simple but are helpful to do them. The class was fun and easy, so that's a win win!

one of the best teacher's I've ever had at Tech. She made me actually want to go to class, and her in class activities helped me remember a lot of the new vocab/verb conjugations. Highly recommend taking her if you can, you won't regret

An amazing Spanish professor! 10/10 would recommend. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. There are so many chances for extra credit and ways to get an A. She's one of the professors where if a the student does badly, they feel bad. Took the class for the humanities credit but now want to learn Spanish

Such a sweet lady. She will always help you out if you need it, even if that means taking a test earlier or later. She has a very unique personality but it grows on you. Very easy class and does not require much outside work at all.

Senora Pilkington is a very kind professor. If you took a couple of years of Spanish in HS, you will be fine. She will get you up to speed if you feel rusty. Keep up with the homework and ask questions and you should receive an A.

I loved Señora Pilkington! She's super sweet and really cares to get to know all of her students. English was her first language so she doesn't have an accent, and repeats important stuff and makes sure you understand. I definitely learned a lot in her class and did more speaking than previous classes, so I definitely recommend!
she's so nice and she gives all the help you need to succeed in her class.
most sweet and nice proffessor ever
The teacher is really great, probably one of my favorites so far at Tech. She'll work with you on anything you're struggling with and if you want an A you'll most likely get one.

It was her first time teaching this class so it wasn't exactly clear what would be expected. She is an awesome professor. Extremely helpful and very patient. Class was completely in Spanish and I really improved my speaking ability. Overall a very nice person and very easy to talk to. Highly recommend!

You have to admire her for her patience; having never taken Spanish before I was hesitant when she put me on the spot in class. She did a great job in working with me in reach an answer. At times I mispronounced easy spanish words and each time she skillfully hinted to the right answer allowing me to say them correctly and sparing me embarrassment.

She is awesome! So nice and really helpful.  She is also a pretty easy grader on oral and written reports. Also, if you're confused on the test, she'll give you helpful little hints.  I'm terrible at spanish, but managed to get an A without taking the final.  Definitely recommend her.  I'm taking her again for 1002.
I took her for 1101 and 1102. She's really nice and approachable. She always sends out a study guide before the test that basically tells you exactly what's on it.
Easy, Easy, Easy. This class is basically a highschool review.
easy class.. i had taken spanish before so it was that much easier.. but her tests are straight from the workbook and she is understanding about absences
Very very easy.  Tests are taken straight from the workbook that you have to do.  I had already taken some spanish before and made an easy A, but some people found it difficult.

Each assignment has different workflow and number of submissions, which gets very confusing. Unlike other courses, very few submissions are allowed on gradescope. Course is made too tough for no reason.
Semester-long project. Not hard if you get a half-decent group. No midterms, 1 take-home final at the end of the semester. Easy A.
CS4605 with Ploetz was my favorite class at Georgia Tech. Super nice guy and always made classes engaging and fun.

He's awesome! Lectures can be a little bit boring sometimes, but if you make an effort to engage with the content, it'll be worth it -- he goes above and beyond to bring demos into class (we got to play around with a bunch of VR tools and wearable tech). Also super reachable on Ed, which I liked. Big bike enthusiast lol

THIS IS FOR CS 4605, MOBILE AND UBIQUITOUS COMPUTING. EASY CLASS. There are just a few projects and a final project, which is all DIY stuff. You should be good if you make the presentation and create a few things for the demo. The rest of the other projects are easy, too. It's a pretty light class. Some days attendance is mandatory, like very few.
This was actually for CS4605 mobile and ubiquitous computing, but ploetz is goated. The class is project based so try to get a good team.

The professor has a very engaging style of teaching and is very interactive during class. The course itself is quite involved and by no means an easy ride. Know what you are getting into and be prepared to code a lot. No complaints about Professor Ploetz though, a great lecturer. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I found myself going to each class.

The lectures were really interesting but because of the flipped classroom style you could learn everything through the online modules (which were really informative). Homework was really hard, coding intensive, and took a long time. Expect to put a lot of time into this class. Exams are long but reasonable in terms of difficulty and content tested.

The class is hard because its coding heavy. You just have to do the work in a timely manner or you are effed. There are multiple extra credit opportunities which was cool. I could have done better but didn't feel like it lol. Enjoyed this class and the professor's energy kept me awake and engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Whoever gave this professor a 1 clearly doesn't understand what grad school at GT means. In order to understand the abstract nature of AI, Dr. Ploetz incorporated examples of real-world AI applications. His syllabus is incredibly thorough and he is one of the few professors to offer bonus. He cares about his students and always available for help.

Talks too much about abstract things not related to the topic (bikes and cars). Too much material and unrelated videos and posts. Unclear what is necessary and what is optional. Gives labels to students in class and likes to interact a lot, will remember you next time. Carries long discussions far from the topic of the lecture.

I took 3600 with Dr. Platt in fall 2020. He is a great person but learning from him was difficult. His teaching style is very disorganized and I struggled to make sense of what was going on in lectures and in assignments. I ended up dropping the class because I felt so lostand took it with a different professor the next semester and did very well.

Dr. Platt is very passionate about what he teaches. I found his lectures very interesting, and it was clear he wanted students to learn a lot from his course. His tests are usually all multiple choice with one free response, which makes it easy to lose a lot of points. Practice quizzes are given, but material on exam can be more challenging.

Dr. Platt has many wonderful qualities: he is very smart and energetic and clearly knows what he is talking about. However, he comes from a biology background, not an engineering background. You won't learn any "Cell Biology" in this class, but you will hurt over poorly worded questions and information he assumed you learned in "AP Bio".

Dr. Platt is the best professor in the BME department at Tech! His lectures are incredibly interesting, and all of the assignments and projects he assigns really make you feel like you're learning something. Most of the material is taught in lectures, and he does not post slides, so make sure to attend every class and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very passionate about teaching and his research. Tests are mostly multiple choice. One group project, and extra credit opportunities.

He provides practice questions that are somewhat helpful for the exams, but sometimes he puts questions that come out of nowhere. Questions tend to be worded poorly & are confusing. He is really bad about springing things on you (journal articles at the last minute) & provided our project rubrics one day before presentations started.
The tests are challenging but you should get done all the practice test problems.  Be familiar with all the topics discussed in the pre-test review. Also know how to convert units efficiently.

It was my worst experience at Georgia Tech! Do NOT take him! I will warn you of this!! You will be lost about what he expects out of the class! He will not teach you anything. He is VERY VAGUE and will test on details. He expects you to read several thousands of pages. He blames the failure of the whole class on the students. Very bad teacher!

I took EAS 4656 lab. Always 1+ hour late to the lab. Used lecture slides from EAS 2750. Often unprepared. Gives little guidance. Very confusing and unprofessional. Literally gave us the wrong material for a lab, and we had to redo it. Lectures for an hour and give little time for lab work. It was the worst.

Had this professor for EAS-1601 Lab, but the class isn't listed. He made me excited to wake up for an 8AM, 3-hour lab, and I can easily say that I wouldn't have succeeded in the lab without him. He teaches well, and you'll never be afraid to ask for help. Above all else, he wants you to learn, and he'll do whatever he can to make that happen easily

Took him for EAS1601 (not listed on RMP for some reason)

I had to get ODS involved as Dr. Porter wouldn't respond to my repeated request to fulfill my accommodations, alongside being 6 weeks behind on grading. He seemed like a nice guy and helpful too, but his lack of presence for the first half of the semester made everything a lot harder.

Mesoscale with him was the most fun, laid-back class I've ever had. He's similar to Jerma, you'll see why. Grades were given back fairly late, but lots of leniency with due dates and assignments. He'd ask when we wanted to take quizzes and give reviews of them beforehand. Final project was a poster case study, super easy to do.

Class is very poorly organized, too much covered & almost nothing in depth. Teaching D3 is useless. The assignment on Spark & cloud computing is too basic with almost no learning outcome, what is the point of implementing the same thing in 3 different technologies. The prof mumbles & is hard to follow. Only upside is no tests & easy to score.

The only vizualization tool you actually get experience in is D3 which is completely useless for most people. Barely covers Tableau, doesnt touch PowerBI, Seaborn, Matplotlib or any other data visualization actually tool used in business.

Building my own random forest model was cool! Not at all relevant for data visualization though!

Everyone complaining about the class being super hard and how the workload was so high clearly didn't heed any of the information given in the very detailed syllabus on the expected workload, starting early, and self motivated learning required. I found his lectures reasonably interesting and informative.

Don't see what D3 has to do with data science, and the autograder is absolutely painful. Not to mention that office hours are horrible- just TA "live" on ed discussion when they're probably playing video games or still in bed. THis course is not very ML-y, just a bunch of useless garbage they force you to do. -1/10.

The lectures all revolve around boosting the ego of the "Polo" club (cringe!) and provides no tangible learning experience. Be prepared to read through documentation and learn the language on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This class is a part-time job.  It requires a lot of effort but exposes you to a wide range of languages and tools.

If you want an easy A with little work, this is not the course for you.  I do not recommend this course unless you're ready to work and take it with friends.

The final report is graded leniently and lectures are optional, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Homeworks are extremely difficult and no guidance is given. I don't usually rate professors but he expects his students to learn completely by themselves without any guidance. Get ready to spend 40+ hours a week on this class

Terrible experience. I'm paying Georgia Tech tuition to scramble to learn a dozen technologies in a semester with 0 guidance from the professor, who just spends lectures reading his resume. The office hour setup is also terrible, just an hour at a time of a TA manning a forum. If it's not mandatory for your program, don't take classes from him.

Lectures were mainly unhelpful. For what it is I think it gives a decent high level idea of all aspects of data analytics, gives concrete technologies that are used, and allows for a final project for students to further explore these topics. Homeworks were very long and tedious and not especially helpful all the time and felt like resume padding.

1) The lectures are meaningless, do not teach any of the class subject or theories, and can be skipped.
2) D3 makes up ~20% of the class grade even though it is not a tool used in data analytics.
3) You get 0 feedback so you will not know what you did wrong on items you get incorrect.
4) Mandatory so you are stuck taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've ever had. Stressful homework assignments with terrible support from TAs. Lectures don't prepare you for homework. And the homework and lectures don't prepare you for the project.

Expects you to learn new programming languages within a week with no guidance. Good luck with this class! Made me consider dropping the entire degree program. Really wishing I chose the Berkeley program for data science.
Didn't actually teach us anything. Huge waste of time and stress on tools I likely won't ever need. Split this into two classes because the work load is obscene.

I cannot emphasize how much this class expects of students. This is a core class and we are expected to know CSS, Java, Python, SQL, Azure, D3, etc... Lectures don't actually go over how to do any of the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach anything. Expects you to learn difficult CS concepts independently.

This class had absolutely no structure or clear objective. Polo said this class would give us hard skills to use in the workforce and we ended up 'learning' D3. Aside from that, we got about a 5 minute overview of random technologies without actually learning how to use them. I didn't learn anything new in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
For the most part the homeworks do a decent job teaching the material, but especially during the D3 Homework 3 it was very hard to pick things up so quickly. Nevertheless is very lenient in grading.
Felt unprepared for the final project if I didn't know alot from taking other ML/CS classes in the past.

Classes in 6242 are unfortunately useless. You're pretty much on your own for most of the semester, don't shy away from working with classmates and if possible learn javascript (and python, of course) before starting.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Average class, but if you don't want to take something like NLP/DL for the ML concentration, this is a good option. Pretty busy class though. There is leeway in grading, you don't need to do all of HW2 to get an A. The project is graded leniently. There's also the opportunity to get 3% extra through bonus quizzes. Don't need to go to lectures

Overall, DVA (campus version, at least) is structured and managed pretty well for a large course. The lectures are not very helpful, but if you're reasonably good at programming you'll pick up the skills you need for HW quickly. Make sure to get a good group for the project. Polo is really an expert in the material and his research is pretty cool.

This Professor is bad++. Get ready to learn nothing and asked to do a lot. As an analogy if he would teach what every tool is for like: A hammer to put nails down, a plane to fly (analogy) but won't ever actually show you how to us the tool. Though the Homeworks which major part of of your grade will ask you to implement different kind of tech.
Complete garbage of a class. Prof doesn't teach anything and you just do assignments for the entire class. Really don't like it and not at all impressed. You'd be better of just doing udemy courses.

Not sure what purpose the "lecture" part of class was. 5 homework assignments and 1 project made up the course load. No tests. You aren't actually taught how to do any of the homework though, lectures are just slideshows of things the Prof. has done. If you've mastered Python, R, SQL, Javascript, D3, Hadoop before you start, you'll be fine?

Going to class is a good idea since some lecture details appear on the tests. Lectures are easy to follow. He gives tons of extra credit, so most people don't fail. The tests aren't too bad. I studied about an hour before each exam and got around 80%. Exams are mostly multiple choice with some multi-select.

Amazing professor, engaging lectures even at 8am, funny and cares enough to learn names of students who participate in class. Attending lecture is highly recommended to do well, as he makes note of specific content that will appear on tests in class and makes specific points that may not appear on slides. Decently easy and enjoyable class overall.

He really cares about the class and tries to engage with the students. If a question is going to be on the test, he'll emphasize it in class so it's somewhat important that you go to class/ have others take notes for you. The final exam is a project and he's generous with the grades.

Very friendly professor, fun lectures, humorous, engaging, numerous extra credit opportunities. Exams' content were straightforward and expectations were clear. He even tells you what specific questions will be on exams. Seemed like he really cared about the subject and his students. Must pick if you take POL1101, he's the GOAT!

lectures are super interesting and honestly enjoyable! i'm not a morning person at all but this class made waking up at 8 am worth it. one thing is even tho attendance isn't mandatory it basically is, since half of the test questions are on things he talks about in lectures, so if you just go through the powerpoint you won't do well.

Easy grader. Only hard part of class are the three tests. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Class attendance is mandatory because there is an assignment every class. No final exam but there is a final project. Final project is graded very lightly.

You have to try not to get an A in this class, Dr. Polak will literally tell you in class, "This will be a question on the test". He's also a funny guy, and you can tell he cares about the content. He offers crazy amounts of extra credit; you could probably get a C on all the exams and still get an A. No final either.
His tests are from very small details he would point out during class. If you dont go to lectures then you cant do well on the tests.
Do not take him if you are not a policy major. It is an easy A but the amount of writting he expects is insane. He's very passionate but the class just ends up being an exhausting experience.

It is clear he cares a lot about what he is teaching and puts a lot of effort into making his class interesting while still understanding that many people are taking it as a requirement. Tests can be a bit tricky, but there is a ridiculous amount of extra credit offered, making it an easy A. Attendance is required only at the end of the semester.

Awesome professor. Hands down one of the best you'll have at Georgia Tech. He memorizes every student's name, wants to get to know everyone better, and is a fair grader. Also, he has a lot of interesting stories, and he tells those stories while also not simply lecturing students the entire time.

Prof Polak is a great professor! I very highly recommend attending lectures because he points out the specifics of what will be on tests. He also makes lectures interesting, and this is coming from someone who isn't very interested in government. Overall an easy A.

Good teacher, tough TA's/random test questions. Interesting class. The test material was given out in study guide format, but a majority of the guides were made by his TA and include things like "discussed in lecture on (X DATE)". They were multiple choice and the hardest part of his class (60~ questions each and questions were random). Great guy.

Dr.Polak is awesome! I will say this class is not an easy A, there's a lot more work than I anticipated. His tests are a bit hard & you HAVE to go to lecture to do well. Also get ready to take detailed notes, bc his TQ's are very specific. He gives out lots of extra credit, just do it & the project at the end is an easy 100 to boost your grade.

tests are based on kind of niche facts that he discusses in class, so even tho attendance isn't mandatory, you really need to go. that said, prof polak offers SO much extra credit that it's hard not to get an A. he is such a nice guy and so excited about teaching, and made an 8am enjoyable. you have to do the work, but it's worth it!!

Prof Polak is a really really nice person. He genuinely wants his students to succeed. However, you do need to go to lectures to get an A in this class, it is very difficult to succeed from cramping the night before midterms. So don't take if you just wants to get free GPA without commitment. But his lectures are amazing and the course is very easy

I did not enjoy this class. Prof. Polak is very nice and engaging, and his lectures are generally interesting, but I dislike the way exams are set up. They are extremely hard to study for. Many of the questions are specific facts from one video watched in lecture/at home weeks ago. Very nitpicky, too difficult considering what the class should be.

Professor Polak is amazing. He really encourages participation, and even though attendance isn't mandatory, I highly encourage you to go. I thought tests were a bit challenging since they require a lot of memorization, but he also gives out a lot of extra credit, so you'll be fine.

Professor Polak was amazing. He went out of his way to learn everyone who participated in class names. He is super caring and funny. The class has 3 exams, 1 group project and assignments. Exams were fine if you go to class and study what he tells you. The final project was extremely easy and fun to do, the assignments were all busy work. Loved!

Not a free class, but not hard either. Great lecturer, funny and very caring for students. Exams are kinda tricky and dependent upon material spoken in lecture, attendance needed to do well on exams. Offers so much extra credit that poor exam performance isnt a problem. Has great guest lecturers; you come away actually feeling like you've learned.

Polak was a pretty good prof. What you need to know:
- Tests are kind of difficult and a little nit picky
- Outside of tests, other assignments are basically completion (though make sure to turn things in on time)
- Lectures are pretty chill and kind of entertaining, would recommend going to lecture

Great lecturer, keeps content engaging. Spends time to memorize names and talk to students during class. If you go to every lecture, his exams aren't too bad, especially with the extra credit throughout the semester. He grades the final group project easy too. Overall made what I thought would be a boring class exciting and engaging

This professor is amazing. I took this course as a freshman and I freaking loved it so much. 2101 is literally the easiest social science class you'll ever take. All you have to do is participate and write a paper. Professor Mike is funny and kind and genuinely cares. He gives you oppurtunities to make up assignments, which are really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Polak is the best! Makes a huge lecture feel like a close-knit class. If you ask/answer a question a single time, he'll know your name the rest of the semester. Important: you must go to class even though attendance isn't required, and there is a group project at the end. But if you put in effort, it's an easy A with all the extra credit

Professor Pollak is an incredibly kind teacher. He often leads interesting in class discussions and makes sure the content we learn is relevant to our real lives. Relatively easy grader and open to flexibility in terms of taking the test. Easily accessible outside of class. Attendance is not mandatory except for tests and guest speakers.

Had him at 8am. He blasts music when you walk in, which was in good spirit, but instead gave me a headache since I'm pretty bad with loud noise. He's pretty interesting but sometimes he can say some...questionable things. Exams were pretty tough and I definitely had to study for them. I know some people who took this course pass/fail after exam 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Polak was personally very understanding. However, this is not a class you expect to go into and get an easy A. You for sure have to put in the work and communicate with him when necessary. He was overall very nice and caring for his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Polak is absolutely my favorite professor on campus. He cares so deeply for students, and you'll always get an A if you prove to him that you put work into the class. Good humor, good environment, made me want to show up for a 9:30 AM class for once

Easy class. The final is optional and to ace midterms, just note down key details he emphasizes in class and take notes from guest speakers and slides. The final group project requires attendance and is easy. He entertains with songs, jokes and political stories and tries to address everyone in the 100+ class directly by first name. Take him!
Addressed many people by name, even in a huge lecture hall with over 100 students, which made lectures engaging.

Not a lot of teaching going on in the classroom, lots of yapping. Tests are not straightforward and contain very niche tidbits that he says in class, but somehow attendance is not required. It was kind of difficult to get an A which was surprising for this sort of class. If you can take a different class or professor I would, but it's doable

Great class. Very engaging. Show up + pay attention to lecture + keep up with workload = A. 3 midterms that you can do very well on since it's mostly memorization. Optional final (replaces lowest midterm) made of questions from the midterms. Make flash cards of all the midterm questions and memorize them (I took the final in 3 minutes and got a 97)

Dr. Polak made every lecture engaging. Has an interesting background and is constantly bringing in guest speakers with relevant stories. Majority of grade is based on 3 midterms (+ an optional final) but these are all based on the lectures/slides and the optional final (extremely easy) pretty much ensures you can bump up at least one letter grade.

I have never been into the social sciences, but Professor Polak may have changed that. He brought expertise and enthusiasm that made me enjoy going to class every day. While not every class was mandatory, some classes were and midterms do have some in-class questions on them. However, he is a very fair grader and you shouldn't need to stress out.

So goated that by the end of the semester the majority of the 200 still attended the 9:30am lectures even though it isn't required. The most understanding professor at GT and you learn so much from the class. There's a decent amount of hw, 3 exams, a project, and optional final that can replace an exam. The "con" is he randomly calls on people :<

Super easy class, they know it's a pre-req and the work matches that mentality. Attendance was optional, except for guest speaker days. Three tests, occasional homework, and one large group project. The final is optional and replaces your lowest test score. Super understanding TA & professor made for an overall great experience.

Professor Polack is a super nice guy who literally learned everyones names day 1. But, this class is not for the faint of heart. Its a LOT more work than any most elective classes, and you never know which assignments he's going to grade really critically. It is interesting and a great resume builder, but just be prepared going in.

Dr. Polak is a MUST if you have any interest in politics. He served in the GA House of Reps & GA Senate for years so he has invaluable firsthand experience he teaches. Let's be clear- it's not an easy A. You have to work. But it is worth it because of what you learn from Dr. Polak. I took his class Spring 2021. Sticks with me strongly still. 10/10.
AMAZING!!! Take him, I've never liked a class more.

Overall an Amazing and Caring professor. I had him in my first semester and I expect him to be among my favorite professors when I graduate. I found the class to be quite similar to classes I took in high school so there wasn't a lot of new material to learn.

Super nice and genuinely cares about getting to know his students! Learned almost all of our names in a 200-person lecture and made it feel a lot smaller by making it extremely interactive. He was involved with government himself in the past, which gives him an interesting perspective when lecturing. Great class!

Professor Polak was extremely great person. You might have to read a lot of textbook pages though because he gives out pretty much of reading materials. There are times when you MUST attend for speakers and group projects. And for the final assignment group project, make sure you DO something contribution because at the end, you MIGHT have to prove
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class was easy, if you have done K-12 education in America, then it's even easier. Polak numerous times told us the resources if we were struggling in the class, especially for the international students(i.e. office hours, TA help). Final is optional, but attendance is required on guest speaker days and when a project for the class has started.

Professor Polak is lots of fun and presents everything clearly.  Brought in speakers are interesting and on topic to the course.  First half of the semester, class isn't required except on speaker days.  Topics are simple, but some test questions are specific to things said during lecture.  Overall, super easy but decently interesting.

Honestly home boy is a really nice guy fr, but like he calls on like 10 people to answer one question bruh. Like my class at 8 am too fr and he calling on so many people bro like honestly im so scared whenever im in class like im fr on the edge of my seat i cant pull up to lecture now its like way too stressful bruh im not even playing.

Mr. Polak was an amazing professor who understood that the majority of those taking his class were freshman who needed the government credit. If you make sure to listen to the lectures and taken notes during class, you will be golden. Tests are partially based on assigned readings which can pile up if you don't stay on top of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really motivating and inspiring professor. He acknowledges that this is a class that people take to fill graduation requirements, so he tries to have a reduced workload and be as accommodating as possible. There was an extremely easy/simple final project at the end of the semester, which was also nice.

Prof Polak gives excellent and inspiring lectures on local government (since he used to be a part of it). He explains course content and his expectations for assignments and projects well. Taking notes carefully is critical for success because the lectures and guest speaker content constitute much of the tests. I generally enjoy this class!

Professor Polak is one of the most enthusiast teachers I have had. Attendance was only required for some classes, but I went to every lecture anyways because he made it super fun and enjoyable. The class did require a bit of work but not bad at all. If you pay attention and take notes, you will be fine. Love this man
(POL 1101): Really really understanding when it comes to assignments. Tests have no curveballs, everything is as expected. Attendance is only mandatory on days with guest speakers. Final is optional.

He really cares about what students think and what they need. Cause I am an international student and I do not have pre-knowledge about the structure of US government, he even offers me a chance after class to tutor me 1 to 1 for almost a whole lecture time. I would definitely take his course again.

I loved Polak. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. He is a former legislator and has an extensive network that he is happy to connect you with. He even took some of us to the state capitol during the semester. There is a pretty heavy workload but he isn't a super harsh grader. He wants you to learn and do something with it.

He randomly grades hard on certain assignments and does not give clear guidelines. There is however a lot of completion grades that can balance your grade but just beware. Also if your looking for an easy class to boost your gpa, this is not the one. There is a 40 page paper due for the midterm. Too much work for no reason. And don't skip.

Prof. Polak is a nice and helpful instructor. His class is an A/B class with required attendance and participation for the grade. The icing on the cake was the final. It required students to conference with elected officials in only a weeks time. Additionally, there was so many other components that made the end of the semester stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mr. Polak does a great job teaching State and Local Government. Assignments can seem scary but they do a good job of giving you a real feel for what you are learning. Sometimes repeats himself but this ensures that you won't miss the most important lessons (take notes!). Work hard and show that you care about the assignments, and you'll do great.

Probably more work than other ENGL 1102 classes, but also probably a lot less reading (and a lot more interesting). The class is based on one semester long group projects with four different checkpoints making up the majority of your grade. Put in the work, you'll be fine. Can be kind of time consuming.
The class seems hard and it will be but grading is super easy. Instructions are sort of unclear but every major assignment has regrades which makes it pretty easy.

Absolutely ridiculous amount of work for ENGL 1102. So much writing, reading, and an extremely weird assignment layout. So much group work made this class impossible to do especially if you're in a bad group. Take any other person for ENGL 1102 and you won't have this much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: As someone who has never liked English, Lainie was an incredible professor. She gave great feedback and made me much more confident in my writing. If your struggling with something, talk to her! She is very kind and understanding. She is very passionate about what she does. She expects a little more than other English professors, but its worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ENGL 1101 F2023. She was really supportive and adorable. She gave detailed feedback and a long period for revision. Revision was absolutely helpful. If you were serious with your first submission, there shouldn't be much work during revision. There were quite a lot of pre-class readings, READ them! I bought Writer/Design but didn't really use it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Pomerleau is my favorite instructor I've had in my time at Georgia Tech. She is smart, calculated, and funny. Her expectations are clear and she obviously wants her students to succeed. She tries to challenge us in ways that I haven't seen before in an English class, and everything about the class was enjoyable. Take her if at all possible.

Dr.Pomerleau is a great speaker and her lectures were never boring. It is a lot of writing and if you do not like Shakespeare this will be a bit boring, but the adaptations you do allow creativity. She also allows revisions so its hard not to get an A.

This professor is very passionate about what she teaches, and if you don't really enjoy Shakespearean literature (like me) then this class will be pretty boring for you. She is a tough grader but always allows make-up for grades less than 90. It isn't a hard A, but it definitely requires a lot of work. Mandatory attendance and no sleeping in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Pomerleau was an engaging lecturer and really helpful in providing feedback. She lets you revise your assignments so if you want a good grade you absolutely can if you put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Pomerleau was great. She made the class fun and educational. She gives students multiple opportunities to raise their grade.

I was in class during her first semester here (spring '22). She was an incredible professor. I enjoyed her use of unique materials, entertaining class discussions, and creative assignments for the dreaded USG-wide portfolio. Wants her students to succeed so her grading is very understanding. Even inspired me to buy/read a book outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, makes the class very engaging and answers all in-class questions with good enthusiasm. Exploratory teaching. Slides content might be little poor but he makes up for it with good lectures

Very caring and passionate professor, who is interested in answering students' questions and helping them out. Good guy, interesting lectures. Easy test(s).The projects were a logistical mess though -- released quite late into the semester, deadlines adjusted, but still we had less time and test cases didn't seem well written, causing stress for me

All the time spent for this class is on the 5 projects. You have the test cases, so pretty much a guaranteed 100 if you spend enough time and finish. 1 midterm that is pretty much IDENTICAL to the practice exam lol. Made our final optional; can use our midterm as final exam grade. Didn't go to lecture because repeat of 2200/4290. Relaxing class

Generally good professor. Exam was super easy (exact same as the practice he gave out). Projects, although usually easy, are plagued with issues in the instructions. In many projects, students had to post their own workarounds for the rest of class to rely on. TA announcements often contradict the assignment instructions, which don't seem to update
Great guy and very understanding. Tests are very easy and projects arent too difficult either.

Milos is very knowledgeable regarding what he teaches. This course was honestly really easy this semester. The lectures were interesting for the first 2/3 of the course, but then he ran out of content and they fell off. The projects weren't too hard, you could have a partner. The instructions were wrong sometimes too.
Processor Design lectures were not very useful, but Milos cares about his students and is a reasonable grader. He also made the final optional if you liked your grade without it
Great Professor. Amazing subject knowledge.

Prasad is not very good or engaging at lecturing. But he is extremely caring and accommodating of students. Prasad always answered all my emails immediately and helped me succeed in any way he could. I mostly learned by reading his posted notes and the textbook.

Homework is optional, but treat as required. Grade based on take-home exams and projects. Material is difficult but important. Course materials are effective. Lectures are the weakness: It is clear he cares and tries to be engaging, but material is still dry. With ADHD, I could not stay focused. 

Start all work early and be ready to teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: JVR is not bad for 4610. I think in the past he gave a final exam, but he no longer does that. Since the class is graded and run mostly by TAs, his impact is relatively minimal, and his lectures are fine. Maybe not the most helpful rating compared to classes he actually teaches, but 4610 is chill.

(AE3530) Prasad is one of the worst lecturers I've had. Honestly if it weren't for the attendance bonus everyone would skip class and learn from his online notes. My advice: do your homework in his lecture and self-learn his notes at home. He doesn't even cover everything in the online notes so you have to do that anyway to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took 3530 with him. Its a hard class and I don't blame him for that. He has well structured well formatted notes that are too technical and complex to understand. Would not be my first choice but way better than other options. (3% bonus for showing up to 90% of classes)

This review is for 3530. Dr. Prasad does not use a slide deck and chooses instead to write on the board - do with that what you will. Some will find his fashion of lecture engaging, others will find it hard to follow. Homeworks and tests were fairly straight forward.

My best friend unfortunately passed away during my time taking this class and this professor had the outright audacity to take off for late submission regardless of the dean-approved excuse I had. Total POS, will never take again. I hated his class in the first place because of his teaching style, but his lack of empathy is why I don't respect him.

Personally can't stand the guy. He teaches in a very old guard manner (mandatory attendance, expects you to take notes and fully lock in for the course, gives a final for a lab class), but it's a lab class so who cares about the lecture. Always was something I could never get behind. Otherwise fine, the course is chump change.

AE 3530 with Prasad only reads off slides in lecture so you might be better doing that on your own time. Got way more out of the class by going to both his and TA's office hours during the week to get help on the homework and know if my answers were right since it's graded harshly. Tests are similar to hw and examples but are graded very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Prasad does a bad job in conveying the difficult content of AE 3530. He mostly reads off slides which upon further inspection contain many errors, resulting in confusion while studying. The exam questions are fair, however are graded very harshly and no crib sheets are permitted, which results in useless memorization based studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Insists on having a final that meaninglessly tests you over concepts in prerequisite courses despite objections from the students and even his own TAs.
Not a good teacher
Bad at teaching
don't take it
awful
insane
Very hard to deal with. Moody. Unprofessional.

FlightD is notorious for being a hard class. Dr. Prasad gave students many opportunities to do well, giving a lot of tips for exams and HW in office hours. Extra credit in exams amounted to 9% of the total grade. HWs are very hard but prepare you well for exams, so start early.

Prof Prasad is not always clear, but if you ask him for clarificatins he is very accomodating. Tests are similar to the homework, so make sure to ask for the hommework solutions! Don't be afraid to stop him and ask for a longer, more detailed explanation. If you don't, he won't give it and you'll be lost
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Helicopter S&C. Prasad explains things very well. Light on derivations and heavy on concepts. Homework was optional but very important to work out for the exams. Lectures aren't exciting, per se, but they are interesting and clear. The exams are somewhat challenging.

Lectures are pretty good, but can get a little dull after 75 minutes. Definitely a course in which you'll learn a lot. Dr. Singh knows a lot and is good at answering questions. Plus the class comes with a fun project.
Lectures are super boring. He does not know how to teach well. For the majority of lectures he will continuously talk for 75 minutes straight and the class with fall asleep.

Reading textbook is a must. Always a quiz after he goes over a chapter so have to alway. Read the textbook unless you know what his talking about in class. Test is fair but good news is he curve base the class average so if you ,re higher than the average than you are sure an A or B

Good teacher. He will answer questions effectively and really cares if you understand. He is hard however. He follows the book very closely, so read. Grades were pretty low due to the material being tough, but he  does curve.
Difficult class, reading book is mandatory, but he helps some. Powerpoints are just a bunch of charts, but he curves a lot

He is an awesome professor. Some of his comments are pretty hilarious. The class was fairly easy. The tests were a bit confusing at times but he curves the final grade. The class is very interesting !!!

She cares about her students/the course. The class is horrible: 30% for two papers and the midterm/final are 35% each. The tests are okay however if you mess up on one of the tests, there is no hope for you. The midterm was harder and had a couple trick questions. If you're premed, DON'T recommend taking. Nothing helpful and I barely learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is enthusiastic about the class but, her teaching technique is horrible. Only graded 4 assignments and the MCQ was super specific. Attendance is not mandatory but if you wanna pass you need to attend. Doesn't post detailed slides. A LOT OF READING and not easy to catch up. Need 4-5 hours a week. Don't take it if not needed for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very great person, good teacher, interesting class. However, the way she grades her class is HORRIBLE! There are 4 assignments the whole year. The essays were subjective and the tests asked super specific questions. One test she asked what the name of the cat was in the book.... Would not recommend if you are premed.

Truly amazing lecturer and brilliant person. Go to office hours! She is really nice to talk to and will explain concepts and open your eyes. Grading scheme is horrible though since the entire grade depended on reflections (in class essays) and 2 exams. A LOT OF READING!!! Reading is not easy to catch up on. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While the lectures open your eyes to the world around you, I believe that the course format ruins the class. Being graded by only 4 assignments leaves very little "wiggle room". Additionally, I believe the reading was very easy to fall behind on and was too much given that we have other classes (sometimes 70+ pages). Good lecturer, bad structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brown is amazing, her lectures are brilliant and she will change the way you see the world.

Great lecturer, very clear on expectations. Lots of readings, but if you pay close attention during lecture when she briefly discusses the reading and maybe skim a summary you'll have enough info to do well on quizzes. Quizzes and the midterm are easy - just overview notes and you're good. Can replace final exam with your quiz average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown is an incredible professor. She really immersed me in the lectures and readings, even as a first-year taking a 3000-level course. Easy to reach outside of class and willing to aid students with their writing or understanding of class material during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class as long as you pay attention in lecture and do the readings. The quizzes consist of very specific questions that you will only know if you attend lecture and do the readings. The lectures & readings were surprisingly interesting and easy to follow, so I recommend this class for anyone needing a social science elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown makes it very easy to do well in her class, but you do have to put in the work for it. You have to write six papers before finals, which is a lot of work, but you are given a lot of flexibility on when you write them, and they are graded pass/fail. The lectures are heavily discussion based, and Dr. Brown encourages class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Incredible lectures with interesting and thought provoking topics Class discussion encouraged but not required Daily reading assignments but excellent selection of literature- covers basics of sociology and topics that apply to modern world Almost entirely quiz/ Exam based- but if you show up to class and do the readings you get an A Kind teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures can be bland sometimes, but if you pay attention and do the reading, you'll be fine. You don't have to do all the readings to be honest, but it does help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's an interesting lecturer, but some of the topics were mediocre at best. Personally, I would have preferred her to focus on a few topics (such as race, crime, etc) instead of teaching new topics every week or so. Quizzes are fair, attend her lecture and there's no way you wouldn't pass. You can skip around on the readings and still pass.
Interesting class. Read 4 books that were relatively quick reads. Has quizzes every few weeks that are easy if and only if you do the readings and show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor who actually cared about his students.  His tests were fairly easy, especially compared to what could have been asked.  Overall, my friends and I who took the class respect him and recommend him.

Caring about students and made sure we understood everything in lecture before moving on. Optional final that averaged with the corresponding midterms if taken. Plenty of HW to get max HW points. Tests were difficult but if you went to lecture/studio and did the HW you will be okay.
Tests were really difficult, but he was very accessible outside of class and clearly cared about students! Extra credit and final exam extra points really helped in the end. Go to lecture!!

Grades will be curved according to class. Finals are easy and good ways to get points back. If you can really show him that you are good with that part, you will get an a. He is very caring and reachable after class. Go to studio if you want extra credits.

Individually cares about all students and their wellbeing, grades are curved and he will round up or adjust your grade if their was one test that the class performed poorly on and you do well on final, great lecturer with lots of examples and lots of extra credit opportunities.

Easily the best professor I've had at Tech so far. Extremely friendly and made sure to go over topics that the class was confused with. If we were not able to cover a topic in the lecture, he made sure that quizzes would be adjusted accordingly to not punish us. Fair grading for tests, clear slides, amazing teacher.

Pu-Ting Yu was an outstanding teacher. I would not have been able to get an A without him constantly being available for questions and providing feedback. Lectures can be a little boring, but overall, he was a caring person who would often take the time to individually check on how we were doing. I would definitely recommend taking his classes.

Very friendly in class and would always be happy to ask questions.  At times when he realized the class was confused he would stop and review the topic.  Really cares about us learning the topic and gave us very clear slides to follow along before each lecture.

Wow, what a gem. She was such a breath of fresh air and she really cared about everyone doing well. She does have kind of a thick accent, but her knowledge of math and how she wants her students to succeed should outweigh that. There was a weekly quiz, weekly homework, and two tests plus the final, all easy. Also, recitation helped a lot too.

She had a really positive energy that really made lectures enjoyable. Her teaching was mostly clear, however, towards the end of the semester, it became a lot more difficult to understand the concepts being taught.
Although she is a really nice person, her lectures were very difficult to understand, and the tests were difficult with trick questions thrown in.

Tests and final were extremely fair.  You can talk with her outside of class anytime. Lectures are unbelievably good, go to them even though they aren't mandatory. Do the MML homework, and you can get an A with some work. Definitely the professor you want for 2551
Cool professor. Very kind and understanding. Lectures are clear, and no surprises in the class. Helpful in office hours as well.
Excellent class with fun, engaging theme. Dr. Harrell is very understanding and easy to contact out of class with a quick email response time. He's fun and his class keeps you engaged!

Actually was 1102 but there was no option for it. Really good prof, super caring, chill , funny and good to talk to. He's lenient on due dates and will give extensions and honestly, if you put in any effort and do the assignments on time you'll get an A
Only thing is you probably won't get feedback until the end of the sem, but grades will be fine
Actually an ENGL1102 review. A chill professor with relatively easy grading. Wants students to succeed and gives interesting (in a good way) assignments. 10 out of 10, would recommend. :)

He is a great professor. He really cares for his students, and I would highly recommend anyone take him. Also, all of his assignments were actually pretty intriguing, and I enjoyed doing them. He is also a relatively easy grader and wants you to succceed.
He cares about his students!

Prof Randall cares a lot about his students and give us abundant time and resources to succeed in this composition course. He sometimes cancels in-person classes to make sure we have enough time to work on with the projects. Just one troublesome thing: he almost grades everything at the end of semester so feedbacks aren't instantaneous.
I love becky. theres a lot of work and participation is graded but it's very doable and takes no effort.

very passionate professor who cares about her students. her lectures are very fun and engaging and I actually learned quite a bit from this class. assignments are very easy to do and its very easy to achieve an A. if you're boring and dont want whimsy in your life then professor becky is not for you

Very nice and enthusiastic professor but does a little too much for health. Attendance is a pretty important part of your grade but she's a nice grader for assignments and you have 2 free skips. There's 3 big projects that happen at roughly the same time but you have like 2 months for each. Also you can get 4% on your final grade with extra credit.

Prof. Reid is a great lecturer who takes feedback and adjusts the class to everyone's needs. Goes through concepts and examples clearly and is easily accessible outside of class. Tests can be hard but they are standardized so they will be hard for everyone.
She was very caring and was easy to talk to. I would say the material is difficult on exams but her lectures make sense and help a lot.

I feel like exams are graded weirdly and do not accurately show your knowledge or progress. There is nothing that I specifically disliked about her, I just don't think she explained the material too deeply or explicitly.
It was obvious that she was new to teaching, however it seemed as if she really cared. Hopefully with time the teaching becomes a lot better and easier to understand.

This might just be me, but I personally had a hard time understanding Professor Reid's lectures. I'd already taken this class in high school, so I didn't learn anything from going to her lectures. However, whenever I did go to them, they explained simple problems in a complicated manner. The tests were always way harder than the lectures as well.
She's such a good teacher for 1551 and gives a lot of additional resources if you need it. She explains concepts well and has good handwriting.
Amazing Math 1551 teacher. Provided the best notes out of all the professors with easy to read handwriting. Super genuine and cares about her class.

Professor Ried is hands down one of the best Math 1551 professors out there. Her lectures are very entertaining and she always uploads her lectures with additional help if needed. Besides her lectures, she is very helpful in Office Hours. If you at least pay attention in class and went to Office Hours, Math 1551 is a breeze. She really is the GOAT!

Very chill professor. I went to about every lecture and at first she didn't use the screen and did everything on white board, but then mid semester she genuinely took the feedback from the surveys and switched to doing it with the screen. She's obviously new at teaching, but for a first ever semester teaching, she did a better job than most profs.
Super chill professor, really understanding of his students. Lectures can be boring if you're not interested in the topic, but prof is funny and is a nice guy.

Goated professor. Very understanding and willing to work with students for extensions, he just asks for clear communication. Grading rubric is very clear. Does ask for in class participation and you will need to speak in front of your class for certain exercises, but everyone is nice.. Brought class outside to be in the sun once! super nice
Really chill professor. Knows how to give a good lecture, and the topics were always interesting/kept me captivated. There aren't many assignments, and they're not that difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to talk a lot to earn the participation grade which I don't like. Overall she was okay.

Professor Silverman is a very sweet lady, she cares about her students a lot. The two main grades are tests and a big group project. The project isn't that bad, the tests require you to really know the details of the textbook though. If you really hammer the required textbook readings (of which there aren't a ton) it is a very enjoyable class

Professor Silverman's class was probably the most engaging seminar-style class I've had. She really cares about the material and wants you to succeed. You have to do HEAVY textbook reading and there is MAJOR group work (you choose the group), but it is very manageable even if you fall slightly behind
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: attendance and participation graded, great lecturer, learned a lot, tests were clear on content, in class group quizzes, big group project, highly recommend

Prof. Silverman was an amazing professor! She was very knowledgeable about what she was teaching and her lectures were super fun to go to! The test did require a lot of studying and reading the textbook was vital to doing well. Her test were hard if you didn't know the content well and they included an essay. We also had a group research project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor, Amazing person will teach you to be moral in your career !
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Silverman was passionate about the content of the class, which translated into her teaching. My main criticism is you HAVE to read the textbook to succeed in the class, and you cannot rely just on class lectures. Most importantly, she is nice and understanding if you need help.
Great person and professor, makes this class very interesting and knows what she is talking about. The class is a little difficult and attendance is mandatory, but great overall.

Professor Silverman is one of the best. She's perfect for Business Law and is very understanding, accessible, and a young professional herself so her lectures are very relevant and helpful. Her class is heavy on group projects, but she gives great feedback and really values class participation. There are readings, but they aren't 100% required.
She is a very caring professor. She encourages students to be engaged.

I had Prof. Silverman her first time teaching and loved her! She lectures from the textbook, which is mandatory to read. Tests come straight from the book and its case examples. She is kind of tough but is very passionate about the material and knows SO MUCH about law. Extremely responsive to feedback and really cares. Would take again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a good teacher that cares about you and your success. Tests are pretty easy to get a B but require more effort for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Despite the exams being graded HEAVILY at first (15% each) and all other work components being about 1-3% each, she gives a NICE curve at the end to reach an A. Exams are not hard AT ALL as long as u understand the study guides to the T. Would take again honestly, she isn't bad at all. BEWARE OF PULSE-CHECKS/POP-QUIZZES SO COME TO LECTURE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor took the time to help me understand math and pass the class so I wouldn't have to take it again. She cares about her students and what we learn throughout the semester. The best Professor in Georgia Techs campus

4 tests worth 15% and a final worth 20%. very sweet and willing to help you if you need it. flipped lecture & goes thru practice problems. comes up with some of her own tricks to remember things that actually help. would take again

She's literally the most unprofessional and unfunny person I've ever seen. She's the type of prof that thinks cussing while teaching a lecture makes her cool, but it got old after about the 150th time she did it. She just doesn't know how to teach and has the mentality of a middle school math teacher, not a college math prof.

I loved Stephanie's office hours because she breaks things down for you. She's a little more down to earth, but I've also heard her negatively discussing students in her class to other students in a gossiping manner. She referred to the students in question as "bad ones" that she wanted out of her class to make room for the "good ones."
