she was a bit rude toward students in the beginning of the course, lectures themselves move pretty quick, take notes before class, a lot of practice available so apply yourself and youll survive with an A. most students who didnt just didnt rlly pay attention in class, i think my grade mostly came from my math background so its different for others

shes a good teacher, goes thru problems pretty well but at times she does seem to rush thru it. its my bad that i dont ask questions, this last unit tho felt soooo rushed and i frankly am losing my mind for this test (writing this the night before said test). other than that, its just precalc so not a bad course.

Can't vouch for how she is outside of class, but she's a good professor. She usually breaks things down step-by-step, but might rush sometimes. Modules are organized and helpful. If you watch the videos before, you'll be set (though it's easy to catch up since notes are posted). Exams aren't too different from what you learn in class.

Her flipped lectures make learning almost impossible. She's a pick-me professor, she curses and pauses for laughs and applause from students. She doesn't teach well and is rude to TA's, which I think is entirely unacceptable. You essentially have to teach yourself the course and she lacks a lot of self awareness.

She is not respectful of TA's at all. She does not teach and expects you to teach yourself. You watch videos of her, but that's not teaching. She's relatively nice, but is so rude to TA's. Her grading is strange.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: An outstanding professor who cares about the success of her students. Stephanie Reikes was the best professor that I had this past semester. Her flipped lecture styles made her lectures more engaging. If you put forth the effort, you will do great in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class material is not hard at all and she is a pretty good lecturer but can come off a tad lazy sometimes in doing practice problems. Tests are heavy and classwork not worth much.

She's been my professor for the past two semesters, and she's willing to help you if you're willing to help yourself. Her explanations can be a bit confusing sometimes, but she was caring about making sure I understood her content and even made time in her schedule to see me and my friends for office hours a few hours before the final exam. Amazing
She provides so many resources to help you understand concepts to the fullest and is always open for questions to help you succeed in the course!
Ms. Reikes was my instructor for MATH 1111, 0999, and 1113. She's great. 10/10; very helpful, provides practice, and accessible outside of the classroom. She helps in any way that she can.

She was fairly easy if you attend studio and practice a lot! Her tests are typically cumulative so you have to make sure you understand each topic. There are a lot of resources provided such as homework, pre-lecture quizzess, and studios that will help you prepare.

prof Reikes is nice for the most part, but at the end of the semester she drops assignments that aren't worth much, so really be careful with your exams and make sure you don't fail those. She doesn't really give good feedback on assignments on gradescope, so you you have to ask her in person, and even then, you still might be confused.

I really loved taking her class its an easy A. Homework and all assignments are assigned at the beginning of a topic and due by your midterm so you have about a month to complete them. Review sessions are held before each exam and the exams are easier than the classwork. She's easily accessible 10/10 recommend.

She is such an amazing teacher. Super accessible outside of class, very caring, and makes it super easy to understand things. Does lots of examples, does review before quizzes which serves a great refresher, always post notes before class, and sometimes gave extra cred on tests. Would 100% take her class again. Lvl of difficulty is like a 2.5
She doesn't care if you have extreme personal or medical emergencies. Will not demonstrate care for you and gives minimal extensions despite hospitalization.

The class was quite easy, the way she had it set up. Choose a good group because that'll be like 70% of your grade going towards the final project and article critiques. Quizzes and discussions were super easy as well. Just stay on top of everything and you shouldn't have a hard time getting an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Recorded lectures which is nice. I'm not sure why this statistics class has coding in it (R), but if coding isn't your strong suit then get ready to study.

Dr. George left GT during the first quarter of the semester to accept a position somewhere else, but if she ever returns, 100% take her! Excellent, straightforward lectures with great pacing. Exams and weekly quizzes are pretty straightforward (quizzes are harder than the exams honestly), and homework is reasonable. Very accessible outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher again, very helpful for students, but course material is hard and mml... well... it was too much work, so... But nonetheless teacher was very caring, gave extensions, etc, and was just overall a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I failed the first time I took multivariable Calc with a different professor, then retook it with her and got an A. she explains well and just the important stuff. exams are fair and only tests what she teaches. very accessible

This professor is so accessible. Ive emailed her multiple times, as Im currently taking another class with her, and she usually responds in the same day. When I had concerns with the class, she met with me the very next day. Yeah, I made a C, but Im bad at math, and I was only 3 points away from a B (my best so far).

If there is any external problem (storm, Gradescope broken, etc.), she always understands and extends the deadline. She is very knowledgeable and proves it in lectures and fantastic online accessibility. Watch lectures: oftentimes midterms use the same questions with different numbers. We replaced our worst midterm grade with our finals grade.
She is very lenient with late assignments and she extends deadlines quite frequently.
no

Linear algebra is hard enough. This professor does not make the process any easier. Her teaching style is to go into irrelevant examples and to virtually skip the definition of ideas and terms. This makes understanding the foreign landscape of linear algebra quite hard to grasp. As this was taken online, her barking dogs were also not fun to hear
Professor George's lectures are generally very helpful, and it's clear she cares about her students. She dealt with the limitations of teaching during COVID very well and

His class is engaging, and he is very passionate about the subject, but some of the test questions can be pulled out of left field no matter how much you prepare. They don't always fairly assess the content harped on in lecture/PowerPoints.

Reinhard's lectures are really interesting and you can tell he genuinely cares about and is excited about the topics. The class itself is also just really easy as most of the grading comes from easy labs and online HW assignments. Overall great professor and I had a really good time in the class

Dr. Reinhard is very passionate about the material and makes his exams very fair. This isn't a hard class, but Dr. Reinhard makes it very fun and enjoyable.

The only negative was the HW and the labs, some labs were a bit too complex and some of the HW was way too long and boring (Argos, you will have to pay)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's very passionate and seems like a great guy, but his lectures were very boring and not engaging. Exams are open note and taken in class which was great, but our homework on Argos was very tedious and annoying to complete. Labs were okay, some were unnecessarily long and complex. But the TAs and Dr. Porter were very helpful!

HW was an easy 100 (trust me). The class was a little boring, which I hate to say because he is passionate and seemingly a good guy. Lectures are just him going over slides. I wish the labs had more experiments and less tedious questions on Canvas. The TAs were great, super helpful, and very friendly. The final project was easy and fun though!

Amazing class! The professor is so passionate and I really enjoyed lecture. His energy really came through it almost felt like he was bouncing with how excited he was to share his knowledge. As a CS major taking this as a required science I almost wanted to switch to EAS I loved this class so much. The tests were open note and not difficult.

Great professor. His class was not difficult. The labs were long and tedious but were doable. You don't even need to attend lectures. For the online and open-book tests, just prepare notes on the slides and you should be fine. Provide thorough answers for the labs and you should succeed in that as well.

Professor was engaging and explained things well. Notes and lectures lined up well with the tests. Labs were pretty easy and generally pretty fast. Definitely a low stress and pretty interesting class.

Prof is very passionate about the topics and makes lectures more engaging even if you're not interested in Earth Sciences. Very easy but somewhat time-consuming weekly assignments, tests are pretty straight-forward and open note (I used a shared google doc with my notes and those of all of my lab group and did very well). Labs are graded leniently.

Great guy, lowkey boring lectures but if you are interested in the course material I can see this class being extremely interesting. He is very passionate about what he teaches- just not my cup of tea. 
Long hard labs but usually TAs go easy on grading 
Do what you have to do and understand the stuff and you should probably get an A

Reinhard is an amazing lecturer and extremely passionate. He gives students everything they need to be successful. Overall, the class was really fun and I would 100% recommend taking this course as your science elective. Labs are long, but fair when it comes to grading. Required HW assignments can be time-consuming but are not difficult.

He's a very passionate professor. Though the material can be a little challenging, the class is set up for you to succeed with open note/canvas tests and straightforward tests. The labs were mostly easy but seemed pointless. If you need a random lab science take this, especially if you are not a stem major.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went to every lecture but it's not really mandatory. All tests are open notes. There are two midterms and then the third midterm is the final. Reinhard is literally so enthusiastic about the stuff he teaches. I would 100% take a class by him again. The only vaguely annoying thing was Argos which was the weekly homework assignment.

The class is mostly just optional lectures that he posts the powerpoints for as well as online homework once a week that takes about an hour. The exams are in-person, online, and open note. Class felt very easy and he wants you to succeed. Labs can be a little bit tedious but you'll get through it. Easy A and took about half a credit hour of work.
Super easy class and interesting lectures!

Dr. Reinhard is very passionate about the material and a consistently good lecturer. Assignments arent difficult and theyre more interesting than most classes. Dont forget to do Smart Sparrow (online assignments) like I did (I have goldfish memory)itll put you in a pickle

Lectures are clear, informative and covers a lot of content although it often repeats stuff from the previous lecture. He is very passionate about the topic, which makes class slightly less boring. He also posts slides and lecture recordings online. Easy lab science credit.
Good solid choice for an easy science class at Tech. Smooth labs as long as you have a decent TA. Enjoyed the course as a whole.

Chillest class at Tech you'll probably ever take. Gives sincere and informational lectures with true passion, but most of the class isn't paying attention because he has a tendency to repeat the information from lecture to lecture. Still can learn a lot if you're interested. Tests are ridiculously easy.

This class was one of the easiest you can take at Tech. The lecture content was interesting and Professor Reinhard clearly explained everything. The labs did drag a little bit because they were basically just filling out a packet, but they normally only took around an hour. I would highly recommend this class to anyone.

This class was so much fun, especially since the material was great and well-laid out by the power points. He made the long lectures fun and loves to show pictures of radioactive burritos, so that's a plus. The 2 essays in the class were graded nicely, and the tests were mediocre to easy, if you took good notes.
Professor Reinhard lays out the material in a clear way; lectures are very straightforward and well-organized. Overall, the class is very easy; just going to lectures will likely get you an A.

Passionate about the subject he's teaching and makes the material very easy to understand. Show up to labs (which are very tedious), pay attention in class, and review his powerpoints for a good grade in the course

Chris was a great Professor, and even though the subject he taught was pretty boring, he did a great job keeping me entertained and focused. I went to 75% of the lectures and just read the slides and studied practice tests and was fine

Professor Reinhard is an unbelievable professor. He cares a lot about his subject but also wants his student's to succeed. Tests are straight from the power point. Show up and listen, and you will pass. Show up and put some effort and I guarantee you will get an a.

Super easy and accessible lab course if that's what you're looking for! Chris is engaging, he puts things in very clear terms, and his enthusiasm for the subject shows. Also, he's hot af, doesn't hurt.
Tests were very straightforward, lectures were very entertaining and I highly recommend!
Literally the easiest lab on campus. Also, Chris isn't hard to look at.

Your grade is based on 2 midterms, final exam, and labs. All the exams were very straightforward that tested to see if you understood various scientific concepts. I only attended 2/3s of his lectures and found the tests very easy by reviewing his lecture slides the day before. You could probably skip most of the lectures and still manage an A.

A hard Georgia Tech STEM course is when you work tirelessly & sleeplessly, only to still feel like you failed miserably. An easy course is when you can guarantee an A by putting in a lot of effort.   Reinhard's class is even easier than a Georgia Tech STEM easy. Listen during lectures and review the slides right before the test. & boom. An A.

Easiest lab science at GT. It's a huge lecture hall class, but he gives great lectures. He is very passionate about his subject, which makes his teaching more interesting. Labs are on the computer and usually only take 1-2 hours. Only 3 tests (including final) and are concept heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Reinhard's class was easily my all time favorite class that I've taken. His lectures are extremely interesting and as long as you go to lectures, pay attention, and review the slides before an exam I guarantee you'll get an A, and that's not asking for much considering it's tech. Seriously, best professor ever.

Dr. Reinhard is one of the best professors I've ever had. He's passionate, extremely intelligent, and knows his stuff. Lectures are super fascinating. He even gives extra credit. It's great. His exams are not difficult if you attend lectures and read the lecture PowerPoint slides. Labs are easy too. Loved his course.

Although it can get boring at times, Dr. Reinhard is a great lecturer. He engages the students and speaks passionately. Super nice guy and very accommodating if you have questions. Powerpoint slides that are used in lecture and posted on T-square reflect the tests. There aren't any curveballs-pretty straightforward! Best professor for EAS1601!

Chris is a great lecturer, and I could always tell that he cared about the material was presenting. I really liked how he structured the course, and the tests reflected his lectures very closely. I always went to his lectures, paid attention, and got an A without much more effort.

This guy is the greatest professor of all time. He's a really genuine and cool guy who is extremely passionate about what he does. He gives phenomenal lectures and is very explicit with what he wants. If you study the slides, you'll do well on the tests. The only homework we got was two writing assignments, which were pretty fun and interesting.

Teaches with clarity and enthusiasm with a obvious passion for his field. His tests are fairly easy with the right amount of studying and effort, of course. The tests are derived directly from his lectures so be sure to attend and pay careful attention! He never includes nit-picky, purely factual questions rather, the exams are more concept based.
probably taught the easiest lab science on campus

All the lectures are pre-recorded & on his website. Homework questions are straightforward & are directly out of lecture videos. TAs are quite helpful. End term is usually waived since the class has 10 HMWK sets. Easy A if one goes through the lectures well. The course provides excellent coverage of optics, and I would strongly recommend it.

Took the grad equivalent to his undergrad course - PHYS 8803 RT. All the lectures are pre-recorded & on his website. Homework questions are straightforward & are directly out of lecture videos. TAs are quite helpful. End term is usually waived since the class has 10 HMWK sets. Easy A if one goes through the lectures well. Great coverage of Optics.

I think that the video format of this course feels odd because it is being forced into a lecture shaped hole. I didn't mind the format for this course, especially for an intro course. I think the videos are great and Trebino is a nice guy. The grading was relaxed and only dependent on HWs and a Final Project. There is usually a midterm.

Completely useless. I used to go to every class only to be sat in front of a prerecorded lecture like it was 6th grade science and I was being forced to watch Bill Nye the Science Guy when the teacher didn't want to teach. But Bill Nye would actually be preferable in this case because at least then I would actually learn something.

Lectures are very engaging and helpful; he's always around to answer questions! Not too much interaction with him because the class was asynchronous. 5 homeworks and a final project, but not graded too harshly. Would definitely recommend!

Class was remote and asynchronous, but he made the most amazing PowerPoint lectures I have ever seen. He explained difficult material well but did not do enough example problems. He's knows the material well, but wants you to go to the TAs for any questions. Sometimes inserts a VERY liberal lean into physics lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rick knows what he's talking about, and he puts a ton of effort into the class. His lectures are the highest quality I've seen. There are 5 homework sets and 2 tests. The homework makes you think, but he and the TAs are available to help. Overall, solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Trebino is super smart and knowledgeable, but he kinda overestimates students' knowledge. He loves to tell you interesting, complicated things you're not expected to know, which means less time going over what you have to know. Your grade is just 1 midterm, 5 homeworks, and the final. Content is tough but he definitely knows what he's talking about
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Trebino really makes you think. There are some oddities, certainly, but I have truly come to enjoy this course. HW is heavily analytic, while tests lean toward concepts. He instructs his TAs to grade very leniently, and you will more than certainly need to go to office hours. Look @ frog. gatech for more info. I took P/F but expect an A or B
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor with a hard modern physics class.
Lecture may get “boring” at times as it usually doesn't directly relate to assignments, but an interesting class and great professor nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof. Rinehart is very passionate, but she can also be very strict, is not afraid to call out and raise her voice at students for being on their phone/talking in class. The 3 sketchbooks are not difficult but are time consuming and graded harshly. They're due immediately when class starts, if its 1 minute late she will call you out in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Michelle's lectures were genuinely interesting & VALUABLE for us architecture students. Lectures become warzones for staying awake if you're not genuinely interested, so take notes, draw, etc! You're graded on 3 sketchbooks + 2 digital assignments that give you a month each, so PACE YOURSELF! Your grade depends on your time management + attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had the opportunity to really engage students during their first year but instead chose to show us a slideshow every day. Weirdly timed (5-6pm) so kind of hard to be engaged. The assignments were lengthy but not hard at all. Not super nice to put into portfolio once you're past first year. Weird about sick excuses. Shes not bad per say.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class only has a few assignments. You have a month for each; just pace yourself. The actual class is just her talking about architecture and buildings. She prefers us to just sketch during class. She will like you if you actually engage with her in class.
She was weird. Content was interesting.

The professor made lectures bearable by sharing personal stories about some of the places on the slides and strongly encouraged class engagement. You are graded only on work outside of class, which is time-consuming but straightforward. All assignments are graded based on completion and effort, so getting an A should be easy; don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are amazing! She gives a lot of work but it isn't hard work, as long as you do what is asked you'll get a 100. It seems intense but it really does a great job of teaching you how to quickly sketch. She truly cares, she even made my class brownies!

I actually had her for ARCH 1060, but that was not an option. She took attendance in every class. The lectures were helpful to gain architecture knowledge, but they were not required to get a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took History of Architecture in the Late short summer session. This was a hard class to cram into a 5 week period, and the class lectures were virtual. Lectures got repetitive, but Rinehart is caring and dropped a quiz at the end of the semester to boost many of us up to an A. Summer session composed of 4 main quizzes and many opinion essays.

Architecture studio, in general, is a lot of work, but Michelle is probably one of the best critics of the freshmen studio. She rambles a lot, but she gives great feedback. Critics care about your grade, but Michelle goes a step beyond. If you ever get her, congrats, but just be ready to hear an extreme amount of stories.

I took her class during the summer. We had 5 open-note tests and a final. I didn't use the textbook at all. Its very lecture heavy so DO NOT MISS A CLASS. Anything that she says in lecture is fair game on tests. She's very energetic and knows her stuff. She's been to almost every place that she talks about in lecture. Very inspiring.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class definitely requires you to pay attention in class every single second because you will be quizzed on everything. Michelle does care about her students success and if you need help, she is accessible. With the right amount of effort, this course is very easy. The book is not required but does help supplement lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about biology and does a good job explaining the material. The exams are not too difficult as long as you do the practice problems and go through the lectures. There is some work outside of class to prepare for each lecture but it does help you understand.

Dr. Richards co-taught 1108 with Dr. Birol. Richards focused more on the plant and fungus concepts. Although my area of focus is animals, I preferred Dr. Richards' lectures. He is a passionate speaker and clearly loves biology. I went to only 70% of the lectures (mostly when Richards was teaching) and got a comfortable A in this class.

richards is a very approachable man, and is also very clearly passionate about what he teaches which makes the class more engaging. however, sometimes he would struggle with finishing the class on time because the lectures were so slide heavy and have so much content to go through. very approachable guy and also clearly cares about the students.
A great professor that had clear expectations for students. Just make sure to attend class and keep up with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Richards clearly cares about our well-being and does not overload us with content or homework. 4401 is a great intro stats class. Last exam was tough though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very beginner friendly and did a good job of explaining a wide range of topics for bio stats. Made the information very digestible and provides everything students need to be successful in the class.
pretty bad lecturer, not very helpful. bios 1108 average gpa dropped 0.18 (5%) as soon as he starting teaching with linda green.

Class used online free textbook. Attendance was technically taken through a short participation quiz meant to be answered during lecture time but it always closed at 5pm so you could just take notes from the textbook and posted slides if you wanted to skip lecture. Also, the lab component was very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Robbie Richards, was by far one of the worst professors I have had as my time as a Georgia Tech student. The class is not terrible but there is a lot of homework and reading that I highly recommend if you want to do good on the tests. He is very rude and unfair when it comes to certain things. Wouldn't take a class with him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good lecturer! Approachable and happy to help. Class was textbook/content heavy, but tests and final exam were easy.

Co-taught with Dr. Linda Green. Nice and respectful, answers all questions. Memorization and detail heavy class, stay on top of reading. 40% of grade free from Learning Catalytics and writing assignments. Final is easy and touches on more broader knowledge.

One of my favorite professors at gatech so far! His class offers a very clear, very beginner-friendly introduction to R. The lectures are very informative and while you technically do not have to attend them, the slides themselves can be dense and he walks through them very clearly in lecture so I would recommend attending class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Richards is very kind and willing to accommodate students. I had an excellent experience when I had an emergency and needed a makeup exam. Accessible in office hours. Engaging lectures with organized lecture slides. Clearly very passionate about material. Class is memorization heavy, so stay on top of material and read textbook

I had Dr. Richards for BIOS 1108. While I liked his personality, the class relied on Learning Catalytics, which I found unhelpful. His lectures often missed key content in the learning objectives, leaving me to teach myself after class. The learning objectives were the most helpful part, guiding my focus on relevant material outside of class.
Great prof! love his class
Helpful and friendly. Exams are take-home and a little difficult, but are worth very little compared to homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Forgiving class structure with 1 test drop, 1 HW drop, 5 quiz drops, and 5 in-class ?'s drop. Exams have two parts, both take-home. Part A has to be taken during class time and part B has to be submitted by the end of the test week. Helps you learn the basics of R and lectures were helpful and engaging. He is also nice and approachable.

Thoroughly enjoyed this class. Prof made the content interesting with the examples & problems. Exams are different, but easy while covering what we did learn. Low-stakes way to learn R and coding for research and grad school. "Textbook" was pre-class readings that were clear & concise. Engaging, funny, & knowledgable- highly recommend Dr. Richards.

He clearly cares about his students' success not only in class but also in their future careers. Grading is structured so most of the grade comes from participation and HWs (which are also mostly graded on completion). Exams are open-note and include a take home portion. He tries (and accomplishes) to make statistics accessible and comprehensible.

Dr Richards is super understanding and flexible. The class is very laid back and he makes it easy for you to succeed. The tests and homeworks are easy and the grading scale provides a lot of cushioning. Definitely one of the best professors I have had at Tech!

Made the class very passable and straightforward even if you didn't understand the material. Lectures did feel fairly rushed and the slides' material was often hard to follow, but he made up for it in office hours. Very nice and receptive to feedback/advice on how to structure the class going forward

Goated professor to have for year 2 studio. Understanding and willing to work with students for extensions. Way funnier than you'd think. Good with communication. Only con is a slight understanding gap of software so he thinks it's easy to change 1 thing. Might tell you to change your idea late into the project. Unclear grading scale. Likes simple.
Charles is a super sweet and funny guy in Arch2211. Class was mostly lectures with two exams, one final, and then a project. Overall, pretty fun time.

Had him for 2211 and 1016 and he was very good. He does NOT understand digital tech for Arch, making 2016 a pain. Constantly changing his opinions on your design, liking it, and then switching up last minute. Hard to get helpful feedback. Heavy workload but a decent grader.

ARCH1016 is a difficult class as is, but the projects are interesting. Prepare to spend LOTS of time in the studio, working on projects. Understands mental health and workload struggles and is willing to work with you. Takes an adjustment to critiques and criticism, but they are just trying to help, and it works. Perfect professor for difficulty.

Architecture major required. The guy is funny and casual with lectures. Understands student struggles and is willing to work with you for deadlines. Study guides are really helpful for the quizzes, and the projects are relatively easy. Projects have optional extra credit, and sometimes quizzes did. Enough resources were provided.

If taking ARCH 2211, wait till your second year. Projects rely heavily on your ability to work in online software like rhino, adobe which is not taught first year. Not much homework except two large projects. ATTEND CLASS. I skipped maybe 5 and my grade dropped a letter.

Rudolph is great, but the lectures can be boring. There is a weekly sketch due Tuesday mornings, 2 tests, and 2 projects. For the projects, it is helpful to know some 3D modelling software like Rhino 6 or Revit, as well as adobe programs like illustrator, InDesign, or photoshop for finalizing drawings and renderings.

Rudolph is a good teacher, his lectures are interesting as long as you are into learning about materiality and notable buildings. The class takes attendance and you cannot miss more than 3 classes otherwise your grade will drop an entire letter (which is what happened to me). There are two big projects, one done with a randomized partner.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Racist.          .
Great professor, but demanding. Learnt alot

Took his fall semester class, did not do well. Retook it in spring... looks like someone higher up let him know that his failure/drop rates were too high. He was completely different in the spring semester. I walked away with a high B. You will have to work, and he does collect HW, and his final is 50% of your final grade, but its not too bad.

Nice guy but the class is structured terribly over the summer. Three separate textbooks as assigned reading for each class and the actual class notes don't follow any of them. Class provided materials to study with are the handwritten notes done in class, which are incoherent outside of the context of class. You have to teach yourself everything.

He effectively taught all the concepts in the class. His exams were usually directly copied over from the practice exams with some crucial changes. There was one 3-4 question problem set every other week. There was 5% extra credit on the final grade by pop quizzes which were easy. The recitation helps to understand applications of topics in class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly knowledgeable but sometimes hard to understand sometimes because of the accent. Took it over the Summer so it was definitely much easier than normal. Had tons of extra credit and tests were not that bad.

He talks very slowly in lectures but it's clear that he really knows what he's talking about. The class is mostly just projects which are pretty interesting. 1601 should be a 2 hour class instead of a 1 hour one but it's still not that much work overall.

Obviously very knowledgeable and is a good prof, but doesn't really care about 1601. Hard to reach outside of class, and kinda boring tbh. Would defiantly take him again for another course, and he wasn't awful, but take someone else for 1601 if possible.
Pretty dry in lecture but ultimately a good guy and fun class (though more like 2 credits instead of 1)

Dr. Ruffin is very competent and good at explaining things, but he talks so slowly. Tests didn't always feel like an accurate reflection of what we spent lecture time on, so make sure to double check what's on the formula sheet because exams aren't open note.
He had very clear lectures and it was overall not bad. Homework was long but very useful to the test go to recitation if you need help the examples are useful

Ruffin's lecture notes are amazing which makes the class a lot easier to comprehend. He does give you a lot of homework, but the practice helps you a lot for the exam. He has a wack homework grading policy where you either get a 100,50,or a 0. This actually ends up helping your grade a lot, as you only need to get half of the homework right for 100
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were decent, but the pace he took made it so we had to review the last few topics by ourselves. He wants you to understand the material, and he's lenient in giving partial credit on tests. If you make sure to do every assignment (and the online discussion EC), attend every class, and ask questions, you should make a solid B or A.

You might think that AE1601 is supposed to be a nice and fun intro course, well not with Dr. Ruffin. I almost fell asleep for every lecture as he is super unenthusiastic about the content he teaches. The class is not hard and the projects are fun but would not recommend the professor.
If you go to class and understand the material, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was kinda funny. Didn't make the projects or homework too difficult. There is extra credit if needed. I would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever met. Not easy, but his standards are clear and he gives you everything you need to at least pass if you put the work in. Lectures are fairly lighthearted and engaging.  The homework and tests clearly stem directly from material covered in class, especially from topics specifically mentioned in lectures.
Avoid if possible
Does not care about students.
Mean spirited person.

Great Teacher and very clear during lectures. You print them before class so you can just pay attention to what he teachers. If you just pay attention in class, do your homework a week in advance! and study his lecture notes you will get a B or A for sure... The book is kinda useful but not entirely... Quizes are 6% each...
He knows his material and i liked his teaching. You have to work hard for your grade and know but not too hard. HW is very important

He is a decent professor in the classroom, but his grading policies SUCK! HW policy -- 100, 50, or 0. Either an A or an F. He has this polocy beacuse he doesen't really grade the HW. Watch the tests, there may be problems from sections of the book he did not cover.
No Comments

Each homework and exam were weight equally(around 14% each iirc). I liked the homework assignments as they were very application based, but my issue was the tests being purely conceptual. Normally this wouldn't be an issue if the assignments prepared you are them, but they did not.

Homeworks were worth around 70% of the final course grade. You were given 3ish weeks to do each of them. Asking TAs for help in office hours did change a lot. 

Content wise, the homework assignments and the exams felt a bit disassociated. The exams were very math and conceptually heavy but both the midterm and final exam did have generous curves.

The exams felt fair and received a generous curve. The professor is smart and kind, though clearly overqualified. Note that homework is long and worth 15% each, so be very careful with hidden test cases. I recommend visiting office hours to have the TAs double-check your submission logic and test cases within gradescope.

I got 100s on every single assignment, I got 100s on almost every single quiz. I had a hard week and took a final, i needed a 0.25% bump to my final grade and the prof denied it. could've showed some compassion towards the rounding.

Great professor, who clearly knows what he's talking about. Lectures can be conceptually and math heavy, but it kind of helps the learning process because you apply it to a situation in the homeworks. Homeworks can be long and hard but you are given about 3 weeks to do them, exams are in person and tough and wish there was more practice for them.

You're kind of thrown into the deep end with exams. No organized prep material and you really have no idea what to expect. Final was kinda cooked ngl, but everything else is fine. Dude definitely knows what he's talking about.
Good lectures, fun homeworks, but HARDDDD final exam. Unfortunately, Riedl will likely not answer a question on Ed Discussion if it was brought up in lecture. Otherwise great professor.

Course content is manageable, but be ready to teach yourself everything via textbook, lectures are confusing and tend to confuse more than educate. Homework is questionable, but professor himself is good. Just the course layout itself is terrible.

Also, basically upload no content online, so if you missed it, you missed it. No exceptions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class structure changed. There is now in person midterm and final. He did not give any practice exams. He gave sample questions but clearly stated it does not have any correlation with the midterm and final and only for our understanding. There was no help and guidance with how to properly prepare.

First half homeworks based on a very broken game. Second half was better after using jupyter notebooks. TAs could never get the autograder to work, always got different results locally. Nothing difficult, just terrible headache-inducing assignments. Exam q's were very subjective. On Ed, Riedl kept responding "answered in class" even to yes/no q's.

Took him for both 3600 and 7632, great professor with clear lectures and records notes (unfortunately lectures aren't recorded). As some reviews have mentioned, there's sometimes problems with the autograder, but if you procrastinate, you should be fine. Only complaint I have is that he switched to in-person exams this semester.

Puts in the bare minimum for this course: doesn't resolve issues that students are facing with the game engine, assignments (which seem to be recycled for nearly a decade) sparsely have autograders, and responses to student questions are often met with: "answered in class".
Avoid Riedl like the plague. Even Starner is better! Him and the TAs provide no support and their assignments are broken.

Riedl is lazy and doesn't even check his assignments. The autograders often don't function and game engines don't run as the instructions claim causing confusion. This class is a waste of time. Don't take it.

Riedl is lazy. He refuses to respond to questions on ed when they point out errors in his assignment. Avoid him at all costs. Further his TAs aren't able to help much. You will be on your own for this course - teach yourself the material and do the assignments with broken autograders.
He cannot teach to save his life. The TAs barely understand the assignments. So disappointing.

Projects and Exams for Game AI are easy to do well on, as long as you put the requisite amount of time into them. Helps to have friends in the class as some collaboration is allowed. I ended up relying on the autograder more than I'd like to get full points on some of these projects. He released some lecture notes via a One Note shared to class

Prof Riedl is a really caring and taught very well. The assignments were decently tough but was able to struggle through them. I wish the TA's helped more, but it is what it is ig. Beware of the exams, the midterm was pretty rough. Spent around 8-9ish hours doing it, ig its take-home for a reason. Overall a good prof, but be proactive.

I think if you don't show up to class it will be easy to fall behind.  Translating the lectures to code is definitely very difficult since there is little coverage of actual code in class.  The take-home midterm took me about 6 hours (pretty difficult), so just be aware of that also.  Professor Riedl himself is a great teacher.  Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The assignments and midterm were all awful and incredibly unclear. Learning the concepts in lecture did not help at all with the assignments, and most of the difficulty came with the opaque library used in the assignments. The TAs answer questions like they are not allowed to help, even if the questions are just for clarification. Prof is cool tho
assignments are rewritten and auto graders aren't even given so you cant even iteratively correct your code. if you try to get direction from TAs, they straight up wont help. no support in this class

The assignments are being rewritten so ignore all past posts now. Testing assignments is a nightmare, TAs are too lazy to even build an autograder and expected outputs for assignments aren't posted either. There is little to no support.

There're too much extra credits which you can loop up online and easy grading with assignment made it too hard to obtain not A. I got 60-70 for both midterm and final yet got 97% overall grade. Group collaboration allowed for exams. Awesome professor in explaination and great course material delivable.

The lectures were not closely related to the projects and the online notes were almost useless. Fortunately, the projects came from from UC Berkeley CS 188 which uploads their notes and lectures for free. Midterm and final were not very well made and were too vague for many questions. Collaboration was allowed.

The class is easy. Autograded projects make up 60% of the grade and are not that time-consuming. Project wrappers made up 10%, which explored the applications of AI in the real world. Midterm/Final are take-home with collaborators allowed. There is so much extra credit with the projects that you can fail the midterm and final and still get an A.

Stopped going to lecture after project 1 due to the disparity between what is taught and what is expected. The textbook is very good though. You will get a lot more out of this class if you took stats beforehand. It is very easy to get an A so long as you are a competent programmer. Interesting material, but not sure it justifies a full course.

Pretty easy class, projects do not line up with lectures, requires reading/outside research, easy A otherwise, take home exams (two total), and four projects with e.c. opportunities, lectures very not very informative so I stopped going
Lectures don't line up with the projects, but he's a good professor overall.
Amazing Lecturer, Reasonable HW's
"addressed in class" or "covered in class" is all he says. laziest prof ever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Riedl for 3600 and liked it, but I was very disappointed in him with Game AI. His responses in Ed Discussion were extremely unhelpful (says 'addressed in class' for everything instead of taking 5 seconds to write an actual response). The lectures were really boring. The HWs are time-consuming. The only solace is that the exams are easy.
passionate lecturer, engaging material. the lectures don't completely line up with projects which can be frustrating. take home exams
Good lecturer, explained things well. The tests were take home and a lot of the grades came from projects which had extra credit.

Fun projects and lecture content. Great intro to AI, taught very well. Extra credit on almost every assignment and only 2 take home tests (collaborators allowed). Lecture notes are a bit hard to follow but that shouldn't matter too much if you pay attention to class.

Riedl is an amazing professor who clearly cares immensely about his students. Lectures were fun and engaging throughout the semester, even if they sometimes felt disjoint from the projects. Lots of extra credit + take-home exams made the course a breeze, but I still felt like I was learning quite a lot. If only Tech had more professors like him.

Really solid choice for 3600. Tons of extra credit (you can probably end up with up to 110%) so as long as you start projects early, the course is pretty easy. Exams were open collaboration and released 3 days before the due date which was plenty of time. Riedl made lectures engaging and added some jokes which made attending worthwhile.

Riedl is a good choice for intro to AI. He does his best to make the lectures engaging and throws in jokes here and there. Attendance isn't required, and a lot of the projects they assign are already out there, so overall it wasn't a difficult class. He gives a take home midterm and a take home final, which made it a pretty low-stress class.
Good experience overall. We were graded on 4 AI projects written in Python. The midterm and final are straightforward. Start the projects early and you'll be fine.

One of the best professors at Tech. Funny, caring, engaging, knowledgeable, understanding, I could use so many positive adjectives. Lectures were great, homeworks fairly easy. Class material was very interesting for me and made me eager to take more Intel classes. Projects are not the greatest tbh, poorly written but that's Berkeley's fault.

Dr. Riedl is absolutely amazing. He is probably the most hilarious college professor I have ever had. He attempts to make the class as easy as possible (Take-home, open-note exams), and there are a lot of extra credit opportunities on the projects (I got a 25/17 once for gosh sake).

If this is your first exposure to Artificial Intelligence, Prof. Riedl is an excellent professor to have! He breaks down a lot of the rather difficult topics this class can have into simpler, digestible chunks. Some of the projects are rather poorly written, and overall, projects can be time intensive, but overall, excellent class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is genuinely a great man. He is a great professor who teaches the class well. This is my second class with him and showed the same amount of care during both the semesters. He understands these are stressful times and will adjust due dates to help relieve stress. His lectures are very entertaining. We had 4 late days, projects & take-home exams.

Truly an amazing professor. Genuinely wants you to learn the content of the class, and puts his heart into the lectures to make them interesting. Inspired me to pursue a career in AI. I wish I could've taken at least one more class with him before I graduate.

Professor Riedl is the best! Lectures are entertaining, and he's very enthusiastic about AI. During COVID, he was very understanding, and most of the grade was projects with lots of extra credit and an autograder that would tell you your score. Tests were take home, and you had several days to work on them. Easy A if you put in effort. TAKE HIM!!!!

Dr. Riedl is a really understanding professor - he gave us 4 days to submit work late without any penalty. The exams were collaborative and take-home. Overall, if you start early on the projects and do the extra credit, you can definitely get an A easily.

The quality of Dr. Riedl's teaching does vary a lot between alright and great depending on the topic. That said, Dr. Riedl is by far the most understanding and compassionate professor I have had in college. Getting a good grade is easy, but you will also learn a lot. He also shows a lot of understanding for issues that may affect class performance.

Dr. Riedl cares about his students, always answering questions and empathizing with us. The tests were collaborative & open-note, and the projects all had significant portions of extra credit. The projects are graded by an autograder, so you can edit till you achieve the grade you want. He's a good speaker too, and the lectures are interesting.

You can tell he cares about students and their wellbeing inside and outside of class. His lectures are actually worth watching, he gives good understandable examples that make it easy to understand difficult concepts, and does not expect live attendance (can watch later). I appreciate his efforts to cater to the current pandemic situation.

He was an interesting lecturer and you can tell he really cares about the subject. Very fair amount of work throughout the semester, as long as you pace yourself and don't procrastinate. Had two take home exams, but that was because I took it during the pandemic. Planning on taking another course from him, definitely recommend.
Made both exams take-home and collaborative; plenty of extra credit opportunities. Great guy overall.

Good professor with a great depth of knowledge and passion for what he teaches. Is very flexible with the course schedule, lots of extra credit, straight forward exams. The class is approachable and he does a good job staying focused on you learning, rather than just striving for grades. Only downside is his handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had some personal issues crop up a few weeks before the pandemic hit and school was moved online. In both cases he was extremely accommodating and understanding of the situation. He cares more about the well being of students over their grades, which was especially appreciated since GATech did not have the Pass/Fail option.

Through out this Corona virus pandemic, he was the only light in my life. He assured me that I would still be graduating. Even prior to the pandemic, he gave us enough opportunities to submit assignments late since frankly, sh!t happens. If given the chance I would like him to adopt me as even my own father was not this kind to me.

He is the most caring professor I had at GT. He wants every student to succeed and will go to any extent to make sure they do. He was happy to explain things to me and make sure I understood the content. His priority is his students learning and I could feel that in every lecture. I highly recommend taking his class.

I think some of these ratings are a little harsh, I dont think he was bad at all, although the class is the Berkeley class and the projects come directly from them. The class still had a solid structure and he taught the material well so I really dont care if it mocked another schools course. 4 projects and 2 open note exams including the final.

Yea why is this prof allowed to even teach at GT? 1. He copied Berkeley's CS 188 course. 2. He didn't copy it well - half of the content was cut out and I just feel that I haven't learnt anything. 3. Doesn't know how to lecture. Makes stupid mistakes all the time. Is super slow and going through content. IF YOU ARE GOING TO COPY, COPY WELL!!

Poor lectures. I fell asleep in most of them. His only course notes are in handwriting that looks like Aramaic, and he gives contrived examples and backtracks on them. Also, the course is a copy of CS188 from Berkeley, but in a haphazard way. Office hours are all the way in CODA.
Copied Berkeley's AI course but made it worse

His lectures were wonderful. Lots of opportunities for extra credit, which really helps to offset the difficulty of the midterm and final. The autograders used for the projects allow one to know what they'll get on the project before they turn it in. Start your projects early! Overall, I would recommend anyone take this class with Professor Riedl.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer and explains the topics very well. The homeworks are easy and all come with autograders. It is also possible to get enough extra credit to take a 0 on the Final and still get an A. His tests are reasonably difficult but nothing exceptional.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fantastic as a professor; lectures are usually worth going to. he also posts his notes online for you to catch up if you miss a class. Specific for CS 3600, projects are given with an autograder, so you know what you'll get before you submit. Overall, a really solid choice.

Dr. Shandler is THE best professor you can take at GT. He is very passionate about what he teaches and I loved the dynamic duo aspect of him and Dr. Bailey co teaching the course. If you attend lectures, you can easily get an A and he WILL inspire you to learn more about the human dimension of cybersecurity (title drop).

prof shandler is my favorite professor i've ever had at tech. explains content incredibly, everything is easy to understand, test matches content, jokes are genuinely funny. pay attention to lecture not bc the tests are on it, but because it is so engaging and interesting. genuinely so fun and ive hated most of my cs classes

Shandler is the best lecturer I've had a GT. Classes are fun and interesting. Exams perfectly reflect lecture content and readings. As long as you study the slides and do the assigned readings, exams will be a breeze. Essays ae also part of the grade. Definitely one of my favorite classes at GT.

(CS 8803) I took his class, in Spring 2024, prior to getting the CS 3237 official name.  Really interesting material and taught really well. Our semester we only had  three papers and a Final paper. Each paper could be related to any of the topics discussed in class, and we were given freedom to analyze any topic in relation to a real world event.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Shandler is a genius whose passion for the subject is contagious—I was hesitant on cybersecurity before taking 3237, but after taking it, I knew this is what I wanted to do. For the most part, the class is a breeze as long as you're paying attention and read extra, which you'll want to do of your own volition anyway. Take if you want to learn!

Honestly an absolutely amazing professor. I have never had a better and more interesting lecturer than Shandler. The class is debate-based. No one is required to talk, but there are many discussions (student-teacher discussions) in class and it's overall an amazing class. If I could give him a 10/5 on RMP, I would. Love the professor and the class.
Most interesting prof you will ever take in your uni career.

Very sweet and caring professor. His lectures were amazing and engaging, but at the same time relaxed. Class engagement was good. There were a few quizzes and a final, but they were very very manageable and straightforward; the content was applicable to my work-related stuff and I loved it!

This class was AWESOME! I usually learn by doing the homework, but in Dr. Shandler's class, I seemed to automatically learn just from being there (if that makes sense). The lectures are engaging and very interesting if you enjoy cybersecurity. I particularly enjoyed the unit on randsomware, RaaS and Conti.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely, a great dude and professor! Made the class interesting, even more so, considering attendance is mandatory. A lot of papers, but clear expectations and fair grading!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. No homework, only 4 exams (all of which are easy if you memorize the lectures). Mandatory attendance but beyond that very relaxed class. Would take again.

Shandler was teaching this course for the first time it was offered. He did very well and is an amazing lecturer. I was very invested. No homework, no assignments, only 4 exams and a final as of Fall 2024. Deals for heavy reliance on test taking, but the exams were very easy to go over the slides before to review. Great class, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far one of my most favorite and best professors I have had at Tech. His lectures are engaging and very interactive. And he always remains open-minded of everyone's viewpoints. Most of the class's grade is dependent on the exams and finals, but they are not too hard to prepare for for the most part. Attending lecture and read slides :)

Professor Ryan Shandel is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are very engaging, and he explains topics in a way that makes you think and easy to understand them.  Attendance is important because the tests are mostly based on what is discussed in class. Grades are based on four tests, attendance, and a final exam.

Very responsive to students & advice, engaging. He's a good speaker and made lectures enjoyable. The grade was basically just attendance, end-of-unit exams, and the final. Exams contain stuff from readings that you have every week, but besides that, there is little work to do outside of lectures.
This is a new class and likely to change.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor who is extremely passionate. He makes it very fun and easy to learn from him. The class is not super difficult as long as you go to class.

Great lecturer! He tries to keep the class energetic and entertaining as well. One homework a week - purely a completion grade. Tests are similar to the practice exams and are graded leniently. You can skip the final if you are happy with your grade after the last midterm.

THIS IS FOR COE3001. He is a fantastic professor especially in terms of student engagement during lectures, very energetic. His lectures and notes are very helpful for exams, which are graded pretty fairly as well. If you understand the material even an average amount it is easy to get an A.
The actual goat.

Class was pretty on par for a 3000 level. No exams but there are unit quizzes, however, these are graded pretty tough. There are also group projects that are graded roughly. Professor Sherman was great though, tried to make class as engaging as possible. Overall, great class!
Fairly accomodating and energetic, but the course is a little to rigorous compared to other 3000-level courses. Tough grader especially on weekly quizzes. Decent guy, but nothing to write home about.

Solid professor and a great choice for statics. Very reasonable with students and respecting of students' opinions. I think his course could have been a little bit rigorous, but I still got a lot out of it.

Really enjoyed the class and Dr. Lively's teaching. This is a very useful class and you learn alot. Spend time on learning the topics and HW as the exams are heavily testing your understanding. Exams are take home, there are pop quizzes once a week,  so make sure you review what was taught on the previous class before you show up.

A really great course with great lectures. You will learn a lot of mass transport. The HWs and exams were really practical and helpful.  Dr. Lively is really accessible. Try making use of the office hours.

Grades things so late. Never gives feedback. Forget about getting your grade back for the final because he doesn't release it. He is very unreasonable when it comes to grade participation. He will give you a 0 for participation if you don't stay to pick up your graded quiz, in his logic, not picking up the quiz after class = absence.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No clear grading criteria & no feedbacks for projects/HWs, grading is always so late that it was impossible to know what to expect and improve during semester, he lectures bare minimum and expects so much from group projects w/o clear instructions. Participation was graded on criteria that was not on syllabus. No final exam score disclosure.
Amazing guy, super helpful
I am taking Lively for CHBE 2801, but the clarity of his explanations would make him an amazing choice for any CHBE class in my opinion. I hope to have this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Had Dr. Lively for 2100 and then Thermo II. Homework was optional, but highly recommended, with very heavily weighted tests (a partial grade replacement policy, though) and weekly quizzes. As with 2100, the tests were very hard (but fair). He is an outstanding lecturer too and is very approachable. If you have the chance, take Dr. Lively's class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Difficult tests. Favorite class I have taken so far.

Really great professor, who does very interesting research as well. His class is not at all easy but sets you up for success in future CHBE classes. He assigns 2 homework problems due every lecture, which keeps you practicing every day, and does 2-hour evening test blocks to reduce time pressure on exams. Has good lectures and provides screencasts.
He's good
Tough

Took his lecture in the spring a bit worried because he was so new, but he is genuinely one of the best professors at explaining the concepts of calc 2. Always super helpful with questions after class, gives great feedback if you have questions on a test problem. Often goes over problems in class that will be on the tests.

He was such a good lecturer for 1552! Just as good as Grodzinsky in my opinion. It was a linked course so he didn't really have control over the difficulty of the tests/other assignments but I managed to get an A in calc 2 without having taken it in high school. He's also very nice/accessible and has a good, dry sense of humor.

I was worried because Dickmann was new but he exceeded all expectations. His class notes were one of the best! He explains the content superbly and repeats to sink it in (he does tend to not notice raised hands). Always available in office hours and post-lectures. Midterms are fairly easy. Buy mymathlab for easier homework. Final is optional!

Dickmann is a very good 1552 lecturer. He uses slides which he sends out and they are very helpful. He knows how to explain concepts and if you go up to him asking questions he will be able to clearly explain it to you. He will also give hints about what's on upcoming tests and help you with asking for any regrades. I would definitely recommend.

Was able to effectively teach the components of Math 1552 and took time for questions frequently as well. Didn't grab my attention as much as other professors, however, and didn't engage me that much.

Didn't have Ryan but went to his lectures. If you're someone who picks up things fast and likes math, he is the goat. If you're someone who needs a little but more time, he isn't the absolute best. His teaching style is more casual and conversational as opposed to rigid, up-and-down teaching. He is the test GOAT though and prepares you amazingly.

Very helpful guy, who while not the greatest lecturer yet (he's barely taught for like a year), is really great at explaining stuff one on one, and cares a lot about making the class as easy and stress free as possible. His notes are great, and I appreciate him asking about and trying to help students feel better about the class and tests.

Honestly, a really nice guys that's just getting started with teaching -- I took 1552 with him last sem (his first one teaching), and I think he might be downed for not being the best communicator yet, but he's getting there and he really tries to help and relate to students. Super helpful 1 on 1, understanding, and excellent resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really nice and approachable guy. His lectures were sometimes confusing but he did really know what he was talking about. You could tell he really cared for us as students and wanted to help us out. The only thing is his lack of experience tended to hurt him. Somethings here and there were a bit odd or poorly done but overall a decent professor.

Lectures are not mandatory, and he posts all of them on canvas. However, recitations are with a 5 point quiz given during every time. He is clear when teaching and is approachable outside of class. He will sometimes walk around before lecture asking students how they feel about tests and other things. It's easy to tell he cares about his students.
My friend attended my lecture on the last day of class as a joke and proceeded to tell me that was the worst lecture he had ever attended.

He is a new teacher so I will give him some of the benefit of the doubt; however, he struggled giving lectures to the point where 80% of the class would stop showing up and just teach themselves the material. He does write good notes which was what I used to study for basically everything.

The best professor I ever had in architecture by far. Cares about and respects her students, goes above and beyond to teach us in comparison with other professors in GT Arch. Feedback was helpful and clear, helped me improve and learn. Listens to students' ideas and gives direction/constructive criticism. Such an amazing person and teacher.

Loved the class! Ryan is extremely nice and is always willing to help if needed. Some assignments were quite time-consuming, but they got easier towards the end of the semester. The annoying part was that the attendance was taken very seriously.

Roark is one of the best Architecture teachers at Tech. Very knowledgeable in the field and is constructive when critiquing, not destructive. Take her if you can, you're lucky if you get her in studio. Rounded my 89 to an A.

Ryan is great! She is very passionate which makes her interesting to listen to. The assignments were not too hard but took time. Overall, the class was not too stressful, and I learned at lots of the basics of architecture that I would otherwise never deep drive into. The TAs graded all of the work, so your grades deepened more on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hollister is great for this Computational Mechanics course. It will give you an introduction to both FEA software and continuum mechanics. The homeworks towards the end of the semester get harder, so use his office hours to get your simulation working.
In quality and regulatory issues, Dr. Hollister gives very long lectures. The class is a semester long project with quizzes over the content mixed in. It can be boring but I liked it overall.

Dr. Hollister is a very caring professor, but do NOT take 4803 Image-Based Tissue Modeling. The class does not teach you particularly relevant information for anything in undergraduate BME, and the homework is extremely frustrating. Dr. Hollister is very approachable but often disorganized, and this class is very confusing.

Very engaging, presents info clearly. Attendance not mandatory and slideshows posted online, but some info is only from lecture. Does review before exams. 3 exams (noncumulative) made 75% of the grade, the rest was from 4 short essay assignments. Up to 5% in extra credit and CIOS bonus offered. Exams are mostly MCQ but test on small details.

decent lecturer and pretty enthusiastic about what he teaches, but he wouldn't know the answer to a lot of questions. the exams are 75 percent of the grade and is fairly challenging but honestly doable. one confusing thing was there were no review session for the first exam even though he himself admitted that first exam is always the lowest.

If you can't learn from nonstop lectures, avoid this class. No study guides, no interaction, and poor explanations. Meeting outside class doesn't help. Unless you write every word (impossible), you'll be lost. Exams are 25% each ,unfair and stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Moffat's biopsyc was difficult, yet I would still take it again. He is very willing to help and answer any questions and break it down until you understand it. I did not have any background knowledge for this class and still succeeded. If you take this class be ready to study and ask questions. I definitely suggest it. Lectures are amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Moffat is so great. He is such a kind, intelligent, and caring professor. He accommodates for students all the time, and will outline exactly what you need to do to succeed in his class. Strongly recommend him to anyone!

one of the best professors i've ever had at GT. he was super caring about all of the students and would start class about 3-4 minutes late because he knew people had to come from other classes. tests were a bit difficult, but it's mostly memorization of concepts covered in class. need to go to lecture to be able to get all the info from lecture
Dr. Moffat is such a kind and amazing professor! He offered so much support and was an amazing lecturer. He is such an amazing professor and I loved the class. I would take again if I could!

Biopsych is definitely one of the harder PSYC classes, but if you attend class and study the powerpoints very well you should be fine. The powerpoints he uploads are pretty skeletal so you need to attend class to fill those in. Overall, pretty good!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Moffat's class was really enjoyable. The material is super interesting, and he does his best to make the lectures entertaining. The class is heavily based on a few exams which require memorization, but it was not too bad if you really study and attend class. He provides the slides for note-taking which is also helpful. Would take again!

One of the nicest professors I have ever had at Tech! His lectures are very engaging and does his best to answer every question in detail. Exam structure is fair (3 + final) but may be a little challenging as they're based on rote memorization.

I had Dr. Schatz during study abroad and he is a great professor! He really wants students to do well and understand the content. He made sure to know everyone's name and overall a nice guy! His lectures can be difficult to understand if you do not attend lecture or pay attention in class, so be sure to do that!

As other reviews mention, he does tend to let a few people's endless questions dominate class for a while. However, he explains stuff well (in my opinion) and is very friendly. He's very accessible before and after class, and overall a great person.

Really nice guy. Gave us his number at the beginning of the class and I reached out to him multiple times during the class. Always happy to meet and explain difficult concepts, especially before exams. I reached out after doing bad on an exam and he worked with me to improve future exam scores. Could not recommend enough.

I wasn't the biggest fan of his lectures because he spends a lot of time deriving formulas and spends less time explaining the applications, although he does that a bit as well. However, if you take his class I recommend his youtube videos. They're much shorter and honestly more helpful for understanding than the lectures. Super nice guy tho.

While Schatz is an okay lecturer, he has a HORRIBLE habit of letting irrelevant questions dominate his class. He needs to be much better at shutting down questions that are out-of-scope or too theoretical – a student should research such questions on his own time, and Schatz needs to make this clear. Especially since attendance is mandatory!

Schatz gave everyone his phone number on the first day of class and said to call him on nights or weekends if you have a question about physics. Physics 2 is hard but the class is structured for students to succeed and Schatz has good lectures and even more importantly keeps up with the schedule of the course (from what I've heard most others lag)
My favorite and best professor in the world!!

He will explain concepts as long as you need and the class is a choose your own grade where at the start of the semester you decide the weights and how the grades will work and at the end you meet with him and reflect on how you did.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online. Due to the setup of it, I never saw or met Schatz. But the online format seemed easier than in-class. There were 5 labs, which were making videos (easy A) and 2 tests, which were pulled straight from GPS, IPS and old tests. Not tricky. 1/3 of grade comes from online meet ups with TA and 4 students. Hard to fail this class

Schatz is a solid choice as far as physics 2 professors go. His style of notes works well for me and he is usually easy to understand except for some really difficult concepts. However, he had a tendency to get impatient with my class at some points and snapped at us a few times.

I thought PHYS 2212 was very easy with Schatz. His lectures focus more on concepts than problem-solving, which may or may not be preferable for you. Funny, up-beat guy. My advice here is mostly course-specific: focus very hard on trying to get a 95-100 on one of the exams. The weighting system will get you very far. Don't miss lab ever.

Schatz is pretty engaging for slightly boring material. Class is much easier than they make it out to be and they have ways to try to help you pass like weighting tests and stuff. Classes are pretty standardized. Schatz was pretty good about reading the room for when people really didn't understand and his notes style worked for me.

Schatz is fine. He is an engaging speaker, but my interest in his lecture style waned over time. He uses a pen and tablet on OneNote to write out very bare-bones notes during class. This means that it's difficult to go back and glean any real conceptual stuff. The class is hard, but it's doable. Lots of weekly work, which can be annoying.

Schatz had good lectures. Information was presented clearly. Tests are tricky, but topics are always clear. Must know how to think critically. I approached him for help several times throughout the semester and he was not very helpful (redirected to other people/no direct answers). Overall teaches well but doesn't care about students personally.

Good professor, always made sure we understood any material before moving on. His lectures are always energetic and clear, though they tend to focus on specific problems to apply concepts learned, rather than giving definitions then an example then moving on.
Great professor. Explains the material very clearly. Course has clear expectations and you will definitely be prepared for the exams if you go to class.
Fair grader and relatively interesting class. Would take again over other professors.

The course is very well organized and expectations and rubrics are layed out right from the beginning. Schatz is great at explaining the material and very willing to help you if you have questions. Definitely suggest especially if you don't have a good background of physics knowledge.

I loved physics until I took this class. Schatz doesn't actually teach anything, because all of his "lectures" are videos online. Lab is terrible. He isn't really approachable, and you work extremely hard just to get a b or a c. Avoid his flipped classroom for sure.

Don't take him! He used lecture videos to teach us. Regular class meeting is actually like a TA section. Every Friday I had a quiz, which counted as one-fourth of the midterm grade. EVERY WEEK!!! Lab every week is painful, with tons of work to do before lab and video lab reports. You have to make a presentation for each lab.
