Great Teacher. Really good at explaining material. Always willing to help a student who puts effort into his/her work. Very interesting!!

I'm not the typical genius at Tech, so thought the class was hard. Prof didn't really help with his too easy SRS questions and examples. Loves to call on people who aren't paying attention. Doesn't round up grades even if its one point away, but I guess that's all phys prof. Annoying as hell and bullies you when you ask a question.
Really good at explaining material. Very helpful when it comes to answering questions. Can contact him at anytime and he will always call(/skype!) you back.

Horrible! Seemed enthusiastic at first, but you realize he doesn't teach what you need to know to pass the exams. My friends and I tried to seek help from him, but he wasn't inviting at all. I remember one horrible episode in class, he singled out students in class that shared answers and made them stand up in front of the class. Horrible! Avoid!

He is incredibly energetic, but his energy overtakes the lecture almost the entire time.  He breezes through the complexities and focuses on the easiest elements for most of the time. I appreciate his enthusiasm for physics, but I'd rather actually learn the complex concepts than only have a basic understanding when the tests are quite complicated.
Took this class 3 times, all in all this class is easy except for the tests are VERY ambiguous. The multiple choice questions will be nearly all the same. Disgusting

This class is tough, but he is a decent teacher. Teaches the concepts, but not enough test like problems. If you were actually a student that wanted to learn physics and didnt care about your grade, he would be a good fit. Tests are tough.

Easily the worst professor I've had.  The multiple choice tests are horribly unfair.  The example problems he will work are far easier than anything on the homework or tests.  His explanations are slow and meander.  Very unwilling to work with students.  Really, just awful.

a bit eccentric, but makes class interresting. very picky about people talking in class. class attendance is a part of your grade, so make sure you pick a good time! overall - pretty good teacher, but the material makes it hard
very concise and to the point, clearly explained  concepts.
Very good professor, explains the material very clearly.  PRS quizzes are very helpful in preparing for the tests.
He's a fun guy who explains the material in understandable terms. He goes over the exact material on the test and provides memorable examples.
good teacher best not at 8am b/c attendance is required but he goes through the type of problems that are on  tests, very helpful

Attendance in  his lecture is required, but this is not a good thing. Because if you want to do well in physics at tech, a good professor is essential, and Schatz is really good. People go to him instead of their own lectures.

Acts like she has something to prove with how legitimate astronomy is as a subject. Yet, simply reads off of incredibly dense and boring lecture slides. Tests are based on random fact memorization, almost impossible to study for. Astro 1102 is one of the worst classes I have ever taken, and absolutely killed the love 8 year old me had for space.

She seems to have the mentality that many people brush this class off, and she wants to make sure it's being taken seriously. Tests are lots of memorization, but you also need to pay attention to her side comments/hints, because those often become test questions (OH can help with figuring that out). Much more work than I was wanting it to be.

Dr. Schmidt was great. Lectures followed the Drake equation for estimating the potential for life outside our planet. If you're into space, you'll enjoy the class and if you've had any exposure to the topic before, you'll probably get an easy A. Not a super rigorous class, covers the basics of a lot of things. Not much math, all VERY simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The class is terrible. The tests are purely memorization and don't test anything practical. Do not take.

Only had 3 exams including the final, each exam more unfair than the last, often asking bad rote memorization questions like "what's the age of _____" and asking questions about things we barely went over in class. Labs are easy, so hopefully those boost you enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Interesting person, good lecturer, tough grader.
She seems like someone who is just here for research and doesn't care about her class much. She's passionate  about the content but lectures are pretty boring.

Prof. Tsikata is very caring and helpful. For fluid mechanics, whilst attendance isn't mandatory, you will really be screwed if you miss a lecture! Also, the lectures themselves are quite long and have SO MUCH material, so I personally found it difficult to digest all of the information and feel comfortable for the exams.

Homework 40%, 2 Midterms 15% each, Final 30%. Lectures were boring, and slides had a lot of information, but not all of it was necessary. Grading took forever. Concepts were difficult, but she was nice and cared. A seemed impossible after M2, but there was a lot of extra credit at the end to get points back on the midterm and a curve for the final.

Dr. Tsikata is a great human being. Her lecture slides can be somewhat uninspired, but she deeply cares about her students. I learned a great deal in her class. She is very busy, so she may seem distant at times due to this. I would recommend her still.

Short Answer: Only take if you don't want to learn the subject or want an easy class. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU WANT TO LEARN.

Dr. Tsikata is by far my least favorite professor I have had at GT. She does not care about you or teaching. She showed up late to class routinely and constantly had excuses for severely delayed grading and posting solutions.

Often unreachable and condescending. She's straight up said she wouldn't respond to emails after I told her she had missed mine for a couple weeks. The one midterm we had was overtly difficult and no one finished in the allotted time. The content wasn't bad but the professor made it worse than it had to be

Dr. Tsikata clearly knows her stuff and does some really interesting research. She also clearly cares about her students and will be helpful during office hours. That being said, she is also clearly still new to teaching and relied almost entirely on reading off of powerpoint slides for all of her lectures. Easy homework and more challenging exams.

Even though this was her first year teaching, this professor clearly showed she was well versed in the material and could answer any question that you would have about Jet Pro. She was super helpful during office hours, and her grading policy was super helpful.
He's very caring and willing to help you. The lectures are boring, but I like the way he proves different theorems, which is much clearer than the textbook.
Not good. Took him for 1554. Watch Warnock's videos and you'll do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was not super great. Kinda hard to understand and the notes were basically illegable. I would def take it w another professor if u could. Tests made up 75% of the course grade so prepare for those. The TAs carried the class

I think I am in love with the professor: Shunyu is the Wan for me. His teaching assistant Shunyu Two was also very helpful.

On a serious note, his lectures were very interesting and engaging.
Kinda hard to understand but the tests are a lot easier compared to other sections. Just watch someone else's lectures if you don't understand him and take his class.

He handwrites his lectures, and I could never read his handwriting. Genuinely, please take another professor. I watched Jankowski's videos. Take Jankowski's lectures, please, he really is the linear god.

He's hard to understand first of all. I'm not giving him a 1 just because he seems like a nice person and will answer any questions you have. People stopped going to his lecture for a reason. His lectures don't really make sense even though he follows Jankowski's almost exactly. Just watch the Jankowski lecture videos if you end up in this class.

MATH 1553 sections have common curriculum, so the instructor's abilities and preferences did not shine through. MATH 1553 closely followed the in-house Interactive Linear Algebra textbook, which was the basis for the lecture notes (which is why the lecture notes feel like they were copied). Instructor has really bad handwriting.

After the first month of class I ended up skipping his lecture to go to Jankowski's. His lectures feel like he is copying someone else's notes. I can tell he is knowledgeable on linear algebra but he has a hard time conveying it, which made it hard to learn. Definitely use the textbook, it outlines things clearly.

Underrated professor. All MATH 1553 sections are the same and online lectures are posted by the course coordinator. By the end of the semester only 10/150 people came to his lectures but I liked them better than the videos. Lectures were admittedly a bit boring but not bad and I think will only improve with more experience. I will be taking again
THE GOAT!!!!! best professor ever!

Not a very harsh grader and is very flexible, and only one paper in the entire semester. Themes change every semester, but from what I know, his topics are pretty cool. Cool projects and we watched Pride and Prejudice as well as Sherlock! Did not take a lot of time out of my week, and was genuinely interesting stuff.

His class was so cool and just let us have some freedom in responding to adaptations and creating things like movie posters. He also enjoyed the stories he taught but let us have our own thoughts about them. He lays out activities really well and the schedule is posted for the whole semester. He should teach more Poe though.

If in doubt take Professor Caddy. I took his class with other hard classes and I can say for sure it is an easy A+ class with less out of class work. Attendance is 10%, Artifact 0 is 5%, Artifact 1 is 15%, Artifact 2 is 20%, Artifact 3 is 25%, and ePortfolio is 10%. Preparation and Participation is 15% of the total grade however it's on canvas.

Super nice guy who definitely loves literature. You get three "free" absences if you need them. Super responsive through email and very understanding if you need an extension or experience some issues with technology. He would've probably liked me more if I participated in class, but that didn't keep me from getting A+ on the three big assignments.
If you're wondering who to take in 1102, just pick Dr. Caddy. He always helps students develop mediocre ideas into good ones. Put in some work, and this should be an easy A.
Funny, kind, helpful and makes class interesting. He didn't shoot my ideas down but talked to me about how to fit them into the class projects. Just very down to earth. Good guy.

He had us do such cool projects all the time! Got to build a web page, shoot a video, and record a podcast -- not a typical English class but learned a lot. He's very nice too and enjoys being in class.

The undisputed GOAT of 1102. I literally did two projects about basketball players and he gave me 100s. Entertaining, caring, super light workload but still useful. If you don't pay attention much, you'll still get an A. If you care about English/Lit, he'll make the class entertaining. Save yourself and take 1102 with this guy, please.

Best English prof in my opinion. The workload isn't crazy and as long as he can see that you're putting effort into the class you'll be fine. Also very understanding & helpful and not strict about late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy who enjoys what he teaches. Easily my favorite class. The reading isn't too bad and the writing work is actually productive so I don't feel like I am just doing busy or difficult work for no reason. I would recommend.
Super easy, understanding professor. Not a lot of work and he's so chill. 10/10
Awesome guy, class was always helpful even if it wasn't super intense some days. Not as much writing as I expected but plenty of different work to do for projects like a video and group podcast.
I FW him heavily

Very chill professor who understands your struggles outside of his own lectures. The course itself is made entertaining and not burdensome. He's very passionate and understanding in those regards, and overall it comes out to be a good experience and easy grade.
Super awesome guy and a chill class. Lots of time in class to work on projects so you don't have to stress about it outside of class. Not difficult but definitely fun. Take him!
Very easy professor but very boring. He grades super easy so it was an easy A but not exciting to go to class. The textbook that's "required" is not actually required, save yourself the money.

He's very understanding and is willing to accommodate as long as you communicate with him. His course theme is very interesting, and he's a chill guy. As long as you put in the effort, making an A is very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Caddy is clearly passionate about what he teaches, and he delivers interesting lectures on interesting topics. He also clearly understands that 1102 is not students' top priority, so he doesn't assign much work outside of a few projects during the semester, which only require a little effort to get a good grade.

Very kind, caring, understanding, and respectful professor. Enthusiastic about his class and you can tell he loves to teach. Gives you a lot of freedom and all you need to do is put some effort in to get an A.

Absolutely lovely class. Such a respectful and kind person. I didn't write an essay or read a book the entire semester. Let us do our projects on essentially whatever we wanted within reason. Take him!!

Dr. Caddy is very, very chill and enjoys being in class. Take him if you can. He won't make you do a lot of busy work but you will have work to do. Gives you time to do the work in and out of class so nothing too crazy. Kinda cute.

Dr. Caddy is great. He understands why students take his class (need credit). He's relaxed and chill and a relatively easy grader. The class is 3 projects, an essay, a video presentation and a podcast project. No final and honestly if you do the work and put in some effort, you'll get a good grade. Should be an easy A.
He was a really chill professor. If you follow the syllabus and show that you put effort into the projects and essays, you'll do fine.
Very smart and empathetic, cares about his students and how they are doing in class and outside of class. Subject matter is dry sometimes but he makes it fun.
This is definitely a fun class in some ways; he definitely wants you to care about the material but in your own way. Easy to talk to and very relaxed with grading, though he gives good feedback too.
He's a good dude, that's all you really need to know. Cares about his class and how well everyone does, not difficult but you do have consistent work to do.

Wish I could take Dr. Caddy again but he only teaches composition courses. Really good when teaching short stories and poetry and clearly invested in his students. He does give a bit of reading to do for homework but easy enough to do since you just get to work on the readings in class and the assignments. Very funny and down to earth too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall great professor, he gives extensions on projects if you really need it. He is really kind and funny; class discussion days were my favorite.
Great class and professor!! He is nice and kinda funny in a dry way, very clear expectations for assignments.

Dr. Caddy can talk for a significant portion of class but his theme about outliers and outlaws is really interesting. He gives extensions when necessary and grades leniently. English is not my favorite subject but Dr. Caddy made it more than manageable and easy to get through.

Dr. Caddy was great; the course theme was a bit all over the place at times, but very fun and he gave us a lot of time for each project. Group project as well but it wasn't too bad. You can work with folks you already know well. Would take again!

This is is a pretty cool section of 1102, but definitely heavy on reading material. Not all of it applies directly to your projects, but it can if you want it to (gives freedom in topic choice). I would take him again because it's just so clear he cares about his students and what he teaches. Very quick to respond to email and is always nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: For an English 1102 class at Tech, I'd say there are better sections to take. The work is easy, but attendance is mandatory. He can talk for quite a bit and you just zone out. There's a lot of reading that happens, but it is not necessary to complete the projects.

Dr. Caddy was great! He made my start of college so much easier than I expected, and he truly cares about what he teaches and his students. I would take any class with him as I know I will learn and enjoy it too. Assignments were not too bad. Each one is different so you do have to be on your toes, but the process is clear. Highly recommend.

Dr. Caddy was great! Obviously cared about his students and their well-being. All assignments had clear rubrics and were not too time consuming. Attendance is mandatory but you get some unexcused absences. Would highly recommend!
She's very nice and cares about her students a lot. Take English with her for your sanity, especially if it's your first semester at Georgia Tech.

Professor Shree was my favorite professor by far this semester! She is so passionate, interesting, and understanding. I am by no means a English major but she has a way of engaging you and making you want to contribute in class discussions. HIGHLY recommend her class, it was an amazing experience!
I LOVED prof Shree. She is the chillest prof. If the class needed an assignment pushed back, then it was. The most understanding and fair grader out
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Shree was a phenomenal professor. She cares about course content and genuinely wants students to learn. She sets clear expectations but is flexible. Her classes aren't boring and the assignment structure is good. I looked forward to attending class because of this. She cares about students, allowing extensions and flexibility if needed. 10/10!

Lectures are pointless based on what the class is mainly about. There are pop quizzes, so you're basically forced to go to lecture at 8 am... Now the rant: I hated how the comp ended this year, since it was based on a coin flip (even though it's in the rules). It was unfair for the teams that worked hard all year just to lose to a coin flip.

It felt like he brought up a horrific crane disaster or someone dying in almost every lecture, which was only loosely related to the topic at hand. 2110 lectures are kind of pointless, but he was pretty entertaining. Go to lecture in case there is a pop quiz.
8 am lectures on 2 days, pop quizzes for  5%, boring lecures. terribly managed group project+ competition that absolutely drans your time but that's more a flaw of the class itself
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
ME 2110 is always tough if you don't have a great group (which was the case for me). Singhose is an entertaining lecturer, but I did not enjoy the lectures as he tends to ramble a LOT - especially at 8 AM...
Pop quizzes make up a portion of the grade, and they're based on things discussed in lectures (lecture slides posted). Large curve at the end.

There's no other way to put it: this class is a LOT of work. Regardless of your professor be ready to spend countless hours in the shop perfecting your machine. Singhose was always energetic during lectures and included insight from his actual projects. Don't worry about Singhose so much as your section prof who ultimately determines your grade.

Poorly designed class. Grading criteria is always extremely vague, but very specific things are expected. You will learn very little in Singhose's class, but you'll spend far more time than you ever have in a class. Competitions are poorly designed to where a lot of it is left up to chance.  All the machines and parts they give you are bad quality.
He is a very good professor and lecturer. I know the main lecture guy changes each semester. I say, make sure you get Singhose. If he isn't teaching, wait till next semester.

The grading system has so many useless components that bring down your grade as compared to a usual ISYE class. Lessons were fun, but lectures were useless. Slow in grading, slow in answering Piazza questions, not very empathetic with students.

Mohit is extremely intelligent and caring, but optimization w him was difficult. This course was very lecture-heavy and he taught at a pretty rapid pace (+ hard to understand sometimes). Typically there were weekly quizzes, a midterm, and a final all of which were very straightforward. There was a lack of communication and organization though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mohit was AWFUL and not transparent. The class was unorganized. The TAs were lost due to the lack of communication. Mohit purposely made the final hard because the grades were too high because he gave out too much extra credit. The final average was a 62. Grading was harsh and inconsistent for quizzes and exams. He never responded to my emails.

Dr Singh taught modelling first then algorithms which sparked my interest in the purpose. Our project prompt was more thought-provoking than previous semesters. He explained simplex as if we already knew it and then re-explained it better the next classes. Grades on Canvas were very disorganized.

Awesome guy, super smart. Class is difficult but fair, no surprises on exams or quizzes. Can be hard to understand him sometimes, but lectures are interesting and fun, and he really cares. Highly recommend Professor Singh for 3133!

Any 3133 review that suggests professor Singh is anything less than difficult is not a real. Singh is very caring (you can get an A) and extremely intelligent, but so much so he leaves students and even PhD TAs in a spin by the speed of his thought and work. *First semester he taught 3133. He previously strictly taught PhDs and 4133.
GOAT. Straight up. Caring and good lecturer. Not gonna get a better professor than this tbh.

Dr. Singh is insanely smart, that's why he just assumes everyone can keep up in his lectures. We are graded by difficult weekly quizzes and 2 exams. Even the TAs are surprised by how difficult he has made the class. I go to the TS's office hours when I have questions, and half the time, even they can't answer them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, he was a decent professor. I found his lectures to be very theory/ notes heavy, but he tried his best to explain the material in alternate ways. The quizzes were usually just one or two questions multiple choice which I found frustrating (probably due to online school.) I would take him again and ask more questions next time.

Really good lecturer. Gave me a much better understanding of topics from 3133. Was willing to move deadlines if the class felt like they didn't have enough time. His one flaw is that he only taught for the first half of the semester

Grad Algo already is quite hard, but Prof. Singla's grading helped make it easier. His lectures are good if you are locked in, and he will go over concepts multiple times. He records too. HWs are not that easy but the grading is pretty lenient. Exams are challenging, with a crib sheet, and ramped up in difficulty. Dropped lowest exams and HWs.

Proof based exams count for a big portion of your grade and are pretty intense due to the short time limit, but prof allows you to drop your lowest exam. Lectures are decent, but the homework is where the real learning happens.
Prof Singla was a decent lecturer but his psets were pretty difficult and had issues. He was pretty nice and was always approachable after class

Probably the most condescending professor I've ever come in contact with. Literally laughed at the faces of 2-3 groups during their final presentation. In class, proofs make little sense and there's no context given - just thrown at you. Zero feedback ever, the only saving grace are the TAs who are constantly apologizing for him.

Not the greatest lectures due to Singla's handwriting and sometimes messy explanations, but he is a fine teacher if you are prepared to come to class daily and focus. There was a significant curve at the end which allowed a lot of students to get an A. Pretty difficult homework and some test questions were too difficult for a 1 hour testing period.
Very lenient grading. If you put effort in the homework and study for tests, getting an A is doable. He is very kind and curved the boundaries such that an A was an 81.5 and a B was a 71.5...
Hard but rewarding. I personally liked most of his problems (though not all), although his exams were still intense.

Singla was definitely one of the CS 3510 professors of all time. The class was exam heavy. The practice exams are absolutely not at all what the actual exam will be like. The homeworks are fine, but you would probably need to rely on outside sources and friends. I benefited a lot from the generous curve (68.5+ was a B).

I took him for 3510, but it would only let me select 3511. Homeworks were tough and could be time consuming, but tests were generally easier than the homeworks. Grading structure was generous and he curved the class end of semester

Generous curve at the end, textbooks are very useful resources for certain units. Homeworks are fairly hard, but going to office hours helps a ton. Do not expect helpful responses on Piazza or helpful exam review sessions since the TAs seem very disorganized; lot of self studying and practice to do well on exams (which are weighed heavily)
Good guy and if you put in the work, you'll get the grade you want. Difficult homework but exams were ok.
Difficult class but lots of resources provided. Very generous curve at the end.

I took 3510, but there's no option for that

the exams range from requiring simple usage of things done in class or coming up with your own ideas. They're  exactly what an exam at Georgia Tech should be like. The homework can be a bit ridiculous sometimes but it isn't that large a portion of your grade. TA's typed notes taught me everything.

Took CS 3510. His problems are significantly harder than other sections, and he's an okay lecturer. HOWEVER, his curve is insanely generous - 75%+ of students will get at least a B. With a curve that kind it is really hard to do bad as long as you try. Take him if you're fine not getting an A but getting a virtually guaranteed pass
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took CS 3511 in Spring 2023. Dr. Singla is super knowedgeable about the course content, and I thought his lectures and homeworks were really interesting. The tests weren't too difficult, either. Definitely one of my favorite classes I've taken here!
I took 3511 with professor Singla in Spring 2023 and had a good experience. Students complaining about his exams would not pass any problem-solving based software interview.

This class gave me severe depression and imposter syndrome. I can't believe his slides are painful and messy and he leaves everything as a "trivial proof". I can't keep up with lectures and homeworks are theoretical and hard, and tests require you to have a eureka moment. Got destroyed by graph algos and not looking forward to 4510. FML.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homeworks were very annoying and tests were nothing like practice tests or homeworks. TAs were useless and harsh, and lectures are disorganized and impossible to follow. Our only hope is a curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were terrible and lectures were hard to follow. TAs were completely useless and homeworks were long and hard. Not to mention that exam review sessions are also useless. Singla is under the illusion that he's teaching 3511, the harder version of 3510. Taking 8 am with Perkins would require waking up super early but might be worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst experience

Brutal, impossible class that hit me hard. It took up too much time and I couldn't sleep well or enjoy life because of 3510. Also office hours were pretty bad, and taking this with 2200 was a daily struggle. I really wish there weren't so many proof and theoretical questions and that exams had less questions. Screw those who think the exam was fair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Singla is the worst prof I've had. His TAs are unreasonable graders and take off points meaninglessly. Also, lectures slides are hard to follow and I got pretty much zero help in office hours. Someone who taught 3511 would certainly make 3510 harder than it should be, right? Ngl this course makes me regret doing cs, coming to gt, and being alive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is harder than before, and the homeworks are all proof-based. I really do not enjoy this class because lectures are hard to follow and office hours are useless. Only Piazza is helpful, and you have to work with other people. I want to drop out of GT taking 3510
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gave a ton of proof and theoretical homeworks that consumed my life. He's trying to weed out students (mostly juniors) and the course really makes me hate myself. I got so stressed doing some of the proofs I had to cry. Had trouble following his lectures notes and office hours were entirely useless. This course is basically grad-level algo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took 3510- each test was worth 20% and people ran out of time on exams. Homeworks were theoretical and proof-based, and office hours were useless. Rubric was often wrong and lecture notes were handwritten and hard to decipher. Spent 20+ hours on this course, and it's worse than 2200. This course should only be required for theory thread imo

Sahil is a caring professor who listens to students and gives many chances to succeed. 5 HW, 2 open-note exams, and he drops your lowest homework and lowest exam. HW is tough and you should start early.
His lectures go fast, but he covers a lot of interesting material and is more than happy to slow down and answer questions.

In my 5 years at Tech, Dr. Singla is the most difficult one I've had. To start, be prepared to Google every homework. The material he teaches is very high-level but the problems are down to the details. He does communicate quickly, but vaguely and just generally unhelpful. I learned later that a 40 in his class was a B. I would avoid his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Silva, although seems to enjoy teaching and is passionate about chemistry, doesn't convey the material very well to students. Just reads slides, and sometimes is wrong about the clicker questions and doesn't even explain it. The textbook is a lifesaver in this course, just make sure you understand the textbook and you'll be fine.

Professor Silva didn't teach anything new because we already needed to read the textbook beforehand for the pre-flight quizzes. His class was extremely boring and almost everyone was on their laptops or phones. Professor Jarrio seemed much better in comparison compared to Silva.

He will read directly from slides from the textbook for lectures, and the will contain all of the information that you have already read(prelecture quizzes). All the professors have the same tests, so you can go to other professors' lectures. Make sure you have the time to do so, as you will also need to go to his class for attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Moved very quickly and explained concepts poorly. I started attending Anh Le's lectures after the 2nd or 3rd week.
somewhat boring with lectures and got behind frequently

Dr. Silva is a nice guy and is clearly very knowledgeable about chemistry, but he is not a good teacher. I learned everything by reading the textbook. Just don't let yourself get behind because you don't even stop to take a breath in this course.
Not the best for me

He literally just reads of his slides. You can tell he's just here to research and the school is sticking him in whatever class to keep him here. Seems to forget that his students are just learning chemistry and explains things in too complex a level for the class.

Silva just reads off of slides and is very hard to contact out of class. He is not very good at explaining concepts and has very slow lectures where we often fall behind. I would recommend taking the other professor over him.

Literally the worst professor ever! He only reads off slides during lectures, reading the textbook yourself is better than attending lectures. Also gives two quizzes per lecture, plus homework! Please take the other prof over him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Silva's lectures were very long and slow and were always just him reading off of slides that we already had access to, with a little extra added information. I attended lectures for the majority of the first half of the semester but eventually figured it wasn't worth it. Almost all the extra information could be found in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Silva is honestly just a bad professor... another lecturer taught my section for about half the classes because he didn't show up and when Silva was there, he seemed fairly uninterested in the subject and did not try to make the material interesting whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Silva obviously knows the general topics when it comes to chemistry, but was often unable to answer direct questions from students about course material we had just been taught. It felt as if he'd been teaching a class on concepts he hasn't studied in years. His lack of both preparation and commitment to teaching made this class a slog. Have fun!

He showed no interest in teaching the material and didn't provide any insight other than reading straight off the lecture slides. Was missing from class 25% of the time and even didn't show up on day without giving the class any notice.

dr.silva was a bit boring during lecture and once i stopped going to lecture and read the textbook instead, i did much better in class. however, he seemed very nice. there is a lot of opportunity to get a 100 on the daily work due to the numerous assignments throughout the semester. i really enjoyed this class and the content was not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think I would've learned the same amount if I didn't go to lectures and had the automated TikTok voice read the lecture slides to me, and it would've been more interesting. Don't bother going, just take notes on the textbook and you'll be fine. Excessive daily assignments, can quickly become a bother if you forget even a few. Just don't.

His lectures are very boring and he doesn't offer much explanation for topics, just reads off the slide. The content itself is not bad, but you'll have to teach it to yourself if you don't get it immediately.

I started going to lecture at the beginning of the semester but I soon gave up, since I felt like it was wasting my time. Lots of technical difficulties and the explanations weren't great either. If I ever watched lectures, it was the recording of another section. The tests were not very fair, compared to other years. Made me lose interest in chem

Hard class but even more difficult online. Easy to tell that he is more interested in his research than his teaching by a long ways. Has no idea how to work technology so made this fall semester really hard.

reviews.comment: Awful teacher. If you are able to understand Silva it won't make much of a difference because his explanations are so poor. He would literally hand his microphone to a kid in our class so that the kid could answer questions. He lost his ability to draw on the lecture slides so the rest of the semester he just clicked through and read them to us.

It seemed like Schurmeier did everything for the class besides teach our section every day. Silva would dance around peoples questions without really answering them, and his explanations were over complicated. He was gone several times to speak at other schools, but Schurmeier usually subbed so it was fine by me. Just go ahead and take Schurmeier

Silva is ok. You can tell he cares about you but lectures often felt rushed and I feel he overcomplicated many things. As long as you read the textbook when you don't understand something, do the recitation worksheets, and pay attention taking notes then you should be ok. Hard class but I survived. Don't freak out if you get him as a prof.

reviews.comment: He was not very good at lectures, and they were usually either boring or were just one big technical difficulty. When I went to class, most of the time I felt like I was wasting time. I definitely learned more from reading the textbook. I think maybe he is more focused on research because he would leave to give seminars at other schools.

He sounds bored while teaching that it makes you want to fall asleep. I don't think I met a single person who thought he was a good teacher. I thought lecturing wasn't his thing, so I went to office hours, which I admit was more helpful, but not by much. He couldn't answer a question I had and told me to email him about it, but he never responded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Going to lecture ends up making you even more confused. Do yourself a favor and teach yourself the material from the textbook.

Took him in Fall 2018. He covers all the content pretty well actually. His explanations can be slightly overcomplicated. His tests are fair and involves application of things learned in class which trips people up (ie. a problem never covered in class but we should be able to solve with the concepts taught). Your grade is dependent on 3 midterms...
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not very exciting, your average chem prof. Explanations are extremely complicated for what they need to be, will answer all questions though.

Stop right now and take Kimberly Schurmeier. Number one she is the better teacher, and she updates grades more consistently and overall teaches the content better. Number two, why wake up at 8 am when you can take a better class at 9 am.

Professor Silva was a pretty boring lecturer but he got through all of the necessary material. He lectures at a slower pace than the other professors. The class is pretty easy and tests are standard across all lectures. Lab is tedious but you can't really do anything about that. To do well on exams do all of the relevant practice exams.

He was a little bit slow in lectures, but overall good professor. You have to study on your own but the class is very reasonable. It was his first semester at Tech so he could improve with time as well.

This was Dr. Silva's first semester at Tech, so there is room for improvement. However, his lectures always seemed quite dry/robotic and ended up feeling too much like a chore (lectures are standardized across 1310). Fell behind on material often, resulting in doing homework that had not yet been covered. Common exams/final, you get a crib sheet.
Funny guy and good lecturer in general. Would take again!

Linear algebra is a bit abstract, but I thought he did a great job explaining concepts in ways that people with no prior exposure could understand. Answered questions in-class very respectfully and clearly as well.
Good lecturer! No explicit homework but did provide problems to reference from the textbook.
While the material was difficult, Simone explained it in a clear manner that really helped with my understanding. He was always super nice and answered in-class questions very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is fairly challenging on its own, but he makes it easier and more simple to understand. He is very good at explaining one-on-one, too. He can talk kind of quietly and be a little hard to hear in lectures sometimes, though. I would definitely recommend Jonathan Simone for 1553!

Professor Simone was a really good lecturer. The content can get difficult, but he does a great job of breaking it down to make it easy to understand, and he is well-paced. The class itself can have difficult homework assignments, but the textbook is free, and the tests are much easier.
Easy exams, covers everything necessary in lectures.
A great professor to have. Very nice and understanding and almost always accessible outside of class for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were straightforward and covered nearly everything you needed for the exam!! Exams were not difficult!!
Not accessible outside the classroom, completely nonaccomodating for emergencies. Lectures are okay but he does not use a microphone so it's difficult to hear if you don't sit up front.
AMAZING went to his lectures despite not being in his class

He was really nice, although his lectures go really fast. He made concepts really clear and easier to understand! There was a lot of homework and we had I think 7 quizzes throughout the semester, but that was for everyone in 1553. I definitely recommend !
Great professor! Lectures were easy to follow and he answers questions very well. Overall, he gave support where needed and was very passionate about the class!

A really good professor, clearly passionate about the subject and makes it quite easy to understand these difficult concepts. Linear Algebra is known for being difficult, but this is definitely one of the better teachers you could have for the subject.

One of the best professors for lecture and great at explaining concepts. Homework every week, online quizzes, and exams aren't too difficult. Jankowski's videos are life-saving and make sure to look at exams from previous years since they are helpful. Understand foundation early bc concepts are repeated throughout course
Bro does a solid job teaching. His tests are a little on the tough side and the material itself is super boring but overall bro is a great professor.

Difficult class, but good teaching techniques. 3+ homeworks a week gets annoying but helps you learn. Power points are easy to follow and usually have example problems. Notes, power points, and the professor are all accessible outside of class. Large class sizes.

reviews.comment: For MATH1554 instead of 1551 but THE BEST PROFESSOR FOR LINEAR ALGEBRA HANDS DOWN! There was construction going on while he was lecturing but overall made one of the hardest courses I've taken at tech a lot easier.
1554 Linear Algebra, not 1551. Phenomenal and caring professor who really considers the students, the content, and even with massive class sizes, manages to be accessible. Definitely take Simone!
TAKE SIMONE FOR 1554 GATECH. DON'T TAKE BARONE.

**This is for 1554, not 1551**
I love Dr. Simone, he explains everything very thoroughly and makes sure everyone understands before moving on to the next topic. He knows what he's talking about and is definitely a great pick for linear algebra.

**1554 not 1551
He is a professor of math 1554 at GT, one of the hardest freshman courses. He helped me significantly through the course, and I would recommend his class without question. One of the best professors at this school. GO TO CLASS AND ASK FOR HELP IF YOU NEED IT.

Dr. Simone creates a welcoming lecture space where I feel comfortable asking questions and participating. He maintains an encouraging, understanding bonhomie with students and enthusiastically explains the "why" behind the "how" of even the most basic concepts. He makes calculus painless. I plan to register for his Linear Algebra section next fall.

Prof Simone is just an amazon professor! He's super caring, understanding and adjusts his pace with the rest of the class. He has intuitive ways to explain concepts and is always very friendly to talk to. Moreover, he always stays back after class to answer doubts and replies to emails in minutes! Amazing choice for any math!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mr. Simone is an amazing professor. He is VERY clear in his lectures: he gets to the point while explaining difficult concepts in a simple manner. Tests were relatively easy because of how great he was! He cares so much about his students and will do his best to accommodate to your personal needs. 10/10 TAKE SIMONE IF YOU CAN! YOU WONT REGRET IT!

He is a great professor! He explains the concepts very clearly and makes his lectures interactive. He is extremely accessible outside class and responds to emails quickly. He's very caring as well. I would 100% recommend taking him.

Professor Simone's lectures were always to the point, and extremely clear when it came to explaining new concepts. He likes to always build up to the concept you are learning by walking you through a proof you would know how to do with current knowledge, which really adds to being able to learn math quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. The lectures are very informative and detailed. He is incredibly caring and non-intimidating to students and is very easy to reach. Responds to emails ridiculously fast.

Mr. Jonathan Simone is an amazing professor at Tech. I had him for MATH 1551 this semester, and he was awesome! He's very detailed and clear in his lectures and is happy to see you in office hours! Sometimes he runs out of time during his lectures, but its okay because the problems he did solve were explained thoroughly! 10/10 would take again.

I am so sad that she is leaving Georgia Tech because I had the best experience taking ENGL 1102 with her in Ignite! She was so kind and caring and despite it being a 5 week course, she really took the effort to get to know her students. She gave great feedback, graded relatively easily, and was very available to contact her.
Had a fantastic experience taking her class.

reviews.comment: Professor is very available after class and answers emails quickly. The books and topics are very interesting too. Not too much workload.

Dr. Slavin made ENGL 1101 quite enjoyable for me, the class theme was fascinating and you could tell that she was very interested in the topic herself, making lectures engaging. The workload was very manageable and grading was fair, with great feedback. She really cares about her students. Take her for English!!

Professor Slavin teaches an amazing course about Atlanta which can be very insightful to those out of state and even eye-opening to those in the area. Lots to read but very interesting content! Prof gives lots of extra credit opportunities, great feedback, and there's a couple group projects but they were graded easier than individual assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Loved this professor. Always gave constructive feedback and seemed extremely enthusiastic about the course content. Best of all, she structured the class clearly and was easily accessible for questions. Do yourself a favor and register her class for english!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love this woman!! She cares about her students as people outside GT, which is huge. Take her for 1102!
Amazing professor, fun topic, and easy grader. Take her!

Dr. Slavin is hands down one of the best teachers I've had in college. She genuinely cares about her students and she is very understanding. You will have to read a bit and participate meaningfully to do well, but she gives great feedback on papers/projects that helps you improve.

I took this class during iGniTe. Professor Slavin was super understanding about deadlines and always available to email. This was a project/essay-based class so no actual tests, my section had an interesting course theme and a very fair amount of work. Make an effort and you'll get an A. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took this class as one of my first 3 classes at Georgia Tech and have absolutely no regrets. The topic was migration and refugee literature and Dr. Slavin made the class interesting even in an online format. Lots of reading but it's super interesting. She's a pretty lenient grader but still gives great feedback. A great choice for ENG 1102.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed her class, we focused on crises in Atl and around the world. The coronavirus took us by surprise but she was lenient on grading and was always available. Very sweet and caring, her classes were a fun to be a part of. Just don't be lazy and contribute, she'll notice you.

Dr. Slavin is one of the most caring professors I've met so far at Georgia Tech. She is very understanding, provides great feedback on your assignments to promote improvement, and always encourages her students to attend office hours (which shows her willingness to help). She's amazing.

She is a very nice person. Dr. Slavin is more than willing to help during office hours or sometime after class if you have any specific questions or concerns. Additionally, she is understanding if you are having trouble outside of class and will definitely be accommodating if you speak with her.

Her class contents are organized, and you will really learn a lot from the class discussions and the readings. There are pop quizzes for the reading assignments but she is not a hard grader so if you do the reading you will be fine. She is caring. Go to her office hours to receive some great feedbacks on your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Slavin is definitely a teacher you'd want to have for English at Tech, she gets that most people are super busy with their major classes, so she doesn't make the class crazy difficult like some other profs. basically if you participate fully in your group projects and do at least 75% of the readings, you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was not a hard class. Much easier than high school English. Dr. Slavin really cares about her students, and she wants you to do well. If you are struggling, just see her outside of class. Otherwise just turn everything in on time, and you should receive a decent grade. Class feels more like a conversation than a lecture.

Requires a smaller amount of work than other english professors, but if you do the work, you'll likely get a respectable grade. A very good portion of the final grade was accumulated by showing up to class for workshops/attendance assignments.

Prof. Slavin is a great professor that seems to understand that you have a lot of work in other classes. The class is not easy, but it also won't make you cry too much. There are several big papers and projects. The class is a nice balance of relaxed and hard.

Dr. Slayton is very understanding and reasonable when it comes to assigning and grading work. Classes are always well structured but not stressful, we sometimes even got time to work in class. Homework consisted only of occasional readings and short responses. Overall it was a very manageable class and she is great choice for any English class.
So caring, so nice, explains stuff really well!
Kendra Slayton is one of the best professors I've had at Tech! She's really chill and doesn't give any unreasonable work.

Dr. Slayton was definitely the right choice. She is a very kind professor and makes sure to only give her students what they can handle for the workload. Even though her class may not seem as easy as other ENG 1102 classes at Georgia Tech, it is definitely still not a difficult class and would recommend for anyone to take.

I had a rough time with a professor last semester and had to withdraw from 1102, so I had to start again this semester. Dr. Slayton was DEFINITELY the right choice. She's incredibly understanding and a wonderful professor. Her course theme may seem a little odd, but it's honestly fun once you get there. One essay, and then simple group projects.

Dr. Slayton is wonderful. She is super caring and knows when to extend deadlines based on workload and if she feels that a project is confusing or too intense, she'll change it to make it easier. Only had to write one essay and the rest of the class was group projects. She lets you revise the essay too. Definitely wish I could take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was awesome. I believe it was her first time teaching bc she seemed nervous a good bit. However, I like how she ran the class. Read book, go over what you read, take end of week quiz, repeat. She was also pretty generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dont listen to the other bad reviews she is the kindest professor I have ever had. She gave us a few forms of extra credit, a project that looked pretty simple and a couple of extra homework problems. Throughout the pandemic she was incredibly accommodating and the structure of the class was always reasonable. Very helpful in office hours.

Lectures are very boring and not that helpful. She uses textbook for everything. A lot of homework and 7 quizzes with no midterms. Quizzes were not too bad, and we could replace lowest grade with a project. The best way to learn dynamics is by doing lots of practice problems.

I felt like most lectures were quite boring, as she took almost all of the material from the book. I realized you don't even have to go to lecture as doing lots of practice problems is the best way to learn. We had lots of short quizzes, which was good in a way since one low grade won't affect you too much if you do well on other quizzes.

Alpha is a great professor. Not many classes, really only this one and 2110, make me feel like I came out a better engineer than I went in. Expect a B, and expect to work a lot outside of class, but for the most part it's worth it. I have been able to manage it with 15 real credits.

Alpha cares a lot about his students. Enthusiastic lecturer with interactive lectures making you want to pay attention. Content is HARD and UNINTUITIVE though; hw takes a long time, DP3 was BRUTAL (ended up being completion grade), tests are hard. However, he teaches well and gives good resources so show up to class and practice and you're fine.

There has been a few classes in my time at tech that are pivotal to my life. Dynamics with Alpha was one of them. Had I not taken this class, I don't think I would have the same understanding of engineering concepts or been at the same mental pedigree to work hard for my grades. Had it not been for alpha, I would've never made it out of tech.

Where to begin? Do NOT take this class. Is a nice guy, but this class is a LUDICROUS amount of work. Design problems that take double-digit hours to complete where 95% of the class fails on the first one, homeworks with parts A-E taking almost another double-digit hours to complete EVERY WEEK. Not to mention his lectures are rambling and terrible.

Bro is a dedicated lecturer. He makes lectures so engaging and well organized. Also recommended for independent learners since no formal attendance is taken (Fall 25) so missing one or two lectures for other important commitments would be just fine. He remembers everyone's name (very respectable) so whoever's there's prob quite clear at a glance.

I took Alpha in the Spring 2025 and imo, he is the best professor I have taken at Tech. I feel that his style of tough hw and design problems were offset by his engaging lectures, canvas resources, and office hours. There's a good chance he doesn't remember my name, but I would die for that man. I owe him everything.

Dr. Smith, great guy, but the class structure is absurd. weekly HW having parts A - E, each A TIMED EXAM, plus regular high difficulty midterms and textbook questions. you'll spend hours doing 5 tests a week ("HW"), just to be contempt with a 60-75% on each HW part because if you make one slight error you have to restart. Ridiculous.

One of the best professors at GT. The class is difficult but it was worth it, it is the most I have learned in any course at GT. Fast paced with 3 projects + 2 midterms, the projects are difficult but you have time, the midterms resemble the practice exams. Office hours and class attendance HIGHLY recommended (especially during design problems).

Highly recommend not taking machine design with Dr. Smith unless you want to waste your time and prolong graduation. He is insistent that his teaching style is the only and correct way to teach so if it doesn't work well then tough luck! It is impossible to learn content when we are given problems that aren't taught and have no step by step example

One of the greatest professors in the ME department hands down. Lectures were very interesting packed full of very important information. Design problems are the primary time sink for this class. It is very normal for people to do poorly on the first one as it is very difficult and time consuming. Exams are similar to homework and design problems.

3057 with Alpha is kind of a nightmare. You NEED to go to lecture, a lot of HW and project hints are presented in class. Unclear on guidelines for lab reports and final project, which makes your grade dependent on how generous the TA's are feeling. Alpha may be a great lecturer, but 3057 needs someone grounded.

Alpha's class is very difficult, but as a professor he's one of the best there is. That class had me pulling  hair out over the DPs, but Alpha is one of the best, most capable, kind, respectful, technically adept professors I've ever met in my life. He's also just a good dude. Machine Design is HARD but Alpha makes it both enjoyable and engaging.

Alpha was an amazing professor, probably the best I have had at Georgia Tech. While this has been the hardest class to succeed in that I have ever taken in my life, I learned a lot. The topics covered in the class are foundational for any engineer. This course will make you feel like an actual engineer. 4 days of office hours and piazza helped too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is eh, he explains things clearly in lecture but is strict and refuses to meet with students and actually help them. He also leaves the TA's confused, but ask TA's for help and guidance on reports to maximize your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some lectures aren't really useful, 5 mandatory workshops to attend. Everything grading is done by TA's. Expectations are somewhat vague at the beginning but you learn from previous reports. Gives vague answers when you ask a question. Unsure if class is curved, but basically do the bare min for a B and fabricate really good reports for an A.

Your experience and grade in 3057 mostly depend on your TA's and group members on reports. Alpha was a good lecturer for this class, but I think the format he was required to make it was not great. There is a lot of confusion in this course as a result of TA's being confused and sometimes unreachable especially at the end of the semester.

Alpha was a great professor, definitely learned a lot about machine design in this course. 1000% recommend getting the textbook. Design problems are A LOT of work, no joke! Alpha probably has the most FAIR exams I have ever taken at GT. I'm not saying they are easy, I am saying the exams are FAIR. He also grades fairly too. HW takes time but useful

All my friends told me to take this guy, but he doesn't show examples in class, basically emphatically reads the textbook (Shigley) to you. The DPs (Design Problem Projects) are graded by TAs that don't hold office hours so you have no clue what they want until they fail the whole class on the first project.

Alpha is absolutely the best professor I've had at GT. His course is definitely a LOT of work but I took 5 other classes and managed fine. Definitely follow his recommendation to buy the textbook- you will be using it a ton.
Don't skip lecture for this class and don't procrastinate design problems & you'll be ok.

Good teacher but lots of work. His class is hard. Insures you learn machine design, but your stress levels will definitely be tested in this class. If you're taking 3 or more classes as well as Machine Design I would suggest finding a different teacher.

Best lecturer at tech and I've never seen a professor genuinely care about their students like he does. The class is difficult and time consuming but in a way that ensures that you learn how to do machine design. It's potentially the most useful class at tech and he does everything in his power to make sure you succeed (office hours 5 days a week).

Alpha's class is incredibly difficult, but this is the one class to challenge yourself in. DPs are hell, but you feel like an engineer after them. He pushes his students, but is incredibly caring. He learns every student's name and doesn't judge no matter where you are in the class. His are the only office hours I've ever regularly attended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The level of difficulty prof smith or 'alpha' makes the class is unreasonable. the design problems take WEEKS and you have to go to office hours or check piazza to uncover vague information. Additionally, most of your grade comes down to 2 exams. I learned almost nothing about design as i was just trying to keep up with this class. Do NOT recommend

Machine Design is HARD but this class is just a lot of work. He cares about students, but the work assigned is at times unfair. The design problems take a lot of time and focus which, ontop a full semester of classes is not always feasible. There is also only one midterm and the final so you HAVE to do well on them to pass

If you enjoy def bods, you should take his machine design class. You learn a lot and you actually feel competent as an engineering student. This class is A LOT of work and office hours aren't really optional if you want to do well or even get a C or above. Take this class when you have a lighter course load and you might actually enjoy it.

Alpha is the best professor. Kept me engaged, incredible lectures, and so caring. He learns everyone's name, even in a huge class. His DPs are time consuming, but you will come out of this class prepared to use knowledge in the real world. Without a doubt I got a lower grade than I would've from another prof, would take him again in a heartbeat.

The design problems are 15-25 hour assignments that you get around two weeks to complete. You absolutely have to start as soon as they're released especially for DP1. Going to office hours and checking Piazza is a *must* for this class as that's where information and clarifications nessicary for doing the design problems correctly comes from.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: First C I got at Tech in Machine Design, definitely the most brutal class in the Mechanical curriculum. Alpha himself is a good professor, super nice and personable, but the design problems trumped that. Incredibly long, super difficult, and almost everyone consistently did poorly on them. Would not recommend simply because of the design problems

The absolute worst professor I have ever had. DO NOT TAKE HIM. His lectures are mandatory and you are better off teaching this to yourself. The book does a better job of showing how to do this than a professor. I absolutely do not recommend it.

Dr. Smith (Alpha) is a very hit-or-miss professor. He gives a lot of homework, and 3 very difficult (10-30hrs each) design problems over the semester. IMO, I learn alot with his lectures and the homework, but I have some friends who hate it. If you liked def bods alot I think you'll like him, if youre a heat transfer kind of person then probably no

The best prof for machine design IMO. explains things clearly, concisely and keeps lectures interesting. Design problems are a grind, >12 hrs for a not great result. But like what others have mentioned, this will be the closest thing you can get to proper engineering structures at tech
The projects will kill you but it's the closest thing you can get to actual test, design, or engineering analysis you will get at this school.

David "Alpha" Smith is an excellent teacher and you will learn a lot from him. His class does require a lot of work, especially the 3 design problems a semester that take 20 hours each. Exams are hard too, but he gives a lot of free points through participation and homework. Very effective at conveying the material and supportive throughout.

Alpha is an absolutely amazing professor. He knows everything about, everything. You will learn a lot when you take this course, but it is challenging. The exams are fair and if you do the homework, you will be fine. The homework is hard, but you learn a lot, and if you need help with them you can ask him in Office Hours. Great choice.

He's a nice guy and really cares about the material he's teaching. However, he is an incredibly difficult professor. The lectures are not as helpful as he thinks, the homework takes hours upon hours to get right, and the design problems are insane. He gives way too much work to make the class worth your time when you are barely learning anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He cares about the class and is passionate about it. Problem is he gives unreasonable amount of work, specially for a 2 credit class... Lectures don't help that much and the HWs take a long time for full credit. There is only one test and final, which he believes he has it like that to be "fair" when it actually just makes it worst.

Alpha is a nice guy and genuinely cares about the material he teaches. With that being said, this class ruined my life this summer. The HWs are god awful and take FOREVER to complete if you want full credit on them. There was only one test and a final and the HWs and lectures were basically useless in helping to prepare for the tests.

Where do I start? He wants to you to do well, but lectures are so generalized and then gives you the most unreasonable homework assignments. It is the most ludicrous amount of work I have ever experienced and he is not helpful during his office hours. He thinks he is being fair but does not realize he is not preparing us at all for anything.

Alpha is a good professor. Hes extremely interested in what he teaches and really wants his students to succeed. The issue is, he makes his classes far more difficult and time-demanding than appropriate. He never really goes into depth during lecture and leaves you to teach yourself through very long HW sets and god awful design problems.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Tech. Has a great personality and truly tried to get to know everyone in the class. The content was tough, but he spends a lot of time with you if you need it, even holding extra sessions in the CULC for us to go and practice more. Best professor I've had at Tech.
If you want to spend 20 hours a week on this class then take his course. Partially online but does not fo a good job at all. Does not seem to want to help anyone learn at all.

Alpha was a great professor. He was accomadating and available when you needed help and his lectures are clear and easy to follow. His class is a lot of work, but he gives you drops on assignments if you miss deadlines and his sylabus is very clear. He clearly cares about the material and the students and it was a good class

reviews.comment: Alpha strikes an interesting balance between drilling the basic concepts in homeworks (sometimes for hours) and great design problems (also long). Seems to be care deeply about us actually learning. He was very receptive when I reached out for help. Didn't quite get to 3d kinetics, but what are modern physics engines for anyway?
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can tell he enjoys teaching and is passionate about the subject and his students, but the design problems, Wiley HW, and canvas HW are insanely difficult and impossible to solve. I would avoid taking this Professor at all costs if GPA is at all important to you, or if you dont want a 2 credit hour class taking up 20 hours of your week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very nice guy but he makes the course unbelievably difficult. 'Design Problems' are insanely challenging, beyond anything I've done at GT. Your GPA will more than likely take a hit. If you are deeply interested in mastering the topic, I recommend him, you will learn a lot from failing. Otherwise, I would advise taking it with another professor.

Ok this class was pretty difficult but Alpha is an amazing professor! I truly learned so much and feel much more confident in my ability as an engineer. You will have to work for it but it will be worth it in the long run! Cannot recommend enough!

Alpha is a really cool guy and clearly cares about his students, however the class structure (especially now that were all online) is absolutely atrocious. Alpha only posts lecture videos and nothing else. You wont be able to access power points, notes, anything. If you cant take quick notes count on rewatching lecture videos constantly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Alpha's a great professor that rly makes the most of the online format. He sets up voice channels for u to discuss with classmates during lecture. Overall very solid choice.

reviews.comment: Highly recommend him for dynamics. The class is challenging, but the tests are very similar to the (less challenging) homework sets. Even though the homework is difficult, Alpha is very helpful in office hours and helps you understand the concepts and homework well. He made the a generally difficult class doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, but the way he structures class around you talking to your neighbor every 5 mins is so tedious. He's like "And why is it like that? Well, why don't you discuss that." Then you and the people next to you make up some nonsense, and then he tells you the answer eventually. Also, the 3 design problems are rough.

Super nice guy and very thorough. Explains things in great detail so just listen and take notes and you wont be confused. He really wants to help and see you succeed. His homework's just take forever, but the tests are just like his homeworks so it comes in clutch. Very well structured class.

I love alpha. He really wants you to succeed and is extremely helpful and accessible at his office hours. He gives out a lot of homework, but its helpful in understanding the material. There was only one midterm and one final, but both were very reasonable. Very funny, awesome guy.

Alpha is a great lecturer and I learned so much in his class! He really cares about his students being able to get practical knowledge out of the course material. Homeworks can be a little tedious, so being comfortable enough to use MATLAB is important to succeed. Make sure to get the textbook, it really helps with understanding the material.

Alpha is the coolest professor I have had at Georgia Tech. I would take any class he teaches. Make sure you buy whatever books he recommends. You will need them. Alpha is extremely fair, but a tough grader. Also make sure your comfortable writing in Matlab, it's the quickest way to get HW done. Really good professor. A real gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. It is obvious that he tries his best and wants you to learn. Put in the effort and you'll get an A. The way he makes his homework is a little tedious but not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bottom line is that he is eager for you to learn and you definitely will learn a lot from him. Very accessible outside of class and will sit with you for hours to help. The only downside is that there is only one mid term and the final in addition to the hw and problem sets which are pretty difficult and graded somewhat harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you keep up with the reading and pop into class every once in a while the tests are more than manageable. The lectures are engaging, and while the course is a survey and cannot cover every topic in as much depth as I would have liked, he clearly cares, just respect his time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly don't get the negative reviews for this professor. The quizzes are EXTREMELY easy and the tests aren't too bad either, as long as you study at least a little bit. He is very passionate and an entertaining lecturer. The books that we were assigned are really good and they inspired me to get into more nonfiction!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He assigns a lot of reading (3 books in a semester), and grades based off of exams and quizzes only. He frequently calls out individual students (usually if they're talking or on their phone) in front of the whole class. He seems passionate about history, but I am uncomfortable with him.

Going into the class I thought it would be manageable. Couldn't be farther from the truth. This class is extremely hard because there are no study guides/review for tests and you have to just go based on what he teaches in lecture (random facts not related to the main ideas). You'll end up studying for something that won't even show up on the test.

Dr. Smith made this class enjoyable & the lectures were engaging & interesting. It's important to take good notes during the video lectures as they have little/no words. The assignments he gave were easy to read & the questions are straightforward. He grades pretty fairly & gives feedback. Exams are fine as long as you take notes & do the readings.

I've had two classes with Dr. Smith and he's amazing. Kind, funny, insightful and an enrapturing storyteller. It's true there is no wasted moment in his class, everything is worth knowing and may be tested on. You can't skate by, you have to be interested and invested, but in his defense, Dr. Smith makes it easy to be both. Can't recommend enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was a very passionate lecturer. However, he was not a good lecturer for me. He liked to lecture in the form of storytelling, which made it difficult to know what needed to be known for the tests. He also talks very quickly, making it difficult to take notes at times. This class shouldn't have been as difficult as it was.

Dr. Smith is the best lecturer I have ever had. He cares deeply about the content and his students, throws in jokes for his lectures, and makes the lectures engaging. The other comments about having to study obscene amounts to get an A aren't entirely true. If you show up to class and study ~2 hours a week, you will easily get an A.

Smith was very caring and super nice throughout the whole semester. He is always willing to answer questions during lecture. But, lectures can be somewhat painful to sit through even though you can tell he is passionate about the subject. You do have to really pay attention, as the only grades are 4-5 quizzes, 3 exams, and the final
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just don't do it. Everyone here is right. Unless you want to put in more time studying for HISTORY than your STEM classes... If you do decide to not take my advice just withdraw while you still have the chance. Stay blessed.

You have to work to get a good grade in the class.  There were weekly written responses which were actually graded pretty harshly, and you did not have much time for them.  There were reading almost everyday which had content that would be on the test.

Do not take this class if you want an easy A. Your grade is only based on 3 (tough) tests and 5 quizzes, and no extra credit. There is no textbook and his slides are extremely vague, so you need to pay attention in class. On the bright side, he is an engaging professor. Also his political views show up in lecture a lot so prepare for that.

The only things that make up your grade in this class are 3 tests and 5 quizzes. Getting just 1 question wrong means your overall grade drops by 0.6%, and the questions are very niche. He did gives us extra credit but only because he was sick for most of the semester. A great professor, and a great story teller, but not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a great lecturer but his tests are extremely specific and it's very hard to do well. Your entire grade depends on 3 tests and 5 quizzes, so if you mess up once you aren't getting a good grade. Sad because this is my favorite class  but my worst grade and I am a STEM student. If you want an easy A, don't take this class. No extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am crying in frustration and laughing at the audacity...
