Why am I putting more work into this class than my STEM classes - let me remind you this is GT - and STILL getting worse grades? 3 tests make up 90% (!!!) of your grade. No study guides, no notes, no extra credit. Impossible to succeed. Wanna pass? Memorize every word he says. Good luck LOL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I wish I could go back & drop this class. 3 tests = 90% of your grade, 5 quizzes = last 10%. Tests & quizzes were ridiculously niche & specific details. He wants you to memorize every word he says. No written notes anywhere. No EC. Everything is MC & confusingly worded like trick questions. Not set up for success whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Smith cared a lot about the content that he taught, and truly inspired students to take a passion to history. His lectures consisted of discussions of the content, so while not necessary, is beneficial to getting a good grade in the class. His tests can be a bit difficult, but if you put in the work necessary you will do fine.

Be prepared to memorize absolutely everything Prof. Smith says. His tests are ridiculously specific, you have to have his lecture memorized and he sometimes puts things in the tests that he didn't even say. The entire grade depends on 3 tests and 5 quizzes, which are all extremely hard. I had a terrible time, don't take this class if u want an A.

Only three tests are given, which your grade depends on. Every single word he says in the lecture should be memorized, as well as every reading given, which are all stupid things that do not lead to an overall understanding of history at all. Irrelevant content, irrelevant class, terrible grade for a humanity.

Prof. Smiths class is extremely test heavy. The tests are 50 questions, 50 minutes, and the questions are incredibly hard. His lectures have practically no words so you basically have to write down every thing he says because his test are very specific. Your entire grade depends on quizzes and tests. Way too hard for a humanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is a great teacher and very passionate about what he does. However his class structure is archaic. You have little to no wiggle room time wise during the exams, the lecture slides have almost 0 words on them so you need to take detailed notes, and there is no opportunity for bonus points. Tough class for a humanity.

This is not the class to take if youre looking for an easy A. Although hes very intelligent and his lectures are very good, his grading scale for this class is quite egregious. Be prepared to study hard for exams in this class if you want to finish with an A. Theres easier classes to take for your legislative credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was caring and willing to help me, but even when I put in the work and had a tutor I was still unsuccessful. He does not allow for any type of grade bump or extra credit so you get what you get. I would not take this class again, it was too tedious and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An overall great professor. I came into the class expecting to be bored, but he made every lecture quite interesting. Good listening/notes are extremely important, as unwritten lecture content will be on quizzes/exams. Review notes from time to time in case of pop quizzes, which are very short and specific. Everything from lecture is worth knowing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best story teller ever

Professor Smith was a great professor. He acknowledges that every student has a different background in history. His lectures were engaging and it felt like listening to a storyteller. However, he also has a good control over the class. There is no "textbook", just required readings, which saves you money.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: can't stress enough how lecture heavy this class is and people still skipped bc attendance wasnt mandatory. The tests and pop quizzes are not hard if you pay attention & take good notes on every lecture. He does talk somewhat fast to cover the content, but he makes his lectures storylike and very interesting (first history class I've EVER enjoyed)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Theres no textbook so if you miss a lecture youre kinda screwed. Theres also pop quizzes that you cant make up. Tests are multiple choice and pretty straight forward. The hard part is he says so much information that anything could be a question. It was hard for me to write everything and remember everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For a class about a decently boring subject his lectures were SO interesting. He was really fun to listen to however it is a ton of information. We had to read his own book for the class but it was super interesting. As long as you come to class (pop quizzes) and stay up on reading its a fun class. Still kinda hard tho tbh

Professor Smith was a great story teller. He made history interesting. Be ready to write though because he speaks SO fast!! Would still take him again because he is a super nice person and I actually enjoyed history with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Reading is not from a textbook, but from other books (based on this year) which are on tests. Lectures are great and tests are not too hard if you study.

The only class I truly looked forward to this semester. His lectures are amazing. I leave each time feeling like I just gained a new prospective to life. Take good notes in class, and study them right before the exam and you'll do fine. There are books you will have to read. This class is graded by 6 things, so each one counts. Don't slack off.

Dr. Smith is a great guy and a great lecturer. You can tell he really loves teaching the material and his lectures are always interesting and engaging. Always available outside of class to review the concepts, ask questions, or just talk. Go to class and read the books and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Johnny Smith is one of the best professors at GT. Do what he says, which is read your books, and take good lecture notes, and voila! You will probably be on your way to an enjoyable history class and a comfortable grade. Lectures are very entertaining and informative. Paper notes only, but this is no biggie. He loves to talk after class as well.
John Smith is a great guy and great professor. He really knows his stuff and truly cares about his students. Also, his tests are pretty easy which is a plus and no papers!!!

Definitely the best professor I have had at Tech, and definitely my favorite. He is a really great guy and easy to get along with and have conversations with. In fact, I still keep in touch with him and will be taking another class with him. I hated History in high school but I loved this class and really enjoyed his lectures and teaching style.

Dr Smith has been my favorite professor so far at Tech, even though I'm not a huge fan of history.  It is clear that he loves his job and the material he is teaching.  He and the TA's will be explicitly clear about what you need to do for an A, you just may need to ask them out side of class time.  Test are non cumulative and easy.

I've always hated learning about history, but his enthusiasm made history bearable! You can hear excitement in his voice when he lectures (even though it was a morning class) and he's very willing to help you if you're struggling!

He's an awesome guy. His lectures are actually entertaining to listen to, and his quizzes are 2 questions long and only cover info from the previous lecture. His tests are 25 MC and 1 essay on a historical novel he assigns. The readings are actually really interesting, and you MUST read the books to do well on the essays. Final is not cumulative.

No Homework, Short Quizzes on previous lecture (was to my detriment), you will know exactly what to expect. His TA's can be tough graders on the Essay portion of the Tests which are on Historial Novels you NEED to read. Final is not Cumulative!!!

Loved his lectures. You can tell he really loves what he is teaching. Although he spoke really quickly, he would slow down if you asked him. He was very funny and friendly. As long as you attend class and pay attention, you can easily get an A.

Prof. Smith is just okay. Clearly knows her stuff but doesn't communicate material sufficiently. HWs are very difficult. Makes mistakes in her notes without correcting them and constantly mispronounces Greek letters, which is incredibly annoying, especially when psi, xi, and z are in one equation. Take only if you are an aerodynamics concentration.

The lectures went over a lot of the derivations which were honestly not that helpful or useful in our career, but as long as you do the homework questions and the few examples she goes over you'll be fine. Final was considerably harder than the quizzes but manageable. Group project is a blast.

Quizzes: 60% (7 Quizzes - 10% each, drop lowest)
Class Participation: 10%
Group Project: 15%
Final Exam: 15%

Go to class, form a relationship with her, and you'll be fine. She keeps a list of who attends office hours/recitation in which she is a lot more open to providing aid (hint's on quizzes, study tips, etc.). She is BETTER than her ratings.

Content on the final was something we've never seen before even though it was "cumulative". She said we should study the past quizzes, and proceeds to put nothing like what we've seen before. Avoid at all cost for AE 2220.

This professor is the absolute worst. I will never be taking another one of her classes. She is so rude to her students. If you ask a question she'll basically call you stupid and say you should already know this. She then explains it in a way that makes it sound so obvious to her, but not obvious to anyone else. You end up understanding it less.

Awful professor. All she worked on was book examples that were already done in the book itself, and she just copied everything from the book. She talked about a topic on the last day of class for 20 seconds and skimmed through it, and half of the cumulative final were about that topic.

This is for AE 4071, that wasn't a choice here. Not the worst at teaching, as her notes are organized and she posts lectures. But horrible in every other way, incredibly tempermental and racist, plays favorites, and is unwilling to compromise. Exams are ridiculously hard and you need the book to pass. Avoid her at all costs!
Avoid this professor if you can. Does not care about teaching or her students. Absolutely do not choose her as a graduate advisor or mentor of any kind.

First time reviewing if that means anything. Out of touch, unapologetic, and uncompromising no matter what she thinks. Being confused about what she says, especially on assignments, usually just means waiting hours and redoing the problem when she changes her wording. Having the specific textbook she uses is critical and the only way to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Guidelines for this site say to not say that the prof uses favoritism for or against students. If only Dr. Smith could take a look at those guidelines herself. Take her class and you'll find out especially if you're not what she likes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Disclaimer: I've got an A in her class. Her lessons are organised and she tries to make them easy to follow. But beware as she can be quite temperamental, so catch her on her 'good' days. Remember the saying "No question is a stupid question"? When it comes to her, make sure your questions ain't stupid, as she can be quite condescending.
Meanest professor ever. Terribly bad-tempered.

Was scared of her by rep and realized i was wrong about her. She was very helpful during office hours and gave extra examples on tsquare. Exams were very straight forward from the class and hw, no surprises. usually hinted on possible exam problems. it's a hard class on its own but not so bad with her teaching. don't do hw night before, start early

She is a very good teacher, I can see where some of the comments could have come from before. She hates laziness, and don't even try to argue w/an attitude, she'll win and not be very fond of you. Attend her class and put effort forth and she will be willing to help. Basically she's like most professors at Tech, work hard and you're fine.

The previous comments are more or less correct, except the caring about students part. She's very selective - laugh at her jokes, don't call her out on errors (even if they impede understanding), and preferably work in her lab. Do that, and you're A-OK. Don't, and with her bad temper and that chip on her shoulder, just take another class.

She has a temper like a child. Also she's very feminist and if you're a guy, anything you say is pretty much disrespectful to her. Academics aside, it's not worth playing her games to get a good grade. find another professor.
Easily Angered. High Expectations. Difficult assignments. No Curves. If you get on her good side, you will do great, if you get on her bad side you will suffer.
She has good teaching abilities.  Well prepared and organized. However, she gets mad really easily.  Do not get on her**** list.

Hard class; super-organized teacher. Demands attention to detail, grades hard, but cares for student. Don't slack off in her class! But those who pay attention and do the work, do very well. Also, easy to get her mad by appearing disrespectful.

Dr. Smith was unbelievably awesome. She actually was so fun and helpful throughout the entirety of ENGL1102. Seriously one of the best and most chill professors out there. She's the real deal. She was so clear in what she expects and her grading style is just based on effort. It was a really easy class to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith was a phenomenal professor this semester—she created a low-stakes, judgment-free environment, and it greatly improved our experience. If you do the work on time, you're guaranteed an A, and it's clear that the class is one where you can learn at your own pace. Feedback is timely/helpful, and her class is one where you get to be creative.

Dr. Smith is an amazing professor, one of the best I have had so far. She's very clear about what she expects from us, and the lectures are very enjoyable. Very caring and gives excellent feedback. Would 100% recommend taking her for English.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a fantastic professor. She made class really enjoyable, she never hesitated to be respectful and honest with us, and always treated her students like equals. Our pre-class readings were fun, ranging from listening to podcasts to reading alien abduction interviews. I would 100% recommend her class.

Dr smith is a great professor she respects the students and is really understanding. You're allowed to miss up to 4 classes w/o it affecting ur grade. All assignments are based on a theme you choose and they all come together as a final portfolio. grading criteria is really clear and if you follow what she explains in class you'll for sure get an a

Dr. Smith is amazing. I 100% would recommend her to anyone. The whole class is built around projects, but if you follow the rubric, they're easy A's. You can tell Dr. Smith really likes what she's teaching because of her enthusiasm and knowledge shown during her lectures. While the subject is a bit boring, she tries to vary her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall a very chill professor. Lectures were stale at times, but you can tell she knows a lot. Participation does matter for some of the projects. If you follow the grading criteria for each project well, you will easily get an A. Not at all stressful but sometimes the readings and projects can take a little bit to finish. Would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was very respectful towards her students, along with being fair and understanding towards deadlines and assignments, just don't take advantage of this. There are always gonna be boring lectures, but she definitely knows what she talks about! One of my favorite professors, take her class!

This professor was great! Class is super easy, assignments are chill and fun, and assignment averages are always high As. Extremely low stress class, and even though she teaches the horror section, nothing we did was much scary, so don't worry if you're worried about that!
She's a very nice teacher and her class topics are fun. The assignments are not hard to complete and are very entertaining if you like the topic.
She was such a caring professor and I would 100% take her again for English! The projects were fun and very doable. If you do the assignments you definitely get an A.
Very easy to get an A, a nice professor as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is an amazing professor, and is very easy to get an A in the class.
keeps the class very engaged and gives insightful feedback. very sweet person. you dont need to worry about your grade as long as you do all the work assigned to the best of your abilities

Had Dr. Smith for ENGL1102, and her lectures and course was amazing! I really enjoyed her lectures, and the reading she assigns is not always mandatory (you can skipt the reading and pass just fine). There are few things you are graded on, but as long as you do the work and show up to class, you can get a good grade in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best professors you can get for Engl 1102. She is very lenient regarding grading, just do what's in the instructions. The homework is mostly just readings. Most of the artifacts (main projects worth the majority of your grades) are pretty straightforward and if you have questions you can just email her. Highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is the best English teacher I've ever had. You get six free skips a semester, so while attendance is taken, it's a short and easy class. There is five projects and no tests, and her material is super interesting. She succeeds at making class exciting and assignments not stressful. no stressful presentations or projects. SUPER EASY grader

This was her first-semester teaching at Tech. Her lectures are boring but she really cares about the topic and the students. Easy A if you turn all projects in on time and follow the grading criteria. Understanding and always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't the most entertaining to sit through but not mandatory (unless there was a group assignment due). Every assignment was very easy, and while some of them were quite long, due dates were VERY spaced out. Final grades are calculated in a way that you don't have to do every assignment to get an A.

You can do whatever assignments you want and however many points you get is your final grade in the class. Not many assignments to choose from but all are super easy. Attendance is not mandatory and it is easy to get good grades without going. Easily accessible outside of class, will respond to emails very fast.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Way too many projects, not allowing students to focus on real coursework.

Lectures were pretty boring, but they weren't mandatory. Some essays that felt like busy work but overall it isn't difficult to get an A. Community service hours are only a small part of the grade, I did 4 out of 8 hours that you can be graded for. Group projects are not that tedious and my group completed ours during one class.
Super easy class and very manageable work. Class wasn't required and neither were the service hours that everyone complains about.
Super easy class. You don't have to show up to any of the classes unless there's a group project. I didn't do the community service and still got a high A.
Super easy class and clear grading expectations. We are expected to do 6 hours of community service, which might be annoying, but overall it was pretty fun and manageable.

This class was incredibly easy with minimal work. Class ended early often and you technically did not have to attend. Showing up to lecture was only beneficial if you were at a borderline grade at the end of the semester and wanted to get bumped up. There was barely any work each week and the only annoying part was the required community service.

insanely boring and pointless class. still would take again bc its insanely easy to get an A. never went to lecture except to meet group members. assignments are all really easy, just plan ahead what assignments u want to do to fill bucket points. overall very easy class but the prof is lowk annoying asf

It is unavoidable that you will have to write reflection essays every other week. You will also be required to complete community service as part of this class. Overall, the class is not difficult, but it is time-consuming and too much work for a 2-credit wellness course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While the lectures are boring, the class itself is pretty easy. The class is graded on a bucket system with 110 points possible, so you can pick and choose which assignments to do. There were a lot of assignments compared to other wellness classes, but they were pretty easy. Other sections may be better, but she's not bad if you have to take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She gave at least one essay a week. For a class that's two credits, I had probably either the most or second most amount of work out of any of my classes thanks to her. The only good part was attendance wasn't mandatory because it was incredibly hard to pay attention. I liked the way she graded things out of total points though.

For starters, why was I writing papers in health class? Idk, but honestly, the class is insanely easy compared to the rigor of other courses, but I would suggest a different professor for this course. We had group assignments, where we had assigned groups, but no one showed up to class, and it just made everything more difficult than it had to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Clear grading scheme: There are 110 points you're able to get, so you can pick and choose what assignments to do or skip. There is a group project with volunteer work, but again it's not mandatory. Quizzes are open book and asynchronous, so not bad. Case studies in groups are tedious but nothing too bad. Lectures are boring but not mandatory.

dont believe the other reviews. this class was an unbelievably easy A and I didnt go to class after mid February. Volunteer work is good for you (and not mandatory), and everything is graded pretty fairly. You pretty much have an assignment every 2 weeks. You'll be okay.

Dr. Snow's okay at lecturing and the powerpoints are easy to follow. Everything's graded very clearly and you can ask TAs if there's any trouble. If you don't like the topic, you might find the lectures dry.

Dr. Snow is a pretty good lecturer. She knows her stuff for health. In general, however, the topic is not very interesting to me so it wasn't particularly fun, but that's subjective. If you want a teacher that has a clear grading system, Dr. Snow's your teacher. If you want engagement in the subject itself, the class does not really do that.
Still a free class, but considerably more work than other APPH professors. Okay to take if it fits better in the schedule, but try to do other sections
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
she expected us to complete 7 hours of outside community service that was limited to only opportunities she found and approved for us. we also had to complete this community service with at least one other person in the class or you were screwed. this is how I made my best friend, but that's not the point.

i never went to class though and i ate.

Please take a different health professor. She took the class WAYYY too seriously for a two hour, institutional requirement. So many assignments that were so annoying to do and random points would always be taken off (I'm talking a 4.8/5 on a 3 page paper). For context, you'll have three 3-page essays, 3 quizzes, 2 group projects, etc.

The lectures are really boring and not very useful for the class. None of the work is hard but if you can take this class with a different teacher do because there are so many essays, projects, volunteering, and just a lot of busy work.

please do NOT take snow. i took her because the time slots matched up with my schedule but that was a mistake. her class is not difficult, but there is way too much work that needs to be put in for a 2 credit hr course (7 hrs of volunteering, 3 group projects, 3 3+ pages papers, 3 quizzes, and way more).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She does too much bruh. Why am I volunteering for 7 hours for this 2-credit hour course... I should not be spending more time on HEALTH than my other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor for health. The semester just started and we have already had multiple assignments while other sections have only had one. There are 3 3 page essays throughout the semester along with other group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Literally like 3 weeks in and we have like 2 group projects, 3 reflections, and a few other miscellaneous assignments while others with different professors have had only one assignment which was taking one of those personality tests. Attendance isn't actually mandatory, but we've had multiple attendance check assignments.
Unbearably boring and dry lectures as well as lots of time-consuming project work. Otherwise, extremely straightforward and easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures. However, the class was really easy, and she seemed passionate about the topic. It was a point system where you had to obtain 90 points to get an A with a little over 100 points offered through projects, quizzes, or other assignments.  Did not spend much time on the class. Take Dr. Snow for an easy A.

So much busy work. Incredibly boring. When I first say the RMP reviews, I thought "as long as the class was easy, idc about the lectures" BUT PLEASE I'm urging you to just take another wellness class. There is so much busy work (3 page essays, podcasts, books, etc) The content isn't hard, just the sheer amount. Lectures are super long and boring.

The class is really boring. It's clear that she is super passionate about this class but she is a very dry lecturer. Its based on a point system so once you get 90 you dont need to show up anymore. Most points come from in class group assignments. If possible you should get a different professor.

If your looking for an easy APPH class to take, don't take it with this professor. She adds extra assignments that were unnecessary that other sections were not taking. One of them included a group project with strict requirements, she allowed no leeway even tho this project was only being taken by her section.
Dry, boring lectures but very easy class to do the bare minimum in. Should be your go-to for 1040; skim the slides before a quiz and you'll end this class with an A+

Professor Snow's lectures are relatively dry, but the materials and overall messages she tried to convey are clearly very important and powerful to be learned from. If you take advantage of her class rather than blowing it off, then it could be a very good opportunity for learning. The class itself is very easy as well, and doesn't provide stress.
Okay lectures and little work to do for the course
Very easy class and great professor who is also very understanding. I would recommend taking the online section for this course if you are able to.

Felt bad because she cares about the stuff she talks about but there's an overall lack of interest by students. You can pick and choose which assignments you want to do to get the easy A. There's a few "team" assignments but they're very easy if you delegate the work early. Quizzes are common sense.

Class is a cake walk. She gives ALOT of busy work, and makes you do community service for your grade lol but the class is not anything to worry about. More of an added assignment or two a week that just takes time but is mindless.

Very "meh" class. Extremely easy but very boing. Interesting grading structure (instead of percentage, based on added points). A LOT of assignments to get to your point goal. But overall would take again if I had to take another health class.

She does point based grading and as long as you reach 90 points out of 115 total, you get an A, but a service project 18 of those points. All the assignments beyond that are very easy, the only thing you might need to put in some work for is the team assignment. Just don't go to lecture, attendance isn't mandatory and her lectures are super boring.

I took this course async, so all lectures and activities were online. They were easy activities due on saturday weekly, took no more than an hour to complete. This course has a point based system, so as long as you rack up enough points doing random assignments, you can finish the class early in the semester with an A and not complete the rest.

I recommend you use the corresponding lecture slides with every quiz, which is allowed. Pick and choose the assignments you want to do go get the A, it's not that hard. Just don't wait until the end of the semester to accumulate the points you need - get your A as early in the semester as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No surprises in this class. On day 1, youre told all the opportunities you have to get however many out of 116 points you want (90 points being all you need to get an A). If you do most of the assignments and dont bomb the pretty easy quizzes, this class should be the least of your worries at Tech.

It's simple: complete the assigned work, get an A. Her lectures are quite boring, but she knows how busy we can be during the semester. She tries to be as lenient as possible and gives so many opportunities to get the A. I would recommend if you want the health requirement out of the way and end up with an A.

Dr. Snow's lectures were boring, but she understands how busy we can get, so she is really flexible with grades and due dates. She responds to emails relatively quickly too. This class requires a good amount of time consuming work to be done. However, she gives a lot of opportunities for points, so we can choose which assignments we want to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's a lecture based health class. Not interesting or fun, but I never expected it to be. The class is based on grade accumulation, so once you've done enough assignments to get a 90+, you can ignore it for the rest of the semester. Prof Snow seems to care about the material and the mental health of her students. Easy A, but very boring.

Professor Snow conducted a straightforward class that allowed me to have more than enough opportunities to make up late work and ask for help. She grades on grade accumulation, so all you have to do is get 90 points worth of grades and then you are finished.

I intensely disliked this class. I found the lectures to be long and boring, the topics to be boring as well, and some of the material was incredibly problematic and not suited for a 21st-century view on health. The only good thing was that Dr. Snow is a very easy grader and like most health classes, the assignments are simple and easy.

You can basically do the bare minimum and get an A. She expects you to do a lot of work, but you really don't have to in all honesty. The quizzes "cover" hour-long TED talks, but you can just google stuff honestly. In-person might be a bit different, but online the class was extremely easy. Grade builds up to an A (certain assignments worth points)
Easy class, do the work and get an A.

She's super nice and understanding, but there is just so much unnecessary work. My roommate was in another section and he had like 5 assignments the whole semester. If you do the work its easy to get an A, but there is just so much more work than other sections. If you have to take her don't worry about doing poorly just spending 2-3 hours/week.
Good professor. If you do the assignments, you will get an A! Nothing to worry about if you feel confident doing the work. There are several extra credit opportunities.

Makes health harder than it should be. I was told it's the easiest course i would take at tech, but she used to make us work way more than the other sections. Super kind and understanding though, just shouldn't be your first choice for this course.
Probably one of the worst, least organized classes I've ever attempted. David is super pompous. If I could give him a 0 I would.

Overall I thought Smith did a good job of teaching the course. In his class, you got what you put into it. He encourages questions and does his best to answer. He cares for his students and wants to help you succeed. His examples are often very confusing and are easy to get lost in.

Wasn't very clear in lectures. I had some background in programming and did fine, but others in the class had difficulty understanding topics - recitations are invaluable if this is your first time with code. Tests are pen and paper so come well prepared and know the language like the back of your hand.

D. Smith does not seem to get enough credit. I took his class and found it easy to understand and entertaining. Many of the other comments here say that he can sometimes go too fast, this is true, but he also greatly values and encourages questions. If you ask him questions he will more often than not explain it very clearly!

Dr. Smith has a very impressive professional background, but he lacks some teaching skills. He does not teach students the basics and logic behind each topic, jumping straight into rather complex examples. Make sure to attend recitation and Help Desk, as these will be your best resources to actually learn the material.

Do not take Dr. Smith! He goes straight into functions with no introduction on basic programming knowledge. I tried to read and learn on my own because the lectures were doing me absolutely no help. Help desk was useful, but having Dr. Smith destroyed my self esteem in that class. I had to withdrawal because I was not going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Your professor really doesn't matter as long as you attend recitation (or even another professor's lecture) and do the homework. Midterms are pretty faithful to the practice tests. That said, I never benefitted from lecture and hardly ever went. He didn't teach so much as go through examples, and his handwriting is completely illegible.

lectures are super unhelpful and he talks as if everyone has been coding for a few years and its just a casual convo. Says some really weird/sometimes insulting things during lecture as well. Go to help desk, do homework early .. or just do wtv it takes to get Kantwon

Professor Smith is a nice guy but his lectures are not that worth it. Go to recitations and do the homework, that's the only way you could succeed in the course. Also, the course is pretty time consuming, so form study groups and and go to the help desks.

Lecture didn't help at all. Most of my learning occurred on my own while doing the homework and using TA resources. Definitely attend recitation and attend TA office hours; they are the only source of hope. There's a fair amount of extra credit on each homework assignment plus a whole extra credit assignment at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I have never done any sort of coding in my life, and it seems like Smith assumes that everyone has a coding background. Every time I went to lecture I would get more frustrated because literally nothing he said made sense. If you do end up with him GO TO RECITATION and get help from your TAs. Clear your confusion right away or else it will pile up.

David Smith is a nice guy but his lectures are not great. But in all honesty matlab is not a hard coding language, it is how the course is set up that makes it difficult. Just go to recitation sessions. The final will replace tests if you do well.
Smith is absolutely terrible. Just make your schedule so that you can go to Kantwon's lectures. Take advantage of the resources like Helpdesk and PLUS sessions for this class.

He's a nice guy. His lectures can be really cool and fun if you have prior coding experiences and really know the material. However, if you do not have prior coding experience, I would not recommend taking him, as his lectures utilize a lot of "next step" rather than the basics. Do all the tedious homework, and utilize TAs and recitation.

There's a LOT of homework. However, it only counts for a relatively low percent of your grade and doesn't get difficult until around 2/3 into the class. Final project was a bit of a joke. He often gets VERY off track (once timed for 17 mins) and can be difficult to understand from too far away. The recitation TAs were better than him in my opinion.

Would not recommend. By not having prior CS knowledge, his lectures can be confusing and unhelpful. Im pretty sure this man is highly skilled in MATLAB but he doesn't know how to explain it effectively to a bunch of kids that know nothing about MATLAB. Couldnt attend Kantwon's lectures but TAs know how bad smith is and do their best to catch us up

The problem with this class is that Smith just gives crazy examples in class and really never covers the fundamentals or goes off on tangent stories that have nothing to do with the concepts. I heard some recitation TAs are good but mine just went over the basics which isn't very helpful when homework is due on Friday and recitation is on Thursday.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I wish I could give Dr. Smith a higher rating because he's absolutely hilarious and easily my favorite professor this past semester but his lectures are not conducive for learning. I came in with no coding experience what-so-ever but i found even having Smith, I was able to learn all the material through recitation and doing homework.

He wrote the literal book on the subject, but neither he nor his book is very helpful. If you want help, go to Kantwon's lectures since he actually teaches. For actual help, you have to go to the TA or the success center. Also, almost all of your grade is from the tests, so study for the tests and skip the homework if you have limited time.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you CAN go to kantwon's lectures, do it. I couldn't, so I stayed with smith and it was fine. Everything is the same in 1371 across sections, so there are tons of resources to get help and do well. If you're in smith's lecture you'll be fine and learn the material, but he's not as fun as Kantwon even though he knows everything there is on MATLAB

Prof. Smith is a nice guy, but an awful teacher. I stopped going to class two weeks in because the lectures were not helpful at all. Fortunately, Matlab is something you can teach yourself for the most part (I did have some prior coding experience though). You are also allowed to go to any recitation you want, so make sure to get a good TA.
Go to Kantwon's lectures. This man does not know how to teach. Most boring class

If you plan on making a good grade, you don't need to go to his lectures. Just go to a recitation early in the week (you can go to any recitation you want) and you'll learn everything you need to know to be able to do the homework, which there is a lot of. Smith knows his stuff, but doesn't explain it very well. Lectures are very boring.

Smith is a nice person, but he is not the best at teaching. If you have no programming experience, I would not advise that you take his class. If you know Java or a C-like language, you can do all right. Homework is given weekly (same homework for all CS 1371 classes), graded by an automated program. TAs and other students are your best resource.

His lectures aren't very interesting and he rambles half of the time. You need to be really focused to understand things. He knows a lot about Matlab but isn't good at explaining what he knows. The homework is slightly challenging and the tests are a little tricky but both are generally very fair.

Smith isn't a teacher by trade. He's a veteran computer scientist/aerospace engineer so he brings experience and stories. Lectures won't help you learn CS1371 but it is worth hearing what he has to say.  Recitations are FLEXIBLE.  I recommend that you find a good one. DO CODE COMMENTING FOR E EXTRA CREDIT. HW is how you learn. Find friends/groups.

If you've never coded before then going to Smith's lectures will be very difficult for you to actually grasp the concept; he uses really strange examples and doesn't just talk about the general idea of what you should know to complete hw. Watch kantwon's videos & go to help desk!! Also make sure you comment your code and do all practice tests.

Smith really does not do a good job of teaching the material. He assumes everyone knows coding and his examples are impossible to understand. His lecture is pointless. Youre better off taking kantwon for this class. TAs are very helpful and theres lots of homework(coursewide- all teachers). Great guy, but he cant teach well
Smith was useless in this course. I skipped lecture and attended Kantwon's lecture and recitation. The TAs were very useful in this course.

Lots of homework, but that's not specific to the professor. Lecture was rarely useful, as he seems to assume the students know a lot more than they actually do. You can definitely get an A only by going to recitation, since the TAs know he's not the best at teaching.

I think Smith is a great professor. However, his teaching style is probably not for everyone, and people who have never programmed before can have a pretty tough time. He lectures a week ahead of the weekly homework and his examples can sometimes get a bit complicated. There's a lot of extra credit, be sure to always do it.

Never coded before, then taking his class would be disaster. Smith is a good guy, he makes efforts to make the lectures interesting, but I just learn nothing from his lecture. Homework and recitation is where I learn everything.
Lectures were next to worthless. Recitations and TAs are much more helpful, but optional too if you have programming experience.

He's a good guy, but his class is awful. When the topic was iteration, he was teaching about putting geese on a sunset. He knows what he's talking about, but his lectures are worthless and you're better off learning from the book that he wrote.

Smith is the sweetest, silliest man, but he cannot teach well at all. I went to help desk weekly, extra recitations, and read the textbook, yet I still struggled with this class. I began to attend Kantwon's lectures, which were incredibly beneficial. If you are in one of Smith's sections, go to Kantwon's lecture.

He is very confusing and his sense of humor is terrible. He teaches next week's subject when the homework is still on last week's subject, so it confuses you because you can't use the new things you learned on the homework until you have homework on that subject. Go to lecture for PRS extra credit then leave. use the MATLAB guide.

Prof. Smith teaches the class as a way to learn problem solving. While it is interesting at times, his lectures don't help that much with the homework. Also, start working on the homework early, and go to the helpdesk if needed.

Smith throws you into the deep end with MATLAB while he explains concepts in terms of Java to CS majors in class, leaving newbies to hang. His humor is awful and the lecture consists of watching him do programming irrelevant to the homework. Tests are extremely challenging. Find a great recitation TA and do the HW at help desk to save time.

Run. Avoid getting this professor. His lectures don't help because half the class he spends telling you about some worthless stuff, and then the other half is him just doing random coding that is pretty abstract. You don't even have to go to lecture. If you get this professor, pray, go to recitation, do your HW, and study hard.

His lectures don't help much because he just codes stuff in class related to the topic, but he doesn't "teach" concepts. You learn concepts and do actual problems related to hw in recitations. The recitations are what you should really go if you want to learn something, and when you are doing your homework.

Unless you have experience with MATLAB, you will have a difficult time with the class. The problem sets are excessively difficult and take up far too much time for an introductory class. Lectures don't help much but there's wrong with the professor. Nice guy. My advice is get a group of friends, work together, work early AND GO TO HELP DESK!

He is really passionate about the material and is a pretty interesting dude. Lectures would be awesome if you already knew the material because he uses difficult terminology and goes at a fast pace. Recitation and homework are crucial. If you do these by yourself you will get an A. What you get on the final is pretty much what you get in the class.

This is a class you have to get through, like it or not. Smith is hilarious but the lectures are useless. You will learn a small bit from recitation and everything else by teaching yourself. FIND AND MAKE FRIENDS WITH PEOPLE WHO KNOW C/C++/JAVA OR YOU WILL STRUGGLE. Helpdesk is essential for harder HWs but they're really slow to help out. Beware.

Funny and engaging lectures! Smith is a great guy but his lectures are pretty useless. He uses way too complicated examples to teach simple concepts which really  takes away from the learning. He knows everything about MATLAB though. He wrote the textbook.

I agree that lectures aren't necessary for tests, but I thought he was hilarious (!!) and told great stories about working in the early (euphemism: legacy) days of CS. Also he was very open to questions on what classes I should take, his views on different programming languages from working with data manipulation &c.

His lectures are a waste of time. Just go to recitation and help desk. DO YOUR HOMEWORK!!!! Doing your homework is he only way to learn in this class. And beware, the homework will take hours and hours, but go to help desk and recitation to get help on it or else you're screwed.
I love him but lectures are absolutely worthless. Go to recitation and do the homework. be diligent!

The class is difficult, but the tests and hw are the same between all of the sections. He wrote the textbook, so he is very knowledgeable  about the topic. He is one of the most passionate professors & truly loves teaching. He wants to make a difference in his students' lives. If you actually attend lecture and get to know him, you will love him.

Don't listen to anybody who tells you that this class is impossible. While the class will be time consuming it's very doable if you just put in the time and effort. Homework is semi-difficult but forces you to know the material.  Tests are challenging but not hard. If you do all the work yourself you can get an A easily.
Tough class but he taught me well. Quirky sense of humor from being British.
Lecture is absolutely useless. Don't expect to learn anything from him - you'll have to figure it out yourself.

He is a very funny and enjoyable man.  His lectures are not confusing other than trying to figure out what you are supposed to take away from it.  He is very willing to help out when you need it.  He made me enjoy going to class and I don't think he deserves that many bad ratings on here because a majority of the people don't even come to class.

Very funny. He's an old British man with a great sense of humor (many times at his own cost). His lectures are sometimes boring and confusing, but he does everything he can to answer your questions completely, so ask questions if you are confused. He is also eager to help in any way he can. He is overall a great person as well. Highly recommend.

A great person, a tough teacher. As someone who has never coded before, I was expecting an easy start, just like a language class. My hopes were quickly shattered. The grammar of MatLab is difficult to understand, and that was only exacerbated by Prof. Smith's tangential lectures. I must admit he will take time to answer your every question, though
Class is useless. Learned everything on my own. Homework wasn't hard if you understand the concepts but they are time consuming.

Avoid him at all costs. This class is awful and this professor does not teach. I have no coding background and this class has been the most stressful class I have taken at tech. When you take this class, make sure you don't have any other hard classes because this takes up so much time.

If you have absolutely no background with coding, you're going to have a bad time. Smith is very unclear and almost assumes everyone has coding experience. He tries to be funny, but just isn't. Recitation is where you do all learning. Overall, tests are not too horrible if you study.  Homework will take up the majority of your time.

Incredibly unhelpful and made it difficult for a beginner to understand programming as a whole or MATLAB-- even with some prior experience, I found it difficult to adapt to an already troublesome program. His teaching was lacking and the homework only served to exacerbate the issue. Going to recitations/review sessions are basically a requirement.
He was good for the summer. He did write the book after all.
His class is fairly interesting and tests are pretty fair. One-on-one, he is one of the most helpful professors I've ever had. Plus, his lectures are pretty funny!

Dr. Smith isn't a bad professor, but he can be frustrating. He likes to do his own thing and have you pick up what you need to know from his work. He wrote the book, so you'd think he'd be more direct, but he wants his students to dig and discover things on their own. Sort of opposite of Marsicano. You learn most from HW anyway, so don't worry.

He's a funny guy, makes the lecture very entertaining. You can tell by the way he teaches in his lectures that he does know his stuff. Read the book before he covers it in lecture, if you ask him questions he will clarify. And he is approachable for help. His TAs are also very helpful.

He's an interesting guy, but his lectures are useless. Instead of explaining HOW to code, he rather goes up and shows the class what cool things HE can do using Matlab. It's a very difficult class in general. He recommends you don't buy the textbook, and I did not, but now I wish I had. There are very helpful entries in it.

As the person below me said, be prepared to learn everything yourself.  He is a simply awful instructor most of the time.  VERY rarely he teaches an informative lesson but most of the time you just watch him doing some gigantic example which doesn't pertain much to what you actually need to know at a rate that you certainly cannot follow.

His lectures are some of the most useless, rambling wastes of time imaginable.  I learned absolutely nothing from attending his class, mostly because he never explained fundamental concepts, choosing instead to jump into pointless, long-winded examples with little-to-no justification.  Be prepared to learn everything on your own or in recitation.

RUN!!! This guy is awful. I promise you will learn C better on your own using "C for dummies". The final is a huge portion of your grade. If you make bad on the final you fail the class. The class averages when were always below 60. Just take someone else if you can.

His lectures are more or less worthless. The best way to learn the material is to go to recitation and do lots of practice on your own. The tests are somewhat difficult, but Smith does full grade replacement with the final exam, so as long as you know the stuff by the end of the semester, you'll get a good grade.

1372 is C programing for the GameBoy Advance. I found this class to be a really easy A. If you hated 1371, 1372 will be hell. I never bought the book, can't comment on it. The professor has slight british accent, NBD. He doesn't teach in class, he just writes a program with the class related to the hw. If I wasn't CompE, that would have been death.

Good guy, likes to joke around, doesn't always go over everything you need to know. Usually will just write code in class to solve a problem related to the material you're learning. Doesn't teach much in class, but very approachable for help if you need it.

Okay, so this class is hard, but it is regardless of lecturer. The TA's are helpful at recitation, and if you find yourself getting lost, find someone to explain the material soon because if you are really on top of things, you'll be fine in his class. Smith is pretty entertaining if you just give him a chance.

Great Teacher. His in-class-examples are far more difficult than the homeworks but if you can keep up by just paying attention then you'll understand what's going on. Homeworks take up the most time and tests are very easy. If you want to get an A on the test, go to recitation. And also, help desks are VERY helpful. I was never turned away.
omg!!!!!!! run while you can! don't ever ever take him! he is horrible!

He wrote the book, and expects that you read the book before class and know that information. In class, he only goes over examples that are more difficult than you'll ever have to do. The recitations are REALLY helpful, they teach the basics that are in the book. Homeworks are hard, but tests aren't too bad if you do your own homework.

He is pretty funny and kind of strange. His examples in class go way over our heads and you leave the class more confused than you were before. By nature, this class is hard, and David Smith does nothing to make it better. TAKE MARSICANO'S CLASS

One of the worst professors. He a horrible teacher, the lecture is useless, and the TAs do nothing. Every time i went to office hours for help i was told to leave and fix my messy code. Practice tests do not resemble the test. Homeworks are extremely difficult. Assumptions are made on your previous knowledge. TAKE BILL LEAHY HE IS AMAZING.

Doesn't know how to teach. You are more confused coming out than going in. Don't waste your time going to this teacher. When teaching a new language, you must start slow and explain things in simple terms. He uses complicated terminology that NO ONE understands. take a different teacher if you can.

Yes, his lectures are absurd, but a decent background of coding is all you need to understand them really. The homework is tough and the tests are nothing like the homework. Recitations are where it's at to ace the tests (i never did). Nobody ever knows for sure how he curves. Just go to class if you can. He does recognize faces.

Funny guy. Teaching methodology consists of him tackling huge coding problems while the class watches. Very good if you are interested in computer science. Otherwise, not so much. Go to recitation, it's where you learn things.
The class is useless, hw are totally irrelevant, test average are around the 60s, horrible teacher over all.
Lectures are terrible. Smith just can't teach very well. Homework is very difficult, due weekly. Class average is very low.

Smith is a genuinely nice man with a good sense of humor but he just cannot teach. He frequently uses terminology that he must think is common knowledge but most of us have no clue what he is talking about, resulting in a lot of confusion. He spends entire lectures spanning several days on example problems yet barely explains what he's even doing.

I appreciate his attempt to get the class to ask questions. However, I get tired of, daily, spending an entire lecture on an example problem, will little to no background of what we are doing, and applying it to a large amount of homework. Its not teaching. If I had not learned several languages previously, I would be struggling. Don't take lightly

Guy is funny, but the applause after every question usually means I don't get to hear what the question OR the answer was. Homework levels are off the charts, w/ massive homework asnmts being due each week meaning Thur is always nthg but me sitting in an uncomfy chair for 14+ hrs. I also have 2 read the book to lrn nythg snc lctrs r 1 stp ahd of HW

The best professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech. He is the author of the textbook for this class, so he really knows the material. I found his explanations to be very logical, but be warned: you must not get behind, else his class will become incomprehensible.  The class is very tough, but if you invest work and time, you will succeed.
Hilarious guy.
if you can take this class over the summer with another professor. going to class will put you to sleep.

One of the most worthless professors you will encounter.  He is a very nice guy, but is completely ineffective at even attempting to teach any useful material what-so-ever...perhaps he relys on the TA's for that...but most of them do a pretty shotty job.  I am quite frankly ashamed that I had to pay money to be put through his 'teaching'.

Fun teacher, Class is normally entertaining, but you will rarely learn anything in class. He is very helpful in Office Hours, and the TA's are always very helpful. Learning C with him was a breeze, but he enjoys giving large amounts of coding homework. His practice tests are usually a mirror of the real test.
Clear, entertaining, helpful.  Great professor, I highly recommend him!

I started the class under the old format, but dropped. Retook under the new format. Somethings have improved, but still not an easy course. If your EE/ECE, you have to take it, and I think Smith is the best choice. He's tough but fair. Seems to truly enjoy teaching.
Smith is really funny and has a different joke every class. He explains things very clearly, and he wrote the book
Smith is really funny and has a different joke every class. He explains things very clearly, and he wrote the book

Unless you have experience with C programming, you will struggle in this class. You'll get 0's on your homework (it's always impossible to do) and fail your tests (along with the majority of the class). The TA's were just as horrible as Smith. He barely curves in the end (despite 70% of the class failing). Avoid taking him if you can.

Also known as CS 1803.   Format has changed since last semester, but Smith is still an excellent teacher.  He really does seem to care about his students and their grades.  Never curves.  One homework a week: 4-5 hours usually if you know what you're doing.  3 tests and a final, all containing lots of tricky questions.   C on a C++ compiler.
Lectures were boring but I attended all of them and it sort of helped me understand the basic concepts. Review sessions and recitations were great and prepared me for the tests.

Smith is quite possibly one of the worst lecturers at Georgia Tech. He is incredibly boring, and he doesn't know how to teach the subject adequately. In class he just plays with the matlab program rather than teaching us the fundamentals of programming. You'll learn more by going to the help desk, recitation, and help sessions. AVOID HIM!!
Kind of get the feeling he doesn't care too much about the students.  Lectures are pointless to attend.

I didn't think attending lecture fo this class was helpful at all. I made an A in the class, but only because I went to the help desk religiously and attended all recitations and review sessions. Toward the end of the semester, I stopped attending lecture because it only confused me. Most of the people who I've talked to agree with me.

Smith's class is WAY overrated. He is not that great of a professor. I often fell asleep during his lectures they were so boring. It is obvious that he cares very little about the welfare of his students. I'm making an A in the class with no prior programming experience whatsoever.

Not a very good professor. I was often lost in his lectures. He does have an ok sense of humor. I learned most of the material on the homework or in recitation. Tests are pretty easy though. No curve.
Smith is a nice guy. He sometimes moves a little too fast in lectures however, and sometimes puts material on the exams that was not covered thoroughly in lecture. Recitation is very important.

He tried to teach the best he could and was nice, funny, and approachable, but I was usually pretty lost during the lectures. But this is a hard class, no matter who you have, I guess. I don't think it really matters who you have for the class, though. Just hope to do well during the Matlab portion.
He is very nice. I went to his office often, and He was very helpful. Actually, the class is difficult, but you can get a better grade by asking questions with TA or Professor.

He is one of the best CS teachers.  He was EXTREMELY helpful.  He wasn't my teacher but I attended his lectures.  The class itself is very hard, not the professor.  It is a newer class so things got very messed up with testing, grading, and such.
He is awsome! and very funny!:)...He is not my teacher but I sit in his class instead of the one I have registered!
boring
Very helpful, as well as fun.
No Comments
No Comments
Very funny in subtle ways.  He'd be a great neighbor.

Literally the perfect professor to have for a first semester freshman. Insanely understanding and willing to work with you to ensure you do your best. Class material is also engaging and interesting to listen to. Some writing but its fun. Small class size so class discussion is not nerve-wracking at all. Very easy to communicate with & accessible.

Snyder is great. The topic of his class is super interesting, and he makes the major projects engaging. The third one is a minecraft build. Attendance is not required like it is in most english classes, but it is highly recommended, and there are some classes you need to attend.

In-class writings were kinda annoying and lectures can sometimes get boring, but he is a good person are cares about everyone in the class. Projects were interesting and something that I would not expect for a ENGL class. Do the assigned readings before each week and dont wait until the last minute to work on assignments.

I love Shane. I would take a bullet for him. This man is so supportive and sweet and is genuinely such a good person an he has actually kept my mental health intact this semester. 10/10. I hope to get him next semester too for 1102.

He actually made the course so interesting, and gave the best feedback on my essays that I have ever received. I felt like I had room to be creative and think outside of the box with his projects. You can also tel he is passionate about what he teaches which makes it all the more interesting. Definitely one of the best professors I have had.

I took English 1101 during the summer semester. The class was centered around video games so be prepared for that. It was overall easy and straightforward. Professor Snyder is fun, interactive, and easily accessible. 9/10 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Snyder is overall a great and caring professor. He is very accessible both during office hours and on Discord. The assignments were pretty fun and relatively easy, very relaxed grading. Only slight complaint I have is that there's a lot of group work. Groups are randomly assigned too. Often felt like my individual learning wasn't being tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Snyder is very caring for his students and wants to help you learn. He is understanding and gives a lot of freedom within projects, as long as you keep him updated, he will support you.
Video Game Rhetoric is a great view of how to teach English, lovely class topics and fun instructions and projects
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's an awesome professor who cares about his students.
Very caring professor, loves to interact with his students and have discussions. Forgiving on assignments and fun topic. Would 100% recommend.

Took his ENGL 1101 course during Ignite. Wonderful professor! Very kind, a good grader, and passionate about his students and class. The discussions were fun and engaging, and the workload was fair, not bad at all. Just do your work and you'll receive the grade you expect. Very fun class to take, even if video games aren't necessarily your thing.

Professor Snyder was a fantastic professor. His class is based on video game rhetoric, so I found his topic really fascinating. Dr. Snyder was also a very caring professor that always went out of his way to make sure his students were doing alright and understanding the course material. His feedback was great and he also grades easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: An extremely approachable and considerate professor. Also the first English teacher to ever give me thorough and actionable feedback on my assignments and discussions. Great prof, 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Shane is an amazing professor who is always willing to help his students succeed. The course isn't too difficult, and the topic(video games) is very interesting.

English is what you make of it. His topic was identity and social change in video games. That topic appealed to me more than the other english topics. However, you may find your appeal for video games to falter after this course. Assignments are not difficult. Just put in effort and you will be fine. Good choice for english.

His instructions are clear, his grading is fair, and I thought his topic was interesting. He is easily available through office hours and email and common questions are usually addressed in the next week's video. The workload is light except for the weeks when you play video games, which take 2-8 hours each. Great course if you don't enjoy English.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is a professor of all time. Lectures were more boring than watching paint dry. During every lecture I would look around the room of 250+ students and noticed that not a single one was paying attention, rather doing other class's homework, coding, listening to music or playing Minecraft.

Very boring, long lectures, but you don't need to go to do well in the class. Just do the work on canvas and get 6 volunteer hours and you'll be fine. Not a good professor, but you'll be fine if you take this class. Her lectures honestly have nothing to do with health, even though it's a health class. A lot about sustainability for some reason.

Professor Snow clearly loves her students and I could see that from day 1. If you have any personal problems that might interfere with your grade in the class, she'll go out of her way to help you. That being said, the class was a LOT of busy work for just a 2 credit class. I'd suggest taking 1050 to get your APPH credit.

Its health so it is gonna be easy. Snow was very easy but she did have some annoying papers and projects that took a while. Her lectures are very dry and I ended up not going at all and just figuring everything out at home. I have a 105 in the class right now and have only been to 3 lectures the entire semester. Easy class to say the least.
It's health. Easy class. She gets the job done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is nice and kind.Seems like she cares about students, like a kind teacher. But the class itself is about exposing us to far left ideologies on the guise of"Health". I dont know if she is just forced to teach them. If you take her, do the work and get the grade, but do not get brain washed. This is criticism of the course and uni more than her.

The team assignments were so time consuming, asking us to create a full business plan or several hours of community service. Lectures were boring and imposed scientifically unproven information, like health at every size, on us. The class was less about health and more like a summary of the far left agenda, and I'm not even republican.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course content itself was pretty easy and she posted all of the slideshows that she used on canvas, and as long as you look through them you can very reasonably get an A. The quizzes were all open note, and there were often small group activities during the lectures for a grade. We did have one assigned reading with a discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the class during the height of covid, quizzes/tests were quite easy and the class worked on a point system where 90 points = A etc. where something like 112 points were offered.

Dr. Snow understands your busy schedule and her class won't take up much of your time. You don't really need to attend lectures just look through the slides before quizzes. Lots of opportunities for credit so getting an A is super simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took this class ASYC. Not my favorite class, but I feel like I learned something in Health, which surprised me. Tests were open note and basically copy-pasted from the lectures, so it's an easy A if you just watch the lectures and do a couple group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Snow is a wonderful choice for APPH. I took her class asynchronously. I really enjoyed the content and there are many different routes to getting an A. I did not even have to do some projects since I was able to do well on the midterms(which are not very difficult). Snow is very approachable and really cares about the wellbeing of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The only reason difficulty is a 3 is because this class takes TIME. Lot's of memorizing misc facts and statistics, very little applicable knowledge. Prof Snow herself is alright, but the group projects were just such a commitment for a 2 credit hour course. You're better off taking APPH1050, glad to be out of this class.

You are basically given the chance to get up to 130 points in this class and if you get at least 90 you get an A. It's easy to do and the tests are very easy with crib sheets. There are lots of projects so it takes some time but it's quite easy.

Dr. Snow is a very caring and understanding person. Though lectures may not be the most engaging, you will still learn the content that you need to know. Not a class I had to stress about. Assignments were simple but do require some effort. Can reach out to her about anything.

Hands down most boring professor I've ever taken. If I didn't have friends in the class I probably wouldn't have ever shown up to lecture. As long as you complete all the assignments do okay on the tests you should be fine; I didn't even submit the final project and got an A. Memorize powerpoints for the tests.

APPH1040 is more lecture/test/assignment based. She was an okay lecturer, but the course was extremely boring. It is graded on a points system, so you only need to accumulate 90 points over the course of the semester to get an A. There's around 120 points that you can get from assignments outside of class. Start early so you don't panic at the end!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: WAY too much work for a 2 credit health class. She cares about health and her students a lot, but her boring lectures aren't fun. Tests aren't worth much, but they are based strictly on memorization of useless facts, hard to study for. Group projects, case studies, essays, guest lectures, reviews.... easy to get an A but so much work to get it.
So much extra credit in this class that its hard not to get an A. I didn't even have to take the final to get the A.

Lecture felt generally uninformative and useless. Exam questions could be from out of left field, and I found that amount of studying didn't affect my scores much. Homeworks are high quantity but exceedingly simple. Just don't forget them. Group project is important but easy enough with fairly free reign. Snow makes the course fair, not fun.

Overall, super annoying teacher with an even more annoying class. This is an engineering school, no one cares about a health class but Snow clearly doesnt understand this as she bogs the class down with pointless projects and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fairly easy grades. Just lots of work and not worth the effort since it's only 2 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graded on the content of visiting lecturers.

Snow is not a bad person. In fact, I think she actually cares about her students a lot, but what makes her so disliked among students is that she takes health far too seriously. I was in section L, and we had to write papers each week, do a group project, do case studies, article critiques, etc... Soooo much work for a 2 credit hour class.

A pretty easy course--you can receive up to 4% extra credit in addition to others. As long as stay on top of easy online quizzes and assignments, the class is not difficult. PPTs (and kinda the online readings) have all needed for tests; I didn't pay attention in lectures much. There is a group assignment that is easy. Snow is pretty generous.

40% of the class grade was guest speaker lectures that required us to write a 2.5-page reflection every week and no actual material taught by the professor. Even the exams were mostly from guest speaker material. The ludicrous amount of assignments and group projects make this class extremely high stress for a 2 credit health class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class is like any other classes you may take at GT: lectures, homework, paper, group project, exams, etc. BUT IT SHOULDN'T BE! APPH is supposed to be one of easy classes w/o a lot of hw but this class does. She gives out high reflection (a total of 5, 4 pages each) grades but tests are a bit hard. I'm borderlining A & B after lots of effort.

Her section of the class is much more work than the same class taught by other professors. She gives the most ludicrous exams which aren't even relevant to "Health" in any way. You literally don't learn anything
Just don't take her. Her class has disproportionately high assignments for a 2-hour class.

Idk what all these bad reviews are about - I never go to class unless there's a guest speaker cause it sometimes shows up on the test. All you have do is study the PPTs for the tests and you'll be fine. Only 1 group project that isn't that strenuous. Weekly Pearson assignments with all of the answers on Quizlet. Very easy class with no final.
Extremely mediocre for the most part. She would probably rather be teaching her biostatistics class, since the exams are full of memorizing seemingly random numbers.

This lady is the worst professor I have ever had. She takes this class way too seriously and knows every student in that class is only there because they have to be and milks it. Seriously, I would've rather taken the 8 am section of this class to avoid her as a teacher. Get ready to be told you're unhealthy for being a college student.

Professor Snow was not as bad as I expected. The class material was relatively interesting and applicable to my life. If you decide to take her class, get started on the extra credit opportunities early or you might end up like me with an 89. I didn't try too hard, just occasionally reviewing the study guide/articles/presentations she gave us.

Dr. Snow cares about health and wants her students to succeed, which is great. However, the lectures were boring, with her simply reading from PowerPoints (making notetaking fairly pointless). The tests had multiple questions relating to arcane statistics from the PowerPoints. The assignments were really easy, and there was lots of extra credit.

The tests are easy to study for but specific, so just memorize the PowerPoints she gave out before the tests and you should be good. There are pretty useless projects, but they're not challenging and help the community, so not too bad. You can also get up 4 points of extra credit fairly simply, so not hard to get an A if you just take it seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class involves too much busy work and doesn't teach you very much if anything at all about health. Test's are hard because they are full of random statistics and stuff never covered in class lectures. Lots of extra credit offered, but be wary, this is not the easy A class that it should be. Prof Snow is passionate, but not the best teacher.

Way too much work for a health class. Get ready for debates/papers/other assignments. Tests are heavily based on statistics. Don't fall for the fact that she has a good GPA record -- it's not worth it and that GPA comes from her outside-of-class extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Snow is pretty knowledgeable about all the concepts we learn, which makes the lectures somewhat interesting.
