She takes it seriously, but she also complicates things for students and herself. There's an okay amount of work; it can get a little confusing if you don't stay on top of it/ don't go to lecture. Gives many extra credit opportunities.
way too much work for a health professor. She warns you thats its at tech so it should be challenging. Save yourselves, take someone else!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Compared to other health professors, Dr. Snow gave so much work! I was jealous how my roommate's health class consisted of 3 easy tests with a couple easy assignments. For Dr. Snow, the tests are bizarre, there is this huge group project, assignments are ridiculous and her lectures are painful. For the test, study the powerpoints and you'll get a B

Means well, but pitakes health class way too seriously. We're just taking this so we can graduate. Tests ask questions about very specific statistics and facts rather than general concepts so I felt like I didn't learn anything. Generous with extra credit, felt like I had to work a little too hard for a health class, but made an A at the end

This class was excessively hard for a health class. Tests asked obscure questions from class and reading. The homework she gives is pointless and her assignments are tedious. Avoid this class with Snow at all costs. Take with a different prof of take 1050. The only reason I didn't get a C in the class was because of the extra credit, annoying.

I was expecting this class to be easy, but the test were so nit picky (multiple choice) but about the stupidest things. You're expected to know statistics and numbers which is ridiculous. She is a boring lecturer but go to class for the extra credit. She is very generous with extra credit but her tests are stupid. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was the most boring class I've ever had to sit through. The tests were really detail oriented and annoying.. But in the end I didn't put in much work and slid through with an A.

Dr. Snow wasn't the best lecturer, but the guest speakers we had were awesome. Maybe it was so boring because it was a 2-hour long class on a Friday afternoon. Tests are very detail-oriented, so be sure to study the PowerPoints and the statistics she puts on them. Easy A if you show up to class and pay attention.

Very boring lectures. Honestly do the extracredits, don't go to class and just know the numbers on the powerpoints and the content on the assigned book chapters, hope for the best on the tests. I liked the subject but she only read from the screen for two hours making it painful.

Her tests include a stupid amount of vocabulary.  Her lecture are verbatim the powerpoint but go to class for the occasional extra credit opportunity.  Overall sucky class to be in and tests are annoyingly in depth.

Definitely not an easy A or good professor. Whether you want to take health seriously or not, Snow is not a far teacher in my opinion. The lectures are easy and boring, and she just reads off the powerpoint. Then the tests are super specific. I read through all the lecture notes and book to study and still am not sure where she finds the material.

40% of the class is participation: if you do it, you'll get a 100, but the other 60% is divided between three, equally difficult exams. Although they are multiple choice, the exams can be very challenging so studying is a necessity. The four points of extra are a life saver, so make sure to do them.
Didnt go to the gym a couple of times and missed a Caffeine study and landed on a B in health. ugh

Takes the material way to seriously, thinks far too highly of herself, and exists solely to bore you for two hours every week. She is the worst of the health professors at Tech; avoid her lecture. If you have to take her section, do all the extra credit.

Health should not be this hard. Dr. Snow does not teach it; it is one of her assistants. The exams are tricky and full of nit-picky details. Doing well requires a ton of memorization. I finished with a B. The 5 points of extra credit on my final average saved me though from a C. Do not take this professor. Most of the other classes are much easier.

Not sure what so many are moaning about. Yes, it isn't the easiest A. What do you expect at GT? Shouldn't matter that it's "just" health class. There's a heavy amount of material to read though (textbook and slides) to prep for tests (multiple choice). But as long as you put that work in, you will get an A. She offers a lot of extra credit options.

Consider other profs first. Not a very interesting or engaging lecturer - I found it difficult to pay attention. Lectures sounded a bit patronizing, like she was lecturing at you, not to you. Tests usually included material from "out-of-the-blue" you wouldn't learn in class. Easy class made unnecessarily hard & aggravating.

Easy class. Just read the powerpoint slides and the textbook before the test and you will get As on tests. You can earn extra credit(at least 4% final grade) with the potential for more. If you pay attention, this class can help you become a more healthy person and boost your GPA.

The class is easy because she gives out so many extra credit, but the amount of work she gave out was completely unnecessary for a useless class like health. Students at tech have better things to do and harder classes like calc 2 to worry about, but instead i find myself wasting my valuable time studying for her tests that has the most random thin

most random test questions of all time. does not test knowledge, tests whether you know the random useless stuff she feeds you during her boring class. overweight, so believing anything she says is difficult. very disappointing semester...

Tests, group work, group projects, and labs...all for 2 credits? The class itself is not terrible, but Snow decided to remake the course. No other teacher does it like Snow. I wonder if she is aware that she's teaching a subject that no one at a engineering school cares about...?
The class itself is easy, the tests are really hard.

The class isn't hard, but it's not an easy A either. She is very specific with her test (the questions are sometimes based off random tidbits in your notes/textbook and she LOVES random statistics). Actually read the textbook, attend class, and study her lecture notes and you'll get an A or a B. She gives up to 4 points of extra credit.

Boring class, not the nicest teacher but not bad.  Nothing special, but just a warning:  Don't blow this class off, the tests are pretty tough if you don't pay attention in class or study for the tests.  But if you do one or the other (or both) then there's no problem.  There's some pretty specific/random stuff on the tests.

max 4 points extra credit. all 4 quizzes are online. boring lectures and barely any HW. lecture not mandantory. tests are very hard b/c they are very very specific. no final. each exam 30 percent and each quizz like 7 percent. when studying, just look for all the specific and useless info, and that will be the subjects on the exams
Class is a pain in the ass... sometimes test questions don't make much sense.  Lots of opportunities for extra credit.

Goes really fast through slides... asks really off random questions on tests about something random said in lecture... can be kind of mean... but all in all for what is left for health professors she's the best

EASY CLASS! I got 98/100 on the first exam with only a couple hours of studying. Numerous chances for extra credit. Moderately interesting lecture. You don't really need the book for this class...just study the powerpoint slides and take good notes.
This class is very easy. If you study the notes and read the assigned material you should get an easy A. Give many opportunities for extra credit also.
This isn't a very hard class. Everything being tested on is on the lecture slides. She is very nice and really interested in helping students become more aware of health issues.

nice person.  Takes the class seriously. Don't underestimate this class. It is certainly not the most challenging, but u won't get a decent grade without studying.  Read the chapters and try to listen in lecture.
She seems kind of tough in class, but is really a sweet lady.  As long as you are respectful and pay attention, you are good to go.  She's a great deal better than other health teachers i've had.
Insane amount of extra credit options.  Tests aren't too bad if you study a bit the night before.
Good teacher, but tests cover very obscure info
Easy class and nice professor.  Tests can be harder than expected.  Easy to get an A.
Tests were a little nit-picky for my tastes, but she didn't do a bad job teaching. She gave plenty of extra credit and was passionate about what she was teaching, which always helps.
No Comments

Theresa is a wonderful health-instructor. Of my freshman yr, I remember the energy with which she encouraged us to train both outside and in the olympic pool. Because of her, I have a much healthier life-style. Jogging helps me sleep like a baby for 5hrs.
No Comments

For special topics Public Health. Very particular when it comes to presenting and grading. He wants things his way. He is not the most compassionate or gentle person, but he does provide help when asked and is good at lecturing. Very interesting class!

Snell is awesome.  He really is very clear and doesn't tell you anything unimportant.  Nice guy, too.  READ THE BOOK.  His test averages were around 60-70 range because no one read.  Top 2.5% get an automatic 100, and he curves.  Take him if possible.
No Comments
Decent lecturer, just don't interrupt his class. Tests aren't bad if you pay close attention to text and online supplements (Lifewire).
Watch out for his test, he pulls them from the book and not the lecture

Great professor, wonderful and clear lectures. You really can't ask for anything more from a professor at tech. Her exams and quizzes were very fair, and not hard if you did and understood the homework.

Pros: Excellent lecturer, can be heard well across the entire hall. Answers questions during lecture and writes work out completely on the board. Really feeds off of class input, several surveys to make sure everything is going well. The final is pretty easy.  Cons: Understandably, is a stickler about electronics & talking in the lecture hall

Amazing teacher. She is very clear in her lectures and on what to expect for the class. Quizzes and tests look like the homework from MyMathLab, so do the homework. She cares about the students and will not hesitate to reexplain a concept.

WONDERFUL teacher! She made Linear Algebra quite fun and even reached out to me after class was over (ie, after I took my finals) to see how my summer was going! Easily the best math teacher I've ever had at Georgia Tech!
She really cares about the students and is a very fair grader. Do the homework and make sure that you understand it, because the test questions mirror those from the homework. Excellent professor!

This was my second time with her, and again, she's amazing. She encourages us to really understand the material, go to office hours, ask questions, etc. Tests were not difficult if you had practiced enough. She's going to teach MATH 3215, and even though I don't need this class for my major, I still signed up to take her for the third time.

Professor Subramanian was a great Calc 3 professor! There are definitely easier professors you can find, but I learned so much in her class, and she was always available to help out. If you work hard in that class, you'll learn a lot and should get a good grade. She's one of my favorite professors! Also, the recitation worksheets are super helpful!
I want to take 3215 from Sneha too. She is a great professor!!!!! Open more slots please.

She is extremely knowledgeable and very helpful.  Actually took mid-term CIOS complaints seriously and altered the class to meet student's needs.  Tests aren't easy, but she covers everything in lecture you need to know and the recitation worksheets are of similar difficulty as the tests.  Overall a very good professor.  Would definitely take again

I felt like her lecture had no vagueness. Material presented was extremely clear and lecture was so helpful. She always encouraged us to ask questions and really grasp the material. Linear algebra, conceptually, was difficult, but the tests were very very fair. With practice, there was no reason to fail. She was my favorite instructor all time!!!!

Recitation is more helpful than lecture, and recitation attendance is taken. Writes notes on the board as she goes, so it's very easy to keep up. Tests and quizzes are fair. Accent is a little thick, but still definitely understandable.

Cares about her students and wants them to learn the material and not just pass. Tests are fair except the true/false section can be hard. Quizzes are very straightforward most of the time. Lectures and long and boring but she writes everything on the board so its easy to keep along with. Skipping class can make it hard but attendance not taken.

Explains the material very clearly and genuinely cares about her students. Tests are straightforward and pretty easy, as long as you actually know the material. Gives very thorough help during office hours. Lectures are boring and kind of slow, but to be fair it's not easy to make math lectures entertaining and going slowly helps some students.

Prof Subramanian really cared about her students and the material. Lectures were clear, and her notes were easy to follow. She held office hours and could always answer questions clearly.  I always knew what was expected of me. To study, you should practice problems and read the book to get the depth of understanding needed for tests/quizzes.

4 homework 3 tests (cheat sheet for each) that are VERY similar to the practice exams. Put practice problems on cheat sheet and your basically guaranteed an 80 on the exam. Sonia is very nice and super knowledgeable and does her best to make lectures interesting. Homework is helpful and directly pertain to class content. Would definitely recommend,

This class was async for my semester, but i still really enjoyed it. Her lectures are really good - she makes sure to explain each concept thoroughly so it's easy to keep up. The projects require a decent understanding of concepts from lecture as well as python, but as long as you don't start the day of they're nothing crazy.

Good lectures. Very nice professor. Projects were most of the grade. They were usually pretty short and simple but sometimes didn't specify important information making them take extra time. The quizzes were the rest of the grade and needed to work pretty fast, but if you went to lecture it was fine. Easy to get a good grade
Excellent class. Highly recommend taking robotics with this professor.

Lectures are a bit heavy and fast. Feel like they would be super interesting if they didn't involve so much unnecessary math. She claims it's not a req, but she kinda expects you to know prob stat already, so take it before 3630. Projects are extremely easy but have vague instructions. Quizzes can be hard but are take-home, open note. Fine overall.
40% quizzes 60% projects, 2 quizzes dropped. Both components of the class were doable.
Great and caring professor! Most of the material covered on quizzes are accessible via the slides posted. Very helpful during office hours and on Piazza for code debugging.

Not exactly the best lecturer but is willing to help most of the time. Labs often had very little to do with what was taught in class and were very open-ended; most of the difficulty of the class came from the labs due to how finicky the robot we used was. Quizzes are very heavily based on lecture material that she posts slides on.
Good prof, explains well. Homeworks are interesting to do.

Professor made the class fully asynchronous and did not review important concepts for the exams. 
His lecture videos even were very short. When students are paying for this degree, I do not think the instruction that was provided warrants the cost.

He is very well spoken and went over the concepts well overall I will say

My first course in Georgia Tech's OMSA program was an excellent decision. Dr. Sokol's lectures are concise, informative, and often humorous. His teaching style made complex material approachable and enjoyable. Dr. Sokol has a gift for not wasting words — I learned more in a 5-minute video than I normally do watching other, longer videos from others

Dr. Sokol is a great teacher and very skilled at summarizing things into their core substance and imparting the knowledge. I did not realize how great Dr Sokol was until I took a few more professors to compare. He's really been the best.

The lectures and assignments are not suited for an exam-heavy class.  TAs are quite passionate about the topics and helpful.  Beware of spending too much time on homework when you should be investing that time on exam prep instead!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sokol is an amazing lecturer and person. I loved his class. He is engaging and clear. I would encourage you to go to Georgia Tech.
Dr. Joel Sokol is the best professor I have ever had the fortune to meet. He is very honest and fair with his students and he is  a very good and inspiring teacher.
An amazing professor, very knowledgeable and clearly interested in going beyond the taught material and engaging in debates with students. Strongly recommend if you ever get the chance!

Dr. Sokol is one of the best professors I've had. He has the knowledge and experience that you'd expect from a program director and can explain advanced concepts in a way that makes it easy to understand. I can also neither confirm nor deny that he has super powers - so, you should take his class and find out for yourself!

Some of the most Aha moments I have witnessed came from this course. Professor Sokol has the breadth and depth of knowledge that is unparalleled. You crave for more. You need to re watch all his videos. Almost every sentence has deep meaning. Have fun enhancing your knowledge with Professor Sokol's ISYE 6501 course.

Sokol is really nice and you can tell he genuinely wants his students to learn the material. Tests make up 75% of your grade and can be a bit tricky, though he does allow crib sheets. Lectures are solid, but you're expected to watch the video lectures beforehand which makes them redundant. Homework is graded by the TA, which leads to less feedback.

This class was 100% taught by TAs. The lecture videos were from the professor, but that was it. They are upfront they are teaching about machine learning techniques, but not how to code; however, then the homeworks are 100% about coding. i.e. you are expected to do homeworks on coding with no help or instruction whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Well structured class (one of my favorite ever), well taught. Joel is great.
Every small detail mentioned is useful for real world applications.

Hands down one of THE best professor I've ever had. She's more than a professor or a lecturer, she's actually passionate about what she's teaching and cares about every single one of the students. On the very first day she took the time to greet everyone of us and know us by name. She's more than awesome, you will NOT regret taking her courses.

This class WILL change your life. Dr. Alvarez is so kind and will probably be the best professor you meet, especially at Tech. She brings guest speakers and her class is participation heavy through discussion, so be ready to talk. She's very accommodating and respects everyone so well. She makes sure you always leave with something new!

Dr. AR is literally the BEST professor at GT. Her class changed my life, and she genuinely wants students to learn and succeed. She makes sure that every student feels loved and cared about. She even brings snacks and invites guest speakers to improve our knowledge. I learned so many life skills that I will forever take with me. Take this class!

Dr. Zhu is a great guy. He truly cares about his students and is an engaging lecturer. I enjoyed his class a lot since I'm interested in math. He strives to explain/prove the theorems we learn in detail. If you find yourself asking "why" before "how," then this class is for you. His slides are top quality. I give my strongest recommendation.

Prof. Zhu's lectures are much more difficult than the actual exams. In class, he tends to spend time on proving theorems and performing complex calculations (which makes sense for a math class), but this depth isn't tested. If you understand the lecture notes, then it's an easy A. He is also very smart and knowledgeable.

Genuine professor that actually is really smart, though I think that goes against the students sometimes since he does move very quickly. Most of the lecture were hard to follow, but if you do the homework & the practice, you'll probably do okay on the exams, though he is a ROUGH grader (avg 60-70 exam grades). No phones/laptops in lectures.

Songhao is very caring and intentional with his teaching. You do get the sense he is too smart to teach intro to prob stats tho, which makes his lectures hard to follow a lot of the time. Tests were very similar to homework and lecture example problems. Grading is fair. Still much much harder of a class than the ISYE version from what I've heard

I was unable to learn from this professor. I found his ability to explain concepts less than satisfactory, and in many cases I witnessed him being quite rude to other students. Furthermore, his exams are not representative of the homework or practice exams. Lastly, he did not provide enough learning material/resources for the course.

An average lecturer but a reakky nice person outside the classroom. I wouldn't necessarily recommend them as a professor, but definitely not the worst! Calculus I is generally a difficult class, so I recommend using all available resources early on and to attend Dr. Zhu's/TAs' office hours for more help.

Really caring and accessible outside of class, if you are proactive you can get a lot of great help. However, his class is significantly harder to get an A in for 2106 compared to the other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor that gives helpful lectures with detailed examples of concepts. Lectures were textbook based but he prepared slides and whiteboard notes. Super caring and open to feedback. Homework was a bit overwhelming for a few weeks but the rest was fine, and we get detailed feedback from the TA. Exams were fair. Overall highly recommend.

MATH 2106. DO NOT take Songhao for foundations of proof. First of all, he does not have lecture slides and just uses the textbook. When he teaches in class he often goes on long rants about topics and ways to solve proofs, then retracts and tell us to ignore everything he said because it was incorrect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Songhao was a nice guy, but not the best professor. I took AP Calc BC in high school, but he managed to make it way more confusing than it needed to be. His lectures were super focused on concepts with barely any time for practice, and the homework didn't really match what we did in class. Exams were nothing like the practice tests or homework.

He cares about students but hard. Writes questions that you will only get right if you really understand the material. Good lectures; his only shortcoming is that he often fails to get to the difficult problems in the notes and so you just get taught the basics, which sucks for someone who took calc in hs. A's are attainable with hard work though!

Professor Zhu was a kind person, but not the best professor. His lectures were concept heavy with minimal practice time; the homework was inconsistent to what we would see in class. The exams poorly reflect the practice exams and homework. I have taken Calc 1 in HS and passed the AP exam, however, this class was still my most difficult.

His lectures were great. He really made sure students understood concepts and definitions before moving onto anything complex. He always asked if students had any questions and would answer multiple before moving on. The exams mostly reflected the provided practice exams from previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu has had great lectures and always asks the class if anything is confusing. He is very accessible outside of the class and insists students come to OH or email him. He is very passionate about math and hopes to instill the same passion in his students. I highly recommend taking him for 1551!

Not a lot to say about Professor Zhu: his lectures are probably the best of the MATH 1551 teachers you can get, his explanations are easy to understand, and he's generally in a good mood inside and outside of class. Highly recommend!

Textbooks are not used/reference books are not useful. Study his in-class examples often. He responds to feedback from students well. Solid professor and the class is flipped, structured to make you learn an exceptional amount. No hard formulas, but master the conceptual info.

Has quizzes every class; only the top 50% are counted for grade. Three tests that you need to lock in for and do well on, it pays to study and make your formula sheet early and review ALL in-class problems. No extra credit and does not round. If you email him a question he'll respond within 1-2 days.

Flipped classroom style, which wasn't actually too bad, as he provides clean and annotated lecture slides. Quiz at the beginning of every class that is pretty easy. Exams were very manageable. Final was optional. Dr. Saha is a clear lecturer and answers questions well.

Dr. Saha is a good choice for ME 3210. The class is taught in a flipped classroom style. There was a quiz every class, but they were straightforward if you watched the video. There were three tests and a final, but they were all open note and straightforward. Homework was optional, but was good review. He also offers extra credit if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Love this man. He does a flipped classroom format so you have double the lectures to go through and there is a quiz at the beginning of every class. Despite this his exams and quizzes are pretty fair, and he gives a ton of study resources. Can honestly say he cares about his students - he's the best choice for this class.

He is a very knowledgable professor who cares about his students. His tests are very fair and test the understanding of the concepts, not the ability to plug in numbers to an equation. He teaches useful skills and topics that students will likely see post-graduation. He's very helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had him his first semester teaching in Fall 2019, and it started it out rough, but halfway through he had us fill out a survey and he changed a lot (more helpful in office hours, more reasonable exams, more partial credit for hw, etc.) based on that for the better, so he does care about his students' success. Overall, not a bad prof for 3210.
Lots of reading, but interesting work and research!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor with highly-relevant industry experience with Operating Systems and security. Attendance is mandatory due to pop-quizzes. Projects are difficult... but it's a difficult course in general. Lectures are helpful in theoretical understanding. Projects test applied understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Specter is a knowledgeable lecturer with seemingly genuine interest in the content. This semester's structure was basically the same as previous 3210 sections, except for addition of some attendance quizzes afaik. Labs are notoriously time consuming but do-able with TA help, reading, and effort. Exams are pretty difficult but curved when needed.

This guy is the least accessible professor I have ever taken a class from. It feels bizarre to be in a class of less than 20 people and still somehow never be able to get in to contact with the professor. If you ever attempt to approach him after class he will instruct you to just email him. If you ever attempt to email him he will not respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's obviously a genius. I think many here are rating his intellect, which is through the roof. But that's not the same as being a 5 star professor. His overly rapid speed, run-on sentences, vague references to "that" and "this" make it exceedingly difficult to follow him. You'll learn most of the content on your own. He's so sweet though.

Incredible professor, if you put the time and genuine effort in trying to understand content outside of lecture, you will learn so much. My favorite class and professor so far, but prepare for a lot of homework and studying. Professor really cares about you and the content, very willing to help outside of class, and it makes learning better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The hardest class I've ever taken, and easily the best professor. You will learn more than seems possible in a semester, at the cost of your free time. Befriend your classmates and you'll do okay. Dr. Speyer's lectures are fantastic, and he makes sure you really understand the content (plus he responds to emails super quickly). Amazing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unless thermo comes naturally to you, you have to do a lot for an A but I don't think it's that bad if you aim for a low B. Speyer is also actually one of the nicest and most understanding profs I've come across.

Exams are a time crunch, homework takes forever, but there is no class that will teach you so much in  such an effective way. The grading is fair, the material is interesting, and Dr. Speyer knows it all inside and out. He cares about his students, and it shows. Favorite professor at Tech so far. If you have the opportunity, take a class of his.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very classy. wears a suit & tie.

How wine, soap, air conditioning, flamethrowers and airplane engines work are just some of the mind-blowing things Dr. Speyer talks about in the class. Definitely the hardest and most fufilling class I've taken at Tech. Homeworks took us 15+ hours to do. You will learn thermo, become a MATLAB god, and strenghten friendships by working together.

Extremely hard professor.  You will hate him while you are taking him, but appreciate him afterwards.  Tests graded on curve, otherwise everyone would fail.  Tests are a time crush, write AFastAP until your hand cramps, more is better.  He also covers a TON of material, so only feasible was is to have a test every other week.

You will learn EVERYTHING in this class, absolutely EVERYTHING. From the stuff underneath the crust to how soap works. Go to lectures and watch him blows your mind. His teaching is great and he responds to your email within 10 minutes at most.
Matlab homeworks are great to apply the content, and the tests can be tough with the amount of memorization needed. Good news is that it's all curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is probably the most efficient packing of content in a course that can be done.

Dr Speyer might be my favorite lecturer in the MSE department. His lectures are really interesting and he knows a lot about what he is teaching. you will learn lots of information that you can use in real life, there are also lots of theory though. tough Hws and exams. Also if you get an A in his class you can get an internship in his company.
Such a great prof, best I've had. You will work for this class, but be oh so proud of yourself after. Hardest class yet, but at least he occasionally brings snacks and coffee/doughnuts for the final.

Allow me to quote one of my favorite Reddit comments of all time:  "His classes are not hard due to the complexity of solving problems. His classes are hard because it's like drinking from a fire hose and you have to hold all of that in long enough to regurgitate it on his lengthy exams while racing the clock."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: For this class, you'll have seven exams over the semester. Besides testing your knowledge of thermo, it will test your will to live.   Speyer's a good guy though. Always enthusiastic to answer questions/explain a topic again, and really intelligent.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Speyer is so smart. SO smart. I've never felt like I should be learning so much. He derives all these things and you write them down and try to memorize them for the test but what do they MEAN. You don't know.  No one knows. So lost. If you're taking this class it's because you have to. I'm sorry. But it brings us all closer together. Godspeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. I have never learned so much in a college class before. His handwriting is hard to read, but he gladly clarifies it. His tests require a lot of memorization but they are very fair. Very approachable for questions after class. Tests are curved.
Apart from being REALLY HOT, Dr. Speyer was very helpful and committed to his students.  I would recommend him without hesitation.
His tests and handwrighting are kind of rediculous but ive learned more in his classes than any others at tech.
Great guy, hard tests, but if you prepare and work at it, it's pretty easy to get a B.

Please someone get through to this guy, total control freak. Not in to teaching as much as making you memorize a lot of material and then respell every last thing on exams. Great practice for your memory, however what does this have to do with being in college? Nothing. Go back to the root definition of what it means to be a professor, im out.

Speyer is a really good professor, his tests are brutal, but almost always only on the material from since the previous test.  So if you start studying from the very first day of class on a new topic, and then ask him the questions you might have, he will really help you to understand it.  If you aren't doing well, you must be shy, or lazy.

Speyer was actually one of my favorite professors. His tests are really difficult, but he puts a lot of work into his classes and is very willing to help students learn the material.  Definately go to see him after class and ask questions.

Very chill professor. Slow grader but not harsh. There are 4 major assignments and weekly writing assignments that are basically completion grades. Other reviewers are just malding CS majors who can't write one paragraph about their thoughts on an article.

This class is annyoing in particular, but AVOID IF YOU CAN. He is one of the worst professors I've taken at GaTech. I found no value from this class nor his teachings. TONS AND TONS of pointless busywork that did not contribute to my education. ALSO he takes FOREVER to return grades. 

Easy class, but just very boring and painful. AVOID IF U CAN.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Echoing the previous poster's thoughts. This prof's class is just annoying. The assignments leave much to be desired and you're doing small writing tasks almost constantly. Don't expect to actually learn anything, this is basically just ENG 1102 again under another name. Do yourself a favor and take with another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've taken at Tech. This class couldn't be further from Tech Comms the way he teaches it. Busy work is endless, and most of the assignments are pointless. I'd recommend taking this class with another professor, where you might actually gain something. You'll end this class with an A, but it is truly painful to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
He's a nice professor. Easily accessible outside of class, gives good feedback. But a slow grader. Lenient grader though!

I think the negative reviews come from the fact that some CS majors have to take this class as a requirement, and there's a lot of writing involved because its a class about *technical communication* and they don't like that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Chalifour is a really nice guy and a caring professor, but is overly pedantic and assigns too much busy work. Each assignment will have 4+ parts to it leading to a lot due every week. However, each submission is quite easy and he grades very leniently. Overall not great but could be worse.
Do not take unless you want to do ambiguous assignments 5 times a week.

It was difficult to follow lectures because he would talk about things that were not relevant. The exams were very difficult for Psych 1101 because they were more conceptual and on small details. The grading was also usually wrong and I had to go in after exams to fix questions graded wrong.
He gives random pop quizzes, lectures are mostly rambling, class isn't hard as long as you take notes and do your homework on time

The professor gives you a topic list to study off for midterms and finals, but questions are very confusing for an intro class. Some questions are too specific and frq grading is pretty strict. No clear guidelines for the frq. Lectures had a lot of unnecessary information and the professor often rambled a lot which can be confusing. $100 textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Spieler is a kind person but psych1101 was very frustrating. Test formats were unclear, I did horrible on the first midterm because the FRQ was difficult to understand. Lectures were easy to understand but I ended up just learning everything outside of the class on my own. TAs did not know what was happening in the class and were unhelpful.

FIND A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR OR DONT TAKE THE CLASS. Seriously it's not worth it. Made psych way to diffuclt for what it is. I was so jealous of my friends who were telling me they had take home online tests while I was working my butt of for a literal 70 on the first midterm. This is an intro class, should not be that hard. Bro deserves more 1 stars

Fair and pretty good professor, but does have his shortcomings. Lectures are all over the place and he is a little unorganized. Attendance is decided by 8 random pop quizzes he'll give without warning, but 2 are dropped and are just completion. Incredibly fair grader, will give full points back if question not on provided study guide. W Teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: The lectures were hard to follow and the exams were difficult, but the class overall was manageable.

Terrible teacher, bogus tests, class average of a 65 or lower on some of the tests. Bro this is psych 1101 and he makes it an unbearable. Do NOT TAKE him. He's a mad yapper who doesn't know how to teach.

Lectures for the entire 1:15 twice a week and has occasional pop quizzes that aren't really that hard but still count towards grade. Hardest part of his class was his grading. If I studied hard I got good grades on the multiple choice, but his grading on short answer was pretty strict. Would recommend other professors, friends said they're better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some of the negative ratings on this website are so over-dramatic. He hands out detailed study guides that cover everything on tests. If something on the test is not on the study guide, he gives everyone points for it. No reason not to get an A in this class if you show up to the lectures and try. Going to lectures is very important!

There are weekly reading quizzes which are quite easy, but the exams are diabolical. Expect to stay up late studying and then regretting doing so, because whatever you studied is never on the actual exam. If you get stuck in this class, I will be praying for you and your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Required to purchase access to a $125 online textbook / learning platform. 10% of your grade is based on quizzes that require digital access from the publisher - no piracy. Attendance (in the form of random in-class quizzes) also counts for 10% of your grade. 4 participations in campus psych research is also required* (Coerced). I would say more.

He seems like a nice guy who's knowledgeable on psychology, but that doesn't translate to good professor. His tests were ridiculously hard for an introductory course being riddled with random facts and his lectures were hard to take much away from. His study guides are useful to a degree and he'll communicate what might be on FRQs but not great.

While a really nice guy who's clearly passionate about psychology, Dr. Spieler's class was extremely confusing. His lectures were really hard to follow, test questions were worded strangely with lots of typos, and the class was overall harder than it should've been. Don't take his class if you want PSYC to be easy, and expect to work if you take.

dont take him, hes so unorganized and someone told me he graded midterm 2 with the scantrons from midterm 1 because he lost the right ones. literally what?????? he should stick to research and stay away from teaching since he clearly doesn't know the first thing about educating people.

He has pretty good lectures and knows what he is talking about, however his tests are way to hard for both an intro class and  will often sneak random facts in the study guide that we never learned but turn up on the test. Additionally he has many quizzes that don't actually help with the topics that much on an online textbook website.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are good, but the tests are awful. The class averages were like 60 on an intro course and included topics never taught in class. He gives study guides and says thats all thats on the exam and then there is so much on the exam that was not on the study guide. Overall not a horrible lecturer but would avoid if you want a guarenteed A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are interesting, very nice and knowledgeable about topics. some reviews on him are a bit dramatic but i do agree he emphasizes that "if it's not on the study guide it won't be on the test" but then about 1/3 of the things on the test weren't on the study guide. otherwise, cares for his students and is very understanding if you talk to him.

honestly a terrible professor. his study guides aren't accurate as he includes more topics on the exam. also, the exam average was a fail, he said he would improve his style, and very much did not. he doesn't give practice problems beforehand because he “doesn't have time”. definitely do not recommend as he overcomplicated simply topics too.
Boring lecturer. Can see that he's passionate about the topics, but lectures very unengaging. Slides are hard to understand. Emphasizes study guide has everything on test, but includes other topics.

Spends a lot of time during lectures talking about things unrelated to midterms so it's really hard to know what to take notes of. Plus, there are questions on midterm that aren't directly written on slides, making it hard to review. Very boring lecturer.

Bruh, this guy doesn't know what he is talking about. The slides are so bad and he will yap whatever comes to his mind. I am so lost in the lectures and have to learn all the materials from textbook. The textbook are super long and complicated to read.
The lectures were interesting overall. He was great at keeping the class engaged with jokes. Exams were heavily lecture-based and he provided great study guides.

I never followed his lectures as it often seemed like an "info-dump," which made it interesting for some. However, I thought there was a lack of a real curriculum. Also, his organization/admin skills are AWFUL. I finished with an A, but because of his unclear grading system, I never knew where I stood in the class until the very end.
Interesting lectures that focus on studies and fun examples. Good course, tests align decently with lectures.

Would have given him a 5 if not for the $90 Macmillan textbook. 2 tests + final come straight from study guide (if you pay attention in class you don't even have to study). Quiz is online (the reason why we bought the book) so do your thing. Overall very fair and expect you to leave with intro knowledge in Psychology (PSYC1101).

Really interesting and cool guy. Very passionate about what he teaches and very knowledgable. Kind when answering questions and makes the class pretty interesting. His tests often focus on what he talks about in lecture which is not always 1-to-1 with the textbook so as long as you show up, the class isn't that bad.
Fast paced
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not the best at teaching but you can tell he is passionate about the subject. He released study guides before every exam and as long as you study those you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Still taking the class, but the two tests so far have been straight forward and very easy if you read the study guide. Class will be interesting if you choose to pay attention (barely any people do). He definitely knows what he is talking about and has a passion for it

On the first day of the semester, he showed us past feedback he received and then proceeded to say how he has not and will not improve/learn from the feedback. The semester showed how he doesn't care about being a good professor. Honestly, he just sucks. Try to avoid him.

This class was both an undergrad class and somehow a grad level course which didn't make sense from the beginning. There were assignments and lab assignments due on the same day every week. There's a final project and a final exam on top of it and not much help. The material is useful but the structure of the class sucks.

Dr. Spieler is a nice and caring person but is actually a terrible professor. He will go on tangents and unimportant details before actually explaining the basics of concepts students are unfamiliar with. Will never work through problems in class and only explain things high level; while all the homework / tests involve problem solving exclusively.

Terrible. During lectures he says a lot of words but not a lot of substance, so it's hard to know what's important. He says a lot of irrelevant things in class and is bad at explaining. Loves to screw us over with homework. Also, my class did good on the first exam, so he made the second exam harder because he wanted us to get B/Cs instead of As.

Spieler is so passionate & knowledgeable. His lectures were 70% engaging and funny and interesting, 30% boring enough to make me zone out. Overall a great prof. The grading is almost all tests which arent super hard but definitely require studying and are based on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Spieler was great! He always tried to be engaging and seemed to love what he was teaching. His tests were very lecture based so if you skipped class you won't get a good grade; however the questions were very easy so if you were there in class it will be very easy to do well on the tests. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Has no idea on how to teach. Just stands and blurts out words during the lecture. Test are nothing like the lecture. Definitely the worst professor I have had at Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is really passionate about the subject and his passion makes the class so good. 10% research parti. + 4% (extra credit): very easy 20% quizzes: very hard but this not the general view 70% exams: mediocre difficulty if you go study the guides. Study guides are really helpful but he made changes even on the last days of exams, which was stressful

I went to all the lectures; he was very fast, but he posts all the powerpoints online so you can look at them after class. There is a free online textbook for the class, but I never felt the need to use it. He provides study guides prior to the tests and if something isn't on them, it's not on the test. Overall pretty easy, just study before tests.

I didn't think I would enjoy a Psych class at all and only took it because it is a requirement for the intelligence CS thread, however Spieler made this class exceptional to me. He is an excellent speaker and although he may occasionally get slightly off track it's because he is so passionate about the content and makes it so enjoyable. Fun class.
Bad. Just awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't bother taking this class you wont learn anything. He's bad. I thought I wanted to major in psychology, not after this. He absolutely ruined my interest, I guess it only takes one bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He doesn't really do anything except for go through slides but he gives study guides for each topic before exams, making them much easier to study for. He also posts two essay questions a week ahead of time, one of which ends up on the exam. The tests aren't easy but he typically applies a slight curve to the class to make up for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible professor. Talks about complete nonsense instead of teaching the class. He is super verbose and uses jargon all the time without ever explaining what it means. Has no idea as to how to explain a concept. Half the class sleeps all the time. By far the worst professor at Georgia Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prioritizes memorization over learning. Doesn't explain concepts at all, I had to watch YouTube to get an idea what he was talking about, waste of my time and money. Don't go to his office hours, it's ever worse than class. I cannot stress enough he's just a horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes not a good teacher at all. Includes irrelevant information in lectures and says lots of words which have little to no content. Do everything to avoid taking him.

I didn't go to lecture because he would talk about nonsense instead of explaining anything. He gave 8 random quizzes. Lab was terrible, always took 3 hours. Homeworks were difficult, don't wait until last minute on those. I failed both exams, although we got 3 crib sheets for the exams. The grading was very harsh, but there is a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures contain some of the most interesting material I have ever learned. Tests are very easy if you come to class, take notes and read the book. Tests are MC and essay. Posts 2 possible essay prompts the week before the test and chooses one for the test. Also posts study guides detailing exactly what will be on the test. Fun and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests are very book-based (recommend getting the book -- it paid for itself after the first exam). Lectures were very enjoyable to attend. He was funny and he very clearly loves what he was teaching.  Gives very low-stakes pop quizzes to encourage attendance.

He is a nice guy, but, he is one of the worst professors I have had at Tech. He is not very good at explaining concepts, which is needed in a stats class. Tests are extremely difficult, so don't be surprised if you fail them. He does curve the class though to compensate (I got a B). Go to class...even if it feels pointless. Good luck...trust me!
No Comments

Pretty interesting guy but lectures were still kinda boring (not mandatory). gives study guides for test 1 week before. gives 3 essay questions before and one of them will be on the test. essay is 1/3 grade and multiple choice is 2/3. 2 exams and 1 final.  each exam is 25 percent of grade. i recommend trying to get easier psych 1101 prof if you can
He's a very eccentric prof, I could tell he really enjoyed Psych and that made the lectures more interesting. Tests are pretty hard b/c it's mainly memorization

He's a great lecturer, always tries his best to explain new concepts. You can really see his passion for physics and biology when he brings up his insect research related to the concept. Livestreams his lectures and uploads his notes. PHYS 2211 is hard, but the course has so many resources for students, take advantage of that.
Pretty good professor. Not the easiest class ever, but her seems to do his best to make it better.
Dr. Sponberg is a good lecturer and is very passionate about physics. PHYS 2211 is a hard class in general but Dr. Sponberg equips with you with the tools to do well in the class
He delivered clear lectures that mainly consisted of working through example problems. He was very helpful in office hours and worked with students to help them succeed.

Dr. Sponberg was a fantastic professor! His lectures were very clear and helpful, and he incorporates a lot of examples from his bio-mechanics research which makes it more interesting. He is also very energetic and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Sponberg is really passionate and always makes lectures interesting. To be completely honest, the material is too dense to be covered completely in lecture so you'll have to do some reading on your own. Tests are pretty tough but it's the same regardless of the professor. Do. The. Practice. Exams.

Simon is a quirky and intelligent dude who is obviously passionate about physics! Although I never learned much in lecture, he does a fair job of explaining the concepts. Class participation/attendance is very important because of clicker questions. Tests are hard but there is a huge curve with the weighting. Definitely the best classical professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sponberg is passionate about Physics and provides plenty of real-world applications in lectures. Compared to the other 2 instructors this semester, he is the best. I find physics challenging so spent time on WebAssign hw, did old practice tests, + went to PLUS. Classical labs, recitations, and bucket points are easy As so don't neglect those!

Professor Sponberg is a very clear, very energetic teacher that clearly enjoys teaching. Although he can get a bit ahead of himself and makes a few occasional mistakes, he is quick to correct himself, clear, and will reach out after class if he feels  something needs more explanation. An all around great guy.
I really enjoyed his class. His lectures used demonstrations to get theories to stick. Fantastic professor who knew his stuff well.

Great professor, it was very easy to talk to her and ask her questions throughout the semester. The weekly homework assignments can be a little difficult, but taking your time to complete them will really help you learn the material. As long as you go to class and pay attention you will be able to understand all of the content.

Great professor, she helped out wherever you needed and provided tons of extra credit. Lectures are printed so you don't need to worry about that, and Excel is used for some lectures. 2 Exams but only the highest is counted, and weekly homework on Excel. Really cool person and super nice, definitely take her.

2 tests were open note. you can drop one. hw wasn't easy but you can drop 2 and it's worth a lot of grade. Really easy quizzes on Thursday. You get credit for attending (even if you go to another section). really chill teacher, and gives a boatload of extra credit.
Class material is difficult to understand, but professor makes up for it with extra credit opportunities and lenient grading. I agree with the other recent ratings.

She is very caring, however her weekly homework is pretty difficult and tedious. She also avoids answering fully when you ask her questions, both in person and through email, which is extremely frustrating. I will say since everyone failed the first exam so bad the second one was very easy which made up for the first one (went from a 45 to a 90).

Prof is extremely sweet and easy to approach. She clearly knows her material, works to integrate current events well, and is willing to allow herself to be openly challenged in class in an effort to give a more holistic learning environment. Grading is not hard, notes are given, and you are only counted for the highest of your two tests. 10/10 time

Overall, the class itself wasn't bad. There were times where students had to correct her work because she didn't do it right. She is passionate about the material and correct most of the time. If you pay attention, and do the homework, you'll be fine. There were 2 exams (highest exam counts), and a group project (no final) which wasn't bad either.

she's a great lecturer and good educator, but the material + tests CAN be difficult. class average for test 1 was a 69. she only counts 1 of 2 exam grades though + final is a video project + there's extra credit so it's manageable if you stay on track w studying. she's v accessible outside of class and answers emails super fast.

first time ever teaching shes absolutely amazing. course content already isnt that hard and she makes it so easy. hws let you work in groups, same for quizzes. exams are somewhat difficult but she prepares you for them very well. awesome person as well would 100% take anything she teaches
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely pretty old school, but he for sure cares. Show up to class and show up on time. If you put in the work, you can do well. Study for the exams, they're tough.

•exams are worth 25/25/40. Didn't curve (1st exam avg was a 50)
•homework doesn't count for grades
•shames students for showing up late, then is angry when students don't come?
•lecture videos are nice. Use them
•if you try to reach him on teams, he sends a vague passive aggressive message in the general channel to respond. Inaccessible after class

Showing up to class does not impact your grade, however, it will help you to round your grade when needed. He will ask you to answer questions in class and if you do not have the correct answer he will make you seem like a fool for not knowing a subject that he has been teaching for years. Overall a very bitter man who picks on his students.

The class was a lot of work, and there were times where the workload and expectations of prior knowledge were a bit unreasonable. All the assignments still felt pretty useful and I learned a lot. He was an interesting professor who cared about us learning.  Lectures were engaging, tests were difficult, project was a lot of work.

Dr. G's class is one that is a no-brainer to take if you are passionate about heat transfer/thermodynamics, but hard to recommend if you aren't. The class is extremely engaging and interesting, but it is a lot of work. Dr. G is a great professor though, and there are only a few professors like him who actually treats students like people.

My least favorite professor in at tech. First of all, he refused to explain examples in class, even after he asked for feedback on his teaching style and multiple students complained. Second, he is incredibly paternalistic bordering on creepy towards female students. He would pat/rub women's (never men's) backs when they answered class questions.

He will try to scare you the first day. Don't come to class if you're late. Letter grade cutoffs are made up at the end of the class. Participation is everything! Go to class and answer questions. He learns almost everyone's names and wants to see students succeed. A very interesting guy for sure, but one of the best professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class might be the hardest I've taken here, but I definitely learned the most. The tests are very hard, but the lectures are great and he cares about people getting the concepts. He keeps class interesting, but just make sure to show up even if attendance isn't required.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesnt require attendance but berates those who miss class. Aggressive and a bit full of himself. Grades based off of difficult exams and 2 projects. Covers material very quickly
He is a good professor that cares about his students. His tests are hard, his projects are pretty easy, his lectures are interesting.

People misunderstand Garimella's methods often, but he genuinely is one of the best profs at tech. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed, and isn't like profs with research programs that don't take undergrad classes seriously. Be prepared to put in the work and deal with some sarcasm, but you'll be a better engineer because of him.

a LOT of homework. tests and grading is mostly fair. he likes to call on people at random and opening criticize wrong answers during lectures. if you don't show up for class he's likely to call you out.
Excellent Professor, he really cares about his students.

If you decide to do the 3-person group projects alone, make sure you're ready to write a lotta C++! Prof discussed fun algorithms that made their way into my dreams. Tests were a challenge, reminiscent of a proof-based algorithms class like 3510. Kind prof who will work with you around unexpected circumstances if needed.

Very difficult class with challenging midterms and programming assignments. However, there is a heafty curve at the end, but expect to learn a decent amount and spend a great deal of thinking in this class. Lectures are a bit hit or miss.

This is an algorithms class. Prof. Aluru is the best lecturer I have had at Tech so far in that his line of thinking is crystal clear. Unlike other many other CS classes, the tests are not straight from the homework, so you'll need to learn the material really well if you want to do well in the class. Hard, but fair class. I learned a lot.
Horrible lecture and the mathematical proof is very imprecise. Lectures have nothing to do with the exam.

READ BELOW. This is a difficult class, so re-consider if you only care about good grades. Besides that, the challenge is worth compared with the knowledge and skills you will acquire in the class. Prof. Aluru is knowledgeable, approachable, and very understanding. YOU WILL NEED TO PUT REAL EFFORT INTO THIS CLASS, but you will have amazing rewards.

Has over 20+ years of teaching HPC and it shows. There's little info on distributed algorithms online so there are only slides to rely on. Rest assured, the slides are very clear. 

HWs and exams are uncomfortably difficult. MPI assignments felt doable (get a good team).
 
Overall, I got a learning experience that is difficult to get elsewhere.

Dr. Srinivasarao appears to be a grouchy professor, but that is only the public appearance from what I experienced. When you talk to him in private, he is very helpful. Justifiably he expects a certain level of background from students, but that level of expectation is legitimate, not unfair or too high.

Dr. Srinivasarao had a pretty .. "confrontational" teaching style the first half of the semester, but had a change of heart and became more mellow. This made class MUCH easier to sit through. Lectures are not organized very well, and topics tend to be covered over and over throughout the semester giving some redundancy.

He really does care for his students and is very kind if you talk to him one-on-one. Sometimes the material is a little difficult/very fast moving for an intro level MSE class, though. I think he would be excellent teaching an upper level MSE course. Definitely use past exams to study for tests because he reuses a lot of the questions.

Nice guy, although he can be very rude and sassy over email. Interesting class- seemed to be based entirely on his interests and not so much the MSE 2001 curriculum. Tests are about 20 pages of short answer questions but not too bad if you pay decent attention in lecture.

He is a great professor! I took MSE 2001 at GTL, and it was very doable. There's extra credit and a wide range of things that got graded, so it wasn't too exam-heavy. Exams themselves are long, but aren't too bad since a decent amount of questions are from the homework and straight out of lecture. He's very kind and wants the best for his students

Lectures are useless from how Dr. Srinivasarao jumps around from topic to topic with no explanation on how they connect; no big picture info is ever discussed and instead specifics are jumped straight into with no background.

Exams do not effectively test course content and have weird questions about niche topics which are pulled out of nowhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly knows too much to be teaching an intro class, expects 3- or 4000 level MSE/chemistry prerequisites and work to succeed, which often leaves him frustrated with students' lack of understanding. Lectures are impossible to follow in class, much less with just the PowerPoint (don't skip). READ TB! DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS! (& avoid him if you can)
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You have to go to class or watch recordings because his slides do not give the needed information. I wrote down everything he said because he wants every single detail on tests. He never gave us our final test grades back so I don't know if he curves. His final was 22 pages and took me 10 hours. I didn't ride the struggle bus; i got hit by the bus
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mohan is a great guy and I love the way he teaches! He encourages you to think about "why" instead of just going through the motions to get a grade. Really appreciate his class and how it changed the way I think about science.

Took this over the summer at GTL. Heard this would be an easy class, but I assume only with other profs. Jumped right in without a lot of bg knowledge given. Never know exactly what's going to be on the test (but for the love of G look at the practice tests he gives). He's definitely smart, but this class was unnecessarily harder than it has to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class already sucks, don't take it with him. He's not difficult (I took it over the summer at GTL), but he's just not at all pleasant to be around.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: here's the thing. mohan srinivasarao is definitely smart. very much so. but he hides it under a layer of inane nonsense and tops that off with a petulant attitude about everything. he won't hesitate to stop class and storm out if he is frustrated that students don't get a concept.  unfortunately, you probably can't avoid taking him. but be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The textbook is all you really need for this class. It'll prepare you for anything he throws at you on tests. His lectures can be off topic and he'll talk a lot about what he researches, but I found this cool more than distracting. The class itself isn't very difficult anyway.

Its hard to know what is on the tests and what isn't, and for a class with loads of information this is a big problem. He overreacts to phone usage yes, but I  liked him as a person and he curves your final grade. He's not that bad

He will get very upset if you use your cell phone.  He can be kind of cranky but he does teach.  I had trouble reading him as in what he will test on and what he will not.  There are things he talks about that are never tested on and things he doesn't talk about that are tested on so be on your toes.  It can be a bit frustrating.

He is a boring lecturer and uses a textbook 20 years old, along with test questions 20 years old. Everything he uses is recycled from when he first made it ages ago, and therefore is rather dull and boring. If he catches you looking at your phone, he will fume like a child and storm out of the class, or simply stand there in silence for two minutes

Super nice lady, teaches almost exclusively by example. This class is probably going to be a challenge if you're new to calculus, but that's true of any calc class. Classroom participation is encouraged and helps you learn. Tests and quizzes are fair, and the recovery policy is generous. Genuinely seems to care for her students as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think she was a good teacher, but the material was difficult which made me struggle a bit in this class. There are in-class polls that are used for participation. She taught a lot through examples which is something I personally appreciated and helped me learn. She wants students to succeed, and she is very helpful in her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She uses a lot of examples in class. This class is hard, but is a lot better if you read ahead. Without reading ahead I was lost in lecture, especially because she basically only uses examples to teach. She really cares about her students and wants them to do well, but her lectures don't help without reading beforehand.

Shes hard to understand. Goes too fast on examples. I learned most of the material in recetation and on my own. Also I thought I had a C in the class when I actually had a D. She posted grades on canvas and Ive been using canvas since 8th grade so I assumed my grade there was my actual grade but it wasnt. Make sure u calculate your grade urself
She's caring and easy to approach.

I learned only from recitation TAs in her class. She has a pretty heavy accent, so it is hard to understand what she says at times. Her lectures are also not well timed, and she ends up rushing to finish the lecture after the "whistle" has rung. Would not recommend for those who never had linear algebra before.

She is extremely caring. I never went to her office hours, but she always encourages students to come and ask questions. She teaches very quickly and is a little bit difficult to follow (read the textbook). Tests were difficult, but fair. She is a very nice lady, but not the best teacher.

She is a nice person, but lectures confuse you and she does not do a good job at working examples. Try avoiding her if possible. Class is really conceptual and for many coming out from calculus (or AP calc), it came across rather hard (for me at least). TA's were really helpful and kind of got me through the class.

Overall, I think that Srinivasan is an extremely caring and passionate professor. She seems to want the class to do well, and she really cares about your success. However, lectures can be difficult to follow if you aren't prepared by reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible. Lectures are very confusing and she tries to focus on conceptual things and ends up never actually working through any problems, which makes things very hard. Her tests/quizzes are generally harder than any other professors and very unclear. She's very nice but she just doesn't seem to understand the level the students are at.

Try to avoid if at all possible. She is a very nice and caring person, but lectures confuse you and she does not do a good job when working examples. She skips steps and insist we do them on our own. I know people who stopped going to lecture completely because it did not help them. Many people end up teaching themselves from the textbook.
Teaches using an overhead projector. Cares about her students, but her accent can make sitting in the back impossible.

I had her for first class @ Tech, so she probably will be better in later classes, but overall she wasn't a terrible teacher. She had clear expectations and would always be available to provide support. You will need to read the book though since her lectures always left me slightly confused, and I highly suggest printing out the notes she provides
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Going to lecture will make you more confused. The only way to learn anything is by reading the textbook or recitation. The homework and quizzes are easy but do not correspond to the tests at all. She dropped the lowest three quizzes and curved the overall grade but did not make it clear what your standing was in the class for the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I taught myself more from the textbook than listening to her. She was a poor choice, but then again, this was her first semester teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: solid prof, made the class engaging and easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made a really hard topic very digestible to someone who has never seen any of the class material before. Tests were just as difficult if not easier than the homework problems, which made the class much less stressful. Would definitely take one of his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was very kind to students, lectures are well organized and very clear. He uses great examples and lectures are very interactive. HW are not very hard and they help you undertsnad the topcis better,

Took during F25. Exams were open note/laptop, and were generally alright. He didn't post practice exams but going over the homework and recitation questions helped before the exams. Lectures leaned theory heavy but still manageable.

He's *fine.* Thermo is hard, his homework are good to practice, most of what he says in lectures is irrelevant. You need to learn a number of formulas and how to apply them. Seems like he leveled the Fall 25 grade distribution to be a bit lower by making the final rly challenging, but if you learn the homework and concepts exams are relatively fair
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is nice and always there to help, the course wasn't that difficult, of course you have to study and work on a final project, he is very fair at grading.

Professor Sun is very knowledgeable on thermo- and fluid dynamics. His lectures tend towards the abstract, spending most of the time deriving equations rather than working through examples.
Homework was graded very late. Very little time was given to look over corrections before the final.
Exams...were lenient. Ample resources provided.

I'll write what people really care about. The class is hard, but he allows the use of laptops for access to lectures and tables during exams, yes most of the students around me had their own notes/formulas included. All of that together with just paying attention to his lectures (actually attend them) and it's a really easy class. All formula based

Probably an easier thermo section compared to the others but hes incredibly unhelpful duirng office hours and is often just rude for no reason. His lectures go through little to no practice problems and only does derivations. Posts 0 practice exams. All exams open note&textbook, but he grades harshly. I have a personal vendetta against this man.

From my experience, Dr. Sun's Thermo and Fluids class was relatively easy compared to my peer's. The tests are very closely related to the homework. The recitation attached with this class was very helpful for my learning and a great study tool that summarizes the course content well. I recommend taking this course with Him.

Very nice and class was generally not too hard. He doesn't post notes tho so you have to get the content from lecture or from someone who went to lecture. Homework wasn't too hard and exams were pretty similar to the homework. Also didn't really grade the hw harshly at all.

A lot of the lectures were based on how to solve problems, rather than gaining a solid conceptual understanding
Didn't do a good job explaining the conceptual part of fluids like Mach wave vs Shock wave, shock waves in tubes, PTs, stagnation props.
Lectures were a bit disorganized. Tests and HW were fair.
Not a good or bad prof.

Professor Sun is definitely one of the better thermo professors, his exams are easy, and homework is mostly understandable. His lectures, however, are rather disorganized. While he is easier than other professors, he is not a great lecturer. Had to learn everything from the textbook or recitation.
Great professor who knows his stuff. Exam questions were based on homework problem sets (and were honestly easier). Class felt very fair, would highly recommend if you're taking thermo.

he's an good professor and answers questions very well but the class content is very difficult and lecture heavy. only had 2 midterms, homework, and the final. recommend paying attention and always going to him bc he was always willing to help. the content was difficult for me bc its a theory heavy course but he was always willing to re-explain
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Sun understands the balance between teaching teaching a class to achieve grades and teaching a class to learn the content well. He is personable and while he is sometimes difficult to communicate with online, he is fantastic at answering questions before/during/after class. You can tell he cares about teaching the content and tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy
