reviews.comment: Class is curved by 5% (A is 85%) and there is extra credit. HARD class, but not the worst. Lectures and homework is harder than tests (tests are heavily weighted). It's not an easy class but the professor is understanding, gives HW extensions, answers questions, explains concepts patiently. It's a tough class, take it with Dr. Wenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are the single most important thing in this class. Do not miss them. Prof Sun is a solid teacher and will do his best to help you understand the concepts if you have questions. Work hard on the homework; it's harder than the tests, and if you understand the homework, you'll be ok on the tests.

Dr. Sun is a great person and an even better lecturer. AE 2010 is a hard class, so you will struggle quite a bit to get all the material down. But Dr. Sun is really good about breaking down complex concepts and moving through a lot of material really efficiently. Besides class, he is a cool person, and has a pretty rare but genuine sense of humor.

Professor Thomas was awesome. She had pretty engaging lectures for the most part and took the time to work with students and make sure they understand. The grading scheme, is very test-heavy but grade replacement by the final is allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 90% of your grade is tests, but the tests themselves are very fair despite having limited practice test questions. Best way to study is to revisit old homework and to be able to explain the concepts presented. Dr. Thomas really wants you to succeed and presents all the material clearly and effectively. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Tests are 90% of grade. She's a good professor however she provides no practice exams and barely tells you what will be on exams. Exams have had very niche topics that were barely gone over in class (10-20% of exam grade).

Dr. Thomas was genuinely one of the best prof's I've had at Tech. Lectures are very helpful including review lectures before exams. Class was 90% exams but that is standard and wasn't an issue as I always felt prepared for the exams! Final was optional. Lectures were recorded and offered online as well as in person. She cares a lot about students!
She was an awesome teacher. Probably my favorite professor at tech. She is clear and knows the subject. Expect HW every week. 3 midterms and a final.

Thomas was really good. I liked her class a lot. She has a lot of energy, and makes deformable bodies as fun a class as possible. I definitely want to take her again for something else, but she doesn't seem to teach anything but def bods.

She tries to make it fun, not to good at it. Several times, it seemed as if she didnt really know what she was talking about. The homework solutions are online. Try not to just copy down, study and do it at least to some extent and a b should be easy enough. Try to review hw for tests.
Not a very good teacher. She would miss class and have some substitute come in that had no idea what he was supposed to be teaching! Caused a real inconsistency in the material!
Be very wary. This prof is quite unclear in her lectures and it is generally necessary to learn most of the topics discussed from the textbook. As mentioned, gives almost no partial credit.
She isn't very clear.  Tests are graded very strictly, not much partial credit.  Proofs deemed very important (25% of tests).

She is not a good professor. The only reason that she does not get a rating of 1 is that she grades the marketing project very easily and that is worth a great deal of your grade. She is passive aggressive and if the material taught in this class was halfway difficult, she would be one of the worst professors I've had. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She really is not as bad as people say, they expect it to be an easy a but its not. You def have to work for it but she is not a horrible person, just meet with her outside of class and she is understanding one on one.

Hated this class, professor lacks any empathy, and lectures are useless since most of the material on quizzes comes from the textbook. This is an intro marketing class, but it felt like an upper-level course with the amount of studying and depth of material. Avoid at any cost.

Was cold called on during drop/add week for zoning out from the boring lecture. She is the most passive aggressive professor I have ever had. Also, you have 3 "quizzes" that are 30 questions long, and each count for 13% of your grade. Attendance is 20% of your grade, and you are only allowed 3 absences, even if you have a medical excuse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor I have ever had. She is very hard to ask for help regarding exams and projects. She lacks empathy. I had to undergo a medical procedure and she wouldn't accept my doctors note and counted it as one of the 3 "unexcused" absences you're allowed to have. Completely a joke of a professor.
would not recommend

Don't recommend taking her for marketing. She is very passive-aggressive towards students. You also have to read the textbook entirely is what it felt like, the lectures almost don't even matter. There is a semester-long group project that is an easy A, but there is nearly 0 direction or instruction towards completing it. Good luck if you have her.

It's just way too overdone for a marketing class. Tests are hard given the level of nuance she feels the need to go into (many 'bright ideas' and concepts are just differences in phrasing that play no role in real life, yet cost test points). Her project is poorly guided and does nothing to reflect what is actually taught in class. meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exam were based on textbook and were very detailed so if you don't read it, you're cooked. Pray that your groupmates are good for semester long project and actually show up to the meetings. She is rather arbitrary when grading the project and is nitpicky. I don't think she is bad as some of the other people say but take another prof if possible.

Do NOT take her. She is extremely passive aggressive and really rude to her students. She tries to honor code and send everyone to OSI for no reason at all. She made interesting content extremely boring and her exams are only based on textbook material. She is very nitpicky with project materials as well.Take any other professor for marketing!!

There were a few tests, but they aligned with the lectures and textbook material. There was a semester-long group project, but she did not grade these very hard Attendance was not required for a grade, but she does keep track. I did not like how she was rude to students and not afraid to call them out or embarrass them in front of their classmates.
Coming to you as a woman, do NOT take this class with her. It will be agonizing.

DON'T take this class! I feel like I'm in preK with the way she treats her students. She just be making up her grades and is so harsh on grading. She treats this class as a big deal but it is BORING. She is so pessimistic and cried on the first day, it was so uncomfortable. She just wants to honor code everyone for no reason, strange vibes for sure

I'm currently taking her class right now, DO NOT LISTEN to the good reviews, she's super picky about everything and is very passive aggressive. The first day of class she posted testimonials of her students painting her as a great professor (first red flag) she will find any reason to refer you to OSI, very nitpicky about everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The concepts were basic marketing principles so nothing too tough. The group simulation is not hard if you read through the materials provided. It seemed as though students who don't believe in or seek to understand marketing are the ones who do poorly.

Very nice professor who really cares about her students. She tells us exactly what to expect on the exams and the averages were usually in the high 80's. I'll admit, her rubrics are not the best for the group projects but she will always be available to answer any questions you have. It is not an easy class, but work hard and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know if these other people are in the same class but I did not have the same experience they had. The prof has grading rubrics that detail exactly how things will be graded. She is tough but also fair. She gave a curve when the class bombed assignments. You need to be in attendance at every class, though, so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I think this is her first semester and it shows. The powerpoints show Halloran as the original author and based on how she doesn't elaborate on slides I'm assuming they are not her material. She changes the syllabus at the last minute (even after group projects are scheduled).

After four years of college, this is the worst professor I have ever had. She has awol grading criteria that she pulls out of her head. She treats her students like 5 year olds: giving candy and assigning seats. She has an extremely negative attitude and is extremely unprofessional. I don't even know how she got this job. She hates students. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had at Tech. Attendance is complicated and even if you're in class online you have to do a short assignment after, which she grades harshly (you could get a 0 for attendance even if you're there and participate). Lots of group projects that she doesn't explain well and grades harshly. Lectures are boring- book is better.

His lectures were very difficult to get through. He sorta mumbles, and he expected everyone to know a lot more than we did, and he's just not great at explaining things. I learned pretty much everything from the textbook and lecture notes. Exam questions are very similar to in class examples and practice questions, not really any curveballs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken at Tech. The four homeworks had 30+ (long!) proof problems, and even with a sacrifice of a week in advance, I could still barely turn them in. The two midterms were rough, but then the final exam kicked in and was absolutely nothing like the rest of his graded assignments (brutal!). Not sure if he's always like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are the same as the textbook. Exams are similar to old exams from old Tech professors. Hw is actually interesting if you take the time to care. He allows a crib sheet and lowers the boundary for an A to be 85, so its not difficult to be successful, just VERY boring. He is honestly really nice though, and I came to appreciate the monotony.

He lectures straight from the textbook and the textbook is just not great. Really dry and mostly unmotivated lectures about the material. No point in going to class. Look at other probability textbooks like harvard stat 110. He already shifts the grading curve where an 85 is an A 70 is a B which is nice. Exams usually have one curveball question.
Least engaging lecturer ever had at Tech. Don't take his section you are not already interested in the material because he will only make it more boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Swiech is a misunderstood math professor. It is true that his classes are hard, however the exams are not unfair, he provides practice problems, and is very accessible outside of class. I strongly encourage attending all lectures. You will probably struggle sometimes, but you will learn a great deal more than with other professors.

Challenging class, but I'm not a math major. The lectures were super theoretical and sometimes above my head. Tests were usually more applications of the theory, so they weren't bad. No proofs on tests. There is only 1 homework assignment that's basically a take-home test. Other than that, your grade is just tests/final. Lectures were ok not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind professor.

Very serious, lectures are dry directly off the textbook, no real need to attend lecture but he sometimes goes through examples and adds some context. He clearly knows a lot. Exams are hard, but the practice ones he gives out are good indicators. The final was quite hard too. He ended up curving pretty heavily.

Lectures were hard to follow, and homeworks and practice tests do not help at all for the actual exams. In hindsight, if I had read the textbook directly and done other professors' practice tests, then it would have been an easy class.

Solid choice. I spent most of my time skipping lecture and reading the textbook instead as he teaches directly from it and felt somewhat prepared for the exams. The final was definitely a 180 in terms of difficulty, so prepare for that. Homeworks were straight forward, but do not help at all for the exams.

A very solid choice - well-tenured and respected. He's kind but serious, and has a very dry sense of humor, which I loved. Lecture style is easy to follow, although it tends to be a bit dry. There were no surprises on the tests. Not a perfect professor, but I would definitely recommend taking a class with him, and I would again too.
No proper partial credits in this class, you either get the points or you don't. There's no similarity between the hws, what the prof teaches, and the exams. It's like learning three different things
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: lectures never made sense to me. they were heavy in theory and light in application
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He rolls from one topic to another with no break for questions and goes from one idea to the next as if the students already know the concepts. He definitely has a great understanding of multivariable calculus but, he cant impart that effectively. Take a different professor and your lecture hours will be much more productive and you won't be lost.

Did a great job teaching a very unintuitive class. He was organized, knowledgeable, and a very fair grader. Although he doesn't seem very approachable at first, he's always willing to help in office hours and wants the class to do well. The tests were straightforward if you do practice problems from the book, but the final was quite tough.
He does a decent job teaching a really difficult subject. However, sometimes he can get too into the theory instead of doing practice problems in lecture. Make sure you make a thorough crib sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Does a good job teaching a very difficult subject. He rarely tests proofs and cares much more that you can solve problems and conceptually understand theory. Does a really good job teaching problem solving mechanics, but has difficulty communicating the basis of the theory. If you are an undergrad, you'll be competing with Ph.D. students for the A.

His first test was easy. Said the class average was too high and the second test would be higher. Class average for second test was about a 35%. He also had a strong accent and talked to the board, so it was impossible to hear.

He is extremely attentive, and very helpful as long as you put forth effort into your work. He is by FAR the best math professor I have ever had at GaTech, and a really cool man if you actually take the time to get to know him.

Did not teach the material well.  Hardly ever did relative examples in class.  TA's did most of the teaching.  Tests had an avg grade of 55%.  All of the tests were too long and very hard.  Prepare to study your brains out.  Only 1 group passed the group project which were selected from the books projects.

Good teacher. He had Polish accent when I took the course, but I got the hang of it in a week. He was very organized in teaching and when using the whiteboard. Writes down definitions, theorems and proofs very clearly. Didn't really stick to the textbook. Tests were a bit easier than expected.
His English is very hard to understand. The content of his lectures is very unstructured and diverges from the book a lot.  It is hard to get a hook into the class.

i'm pretty ambivalent on him... not exactly a ray of sunshine, but a nice guy if you take the time to know him. almost verbatim out of the book, but he does explain nontrivial material with sufficient clarity, and contingent on your willingness to work hard, an easy B.
Not the most personable but very fair. Easy 'B' if you put forth the effort.

He isn't a very good teacher and his accent makes him pretty hard to understand. He likes to go over the same thing over and over which gets repetitive. We did too well on one test so he told us the next oune would "fix the gpa". I dont think an

A great professor that knows how to connect with students and keep them tuned in. The material he teaches is very applicable and valuable for future managers. His final project and the exam are challenging, but he gives a fantastic curve. The only thing I did not like where I would be critical of him is that the final exam is too confusing.
Really enjoyable Professor. He is knowledgeable, funny, and very clear about what it takes to succeed.

He was a really touch teacher, but he keeps the students to engage in the class. However, he doesn't really give bonus credits. His tests are really tricky. His words are super confusing at the same time. He is really a nice teacher though. But the class itself, is pretty hard.

I was having a really rough semester and his class kept me motivated.  I wished every professor enjoyed teaching as much as he did, I learned so much! You could tell he was REALLY into the subject matter and cared about his students.  It also didn't hurt that he was "easy on the eyes" - I would give him an 11 out 10 in looks and intellect.
Great prof!
Professor Swami is very inspirational. He teaches a very hard class, but is a great professor and truly cares about his students. 10/10!

His lectures can be tough to keep up with, the tests are challenging, but if you keep up with the homework and simulation/project assignments, you'll do fine.  I must stress, READ THE BOOKS, you will almost certainly not pass if you don't. Prof. Swami is very approachable and happy to answer questions. Great class, I loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: his teaching is good but tests are hard

Prof. Sy was a great French teacher! He goes off the textbook, which makes it easy to follow along in class. There are five tests in the same format, which makes it easy to recognize patterns. This class places a heavy emphasis on grammar, which can be tricky on tests. Overall, a great class, but you do need to know French going into it to do well.
Attendance is super important but it's a fun class and he genuinely cares and wants to see you succeed.
Emphasises in class discussion. Easy test grader. Very worth it to take his class.

The absolute best prof you can get for French. Hilarious and truly cares about you as a person and helping you learn more French. Attendance and participation in class are incredibly important towards your grade, but he really just wants you to try and to practice the new skills in class so that he can help you.

He is a very good professor, the tests can be difficult but if you pay attention in lecture you can do pretty well on them. Attendance and in-class participation are VERY important towards your grade.

He is phenomenal. Never want to take a french class with anyone else. Super accessible for when you need help and really really cares about his students. Wants everyone to get A's. Absolutely the best!! Lots of tests though but if you go to class you can get a B without studying for them.

Genuinely one of the kindest professors you could have. Greatly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed while learning French. If he is an option, pick him! Very funny in class and very straightforward about what he expects from your answers on the test. Extremely accessible outside of class.

Professor Sy was such a great professor. He really emphasizes class participation when learning French, which greatly helped my speaking skills. His tests and homework assignments are fair and not too difficult. He's a fun person and is very accommodating.

Best professor I've had so far. Extremely engaging lectures and relates to personal life so they stick better. Expensive textbook necessary to finish homework assignments, and around 3-5 hours required of it each week. Group project w/ partner required integrating all learned into a conversation w/ classmate near end. Overall, enjoyed the class.

Professor Sy is a great teacher. He explains things clearly and cares about his students. Attendance and participation is very important. Also, he gives quite a few tests. In FREN 1002, he will only speak French, but it is not difficult to understand him if you payed attention in FREN 1001!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sy is great and caring. Lectures are laid back, however they are in French. It becomes less intimidating as the semester takes course, and they're pretty fun. The tests were fair if you did the practice sheet. There is also online homework, so you have to buy the textbook. There a couple other assignments, but pretty easy class overall.

Professor Sy was a great professor to really bolster your french speaking. He is a major proponent of speaking only french in his class so it's challenging in a good way. Tests are graded fairly harshly but repeat the same format so they get easier over time. Homeworks are a breeze but are through the textbook so you must buy it.
Sy really cares, come in with some basic knowledge and pay attention and you'll probably get an A.

He's an all-around great professor. He's very understanding of situations and schedules. He has great and interactive lectures, which is the best way to learn a language. The tests and homework are all easy. If you go to class and pay attention, you should get about a 95 or above, no sweat.
Very kind professor and the material is very easy.

This dude is awesome. Had him my first semester at Tech while I had linear and Physics 1 which was awful. He was the one class I was excited to go to. Ask him for a study guide before the test and show up to his class and it's an ez A. Pay attention to the two writing assignment deadlines. Cares so much about students.

Way easier than I expected for 2002. Class was asynchronous so I didn't really get to know him, but he was really nice at the oral final. He gives good feedback for essays and conversation assignments and grades very easy- he's forgiving and usually gives partial credit for wrong answers. Only issue is sometimes had to email twice to get a reply

Tough grader on oral and conversational assignments. Other than that the class isn't too hard. Did not communicate as much as I wished he had or send out announcements for assignment and test deadlines. Hard to reach by email. Not the best professor to take for an online class, but there are many opportunities for extra credit.
Not good at communicating course expectations, assignments and deadlines. Did very little to make the class engaging or interactive.
This guy the goat
Amazing prof

- HAVE to speak French in this class. No sitting in the corner because you WILL get called on and he knows everyone's name. It's fun when you get used to it - Funny professor, my only engaging class - Allowed 3 absences, but it's pretty chill anyway, so it's not hard to come to class - His class made French less intimidating to learn-highly rec!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This guy is great. You just have to make sure you attend class and pay attention and you'll get an easy A. He cares a lot about his students and it is evident in the way he runs his class. If I were to take another French class, I would definitely take from him again.
Best French Prof!
Really nice and funny guy. The class itself isn't that hard, but he always keeps the class engaged and it seems like he genuinely cares about his students.

This dude is so funny. He takes the time to learn people's names, notices when they are absent, and asks about them because he genuinely cares. The homework is super easy. The compositions are pretty easy. The only potentially annoying part of the class is all the speaking. Easy A, great and caring professor.

Really really nice and funny guy. Sometimes you have to write essays and have online homework which can be frustrating but he is always helpful. If you actually want to learn french, he is a great choice!

Monsieur Sy is a fabulous dude. Very charismatic and cares so much about students. He curves the exams/quizzes a ton, and offers lots of extra credit. He teaches straight from the textbook. You're guaranteed an A if you show up to class, speak a few times, and study for exams/quizzes the night before. Easiest class I've taken thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy is a great professor who really cares about his students. I had him for both FREN 2001 and FREN 2002 and he was extremely nice, always tries to give you credit for whatever you did right. If you speak in class, study the night before for tests, and do super easy online hw it's not hard to get an A.

This class was a giant mess (taught jointly by Sy and Caille). Caille was great, but Sy was absolutely terrible. He was very unclear about deadlines and assignments and what he expected. He seemed to cater to the native speakers (why they were in this class, I have no clue) and was very condescending to others.

Professor Sy is really caring and really engages the class by making sure everyone understands the material. He is flexible and makes sure that everyone understands what's going on. He is an easy grader.

I had her for Summer 2025 in Barcelona (she only teaches on that program in the summer now). She's amazing. Tests were chill except for the last one--that one was crazy. But tests were typically just like the practice exams she puts out, if not easier. She's really funny and will keep you updated on what's going on around in Barcelona.

I had her during the Barcelona summer program. She knows what she's talking about and is great at explaining any concept. My only gripe was that she didn't cover a few topics as in depth as she needed to for exams, but I think that's due to the constraints of a summer semester, since we were already covering a lot of material. Tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Worst professor I've had at this school. Blatantly picked favorites and completely inaccessible for questions. Gossiped about students to others in the class. 

Didn't even show up for final presentations with little to no explaination showing massive disrespect to students

Professor Sweat is a great instructor. She always made sure students were understanding the material and was approachable and helpful when answering questions. Would definitely recommend taking any course with her!

The key to her class and her HWs is to do EXACTLY what she does and/or what the TAs doe in lecture/recitation. Almost verbatim. The scary thing about this class was the tests. Exams worth 80% of grade. There were 4 exams, each with 20 multiple choice questions. Some material near the end was difficult, but asking students/TAs helped.
Homework is graded strictly but tests are doable. I've observed that the actual exams are about 15% more difficult than the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very tough grader, but that's the point of discrete math. Lectures were enjoyable although the answer formats were misleading at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homeworks are very nit picky and not graded consistently. It doesnt matter if you understand the material on the homework, it matters if you write everything out the way Sweat wants. exams take an unreasonable amount of time to get back even though they are multiple choice.

Dr. Sweat is pretty funny, and she teaches the subject really well. She seems very caring from what I saw of her. Her tests were fair, and the homework and feedback were helpful in preparing for the tests. A solid choice for 2050.

My favorite professor so far at Tech. She taught us exactly what we needed to know and was very nice. Her lectures were engaging and thorough. If you understand the homework problems, the tests are a breeze with no surprises. Amazing professor, and an easy A if you attend lecture and pay attention. Don't buy the textbook, there's a free pdf online.

Monica is very passionate about her subject, and her lectures are always a lot of fun. Homework can be a little rough if you don't follow their guidelines, but it's pretty straightforward once you get the hang of it. I loved this class!

Lectures can be a little boring, but are super informative and go over exactly what you need to know for the exam. Midterms are very similar to the practice exams and trying hard on the homework really prepares you well for them. TAs were also super helpful in clearing things up. All around would definitely take her again.
Pretty good lectures, and problems can be similar to those on the tests. The first exam was the hardest IMO, and exams are 90% of the grade, so make sure to do HW well and understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed CS 2050, and it turned out to be an easy class as well. If you go to the lectures, that's all you really need to do the homework. Understand how to do the homework and do the practice tests she posts before midterms -- the midterms are really pretty much the same thing (go to recitation as well). She's also a great lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The classes are boring but all the stuff in homeworks and test is from them. Most of the questions are repeated from tests of previous semsters so take them from your friends and do the practice test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Sweat is an amazing lecturer and you can really tell that she cares about her students!

Prof. Sweat's lectures are quite good. Topics are a little boring but she's a great teacher. Grading criteria can be difficult at times, as they deduct points for very minute details. Tests are reflective of the homework. You'll do well in the class if you do the homework sincerely and independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty clear and helpful but got a little boring halfway through the course. Tests are reflective of what we learned in class and aren't much different from homework problems. Definitely go to recitations to understand how the TAs will grade your test answers.

Prof. Sweat is a great lecturer, but recitations are a must. Each recitation has a worksheet with questions very similar to the tests and homeworks, and following how the TAs solve the problems will ensure you get the most credit possible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures got boring after a while especially during some modules where I felt reading textbook was better. The HW were 10% of the grade and exams consisted of rest 90%, 22.5% each including final. Exams weren't very tough but TAs took a lot of points for smalls mistakes which added up quickly. Don't start HW early as TA go over it in recitation
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One homework per week due on Fridays, and the questions come from the textbook. Exams are 90% of your grade. Lectures are good, albeit they are almost exactly what is in the textbook. Otherwise, the textbook isn't really required. Tests are easier than what is covered in the homework, so it's good prep.

Dr. Sweat is a great lecturer; she makes things very clear and easy to follow. The tests are predictable based on the homework and the recitation worksheets. My only complaint is that the grading can be very nitpicky. Overall, an easy yet informative class.

Taking discrete with her was the best choice for my first semester at tech. I didn't like how I did on the first exam, scheduled a meeting with her, and she walked me through the lapses in my work and how to fix it in the future. Honestly if you just go to lecture which is normally pretty entertaining and take notes you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is not useful. The professor seems a nice person but this class is far from relevant. The class has some weird grading. Definitely needs improvement
Super funny instructor. Very knowledgeable as well. Explains concepts clearly and is always open for consultation. One of the best at the CoC! Grading is a bit harsh, so beware.

Good class. Pretty much what she teaches is what is on the test. I stopped reading the book halfway thru the class bc of this. Homework is good practice as well as old exam questions she gives you but don't expect the problems to be the exact same on the test. Just take good notes in lecture and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you've had any exposure whatsoever to discrete math, you will likely find CS 2050 to be insultingly easy. If not, the pace of instruction is slow enough to where you might think that anyway. The only caveat is that Prof. Sweat is extremely nitpicky about notation and such when grading homeworks - far worse than in actual math classes.

Her lectures are clear and informative. I feel like this class could be taught in a much smaller time frame; I found that I got very bored in lectures. The project is worth SO much, and the TAs are very picky graders. Definitely make sure you have a good group going into it, or you're screwed. Tests weren't bad if you do practice tests beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Her class average has dropped from a 3.4 to 2.8 in recent years. I took this thinking it'd be relatively easy hearing it from an older year, but it's not. Make sure to go to class and do well on her quizzes. There are 4, 25 question multiple choice worth 60% of your grade. Go over old quizzes as well, she some times reuses questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Organized and really caring. I enjoyed taking 2050 with her, and was always helpful whenever anyone needed any help. Real pleasant person too.
Monica's lectures are really good and easy to understand. Most of the grading is based on tests, which are very doable if you understand the material. Homework is weekly but never takes too long.

Sweat is a great professor. I'm was pretty irresponsible and bombed the first test due to not showing up to class, but got it together and began attending lecture much more often. She's incredibly pleasant, and very fair. If you make a reasonable effort you should definitely be able to get an A.

She tells you exactly what is expected of you and as long as you follow the guidelines you'll get an A. The material itself is not complex -until the last unit-, you just have to format your answers *perfectly* to not get points taken off.
Lectures were a little boring, but I found them helpful. Homework was harder than the tests. Overall not a very difficult class.

Monica is a very sweet professor who really cares about her students, both learning and well-being. Her class and grading are very straight-forward. She teaches at a very good pace and explains material very well. Do the work and study everything and you'll do great. The course material is actually pretty simple.
Easy tests and helpful recitations, easy to get a good grade as long as you put forth effort. Weekly homework that can sometimes be a little long though.
Great teacher, /very/ easy class so far. Have yet to take the last test, which is supposed to be harder than the others. Would recommend!!!
Her tests are straight forward, she does her best to make the subject matter interesting, and make sure you go to workshops because that is where you learn the  majority of the information.

3 midterms, hw each week, and an optional final. You mostly learn how to solve simple math problems, manipulate pictures, and create basic web pages. As long as you attend lectures and recitation, the homeworks and exams are reasonable. Professor Sweat is a fair lecturer and her and the TAs do not hesitate to help you if you ask for help.

Uninteresting & unhelpful lectures. Spends a decent amount of time rambling. The TA's are really helpful so you should get acquainted with them early in the semester. I received a sizable amount of help from friends that were CS majors. The lectures don't help with the homework, but the tests aren't that bad as long as you understand the material.
Lectures are clear and informative, though occasionally a bit dry. Still, Prof. Sweat does have a personality and writes very fair tests. A decent amount of absences.

1 homework per week. 3 tests throughout the semester (plus a final), and they're all pretty easy and not in depth. The TAs are incredibly helpful and active Piazza, so you can get help and your questions answered quickly. Professor lectures and clear and concise. Attending class helps because there are pop assignments now and then.

She is an averagely decent person (sometimes rude, but tolerable)  outside of class, but honestly a horrible lecturer. She doesn't even take the time to make her own lecture notes, and just uses the lecture power points made by the textbook authors. She regularly CANNOT answer hard questions, and then the TAs take over to explain concepts.
Great professor. Fantastic at explaining difficult concepts, and she's not nitpicky on tests (she tests for overall understanding of concepts). If you go to class and do the homework, you'll be fine.

Monica is my favorite professor in the College of Computing. She is extremely approachable and easy to talk to. Her classes are challenging but fair, and as long as you go to class and do the homework you should be able to pull out an A.

An exciting and funny professor. Having never programmed before, I was able to understand everything clearly. There's homework every week and no curve for any tests. Test questions are very similar to examples done in class.

Probably the best pick for CS 1331. The material/class is difficult, but she's helpful and accommodating if you go to class and do the work; definitely a good teacher to have on your side. She cares about you knowing the material and is open and approachable for questions.
Best Teacher Ever!!! Learned a lot.

She is an pretty good teacher as long as you pay attention in her class or read the textbook (since she pretty much follows along with it). She's easy to talk to if you have any questions or problems. Her tests are basically straight from the study guides she puts out, give or take the wording and a few numbers.
You can get a B in her Java class without too much work. However, it takes a considerable effort and/or significant foreknowledge of Java to get an A.
she's AWESOME!

I had this teacher twice  and both times her lectures proved to be less than helpful.  They're not engaging and even the most dedicated student would have trouble paying attention let alone following along.  The second exam I took for 1331 was from what I heard designed for a longer class which would explain why almost no one finished it.

Interested in teaching students the material so that they will be interested and actually learn it.  She is always willing to help out with homework or other issues that arise.  Puts out study guides before tests that are extremely helpful and is gracious in her grading - sometimes allowing for final exemptions if you have an A.
Monica is awesome. I wold gladly take another CS class if she were teaching it, and I don't like CS.

The lecture isn't all that interesting (the majority of people seem to be surfing the internet or playing games during class) but I felt like I learned a lot from the class and the tests were pretty easy
Good teacher.  Explains it so a liberal arts major could understand. Might b too easy for a CS major.
Was very helpful. Always answers questions. Easy to talk to

Java is the epitome of all that is boring, and Sweat doesn't make it much more bearable... she is a nice person, but a very dry lecturer (not to mention advocating the gay rights agenda during class). I was bored out of my mind during lecture, and the homeworks made me want to put a gun in my mouth. The tests and final were really easy though.

Absolutely incompetent; she has recently asked the head TA to lecture in her place because she does not have a solid grasp of the material. That said, she's extremely easy (as she usually writes her tests so that she can do them---which means they are laughably easy).
I'd imagine this class would be good if you weren't a CS major.  If you want to learn something useful don't take this woman's class.

She is a great teacher. Very funny and easy to talk to. She teaches the class in a way that computer and non-computer majors are interested. If you go to the lectures and do your homeworks this should be an easy A
funny
she was my favorite teacher.  really easy to understand, communicates well, very friendly.  get monica if you can.
How people could not love Monica is beyond me.  She's an awesome professor, even if she is rather easy.  XD

As a non computer major, I would recomend other non computer majors take this class.  She attempts to teach this class so students with no programming experience won't get lost.  The computer majors will drive you crazy with their arrogant questions but she tries to minimize this.  Very easy tests.

Eh, I thought this class was a breeze. But I had previous programming experience. Monica is really cool, and easy to talk to. Just go to class all the time, pay attention, do the homework, you'll get an A. I did. My test grades were 97,91,96, and my final was a 99. No problem.

Sweat didn't even her own slides. They were someone elses. That class was so boring, on test days we had about 150 people, on regular days there were only about 10-15 people there. My best memory, I asked her about Scheme, and she said to find Kurt.
not bad, but the class itself is very hard.  Her lectures were not that great.  Most of the material is learned in lab/recetation
wasn't bad...better than Smith
I slept every damn lecture until I stopped going.  Easy class though.
It's CS 1321, you can't expect it to be easy.  She does the best a teacher can with the material she has to cover.

Thank God I took her as my teacher! The course itself is pretty hard but you can surely count on Monica to help you out, either right after class or, she will gladly arrange office hours that will fit you! She explains very well.
No Comments
Not bad, but not anything special.  Just expect the normal CS type of lecture.
Fun class, taught very well.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Really smart guy and pretty nice but the class is insanely disorganized and not taught well. So many problems with this course.

Extremely tough grader. Topics pop up on tests that weren't talked about. Many topics such as the cold war, we only learned about in reading, and were not really taught in class. Tests have no multiple choice. Midterm grades were exceptionally hard. Rambles on in lecture and doesn't use any visual aid for lectures so they are impossible to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I wouldnt take this class again. Students required to purchase and read 4 lengthy novels over the semester (No skipping out on those for tests). Also doesnt use Canvas whatsoever, so grades are kind of a mystery. In my opinion, this class was just as hard if not harder than my Differential Equations class... Not a good experience :(

Very knowledgable professor. His lectures are long and can be boring, but you have to go to class or your grade will suffer. There is a lot of reading, but most of the test material is based off of in class discussion, so skimming and understanding key points will suffice when reading. If you pay attention, tests are very easy and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures can be kinda boring, but he's pretty approachable outside of class. Not a lot of work but have to remember specific details from class. As long as you keep up with the reading you should make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Classes are super boring.  Lectures go off on tangents several times a class, and it's hard to take notes.  He doesn't use powerpoint aka he makes it really hard to want to go to class.  KEEP UP WITH THE READING and you'll be fine for this class.  If you can't do 100 pages of reading a week then this class isn't for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Difficult to take notes b/c he goes off on a tangent. He doesn't like multiple choice tests b/c "there are concepts that can be interpreted different ways"... but if you don't have the EXACT words in your short answer that he has he the key, he doesn't give credit. I ended up dropping the course 3 months in b/c of how much reading is assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Incredibly difficult class. Get ready to do your own research and prompt engineering. He teaches the concepts very well, but the labs use lectures' contents as fundamentals, but you need to do extra research and understanding in order to solve a problem. It was my first time doing a CTF and the struggle was fun.

I loved this class overall. Taking a class based entirely around applying knowledge feels practical and fun. My one gripe is the cheating problem. It is tilting to have a leaderboard in a class where huge groups of people share flags every lab. I really wish they would take that a little more seriously. Still recommend this class though.

Projects demand your attention and require abstract thinking. While the professor and TAs get back to you fairly quickly, the course allows open discussion of what everyone is doing to solve the homework. CS 6265 uses cumulative scoring, if you do more work early on later projects will require less work for you to get a high grade. No quizzes/exams
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best course I took at Georgia Tech!

Probably one of the smartest people in the institute. Unlike the many other courses/professors, Dr. Kim speaks from experience and teaches functional and practical things instead of theories and nonsense.

Crafting one CTF challenge is hard nevermind 10 labs, CS 6265 is a fun deep dive into binary exploitation. If you do not know your basics of how binaries work/ their assembly, brush up before taking this as it is not an intro course. It is a great learning curve for everybody and kudos to Prof. Kim and staff for this amazing setup!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely based professor. People just rate Prof. Kim low because his course is challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The absolute worst professor at Georgia Tech. He is arrogant and condescending, doesn't care about students one bit and only cares about his research. Avoid taking him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Harris is less of a teacher and more of an obstacle. My advice is to engage as less as possible and do your work. She likes to hear the sound of her own voice.

Dr. Harrismakes the classroom a hostile learning enviornment. She would scold students who ask questions during her lecture that was hard to follow. You are graded by homework and exams. I would suggest writing down as much information as possible on the cheat sheets if you find yourself in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: [ME 6222]: You wouldn't be able to tell this woman has a PhD from the way she gives a lecture. She relies heavily on reading the slides, if you're hoping to get real-world insight on a topic she's not the one (she went straight from her PhD to assistant prof). She's very sassy, has a know-it-all attitude, poor grades with little to no explanation.

Prof. Harris is incredibly strict with grading and grading criteria. Made a 35 on my first group report (highest grade in the class was a 65), which would have likely earned roughly a 75 in other sections. However, she truly does care about the success of her students, which is the cause of her toughness. You will learn a lot, but it will be tough.

Will not tell you what your grade is and have to find out what you got after the semester is over. Grades are not organized in Canvas and are all over the place, with wrong weights and wrong categories. Treated like you are wasting her time and get a grade that is significantly lower than what Canvas says. Do not take, avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst 2110 studio professor. Do not take, extremely strict and unforgiving non sensical grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is the toughest grader, and she tells you that first day. She is super strict about everything in this class, but she definitely prepares you. As annoying as her tough grading was and her being picky, I definitely saw improvement in my writing, ideas, and presentation skills. Get ready to go through the mud with her, but she does help prepare.

Dr. Harris is a nice person, just too nit-picky of a grader for 2110. The class is super time-consuming, and having her take points off for the tiniest details on reports was very frustrating. I had friends in other studios saying theirs were much easier. She had lots of feedback, but would just grade harder on the next report. Avoid if possible

Dr. Harris is a very unpleasant person. I would try to avoid her as a teacher if at all possible. Her expectations are very high, and she does not really give any actual guidance on what she wants. She expects you to go to office hours all the time to get clarification on assignments. My least favorite professor at GT.
Great professor. Very in depth lectures with good examples. Tough grader, but enough extra credit that you can make up for it.

Be prepared to be stressed, feel defeated, and frustrated. She is a tough grader and not always good at clarifying, and can seem condescending towards her students when they don't perform to her VERY high standards. Overall though, Dr. Harris is a good teacher. YOU WILL LEARN A LOT. And she spends a lot of time giving in depth feed back on HW.
She is a nit picky grader and will question the smallest details of your work. She wants you to succeed, but at the cost of your grade.

She uses powerpoints that have inaccurate material to teach. Her lectures consist of her reading her powerpoints word for word and getting other students to answer in class questions that she does not seem to know the answer to.
Dr. Harris was thorough in and extremely helpful giving step by step instructions to produce a quality material in a manufacturing environment Thank you Dr. Harris for you support.

Worst choice for a studio professor.  She is subjective in grading, condescending, and pompous.  Plan to stay the full 3 hours EVERY time, even if it's just to hear her complain about her opinion of class presentations (I don't like the border, etc).  I got an A but I wish I had a better professor.

He is really nice. Grade is 90% exams 10% homework and 10% optional extra credit. Tests are just like the study guide and homeworks are not too bad. His lectures are straight from the slides but not too boring. Recommend for a pretty easy A.

Even though the 10% Extra Credit is listed as optional, do it if you want an A, you won't get it otherwise. The tests are easy as they are very similar to the practice exams he gives out. The final is a lot tougher but he does give out a decent amount of partial credit. HW is long but the same every semester and there are only 5. Take for passing.

I took the class couple of years back and here is what I felt. Prof Manos makes you well prepared for the exam, he is very gentle when approached and explains concepts behind every equation he writes. I started liking Electromagnetics because of an amazing professor like him. For me with no prior background, he made it interesting and practical.
Not a good professor
Not sure what to say, I just did not feel connected at all. Chris, provides answers that are of not much help. I would rather find out things by myself rather going to him.
Semester just started and this guy already has a bad attitude. I can clearly see how the other reviewers on here had issues. This person should never be a TA/instructor anywhere.

The kid clearly has a 9-5 job in the industry, which means he's not held accountable for his behavior towards the GT students, only his employer as a programmer. You can easily see his character flaws in his demeanor. Not sure why he even wants to be a TA if he's not good at it, and people obviously do not like him.

He could be a little kinder in his piazza replies, seems power controlling, likes to lay down policy immediately after any push back. If you are reading this please try different approach when working with students, even in the real world, you may end up coming off just a little likeable, who knows?
All around a bad TA; such a shame as it would be a good class otherwise. Arrogant and has a poor attitude towards students. Very disrespectful.

I was alarmed to find out this individual was the head TA - extremely unprofessional. Some "highlights" include: 1) Posting student grades 2) Mocking students over grades 3) Posting venmo account to accept bribes (as a joke) I'm all for a good joke when the time and place is appropriate - but official course communication isn't the time or place.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was my first course and loved the way the course was structured. Chris was very helpful and the way projects were structured, it was challenging, fun and knowledge gaining at the same time. so Kudos to you chris, very happy that I have taken CS6035 as my first class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Agree with many of the other comments here; this guy should not be a student facing TA. He needs to mature.
Like others have experienced; he is probably the worst TA Ive had at GaTech. Needs to learn how to act professionally.

The absolute worst TA i have had in a class so far in my 2yrs at GA Tech. Demeaning and unprofessional attitude. Acts like he is doing a favor to students by being a TA. I can't believe he is permitted to talk how he does about students in the course slack.

Is supposedly a Head TA for the course; but acts extremely unprofessionally when dealing with students. His behavior in slack towards students is appalling; even after being called by people to act more professional he continued to conduct himself poorly. Gives Georgia Tech a bad name. Should not be a TA.

Probably the worst TA in the program. Unprofessional, obnoxious, bent on making sure the class runs exactly how he wants. Unfortunately, since he sets the culture, even some of the good TAs I saw were drowned out.

Poor TA. Very unprofessional conduct in the course slack channel. Doesn't like students who are asking for help. Condescending & talks down to students who reach out. Does not meet the standards would expect from a TA at Georgia Tech. Poor experience.

Excellent TA. Doesn't tolerate students who put in zero effort before asking for help. Incredibly knowledgeable and helpful with anything you might need. I hope there are future opportunities where he is TA'ing for other classes that I am attending :)
Pretty fair, like I've not taken a class in a long time with someone who CONSTANTLY reminds you that a deadline is coming up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chris is an awesome teacher and provides exemplary support and guidance to students.
He wants students to be successful. Direct and to the point. Willing to help. Expects students to manage their time and work and read directions.
Very intelligent, upfront, and gives clear information. Definitely would take any classes with him as Head TA again
Very arrogant and student hostile. Not a good TA. Needs to be more professional.

Took this class online with Chris as the Head TA. He is awesome. He is definitely passive aggressive and gives you a hard time when you ask him a question that is contained in the instructions, but overall extremely fair. He is on slack basically all day everyday and will help if you put in the effort. Would take any class he oversees.

The office hours were good, the lectures were a bit rambly, the textbook was amazing, and the homeworks were fair. The tests were a bit all over the place with difficulty, but the professor was lenient and tried to make sure that everyone who took the class and tried their best, succeeded. Solid Class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, class was enjoyable and we covered topics beyond the scope of the general CS 3510, which was exciting. Would definitely take the class again. Professor was also very approachable outside of class for any clarifications you may have on the subject.
Amazing professor: super nice, and always stayed long after class to answer questions and even talk about extra topics. Only complaint is that there was no homework, only tests.

Awesome professor who genuinely cares about the student's understanding of the material. Lectures are on the dry side, but they are often still worth attending. He is a tough professor, but it is also a very rewarding experience. He's also very accessible outside of class through office hours and email. One of the best I've ever had.

Goes very in depth on lecture material which is a double-edged sword: easier to understand but lectures tend to carry onto the next day. Recognizes if he doesn't have time to go over something before a test, and removes unreviewed material from real/practice exams. Exams are reasonable and line up with practice. Doesn't post notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's a nice guy and is easily accessible outside of class, but is definitely more helpful in office hours than in lecture, so go to those when you can. lots of extra credit opportunities offered on the exams if u attend tutoring sessions. content is a bit hard if you're not strong at math but the practice exams are nearly identical to the real ones

Dr. Tran is a very nice professor, he is always willing to help. Class material is hard tho so sometimes it can be time consuming but overall he is very clear with what to learn. Exams are very similar to practice exams just different numbers and wording I say.

I can barely understand him. He's extremely quiet, slow, and bad at explaining things. Attendance is mandatory. He also doesn't allow certain electronics, laptops for instance, even if you're taking notes on them. He's also low key rude and demeaning. I think he has a fragile ego and a superiority complex but is just too quiet for people to notice.

Great dude and very kind but he often struggles to explain specific things when one asks about them. I don't have many people to compare to for this course for obvious reasons, but I'm not sure I'd recommend if you are not great at math like me.
His lectures aren't bad per say but he isn't great at explaining stuff when you ask questions. The tests themselves are kind of difficult if you don't study a ton but it's definitely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely a NO.

He is a very nice person, but he spends the first 20 minutes of lecture going over stuff from the previous class. It is also a little bit annoying that he doesn't let students have laptops open during lecture and that he goes very slow over simple material.

Great lecturer, really broke down problems in an easy to understand way. Homework was just weekly Webwork, and exams were somewhat difficult but he drops your lowest midterm which is helpful. Final grade is about 80 percent exams, but he does curve the final grades. Great professor!

Very sweet professor. Had him for summer, I wouldn't do it again tbh, we fell behind even before exam 2 started and mostly self taught the course. He is always willing to understand any circumstances you can encounter and explain as much as possible to help you out, even during exams. I do not like the WebWorks tho, they were unnecessarily hard.

MATH1551 was harder than MATH1554 for me. Professor Tran isn't great but isn't terrible. Go to office hours and get one one-on-one help because you won't "learn" in lecture. Tests were unnecessarily difficult and were different than the practice exams. All of the averages being below 70 should say enough.
He is very sweet and explains problems well and in-depth during the lectures. The guided notes he provides are very helpful.

His lectures were boring and the first 20 minutes of a 50 minute lecture was spent reviewing previous lecture material and examples. Tests contained problems that were worded weird and weren't close to types of examples gone over in class or studio. He was a nice guy but also became a mega stickler about laptops and sitting near others

Professor Tran is very kind and clearly cares about your success in the course--quick responses on Piazza and to emails, many office hours. The tests are difficult but there are lots of resources including Plus Sessions, help desks, study support, and exam reviews you should take advantage of!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved having him as my professor. He was so caring and gave some opporutnities for grade improvement. This is a professor that wants students to do well in his class. With that being said, his exams are HARD. He gives lots of practice problems but the test is always hard. Also be prepared to do a lot of Webworks.

Lectures are heavy but participation is not required. VERY webworks heavy. Studio worksheets / class are very confusing and fast paced so give yourself grace. He offers extra credit for attending office hours towards the end of the semester / completing all your webworks. Very understanding and wants students to succeed. He came through for me.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him in fall 2023. He is a good lecturer with good notes to fill in. If he sees you struggling or not performing as expected, he will reach out to you.

He's a good professor! Maybe not the best at answering questions at times and sometimes we'd get behind a bit because he'd spend too much time reviewing stuff (causing him to rush a bit at the end), but he genuinely cares for your success in the class and even offers extra office hours before the exams. 
 & Def recommend going to the plus sessions!

He seems kind and makes time esp during exam week but I had a hard time following his lectures and often found myself struggling to stay awake. Has def been annoying towards the end of the sem and been forceful about students talking to each other to the point of coming up to students individually, which is frustrating as someone w/ bad anxiety...

Great at teaching and explaining the content, and you can tell that he cares about his students! He always reminded us about any upcoming tests or quizzes, and he always made sure we were aware of what content they would be over. Practice exams are a big help for test prep. Highly recommend taking his class if you get the chance!

This was definitely a hard class for me since it was my first time taking calculus, and I had skipped pre-calculus. I attended the majority of his office hours, and he truly cares about his students. Additionally, he would hold extended office hours in the days leading up to exams to help us prepare.

Dr. Tran was an amazing professor and by far my favorite professor this semester. He is exceptionally good at his job, extremely caring, and truly wants his students to succeed. Exams were fine if you studied. Lecture attendance is not mandatory. Extremely accessible outside of class. I have nothing negative to say about Dr. Tran.

He was very nice and always open to talking if you had questions. Only problem is that he is bad at answering questions. He was pretty good during lectures, but if you had a specific question or need help on a problem, you are better off asking your TA. He also reviews a lot of the previous content during lectures which gets us behind.

Super kind professor!! Would give us reminders before class and make sure we were up to date on things like quizzes and exams. He is also very good at lecturing and will help answer your questions. Overall, very nice and caring of his students.

Great lecture explanations and office hours he makes sure you understand thoroughly to the point you are scared to not ask for help. Asian accent is no big deal and you can tell he cares about if you understand what he is saying by repeating important information and being as concise as possible to avoid filler words. Great teacher 5/5 on yelp.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was nervous about Calc 1 since I didn't take it in HS but Professor Tran broke things down well in the lecture! Plus, if you go to his office hours or come to class early he will help you with any homework or questions (he walks up to everyone too). My biggest tips are to do Studio Worksheets before each studio and complete every practice exam!
really cares about students. will answer an email at any hour. once set up a no-video call at 10pm because I emailed needing help with homework. underrated because of his patience
Very caring professor, always made the lectures more interesting. Very accessible outside of class.

Dr. Tran is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is very caring and extremely accessible outside of class. I always went to office hours, which were super helpful. Very kind and encouraging. He held extra office hours (virtual and in-person) leading up to each exam. Dr. Tran is incredible, and I highly recommend his class to anyone!

Very caring professor! Remembers his students even though it is a bigger class of about 90 students. He would personally email me to check in with my progress and always encouraged students to set up appointments with him for extra help. It's a coordinated Math 1551 class so he doesn't have the freedom to grade outside of that/give own extra credit

I went to the first few lectures, but then realized that all of the annotated notes are posted online. Attendance is not mandatory. Studio attendance is necessary, there are quizzes in studio every Friday. Tran is literally so enthusiastic about math, it's pretty cool. I appreciate him for that.

Seems like a sweet guy, but his lectures weren't very engaging and he could be hard to understand. Not his fault but the homework in this class was atrocious with the platform constantly being down. Also, tests were really hard and weren't similar to the practice tests we were given.
Really clear lectures, fast Piazza responses, and fair grading. Great professor overall.

3 exams, 3 quizzes, weekly homework. Only half of the hw assignments are graded, but it is really helpful to do all of them. he pulls from the homework questions and examples done in lecture for exams. great professor, learned a lot

The content can be difficult to understand, but quizzes and exams are made up almost entirely of lecture and homework problems. Only complaint is that the only way to access lecture content is through typed-up lecture notes posted after class that don't contain worked-out examples, just theorems with proofs and listed examples.

Clear lectures and provides notes after class. Tests/quizzes are almost identical to what you see in class and on homeworks, so you'll know exactly what to expect. Lowers cutoffs for grades. Provides solutions to exams and quizzes. Incredibly knowledgeable prof.

Will be overhated this year. 1st time teaching 3406, content is tough. Very clear about what's on exams (HW/lecture problems exclusively). Super passionate about the class and loves answering questions. Can be hard to understand but posts lecture notes (with minor typos). Lowered grade floor 5% and curved a test and a quiz to help people's grades.

I took this course in Spring 2024. Le was a tough professor. His lectures were very dry and difficult to follow. 3012 is a challenging class, but I felt that taking it with Le made it harder. He is in no way the worst prof to have 3012 with, though! Be prepared to self study a lot and take heavily weighted tests.

Professor Le is a very smart guy and a great lecturer. If you attend lecture, you will do just fine. There seem to be a lot of reviews mentioning the difficulty, but with a class as difficult as combo you can't expect to skip class every day and magically earn an A. If you have solid attendance and do well on exams he lets you exempt the final.

His accent makes it a bit tough to understand what he is saying. Exams/quizzes are DIFFICULT, but they are based on lecture/HW questions, so kind of fair. If a question is discussed in lecture, he will not give out the answer on Piazza, and just say "Discussed in Lecture". He is a caring professor, but I suggest taking someone else.

Thang Le is a good lecturer, and his slides are thorough. He does withhold answers to his practice questions if they're discussed in lecture, but this isn't damning. He likely just wants a decent level of engagement from students. Be consistent with studying, engage in lectures when you don't understand the content, and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking other professors because their classes would be much easier. Homework is graded harshly for no good reason, quizzes are quite difficult, and the tests aren't the easiest either. He makes the class very time consuming as a lot of studying needs to be done in order to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reviews seem suspiciously high. Although he is nice, the other combo professors are significantly easier. By the final exam, I would guess that at least 20% of the class had dropped
Doesn't provide answers to some questions and says "lecture" instead. Textbook is weirdly structured and barely helps.

If you want to succeed in the class, attend lectures! Le is a great lecturer and runs the class very well - the homeworks are extremely helpful for quizzes and exams. He does great for the difficulty of the concepts, and there is always a generous curve at the end (86 to an A my semester). Study for the exams and you will be more than fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is pretty tough. However, he is a great professor and explains the material very easily. Attendance was never checked but I highly recommend going to class all the time since every problem for HWs, Quizzes, and even Exams is from the lecture. If I had to take the MATH3012 class, I would take his class again.
Only answers "discussed in lecture" to a majority of the posts on piazza

The lectures are fast paced but interesting. You'll do bad in the class if you skip lecture, since he provides a lot of problems that end up on quizzes/exams there. Homework is difficult and time consuming bc it's a hard class in general. I recommend this prof of you're someone who goes to class.
Yells at students during lecture, very inaccessible.

The GOAT. Not the easiest professor for sure, but his lectures were really good. He curved all exams, and adjusted the grade boundaries at the end of semester to make up for how tough the class is. Side note: ATTEND ALL LECTURES and actually do the optional homeworks if you want to do well in this class.

My main problem with this professor is that he refuses to explain things if they were covered in lecture. If a certain problem was solved in class and you asked questions about it later, such as on Piazza, all he would say is "covered in lecture." It's almost like he was gatekeeping the course content, which made it incredibly difficult to learn.

One of the best classes I've taken at tech! Professor Le is very difficult but all his questions are similar to those from lectures and homework. If you do every homework/lecture problem, you will breeze through the class and have fun. If you want to talk to him during office hours, ask him about his perfect score in the IMO. He's truly brilliant.
I have no idea what everyone is saying because thang Le is an amazing prof that made combo simple and clear

Thang Le is a great professor but combo is a hard class. Tests are hard but fair because almost all questions are pulled from homework or lectures. Attendance is not required, but it would be hard to do well without at least watching the recordings. There is a small curve dependent on class average, but don't expect large grade increases.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was nice but made content difficult. Exams and quizzes were not challenging, but you have to prepare well with guides and hw. Notes were on canvas, so it was easy to catch up. He curves for midterms and might lower the cutoff at the end of the semester, but otherwise, you have to get good scores. Loved the class though, very interesting!

Professor Le is a very nice and hilarious guy, and I do think that he is good at what he teaches. However, and this is not his fault, I found it very difficult to understand him (and ultimately his test questions). Prepare to spend lots of time on homework and studying. I could have made it easier on myself if I just attended class more.

He was a great lecturer who made expectations clear. If you pay attention in lecture and do the homework, there's a high chance of doing great on quizzes/tests. He answers student questions quickly, and I think he is funny too. He will curve within reason, but he won't curve too much. I learned a lot from him and thought he was a great teacher.

Almost all questions on exams or quizzes are similar to the homework or lectures. He is a great lecturer but pretty harsh grader. If your work on exams/quizzes is not good enough for someone who doesn't know combinatorics to understand what you did, you will get many points deducted even if you get the right answer. Overall, I enjoyed his class.

i went to lectures and took nothing out of it as I couldnt understand what he was saying and I wasn't able to follow him as he solved questions because I could barely see the slides. the studios and TAs were really good as that's how I literally learned everything and got an A. the tests were hard but curved and there was a lot of extra credit.

First, I am assuming this is MATH 1552 or integral calculus. Thang Le was a very enjoyable lecturer. He was a bit confusing at times, but would clear anything up if asked. If you are not afraid to ask questions, it will be a breeze. Many people complained about his methods and difficulty, but study weekly, and you will do fine.

He doesn't explain anything well, I taught myself the entire class myself using YouTube videos. The canvas assignments are glitchy and nothing is done about it. He reiterates the wrong material and the test problems came out of nowhere, nothing at all like the quizzes or review guide. Lots of curves really well even if you fail.

One of the most difficult classes I have taken so far at Tech. The professor definitely could have taught this course a lot better, but was funny during lecture and good at teaching. Few tests and quizzes that count for a lot, most people fail/do poorly but they are curved. Difficult course material made this an extremely stressful class.

As a lecturer, I really appreciated Professor Le. The course, on the other hand, covers a lot of ground and can be overwhelming. Some topics are much harder than others, but the tough part about this class is how everything is tested (tests are fairly difficult). However, with good practice, you can expect to do well since he usually curves.

His lectures can be a lot at times, but he 100% cares about his students. 3012 is a very hard class, and he curves to show it. Expect to just not know how to do some things, but no one else does either. Still, this is one of the classes I learned the most in this semester. I failed an exam and still got an A in the class, so anything is possible.

Classic amazing lecturer, but hard class situation. Very understanding person.
One of the best teachers I've had at Tech.

Le's a a good lecturer, but the content he lectures on is extremely vague and abstract so it's very difficult to grasp if you're new to this side of math. A large number of quizzes/tests (which are curved very generously), all problems come from class and HW - the problem is that there are just so many different types of abstract problems.
