Topology is a tough class and he covers a lot of material but his lectures are very helpful. He often stops and goes through examples and draws on the board, which makes things clearer. He answers questions helpfully too and he holds extra office hours before exams. It wasn't easy but it was fun, and if you enjoyed real analysis, you'll enjoy this.
I usually wished I got sick or something hit me so I wouldn't have to endure his boring lectures

Dr. Le is a pretty good lecturer, and the homework always came out of the textbook so it was easy to find support when stuck. Most of the test questions came from either the homework questions or variations of examples he went over during class.
He's a decent enough professor. The class itself is very hard. There were quite a few hiccups with the transition to online classes, but that's the case for everyone.

One of the most uncooperative professors. In this semester's transition to online classes, every other professor has somewhat altered their class structure to better suit the online format. But he gives us 15 minutes to take a quiz on paper, scan it with an app, airdrop it to yourself, upload and submit it, despite students' pleas for flexibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Le is very funny, but the classes he teaches are quite difficult. He gives pop quizzes so be prepared to come to class. Overall, his expectations are clear even if the material is a bit vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Make sure you take good lecture notes as he bases the quizzes and test problems on this rather than the textbook. Not an easy class by any means, but made substantially more difficult if you miss class consistently.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: good lecturer. Doing the HWs and practice problems is very helpful to understanding the material. He gives good practice problems for exams too. 2 midterm exams, curved 10 points each
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Combinatorics is a really tough class, but Le has this great teaching style that makes it really accessible and almost exciting. He'll explain each example in 2-3 ways so it appeals to many ways of thinking. He does a really good job of connecting concepts.

Pop quizzes can be annoying. Homework can be long and tedious. Combinatorics is rough, but that's just combinatorics. Le lectures well (has slight accent), but is fair and provides the resources need for one to succeed in the class. He posts practice problems before each test! Take Le if you cannot get Trotter for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! He was a very suitable professor for the Problem Solving class (for preparation for the Putnam Exam) with his former experiences in mathematical olympiads and his perfect score in the 1982 International Mathematical Olympiad. I hope he will teach 4802 again next year since I learned so much in that class!
Great Professor! Highly recommend!
Tests are tricky but he explains concepts very clearly and provides good examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His accent takes getting used to, and he moves at a break neck pace. However, the examples he does in class, the hw he assigns, and the quizzes he gives are all similar to the exams. If you are willing to put in work you should be fine.

Impossible professor. Can't understand a single word he says. Runs through the material so fast in the most unclear way possible, asks "is that clear?" and moves on, erasing the entire board. Uses pointless notation that has nothing to do with the material. Tests are insanely hard, quizzes and worksheets are impossible. Do not take a class with him
Awesome Prof!
This guy is the most worthless teacher ever. Horrible teaching, difficult testing, and very unapproachable. He is definitely the worst professor i've taken so far.

Calc II at Gatech = hardest math class non-math majors will ever have to take. This professor took the difficulty of the class to a whole new level. His teaching of the Linear algebra stuff was confusing. Going to his office hours is just a waste of time.  can't tell if he is speaking english

abstract vector spaces. he has accent, smug ego; went to office hrs, he never solved one problem, ridiculed a student once for not knowing something; paid attention to best kid in class, taught to their level; not willing to help; dont take unless you're already very good wtih linear algebra, have some background in proofs; txtbk was godawful;

His lectures don't make sense, and sometimes the lecture notes aren't very clear either, and he doesn't follow a textbook. He usually gives 2 or 3 homeworks a week, and the exams are take home, so getting a good grade isn't too difficult. Sometimes, the hws or exams will have some math that was never covered in this class or any prereqs though.
Allows take home exams. Lectures are slow and do require point solution participation.
He's very funny! His lectures don't always make complete sense and there's a lot of homework , but he's very good at answering questions, clarifying, and making things interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There are actually around thirty homework for the class. He also forgets what he even puts on the test. I passed a test with a B and made a 47
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: he is humerous

Learned more about Thad than I did about ubiquitous computing. Like dude, we don't want to watch the Google glass ad 60 times. 

On a more serious note, this class will have you doing free labor for random labs.
No grace, no compassion. Wouldn't recommend. Thinks his failed google glass is a gift to humanity.
Threatens students to an extreme degree.
What a joke.
actual bafoon

The class is a great idea, but very poorly executed or taught.  The videos that were made are helpful and the textbook is good, but this class really should be called Unsupervised Learning AI.   There is a ton of supplementary reading material he gives you, but you just need to figure out how to teach yourself!

I spent over 20+ hours per week.

Lectures were pretty boring and monotonous. Almost no one in class would pay attention and everyone went on their laptops, but attendance wasn't mandatory anyways. Exercises were a little difficult and projects are a lot but the deliverables are reasonable.
terrible guy, doesn't do anything

Extremely knowledgeable professor but not very nice. Tests were surprisingly difficult. Projects were often pretty difficult and time consuming. Definitely start them very early. Plenty of extra credit was available. Between that and the projects being auto-graded, you could get an A pretty easily with enough time invested.

Prof. Starner is a person who knows many things but doesn't know how to teach them properly to students. The lecture was mostly about him and not the materials. TAs are not very responsive and I don't think they know what they are doing. Most of the materials from this class were self-taught and it was the hardest class I've ever taken.

Starner is the WORST professor, teacher, whatever, that I have EVER had. From someone who attended most lectures, I can say that I learned more about him than AI, and I am VERY disappointed by how this class was ran. Unresponsive TAs, a terrible teacher, essentially pseudocode-translation homework, and a terrible introduction to AI. Big let down.

I think Thad is just a bad lecturer or never prepares to teach this class.There were no issues with his assignments like last time since he just used Dr. Riedl / Berkekely's, but he is always late to class, always goes on tangents, barely teaches and always very dry. Could be worse, could be better.

Very knowledgeable with course concepts however lectures were a bit all over the place and led to some tangents. Overall a very interesting guy and course, but a tad unorganized and cared a little too much about cheating. Definitely isn't the grad version being taught as a 3000 level anymore!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This semester the class was really easy, but I legitimately learned nothing in this class. I try and go to lectures but they can be so dry and boring. Also, he's always preaching about not teaching but every single assignment in this class is completely online and copied from berkeley.

Ok I know everyone was like he's terrible after that one semester - but no he's not that bad at all. The lectures do tend to overview material too quickly in a sort of hand-wavy unplanned way, so you feel like you haven't gotten much of examples and understanding from lectures, but overall, it's still good. "Projects" aren't too bad.

Starner's lectures definitely aren't carefully planned + executed to optimize understanding of course material, but he is an interesting and passionate person. Overall, there's the vibe of: "I'll give you the basics and go off on tangents about examples from my life and you figure out the rest." Could certainly be better, could be worse.
terrible man.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. cared more about catching students cheating than teaching to the point that you could not google simple concepts or use textbook without being flagged - with no usable resources provided. was so full of himself and his lectures were recorded conversations rather than real lectures. did not care about us at all.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. I heard him tell a child to go learn something himself instead of teaching content in his own class. Lazily copied content from a grad course without giving credit and then focused on catching "cheaters" instead of actually doing anything himself. We paid for a course and learnt nothing bc of one ego.

Thad Starner may be a decent human but is a terrible professor. He cared more about catching cheaters than teaching students content. The course was lazily copied from 6601 and no dual credit was given. Further, in a country where students are paying thousands of dollars a course, schools have the responsibility to figure out their business.

This course was lazily copied over from CS 6601. The homeworks were incredibly time consuming because they were intended for graduate students who already have significant experience. Even after cutting out some parts, they were difficult because resources were not relevant. Exams were completely unrelated to homework and highly time-consuming.

Homework could be really hard and time-consuming. While I learned a lot from it, I think some of the expectations set for the students were a bit extreme (i.e undergrads doing grad level work). While it's not necessarily difficult to get an A given you have the time, the time commitment is well beyond 3 credit hours for this course with Thad.

Always feels like he's working against you: difficult/lengthy assignments, TA's don't know the material, exams/hw greatly differ from lectures
Pros: Receives criticism and feedback well- willing to help out (to an extent)
Cons: Neurotic about his plagiarism research, cares more about catching cheaters than helping students understand the material

Pros:
- Amazing homework.
- Smart prof.
- Good curriculum.
Cons:
- Gradescope submission limit
- TA's were not very useful.
- Plagiarism software made me scared to watch a youtube video (makes the lectures and textbook the only thing to help with hw, which makes no sense).
- Even going in person it feels like an online coursera class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: TAs don't come to office hours & there is no shot the professor will respond to your emails. Not sure why there even needs to be a "teaching team"- just having graders and plagarism checkers will accomplish the same thing. I learned more about Thad's career than AI

The Prof attempted innovative teaching ways for a large class, but resources for assignments could've been improved. Content that should've been on assignment instructions was buried in discussions. Exams were chaotic lead to numerous regrade requests, looked like even TAs didn't know how to solve questions (as seen in office hours too).

Prof. Thad had a great vision for this class. The first few weeks were genuinely pretty fun, and adding difficulty to the intel thread is extremely necessary if everyone and their mom select intel for no reason other than hype. My biggest issue is the TAs though. Massive skill issue.
Easily the worst class I haver ever taken. Thad cares more about his plagiarism AI than his students. Assignments are made to bait collaboration to feed into his plagiarism software.

This revamp of 3600 took a medium difficulty class as an intro to AI and made it much harder with the exact same material as the graduate version without making any concessions on changing the grading scale until some time into the semester. I respect Thad for trying to increase the accessibility of CS 3600 but students had little to no resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I wanted to say for anyone reading this in the future, the majority of 1's you see here are from one semester. They tried an experimental model for this class; I see how this class would have been incredible in theory, just failed in execution. I think Thad has good intentions, but the experience for the students was full of anxiety/struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: This professor does not deserve all the hate he gets. He definitely has some problems with communication, but he is clearly brilliant and wants his students to succeed. Some assignments are VERY hard, but all of them are super interesting to work on and teach you way more than the material from any other 3600 prof. People need to stop complaining.
Great guy with poor teaching abilities. Over-applies expertise in his prestigious research to an undergraduate-level course. Hardly accessible with little sympathy for students.

Any spark of interest I had in AI was almost immediately snuffed out within the few weeks of Thad's class. This was the most demotivating and unenjoyable experience I've ever had with learning at Tech. The best thing about this class is that it made me incredibly grateful for my other classes, TAs, and professors this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
How better can I sum up my experience in this class than by saying that you can expect 20+ hours of homework a week, and you'll have 0 resources to help you on that homework.

You're expected to be able to apply complex AI algorithms with no other resources than a 2 minute skit of him describing the general idea. It's laughable.

While Starner is admittedly intelligent, he has no clue how to educate. He will give you a multivariate GMM homework with his only "lesson" being about 2 minutes long on the topic. He expects you to already know many AI and ML-specific terms, despite this being an introductory AI class. TAs genuinely try to ignore your Ed discussion posts.
I don't know why everybody is upset! Hilarious guy, a great teacher, and has inspired me to wear Google Glass to school everyday.

Thad, what a guy. What to say, so many things. Homeworks are extremely hard. For lectures, only go if you're interested in knowing Thad's career, and how cool his Google glasses are! Make sure if you do take this class, Dr. Mark Riedl is teaching. Thad should go back to industry jobs because his idea of teaching is disgusting. He makes me sick.
meanie

I respect Professor Starner for his research and intelligence; however, as an instructor, Thad is woefully inadequate. He gives the bare minimum in terms of content, the rest is self-taught. This class is the grad class, even after promises of change. Due to the poor structure of this class, I will walk out of this class learning nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. He got awful grading for midterm exams and hilarious regrade requests. If you would like to suffer, I would suggest you take Thad's class. It is endless torture. Also, his grading is so funny that even if you get a score above 90 for an exam/assignment, you still might get a B for that exam/assignment.

Dear Thad is the worst professor I have ever had. He had invested so little to improve the student experience. For example, you have to wait for several days to finally get to the TA Office hour, where we can get 10 min to talk to the TA about our hundreds of lines of code. Thus, we usually get nothing done in these 10 minutes.

The course, the professor, and the TAs are a joke. There is no guidance or support, the lectures are borderline useless, and the TAs... well, they are awful at their jobs. They are utterly useless. They do not help, and don't have the students best interest in mind. This course needs an overhaul, from top to bottom.

He changed the style of teaching this semester and it was bad. The assignments for undergrads are the same as masters students and in addition to that he also implemented the AI plagiarism detectors which are not at all properly made. It just gives additional avoidable stress to everyone.

This is the best professor ever. He makes CS 3600, a notoriously difficult class, a piece of cake. If you hate him, you are just a lazy bum that will never work for google, attend MIT, or create the google glasses.

The assignents are mad difficult. That's fine. BUT WE NEED THE RESOURCES TO BE ABLE TO COMPLETE THE ASSIGNMENT. WE CANNOT DO THE ASSN BY OURSELVES. The office hours are incredibly useless. The TAs have never done the assignments themselves so they don't know what they're talking about half the time. Ed questions are never answered w detail.

starner is extremely rude and egotistical, the TAs are essentially comedians, autograding is garbo and not at all proportional to the work you did (ie. some obscure useless search algorithm explores 0.8 more nodes on average than their optimal reference implementation and u get a 6/11)

This class is not an undergrad class, so you are expected to do graduate-level work. Most grad students are taking 1 or 2 classes so they can balance the assignments while I'm having to neglect other classes. The prof doesn't do anything to acknowledge the unfairness of this and just mentions how this is applicable to Google interviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Useless lectures and the homework are ridiculously long and taken straight from a masters class. Avoid him at all cost.

Terrible class. He expects you to dedicate every living fiber of your soul to his class, which is SURPRISINGLY not possible! Believe it or not, I do not have 30+ hours to spend to even get a B on the assignments/class. Pray to every God you know that you dont get this professor, and wait until this class changes. This class is a grad class BTW.

Thad expects students to excel in a course where in lieu of teaching the material, he relies on either 1-minute module videos or lengthy, high-level papers. Students with a solid foundation in AI are rewarded with gift cards; undergraduates entering their first AI course are effectively on their own. Asymmetric workload for a 3-credit course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prepare to have no life outside of this class. Extremely long homework that takes 40-plus hours to somewhat complete.

Thad may be a great innovator, but is unfit to teach an undergrad class. Bad organization led to a 100+ drop in enrollment in his flipped classroom (though I do enjoy the style of work encouraged). He made the course unreasonable by using his grad curriculum. Inactive staff & Thad's lack of self-awareness make this one of the worst courses at Tech.

Starner has a god complex and expects everyone to be one the level that he thinks he is. Flipped classroom setting is abysmal and modules barely cover topics (zero mention of implementation), but homework requires deep knowledge (and 30 hours a week). Textbook hides information across hundreds of pages. Im getting slapped with my own tuition money

If I'm gonna go to a class at 8pm I better learn. I'm not trynna be in a cesspool of nerds that did too many Rubik's in highschool on a wednesday night. Some people have real lives, unlike some of the "billionare grindset" ppl in the comments

I am taking this class for my minor. It is absurd that I'm expected to be at the 1000% dedication level to a singular class as try-hard CS majors and MSCS students. Great class no doubt, if you have the time and masochistic tendencies needed to endure it (I wish I did, truly). But I, along with around ~500 other people, did not sign up for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Unreasonable workload for intro course. In addition, taking points off for one single extra node explored for one test-case sucks.

I have the good fortune of having lots of practice with coding in general, and even then, project 1 took forever to complete. I can imagine the pain for someon taking this their second semester without a CS foundation.

from an undergrad pov who has no experience whatsoever in the field of AI, this class so far has been outrageous, to say the least. spent crazy hours over the first hw with absolutely no help whatsoever (office hours system is a joke, no one replies on ED) and i have just been able to complete 30% after spending nearly 2 whole days.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoy this class. I can see why the undergrads may be disgruntled due to workload, but as someone coming into a MSCS with a non-CS degree/minimal coding experience, the course has been great. Dr. Starner's teaching method works really well if you're prepared and have an introductory level understanding of the material before each lecture.

Tbh, homeworks are as hard as GT should be. Thad Starner, however, is an awful teacher and the sole reason why students struggle. He gave us resources, but any useful info is scattered over hundreds of pages. A good teacher would not only provide resources, but explain/teach them. Starner makes 2-minute long comedy skits with no substance.

Professor Thad Starner is an amazing instructor! The combination of video lectures and interactive classroom sessions is an extremely good way of learning the material! The homework assignments are difficult, but fair, as they provide all the necessary resources to understand the concepts required to complete the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Driven, inspirational, willing to help. TA staff is a mix. Lots and lots of work, do not attempt if you have family/work obligations, easily 30-40 hours a week on weeks of heavy assignments and tests. average is ~20 per reviews but it can be uneven. not a lot of avenues for making up points lost in exams. Overall, rewarding, but expect workload

Professor Starner refuses to acknowledge that it is wrong to not tell students ahead of time that CS 3600 would be merged with CS 6601, a grad course for AI.

Homework 1 is extremely long and the resources the professor gives are not helpful. He fails to understand that students cannot dedicate the time of a part-time job to one 3 credit class.

Worst course ever had ! ! ! Online office hour sucks ! ! ! Either the TA never shows up or you waited hours until the meeting was over and it still wasn't your turn. They teach you really easy concepts but expect you to figure out/ invent those insanely difficult algorithms on your own without accessing any external resources

This class is insane. The 'modules' trace through basic and easy examples of search algorithms (A*, UCS, BFS, etc) and then the homework assignments expect you to code bi-directional and tri-directional versions of those algorithms with no pseudocode or class slides. The only resource is the textbook which is incomplete. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of work on the assignment 1 (30+ hours), still failing. Professor seems to be able to shift his method of teaching but the pace is too slow. The workload is the same as the masters program while this is labeled as an undergraduate course. The amount of time required is not equivalent to the # of credits. I remain hopeful for change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: TAs are laughably unhelpful or incompetent. Starner doesn't teach, you have to self learn the content yourself. Expect little to no help from them

This is one of the worst classes I have ever seen, the professor thinks that everyone has the knowledge he learned as a PhD student and in industry for many years, he is rude to students that seek help. He does not teach and yet has insane homework assignments and has said he expects it to take us over 8 hr for midterms.
Does not teach and has very long home works expert to spend over 20 hr per home work. Limited TA help and no external resources, has a god complex
Unclear expectations on homework for undergrads, extremely difficult to find any help at all (either office hours or prof himself). Homeworks are unreasonably difficult to complete
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom is inherently stupid for multiple reasons, mainly being that you're using auxiliary materials to study. Also, if you want help with HW, office hours exist, the 8-9:15 thing is useless. Also why would you combine undergrad with grad classes? That's obviously a recipe for disaster
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was really cool how he has us do Tri-Directional Search.  At first, I thought it would be tough, but after looking at the problem again, the solution was clear. Took about an hour and thats all we had to do for a full 2 weeks. Plus, Thad gave me a Moes giftcard.

Possibly the hardest class I have taken with a terrible professor. He doesn't explain what is to be done and expects work far beyond an undergraduate level. In fact, GT has combined this with 6601 or the graduate AI course. Please reorganize this course or don't have him teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: While there is very little support in this course, I appreciate the concept Thad is attempting. The bottom line is that the Intelligence thread should be tough and competitive--if it wasn't the skill would no be valuable. Mastering AI now will pay dividends in job prospects later. That said, I feel bad for any cs-minors in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No resources to help whatsoever. No lectures. Tough scenes
Y'all wild for this lol the class is fine and the assignments aren't that bad.

I understand and appreciate his approach of the flipped classroom and trying to get a wider audience to engage with the material, but the execution is abysmal. This structure does not work for a class that is (a) very large (500+ students) and (b) combined grad/undergrad. Fix the assignments, fix the format, and get it together.

Where to begin? No lectures, you'll have to read the textbook to learn everything. The assignments are insanely difficult, expect to spend 40+ hours per assignment (assignments are due 2 weeks after the release date). This course is the embodiment of everything wrong with OMSCS. Yeah, also grad and undergrad students are lumped together. Go figure.

Clearly, the only 5-star review below is complete cap and is obviously written by Starner. This class is actually the graduate section 6601. The course is obviously just a copy and paste from the grad class and the difficulty has not been lowered for undergrad. Have fun with this as the homework are impossible, and it is a flipped classroom!!!!!!!!

This professor really cares about the success of his students and makes lectures very entertaining and engaging. I am able to learn a lot through the online modules and class textbook, and the homework assignments are challenging :)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is impossibly difficult and we are combined with the graduate level section. Little to no resources available and the class is 100% taught by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: With a flipped lecture model, the class has become a total nightmare. There are over 900 students in the class so office hours are a complete joke when it comes to receiving help, and the first homework itself is insanely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is hell on earth. Complete chaos. Grad and undergrad classes are combined (CS6601). Lectures are completely useless especially since it's in flipped classroom format. All the learning is done by yourself reading through the textbook. The homeworks are literally impossible and take like 40 hours each. AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Actually the worst class I have ever taken. Have spent endless hours in this class and am still behind according to where he says we should be at. The course completely changed from previous years with no warning. Dont take Starners classes at all, ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class has been rebranded into CS 6601. You have the same exact lectures and assignments as OMSCS. It has graduate-level assignments and expectations, yet is only a 3000-level undergraduate class. To get a 100 on an assignment you are expected to do research on the topic by yourself yet there is a STRICT plagiarism policy.

The lectures aren't even lectures so we basically have to rely on a gibberish textbook  and 1 min video modules that teach AI using pen and paper like wut. FIRST HW is taking ppl 20+ hours. we get 2 weeks to do it, but 20+ hours is ridiculous when you have other tough courses plus extracurriculars plus daily life stuff you're trying to balance.
I'm a CS minor and I spent about 15 hours doing the first few warm-up tasks. All the people I know in this class suffer a lot and we're not learning. Horribly-designed, don't take
Don't take his class

changed to "flipped format" AKA he shows some laughable animations in class and you teach the whole course (the content is not trivial by any means) TO YOURSELF. Nothing is taught, and the (grad section) homeworks are unnecessarily annoying (work with annoying apis/tests, implement obscure algorithms without any references online). Horrible, garb

Great lecturer. Class structure was not well defined at times (received deadlines last minute) and exam questions were sometimes questionable (may be determined by TAs though). Only a midterm and final exam, both open internet (VERY strict anti-cheating policy). Great professor overall, recommend taking it if you have the chance.

Thad really likes what he does; you will definitely understand and appreciate that in his classes (Especially if it's Mob. & Ubi. computing). The class I was in was a bit chaotic, and the exercises would sometimes take time outside of class. The group project WILL be tough if you don't start on time but should be fine otherwise. Tests were random.

Professor's lack of trust in students makes it hard to learn and feel supported. All assignments are auto-graded and when things fail it is very frustrating and feels impossible to try to figure out what went wrong and learn from it. TA hours were very unhelpful and often sent me on a wild goose chase when in reality it was a small unrelated error.
Really cares about his courses. Material excellent but a lot of work.

Class is interesting and Thad is good guy.  He will you out.  All the projects are in LISP and are very time consuming.  If you aren't experienced in LISP, you sure will be.  Tests are long and difficult but open book/note.  You will have a rock-solid grasp on the fundamentals of AI after this course.
No Comments
AI class: interesting
Thad's awesome.

Taking this class online is maybe not the move but it's really not that hard. Tests are open note and fairly straightforward. Only big complaint is the occasional assignments seem impossible to do completely right. I'm getting fractions of a point off for trivial mistakes that I'd still get credit for on a test. Not demanding, but don't sleep on it
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was really great! Good lectures and exams that I was able to do well on. He is also super nice and really wants you to succeed!

Very bad professor. Doesn't seem to care for student success. Not helpful at all outside of the classroom. Exams are moderately tough for no reason. When asked how to prepare for the exam his answer was "I don't know."  Avoid taking his class.

He's not accessible after class, he doesn't respond to emails. He's not considerate of students or their lives. Don't think he's helped in anything outside of going through lectures and not giving feedback on any assignments or exams. Don't listen to any of the good comments about him.

No rubrics for anything. He is assigning a final exam that he says is designed for not everyone to be able to finish in time. The feedback he gives on checkpoints is never anything of substance, so I'm aimlessly walking into my final project. Also, groups are randomly assigned so you end up with group members who do absolutely nothing.

I do not recommend taking this class online. There were very few assignments to get your grade up. There was one quiz that the class did well on, but the professor ended up taking it off due to the questions "being wrong." There was not nearly enough information in the lecture videos and it was hard to know what to study for the exams.
One of my favorite profs at scheller. Cares a lot about his students and knows a lot about what he is teaching. Has very clear expectations for how to get an A. Can't go wrong with Tim!

Do not take this class online. The video lectures do not give enough information and are very vague. There is not enough time for the exams or quizzes. When reaching out, it can take around 3 days to receive a response. He does not give enough resources for you to succeed in course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course was very focused on cases and news, but lectures are necessary to achieve a good grade as he might ask during exams/class quizzes for details of something he or a guest speaker said during lectures. Overall, the class wasn't too difficult for my European standards.

Good experience overall. His class is pretty easy if you pay attention and take notes during lectures. He's quite knowledgeable and knows what he's teaching. Tests were a little confusing at times. You should get an easy A if you attend all lectures, pay attention and do all the activities.

This professor was alright. The class was pretty average, no text book needed. What I didn't like were the tests, some of the questions were vague and I couldn't ask about them since the tests were honorlocked online. Also I have struggled to finish some of the tests confidently due to the time constraint.

Easy prof and great lecturer. Taught three sections of this class three different ways as a part of his research for his PhD, mine had a semester long group business plan that we had a lot of class to work on. Not much outside work aside from the flipped classroom setup where we had to watch lectures before class. Sassy at times but great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to show up for class and come for his spontaneous in class assignments. But, they're not very hard and the material is fairly light. He gives REALLY good lectures though that teach you a lot. Everything is simple and easy to understand, and yet the information is so valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There are no tests other than a final and a random pop midterm that may or may not count. He doesn't really give feedback on most assignments. He teaches in a flipped classroom style so actual class time is mainly just working on different assignments within your groups that he assigns at the beginning of the semester.

Professor Martin's class has very clear expectations. He tells you exactly what he wants on every assignment and is a totally fair grader. He is possibly the nicest professor I have ever had and is super accessible outside of class. Great person to talk to for advice outside of class as he has a lot of knowledge on non-academic related items.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hands down my favorite professor at GT. So accessible to students. Helpful. Gives great feedback. Helps on homeworks. Answers questions without making you feel dumb. Cares about his students and their grades. His lectures drag slightly as he's a little monotone but the material is pretty easy. Tests are a little tricky. Worth it though. Take him!

I took Professor Martin for Operations Management during Fall 2020, meaning our class was online (asynchronous) due to COVID. All assignments (including tests) were open note. His lectures were engaging, and the class was fairly easy. Would definitely recommend taking Professor Martin!

This class was super easy. He teaches the material and you learn. He said the textbook was optional but you needed it for an A. I did not need the book. If you take him online make sure to do the equations first then the multiple choice so you don't run out of time. Answers questions with awesome explanations! Definitely take him if you can!

Great professor. Sometimes, especially towards the middle of the year, his lectures drag a little. Generally makes lectures interesting and engaging. I've taken him twice, once for supply chain modeling and once for operations management. They feel like basically the same class besides SCM having more case studies. Would take him again if I could!
Very interesting and really tries to engage the class in either discussions or fun class activities! Tests were a bit tough in my opinion but he'll take your participation in the class into account.

Take ops with Martin! He's a super nice + charming guy, and he makes ops pretty engaging; operations is not at all my concentration or area of interest but I never felt bored by his lectures. Course is fairly balanced between exams, quizzes, + assignments. Can take minimal notes in class + just review his slides (that he posts) to study for exams.

Very good professor if you are already interested in history. Has an excellent level of knowledge on the subject, and does well at creating an environment where students are encouraged to participate. Field trips are also a fun time, alongside movie nights. Overall a great prof for a great class.

This has been one of my favorite classes I've taken so far, much of that has to do with how much thought and effort Professor Stoneman has put into this class. He is constantly asking for feedback and very mindful of his students. The reading is important, but if you put the effort in its more than worth it. He creates a great learning environment.
Overall great guy. Was very accommodating to students needs. Cared about the class and students learning. If you try, you'll have a great experience.

Took HTS2037 at GTE. Dr Stoneman believes in discussions rather than lectures, so class involves a lot of participation as well as long readings before each class. Had a great experience, classes were always entertaining, and multiple field trips and out-of-class activities were enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ignore the class tag, there was no option for this class. I took his HTS 2037 Europe at War + Peace while at GTE. Professor Stoneman is very caring, and wants to make sure we enjoy our experience about learning about Europe. He didn't give us exams or quizzes, which was nice. The best part was going on field trips! Take this class while abroad. :)

Ok class, just lots of work/assignments and complicated grading system. Lectures are mid. Tests are hard but the busy work will carry your grade. Attendance is basically mandatory bc of reading quizzes, in class assignments, discussion posts, etc. If you go to class and do the work you'll be fine. There are much easier ethics/social science at GTE.

even if you attend class and don't participate in the discussion, your grade will be fine, which is kinda unfair for the students who actually go and take part in the class discussions. all in all, the trips we took as part of the class were pretty fun and cool to go on!

Took this class at GTL and really liked the professor in the beginning until he refused to grade assignments. My grade dropped 8 points in the last 2 weeks when he actually put in grades. Very passionate, but super unorganized. Easy class but lots of busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Stoneman is very sincere and honest with students. The midterm was probably more difficult than it needed, but still manageable. He did take the entire semester to grade everything, so we were unsure of how tough of a grader he would be, but it turned out fine - I think most people got As - and he gave extra credit for taking so much time.

He's not as bad as I had heard before taking the class. I took his class at GTL and overall, it wasn't ridiculously hard, but the 1 test you have is harder than you think it will be, so go to the review session. It's definitely harder than it needs to be, but overall the easiest class I took at GTL (I took thermo and def bods).

Wish I was more attentive in class, lost a chance to learn really cool stuff. Organised 2 field trips where committed students didn't show. Very caring (offered make-up test when students missed morning Monday class due to train delays, taken at GTL). Gave full outline of tests & exam review was 20 essay Qs where 3 would appear on exam. Great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but extremely unorganized. Assignments never released on time. Consistently late in field trips. Very unclear grading criteria. Grades assigned seemingly at random, and he grades pretty harshly given his level of organization. Really boring lectures and discussions. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I wouldn't take him again because this class was considered an elective for me while at GTL and I got a B--it was harder than I anticipated mostly because his tests are very difficult and grading is somewhat subjective. His class is pretty boring and he discourages laptop use. Still, he was a very nice guy and always acted respectfully towards us.

Dr. Stoneman cares about the topics he lectures on. Grading was not very straight forward and highly arbitrary both in the multi-choice portion of exams and in the essays. Everyone I knew got between a 80 and 95 on every assignment in the course. Lectures were hit or miss based mainly on the topics of the course. There are many class discussions.

Stay clear, seriously! His class is the most boring and bizarre courses I've ever taken. The essays you write for his tests require such specific responses to always confusing prompts that for one test 1/4 of the class got a whole letter grade off as they didn't respond to a question correctly. Joke of a class, if you want A choose something else.

Dr. S is a great prof. He gives you notes which basically outline everything you need to know for the course, and his lectures incorporate a variety of activities which make for a very enjoyable and interesting experience. He's a bit nitpicky on his essay questions on exams, but on the whole it's not a difficult class. He's a pretty nice guy too.

He makes the class be "all about him". He does not care much for students' needs, and takes his time in field trips to do what he wants to do. His lectures are pretty much just spoken, and his feedback is not at all useful.

Dr. S ranks as one of the worst professors I've had in my collegiate career. The readings assigned are interesting and fun, but this quickly disintegrates as his lectures (and tests) are dominated by nothing but his opinions. Prepare for a class on Dr. S's opinions and ludicrous conjectures, and be ready visually identify cathedrals!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Stoneman gives verbal lectures, so if you are a visual or tactile learner, you must take extensive notes. He writes very little down, as is his teaching philosophy. He is not relaible in showing up to student meetings on time or at all. He changes schedules on a whim. He is extremely vague in his project assignment prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are very easy and he grades generously on the test essays and final project, as long as you put in the work.  There were lots of readings to do, but there were no quizzes or anything. He can be a bit vague with the finer details of his material, but the class is more about showing him you understand the concepts and put in the work. Easy A.
Very boring. Hard class. Way too much effort for a history course. Definitely least favorite course I have ever taken. Avoid at all costs
Definitely avoid

This is one of the hardest classes I've taken, but the professor was very helpful. He explains concepts clearly and has a great sense of humor. Lectures are informative, though it can be hard to keep up with notes since laptops aren't allowed. Because the material builds quickly, it's easy to fall behind, but he provides many resources to catch up.

He's got a great sense of humor, explains things well, and you can tell he really cares. Lectures were informative and entertaining, but often difficult to keep up with when taking notes since he disallowed laptops. It's easy to fall behind or get lost, since everything builds off what's before it, but he gives enough resources to catch up easily.

Loved Conte's lectures. Definitely a hit-or-miss depending on personal preference, but I thought his lectures were fairly straight forward and in logical order. As long as you paid attention in lecture, there wasn't really a need to open the textbook. Projects, homework, and quizzes were clear and reasonable. Would recommend 10/10.

Lectures weren't very useful and made the content seem confusing. Labs simplified material and were very useful. I did not pay attention during any lecture (had to attend because there was geo-fenced PointSolutions) and understood everything through lab and the textbook. 45% of grade is auto-graded projects, only 4 quizzes 5% each and 20% final.

This is the hardest course I have ever taken. Not a big deal, as I learned a ton and the subject was interesting. However, I found Dr. Conte to be unnecessarily mean. His style of "humor" of making fun of people and trying to bust people for cheating wasn't fun. I attended every lecture, but learned almost everything from the TAs and the slides.
Great professor, knows his stuff and is very effective at instilling his passion to his students! Great experience and would recommend people to take computer arch with him.

Prof Conte is a great guy who gives very enjoyable lectures. The projects, especially if you don't have a great background in architecture, are really hard. They are also graded in an interesting way, where you basically get a 65% credit by default, but to earn the rest of the points you need to get the project 100% correctly implemented.

Enjoyable, easy-to-follow lectures. Projects were a solid introduction to C and were good preparation for future systems coursework. And quite an understanding fella – he once allowed a student to make up a final exam he missed because he was in jail.

Prof.Conte is the best prof I've had at GT. The course content seemed difficult at first but his instructions made it clear and easy to follow. His OH is also helpful if you have questions regarding lectures and homework assignments. Projects are individual but if you start early you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Conte is the absolute greatest. Anyone who is saying otherwise must've had a bad experience with the class and not the professor. He has very interesting and high quality lectures and I adored attending lecture.

Knowledgeable but lecture is very loosely tied to class assignments. Uploads unreadable scratch work for notes but is in possession of digital slides from prev sems (???). Self-taught myself with textbook and Lab/TAs (godsends). 50% of grade autograded prjs, make sure to get all points. Understand hw & prjs, quizzes will be light and youll get an A

Conte clearly has a lot of experience in the topics that he teaches. However, the class can become quite drab at times. 50 percent of the grades are autograded projects, so as long as you do good on those (and don't get caught cheating), you will get a good grade. TA office hours are a life saver.

Conte is not a great lecturer - I personally find him very dramatic in the way he talks and when he got to the C part of the course he coded everything in vim instead of an IDE. I only care about this because the amount of time he spent compiling to find errors and then search to fix them was annoying. He was a pretty average professor.

Conte is an extremely knowledgeable professor. His lectures help you learn the content, and the homework and projects solidify your knowledge. HPCA is a wonderful course; lots of work, but extremely rewarding, and you will learn a ton.

Conte is a great professor and his extensive knowledge of the content is clear from day 1. You will learn a ton but a lot is expected as well. I spent well over 30 hours each for project 1 and 2, while project 3 seemed quickly put together and only took around 5 hours. Exams can be tricky, so make sure you do well on HWs and projects if you want A.

Lectures fairly well, but easy to get lost. Biweekly labs (recitations run by TAs), office hours, and projects are what made me learn. 50% of the grade was projects (which were very doable and autograded with unlimited submissions; should be 100s if you put in the work). The 5 quizzes were hard but only make up 20% of the grade. No timed labs.

Dr. Conte is a great professor and lecturer. The structure of the course is well-designed. Five auto-graded projects made up 50% of the grade, and it is not too hard to get a 100 as long as you don't wait until the last second to start on them. Quizzes and exams can be difficult, and require a very deep understanding of the material.

Good professor for CS 2110, made a well-structured class that prioritized projects as learning opportunities. Engaging lecturer. Note that lab sections (basically studio tho, not really "lab") were mandatory, not lecture itself.

Great professor overall. The content is already interesting but he made attending the class fun and enjoyable. Overall highly recommend for advanced computer architecture. I found the project to be super interesting and helped me to understand the material. One note when it comes to project 3 (Tomasulo and superscalar simulation) start early lol

Incredible professor. Their teaching style is anti-technology, but once you get the hang of it it's really not that bad. While they didn't grade for attendance there is no recordings (lecture notes were posted, though) so you are heavily incentivized to attend lecture. Attending Conte's lecture was worth it though. A very enthusiastic and funny guy

Conte's an entertaining lecturer and comes across as pretty nice. The only frustrating thing about his class is that he lectures kinda slowly. On the worst days in the beginning-middle of the semester he could spend near half the class answering questions. Personally, I wished he'd cover more content, but I get why he needs to answer questions.

This class felt really fair. If you wanted an A, it was pretty achievable. The almost weekly homework wasn't bad, and it was based on content in the textbook. The exams were not hard if you actually understood the content. I think this class depends on the TA team and I relied on them. The head TA Jason at the time was super useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. Class material and projects are very difficult, getting a good grade is not easy in this class. But trust me you will find it beneficial for the rest of life. It's been 2 years after took professor Conte's class and I still find the class projects very valuable whenever I need reference for computer architecture.

Lectures are very interesting, and grading breakdown is in your favor. Basically 50% of the final grade is completely autograded with unlimited submissions, but the in-person demos can get you if you didn't understand what you were doing. Tests are moderate, homeworks are a little rough, but all-in-all, probably your best choice.

He has in-depth knowledge about the class. The TAs are the one who save your grade. Attend the recitation, since Dr. Conte tends to teach topics not necessary for the course. He is funny, understanding, and helpful. Head TA Jason was amazing. The projects require time, but very interesting.

I loved Conte's section - the grading scale was 50% projects, which are doable if you start early! The projects solidified my understanding of the material as well. Halfway through the semesters the lectures were disorganized, but HW, projects, textbook, & recitation are all you need!

Conte is a great professor and really knows his stuff. 2110 is historically a difficult course, but it is mainly the subject matter, not the professor. Also, his version of the class is easier than the Southern section in my opinion. His lectures are good most of the time, and the projects, tests, and exams are balanced. The TAs are amazing too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Conte is the best professor I have ever had. He is an incredible lecturer, and he makes CS funny. Every Tuesday/Thursday I was excited to go to his lecture. This class made me understand why I pay money for college. I will never forget the Lecture on John Van Neuman. It was mind blowing and it changed my way of thinking.

Conte is awesome. Workload is much more manageable than Southerns section. I found that his class focused more on the lower level computer stuff and hardware, and less coding than Southerns, but both end up teaching the same stuff. His grading scheme is quite generous, with projects making up the bulk of your grade (projects have autograders).

Dr. Conte's class was great. I had heard that 2110 was the "first hard class" for cs, but it wasn't that bad. Projects (with demos) make up the bulk of your grade, and the autograder is provided. Tests were easy and only make up 35% of the grade total (10% for exam 1 and 2, 15% for final). Conte's lectures are funny and engaging.

Really good class. Everyone knows 2110 is super difficult but his format (5 projects, 11 homeworks, no lab quizzes, 2 tests, 1 final) allows for way less stress than other sections. Projects are do-able but will probably need TA support and make up for majority of grade. Tests are light work, study lab guides. Lab recitations are really helpful.
Dr. Conte is one of my most favourite professors at Tech. His lectures are engaging and homeworks help to understand concepts. Totally recommend him.

Dr. Conte is a real gem of a lecturer in the college of computing. Consider yourself extremely lucky to have him as a prof for 2110. The class is mostly project-based, but the course covers a ton of material. Conte himself is extremely witty, knowledgeable, and funny. Don't hesitate, he makes a hard course fun.

Electrons live in the ground! :)
Dr. Conte is an outstanding profesor. His lectures are fun and informative. Tests are fair, and projects are well-explained. TAs are very supportive and approachable.

I loved CS 2110 because of Conte! He's funny and I went in person just for his class. The class is much less stressful than Southern's imo, which I think made me like the subject even more. The projects were really fun and you have 2 weeks to do them and there's so many resources that give students breathing space considering this is a 4 cred class

2110 is a hard course, but I feel with Conte, if you follow his guidelines, it is easily doable. He has a pretty generous grading scheme with 50% being projects, and half of that being demos for projects, and the other half being code with auto graders. His lectures are clear, concise, and entertaining. Solid professor for a hard class.

Conte is the best professor I've had at Georgia Tech. He has a lot of material to cover for 2110 but he makes sure to follow his syllabus and covers everything effectively. Easy to understand as long as you pay attention in lecture. Just make sure you don't miss a lecture or it might be hard to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Conte was a solid professor. His lectures were decently informative, and if you attend those plus recitation and review material with the textbook, an A is very achievable. There are a decent number of projects and homeworks, and a few exams were hard, but nothing unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The projects were challenging but fulfilling once you figured it out. Start on the first day that they get released so you can ask ta questions. There were some errors in the projects and malloc was hard in the final project but overall I liked them. The only thing I didnt like was that Conte wrote the tests and was a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is very difficult, but if you like the subject material, very rewarding. He's one of the best lecturers in the school, but he's a bit of a hard ass when it comes to grading. The projects are very difficult, be prepared to work very hard, but also be prepared to learn a lot. Not an easy A at all, but one of the most rewarding A's.
He knows how the university evaluates a class. He knows weak points of a student. He knows how to secure a job.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Other class 9 credit <<<<<<<<< This class 3 credit The projects are extremely difficult, among the most difficult I've ever done. Notes and lectures aren't helpful. Do yourself a favor: take this class with another professor.
Recommend to take another prof.

CS 2110 is not an easy class, but Conte is a great lecturer and makes the material not only interesting, but understandable. Projects were difficult, and got more so as the semester went on, but as long as you get started early it isn't too bad. Lecture and office hours were more than enough to complete the work at hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very smart professor, he can answer any question you throw at him. He also relates lessons in class to the industry which was cool. You gotta show up for lecture because if you miss you will fall behind and he does not slow down; however, if you show up the class should be easy.
Don't take from him. He claims he is a fair grader and never actually listen to student's request. Lowest grade statistic among all professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ignore questions during class. Piazza is a place for TA's unjustified answers, never trust 100%. Requesting assistance? -> He will guide you to contact the office of division, while the office of division tosses to the professor again.
Well... Tenured professor with giving lowest gpa among the course. Low accessibility.

Dr. Conte is a fantastic lecturer and professor. However, the course was completely unorganized with assignments, parts of projects, grades, and missing details being released way too late. However, these things were out of Dr. Conte's control.
Don't take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He only the one that claims he has a reputation as a fair grader. Only worse course professor that I took in GT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Also took during COVID. Conte is not a bad man, okay. He doesn't do malicious things and wants you to succeed. My main issue with his teaching is that he doesn't prepare lecture notes, at least not often. The guy is super smart which is great, and there probably isn't a question you can ask him he can't answer, but his lectures are improvised.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took class online during COVID. His lectures were detailed & interesting, and he's always eager to answer questions. He's enthusiastic and knows the material well, but sometimes he doesn't explain things great because it's so simple to him. Class took a lot of effort (especially projects/homeworks) and quizzes were hard, but an A is attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Conte is a good choice for 2110. His class is structured around projects rather than timed labs like the other sections. Projects aren't too bad, and they carry your overall grade. He's a good lecturer but going to lab is the best way to prepare for exams.

He's a pretty solid professor. I took his CS2110 class online (during the mostly online fall semester), so the class might not be all the same going onward. The class was mostly project and homework based, which is cool. I also got in the ungraded untimed lab section which was great. If you do choose this class, please go to lab and lecture.
Wonderful professor. One of the best I have ever had on campus. Don't miss lecture though as it will get you behind and that will make it hard to catch up!

Conte is a great person and great professor. He along with the TAs made this class quite easy. Overall this did feel much easier than 1332 and I wasn't worried about the grade at all. This was an experimental section so timing of projects is something they need to work on. Tests were easy and short for 75 min.

Very good professor. Homeworks and projects can be a bit of work, but never too difficult. Tests are easy. My only gripe is that Conte is too nice and answers every single question students have, which really slows down the class. Does not allow electronics, but lectures are decently interesting.

Conte is a pretty good professor, but 2110 is just a super hard class at GT. The tests are tough, but the projects weren't too bad. He is a good lecturer, but can sometimes come across a bit condescending to students.

The material is dense, advanced, and complicated. The projects are extremely difficult, among the most difficult I've ever done, and there's a strict no collaboration policy. Notes and lectures aren't helpful. The tests are average in difficulty. Do yourself a favor: take this class with another professor.

As he will tell you within the first week or so, Conte is "tough, but fair". My experience has mirrored that exactly. He is an insanely good lecturer, and also goes out of his way to make himself available for consultation to clear anything up. His projects are very time consuming, and difficult. His class is tough, but doable.
Great professor Did an excellent job of explaining topics to students. Everything learned in one class tied in really well with the next class. Skipping class will really mess you up though...
Interesting, enthusiastic, and brilliant!

This class is hard but he made it easier. I started off not so great but was able to save it with the make up and the final exam. The test were very similar to the practice exams he would do the week of the exam.
Professor Wee is really good at explaining his subject. Also, he makes his exams so that if you've been doing both the homework and the review sheets he makes, you should be all set for his tests.

Professor Wee is extremely qualified and passionate, and cares about his students' success. However, this was a very difficult course: the breadth and depth of concepts covered was well beyond what I expected. I thought Professor Wee was great, but would recommend avoiding MATH 3670 in general if you have easier stats options available.
He was a really good professor with great lecture notes and really cared about his students. Would recommend

Very passionate about the content, with really well made and funny lectures that always connected the material to real world examples. 35% of the grade was homework, which could be quite challenging, but he held lots of office hours. Exams were never unreasonably difficult and were really well made. I would take Dr. Wee again for any course.
Took MATH 3670 with him but he was really funny and a great lecturer.

Professor Wee is the best! He is very caring and definitely wants his students to fully understand the content rather than memorizing it for the exam. He goes into great detail on problems during lectures, which is very helpful. He offers a lot of additional resources for students. He is always happy to answer any questions without any judgment.
Really good teacher. Lectures clutched up for me. Prepares you well.

Dr. Wee did his absolute best to help us understand. The class itself is just super hard and is not easy to teach in such a short amount of time. Super helpful during office hours. Tests were insane though and the averages were Cs to failing.
The class was hard, but Dr. Wee was a good professor and helpful in office hours.

Super sweet professor, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS for any doubts !! He is a great explainer, and will not judge you even for the smallest doubts. Do not fall back on this class and dont just rely on the final. Do better. He's a great supportive teacher, also ask doubts in class. He will remember you from class participation.
Great guy, extremely helpful and knows what he is talking about. Only downside is his handwriting is awful so its sometimes really hard to understand what he is writing. However, I would recommend.

Professor Wee saved my grade. This course was rough, and I didn't even need to take it for my major, lol (I found out too late). I literally failed the second midterm, so it was a rough comeback. Thanks to Professor Wee, I managed to barely get the A. He is also one of the only teachers still doing in-person office hours, which I really appreciate.

Dr. Wee is a great professor! You should def attend lectures as he goes over important practice problems that are somewhat challenging. The content of the course isn't super hard to understand, but putting in work outside of class is a must to do well. If you can register for his class, then you're in good hands for passing the class with an A.

He is a very kind professor and really cares. The structure of the class is not really up to his decision, since he isn't the person over all of the 1552 classes, but works well with the structure he was given. He does allow you to use your iPad, computer, or whatever technology you use for notes. Optional final (like all 1552 classes)
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wee is a super nice guy and very easy to access outside of class. He responds to email really fast even on weekends. I did have a bit of trouble understanding him at times and found lectures in general boring. Definitely try to avoid the morning class. Participation is part of your grade

Dr. Wee is my g. His lectures are straightforward, though he does use technical terms and moves briskly, so make sure you are focused or else you may miss content. He is always attentive to students who have questions and will clarify if you ask him. One thing to note is that he has a thick-ish accent, but I could still completely understand him.

Expects that you prepare for rehearsal but understands that everyone is busy with other work as well. Very reasonable as a conductor - not sure why there are so many negative reviews claiming otherwise...
Very nice, caring, and funny music director who programs a lot of cool music. Rehearsals are mandatory but she is very understanding if you talk to her.

Absolutely horrible person who has absolutely no dignity and zero respect for anyone. Extremely rude and condescending and does not hold back in insulting others in petty and rude ways. Do not take orchestra or any of her classes.
Her ego is bigger than Shaq
Dr. Ting is a solid teacher. She requires students to show up to classes and rehearsals, but most importantly, she chooses good repertoire for the orchestra.

Symphony Orchestra is a great option if you are a musician at Tech. Dr. Ting is funny and witty and the music selection is wonderful. She's really understanding and lets you skip rehearsal for academic/personal reasons if needed. The class is fun and a good stress-reliever from academics.

Dr. Ting is so nice! Symphony Orchestra is a 1 credit hour class and very fun. Dr. Ting is engaging and the music we play is great. She expects you to learn it really fast though. Also, you have to audition to get in. You're allowed to miss a few classes without penalty. Don't be on your phone during class and you'll be set for an easy A!

If you expect your students to attend class and be on time, the professor should hold himself to those standards. He was late almost every class and took about 20 minutes each class (not exaggerating) to set up his ipad and talk about off topic things. I got an A in physics 2, but had to withdraw from this class.  Please be on time to teach.

One of the best profs I've ever had at Tech. Dynamics is hard, but he's put A LOT of work into giving you all the resources you need to succeed. The class is very organized imo; he has loads of review problems, class notes, and office hours are always helpful (he gives free snacks 😎). He's lenient on due dates and super understanding.

Graded on 5 projects, first 2 were with a partner which made it a lot less overwhelming. Office hours were a great resource for anything relating to the project. Every single project got extended which was nice, but good luck trying to contact him outside of class. Super nice guy, lectures were just inherently boring but he tried his best
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I have ever had!  He is really nice and makes classes pretty entertaining. His grading criteria is this pass or fail thing which is honestly pretty forgiving but damn it stressed me out. Like every exam question is essentially a letter grade in weight but he lets you redo one per test.  Super hard to reach very busy guy.

Dynamics is a really hard class, but he did his best to make it digestible in his lectures. Did not grade on percentages, instead does pass/fail on worksheets and test problems. Need to pass 9/10 test problems and 23/25 homework problems for an A. Lets you resubmit worksheets and retake one problem per test. Overall fantastic professor.

Although the worksheets (weekly homework) and tests were graded on a pass-fail system, where you needed to pass 9 exam problems to get an A in the class, which was very stressful, he explained things in a very straightforward, yet exciting and engaging way. Amazing professor, definitely recommend for dynamics, would take again. 9/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor, probably the best lecturer I've ever had. Definitely take for 2202. However, he is incredibly hard to reach, busy man.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Torello was the GOAT when it came to teaching, super great lecturer. That being said, the grading is really tough (3 midterms with three questions each). To get an A you need to pass all 9 (incredibly stressful). He also took forever to grade things. It was a week before Thanksgiving, and I was unsure whether I was even going to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything is graded as pass-fail, and there are 3 tests with 3 problems each and you need to pass 9 to get an A. I got a fail when another student that made the same mistakes got a pass, and he yelled at me for asking about it. At the end of the course (Spring 2024), he said he didn't teach the course well that year and just laughed about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's really nice, willing to meet to help you and give extensions. The projects are really hard and the whole grade is determined by only a few projects. If you start early and get help the class isn't too bad but if you procrastinate you're screwed.
Good teacher, better man. Torello will prepare you for real life problems you may face in the workplace or your personal life.

Went in fearing Dynamics and came out grudgingly admitting I liked it. He's THAT prof: has clear lectures breaking down intimidating material, has infectious enthusiasm, builds community, has unhinged idgaf humor, deeply cares about each student. Dynamics is HARD, but his grading criteria makes it very possible to do well & is oddly forgiving.

Engaging, super nice, passionate about the subject, focused in class, and gives ample reattempts / retakes for homework and test problems. Is totally willing to give extensions on work if you request. Awesome prof! However, he is a super busy guy, is difficult to reach at times.

He's a pretty good lecturer but outside of that he's bad. Grades with super specific criteria which he won't tell you, so it's really hard to get high grades even on HW. He also takes weeks to get anything graded, and sometimes just won't respond to emails. Also he's like insanely millenial. To a worrying degree.
Funny guy with engaging lectures. His lectures and practice exams follow well with the tests. He is a bit self indulgent sometimes but overall a very enjoyable class

Every class Dr. Torello was soaked into the lecture and genuinely cared about his students. However, his grading criteria makes tests worth all of your grade and his 'specification system' makes them very stressful. Additionally, it was very hard to consistently reach him on teams.

Torello is very passionate about what he teaches. He wants the students to understand the material and takes lots of feedback. He is very understanding and you can fail 3/10 modules (3 modules per midterm + a project) on the first try and still get an A. Definitely go to lecture because he talks through how to solve problems very well.

Personality-wise, Torello is my favorite professor I have ever had. He is funny, genuine, relatable, and kind to his students. However, this class is really hard. He gives great lectures and you can not miss them because the worksheet assignments are also difficult and he can help guide you through them in class. Final was not mandatory thankfully.

Dont even think about slacking off in this class. You sold your soul to GT, you have no more free time. Dont fall behind even 2 days in this class. Recovery is almost impossible. Torello is a decent prof, not very accessible outside class. Shell tutor cant help on his HW's. In other words if you need external help, dont take this class.

Semester isnt over, but time ticketscoming up. Torello is an okay guy but lack of help from TA's /Torello. You do get 2hrs a week of in person office hrs with him. But as mentioned there will be a long que and only ~2 problems are covered in the entire 2hrs. Goodluck contacting him outside of class. You can make an A, just dont expect to be helped

OH is usually filled with at least a dozen people, so dont expect your specific questions to be answered. Torello is enthusiastic during lecture, overall a good prof but damn near impossible to reach outside of class or OH. Same goes for the TA's, only accessible during "lecture time" (flipped model class).

Dr. Torello is great! Dynamics is challenging, but he provides plenty of resources. Lectures aren't mandatory, but you should attend all of them. The tests are do-able if you dedicate enough time to studying, and the grading system is relatively forgiving. He is available outside of class- review sessions and office hours are very helpful.
Best professor at tech, and if your giving him a 1 you can jump off CULC.

Great Professor, hard class. Go to class, go to office hours and review sessions. 10 test problems makeup most of the class grade. Stuff I wish I knew: The beginning material is far easier than the later material and it will help you SO much if you do well on the first test. Final is optional but is easier because you have way more time on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Torello is the GOAT. Dynamics is a really tough course, but his class structure and amazing lectures really help make the content understandable and doable. Torello really cares about his student's success and wants everyone to do well. The only thing is his grading specs are a little tough and he's always behind on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Torello is a super interesting and fun guy. Very qualified as well as you can obviously tell. His classes are very engaging -- he tells lots of jokes and does lots of funny physical demonstrations (like throwing his poor pen and eraser around). He does have a relatively strict rubric on assignments, but you'll be fine if you do what he says.

One of the best professors I have had at Tech. He cares a lot about his students. It is a flipped classroom style with specification grading. Comments say grading is harsh, but its actually quite forgiving. By the end of all the chances you get, you should get it right, especially if you go to office hours. A must take for dynamics. A literal god
