reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: literally the best professor I have ever taken in my life. His assignment style and grading criteria is very unorthodox, yes. But I have never met a professor that A. cares for students as much as Torello and B. that explains difficult concepts better than Torello. If you are not taking him for Dynamics you are missing out.

Very caring and understanding professor. He struggles to get grades out on time, which really starts to add up by the end of the semester, but if you stay on top of your challenge problems and worksheets, you will do just fine. He has some kinks to work out in his class but would recommend him for his efforts to make the class as easy as possible.

Seems like a nice guy in person, but is really terrible from his actions. Gatech final instructional days mean no assessments or assignments due at any time after that day and ALL grades are given back to students on or before that day. BUT not Torello! He makes his own rules just to screw over his students! Take him and make your life miserable :)

Dr. Torello is an amazing professor, who cares about us and is WILLING to change the course structure to help students succeed. His worksheets and these challenge problems are not easy, but you can resubmit it based on feedback. Dynamics is hard, and stop blaming him for your incompetence.

The professor is very understanding and caring. However, the course structure is flipped classroom and the grading structure is something called 'specification grading', which makes it unnecessarily difficult. Basically it means homeworks and exams are all pass fail, but passing is like 90%. Would not recommend.
Bad... really bad

He uses specification grading which is like a pass-fail but its more likely you will fail than pass. Wish he would use normal grading instead. If you fail 2 modules (ie worksheet or challenge problem) you drop a grade level and can't ever move up a grade level. Essentially, if you fail, you will keep dropping grade levels. Please avoid at all cost.

Overall the best professor I've had at Tech. A very passionate teacher and a good person. He uses a unique specifications-based grading system in which the course is divided into modules that you either pass or fail. It's tricky to adjust to this system, but he helps you as best as he can if you reach out to him.

Challenging but satisfying, dynamics was a flipped classroom. We watched videos before class and did review/practice in class. Dr. Whiteman's videos were quality, and Dr. Torello's worksheets and homeworks were very good test practice. He is wonderful in office hours, responsive to emails, and very understanding. Still you gotta WORK for the grade!

First time I enjoyed flipped classroom. Application of material is difficult but he does a great job reviewing and summarizing online lectures. In class WS really help to understand material. Textbook wasn't required and not a necessity. Holds review sessions a couple days before exams (HIGHLY recommend). Grading is very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Torello is awesome! Really loves to teach and is passionate about dynamics. There are almost weekly hw's but answers are mostly on chegg. Any day a hw is due you can expect a quiz, but if you participate/pay attention in class they are pretty easy. Tests are reasonable based on worksheets and practice tests. Very understanding and he curves.

Lectures are not engaging and are hard to follow. The tests are so hard that I would audibly laugh during the test session because I knew I was cooked. I spent 5 hours studying for one exam, got a 75, and studied 18 HOURS AND GOT A 72. Tibor himself is a great guy, very sweet, and will help if needed, but this was my hardest class.

Easy enough class if you already took econ in highschool. He doesn't post notes or anything, and there's a required $75 textbook in order to access the homework. The exams were all multiple choice and asked more conceptual questions than anything relating to numbers / graphs. HW does not prepare you for the exam at all
There was a lot of homework which were often easier than the tests. The material did not match up at all and his presentations are slightly boring.

For an intro Econ class, does a good job making a boring class more interesting. Good lectures, explains concepts clearly. If you use the resources in the online textbook you will do good on the tests. Attendance not mandatory, but games are played during some classes that count for a participation grade.

His long lectures of reading off slides with no personality or enthusiasm makes it hard to pay attention and understand the content. Homework assigned is easy, and helped to better understand the topics we learned in class, however it did not relate heavily to his exams, which felt overly hard for a class I was taking for a humanities credit.
Awful teacher, home work and practice have no reflection to the tests and his lectures are not great either. Highly recommend choosing someone else.
Fantastic lectures.
His presentations are good, and sample paper cover a lot of questions, but the questions tested in the exam are much more difficult. Tests are hard, and he does not not round no matter what.

Take any other econ professor. His lectures are very superficial and just give you big concept ideas. The HWs don't really reflect the test at all. This could all just be biased though because I am not good at econ. I cant say I really learned anything in this class

I took his class in the summer and it was a tough one. He's a good teacher but the tests were pretty difficult. Not the best at explaining and can easily get off track. Lots of self-learning is needed!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Horrible. Most of your grade is based on absurdly hard tests. All tests so far have had below a C average. His lectures make no sense and are extremely fast. Better to just read the textbook. Participation grade from online games, though they're often hard to understand due to bad teaching.

TA Ian is amazing though. He should teach this class tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tibor truly does not care about his students in any way. There were 3 extremely difficult exams that had failing averages and were worth 30% each. There were never any homework problems given and lectures were a confusing and boring repeat of the textbook. Our TA Ian was the only good part about this class and was 10 times better than our professor

Took ap micro yet this class was extremely difficult for no reason. Grade based on 3 exams. Many mistakes on each exam. Exams curved bc of failing avg. grade. Does not care whether students pass and difficult to understand during lectures. Textbook somewhat helpful. TA's review questions was the only good part. Never knew what grade in class was.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Econ 2106 was a nightmare. Dr. Besedes did not seem to care about the class at all. 3 exams, no homework, dry lectures, and unclear grades. 

The only good part was the TA, Ian Helfrich. 
His three guest lectures, review sessions, and office hours were what really motivated me to learn. I can honestly say Ian is the best teacher I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I recently took ECON 2106 at Georgia Tech with Dr. Besedes. 
Grade = 3 hard exams + participation. Lectures didn't help. Dr. B doesn't care.
One positive: The TA, Ian Helfrich, is a GOD. He gave the best 3 lectures I've ever been to and carried the whole class with his reviews and study boards. He is brilliant. GT should fire Tibor and hire Ian.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Recommend reading the textbook every day after lecture. Lectures are 75 minutes long and boring. You should probably prepare for the exams at least 2 weeks out, so you absolutely know all the concepts. He offered two makeup quizzes to replace exam grades for the first two exams because the averages were poor for those exams. 3 exams, 90% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Economics shouldn't be challenging, but it is hard when you get no practice with the concepts. Class is useless, textbook is imparative. 10% participation, 3x30% exams. Honestly, without putting much effort into the class, a C is easily obtained if you want to P/F this class. The choice is yours.

Tibor's class is extremely difficult. The class is an intro-level microeconomics course, yet the material is extremely difficult and poorly taught. Tibor has little care for his students and is unresponsive to emails his tests are ambiguous and often include material that was never taught. Just take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tibor is such a confusing lecturer. He teaches an intro to economics class as if all the students have already taken it and have a deep understanding of the economy. His tests are unnecessarily hard because he believes that a 70% average is what students "deserve" for working hard, and A's are reserved for those who go above and beyond. Beware.

Just take a different professor. As an engineering major who only took this class for credit it was super hard for no reason. Tests are literally 90% (30% each) 30 questions so each question missed is a percent lost. Not really sure the reading tip i can give you for this class. extremely hard tests, unless you're a business major DON'T TAKE

This class was inordinately difficult. The 3 tests count for majority of your grade, extremely difficult compared to practice materials, poor curve. Besedes' lectures are monotonous and difficult to follow unless you've read the textbook, yet are just a regurgitation of the textbook. Huge props to the TA Ian Helfrich, who's amazing at teaching econ
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In our class, each test was 30% of our grade with only three tests and then 10% was attendence in lectures. If you messed up on one exam, you were screwed. His average on all 3 tests were 68%. Just take the online course instead.

The grade for this class was based on 90% tests and 10% participation games that we played during class. The tests were unnecessarily difficult, and since we were given no homework or practice material (except for short quizzes on the textbook website) it was hard to know what to expect on the first exam. The TA was awesome though.

Knowing all the things done before was helpful to do well in the class but a lot of my friends who did not know a lot of economics struggled in this class and barely escaped with a B. Very boring lectures and the tests are purely ambiguous MCQs which have no partial credit.

I taught myself this entire class!! His lectures were too fast, and he didn't explain anything or any of the graphs. I taught myself by reading the entire textbook and it took me hours each day to stay on track. This was the first B I have received EVER, and I worked so hard to edge it out. He doesn't care about his students and was rude in emails

His lectures are pretty helpful, though please, please, please read the textbook thoroughly. They are what will help you pass the class. The class itself is midterm-heavy with no final so if you mess up a midterm, your grade will be hanging. Definitely makes you work for it despite being an introductory course. No longer an econ major :D

I had taken so many macro courses before this. I even took the macro AP exam. I thought that I hated economics. But this class (both the prof and micro) made me realize that econ is my future. Make econ your future and take this class!

Professor Besedes did a good job at teaching ECON 2106. His lectures were fine, and he got the material across, but unless you're really into microeconomics the material can often feel boring. It's not very difficult to understand, though. Averaged about 1.5 hours/week on out-of-class homework & studying to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The WORST and confusing professor I'll probably ever have. I got my first B since middle school through this class. You have 3 exams which are 25% each. They are HARD and are not like the homework questions. His lectures are confusing. Take another professor. I took AP Macro and got a 5 on the exam but struggled in Micro because of the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: (Taken during COVID-19 Fall 2020.) This class was just... meh? It was relatively easy if you worked at making sure you did your work. During this online section, we had weekly synchronous meetings to do "games" related to our subjects. These were more confusing than helpful. A solid choice if you need micro.

Tibor is a great professor. Highly recommend taking him asynchronous if possible as content is easy to follow along online. If you do the work you get an A. Period. His lectures can be long, but overall his class is not something people stress about.

I am terrible at anything economics, without participation (and two attempts on homework) I most likely would have failed. He does curve tests if there is a C average, that never happened. All of his lectures contain information necessary to do well on the test, and if something is unclear the book does a good job of breaking it down.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lectures, organized with several examples. Uses moblab activities which are pretty fun and easy participation grade. Asynchronous content gets kind of boring, but manageable. Exams just like HW. Teaches you a great deal and doesn't require an insane amount of work, solid choice.
Lectures can be boring, but tests are generally pretty easy and questions are similar to homework questions. He's willing to help during office hours, and the amount of homework every week is minimal

Really wonderful professor. I reached out to him a few times outside of class and he responded through email quickly. He gave my class extra credit a lot, and the homework that was assigned once a week was easily manageable. The only downside was a majority of the grade was determined by exams, but they are not bad at all if you do the homework.

Professor Besedes made microecon enjoyable and interesting without making the workload anything unbearable. There was weekly online homework that was multiple choice. Most of the grade was from a few tests and the final, but everything was multiple choice and curved by 2 or more questions. Definitely recommend him if you have an econ requirement.

Participation in this class can be easy to fake; based off of playing games, which can be done off-site. Drops 4 lowest homework grades, gives bonus on CIOS, and gives a good - but complicated - final bonus. Accent and handwriting can be hard to understand. Always gives extra credit on exams
He knows the subject very well but the lecture's are dull and if you screw up any of the exams you'll get a crap grade

Our final was worth 50% of our grade, homework was worth 15% and midterm was 35%. He curves up to 70, which saved me. His tests have a problem worth extra credit, but he doesn't tell you which one it is, so even if you think you did bad, it might have been just an extra credit problem. Suggest reading book instead. He just gives examples.

Lectures are extremely helpful, and he does an excellent job of explaining the material.  The class itself is not difficult, but you only have three test which makes up 85% of your grade, so it is hard to bounce back if you mess up one.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: he's ok and not too hard

I've had better. His notes/handwriting can get messy. Sometimes students would question his calculations in lecture and he'd have to go back and change it. This happened plenty of times throughout the semester. Exams are difficult. No formulas given. The final was awful. How does he expect us to memorize every single formula throughout 14 chapters?

I took notes from the textbook & attended every lecture - only managed a B. He provides lots of resources (past exams, practice sets), moves hw deadlines, generous with partial credit, & gives 10 extra credit points on every exam (including the final). TO DO WELL IN THIS CLASS, DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS. If you miss class, get the notes from someone!!

A very good professor. He would give short, condensed lectures and then assign homework to be completed by a certain date, so you could do it when convenient. He was interested in the topic and often liked explaining how things related to the real world. He seemed happy about questions and made a good effort to be fair. Book was hardly necessary.

I thought he was very good at explaining economic concepts. His tests were fairly straightforward and, if you're going to lecture and listening, you should know the material on them. I would recommend you take him for microeconomics.

Nice teacher. Just hard to understand him somtimes because of the slight Spanish accent. Going to class felt pointless because he just reads off the slides and the slides are from the book. pretty helpful when needed to be, responds to emails quickly. Used EconPortal, the tests are questions from the hws and quizzes.

In class he shows powerpoints straight from the book, and posts them online. If you read the book and/or look at the powerpoints, you don't even need to go to class. All of the tests are multiple choice with a 10% bonus. As long as you don't blow it off completely you'll do fine.

going to his class is pretty useless. he reads off slides and any examples he gives for better understanding are directly from the book. but reading the book is essential. if you do the assignments and keep up with the powerpoints you'll be fine. he gives you 10 points extra credit on every test. he helps your grade out in the end too. not hard.

Have absolutely no idea why his ratings aren't all 5's. He's incredibly kind and made poetry interesting to me. Very understanding man as well and treats everyone with respect. Definitely take his class

The class is easy but the content makes it something you have to grit your teeth through. The professor's understanding of the world is very indicative of his cultural background, palm colored southern man, and it is clear in the perspective he teaches. If that's someone you look for in professors then godbless your soul.

I don't know how he became a professor. He made us read a piece that was clearly about femicide and sexual violence against women but said it was about resting after the losses you take so you don't stop following your dreams. It was all very unnerving to hear from a place of high education. His rubric was barely there but grades leniently.

This class was extremely frustrating. The expectations were unclear throughout the semester and the syllabus didn't include a schedule. Communication was lacking, and assignments often felt disorganized or last-minute and only communicated verbally. I rarely understood what was expected or how we were being graded.

Denton offered extremely shallow perspectives in literature. He is unable to understand the cruelties written in the literature he assigns and pushes a narrative that is anthropologically inaccurate. He consistently sides with the ignorance and fosters a learning environment that rivals the current Department of Education.
Not a well structured class and is unable to clearly explain his reasoning for why he believes a poem is good or bad
Good class for easy credit but not it you want to learn anything or develop your writing
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Denton serves as an acceptable poet for this course but lacks congruency in what he believes is considered good poetry. His feedback lacks depth and he is unwilling or unable to elaborate into further detail beyond rewording his  thoughts. He is able to foster an amicable learning environment but clear ostensible understanding of respect.

Professor Denton is the absolute best! He's very understanding about due dates and ensures all the feedback our poems receive is constructive and meaningful. He makes sure the class feels like a big family and I'm sure you will laugh, smile, and write lots of poetry as you improve over his course with your classmates just like I did.

You won't get away with passively sitting in class, doing nothing. But that's a good thing. You will legitimately be a poet by the end of this class. Travis is a down-to-earth instructor and genuinely cares about the thoughts of each of his students. Take this class with Travis!

One of the best professors I've had in LMC. He is thoughtful and his feedback on poems is extremely insightful, and his feedback makes you feel like you can improve and succeed. The way he interacts with students in his class makes participation feel very easy and engaging.

Poetry with Dr. Denton was both a breeze and unbelievably enjoyable. No matter your major, he makes you really enjoy poetry. Very tough class to get into but absolutely worth it. He's incredibly kind to wherever you are in your knowledge of poetry. Have to take it if you need something as a break from the standard Tech class.

Lectures almost always get cut short because of the sheer amount of information. Exams are fully written and lowkey rough. There is CIOS, but only for 100% completion, which is practically impossible. He is very passionate and seems quite nice, but the amount of content is just too much. I spent more time on this class than both orgo and physics.

He is very enthusiastic about genetics. The class is just too much information, and the tests are all written no multiple choice. If I had the choice again, I would not take Torres. He does too much and his lectures are often rushed due to the obsurd amount of material he has to cover in each midterm.

He was a great lecturer and sparked my interest in genetics. Although attendance is not mandatory, I recommend going to class because he provides more in-depth explanations in person. He was helpful and hosted a review session before the exam. He co-taught with Dr. Birol, but the grading system was not clearly outlined.

Good lecturer, lots of info on exams, but if you study hard you can do well. He gives study guides and answers questions well, even knew the names of many people in a huge lecture hall. Posts pretty long extended lectures when we didn't cover everything in class which can add to workload, but understandable given the amount of material.

Great professor! Very caring and even knew the names of many students in a 200 person class. The content was a lot, but the exams were fair. You cannot skip lecture because you learn a lot in a single lecture!

By far one of the worst professors I've ever had. He cares about students on the surface, but is never actually helpful. The grading schemes for this class are still unclear and the final is tomorrow. Exam content was always vague and hardly ever related to what was actually taught. Co-taught with Birol and there was no organization.

He is one of my favorite professors I have had at GT, he is a really amazing lecturer. You can tell he really cares whether you understand the content or not. His tests were extremely fair and really emphasized what we talked the most about in class making them pretty straightforward to study for. Overall, an amazing prof.

He makes this class way harder than it should be and exams are not fair at all. Not clear on what information is necessary to know for each exam. There have been many instances where I would ask him a question, and he'll reply with an extremely condescending answer, as if I should've already known the answer. Not a very understanding professor.
This class was terrible. Flipped classroom structure did not work with me. felt the tests were not very reflective of the difficulty of content we learned in class. would not recommend

Prof Torres is an interesting guy, and he is very knowledgeable about the foundation of genetics. However, taking this class as an 8AM was the most challenging thing I had to do last semester. He loads you with an unnecessary amount of info in lectures, and he expects you to memorize it all for the exams. Be ready to study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is very knowledgeable about the foundations of genetics but his attitude towards students needs serious improvement. He is very rude and inconsiderate to students. He ended up drowning us in material right before the final. Expect to memorize every single detail on the slides unless told not to. HW is a waste of time.

Dr Torres is a cool guy & he seems to care, but his class is difficult. There is a pre and post homework for each class that can be difficult to keep up with. Just because it wasn't taught in class doesn't mean you don't need to know it, and if he runs over on class (happens frequently) he posts the rest of the lecture later to finish on your time.

Dr. Torres has really interesting lectures but his tests are almost vindictive with what they include. Something will be mentioned on a lecture slide once and still be on the test. Grades are based more on memorization than comprehension of class concepts. An interesting class, just more difficult than it needs to be. Dont recommend as a 1st year.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Torres is a kind man but if you have him for Integrative Genetics just know that you will need to memorize literally everything from his lecture slides to have a chance at an A. It's an extremely tough class but it's very interesting and he's clearly passionate about the topic. Get ready to memorize!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Torres' lectures frequently runs overtime! His powerpoints are so disorganized and the wording of his tests and homework make no sense. When someone asks him a question, he likes to dance around the answer instead of just being direct. Would not recommend taking him.

This class was mostly graded by tests, and the test questions often time did not make a lot of sense/ were not clear. There is also no practice questions ever given or any help with grades really. Gives way too many questions for exams with little time to work through and answer them. Also pop quizzes in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures move fast; read the textbook! While Dr. Torres is a caring professor in office hours, he is quite confusing in class. He moves on as long as the top students in the class understand what is going on. The exams will cover EVERYTHING on the lecture slides, and you should probably have them memorized by heart if you expect to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors by far! Really passionate and caring about the subject, but you really have to sit down and study for this class. The tests are challenging and you have to sit down 1-2 weeks ahead and study. I'd really recommend taking the class, just make sure you put forth the effort. I loved the class despite the difficulty.

Dr. Torres care about his students and lectures well but he is unclear about grading criteria. The tests require detailed knowledge of A LOT of material and although he says you will only be tested on "useful information", anything on the slides is fair game. He does offer extra credit, but it is not worth as much as he makes it out to be.

Dr. Torres is a funny and charismatic guy who cares a lot about teaching and is good at explaining and gauging class understanding, but there is unfortunately A LOT of content you will have to get to know. His slideshows are very long so start reviewing early, but he's very approachable if you have any questions. He gives extra credit, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Pay attention in class and take good notes. Review notes and email any questions you may have. Allows you to ask questions during class, but doesn't always answer them clearly, or rushes through the answer. Sometimes has "pop" quizzes, but he usually drops a hint a class or two before.

Dr. Torres' H. Genetics class has been my favorite class at GT so far. He is extremely passionate about the subject, which I loved. A few times we worked through primary literature in depth, which was really beneficial for me. Tests are long, and you have to put in the time to study, but they are completely taken from lectures, so no big surprises.

Really kind and unassuming, but gives a lot of work. I turned in half my assignments in late with no penalty. Very feminist - the kind that makes us constantly analyze art, literature, and music that alludes to or outright shows female anatomy. Grades everything an A, but you have to go to class and participate. Loves climate change activism.

Very fun classes and interesting topics covered in Dr. Truran's classes. It does seem that she gives out more homework than other ENGL 1101 courses but it is all manageable. Make sure you show up to class and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I hate English classes, so while I can't say professor Truran made me enjoy this class, she definitely made it more bearable than any English class I've taken before this. She encourages interesting discussions and gives students broad choice for the topics of projects and essays.
Dr. Truran is a wonderful teacher. The class takes a moderate amount of work but she grades easy. She's probably the best English teacher I've ever had.

She is a wonderful teacher and person. Her assignments are work and research heavy. Compared to that of other English 1102 classes here, you will be doing more work. She is a fairly easy grader though, will give you extensions if you need it, and majority of people receive an A in the class. Attendance and Participation are required.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. T is hands down the best professor I've had for a non-technical class. I thought I was going to hate ENGL1102, because I'm normally only interested in my STEM classes. She managed to make this class engaging and valuable for a bunch on engineering nerds. There's a lot of freedom in the projects and her feedback is top notch. A+ prof.

Dr. Truran is the best! She is a great lecturer and is always open to hearing the ideas of her students. I never felt judged while expressing my ideas in her class and I absolutely loved all the content the we were able to read. She is a fair grader and gives great feedback!

I really love studying with Professor Truran: she is very helpful and gives lots of ideas and feedback for every big assignment. However, getting an A in her class means you will need to put a lot of effort into assignments, especially someone who takes more than 18 credit hours in a semester.

Dr. Truran has a good understanding that students are loaded with work from other classes so she always extends deadlines. The assignments are also not very heavy. The readings are super easy. Definitely recommended.

Dr. Truran is a great person and genuinely cares about her students. She definitely prepares you well for the final portfolio, is easy to approach and honest, and is a solid choice as an English teacher. If you're here for an easy time though... not suggested.

Dr. Truran is an excellent professor. She cares a lot about the progress of her students and is super accessible for feedback. Although our section and topic (Modernism) felt like there was more reading and work assigned than other sections, Dr. Truran was effective helping us become better writers.
Love this guy, super cool. His class was amazing.
Overall awesome lectures, 100% would take again.

Only saw recordings of his lectures, but he is for the most part a great lecturer. Clearly very smart and good at explaining all his concepts. He is also pretty humorous. However, I would not recommend using his textbook. It can be much more difficult to understand than his lectures.

Watching his lectures, he clearly cares about teaching. He is able to explain difficult concepts from the textbook in one or two sentences, and he does so in a way that not only makes sense, but it is illustrative and memorable as well. He usually cracks a joke per lecture or so, and they're mostly on topic as well, so overall, a solid professor.
He is fair. Good sense of humor. Easy to understand if you pay attention. Grading is relatively easy on tests.
Didn't require homework. Recitation quizzes for attendance. Tests were not too bad. He's a cool guy. Had some stories about his days at NASA

He was a strong teacher and was awake and enthusiastic each day. I would reccomend taking him over other teachers teaching this course. He is nt too difiicult if you study his practice tests and show up to class.
If you care even remotely about the development of calculus, this is the class for you. Extremely easy and really interesting lectures - made me want to change my major. Dr Trotter is awesome.
Easy class because I had calc before. His lectures are boring but the tests are not too bad. Just do the practice tests posted online and you will be fine.

Trotter is a grown up "Good Will Hunting".  He's rough around the edges, but he is brilliant and clear.  He expects a lot of you, but equips you adequately for the journey.  There was no textbook for this class, as he was writing it as we went.

The primary problem was that all of the combinatorial analysis material was taken from Trotter's own volume of work, so you won't get a survey of combinatorial analysis. Homework was easy and occassionally obtuse, and the single test was nearly straight regurgitation of long, drawn-out proofs. Try taking the grad-level graph theory course instead.

Trotter was an awesome teacher. His lectures were really long and boring and I slept through a lot of them, but I had never had Calculus before and I got a B in this class even though we covered more material than most of the other Calc classes. His tests are extremely clear and he tells you exactly what things you need to know for the tests.
Kind and caring professor. Very easy A.

The class was super chill. He made it enjoyable the best he could in each class. The only thing that is mandatory is the attendance question at the start of each class but outside of that, the few assignments were extremely easy. Taking him would be your best bet in getting much out of CS 1100.
Easiest class ever. Technically you're supposed to go every week but you really don't need to. Peace was super chill, didn't give many assignments, no homework. Easy A, chill professor.
Let's clap it up for Troy Peace
Classes were pretty useless overall. There were some guest lectures which were interesting. Class was canceled a lot with very little notice

This professor was super chill and funny, attendance was easily done, and there were some cool presentations from renowned companies. Only a few assignments were graded and they seriously weren't that hard.
Very pointless class, lectures were boring, did not learn anything of value. Sometimes grading was a bit harsh. Made us make a resume without teaching us how to.

Prof was often absent at lecture or cancelled it completely. Attendance was "mandatory" but poorly enforced. A couple of the guest-led lectures were interesting but it was mostly a waste of a class and the professor did not improve that. The grading was wildly inconsistent. The best class was the first one, and it was downhill from there.

Keeps class somewhat engaged in a completely useless class. 
Graders occasionally grade harshly but most are fine.
Please teach us to actually write a resume before making us write a resume.

"No hope" is the advice he gave for studying for one of our exams. I really liked his lecturing style, he was very funny.

Be prepared to see things on exams you haven't seen before is my only warning.
Funniest prof i ever had

Where do I even begin with Denis... he's just been an amazing professor each time I have had him. He's nice and understanding and is by far one of the most human and enjoyable professors in the BMED department. If I ever see a course being taught by this man, I'm snagging it as fast as I can!

The lectures are okay. The PSS sessions are the most helpful and generally indicate what will be on the test or quiz.

He leans heavily on prior knowledge, especially from statics. He will teach you the problem solving methods which are straightforward, but get harder through the semester, and he expects a lot of self learning.

Great Professor! The real gem comes during PSS where his humor, talent, & knowledge shines. Makes PSS fun to attend and also allows you to learn a lot during class through focusing on problem solving. Biomechanics is primarily graded by (2 tests + final) which are 25% each, so watch out for them and DO THE HOMEWORK without looking at the answer key

He teaches concepts well and always points out the details that are important. His PSS is more helpful than the lectures. Just pay attention and ask questions during the PSS, you will learn everything you need for the exams.

This class is a mess. It combines def bods and dynamics into one class and is bascially graded all by quizzes and exams that will be as hard as they feel like making it that day. The only lectures that were helpful were Desai's in the last third of the semester. Learned everything else through youtube.
The class is difficult, but Denis is so fun and easy to understand. I am always excited to come to lecture. Attendance is very important.

Denis is a great professor. I had him for PSS and found it much more helpful than lectures. He does a great job explaining his work and really lets us know how to succeed in the course. He's pretty funny and blunt and makes class enjoyable. I would recommend him for this course!

Denis is one of my favorite professors I've had. He's funny, lighthearted, and wants you to succeed. "I want to give you all A's- you just have to help me out a little" - Denis. The class is math and computer science heavy. Recitation sections were set up as group activities that was similar to homework and exam questions.

Worst class I have ever taken. Denis is completely useless when it comes to teaching the material and leaves you incredibly unprepared for the tests that are created by the other class instructors. All other sections were taught the material and given reviews sessions before tests, while we got nothing. Everything about this class was miserable.

Really caring and passionate teacher. This class was a pretty good amount of work, but if you do it you'll get a good grade. As long as you do it, this class is an easy A. She obviously loves her students and is passionate about what she does, which makes the class engaging. Super accessible outside of class, and extension logs are a big plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Listen, if you see this teacher for 1101, take her. She's 1. Super sweet, 2. Easy grader, 3. Amazing at guiding you throughout the process. This is an easy A, and if you pay attention, you can easily learn a thing or two. Just do the work, and submit it on time. :)
Pretty fun class, very difficult to get a B unless you flat out don't do the work. Attendance is required and is a grade, but other than that the class is pretty fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is really kind and patient.

Took her for ENGL 1101. I rated her a 4 because she is a good teacher, and helps us analyze the topics better. I didn't give a perfect 5 solely for the reason of our section having more work than others. Assignments aren't difficult, but they can just be tedious at times. She has a fair grading criteria, and makes it very achievable to get an A.

Professor Tsiotras is very clearly an expert in the subject matter for this course and cares about whether or not his students understand it. He is a fairly forgiving grader and a clear lecturer. Expect difficult (but overall fair) exams without curves.

His AE3530 course is really hard. But that's mostly because he chooses to focus on really complex problems and go in depth on the topics. If you go to his office hours he will always explain concepts and help you with the homework so its not as if he's trying to make things unnecessarily annoying; but the class is still really hard.

Extremely tough professor that gives interesting lectures. Very funny guy, but you'll have to lean on the TA for additional assistance and get used to using Ogata for practice (textbook). Solution manual can be found online for Ogata, but homeworks are often not directly from the book. You'll definitely know the content by the end of the semester.
So much math

Professor states lots of theorems to students without making any effort explaining the proof. This causes tremendous trouble for me to grasp the materials. I can only blindly apply the theorems without knowing what I am doing. I tried to read the book, but the details there are just so many there is no way to understand them all by reading it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Absolutely the best professor I ever had at Tech. He is always well prepared and his teaching is systematic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Took this class last semester. (Content was about food). She really helps you if you ask for it and considers your circumstances e.g. if you get injured. Grades pretty tough but she will lead an exciting class.
She's awesome. Really understanding and always willing to help, with critque, but help that steers you in the right direction for sure. Loved her class.

I really like Dr Tiff and her brand of teaching. She is harder than other instructors here, but her classes are far more stimulating & intellectually challenging as well. Don't sign up if you're looking for an easy A, but if you'd like to have fun, be challenged and enjoy the experience, then she is the one for you.
Initially her class seems interesting, but later on you will find she is really tough and the stuff she talked about is dull..in the end hardly anybody answered her questions.
Dr. Tsao's classes are very entertaining,along with her unique sense of humor that makes the class what it is.She is a little tough with grading,But grades fairly.I enjoy her classes a lot.

While Professor Balch is extremely nice, these past reviews don't reflect my Emory experience. When he entered the Master of Finance program, it felt like he didn't know what he was doing as he struggled to operate Excel and Tableau. His assignments went from trivially easy to not reflecting his class materials at all. He also repeats himself a LOT
Professor Balch is amazing! He's funny and very renowned in the quantitive finance industry. His videos on Udacity are extremely useful, and altogether the class was very doable.

This professor will forever be part of my top 3 lecturers at Tech. He made the course content very interesting and easy to understand (mainly thanks to his Udacity course). Almost all the questions in the tests are from the practice tests (a bit too many in my opinion). Homework is fairly challenging so start early and go to office hours!

Course is manageable but some of the assignments are quite challenging, seek help sooner. ML4T ended up being a weed out class for grad students (I thought we were all beyond such classes but I guess not). The professor seems nice overall, quite humorous during lectures. I am however not a fan of required Piazza, lots of useless posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Taking his class on machine learning for trading right now. He is no doubt one of my favorite professors ever and I've been at Georgia Tech for 5 years. Going to his lectures aren't necessary but he does drop a hint at test questions every now and then. Also, be prepared to watch a lot of videos from his Udacity course on ML4T.
He's funny. Knows his stuff

I am just taking his CS 6446 ML4T class. He is a great professor. He is not condescending at all. He is very humble, which I think is a great attribute. So you do not feel intimidated. I wish he offered more classes!
I am the instructor.  Thought I would start by giving myself a good review :-)
Love her; she is so sweet and caring. No phones, she gives a big organized binder. Concepts can be sometimes difficult but TA was quite helpful. Recommend her!

there was 2 exam, final, daily quizzes and 7/8 hws. overall the class wasn't that hard, just pay attention in class and study what is in the binder and you should pass. turner does tend to go off topic and rush at the end to cover everything so you do need to teach yourself sometimes

Prof Turner is excellent and helped me set myself up for success in the beginning of the semester. Very intelligent, kind, charismatic and communicates her ideas well. I enjoyed real life examples during class as they helped me better understand applications of various topics. Felt bittersweet during the last class because she is a 11/10 prof.

I LOVED professor turner. She reminds me so much of a squirrel , but she is just so funny and caring and extremely fair. She provides so many resources and specific problems from past exams it's impossible to fail. She has tons of real world accounting experiences it makes class interesting. The binder was my lifesaver and i wish her the best!

It is clear that she loves accounting and loves teaching. There is a mandatory binder for the class filled with all of the study materials you could need. She always makes sure to say which topics could be on the quizzes and gives thorough study guides for the exams. I don't like accounting, but I can genuinely say that I loved 2102 with Debby.

Very easy and straightforward class, but very informative! Felt like an accounting history class, but as someone who generally hates history I found it interesting. She incorporates recent events too. If you participate in class and do your assignments on time, it's pretty hard to not get an A. Also just a super sweet and knowledgeable person!

Besides only being allowed to use the binder she provides to us for note-taking and not being able to use our laptops, this was one of the most well structured classes I've taken at Scheller. All homework is online, you don't have to read the textbook, and all exam questions are close repeats from the multiple past exams and practice she provides.

This professor is genuinely the best professor I have taken at Tech. She made accounting so easy and honestly fun. I looked forward to her class every single day. She made sure that you understood accounting and was always available to help. No technology allowed. She cared so much for her students and is a very fair teacher and grader. Loved her.

Dr Turner breaks down accounting into easy steps with lots of practice. The tests mirror the classwork, hw & practice tests & she gives extra credit on tests. She is very strict about being on time & not using technology in class and focuses on pencil/paper practice. She really cares about her students and making sure they understand accounting.

Take her for ACCT2101!! 
Gives you lots of practice problems, old exams, and extra credit. Attendance is required (can miss 2), 2 lowest quizzes dropped, and cheat sheet on exams. Only weird thing is that this class is completely offline -- no tech allowed, required to purchase class binder ($10), powerpoints/worksheets all given to you on paper.

Professor Turner is absolutely amazing. She is the most caring and effective teacher I've had at Tech thus far. Even with a family emergency mid-semester, she was always available if I had questions or needed to catch up on anything. She also made accounting super interesting and digestible with her organized lectures. Absolute gem of a teacher!

Deborah was by far my favorite professor throughout my freshman year. The lectures were relevant and very helpful. Just be present, read the textbook, and ask questions, and you will be just fine. She has very strict classroom rules, so beware of those. NO TECHNOLOGY!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Turner is a great professor and mentor. You need to be in class and participate but you can literally say anything as long as it is relevant to the current discussion. Best class I've taken, best professor, she also gives food a lot and we watch many documentaries. Also, you don't need any accounting knowledge to get a 100 in the class.
Great teacher with relevant course material. I will use her class content for many years to come

Dr. Turner is an amazing professor! You can tell that she is very passionate about what she does, and she genuinely cares about the students in her class. She does enforce her class rules, but as long as you're a responsible student, you should be fine. The course material can be difficult, but she teaches in a way that simplifies it really well!

She runs a tight ship, but her strict classroom makes you learn what you need to. I don't find accounting interesting, but she's an engaging professor who's enjoyable to listen to; she can get off on amusing tangents but then she'll reel herself back in and go back to teaching the concepts in a clear way, illustrated by many daily class exercises.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't know what other people are saying here but if you are an engineering major and just want a chill class DONT TAKE HER. She is very very very strict. You can't enter class late, look at your phone, go to the bathroom, use laptops etc. She teaches very poorly and gives like 19 page exams. Makes accounting hard when it actually isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My FAVORITE professor at Tech thus far. Participation is mandatory, but her lectures are extremely informative. I never thought I would like Accounting, now I am thinking about getting a minor in it all because of her. I wish she was teaching ACCT 2102 this semester so I could take her again! She is one of the first teachers I met that really care!

Dr. Turner was my fav professor last semester! She is so caring about her students and is always always fair. Made the class a little bit tougher this semester (harder exams and no tests were "given") but definitely manageable. If you are engaged in class and do all assignments you should get an A. Loved hearing her anecdotes and cheerful attitude!

Debbie continues to be a great teacher; one of the strongest professors I've ever had. She's very clear & thorough going though the course, & keeps you learning & following the accounting. No electronics allowed in class. Lots of in-class exercises for practice/participation, a few HWs, weekly quizzes, & exams (studied for by reviewing old ones).

Debbie was the best professor I've had at Tech. Although her exams are tough and she'll call you out for not paying attention in class, she cares so much about her students and their success. She gives out a ton of extra credit if the exam averages are too low, quizzes/homeworks are super easy, exams are very similar to old tests that she gives you
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Turner is an amazing professor who cares about her students. She frequently checks for students' understanding. She can be a bit quirky and can come across as a bit harsh and peculiar, but don't let that worry you. Her assessments are basically re-formatted versions of previous exams/quizzes, so if you study those thoroughly, you'll do alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Turner is one of the very best that I've ever had. I took her Advanced Accounting Seminar, and it was a real treat. Do the readings, do your assignments, show up, speak up. If you do those 4 things, you are guaranteed an A.

Her tests have been very easy in the past because she reuses the same material. This yr was different. The first test was like prior, but the last two tests I took were 60% multiple choice on concept questions, which are hard because all she does in class are computational examples. I would not recommend the teacher! choose a more laid back one!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Debbie is absolutely amazing. She cares so much about the students. While her class is tough, she works very hard to make sure students understand the course matter. She is very accessible outside of class. Go to class because she is a great lecturer and the knowledge she imparts in class is invaluable. She contributes a lot of life experience!
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Participation matters--Respected by students

reviews.comment: She is amazing and actually cares about your understanding of the material. Take her accounting I class!
So sweet, so helpful. I would take her for every finance class if I could.
My favorite teacher at Tech.  She is not easy, but she wants her students to do well and is more then willing to help you learn the material

Debby Turner is amazing! She's passionate about accounting and teaches it in a way that's both interesting and very educational. I've learned so much from this class. DO NOT GRADUATE FROM TECH WITHOUT TAKING A CLASS FROM DEBBY! She's one the best professors Tech has because she not only loves the school, she loves teaching, and she loves her pupils

She is really good at teaching. She makes an effort to make sure everyone in class is understanding the material. Class attendance is essential for a good grade. Tests are similar to her previous exams which she gives you. She doesn't curve final grades but she does inflate grades during the semester.
Absolutely interested in making sure all students learn and that the material is comprehensible.  Everything is incredibly fair.
Excellent.  Just attend class and you'll do fine

She's an alright teacher. She's really hyped up all the time.  She does kick people out for yawning or doing anything not accounting related. If you don't study, you will get swamped.  You either get it or you dont.  I had a rough time in the class, but other people did fine.  first 2 quizes were open book, other 5 werent, final was 50 mult. choice
just show up and learn
I liked the class. You learn a lot and get and open note final exam, not a difficult A.
Prof. Turner genuinely cares about your education. You have to put in some effort to do well, but that goes without saying. She is a great teacher, and gives students every opportunity to succeed.

Anything is fair game for being targeted/kicked out of class. A student almost got kicked out for yawning, and another for opening her planner.  She became enraged when she found out someone said they took her class because of the high GPA. Interestingly, our GPA was a 2.59 while the prior 2102 class taught by Professor Turner was a 3.13.

prof turner was an AWESOME professor! she knows what shes teaching! you need to review the material on your own some but she is not out there to trick her students. she gives you lots of little "presents" to help boost your grade!

Wonderful professor; very amiable with students (she makes it a point to memorize EVERY SINGLE ONE of her students' names by the middle of the semester... and she has many.  She'll remember your names for years to come!) - but very structured and very disciplined with her teaching style and students.  Best professor at GT I've had in 4 1/2 years, a
Best teacher I have had at GT by far!!
No Comments

Turner is awesome! She covers lots of material, is straightforward in explanations and on exams and gives ample opportunities for extra credit. She loves students and it shows (she gave us free pizza the last day of class). I can't wait to take her for another class.

Amazing professor, but he's not for everyone. His grading is tough but he clearly cares about your learning. He gives a lot of extra credit & will sometimes post lecture recordings, but don't skip class. There are a few group HWs & several long individual HWs.

Dr. Zaidi was fantastic for my introduction into AE. His lectures, although not often, were plentiful in information and engaging. The rubrics were super clear, a full calendar of assignments was given, and grading was extremely easy. There should be no reason you do not end with an A. Great class.

The two major projects just throw you in the deep end with little knowledge on how to do them but just ask someone at the makerspace and they'll tell you know to do it. Just do all assignments and it's an easy A, just more work than necessary for the 2 major projects. He also very clearly loves his job.
Very nice and caring professor. Since it's AE1601 the workload wasn't that bad, but as a professor you can tell he cares for each of his students. Definitely someone I want for future classes.

its AE1601, prof doesn't matter cuz its an easy A class. Just turn in work. Can't say much about Zaidi cuz I skipped basically every class but not too bad of a teacher. Turn in your work, understanding of problems, especially cuz the TA was so involved w my class. Make friends with AMS though, helps for projects.

Had this prof for 1601 and he was a great lecturer who put in effort to have engagement from the entire class despite the class size. He set up group projects and to give students a taste of what a career in AE would look like with some pretty fun group projects. Just dont procastinate!

Had him for 1601 and he's got to be one of the best lecturers on campus. Very passionate and constantly tries to improve the class for students. He's lectures are valuable and he expects you to attend all lectures so you are getting your worth. Took him over the summer; 3 hr long lectures and you have to work every single day on thermo to succeed.

Goated lecturer. Take if you really want to learn the fundamentals of thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. It's insane that the course combines both, but he really makes an effort convey information properly without diluting the material. That said, the class is tough but manageable if you make the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Personally I really enjoyed attending Zaidi's Thermo lectures despite the difficulty of the class. More than difficult, the class just has so much content that is thrown at us in such long classes. There are readings before each class but they are not necessary to succeed at all. Just do the homework early and understand the problems.

Exam 1 & 2 (each): 13.3%; Quizzes (3): 13.3%; Individual HW: 20%; Group HW: 10%; Final: 23.3%; Attendance: 6.6%. Thermo is tough. However Zaidi makes it feel "achievable". He truly cares about understanding the material and it shows with his personality in an 8 a.m. lecture. Quizzes and Tests were tough but clear. Would take him 100% again!!

Thermo is a tough class, but Zaidi is a really good lecturer and clearly cares about his students doing well and learning the material. His attendance policy is pretty strict and homeworks can be a little tricky sometimes, but exams are fair and only cover the material we learned in class.

He is really good at explaining the subject in a way that is easy to follow and he makes his lectures engaging. That is why he makes attendance mandatory, and bc he tells you in his lectures stuff that might be "seen later," and it is literally the answer to a test question he will ask you. HW isn't unreasonable, usually good test prep. he's goated

AE1601 is a very easy class no matter who you have, but Zaidi was not the best. He overexplained a lot of material that we didn't really need to go over. In addition, he would say "um" every 5 seconds. But nonetheless, AE1601 is a very chill class with fun projects. Zaidi will help you with questions but it might be overdone.

You need to show how you cancel your units, follow a pointless homework format, be not even a second late to class, etc. This is not an easy class in terms of content already, and Zaidi and his TA are working together very hard to deduct points from your HW, quizzes, and tests for the most trivial reasons you can imagine
Horrendous professor. Inhumane amounts of work and terribly difficult tests. Not worth taking.

Dr. Zaidi makes you swipe your buzzcards at 8:25 AM for attendance, so beware if you're even 30 seconds late. It feels like most AE profs (Zaidi included) have no idea how to actually teach a class, even if they are "experts" in the material. Lastly, I'll just leave it at this: title IX should've been pulled on this guy a long time ago.

Very strict on attendance (don't even be late). His lectures are some of the best in AE and he is very thorough on teaching the subject. The exams are very difficult but you just need to make sure you practice a lot and understand the vocabulary and concepts.
Good lecturer, awful professor. Inhumane amounts of work coupled with impossible tests and an incredibly tough grading scheme. Take someone else for your sake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely do NOT take Dr. Zaidi. A truly awful grader with no sympathy for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely hard, unforgiving professor. A good lecturer, but that's about it. Tests are incredibly difficult and NO partial credit is given for incorrect answers, despite tests being worth 63% of the grade. 27% of the grade are extremely difficult homework assignments as well. There is no curve nor extra credit. Avoid taking him at all costs.

He's an amazing professor who loves what he is teaching. There is a lot of content and he does well in making sure he goes over all of it. A lot of reading is needed especially since the class should be 5-6 credit hours instead of 4 credit hours (Zaidid even said this).

No partial credit given with no curve. Extremely time intensive and an overall unhealthy course taught by an extremely strict, difficult professor. Solid lectures. Not worth the pain you will endure, however

Insanely strict attendance policy. Ridiculously hard exams and extremely long homework. He's a good lecturer, but you will not have a great experience with him. Absolutely no partial credit is given on exams, and you are expected to digest an unbelievable amount of content with no room for error. Do NOT take him if you want a good experience.

An inhumanely strict, extremely difficult professor. A great lecturer, but not much else to say about his class other than the fact that he makes it as difficult and unforgiving as possible. No curve whatsoever and disgustingly difficult tests make sure there is no room for error whatsoever. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Zaidi clearly cares about his class and his students' learning. His attendance policy is draconian and is very inflexible if you are sick or have extenuating circumstances. Despite this, he is one of the best lecturers I have had at this school and I feel like I learned a lot. Genuinely would take him again, even if it increased my stress greatly.

Dr. Zaidi is a great professor and lecturer. This class, however, is extremely difficult, albeit much more bearable than his thermodynamics course. HWs are hard, and tests are harder. Despite this, I'd suggest taking Zaidi for this course. You will learn a lot and he is a very friendly and proactive professor.

Professor Zaidi is a fantastic professor and lecturer. However, note that his class is HARD. His tests are ridiculously difficult and his HWs are exceptionally tedious. If you take his AE2220 course simultaneously, you will have exams on the same day, including the final exam. He is great, but if you want an A, this might not be the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had him for Thermo and Dynamics in the same semester and it was the hardest thing I've ever done so far. However, he's a great lecturer and although the classes are hard, he tries his very best to be a good professor. The start will be hard, but it will get better as it goes. Do a BUNCH of practice problems and if you do you should be okay.

You will do well if you put in effort. Attendance was required, but he made sure it was interesting. He's funny and really caring. One of the best professor's I've had. Will memorize every student's name and genuinely cares about your aspirations and interests. Some assignments were a little nitpicked (TA grading) but he helps with any questions

AE 1601 gave surprisingly a lot of work for being a 1 credit hour class. However, this wasn't a bad class in the slightest. Zaidi gives you all the tools you need to make it work, and it's up to you to innovate your own solutions for the projects. He's also really caring and considerate with the submissions, so just turn things in on time. :)
Zaidi is a good prof and knows what he is talking about. For 1601 just beware that assignments are nitpicked for seemingly no reason, but you will still get an A as long as you do all the work.

Probably the best professor to take for 1601, he knows what he's talking about and can easily find the solutions that are bugging you during your projects (A model rocket and a glider). Fun guy to talk to, and makes an effort to connect to every student. Fell asleep in class often (not his fault), and still managed to do pretty well.

if you go to class and put in the effort you WILL do well. i am not even one to normally go to class but it is required but he makes it worth your time. class is very fair, lectures are interesting, he is funny, and he cares a lot about his students. he memorizes every students name. best professor i ever had.

I had this professor for three classes, AE 1601, AE 2010, and now AE 2220, and I spent a lot of time in office hours. This professor is one of the best in the AE department; however, the content he teaches is difficult. Get this teacher; most people get an A or B. He has the most TA help. Pro-tip, go to recitation, or at least review the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great choice for a professor for a class that will be difficult no matter who teaches it. He sets out very clear expectations about homework and attendance, and as strict as they may be, they really do help you focus on the class. Alternates between group and individual homework, and gives extra credit if you turn it in early. Tough, but great.

Dr Zaidi is an amazing professor if you follow his class guidelines; he has lots of rules to make sure everyone succeeds. Lectures are very dense, so zoning out in class can cost you a lot. He frequently goes over past material though. He clearly cares a lot about his students and doing well in his class might be more accessible than you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaidi is an amazingly good professor and will make time for you if you ask in advance, even not during office hours. He goes somewhat fast, which can get really annoying at times, but recitation definitely helps with that.
Lots of work but he teaches the class very well and the exams are very reasonable. One of the best lecturers I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zaidi is by far my favorite professor taken at Tech. He is amazing I have taken AE-1601 and AE-2220 with him and he is amazing. Be prepared to work hard but as A.E.'s this major isn't easy so just give it a good solid effort and you will do just fine. I wish he did higher level courses because I would take his classes in a heartbeat.

Best professor I had this semester. Zaidi is very good at getting straight to the point while also providing great explanations. He gives a very good introduction to the aerospace field, so I would definitely recommend taking this class in you first year if possible. He is very good at responding to discussion posts and will help if you just ask.

Zaidi is a very capable instructor. He moves quickly through material, but answers questions well. His lectures focus heavily on derivations and leave the problem solving to the homework sets, so be wary of that. Class is mandatory for participation points, and I encourage going regardless because lectures help set up the foundations for problems.

Dr. Zaidi's classes run like well-oiled machines. Lectures are very to-the-point while still giving enough background information for the derivations to make sense. Homeworks are short, but extra practice problems are provided for exam preparation. The exams weren't exactly easy, but if you adequately prepare for them you'll be fine.

Dr. Zaidi is one of my favorite professors I have had. Granted AE 1601 is meant to be an introductory class, but he made it very enjoyable. You could tell he was passionate about his work and cared about all the students. Almost everyone in the class got an A as long as they did the work.

Prof. Zaidi is awesome. Lectures were super interesting. Clearly goes over all of the material (although sometimes quickly). If you go to class awake and prepared to learn, you'll do well. If you don't stay engaged then it gets difficult. Study homeworks and go to recitation. Dedicate time to the class and you'll do fine.

He makes sure to give as many resources to students as he can in order for them to succeed. So many office hours available; if you ask questions he will answer and try to really help you understand. He's very passionate about making sure his students learn.

Dr. Zaidi is a very nice professor. On the other hand, his tests were not particularly, and there was a lack of consistency in them. Difficulty varied widely, and the final was substantially different than the previous exams.

The material in this class is a lot, but Zaidi sets clear expectations of how to do well. His lectures are incredibly thorough and interactive. Tests are tough but fair. Taking this class made me know the material by heart which will be incredibly useful for future classes. Zaidi cares a lot about his students' success, highly recommend. fav prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course is just as hard to take as it is to teach. Despite this, Dr. Zaidi was amazing, not to mention incredibly professional.  If you follow the workflow as needed and are patient you will get an A in the class.  Zaidi's approach to teaching inspired me to want to do well, and you feel good when you can manhandle this behemoth of a course.
Just plain bad. If I could sum up my experience with him it would be just as well as Geoff Collins tenure. Never take him

Professor Zaidi clearly knew how to teach the class and taught it amazingly. The only gripes I have about this class is that it was at 8:25 am and was a two hour lecture. Neither of these aspects are in Zaidi's control so make sure your class is not at this time.

Had him for AE1601 Fall 2021. He is the fastest talker on the planet. If you focus, though, you will realize that everything he says has a purpose and thought behind it. He is a good professor because he will teach you exactly what you are supposed to learn. Semester was front-heavy with work, but relaxed at the end. He knows what he's saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class

The lectures are way too specific for an overview class and are meaningless to the work you'll do. Assignments are easy but graded extremely poorly and don't reflect the work you put in. Still, it's not a difficult class, you just have to be picky about the rubric.

Really cool professor, cares a lot. Go to class! He covers a lot of material in lecture and usually goes over homework as well. Class was pretty easy, fun and informative but be warned: I found that the workload was a little bit inconsistent. Some weeks, by no exaggeration, had less than 5 minutes of homework. Others were way worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is very accessible outside of class, and he clearly enjoys teaching the subject. At certain points, he did go too fast, but this class is introductory so understanding the concepts is the most important, which he teaches well. If you take this class, I'd recommend not focusing heavily on taking notes, and more on listening fully.

Prof. Zaidi cares a lot for his students and gives really good lectures. Lots of homework and quizzes that are fair content-wise but can be graded harshly. He tried to make the most of the pandemic situation and offered multiple extra credit opportunities. Did seem to get frustrated at times with students requesting accommodations.

Dr. Zaidi made the most out of an online format due to Covid-19. His lectures are incredibly clear and helpful, and he is very passionate about the course. Cares a lot for his students and helps you if you email him questions. Lots of homework and assessments that are tough but fair. Definitely requires a lot of work and time.

I liked the content, even though there were a ton of lectures. But maybe Dr. Zaidi isn't cut out for virtual because most of us struggled in the class, and he almost never listed to our worries or accommodated our concerns. Because of this, this class was very draining and depressing even though it could have been fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took him because he had good ratings and I'd heard great things from friends. I don't know if it was COVID, virtual, or what, but mine (and most of my classmates' experience) was not the same this year. Interesting lectures and I ended with an A (due to a huge curve), but the extreme stress, unfair quizzes, and brutal grading wasn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of hard homework and the assessments are tough and fair. He is very strict but is very passionate about the material he teaches and ensures that his students learn a lot.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Tech (taken at GTL). Homework is tough, exams are tough but fair. Zaidi will do whatever it takes to ensure you understand the material and internalize it. He cares about student success and it shows. Be prepared to work in Zaidi's class, but you'll definitely learn a lot. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great at actual teaching, tests and quizzes are usually very fair but the grading on all assignments is very unforgiving. Kinda hard to find outside of class, and you will need to find him outside of class. Will deduct points and give you a lecture about your work ethic if you're ever late. Crib sheets allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is a very knowledgeable professor who genuinely wants students to learn the material and not just memorize it. With that being said he gives a lot of difficult homework, but tests and quizzes aren't as hard. He's sometimes a little hard to get in touch with. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Zaidi was someone who could really pique interest in the subject. Despite it being condensed into a three month course at GTL, he paced the course amazingly well and I kept showing up to class expecting something new every time. All in all, I would highly recommend you take him if you're really interested in AE, because he sure is.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaidi really tries to improve his student's learning process. Because of this he expects people to read the book before class and to attend most/all lectures. No late work accepted. Also, he will call on students at random in class and expects people to have read. His exams were pretty straight forward but he won't give practice exam materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent at actual teaching; however, the class is filled with too many arbitrary rules. Grading for homework and tests is done harshly, although tests are fair. Homeworks are very lengthy and demanding. His class policies are uncompromising and he is unwilling to accommodate special circumstances. Do not take if you plan on traveling at GTL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Zaidi is an incredible professor. I went to his lectures not because it was mandatory but because it was worth the time. His explanation added to the textbook in a very helpful manner. That said, keep up with the readings. Homework is hard but he is available to help and the tests are easier than the homework so just put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor and TAs are not accessible at all!! Only one TA's email is available in syllabus. They use Piazza but nobody replies!! This course uses a crappy platform for hws which breaks down from time to time. Couldn't learn anything from lecture and HWs are almost irrelavant to lectures. Worst experience in GT so far.

Allows extensions (provided documentation). Clear lectures, definitely cares. Tests are very fair and based off HW problems. Go to lecture, pay attention, do HW, and you're solid. Also gives random "pop quizzes" - a participation thing, if you're there, you get extra credit. I'd definitely take him again. Students are too harsh against him I feel.

Professor Tuo Zhao is one of the best professors I have ever met. What impressed me so much is his deep knowledge in statistical inference.
