His class is the hardest core class I have ever learned, and I enjoy such an intensive class. For the people who rated 1-2 for this class, this class is just too hard for you.
Professor Zhao is knowledgeable of his field. He teaches in an articulate and concise manner which is appreciated. Learnt about from his course.
Prof. Zhao is the most awesome prof. that I have ever known. He can transfuse the class into a profound yet easy-to-understand feast of knowledge. I highly recommend his course.

I like Dr Zhao as a person, but I admit he struggles to explain lectures. Once it took 6 minutes to answer a student confused that he wrote "p" instead of "9". He prints code and walks around the giant lecture hall passing it out instead of posting on Canvas. His tests and homework are straightforward and you do learn. Big curve and extra credit.

I would never recommend taking his classes. You will learn nothing from lectures and the practice test asks you materials that are hardly covered during class. He provides no clear answers and lets students solve his problem and move on without checking if it's the correct answer. One of the worst professors I had in Georgia Tech.

He was very difficult to understand, so attending class was honestly a waste of time, except for the occasional extra credit he gave at the end. I learned nothing in the class, so I feel like I am unprepared for future classes. He is also very hard to reach. He graded my exam incorrectly and I emailed him a couple of times, but he never fixed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not exactly great at teaching, but he tried to be caring. Tests were curved to have an average of at least 80 and there was plenty of extra credit (extra credit for attendance on random days). If you took AP Stats you should be able to breeze through this class (ISYE 3030), otherwise I'd avoid or be prepared to study a lot yourself.

Honestly, Zhao is a very nice guy and he cares about his students however, I had a very hard time understanding him. I learned nothing from him and just had to teach myself the material. He ends up curving and has lots of extra credit in class.

The class is tough but fair. Tests are always curved so that the average is at least a B. You need to go to class and pay attention to the lectures to be successful. There are a lot of extra opportunities for extra credit. Grade is Homeworks + 2 midterms + final exam + extra credit. Lowest homework is dropped and you get extra credit for showing up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tuo was, simply put, a bad professor. He ignored almost all of my emails and made homework and exams nearly impossible. The class average on our exams was consistently about a low 60. Don't expect to learn anything useful with him. Now that he's teaching in-person classes, his course is no longer an easy A -- it's a struggle for a B.

Ppl have given him bad reviews but honestly it's an easy A. He showed that he cares about his students by giving them extra credit during the pandemic. If you put some effort in, you'll get an A. Just accept the free A, no need for complaints.

It's an easy A if you understand the formulas and do the practice tests, but you learn nothing out of this class. He does not post lecture videos in a timely manner and simply reads off the slides in the "recorded" lectures, and his explanations were not very clear. Also, the TA had to spend at least one month to grade most homeworks & exams.

Okay so this is one of the easiest classes I have taken at Tech, but I didn't learn a single thing. Tuo is kinda hard to understand and is not the most engaging prof. But his tests are super similar to the practice tests, and the homeworks aren't too bad. The final was hard, but open for a whole day. I'm kinda screwed for my upper level classes now

Amazing professor! Had him onBarcelona program and he was super approachable and caring. Even with the long classes, he makes time pass quickly with interesting lectures. Dr. Tyson made CHEM 2311 worlds easier, and I had a much better understanding of chem than students on campus. Super responsive to students needs and just overall a great guy.
Super great teacher. He is really approachable and fair.  He makes you think about the material....definitely go to lecture. I enjoyed his class stories.

Tyson was an overall effective teacher. His lectures were very quick, so reading the book is a must to understand. The homework was very different than the tests, but the practice exams online were very helpful. His TAs were great and held numerous review sessions. His grading scale is somewhat forgiving with several tests and final exemptions.
Tyson Rocks!
Great teacher...super helpful...wish I could have him for every class...excellent communication skills...a perfect choice

he is very pleasant and agreeable. easily approachable if you need help with material. 5 tests and about 10 hw, can exempt out of final if scored an A average on 5 of those 6 things. PRS quizzes during class. moves at a good pace and makes lecture interesting and shares life experiences. i love class with him. he is quite the charming southern gent

Would not recommend. Rude, impatient, and disrespectful to students. Gives almost all instructions in Spanish, so students dont know whats going on half the time. She once clarified instructions before class when many students werent there yet, and then ranted later when they didnt follow the instructions that werent given to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really great Spanish professor, conducts the entire class in Spanish but makes sure to email you important deadlines in English. Really cares, participation in class is key and it never hurts to go to her office hours. Also, do the homework.

I loved Senora Tyler! She legitimately cares about her students, but you have to work hard. Ask for clarification because sometimes she is unclear, but if you work hard and have a good attitude, you will succeed!

Do exactly what she says, and you'll succeed. Participate in class to improve your skills. She gave everyone in our class a 100 for participation. Don't worry too much about harsh grading on projects or interviews--she's looking for growth and to see if you're actually trying. DO study for the vocab quizzes. The first one is the hardest.

Very impatient and disrespectful. Minimal thought put into lessons. Demeaning to students. Communication is awful since she speaks extremely broken English. Does not use  tsquare so you never know your grade or due dates. Throws a fit in class when students dont know what's going on. Humiliates students when they mess up. Worst teacher I ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I had a really tough semester with personal issues, and Señora Tyler was seriously amazing. She showed me so much compassion and empathy, and she gave me the chance to make everything up and helped me when I needed it. Sometimes her accent is hard to understand, but she will repeat in English if needed. I seriously LOVED her, would take her again.

Gives all instructions and homework assignments in Spanish, hard to know what you're supposed to be doing sometimes. Also tells lots of stories in Spanish, just nod and smile like you know what she's saying.
This class was awesome!!!! I think is an easy A with a little bit of effort! It's one of the most helpful and funny teacher that GT has

I have taken Spanish in High School, and believe that this is a great place to start coming out of HS. I recieved an A in the class and got it through participating and doing a lot of extra credit work. I did badly on the quizez, which I never studied for, but showed improvemnt and she rewarded me for it.

She is a great and helpful professor. She speaks spanish all of the time so make sure you are ready for that. She keeps you interested with various stories and tries her hardest to make sure that you understand. Definitely take her!
Great teacher! This class is not an easy A, but as long as you do the homework and pay attention in class, you will be fine.

Getting an A in her class is easy if you do the following things: Attend class, do homework, participate in class, and if you have further trouble, go to office hours. If you do these things she is more than willing to help you in every way possible. She's a very nice teacher and she doesn't expect anything unreasonable.

Wonderful professor! She has a good personality and is interested in helping you learn and loves what she teaches. It's not a guaranteed A, but if you pay attention and go to class you'll be fine. And she's pretty funny too

I think she is a great teacher. Her personality is amazing, she is fun, youthful and helpful. She only speaks spanish in the class (by the way she talks a lot!), which was such a great help for me. At the end of the class, I was at a level to understand spanish TV channels.
The class was not incredibly hard, but I had a lot of issues with her personally which made this class miserable for me. She talks way too fast to be teaching a 2000 level class.

She is incredibly vague and assigns essays every other day. Other LMC courses are turning in easy and small assignments, while we are creating 30+ page essays. You have to keep asking her questions to understand the assignment, but then she goes on insane tangents that have no relevance to your question. One of the worst classes I've ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Assignments are insanely vague, and just back to back to back to back. She also is really passionate about visual rhetoric, which, I assure you, you PROBABLY don't care about you. Don't take this class. It's a major snoozefest to be in the room, and you'll work like a horse outside.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She claims to be an easy grader, and if you're willing to put in the work this is mostly true. You're probably not going to fail, but it isn't an easy A. Her clarity on assignment topics is non-existent, though the parameters for assignments are clear once you pass that initial hurdle. Get on her good side, and you're fine. Otherwise, good luck.

Among the worst professors I've ever had. The class created a group me just to cope with how poorly she explained things, and she got angry at the class several times for not understanding. She is insulting (repeatedly told us we'd just be getting people coffee the rest of our lives). One saving grace is her office hour availability.
The class was hard, but she is doing her best to make sure that we get it. A lot of grammar that is hard to understand.

She is really nice and helpful. She lets you choose the article/literary work you want to analyze, and you focus on that the entire semester. You don't have to do any small assignments like journals and such. Half of the time you don't need to go to class because it is online on a webboard. Plus she is a very easy grader.

Super passionate guy. He can inspire anyone to enjoy higher level mathematics, makes it enjoyable and always ready to help. He often curves to make up for the difficulty of the class. I took both 1564 and 2561 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you are truly passionate about math; this is perhaps the most knowledgeable, passionate, and inspiring professor I've met at Tech. If you put in the work, the class is very rewarding.

Don't take this class unless you're ready for a bunch of proofs. You have to really like  abstract math stuff to do well. The first test was super easy and then everyone bombed the second one, but he curves the final averages and gives A's to about 20% of the class and doesn't want anyone to fail. GO TO RECITATION!

- English isn't his first language - He is very strict, ridiculous policies. (plug in one wrong number on an exam problem, there goes a letter grade, as I did.) - most of his policies seem to be there to hurt your grade. - He doesn't know the subject - by far the worst professor I've had. Just very frustrating to try to pass his class.

Test typically include 2 problems and an "essay" section.  Ume's first language is not English and his comprehension of student's essay answers is low.  Asks very vague questions but will only accept a few possible answers.  You are wrong, even if you put down the correct answer.  Problems are easy, but you'll lose most of your points on the essay.

Unwilling to work with students. Would go to him or email him for more help and he would reply with rude emails saying he was too busy. The Mechatronics class requires a lab. During class if you ask a friend a question he will get onto you for talking and if one person doesn't understand will go back over the material but nonetheless he is unclear.

He is a very easy professor. The class for Mechatronics was very difficult to not get an "A" in it. However,that does not mean it is a useful class or that you'd learn very much from the experience. It was a very generalized course with a general brush-through of different mechatronic topics. Could learn basically whole course from Wikipedia.

This guy is a first rate SOB. I am surprised I am the first one rating him! I got out of Tech couple of years ago but I just found this site. Do NOT take him. This guy has tenure and as such is untouchable. He is deliberately unhelpful and a bad teaher.

Professor Usselman was a great lecturer and I recommend this course to anyone if he is taking it. The class was online and he prerecorded lectures that you could watch anytime. Grades were based on three essay writing exams (very easy if you had looked at the slides) and were open note. Despite being an online class it really seemed like he cared.

The lectures were pretty interesting, and the tests were very challenging, but I guess "Fair".  He is a really hard grader, and his TA is just as hard grading.  I would say if you're an engineering major, don't take this class, but if you're good at history and expanding on very theoretical questions go for it.
He lectures well, and the class is interesting.  The exams are challenging but fair.

Valeriya is such a sweet professor! She's always available for help outside of class, and her lectures are always fun and engaging. Getting a good grade is fairly straightforward and mostly comes from actually participating in class.

I love Valeriya, she's the sweetest. As long as you put the work in, you'll get an A, but homework can be really time consuming (2-3 hour assignments on MWF). The class was still so worth it!! Take Russian @ Tech, there's so many fun events and the profs are all the kindest people ever.

There is homework due 3x a week, but that seems standard for the Russian program. The professor lets you retake pretty much everything so you will get an A if you put in the effort. I think I learned a lot, however it was rather disappointing that class was only 50 minutes a day, seemed like we were always going pretty fast because of that,

I love Professor Chekalina, she is a great person and cares about her students. I found her course difficult but she made it easy to meet with her and discuss, she is very patient and understanding. There is lots of homework, the class is very active participation. It requires lots of work but I can only fully recommend her as a professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Valeriya is probably my favorite professor that I have ever had at Georgia Tech. She is very knowledgeable about what she teaches and clearly conveys the information, even when the material seems difficult. She is also HILARIOUS in class and promotes a great environment for language practice.

Professor Valeriya is not only an amazing professor but an amazing person, too! She cares about all her students deeply and is always trying to make sure everyone understands the material. Professor Valeriya teaches in a very simple, reasonable way and is always engaging and quick with a joke in class. Highly recommend taking any of her classes!

Professor Chekalina is such an exceptional teacher! She is so unintentionally funny during lectures, and genuinely cares about all of her students. Also, she lets you retake any quiz or test so she's GOATED. so so excited to have her again next semester.

I really enjoyed professor Valeriya's class. Although the content is not the easiest, she always tries her best to get her students to understand the topics. Her exams are fair and she does not grade harshly. The environment in the classroom is great, and I actually look forward to going to class.

Professor Valeriya is a very sweet, fun, and caring professor. She is willing to help if you need any and is very knowledgeable about her subject and loves discussion. I love the way she teaches as class is very engaging and she makes sure everyone understands. She is overall a great professor!

Although her course can be difficult at times, Valeriya is definitely one of my favorite teachers of all time! Her lectures are always informational and entertaining, and she is always willing to take class time to explain a hard concept. Also, you can retake any exam or quiz with no strings attached for a higher grade! Love her
Professor van Hentenryck is nice and smart, but he is not interested in teaching. It feels like he should be running a company, not being a professor.

Pascal is the smartest and funniest professor I have ever taken at this school. This class is structured very differently than others at the school, with most grades being either 0,30,70, or 100. prof/TA's are inaccesible outside of class. Class/office hours are combined into one session, and it is impossible to meet any of the class face to face.

Great professor.  Very clearly cares about his students and always makes lectures interesting - get ready to rewatch Star Wars!  Class wasn't too difficult if you have a programming background.  30% HW, 30% midterm, 40% final.  Double check your submissions, as the problems are easy but the grading is harsh.  The hw is the best prep for the final!

Really smart guy. Great recorded lectures (async class) but limited in scope. synchronous zooms but we weren't told about them before registration (I had a class at the same time and they weren't recorded) no help outside of zooms (profs unresponsive on edstem and no help on stack overflow etc) hws are easy but graded crazy harsh if you mess up.

Only graded on homework. You form constraints and implement in OPL, a language managed by IBM that he invented. The course teaches a lot, starting slow and increasing in difficulty. TAs are very active in office hours and EdStem.
Hardest course I have taken, but the quality instruction made it my favorite and very manageable.

Homework were challenging at times but Pascal and his team of TA's were flexible with deadlines and often offered extensions. Ed discussion was a great place to get help and discuss with fellow students. During OH, Pascal is always caring and knows students by name if you are a regular attendee. Overall effective class and fun professor!
Yoda has a cheery attitude but this course does not seem like it is organized with students in mind.  Very difficult assignments are due every few days and getting help is a nightmare.

Overly difficult course.  Prof & TA's give extremely vague hints to people looking for help on any of the many difficult hw assignments.  You simultaneously learn a programming language and a problem modelling framework, which is NOT ideal.  Not as fun as they say...
Amazing guy

Pascal is a very funny and nice professor, often giving deadline extensions for the homework. The class is entirely themed around Star Wars, which makes it more interesting. It's also easy if you pay attention to lectures and attend his weekly sessions for help on the homework. The only downside is the language (OPL) may not be applicable at jobs.

Fantastic lecturer. Always took time to answer questions. Very lenient on grading (1 exam dropped and 2 problem sets dropped). Extra credit on every homework as well! Difficult course, but I feel like I learned a lot, and I enjoyed the material.

Not to trivialize others' struggles, but I found this class alright - even as someone who struggles in harder CS classes. One exam dropped, HW dropped generously on a per-problem basis. Exams are easier than HW and non-cumulative. Prof's nice too. If you did okay in 3510/3511, this class (which mostly repeats that material) shouldn't be too hard.

(CS 6515) I disagree with others on his teaching since I actually understand Algorithms now, unlike my undergrad Algos course. If lock in during lectures and show up to office hours whenever you are stuck, you'll have no issue with the HW and exams (grading is absolutely fair). In fact, during OH he's SUPER helpful so idk what the hate is about
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't give good explanation of concepts, and has very tough grading. Bring back Brito for CS 6515!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is the price you pay for doing grad school. He writes algorithms in class and doesn't explain why they work. Homeworks are arbitarily difficult and TA's are barely helpful on Piazza. Not worth taking, and I'm mad Brito isn't teaching 6515 anymore. Do yourself a favor and do interactive intelligence not machine learning in grad school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He should not be teaching this class. He doesn't know what he's teaching, and I don't get why we're covering linear programs. I just can't wait to be done with this class and then I'll never think about these things ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 6515 with him is basically a full-time job. Each homework easily took up 30-40 hours a week, and concepts were poorly explained in class. Exams are brutal, and regrade requests are basically impossible because prof and his TA's are super stingy on giving points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Doesn't teach much in lecture and homeworks are far removed from lecture, and there's a horrible proof problem on each hw. TA's refuse to give back points on regrade requests and stubbornly insist they are correct. Crams way too much into class, and homeworks and exams are an uphill battle. 6515 with him is not worth the pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super thoughtful and caring professor, which can be hard to come by in MSCS. Patient and willing to answer any question. Humble. Clearly talented and loves what he does. Covers difficult content, but is fair. Take Jan if you can. (I took 6515, but not showing up as an option).
Really good lecturer and I enjoyed the class! The homeworks were a bit disorganized but the generous grading policy made up for it. Jan is also really approachable and very enthusiastic to help.

Homeworks are incredibly difficult- go to office hours. Tests are rather straight forward, but graded out of 40 points, so a few little mistakes can easily become a B. Dropped lowest HW and test (so final was optional), but I didn't enjoy his lecture style of handwritten notes.

Solid lecturer and a pretty structured course. The prof is able to provide satisfying answers to questions quickly in lecture while still being able to cover all the material. Homeworks are reasonable in length and difficulty, and generally pretty representative of the topics. Exams are actually on the easier side.
If Van Den Brand was standing near a fissure I would lie across it so he could cross safely. He is amazing, he has GOATED lectures, WELL DESIGNED HW, and AMAZING HAIR.

No extra credit in project/homework. Have moderate curve on exam made me B but still, hard. Spending so much time on assignment for 33% full grade, which is strict in grading. 67% in 2 exams. Not reluctant to give out chances of improving grade. He's a okay professor, but hard to obtain A in this class.

Good lecturer despite the material sometimes being dry. Biweekly homework sets are very challenging, as I made the mistake of never going to office hours. However the curves on all assignments are so large its basically impossible not to do well in the class. Lecture notes are published online, though lectures is much more useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HW is almost impossible to complete on your own, OH is useful. Grade is 1/3 HW (6 of them), 1/3 Test 1, and 1/3 Test 2. HWs are curved and capped at 100%. Test 1 was also curved. Seems to be lenient and understanding of students, has extended deadlines multiple times. But lectures are kind of high level and difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are pretty interesting, and the homework assignments are difficult but engaging. Every homework gets curved but are capped at 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: course material is actually interesting and relevant to the real world. lectures are SO boring and unhelpful. weekly challenges count for 40% of your grade and they are tough; he doesn't really help at all in class with those. the review about him being like joe biden? very true. slowww talker, rambles, hard to follow...weird

this guy is like no other...strangest IE class experience. nice person, wants people to learn, but his style is unique. 40% of your grade is based on weekly group assignments. tests were very tough- it's like he prides himself on hard exams. wouldn't take this professor if you want to enjoy the material or actually learn. prepare to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Answers questions on the spot and is clearly trying but this course is ... something else. Gives the whole IE department a bad name.
Feels like taking a class with Joe Biden

The perfect professor for over-achievers that want to put in a lot of work outside class and learn the material deeply. He gives a ton of homework and expects you to go over book chapters and modules outside of class, but he'll be extremely accessible for feedback and help too. Don't take him if you can't afford the time or need good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The class is structured to gradually build and teach the theory of modern supply chains. He gives great feedback on all projects. Make sure you choose a good group and work together. Tests are hit or miss with difficulty but are curved; just do your best and show your work for partial credit.
Quizzes, challenges weekly, 1 midterm, 1 final - There're a lot of material to read to complete challenges.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class structure is appalling. He doesn't teach and expects that you will go to class having read about the topic (from his really bad notes), take a quiz and do a weekly homework. He goes to class only to answer questions, to which he doesn't even provide a proper answer. The exam wasn't even similar to the quizzes, homework, or practice exams.

TLDR: Has a VERY POORLY structured class, recycles material from previous years, and puts a minimal amount of effort into the class. He makes you watch lectures and do most of the learning at home and spends time in class to answer questions. He provides Excel spreadsheets as homework, which makes learning the content infinitely many times harder.

This professor is creepy and condescending to students of color and he is very typical old school white man with 60s vibe towards people of color. He only invites white young jockey male lecturers and he randomly chooses students papers to select for completion and is rude.
might as well use Ted talk

The only highlight of the class was listening to his guest speakers. I learned more from them than I ever did from him. I wouldnt waste my tuition in his class. His tests are pure memorization from the textbook which is boring.
Lousy professor with little use. Hes also really condescending.
One of my all time favorites.

teaching style is dry and the class was useless. It was a waste of time and unless you are planning on being a sales, I would recommend you take other classes with tangible content. He comes off as condescending and arrogant especially to certain non-white students. One student had to see the assistant dean for his lack of grading criteria.

Vantine has no scruples and picks out students to bully . He gave me an arbitrary grade on a project which he could NOT justify . He didn't use a rubric. I raised the issue to the Assistant Dean who said often times, if professor can't explain it, it means they don't have a clear guide. Worst thing his class is all fluff.

He does a great job of trying to keep everyone awake at 8am. Even though the tests are a little hard he curves all of them and the class. There are also a bunch of guest speakers to switch it up and they were all incredible.

Professor Vantine is extremely boring. Everything that is on the test is on the lecture slides. But he includes some details from the book so the book is useful. Attendance is mandatory also, because he gives random pop quizzes. Overall, this class was a waste of my time.
Class content was helpful and interesting. He is a bit arrogant in his teaching style which can rub students the wrong way.
Great teacher!!! Read the chapters along with class slides and you will be fine.

One of the nicest and most helpful teachers I have ever had at GT. He knows a lot about International Business and brings in great speakers who can relate it to the real world. Not the most interesting stuff in the world, but he does a good job of covering the material. Goes out of his way to help if you go to his office hours.
He was great. We did a lot of extra things in class that added to the reading! Tests were pretty easy if you read the book and go to class. LOVED IT!
Fair teacher, but you learn everything from the book.  Doesn't teach much that isn't from the book.   However, a nice guy that wants his students to do well.
good prof
great teacher!

Attendance isn't required for this class at all. If the lectures are difficult to understand, as it was for me, I recommend studying the homework and the practice exams. The real exams will be just like the practice exams. I feel like Vempati is an easy grader compared to the other courses I've taken. If you study, it should be okay.
Slow enough for everyone to understand.
Great lectures and detailed examples. Really fair exams if you prepare the practice. But there is no "Piazza" and the resources are relatively scarce.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy tests and pretty good lectures overall.

This class is ridiculously hard, but it was clear from the beginning of the semester so not a problem. The homework was fine, took hours but tested the material well. The TAs were helpful too. However the exams did not test us on the material well at all and were 60% of the grade. I think 20% of my grade in the course was just matrix derivatives.
Hardest class I've ever take in 5 years. In hws you even don't understand what it's talking about and you need to prove it.

Class is hard, but the professor is amazing, Grading is not tough, and just for trying you can get some partial points. Also, you need to go to TA office hours to complete your homework. Also, course grading is pretty chill as well.
Ridiculously difficult class. Lectures don't make any sense. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favourite professor at Georgia Tech so far! Very caring; makes an effort to know everyone's name in even large classes and keep classes interactive. Excellent lecturer whose passion comes through when he lectures. Grading criteria is clear and the homework is very instructive.

No clear grading criteria but all based on grader's own opinion. Professor himself just disappeared from the online course. He gave the grader 99% of the power of administration and decisioning. Require students to do a lot of self-learning. Cannot find him in discussion thread or anytime necessary and don't know what he actually did for the class.

One of the worst classes in OMSA program. Lectures are so messy, not enough explanations, homework questions come from somewhere unknown. You will be very lost in this class although a lot of students maintaining an A. All pointless topics!

I took ISYE 6420 as part of OMSCS - my experience is limited to an online course. Although I received an A, I attribute this to the TA's, who made up entirely for the professor's absence. Dr. Roshan participated on EdStem fewer than 10 times total and did not have any presence running the course.

Used a book as a guide for the course, but rushed through the chapters. Mistakes on homework and tests are penalized heavily. Exam is much more complicated that any examples we go through in class or in the homework. Provided sections of the textbook to study for the exam, but a question came from a section that he specifically told us to skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Insufficient exam duration time for both the midterm and the end-term exams. The exams didn't test my subject knowledge but my R coding ability, which shouldn't be the case. Assignments take a lot of time and effort to complete. He rushed through a lot of chapters. It is more like covering a 5 or 6 credits course in 3 credits time.

This might be one of the WORST professors I have ever taken. Tough grader, bad teacher and shows no concern towards students. Attendance carries a grade even though this is a graduate level class. Homework grade for specific things that were not asked for, everything he teaches is surface level because he is rushing through the textbook. AVOID!

Waits until the last minute before homework is due to teach us what is required.  He goes over class time every single period.  When questions are asked, he does his best to answer, but often the response falls short of answering the actual question.  Unresponsive on Ed Discussion.  There are even several questions that have never seen a response.
Great content constitution. Tests are a bit tough, but you learn a lot.

Clearly knows a lot about the subject and works to improve his teaching abilities. I'm enjoying the class but it's a little inconsistent in difficulty and pacing. He is happy to take questions during lecture and his answers are almost always helpful :P He now uses coding/computer based exams which are challenging but graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he was great at teaching the material conceptually and was caring. However, the tests were 3 questions, 10 points each and were all in R and pretty confusing/ stressful. He always threw curveballs and you really had to be an expert at R to do well. I felt like I knew the material way better than my test grades indicated.

He asks difficult questions on exams over topics that are barely referenced in the lecture and lab. He removes FAR too many points for minor mistakes; my test scores were significantly lower than what they should've been. On the bright side, lectures are mediocre.

Don't understand why there was lecture and lab for a 3 hour class. Very random lectures that didn't really help, the only thing that was useful were the lab session led by the TAs. HW was easy but tests and the final were unnecessarily hard and he took way too many points off for the smallest things.

Lectures and homework assignments are very straightforward, however the content and grading of his tests are way too harsh. He made a third of our final about a topic we learned about briefly in one lecture and never had a test or homework assignment about. Also if you miss a part of a part of a question, could bring you down whole letter grades.

Professor Joseph grades very tough on all heavy-weight assignments. If you get one simple part of a question wrong on a test, it can set you back 10% points, no partial credit. His lectures are fine, but his grading is too tough and it's difficult to do well on large assignments as a result.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I respect his knowledge, but his lecture is too dry to learn anything. His lecture is only composed of hand-written notes full of derivations. His note on a random day has 8 pages, with a total of only 27 words including "see the textbook" at its end. I would rather have the course taught by a TA who can at least prepare some explanatory slides.
Tough tests but  you would learn a lot
I enjoyed this class, and all information was directly useful to understand and create models for my real employment. Thanks to Professor

Set up of the class is odd.  All of the homework is done using R software but the tests are all handwritten which has no overlap.  Making the tests difficult.  Knowledgeable about the material but boring at 8am.

Makes a lot of mistakes in class, can't reach him easily outside of it. Is rude to students sometimes. Kept altering instructions/they were never clear in the first place - especially for the final project. He randomly changes the guidelines and of course we fail to meet them. Glad to be done with class but had to leave a review here so people know

Before taking this course, take the nonlinear system. The professor swift through a lot of basic concepts. He will put the parts of final project into the last two homework, and he came up with additional steps the Friday before final week. He graded the final project with rules that he never mentioned before. You will learn something at the end.

Dr. Vela is one of the the best professors I have met during my time at Georgia Tech. His knowledge in robotics is truly amazing. He derived everything from scratch which may be frustrating for some but I truly enjoy seeing where it all comes from. In addition, he does some truly cool research which I was able to participate in. Really nice guy too

Worst professor ever. Stopped going to class cuz he would make so many mistakes in the lectures and students had to fix. Didn't get any lab grades until after they were all due. Then after they were all due new expectations were added. Students were never told to submit there code with the hw yet we were graded on that. Got many 50% cuz didn't know
rude

Such a hard class! (The hardest I've ever done?) He cares a lot about the material & is an expert in the field. Trying to get help as a distance student was difficult; he was a little rude sometimes, but he took time out of his day to help, which was great. The Homeworks/Project were very relevant to lecture material &VERY useful in real life

I disagree with the comments below. his teaching is fast-paced and he makes mistakes often, but his flow of logic is wonderful. He can point out what really matters. AND MATH IS CRUCIAL FOR ROBOTICS!!! He seems not preparing course seriously. The note he provides is actually from a previous student. BUT, I'm learning a lot from lectures and notes!

Very math heavy course, which would be fine if he actually knew how to do the problems. Stumbles through lecture, constantly changes his notation, his work is sometimes missing steps. Expect to read a ton in order to be able to do the weekly homeworks, his lectures are almost useless in that regard. Upside, no tests. Fun group projects.

He does not grade HWs until end of semester. There is no need to go to class; its useless and you don't learn anything. It is very hard to get in contact with him and his attitude is very unapproachable. Too lazy to take care of his students or class materials.

His class contained nothing but proofs and derivations. When it came down to putting the equations into Matlab he was useless in helping everyone. If you did see him in his office hours he always gave you the feeling that "how dare you come to my office". He is very intelligent but expects us all to be grad students even though the prereq is DSP

I took this class over the summer in a five week period and although it was an asynchronous course, Dr. Ventresca's love for teaching this class shone through. This was a legitimately fun subject to write and learn about and an A is all but guaranteed as long as you participate and provide thoughtful input.
Prof. Ventresca was an amazing lecturer, and made every single class an interesting discussion on current issues in sports. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Dr. Ventresca was very passionate about the subject and made it interesting. The class had no test but had a lot of writing/oral presentation type projects. He graded fairly and sometimes pretty leniently. Would definitely take him for the social science credit.

The worst professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech. Exams should not be worth 90%, and top of that hw that are worth 10% but require hours to complete. He provides no recording for reference, and his textbook is horribly written. He thinks he is teaching but in reality just writing scribble scrabble on the board.
the worst prof ever

Makes the already hard class demoralizingly difficult because of the way he teaches it. My gripes include his own notations for everything, extremely convoluted solution explanations, and brutal exams. If you are taking this class for auton thread but he is the only prof, take 3084 as the 4550 prereq and wait until a different semester for 3550

Avoid him to save your tuition and mental health. He relies solely on an obscure textbook he wrote, teaching via whiteboard with no recordings. Grading is 90% exams, 10% homework. After midterm1, enrollment dropped from 39 to 29. No one fully understood his lectures. If you don't believe it like I did, you may suffer for the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I dropped this class after about three weeks because every negative review about Erik is true. For context, I have a high GPA and even though this class only requires a 50% to pass, everyone I knew and myself dropped due to how difficult it is. Please do not waste your time with this guy. By far one of the worst professors in ECE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can respect how much effort he puts into making us understand the fundamental Theory. I won't ever fully understand some of the material he taught but the things I do know, I know to a T because of him. If you only care about grades avoid him but if you want to know the theory I highly recommend him. I was fed up now I'm thankful. 50% is passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emphasis is (almost) entirely on the mathematical side of control theory. Devoted 3 lectures to complex analysis and deriving the Residue theorem, which was only tangentially related to the syllabus material. 50%+ is a B and 75%+ is an A; this is not conducive to learning since you can pass with a 50% gap in your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid if you can. He assumes a level of mathematical background higher than most engineers I know. His test are only tangentially related to the material. Homework is very difficult. The majority of our time was spent on mathematical proofs with little discussion of applications. Sometimes genius does not translate well to teaching ability.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unless you are a math pro, I do not recommend this class, and many current and previous students agree with this. Consider taking it with someone else. He lectures by writing equations without explaining the logic or motivation behind them. The class lacks a textbook or coherent curriculum, so your only resources are his arcane and abstract notes.
The lectures are all math theory. There's no application based examples. If you do not have a solid background in proof-based mathematics, do not take this class.
He makes the class unnecessarily difficult by using weird notations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Verriest seemed to be trying to make the class as hard as possible. He expects you to memorize complex proofs and often assigns homework on topics he either (i) hasn't covered or (ii) did not mention in class but there is one sentence in the lecture notes about a related theory that you are supposed to understand the application for.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had at Georgia Tech. The material for ECE3550 is actually some pretty interesting stuff, as it prepares you to work on robotic and controls systems. Unfortunately Prof. Verriest makes it nearly impossible to learn with incoherent lectures. His tests are also extremely difficult and the final was worth 40%. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love theoretical math, so the class material was pretty interesting to me. This class is great for people who genuinely would like to understand the math and theory behind controls, so it may not be as practical as other classes. The one complaint I have is that sometimes Prof. Verriest would assign homework on things he hasn't taught yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: after teaching you his stupid math notation for a month and random stuff he finally gets to controls and you really find out how terrible he is at teaching. The worst class Ive ever taken a Georgia Tech. He spends the entire class rambling at the board and you are so far lost that you dont even know what you dont understand. Please dont do it.

The professor means to make his students not be just users of knowledge but be creators of knowledge. The proofs in homeworks and exams are not so difficult and will shed light on your future skills in designing control algorithms. A strong passion and talent for math is required but since control has a large bearing on math, it is reasonable.

This professor is a theoretical mathematician. If you love pure math, take this course. Otherwise, I don't recommend him bc a) he often gives homework problems not covered yet, or with important semantic errors b) he makes critical mistakes in lecture as he doesn't follow notes c) he teaches non-standard material/methods.

Very difficult professor, often homework and test solutions require high-level mathematics knowledge not taught in class, and the topics taught in class are very heavy into mathematical proofs with little direct application to control theory. I spent 10+ hours per week on studying and homework for this class and still had to drop.

Take ECE6550 under this Prof as a challenge. ECE6550 is listed as a pre-req for many other controls graduate courses.  You won't find many sub-in formula questions for this class, but rather, mathematical proofs underlying control theory. As a result, future control classes will come easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He really is a math teacher teaching an ECE class.  Expect lots of proofs and expect the exams to also be lots of proofs that you may not have seen before.

He has a deep understanding of the subject matter and is very enthusiastic and helpful. One of my favorite professors at Georgia Tech. Yes, his class has a lot of proofs, but it gives you a through understanding of the techniques used in control theory.

Worst professor ever. His tests & homework seem to be designed with almost sadistic fervor. You will learn NOTHING about control in this course. Taking this course under this professor is a BIG waste of time & money.

Do NOT take this professor's course if you want to learn anything practical in Control Engineering. He delves too deep into the math part and most of the time, there were no control concepts in sight. What was supposed to be an exciting class on Linear Systems, turned into a boring mathematical monologue. Unless you're in love with math, stay away.

Best prof I have. Don't know what the others are talking about. Always extremely helpful and builds great understanding of mathematics. After all, control theory is just mathematics. I highly recommend this professor. His methods have impacted my success in other classes.

Absolutely horrible! He should be teaching mathematics and not control theory. His exam questions have nothing but proofs and he spends most lectures doing abstract proofs. You'll learn more from Wikipedia than you ever will in his class. Definitely do not recommend him.
Useless. I agree with the other reviews here, his homeworks and tests are just trick questions. This guy is WAY out of touch.

This is teacher is no good. He does not teach what is in his syllabus. Instead he goes on for ever into useless proofs that have almost nothing to do with the subject matter. His tests were very hard, but he seems to be generous on the grading.If you want to learn something practical in Electrical engineering do not take his class.

This professor turned what was supposed to be a class on modern control theory into an abstract algebra class. He let his research interests get in the way of what should have been taught. His tests were full of trickery and class tests averages were often below 50%. This teacher loves proofs by the way, so don't expect to learn anything practical.

Be extremely wary of Yang's jet propulsion course. The department made him restructure the exams, so the class is no longer easy. The disorganized lectures throw hundreds of facts that you must recite on the exams with no notes to bring along with you. He also asked a question on the final that was material that actually was not even covered!
They made him change his curriculum, so it is no longer an easy class. Uneventful lectures and bizarre grading scheme. He's still probably better than all of the alternatives.

Yang is THE expert on propulsion, but his class will not teach you anything useful. The AE department recently made him change the course structure from online async tests to all in person tests and a project. It was obvious that this did not work well this semester, and the lectures did not prepare us at all for assignments. Very disappointing.

Incredibly disorganized and the whole class was just trivia at best... He's a nice person, and I wouldn't be writing a review if he hadn't just destroyed the class with a the final exam. He completely lied about the content, class was in uproar, and it wasn't possible to even get 80% unless you had equations that weren't in the 600 slides he gave.
He gave us a Christmas, halloween, and thanksgiving gift in the form of half of our final exam and asked for several peoples autographs, most entertaining teacher in AE at gt.

Dr. Yang is the most entertaining and kind AE professor at Tech. It's very conceptual and you'll learn the basics of propulsion engineering, as well as some economics behind the scenes. He may not make you a propulsion master, but he has some industry secrets up his sleeves and truly cares about the real-world success of his students.

Prof. Yang is probably the nicest AE prof you'll meet. His lecturing leaves something to be desired: not very organized and sprinkles *very* important facts here and there without any special detail. Homework tasks are mostly explanation based and not numerical which can be good and bad depending on how much you value being a propulsion engineer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: SUPER NICE GUY, but class had poor organization. He posts great resources, but hard to really parse their meanings in a useful way. Exams are open note and open internet, but will test your time management. HWs are more explanation based than numerical based. He does drop hints on what to expect on HWs or exams which is nice. Good, but not great.

Dr. Yang's class was the most unorganized class I've been in. No communication whatsoever about what is expected on exams. Sure, I wasn't a perfect student and should have gotten a B, but in no world did I deserve a C. The TA was unnecessarily harsh and basically did not know what material (or lack thereof) was being covered in lecture. Never take.

Dr. Yang is a great guy, and a fun lecturer that will teach you a lot about jet and rocket engines. However, his class on the other hand, has a complete and total lack of structure. He arbitrarily ramped up the difficulty midway through the semester, and the final exam seemed like a combination of trivia with complex thermodynamics on the side.

DO NOT TAKE. Dr. Yang is a nice guy but you will not learn a single thing. He expected us to do complex thermo problems without having taught any thermo. The grading was very harsh, would not take again.

Prof. Yang and his class are what you make it; for me, he was one of the best professors I've ever had and the knowledge and enthusiasm he brings to the class are what makes GT the #1 AE school. He wrote half of the books in jet and rocket propulsion- be ready to listen and enjoy. This is a lecture class, but for me, it kept me in AE.

Dr. Yang teaches at a very conceptual level. Exams and homeworks sometimes included calculations that hadn't been covered in class so try to take this right after thermo. The final project is the design of 3 different engines and analysis in MATLAB. The conceptual level topics did not provide enough material for the project to be done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you value getting an A rather than learning anything, take him. Yang is nice, caring, and funny. He's also quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had. The format of his course is disorganized, and his assignments are nonsense. I can confidently say I learned nothing in this class, and most of my peers feel the same way. Don't take him.
You'll get a good grade. You'll learn a lot of stories. Don't expect to learn enough propulsion to become a chief engineer

TAKE HIM! TAKE HIM! TAKE HIM! HE'S THE BEST! Jet & Rocket Propulsion is supposed to be one of the more difficult classes in AE, but the way Professor Yang teaches it makes the class so much easier than it would normally be! He asks students to suggest midterm questions, and HE LITERALLY ALLOWS YOU TO DO TEST CORRECTIONS FOR FULL CREDIT BACK!

Yang is amazing. Homework problems are directly from concepts discussed in class. Exams are take home open note and consist of conceptual questions (there's very little math) that from the homework, or sometimes he will tell you the exact questions and answers in class. He moves fast though since there's a lot of content to be covered in AE 4451.

Dr. Yang is probably my favorite professor I've had thus far. He's extremely knowledgeable, and his teaching style of AE 4451 focuses heavily on conceptual understanding and engine design considerations rather than mathematics. He very clearly states what will be on his midterms and is even willing to tell you the answers to it beforehand!

If you're looking for the math behind jet propulsion, this class isn't for you. If you're looking for a conceptual explanation of it, why it works, and the evolution of jet/rocket propulsion, this is your guy! Talks fast, so make sure you record, b/c pretty much everything he says is important. His class is more of a hist/evolution of jet/rock prop
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Yang is not a bad person. He is more of a businessman than an academic. He teaches mostly superficial and top level concepts. Don't expect lots of mathematical understanding of propulsion phenomena. If you ask something more in depth, you will be told to "read it by yourself". Slides are a series of pictures and lack explanations.

HTS 3033 Oxford Study Abroad. Daily readings, you don't have to read them, just make sure you know the general content of them. Discussion based class so make sure you participate a good amount. Quizzes are based on readings so no need to take in class notes. Very lax class and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved her! Took her at Oxford over the summer and she's easily one of the best lecturers I've ever seen. Dr. Viezure is super knowledgable and passionate and always has an eloquent, thought-out answer to any question you may ask. Make sure you do the readings (or don't, but make sure you still understand them) and you'll do great.
If you participate and do the assigned readings the class is easy and Dr. Viezure is extremely lenient and nice while also being informative.

Nice lady, but her class is far too much work especially if you're simply taking her class as a general ed. class like I did. Her class starts with simple hw assignments and 5 question in-class quizzes. However, near the end of the semester, she piles on many 1200+ essays and a roleplaying game far too close to finals week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: for quizzes, she looks to see that you have the right idea with a given author. grading isn't harsh along as if you can answer the reading questions, you'll be good. test are all essay-based, but they're not bad if you take notes/pay attention. in-class participation matter lots!! she's super sweet and you can tell her passion for the material.

Dr. Viezure's class is very fun and engaging if you are interested in the topic. She is very passionate about the subject she teaches, and she is extremely well-prepared! That being said, learning history is a time commitment; if you put in the effort and approach the course with the right energy, I guarantee you, you won't regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I used the "get ready to read" tag and I REALLY mean it. Pages of readings for every class; some are fun and interesting, but most readings and lectures will drag on and be boring if you don't have a preexisting hyper-fixation on medieval history. Dr. Viezure is easily the most passionate professor I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most passionate professors at Tech, certainly the most passionate history professor I've taken. Her classes are a blast; this is my second from her and she normally has her students play a role playing game for a third of the semester which is a super unique way of learning history and (in my experience) has been super effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Viezure was really nice, however there were a lot of dense readings which I did not find too enjoyable. This class was not difficult, as long as you participate sufficiently you should be fine.

Dr. Viezure is a fantastic professor, it just takes some time to get used to her teach style. Very heavy on participation (had a role-play simulation & used discord to discuss readings). Good bit of readings with quizzes on them, but you can get away with skimming. Doesn't give grades or feedback immediately, but is a soft grader

I really enjoyed my class with Dr. Viezure and am taking another one next semester. She is very reading and participation heavy, but also nice and forgiving. Her lectures tend to be a little rambling and the readings dense, but I enjoyed myself and never worried about my grade. Make sure you are present in discussions and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Viezure is super sweet but this class was very difficult for me because- as I found out- I'm not interested in European philosophers and that's all the class is on. Readings every night (very boring and hard to understand), weekly quizzes, and participation is huge- you won't get an A if you don't say something every class. Lucky I got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Viezure requires a TON of reading. The readings are pretty dense, too, so be prepared to spend a lot of time with the texts. However, she does a great job explaining them in class and making them interesting. Her grading is really fair and not too harsh. Just be prepared to participate! Can make the difference between a full letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Tech. He gives amazing lectures and explains concepts really well. I'm still not sure how he managed to make heat and mass transfer fun. He's also funny. The tests are tough but I truly learned a lot from this course. He brought back my passion for learning. This is the kind of professor who really grabs your attention.

Super quizzes are a really foolish idea, feels like you have an exam every week. Not conducive to learning. Granted I barely studied but I like the material. Scored above average on the final and made a C. I knew people who scored like 10 points below on the final but got a B. Silly course format but good lectures. Also takes -1/2 for incorrect t/f

His critique on tests is incredibly unhelpful and is usually just a question mark randomly or and random why. Go to TA office hours for help and make sure to attend lectures. He was extremely condescending and told us the test wasnt that hard. Made someone go to GROUP quiz when they were symptomatic and their covid results were taking a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Breedveld is the best ChemE professor Ive had at Tech. Ive barely passed most chemE classes, but was borderline A/B throughout this class. Everything is taught to the tests, the homework is often old exam problems. Hes a bit harsh in grading, & has a pretty blunt personality, but he truly sets you up for success, you just have to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This Professor will make you work your butt off. One of the most challenging courses I've taken. However, I feel as though I know this material better than any peers that did not have to pleasure of taking Dr. Breedveld. This man is extremely smart, but more importantly, he is just an all around fantastic Professor.

He's a good teacher but definitely not easy. Also, he's a bit snooty sometimes. He teaches difficult concepts fairly clearly but it'll take lots of practice to do well on his tests. Doing all the homework (even the optional ones every other week) is highly recommended but not a guarantee that the tests look like the homeworks.

Prof. Ganesh explains concepts very well and always makes sure that students had understood them fully before moving on to the next one. He is very enthusiastic and patient during lectures, and is always available after class to discuss topics. It is encouraged to ask and answer questions to get the most out of the class. Would highly recommended.

Prof. Ganesh's passion for the course content (SAT/SMT solving: theory, practice and real-world applications) showed in the lectures where a great deal of depth in the topics was covered. We were encouraged to ask clarifying questions making for an interactive atmosphere. The course project also allowed us to explore interesting research questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a graduate level course on SAT/SMT solvers. The prof covers every topic in great depth and explains concepts clearly, which is very important in the graduate level. He is available after class if you want to discuss topics related to the course or have interesting research questions.

Prof. Vijay's teaching style is highly systematic and focused, ensuring a smooth and effective learning process throughout the course. He is exceptionally approachable, always available outside of class to address questions and provide guidance, and explains complex concepts with patience and clarity. The course includes a research-level project.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is approachable and easy to communicate with, and extending homework deadlines is generally acceptable. The course material is well-structured and thoughtfully designed. While the content may be challenging for students unfamiliar with logic, the professor ensures to revisit all the basics.

Professor Vijay is great at explaining tough concepts in a simple way that makes them easy to understand. The course mixes theory and practical examples really well. Professor is quite approachable and encourages questions, making the class feel interactive and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: HE IS AWESOME. He is so nice. Easy class. Definitely recommend taking def. bods with him if you can.

Super chill professor, highly recommend taking defbods at GTE if hes an option. The lectures are interesting and he makes it very easy to get an A and he will always be willing to help. You should be fine to miss classes if you want to travel or something.

Chillest prof you will ever have. He clearly WANTS to help you get an A in the class. Very accessible outside of class. Very minimal HW (which he goes over in class sometimes too). He's very kind, and his exams are very clear. The first exam was ok. The second exam was a group "lab". And he basically told us what was on the final  :)

Dr. Taupin is a very patient and caring professor. Tests were easy if you did the homework and worked through lecture slides. You can sometimes get extra credit by going to office hours. The material was explained clearly and assignments were straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A more timid character, willing to help and gives tests and homework that fall on the easier side.

One of the most reasonable professors I have ever had. Bottom line he really just wants you to know the material and how to do the problems. As long as you learn how to approach and solve the problems on your own you will get an A. He is very accessible/approachable for help and very kind. A great teacher to have during a study abroad semester.

Vincent is an awesome Def Bods professor at GT Lorraine. His homework and tests were super easy, he made lectures fun and gave good feedback if students didn't understand material. If you can take def bods with Vincent at GTL, it's highly worth it because he turned one of the hardest classes at Tech into a breeze.

His lectures were very good and he was clearly knowledgeable about the material being presented. The tests were quite challenging with careful reading being key to get the answers correctly. There are easier sections for this class but I think it will be hard to find a better and more informative professor. I really understand the material.

Even though MSE 2001 is a difficult class because of its broad scope, Professor Vogel helped make it an enjoyable class because he was obviously passionate about the subject and was great at helping students. If you really study the material he gives you, you can get by with an A or B in the class.

The best professor I have had so far. His notes are fairly easy to understand, and I only had to clarify a few points. He is a very jovial and easy-going guy. I attended every one of his lectures. He is accessible outside of class, and willing to help students succeed. Tests are hard but fair. You will need to put in effort but you will learn.

all over the place, nothing makes sense, impossible without ai, she doesn't even know what we're doing, always holds us past time, expects us to always be available and act like this is the only class we're talking, everything is so disorganized. not even learning coding. would never take this again in my life even if i was half at gunpoint for rea
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course requires a HUGE time commitment. In the journal club sessions, each of the roughly 40 students presents and critiques one paper for about 30 minutes, resulting in extremely long meetings. The mandatory session times are inconvenient, scheduled either on weekends (8 am~3 pm) or on weekdays (5 pm~10 pm).

Lectures were super disorganized and the slides looked like they were from a decade ago. When it was time for projects, a bunch of her PhD students would show up. Honestly, they gave way better feedback than she ever did.

Easy teacher if you have a background in stats. Class is horribly organized, assignments always have errors in them, no slides/notes to follow if you miss class. Additionally, a major part of your grade is a group project, which has no rubric/guidelines. She obviously cares about her students, and the content, and her exams are relatively simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice person but cannot teach. You will have to learn it yourself. Useless lectures. Off topic and disorganized. Don't take her unless you really need the credit.

The content is easy, but the class is quite disorganized. The professor seems inexperienced with teaching, which causes the class to be quite confusing and chaotic. However, she is very caring, and will listen to and act upon feedback, so do not hesitate to contact her or the TA if in her class. Unique/interesting projects. Wish her the best:)
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very sweet, but her lectures are nonsensical and often are just repeating the same things over and over again. The class is very easy, but you won't learn anything. She never explains how to do problems, instead spending hours on end talking about how important biostats is. I'm convinced it's important, but I still don't know how to do it.

Class had a syllabus but did not feel like it. The concepts felt like they were generated from AI which made them wordy. (Ex. One week was themed "Machines of Loving Grace") While the class wasn't exactly hard, he didn't grade assignments until the last week so you really had no clue how you're doing.

Class was easy but completely disorganized. No assignments were graded all semester, so you never knew your standing. Instructions were unclear, attendance wasn't taken, and you could honestly skip until presentation day. The course was mainly open-ended conversations, and the professor was unreachable by email.

This has been the most unorganized class I've taken. The professor teaches in a extremely convoluted way, and we often have no idea what we're supposed to do in class sometimes. He also promised multiple times to return grades, yet as the semester ends, none have been posted.

instructions are always unclear and my friends and I were always confused. the beginning of the semester was extremely unorganized and we didn't have a syllabus to access for a while. take another prof if you can

Even getting the final grade of an A (which he put in days after the deadline only after many emails to him and the dean of IAC) was no reward compared to the torture of taking this class with him. No grades the whole semester. Pointless papers with no feedback. Unresponsive to emails. Save yourself, it could have been great with a different prof.
Worst experience of my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not post exam grades on Canvas, does not post any notes, no practice exams, tests are 90% of your grade, made us do three labs in class (which btw I have no idea what I got grade-wise on them because he did not post them), very harsh grader on exams. I have had literal master's students teach better. Worst prof ever idk how you can be worse
Toughest professor I have taken at gt. Take someone else to save urself and ur time

Wardi's GPA was 2.9 after curve. Every other professor this sem had 3.7-3.8 gpa. That's what happens if you get no notes, no practice exams, no grades back. Dr. West was a great professor, he teaches the course content well and is very willing to work with students to help them understand the content. He was very lenient on grading and offers a lot of extra credit.

Dr. West did a great job in 3550. I was happy to come to lecture every time, as he enjoys teaching students material he really loves. He is tough and the content can get difficult, but the exams are very fair and do indeed test your understanding. Perfect balance of a tough Tech ECE course and knowing success meant understanding. Awesome prof!

Mick West is a chill guy and pretty lenient on grading so he doesn't try to hurt your grades. Huis lectures aren't very dynamic though he normally just reads off slides and it's hard to learn the material without Youtube videos

This was Dr. West's first time teaching ECE2040, but I thought he did a great job! The content can be pretty difficult, and he goes through lecture slides pretty fast sometimes without thoroughly explaining content/formulas, but overall, he was a good professor to have. He also has a good sense of humor!

I'm taking him online in covid summer. Knows and loves the material he teaches, but I wish he'd do more example problems in class. The homeworks were great and prepared me for the exams, but I had to figure out a lot by myself because he didn't do enough examples. He's tough, but I've learned a lot with him and his research is really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love the class. The homework is not too hard and not too easy. The group projects stuff are cray though for certain topics but she's pretty caring with the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Passionate, knowledgeable, helpful and kind. Difficulty is moderate, homework is long, and exams can be difficult, but lectures are effective. She is very responsive to questions, and its clear she wants to see students learn. 

Make sure to start homework early, and learn the "why's" of the math rather than just the processes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 3215 is not an easy class but this professor is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. She makes the tests from the homework problems, so there are no real surprises on the exams. That being said, the exams are not easy and make up almost the entire grade. Relatively generous with partial credit.

Wenjing Liao was a great professor, her lectures primarily came from the textbook directly, and as long as you did the homework and read the textbook, you were guaranteed an A as her test questions came from the hw. The semester I had taken this class was her first time teaching, so the difficulty might change significantly in the coming semesters.

Dr. Liao has been my favorite professor in my time at GT. Fantastic lectures, explains clearly, and is accessible outside of class. Her HW's give a good understanding on how to study for the exams. 5 HW, 2 exams, 1 class project which was very fun. Overall, 10/10. Try and attend her lectures! I hope to take more courses with her during my PhD here.

Dr. Liao is incredibly brilliant and an amazing professor. Her lectures were very dense with mathematical notation which was difficult for my limited proofs experience at the time, but, that's to be expected from numerical analysis. She was deeply caring of her students and was quite accessible. Love her and hope I get to take her again.

I would give Dr. Liao a 3.5/5 tbh. She's a good teacher and does make herself available after class. But it honestly felt like she made the class harder than it needed to be. Many other ME majors took this class thinking it would be an easy A, but it definitely wasnt. Had to work a lot more than I expected to end with A. Exams got pretty tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liao is clear in lectures and makes excellent lecture notes. Office hours are very helpful. Grading isnt super tough but there are only 6 graded assignments total. Overall very highly recommended for probstat
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liao is incredible. She takes student feedback very, very seriously and will try to accommodate and help students. She really wants us to do well. On the other hand, prob/stats is very hard and needs a good amount of work put into to make sense. Do the necessary work and you will do well.

This was her first semester teaching so she might make it harder. Statistics has historically been my worst subject, but she made it bearable because she is good at lecturing although she tends to repeat herself, which you'll appreciate later when the material gets harder. She follows the (free) textbook, which can help you get your bearings;do HW.

Dr. Liao is the best professor I met at Georgia Tech! She explains concepts clearly in class and engages with students. She is very willing to help us understand the material both in class and outside class. She truly cares about our feedback and adjusted the course accordingly (added practice tests to make exams more predictable).

I absolutely loved Dr. Liao. She is extremely caring and takes student's inputs about assignments into consideration. There were 5 quizzes and 2 midterms when I took the course however she had 3 different grading options that still allowed for you to do well if you did bad on one of those. Go to lecture (or watch it on your own); they are amazing.

Very nice person, encourages questions and always clarifies. Lots of extra credit opportunities. There's 5 quizzes, 3 midterms, 1 final. The hardest is the final so work on the quizzes and midterms. Overall pretty positive experience.

Great person and excellent prof! Gives A LOT of examples and makes summaries with steps to perform each method. Lectures are long but clear and organized.
