She has a positive atitude towards teaching and cares about students' inputs. Exams and quizzes are lengthy with long calculations, but closely related to lecture content. Had 2% extra credit.

Dr. Liao is an amazing professor. Her lectures can be quite hard to follow, but she does her best to help everyone understand. She genuinely wants to see every student succeed and is very understanding and approachable. Probably one of the best professors I've had--cares more about student learning than the numbers in the grade book.

This class is mostly reading the textbook and memorizing terms. You have to fight for an A, grade = 5 tests basically. I don't know how people were dropping 100s on exams, I wish I knew before taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: be ready to read EVERY SINGLE PAGE of that textbook because his exam questions WILL have a random question from the tiniest block of text in the book. not joking. if you have good memorization then it will help. he confused himself sometimes during lectures and wasn't the greatest speaker but overall was a nice guy. exams & quizzes worth everything
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only uses 5 exams as grade makeup. Drops lowest. Very hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wheeler focuses all of his exams on minute details in the textbook or lecture. For the exams, be prepared to have extremely specific facts memorized in order to do well. Additionally, a majority of your grade is made up of tests, so make sure to do well on each one or it's really difficult to maintain a high grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades based on 4 mcq exams, optional final replaces lowest midterm. He's a good lecturer, makes class interesting, but attendance isn't necessary.  Heavy memorization, but if you attend lectures consistently, know general concepts, it's not hard. No extra credit. TAs are great, lock in w lecture slides. not easy A, but doable. textbook not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you want an easy A. The lectures are interactive and informative, but the tests are poorly written. It's like the professor wants you to read the nooks and crannies of the textbook for some questions. If you must take him, just skim the textbook and give all his slides to AI for practice questions. "Psyc is an easy A" 😂

Lecture-heavy class, but the material is relatively easy and just memorization that you can find with the online textbook activities. When I took it, you could either take only tests or have a combination of tests and homework; I just did the tests and passed relatively easily. I enjoyed his lecture style a lot and highly recommend attending them.

PSYC 1101: The lectures were interesting, but don't take this class if you're not prepared to write down ALL lecture information and read EVERY sentence of every chapter he assigns. As someone who did read each chapter, took notes and studied for hours each exam, the class is ridiculously specific, with many test questions that don't make sense.
About 10 pop quizzes throughout the semester, so attendance is pretty much mandatory. Exam questions come from powerpoints and textbook that needs to be read outside of class.
If you can help it, take another professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She has very high expectations for a class where a lot of students haven't written a research paper before. I would attend office hours for extra guidance, but her advice was sometimes unhelpful and/or confusing. Also, participation is credit given when you speak, not just credit given for showing up. I don't recommend taking this class with her.

Dr. W is the best INTA4500 prof! Participation & attendance is a must. If you approach the class earnestly & show you care about the research, it's an easy A. However, you have to put work into this course. The assignments are not something you can do last minute so plan accordingly! Take in the feedback, apply it, and you should be good.
mixed opinions on the class. a lot of reading and a harsh grader with high expectations. however great lecturer and very responsive.

She turned a stressful, enormous original research paper into something manageable and enjoyable. She breaks it up into mini assignments, (work on them well in advance). She assigns a lot of reading to help, but I only read a few. For the final paper, she only expects a good first draft, and she emphasizes explaining decisions over perfection.

Very funny and very qualified. Dr Whitlark can be a tough cookie, but if you participate and show interest in the class and subject material, you should have no issue. She is blunt about grading, but for a pro-seminar class that's important. Overall one of my favorite courses I've had at Tech. Whitlark was insightful and always helpful.

One of the worst experiences for me; don't take her class if you aren't willing to put in lots of effort for a social science class. Readings before every class (sometimes up to 70 pages). One semester-long paper, and a final that's essentially essay-based. Who would have thought this would be my lowest grade (and I took physics here).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Definitely fave prof I've had at Tech. She is SO smart and a great lecturer. Also not too bad of a grader - she tells you exactly what she wants, so if you give her that you can get an A. Attendance isn't mandatory technically but it pretty much is if you want to pass.

FOR 1553 Likes to show the theory of everything he teaches, and in that regard he is good, but he does this and glosses over the stuff that we need to know for the exams, luckily the other professors post great material including practice exams. The friday classes are great too if you get a good TA, and I learned more there than the actual lecture.

Great with answering questions in and outside of class. Cares about the material and does a good job teaching. Lectures are proof heavy, whereas the tests are mostly computation, but they introduce so much more to the subject. I definitely learned a lot and have grown my appreciation for math greatly.

Pretty knowledgeable, but only teaches proofs which are not useful for the test and makes the material more confusing. We did not do many examples in class so it was hard to study for the test because I had to teach myself then. The main way to do well in this class in general is just review the practice exams which are very similar to the actual.

awful!! during lectures he would go on 10 minute+ tangents just to realize (or have to be told by a student) that all the work he was doing was wrong. He would then erase it all, write the correct answer, and move on. This happened every lecture I learned nothing, in fact I just left more confused. 
if you dont alr know the class - AVOID!!!
Impressed by Professor Van Why's command of mathematics and his careful instruction. Although he does pronounce his "you's" weirdly -- as in English Yew.

Overall 1551 is a good class and he is a good professor. He follows detailed lecture notes which he posts after class. Tests do require keen attention to detail, so do pay attention to how problems are solved as grading is very specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very blunt and honest, but in a constructive way; didn't sugarcoat what we would need to succeed both in the class and in the industry once we graduate. even with the class being new, she made it insanely effective. she's very accessible and gives great feedback while letting students run their own projects and learn for themselves.

Professor Whitlow does as good as she can in this course. The course content is boring, but helps students to figure out the path they want to take with their CS degree. Absolutely every piece of information provided in this course can be found on the CoC website. There was a project at the end that had us proof why our degree track would be chosen

Whitlow can tend to focus on herself during lectures which can be annoying for the student. Overall, CS 1100 is nothing serious and it would be hard not to get an A so the lecturer is not really important.

Took for entrepreneurship- she said on first day she has given out only 1 B, and almost all (probably around 100 now) As. You get out as much as you want to put in for the class, some students asked questions and made good connections, others showed up and worked on other class HW. Easy A if you do the easy work, good opportunities from class
Such a dumb class, class shouldn't even exist. Professor was asinine and I didn't learn anything that I couldn't learn from about five minutes of Googling.

This class itself is mainly a giver of resources rather than lecture-based and Prof Whitlow does a great job at giving those resources and explaining how they can be used. The only drawback in my opinion is her other roles are her priority so some assignments and resources are posted quite late, but it is understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Whitlow understood students had other priorities, but also provided a few bits of helpful advice when it came to writing resumes, applying for internships, etc. This is an easy A if you do the assignments on time. Attendance is not required, but there are required participation activities that you can complete on your own time.

This class is a free A if you do the few assignments, and its pass-fail. The lectures were borderline useless though, and she often just talked about herself or read off of the website. I learned very little new information, but if you need to ask her things she is approachable.

Professor Whitlow is great! She gives amazing feedback and her lectures are pretty informational to attend. She also addresses some challenges we might face in CS over the years. Further, she's very caring and understands the workload we have.
Easy A, but you don't even need an A since it's pass/fail.
Barely any homework so gradewise, this class is an easy a. Whitlow herself is clearly knowledgable and caring but in general lectures were boring / not very useful.

Whitlow is a relatable professor and she understands the workload we can get because she's currently a student too. She assigns few homeworks, but they are normally large/busy homeworks, and she assigns participation assignments based on what that day's class was about. If you just show up and do the work, it's a really easy A.
Very easy class but utterly useless course content. Professor seems very unenthusiastic about teaching but it doesn't really matter because the class is meant to be an easy pass.
CS1100 is not a difficult class and only requires attendance and some CS/CM degree related content. Professor Whitlow is lenient and a good instuctor.

This class was pass/fail when I took it. Content of the class is completely useless if you are upperclass. Ended up with A/B ish without really trying. Maybe put in 10 to 20mins per assignment which are given each week. If you have a pulse and turn in all assignments, you should be able to pass this class without any issues.
The class is rigged so you have to do the final project. The work you have to do is minimal, but boring. Maybe it's different in person, but I wish this class wasn't a graduation requirement.

She's a great professor, and the class is really easy. The class was virtual, and there were random participation checks (not quizzes but breakout group activities every so often). Overall, the homework is pretty easy, and every assignment has a rubric. If you follow it perfectly for all homeworks, you should be fine. The professor is nice as well.
Good professor.

Took Whitlow for CS1100. Really an easy class, maybe max 20min of work a week, and even easier because it's async. I would say I learned a bit though and it's nice to get some resume critique and learn a bit more about threads.

This was a class were you hear successful entrepreneurs from GaTech lecture about their journey and give good advice. Class met once a week on monday nights for 1-2 hours. Work was extremely minimal and getting an A is super easy. I even think Jenn wants to give everyone an A in this class. Recommend even if you dont want to be an entrepreneur.

This was one of my favorite classes at GT. I had an amazing experience in this course, and Dr. Wheaton does a great job of breaking down everything to a level that is understandable. He prefaces the class by saying we'll understand the intricacies behind the startle response, and he really helped build our understanding to that level.

Professor Wheaton is great! He does a great job of covering just what is necessary for understanding human neuroanatomy without going too deep into the chemical and biological processes. I really enjoyed the course and would highly recommend others check it out!

Dr. Wheaton was one of the best professor's I've had at Tech. He takes what could be an extremely dry topic and makes it interesting by connecting different parts of the brain and behaviors. There's a lot of material and keeping all the different pathways separate is difficult, but lectures are enjoyable and he offers a lot of extra credit!

Dr. Wheaton is a very well-respected and intelligent professor that has a great understanding of his craft. His presentations are clear, and he covers all course material very well. The course itself is quite difficult (simply the nature of neuroanatomy, brains are complicated), but he provides regular extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Wheaton. He's just the coolest, smartest guy and I want him to be my best friend/mentor. I had him for human neuroanatomy which is a REALLY hard class. DO NOT take this class thinking its going to be easy, cause it won't be, but Wheaton is just amazing and he gave a lot of opportunities to raise our test grades. He's super nice too

Took Neuroanatomy as a pre-health elective, thinking it would be relatively straight forward and easy. Boy, was I wrong. Even though he teaches straight from the slides (which he provides online), test questions are incredibly detailed and require a lot of thinking and familiarity with the material. He did offer very fair and helpful extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The goat. His lectures are incredibly informative, and he's very clearly well-versed in what he's teaching. The content is very in-depth, and he "soft enforces" attendance by not publishing any lecture notes until exams. So you either attend lecture or already have a very in-depth knowledge of Java. Homework is long but helpful. Exams are fair.

Chambers is him. He explains stuff extremely clearly, practically, and is a very genuine + kind person. He cares about student success and it's clear that he wants everyone to succeed. He has lots of experience with the class and teaches in an accessible way. I knew very little Java going into the class and I'm now very comfortable with it.
Great professor, considerate, knows the course content well (he's been the head TA of CS 1331 for several years in the past)

He did an amazing job. There weren't many outside resources for you to use but he did a great job explaining everything in class. You could always go up to him afterwards and ask for clarification on something too and he would explain it more in depth if needed.

Awesome dude who's really passionate about teaching intro CS in an applied manner that helps students in the long run. 

Would heavily suggest his class. I personally didn't go to lecture, but I would suggest going since he teaches CS fundamentals that are beneficial for internships, work, etc.

He was good, especially given that this was his first semester. Exams are mostly fair, the final did have an entire section that wasn't directly covered in lectures, but based on the knowledge of Java that everyone should have by the end of the class it was definetly fair (one homework was very related to it as well).
He gave good lectures and was helpful to talk to. However, given this was his first semester teaching there weren't many resources to study with. His tests were fair though.
Great lectures, seems to care a lot about what he's teaching, and doesn't try to screw you over with the exams.

He made all the tests fair until the final, it was not a good reflection of what was taught in class. I did really well all semester, and studied hard for the final, but he put something that was brushed over in one lecture, had only 4 recitation slides for and is mostly a 1332 topic; it was worth 50% of our final which outweighs all midterms.

Chambers is awesome!! The exams truly reflect what was taught in class. At no point did I think, "Is this man going to screw us over by putting something random on this test?" Attendance is done through an online participation activity, which you don't need to be in class for. He's funny and knows his stuff!! Very similar to AP CSA tbh
hes him. nothing else i can say
He is the goat

AMAZING PROFESSOR, actually teaches the subject like you've never learned Java before. I failed this class before, am taking it with him, and am now on track for a B or an A. Caring towards students, actually wants them to succeed, and exams are RELEVANT to what is learned in class, not deceiving or difficult.

Absolutely amazing professor. Lecutres feel like IRL Organic Chemistry Tutor. Actually an amazing teacher, cares about students, and wants us to succeed. Doesn't stroke his ego by making hard tests or anything of the sort. 1000% would take again, and I hope to get the chance to in upcoming semesters.

W Teacher. Dude is the goat. Take this class if you want to pass and actually learn the material. Plays music and gatech football highlights at the beginning of class, and always walks in with a chick-fil-a lemonade. Im tryna be like bro when I grow up fr.

Really nice professor that genuinely cares about his students. Starts each lecture with football highlights which is great. Great in office hours and explains things well. If theres a question that brings up something he doesn't know he tries to answer it via coding demonstrations which is nice
Hes goated at teaching 1331.

Dr. Stern is amazing. His lectures are so amazing, and you can tell he is really passionate about the class. His examples during class keep you engaged and this was genuinely one of my favorite classes I took at Tech. Test questions comes from lectures as long as you go and study a little you will be fine.
After completing 5 in-class assignments, you never need to come to class. The tests can be self-studied using the slides in a few hours the night before. Very easy class.

He is a very fun/engaging lecturer and I enjoyed the content. Some tests questions were tricky and he would add in minor details that he would only say in class. The final consisted of some of the hardest questions taken from the 4 midterms, but if you go to his office hours to review your tests it will be easy.

Dr. Stern gave great lectures. He does a lot of story-telling to keep the lectures engaging. Beware of the random attendance checks. His assignments didn't take long to complete. Exams covered material discussed in class, so if you study and remember the material, you will pass :)
Dr. Stern is one of the best profs at TECH!

Dr. Stern is very good at making the lectures engaging and adding humor. Very little work outside of class, the assignments are very easy and not very time consuming, and the exams are over the lecture content. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does give in class assignments sometimes. You can miss a few without hurting your grade. Would take again

Dr. Stern is very fun to listen to and adds lighthearted humor to his lectures to keep them engaging! He always makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving on and never makes anyone feel outed for asking a question. Just make sure to go to class because most of the test material will be pulled from lectures! I would absolutely take again!

Great prof. Technically not mandatory attendance, but there are several random in-class assignments (only 5 get graded, the rest get dropped so missing several lectures will not hurt you). Tests are straight from his slides that are on Canvas, with just a few questions from lectures that you can usually guess correctly.

I took PSYC 1101 with him. Attendance was not mandatory but there were random participation assignments given throughout the year. He gives very engaging lectures so attending class is pretty fun. I went to lecture often so exams were not very difficult. I would highly recommend taking this professor for a great time in introductory psych!

Attendance isn't mandatory, but the lectures were the best part of this course! I spent maybe an hour outside of class otherwise: his lectures were clear with great analogies and examples. There are random in-class participation grades. Great professor who makes a memorization-heavy class really enjoyable.
Best prof ever

Dr. Stern is easily my favorite lecturer in my time at Tech. His lectures were fun and engaging, and his assignments were directly tailored to them (he also posted all his powerpoints, but they don't quite have the same depth as his lecture). Assignments were all doable, and overall the class was awesome. 100% recommend.

Dr. Stern makes every lecture fun and memorable! I genuinely enjoy that class and look forward to it. The lectures are very engaging and interesting. A lot of information is covered in a short time, but exams and assignments are pretty straight forward. Be sure to keep track of dates as he does not give reminders often
Stern should be a go-to for anyone taking intro Psych. Transformed what could have been a tedious, memorization-heavy class into a pretty decent time overall. Cool dude.

Funny professor, engaging lectures. Everything is clear and on the slides making the tests fairly straightforward if you can just process that information. Work is minimal, basically just 30 min per week outside of showing up to lectures.

Great lectures, even though not technically mandatory, show up anyways

Easy class. Weekly short reflections, occassional in-class assignments, 4 larger assignments, and 4 hours required research participation, but it's all very low effort. Exams are multiple choice + fill in the blank. Exam 2 has a low average, not because it is harder as Stern claims, but because he gives no reminder or announcement for it.

William Stern is the best professor I've ever had at GT and inspired me to get a PSYC minor. Social Psychology, specifically was amazing. He covers a lot of material yet still keeps it engaging and easy to understand.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Dr. Stern made me excited to learn about psychology every week through interesting, informative, and entertaining lectures. He's incredibly charismatic and his lectures are quite clear. Attend lectures and you'll do well on all the exams.

Dr. Stern is a very enthusiastic lecturer who uses modern and relevant examples to teach the concepts his class covers. He covers all of the test material in his lectures and always takes time to address questions as thoroughly as he can. He also holds review sessions which double as extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Stern is an amazing professor! His lectures are incredible (textbook is available but definitely not needed if you pay attention to lectures) and entertaining. Would definitely take the class again!

i had him for social psyc. and loved it. it's an easy but informative class, just be careful with assignment deadlines, as he won't always remind you. extra credit is awarded for doing well in review sessions, but you probably won't need it. he's understanding with a lot of personality.

Prof. Stern is pretty good at teaching the content. Lectures can be a bit content-heavy but he uses a lot of pictures and anecdotes to make it easier to process. Participation isn't mandatory in the sense that he takes attendance, but on random days he will give an in-class assignment and some exam questions ask about examples he only gave in class

Prof Stern is a fun prof to take any psychology class with. In social psyc, if you attend the lectures, study for the midterms and the final, and turn in all the assignments on time, you will succeed. His lectures are very clear and the papers are quite easy. Just put in your side of the effort and you will succeed!

Dr. Stern is a great professor! Grades consist of short reflections, random in class activities, 4 short assignments ~500 words during the semester, and 4 research hours obtained by surveys or alt. assignments if

Professor Stern is a great professor! He cares for his students and is very accommodating. He also makes lectures fun and adds a healthy competition in class. Quizzes are pretty decent and not many assignments in class. I actually learned in this class without taking much pressure at all.

I had Dr. Winders for Food and Society. He was clearly passionate about the course content; he even authored a book related to the class, "Grains." While tests make up 70% of your grade, they are all based on info discussed in lecture, where he would also allude to test questions. If you are somewhat interested in food, this is an easy class.

the tests are fairly easy relative to the lectures since a lot of it is just pure memorization. there is good portion of writing in the class for homeworks and exams. one thing is that he grades pretty strictly on written portions and can have minor points taken off for smallest things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Winders was extremely kind and while he may talk extremely slow in the videos, he really did make the class enjoyable w/ his passion and flexibilty. The papers are long, but not horrible. Someone complained abt the quizzes not being open-note but its literally a college class idk what they expected. I only wouldnt take again bc LOTS of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: To clarify the negative comments below, just watch his lectures on 2x speed, write out bullet points according to the exam study guides, and skim the readings to get a basic understanding. His exams really are not that difficult if you know most of the definitions and concepts, and make sure to clearly define class concepts in your essays.

This class had a lot of reading and writing, but if you put in the time to watch all the lectures, it is a very enjoyable and easy class that does broaden your perspectives. He is very understanding, thorough, and gives students a nice challenge to apply their knowledge and also develop critical thinking about real-life concepts or problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are great, but tests are hard and aren't open notes. If I had known that beforehand, I wouldn't have signed up.

There are at least 25 pages of readings every week. Some of them are very hard to read, since they cover a lot of concepts and use older English. The tests have Honorlock on them and are closed-notes, and direct questions about the readings are asked, making it unfair if one doesn't have a photographic memory of the lectures/readings in their head.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had him during a late summer session. He uses lockdown browser and has a quiz and essay every week. Lockdown quizzes include short essay questions. He grades harsh, especially for a summer class. Its hard to get an A on essays and quizzes. If you think this will be an easy summer elective A, you're wrong, he will make you really work for it.
He is very knowledgeable about sociology and gives good (but long) lectures. Good grader.
Heinously boring lectures. Made us take exams in the classroom on lockdown browser

The course was delivered async during summer session. There are a LOT of readings and several lectures to watch each week. Professor Winders, while knowledgeable, talked too slowly, to the degree that 2x speed was necessary to absorb information in a reasonable timeframe. The writing assignments did not have a rubric, and feedback was subjective.

Dr. Winders is extremely caring and flexible. He is super passionate about the subject and overall a very nice guy. His lectures can be a bit slow at times, but I would usually watch them in 2x speed and still do well on the quizzes. Lots of reading, but you can skim. Quizzes/exams are cake!

All of the lectures are prerecorded and follow a MWF pattern for watching them, but you dont have to. The lectures are kinda long and not the most interesting, so it is worth your time 2Xing them. The readings are some that you can skim through to get the info you needed. Overall, I did not find it the most interesting class, but easy to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class wasn't too bad. It was one my first ever college classes and it was online in Summer 2021. TONS of reading and lecture watching. HIGHLY recommend watching the lectures in x1.5 or x2 speed because they are long and dry. The writing assignments were fine, but the quizzes were a little tedious. But overall, I got the credit and got out.

Took an asynch class with him so lectures were prerecorded. They ran long but were well made and he was respectful and always available over email when I needed anything. Assignemnts were light and easy as were quizzes, and the final was reused quiz questions. Easy, pain-free class overall. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was completely asynchronous. Office hours were weekly on Zoom. Lectures were recorded, and most had captions, so you could put them on 1.5x or 2x speed and still understand him. There's a lot of reading, but he gave us study guides for each quiz, with only a few general questions that weren't on the guide. Very nice guy.

He was very lenient and allowed for extra time if you need to get an assignment done a little late. He taught mainly by lectures but a few outside videos were used in the class. There is a lot of reading, but none of the reading requirements take more than 30 minutes to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Winders is an easy teacher. The class is entirely made up of lectures which I had to speed up a good bit just because they are long and he can speak slow sometimes. However, as long as you watch the lectures, you could do without reading the numerous textbooks as the lectures are based on the readings. Quizzes are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Winders was really great. Quizzes, tests, and writing assignments are based heavily on the pre-recorded lectures, so as long as you even somewhat pay attention, youll do well. There was a lot of reading but the textbooks were easily accessible on online platforms so no purchase necessary. He was very lenient and I would take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure that you focus on the readings and listen to his commentary on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really easy class as long as you take notes on lectures and do the readings. I just skimmed the readings and I was fine. He says to do the readings before the lecture, but don't do that!! Do the readings after the lecture because he talks about the readings during the lecture and SKIM! Easy A!!
Lot of readings but other than that, the class is pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Winders was super nice in my first SOC class and was really interesting after class too. I really recommend this class for everyone to take and learn more about our society with a relatively minimal workload.

His lectures are sometimes longer than necessary because he talks slowly, but they are prerecorded videos (online course) so you can just watch at 1.5x. The exams are entirely based on lecture content and readings, so as long as you take detailed notes and keep up with the readings, you'll be fine. He is a pretty chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class online, there weren't any online classes to attend, but there were office hours. This class is very lecture heavy, I took a lot of notes, but I didn't mind it since this class was interesting. There were only 3 exams and 3 small assignments. There's no extra credit but you'll be fine if you just keep up with the lectures.

Pretty standard teacher. 2 tests, 3 short but chill papers, and a heavy final. You honestly just need to take notes on the lectures, do the study guide he gives, and you'll most likely get an A on the tests. Readings are big in this class, but they're not hard. Learned a lot, but some content just required basic logic.

While the class is easy, Dr. Winders lectures drag. He basically circles around one idea/concept/topic over and over. Not sure if it's just the nature of sociology as a whole, but the class seems to state a lot of what's common sense. Also, Dr. Winders will explain graphs and diagrams as though you're at the intellectual level of middle schoolers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this course remotely and never met a single person in the class. This was hard but lectures are pretty explicit. Readings are super interesting and never skip them! TAs and Dr. Winders were always very accessible and excited to respond. Super interesting course, maybe a little too much readings and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took QUP section of sociology (online) over the summer. Dr. Winders is very organized and will respond very quickly to emails/any questions you have. He is an enthusiastic lecture, but speaks really slowly, even in video lectures. Readings are pretty interesting, although a bit outdated. Keep up with the readings or you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I am taking Dr. Winders for an online version of Social Movements. He had until mid June to create a course plan, and it is the worst made class Ive ever had the displeasure to take. Not available for consultation, ridiculous quizzes, no email or correspondence from him. Just heres the reading and videos, have fun. The worst course Ive had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super chill dude. Knows what he's talking about. 5 quizzes, 2 papers, and a final. Quizzes and the final were all multiple-choice questions. They're based on the lecture notes. The papers were super easy. Be ready to read the textbook. The stories are super easy to read; it's not like a regular boring textbook. You'll enjoy it. Easy class!!!

Grade breakdown: 3 short papers to write - 10%, 2 tests - 26% each, 1 final - 34%. Obviously, you have to do well in the exams to do well in the class. Just read through the lecture notes a few times. Readings are annoying, but you only have to know the gist of what happens. Easy A, as long as you have the words from his ppt presentation down
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very few assignments and tests so its important to do well on them. Lectures aren't super interesting but the class is easy enough. Readings aren't super important but lectures are so as long as you take notes or get them from someone you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is lecture heavy and very boring, but it is an easy A. There is lots of reading required, but you can get by without doing it. This class is very low stress.

Professor Winders is a really good instructor in the sense that he truly cares about what he's teaching. The class is EXTREMELY reading heavy - be ready to read or you will struggle to pass. The lectures get boring fast, and he's very student-discussion oriented. Just make sure you write down the slides and pay attention every now and then.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It is important to be in class because he doesn't post all the power points and 90% of what's on the quizzes comes from lecture or class discussion. He is very passionate about what he is teaching and an all around enjoyable professor to have!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Never thought I could be so interested in sociology! Lectures can be long, but he makes them interesting and I don't mind going to class. A lot of readings but they're interesting. Quizzes were straightforward and as long as you paid attention to concepts you'll do well. Would 100% take him again if I get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Seriously the worst professor I've ever had. He's nice in class but a few weeks into the semester I had to go to the hospital because I was diagnosed with pretty serious and heavy stuff, I went to his office hours to try and ask to work with me, and he basically told me I need to withdraw from the whole school and he didn't care about me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took his class in the late short summer session, and it was a good choice. He really cares about if his students are learning, and he will go the extra mile to re-explain things that he thought he explained poorly before. He tends to be a tough grader so, word of advise- on the tests/quizzes, make your answers concise and to the point.

I had him for a summer short session so the amount of reading outside of class each day was unreal.  However towards the end of the semester I learned you could get away with not reading as long as you paid attention in class and took good notes.  He is a great professor who cares about students and Social movements.

Very easy class.  He makes the lectures interesting as well as the readings outside of class.  He is a good guy who cares about his students and his profession.  Would recommend.  Btw I had him for summer short session, and the class was well worth it.

Professor Winders' class had several readings each night, but each was relatively interesting. His lectures were interesting, but would sometimes drag on, especially since he likes to teach until the very last minute of class. The quizzes were pretty easy and so was the final.

Professor Winders is very engaging and knows how to connect with his students. There are many readings each night, but they are interesting and enjoyable, which makes it easy to remember the course material as discussed in class. If you do the assignments and readings, take notes, and pay attention in class, you will be successful.

Very good professor that understands that his classes don't need to be stupidly hard. The tests are easy As as long as you go to lecture and at least know what the readings are talking about. I'd highly recommend.  Lectures could be condensed into half the time that they take, so it's very easy to understand and multitask during them if you want.

I took Sociology with Winders in a late short summer session. The information was fairly easy to understand and most was common sense. You'll do well on the tests if you take notes and listen during class. The reading homework is heavy, but you only need to understand a basic concept of each chapter for the tests. Pretty easy class overall. (:

All of his notes came straight from the slides. The only thing you really need for the reading is the very basic idea and what it demonstrates within the lesson you are learning. I don't recommend. T trying to read it all. Tests were pretty fair. The papers were easy and graded fairly as well. I took this in a short summer session.

I don't know how hard he is as an actual teacher because I only had him for GT1000, but I had to give a rating because I love this guy!  He's so relatable and funny and easy to talk to!  Definitely looking forward to taking classes from him in the future!

I took social movements with him Spring 2009. he is a great guy, really passionate and has a great sense of humor. The class was basically reading and lecture (supposed to be discussion). The books are not a few hundred pages each at most. We wrote two papers. One test and one final as well, both take home with about 6 pgs of essays, double spaced
Great teacher!  He got me interested in a subject that I originally had very little interest in.  Would take another of his classes in a second.

This prof took over for my online econ class and made this class have so much more busy work than needed. Literally infinite assignments that were, for the most part, not necessary. Otherwise class is easy. Tests are mcq, honorlock. I would say relatively easy, but these homework assignments suck and the worst part is that he actually grades them.

Dr. Woodbury cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. Just make sure you keep up with the homework deadlines as they aren't the midnight standard. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in-class work (for credit) that you may miss if you skip class. Make sure to use the scheduling site to setup an appt with him if you need help.

I do not have a good experience with this professor. Difficult to get a hold of and not very willing to go out of his way to support individual students. His lectures are hard to follow along with the criteria he is producing. Some may disagree but not the professor for me.

Very awkward, both him and his lectures. he only cares about student from econ Econ club. He likes to brags his jd degree that wasn't even from an ABA accredited school. Also weird that Econ department let a lecturer lead the undergrad program.
The exams are a big part of the final grade. He was okay and does offer a little extra credit.

Class meets in-person 1x a week. I'd recommend showing up to that class because of occasional in-class assignments and extra credit opportunities. The exam's are very similar in structure (MCQ, Multiple Select, and FRQ). FRQ were always practice problems. MCQ and Multiple Select were difficult, I'd take notes on textbook chapters. Not-too-hard A.
make sure you go to class because he will spring assignments on you. Easy class if you pay attention and do some studying for tests.

Take him!! I have nothing but great things to say. If you do the homework on time and study the practice problems he gives, you have absolutely nothing to worry about. We also only meet once a week instead of twice. I've thoroughly enjoyed his class so far, I'm understanding the content, and don't feel stressed at all. HIGHLY recommend.

Woodbury is a good professor. Class has two parts: watch online lecture and answer some homework questions online, then in class he builds on the lecture and you do a worksheet graded on completion (so go to class). You have 2 midterms and 1 final which combined are probably 60% of your grade. Tests & class not too hard. There is some extra credit.

I initially had no interest in economics but he managed to make me enjoy the class and like econ.  Class is pretty tough for a GED imo but very doable.  If you do all the homeworks and do well on the final he will round up ur grade very nice guy.  Like I did very bad on exam 1 but very well on final so he gave me an A despite being at a ~88.

Class time was useless, no study guides, no TAs, just him and the fact that he knows nothing about the textbook. Had no office hours on finals week, his in person ones were when everyone has class. no direction on tests, but are weighted so much, the rest is completion. Many people between a B and an A. somehow better than bolton's grading scale..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor and keeps lectures pretty light (he has async lectures with more detail). He is really clear on how you can do well in the class and what to look out for in exams. Even if you don't get a lot of extra credit during the semester, he'll bump up your grade if you're close enough and put effort in the class.

I took 2100 with Dr. Woodbury and he was an excellent instructor. He was accommodating and kind, and many times allowed the students to make a collaborative decision regarding exam dates. He also provided extra optional assignments at the end of the course for students to boost their grades. He cares about his students, and is a great teacher.
Dr.Woodbury is one of the best econ professors at Gatech. So nice and very helpful, really really learned a lot from him. Very funny too

Great professor! Emphasizes that students understand the derived, practical concepts from mathematical models to succeed. Exams reflect this by asking questions that require reasoning through different models with no math necessary. Personally would prefer a bit more depth to the mathematical models, but an awesome professor nonetheless.

Incredibly chill dude and was gave informative and interesting lectures in class. I had his 8am class and managed to stay awake so it definitely isn't a boring class. The tests are all written response but as long as he gets a general idea of what you are saying (& you aren't just wrong) it shouldn't be hard at all to get an A in this class.

Dr. Woodbury is great! The class is organized into pre-lectures and lecture time with paired in class activities. He cares about students' success and is accessible outside of class. I recommend reading the textbook and taking advantage of any extra credit opportunities. Not too difficult as long as you study and use available resources.
I was amazed by how such a person who basically doesn't know about anything besides the textbook became a professor at GT. Plus he's not a nice person in general.

Dr. Woodbury is a fantastic professor and I would highly recommend taking his class. His exams can be a little tough but as long as you're putting the work in and participating, he makes it very easy to do well in the class. Lots of extra credit opportunities available as well

He definitely was a tough grader and the class weighed exams pretty high, but his online lecture videos were pretty clear. He was also fairly clear on his grading criteria for exams. An average professor at best--the class didn't teach me too much about macro, but wasn't too intensive except for the exams.

Prof. Woodbury is a really great professor. his exam are NOT multiple choice, they are free response. harder or not idk. Definitely teaches you a lot more about macro economics and is very kind. he gives extra credit work which boosts grades. and is a very understanding and caring professor. Definitely would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very understanding and engaging professor. bad luck if you got his 8am. he will ask you to speak in front of the class, especially if you look like you're falling asleep. but he'll also tell you so much in office hours and bring candy after halloween
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The actual classes weren't super informative because we just went over homework but he is super receptive to questions during office hours and a really sweet person. Grades test pretty intensely but give a ton of extra credit so it is possible to get an A even with poor test grades.

One or two lectures posted on Canvas each week to watch to prepare for class. The class is mostly discussion of the material, and engaging in those discussions usually leads to discussion of what will be on the exam. ASK QUESTIONS or you won't do well. There are a ton of opportunities to gain extra credit, so take advantage of them!

He is very random when it comes to grading and what he likes. It was hard to figure out how he wanted your answers. You have to go to office hours to get answers to the homework and you have to participate in class a lot. Best part is he gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. Also, it's completely points based, no weighting.

The format of this class makes it very un-enjoyable. He won't lecture in class and posts lectures to watch each week where he just reads from minimal slides. In class, you present your homework and do problems from the textbook. He is a pretty harsh grader which sucks considering the two midterms and the final are heavily weighted.

He does not teach the material well. His lecture videos are him reading word for word from the textbook, and if you ask him a question outside the realm of the textbook he does not know. He grades very harshly for someone who does not teach well. Seems like most my class won't make an A in the class. He makes the class way harder than it should be.

Good professor and knows what he's talking about with Econ. Make sure you participate in the questions he asks the class because they tend to be similar concepts to what he has on the test. Tests are graded pretty harshly, but you'll get a lot of extra credit throughout the semester. Make sure you talk about institutions' influence during tests.

Took this Spring 2024, was a really fun class very interesting. Class was made up of mostly discussion posts/research project, with one multiple choice test that's a bit tricky (basically pure memorization) but totally doable. Professor is really understanding and willing to help if you reach out to him as well.

This guy's the goat. Such an easy class - if you do the work you should not only pass, but get an A as well. His lectures aren't the most engaging but he always ends well before class is over. The whole last month is a project and we didn't actually meet once. We don't really go over the readings on the syllabus in class.
Professor Woodall is a great lecturer and would recommend! He gives great feedback and lectures are easy to follow. All courses taught by him follow the same format.
Passionate about the subject, loves questions and feedback, and sets clear, easy standards for assignments.

Really easy class. I took this to fulfill my social science credit and even without previous knowledge it wasn't that bad. Almost because there was very little homework, one test the entire year (20 question multiple choice), and the entire last month is a group project

I always enjoy Dr. Woodall's classes immensely. He's an extremely kind and genuine professor and gives interesting lectures that are actually engaging. The structure of his projects is straightforward and it's easy to get an A as long as you put a little effort into the class. He's hands down the best professor I've had.
I loved this class! The professor is a great lecturer and the class was very easy. The two bests were both 15 simple multiple choice questions. The projects are graded leniently.
Great professor, clear about how everything is graded and what he wants out of assignments. Not work intensive besides end of semester. Lecture heavy but fun and interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Woodall's class. His love for what he teaches reflects on the way he lectures, and it makes class really enjoyable. One of my favorite classes this semester, 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Woodall is the best INTA professor Ive had. His lectures are clear and he provides a study guide for his tests. Hes had some super interesting experiences and met some unique people which he ties into his lectures. I definitely would recommend

Dr. Woodall is a fair grader, and this course was not too difficult, although it was online and taken during the Summer. I recommend taking his INTA 3040 class as part of the global development minor.
Easily the best professor I have had. He really cares about what he does and who he teaches. Do not miss out on any chances to talk to him after class, ask questions, or express a genuine interest

Such a sweet professor! Several of my classmates in his INTA 3203 (Comparative Politics) class all agreed that it was the easiest international affairs classes that they had ever taken. If you take the notes and study a little bit before each quiz, then you should be able to get an A. There were two projects which were very clear & straightforward.

Dr. Woodall is a great professor! His lectures are full of important information. Hes got a caring energy and hes very kind. And he really knows whats hes talking about. He lets us know the concepts that will be on the test so as long as you go through all of those, youll get an A.

This professor is so genuine. You can tell he loves what he teaches and hes a great person. Lectures are very informative, hes able to condense a lot of information into just what we need to know. Tells you what he looks for on the tests, and the tests are really easy. Take him if you want a laid back yet informative class.

You'll learn a lot - there is plenty of content, but don't worry about being tested on ALL of it, just the main points. This is truly one of the classes where you go simply to learn with little pressure, which is nice. Professor is also very funny and passionate about their class so it makes it very enjoyable. Would absolutely recommend

Prof Wood was nice and all, but gave NO grading criteria on papers, and when I asked for feedback on said papers, he was unable to tell me why I lost so many points on the papers. He didn't offer much help at all and I kept getting the same grades (C and B), when I thought I thoroughly answered the prompts of the essays. Very tangential in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy but very tough grader and basically admitted that he grades papers based off vibes.  Said he just reads your paper and gives you a grade he thinks is right.  No clear criteria for papers, just a couple vague sentences. Would not recommend this class at all. Just lectures at you the whole time, really disappointed by this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Syllabus was a single page of dates, the only mention of grades being there were three. Complains the maths have it easy, yet no rubric for any assignment just a couple sentences. No meaningful feedback for very harsh grades. Seems almost random after talking with others. Each class was just YouTube videos and occasional vague questions.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I want to preface with the fact that Dr. Wood is incredibly kind and a great man. But his course is one of the most tired I have ever been in a class. Graded on four assignments. Entirely lectures from personal thoughts and YouTube videos. No PowerPoints. Will never agree with your opinion on a film. Take a different professor or bring a Monster.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: this class was such a mess. he is the most boring teacher I have ever had and gives no material for the assignments. I have such a love for film and the history and he made this the worst experience and his grading made no sense. what ever you do do not take this his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty boring, he just drones on for the whole time and there's no engagement. The readings are not difficult and there are four essays which are not too hard but he does not give much feedback and does not use a rubric, so the grades seem pretty arbitrary. Not a horrible class if you need the credit, but not very interesting either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't use technology. His lectures are incredibly boring. There is not enough class discussion. He honestly just rambles. I didn't learn a lot in the class. He's a nice guy. He just doesn't know what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A really nice guy, but his lectures can be kind of boring. For this class, we were required to read a Shakespeare book every week, which can be kinda overwhelming if you are taking other hard classes. The course load consists of two papers, one short and one long; a midterm, and a final. Overall, a good class to take if you need an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring. Does not use any technology (Canvas/Tsquare) or technology to present (no lecture slides). The class is basically sitting there listening (or not) to him rambling for 1 1/2 hours. There is no discussion, only him talking. Lectures are so boring they're hard to pay attention to. Nice guy, but ultimately poor professor and BORING.

Nice guy,but soo boring. Attendance matters, but don't need to participate or read at all and can work on other homework during class-don't think he even wants you to participate. Assigned 6-8 papers, gives higher grades as semester goes on. Doesn't assign portfolio, just have to edit original papers and turn them in again!!! HUGE PLUS!
Dr. Wood is one of the most accessible professors I have ever had. His office hours are extremely useful and he goes over homework problems during them.

Dynamics is a very, very hard class conceptually, and that shows in the tests, but Prof. Wood is really really good at softening the blow. Extremely generous with homework deadlines, extra credit and regrades, he basically gave everyone 100s on a quiz just for showing up. If you can, I'd highly recommend you take him.
Other profs are easier

Dr. Wood is probably the most caring and engaging professor I have ever taken. His lectures were genuinely entertaining and I felt like the pacing was extremely manageable. The class is hard but if you go to office hours and put in the effort its completely doable. He is such a nice and understanding professor, and will push back any due date.

Dr. Wood was amazing. His lectures were very enjoyable and really wanted you to do well. His office hours are also very helpful and is very accessible outside of class. He genuinely is one of the best professors at Tech. Pay attention to class and do the homework and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not letting me use the computer for saying "Can I fix that computer" like what the heck?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about the students and acknowledges the fact that we have other classes and lives outside education. He would always move back deadlines when we asked if we had a lot of exams or projects due in other classes. Office hours are your best friend for homework assignments. Also textbook pdf is easily found searching online

Professor wood is amazing! Dynamics is a hard class and his hw problems aren't really possible without going to office hours. But he's a very generous grader (if you have the right answer and cross it out he will still give you full credit). He also curves a lot.

Awesome prof, he's very understanding and would move stuff around if several people had a heavy week like for 2110. Office hours are super helpful and save a lot of time on HW. He even hosted office hours during finals week which helped significantly.
tough class great prof

Dynamics is a hard class in and of itself but Dr. Wood makes it so much better. He is very thorough in his lectures and is accessible outside of class like during office hours and extra office hours to practice before exams and help with weekly homeworks (highly recommend attending these). He is also super kind and caring and curves grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome Prof. VERY helpful in OH; there were always ~10 students there and he would go over the homework questions. HE is very caring and flexible. I had to go out of town and he was going to let me take an exam early. A lot of students were taking ME 2110 at the same time and he would often ask the class (vote) when we wanted tests/homework due.

Top 3 professors I've had at GT. He is the most caring guy. He literally pushes homework due dates back for the smallest of reasons and is so accessible outside of class. The material is tough but the tests are pretty similar to the practice tests and in many cases easier than the homework. He typically offers credit back on test questions too.

Dr. Wood is one of the best instructors I've had. He knows the class is hard & is willing to help students. He is very generous, and kind and gives points back on exams. Also alots students the grade they deserve- THE WAY IT SHOULD BE. Dr. Wood has plenty of office hrs & really wants to see students succeed. If you put in effort, he will reward you

I love this man more than life itself. He is so sweet and caring and the best professor I've ever had. I won't lie, the content is a struggle, but he provides so much help inside and outside of class. He will literally push back homework for almost any reason and is very flexible about scheduling exams to not swamp his students

He is an amazing professor. I had him during COVID, and even online he tried his best to accommodate. If you go to the office hour he and the TA work through the homework with you, and he doesn't lecture from a textbook so the exams are very similar to what is given in the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Dynamics is a tough course, but he does an outstanding job of teaching it. That being said, you will definitely have to work for the grade you want. His extended office hours are super helpful on the homeworks, and he's very good about helping students understand topics and working with them outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is very understanding of the pressure on students. He is very flexible with due dates if it seems that many students are struggling the homework. The tests are challenging, and you will need to do more practice beyond the assigned homework. If you study and have a good intuition for dynamics, an A is achievable.

Dr. Wood is the most kind professor at Gatech. He is very flexible with everything, and wants to help students learn in the best way possible. His dynamics class is also perhaps the hardest at gatech which says something. Lectures, office hours, and homework alone wont help you. Be prepared to study A LOT if you want an A

Levi Wood is genuinely the nicest professor at Gatech. He was very flexible with everything and offer some credit back on exams. With that being said I have never wanted to not take a class with a professor so much in my life. You learn everything on your own, and tests extremely difficult. I am so glad its over and never want him for 2202 again

Cares for the students. He makes sure that everyone follows his thought. Will add 15/100 pts to the test score for any 100% correct test-rework, regardless of the current test grade. If you can show that you 1/ understand the concepts & 2/ write down the formulas correctly, he will give you most the points. Tests are similar homework & quizzes.

Dr. Wood is definitely one of the best professors Ive had. He cares about his students and really does his best to get you to understand what youre learning. That being said, expect to spend 6+ hours on his HW every week. His 3 hour office hours are effectively mandatory to do well. If you arent willing to put in the time, take another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dynamics is a VERY difficult class. Dr. Wood is by no means a difficult professor, its just the nature of this class. He is very lenient with homework due dates. His homeworks took a long time but you can go to office hours for one on one help. His tests are incredibly fair and are not unexpected by any means (they're still very difficult haha).

It's amazing how caring Dr. Wood is. Dynamics is going to be hard no matter who you take it with. Don't make the mistake in thinking the homework or the practice tests are similar to the tests, though.
Great teacher and super caring, but office hours are effectively mandatory if you want to succeed in the course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dynamics is hard no matter who you have, but he is very willing to help struggling students. Office hours tend to be more helpful than lectures, but I'd still recommend going to both. Tests and quizzes are very difficult, but he gives generous partial credit and lets students re-do test problems for additional credit.

Great teacher but the material is HARD. Be prepared to spend minimum 5 hours on each weekly HW after week 2. Go to office hours to work problems with him and classmates. You can rework exams for extra credit (test 1 avg 68, test 2 60, final 66). Sizable curve at end but avg was still a C. Online vids do not replace lecture but are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is a very caring person. That being said, I find that his lectures are not enough to do well in the course. You will most likely be surprised by the difficulty of his tests and quizzes but he gives a lot of partial credits but his classes do not prepare well for the tests. Go to his office hours, its a lot better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is the most caring professor I've had so far at Tech! He knows his students by name, gives plenty of partial credit, and has easy-to-follow lectures. Dynamics isn't an easy class for most, but he tries very hard to have lots of available times for office hours and outside help with him or the TA.

Dr. Wood is one of the most caring professors at Tech. He is always willing to alter due dates based on how your semester is going. One negative to his class is that his lectures are COMPLETELY useless. He does wayyyy to many derivations and not enough examples. Watch the Coursera videos and ALWAYS attend office hours and youll do fine!

Dr. Wood is really kind and caring. He always has office hours the day before homework is due, which is where I learned the most. It's easy to get lost in lecture, but he always thoroughly answers any questions. Also, he gives credit for stuff that's crossed out on tests. You can try a bunch of things and if anything is right you get full credit.

Dr. Wood is a nice guy, but his lectures are almost useless. He spends way too much time doing derivation and does not go over enough examples, so you end up spending most of the HW time trying to understand the material. Do not take this professor, you will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is without a doubt the best professor I've had at Tech. He's really nice, extremely smart, and cares more than anything that you understand the material. The lectures are helpful and in-class examples are also very good. He is always willing to set up a time to meet in his office. I cannot recommend Dr. Wood enough!

Dr. Wood's lectures can be easy to get lost in if you're not paying attention. For a smaller setting and personalized help, his office hours are phenomenal! He has a long (2 or 3 hour) session once a week for group work and help with the homework assignments. His traditional office hours are great too. He wants you to learn and is willing to help.

Clearly very passionate about film, the class and lectures are very informative and interesting though they may drag on at times. There is a fair amount of homework and attendance is mandatory, but grading on both is fairly lenient. Gives plenty of feedback on writings and exam review sessions basically give the exam questions away.

He's a really good professor! Transformed what I thought was going to be a tedious LMC class into a surprisingly engaging experience. Midterms were easy, and the final project was a breeze. I would not recommend doing all the "required" reading and stick to the sparknotes. Recommend!
Very good professor, passionate about film and overall decent lecturer. As long as you attend lecture and watch weekly films he will give you the resources you need to succeed

Prof is seriously passionate about Shakespeare. This was his first semester at Tech and first semester teaching Shakespeare, but he did a great job. Class has a good bit of reading, but you can survive not doing all of it, a mini-project, a midterm, and a final group project. If you spend your time well, and you participate, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Passionate and very knowledgeable about film, although his lectures were not always the most interesting. Some films were boring, but make sure to watch them in case of a pop quiz (reading summary is not enough). Midterm and Final were very easy if you go to the review sessions, but he graded papers kind of harshly with the feedback being vague.

Great guy, passionate about what he does. Enjoyed some aspects of the class but found lots of the films we saw boring. The papers were pretty easy, he posts example papers beforehand and grades very fairly. He does review for tests that pretty much gives away the answers... you just have to put the effort in to attend and study a bit.
Terrible at time management
pretty cool guy.
mentally prepare but learned good things :)

Wray is a really nice professor and he makes the class pretty easy. My main piece of advice for this class is to take the effort to make a in depth cheat sheet. The quizzes are all based on the slides so if you can write down majority of the material on your cheat sheet, the quizzes should be easy.

Dr. Wray is an amazing lector, and 1601 is a very chill class. Labs are probably the most difficult part of the class, and they aren't that bad at all - just long. He gives you all the resources you need to succeed, and if you were satisfied with your grade, the final exam is optional.

Hands down, the nicest professor ever. There are no exams, just 6 quizzes, and you get a note sheet for each one. You only have to attend 10 lectures to get the participation grade. He's so nice, and there's not much homework. The labs are easy too.

Super easy class! Love that there were no tests, and in all of the quizzes we were able to have a printed sheet of stuff front/back. Final exam was optional, its just to replace quiz grades. Attendance mandatory for a certain number of lectures (in-person or zoom) and labs were typically self-explantory with help from online resources.

Dr Wray is a great prof, who is passionate on what he teaches. If you're interested in what's happening, you'll have a blast. Even if not, the assignments & labs are super easy. He is very kind & you won't have a problem enjoying his class. You are required to attend 10 out of 26 lectures, but you can go online. Take prof Wray, you won't regret.

Dr. James Wray is very passionate about the content of the lectures which makes them more enjoyable. There are only 6 quizzes (you can bring a cheat sheet to all of them). There are also virtual labs which require tedious work but definitely doable. The in-person labs can be completed quickly and are straight-forward. The best EAS class at Tech.

Dr. Wray is a great professor. He is very knowledgable and passionate about his subject, and lectures were always very entertaining. The class is very straightforward, as he posts the lecture slides after class and gives clear guidelines about what will be on the quizzes. We were allowed a page of notes on the quizzes and the final was optional.

Because of the pandemic, the class went online for a large portion of the year. The lectures were fairly straight-forward, and the information was presented in a really nice manner. The lecture quizzes were straight from the lectures. The labs take a good amount of time to complete, but they are fairly easy to finish.

Dr. Wray is very nice and cares about his students but lectures are a little tedious. You don't have to go to class but he says a lot of specific in class that are on tests. Labs are very easy and don't take long. If you're a non-science/engineer major take this class
Nice guy, but pretty average professor. Lectures are not engaging at all and he posts them online right after class. Write a joke on the back of your test and you might get +2.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wray is my man, he just nerds out about Mars every class, lectures are interesting and entertaining af, tons of extra credit opportunities, literally show up to lecture and remember like 60% of it and you get an A on the test. Labs are easy to get 100% on and <1 hour, but there's a quiz at the start of every lab so don't be late. Take this.

The class isn't too difficult but his lectures are unbearable, and the tests have questions straight out of left field. He reads off the slides as if it's too his first time seeing them. He spends first 15 minutes of lecture just talking about how he loves Mars, which isn't even tested on! TLDR; class: not too difficult besides test. Wray? HARD NO
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really cool guy. Usually teaches more advanced classes but I was lucky to have him for Habitable Planet. It was definitely an easy class - I didn't have to go to lectures to do well, but I wanted to go anyways. I learned a lot about how our planet and solar system work.

He's very quiet and hard to hear but offers online zoom for non quiz days. Lab is insanely weird with wording but easy. Just ask someone who took the class before for help with labs since they are easy but weirdly worded. Argos is the only thing you need to buy but besides that he has cheat sheet quizzes that all 6 make up your final. tbh easy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wray is one of the best professors I have ever had. Witty, incredibly knowledgeable, and very approachable. Makes lectures super engaging, especially when he talks about his own research. If you take the undergrad version of 4370, you can get a ton of extra credit by completing grad-level problems on homework. Take Physics of Planets with him!

I loveeee Prof. Wray. Personally I think hes a funny guy and though his lectures were sometimes a little off-topic hes a great lecturer! Theres a lot of extra credit in the class to boost your grade and the tests are literally everything from the slides

He's a really nice guy who has a lot of research experience in EAS fields. He can tend to go off on tangents during lecture about his own research, so his lecture may not be the most productive for learning.

Dr. Wray is a great lecturer he always kept things interesting even though lecture tends to drag on some days. He started every lecture with current events which was cool and he obviously has a real passion for the material as even though this was an intro level course he seemed excited to be lecturing every class. Test can be tricky so study.

Dr. Wray is my man, he just nerds out about Mars every class, lectures are interesting and entertaining af, tons of extra credit opportunities, literally show up to lecture and remember like 60% of it and you get an A on the test. Labs are easy to get 100% on and <1 hour, but there's a quiz at the start of every lab so don't be late. Take this.

Dr. Wray is an incredibly smart guy with incredible lectures. He often speaks about his research in class and gives a lot of interesting information on NASA's Mars exploration projects very often on the lectures. He is a must for EAS 1601! Easy A and interesting class!
Take him for EAS 1601. Easy A and is incredibly smart with good lectures. Labs also take less than an hour.

Do not take. Lectures are confusing. She gets confused by her own slides, so how are we supposed to understand? Clearly doesn't prepare for lecture. Midterm (early, easier topics) had mean and median of 50ish. Exam not returned to students so no change to learn from mistakes or contest bad grading. Free content (books, YouTube) more helpful.

If you want to learn whatever she's teaching, find a free online course and teach yourself. You will have to teach yourself regardless, and her involvement just adds to the confusion. She never releases rubrics for anything, whether it's a homework, project, or presentation. She doesn't care

Very disappointed after finishing this class, was meant to focus on Neural and Behavioral Data but Prof Wu essentially turned it into a core Machine Learning class, with unclear slides, tangential and contrived explanations, lack of appropriate expectations and shoddy homework assignments. I did fine on the class but it was a serious waste of time.
Loved the lectures, and the TAs

Horrible lectures that don't teach anything, super incompetent TA's who don't bother to help at all, and really hard homeworks. I hate this course- only thing I got out of it is a group project. I absolutely hate this class, the prof, and the TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are ineffective for learning course content compared to following the syllabus and searching on Google. Notation in the class slides is unclear and inconsistent, causing confusion during lectures. The pace of teaching is too fast, with important details glossed over. Overall, the course seems unsuitable for beginners.

The lectures are way too technical and move way too fast, even for people who have a strong math and programming background. Homeworks are extremely confusing and the "extra credit" questions are not fair. Furthermore the grading policy is constantly being changed and updated without clear communication to the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things
