reviews.comment: Too many terminologies make lecture hard to follow, many of them are not necessary to be introduced at very first. The definition of this course is ambiguous -- is it for experts or tyro? For experts, the course content is too out of date. For tyro, nana, it's not that friendly. Prof. Wu usually won't explain the foundation stuff. take again?No.

Some homework and exam problems are worded so confusingly and different from what's taught in lectures that make you wonder if she reads her homework and exams before giving them out. Piazza questions can be left unanswered for days but when students complain, it's apparently our fault for not "not having an idea of the workload".
Boring lecture, total waste of time. The homework also makes no sense. No help before the exam. Make easy topics complicate and irritating.
Dr. Wu cares a lot about students. He is very knowledgeable. He presented the contents very clearly. Overall, the course is a bit challenging, but it is manageable if you really work on it.

Clear grading material eg says to expect this topic on the exam whilst lecturing. Minimal practice but very similar to exams so its fine. Wants to see us succeed and is happy to hear feedback from students. TB not necessary but helpful - he pulls lots of questions from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally loved Dr. Wus lectures, and I thought he was pretty clear in what we was saying, but some of classmates did not agree. Some of the contents you learn are weird, and the TA and lab TAs told us he was teaching stuff most other analytical courses didnt cover. He includes practice problems in the slides, and he often reuses them for test
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took CHEM 2211 with Prof. Wu in 2016. I believe a few of the recent reviews are unfair. His lectures were structured based off of powerpoint slides that are easy to follow. This class is more challenging than Gen. Chem., so don't expect the material to presented at that level. If you study for this class, you should do well.

Dr. Wu cares about his students and their understanding but cannot get the material across well. He knows what he is talking about but the way he teaches is not easy to understand. I learned all the course material either by teaching myself or from the TAs. He also spends a good chunk of the time lecturing the students on how we can do better.

Professor Wu cares about students' understanding of the course material, however in my case he failed to explain the material clearly enough. In the redesigned course, he never worked example questions in class, leaving us puzzled until recitation TA's clarified on Friday's. He spends a lot of time on announcements/course policies each lecture.

A really excellent professor. The material can be difficult, but paying attention in lecture and reading the book help a lot. The best thing about Dr. Wu as a teacher is how much he cares about each student's individual understanding of the material. He wants you to do well, and if you put in the proper effort, he will definitely help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a very nice professor and truly wants all of his students to succeed.  But he does expect close to perfect work on exams, and does not give much partial credit.  Fortunately, there is usually one exam question from homework, and one from his lecture slides so be sure to review them beforehand!  Occasionally gives pop-quizzes.

Dr. Wu is one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech. He has high expectations of his students (as he will tell you frequently), but he gives a lot of respect. Be sure to know your basic chemistry before taking Quantitative Analysis. Has thick accent, but makes up for it with PowerPoints. Tests are straight forward.
mid guy and makes things hard
Very nice professor. Clear on instruction and materials.

Dr. Wunderly is very invested in actually understanding and applying the material. Even with the midterm and final amounting to 70% of the grade, he provides plenty of practice. He's very accessible with 1:1 office hours as needed. Know your basic derivative rules...knowing how to do partial derivatives will help. Very manageable A and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Legendary and funny. Caring and very accessible, overall W mans.

Very engaging professor, super nice and is always getting people to laugh. Lectures were good and does everything to make sure students can succeed. Attendence taken for extra credit, not a lot of homework, however bulk of grade relys on two exams. Holds a zoom during class for people who want to attend online.

He was always very clear about how to succeed in the class. Attendance is not mandatory but is rewarded with extra credit and really helpful advice for exams. We had the option to join classes on zoom and every lecture was recorded and posted on Canvas. Overall, he was a great professor who clearly wants every person to get an A.
GREAT PROFESSOR! minimum amount of homework. Exams were explained explicitly, easily passable. Tons of extra credit! Would take again if I was a econ major. Definitely recommend!
good
Hard to understand him with his accent, lectures are pretty boring too.
Li is a great instructor, I really enjoy his class.

Professor is super nice, accommodating, and shows genuine interest in the subject.
Grade is just 4 projects and a few homework throughout.
I didn't learn tha much more about DSP (Heavy lifting via ECE4270) and while there were interesting concepts of the applications thereof, it wasn't presented in an interesting manner.
Clear message always! Willing to take her course again!

Nice person and always willing to help, but she does nothing to make boring classes exciting. Graded on a couple projects and homeworks that were really easy so you won't learn much. The extra credit assignments are really interesting and everyone could easily get over 100% in the class. The class was hybrid but she made it completely virtual.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Xingxing's lectures were some of the highest quality I've seen. His HW was really difficult, and he only gave us around a week to do each one. The pace of the class was also quite fast. However, he was extremely caring and considerate, and the whole class able to bond really well with each other.
Weeks of MW and midterms in a row. Less than a week between assigning the HW and the due date. Great lecturer, but disorganized and grades cruelly

He's a really nice professor who knows the subject well and tries to help students as much as possible but the course (Graph Theory) was simply brutal. I had a 4.0 before this class and got a C on it - the final was simply impossibly hard.

He explains concepts quite clearly. The homework problems are pretty challenging unlike what I have experienced from other classes at Tech. It's nice how he pushes for us to use formalized mathematical notation so that we would have the "same language" as mathematicians. This is probably my most challenging class, but I hope to get a lot out of it!
Dr. Yu was always very thorough in his lectures. In office hours he was very helpful too. I was never bored during thermo with him.

Organized teaching methods, follows textbook. Homework load is big but will train you for tests. curves at the end if he felt that the class need that. Take him if you can, overall he is great and very sweet teacher.

Yu went primarily along with the Graph Theory text, but he supplemented it well with lectures and pruned unecessary sections. The clarity of the lectures and the problem solving made this class great, but with a slightly higher than average workload. I highly recommend it to Math and Computer Science majors.
She basically handed out As to everyone.

This professor truly cares about your understanding of the material, and takes a lot of effort to make sure that you have the resources needed to complete the homework. Professor X has been one of the best professors I have taken at Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Xie is so caring and very clear in explaining stuffs. She spent so much time  guiding through homework.

Professor Xie genuinely wants to see students succeed and it shows in the time she takes to answer specific questions and the videos she makes to help explain assignments. Took her course during COVID and her recorded lectures were really helpful!

Prof. X was honestly one of the best professors Ive had during my time at Tech. You could tell she truly cared for her students and their success and understanding of the material she taught. Was pretty lenient with her quizzes and allowed 8 pages of crib sheets for tests so its hard not to do well in her class. Definitely recommend taking!
probably the best professor you can take for 3030 (2028). Super nice!
Super nice, gives practice questions that are similar to tests and is genuinely passionate about how statistics relates to research and real life applications. Very solid choice.
Super sweet lady - the class isn't very difficult as the TAs grade very easy. Definitely would recommend.

Very sweet lady but bad professor. She often asked some questions on tests that we did not go over in lecture at all. Her lecture slides are horrible, the examples aren't clear and they don't work through the whole problem. I would avoid her if you can, but if you can't you'll probably do fine, it'll just be an annoying class.
Prof. X is amazing. She is one of the nicest, most caring professor's I've had at Tech. Would 100% recommend

Projects/Homeworks are hard, but doable. TA were helpful, but tests were ridiculously hard and essentially designed to fail students. My class's midterm and final average was just around 60%. This professor tries to answer some questions, but gives vague answers or even just ignores student questions, especially when asked through emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tests were insanely difficult and the final required knowledge that wasn't taught in class. Professor doesn't care about the students and doesn't answer questions on piazza. TAs are lost half of the time and tell you to "read the textbook". Other class got 21 MCQs on their midterm while ours was 18 questions (many FRQs) in the same time frame.

Tests were significantly harder than in other sections and the professor didn't acknowledge the disparity in difficulty between the two classes. When asked about this in class he never gave a straightforward answer. He doesn't consider student feedback. TAs were very unhelpful, and there is not enough communication between the TAs and professor.

Students had to beg for homeworks to be graded in time to help them study for tests and no partial credit was given for the midterm while the other section got multiple choice. Majority of questions on piazza were straight up ignored, and there was no clarification on what content would be covered for the final.

To summarize the semester:
- TA's haven't released 3/6 assignments for the class before finals
- My section's midterm was harder
- TAs failed to answer ton questions on Piazza
- Second programming assignment auto grader made the project 10x harder than it needed to be.
- Professor is enthusiastic but reads from slides
- Entire class is on slides
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were the most boring lectures I've had and I learnt literally nothing. Halfway through semester there were 10/200 students attending class. He does not care about students, and refused to listen to them. No partial credit on midterm exam, and average was 75% and inspite of asking for partial credit on piazza and in person, nothing happened

This is the most caring and kind professor I have ever met in my four year's college life. His support and encouragement when I was down helped me get through the most difficult time during that semester. I am so happy to have Dr.Xu as my professor.

We had 4 difficult homeworks, one easy project, and one very hard project. Additionally, we had a midterm near the end of the semester covering 75% of class material, and then a final exam 2 weeks later, which made no sense. Stopped going to lectures halfway through. He gave 2 points of CIOS bonus and 7 late days however, which made things better.

A very knowledgeable guy but not the most engaging professor. His lectures may feel a little dry as he typically reads directly from the textbook slides. Fair grader and provides you with enough material to pass the exams and projects.

Useless professor with incredibly boring and useless lectures. You are almost guaranteed to learn nothing. No one was going to lectures. The tests are not hard but are 50% or more of the grade which makes one slip catastrophic. He doesn't care about students.
crazy dude, but always energetic. if you go to class with an open mind, you'll find him funny and charming. goes on lots of tangents, but theyre always fun to listen to.

Went over concepts through PowerPoint pretty well. Sometimes a bit dry, but he is quite a mix of energetic, caring, and humorous during lecture. Answers questions during class well, but defers a lot of questions regarding tests and assignments to the professor of the other section and the TAs. Fair tests and simple projects with some bonus.
One of the best professors at Scheller. His enthusiasm for the course material is unparalleled.
Loved him! He's very knowledgeable about what he's teaching and super nice.

Very difficult to get in contact with the teacher, only possible through email. TA's grade everything and are terrible at grading. If you make a small mistake, even if you still get the right answer, be prepared to lose 2 points for each mistake (HW is literally 50/50, so that's 4% of your grade per mistake). Tests are heavily based on slides.

Class was pretty boring and he never responds to emails. The exams cover a decent amount of material so study in advance. The smallest details make it to the exams. Homework was pretty easy but if you make one small mistake be prepared to get a ton of points off.

Class itself is tough (now mgt 2210), but he at least makes it really applicable to everyone. Can drone on during lecture sometimes but he's one of the most considerate and kind professors i've had so definitely take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: It was a pretty boring class, but it wasn't hard. Show up, do your homework, and pay attention on occasion. A complete BS class, but an easy A.
Awesome Teacher. Really smart on the topic. Would highly recommend.

Amazing professor!! The exams come from the slides and are really fair, I got As on all of them! Do NOT buy the book, just pay attention in class. He makes the subject really interesting and is funny.
Great professor. Always willing to help. Exams come directly from the slides, and all the information presented on the slides come from the text so there is no need to purchase the book.

Great professor! So enthusiastic, absolutely loves what he does. Attendance is mandatory but class slides are provided online. Everything you need for the tests is on the slides, don't waste your time with the book. 5 relatively simple homework assignments throughout the semester on excel and database. Grades generously. Pretty easy A

Section X is a little different, I highly recommend it. Less time on useless things, more time on interesting topics including an optional ML extra credit project. Lectures are technically option but I'd highly recommend them. Workload is very light, and I felt like I learnt a good amount about SQL and databases.

Took his 8803 (Data Management & ML) in the Fall. Pretty good lecturer, though in this course students give paper presentations on most days. Prof is understanding and helpful. Other than one paper presentation, workload is a paper review every week and a big course-long project. If you complete your work with an honest effort, you'll get an A.

Section X is different from the other CS 4400 sections. Only one month on SQL and we got to just as advanced queries. We also talked about other topics (without coding) and had an extra credit project on entity matching in Python. Grade is 60% homework (4 assignments) and 40% final. Search "chu CS4400X" on Google, he posts his schedule and slides.

This course is extremely dense. The toughest thing about this class is that you need to be able to pick up on the material extremely quickly, and the TAs and the professors are unlikely to help with the homeworks in specific because they are graded assignments, but you barely have time to review past assignments because the class moves on.

There are way too many assignments for this class. He basically teaches this class by having you do 15 Homework assignments, you are not going to get any additional practice problems, but he won't fail you. We literally had a pair of homework assignments to work on the week of the midterm. The amount of effort I need to put in is absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Solid professor that knows the course material well. Lectures were a bit dry sometimes but he reiterated the important concepts well. There were also many opportunities for bonus points and grading wasn't too bad

The class itself was pretty easy but the professor's lectures were not. He seemed to be all over the place during his explanations which made it very hard to follow along. Also the lectures were supposed to be 50 min long but many of the lectures he posted were over an hour long which shouldn't be okay just because the class was online due to COVID
Excellent course by an excellent professor. Final project adds a nice touch.

Dr. Sun's course (Economic Dec. Analysis) isn't difficult; follow the book and don't stop asking questions and he won't let you fail.  Dr. Sun is engaged and will help you succeed.  The final course project (group work) was extremely interesting and served as a great application of coursework.

Dr. Yan was not a good lecturer. She almost never would do examples of the calc problems, she would instead spend the entire lecture on proofs. Every time she was asked a question she'd go off on a math tangent that seemed to knock people asleep. Only redeeming quality was that office hours were useful.

I got a 90% in final, still B. BUT, she's a great prof. I don't know why people are so hard on her, go and see her office hours (or ask to see another time if you can't) and she explains really well and patiently. She made time to see us the morning of the final with last minute Qs. And she lectures nicely, explains theory then solves examples.

Xukai's lectures are very dry, and I just sat there bored and struggling to focus. I took her class during Spring 2020, and after class went online, she was uncaring toward her students. One exam was held during a 1 hour window, with no regard to students in different time zones. Also, she didn't lecture, but assigned videos longer than lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst part of the class for me was how dreadfully boring lecture was. Some professors tend to be more animated and engaging than others, however other than that she was a good professor. She knew what she was talking about and was very nice in person. I just had a hard time focusing in thatclass.

Dr. Yan was a good professor. Her accent was a bit hard to understand at times, but it made sense. She sometimes writes too quickly to catch up, and while lecture technically isn't required, you will have to submit lecture notes (that she posts on Canvas every lecture day around 5 or so). She's more theory focused than example-based. OFFICE HOURS.

I like her teaching style where she will first present the theory and then give you problem examples. It's hard to understand her sometimes but you get used to it. She goes a little fast sometimes so it's common to have to review the notes you took. I didn't like her at first but by the end I thought she was fine. Not the best but it could be worse
Not much else to say, my apologies

The grading for this class is corporate style so toughness of it isn't really on her. I will say that it can be difficult to understand her and follow along. She moves way too quickly and moves on without notice. Recitation and how good your TA is will make or break you. Take lecture notes but don't think you are going to come away understanding.

Dr. Yand doesn't understand how to use the technology given to her to teach. Students constantly have to tell her to move her paper up or over when she writes notes on her projector. There have been numerous microphone and lighting issues that you would think would be easy to resolve. She's nice, but she writes WAY too quick sometimes.
Made differential calculus the definition of a weed out class. She taught it in a way that sometimes seemed more complicated than it should be.

She talked with her back to the class most of the time, making it extremely hard to understand her. She didn't explain things that well and most of class time was spent working out long drawn out problems and providing little explanation to what she was doing.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a really good teacher and really cares about the students. Always gives problem banks as study guides for all the midterms and tells you exactly how to study for the quizzes. Don't worry if you fail the first quiz one gets dropped at the end.

Still taking this course but really like the research presentation portion of the course and the D3.js labs are really useful. Assignments can be a little tough to understand but Dr. Yang or the ta's are pretty quick to respond to any questions. Just make sure you start assignments early.
Overall really great and interesting course! Really loved the TAs! I recommended the course to a few of my friends as it was really fun doing web development and making visualizations in d3.

Well-run class with clearly graded homeworks, labs, and projects making up most of the grade, tests are tough and memorization heavy. Usually no attendance required, 1 lecture a week and the other day is a coding lab on assignments. Dr. Yang himself is pretty caring, funny, and knowledgeable, and some weeks are very heavy, but overall great prof
Tough but worth it. Pushes you to actually learn the material. One of my favorite professors.
Horrendous! Dr. Yahaya please quit your job or get a life because you can't take 20 points off a paper for not having headings or subheadings when you give us zero instructions.

Graded on 10 discussions and a final paper, each category was 50% of the final grade. The syllabus was outdated and had information about a project we didn't do. There was no rubric for the paper, just a loose set of guidelines. Minimal feedback was given for the final and he had expectations for the paper that were not explicitly stated anywhere.

His lectures were all over the place and provided very little concrete information, class discussions were frequently frustrating and contradictory, and most quiz and test questions came directly from the textbook but were often specific details and confusing definitions. Makes international affairs feel impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor did not know the course structure and syllabus. Also fought with students that did not agree with him. Did not stick to the powerpoint slides and always went off course. Never went over the quiz material. Do not take!

Obviously did not know the course content and did not make the slides, quizzes, or tests. The course is only an assessment of one's ability to memorize the textbook, and the lectures (which were mandatory) were a complete waste of my time. Derailed class to talk about whatever was on his mind and argued with students about his bad, biased takes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had, with both an extremely bad attitude and an inconsistent grading scale. We have open discussions on material not even on the quizzes! The discussions are irrelevant, he also silences you if your opinion differs from his while allowing for unfactual information to support his ego.

Super rude to students, often cold-calling them and then bashing their answers. He changed the grading scale on the syllabus with two weeks left in class to hurt the grades of students w/ low attendance & threatened to change it again to restrict students from taking the final that did not attend enough classes. Very unprofessional & unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In all of my experience, I have never came across a professor I disliked more than professor Yahaya. He is a childish man, with a hatred for any view he does not agree with. For a professor that claims to be schooled in ethics, he is a very single minded seemingly unethical person. The other reviews on here emphasize my points. Do not take.

TERRIBLE. AVOID. Worst professor I have ever had. Unclear PowerPoint presentations, test content not clarified, terrible teaching/instruction, messy syllabus(changed 2 weeks prior to the end of the semester), and intimidating towards students. Content covered in the textbook never discussed in class. Class was way harder than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally one of the worst profs I've ever had. Changed the syllabus grading criteria in NOVEMBER. Constantly talked down to students. Test content was never talked about in class. No homework and very little classwork opportunities to bring up your grade. Told students the wrong date for the final which caused MANY problems. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Completely unorganized. Clear that he didn't make the PowerPoints or quizzes so class discussions were driven completely off topic making class unnecessary for learning for necessary for attendance credit. Changed the grading scheme 2 weeks before class ended. Spoke back to students in a way that made you intimidated to speak up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID. Very unprofessional. Made the class so much harder than it needed to be. Wasn't clear with the grading scale and changed the syllabus multiple times. Very inconsistent and hostile. Often got into arguments with students if they had a different opinion than him even though we were asked to only "speak facts".
She took points off for doing an assignment in red

I had her for gt1000 I was originally told this class was a easy A but she is the strictest grader alive. Will mark you wrong for the littlest thing. I turned in all my work and following the rubric which was unclear and and got a B. Do not take her class if you can

The grading is harsher than it states in each rubric. Several times she said contradictory things and took off points when we didn't know what to use. She had an attitude like she could do everything better.

For a teacher that preached kindness, she was very condescending and mean to students. She told us that attendance would be corrected at the end of the semester for illness and did not correct participation points ever. The grading is very unclear as she often disagrees with the rubric she publishes but still has a strict rubric of her own.
Very passive aggressive. Blames students for her own mistakes. Always looks for a way out when she is in the wrong. Class is easy if you show up and complete all the assignments.
passive aggressive with a smiling face. that's all you have to know.

I had Rivera for GT1000, and she made the class much more difficult than it needed to be. Her instructions and grading criteria were unclear, and she had very low patience with our class. I would avoid taking her class as much as possible, but if you don't have a choice, it's still an easy A.

20% For two each of midterms, 40% for the final, and 20% for HW, for which he normally gives a 100 for participation. Tests are graded INCREDIBLY strict but are take-home. Attendance is not required, and the notes he posts often teach better than lectures. Would take the course with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly hard to follow. Clear notes posted on Canvas. Exams are extremely difficult (in a way if you got the question right but didn't explain it enough you got points off so it feels impossible to get a 100). HWs are graded on participation. He answers emails quickly even on weekends, but overall would not recommend.

Exams are difficult but the class is curved. Aside from that, Yeung is just a very bad lecturer. He mumbles the entire lecture and covers what he is writing with his body, so once you can see what he was writing you have no idea what he was talking about. Wouldn't take again under any circumstance.

Very test heavy, but replies quickly to emails and gives helpful feedback. Go to recitation, don't skip lectures, ask questions, and read notes multiple times to really understand them. Most people who complain about him do terribly because of the fact that ~80% of the class skips lecture near the end of the semester.

Exams take up 80% of grade and are graded harshly, format is open-book open-note, but still incredibly difficult. PK expects theoretical and conceptual understanding, can't always get both from lectures/notes. HWs are graded on effort based, and TA's/PK give good feedback. Lectures not super helpful, hard to understand, but clear notes are posted.

Dr. PK Yeung is an exceptional professor who brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the classroom. Taking his course on Aerodynamics (AE 3030) was a transformative experience for me. The main drawbacks is that his exams are extraordinarily awful, in the sense that he expects you to provide everything you have ever known about aerodynamics.

Professor Yeung's lectures are theory heavy, which leaves you with a strong conceptual understanding of aerodynamics. I would recommend reading/taking notes on his notes and the textbook readings instead of attending lecture. Submit the practice exams for feedback because they are extremely similar to tests!  He curves the class (A~75).

Yeung is a VERY TOUGH GRADER and has really weird exams. Our first exam average was a 50. Even though people may say that he curves like crazy, it's because of how low hey exam grades were. When I took it, a 72 was an A. He's also very hard to understand during lecture (he uses a hearing aid and he has a very thick accent).

You'll have to work for your grade and lectures are material heavy. That being said, tests are quite clear and if you actually do the homework, you'll do fine on them. Is extremely passionate about the subject and will go out of his way to help students. Overall, great professor and would take again.

Honestly, if you can just read the textbook and write everything you can think of on the exams you will do fine in the course. The prof. is good when you have specific questions but I had a hard time paying attention in lectures.

He posts all his notes online which is really nice for an early class. He is a really nice guy and clearly loves aerodynamics. The class is graded from the 10 HWs, 2 tests, and the final so the HW is very important. For the tests you have to go really in depth with the answers or else he will take off points. Do not expect an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As someone else said, Yueng's grading is pretty fickle. To receive full credit, you must go to the moon and back because this man wants to see that you understand the content thoroughly. Merely providing the right answer is not enough. Go to class and take thorough notes because what he posts online can often be hard to understand.

He is a very vanilla professor, but do keep in mind he is a very fickle test grader. And in a class where the final is 40 percent of your grade. That can be a little alarming. But if you need to take AE 3030 and Yeung is one of your options, don't worry too much about signing up for him. It is a lot of work though. A lot.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His exams are fair and if you read the book and do the homework then you'll be fine. Make sure that you know the material as you go along, and consult him if you ever fall behind. He's good at explaining the material, but I encourage you to read the book. People may complain about him, but their qualms are most likely due to their own laziness.

One thing about professor Yeung: DO THE HW! Quizzes and Tests are extremely fair, but you'll only understand what he's asking if you do the hw.  He explains clearly that you don't need to do the hw right, just attempt it and understand how the material is used.  Yeung is excellent and I recommend him to anyone.
This is the professor you take if you want to learn Thermodynamics. Yes, it's a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Yee is a great lecturer and genuinely cares about his students. Work hard and you will be rewarded. He only cares to see you learning

Dr. Yee is the BEST lecturer I have ever had. The first class at tech where I felt like I was learning, not cramming, he kept entire class engaged and made thermo easy to understand (eg. by using physical demos). HW-heavy but grade is test-based, first test will be HARD but focus on getting partial credit and not going over time and you'll do well.
Could say he is my best professor in my ME journey so far. Exam is hard. But he was very chill to talk to and love to help you if you reach out and ask. Loved this class.

This class is really challenging but you will learn so much. You need to go to lectures and work hard/ahead of time to do well, but the content is interesting and Dr. Yee explains it well. Homework is 5-10 hours weekly but the exams are exactly like the homework problems so you'll be prepared. He's also really nice and helpful during office hours!

This man is the epitome of a state school professor. He gives way to much homework, and does not prepare students for the exams, which make up 90% of you grade. It bugs me because I have also had professors in upper level classes do the exact opposite of him, and things went so much better. Taking this class is a terrible decision.

He missed like 75% of the lectures leading up to an exam and still gave it and would have extremely long homeworks due the day of an exam and instead of talking about or reviewing the final he just did lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Homework regularly took 10+ hours. Test questions were much harder than homework questions. Lecture pace was very quick. His TA taught one class and that was the most helpful lecture of the semester. :(
The best professor I've had at Tech so far. There's a lot of homework, but you come out of his class really understanding the material. He works to make lectures easy to pay attention to.
Good guy. Chill guy. Homework takes a good amount of time to complete, but spending the time to understand the homework really helps on the exams.

One of the best professors I've had at Tech! Enthusiastic lectures, explains difficult concepts very well, but very quickly. Homeworks take about 10-12 hours to finish, but his exams are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was a good teacher and made class interesting, but his expectations of the students were incredibly high.  Homework assignments regularly took as long as 30+ hours to complete.

Awesome professor, chill, and very helpful! Hard class by nature, but definitely a great teacher! He makes his tests as hard as they should be for this class and nothing more. Curves and is very fair.

Epitome of bad grading policy. Tests are easy but messing up in the smallest way means you can lose 10% of your grade in class instantly. Horrible grading policy and unwilling to work with students. Not to mention his class is heavily test driven, making it far more stressful than need be.

Dr. Chen is a very clear lecturer. He comes off gruff and unfriendly, however, his class is very straightforward. Unproctored/open note/open book tests with content that comes almost directly from homework and lecture. He gives almost no partial credit so there is no room for error. I really enjoyed his class and found the workload was reasonable.

Chen's lectures are filled with examples, which is great, but he doesnt respond well to students asking questions. Also, his exams are relatively straightforward, but if you make a small mistake, you will lose so many points, and the tests account for 90% of your overall grade so you better not make a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is so bad. Exams were fairly simple but my goodness he had homeworks every week in his class. Even during exam weeks he gave a HW during the first exam. And if you make simple mistakes so many points are gone. He's a pretty average professor all things considered but not one I would like to take again.

Professor Chen is honestly a gem among professors. I have never been so painfully (and I do mean painfully) clear about the subject material of a class. His homework is very concise, and the tests are reasonable. Some words of caution: he's bad at answering questions in class, hopelessly boring, and a tough grader (with no latework).

He is kind of rude and does not care about students. No homework announcements online or lecture stuff online. However, if you go to his lectures and take notes, he makes stuff very easy and straightforward. His exams are very simple and always multiple 100's in class. Homework every week but only 10% so meh.

I took this course online, but viewed the same lectures and took the same tests as in class students over Summer 2015. I watched all lectures and completed all homework. Exams were open book and straight from taught material; no surprises. He is very simple and straightforward, knows the material well. However, partial credit is minimal.
Clearest and best lectures I've had. But avoiding asking questions. Attendance is mandatory. Toughest grader I've ever had. Would not recommend him.
clear and thorough in lectures; tests are hard; he doesn't like to answer questions, but you shouldn't have to ask many

Great prof.  Very clear and straightforward (taught straight from the book and assigned hw similarly). HW was easy using the book and tests threw no major curve balls if you took good notes.  However, he was not very merciful with partial credit on one of our tests.  The book is REQURIED during tests as he references it for test questions.

He is a very strict grader and can be intimidating (even condescending) in lectures, but he's still one of the best professors I've had. He knows his stuff and is very clear. Homework from the book almost every week (usually around 5 problems).  His tests are straight forward and similar to homework/classwork problems.

He has very clear and organized lectures. The homework is completely doable from lecture notes, which is a nice change of pace for Tech.  He doesn't like to answer questions and can be condescending, but I think it is worth it for the lecture quality.  His tests are multiple choice, but otherwise not particularly difficult.
He's a very rude professor who's not at all interested in the student. Home works every week from the text book.
He is very rude to all students and has a bad grading policy. Even though his tests are easy, you will lose half the points if you make even a trivial calculation error.
Very rude to students, so do not bother asking questions in lecture. Accused many people of plagiarism on homework, I will probably fail since I was falsely accused.
Don't miss lecture and don't bother reading any of the textbook.

Easy A. If you care about the subject you will learn a lot from PowerPoints, but everything is very disorganized, and not a lot of incentive to put in solid work. Yen is very funny though, understanding if you need to miss class, and will put in the effort to get to know you and talk to you about things outside of class. Low stress, low-risk class.

Great professor overall, definitely cares about her students. Tests are textbook heavy, if you create a study guide based on the chapters covered (vocab, hypotheses, figures) you will do well. Lectures are redundant on the textbook material. Engagement & participation is a large part of the class as well as a semester long project & research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her classes are entirely disorganized. She never sticks to syllabus and rarely answers emails. The work itself isn't hard but there is no rubric or grading scheme. 3/4 of the lectures are student presentations and she rarely teaches any actual material. Overall the class was easy but needed way more work than necessary to figure out what to do.

Lots of random busy work, but if you do it all, you get an A. Lets you use your textbook on quizzes in class, so always bring it. Tests are easy if you read the sections of the book that are presented in the power point.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She does not follow the syllabus. She frequently emails students 2 days before class saying we all have to present on some topic. Over the semester, each person probably had to present about 15 times. When students talk about something they read in the book she acts surprised like she has never heard it before. All homework comes from the textbook

If Dr. Zhang is teaching 2040, sign up asap. Provides tons of practice on the material, and her videos explain the concepts very well (didn't need to read the textbook at all). Tests are like the textbook and practice problems she provides.

One of the most considerate people you will ever meet. She genuinely cares about your well-being and will adjust homework due dates if you ask her. Her tests are exactly like her homework, so if you prepare properly, you'll be fine. The class exercises are kind of abundant, but they're similar to the homework and tests, only preparing you further.

Very boring lectures, but she went through all the problems and techniques we needed for the tests. Homework solutions and lecture notes are all posted online, which makes prepping for exams pretty straightforward.
Be ready for the dullest lecture at Tech. Other than that, she's a solid teacher, explains everything pretty well, and publishes her notes regularly. Tests are fair.

She explained concepts very well during lectures and taught what was on the tests. The homework was also pretty easy to do based on the concepts taught. My only gripe were the pop quizzes since there was not enough time given. However, only about 2 of the 7 ended up counting since she dropped most of them. Would highly recommend taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang really explained the concepts for ECE 2040 well and structures the class well-enough (via sample q's and HW) that you'll be prepared for her tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is a really good professor; if you're taking ECE 2040, please consider her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lectures were extremely clear: discuss new concept, then go through examples. All notes were written on the projector and uploaded online, and there were quizzes most days, but they didn't count for a lot and helped make sure I didn't get behind. Homework was helpful, and helped immensely for tests.

Terrible lecturer, the best strategy is to read the textbook beforehand so that you are able to follow along in class (or just attend at all and solely rely on the textbook). Tests are quite easy though and if you do the suggested exercises it is easy to do well. 
tl;dr easy, but you have to teach yourself.

Lecture is just Yi going over basic concepts and "working" example problems. A little hard to understand and skips LOTS of steps with examples. Tests are really easy though if you know the materials. Tells you what will be on it. Homework not mandatory and if you can do the homework tests are easy.
Not too hard of a class if you do all the homework.  Hard to understand him.  Tests are fair because he tells you what will be on them, and there are no tricks in his questions.

Chen's lectures were usually boring and hard to follow so I had to learn through doing the homework and going to studio but compared to other professors his tests and quizzes were a lot easier which made up the majority of the grade.

His lectures are super boring and hard to pay attention in, especially online. He is definitely not the best at explaining things, and rushes through topics he think we should already understand. The class was not so difficult be he makes it hard to stay motivated. He does mean well though, just isn't the best at expressing it.

Professor Chen really means well and is a caring professor. However, his lectures are very monotonous, which makes it really challenging to pay attention, especially online. Textbook really carried through the course.
not good
He's boring as hell but his tests are easier than Jankowski's. Also gave us candy on Halloween. Means well and is very good at explaining. Overall a solid choice for linear.
he can't teach. I self studied. His tests are not similar at all to practice exams given. Do not pick

This class is honestly a lot more work than 2 credit hours. However, Professor Liu is quite nice and is accessible after class. His lectures are the same as the textbook so you can just read it instead. Definitely focus on the homework since a lot of the questions on the tests/quizzes are from there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yea let's make a 2 credit multi class require the effort of a 3 credit class while simultaneously being a incompetent professor whose exams are not representative of content and also have preposterous grading rubrics!!!!

This guy is so bad at teaching. Literally read the textbook, you will be so much better off than going to his lectures. His lecture hall was full the first day of class, and by the second week, it was only 1/4 full. 

Seriously, don't waste your time going to his lectures and just read the textbook.

Saw someone describe him as "too smart for his own good" and agree. He's definitely very smart but not great at teaching. Lectures are slides straight out of the textbook. Very forgiving grading scheme as long as you do the homework. Lots of partial credit on exams. No Piazza or Ed so you have to go to office hours for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu might have taught the only math class I didn't genuinely hate at Georgia Tech. His lectures were smooth, with the occasional random joke thrown in, and attendance was not mandated at all. His tests were based almost exactly off of the homework so if you did well on the homework, you knew you'd do well on the tests. Would Recommend.

His lectures are a little hard to follow, and he posts notes but they aren't useful without him talking (he doesn't post lecture videos). It mostly working thru something conceptually (it's confusing) and the actual notes are just excerpts from the textbook. The textbook is much more helpful. The quizzes, however, are a good knowledge check.

Professor Liu is definitely not everybody's cup of tea but he was mine. Amazing lectures because he cracks jokes but also knows when to be serious. Also he is nice most of the time. Would highly recommend, especially if you don't know too much about Calc 3 (but be prepared to do a lot of homework and take quizzes).

This class is no joke, but the tests and quizzes were open-note to compensate for the pandemic situation. Given that, you still need to either attend lectures or read the textbook on your own. I read the textbook on my own since the professor just read from the textbook during lectures. The recitations were helpful, but there is a lot of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor reads straight from the textbook during lectures, so going to class is basically pointless. Never answers Piazza questions or posts solutions to practice tests. Youre really on your own for the class if you take this professor, and multivariable calculus by yourself is no walk in the park.

He pretty much copied the textbook on the board and (poorly) explained the concepts, so the only reason you have to actually show up is to get the attendance credit via "in class exercises". Posts practice exams online, but not the solutions to them, so there's no convenient way to check your work while working through them. Attend recitation!!!

Mr Liu is too smart for his own good. While he is very nice and is a fair grader, the lecture are really hardcore, and the homeworks are the hardest I've ever done in my life, and I am a 4.0 student in mechanical engineering. The only way to pass is to work like a maniac. However, I still learned a lot and don't regret.

teaches straight from the textbook and is very difficult to understand at first, but I actually liked it because it made me pay attention in class and learn the material. His tests and quizzes are very fair, defintely based off of the textbook and no trick problems. I would recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: All he does is put the textbook on the board. Literally started studying for a test and realised I had 50 pages of the textbook in my notebook, including "remarks" and "facts". If I wanted someone to read the textbook out to me without providing anything else, I'd get an Audible subscription. He's terrible.

Hope you like true false questions because that's about all you get to show what you know in this class. He lectures directly from the textbook to the board, yes he speaks only to the board. Because of the true false questions on all of the exams, quizzes and the final, there is no partial credit and it is entirely conceptual. yikes.

Exams were very difficult and lectures were almost word for word from the textbook. Very difficult to understand when talking (faced board almost the entire time). Very difficult to reach via email (3-5 days to respond if at all). Daily quizzes made attendance almost mandatory and exams were very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very smart professor, interesting course.
Quizzes everyday but go in with homework.  Hard to understand, but really easy class.  He tries his best to be clear.  85 is an A.. sooo... ya

He makes no sense and talks to the board. Make friends with the PLUS leader and the TAs and you will be able to make a decent grade because he has a different grading scale (60-69 is C, 70-84 is B, 85 up is A). He was literally the worst and I am so scared for Calc 2 because I learned nothing in this class.

Hard to understand and lectures would be useless except the daily quizes make it pretty mandatory. If you actually want to learn you have to use the textbook or hope for a good TA. Do not take if you want to learn Calc.

Do not take if you want to learn Calc 1. Hard to understand and his lectures are DIRECTLY from the textbook. He does not explain the concepts well. He just rewrites directly on the board. daily quizzes are pretty difficult. To get a good grade you have to rely on the curve at the end of class

His tests are very hard and the daily quizzes make class pretty mandatory. His very hard to understand and is terrible at teaching the topics discussed. Having never taken Calc before this class, I'm pretty sure I know just as much now as I did going into the class. Too bad other teachers don't let you use a TI-89. Avoid at all costs!!!

He gives quizzes every class, so it makes lecture kinda mandatory (which is really boring). But he does sometimes slip in jokes which are funny if you can understand him. And he is an easy grader, for Calc 1, he allowed the use of the TI89 and he drops the lowest exam grade!
I am honestly terrified of receiving my final grade.

Professor Liu is extremely hard to understand. He writes what he is saying on the board, but his English is so bad that it still makes very little sense. His tests are ridiculously hard, and he seems to get joy out of people failing them. If you have not ever taken calculus avoid him at all costs!

horrible, test averages were 25,50,50. only way to pass is with curve. open notes-book-laptop tests, but no time to use them. hw is easy b/c you can just copy solution manual from library. impossible to understand, lecture is useless, avoid

Not only are his tests open notes and open book, but they're open-laptop as well. (But only "for information, not communication." Right.) I had him for Calc 3. The first time I took Calc 3 I had Ken Baker and got a D. With Dr. Liu, I got an A, and if anything I know less calculus now than I did the first time around. Awesome.
Lectures were useless. I had to learn everything from my TA.  Got a B in the class because of his easy grading scale.  One of those classes were you can do well and not learn much.

Professor was very responsive to any questions/concerns via piazza or email. She is super caring and wants you to do well - she organizes a review session before each exam and basically tells you what types of problems will be on the test (2 pts extra credit for crib sheet). The content is hard though if you're not that great with mass balances.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Yiacoumi really wants you to succeed and tries really hard to be there for you, but lectures are disorganized and she always seems surprised at what is on her own powerpoints. Overall, gives a lot of hints about what will be on the tests but you are graded by basically nothing so one bad grade tanks you forever. But an 85 was an A, 70 was a B.
Shes caring but doesnt explain the topics very well, maybe because her accent is difficult to understand at times.

A great professor that is very knowledgable about the subject. Wants the student to succeed on tests, so make sure that you are there on review days. Homework and lecture examples show up on the test and she gives you a lot of hints on what could be on the test during review day. 25% hw, 25% test 1, 25% test 2 and 25% final that is not cumulative.
Makes the course more interesting. Great professor to talk to about grad school.

Great professor. Very interested in student success and fair tests. Attendance recommended because you learn a lot in class but non mandatory. Homework comes from the textbook and she shows on her powerpoints which problems are relevant to what example so it can be solved

Summer 2020. He was fair. If I struggled, I read the book. HW was 100% of grade. There was ec, and he dropped the lowest hw. (He gives hw hints in lecs.) There were coding hws, and I saved time by using Desmos. HW was challenging, and it took me 4+ days. Start ASAP. This class could be MUCH harder with a different teacher, so Yao is a good choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is definitely a nice person. He isn't the best lecturer, but his office hours are a lot more clearer. The PLUS sessions and recitation helped me the most with understanding diffeq. There are a lot of bonus problems, but most times, they are hard, so you wouldn't always be able to get full points on them. Use the book for practice.

He is a nice guy and great at math, but not teaching. He writes a lot on the board in lecture with insufficient verbal explanation. I learned most of the material from the TA. Dr. Yao gives a ton of bonus problems on assessments, but midterms are harder than what the class prepares you for. Optional homework from book; MML would have been helpful.

I took Diff Eq with him online summer and was pleasantly surprised. Lectures were understandable, and he taught the concepts well. Because it was online, the grading almost totally had to come from the tests, which some people found hard, but he did curve at the end as necessary. I especially liked he used class time to do test-level examples.

The class itself is easy and fun. The class did not have much busy work but just homework due each night before the class, which took like 30 minutes max. Class itself is fun too, a lot of discussion and talking.
easy class, just watch 4 films a week and write discussion posts on them. no final, but you have to film a youtube video and youtube short about one of the films. really lenient in grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a very easy humanities class and is interesting topics. I think the professor was a little tough on some grading and even though the class is an easy A there were times I was worried due to the weighting of assignments and how easily you could lose points so watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I found this class pretty annoying - two full movies of mixed quality each week. Quickly skimming through films and online reviews was enough to get by. The discussion posts were trivial (only 5-10 sentences per movie), and the final project was slightly longer but still easy.

I didn't get much out of it, but it was an easy A for elective credit.

Class just consists of watching Korean historical movies, writing discussion posts, and a final project. Movies are super enjoyable and interesting. Though a bit of a time commitment (since each movie is ~2 hrs long & you have 4 a week (took late summer)), super fun & easy humanity to take.
The class was just watching several movies and talking about them. Good free elective to take (guaranteed A with low effort) and the movies are pretty fun to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I have taken his course for 2023 Spring after reading this reviews, and I think that he was pretty nice person. Try to get along with the class with participation, and do all the assignments then you will be just fine! Also attendance of course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is a great teacher; he is always readily available through email and sets up zoom meetings every couple of weeks. This class is consisted entirely of watching 2-4 movies a week and a short discussion following. They are very easy A's as long as you make sure you have all the required information.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really easy class. All you needed to do was do a discussion post every day (summer semester).
Just don't take it. This is not a Korean class. If you support democrats you'll love it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Just don't take this professor's class. He is supposed to teach a Korean, but he is talking about politics entire lectures. I'm not quite sure about the reason why this class considered as a KOREAN class instead of POLITICS. Most importantly, he has the most annoying grading system. You have to submit discussion at least 6 hours before the deadline
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Watch two films a week, and do a basic discussion. Not very hard although the final projects original option seemed more tedious, however he changed the project midway through the semester to make it more simple. The course was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I started the class with no foundation, after the course, I improve a lot. Take this course if you really love Korean.

Strict attendance policy and curriculum is all over the place. We did use a textbook, but none of the tests reflected them. The average on the first test was in the 90's, but the second was the low 70's. Never really explained grammar concepts until people got them wrong. He gives a lot of extra credit, and the classes themselves are easy though.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS CLASS!!! Probably by far the best one I've taken. She is so thorough with Korean history and every class was super engaging. It was a lot of essays, discussions, readings, and movies, but it really taught me a lot and opened my eyes to so many types of media. She can be hard grading, but I think it's mostly fair. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!
Her grading is rather arbitrary. She is also rude when she gives you feedback sometimes. Maybe she is taking out her grievances on the STEM students idk lol
Too much assignments with tough grading system. There was no rubric how she's going to grade each assignment. It was very confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is a lot of assignment to work on every week which requires you to write. She is a tough grader and your participation matters a lot.

This class pleasantly surprised me. We talked about a lot of nuanced topics such as cultural appropriation, male gaze, and soft power while enjoying the best of Korean media. Prof Bae had interesting videos and discussions, and I did learn a lot about the good and the bad of Korean culture. Workload was just discussions posts and a final video.

Parisa is a very nice lady but her lectures are incredibly boring. 25% Group Project, 50% 2 Midterms, 5% Participation, and 20% Homework. Her first midterm was incredibly hard this semester after being a lot easier in the past, she was considerate and reweighted the midterm grades if you did better on the second one (very much helped me get an A).

Parisa is a very nice person, but god her lectures were hard to pay attention to, much less follow along. Homework was fair, but exams tend to be a good deal harder - though they are pretty similar to previous years' tests. Be prepared to self-teach.

Lectures are boring, she's knowledgable about the content but mostly rambles on and on about the same concept. Homeworks are short. Exams are fine as long as you know when to use which equation and write down all equations from the lecture slides on your crib sheets. Final project is easy, she grades them pretty leniently.

Looks like the ratings have tanked since I took this class in Fall 2023. I thought she was okay - didn't leave either a good or bad impression. Graded final project super leniently and crib sheet was allowed on exams which made them relatively easy.

Honestly, she reads a lot off of the slides and does not like to explain concepts more easily or digestible. She is smart but not helpful when it comes to communication and like to blame students for some of her faults. I would not suggest taking her, take McDonald.

She was very irresponsive, does not respond to email and fails to address questions students have. Completely bamboozled the entire class when she said at the end of the semester that the attendance grade is either you get all of it or none of it. She definitely is smart and knows what she is doing, just not very responsive to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She made lecture required and had an all or nothing policy (you either get 5% or you don't), which was very annoying. Lectures are incredibly boring -- to be fair the course content is very dry. She does care about student success though and has opportunities to improve your grade. However communication through our the course straight horrible.
terrible at teaching. didn't know stats herself.
got mad, didn't know how to teach, didn't teach anything.
Got angry and blamed students for not knowing things she didn't even teach.
Graded HWs and participation exercises at very end of the semester, so you never know how you're going to do. Horrendous professor overall.
Terrible professor. Didn't send any instructions for final project until a week before and we had to submit an abstract early with no instructions. Doesn't grade things until late!!

Very bad lecturer and was tougher for many of my friends who had lesser math experience. Expected us to just know some things that weren't prereqs, and never said what would be included on tests. you kind of go into exams with no experience.

Worst professor ever. Ignored emails about excused absences for interviews, violating GaTech policies, and got angry when my advisor intervened. If I wasn't a math major, I would've done worse. Terrible at teaching with poor explanations, making it even harder for less-experienced students. Completely unacceptable.

The worst IE teacher I've had so far. She did not tell us what to study or know for tests. The tests always took more time than the class period. Has a terrible teaching style of writing derivations on the board, not explaining half of it, and not telling you if you need to know it for the test. Gets angry at the class for not knowing things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HWs aren't auto-100s but TAs are helpful if you reach out. Averaged 87 on both by just redoing the HWs and the sample exam. Group final project in place of final - directions pretty vague but just start early so you can ask her questions and the rest is easy. Relaxed class.
Parisa really cares about her students and actually wants them to do well and it's evident. It just comes down to you whether you seek out/use the help that she provides.
Good lecturer.

Definitely cares about her students and tries her best to spice up the material during lecture, but it's hard to make statistics fun.  3% extra credit boost and an easy group project instead of a final means you should get an A if you put in a reasonable amount of effort.  The two midterms are tough though, and attendance is randomly checked.

Good prof. The lecture structure was hard to follow, but the content easy enough that you can self teach everything. Not a hard class if you put in the work. She cares about student success and is always ready to answer student questions, even if she may be a little hard to approach. The group final paper was better than having a cumulative final.

This was probably the easiest engineering class I've taken at Tech. The content is a little boring but it's really easy to do well. There was a total of 6 homework, 2 midterms, and one final project  + could get  3% bonus for CIOs and she replaced the 1st midterm score if you did better on the 2nd. In other words, if you try, you should get an A!

In the beginning, I found myself struggling since I never took statistics. In class, I couldn't follow the lectures since I needed time to understand everything. When I explained my concerns, she allowed me to look at her old video lectures. If you take the time, you will learn a lot considering the professor understands the students!
cares about student success, curves. lectures and material isn't always the most engaging and clear
One of the best professors. If you do the necessary minimum, you should be good. She even gave us a 3% curve at the end for CIOS.

Lectures are a little dull, but Professor Zowj is really nice. Homeworks are pretty easy, there's one every week. Tests are a little difficult but there's tons of partial credit. The group project at the end was really straightforward and easy.
Boring lectures. Material is pretty easy.

Taken during COVID as an online course. All the class was was hour long recordings of her working through powerpoint slides that were very dull to watch. Homework was easy and from the textbook. The tests were very fair, and the final was a group project. Easy class, but you will not learn anything if you don't want to.
She's not the greatest lecturer. By no means bad, just standard and dry sometimes. The content is super easy though, and she wants you to do well in the class.

She is a great teacher that makes very simple tests and homework. You still have to study for them, but everything in the hw and tests are covered in the lectures and there are no trick questions. If you practice, the class is a very easy A. She is a little boring, but otherwise great professor.

Course is extremely easy especially if you took AP Statistics. She isn't that great of a professor, but because the content is so easy, it is very easy to self learn. Class is weighted heavily on tests, but she allows a cheat sheet for them and gives practice problems/exams beforehand. Caring and nice professor, but not a great instructor.

Parisa is a very kind professor. Her lectures are pretty average, which is not a bad thing. Homework and exams are not that difficult. She allows use of a crib sheet for each exam. It is very clear that Parisa cares a lot about her students, and also remembers that we have lives outside of her class.

A great teacher! She really tried not to focus on grades and more on learning and gave projects as chances to get any credit back you had lost. All you need to do is try and you can get an A. I learned so much!

Great if you want an A, but not to have a firm understanding of fluids. At the end of the semester I had a D, but  she lets us grade replace quiz grades with 5 hr extra credit projects (plural), which were time consuming when finals were right around the corner. No final/mid exam, just final/mid project. Supplement video lect provided.
She is super fun and very passionate about the course. She also cares a lot about her students. Class is very well structured with quizzes and projects. Do not take fluids with anyone else.

Very passionate lecturer + relates to students easily. Only spent 3hrs outside of class to prepare for quizzes. Her class is set up very well: Optional HW, 6 quizzes, fun Midterm and Final Proj. I found studying the notes to be sufficient for the quizzes. Had the option to grade replace all quizzes. Would not have wanted fluids w/ anyone else.

Possibly the nicest professor at Tech? She really loves what she teaches, and provides lecture notes and videos from a previous online semester. If you want an A in this class, you can put in the effort to get it.

Boni is such an awesome professor. Fluid mechanics is a very difficult class, but the way Boni set up this class made it so that you actually learned each section of material. She gives a lot of ways to improve your grade and understanding of the class. Definitely watch and attend lectures, as they are super helpful and entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very fun person and knowledgeable in fluids. Gives a lot of opportunities to make up for bad grades and makes the course interesting. Fluids is one of the tougher courses at GT but she made it decent, if not enjoyable.

If I could give her a 10 I would. I had a really difficult semester, and she gave me SO SO SO MUCH GRACE in her grading. She's not only an amazing teacher, but a very caring person who I plan to stay in contact with even though I am done with her classes. Take her!!
Parks sensei is the best, very nice professor and super easy on grading. Highly recommend!!

Parks Sensei is the nicest, funniest Professor at GT. Any class you take with her will be great. 3401 doesn't have a lot of assignments, but she is also a very nice grader and genuinely cares for her students. Got lunch with her once, very fun to talk to.

Sensee is one of the best professors I've had at Tech. She's fashionable, silly, and so open to her students. She treats you as a friend. I took JAPN3401, which is a discussion-based class with few assignments throughout the semester. I took this for a free-elective credit, and I would 100% take her again for no credit at all.

I took her lbat class; she's very fun and engaging! She always makes a massive effort to engage with students' individual interests and she likes to talk about music/rap. Feedback is good and she's accessible for questions :)

Professor Parks was an incredible teacher to be around, always bringing a cheerful atmosphere and attitude to everything she did. So long as you put in the work and did your best to participate in class, you can guarantee that you'll do well. her online course is a lot of homework so make sure you pace yourself & don't procrastinate.

Parks sensei is an amazing prof, not to mention her fashion sense is top tier lol. While she does give many assignments for homework, she is a funny, sweet, and understanding professor and an easy grader! Pretty easy A! All quizzes, tests, & HW are online, too. Great lecturer as well :))

Parks Sensei was my favorite teacher I've ever had at GT. Always accessible and caring. Absolutely hilarious and super friendly! If I could take her for every single JAPN class I would. She is amazing. :)
Yumi sensei is very caring and fun professor. She gives out a good amount of work each week but they are all very doable and doesn't take much time.

If I could give this professor every single one of the good tags, I would. Parks sensee is very easy to work with, communicates clearly, and she truly cares. Learning a language takes effort, but you will have many easy-100% practice assignments for grammar, vocab, and kanji, which help to pad the grade. You also practice speaking in class a lot.

Please just read and collaborate with people in the course to understand stuff. Tests are not hard, though you should be prepared for anything. He's mediocre at teaching concepts, with the homeworks taking anywhere between 30 minutes and 10 hours. He's pretty generous on deadlines. Please prepare for tests a week in advance, as HW is a lost cause.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decently chill dude, is pretty reasonable when it comes to any discrepancies in deadlines/HW because sometimes his directions aren't 100% clear. He gives lots of partial credit for exams. they feel hard in the moment, but my grades were surprising. Expect test grade releases to take long and expect some miscommunication about assignment details.

The class itself is very easy with the first ~14 lectures being trivial. Midterm 1 and 2 and finals are trivially easy. However, the prof does not teach his class well, with lectures being a waste of time. You can self study using the textbook though. Homework "extra credit" is capped 15% effectively making it worthless.

I have never written a review for a professor before but this professor made me want to warn other people. His lectures and lecture slides are entirely useless, and all his tests are some obscure problems from the textbook and homework is 10hrs/week minimum. He promises extra credit on homework but that extra credit is limited to only the homework.

Does not explain things well and barely provides anything useful on the lecture slides. He gives lots of extra credit on homework, which is nice, but the assignments start getting ridiculously hard because he simply pulls random questions from the textbook that no one can solve and puts them on the homework and tests. 8 hours of homework per week.

Prof. Kim is very nice, though sometimes hard to understand. The class is structured for an easy A. Grades focus on participation, 2 group projects, and 3 tests (only 10% each). Huge plus: You can earn up to 10 points of extra credit (a full letter grade), so take advantage of it!

He seems like he might be mean, but he is very nice. He is understanding. He does make this class more work than it has to be, but he is a very easy grader. I would recommend taking with him! He doesn't have a final, and he has three tests and participation is what matters the most and is fairly easy to earn.

Class was fairly easy, however, the tests were so difficult for it being an easier class. Lots of self-learning and reading the textbook will help. Group projects weren't so bad but the whole semester was group based.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is super chill and he allows you to take quizzes online/open note. The exams were team and essay based. He was really kind and understanding. His overall goal is to help people with their GPA and make sure that you can apply the knowledge instead of just memorizing. He gives homework but it is not so much where you are dying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is one of the kindest professors I have had. He cares about his students and his class reflects that. The material is fairly easy and most of it is common sense. Most of the grades are group based, but the homework is individual journal entries that usually take up one whole word document.
Monotone and just rereads the textbook, but you'll get an A.

So I hate group projects and more than that papers... This class is based soley off those things BUT it is super easy. Pretty much everyone gets an A atleast until the final. If you search each practice question he gives you on the powerpoints in quizlet you'll be good to go for that. Suprisingly I felt like I learned the subject and didn't do much

Almost all the exams and homework had extra credit. Her lectures were very informative, and though she does have a slight accent if you ask questions she will clear it up. Recorded lectures and notes are online. Just put in minimum effort and you good for a A or B.
She isn't the best lecturer but she's very smart with the material and approachable for questions. Her tests are very fair as long as you understand the homeworks you will get an A or B

Dr. Hu was a really good professor. I never read the textbook and only came to lectures and I feel like I have a strong grasp of the concepts.
