You have to go to office hours to see corrections on your tests which is a little annoying, but she has a lot of potential extra credit available in the form of an extra 1-2 problems on every homework
Her lectures mainly came from the textbook. The exams were predictable, but somewhat difficult.

Dr Hu set clear guidelines from the start about what to expect. Attendance was mandatory and was 5% of our grade. Tests were straight from hw problems, and the final was harder than the others. She curved, but I had trouble and thought I wouldn't get an A. I suggest going to graders' office hours so they get to know you (and grade easier).

Lectures are pretty boring and she uses clicker questions but homeworks are straightforward and not too heavy if you plan properly, and then tests are very similar to the homework questions.  Lots of partial credit on tests and reasonable expectations.  Watch Wayne Whiteman's coursera videos for the content, take Dr. Hu for her reasonable tests.

Nice teacher who seemed like she decently cared about our success. Lectures basically came from the book but you'll have to end up reading the book anyway. The practice problems in the book and the HWs will help you learn the material. HWs took forever to get back because you had to turn it in on paper. OHs were helpful for HWs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CHBE 2130 I did not like the way this class was structured. While her lectures were informative, I feel that they did not prepare us to do the homeworks (which were brutal) and for the exams. The class started off easy, but by the end of the semester, it was rough. She WANTS to give out good grades, so you will most likely end up with an A or B.
Dr. Hu lays down a fundamental guideline for what is to be expected from the course. Her midterms are right from the lecture problems. The final is a bit harder but the class has a decent curve.

Teaches the material well, however you need to come to class prepared having already read the textbook. You also need to pay attention during lecture, if you look down for a second she's already on a entirely different problem or nearly done with the problem.

Great professor and class. Although the content was pretty advanced, she was really caring and gave extensions when needed. The homework problems were challenging but engaging, and her lectures were pleasant and interesting. I was happy to see that MATH 7012 was offered for the first time in years, and Dr. Yu did a great job with teaching it.

While sometimes her lectures were sometimes difficult to follow, they were adequate to come away with a solid understanding. Be sure to stay on top of the material. Where Yu shines as a professor is during office hours, where she is very helpful and kind and always makes herself available. I had her fall 2023.

Professor Yu is a solid lecturer. It was slightly easier for me because I took AP Calc in high school. Just show up to class, review your notes/posted lecture notes, and do the practice exams and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: First midterm was very different than the practice material, and I know a lot of students had difficulties with that. Dr. Yu is a great lecturer though, and she was always prepared with relevant examples and explained things clearly.

this class was the first b i've ever gotten, but that's not her fault. the material is difficult (especially if you've never taken a calc class before like me) and she covers it quickly but if you don't slack off you'll be fine. it's a standardized class at gt so the material, tests, and grading schemes will be the same for every professor.

Dr. Yu's lectures oftentimes were confusing and a little bit hard to follow, but she always made up for it with her kindness and willingness to meet with students outside of the classroom. She was never condescending, and always came across as a calm, kind, and understanding individual. Not a great teacher, but a good person.

This class proved to be extremely difficult even with an AP Calc background from hs. Dr. Yu was amazing, but the practice exams provided by the dept were misleading. Practice exams were easy 100s in 20 minutes, but the exams were a challenge. Study hard from the beginning and ask a lot of questions. Sharpen up your algebra skills before this class.

Prof Yu is easily accessible outside of class. She was understanding and gracious in making accommodations for me due to extenuating circumstances. She is kind and genuinely cares about her students. Linear itself was very confusing for me so I struggled a lot with the concepts, but I think Dr Yu did her best to teach it. ** Get a good TA / tutor !
Loved her lecture style! She somehow made linear algebra the best class of the semester.

One of the best, maybe THE best, professor I've had at Tech. Would've marked difficulty higher had it not been for her excellent lectures. Focus on techniques and proofs equally. Breaks up lecture with problems to work, which helps me focus. Proofs during lecture are easier to follow than reading the book (rare imo). Balances rigor with intuition.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at Tech; very caring, encourages peer interaction during lectures, and homework/exams are challenging but fair. Only thing I will say though is her teaching style is definitely best suited for smaller, upper level math courses. I could see her lectures being hard to grasp in a 1000/2000 level course
I loved Dr. Yu!! She did a great job.

personally loved her lecture style!! it took until the homework for the material to stick, but i blame that on the nature of the class as a whole. her teaching is clear and concise, and in the worst-case scenario, there are jankowski's videos to further explain the concepts.

Linear Algebra is a hard concept in general so I feel like Prof Yu did a pretty good job at giving good example and connecting the theorems to the math (linear is heavily reliant on understanding theorems). Only complaint is she would use the vocab like we already should know what they mean (this can be resolved by reading before lecture).

Professor Yu is a solid lecturer, and if you need help outside of class, she makes sure her office hours are readily available. While linear algebra can be a very conceptual subject, she made it understandable as well as doing plenty of problem-solving examples in class. The textbook is free/online as well, and a great resource.
Prof. Yu had great lectures, though they were fast-paced so it took some time outside to understand everything. She is also really caring and always available to answer questions and help students.

Easy class. I never really paid attention to Prof. Yu but the few times I did I just got confused and there were a lot of basic arithmetic mistakes while she did out problems. On the whole she seemed like a nice and accessible professor, however. My advice would be to just watch Chris Jankowski's video lectures.

This class was a challenge for everyone I knew in it, including many people with prior calculus experience. This course's design harshly punishes laziness and failure to attend lecture; the exams were brutally difficult, and the weekly timed quizzes were never easy. If you take Dr. Yu, be prepared to put in lots of time outside of class for an A.

Professor Yu was a really good professor, she is caring and is often available outside of class. Be careful of the exams in general as they do have a greater difficulty than the exercises seen on class or in the homework, however extra problems are given to solve this issue. As well a list of the type of problems on the exams is given beforehand.

1551 for Spring 2022 was extremely hard for no reason. The class was a mess. The average on the first exam was around 55. The test was completely different than anything she taught us. We had to beg her to give extra credit so that it would help our class. Her lectures are very all over the place. Do not take her if you can help it.

Lectures were recorded and based of a worksheet we did in class. Class was difficult but huge curve was applied to first exam due to poor class performance. 1 homework and 1 quiz dropped, 2 quizzes replaced with 100. If you were failing the class but could pass the final she said she will pass you in the class. Easy HW, with fair test and quizzes.
Professor Yu is a wonderful person but, her lectures are difficult to follow and the quizzes/ tests are extremely hard.

This was Professor Yu's first time teaching MATH 1551 at tech I believe, and she did a very good job. first test was an outlier but a curve was applied that helped everyone and all tests after weren't too hard. She has very good lectures where she carefully walks through all of her procedures as well, and even records them if you miss a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu is a nice lady but she's not a good professor. Her lectures are confusing, her quizzes are extremely difficult (sometimes the TAs couldn't even help), and her exams are SO HARD. She was reluctant to provide extra credit or curve exams despite most of the class failing. Even people that took AP Calc in high school struggled with this class.

First test was skewed because it tested on different material than what we covered. Prof offered a huge curve.
Second exam and final she also gave us a 'practice' exam that was basically identical. For the final we were allowed two pages of notes and a grade of 70% guaranteed a C in class.

The same ~15 people showed up to lecture hall of 100.

This class is tough and you'll need to be prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material, but kinda in a good way. In class, students just present proofs & she picks them apart. Homework & test heavy, but she is pretty fair with grading. The worst part are the super fast timed quizzes, but not worth too much. Work hard & you can do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: An amazing professor! Lectures were interactive and I felt really prepared for the tests, which were fair. She welcomes questions in office hours and always helps with the homework. So patient, caring, and helpful, especially during the pandemic. Not condescending at all, and I learned so much. Wish I could have her for all my classes.

One of those professors who isn't really interested in their students, just knows that she's responsible for teaching them material. Read the textbook before the lectures and you'll understand the material better. She isn't very helpful during office hours and she's pretty condescending when you ask questions in office hours or class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her when it was her first time teaching Calc2. She was very passionate about what she was teaching and had incredible knowledge about the topic. She was very accessible outside of class and very helpful whenever you would go to her for help. Going to every lecture and then finding time to go to her office hours, makes a big difference.

Definitely need the online textbook- you do homework through it. Also, there are a few problems to do (online) at the beginning of the class that count for attendance as well. She's great, really wants you to pass, and has helpful office hours. Definitely start going to office hours early- if she recognizes you, she likes you and helps you first.

Dr. Yu was not perfect (this was her first time teaching Calc 2)! While class lectures were tedious, she proved to be very effective in office hours. She was very patient and understanding when you had questions about grading or why one approach to a problem is incorrect! Just make sure to do a bunch of studying on your own and office hours!

If you haven't already taken calc, her lectures don't really make all that much sense. I could only get the material once I went to recitation and my TA explained it, and I had to go to the PLUS sessions to get extra help. Homework and in class clickers are a joke, so unless you're willing to give 120% for this class, pick a different teacher.
she did not seem interested in curving my 73 to a B and I really can't forgive her for that

Dr. Yu conveyed material well and was well-versed in calculus. It was odd how she would devise weird/challenging examples in class that were mostly unhelpful. Participation can be dropped. Tests/quizzes were somewhat difficult -- doing study guides are key to doing well. She takes questions right from them. Overall, a decent choice.

If you haven't taken calculus before, you probably won't do all that well. She'll write out examples on the board and not realize a mistake until someone points it out, which usually won't be until she's done working it out and realizes she got the wrong answer. Nice handwriting. She wants to help, but doesn't understand what people struggle with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I am currently taking MATH1552 with Dr. Yu and after attending one of Barone's lectures I can totally see the difference between their method of teaching. I personally cannot concentrate in her class no matter how hard I try. She does very extra explanations that sometimes are not even going to be applied on the test. Look for another professor!!

Dr. Yu is a very cool cat. Her homework is not easy, and her tests were pretty hard for a mortal like me. However, she has a clear passion for mathematics, and that clearly shows in her teaching. Sometimes her explanations are a little murky, but she's always happy to try to clarify. She also grades on the easy side. Good professor.

I had an excellent experience in this class. The lectures were very good in my opinion, but the homework is very difficult. Expect to put a lot of time into the homework. Generally, I found her to be a very reasonable and caring professor. It's hard, but I'd recommend her. I learned a ton.

She's a pretty reasonable professor overall, she explains things pretty well, her tests and quizzes are not easy, but if you know the material, you should be okay, going to class isn't mandatory, but it can help

Very fair professor, course consisted of a mix of group and individual quizzes, and lots of in-class practice to help you succeed. Did do some studying outside of class and labs were long but never a class I would stress out about. Easy lab science and Zachary makes it a wonderful experience. TAs were great too.

He is very passionate about what he teaches and the lecture material is easy. No midterms, only individual and group quizzes, and optional final exam. Lab is worth like 25% of your grade (and is very easy) so you're practically guaranteed an A if you study the TA lecture notes.

Dr. Handlos is extremely passionate about the material, and he has a way of making you care about it too, even on boring topics I never thought I would care about. He also really cares about the students and is very accessible and willing to answer questions. One time when the class did really poorly on one of the quizzes he even let us revise it.
EAS 1600 was a very fun and easy class, like I was genuinely excited to go to it. Dr. Handlos seemed super passionate about the material and he was helpful during office hours.

Very nice and genuine professor. Lectures are okay but survivable, attendance is "mandatory" but only requires a code to be typed on canvas. Quizzes are very straightforward and sufficient study materials are provided. Overall a great class and a good way to fill the science requirement.
Great intro to weather and a fun class. Handlos is into "ungrading" and uses it for most his smaller sized classes, so this is an easy A if you put in the appropriate effort.

Dr. Handlos is an outstanding professor. Even having no prior experience to weather studies, I found his weather physics course extremely accessible due to his engaging lectures and fun personality. PHYS 2750 was "ungraded" this semester, so it is clear that he values his students' success above all else.

Pretty good class overall. Half of your quizzes will be group quizzes, and it will feel like just about every week there's a quiz. Quizzes are mostly conceptual, so the study guides don't really help, as long as you listen to and review the lectures, you'll be fine. Minimal homework too !

I took EAS 2750. Absolutely one of my favorite profs. Actually cares about students. Amazing lectures, really interesting. Class was ungrading. Great projects. Really nice. Great communication. Great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class, 4 group quizzes + 4 individual quizzes, optional final! Attendance is mandatory and there are often in class activities, but most people just do work for other classes in lecture. Labs are really annoying and long (takes at least 2 hrs every time), but easy. He's a very kind professor and obviously very passionate, def recommend!

Prof. Handlos is a great lecturer! He is very passionate about the material and very easy to approach. He makes attendance mandatory, which is totally fine, since we sometimes have in-class activities which are free 100s. We also have either individual quizzes or group quizzes, which are all short and easy if you study the material a bit. No HW :)

Professor Handlos is easily one of the best professors I have had since coming to GT. He is very good at keeping students engaged in lecture and is very passionate about what he teaches. As long as you keep up with the lectures and labs you will have no problem getting an A.

Handlos is very kind and passionate when it comes to his teaching. He has an infectious energy that makes you want to learn more. This is a great EAS Lab science to take. No tests, only 6 small quizzes that counted the same. A lot of formulas but he gave us most of them.

Great professor but made things harder than it needed to be. Some quizzes were quite difficult, and that's especially frustrating for one who just wants to satisfy graduation requirements. Other than that, he is extremely knowledgeable and super passionate about EAS.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Handlos is such an awesome teacher. He is very considerate and caring for his students. Always with a great attitude and willing to help whenever you ask for. Thanks Dr. Handlos!

Super great! Grade is just 6 quizzes at 6 percent each, non cumulative. Final is optional and if you do take it your two lowest quiz scores get replaced. Quiz content is straight from lecture. Your grade is combined with lab, mandatory attendance, and participation. It's a light work course but you do need to study for the quizzes. Prof is amazing!
Relaxed atmosphere and organized course structure, but not an easy class. The course material can be quite challenge and time demanding. You need to work for it to earn an A.

Dr. Handlos is a saint. He is definitely very knowledgable over what he teaches so sometimes there seems to be a gap, but if you meet with him outside of lecture he is able to break it down to the basics if needed. He's one of the most considerate professors I've had at GT.
The class is pretty relaxed, and the professor is very enthusiastic about environmental science. The lectures were often interesting even with two-hour lectures.

Zak is INCREDIBLY knowledgeable and a wonderful resource. This was not an easy class by any means and got into the meat of remote sensing. He explains everything to an understandable level, always. The quizzes were fairly hard, and the final project is a lot especially if you aren't in the major. You do walk away with the knowledge you need!

Professor Handlos obviously cared about his students and actively tried to make class interesting even though it was online. His lectures are helpful and informative and as long as you study and understand the lecture slides you should be able to earn an A.

Zak is a really nice guy, and you can tell from day 1 that he cares about his students. Quizzes could be really difficult and try to trick you. Class averages were usually in the C range, and despite receiving negative feedback about quizzes he didn't change much. I made an A because lab is easy points and worth 30% of your grade.

Prof. Handlos is very enthusiastic about teaching the course. He takes the time to answer every question and is very understanding. I took light notes and mostly followed the lectures during class time. He posts all lecture slides and recordings. I go back to review for quizzes and homework. Quizzes can be tricky, but very manageable!

Super straightforward class: go to lecture, follow along on the slides that you can download. 10 question canvas quiz every other week which is super easy. Short homeworks and discussion posts every once in a while. Lab is super easy if you go to your assigned time slot, an hour of effort, the TA basically gives you the answers. Would take again.

Since switching to online, has made class much more difficult. 3 hour time slot labs take 4-5 hours each week, and on top of that you have a major quiz or 2-3 page homework every week. This is also coupled with graded practice quizzes and prelabs. Together you are spending MUCH more than 4 credit hours worth of time on this class each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Zak is a great guy with great energy. For this reason, it's almost impossible to dislike him. Nonetheless, the lectures for this course weren't necessarily interesting. I went to lectures for the participation quizzes and just reviewed the slides later on my own. Grading was really fair. An A is pretty much secured as long as you try!

Prof Handlos is a pretty caring and relaxed professor. Sometimes lectures can be a bit boring, but it's all pretty much in whether you care about the subject. You need to go to class because there are participation quizzes. Tests can be a little tough, but labs and discussion posts are pretty easy.
Very relaxed professor and extremely passionate about weather. He is really smart, but breaks complex concepts down so they're easy to understand. Extremely accessible outside of class.

Dr. Handlos is one of the best professors I have had so far. He explains the material well, and always answers students questions about the subject. Very good professor and I would take him again for other classes if I needed to.

Dr. Handlos is a very nice man. You can tell he really cares about his students and is passionate about the material. The material for 1601 is easy enough, though his class (which was entirely lecture based) was pretty boring and I felt like I was wasting time at points. I would take him again though.

Professor Handlos is such a great professor! Although the lecture slides are posted online, he does a good job of expanding on them in class and giving cool examples for them as well. He really cares about his students! The tests are pretty easy, and it's good to go to class to get Learning Catalytics points.

Absolutely loved this class. Great professor for this subject, lectures were great and you learn a lot. Class was recorded when I took it which was super helpful for going back and reviewing material. One of the classes it's actually worth attending despite not mandatory attendance. Exams were fair as well.

Very patient professor and incredibly accessible outside of class. Lectures were a little boring but he records it. Super test heavy, tests made up 85% the rest was homework. He is lenient in grading and overall great at listening to students and trying to understand their issues.

Very kind, knowledgable, and wants students to succeed. Lectures are extremely helpful and tests are very fair (the practice exams prepare you well for the test) - homework is manageable, and he is very kind and accessible during office hours and over email. Highly recommend - one of the best professors I have had at Tech.

This rating is for MATH 2603, as I couldn't find an option to add this course.

Great prof.  Lectures are fantastic and he posts lecture notes and occasionally zoom meetings online, as well as practice exams and exam solutions.  Homeworks are simple, but don't be fooled - exams can be tougher, so ensure you attend lecture to understand concepts.

Favorite prof so far. The lectures are great and adequately prepare you for the hw and exams. I'd recommend attending every class, even though its not required. It starts out easy and gets trickier with graph theory, but the exams keep pace. Walsh is nice, well-spoken, and smart. If you're ever confused, he's very approachable in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: good notes, very friendly and gives lots of partial credit on the exam. take this prof!!
Great guy, intuitive lectures, light grading.

Interesting and incredibly useful lectures. All lecture recordings and notes (and even HW & recitation problem solutions) are posted. Examples in class teach you how to approach problems very well, and the questions on the tests are perfectly in line with what he teaches -- no curveballs. Best professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very patient lecturer who gave many resources to prepare for exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Walsh's lectures are very clear and interesting. His notes align well with homework, quiz, and exam material. He has video recordings of lectures. He releases a practice exam and they will prepare you well for the actual exam. He is a very nice and motivated professor, going to Professor Walsh's office hours help a lot.

Exceptional teaching ability. Short weekly HWs and Sample quizzes/exams prepare you adequately for the exams. This class is test heavy, and the tests are fairly difficult, but he offers enough resources to prepare for them. Very helpful over Piazza, email, and OH. Also grades assignments very quickly and with feedback. Overall, solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Walsh was one of the best professors I've had at Georgia Tech. His lectures were clear and had many examples and problem walkthroughs to help students grasp concepts. Homeworks weren't very long, but were good practice, and exams were extremely fair. He also released practice tests for each exam to help us prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Walsh is the best option for 3012 if you can get into his class. He is extremely fair in grading, records lectures, and uses Piazza. He also takes all his HW questions from the textbook and quizzes/tests are similar to the practice so it feels fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs.
He's the goat. Definitely recommend and he's generous with partial credit on the exams. Absolutely based

Phenomenal teaching ability. It's like having the Organic Chemistry Tutor as your professor. Lectures are digestible and example heavy. Every homework was just 2-3 problems each. Tests were reasonable and are exactly like the practice tests. Lectures were recorded. Got real lucky taking a risk signing up with this new professor.

Walsh is goated. Each lecture is short and digestible; he explains things very well. He's flexible, lectures are recorded, just super chill. Office hrs are useful. Weighting kinda sucks tho: exam heavy, you aren't graded on much, which means less work but more on the line. No curve rn. I still think he's one of the best profs I've had-- lucked out.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who teaches content well and is fair with grading. Would highly recommend. The course material may be challenging but he explains it clearly.

Great professor. Math concepts are explained clearly in lecture and lecture content is paced well. HW assignments are graded promptly. Course expectations are clear, and the exams follow textbook homework and lecture content.

I wasn't a fan at first, but as soon as I started attending office hours he easily became one of my favorite teachers. His lectures aren't the best and exams are really really difficult BUT he's so sweet and if you just go to office hours you'll do fine. The homework assignments are difficult so ask him for help!

Hani is a very empathetic professor on top of being very knowledgeable. His lectures can be hard to follow but go to his office hours with questions/concerns and he'll hear you out & will slowly go over problems with you. Calc 2 in general at GT is a challenge but Hani's kindness & patience is a huge comfort. GO TO OFFICE HOURS & YOU WILL PASS!!!

I failed every test and quiz there was, but made 20 points above average on the final. I was half a point away from getting a B in the course. Hani said no. Whenever I went to ask for regrades, he would deny me even though the syllabus says to go to your professor for regrades. He gave breaks in class. Only aced the final because of my TA

Dr. Hani is a caring professor and knows the subject very well. However, his lecture is hard to follow sometimes because he usually does proofs. His tests and quizzes can be a bit hard but fair. Hope for a good TA!

I found Linear Algebra tricky so did struggle a bit. Professor Hani could also be wordy/confusing when explaining definitions/theorems and wrote quickly. But he did post all his lecture notes/examples on t-square. His quizzes/tests were of expected difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. I struggled in the beginning with linear algebra, but he was always available during office hours to help. Clear/straightforward lecturer. Would definitely recommend.

He's a very nice guy and cares about students. I like him both as a professor and as a person. I used the textbook to get a better grasp of the concepts and practiced using MathLab. His tests and quizzes are reflective of his lectures. I would definitely take him for another math course.

Hani is not the clearest lecturer for linear algebra. You'll definitely have to work outside of class to understand the concepts. He's helpful during his office hours for further understanding. His tests and quizzes are extremely fair. Comparing Hani to other professors who are better lecturers like Barone/Short, his test questions are WAAY nicer.

Dr. Hani was a pretty terrible teacher. He couldn't clearly explain anything in class, and he wasn't very accessible outside of class as he never responded to any of my emails. The only way I learned in this class was doing the homework and maybe a recitation or two.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hani is an awesome guy, but just an OK professor. The class is a joke, and Hani's lectures are extremely slow. In NO WAY is this class difficult, as Hani gives you more than enough time to grasp concepts.

Dr. Hani is my favorite professor so far. He is very clear in what you need to do to get a good grade and is also a good lecturer. He knew that 90 minute math lectures could get long, so he'd give breaks and tell jokes to break it up.  You can do well on his exams/quizzes if you pay attention and take somewhat decent notes.

Pretty easy.  Don't really need to textbook except for maybe the last section.  Really good about curving! Make sure you go to recitation, especially if you don't go to class, plus all quizzes and tests are in recitation.

He is a great teacher. He always seemed like he wanted the class to succeed. He gave homework that were similar to recitation worksheet problems and recitation worksheet problems that were similar to test problems. The tests were honestly not very hard. I rarely attended lecture but I was still able to get an A in the class. I would take him again!

Hani was incredibly nice and very approachable. He is fair in his policies/grading and an excellent teacher. I never actually went to lecture (my mistake) but even though TA sections I learned a lot. Any mistakes made are completely the student's fault, yet he is still willing to help. Would definitely recommend.

He's a very nice guy who's extremely willing to help you. He's also very approachable. The tests were very similar to the homework and recitation work sheets so I always knew what to expect. His lecture can be a tiny bit boring and confusing but the material isnt hard to learn if you liked/were good at cal 1. I would definitely take his class again
Favorite professor at Tech.

By far my favorite calc professor I've had at Tech! His lectures can be confusing, just like most math professors at Tech, but they're straight from the book so you can reference that for clarity. Doing problems in the book really helps because they're similar to his test questions. Grading is pretty lenient. Also very friendly and knowledgeable.
Spends a lot of time on proofs and is very abstract. Talks like a textbook. Very hard to pay attention in class, but he knows his stuff. I learned everything in recitation and doing the homework.
Great teacher and very friendly
He doesn't get how to explain material clearly. If you want to do well or even pass you need to do a lot of work on your own, or hope for a great TA.
He is a great guy but this is too hard of a class.

I extremely recommend reading the free textbooks he provides. Proofs is a hard class, and this helps to give a good background on a lot of the information in the class and shows example problems. The class is very test-weighted with two 20% exams and one 40% final. Lectures are dense, but the professor is knowledgeable and helpful.

Good lectures that teach you how to think about proving things and provide an excellent introduction to the foundations of higher math. Lectures are intense and pretty quickly-paced, but enjoyable if you pay attention and go to class. 2 midterms are 20% each, final is 40%, and they aren't easy, but definitely doable. HW is difficult but helpful.

2106 was my first entirely-conceptual math class, so I struggled at the beginning. Dr. Zeng explains things intuitively and that's ideal for someone like me. He is also very reachable and cares about his students. Don't miss class though, lectures are dense. Exams are usually similar to practice. If you know you're a good student, you'll be happy.

Lectures are well-planned, dense, and interesting--you miss a lot if you skip a day of class, but the stuff you cover in class is well reflected in tests. Prof. Zeng emphasizes the thinking process that gets gets you to conclusions, which can be tricky to master but helps with doing well on the homework and tests. Ask questions if you're lost!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor. Sometimes you will get lost during lectures, but he welcomes questions and treats class more like a discussion. Multiple times during class I felt like my brain was being expanded with some really cool knowledge. Sample tests are very similar to the actual test so study those and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was really hard, but Zeng does his best to teach thoroughly and make things interesting. Definitely one of the better mathematics lecturers I've had. His structuring of the class feels very intuitive and his notes are very thorough.

While his lectures are fast paced and condensed, I was able to familiarize myself with the concepts fairly well. He may seem a bit intimidating but he actually grades quite mercifully, giving out quite a bit of partial credits. Midterm + final make up 80% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: professor Zeng is a really good professor. He is very mathmaticaly precise and can often catch your false thinking process. Lectures are pretty dense, which is good. And is covered for all levels of difficulty. I felt my mind is stretched and start to realise what I need to improve in my logical thinking as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is an okay lecturer, sometimes hard to understand. If you want to be successful reading and understanding the textbook could be your best bet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, this is one of the most frustrating classes and professors I have ever had. Zeng is a terrible lecturer so if you want to survive you must be good at reading textbooks. I am good at math, but I spend almost 10 hours weekly on this class. The prof seems to assume you have a lot of background knowledge and doesn't explain much.

Prof. Zeng spent most lectures on proofs and derivations, whereas homework/exams were computational based. You basically had to learn by yourself from the textbook, which was a tough task. The exams didn't contain any surprises not covered by the homeworks, and were graded leniently, but my final grade of 87.4 was NOT curved to an A. Beware.

Dr. Zeng understands the material well, and can often convey it well. Occasionally, he fails to motivate a proof or derivation properly. Many times in lecture, he would write long proofs/derivations that were relevant to the material but not covered by the exams. Tests and homework is largely computational.

I took his class (reluctantly) after having him for pdes and hating it. However, with lower expectations, I actually ended up enjoying the class. Homeworks are straight forward and time commitment is minimal. Exam and final turn up the heat a ton, and he tends to grade pretty harshly. Also half of your grade being decided by a final sucks but alas

I took both 4347 and 4541 with him. Just an unhelpful professor. Lectures didn't make any sense, and office hours were not very helpful either. I ended up learning just about everything from the textbook. Grading is more or less lenient. Definitely avoid if you can.

Overall just unhelpful. The lectures were just the textbook but it still made no sense. I excepted it to relate to ODEs, but I found myself completely lost in every lecture. The one midterm (26%) and one final (50%) were all computations, even though he spent his lectures on proofs. With any other professor, I think I could've been fine.

The test looks like the homework, so if you can understand the homework, you'll be fine. He's not a good lecturer, but I had Josh as my TA and he was amazing. What a dude. To study I just went over the homeworks and the math plus worksheets because that's the test with slightly different numbers. It was pretty minimal work for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Zeng is a pretty good professor. He is very clear about the material he is covering in each lecture, and what will be covered on exams. Exams themselves are graded quite leniently. He recognizes that the material (for this class atleast) is very difficult, so he ends up giving tons of partial credit even if you get the question completely wrong.

You need to either read the textbook or be able to follow his lectures, which sometimes lost me. He does not provide additional study resources beyond the textbook problems, which don't always have answers. Homework is not graded, but there are pop quizzes, usually a problem from the homework. Textbook problems were harder than the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The 2 midterms had 3 ?s each. If you do every practice ? from the textbook you'll be fine. No one goes to lecture - it's a waste of time. Pop quizzes (which are basically weekly but are unannounced) will be the hardest questions from the textbook that was assigned from hw. It's open note so do the hw. A GT prof's youtube videos taught me concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor to take differential equations with. Absolutely useless. 7 pop quizzes, homework not for a grade. Have fun teaching yourself if you unfortunately get in his section.

Basically he is like the energizer bunny - never stops talking through the entire lecture. Throws so much info at you that you will almost inevitably get lost. Reading the textbook is significantly more helpful than lecture. Quizzes are homework questions and open notes though. He's a really nice guy but try to avoid his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Zeng is very mathematically precise. Im not sure about 2000 level classes and below, but for 4581 (basically a Fourier series and PDEs class), he was very very good. Lectures were insightful and almost cinematic. The few homework assignments given were large, but doable if you started on time. One con: not too helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are mediocre. I learned almost everything through recitation, PLUS sessions (go to these always), and 1 to 1 tutoring. Final is worth 40% of the grade. All  quizzes are open book/notes and the problems come directly from the homework so do the homework beforehand. Not the worst class to take but if you see another option... well...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. If you do though... be ready to read the book. Going to lectures is useless. Recitation and the book is incredibly useful. Seriously. Tests do come straight from the homework though, so that's nice. Get ready for a lot of stress and a lot of work.
He's good if you know math already. If not, well...
A very stressful class because of the obscurity in lectures.

Professor that knows what he talks about, it's just that you will likely be unable to understand the things he is trying to say (mostly irrelevant derivations).  The textbook is absolutely ESSENTIAL to the course.  Attendance? Not mandatory at all. Go to recitation and study from book and you will pass.

I'd avoid Zeng if at all possible. He's smart and clearly knows math, he simply has no idea how to teach it. He has a tough accent to understand and can be really confusing. If you get him, I wouldn't go to lecture, but simply read the book (it's honestly a lifesaver) and go to recitation.

Dr. Zeng is a very nice man and he is understanding and sometimes funny in lectures. Unfortunately, he rushes through a lot of problems without explaining them and for some people his accent is hard to understand. I would recommend changing professors if you can't understand him. If that is not an option, then be ready to do a lot of self learning.
He knows his stuff, but its very difficult to understand him.

Teaches too fast and he is hard to understand. For some reason, we had pop quizzes right after lecture. We didn't go over the material in recitation before the quizzes which resulted in low scores. Also, he will give the hardest problems for quizzes. Lecture is useless (atleast for me). Be prepared for a lot of self learning and unnecessary stress.

I had this guy 2403(Diff. EQ) and his class was really difficult. The Class average on quizzes which account for 24% of your final grade was about 60% while the class average on Exams which counts for 36% of your grade was around 50%. This was byfar the most unnecesarily difficult math class I've taken in a class that should have been easy.

This guy didn't really know what he was doing.  First exam was really hard and second one was ridiculously easy.  I recommend skipping the lecture as they are basically a waste of time.  Just study on your own and go to recitation.  His class was pretty easy overall

He rushes through things and makes everything very complex and you can't understand him very well. I basically learned everything from myself and the TA in recitation. I would highly recommend another if available

Took Prof. Taylor's POL1101 back in Fall 2021. For a subject I don't really care for, Taylor made it surprisingly enjoyable. He does a great job making lectures interesting and he's far from monotone. He felt really overqualified for teaching the class but still did a great job explaining anything students didn't understand.
Super nice guy, very engaging lectures, the exams are not always reflective completely of the class lecture content.

I think this class was enjoyable to take as someone who is not majoring in this field but am generally interested in American politics. The class, at least for the past semester, was graded purely on about 10 multiple-choice quizzes. It's not a super difficult class if you actually listen during lecture and read the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taylor makes this class so unnecessarily hard. Grades are made up of 8 quizzes and the final - every quiz question is annoyingly specific, which makes it almost impossible to do well on these quizzes. The class is decently easy to get a B in, but extremely difficult to get an A in. Take any other professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really good choice
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Taylor is a very good professor who definitely knows his stuff, and makes the class super interesting. I learned a lot from the course. His main downfall is that he tends to make students feel badly if they don't understand the material which makes it difficult to ask him questions/makes you feel incompetent.
Just finished this course. Learned a ton of very useful real-world stuff about politics. Every student at Georgia Tech should take this course. EVERY. STUDENT.

As the class is recorded and provided online the professor gives ridiculous amounts of papers to read. I took 16 credits for the semester, however, this class acts as if it has 5-6 credits. Too much time needed to invest in this class makes it obnoxious that you can't focus or have sufficient time for other classes as well.

Great class! Took him in 2021 when its been difficult to say anything political without getting cancelled. But Taylor dove right into the controversial stuff. He made it really interesting. Online office hours usually turned into REALLY interesting debates. And he was never biased or disrespectful...I even "won" a few arguments, lol.
Great lecturer! Really makes politics and history interesting. I hate political science and didn't expect much going into this class. But sometimes it blew my mind.
Uses async classes to get away with assigning disproportionate amounts of work. How exactly am I supposed to read a 90 page pdf in the 50 minute timeslot for a class? Tests are very vaguely worded.

- He is always fair when grading - He will either give a lot of feedback or almost none - May say things that tend to may make one uncomfortable (regardless of context) - (And my personal favorite) "Thought Pieces" - short weekly writings where he essentially grades how well you thought about something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Taylor is a tough grader, especially because it is difficult to figure out what he personally views as a good answer to a question. By the end of the class it became clear that he does not want your opinion or analysis, he wants answers directly from the reading and that's it. Blah. He also has a habit of talking down to students. Disappointing.

His lectures are interesting, but not related to the "quizzes" at all. He assigns way too much homework for one week (readings, recordings, articles, etc). We had a total of 10 quizzes (basically tests), and they came straight from the study guides, but he wanted very specific answers. If you have a question about the study guide, he won't answer.

Very lenient with due dates but a very tough grader. Some weeks were manageable: recorded lectures and a short paper answering a prompt related to the lecture. Some weeks though, it felt like a four-credit hour class. Had to read a book in one week 2x, long reports for a midterm paper, and even more reports for final project. All in all, too much!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This guy is just a real dude, he gets that you got other things to do. If you pay attention in lectures and kinda do the reading, you are set for an A. Tests rely on pretty specific answers so even though he doesn't take attendance, show up to lectures if you wanna do better on the tests.
What a guy
Loved his class. Taylor loves what he teaches and it comes off in the lectures. Definitely makes an intro Gov't class way more interesting than a bunch of facts about the branches of government.

Dr. Taylor is super passionate throughout all his lectures which helps make govt interesting for everyone regardless of their major. The readings are very diverse and the study guides make the class manageable. Highly recommend

Dr. Taylor is one of the best lecturers I've had at Tech. Grading is clear from the beginning of the semester, and is fairly easy to get an A or B. Taking his class is an excellent way to get a good introduction to American government and why it is relevant as a college student. He is very caring about each one of his students. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love his lectures but his grading is really rough or maybe it was just the TA being a tough grader. The class is based of quizzes and final exam. His lectures are not the most useful for the quizzes, but his lectures are really enthusiastic and interesting.

Best lecture class I've had at Tech, period! It wasn't clear whether attendance was mandatory, but I found myself going to almost every class. Just really freakin' interesting. And yup, it's totally easy too.
his overall quality is 4.4? interesting haha ..

This class is an easy B, but a very hard A. There are 10 quizzes with most of them being short answer and 3 of them being multiple choice. He sends out a study guide before each, but it's still very difficult as you must give the exact answer he wants or zero points. An A for the course was 80+. B was 70-80, C 60-70, and so on. He does not round.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taylor is the freaking bomb. Best teacher at Tech. You don't HAVE to go to class, but if you want an enjoyable day - go to his class. Put all your crap away and listen to what he is saying. He is so interesting.

Would definitely recommend Prof. Taylor. His lectures can get boring, but you don't really need to take notes to pass. His study guides are very, very similar to the quizzes. At the end, he ended up giving a generous curve. The book is helpful but definitely not required to get a good grade. He also posts all of his lecture slides on t2.

Easy A. Do the study guides for each quiz, and you'll be fine. At the end of the semester, he gave everyone a letter grade higher (A80-100, B70-80, C60-70, etc.) The lectures are interesting, but you can easily find/learn the material without going to lecture.

Professor Taylor was honestly the best lecturer I've had so far at Tech. He kept it extremely upbeat and easy to pay attention to. The quizzes weren't hard at all as long as you did the study guide the night before. He ended up curving the class by ten points at the end. Really an awesome professor, easy on the eyes too.

He's a really great lecturer and always helpful with the course content. Gave a 5 point curve at the end, and thats why my score went up to an A. provides study guides for the quizes which are similar to the quizes, but need to study every material. I found the quizes very difficult, and there are easier classes for US Govt. perspective.
4 words: Best professor at Tech! Seriously. (OK fine, I did think the textbook was kinda average, but at least he kept it brief and inexpensive).

He's fantastic at giving lectures. You will not fall asleep when he teaches. Make sure you pay attention in class- a lot of the material he goes over will be on the quizzes. He gives a huge curve at the end of the semester- if you have and 80 or above you will get an A. There are 8 quizzes and 1 final-that's all the class is based on.
Amazing teacher, really opened up my world view with his lectures and examples. Easy tests because he gives study guides before hand.

Great lecturer and cool class. Gives out study guides before each test, and the test questions are pretty much the exact same questions from the study guide. I forgot we had a test once, and I still made an 16/20. Not too much reading. Didn't need to take notes, just studied the powerpoints after class. Pay attention in class though.
Fun, high energy lectures. Good discussion leader and responsive to Q&A. Does a good job of tying the class to the real world. Big focus in this class was professional writing skills, totally useful!

Great lectures, and lecture notes are posted online. Really strict about his rules (no electronics, can only miss 3 classes), but they aren't bad to follow. The quizzes can trip you up, but he provides a really thorough study guide. Provides relevant, currant examples. Pretty hot in a nerdy way. Knows gov isn't top priority with students. No HW.
Usually a fun interesting lecturer. Tries to make it relevant to real world. Assignments are doable, not too heavy, but you still gotta think. Agree with the hot comment, lol
Good lecturer, really makes it interesting and real-world. Tests are easy as long as you study and use his studyguides

Great lecturer. I thought the class would be really dull & boring, but its become one of my favorites. Tests are hard, lots to read and understand. But prof provides studyguides that are totally on point. Otherwise, never bends the rules. Hot! Wish he'd lecture just once with his shirt off, lol.
awesome teacher made history and economics fun. tests are easy as long as you answer all quiz review sheets questions not to many since he has 20 question test. little no real homework
He's tough but really good. Made world politics and economics interesting for a change. Most useful class I've had in a while.
One-third of the class had D or F.  Gives tests during Dead Week.
Yuck.  Good professor but grading is completely unpredictable.  My first C.
No Comments
She was just okay. Very tough grader does not miss ANYTHING and little to no lenience. There's no reason to avoid her, but just was not my favorite, and there are more chill professors.

she's a really good professor but she grades REALLY harshly. when they say you can't miss anything from the rubric your REALLY cannot miss anything from the rubric. make sure your group has the same work all around consistently and always tell your group mates when you change something because it WILL affect their grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Zerbe for BMED1000 and really appreciated her engagement and enthusiasm in the class. She genuinely seemed to want us to succeed in the course and beyond and has made me more excited for what my future in BME could hold.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BMED 1000 isn't a hard class, and Dr. Zerbe is great.

I took BMED 1000 with Dr. Zerbe and thought she was great. The class itself wasn't my favorite, but she clearly cared about all of us and was passionate and knowledgeable. All of her expectations with assignments are clearly laid out in rubrics and you have opportunities to resubmit work if you really mess it up. Overall great prof!
Shes a good professor. The class is very group project heavy and is graded by a few things, which she can be a little tough on. Very nice person, good for advice as well!

Made it clear how each unit was supposed to contribute to something broader. Some of the assignments felt redundant but none of them were hard. If you get a good group (they're randomly assigned at the beginning) then it's light

The professor is chill and passionate about what she teaches. The class is fine, but be careful of due dates since they don't post those on Canvas. You're responsible for submitting the assignments on time, but figuring out when is confusing.
Dr. Zerbe was a good professor. She was understanding and passionate about the field. The class, however, did not have due dates on canvas so it was a bit difficult to keep and turn in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kind lady, but not good at teaching.

One of the worst professors I have taken at this school. Her lectures are soo bad that most of the students decide to attend other professors' lectures or just not attend at all. I learned the entire course from the slides of other professors' lectures and YouTube. She also wants to grade everyone harshly. It's an easy class but just don't take her
She's a sweet cat lady, but not good at lecturing. I would go to another lecturer's lectures or just study from Howard's notes.

Probably the best professor at Georgia Tech. Don't let the past reviews scare you, but she was very caring for the students and gave extensions and explained homework clearly. Lectures were a bit confusing but textbook helped a lot.
Also, she let the class choose another time for the final for those watching the World Cup. Best professor there is!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really sweet woman, but lectures were awful (disorganized and did not tell us what we needed for the exam in the correct format). Ended up not attending after the first week and learned everything I needed to know from TAs and recitation. Choose Ronnie Howard if you can!

This professor simply does not know what she is talking about. I'm sure she's smart and all, but she just doesn't care about this class. She struggles to solve problems that are on her lecture slides. You won't learn from the lectures; you'll need to rely on the textbooks to go through this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless you get the good professor. The teacher is so bad that I lose my understanding of concepts when i attend lecture. She doesn't know how to teach well and stumbles over her own examples. The graders are so bad. They take off half the question if you don't have the exact answer. write a step that's one word off and minus 5
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were confusing and not very helpful when it came to the homeworks and quizzes. The textbook is alright, though. The quizzes were horrible and not representative of what we covered in class. However, Dr. Zegura did take student feedback and the quizzes improved. She is nice but not a great professor.

Lectures are broad and the homeworks take hours since the problems' concepts are not presented in depth in class and the textbook is weak in that area too. TAs are also quite unresponsive. She is very caring though and does curve at the end.

The class was poorly structured and very difficult. The TAs didn't have a rubric to grade projects and we were provided little to no guidance. She put things on quizzes that she said weren't going to be on quizzes. Please spare yourself and take this class with the other professor.

Very poorly organized class. Material on quizzes did not reflect material from lectures, and there was not near enough time. Projects were difficult, with little to no guidance. TAs rarely available. Class overall is genuinely one of the worst I have taken so far as far as structure goes.
You cant give quizzes with content completely different from from course covered in class and in the textbook

She does teach in a way which didn't really help me with the quizzes but reading textbook early does make you understand the concepts really well. So I used the lecture as means to fill in the gaps. She is genuinely caring and engages with class well. She doesn't make projects or homeworks so no help there but class will require effort overall.

Lectures were broad overviews of different concepts, with almost no examples of actually using them; the few examples that are used are oversimplified examples that often don't even show the unique situations you have to consider when approaching complex problems. Textbook helps a little, but still doesn't explain things to the complexity required
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were quite boring and long. We started with a full class but ended with 5 people showing up to class. The exams themselves were super easy, and she made the course easy, but it can be really boring at times and the homework's are almost impossible unless you go to class and she does it in- front of you.
Very nice. Cares about students and grades. Tests are similar to practice questions and homeworks.

She is such a nice professor, and there is extra credit along the way. The topics are difficult and the lectures are LONG (and not well organized, in my opinion). If you do the homework and study for the tests, you'll be fine, but it isn't necessarily a walk in the park.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The concepts are already generally difficult (imo) by themselves, but paired with long/uninteresting lectures was kind of brutal. The homeworks were extremely lengthy and the exams pulled heavily from the textbook (which is wild considering how many slides she uses). She is nice and there was a good curve, but still would not recommend this class.

Not really big in ITM so a bit biased on lectures, but Prof. Zhu can be mundane. HW & minis are pretty fair; sometimes lectures will go into them, other times you need to read the Module, but they're not impossible. Theory tests were slides & textbook heavy & can be tedious, but SQL & Excel tests were easy. Dates were all over the place though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's really sweet but her lectures are all over the place, the homework's take forever because you have to look up how to do everything, and half the exam questions aren't from the lectures nor the textbook (literally had no clue what half the concepts were). She also takes attendance out of spite when there aren't a lot of people in class.
Denied my accommodations with Office of Disability Services. Overall, a bad professor. Doesn't know how to teach or communicate. Should have chose a different profession.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I deeply disliked this professor. She is such a sweet person, but she was the worst professor I've EVER had. I could NOT understand her accent no exaggeration. This has never been an issue for me. She grades randomly (attendance), her instructions are unclear, and she is scattered. Fast paced lecture. Save the headache. Take ONLINE or w/ diff prof

Very easy class and the exams are the exact questions as the practice questions. Also just 5 easy homeworks throughout the semester that can be with a partner. Only reason for a 4 is her accent and sometimes quick explanations, but you can always go back and read the slides after class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's pretty buns ngl. Absolutely horrible at teaching technical skills, just flys through a slide deck then expects you to complete 2 hws and tests. She is very smart and nice but not good @ teaching. hard to understand The classes she teaches aren't that hard but I would have really enjoyed the class and been more engaged if she wasn't my teacher

40 mins of the lecture is on things we'll never touch on again/ never tested on. HW + "mini" assignments took 5 years to do. LOTS of effort for a 2000s level class. it's pretty hard to understand what is going on and there are 100+ slides per lecture. she also takes forever to update slides so if you have to redownload them every lecture T.T

Great class and amazing professor! She is knowledgeable, and her lectures are organized and easy to follow. A good portion of test problems are based on class slides, making it manageable to prepare. She is always willing to help answer questions and offer extra credits, so it's not hard to get an A.

At least when I took the class her lectures were very unhelpful, by the end of the year there was pretty much nobody in class. You will end up teaching yourself just about everything, but the tests aren't too difficult so its not that bad. Half the tests are just over the slideshows and the other half you will have to learn to use excel or SQL.

Most of the exams were based off the textbook. Be prepared to teach yourself some of the information. The homework does not go along with the lessons, and you have to search up most of it. Gave a lot of extra credit tho. Failed some of the exams, and ended the class with a B.

This class really put me through it all semester. I enjoyed the coding sections of the class, but the theory was a lot to keep up with and the lectures were boring. On the other hand, Mingxi was helpful with homework and generous with extra credit. I got Cs on three of my tests (including the final) and I still somehow got an A in the class.
She is a very kind professor. Very willing to help students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Agree that the first review is off the mark. Course covers a lot of material but is presented well and examined fairly in my opinion. Homeworks can be tough but the professor often stayed extra to help students with it. You should skim the textbook for bolded vocabulary like your told, but a lot of the exam material is from lectures.

The other rating is completely wrong: this was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken at Scheller. All tests are multiple choice which are easy As granted you study the slides. I only went to a few lectures and have put in minimal effort for an A. It might be slightly harder if you've never coded, but the SQL and Excel you learn is very simple.

As other reviews have mentioned, lectures are not helpful. This semester, Dr. Zhu began his unit by saying that he had put the slides into AI to generate AI lectures for us to watch. He noted that some of it is incorrect so we should use our better judgement to know what is right. After 4 lectures, less than a quarter of the class was attending

One of the worst professors I have EVER had. Do NOT take him if you have the option. He could not care less about the students and their understanding of the material; his lectures are trash and the syllabus is ridiculous. The midterms and final are weighted ridiculously heavily and does not measure what was taught accurately at all.

Ineffective lectures. The grading schemes for quizzes and tests are not representative of processes taught in class, and zero consistency in what's important to understand. TAs are unhelpful and often misleading. Average on half the assignments was under 40% Never have I felt less control over my grades in a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. He made our test too long on purpose, then told us in an announcement that it was designed not to be finished in our allotted time. His lectures are terrible as he faces the board and lectures to himself. The slide decks have to be downloaded to PowerPoint and rearranged for viewing. Tech BME

He is smart and knows what he is talking about, however he is horrible at getting everyone else to understand that. He is tough to understand, and his explanations are never detailed enough to actually give you s good understanding. This whole class is so badly structured I am shocked it is still allowed to progress the way it has been.
Smart and nice, but not a good teacher. The other posts are true.

He is rude, unfair, and he lies. He was grading prof for a study abroad lab (not PI). Was taking full load and wanted research but worried it was too much. He said if you show up you get an A. He gave me a C. When asked why, he said so I would come in. Changed to B but refused A becuz that's for above and beyond. Much more to this but word limit.

Lectures were super dry and confusing - in some cases, students were better off not attending lecture in order to receive a better grade. I only survived because I had Costas Arvanitis for PSS and a supportive TA. Try to get another prof for biomechanics!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
It's awful. Exams are weighted very heavily and the questions on the exams were not representative of any of the material we were given, especially for the second and final exams.
Quite frankly it sucked. Also very unclear on how the class will be curved and the class needs to be curved since almost everyone had failing grades going into the final.

He is extremely difficult to understand and his lectures are super complex. he shows slides with about 10 transitions each and he doesn't really explain what he's presenting. he'll give a super complex example with several derivatives and just click through it in like 30 seconds. you have to do a ton of work outside the class for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Zhu, although very informed in his course material, is often defensive and attacks students for disagreeing with quizzes and exam questions. He expects students to be as well-equipped and informed as the TAs but lacks proper direction in lecture. Lecture is very non-engaging and focused on supplementary material instead of test material.

Just dont take this professor for your own sanity. The class feels like a battlefield, the professor vs. the students. Good luck giving him any constructive feedback on his exams or the course overall, he wont hear students out. Lacks motivation to actually teach, speeds past the math of all example problems and expects you to make sense of it.

Dr. Zhu might be the worst professor I've ever had in the BME department. His lectures are so dry and hard to follow. He gave us questions on our tests that were literally impossible to solve and refused to curve. I also went to office hours and he did not at all want to help us understand the course material, and was frankly a jerk. Don't take him

Decent professor. Cares for his students. Wants his students to understand. One of the best professors that I have in BMED. YOU SHOULD DO ALL THE HW AND THE PRACTICE TESTS!!! HE LIKES TO REPEAT PROBLEMS!!

If you have the choice take this professor. He is super flexible about finding a time to meet for extra help, he genuinly care about helping you. Yes thermo is extreamly hard but if you go to class, and reach out for help, dr. ziegler makes it managable.

It's a very difficult class, and he does a good job with managing your expectations about this class. The grading criteria is very forgiving with homework moreso for credit, and generous curving when the exam average is low. It's pretty lecture heavy, which is fine in the beginning but when content gets complicated it's easy to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ziegler is a great lecturer! His initial tests were difficult due to length and conceptual understanding. However, the final was extremely fair and he always took feedback on how to do better. His lecture slides were awesome study resources! He is also very kind and always willing to talk you through a concept or answer any questions.

As a whole, Dr. Ziegler is amazing. While his initial exams were difficult, it was his first time teaching. His exams focus on conceptual understanding, and were very long There were no questions that covered topics that weren't covered in lecture. Furthermore, Dr. Ziegler is an amazing lecturer, and his slides are very thorough.

I loved Dr. Ziegler! He is so passionate about learning and helping his students. His tests were extremely hard, but this was also his first time teaching. By the end of the course he was starting to get the hang of how to write tests that wouldn't be impossibly long that also had a good balance of conceptual and not problems. He curved heavily.

Really engaging lectures and fun class discussions. Most work you do will require peer reviews, but the feedback was very helpful and effectively improved my work. 

My favorite instructor for the semester

Overall great professor. We did all our artifacts extremely fast compared to other English classes, which sucked a little during the semester, but you'll be thankful when you have virtually no English work during finals time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Huesing was an amazing 1102 professor. She genuinely cares about her students and knows how to make things interesting. She's very easy to talk to if you have any concerns. The class wasn't difficult, and there are about 5 major assignments (like the rest of the 1102 classes). Just follow the rubric and listen to feedback, and you'll do well!
A super cool and very fun professor whose class topics are actually interesting (we studied stuff like the matrix, black mirror, and westworld)! She's a super easy grader too
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Huesing was every enthusiastic and her class topic was more interesting than the other 1102 classes. The class was also graded very easy. As long as you put in some effort in following the rubric, you will receive an A on everything. Dr. Huesing also gave us sweets on her birthday; she is a very kind professor.

Dr. Huesing was very easy to communicate with, even outside of class she responded to my emails really quickly (same day) which made it easier to ask questions. She would give a lot of constructive feedback as well when we turned in a draft or even our final project. The topic of science fiction in class was really fun too!

Dr. Huesing was a great English teacher to take. Very easy class and kept the lectures light and humorous. Gave great feedback on all artifact drafts so it's hard to fail. Our course theme was Science Fiction Franchises and she even asked our class for recommendations on course themes for her next semester. Take her if you can!

Dr. Huesing is a great professor! She cares a lot about every student and tries to make her class as easy as possible. The lectures were pretty chill, she gave us lots of time to finish our main assignments, and the homework was minimal. She was also super helpful when we started creating our final portfolios.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! She's so kind and really cares about her students. The class discussions were interesting and there were a total of 3 assignments along with the final portfolio for the semester. The assignments weren't too strenuous and she made sure we didn't procrastinate. The theme was also really great, mine was sci-fi! Take her if you can!
Amazing professor. She is super funny and caring. Doesn't give much homework besides the main projects. She also has the best themes for ENGL 1102, which was science fiction for me.
This dude is awesome. I literally just made a RMP account to give him a review. Take. His. Class

Amazing prof and extremely qualified. Made me super interested in the course material. There were a lot of films to watch, but class time is usually discussion based and he is very nice and funny. Great atmosphere and the classmates bonded a lot through this class.

Prof Zinman is super sweet and funny, and he knows a lot about film and what he's teaching. The only weekly work is blogging, and he outlines exactly what's on the midterm and final. You learn a lot of info about film and how to analyze film sequences but if you pay attention, you'll know exactly what he's looking for on tests. Super fun class!

Dr. Zinman is an absolute gem of a professor. He truly cares about his class and is an amazing lecturer. In addition, his class is also very intriguing and easy to get an A in. If you are looking to knock out your humanities, take this man's class. You won't regret it.

My favorite professor I've had at Tech so far. It really shows that he is involved in the field and the local film scene. I always really loved the lectures and discussions we had in class, more than any other class I've had. Everyone was super engaged.
Great guy, great professor
He is a great researcher but his teaching style is a bit off !!

First-class professor at Tech.  One statement of caution though: Be prepared to work/study very hard.  He claims he doesn't curve, although the test1 avg was ~35 and test2 a 50 even... BUT, he is a very smart man with a great track record, so if you want to learn one of the more difficult classes in AE, I'd recommend Ben Zinn
Extremely intelligent, though can be a bit condescending sometimes.

This was supposed to be an easy class but he randomly changed the course load to be extremely hard. No prerequisites but used multi-variable calculus and a graduate-level textbook. Nice guy but a terrible teacher. Luckily, he realized it was too hard and curved us to an A. Would recommend you don't put yourself through this.

Honestly I need to give props to Professor Zou because he really tried his best to make this newly revised (and much harder) class as easy to digest as possible. His handwriting was a little hard to read if you sit in the back of the class, and sometimes it's easy to get lost in his lectures, but he puts in a lot of effort to help each student.

First time teaching a revised and significantly harder course. The main problem is that he sometimes doesn't fully grasp the content during lectures, going down tangents for the math behind statistics without building strong foundations. Other than that, he is accessible outside of class and takes time to go over content he isn't confident in.
