reviews.comment: this professor is very considerate of students needs and very lenient with grading policy, however, since the class was freshly redesigned and this prof is new to teaching it, it was pretty self-guided since the slides weren't very comprehensive and included very few examples. but homework was for completion and he spells out what is on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a difficult class, but Hoaqian deeply cares about his students. His first time teaching a new course, and it showed. He sometimes can breeze through slides, but when he gives practice exams in class to prepare for the real exams, you'll do much better. He gives partial credit on the exams, and curves them so the average is around an 80.

Parisa is one of the best professors in the ISYE department. She is caring, understanding, accessible, and fair. The class grade was 50% midterms, 25% homework, and 25% final project. The midterms were fair. The homework assignments were fairly easy and took 1-3 hours to complete. There is a final project instead of a final that is not too bad.

Her lectures can be a little monotonous and aren't terribly engaging; however, her worked examples are very helpful. She's extremely responsive to emails, but not to Piazza. She is a very sweet professor and wants to see you succeed. Tests are not bad at all, but you MUST work practice problems for the first midterm. It will help you tons.

Not too hard of a class, just watched lectures every week and got a corresponding HW that didn't take too long. Asynchronous lectures made it not too engaging but over a good class and I learned a lot! Test wasn't bad and group project to take place of a final was pretty easy

She was not extremely engaging during the lecture, but office hours were really helpful, and she is a joy to work with. Her expectations are clear, and she is always a joy to work with. You will learn in her class, lecture engagement is probably the only drawback, but it was not even a big deal, in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Galil seems nice enough, but I did not understand his lectures at all. They are hard to follow. I simply went to class because attendance was mandatory. Exams and HW are doable but graded harshly so make sure you get your answers verified at OH. I will end up with a very easy A but I admit I learned absolutely nothing from lecture.

yes it's an easy A and exams are take home. but if u want or care about learning any content then ure better off reading the text or watching yt videos. he doesn't speak clearly, his hand writing is awful, no slides, low engagement, shows little interest in lctrs. i wish i had more room to give details but he is probably the worst prof at GT

Professor was a great lecturer! Some people say his accent is heavy but I personally found him easy to understand and his lectures were very engaging and easy to follow. This class is made up of 6 homework assignments (35%), 3 take home exams (45%), a final project (10%), and attendance (10%). Definitely recommend taking!!

People ditched lecture b/c his explanation of concepts was garbage. Exams were really hard and took a whole day to complete. The content is hard, and the TA's are barely accessible, and literally don't want to help. I'm taking this class because it's the cost you pay for doing Intelligence thread, not because I care about it.

Lectures are more or less useless, homeworks are good and informative along with the lecture notes. The exams are take home, but just about the hardest grading scheme possible. The TAs are good graders and adhere to the criteria, but the criteria literally penalizes typos. I lost 20% on an exam because I missed a '->' in one diagram.

Terrible homeworks and exams. Galil isn't as bad as Starner, but I hated the course. Do yourself a favor and don't take 4510 if you're intel but not theory. The content is utterly useless, and the stuff you learn is boring (regardless of Galil or Ladha or whoever). This course ruined my final semester at GT.

Hard to follow lectures due to accent and handwriting. One TA even told students they had enough time so he refused to help students on homework. Exams were horribly theoretical and 4510 is useless for intelligence. This class gives me flashbacks to 2200 with ramachandran. Homeworks were poorly documented and took forever to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Lectures are can be hard to understand due to his accent and handwriting. However, typed notes are posted after each class. Grading is often incredibly inconsistent and is based on the TA you get assigned to.
Honestly, I went to exactly one lecture. Fully typed notes of the lecture were posted after each lecture and his handwriting is awful. However, these notes are very good. All exams take home. Easy A.
Hella chill professor. Grade depends on test. Fairly clam tests.

His lectures were very effective and he gave lots of extra credit opportunities on homeworks, tests, and through the CIOS bonus. Difficult course, but Zongchen made the content more interesting and understandable.

A lot of the negative reviews are from the start of the first semester when he was still figuring stuff out, as the semester went on he got a lot better. His lectures are amazing to learn from (especially compared to Brito) and he gave us extra credit on HW & tests and curved EVERY test. The CIOS bonus was a 2% boost to our cumulative grade!

Yeah this class was pretty hard but Zongchen was very nice throughout the course. He gave 2 points of extra cred if we hit the CIOS goal, he made the HW category out of 680 (as opposed to the full 715 points) which is more extra cred, and he was willing to round up 89.5 (and a bit below) to an A. Tests were hard but were curved a lot.

If you are going to take him, focus on the textbook and ask chatgpt about the algorithms. I repeat, ASK CHATGPT about the algorithms. It will break them down much more effectively than the TAs who will lowkey insult your intelligence (or in my case lack thereof).

Class was initially way too hard, and people left a bunch of low reviews because of that. But they realized this midway through the semester and made the exams more fair, and gave generous curves. The psets were hard, but they prepped you pretty well for exams. A lot of very useful online resources as well. If you can self-study, you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: taking my review back, he def improved his way of teaching. I decided to go to lecture and give him a second chance and I can tell he has listen to the feedback, maybe not the best lecturer but you can tell is the first time teaching the class so obviously its not the best. based on the HW, if you can do the HW problems, you can ace the exam.

I came back to change my old review of him. He clearly changed over time and listened to feedback. I would give him a shot if you are considering taking CS 3510 - it was his first semester here and in the beginning he kind of messed up - but who hasn't?

He had a lot of resources and was a lenient grader. Problems were challenging but he gave buncha extra credit. His problems sets helped you learn and if you do the practice problems you will do good. Use chatgpt to help you learn the content when studying and go to office hours and you will do good. He didnt lecture great but was good otherwise.

Update: I initially thought this guy was insanely hard but now I am ending the semester with a exam average >100. He is an easy A if you have some mathematic intuition but still, his lectures move really slowly and you don't learn anything worthwhile. But you never have to slow up to lecture and can still do really well in this course

I don't understand all the low ratings since this course relies on what you do on your own mostly. Basically the only way to succeed is to just practice a lot which is also what he told us to do. He's helpful in OH and he curved every exam to an 83 average which he did right after the exams so we didn't have to wait for a big curve later.

The class is very hard but he is super nice! He gives so many opportunities for extra credit. As for the actual teaching, its alright. The notes are super clean to follow. It takes some time to get used to his teaching. He uses a LOT of symbols and its easy to get lost initially. The HWs are hard but set you up well for the exams.
This guy is chill. lectures are alright, but the tests are curved like crazy and they're not bad in terms of difficulty. HWs are lowk hard. Being able to grade replace/exempt the final is goated.

reviews.comment: For the first test and first couple homeworks, they were extremely challenging, but I think they got much easier down into the semester. Homeworks do take a long time but they prepare you for the tests. If you go to lectures, do homework, and read book you will do good. Also the TAs seemed fine to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class gave me a strong intuition for algorithms that will definitely be useful for technical interviews. Tests are very fair as long as you attend class. Homework is on the more difficult side, but nonetheless doable, and if you can do the homework well, then you will practically ace the exam. Well-written notes and intuitive lectures.

Midterms make up 80% of grading, but you will be fine if you show up to class, do the homeworks, and study some what liberally. The homeworks over prepare for whatever might show up on the exams. Each exam, he provides a 10 point bonus question + a potential curve. He curved the first exam by 10 points. I have no comment about the TAs though.

It's okay that its hard, but I will receive a lower grade than other people in other classes for the same level of understanding. The homeworks aren't hard if you leetcode already but if you don't it's going to be difficult. The negative TA comments also reflect my experience. They do not help you. Britto's is better for first timers.

He's not that bad if you stay on top of things. Go to lecture—it helps build a solid foundation, even if some parts are confusing at first. Office hours are super helpful for homework and clearing up concepts. Some TAs are better than others, so find the good ones. He adjusts grades fairly. Spend time understanding homework and review to do well.

Honesty 3510 is just a challenging course overall. I have never been to office hours nor lectures so I have no comment on the instructional staff. However, the hw and exams are fair not as bad as other people said. Plus, there are also a lot of extra credit opportunities.

He's really not that bad. Very sweet and willing to explain things in office hours. Lectures cover overviews of algorithms, and maybe an example, but mostly it's up to you to apply the general patterns/problem solving in HW, which I feel is reasonable. It's very doable. Exam 1 was rough, but he made them easier after. Has an accent, but idrc.

reviews.comment: To the person who gave a rating of 4 and said "yea the exams are harder than the other section but big whoop" ARE U SLOW OR WHAT? HOW IS IT FAIR THAT OUR HWs AND EXAMS ARE DOUBLE THE DIFFICULTY OF THE OTHER SECTION ALL WHILE HAVING THE WORST PROFESSOR AND TAs AT THIS SCHOOL?!?!??

Was a very hard class at first but I think he made subsequent exams easier and he gave a slight boost to HW grades. That plus the final which allows you to replace an exam makes this not super difficult. Lectures are hella boring as he simply writes down stuff, slight pause, and then says it, pause to write more stuff, says it out loud, repeat...

To the guy that says "CS students are so entitled", you're just shifting the post on what the issue is at hand. It's not that students are complaining that the class is hard, but rather the fact that the combination of reactive instructional staff, irrelevant study guides and shallow covering of any of the topics hinders any chance of success.

There's no reason a class should be this difficult. TAs are difficult to work with, questions aren't nearly representative of any level to which we learned concepts in class, and his accent is hard to understand. Content isn't covered in depth to what is covered on the homework and the exam.

Imagine if Sheldon Cooper from the Big Bang Theory taught an algorithms class. And trust me he will make one of the hardest CS classes harder on you. If you don't get britto then don't do the class. Learn from my mistakes I beg you.

I don't mind getting a bad grade. What I do mind is the TAs' attitudes to helping you. If you ask a question that shows you only 50% understood rather than 99% understood, you would be practically laughed at. I actively felt discouraged from trying. Only good one was the head TA.

First class at Tech that I withdrew. In lecture, we get shown examples of algorithms, but not how to create one generally. The TAs are pretty condescending if you're not smart like them. Looking at the other professor that teaches the same class, there doesn't seem to be as big of a fuss, so it could just be the professor/TAs. Very strict grading.

Worst class I have taken so far at Tech. I feel like I'm learning something, but then nothing at the same time. If I wanted to do leetcode I would have done it at my own time and not be stressed. The TAs are of barely any help. The exams are 80% of the grade and the rest are homeworks, of which are unnecessarily hard, and I got As on1332 and 2050.

I have seen this guy and his army of egotistical TAs defeat some of the smartest people I've ever met. Take this class with ANYONE else.
